english_verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
translation_verse: Ahyɛaseɛ ne, Nyameɛ bɔle anwuro ne aseɛ.

english_verse: The earth was barren, with no form of life; it was under a roaring ocean covered with darkness. But the Spirit of God was moving over the water. The First Day
translation_verse: Né aseɛ te sesakaa bɔ olle bɔbea biala ɔ. Né awosii akata buma ne anye; na né Nyameɛ Sunzum natenate nzue ne anyeso faa.

english_verse: God said, “I command light to shine!” And light started shining.
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ hane kyɛ, “Ɔ́ta hyireinn!” Na ɔtale hyireinn.

english_verse: God looked at the light and saw that it was good. He separated light from darkness
translation_verse: Nyameɛ nwuni kyɛ hyireinn ne te paa, na ɔtele hyireinn ne fili awosii ne anwo.

english_verse: and named the light “Day” and the darkness “Night.” Evening came, then morning—that was the first day. The Second Day
translation_verse: Nyameɛ tole hyireinn ne dumaa Alehyeleɛ, yeɛ ɔtole awosii ne dumaa Alesaleɛ. Aleɛ sane, na aleɛ hyene: kyẽa bɔ oli moa ɛne.

english_verse: God said, “I command a dome to separate the water above it from the water below it.”
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ hane kyɛ, “Ewienu bra, na ɔɔtete nzue nemɔ anu!” Na ɔwale nu sɔ.

english_verse: And that's what happened. God made the dome
translation_verse: Nyameɛ yɔle ewienu, na ɔtele nzue bɔ ɔwɔ ewienu bo fili bɔ ɔwɔ ewienu anwuro nwo.

english_verse: and named it “Sky.” Evening came, then morning—that was the second day. The Third Day
translation_verse: Nyameɛ tole ewienu ne dumaa Anwuro. Aleɛ sane, na aleɛ hyene: kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ɛne.

english_verse: God said, “I command the water under the sky to come together in one place, so there will be dry ground.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ hane kyɛ, “Nzue bɔ ɔwɔ ewienu bo ne, ɔ́boa ye noa neka horɛ, na aseɛ wosee bra!” Na ɔwale nu sɔ.

english_verse: God named the dry ground “Land,” and he named the water “Ocean.” God looked at what he had done and saw that it was good.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ tole nekaa wosee ne dumaa Aseɛ, yeɛ nzue bɔ ye noa aboa ne koso, ɔtole ye dumaa Ɛpo. Na Nyameɛ nwuni kyɛ ɔte paa.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to produce all kinds of plants, including fruit trees and grain.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ hane kyɛ, “Aseɛ ófifi ndire, mmakaa bɔ osu mmaa, ɔne mmakaa bɔ ye mma wɔ ye aleɛ nu, ebiala kyɛbɔ ye sue si te ɔ wɔ aseɛ so!” Na ɔwale nu sɔ.

english_verse: The earth produced all kinds of vegetation. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Aseɛ fifili ndire, mmakaa bɔ osu mmaa, ɔne mmakaa bɔ mmaa wɔ ye aleɛ nu, ebiala kyɛbɔ ye sue si te ɔ. Na Nyameɛ nwuni kyɛ ɔte paa.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the third day. The Fourth Day
translation_verse: Aleɛ sane, na aleɛ hyene: kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nza ɛne.

english_verse: God said, “I command lights to appear in the sky and to separate day from night and to show the time for seasons, special days, and years.
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ hane kyɛ, “Nganea bra ewienu, na bɛɛtete alehyeleɛ ne alesaleɛ bɛ nu, na bɛ́yɛ mmerɛ, ngyẽa ne afoɛ mɔ nwo nzɛngyerɛnneɛ;

english_verse: I command them to shine on the earth.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: bɛɛyɛ nganea wɔ ewienu, ná bɛta aseɛ so!” Na ɔwale nu sɔ.

english_verse: God made two powerful lights, the brighter one to rule the day and the other to rule the night. He also made the stars.
translation_verse: Yiti Nyameɛ yɔle nganea mbiri nyɔ ne, kyɛ pirikua ne oli alehyeleɛ so, na kaaba ne oli alesaleɛ so; ɔyɔle nzramaa mɔ koso.

english_verse: Then God put these lights in the sky to shine on the earth,
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ fale bɛ tuatuale ewienu kyɛ bɛta aseɛ so,

english_verse: to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: kyɛ beli alehyeleɛ ne alesaleɛ so, na bɛtete hyireinn ne awosii ne anu. Na Nyameɛ nwuni kyɛ ɔte paa.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fourth day. The Fifth Day
translation_verse: Aleɛ sane, na aleɛ hyene: kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nna ɛne.

english_verse: God said, “I command the ocean to be full of living creatures, and I command birds to fly above the earth.”
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ hane kyɛ, “Nzue ɔlɔ abɔdeɛ ahoroɔ pee bɔ bele ngoa ɔ, ná nnomaa koso bétu bɛ́fa aseɛ so wɔ ewienu!”

english_verse: So God made the giant sea monsters and all the living creatures that swim in the ocean. He also made every kind of bird. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Yiti Nyameɛ bɔle ɛpo nu ngaka mbiri mbiri ne mmaa mmaa mukoraa kyɛbɔ bɛ nu biala sue si te ɔ, ɔne nnomaa mukoraa kyɛbɔ bɛ nu biala sue si te ɔ. Na Nyameɛ nwuni kyɛ ɔte paa.

english_verse: Then he gave the living creatures his blessing—he told the ocean creatures to increase and live everywhere in the ocean and the birds to increase everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ yirale bɛ, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔwo ná ɛmɔlɔ pee, ná ɛ́mɔyi ɛpo nu tɛkyɛ; nnomaa koso ɛ́mɔta pee wɔ aseɛ so!”

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fifth day. The Sixth Day
translation_verse: Aleɛ sane, na aleɛ hyene: kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nnu ɛne.

english_verse: God made every one of them. Then he looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ yɔle aseɛ so ngaka mbiri, awuro ngaka, yeɛ ngaka mmaa ne ngaka bɔ bɛtwe bɛ nwo ase, kyɛbɔ bɛ sue si te ɔ. Na Nyameɛ nwuni kyɛ ɔte paa.

english_verse: God said, “Now we will make humans, and they will be like us. We will let them rule the fish, the birds, and all other living creatures.”
translation_verse: Afei Nyameɛ sele kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔma yɛyɔ sona kyɛ yɛ sɛso, ma osoma yɛ; ná yɛ́ma benya tumi wɔ ɛpo nu ngaka so, ewienu nnomaa so, awuro ngaka so, aseɛ amukoraa so, ɔne kaka biala bɔ ɔtwe ye nwo ase wɔ aseɛ so ɔ so.”

english_verse: So God created humans to be like himself; he made men and women.
translation_verse: Yiti Nyameɛ bɔle sona kyɛ ye bɔbɔ ye sɛso, Nyameɛ sɛso yeɛ ɔbɔle ye ɔ; ɔbɔle bienzua ne brasua.

english_verse: God gave them his blessing and said: Have a lot of children! Fill the earth with people and bring it under your control. Rule over the fish in the ocean, the birds in the sky, and every animal on the earth.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ yirale bɛ, na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔwo ná ɛmɔta, ɛ́mɔyi aseɛ so tɛkyɛ ná ɛmɔli so; ná ɛ́mɔnya tumi wɔ ɛpo nu naen so, ɔne ewienu nnomaa ne kaka biala bɔ ɔwɔ aseɛ so ɔ so.”

english_verse: And I have given the green plants as food for everything else that breathes, including animals, both wild and tame, and birds. And so it was.
translation_verse: Na kaka biala bɔ ngoa wɔ ye nu: aseɛ so ngaka mukoraa, ewienu nnomaa mukoraa, yeɛ kaka biala bɔ ɔtwe ye nwo ase wɔ aseɛ so ne, mafa nyaanyaa mukoraa mama bɛ kyɛ beli.” Na ɔwale nu sɔ.

english_verse: God looked at what he had done. All of it was very good! Evening came, then morning—that was the sixth day.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ nwuni kyɛ nningyein bɔ wayɔ ne amukoraa te paa paa. Aleɛ sane, na aleɛ hyene: kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nzia ɛne.

english_verse: So the heavens and the earth and everything else were created. The Seventh Day
translation_verse: Yiti sɔ yeɛ Nyameɛ bɔle anwuro ne aseɛ ne bɛ nu nningyein mukoraa yiele ɔ.

english_verse: God blessed the seventh day and made it special, because on that day he rested from his work.
translation_verse: Yiti Nyameɛ yirale kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nzoo ne, na ɔyɛle ye krongron, ofikyɛ ye adwuma bɔ ɔyɔle ye wɔ nningyein bɔlɛ nu ne, sɔ kyẽa ne yeɛ olele ye nwome ɔ. Eden turo ne

english_verse: That's how God created the heavens and the earth. The Garden of Eden When the Lord God made the heavens and the earth,
translation_verse: Kyɛbɔ Ɛdangama si bɔle anwuro ne aseɛ ne, ye nwo dwirɛ ɛhe. Mmerɛ bɔ AWURADE Nyameɛ bɔle aseɛ ne anwuro ne,

english_verse: no grass or plants were growing anywhere. God had not yet sent any rain, and there was no one to work the land.
translation_verse: né bakaa biala nne aseɛ so, yeɛ né ndire biala onnya offifili, ofikyɛ né AWURADE Nyameɛ onnya ɔttɔle nzue ogguale aseɛ so, yeɛ né sona biala nne berɛ bɔ ɔkɔyɔ so boo koso ɔ.

english_verse: But streams came up from the ground and watered the earth.
translation_verse: Nakoso nzue fili aseɛnwo loaloale aseɛ so amukoraa.

english_verse: The Lord God took some soil from the ground and made a man. God breathed life into the man, and the man started breathing.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyameɛ fale aseɛnwo nnɛterɛ nwone kuro sona, na olele ngoa nwomeɛ guale ye bonyi anu, na kuro sona ɔɔyɛle teasefoɛ.

english_verse: The Lord made a garden in a place called Eden, which was in the east, and he put the man there.
translation_verse: Afei AWURADE Nyameɛ yɔle turo bie wɔ Eden, bɔ ɔwɔ eyia afiteleɛ, na ɔmane biaa bɔ ɔnwone ye ne tenane berɛ.

english_verse: The Lord God filled the garden with all kinds of beautiful trees and fruit trees. Two other trees were in the middle of the garden. One of these gave life—the other gave the wisdom to know the difference between right and wrong.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyameɛ mane mmakaa mukoraa bɔ bɛyɛ nyemene ná ɔte paa kyɛ bedi ɔ fifili aseɛnwo wɔ turo ne anu; ɔmane ngoa bakaa fifili turo n’afia, yeɛ paa ne bɔne nwo nimdeɛ bakaa koso fifili nu.

english_verse: From Eden a river flowed out to water the garden, then it divided into four rivers.
translation_verse: Né asue bie tengyɛ fi Eden ba doadoa turo ne anu berɛ, na asue ne fi berɛ a, nu pakyepakye yɛ asue sa nna.

english_verse: The first one is the Pishon River that flows through the land of Havilah,
translation_verse: Bɔ oli moa ne li Pisɔn; na ɔtengyɛ pɛ Hawila aseɛ mukoraa, bɔ sikaa kɔkorɛ wɔ so ne nwo bra yia.

english_verse: The second is the Gihon River that winds through Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Asue bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ne li Gihon; na ɔtengyɛ pɛ Kuse aseɛ nwo amu bra yia.

english_verse: The Tigris River that flows east of Assyria is the third, and the fourth is the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Asue bɔ ɔtɔ so nza ne li Tigrise, na ɔtengyɛ wɔ Asiria eyia afiteleɛ. Asue bɔ ɔtɔ so nna ne li Yufreti.

english_verse: The Lord God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and to look after it.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyameɛ fale biaa ne ɔɔtenane Eden turo ne anu, kyɛ ɔyɔ nu adwuma ná ɔnea so.

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “You may eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyameɛ kanzole biaa ne kyɛ, “Ɛkora di turo ne anu bakaa mmaa biala;

english_verse: except the one that has the power to let you know the difference between right and wrong. If you eat any fruit from that tree, you will die before the day is over!”
translation_verse: nakoso paa ne bɔne nwo nimdeɛ bakaa ne de, nnɛdi bie, ofikyɛ kyẽa bɔ ekoli bie ne, ewue yeɛ ekowu ɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord God said, “It isn't good for the man to live alone. I will make a suitable partner for him.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyameɛ sele kyɛ, “Ɔtte mayee kyɛ sona ne ngome kɔtena ɔ; ngɔyɛ bokafoɛ bɔ ɔfata ye ɔ ngɔma ye.”

english_verse: So the Lord God made him fall into a deep sleep, and he took out one of the man's ribs. Then after closing the man's side,
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE Nyameɛ mane sona ne lafele hatee. Na ɔlale nen, ɔyele ye mvenu mbaleɛ ko, na ɔfale anwoɔnaen tuale ye boso.

english_verse: the Lord made a woman out of the rib. The Lord God brought her to the man,
translation_verse: Na mbaleɛ bɔ AWURADE Nyameɛ ye fili sona ne anu ne, ɔfa yɛle brasua, na ɔfale ye brɛle sona ne.

english_verse: and the man exclaimed, “Here is someone like me! She is part of my body, my own flesh and bones. She came from me, a man. So I will name her Woman!”
translation_verse: Na sona ne sele kyɛ, “Afei de, me mmowue nu bowue ne me nwonaen nu anwoɔnaen ɛhe; bɛkɔfrɛ ye Brasua, ofikyɛ Bienzua nu yeɛ bɛyele ye befili ɔ.”

english_verse: That's why a man will leave his own father and mother. He marries a woman, and the two of them become like one person.
translation_verse: Yiti bienzua kofi ɔse ne oni anwo, ná waafa ye nwo wabata ɔye, na bayɛ anwoɔnaen ko.

english_verse: Although the man and his wife were both naked, they were not ashamed.
translation_verse: Né biaa ne ne ɔye ne bɛ nwo la so, nakoso né ɔnyɛ bɛ nya.

english_verse: The snake was sneakier than any of the other wild animals that the Lord God had made. One day it came to the woman and asked, “Did God tell you not to eat fruit from any tree in the garden?”
translation_verse: Né ewoo te kanda tra eburo kaka biala bɔ AWURADE Nyameɛ ayɔ ɔ. Na obisale braa ne kyɛ, “Yiti Nyameɛ aha kyɛ, ‘Nnɛma ɛmɔdi turo ye anu bakaammaa biala bie’?”

english_verse: The woman answered, “God said we could eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Na braa ne buale ewoo ne kyɛ, “Atee wɔ berɛ kyɛ yɛdi turo ne anu mmakaammaa ne bie;

english_verse: except the one in the middle. He told us not to eat fruit from that tree or even to touch it. If we do, we will die.”
translation_verse: nakoso Nyameɛ nwa: ‘Bakaa bɔ ogyi turo n’afia ne mma de, nnɛma ɛmɔdi bie, yeɛ nnɛma ɛmɔfa bɛ sa bɛka ye. Sɛ ɛmɔdi a, ewue yeɛ ɛmɔkowu ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: “No, you won't!” the snake replied.
translation_verse: Nakoso ewoo ne sele braa ne kyɛ, “Ɛmɔngowu biala.

english_verse: “God understands what will happen on the day you eat fruit from that tree. You will see what you have done, and you will know the difference between right and wrong, just as God does.”
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ Nyameɛ se kyɛ kyẽa bɔ ɛmɔkoli bie ne, ɛmɔ nye kobukye, na ɛmɔkɔyɛ kyɛ Nyameɛ ala, na ɛmɔanwu paa ne bɔne.”

english_verse: The woman stared at the fruit. It looked beautiful and tasty. She wanted the wisdom that it would give her, and she ate some of the fruit. Her husband was there with her, so she gave some to him, and he ate it too.
translation_verse: Na braa ne nwuni kyɛ saa bedi bakaa ne mma a ɔyɛ yee, ɔyɛ nyemene, na ɔkora ma sona nwu nworɛ. Yiti ɔtele ye mma ne bie lili, ɔmane ohu ne koso bie, na ye koso olili.

english_verse: At once they saw what they had done, and they realized they were naked. Then they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.
translation_verse: Afei bɛ munyɔ bɛ nye wale bɛ nwo so, na benwuni kyɛ bɛ nwo lela so; yiti bɛpale borɔdoma nyaa bɛfa bɛkatale bɛ nwo.

english_verse: Late in the afternoon, when the breeze began to blow, the man and woman heard the Lord God walking in the garden. So they hid behind some trees. Sin Brings a Curse
translation_verse: Na aleɛ dwole ne, bɛtele AWURADE Nyameɛ gya boso kyɛ ɔnatenate turo ne anu, yiti biaa ne ne ɔye ne bɛɛfeale AWURADE Nyameɛ wɔ turo nu berɛ mmakaa ne anu.

english_verse: The Lord God called out to the man and asked, “Where are you?”
translation_verse: Nakoso AWURADE Nyameɛ frɛle biaa ne bisale ye kyɛ, “Ɛwɔ nisua?”

english_verse: The man answered, “I was naked, and when I heard you walking through the garden, I was frightened and hid!”
translation_verse: Na biaa ne buale kyɛ, “Ndele wɔ gya boso wɔ turo ne anu, na ɛserɛ hane me, ofikyɛ né me nwo la so, yiti ngɔmveale.”

english_verse: “How did you know you were naked?” God asked. “Did you eat any fruit from that tree in the middle of the garden?”
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ bisale ye kyɛ, “Nwa yeɛ osele wɔ kyɛ wɔ nwo la so ɔ? Bakaa bɔ nganzole wɔ kyɛ nnɛdi ye mma ne bie ne, ali bie hɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: “It was the woman you put here with me,” the man said. “She gave me some of the fruit, and I ate it.”
translation_verse: Na biaa ne buale kyɛ, “Braa ne bɔ ɛfale ye ɛɛbokale me so ne, ye yeɛ ɔfale bakaa ne mma ne mane me ɔ, yeɛ me koso nnili ɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord God then asked the woman, “What have you done?” “The snake tricked me,” she answered, “and I ate some of that fruit.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyameɛ bisale braa ne kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ nikye yeɛ ayɔ ye?” Na braa ne buale kyɛ, “Ewoo ne yeɛ ɔlakalakale me maa nnili ɔ.”

english_verse: So the Lord God said to the snake: “Because of what you have done, you will be the only animal to suffer this curse— For as long as you live, you will crawl on your stomach and eat dirt.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyameɛ sele ewoo ne kyɛ, “Ɔnate ɛhe bɔ ayɔ ne ati, musue to wɔ wɔ kuro ngaka mukoraa, ɔne eburo ngaka mukoraa nu. Ɛkɔhwe wɔ nwo ase wɔ ko so, na ekoli nnɛterɛ w’asetena nu amukoraa.

english_verse: You and this woman will hate each other; your descendants and hers will always be enemies. One of hers will strike you on the head, and you will strike him on the heel.”
translation_verse: Ngɔfa ɛpɔen ngɔto wɔ ne braa n’afia, yeɛ wɔ boso ama ne ye boso ama b’afia; ɔkɔgyerɛgyerɛ wɔ ti, na wɔ wora aha ye gya si.”

english_verse: Then the Lord God said to the woman, “You will suffer terribly when you give birth. But you will still desire your husband, and he will rule over you.”
translation_verse: Na braa ne wora, Nyameɛ sele ye kyɛ, “Ngɔmaa ɛkɔte aworɛ nu yealɛ paa, na yealɛ nu yeɛ ɛkɔwo mmaa ɔ. Nakoso wɔ wora kɔlɔ ehu, na okoli wɔ so.”

english_verse: The Lord said to the man, “You listened to your wife and ate the fruit I told you not to eat. And so, the ground will be under a curse because of what you did. As long as you live, you will have to struggle to grow enough food.
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ sele Adam koso kyɛ, “Kyɛbɔ atie bɔ ɛye hane, na ali bakaa bɔ nganzole wɔ kyɛ ‘nnɛdi ye mma ne bie’ ne ati, ɔnate wɔ ti, musue aha aseɛ. Na ɛfɛɛ paa yeɛ ɛkɔfɛ koraa né adidi so w’asetena mukoraa nu ɔ.

english_verse: Your food will be plants, but the ground will produce thorns and thistles.
translation_verse: Okofifi mmowue ne ɛfone kɔma wɔ, na eburo mmakaa so aleɛ yeɛ ekoli ɔ.

english_verse: You will sweat all your life to earn a living; you were made out of soil, and you will once again turn into soil.”
translation_verse: Mvifire kosongyi wɔ ti anwo koraka né anya aleɛ ali, kɔpem kyɛ ekosa kɔhɔ nnɛterɛ nu ɔ; ofikyɛ nnɛterɛ nu yeɛ nyele wɔ mvili ɔ, ɛte nnɛterɛ, na nnɛterɛ nu ala yeɛ ekosa kɔhɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: The man Adam named his wife Eve because she would become the mother of all who live.
translation_verse: Na biaa ne tole ɔye ne dumaa Hawa, ofikyɛ ɔte teasefoɛ mukoraati bɛ ni.

english_verse: Then the Lord God made clothes out of animal skins for the man and his wife.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Nyameɛ fale nwomaa pombale ɛtena mane Adam ne ɔye maa bɛherale. Nyameɛ foa Adam ne Hawa fi Eden

english_verse: The Lord said, “They now know the difference between right and wrong, just as we do. But they must not be allowed to eat fruit from the tree that lets them live forever.”
translation_verse: Afei AWURADE Nyameɛ sele kyɛ, “Nea, kuro sona ne ayɛ kyɛ yɛ nu ko ala, wanwu paa ne bɔne. Annea a, né watengyɛ ye sa wate ngoa bakaa ne koso bie wali, ná watena ase daa.”

english_verse: So the Lord God sent them out of the Garden of Eden, where they would have to work the ground from which the man had been made.
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE Nyameɛ foane ye fili Eden turo ne anu, kyɛ ɔɔyɔ kua wɔ aseɛ bɔ ɔyele ye fili nu ne aso.

english_verse: Then God put winged creatures at the entrance to the garden and a flaming, flashing sword to guard the way to the life-giving tree.
translation_verse: Ɔfoane kuro sona ne fili berɛ, na ɔfale kɛrubim, ɔne ngrandɛ bɔ ogye wuronyiwuronyi, na osa pɛ ye nwo osiele Eden turo ne nyunu wɔ eyia afiteleɛ, kyɛ ɔbɔ atee bɔ ɔkɔ ngoa bakaa ne nwo waen.

english_verse: Adam and Eve had a son. Then Eve said, “I'll name him Cain because I got him with the help of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Adam ne ɔye Hawa bɛlale, ɔnwonzɛle, na ɔwole Kein. Na Hawa hane kyɛ, “AWURADE adaworoma, mawo bienzua.”

english_verse: Later she had another son and named him Abel. Abel became a sheep farmer, but Cain farmed the land.
translation_verse: Nziɛ ye, ɔwole oliɛma bienzua Abel. Né Abel te mmoaenneafoɛ, yeɛ Kein koso te kuaniɛ.

english_verse: One day, Cain gave part of his harvest to the Lord,
translation_verse: Nziɛ ye ne, Kein fale fieso nningyein ne bie ɔɔbɔle afɔleɛ mane AWURADE.

english_verse: and Abel also gave an offering to the Lord. He killed the first-born lamb from one of his sheep and gave the Lord the best parts of it. The Lord was pleased with Abel and his offering,
translation_verse: Na Abel koso fale ye mmoaen ne anu nyii bɔ belili moa bɛwole bɛ ne, na ɔfale bɛ loe ne ɔɔbɔle afɔleɛ. Na AWURADE nye sɔle Abel ne ye afɔleɛ ne,

english_verse: but not with Cain and his offering. This made Cain so angry that he could not hide his feelings.
translation_verse: nakoso ye nye anzɔ Kein ne ye afɔleɛ ne. Yiti Kein fɛle yaa hahii, na ye wora bɔle.

english_verse: The Lord said to Cain: What's wrong with you? Why do you look so angry?
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bisale Kein kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ afɛ yaa ye? Nzu ati yeɛ wɔ wora abɔ ye?

english_verse: If you had done the right thing, you would be smiling. But you did the wrong thing, and now sin is waiting to attack you like a lion. Sin wants to destroy you, but don't let it!
translation_verse: Aso ɛyɔ bɔ ɔte paa a, engonya animnyam? Nakoso anyɔ bɔ ɔte paa ne ati, bɔne tetɛ wɔ w’anoa nu berɛ. Ɔpena kyɛ onya wɔ nwo ate, nakoso odi kyɛ edi ye so”

english_verse: Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let's go for a walk.” And when they were out in a field, Cain attacked and killed him.
translation_verse: Na Kein sele oliɛma Abel kyɛ, “Maa yɛhɔ fieso.” Na bɛwɔ fie ne aso nen, Kein hɔle oliɛma Abel so, na ohuni ye.

english_verse: Afterwards the Lord asked Cain, “Where is Abel?” “How should I know?” he answered. “Am I supposed to look after my brother?”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bisale Kein kyɛ, “Eliɛma Abel wɔ nisua?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Menze. Nniɛma ne, me yeɛ menea ye so hɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: Then the Lord said: Why have you done this terrible thing? You killed your own brother, and his blood flowed onto the ground. Now his blood is calling out for me to punish you.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ nikye yeɛ ayɔ ye? Eliɛma ne, ye mogya ɔteatea nu sũ frɛ me fi aseɛnwo.

english_verse: And so, I'll put you under a curse. Because you killed Abel and made his blood run out on the ground, you will never be able to farm it again.
translation_verse: Na aseɛ bɔ wabukye ye noa nu wano eliɛma ne mogya bɔ ɛha guale nen, musue ato wɔ wɔ so.

english_verse: When you try to farm the land, it won't produce anything for you. From now on, you'll be without a home, and you'll spend the rest of your life wandering from place to place.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛyɔ aseɛ ne aso boo a, ɔngɔhye aleɛ ngɔma wɔ ko. Ɛkɔyɛ kobɔniɛ, na engonya amandena wɔ aseɛ so.”

english_verse: “This punishment is too hard!” Cain said.
translation_verse: Na Kein sele AWURADE kyɛ, “M’asohwenɛ ne ɔbo me so.

english_verse: “You're making me leave my home and live far from you. I will have to wander about without a home, and just anyone could kill me.”
translation_verse: Ɛnɛ afoa me afi aseɛ ye aso, ngɔfa me nwo ngɔfea wɔ. Ngɔyɛ kobɔniɛ bɔ nnne amandena wɔ aseɛ ye aso ɔ, na ebiala bɔ okonwu me ne, okohu me.”

english_verse: “No!” the Lord answered. “Anyone who kills you will be punished seven times worse than I am punishing you.” So the Lord put a mark on Cain to warn everyone not to kill him.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele ye kyɛ, “Nna sɔ ɔ! Sɛ ebie ku Kein a, bɛkɔtɔ sɔ sona ne so wereɛ pɛen nzoo.” Na AWURADE hyɛle Kein nzorɛ, kyɛbɔ ɔkɔyɛ na ebie nwu ye a ongohu ye ɔ.

english_verse: But Cain had to go far from the Lord and live in the Land of Wandering, which is east of Eden. More and More People
translation_verse: Afei Kein fili AWURADE nyunu berɛ hɔle, na ɔɔtenane Nɔɔdo aseɛ so wɔ Eden eyia afiteleɛ.

english_verse: Later, Cain and his wife had a son named Enoch. At the time Cain was building a town, and so he named it Enoch after his son.
translation_verse: Kein ne ɔye bɛlale, ɔnwonzɛle, na ɔwole Henɔke. Kein kyekyele kuro bie, na ɔfale ɔwa Henɔke dumaa tole kuro ne.

english_verse: Then Enoch had a son named Irad, who had a son named Mehujael, who had a son named Methushael, who had a son named Lamech.
translation_verse: Henɔke wole Yirade, Yirade wole Mehuyael, Mehuyael wole Metusael, yeɛ Metusael wole Lamɛke.

english_verse: Lamech and Adah had two sons, Jabal and Jubal. Their son Jabal was the first to live in tents and raise sheep and goats. Jubal was the first to play harps and flutes.
translation_verse: Né oliɛma bienzua ole Yubal, bɔ ye bosofoɛ te mmenia bɔ bɛbɔ sangoo na behu awɛen ɔ.

english_verse: Lamech and Zillah had a son named Tubal Cain who made tools out of bronze and iron. They also had a daughter, whose name was Naamah.
translation_verse: Sila wole Tubal Kein, bɔ né ɔte kɔɔbere ne mmuralɛ mukoraa dwumvoɛ ne. Né Tubal Kein aliɛma brasua ole Naama.

english_verse: Anyone who tries to get even with me will be punished ten times more than anyone who tries to get even with Cain.”
translation_verse: Sɛ bɛkɔtɔ Kein so wereɛ pɛen nzoo de a, nzaade bɛkɔtɔ Lamɛke so wereɛ aburasoo ne nzoo.”

english_verse: Adam and his wife had another son. They named him Seth, because they said, “God has given us a son to take the place of Abel, who was killed by his brother Cain.”
translation_verse: Adam ne ɔye lale bieku; braa ne wole bienzua, na ɔtole ye dumaa Sɛte, ofikyɛ braa ne hane kyɛ, “Nyameɛ amaa manya baa foforɛ masi Abel bɔ Kein huni ye ne gya nu.”

english_verse: Later, Seth had a son and named him Enosh. About this time people started worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Sɛte koso wole baa bienzua, na ɔtole ye dumaa Enose. Na sɔ mmerɛ ne yeɛ mmenia hyɛle ye bo kyɛ bɛ́bɔ AWURADE dumaa bɛsɔne ye ɔ.

english_verse: God created men and women to be like himself. He gave them his blessing and called them human beings. The following is a list of the descendants of Adam, the first man:
translation_verse: Ɔbɔle bɛ bienzua ne brasua, na oyirale bɛ. Na ɔtole bɛ dumaa ‘Sona’ wɔ mmerɛ bɔ ɔbɔle bɛ ne.

english_verse: and God took him away at the age of
translation_verse: Henɔke ne Nyameɛ natele, na otu minini, ofikyɛ Nyameɛ fale ye hɔle.

english_verse: Lamech said, “I'll name him Noah because he will give us comfort, as we struggle hard to make a living on this land that the Lord has put under a curse.”
translation_verse: Ɔtole ye dumaa Nowa, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Ye yeɛ okofi aseɛ bɔ AWURADE anoma ye ne anu ɔkɔkyekye yɛ wora wɔ yɛ adwuma, ɔne ɛfɛɛ wora bɔ yɛfɛ yɛ sa nu ɔ.”

english_verse: More and more people were born, until finally they spread all over the earth. Some of their daughters were so beautiful that supernatural beings came down and married the ones they wanted.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ mma nemɔ benwuni kyɛ mmenia mma mmrasua nemɔ bɛ nwo yɛ nyemene, yiti begyigyale bɛ nu biala bɔ bekuro ɔ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “I won't let my life-giving breath remain in anyone forever. No one will live for more than
translation_verse: Na AWURADE hane kyɛ, “Me sunzum ngɔtena kuro sona nu afebɔɔ, ofikyɛ ɔte anwoɔnaen, ye afoɛ mukoraa bɔ okoli ɔ kɔyɛ ɛyaa ko ne aburanyɔ.”

english_verse: The children of the supernatural beings who had married these women became famous heroes and warriors. They were called Nephilim and lived on the earth at that time and even later.
translation_verse: Na sɔ mmerɛ ne anu, yeɛ ye si ye po, né Nefilifoɛ wɔ aseɛ so. Na ɔwale kyɛ Nyameɛ mma nemɔ bɛɛfale mmenia mma mmrasua nemɔ, na bɛ ne bɛ wowole mmaa. Na sɔ mmaa nemɔ ole daa tete anwoserɛfoɛ, mmenia bɔ belele dumaa ne.

english_verse: The Lord saw how bad the people on earth were and that everything they thought and planned was evil.
translation_verse: Afei AWURADE nwuni kyɛ kuro sona amumuyɛɛ asone pee wɔ aseɛ ye aso, na nzusuleɛ tɛɛ ngome ayi ye ti anu tɛkyɛ daa.

english_verse: and he said, “I'm going to destroy every person on earth! I'll even wipe out animals, birds, and reptiles. I'm sorry I ever made them.”
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE hane kyɛ, “Ngonua kuro sona bɔ mabɔ ye ne boso ngofi aseɛ ye aso: mmenia ne ngaka mbiri ne ngaka bɔ bɛtwe bɛ nwo ase ne ewienu nnomaa, ofikyɛ manu me nwo kyɛ nyɔle bɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: But the Lord was pleased with Noah,
translation_verse: Nakoso Nowa de, ye yɔleɛ sɔle AWURADE nye. Nowa apam alaka ne

english_verse: and this is the story about him. Noah was the only person who lived right and obeyed God.
translation_verse: Nowa boso ama ɛhe: Né Nowa te sona bɔ ɔtengyɛ, bɔ ngekalewa biala nne ye bra nu wɔ ye aberɛ so mmenia nu ɔ. Nowa fale ye nwo bɔle Nyameɛ.

english_verse: He had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
translation_verse: Nowa wole mmienzua nza: Sem, Ham yeɛ Yafɛte.

english_verse: Get some good lumber and build a boat. Put rooms in it and cover it with tar inside and out.
translation_verse: Yiti fa ɛframmire bobɔ ɛlɛen alaka ma wɔ nwo. Kyekyɛ nu ma pumbu mɔ bra nu, na fa ehwaa fa ye kunu ne ye si amu.

english_verse: Noah did everything God told him to do.
translation_verse: Na Nowa yɔle bɔ Nyameɛ hyɛle ye kyɛ ɔyɔ ne amukoraa.

english_verse: I'm going to send a flood that will destroy everything that breathes! Nothing will be left alive.
translation_verse: Tie, ngɔma nzueyilɛ kɔwa aseɛ so kɔɔsɛkye anwoɔnaen biala bɔ owura ewienu bo bɔ ngoa nwomeɛ wɔ ye nu; na nikyee biala bɔ ɔwɔ aseɛ so kowu.

english_verse: But I solemnly promise that you, your wife, your sons, and your daughters-in-law will be kept safe in the boat.
translation_verse: Nakoso wɔ de, me ne wɔ yɛkɔyɛ apam. Ɛkɔɔfo ɛlɛen alaka ne anu, wɔ, wɔ mma mmienzua ne, ɛye, yeɛ wɔ mma nemɔ bɛ ye mɔ kɔboka wɔ so.

english_verse: Take into the boat with you a male and a female of every kind of animal and bird, as well as a male and a female of every reptile. I don't want them to be destroyed.
translation_verse: Nnomaa ahoroɔ, ngaka ahoroɔ, ne ngaka ahoroɔ bɔ bɛkongo ɔ, ebiala kyɛbɔ ye sue si te ɔ, bɛ nu biala nyɔ nyɔ kɔɔboka wɔ so, amaa ɔnate so banya ngoa.

english_verse: The Lord told Noah: Take your whole family with you into the boat, because you are the only one on this earth who pleases me.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Nowa kyɛ, “Kɔfo ɛlɛen alaka ne anu, ɛne w’awuro ama mukoraa, ofikyɛ, manwu kyɛ wɔ de ɛtengyɛ wɔ me nyunu wɔ sɔ aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ he anu.

english_verse: Take seven pairs of every kind of animal that can be used for sacrifice and one pair of all others.
translation_verse: Ngaka mukoraa bɔ bɛ nwo te ne, fa nyii ne beleɛ nzoo nzoo; ngaka bɔ bɛ nwo nde ne, fa nyii ne beleɛ nyɔ nyɔ;

english_verse: Also take seven pairs of every kind of bird with you. Do this so there will always be animals and birds on the earth.
translation_verse: ewienu nnomaa mɔ koso, fa nyii ne beleɛ nzoo nzoo, amaa bɛ boso annua wɔ aseɛ ye aso amukoraa.

english_verse: He obeyed God and took a male and a female of each kind of animal and bird into the boat with him.
translation_verse: bɛ nu biala nyii ne beleɛ, bɛ ne Nowa hɔle ɛlɛen alaka ne anu, kyɛbɔ Nyameɛ hyɛle Nowa nen.

english_verse: Seven days later a flood began to cover the earth.
translation_verse: Na ɛlɛsoo pɛle nu ne, nzue yili fale aseɛ ye.

english_verse: The water under the earth started gushing out everywhere, the sky opened like windows, and rain poured down for
translation_verse: Na esue tɔle aseɛ so toonn eleburanna, alehyeleɛ ne alesaleɛ.

english_verse: On that day Noah and his wife went into the boat with their three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their wives.
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne ala, Nowa ne ɔye ne ye mma Sem, Ham, ne Yafɛte, yeɛ ye mma nemɔ aye nza bɔ bɛboka so ne bɛfole ɛlɛen alaka ne.

english_verse: Noah took a male and a female of every living creature with him,
translation_verse: Kaka biala bɔ nwomeɛ wɔ ye nu ne, nyɔ nyɔ yeɛ bɛ ne Nowa fole ɛlɛen alaka ne ɔ.

english_verse: just as God had told him to do. And when they were all in the boat, the Lord closed the door.
translation_verse: Kaka biala nyii ne beleɛ fole nu, kyɛbɔ Nyameɛ hyɛle Nowa ne, na afei AWURADE tole Nowa anoa nu.

english_verse: Finally, the mighty flood was so deep that even the highest mountain peaks were about seven meters below the surface of the water.
translation_verse: Nzue ne yili maa mmokaa nemɔ monone, na ɔtrale bɛ hɔle anwuro agyirɛ buru ne nnu.

english_verse: Not a bird, animal, reptile, or human was left alive anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Na abɔdeɛ biala bɔ ɔnate aseɛ ye aso wuli: nnomaa, nyɛmmoa, eburo ngaka, ngaka bɔ bɛtwe bɛ nwo ase amu, kuro sona biala,

english_verse: A hundred fifty days later, the water started going down.
translation_verse: Na nzue ne yili wɔ aseɛ so ngyẽa ɛyaa ko ne aburannu.

english_verse: God did not forget about Noah and the animals with him in the boat. So God made a wind blow, and the water started going down.
translation_verse: Nakoso Nyameɛ lole Nowa ne ngaka ne nyɛmmoa mukoraa bɔ bɛ ne ye wɔ ɛlɛen alaka ne anu. Nyameɛ mane mvrama tu fale aseɛ so, na nzue ne hwene.

english_verse: God stopped up the places where the water had been gushing out from under the earth. He also closed up the sky, and the rain stopped.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ mane aseɛ bo dɔ nzue ne pɛle, ɔtotole anwuro nzue mboma nemɔ anu, na ɔmane esue ne koso yakyili tɔlɛ.

english_verse: Then on the seventeenth day of the seventh month of the year, the boat came to rest somewhere in the Ararat mountains.
translation_verse: Na ye bosome nzoo ne anu, ngyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nzoo ne aso, ɛlɛen alaka ne oogyinane Ararate mmokaa ne aso.

english_verse: The water kept going down, and the mountain tops could be seen on the first day of the tenth month.
translation_verse: Nzue ne hɔle so hwene alaa maa oodwuli bosome buru ne anu. Na kyẽa bɔ oli moa wɔ bosome buru ne anu nen, mmokaa nemɔ ti tetɛle berɛ.

english_verse: Forty days later Noah opened a window to send out a raven, but it kept flying around until the water had dried up.
translation_verse: na ɔsomane adene; na adene ne oohyinihyini toonn maa oodwuli kyɛ nzue ne wewele wɔ aseɛ so ɔ.

english_verse: Noah wanted to find out if the water had gone down, so he sent out a dove.
translation_verse: Afei ɔsomane abubure kyɛ ɔɔnea sɛ nzue bɔ ɔwɔ aseɛ so ne ahwe a;

english_verse: Deep water was still everywhere, and when the dove could not find a place to land, it flew back to the boat. Then Noah held out his hand and helped it back in.
translation_verse: nakoso abubure ne annya neka fee wandena, yiti osa wale Nowa berɛ wɔ ɛlɛen alaka ne anu, ofikyɛ né nzue ne afa aseɛ so amukoraa. Yiti Nowa tengyɛle ye sa sɔle ye nu, na ɔfale ye wale ye nwo berɛ wɔ ɛlɛen alaka ne anu.

english_verse: Seven days later Noah sent the dove out again.
translation_verse: Nowa nwondɛle ɛlɛsoo bieku, na ɔsomane abubure ne fili ɛlɛen alaka ne anu.

english_verse: It returned in the evening, holding in its beak a green leaf from an olive tree. Noah knew the water was finally going down.
translation_verse: Abubure ne sá wale ye berɛ nɔsoa, na edwirɛ nwanwa, né olive nyaa monɛ tua ye noa, na ɛhe mane Nowa nwuni kyɛ nzue ne awewe wɔ aseɛ so.

english_verse: He waited seven more days before sending the dove out again, and this time it did not return.
translation_verse: Nowa nwondɛle ngyẽa ɛlɛsoo bieku, na osa somane abubure ne, nakoso abubure ne anza amma ye nwo berɛ ko.

english_verse: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was completely dry.
translation_verse: Kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nzoo wɔ bosome bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ne anu, né aseɛnwo awo wosee.

english_verse: God said to Noah,
translation_verse: Na afei Nyameɛ sele Nowa kyɛ,

english_verse: “You, your wife, your sons, and your daughters-in-law may now leave the boat.
translation_verse: “Fi ɛlɛen alaka ne anu dwu ase, wɔ, ɛye, wɔ mma mɔ ne bɛ ye mɔ.

english_verse: After Noah and his family had left the boat,
translation_verse: Yiti Nowa ne ɔye, ye mma mɔ ne bɛ ye mɔ befili ɛlɛen ne anu bedwuli ase.

english_verse: Noah built an altar where he could offer sacrifices to the Lord. Then he offered on the altar one of each kind of animal and bird that could be used for a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Nowa sili afɔleɛ bokyea mane AWURADE; na kaka biala bɔ ye nwo te, ɔne anomaa biala bɔ ye nwo te ne, ɔfale nu bie bɔle naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ wɔ bokyea ne aso.

english_verse: The smell of the burning offering pleased the Lord, and he said: Never again will I punish the earth for the sinful things its people do. All of them have evil thoughts from the time they are young, but I will never destroy everything that breathes, as I did this time.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE tele afɔleɛ ne fona nen, ɔhane ye ye ti anu kyɛ, “Ɔnate kuro sona ti mengɔnoma aseɛ ko, ofikyɛ sona ti anu nzusuleɛ te bɔne fite ye ngwadaa nu; na sɔ ala yeɛ mengɔsɛkye abɔdeɛ biala ko kyɛbɔ mayɔ ye ɔ.”

english_verse: As long as the earth remains, there will be planting and harvest, cold and heat; winter and summer, day and night.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ biala bɔ aseɛ tɛ wɔ berɛ ye de, mmakaammaa lualɛ ne ye bulɛ, ɛyerɛ ne ahuhuro, asuso ne wawa, alehyeleɛ ne alesaleɛ ngɔyakyi le.”

english_verse: God said to Noah and his sons: I am giving you my blessing. Have a lot of children and grandchildren, so people will live everywhere on this earth.
translation_verse: Afei Nyameɛ yirale Nowa ne ye mma mɔ, na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔwo ná ɛ́mɔta pee, ná ɛ́mɔyi aseɛ so tɛkyɛ.

english_verse: and I have given them to you for food. From now on, you may eat them, as well as the green plants that you have always eaten.
translation_verse: Nikyee biala bɔ nwomeɛ wɔ ye nu ne, ɔkɔyɛ ɛmɔ aleɛ. Na kyɛbɔ mvale nyaanyaa monɛ mane ɛmɔ ne, sɔ ala yeɛ méfa nikyee biala méma ɛmɔ ɔ.

english_verse: But life is in the blood, and you must not eat any meat that still has blood in it.
translation_verse: Nakoso naen bɔ ye ngoa, bɔ ɔte ye mogya tɛ wɔ ye nu de, nnɛma ɛmɔdi.

english_verse: I created humans to be like me, and I will punish any animal or person that takes a human life. If an animal kills someone, that animal must die. And if a person takes the life of another, that person must be put to death.
translation_verse: Sona biala bɔ ɔkɔha obiɛngo mogya kogua ne, ye wora sona yeɛ ɔkɔha ye mogya kogua ɔ, ofikyɛ Nyameɛ sɛso yeɛ ɔyɔle sona ɔ.

english_verse: I want you and your descendants to have many children, so people will live everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Nakoso ɛmɔ de, ɛ́mɔwo ná ɛ́mɔta, ná ɛ́mɔsone pee wɔ aseɛ so.”

english_verse: Again, God said to Noah and his sons:
translation_verse: Afei Nyameɛ sele Nowa ne ye mma bɔ bɛboka ye so ne kyɛ,

english_verse: I am going to make a solemn promise to you and to everyone who will live after you.
translation_verse: “Nea, me ne ɛmɔ ne kyẽa bie ɛmɔ boso ama yɛ́yɛ m’apam;

english_verse: I promise every living creature that the earth and those living on it will never again be destroyed by a flood.
translation_verse: M’apam he yeɛ me ne ɛmɔ yɛ́yɛ ɔ, kyɛ ofi ɛnɛ bɔ ɔkɔ ɔ, mengɔfa nzueyilɛ ngɔsɛkye abɔdeɛ mukoraa ko, na mengɔfa nzueyilɛ ngɔsɛkye aseɛ ko.”

english_verse: The rainbow that I have put in the sky will be my sign to you and to every living creature on earth. It will remind you that I will keep this promise forever.
translation_verse: Mafa me nyangondoen mabea munungum nu, na ɔkɔyɛ apam bɔ me ne aseɛ yayɛ ne nwo sɛngyerɛnneɛ.

english_verse: When I send clouds over the earth, and a rainbow appears in the sky,
translation_verse: Na sɛ esue muna wɔ aseɛ so na nyangondoen to wɔ munungum ne anu a,

english_verse: I will remember my promise to you and to all other living creatures. Never again will I let floodwaters destroy all life.
translation_verse: ngɔkaye m’apam bɔ me ne ɛmɔ ne abɔdeɛ teasefoɛ mukoraa yayɛ ne. Na nzue ne ngɔkakyi nzueyilɛ ngɔsɛkye abɔdeɛ mukoraa ko.

english_verse: When I see the rainbow in the sky, I will always remember the promise that I have made to every living creature.
translation_verse: Na sɛ nyangondoen ne to wɔ munungum ne anu a, ngɔnea na makaye apam afebɔɔ bɔ ɔwɔ Nyameɛ ne abɔdeɛ teasefoɛ mukoraa b’afia ne.”

english_verse: The rainbow will be the sign of that solemn promise. Noah and His Family
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ sele Nowa kyɛ, “Apam bɔ mayɛ mato berɛ mama me ne abɔdeɛ mukoraa bɔ bɛwɔ aseɛ so ne, ye nwo sɛngyerɛnneɛ ɛne.” Nowa boso ama

english_verse: Noah and his sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, left the boat. Ham later had a son named Canaan.
translation_verse: Nowa mma mmienzua bɔ befili ɛlɛen alaka ne anu bedwuli ase ne, bɛ ole Sem, Ham ne Yafɛte. Né Ham te Kanaan baba.

english_verse: All people on earth are descendants of Noah's three sons.
translation_verse: Né sɔ mmenia nza hemɔ te Nowa mma, na bɛ yeɛ besuli aseɛ so mmenia mukoraati ɔ.

english_verse: Noah farmed the land and was the first to plant a vineyard.
translation_verse: Nowa yeɛ ɔbɔle kuayɔlɛ bo ɔ, na ɔyɛle bobe boo.

english_verse: One day he got drunk and was lying naked in his tent.
translation_verse: Ɔnone bobe nzaa ne bie, ɔbole, na ɔlale ye ɛtena sua nu bɔ né ye nwo la so ɔ.

english_verse: Ham entered the tent and saw him naked, then went back outside and told his brothers.
translation_verse: Kanaan baba Ham nwuni kyɛ ɔse Nowa nwo la so, na ofitele ɔɔbɔle oliɛma nyɔ nemɔ amaneɛ.

english_verse: Shem and Japheth put a robe over their shoulders and walked backwards into the tent. Without looking at their father, they placed it over his body.
translation_verse: Na Sem ne Yafɛte fale ɛtena beguale bɛ bati so, na bele bɛ si bɛhɔle toonn bɛɛfa bɛkatale bɛ se anwo. Bɛyele bɛ nye bɛtole eburo, na bannwu bɛ se nwo bɔ né ɔla so ne.

english_verse: When Noah sobered up and learned what his youngest son had done,
translation_verse: Nzaa ne tetele Nowa nye so, ná ɔtele bɔ ɔwa kãa paa ne afa ayɛ ye nen,

english_verse: he said, “I now put a curse on Canaan! He will be the lowest slave of his brothers.
translation_verse: ɔhane kyɛ, “Musue to Kanaan! Ɔkɔyɛ kanga nu kanga kɔma oliɛma mɔ.”

english_verse: I ask the Lord my God to bless Shem and make Canaan his slave.
translation_verse: Na osa hane kyɛ, “AWURADE me Nyameɛ óyira Sem. Kanaan kɔyɛ Sem kanganiɛ!

english_verse: I pray God will give Japheth more and more land and let him take over the territory of Shem. May Canaan be his slave.”
translation_verse: Nyameɛ ɔ́ma Yafɛte boso ɔ́trɛ, ɔ́ma ɔtena Sem ɛtena sua nu, ná ɔma Kanaan ɔyɛ Yafɛte kanganiɛ.”

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Nowa afoɛ mukoraa bɔ olili te ɛyaa ngona ne aburannu, na owuli.

english_verse: After the flood Shem, Ham, and Japheth had many descendants. The Descendants of Japheth
translation_verse: Nowa mma mmienzua Sem, Ham ne Yafɛte bɛ boso ama ɛhe: Nzueyilɛ ne asi ne, bɛwole mmaa.

english_verse: Japheth's descendants had their own languages, tribes, and land. They were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras. Gomer was the ancestor of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah. Javan was the ancestor of Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim, who settled along the coast. The Descendants of Ham
translation_verse: Bɛ boso ama ole mmenia bɔ bato bapete mboanoa aseɛ so ne. Yafɛte mma mɔ bɔ bɛwɔ b’aseɛ so ɛhe: asora fekue biala ne ye dwudwolɛ, ye abusua ne ye maen.

english_verse: This completes the list of Noah's descendants. After the flood their descendants became nations and spread all over the world.
translation_verse: Nowa mma nemɔ b’abusua, kyɛbɔ b’aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ te wɔ bɛ maen nu ɛhe. Na ofi bɛ nu yeɛ nzueyilɛ ne asi ne maen maen fifili na bɛto bɛpetene aseɛ so ɔ.

english_verse: but after some of them moved from the east and settled in Babylonia,
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ mmenia tu fili eyia afiteleɛ nen, benwuni aseɛ frɛtɛɛ bie wɔ Sinari aseɛ so, na bɛtenane berɛ.

english_verse: they said: Let's build a city with a tower that reaches to the sky! We'll use hard bricks and tar instead of stone and mortar. We'll become famous, and we won't be scattered all over the world.
translation_verse: Afei besele kyɛ, “Biamɔ, ɛ́mɔma yɛkyekye yɛ kuro, ná yɛsi abandenden bɔ odwu nyameɛso yɛsie so, ná yɛfa yɛle dumaa, amaa yammɔ aya wɔ aseɛ ye aso amukoraa.”

english_verse: But when the Lord came down to look at the city and the tower,
translation_verse: AWURADE dwu wale ase ɔɔneane kuro ne abandenden bɔ né mmenia mmaa bési ne.

english_verse: he said: These people are working together because they all speak the same language. This is just the beginning. Soon they will be able to do anything they want.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele kyɛ, “Bɛte mmenia komapɛ, na bɛ mukoraa bɛka edwudwolɛ ko. Ɔ́hyɛ ye bo ye po yeɛ bɛ́yɔ sɔaa ye. Nzaade bɔ bekosusu kyɛ bɛkɔyɔ biala ne, nikye fee ngosi bɛ ate.

english_verse: Let's go down and confuse them! We'll make them speak different languages, and they won't be able to understand each other.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔbra, ɛ́mɔma yɛdwu yɛhɔ ase, ná yɛkakyi bɛ dwudwolɛ ne ma ɔyɛ nwunyaenn, amaa bɛ nu biala ande obiɛngo dwudwolɛ bo ko.”

english_verse: So the people had to stop building the city, because the Lord confused their language and scattered them all over the earth. That's how the city of Babel got its name. The Descendants of Shem
translation_verse: Ɛhe ati yeɛ ɔmaa bɛfrɛ berɛ Babɛl, ofikyɛ AWURADE mane aseɛ so amukoraa dwudwolɛ yɛle nwunyaenn. Na ofi sɔ mmerɛ ne, AWURADE maa bɛbɔle aya wɔ aseɛ ye aso amukoraa. Sem boso ama (

english_verse: Serug had more children and died at the age of
translation_verse: Na Seruge wole Nahɔ nen, ye si ye olili afoɛ ɛyaa nyɔ, na ɔwole mmaa mmienzua ne mmrasua mɔ koso.

english_verse: Terah decided to move from Ur to the land of Canaan. He took along Abram and Sarai and his grandson Lot, the son of Haran. But when they came to the city of Haran, they settled there instead.
translation_verse: Tera fale ɔwa Abram, ye anomaa Lɔto bɔ ɔte Haran awa ne, ye sia Sarae bɔ ɔte ɔwa Abram aye ne, na ɔne bɛ betu befili Yure bɔ ɔwɔ Kaldea kyɛ bɛ́kɔ Kanaan aseɛ so. Nakoso bedwuli Haran nen, bɛtenane berɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Abram: Leave your country, your family, and your relatives and go to the land that I will show you.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Abram kyɛ, “Tu fi wɔ maen nu, w’abusuafoɛ nu, ɔne ɛse awuro, ná kɔ aseɛ bɔ mebaahyire wɔ ne aso.

english_verse: I will bless you and make your descendants into a great nation. You will become famous and be a blessing to others.
translation_verse: Ngɔmaa ɛkɔyɛ maen pirikua, ngoyira wɔ, ná mama wɔ dumaa ahɔ anwuro, amaa ɔnate so ayɛ saleɛ.

english_verse: I will bless those who bless you, but I will put a curse on anyone who puts a curse on you. Everyone on earth will be blessed because of you.
translation_verse: Ngoyira bɛ bɔ beyira wɔ, na ebiala bɔ ɔnoma wɔ ne, me koso ngɔnoma ye; na ɔnate wɔ so yeɛ aseɛ so mmusua amukoraa bekonya saleɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Abram went as far as the sacred tree of Moreh in a place called Shechem. The Canaanites were still living in the land at that time,
translation_verse: Abram pɛle nu wɔ aseɛ ne aso, na oodwuli More eluii bakaa bɔ ɔwɔ Sɛkem ne anwo. Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Kanaanfoɛ wɔ aseɛ ne aso.

english_verse: but the Lord appeared to Abram and promised, “I will give this land to your family forever.” Abram then built an altar there for the Lord.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE yele ye nwo ali hyirele Abram, na osele kyɛ, “Wɔ bosofoɛ yeɛ ngɔfa sɔ aseɛ he ngɔma bɛ ɔ.” Yiti Abram sili afɔleɛ bokyea berɛ mane AWURADE bɔ ɔyele ye nwo ali hyirele ye ne.

english_verse: Abram traveled to the hill country east of Bethel and camped between Bethel and Ai, where he built another altar and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Afei otu fili berɛ hɔle mmokaa aseɛ bɔ ɔwɔ Betel eyia afiteleɛ ne aso dɔ, na osili ye ɛtena sua wɔ berɛ; bɔ né Betel wɔ ye eyia atɔleɛ, yeɛ Aye koso wɔ ye eyia afiteleɛ. Osili afɔleɛ bokyea berɛ mane AWURADE, na ɔsɔnene AWURADE.

english_verse: Later, Abram started out toward the Southern Desert. Abram in Egypt
translation_verse: Abram toale ye ateetulɛ ne aso fale ye nye hyirele ngwaen dɔ aseɛ ne. Abram wɔ Misraim

english_verse: The crops failed, and there was no food anywhere in Canaan. So Abram and his wife Sarai went to live in Egypt for a while. But just before they got there, Abram said, “Sarai, you are really beautiful!
translation_verse: Na ɔka kãa maa odwu Misraim nen, osele ɔye Sarae kyɛ, “Mese kyɛ ɛte brasua bɔ wɔ nwo yɛ nyemene ɔ;

english_verse: When the Egyptians see you, they will murder me because I am your husband. But they won't kill you.
translation_verse: na sɛ Misraimfoɛ nwu wɔ a, bɛkɔhã kyɛ, ‘Ɔye ɔ’; ná bahu me, nakoso wɔ de bɛkɔyakyi wɔ.

english_verse: As soon as Abram and Sarai arrived in Egypt, the Egyptians noticed how beautiful she was.
translation_verse: Abram dwuli Misraim nen, Misraimfoɛ nemɔ nwuni kyɛ braa ne nwo yɛ nyemene paa.

english_verse: The king's officials told him about her, and she was taken to his house.
translation_verse: Faro mbanyi nemɔ nwuni ye, na bɛkamvole ye behyirele Faro. Na bɛfale braa ne bɛhɔle Faro awuro.

english_verse: The king was good to Abram because of Sarai, and Abram was given sheep, cattle, donkeys, slaves, and camels.
translation_verse: Na ɔnate ye ti Faro lele Abram nyemene so; na Abram nyane mmoaen, nandwie, afunum nyii mɔ, ngoaa ne afaneɛ mɔ, afunum beleɛ mɔ ne afupɔngɔ mɔ.

english_verse: Because of Sarai, the Lord struck the king and everyone in his palace with terrible diseases.
translation_verse: Na ɔnate Abram aye Sarae ti, AWURADE fale amaneɛ pirikua tole Faro ne ye awuro ama so.

english_verse: Finally, the king sent for Abram and said to him, “What have you done to me? Why didn't you tell me Sarai was your wife?
translation_verse: Yiti Faro frɛle Abram bisale ye kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ dwirɛ paa yeɛ afa ali me e? Nzu ati yeɛ anga angyire me kyɛ ɛye ahɔ ɔ?

english_verse: Why did you make me believe she was your sister? Now I've married her. Take her and go! She's your wife.”
translation_verse: Nzu ati yeɛ ɛhane kyɛ ‘Nniɛma ɔ,’ bɔ ahaa ɛmaa mefa ye meyɛ me ye ɔ? Nea, ɛye ne ɛhe. Fa ye na ɛne ye befi wa bɛhɔ!”

english_verse: So the king told his men to let Abram and Sarai take their possessions and leave.
translation_verse: Na Faro hyɛle mmenia kyɛ bɛma Abram ɔhɔ, na bɛhane Abram ne ɔye, ɔne bɔ banya ye amukoraa beguale atee so maa bɛhɔle.

english_verse: Abram and Sarai took everything they owned and went to the Southern Desert. Lot went with them.
translation_verse: Yiti Abram fili Misraim hɔle ngwaen dɔ aseɛ ne aso dɔ, ɔne ɔye ne bɔ wanya ye amukoraa, na Lɔto ne ye bɛhɔle.

english_verse: Abram was very rich. He owned many cattle, sheep, and goats, and had a lot of silver and gold.
translation_verse: Né Abram anya ye nwo tam wɔ nyɛmmoa, ɛdwetɛ ne sikaa kɔkorɛ nu.

english_verse: Abram moved from place to place in the Southern Desert. And finally, he went north and set up his tents between Bethel and Ai,
translation_verse: Olili tutena toonn fili ngwaen dɔ aseɛ ne aso oodwuli Betel, na odwuli nekaa bɔ olili moa sili ye ɛtena sua ne, wɔ Betel ne Aye b’afia.

english_verse: where he had earlier camped and built an altar. There he worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Oodwuli nekaa bɔ olili moa sili afɔleɛ bokyea ne. Na Abram sɔnene AWURADE berɛ.

english_verse: Lot, who was traveling with him, also had sheep, goats, and cattle, as well as his own family and slaves.
translation_verse: Né Lɔto bɔ ɔne Abram bɛnate ne koso ole mmoaen ne nandwie ne ɛtena sua mɔ.

english_verse: At this time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were still living in the same area, and so there wasn't enough pastureland left for Abram and Lot with all of their animals. Besides this, the men who took care of Abram's animals and the ones who took care of Lot's animals started quarreling.
translation_verse: Na edwudwolɛ wale Abram ngaka neafoɛ nemɔ ne Lɔto ngaka neafoɛ nemɔ afia. Na sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Kanaanfoɛ ne Perisifoɛ wɔ sɔ aseɛ ne aso.

english_verse: Abram said to Lot, “We are close relatives. We shouldn't argue, and our men shouldn't be fighting one another.
translation_verse: Na Abram sele Lɔto kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, nnɛma aporowaa biala ba me ne wɔ afia, ɔne wɔ ngaka neafoɛ ne me ngaka neafoɛ afia, ofikyɛ yɛbɔ abusua.

english_verse: There is plenty of land for you to choose from. Let's separate. If you go north, I'll go south; if you go south, I'll go north.”
translation_verse: Aso nna aseɛ yeɛ ɔla wɔ nyunu tɛtrɛtɛɛ ye? Mesrɛ wɔ, te wɔ nwo fi me nwo. Na sɛ ɛfa bɛen so a, me wora ngɔfa famaa so; yeɛ sɛ ɛfa famaa so koso a, me wora ngɔfa bɛen so.”

english_verse: This happened before the Lord had destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. And when Lot looked around, he saw there was plenty of water in the Jordan Valley. All the way to Zoar the valley was as green as the garden of the Lord or the land of Egypt.
translation_verse: Lɔto totole ye nye neane Yɔɔdan noa aseɛ frɛtɛɛ ne amukoraa, bɔ ɔkɔ Soa bue nu dɔ ne, na onwuni kyɛ nzue doadoa ye nekaa biala te kyɛ AWURADE turo ne, kyɛ Misraim aseɛ. Ɛhe sili koraka yeɛ AWURADE baasɛkye Sodom ne Gomora ɔ.

english_verse: So Lot chose the whole Jordan Valley for himself, and as he started out toward the east, he and Abram separated.
translation_verse: Yiti Lɔto yele Yɔɔdan noa aseɛ frɛtɛɛ ne amukoraa, na ɔfale ye ti bɔle eyia afiteleɛ bue nu dɔ. Na bɛpakyepakyele nu.

english_verse: Abram stayed in the land of Canaan. But Lot settled near the cities of the valley and put up his tents not far from Sodom,
translation_verse: Abram tenane Kanaan aseɛ so, nakoso Lɔto de, ɔtenane Yɔɔdan noa aseɛ frɛtɛɛ nguro nemɔ aso, na oosili ye ɛtena sua pingyele Sodom.

english_verse: where the people were evil and sinned terribly against the Lord. Abram Moves to Hebron
translation_verse: Né Sodomfoɛ te amumuyɛɛfoɛ, bɔ bɛyɔ bɔne mbirikua mbirikua betia AWURADE ɔ. Abram tu kɔ Hebron

english_verse: After Abram and Lot had gone their separate ways, the Lord said to Abram: Look around to the north, south, east, and west.
translation_verse: Lɔto tele ye nwo fili Abram nwo ne, ye si ye AWURADE sele Abram kyɛ, “Gyina nekaa bɔ ɛwɔ ne, ná ma wɔ nye so nea sorɔ ne ngwaen, eyia afiteleɛ ne atɔleɛ.

english_verse: I will give you and your family all the land you can see. It will be theirs forever!
translation_verse: Na ngɔfa aseɛ bɔ enwu ye ne amukoraa ngɔma wɔ ne wɔ boso ama afebɔɔ.

english_verse: I will give you more descendants than there are specks of dust on the earth, and someday it will be easier to count those specks of dust than to count your descendants.
translation_verse: Ngɔma wɔ boso ama kɔta kyɛ aseɛ so mvuture. Na sɛ ebie kora ka aseɛ so mvuture a, ye de ɔkɔhora kɔha wɔ boso ama koso.

english_verse: Now walk back and forth across the land, because I am going to give it to you.
translation_verse: Ma wɔ nwo yɛ nyera, na nate fa aseɛ ne tendenn ne ye tɛtrɛtɛɛ nu, ofikyɛ mebaafa mema wɔ.”

english_verse: Abram took down his tents and went to live near the sacred trees of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Yiti Abram tutuli ye ɛtena sua ne, na ɔɔtenane pingyele Mamre eluii mmakaa bɔ bɛwɔ Hebron ne, na osili afɔleɛ bokyea berɛ mane AWURADE.

english_verse: About this time, King Amraphel of Babylonia, King Arioch of Ellasar, King Chedorlaomer of Elam, and King Tidal of Goiim
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, Sinari hene Amrafɛl, Elasare hene Arioke, Elam hene Kedolaoma ne Goyim hene Tidal,

english_verse: attacked King Bera of Sodom, King Birsha of Gomorrah, King Shinab of Admah, King Shemeber of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, a city also known as Zoar.
translation_verse: bɛɛfale koɛ bɛtetale Sodom hene Bera, Gomora hene Biresa, Adema hene Sinabo, Seboyim hene Semebere, ɔne Bɛla hene ne.

english_verse: King Chedorlaomer and his allies had ruled these last five kings for twelve years, but in the thirteenth year the kings rebelled and joined forces in Siddim Valley, which is now covered by the southern part of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Né baso Kedolaoma afoɛ buru ne nyɔ mumua, nakoso bɛyɛle ye nwo lɔen afoɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nza ne anu.

english_verse: A year later King Chedorlaomer and his allies attacked and defeated the Rephaites in Ashteroth-Karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, and the Emites in Shaveh-Kiriathaim.
translation_verse: Na afoɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nna ne anu, Kedolaoma ne ahemvo mɔ bɔ bɛwɔ ye bue nu ne, bɛɛbole Refaimfoɛ wɔ Asterote Kanaim, Susimfoɛ wɔ Ham, Emimfoɛ wɔ Sawe Kiriatim,

english_verse: They also defeated the Horites in the hill country of Edom, as far as El-Paran, near the desert.
translation_verse: na bɛɛbole Horifoɛ wɔ bɛ bokaa Sɛre so toonn beedwuli Ɛl Paran bɔ opingye ɛserɛ so ne.

english_verse: They went back to the city of Enmishpat, better known as Kadesh. Then they captured all the land that belonged to the Amalekites, and they defeated the Amorites who were living in Hazazon-Tamar.
translation_verse: Afei besale bɛ si bɛwale Ɛn Misepate , na belili Amalɛkefoɛ maen ne amukoraa ne Amorifoɛ bɔ bɛte Hasason Tamar so ngonim.

english_verse: At Siddim Valley, the armies of the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela fought the armies of King Chedorlaomer of Elam, King Tidal of Goiim, King Amraphel of Babylonia, and King Arioch of Ellasar. The valley
translation_verse: na bɛ ne Elam hene Kedolaoma, Goyim hene Tidal, Sinari hene Amrafɛl, yeɛ Elasare hene Arioke bɛhone koɛ wɔ Sidim bɔnza nu; ahemvo nna yeɛ bɛ ne ahemvo nnu bɛhone ɔ.

english_verse: was full of tar pits, and when the troops from Sodom and Gomorrah started running away, some of them fell into the pits. Others escaped to the hill country.
translation_verse: Né ngono pee bɔ nu ayɛ pikaa wɔ Sidim bɔnza ne anu, yiti mmerɛ bɔ Sodom ne Gomora ahemvo mɔ bɛ́nwati bɛ́kɔ nen, ebiemɔ totɔle ngumaa ne anu, na bɛ ngaa ne koso bɛnwatili bɛhɔle mmokaa aseɛ ne aso dɔ.

english_verse: Their enemies took everything of value from Sodom and Gomorrah, including their food supplies.
translation_verse: Yiti bɛ pɔfoɛ nemɔ sesale Sodom ne Gomora nningyein mukoraa, ɔne b’aleɛ mukoraa, na besili nu bɛhɔle.

english_verse: They also captured Abram's nephew Lot, who lived in Sodom. They took him and his possessions and then left.
translation_verse: Besa bɛhyele Abram aliɛma bienzua awa Lɔto bɔ né ɔte Sodom ne; na bɛsesale ye nningyein bɛbokale so bɛ ne ye hɔle.

english_verse: At this time Abram the Hebrew was living near the oaks that belonged to Mamre the Amorite. Mamre and his brothers Eshcol and Aner were Abram's friends. Someone who had escaped from the battle told Abram
translation_verse: Ebie nwatili fili koɛ ne anoa, na ɔɔbɔle Hebriniɛ Abram amaneɛ. Né Abram te pingye Amoriniɛ Mamre eluii mmakaa ne. Né Mamre aliɛma mɔ Ɛseko ne Anere bɛte Abram koɛ nu bokafoɛ.

english_verse: that his nephew Lot had been taken away. Three hundred and eighteen of Abram's servants were fighting men, so he took them and followed the enemy as far north as the city of Dan.
translation_verse: Na Abram tele kyɛ bahye oliɛma bienzua awa nnure nen, ɔboaboale koɛhonɛfoɛ ɛyaa nza ne buru ne mmɔtwɛ bɔ banya koɛ nu ndeteyɛɛ, bɔ bɛwole bɛ wɔ ye awuro noa, na ɔpole so alaa oodwuli Dan.

english_verse: That night, Abram divided up his troops, attacked from all sides, and won a great victory. But some of the enemy escaped to the town of Hobah north of Damascus,
translation_verse: Abram hyɛle ye mmenia ne anu kure kure kɔngɔen maa bɛhɔle ye pɔfoɛ nemɔ so. Ɔbole bɛ, na ɔfoane bɛ toonn oodwuli Hoba bɔ ɔwɔ Damasko sorɔ ne.

english_verse: and Abram went after them. He brought back his nephew Lot, together with Lot's possessions and the women and everyone else who had been captured. Abram Is Blessed by Melchizedek
translation_verse: Afei ɔfale nningyein ne amukoraa, oliɛma bienzua awa Lɔto ne ye nwo nningyein, mmrasua mɔ ne mmenia ne, na osa wale. Mɛlkisɛdɛke yira Abram

english_verse: Abram returned after he had defeated King Chedorlaomer and the other kings. Then the king of Sodom went to meet Abram in Shaveh Valley, which is also known as King's Valley.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Abram lili Kedolaoma ne ye mmango hene mɔ so ngonim na osa ba ne, Sodom hene ooyiale ye wɔ Sawe bɔnza ne anu.

english_verse: King Melchizedek of Salem was a priest of God Most High. He brought out some bread and wine
translation_verse: Na Salem hene Mɛlkisɛdɛke bɔ né ɔte Anwuro Anwuro Nyameɛ sɔfo nen, ɔfale paanoo ne bobe nzaa brɛle Abram.

english_verse: and said to Abram: “I bless you in the name of God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth.
translation_verse: Oyirale ye kyɛ, “Anwuro Anwuro Nyameɛ, bɔ ɔbɔle anwuro ne aseɛ ne, óyira Abram;

english_verse: All praise belongs to God Most High for helping you defeat your enemies.” Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.
translation_verse: na animnyam hã Anwuro Anwuro Nyameɛ, bɔ wafa wɔ pɔfoɛ mɔ wawura wɔ sa ne!” Na Abram mane Mɛlkisɛdɛke nningyein ne amukoraa nu buru nu ngyɛmuɛ ko.

english_verse: The king of Sodom said to Abram, “All I want are my people. You can keep everything else.”
translation_verse: Afei Sodom hene sele Abram kyɛ, “Fa mmenia nemɔ ma me, na wɔ wora fa nningyein ne.”

english_verse: Abram answered: The Lord God Most High made the heavens and the earth. And I have promised him
translation_verse: Nakoso Abram sele Sodom hene ne kyɛ, “Mata ndaen mahyire AWURADE, Anwuro Anwuro Nyameɛ bɔ ɔbɔle anwuro ne aseɛ ne,

english_verse: that I won't keep anything of yours, not even a sandal strap or a piece of thread. Then you can never say that you are the one who made me rich.
translation_verse: kyɛ, mengɔfa wɔ gyese, anaa mbaboa nyamaa, anaa wɔ nikyee biala, ná anga kyɛ, ‘Me yeɛ mama Abram anya ye nwo ɔ.’

english_verse: Let my share be the food that my men have eaten. But Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre went with me, so give them their share of what we brought back.
translation_verse: Mengɔfa nikyee fee, sana bɔ mmerandeɛ nemɔ ali ne ngome; yeɛ afei ma Anere, Ɛseko ne Mamre bɛfa me mmenia bɔ bɛ ne me hɔle ne bɛ koɛ nu nzesadeɛ deɛ.”

english_verse: Later the Lord spoke to Abram in a vision, “Abram, don't be afraid! I will protect you and reward you greatly.”
translation_verse: Ɛhemɔ asi ne, AWURADE lale ye dwirɛ ali hyirele Abram wɔ nyekyire nu kyɛ, “Nnɛsuro, Abram. Me yeɛ mebɔ wɔ nwo waen ɔ, na w’akatuaa kɔsone pee.”

english_verse: But Abram answered, “Lord All-Powerful, you have given me everything I could ask for, except children. And when I die, Eliezer of Damascus will get all I own.
translation_verse: Nakoso Abram bisale kyɛ, “O, AWURADE Nyameɛ, nzikyɛ yeɛ ɛkɔfa kɔma me ɔ? Nea kyɛ nnne ba, na Eliesa bɔ ofi Damasko yeɛ okoli me bia ɔ.”

english_verse: You have not given me any children, and this servant of mine will inherit everything.”
translation_verse: Na Abram hane kyɛ, “Nea kyɛ ɛmmane me ba, na kanganiɛ bɔ bawo ye m’awuro yeɛ ɔbaali me bia ɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “No, he won't! You will have a son of your own, and everything you have will be his.”
translation_verse: Nakoso AWURADE lale ye dwirɛ ali hyirele ye kyɛ, “Nna sɔ akoaa he yeɛ okoli wɔ bia ɔ, na mmom wɔ bɔbɔ ɛwa yeɛ okoli wɔ bia ɔ.”

english_verse: Then the Lord took Abram outside and said, “Look at the sky and see if you can count the stars. That's how many descendants you will have.”
translation_verse: Afei Nyameɛ fale ye fitele, na osele kyɛ, “To wɔ nye anwuro na ka nzramaa nemɔ, na nea sɛ ɛkɔhora kɔha bɛ a.” Na osele ye kyɛ, “Sɔ ala yeɛ wɔ boso ama kɔyɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Abram believed the Lord, so the Lord was pleased with him and accepted him. The Lord Makes Another Promise to Abram
translation_verse: Abram lele AWURADE lili, yiti AWURADE buli sɔ nikyee ne kyɛ ɔtengyɛ wɔ ye nyunu.

english_verse: The Lord said to Abram, “I brought you here from Ur in Chaldea, and I gave you this land.”
translation_verse: Na osele ye kyɛ, “Me ole AWURADE bɔ mvale wɔ mvili Yure bɔ ɔwɔ Kaldea mmale ɔ, kyɛ méfa aseɛ he mema wɔ maa ɔyɛ wɔ deɛ.”

english_verse: Abram asked, “Lord God, how can I know the land will be mine?”
translation_verse: Nakoso obisale kyɛ, “O, AWURADE Nyameɛ, ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ né manwu ye kyɛ ɔkɔyɛ m’agyapadeɛ?”

english_verse: Then the Lord told him, “Bring me a three-year-old cow, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a dove, and a young pigeon.”
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ buale ye kyɛ, “Fa nandwie beleɛ akrɔngrɔma bɔ wali afoɛ nza, abɔngye beleɛ bɔ wali afoɛ nza, boaen nyii bɔ wali afoɛ nza, aborɔma, ɔne mmorɔnoma buruwa brɛ me.”

english_verse: Abram obeyed the Lord. Then he cut the animals in half and laid the two halves of each animal opposite each other on the ground. But he did not cut the doves and pigeons in half.
translation_verse: Ɔfale ye mukoraa brɛle ye, ɔpakyepakyele bɛ nu nyɔ nyɔ, na ɔfale ko biala bue tole ye bue ne anwo; nakoso nnomaa nemɔ de, wambakyepakye bɛ nu.

english_verse: And when birds came down to eat the animals, Abram chased them away.
translation_verse: Na sɛ nnomaa bɔ bedi naen batena naen fuin nemɔ aso a, né Abram afoa bɛ.

english_verse: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and everything became dark and frightening.
translation_verse: Na eyia yɛle kyɛ ɔkwaatɔ nen, nnafelɛ hatee wuale Abram, na awosii tunn suronyisuronyi tole ye.

english_verse: Four generations later, your descendants will return here and take this land, because only then will the people who live here be so sinful that they deserve to be punished.
translation_verse: Na sɛ odwu wɔ boso ama mɔ aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so nna ne aso a, bekosa bɛkɔwa wa; ofikyɛ Amorifoɛ amumuyɛɛ kwangoa ne onnya oyyili [bɔ ɔkɔmaa ngɔfoa bɛ ngofi aseɛ ne aso ɔ].

english_verse: Sometime after sunset, when it was very dark, a smoking cooking pot and a flaming fire passed between the two halves of each animal.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ eyia tɔle ná awosii wale nen, mvum nu, foonoo bɔ otu nwosina, ɔne see bɔ ogye wuronyiwuronyi wale bɛɛfale naen bue bue nemɔ afia.

english_verse: At that time the Lord made an agreement with Abram and told him: I will give your descendants the land east of the Shihor River on the border of Egypt as far as the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Na sɔ kyẽa ne ala, AWURADE ne Abram yɛle apam, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Wɔ boso ama yeɛ méfa sɔ aseɛ he méma bɛ ɔ: ofi Misraim asue noa bɔ ɔkwaadwu asue piri Yufreti noa,

english_verse: the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaites,
translation_verse: Hitifoɛ, Perisifoɛ, Refaimfoɛ,

english_verse: the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.
translation_verse: Amorifoɛ, Kanaanfoɛ, Gɛgasifoɛ ne Yebusifoɛ aseɛ ne.”

english_verse: Abram's wife Sarai had not been able to have any children. But she owned a young Egyptian slave woman named Hagar,
translation_verse: Né Abram ne ɔye Sarae bɛwwole baa biala. Né Sarae le Misraimniɛ afaneɛ bie bɔ oli Hagar.

english_verse: and Sarai said to Abram, “The Lord has not given me any children. Sleep with my slave, and if she has a child, it will be mine.” Abram agreed,
translation_verse: Na Sarae sele Abram kyɛ, “Anwu ye kyɛ AWURADE mma menwo, yiti mesrɛ wɔ, ɛne m’afaneɛ ne bɛla; na ebiaa né ɔnate ye so manya mmaa.” Na Abram tiele bɔ Sarae hane ne.

english_verse: and Sarai gave him Hagar to be his wife. This happened after Abram had lived in the land of Canaan for ten years.
translation_verse: Yiti Abram lili afoɛ buru wɔ Kanaan aseɛ so nen, Abram aye Sarae fale ye afaneɛ Hagar bɔ ɔte Misraimniɛ ne mane ohu maa ɔyɛle ɔye.

english_verse: Later, when Hagar knew she was going to have a baby, she became proud and treated Sarai hatefully.
translation_verse: Ɔne Hagar bɛlale, na ɔnwonzɛle. Na mmerɛ bɔ Hagar nwuni kyɛ ɔnwonzɛ nen, afei né ommu ye mene aye ne.

english_verse: Then Sarai said to Abram, “It's all your fault! I gave you my slave woman, but she has been hateful to me ever since she found out she was pregnant. You have done me wrong, and you will have to answer to the Lord for this.”
translation_verse: Na Sarae sele Abram kyɛ, “Edwirɛ tɛɛ bɔ ɔfa di me ne, ɔkɔbɔ wɔ ti so. Me yeɛ mvale m’afaneɛ mane wɔ kyɛ ɛne ye bɛla ɔ, nakoso onwuni kyɛ ɔnwonzɛ nen, afei de ommu me. Mesrɛ kyɛ AWURADE obua wɔ ne me y’afia ndɛen!”

english_verse: Abram said, “All right! She's your slave—do whatever you want with her.” Then Sarai began treating Hagar so harshly that she finally ran away.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Abram buale Sarae kyɛ, “Tie, w’afaneɛ ɔ, na owura wɔ sa; ɛne ye beli ye kyɛbɔ ɛnea a ɔte paa ɔ.” Yiti Sarae tanene Hagar nye maa ɔnwatili fili ye nwo hɔle.

english_verse: Hagar stopped to rest at a spring in the desert on the road to Shur. While she was there, the angel of the Lord came to her
translation_verse: AWURADE abɔfo nwuni Hagar wɔ ɛserɛ so nekaa bie bɔ nzue pu fi aseɛnwo ɔ. Sɔ nzue ne wɔ Sure atee so.

english_verse: and asked, “Hagar, where have you come from, and where are you going?” She answered, “I'm running away from Sarai, my owner.”
translation_verse: Na obisale ye kyɛ, “Sarae afaneɛ Hagar, nisua yeɛ efi wale ɔ, na nisua yeɛ ɛkɔ ɔ?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Me mene aye Sarae sa nu yeɛ ménwati méfi ɔ.”

english_verse: The angel said, “Go back to Sarai and be her slave.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE abɔfo ne sele ye kyɛ, “Sá kɔ wɔ mene aye ne berɛ, na kɔbrɛ wɔ nwo ase ma ye.”

english_verse: I will give you a son, who will be called Ishmael, because I have heard your cry for help. And someday I will give you so many descendants that no one will be able to count them all.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE abɔfo ne sele ye bieku kyɛ, “Nea, ɛnwonzɛ, ɛkɔwo baa bienzua, na ɛkɔto ye dumaa Yismael, ofikyɛ w’aworabɔlɛ ne adwu AWURADE nyunu.

english_verse: But your son will live far from his relatives; he will be like a wild donkey, fighting everyone, and everyone fighting him.”
translation_verse: Ye suban kɔyɛ kyɛ eburo afunum; ɔkɔho kotia sona biala, ná sona biala koso aho atia ye, na ɛpɔen kɔla ye ne ye abusuafoɛ amukoraa b’afia.”

english_verse: Hagar thought, “Have I really seen God and lived to tell about it?” So from then on she called him, “The God Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Yiti Hagar frɛle AWURADE bɔ odwudwo hyirele ye ne kyɛ, “Ɛte Nyameɛ bɔ enwu nikye ɔ”, na Hagar hane kyɛ, “Aso manwu AWURADE yeɛ ndɛ te ase ye?”

english_verse: That's why people call the well between Kadesh and Bered, “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Ye sɔ ne ati, bɛfrɛ sɔ abura ne Beɛ Lahai Roi, na ɔwɔ Kadese ne Berede b’afia.

english_verse: I will keep my solemn promise to you and give you more descendants than can be counted.”
translation_verse: Ngɔma m’apam kɔla me ne wɔ y’afia, na mama wɔ boso ata pee.”

english_verse: Abram bowed with his face to the ground, and God said:
translation_verse: Afei Abram fale ye nyunu butuli berɛ, na Nyameɛ sele ye kyɛ,

english_verse: I promise that you will be the father of many nations. So now I'm changing your name from Abram to Abraham.
translation_verse: Bɛngɔfrɛ wɔ Abram ko, na mmom bɛkɔfrɛ wɔ Abraham, ofikyɛ mayɛ wɔ maen maen pee bɛ baba.

english_verse: I will give you a lot of descendants, and they will become great nations. Some of them will even be kings.
translation_verse: Ngɔma wɔ boso kɔta pee; ngɔmaa ekosu maen maen pee, na mama ahemvo mɔ afi wɔ nu awa.

english_verse: I will always keep the promise I have made to you and your descendants, because I am your God and their God.
translation_verse: Ngɔyɛ m’apam maa ɔkɔyɛ apam afebɔɔ, bɔ ɔwɔ berɛ ma me ne wɔ ne kyẽa bie wɔ boso ama wɔ b’aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ mukoraa nu. Na ngɔyɛ wɔ ne kyẽa bie wɔ boso ama Nyameɛ.

english_verse: I will give you and them the land in which you are now a foreigner. I will give the whole land of Canaan to your family forever, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Ngɔfa aseɛ bɔ aayɛ so wɔfoɛ ne, yeɛ Kanaan aseɛ mukoraa ngɔma wɔ ne kyẽa bie wɔ boso ama maa ɔkɔyɛ ɛmɔ deɛ afebɔɔ; na ngɔyɛ bɛ Nyameɛ”

english_verse: Abraham, you and all future members of your family must promise to obey me.
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ sele Abraham kyɛ, “Odi kyɛ edi m’apam ne aso, ɛne kyẽa bie wɔ boso ama ne b’aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ mukoraa nu.

english_verse: As the sign that you are keeping this promise, you must circumcise every man and boy in your family.
translation_verse: Odi kyɛ ɛmɔpɛ ɛmɔ bienzua, na ɛhe yeɛ ɔkɔyɛ apam bɔ ɔwɔ me ne ɛmɔ afia ne nwo sɛngyerɛnneɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Any man who isn't circumcised hasn't kept his part of the promise and cannot be one of my people.
translation_verse: Na bienzua biala bɔ bambɛ ye bienzua nen, bɛkɔpɛ ye asue bekofi ye maen nu, ofikyɛ wabu m’apam ne aso.”

english_verse: Abraham, from now on your wife's name will be Sarah instead of Sarai.
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ sele Abraham kyɛ, “Ɛye Sarae de, nnɛfrɛ ye Sarae ko, ye dumaa ole Sara.

english_verse: I will bless her, and you will have a son by her. She will become the mother of nations, and some of her descendants will even be kings.
translation_verse: Ngoyira ye, ná afei mamaa ɛne ye bawo bienzua. Ngoyira ye, na ɔkɔyɛ maen maen bɛ maame; na ye boso ama kɔyɛ ahemvo mɔ.”

english_verse: Then he asked God, “Why not let Ishmael inherit what you have promised me?”
translation_verse: Na Abraham sele Nyameɛ kyɛ, “Sɛ ahaa ɛma Yismael sɔ wɔ nye a!”

english_verse: But God answered: No! You and Sarah will have a son. His name will be Isaac, and I will make an everlasting promise to him and his descendants.
translation_verse: Nakoso Nyameɛ sele kyɛ, “Daabi, ɛye Sara kɔwo baa bienzua kɔma wɔ, na ɛkɔto ye dumaa Yisake. Me ne ye yɛkɔyɛ m’apam maa ɔkɔyɛ apam afebɔɔ kɔma ye boso ama.

english_verse: However, I have heard what you asked me to do for Ishmael, and so I will also bless him with many descendants. He will be the father of twelve princes, and I will make his family a great nation.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yismael deɛ ne wora, mate bɔ aha ne; ngoyira ye, na mama ye boso ata, na basone pee. Ɔkɔwo atitirefoɛ buru ne nyɔ, na ngɔmaa ɔkɔyɛ maen piri.

english_verse: But your son Isaac will be born about this time next year, and the promise I am making to you and your family will be for him and his descendants forever.
translation_verse: Nakoso m’apam ne de, Yisake bɔ afoɛ bieku bekye sɔa ala né ɛne Sara bawo ye ne, yeɛ me ne ye yɛkɔyɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: God finished speaking to Abraham and then left.
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ ne Abraham dwudwole yiele nen, Nyameɛ yakyili ye berɛ hɔle anwuro.

english_verse: On that same day Abraham obeyed God by circumcising Ishmael. Abraham was also circumcised, and so were all the other men and boys in his household, including his servants and slaves. He was
translation_verse: ye awuro mmienzua mukoraa, bɛ bɔ bɛwole bɛ wɔ ye awuro, ɔne bɛ bɔ ɔtɔle bɛ fili amanvrafoɛ berɛ koso bɛpepɛle bɛ bienzua bɛbokale ye so.

english_verse: One hot summer afternoon while Abraham was sitting by the entrance to his tent near the sacred trees of Mamre, the Lord appeared to him.
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie eyia ketee, né Abraham te ye ɛtena sua ne anoa nu, na AWURADE yele ye nwo ali hyirele ye wɔ nekaa bie bɔ opingye Mamre eluii mmakaa ne.

english_verse: Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. He quickly ran to meet them, bowed with his face to the ground,
translation_verse: Ɔmane ye nye so, na onwuni kyɛ mmienzua nza bie gyigyi ye nyunu moa dɔ. Onwuni bɛ nen, ofili ɛtena sua ne anoa nu berɛ otuli amirika ooyiale bɛ, na ɔkotole bɛ,

english_verse: and said, “Please come to my home where I can serve you.
translation_verse: na ɔhane kyɛ, “Me Mene, sɛ alo me anwu me anwumvoin de a, nzaade mesrɛ wɔ, nnesã w’akoaa nwo kɔ.

english_verse: I'll have some water brought, so you can wash your feet, then you can rest under a tree.
translation_verse: Maa mmrɛ ɛmɔ nzue kãa, ná ɛmɔnwunzi ɛmɔ gya bo, ná afei ɛmɔale bɛ nwome wɔ bakaa ne abo.

english_verse: Let me get you some food to give you strength before you leave. I would be honored to serve you.” “Thank you very much,” they answered. “We accept your offer.”
translation_verse: Ɛmɔawa ɛmɔ akoaa berɛ, yiti ɛ́mɔma ngɔmbena nikyee kãa ma ɛmɔhã bɛ noa, ma ɔma ɛmɔ anwoserɛ koraka né ɛmɔahɔ.” Na bebuale kyɛ, “Yɔ kyɛbɔ aha ne.”

english_verse: Abraham went quickly to his tent and said to Sarah, “Hurry! Get a large sack of flour and make some bread.”
translation_verse: Na Abraham hane ye nwo hɔle Sara berɛ wɔ ɛtena sua ne anu oosele ye kyɛ, “Ma wɔ nwo yɛ nyera ná fa esam paa kongo nza, fete ná fa yɛ taterɛ.”

english_verse: After saying this, he rushed off to his herd of cattle and picked out one of the best calves, which his servant quickly prepared.
translation_verse: Afei Abraham tuli amirika hɔle nandwie nemɔ anu ɔɔhyele nandwie ba ko bɔ ɔyɛ nyemene, bɔ ye naen kɔyɛ mmerɛ, ɔfa mane ye somvoɛ, na ye koso ɔhane ye nwo oohuni ye, na obiale ye fa yɛle aleɛ.

english_verse: He then served his guests some yogurt and milk together with the meat. While they were eating, he stood near them under the tree,
translation_verse: Afei Abraham fale nandwie nyɔfonesue nye loe, nyɔfonesue ne nandwie akrɔngrɔma bɔ bafa bayɛ aleɛ ne, ɔfa siele ɛwɔfoɛ nemɔ anyunu berɛ, na ogyinane bɛ nwo wɔ bakaa ne abo maa bedidili.

english_verse: and they asked, “Where's your wife Sarah?” “She is right there in the tent,” Abraham answered.
translation_verse: Bebisale ye kyɛ, “Ɛye Sara wɔ ni?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Ɔwɔ ɛtena sua ne anu dɔ.”

english_verse: Abraham and Sarah were very old, and Sarah was well past the age for having children.
translation_verse: Né Abraham ne Sara banyi bayɛ nworowaa; na né Sara mmu ye sa ko.

english_verse: So she laughed and said to herself, “Now that I am worn out and my husband is old, will I really know such happiness?”
translation_verse: Yiti Sara serele ye ti anu hane kyɛ, “Mayɛ aworowaa bɔ me hu wora wayɛ aworowaa ye, aso bekye yeɛ mebaagye me nye ɔ?”

english_verse: The Lord asked Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh? Does she doubt that she can have a child in her old age?
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bisale Abraham kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ Sara serele na ɔhane kyɛ, ‘Aso bekye bɔ mayɛ aworowaa ye yeɛ mebaawo ɔ?’

english_verse: I am the Lord! There is nothing too difficult for me. I'll come back next year at the time I promised, and Sarah will already have a son.”
translation_verse: Aso nikyee bie wɔ berɛ bɔ ɔyɛ se ma AWURADE hɔ ɔ? Na mmerɛ bɔ mahyɛ ne, afoɛ bieku bekye sɔa ala, ngosa ngɔwa wɔ wa, na Sara konya baa bienzua.”

english_verse: Sarah was so frightened that she lied and said, “I didn't laugh.” “Yes, you did!” he answered. Abraham Prays for Sodom
translation_verse: Né Sara suro, yiti ɔsale kyɛ, “Nnzerele.” Nakoso ɔhane kyɛ, “Daabi, ɛserele.” Abraham pa kyerɛ ma Sodomfoɛ

english_verse: When the three men got ready to leave, they looked down toward Sodom, and Abraham walked part of the way with them.
translation_verse: Afei mmenia nemɔ dwɔsole kyɛ bɛ́kɔ, na bɛfale bɛ nye behyirele Sodom; na Abraham ne bɛ sili nu kyɛ ɔkwaagua bɛ ate.

english_verse: The Lord said to himself, “I should tell Abraham what I am going to do,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele kyɛ, “Aso mva bɔ mebaayɔ ye mvea Abraham anaa?

english_verse: since his family will become a great and powerful nation that will be a blessing to all the other nations on earth.
translation_verse: Susu amba kyɛ, Abraham boso ama kɔyɛ maen pirikua bɔ ole tumi, na ɔnate ye so yeɛ ewiase maen mukoraa bekonya saleɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I have chosen him to teach his family to obey me forever and to do what is right and fair. If they do, I will give Abraham many descendants, just as I promised.”
translation_verse: Mapa nu maye ye, kyɛ ɔ́hyɛ ye mma ne ye boso ama bɔ bɛkɔwa nziɛ ye ma bɛnate AWURADE atee so, ma bɛyɔ bɔ ɔtengyɛ, ɔne bɔ ɔte pɛpɛɛpɛ ɔ; amaa ɔnate so AWURADE ama ɛbɔ bɔ wahyɛ Abraham ne awa nu.”

english_verse: ?” “Because of them, I won't destroy the city,” was the Lord's answer.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE hane kyɛ, “Ɔnate kyɛ abubue bɔ bɛbɔ begua Sodom ne Gomora so ne sone soma, na bɛ bɔne te piri paa ne ati,

english_verse: Now I am going down to see for myself if those people really are that bad. If they aren't, I would like to know.”
translation_verse: ngodwu ngɔɔnea sɛ bɔ bayɔ ne, ye nwo abubue yeɛ waadwu me nyunu ne anaa. Na sɛ nna sɔ yeɛ ɔte hɔ a, ngonwu ye.”

english_verse: The men turned and started toward Sodom. But the Lord stayed with Abraham.
