english_verse: Rebekah later told Isaac, “Those Hittite wives of Esau are making my life miserable! If Jacob marries a Hittite woman, I'd be better off dead.”
translation_verse: Na Rebɛka sele Yisake kyɛ, “Hiti mmrasua nemɔ amaa wiase afono me. Sɛ ɔkɔba kyɛ Yakob gya Hiti mmrasua nemɔ bie kyɛ Yisɔ deɛ nemɔ a, ye de né nwuli po a ahaa ɔte paa.”

english_verse: Isaac called in Jacob, then gave him a blessing, and said: Don't marry any of those Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Yiti Yisake frɛle Yakob na oyirale ye, na ɔkanzole ye kyɛ, “Nnɛgya Kanaanniɛ brasua biala.

english_verse: Go at once to your mother's father Bethuel in northern Syria and choose a wife from one of the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.
translation_verse: Dwɔso kɔ wɔ maame ase Betuel awuro wɔ Padan Aram na kogya wɔ wɔfa Laban ye mma mmrasua nemɔ nu ko.

english_verse: I pray that God All-Powerful will bless you with many descendants and let you become a great nation.
translation_verse: Ɛdangama Nyameɛ óyira wɔ ná ɔma ɛwo, ná wɔ boso ɔtrɛ, amaa ɔnate so ayɛ maen maen pee bɛ nana.

english_verse: May he bless you with the land he promised Abraham, so that you will take over this land where we now live as foreigners.
translation_verse: Ɔ́ma wɔ ne wɔ bosofoɛ bɛ sa ha Abraham saleɛ ne, amaa ɔnate so ɛmɔ sa aha aseɛ bɔ yeɛ Nyameɛ fa mane Abraham, bɔ yeɛ aayɛ so ɛwɔfoɛ ye.”

english_verse: Isaac then sent Jacob to stay with Rebekah's brother Laban, the son of Bethuel the Aramean. Esau Marries the Daughter of Ishmael
translation_verse: Yiti Yisake guale Yakob ate maa ɔhɔle. Yakob hɔle Aramniɛ Betuel awa Laban berɛ wɔ Padan Aram. Laban te Yisɔ ne Yakob ani Rebɛka aliɛma bienzua. Yisɔ gya braa bieku

english_verse: Esau found out that his father Isaac had blessed Jacob and had warned him not to marry any of the Canaanite women. He also learned that Jacob had been sent to find a wife in northern Syria
translation_verse: Na Yisɔ tele kyɛ Yisake ayira Yakob na wamaa wahɔ Padan Aram kyɛ oogya braa dɔ. Ɔtele kyɛ óyira ye ne, ɔkanzole ye kyɛ, “Nnɛgya Kanaanfoɛ mmrasua nemɔ nu bie,”

english_verse: and that he had obeyed his father and mother.
translation_verse: na ɔnate sɔ ati Yakob ayɛ sotie ama ɔse ne oni na wahɔ Padan Aram.

english_verse: Esau already had several wives, but he now realized how much his father hated the Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Yiti Yisɔ nwuni kyɛ Yisake nye ngye Kanaan mmrasua nemɔ nwo ne,

english_verse: So he married Ishmael's daughter Mahalath, who was the sister of Nebaioth and the granddaughter of Abraham. Jacob's Dream at Bethel
translation_verse: ɔhɔle Abraham awa Yismael dɔ, na oogyale Yismael awa brasua Mahalate bokale ɔye mɔ aso. Né Mahalate te Nebayote aliɛma brasua. Yakob kye laleɛ wɔ Betel

english_verse: Jacob left the town of Beersheba and started out for Haran.
translation_verse: Yakob fili Beɛ Hyeba na ɔfale ye nye hyirele Haran.

english_verse: At sunset he stopped for the night and went to sleep, resting his head on a large rock.
translation_verse: Odwuli nekaa bie, na ɔtenane berɛ kɔngɔen ne, ofikyɛ né aleɛ adwo. Ɔfale berɛ nyɔboɛ ne ko suane, na ɔlale berɛ.

english_verse: In a dream he saw a ladder that reached from earth to heaven, and God's angels were going up and down on it.
translation_verse: Ɔhyene laleɛ, onwuni atweleɛ bie bɔ ofi aseɛ so kɔka nyameɛso ɔ, na né Nyameɛ abɔfo mɔ bɛfo bedwu wɔ so!

english_verse: The Lord was standing beside the ladder and said: I am the Lord God who was worshiped by Abraham and Isaac. I will give to you and your family the land on which you are now sleeping.
translation_verse: Ɛlaleɛ ne anu, né AWURADE gyi ye ti sorɔ, na osele kyɛ, “Me ole AWURADE, wɔ nana Abraham ye Nyameɛ bɔ ɔte Yisake koso ye Nyameɛ ne. Ngɔfa aseɛ he bɔ yeɛ ɛla so kekesaala ye ngɔma wɔ ne wɔ bosofoɛ.

english_verse: Your descendants will spread over the earth in all directions and will become as numerous as the specks of dust. Your family will be a blessing to all people.
translation_verse: Wɔ bosofoɛ kɔsone kyɛ aseɛ so mvuture. Na wɔ boso kɔtrɛ kofi eyia afiteleɛ koodwu eyia atɔleɛ; fi sorɔ kodwu ngwaen, na ɔnate wɔ ne wɔ bosofoɛ so yeɛ ewiase mmenia amu konya saleɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Wherever you go, I will watch over you, then later I will bring you back to this land. I won't leave you—I will do all I have promised.
translation_verse: Nea, ngyi wɔ si na ngɔbɔ wɔ nwo waen nekaa biala bɔ ɛkɔhɔ ɔ, na ngosa ngɔfa wɔ ngɔwa aseɛ ye aso. Ofikyɛ mengɔyakyi wɔ nu kɔpem kyɛ ngɔyɔ bɔ mafa mahyɛ wɔ bɔ ne amu ɔ.”

english_verse: Jacob woke up suddenly and thought, “The Lord is in this place, and I didn't even know it.”
translation_verse: Yakob fili nnaa nu tingyele na osele kyɛ, “Amba, AWURADE wɔ wa, yeɛ saa né menze ye!”

english_verse: Then Jacob became frightened and said, “What a frightening place! It must be the house of God and the gateway to heaven.”
translation_verse: Ɛserɛ hane ye, na osele kyɛ, “Kyɛ ɛwa yɛ suro paa hɔ ɛhe! Nna hwee kyɛ Nyameɛ awuro ɔ, nyameɛso anoa ɔ.”

english_verse: When Jacob got up early the next morning, he took the rock that he had used for a pillow and stood it up as a place of worship. Then he poured olive oil on the rock to dedicate it to God,
translation_verse: Yiti Yakob dwɔsole ngyerɛmɔ tutututu, na ɔfale nyɔboɛ bɔ ɔfa suane ne, na ɔfa penane berɛ kyɛ ngayeɛ nyɔboɛ, na ohwiele ngoo guale so.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Before that it had been named Luz.
translation_verse: Na ɔfrɛle berɛ Betel, nakoso daa ne de, né bɛfrɛ kuro ne Luse.

english_verse: Jacob solemnly promised God, “If you go with me and watch over me as I travel, and if you give me food and clothes
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yakob hyɛle Nyameɛ bɔ kyɛ, “Sɛ Nyameɛ kogyina me si, na ɔkɔnea me so wɔ m’ateetulɛ ye anu, na ɔkɔma me aleɛ maa ngoli ɔne ɛtena maa ngɔhera,

english_verse: and bring me safely home again, you will be my God.
translation_verse: na ɔmaa mesa meba me se awuro asomdwee nu a, ye de AWURADE kɔyɛ me Nyameɛ.

english_verse: This rock will be your house, and I will give back to you a tenth of everything you give me.”
translation_verse: Na nyɔboɛ he bɔ mafa mapena berɛ mayɛ ngayeɛ nyɔboɛ ye kɔyɛ Nyameɛ awuro, na nikyee biala bɔ ɛkɔma me ne, ngɔma wɔ so buru nu ngyɛmuɛ ko.”

english_verse: As Jacob continued on his way to the east,
translation_verse: Yakob toale ye ateetulɛ ne aso, na oodwuli eyia afiteleɛfoɛ nemɔ maen nu.

english_verse: he looked out in a field and saw a well where shepherds took their sheep for water. Three flocks of sheep were lying around the well, which was covered with a large rock.
translation_verse: Na ɔtole ye nye ne, onwuni abura bie wɔ eburo berɛ, na edwirɛ nwanwa ne mmoaen kure nza lela ye nwo ɔ, ofikyɛ sɔ abura ne anu yeɛ né bɛsa nzue bɛma ngaka nemɔ ɔ. Né nyɔboɛ bɔ ɔkata abura ne aso ne te piri.

english_verse: Shepherds would roll the rock away when all their sheep had gathered there. Then after the sheep had been watered, the shepherds would roll the rock back over the mouth of the well.
translation_verse: Yiti sɛ mmoaen ne amukoraa bɛ noa baboa berɛ a, mmoaenneafoɛ nemɔ muni nyɔboɛ ne befi abura ne anoa koraka né bama ngaka nemɔ nzue maa bano. Na sɛ beyie a, né basa bamunu nyɔboɛ ne bakata abura ne noa.

english_verse: Jacob asked the shepherds, “Where are you from?” “We're from Haran,” they answered.
translation_verse: Yakob bisale bɛ kyɛ, “Aliɛmaa mɔ, ɛmɔfi ni?” Na bebuale ye kyɛ, “Yɛfi Haran.”

english_verse: Then he asked, “Do you know Nahor's grandson Laban?” “Yes we do,” they replied.
translation_verse: Yakob sá bisale bɛ kyɛ, “Aso ɛmɔse Nahɔ anomaa Laban. Na bebuale ye kyɛ, “Yoo, yɛse ye.”

english_verse: “How is he?” Jacob asked. “He's fine,” they answered. “And here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.”
translation_verse: Yakob sá bisale bɛ kyɛ, “Ye nwo te paa?” Na besele ye kyɛ, “Yoo, ye nwo te paa. Nea ɔwa brasua Rahɛl po yeɛ ɔne mmoaen nemɔ ba ne.”

english_verse: Jacob told them, “Look, the sun is still high up in the sky, and it's too early to bring in the rest of the flocks. Water your sheep and take them back to the pasture.”
translation_verse: Na Yakob sele kyɛ, “Ɔtɛte eyiagyina; mmerɛ bɔ bɛfa bɛboaboa ngaka nemɔ noa ne onnya oddwuli. Ɛ́mɔma bɛ nzue ma bɛ no na ɛ́mɔfa bɛ bɛhɔ adidie.”

english_verse: But they replied, “We can't do that until they all get here, and the rock has been rolled away from the well.”
translation_verse: Nakoso besele ye kyɛ, “Daabi, yɛngɔhora ngɔyɔ ye sɔ. Sana bɛboaboa ngaka ne amukoraa noa ná yɛmunu nyɔboɛ ne yɛfi abura ne anoa koraka né yama ngaka nemɔ nzue.”

english_verse: While Jacob was still talking with the men, his cousin Rachel came up with her father's sheep.
translation_verse: Na Yakob noa wɔ so bɔ ɔne bɛ dwudwo ne, Rahɛl ne ɔse mmoaen ne wale, ofikyɛ ye yeɛ né ɔnea bɛ so ɔ.

english_verse: When Jacob saw her and his uncle's sheep, he rolled the rock away and watered the sheep.
translation_verse: Yakob nwuni ye wɔfa Laban awa Rahɛl ɔne Laban mmoaen nen, ɔhɔle oomununi nyɔboɛ ne fili abura ne anoa, na ɔmane ye wɔfa Laban mmoaen nemɔ nzue.

english_verse: He then kissed Rachel and started crying because he was so happy.
translation_verse: Yakob fele Rahɛl noa, na ɔteateane nu osuni.

english_verse: He told her that he was the son of her aunt Rebekah, and she ran and told her father about him.
translation_verse: Yakob sele Rahɛl kyɛ ɔte ɔse busuaniɛ, na Rebɛka awa ole ye. Na Rahɛl tuli amirika ɔbɔle ɔse amaneɛ.

english_verse: As soon as Laban heard the news, he ran out to meet Jacob. He hugged and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Laban tele ye awosea Yakob nga nen, ole amirika ooyiale ye, ɔtɔle ye nu, na ɔfele ye noa, na ɔfale ye wale ye awuro. Yakob fale edwirɛ ne amukoraa bɔle Laban amaneɛ,

english_verse: Laban said, “You are my nephew, and you are like one of my own family.” Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel After Jacob had been there for a month,
translation_verse: na Laban sele ye kyɛ, “Amba ɛte me dehyeɛ kaenn.” Na Yakob tenane Laban nwo berɛ ɛsraen ko. Rahɛl ne Lea ti Yakob so Laban

english_verse: Laban said to him, “You shouldn't have to work without pay, just because you are a relative of mine. What do you want me to give you?”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Laban sele Yakob kyɛ, “Ɛte me dehyeɛ ne ati, aso odi kyɛ ɛso me mbaen anaa? Ka kyire me, akatuaa sɛɛ yeɛ ekole ɔ?”

english_verse: Laban had two daughters. Leah was older than Rachel, but her eyes didn't sparkle, while Rachel was beautiful and had a good figure.
translation_verse: Lea nye mmaa te mmosonoo, nakoso Rahɛl de, né ye nwo yɛ nyemene, yeɛ ye nwo yɛ ahomeka.

english_verse: Since Jacob was in love with Rachel, he answered, “If you will let me marry Rachel, I'll work seven years for you.”
translation_verse: Né Yakob kuro Rahɛl, yiti ɔhane kyɛ, “Ɛwa kãa Rahɛl ti ngɔso wɔ afoɛ nzoo.”

english_verse: Laban replied, “It's better for me to let you marry Rachel than for someone else to have her. So stay and work for me.”
translation_verse: Laban sele kyɛ, “Ɔte paa kyɛ ngɔfa ye ngɔma wɔ tra kyɛ ngɔfa ye ngɔma biaa foforɛ ɔ; yiti ɛne me tena.”

english_verse: Jacob worked seven years for Laban, but the time seemed like only a few days, because he loved Rachel so much.
translation_verse: Rahɛl ti, Yakob sole afoɛ nzoo, na ɔnate ehurolɛ bɔ né okuro ye ne ati, ɔyɛle ye nye so kyɛ ngyẽa kãa bie.

english_verse: Jacob said to Laban, “The time is up, and I want to marry Rachel now!”
translation_verse: Nziɛ ye Yakob sele Laban kyɛ, “Fa me ye ne ma me maa me ne ye yɛɛla, ofikyɛ mmerɛ bɔ mefa me so wɔ ne awa ayieleɛ.”

english_verse: So Laban gave a big feast and invited all their neighbors.
translation_verse: Yiti Laban tole ye sa frɛle kuro berɛ ama mukoraa, na ɔtole poen.

english_verse: But that evening he brought Leah to Jacob, who married her and spent the night with her.
translation_verse: Nakoso aleɛ dwole ne, ɔfale ɔwa brasua Lea brɛle Yakob, na ɔne ye lale.

english_verse: The next morning Jacob found out that he had married Leah, and he asked Laban, “Why did you do this to me? Didn't I work to get Rachel? Why did you trick me?”
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, Yakob kwaanea a, saa Lea mmom ɔ! Yiti obisale Laban kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ dwirɛ yeɛ afa ali me ye? Nna Rahɛl ti yeɛ nzole wɔ ɔ? Nzu ati yeɛ alakalaka me ye?”

english_verse: Laban replied, “In our country the older daughter must get married first.
translation_verse: Laban buale ye kyɛ, “Yɛ maen ye anu de yɛnyɔ ye sɔ; yɛmva baa kãa yɛmma agyaa koraka né yafa bamuɛbaa yama.

english_verse: After you spend this week with Leah, you may also marry Rachel. But you will have to work for me another seven years.”
translation_verse: Ɛne ye beli atɔmvorɛ poentolɛ ɛlɛbɔtwɛ ne beyie. Ye si ye, yɛkɔfa ko ne koso yɛkɔma wɔ, na sana ɛso me afoɛ nzoo boka so.”

english_verse: At the end of the week of celebration, Laban let Jacob marry Rachel, and he gave her his servant woman Bilhah. Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, but he had to work another seven years for Laban.
translation_verse: Yiti Yakob ne Rahɛl koso lale; né okuro Rahɛl tra Lea, na osa sole Laban afoɛ nzoo bieku. Yakob wo mmaa

english_verse: The Lord knew that Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, and so he gave children to Leah, but not to Rachel.
translation_verse: AWURADE nwuni kyɛ Yakob nguro Lea, yiti ɔmane Lea wole mmaa, nakoso Rahɛl de ɔyɛle mmotaen.

english_verse: Leah gave birth to a son and named him Reuben. Then she said, “The Lord has taken away my sorrow. Now my husband will love me more than he does Rachel.”
translation_verse: Lea nwonzɛle, na ɔwole baa bienzua, na ɔtole ye dumaa Ruben. Na ɔhane kyɛ, “AWURADE anwu m’amaneɛ bɔ méfa nu ne ati, kekesaala ye de me hu kohuro me.”

english_verse: She had a second son and named him Simeon, because she said, “The Lord has heard that my husband doesn't love me.”
translation_verse: Ɔnwonzɛle bieku na ɔwole bienzua, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Ɔnate kyɛ AWURADE anwu kyɛ benguro me ne ati yeɛ watie me na wafa baa bienzua he koso wahyɛ me ɔ.” Na ɔtole ye dumaa Simeon.

english_verse: When Leah's third son was born, she said, “Now my husband will hold me close.” So this son was named Levi.
translation_verse: Osa nwonzɛle na ɔwole bienzua, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Afei de me hu kɔha kɔwa me nwo, ofikyɛ mawo mmaa mmienzua nza mama ye. Yiti ɔfrɛle ye Lewi.

english_verse: She had one more son and named him Judah, because she said, “I'll praise the Lord!”
translation_verse: Osa nwonzɛle bieku na ɔwole bienzua, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Afei de ngɔye AWURADE ayɛ,” yiti ɔtole ye dumaa Yuda. Na ye aworɛ te hɔle.

english_verse: Rachel was very jealous of Leah for having children, and she said to Jacob, “I'll die if you don't give me some children!”
translation_verse: Rahɛl nwuni kyɛ ɔne Yakob bɛnwo ne, ye nye borole oliɛma ne, na osele Yakob kyɛ, “Ɛne me wo mmaa, anyɔ sɔ a ngowu!”

english_verse: But Jacob became upset with Rachel and answered, “Don't blame me! I'm not God.”
translation_verse: Na Yakob fɛle Rahɛl so yaa paa. Yiti obisale ye kyɛ, “Aso Nyameɛ bɔ wasi wɔ aworɛ nwo ate ne, me yeɛ ngyi ye gya nu anaa?”

english_verse: “Here, take my servant Bilhah,” Rachel told him. “Have children by her, and I'll let them be born on my knees to show that they are mine.”
translation_verse: Na Rahɛl sele ye kyɛ, “M’afaneɛ Bilha ɛhe. Ɛne ye bɛla maa ɔwo to me gya so, amaa ɔnate ye so manya mmaa.”

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Bilha nwonzɛle, na ɔwole baa bienzua mane Yakob.

english_verse: Rachel named him Dan, because she said, “God has answered my prayers. He judged in my favor and has given me a son.”
translation_verse: Na Rahɛl hane kyɛ, “Nyameɛ ali me dwirɛ ama me. Watie me dwirɛ na wama me baa bienzua,” yiti ɔtole ye dumaa Dan.

english_verse: When Bilhah and Jacob had a second son,
translation_verse: Rahɛl afaneɛ Bilha nwonzɛle bieku, na ɔwole baa bienzua bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ɔ mane Yakob.

english_verse: Rachel said, “I've struggled hard with my sister, and I've won!” So she named the boy Naphtali.
translation_verse: Na Rahɛl hane kyɛ, “Apereapereɛ yeɛ me ne nniɛma brasua ye yapere ɔ, na mali ye so ngonim.” Yiti ɔtole ye dumaa Nafetali.

english_verse: When Leah realized she could not have any more children, she let Jacob marry her servant Zilpah,
translation_verse: Lea nwuni kyɛ ye aworɛ ate ahɔ nen, ɔfale ye afaneɛ Silpa mane Yakob maa ɔyɛle ɔye.

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Lea afaneɛ Silpa wole baa bienzua mane Yakob.

english_verse: “I'm really lucky,” Leah said, and she named the boy Gad.
translation_verse: Na Lea sele kyɛ, “Me ti ayɛ paa.” Yiti ɔtole ye dumaa Gade.

english_verse: Leah exclaimed, “I'm happy now, and all the women will say how happy I am.” So she named him Asher. Love Flowers
translation_verse: na Lea hane kyɛ, “Me nye agye paa! Mmrasua kɔfrɛ me ‘bɔ ye nye agye ɔ’ ”. Yiti ɔtole ye dumaa Asɛ.

english_verse: During the time of the wheat harvest, Reuben found some love flowers and took them to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah for some of them,
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ atokoɔ telɛ dwuli ne, Ruben hɔle eburo, na ɔɔtetele nwonzɛenyire mmakaammaa, na ɔfa brɛle oni Lea. Yeɛ Rahɛl srɛle Lea kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, ma me ɛwa ne nwonzɛenyire bakaammaa ne bie.”

english_verse: but Leah said, “It's bad enough that you stole my husband! Now you want my son's love flowers too.” “All right,” Rachel answered. “Let me have the flowers, and you can sleep with Jacob tonight.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Lea bisale ye kyɛ, “Aso me hu bɔ ale ye ne, ɛhene angome anzo wɔ? Ɛpena kyɛ ede mma nwonzɛenyire mmakaammaa ne koso boka so?” Na Rahɛl sele kyɛ, “Nzaade maa ɔne wɔ bɛla ɛnɛ kɔngɔen ye na fa tua ɛwa ne nwonzɛenyire mmakaammaa ne kerɛ.”

english_verse: That evening when Jacob came in from the fields, Leah told him, “You're sleeping with me tonight. I hired you with my son's love flowers.” They slept together that night,
translation_verse: Yiti Yakob fili fieso wale nɔsoa nen, Lea ooyiale ye, na osele ye kyɛ, “Bra baala me berɛ, ofikyɛ mafa mma nwonzɛenyire mmakaammaa ne matua wɔ nnaa ne kerɛ. Na Yakob ne Lea bɛɛlale sɔ kɔngɔen ne.

english_verse: and God answered Leah's prayers by giving her a fifth son.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ tiele Lea, ɔnwonzɛle, na ɔne Yakob bɛwole ɔwa bienzua bɔ ɔtɔ so nnu ɔ.

english_verse: Leah shouted, “God has rewarded me for letting Jacob marry my servant,” and she named the boy Issachar.
translation_verse: Lea sele kyɛ, “Nyameɛ afa m’akatuaa wama me, ofikyɛ mvale m’afaneɛ mane me hu.” Yiti ɔtole ye dumaa Yisaka.

english_verse: she exclaimed, “God has given me a wonderful gift, and my husband will praise me for giving him six sons.” So she named the boy Zebulun.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Lea sele kyɛ, “Nyameɛ ahyɛ me akyɛdeɛ paa, afei de me hu kobu me bie, ofikyɛ mawo mmaa mmienzua nzia mama ye.” Yiti ɔtole ye dumaa Sebulɔn.

english_verse: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
translation_verse: Ɛhe asi ne, ɔwole brasua, na ɔtole ye dumaa Dina.

english_verse: Finally, God remembered Rachel—he answered her prayer by giving her a son. “God has taken away my disgrace,” she said.
translation_verse: Ɔnwonzɛle, ɔwole baa bienzua, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Nyameɛ akyikyi m’animguaseɛ”;

english_verse: “I'll name the boy Joseph, and I'll pray that the Lord will give me another son.” Jacob and Laban
translation_verse: ɔtole ye dumaa Yosef, na ɔhane kyɛ, “AWURADE, ma me baa bienzua bieku boka ɛhe aso!” Yakob ne Laban nnakannaka

english_verse: After Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Release me from our agreement and let me return to my own country.
translation_verse: Rahɛl wole Yosef ne, ye si ye, Yakob sele Laban kyɛ, “Ma me ate maa ngɔ me kuro ne me maen nu.

english_verse: You know how hard I've worked for you, so let me take my wives and children and leave.”
translation_verse: Me ye mɔ bɔ bɛ ti yeɛ maso wɔ ne, fa bɛ ne me mma mɔ maa ngɔ; ofikyɛ wɔ bɔbɔ ɛse ɛsolɛ bɔ yeɛ maso wɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: Jacob answered: You've seen how hard I've worked for you, and you know how your flocks and herds have grown under my care.
translation_verse: Yakob sele ye kyɛ, “Wɔ bɔbɔ deinn ɛse kyɛbɔ masi maso wɔ ɔ, ɔne kyɛbɔ wɔ nyɛmmoa asi ata wɔ me sa nu ɔ.

english_verse: You didn't have much before I came, but the Lord has blessed everything I have ever done for you. Now it's time for me to start looking out for my own family.
translation_verse: Mmmale ɛwa ne, né wɔ ngaka nemɔ anzo. Ɛnɛ nea bɛ somaa. AWURADE ayira wɔ nikyee biala bɔ mvale me sa nzɔle nu anwo. Na afei kyinzu yeɛ ngoli me bɔbɔ m’awuro so ɔ?”

english_verse: “How much do you want me to pay you?” Laban asked. Then Jacob told him: I don't want you to pay me anything. Just do one thing, and I'll take care of your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Laban bisale ye kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ yeɛ ede ɔ?” Na Yakob buale kyɛ, “Nnɛma me nikye fee; na mmom sɛ ɛkɔyɔ sɔ nikyee ye kɔma me a de a, ngɔhɔ so ngɔyɛne wɔ ngaka nemɔ na manea bɛ:

english_verse: Let me go through your flocks and herds and take the sheep and goats that are either spotted or speckled and the black lambs. That's all you need to give me.
translation_verse: ɛnɛ kyẽa ye, maa mva wɔ mmoaen ne amu nu, na nyeye mmoaen bɔ bɛ nwo te kyerekyerɛɛ ne ndetaa ndetaa ɔne mmoaen mmaa bɔ bɛ nwo te bire, ɔne mbɔngye bɔ bɛ nwo te kyerekyerɛɛ ne ndetaa ndetaa; na sɔ ngaka nemɔ yeɛ bɛkɔyɛ m’akatuaa ɔ.

english_verse: In the future you can easily find out if I've been honest. Just look and see if my animals are either spotted or speckled, or if the lambs are black. If they aren't, they've been stolen from you.
translation_verse: Yiti kyẽa bie sɛ ɛbaneanea m’akatuaa nu a, me nahorɛlilɛ kobua me be. Sɛ enwu abɔngye bɔ ye nwo ɔtte kyerekyerɛɛ anaa ndetaa ndetaa, anaakyɛ boaen ba bɔ ɔtte bire wɔ me deɛ nu a, bu sɔ kaka ne kyɛ mawua.”

english_verse: “I agree to that,” was Laban's response.
translation_verse: Na Laban sele kyɛ, “Yoo, mede meto nu.”

english_verse: Before the end of the day, Laban had separated his spotted and speckled animals and the black lambs from the others and had put his sons in charge of them.
translation_verse: Nakoso sɔ kyẽa ne ala, Laban yeyele mbɔngye nyii bɔ bɛ nwo te kyerekyerɛɛ ne ndetaa ndetaa ne, ɔne mbɔngye mmeleɛ bɔ bɛ nwo te kyerekyerɛɛ ne ndetaa ndetaa mukoraa, ɔne kaka biala bɔ fufue wɔ ye nwo, ɔne boaen ba biala bɔ ɔte bire, na ɔfale bɛ wurale ye mma mmienzua mɔ sa;

english_verse: Then Laban made Jacob keep the rest of the sheep and goats at a distance of three days' journey.
translation_verse: na ɔmane atee bɔ bɛfa ɛlɛsa yeɛ bɛpɛ ɔ lale ye ne Yakob b’afia, na Yakob hɔle so neane mmoaen ngaa nemɔ aso.

english_verse: Jacob cut branches from some poplar trees and from some almond and evergreen trees. He peeled off part of the bark and made the branches look spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Yakob pepɛle tanure ne atonwaa ne ekue, na ɔwɔngyewɔngyele bɛ nwo boen maa ɔsesane nu, maa bɛ nwo fufue ne lale berɛ.

english_verse: Then he put the branches where the sheep and goats would see them while they were drinking from the water trough. The goats mated there
translation_verse: Ɔfale mmakaa bɔ wawɔngyewɔngye bɛ nwo ne guale nningyein bɔ ngaka nemɔ no nu nzue ne anwo. Né sɛ ngaka nemɔ ba kyɛ bɛbaano nzue a, berɛ yeɛ bɛfo bɛ nwo ɔ.

english_verse: Some of the sheep that Jacob was keeping for Laban were already spotted. And when the others were ready to mate, he made sure that they faced in the direction of the spotted and black ones. In this way, Jacob built up a flock of sheep for himself and did not put them with the other sheep.
translation_verse: Yakob yeyele mmoaen mmaa nemɔ siele ahameɛ, ɔmane bɛ ngaa ne fale bɛ nye hyirele Laban mmoaen bɔ bɛ nwo te krukyerɛɛ ɔne bɛ bɔ bɛ nwo te bire ne amukoraa. Yakob fale atee he aso siele ye ngaka deɛ mɔ wɔ nekaa foforɛ bɔ wamva bɛ wamvora Laban deɛ nu ɔ.

english_verse: But he would not put out the branches when the weaker animals were mating. So Jacob got all of the healthy animals, and Laban got what was left.
translation_verse: Nakoso ngaka nemɔ bɔ bɛ nwo nyɛ se ne de, ɔmva mmakaa ne ngua berɛ. Ye sɔ ne ati, bɛ bɔ bɛ nwo nyɛ se ne yɛle Laban deɛ maa bɛ bɔ bɛ nwo yɛ se ne yɛle Yakob deɛ.

english_verse: Jacob soon became rich and successful. He owned many sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of slaves.
translation_verse: Ɔmaa Yakob nyane ye nwo tam; onyane mmoaen pee, ngoaa ne afaneɛ mɔ, afupɔngɔ ne afunum pee.

english_verse: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining, “Jacob is now a rich man, and he got everything he owns from our father.”
translation_verse: Yakob tele kyɛ Laban mma mmienzua nemɔ kekã kyɛ, “Yakob afa yɛ baba nningyein mukoraa; yɛ baba nwo yeɛ wafa wanya sɔ agyapadeɛ ye amu ɔ.”

english_verse: Jacob also noticed that Laban was not as friendly as he had been before.
translation_verse: Onwuni kyɛ Laban olle ye nwo adwene paa kyɛ daa ne ko.

english_verse: One day the Lord said, “Jacob, go back to your relatives in the land of your ancestors, and I will be with you.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Yakob kyɛ, “Sá kɔ wɔ nana mɔ maen nu ne w’abusua nu, na ngogyina wɔ si.”

english_verse: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him in the pasture where he kept his sheep,
translation_verse: Yiti Yakob somane maa bɛɛfrɛle Rahɛl ne Lea bɛbrɛle ye wɔ eburo dɔ nekaa bɔ né ye nyɛmmoa nemɔ wɔ ne,

english_verse: and he told them: Your father isn't as friendly with me as he used to be, but the God my ancestors worshiped has been on my side.
translation_verse: na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Manwu ye kyɛ ɛmɔ ase ɔne me y’asetena ne anu ɔnyɛ nyemene kyɛ daa ne ko, nakoso me nana mɔ Nyameɛ ne agyina me si.

english_verse: years to buy your sheep and goats. During that time you kept changing my wages.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔse ye kyɛ mafia me kunu mafa m’anwoserɛ amu maso ɛmɔ ase.

english_verse: and that he keeps cheating me by changing my wages time after time. But God has protected me.
translation_verse: Nakoso ɛmɔ ase asisi me. Wasesã m’akatuaa sɔ alaa buru mumua, nakoso Nyameɛ amma ye ate maa wambura me.

english_verse: When your father said the speckled sheep would be my wages, all of them were speckled. And when he said the spotted ones would be mine, all of them were spotted.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɔka kyɛ, ‘W’akatuaa kɔyɛ ngaka bɔ bɛ nwo te ndetaa ndetaa ne’ a, né ngaka ne amu bawo anwo ndetaa ndetaa. Yeɛ sɛ ɔka kyɛ w’akatuaa kɔyɛ ngaka bɛ nwo te kyerekyerɛɛ ne a, né ngaka ne amu bawo anwo kyerekyerɛɛ.

english_verse: That's how God has taken sheep and goats from your father and given them to me.
translation_verse: Sɔ atee he aso yeɛ Nyameɛ nate wale ɛmɔ baba ngaka kure ne wafi ye sa nu na wafa wama me ye.

english_verse: Once, when the flocks were mating, I dreamed that all the rams were either spotted or speckled.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ ngaka nemɔ sɔle ne, ngyene laleɛ. Laleɛ ne anu, mbagyale me ti, na nwuni kyɛ mbɔngye nyii bɔ bɛ́fo mmeleɛ nemɔ ne, bɛ nwo te kyerekyerɛɛ ne ndetaa ndetaa ne nworonworaen.

english_verse: Then God's angel called me by name. I answered,
translation_verse: Laleɛ ne anu, Nyameɛ abɔfo frɛle me kyɛ, ‘Yakob.’ Na nzurole kyɛ, ‘Me ɛhe!’

english_verse: and he said, “Notice that all the rams are either spotted or speckled. I know everything Laban is doing to you,
translation_verse: Osele me kyɛ, ‘Pagya wɔ ti na nea: ngaka nyii bɔ bɛ́fo mmeleɛ ne amukoraa bɛ nwo te kyerekyerɛɛ, ndetaa ndetaa ne nworonworaen; ofikyɛ me nye tua bɔ Laban ɔ́fa di wɔ ne amu.

english_verse: and I am the God you worshiped at Bethel, when you poured olive oil on a rock and made a promise to me. Leave here at once and return to the land where you were born.”
translation_verse: Me ole Betel Nyameɛ, nekaa bɔ yeɛ ehwiele ngoo guale ngayeɛ nyɔboɛ so na ɛhyɛle me bɔ ne. Afei dwɔso na fi sɔ maen ye anu na sá kɔ aseɛ bɔ yeɛ bɛpɛle wɔ kotoa wɔ so ne aso.’ ”

english_verse: He treats us like foreigners and has even cheated us out of the bride price that should have been ours.
translation_verse: Aso ommu yɛ amanvrafoɛ? Wayɛ yɛ atɔen, na ódi yɛ ti sikaa ne.

english_verse: So do whatever God tells you to do. Even the property God took from our father and gave to you really belongs to us and our children.
translation_verse: Agyapadeɛ bɔ Nyameɛ ale afi yɛ baba sa nu ne amukoraa te yɛ ne yɛ mma deɛ. Yiti afei de, yɔ bɔ Nyameɛ aha ahyire wɔ biala.”

english_verse: Then Jacob, his wives, and his children got on camels and left
translation_verse: Na Yakob dwɔsole fale ye mma mɔ ne ɔye mɔ tenatenane afupɔngɔ so.

english_verse: northern Syria for the home of his father Isaac in Canaan. Jacob took along all his flocks, herds, and other property.
translation_verse: Ɔhane ye nyɛmmoa amukoraa lili ye nyunu, ɔsesale ye agyapadeɛ ne ye ngaka bɔ onyane ye wɔ Padan Aram amukoraati, na ɔfale ye nye hyirele Kanaan aseɛ so kyɛ ɔ́kɔ ɔse Yisake dɔ.

english_verse: Before Rachel left, she stole the household idols while Laban was out shearing his sheep.
translation_verse: Né Laban ahɔ kyɛ ɔkwaapepɛ ye mmoaen nwo nwiaa, na Rahɛl wuale ɔse awuro mmosoen.

translation_verse: Ɔsesale ye bɔbɔ ye nwo nningyein amukoraa nwatili, ɔpɛle asue Yufreti, na ɔfale ye nye hyirele Gileade mmokaa aseɛ ne aso. Laban po Yakob so

english_verse: Three days later Laban found out that Jacob had gone.
translation_verse: Ye ɛlɛsa ne aso, bɛbɔle Laban amaneɛ kyɛ Yakob anwati,

english_verse: So he took some of his relatives along and chased after Jacob for seven days, before catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
translation_verse: yiti ɔfale ye awuro ama bokale ye nwo so, na ɔpole Yakob so alaa ɛlɛsoo, maa oodwuli kyɛ opingyele Yakob wɔ Gileade mmokaa aseɛ ne aso ɔ.

english_verse: But God appeared to Laban in a dream that night and warned, “Don't say a word to Jacob. Don't make a threat or a promise.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Nyameɛ yele ye nwo ali hyirele Aramniɛ Laban kɔngɔen ne wɔ laleɛ nu, na ɔkanzole ye kyɛ, “Nea yé né anga edwirɛ biala, paa anaakyɛ tɛɛ angyire Yakob.”

english_verse: Jacob had set up camp in the hill country of Gilead, when Laban and his relatives came and set up camp in another part of the hill country. Laban went to Jacob
translation_verse: Laban ɔɔtole Yakob. Né Yakob asi ye ɛtena sua wɔ mmokaa aseɛ ne aso. Na Laban ne ye mmenia koso sili bɛ deɛ wɔ Gileade mmokaa aseɛ ne aso.

english_verse: and said: Look what you've done! You've tricked me and run off with my daughters like a kidnapper.
translation_verse: Na Laban bisale Yakob kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ nikye yeɛ ayɔ ye, bɔ alakalaka me na asesa me mma mmrasua mɔ anwati kyɛ mmenia bɔ bele ngrandɛ bahye bɛ nnure ye?

english_verse: Why did you sneak away without telling me? I would have given you a going-away party with singing and with music on tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Nzu ati yeɛ ɛyɛle kudɛɛ nwatili na ɛlakalakale me ɔ? Nzu ati yeɛ ammɔ me amaneɛ maa mamva anigye ne edwein ne akasaa ne sangoo mangua wɔ ate ɔ?

english_verse: You didn't even give me a chance to kiss my own grandchildren and daughters goodbye. That was really foolish.
translation_verse: Na nzu ati yeɛ amma mamve me nnomaa ne me mma mɔ noa, na me ne bɛ yanni ngraa ɔ? Ali ngwaseasɛm!

english_verse: I could easily hurt you, but the God your father worshiped has warned me not to make any threats or promises.
translation_verse: Ahaa nne ye nwo ate kyɛ me ne ɛmɔ di ye weewee, nakoso wɔ baba ye Nyameɛ ɔne me dwudwole ɛnɛ kɔngɔen kyɛ, ‘Nea yé né anga edwirɛ biala, paa anaakyɛ tɛɛ angyire Yakob.’

english_verse: I can understand why you were eager to return to your father, but why did you have to steal my idols?
translation_verse: Kekesaala ye de, wɔ wora adɔ ɛse awuro ti yeɛ ɛkɔ ɔ, na nzu ati yeɛ ewuale me mmosoen ɔ?”

english_verse: Jacob answered, “I left secretly because I was afraid you would take your daughters from me by force.
translation_verse: Na Yakob buale Laban kyɛ, “Né mesuro, ofikyɛ né medwene kyɛ ɛkɔhyɛ me kole wɔ mma mmrasua nemɔ kofi me sa nu.

english_verse: If you find that any one of us has taken your idols, I'll have that person killed. Let your relatives be witnesses. Show me what belongs to you, and you can take it back.” Jacob did not realize that Rachel had stolen the household idols.
translation_verse: Wɔ mmosoen nemɔ de, ebiala bɔ ekonwu bɛ wɔ ye dɔ ne, odi kyɛ beku ye ɔ. Y’eliɛma ye mɔ anyunu wa ala, neanea me nningyein nu nea sɛ wɔ nikyee bie wɔ nu a, ye.” Né Yakob nze kyɛ Rahɛl awua mmosoen ne ɔ.

english_verse: Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah, and the two servant women, but did not find the idols. Then he went to Rachel's tent.
translation_verse: Yiti Laban hɔle Yakob ɛtena sua nu, Lea ɛtena sua nu, ɔne afaneɛ nyɔ nemɔ deɛ nu nakoso wannwu bɛ. Na ofili Lea ɛtena sua ne anu oowurale Rahɛl deɛ nu.

english_verse: She had already hidden them in the cushion she used as a saddle and was sitting on it. Laban searched everywhere and did not find them.
translation_verse: Né Rahɛl asesa awuro mmosoen ne wafea afupɔngɔ so atɛ ne anu watena so. Laban tuli ɛtena sua ne anu nningyein amu, nakoso wannwu bɛ.

english_verse: Rachel said, “Father, please don't be angry with me for not getting up; I'm having my period.” Laban kept on searching, but still did not find the idols.
translation_verse: Na Rahɛl sele ɔse kyɛ, “Nnɛma me mene fɛ ɛyaa kyɛ mengɔhora dwɔso wɔ wɔ nyunu ɔ, ofikyɛ mabu me sa.” Yiti Laban hɔle so penane, nakoso wannwu ye awuro mmosoen nemɔ.

english_verse: Jacob became very angry and said to Laban: What have I done wrong? Have I committed some crime? Is that why you hunted me down?
translation_verse: Yiti Yakob fɛle ɛyaa, na ɔbɔle Laban kwaadu kyɛ, “Me mvomsoɛ ole sɛɛ? Ɛtɛɛ beni yeɛ mayɔ bɔ yeɛ egu me so anyeborolɛ so sɔa ye?

english_verse: After searching through everything I have, did you find anything of yours? If so, put it here, where your relatives and mine can see it. Then we can decide what to do.
translation_verse: Aso etuli me nningyein amukoraati ne, enwuni w’awuro nikyee bie wɔ nu? Sɛ anwu bie a, fa baato nniɛma mɔ ne eliɛma ye mɔ anyunu wa maa bebua yɛ munyɔ y’afia ndɛen.

english_verse: If a wild animal killed one of your sheep or goats, I paid for it myself. In fact, you demanded the full price, whether the animal was killed during the day or at night.
translation_verse: Bɛ bɔ ngaka aboyaa huni bɛ ne po, mamva mammrɛ wɔ, na mmom mmaa ɔyɛle me kerɛ. Na bɛ bɔ bewuale bɛ eyia anaa kɔngɔen ne wora, ɛmaa nduale ye kerɛ.

english_verse: I sweated every day, and I couldn't sleep at night because of the cold.
translation_verse: Tebea he yeɛ mvale nu ɔ: eyia yerale me, na ɛyerɛ koso huni me, na mannya nnaa kaala manna.

english_verse: If the fearsome God worshiped by Abraham and my father Isaac had not been on my side, you would have sent me away without a thing. But God saw my hard work, and he knew the trouble I was in, so he helped me. Then last night he told you how wrong you were. Jacob and Laban Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Me baba ye Nyameɛ bɔ yeɛ ɔte Abraham ye Nyameɛ, na osa te Nyameɛ bɔ Yisake suro ye ne, sɛ wangyina me si a, ahaa ɛmaa mvale nzanza ngɔle. Na Nyameɛ nwuni m’ateetee ne me fɛɛ, yiti yeɛ ɔmaa ɔhane wɔ nyunu anoma kɔngɔen ne.” Yakob ne Laban yɛ apam

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “Leah and Rachel are my daughters, and their children belong to me. All these sheep you are taking are really mine too. In fact, everything you have belongs to me. But there is nothing I can do to keep my daughters and their children.
translation_verse: Na Laban buale Yakob kyɛ, “Ndaluwa ye mɔ, me bɔbɔ me mma ɔ, ngwadaa ye mɔ koso, me bɔbɔ me nnomaa ɔ, na ngaka kure ne ɔne bɔ wɔ nye tua ye amu, me deɛ ɔ. Nakoso me mma mmrasua anaakyɛ bɛ mma bɔ bawo bɛ ye, nzikyɛ yeɛ ngɔhora ngɔyɔ ngɔfa bɛ nwo ɛnɛ ɔ?

english_verse: So I am ready to make an agreement with you, and we will pile up some large rocks here to remind us of the agreement.”
translation_verse: Afei bra maa yɛyɛ apam, na ɔyɛ adanzeɛ la me ne wɔ y’afia.”

english_verse: After Jacob had set up a large rock,
translation_verse: Yiti Yakob fale nyɔboɛ penane berɛ yɛle ngayeɛ nyɔboɛ wɔ berɛ.

english_verse: he told his men to get some more rocks and pile them up next to it. Then Jacob and Laban ate a meal together beside the rocks.
translation_verse: Yakob sele ye mmenia ne kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔboaboa nyɔboɛ noa.” Yiti bɛboale nyɔboɛ noa maa ɔyɛle kure, ne bɛtenane nyɔboɛ kure ne anwo berɛ bedidili.

english_verse: Laban named the pile of rocks Jegar Sahadutha. But Jacob named it Galeed.
translation_verse: Laban frɛle nyɔboɛ kure ne Yega Sahaduta, yeɛ Yakob wora ɔfrɛle ye Galeede.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “This pile of rocks will remind us of our agreement.” That's why the place was named Galeed.
translation_verse: Na Laban hane kyɛ, “Sɔ nyɔboɛ kure ye te me ne wɔ afia adanzeɛ ɛnɛ.” Yiti yeɛ ɔmaa bɛfrɛle berɛ Galeede ɔ.

english_verse: Laban also said, “This pile of rocks means that the Lord will watch us both while we are apart from each other.” So the place was also named Mizpah.
translation_verse: Na osa frɛle berɛ Misepa, ofikyɛ ɔhane kyɛ, “Sɛ yɛpakyepakye nu a, AWURADE osisa yɛ munyɔ.

english_verse: Then Laban said: If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women, I may not know about it, but remember, God is watching us!
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛteetee me mma mmrasua nemɔ, anaa sɛ egya braa foforɛ boka me mma nemɔ aso a, ɔwɔ nu kyɛ sona biala ɔbboka yɛ so wɔ ɛwa de, nakoso kaye kyɛ Nyameɛ yeɛ ɔte yɛ munyɔ y’afia danzeniɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Both this pile of rocks and this large rock have been set up between us as a reminder. I must never go past them to attack you, and you must never come past them to attack me.
translation_verse: Nyɔboɛ kure he te adanzeɛ, yeɛ ngayeɛ nyɔboɛ ye koso te adanzeɛ kyɛ mengɔtra sɔ nyɔboɛ kure he mengɔwa wɔ so mengɔyɔ wɔ hwee, na wɔ koso ɛngɔtra sɔ nyɔboɛ kure ye ne ngayeɛ nyɔboɛ ye ɛngɔwa me so na ɛngɔyɔ me hwee.

english_verse: My father Nahor, your grandfather Abraham, and their ancestors all worshiped the same God, and he will make sure that we each keep the agreement. Then Jacob made a promise in the name of the fearsome God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Abraham Nyameɛ bɔ ɔte Nahɔ Nyameɛ na osa te bɛ baba Nyameɛ ne, óbua me ne wɔ y’afia ndɛen.” Yiti Yakob fale Nyameɛ bɔ ɔse Yisake suro ye ne tale ndaen.

english_verse: Jacob killed an animal and offered it as a sacrifice there on the mountain, and he invited his men to eat with him. After the meal they spent the night on the mountain.
translation_verse: Na Yakob bɔle afɔleɛ wɔ bokaa ne aso, na ɔfrɛle ye mmenia kyɛ beedidi; bedidili na bɛbɔle asiripɛ wɔ mmokaa aseɛ ne aso.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Laban kissed his daughters and his grandchildren goodbye, then he left to go back home.
translation_verse: Laban dwɔsole ngyerɛmɔ tutututu, ɔfele ye nnomaa mɔ ne ye mma mmrasua nemɔ noa, na oyirale bɛ. Na osili nu hɔle ye kuro.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Yakob sili nu toale ye ateetulɛ ne aso, na Nyameɛ abɔfo mɔ yiale ye.

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Na Yakob nwuni bɛ ne, osele kyɛ, “Nyameɛ asraafoɛ mɔ ɛhe!” Yiti ɔtole berɛ dumaa Mahanaim.

english_verse: Jacob sent messengers on ahead to Esau, who lived in the land of Seir, also known as Edom.

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: Ɛbɔfoɛ nemɔ sá wale Yakob berɛ, na beesele ye kyɛ, “Yɛhɔle yɛɛtole eliɛma Yisɔ, na ɔbaayia wɔ; mmienzua ɛyaa nna boka ye so.”

english_verse: Jacob was so frightened that he divided his people, sheep, cattle, and camels into two groups.
translation_verse: Edwirɛ ne mane ɛserɛ piri hane Yakob; ɔhyɛle mmenia bɔ né bɛboka ye so ne anu nyɔ, ɔne mmoaen ne nandwie ne mbɔngɔ mɔ koso nu kure nyɔ.

english_verse: He thought, “If Esau attacks one group, perhaps the other can escape.”
translation_verse: Né ɔdwene kyɛ, “Sɛ Yisɔ ba kuku kure ko ná ɔdwerɛm bɛ a, kure ko bɔ waha ne, bekonya atee bɛkɔnwati.”

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.
translation_verse: Na Yakob bɔle mbaeɛ kyɛ, “O me nana Abraham Nyameɛ bɔ ɛte me baba Yisake Nyameɛ, O AWURADE bɔ esele me kyɛ, ‘Sá kɔ wɔ maen nu ne wɔ mmenia berɛ, na ngogyina wɔ si’ ɔ,

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: Mesrɛ wɔ, de me fi nniɛma Yisɔ sa nu, ofikyɛ me suro ye; anyɔ a, né waahũhũ yɛ mukoraa: niɛ mɔ ne mmaa mɔ.

english_verse: But you have promised that I would be a success and that someday it will be as hard to count my descendants as it is to count the grains of sand along the seashore.
translation_verse: Nakoso aha kyɛ, ‘Ngogyina wɔ si, na ngɔma wɔ bosofoɛ kɔsone kyɛ mboanoa anweaa bɔ bɛngora ye ka ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: After Jacob had spent the night there, he chose some animals as gifts for Esau:

english_verse: And Jacob told them to be sure to say that he was right behind them. Jacob hoped the gifts would make Esau friendly, so Esau would be glad to see him when they met.
translation_verse: na ɛmɔhã behyire ye kyɛ, ‘Asa koso, w’akoaa Yakob li yɛ si.’ ” Osusuli kyɛ, “Ngɔfa akyɛdeɛ bɔ wali me nyunu moa ye ngɔpata ye, na sɛ nziɛ ye me ne ye yɛyia a, mede medi kyɛ okole me kɔto nu.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face, and I am still alive.” So he named the place Peniel.
translation_verse: Yiti Yakob frɛle berɛ Peniɛl, ofikyɛ ɔnwa, “Me nye abɔ Nyameɛ nyunu, nakoso me ngoa tɛ tira me.”

translation_verse: Na ɔfa wurale ye ngoaa mɔ sa. Né kure biala akoaa ko yeɛ ɔla ye noa ɔ, na osele ngoaa nemɔ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔse beli me nyunu na ɛ́mɔma atee lela kure ne kure afia.”

english_verse: Then he said to the servant in charge of the first herd, “When Esau meets you, he will ask whose servant you are. He will want to know where you are going and who owns those animals in front of you.
translation_verse: Ɔhyɛle bɔ oli anyunu paa ne kyɛ, “Sɛ nniɛma Yisɔ yia wɔ na obisa wɔ kyɛ, ‘Nwa akoaa yeɛ ole wɔ? Ɛkɔ ni? Na ɛhemɔ bɔ beli wɔ nyunu ye nwa deɛ ɔ?’ a,

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: Yiti akyɛdeɛ ne lili Yakob nyunu moa hɔle, na ye bɔbɔ de ɔlale asikyeleɛ ne anu berɛ maa aleɛ hyene. Yakob ne abɔfo pere so

english_verse: Afterwards, Jacob went back and spent the rest of the night alone. A man came and fought with Jacob until just before daybreak.
translation_verse: Ɔhale Yakob ngome né, biaa bie ne ye besuale ngɔtɔfaen maa aleɛ hyene.

english_verse: When the man saw that he could not win, he struck Jacob on the hip and threw it out of joint.
translation_verse: Na biaa ne nwuni ye kyɛ ɔngora nni Yakob so ngonim ne, ɔbɔle Yakob taku so, na Yakob dwongu fandili wɔ ngɔtɔfaen ne anu.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.
translation_verse: Na osele kyɛ, “Yakyi me maa ngɔ na aleɛ ɔ́kye.” Nakoso Yakob buale kyɛ, “Mengɔma ɛngɔhɔ, sana eyira me koraka.”

translation_verse: Yiti me mene, se di w’akoaa nyunu. Me de meto me bo ase me ne nyɛmmoa ne ngwadaa bɔ bɛboka me so ne yɛdi wɔ si ngaka ngaka, kɔpem kyɛ ngoodwu wɔ berɛ wɔ Sɛre ɔ.”

english_verse: Esau replied, “Let me leave some of my men with you.” “You don't have to do that,” Jacob answered. “I am happy, simply knowing that you are friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Na Yisɔ sele kyɛ, “Maa me mmenia ne bie bɛboka wɔ so.” Nakoso Yakob hane kyɛ, “Aso ye nwo hia? Me mene, wɔ de kɔ so do me ala.”

english_verse: But Jacob went to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and set up shelters for his animals. That's why the place is called Succoth. Jacob Arrives at Shechem
translation_verse: Nakoso Yakob de ɔtoale so hɔle Sukote, na osili ye awuro wɔ berɛ, na osisili tuin mane ye nandwie mɔ; yiti bɛfrɛ berɛ Sukote.

english_verse: After leaving northern Syria, Jacob arrived safely at Shechem in Canaan and set up camp outside the city.
translation_verse: Yakob fili Padan Aram oodwuli Sɛkem bɔ ɔwɔ Kanaan aseɛ so asomdwee nu, na ɔkyekyele ɛtena sua wɔ kuro ne nyunu.

english_verse: The land where he camped was owned by the descendants of Hamor, the father of Shechem. So Jacob paid them
translation_verse: Na ɔtɔle aseɛ bɔ osili ye ɛtena sua wɔ so ne fili Sɛkem baba Hamɔ mma nemɔ berɛ. Ɔtɔle ye esikaa ɛdwetɛ ɛyaa ko.

english_verse: then he set up his tents and built an altar there to honor the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Osili afɔleɛ bokyea berɛ, na ɔfrɛle ye Ɛl Elohe Yisrael.

english_verse: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went to visit some of the women who lived nearby.
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, Lea ne Yakob bɛ wa brasua bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Dina ne, ofitele kyɛ ɔkwaapasa aseɛ ne aso mmrasua nemɔ anwo.

english_verse: She was seen by Hamor's son Shechem, the leader of the Hivites, and he grabbed her and raped her.
translation_verse: Hiwiniɛ Hamɔ bɔ ɔte aseɛ ne aso hene ne, ɔwa Sɛkem nwuni Dina, na ɔhyɛle ye ɔne ye bɛlale.

english_verse: But Shechem was attracted to Dinah, so he told her how much he loved her.
translation_verse: Na Sɛkem nye gyele Yakob awa brasua Dina nwo, ohurole taluwa ne, na ɔkorɔkorɔle ye.

english_verse: Shechem even asked his father to arrange for him to marry her.
translation_verse: Yiti Sɛkem sele ɔse Hamɔ kyɛ, “Kogya taluwa ye ma me.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Jacob heard what had happened. But his sons were out in the fields with the cattle, so he did not do anything at the time.
translation_verse: Yakob tele kyɛ Sɛkem ato ɔwa brasua Dina mmɔnaa, nakoso ɔnate kyɛ né ye mma mmienzua nemɔ bafa nandwie bahɔ adidie wɔ eburo ne ati, ɔyɛle konn kɔpem kyɛ besa bɛwale awuro ɔ.

english_verse: just as Jacob's sons were coming in from work. When they learned that their sister had been raped, they became furiously angry, because nothing is more disgraceful than rape, and it must not be tolerated.
translation_verse: Yakob mma mmienzua nemɔ tele bɔ wasi ne, befili eburo dɔ bɛwale. Ɔyɛle bɛ yea, na bɛfɛle yaa paa ofikyɛ Sɛkem ali ngwaseasɛm wɔ Yisrael; wayɔ bɔ bɛnyɔ ɔ, kyɛ ɔne Yakob awa brasua ala ɔ.

english_verse: Hamor said to Jacob and his sons: My son Shechem really loves Dinah. Please let him marry her.
translation_verse: Nakoso Hamɔ sele bɛ kyɛ, “Mma Sɛkem kuro ɛmɔ awa brasua ne. Mesrɛ ɛmɔ, ɛ́mɔfa ye bɛma ogya.

english_verse: Why don't you start letting your families marry into our families and ours marry into yours?
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔma yɛ́gyigya yɛ nwo; ɛ́mɔfa ɛmɔ mma mmrasua bɛ́ma yɛ́gya, na ɛmɔ koso ɛ́mɔgyigya yɛ deɛ mɔ.

english_verse: You can share this land with us. Move freely about until you find the property you want; then buy it and settle down here.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ ne yɛ bɛ́tena, na aseɛ yeɛ ɔla berɛ ye, ɛ́mɔtena so na ɛ́mɔyɔ so adwuma, na ɛ́mɔnya so agyapadeɛ.”

english_verse: Shechem added, “Do this favor for me, and I'll give whatever you want.
translation_verse: Sɛkem toale so sele Dina baba ne Dina aliɛma mmienzua nemɔ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔpene so bɛ́ma me, na bɔ ɛmɔpena biala ngɔfa ngɔma ɛmɔ.

english_verse: Jacob's sons wanted to get even with Shechem and his father because of what had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Ɔnate kyɛ Sɛkem ato Dina mmɔnaa ne ati, Yakob mma mmienzua nemɔ buale Sɛkem ne ɔse Hamɔ wɔ nnakannaka atee so.

english_verse: So they tricked them by saying: You're not circumcised! It would be a disgrace for us to let you marry Dinah now.
translation_verse: Bebuale bɛ kyɛ, “Yɛyɔ ye sɔ a ɔngɔyɛ yee! Ɔte animguaseɛ ma yɛ kyɛ yɛkɔfa y’eliɛma brasua yɛkɔma sona bɔ ɔppɛle ye bienzua ɔ.

english_verse: But we will let you marry her, if you and the other men in your tribe agree to be circumcised.
translation_verse: Nikyee komapɛ yeɛ ɔkɔmaa yɛkɔpene ɔ: kyɛ ɛmɔ anu biala kɔpɛ ye bienzua na ɛmɔayɛ kyɛ yɛ ala ɔ.

english_verse: Then your families can marry into ours, and ours can marry into yours, and we can live together like one nation.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛmɔyɔ sɔ de a, yɛkɔfa yɛ mma mmrasua yɛkɔma ɛmɔ agyaa, na yɛ koso yagyigya ɛmɔ mma mmrasua, na yɛ ne ɛmɔ atena, na yayɛ mmenia ko.

english_verse: But if you don't agree to be circumcised, we'll take Dinah and leave this place.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɛmɔngɔpene maa bɛngɔpɛ ɛmɔ bienzua de a, ye de yɛfa yɛ wa brasua ne, na yɛkɔ.”

english_verse: Hamor and Shechem liked what was said.
translation_verse: Bɛ dwirɛ ne yɛle Hamɔ ne ɔwa Sɛkem fɛ.

english_verse: Shechem was the most respected person in his family, and he was so in love with Dinah that he hurried off to get everything done.
translation_verse: Na ɔnate kyɛ né aberandeɛ Sɛkem nye gye Yakob awa brasua ne nwo ne ati, wanyɛ bɛ nzusuleɛ ne nwo ngyɛkyerɛ koraa. Né Sɛkem yeɛ ɔte titire paa wɔ ye abusua nu ɔ.

english_verse: The two men met with the other leaders of their city and told them:
translation_verse: Yiti Hamɔ ne ɔwa Sɛkem bɛhɔle bɛ kuro n’anoa nu dɔ, na besele kuro berɛ mmienzua ne kyɛ,

english_verse: These people really are friendly. Why not let them move freely about until they find the property they want? There's enough land here for them and for us. Then our families can marry into theirs, and theirs can marry into ours.
translation_verse: “Sɔ mmenia ye mɔ, bɛ ne yɛ te asomdwee nu, yiti ɛ́mɔma bɛ́tena aseɛ ye aso na beli bɛ dwaa. Aseɛ ne la berɛ pralalala ma bɛ, yiti ɛ́mɔma yɛ́gyigya bɛ mma mmrasua, na yɛ koso yɛfa yɛ deɛ mɔ yɛma begya.

english_verse: We have to do only one thing before they will agree to stay here and become one nation with us. Our men will have to be circumcised just like theirs.
translation_verse: Nakoso nikyee komapɛ yeɛ sɛ yɛyɔ a mmenia nemɔ kɔpene so na bɛ ne yɛ atena maa yayɛ mmenia ko ɔ: kyɛ yɛ nu biala kɔmaa bɛkɔpɛ ye bienzua kyɛbɔ bapɛ bɛ deɛ ne ɔ.

english_verse: Just think! We'll get their property, as well as their flocks and herds. All we have to do is to agree, and they will live here with us.
translation_verse: Aso bɛ nandwie, b’agyapadeɛ ne bɛ nyɛmmoa mukoraa ngɔyɛ yɛ deɛ? Ɛmɔ de ɛ́mɔma yɛne bɛ yɛyɛ adwene, na bɛ ne yɛ kɔtena.”

english_verse: Three days later the men who had been circumcised were still weak from pain. So Simeon and Levi, two of Dinah's brothers, attacked with their swords and killed every man in the town,
translation_verse: Ye ɛlɛsa ne aso bɔ bɛ kena ne tutu bɛ nen, Yakob mma nemɔ anu nyɔ bɔ beli Simeon ne Lewi, bɔ bɛte Dina aliɛma mmienzua ne, bɛhwehwene bɛ ngrandɛ. Bɛhɔle kuro ne aso mvum nu, na behuhuni mmienzua ne amukoraati.

english_verse: including Hamor and Shechem. Then they took Dinah and left.
translation_verse: Bele ngrandɛ behuni Hamɔ ne ɔwa Sɛkem, na bɛɛyele Dina befili Sɛkem awuro bɛhɔle.

english_verse: Jacob's other sons came and took everything they wanted. All this was done because of the horrible thing that had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Yakob mma mmienzua nemɔ fitele awufoɛ nemɔ aso ne, bɛfene kuro ne anu nningyein, ofikyɛ Sɛkem agua b’eliɛma brasua ne anwo fiɛ.

english_verse: They took sheep, goats, donkeys, and everything else that was in the town or the countryside.
translation_verse: Bɛsesale bɛ mmoaen ne bɛ nandwie ne b’afunum mɔ, ɔne nikyee biala bɔ ɔwɔ kuro ne fieso ɔ.

english_verse: After taking everything of value from the houses, they dragged away the wives and children of their victims.
translation_verse: Bɛsesale b’awuro nningyein amukoraa, bɛhyele bɛ mma ne bɛ ye mɔ amukoraa nnure, na bɛsesale b’anwonyadeɛ amukoraati.

english_verse: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “Look what you've done! Now I'm in real trouble with the Canaanites and Perizzites who live around here. There aren't many of us, and if they attack, they'll kill everyone in my household.”
translation_verse: Na Yakob sele Simeon ne Lewi kyɛ, “Ɛmɔahwe edwirɛ piri babrɛ me. Ɛmɔamaa manya ɛpɔen wɔ bɛ bɔ bɛte aseɛ ye asofoɛ ne Kanaanfoɛ ne Perisifoɛ bɛ sa nu. Me nwo mmenia anzo. Na sɛ bɛyɛ ko na bɛboaboa bɛ noa bedwɔso betia me a, bekonua me ne m’awuro ama mukoraa bo.”

english_verse: They answered, “Was it right to let our own sister be treated that way?”
translation_verse: Nakoso bebuale kyɛ, “Né yiti yɛtena berɛ ma ɔyɛ y’eliɛma brasua ne kyɛ gyanderaniɛ anaa?”

english_verse: God told Jacob, “Return to Bethel, where I appeared to you when you were running from your brother Esau. Make your home there and build an altar for me.”
translation_verse: Nyameɛ sele Yakob kyɛ, “Dwɔso kɔ Betel kɔtena dɔ; na si afɔleɛ bokyea ma Nyameɛ bɔ ɔyele ye nwo ali hyirele wɔ wɔ mmerɛ bɔ ɔnate eliɛma Yisɔ ti ɛnwatili ne.”

english_verse: Jacob said to his family and to everyone else who was traveling with him: Get rid of your foreign gods! Then make yourselves acceptable to worship God and put on clean clothes.
translation_verse: Yiti Yakob sele ye awuro ama ne bɛ bɔ bɛboka ye so amu kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔgyi Amaenmaensofoɛ nyameɛ mɔ bɔ bɛwɔ ɛmɔ nwo ne begua, ɛ́mɔpete ɛmɔ nwo, na ɛ́mɔsesã ɛmɔ ndaadeɛ.

english_verse: Afterwards, we'll go to Bethel. I will build an altar there for God, who answered my prayers when I was in trouble and who has always been at my side.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔma yɛdwɔso yɛhɔ Betel, maa ngonzi afɔleɛ bokyea berɛ ma Nyameɛ bɔ otiele me wɔ mmerɛ bɔ me nwo hyerele me ne, na wagyina me si nekaa biala bɔ mahɔ ne.”

english_verse: So everyone gave Jacob their idols and their earrings, and he buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
translation_verse: Yiti bɛsesale Amaenmaensofoɛ nyameɛ mukoraa bɔ ɔwɔ bɛ nwo ne, ɔne b’asomade bɔ owura bɛ ne bɛmane Yakob; na Yakob fu wurale eluii bɔ né opingye Sɛkem ne abo.

english_verse: While Jacob and his family were traveling through Canaan, God terrified the people in the towns so much that no one dared bother them.
translation_verse: Na besili nu bɔ bɛ́kɔ ne, Nyameɛ mane esuronyi kandinga tɔle nguro bɔ né bapɛ bɛ nwo bayia ne aso, yiti bangora bamvoa Yakob mma mmienzua nemɔ.

english_verse: Jacob built an altar there and called it “God of Bethel,” because that was the place where God had appeared to him when he was running from Esau.
translation_verse: Osili afɔleɛ bokyea wɔ berɛ, na ɔfrɛle berɛ Ɛl Betel ofikyɛ mmerɛ bɔ né ɔnwati oliɛma ne nen, berɛ yeɛ Nyameɛ yele ye nwo ali hyirele ye ɔ.

english_verse: While they were there, Rebekah's personal servant Deborah died. They buried her under an oak tree and called it “Weeping Oak.” God Blesses Jacob at Bethel
translation_verse: Debora bɔ né ɔte Rebɛka afaneɛ ne wuli, na besiele ye wɔ eluii bie abo wɔ Betel ngwaen; yiti bɛfrɛle berɛ Alɔnbakute.

english_verse: I will give you the land that I promised Abraham and Isaac, and it will belong to your family forever.
translation_verse: Na aseɛ bɔ mva mane Abraham ne Yisake ne, ngɔfa ngɔma wɔ ne kyẽa bie wɔ boso ama.”

english_verse: Jacob set up a large rock, so that he would remember what had happened there. Then he poured wine and olive oil on the rock to show that it was dedicated to God,
translation_verse: Na Yakob fale ngayeɛ nyɔboɛ penane nekaa bɔ ɔne Nyameɛ bedwudwole ne, ohwiele anonneɛ afɔleɛ guale so na ohwiele ngoo koso guale so.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Benjamin Is Born
translation_verse: Na Yakob frɛle nekaa bɔ Nyameɛ ne ye bedwudwole ne Betel. Rahɛl wue

english_verse: Jacob and his family had left Bethel and were still a long way from Ephrath, when the time came for Rachel's baby to be born.
translation_verse: Afei befili Betel. Na ɔka kãa maa bedwu Efrate ne, aworɛ hane Rahɛl, na ye aworɛ ne anu yɛle se.

english_verse: She was having a rough time, but the woman who was helping her said, “Don't worry! It's a boy.”
translation_verse: Rahɛl aworɛ ne anu yɛle se ne, braa bɔ ode ye aworɛ ne sele ye kyɛ, “Nnɛsuro, na ɛhe koso ɛkɔwo bienzua.”

english_verse: Rachel was at the point of death, and right before dying, she said, “I'll name him Benoni.” But Jacob called him Benjamin.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ ɔ́fa ne, ɔtole ye dumaa Benoni, nakoso ɔse Yakob de ɔfrɛle ye Benyamin.

english_verse: Rachel was buried beside the road to Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Yiti Rahɛl wuli, na besiele ye wɔ Efrate atee ne aso dɔ.

english_verse: Jacob set up a tombstone over her grave, and it is still there.
translation_verse: Na Yakob fale ngayeɛ nyɔboɛ penane ye asieleɛ ne aso; ɛhe te Rahɛl asieleɛ so ngayeɛ nyɔboɛ bɔ ɔwɔ berɛ ɔbaadwu ɛnɛ ye.

english_verse: Jacob, also known as Israel, traveled to the south of Eder Tower, where he set up camp.
translation_verse: Yisrael toale ye ateetulɛ ne aso, na oosili ye ɛtena sua wɔ Edere abandenden ne asi dɔ. Yakob mma mmienzua nemɔ

english_verse: During their time there, Jacob's oldest son Reuben slept with Bilhah, who was one of Jacob's other wives. And Jacob found out about it. Jacob's Twelve Sons
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ né Yisrael te sɔ aseɛ ne aso nen, Ruben ne ye baba sómaa Bilha bɛlale, na Yisrael tele sɔ dwirɛ ne. Né Yakob mma mmienzua nemɔ bɛte buru ne nyɔ:

english_verse: Jacob went to his father Isaac at Hebron, also called Mamre or Kiriath-Arba, where Isaac's father Abraham had lived as a foreigner.
translation_verse: Yakob oodwuli ɔse Yisake berɛ wɔ Mamre, bɔ opingye Kiriate Aba nekaa bɔ Abraham ne Yisake bɛɛtenane bɛyɛle ɛwɔfoɛ ne.

english_verse: Esau, also known as Edom, had many descendants.
translation_verse: Yisɔ, bɔ yeɛ bɛfrɛ ye Edom ne, ye boso ama ɛhe:

english_verse: He married three Canaanite women: The first was Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite; the second was Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah and the granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
translation_verse: Yisɔ gyale ɔye mɔ fili Kanaanfoɛ nu; bɛ ɛhe: Hitiniɛ Elon ɔwa brasua Ada, Ana bɔ ye baba ole Hiwiniɛ Sibeon ne, ɔwa brasua Oholibama;

english_verse: the third was Basemath, who was Ishmael's daughter and Nebaioth's sister.
translation_verse: yeɛ Yismael awa brasua Basemate bɔ oliɛma brasua ole Nebayote ne.

english_verse: Esau and his three wives had five sons while in Canaan. Adah's son was Eliphaz; Basemath's son was Reuel; Oholibamah's three sons were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: yeɛ Oholibama wole Yeyuse, Yalam ne Kora. Yisɔ mma bɔ bɛwole bɛ wɔ Kanaan aseɛ so nemɔ ɛne.

english_verse: Esau took his children and wives, his relatives and servants, his animals and possessions he had acquired while in Canaan, and moved far from Jacob.
translation_verse: Na Yisɔ sesale ɔye mɔ, ye mma mmienzua, ye mma mmrasua, ɔne ye awuro ama mukoraa ɔne ye nandwie ne ye nyɛmmoa mukoraa, ɔne ye agyapadeɛ bɔ onyane ye wɔ Kanaan aseɛ so amu, na ɔtele ye nwo fili oliɛma Yakob nwo ɔɔtenane aseɛ foforɛ aso;

english_verse: He did this because the land was too crowded and could not support him and his brother with their flocks and herds.
translation_verse: ofikyɛ né b’agyapadeɛ sone paa maa bɛ munyɔ bɛnzo neka horɛ. Aseɛ bɔ né bɛte so ɛwɔfoɛ ne, ɔnate bɛ nyɛmmoa pee ne ati, né ɔte kãa ma bɛ.

english_verse: That's why Esau made his home in the hill country of Seir.
translation_verse: Yiti Yisɔ ɔɔtenane Sɛre mmokaa aseɛ ne aso dɔ.

english_verse: Esau and Adah's oldest son was Eliphaz, and the clans that descended from him were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
translation_verse: Yisɔ boso ama nemɔ, bɛ nu atitire mɔ ɛhe: Yisɔ bamuɛbaa Elifase mma mɔ ɛhe: atitirefoɛ Teman, Omare, Sefo ne Kenase,

english_verse: Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. These and Esau's other descendants lived in the land of Edom.
translation_verse: Kora, Gatam ne Amalɛke; bɛ yeɛ bɛte Elifase bosofoɛ atitire bɔ bɛwɔ Edom aseɛ so ne. Bɛte Ada mma.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Basemath's son Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
translation_verse: Yisɔ awa bienzua Rewel ye mma mmienzua mɔ ɛhe: atitirefoɛ Nahate, Sera, Sama ne Misa; bɛ yeɛ bɛte Rewel bosofoɛ atitire wɔ Edom aseɛ so ɔ. Bɛte Yisɔ aye Basemate nnomaa.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Yisɔ aye Oholibama ye mma mmienzua mɔ ɛhe: atitirefoɛ Yeyuse, Yalam ɔne Kora; atitirefoɛ bɔ yeɛ Ana awa brasua Oholibama ɔne Yisɔ bɛwole bɛ hɔ ɛne.

english_verse: All of these clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom.
translation_verse: Yisɔ ye mma mmienzua mɔ ɛne, na ɛhemɔ yeɛ bɛte bɛ nu atitirefoɛ ɔ. Sɛre bosofoɛ

english_verse: Seir was from the Horite tribe that had lived in Edom before the time of Esau. The clans that had descended from him were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Horiniɛ Sɛre mma bɔ né bɛte aseɛ ne asofoɛ nemɔ ɛhe: Lotan, Sobal, Sibeon ne Ana,

english_verse: Lotan's sons were Hori and Heman; his sister was Timna.
translation_verse: Né Lotan mma mɔ ole Hori ne Heman, yeɛ oliɛma brasua koso ole Timina.

english_verse: Shobal's sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
translation_verse: Sobal mma mmienzua mɔ ɛhe: Alwan, Manahate, Ebal, Sefo ne Onam.

english_verse: Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah—the same Anah who found an oasis in the desert while taking the donkeys of his father out to pasture.
translation_verse: Sibeon mma mmienzua mɔ ɛhe: Aya ne Ana. Sɔ Ana he yeɛ mmerɛ bɔ ɔfale ye baba Sibeon afunum mɔ hɔle adidie ne, oofitele nzuehyerɛ asue ti so wɔ ɛserɛ so ne.

english_verse: Anah's children were Dishon and Oholibamah.
translation_verse: Ana mma mɔ ɛhe: Dison, yeɛ Ana awa brasua Oholibama.

english_verse: Dishon's sons were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
translation_verse: Dison mma mmienzua mɔ ɛhe: Hemdan, Eseban, Yitran ne Kyeran.

english_verse: Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
translation_verse: Esere mma mmienzua mɔ ɛhe: Bilhan, Saawan na Akan.

english_verse: Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
translation_verse: Disan mma mmienzua mɔ ɛhe: Yuse ne Aran.

english_verse: The clans of the Horites were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Horifoɛ b’atitirefoɛ mɔ ɛhe: atitirefoɛ Lotan, Sobal, Sibeon, Ana,

english_verse: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan, and they lived in the land of Seir.
translation_verse: Dison, Esere ne Disan. Ɛhemɔ ole Horifoɛ b’atitire kyɛbɔ bɛ mmusua te wɔ Sɛre aseɛ so ne. Edom ɛhene mɔ

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau took their names from their families and the places where they lived. They are Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
translation_verse: Yisɔ bosofoɛ atitire nemɔ dumaa, kyɛbɔ bɛ mmusua kure, b’atenaleɛ ɔne bɛ dumaa te ɛhe: Atitirefoɛ Timina, Alwa, Yetete,

english_verse: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
translation_verse: Oholibama, Ela, Pinon,

english_verse: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
translation_verse: Kenase, Teman, Mibesa,

translation_verse: Magediɛl ne Yiram; ɛhemɔ yeɛ bɛte Edom ye bosofoɛ atitirefoɛ, kyɛbɔ b’atenaleɛ te wɔ aseɛ bɔ benyane ye ne aso ɔ. Edom ye ala ole Yisɔ bɔ ɔte Edomfoɛ bɛ nana ne.

english_verse: Jacob lived in the land of Canaan, where his father Isaac had lived,
translation_verse: Yakob tenane Kanaan, aseɛ bɔ né ɔse te so ɛwɔfoɛ ne aso.

english_verse: “They're not here anymore,” the man replied. “I overheard them say they were going to Dothan.” Joseph left and found his brothers in Dothan.
translation_verse: Biaa ne buale kyɛ, “Bafi wa bahɔ moa paa, ofikyɛ ndele kyɛ né bɛkeka kyɛ, ‘Ɛ́mɔma yɛhɔ Dotan.’ ” Yiti Yosef pole oliɛma nemɔ aso, na oonwuni bɛ wɔ Dotan.

english_verse: Jacob loved Joseph more than he did any of his other sons, because Joseph was born when Jacob was very old. Jacob had even given Joseph a fancy coat
translation_verse: Né Yisrael kuro Yosef dwirɛ tra ye mma mɔ ngaa ne amu, ofikyɛ ɔte ye nworowaa nu ba. Yiti ɔpale ataadeɛ tendenn bie mane ye.

english_verse: which showed that Joseph was his favorite son, and so Joseph's brothers hated him and would not be friendly to him.
translation_verse: Na oliɛma mmienzua nemɔ nwuni kyɛ bɛ baba kuro Yosef dwirɛ tra bɛ mu nen, bɛpɔle ye, yiti né bɛ ne ye dwudwo ɛyaa so.

english_verse: One day, Joseph told his brothers what he had dreamed, and they hated him even more.
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, Yosef hyene laleɛ, na ɔhane laleɛ ne hyirele oliɛma nemɔ nen, bɛpɔle ye bɛtrale daa ne po.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Let me tell you about my dream.
translation_verse: Osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔtie laleɛ bɔ mahye ɔ:

english_verse: We were out in the field, tying up bundles of wheat. Suddenly my bundle stood up, and your bundles gathered around and bowed down to it.”
translation_verse: “Né yɛkyekye ɛmo tire tire wɔ fieso, na mvum nu, me mo tire bɔ makyekye ne dwɔsole gyinane kyirebeinn, na ɛmɔ mo tire deɛ nemɔ pɛle me deɛ ne anwo beyiale, na bɛkotole ye.”

english_verse: His brothers asked, “Do you really think you are going to be king and rule over us?” Now they hated Joseph more than ever because of what he had said about his dream.
translation_verse: Na oliɛma nemɔ bisale ye kyɛ, “Ɛpena kyire kyɛ ɛbaayɛ yɛ so hene anaa? Anaakyɛ ɛbaali yɛ so tumi anaa?” Na ye laleɛ ɔne ye noa dwirɛ ne mane oliɛma nemɔ hɔle so bɛpɔle ye kɔkɔkɔkɔ.

english_verse: Joseph later had another dream, and he told his brothers, “Listen to what else I dreamed. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.”
translation_verse: Yosef hyene laleɛ bieku, na ɔbɔle oliɛma nemɔ amaneɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔtie, mahye laleɛ bieku, na nwuni kyɛ eyia, ɛsraen ne nzramaa buru ne ko bɛkoto me.”

english_verse: When he told his father about this dream, his father became angry and said, “What's that supposed to mean? Are your mother and I and your brothers all going to come and bow down to you?”
translation_verse: Nakoso Yosef hane ɛhe hyirele ye baba ne oliɛma mmienzua nemɔ nen, ye baba teateane ye, na osele ye kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ laleɛ yeɛ ahye ye? Ekyire kyɛ me ne eni ne eliɛma mmienzua mɔ kɔɔkoto wɔ nyunu anaa?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept wondering about the dream. Joseph Is Sold and Taken to Egypt
translation_verse: Yosef aliɛma nemɔ nye borole ye, nakoso ɔse de ɔfale edwirɛ nemɔ siele ye ti anu. Bɛtɔne Yosef maa okofite Misraim

english_verse: One day when Joseph's brothers had taken the sheep to a pasture near Shechem,
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, oliɛma mmienzua nemɔ fale bɛ se mmoaen ne bɛhɔle adidie wɔ Sɛkem.

english_verse: his father Jacob said to him, “I want you to go to your brothers. They are with the sheep near Shechem.” “Yes, sir,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yisrael sele Yosef kyɛ, “Eliɛma nemɔ afa mmoaen bahɔ adidie wɔ Sɛkem, yiti bra maa nzoma wɔ bɛ berɛ.” Yosef sele ye kyɛ, “Me ɛhe.”

english_verse: His father said, “Go and find out how your brothers and the sheep are doing. Then come back and let me know.” So he sent him from Hebron Valley. Joseph was near Shechem
translation_verse: Na Yakob sele ye kyɛ, “Kɔnea sɛ eliɛma nemɔ ne mmoaen ne bɛ nwo te paa a, na sá bra baabɔ me amaneɛ.” Yiti ɔsomane ye fili Hebron bɔnza ne anu maa ɔhɔle Sɛkem.

english_verse: and wandering through the fields, when a man asked, “What are you looking for?”
translation_verse: Biaa bie nwuni kyɛ Yosef amini na ɔpɛ ye nwo wɔ porɛ ne anu nen, obisale ye kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ yeɛ ɛpena ɔ?”

english_verse: Joseph answered, “I'm looking for my brothers who are watching the sheep. Can you tell me where they are?”
translation_verse: Na Yosef buale kyɛ, “Mepena nniɛma mmienzua mɔ. Mesrɛ wɔ, kyire me nekaa bɔ bafa mmoaen bahɔ adidie ne.”

english_verse: But before he got there, they saw him coming and made plans to kill him.
translation_verse: Oliɛma nemɔ nwuni ye wɔ nziɛ nziɛ kyɛ ɔba ɔ, na anzana ɔbaadwu bɛ nwo berɛ ne, bɛbɔle ye nwo porɛ kyɛ bekohu ye.

english_verse: They said to one another, “Look, here comes the hero of those dreams!
translation_verse: Besisele bɛ nwo kyɛ, “Laleɛhyenɛniɛ ne yeɛ ɔ́ba ne!

english_verse: pieces of silver they sold him to the Ishmaelites who took him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔma yɛhu ye ná yɛgyi ye yɛto ngono ne ko anu; yɛkɔɔha kyɛ kaka aboyaa bie ahye ye ali, ná yanea sɛ ye laleɛ nemɔ kɔwa nu a.

english_verse: Reuben heard this and tried to protect Joseph from them. “Let's not kill him,” he said.
translation_verse: Nakoso Ruben tele ne, ɔpepɛ lele ye, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Nnɛmɔmaa yɛku ye.”

english_verse: “Don't murder him or even harm him. Just throw him into a well out here in the desert.” Reuben planned to rescue Joseph later and take him back to his father.
translation_verse: Ruben sele bɛ kyɛ, “Nnɛma ɛmɔkã mogya begua, ɛ́mɔgyi ye bɛ́to kumaa ye anu ɛserɛ ye aso wa, na mmom nnɛma ebiala fa ye sa ka ye.” Né wayɛ ye adwene kyɛ ode ye fi bɛ sa nu na ɔfa ye sa kɔma ye baba.

english_verse: When Joseph came to his brothers, they pulled off his fancy coat
translation_verse: Yiti Yosef oodwuli oliɛma nemɔ anwo berɛ ne, bepurole ye ataadeɛ tendenn bɔ owura ye ne,

english_verse: As Joseph's brothers sat down to eat, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with all kinds of spices that they were taking to Egypt.
translation_verse: Ye si ye, bɛtenane ase kyɛ bedidi. Na bɛmane bɛ ti so ne, benwuni Yismaelfoɛ dwadifoɛ bɔ bɛtete afupɔngɔ so, bɔ befi Gileade bɛ́kɔ Misraim ɔ. Né b’afupɔngɔ mɔ bɛsoso pɔweɛ, sakyeɛ ne asãa.

english_verse: So Judah said, “What will we gain if we kill our brother and hide his body?
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yuda sele oliɛma nemɔ kyɛ, “Mvasoɛ beni yeɛ ɔwɔ so kyɛ yɛkohu y’eliɛma bienzua na yɛkɔkata ye mogya so ɔ?”

english_verse: Let's sell him to the Ishmaelites and not harm him. After all, he is our brother.” And the others agreed.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔma yɛ́yɛ ye atɔen yɛ́ma Yismaelfoɛ ne. Nnɛmɔmaa yɛfa yɛ sa yɛkã ye, ofikyɛ ɔte y’eliɛma ne yɛ bɔbɔ yɛ deɛ.” Na oliɛma nemɔ penene so.

english_verse: When the Midianite merchants came by, Joseph's brothers took him out of the well, and for
translation_verse: Né Midianfoɛ dwadifoɛ biemɔ bɛbaase. Yosef aliɛma nemɔ yele ye befili abura ne anu, na bɛtɔnene ye ɛdwetɛ kilo ko bɔ bahyɛ nu nnu bɛmane Yismaelfoɛ nemɔ maa bɛfale ye bɛhɔle Misraim.

english_verse: When Reuben returned to the well and did not find Joseph there, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Ruben sa wale abura ne anwo, na onwuni kyɛ Yosef nne nu ne, osunzuale ye ndaadeɛ nu;

english_verse: Then he went back to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?”
translation_verse: osa wale oliɛma nemɔ berɛ, na oosele kyɛ, “Abɛɛmaa ne nne berɛ, na nyɔ me nwo sɛ?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers killed a goat and dipped Joseph's fancy coat in its blood.
translation_verse: Na bɛfale Yosef ataadeɛ ne, behuni abɔngye, na bɛfale ataadeɛ ne bɛfɔlefɔlele ye mogya ne.

english_verse: After this, they took the coat to their father and said, “We found this! Look at it carefully and see if it belongs to your son.”
translation_verse: Bɛfale ataadeɛ tendenn ne bɛbrɛle bɛ baba, na besele kyɛ, “Nea ataadeɛ bie bɔ yanwu ye ɔ, sɛ ɛwa ne deɛ ne ahɔ a.”

english_verse: Jacob knew it was Joseph's coat and said, “It's my son's coat! Joseph has been torn to pieces and eaten by some wild animal.”
translation_verse: Ɔneane, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Mma ne deɛ ne ɔ. Kaka aboyaa bie ahye ye ali. Aporowaa biala nne ye nwo kyɛ watete Yosef nu pasaa.”

english_verse: Jacob mourned for Joseph a long time, and to show his sorrow he tore his clothes and wore sackcloth.
translation_verse: Yiti Yakob sunzuale ye ndaadeɛ nu, ɔfale ɛsɛen tena pɛle ye bo, na olili ɔwa ne wue nwo aworabɔlɛ ngyẽa pee.

english_verse: All of Jacob's children came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said, “I will go to my grave, mourning for my son.” So Jacob kept on grieving.
translation_verse: Na ye mma mmienzua mukoraa ne ye mma mmrasua mukoraa bɔle mmɔden kyɛ bɛkɔkyekye ye wora, nakoso wambene. Yakob sele kyɛ, “Méfa aworabɔlɛ mépo mma ne wɔ ɛborɔ.” Na ye baba suni ye paa.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to a man named Potiphar, who was the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Midianfoɛ nemɔ tɔnene ye wɔ Misraim bɛmane Faro ye panyi ko bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Pɔtifa. Né ɔte ye angɔbeahene.

english_verse: About that time Judah left his brothers in the hill country and went to live near his friend Hirah in the town of Adullam.
translation_verse: Na sɔ mmerɛ ne, Yuda fili oliɛma mɔ anwo, na ɔhɔle ɔne Adulamniɛ bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Hira bɛɛtenane.

english_verse: While there he met the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite man. Judah married her,
translation_verse: Berɛ yeɛ Yuda nwuni Kanaanniɛ bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Suwa ɔwa brasua ɔ. Ogyale ye, na ɔne ye bɛlale.

english_verse: and they had three sons. He named the first one Er;
translation_verse: Braa ne nwonzɛle, ɔwole bienzua, na ɔtole ye dumaa Ɛre.

english_verse: she named the next one Onan.
translation_verse: Osa nwonzɛle, ɔwole bienzua, na ɔtole ye dumaa Onan.

english_verse: The third one was born when Judah was in Chezib, and she named him Shelah.
translation_verse: Braa ne sá wole bienzua bieku, na ɔtole ye dumaa Hyela. Ɔwole ye ne, né ɔwɔ kuro bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Kesibo so.

english_verse: Later, Judah chose Tamar as a wife for Er, his oldest son.
translation_verse: Yuda gyale braa bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Tamar mane ye bamuɛbaa Ɛre.

english_verse: But Er was very evil, and the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Nakoso Ɛre, bɔ ɔte Yuda bamuɛbaa ne yɔle AWURADE nyunu amumuyɛɛ, na AWURADE huni ye.

english_verse: So Judah told Onan, “It's your duty to marry Tamar and have a child for your brother.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yuda sele Onan kyɛ, “Kɔ eliɛma n’aye ne nekaa, yɔ w’asɛdeɛ ma ye kyɛ ohu aliɛma, na wo mmaa ma eliɛma ne.

english_verse: Onan knew the child would not be his, and when he had sex with Tamar, he made sure that she would not get pregnant.
translation_verse: Nakoso né Onan se kyɛ mmaa nemɔ ngɔyɛ ye deɛ. Yiti ɔne oliɛma n’aye ne lale ne, ɔmane ye nwo nzue guale ase, kyɛbɔ ɔkɔyɛ na ɔngɔwo ngɔma oliɛma ne ɔ.

english_verse: The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE anguro bɔ Onan yɔle ne, yiti ohuni ye koso.

english_verse: Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
translation_verse: Yiti Yuda sele ye sia brasua Tamar kyɛ, “Kɔtena wɔ kuna nu wɔ ɛse awuro kɔpem kyɛ mma Hyela konyi ɔ.” Ofikyɛ né osuro kyɛ annea a, ye koso okowu kyɛbɔ oliɛma nemɔ wuli ne. Yiti Tamar hɔle ɔɔtenane ɔse awuro.

english_verse: Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared.
translation_verse: Ngyẽa kãa pɛle nu ne, Suwa awa brasua bɔ ɔte Yuda aye ne wuli. Na Yuda lili ye kuna yiele ne, ɔhɔle ye mmenia bɔ bɛpepɛ ye mmoaen nwo nwiaa ne berɛ wɔ Timina. Ɔne obiɛngo Adulamniɛ Hira yeɛ bɛhɔle ɔ.

english_verse: Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep.
translation_verse: Na bɛbɔle Tamar amaneɛ kyɛ, “Wɔ sia ɔ́kɔ Timina ɔkɔpepɛ ye mmoaen nwo nwiaa” nen,

english_verse: She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
translation_verse: ɔyele ye kuna ɛtena ne guale berɛ, na ɔfale ngatanyunu katale ye nyunu, na ɔfale ɛtena kuruli ye nwo ɔɔtenane Enaim tiwaa wɔ Timina atee so. Né wanwu kyɛ Hyela anyi, nakoso bamva Hyela bamma wangya ye.

english_verse: When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute
translation_verse: Ɔnate kyɛ né Tamar afa ɛtena akuru ye ti ne ati, Yuda nwuni ye ne, obuli ye kyɛ ɔte gyanderaniɛ.

english_verse: “One of my young goats,” he answered. “What will you give me to keep until you send the goat?” she asked.
translation_verse: Yuda buale kyɛ, “Ngɔbrɛ wɔ nyɛmmoa ne anu abɔngye akrɔngrɔma ko.” Na obisale Yuda kyɛ, “Ɛkɔfa nikyee bie kosi awowaa koraka né afa abrɛ me anaa?”

english_verse: “What do you want?” he asked in return. “The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
translation_verse: Na Yuda koso bisale ye kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ yeɛ mva nzi wɔ berɛ awowaa ɔ?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Wɔ nzɔanoɛ pɛteaa, ɔne nyamaa bɔ osinze so ne, yeɛ pɔmaa bɔ otira wɔ ne.” Yiti Yuda fa mane ye. Ɔne ye lale, na ɔne ye nwonzɛle.

english_verse: After returning home, Tamar took off the veil and dressed in her widow's clothes again.
translation_verse: Tamar dwɔsole hɔle. Ɔyele ye ngatanyunu ne, na osa fale ye kuna ɛtena ne herale.

english_verse: Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there.
translation_verse: Yuda fale abɔngye akrɔngrɔma ne somane ye damvo Adulamniɛ ne kyɛ ɔfa ɔɔpɔ awowaa nningyein ne ofi braa ne berɛ ɔbrɛ ye. Nakoso ɔhɔle ne, wannwu ye.

english_verse: Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?” “There's never been one here,” they answered.
translation_verse: Na obisale kuro berɛ ama ne kyɛ, “Gyanderaniɛ bie bɔ né ɔte Enaim atee noa ne, ɔwɔ ni?” Na bebuale kyɛ, “Gyanderaniɛ biala ɔwwale wa.”

english_verse: Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
translation_verse: Yiti osa wale Yuda berɛ oosele ye kyɛ, “Mannwu ye, na berɛ ama nemɔ po nwa: ‘Gyanderaniɛ biala ɔwwale wa.’ ”

english_verse: “If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yuda sele obiɛngo ne kyɛ, “Maa ɔ́fa nningyein ne na banzere yɛ. Anwu ye oo, mmaa ɛfale abɔngye ne hɔle, nakoso annwu ye.”

english_verse: About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!” “Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
translation_verse: Kɔyɛ ɛsraen nza asi ne, bɛbɔle Yuda amaneɛ kyɛ, “Wɔ sia Tamar wabɔ adwaman, na ɔnate so po ɔnwonzɛ.” Na Yuda hyɛle kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhwe ye befite ma bɛyera ye.”

english_verse: As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
translation_verse: Na bɛ́fa Tamar befite bɛ́ba ne, ɔsomane maa beesele ye sia ne kyɛ, “Biaa bɔ ole sɔ nningyein hemɔ nen, ye yeɛ me ne ye yɛnwonzɛ ɔ.” Na ɔtoale so sele ye kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, nea nningyein hemɔ: pɛteaa ye, nyamaa ye, ɔne pɔmaa ye, nwa deɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: “Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
translation_verse: Yuda lele tole nu kyɛ ye deɛ ɔ, na osele kyɛ, “Ɔtengyɛ tra ne, ofikyɛ mamva ye mamma mma bienzua Hyela maa wangya ye.” Na Yuda ne ye anna ko.

english_verse: Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
translation_verse: Na ɔ́wo ne, bɛ nu ko yele ye sa fitele. Braa bɔ ode ye aworɛ ne sɔle nu, ɔfale adaabene kyekyele ye sa kɔm, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Ɛhe yeɛ olili moa wale ɔ.”

english_verse: At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez.
translation_verse: Na osa twe ye sa ne kɔ nu nen, oliɛma ne koso wale. Braa bɔ ode aworɛ ne sele kyɛ, “Nea kyɛbɔ asi afɛ nu na afite awa ɔ.” Yiti ɔfrɛle ye Pɛrɛse.

english_verse: When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
