translation_verse: Ye si ye, oliɛma ne koso wale, né adaabene ne kyekye ye sa, na bɛfrɛle ye Sera.

english_verse: The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Yismaelfoɛ nemɔ fale Yosef bɛhɔle Misraim. Na Faro ye panyi ko bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Pɔtifa, bɔ ɔte Misraimniɛ na osa te ye angɔbeahene ne, ɔtɔle ye fili Yismaelfoɛ nemɔ berɛ.

english_verse: So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner. Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did.
translation_verse: Na ye mene nwuni kyɛ AWURADE gyi ye si, na AWURADE sá ma nikyee biala bɔ ɔyɔ yɛ yee.

english_verse: Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property.
translation_verse: Yosef sɔle ye mene nye. Ɔsole ye, na biaa ne fale ye tuale ye awuro ne anoa, na ɔfale bɔ ole ye amukoraa wurale ye sa.

english_verse: Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat. Joseph was well-built and handsome,
translation_verse: Yiti ɔfale ye nningyein amukoraati wurale Yosef sa. Na ɔnate kyɛ Yosef wɔ berɛ ne ati, né ɔnha ye nwo wɔ nikye fee nwo, sana aleɛ bɔ okoli angome. Né Yosef nwo yɛ nyemene na ɔbɔ pe.

english_verse: and Potiphar's wife soon noticed him. She asked him to make love to her,
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bie asi ne, Yosef ye mene aye tuli ye nye siele ye so, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Ɛne me la.”

english_verse: but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yosef ambene, na osele ye mene aye ne kyɛ, “Eh, ɔnate me bɔ nwɔ wa ne ati, me mene ɔnha ye nwo wɔ awuro wa nikyee biala nwo; wafa ye nningyein amukoraati wawura me sa.

english_verse: No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.”
translation_verse: Awuro wa de, ebiala nni mu ndra me, yeɛ ɔmva hwee mmɔ me aheɛ, sana wɔ ngome, ofikyɛ ɔye ole wɔ. Nzu ati yeɛ nyɔ sɔ amumuyɛɛ piri ye na nyɔ bɔne ndia Nyameɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ daa biala né ɔka sɔ dwirɛ ne kyire Yosef de, nakoso Yosef ambene so ɔne ye banna anaakyɛ wanga wangɔ ye nwo.

english_verse: One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there.
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, Yosef hɔle awuro berɛ kyɛ ɔkwaayɔ ye adwuma, na né sona fee nne awuro berɛ.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
translation_verse: Braa ne sɔle Yosef ataadeɛ nu hyɛle ye kyɛ, “Ɛne me la!” Nakoso ofotili, na ɔyakyili ye ataadeɛ ne wɔ braa ne sa nu nwatili fili awuro berɛ.

english_verse: she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help.
translation_verse: ɔteane nu frɛfrɛle awuro berɛ ama sele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔnea oo, me hu waafa Hebriniɛ wawa yɛ wa kyɛ ɔɔgoro yɛ nwo; ɔwale kyɛ ahaa ɔne me baala, nakoso ndeateane nu serɛ paa!

english_verse: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
translation_verse: Na onwuni kyɛ meteatea nu ne, ɔyakyili ye ataadeɛ ne wɔ me sa nu, na ɔnwatili fili awuro wa.”

english_verse: Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home.
translation_verse: Ɔfale Yosef ataadeɛ ne guale ye nwo berɛ maa oodwuli kyɛ ye mene wale awuro ɔ.

english_verse: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
translation_verse: Nakoso nhyɛle ye bo kyɛ meteatea nu ne, ɔyakyili ye ataadeɛ me sa nu, na ɔnwatili fili awuro wa.”

english_verse: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
translation_verse: Yiti Yosef ye mene fale Yosef ɔɔtole kuku nu, nekaa bɔ bɛfa Faro kukunufoɛ begua ne, na ɔlale kuku nu.

english_verse: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
translation_verse: Nakoso AWURADE gyinane Yosef si, na ɔlole ye; onwuni ye anwumvoin maa kuku nu neafoɛ ne hurole ye dwirɛ.

english_verse: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
translation_verse: Kuku nu neafoɛ ne fale bɛ bɔ begua kuku nu berɛ amukoraa wurale Yosef sa, na bɔ ɔhɔle so berɛ biala Yosef yeɛ né ɔnea so ɔ.

english_verse: The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_verse: Nikyee biala bɔ né owura Yosef sa ne, kuku nu neafoɛ ne anha ye nwo wɔ ye nwo, ofikyɛ né AWURADE gyi Yosef si, na bɔ ɔyɔle biala AWURADE maa ɔyɛle yee.

english_verse: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
translation_verse: Yiti ɔhyele bɛ guale kuku nu wɔ angɔbeahene n’awuro. Né Yosef koso la sɔ kuku ne anu bie.

english_verse: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
translation_verse: Angɔbeahene ne fale bɛ wurale Yosef sa, na Yosef sole bɛ; bɛlale kuku nu berɛ bɛhyɛle kãa.

english_verse: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
translation_verse: Yosef wale bɛ nwo berɛ ngyerɛmɔ nen, onwuni kyɛ nikyee ha bɛ.

english_verse: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
translation_verse: Na bebuale ye kyɛ, “Yahyehye laleɛ, nakoso yɛnnya sona maa ongyire yɛ bɛ bo.” Yeɛ Yosef sele bɛ kyɛ, “Aso nna Nyameɛ ala yeɛ ɔkora kyire laleɛ bo ɔ? Mesrɛ ɛmɔ, ɛ́mɔhã laleɛ ne behyire me.”

english_verse: The king's personal servant told Joseph, “In my dream I saw a vine
translation_verse: Yiti nzaasulɛfoɛ so panyi ne hane ye laleɛ ne hyirele Yosef kyɛ, “Laleɛ ne anu, né bobe bakaa gyi me nyunu.

english_verse: with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe.
translation_verse: Né bobe ne le asa mmaa nza. Ɔfefɛle pɛ, yeɛ ɔbɔle nyerɛen ɔ, na nyerɛen kure kure ne borole yɛle bobe mmaa.

english_verse: I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
translation_verse: Né ndira Faro kulie ne. Mvale bobe mmaa ne, ndwini nguale Faro kulie ne anu, na mvale kulie ne mane ye.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
translation_verse: Na Yosef sele ye kyɛ, “Laleɛ ne bo ɛhe: bakaa sa mmaa nza ne kyire ɛlɛsa;

english_verse: and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do.
translation_verse: kyɛ ódwu ɛlɛsa nen, Faro kɔɔye wɔ kofi kuku nu wa maa ekosa kooli wɔ dibea, na ekosa kosu Faro nzaa kyɛbɔ daa né ɛyɔ ne ala.

english_verse: But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place.
translation_verse: Na sɛ nningyein kɔ yee ma wɔ a, mesrɛ wɔ, kaye me na boka me: di me nwo ngɔmɔ kyire Faro, maa bɛ́ye me béfi kuku ye anu.

english_verse: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ nahorɛ nu, bɛhyele me nnure befili Hebrifoɛ aseɛ so; na ɛwa po, nnyɔle hwee bɔ ɔsɛ kyɛ bɛfa me bɛto kumaa nu kuku nu ɔ.”

english_verse: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
translation_verse: Na paanootonɛfoɛ so panyi ne tele kyɛ Yosef aha edwirɛ fɛɛ wafa laleɛ ne anwo nen, osele Yosef kyɛ, “Me koso ngyene laleɛ ɔ, né paanoo kɛndɛen nza gyigyi so wɔ me ti so.

english_verse: The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
translation_verse: Na kɛndɛen bɔ ogyi anwuro paa ne anu, né aleɛ ahoroɔ bɔ bato ye foonoo nu bɔ bɛfa bɛma Faro ɔ wɔ nu. Nakoso né nnomaa suso aleɛ ne fi kɛndɛen ne anu wɔ me ti so.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
translation_verse: Na Yosef buale kyɛ, “Laleɛ ne bo ɛhe: kɛndɛen nza ne kyire ɛlɛsa.

english_verse: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
translation_verse: Kyɛ odwu ɛlɛsa ne, Faro kɔpɛ wɔ ti kofi so, na ɔkɔmaa bɛkɔfa wɔ kundunzii ne bekosinze bakaa so maa nnomaa kosuso wɔ naen bekoli.”

english_verse: Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook.
translation_verse: Ye ɛlɛsa ne aso, né ɔte Faro krakyẽa. Ɔtole poen mane ye mbanyi amukoraa. Na ɔyele nzaasulɛfoɛ so panyi ne paanootonɛfoɛ so panyi ne fili kuku nu maa beegyinane ye mbanyi nemɔ anyunu.

english_verse: He put the personal servant back in his old job
translation_verse: Faro sá fale nzaasulɛfoɛ so panyi n’adwuma wurale ye sa maa ɔhɔle so suli ye nzaa.

english_verse: and had the cook put to death. Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would,
translation_verse: Nakoso paanootonɛfoɛ so panyi ne de, ɔmaa behuni ye, kyɛbɔ Yosef hyirele bɛ laleɛ nemɔ abo nen.

english_verse: but the king's personal servant completely forgot about Joseph.
translation_verse: Nakoso nzaasulɛfoɛ so panyi ne angaye Yosef, na mmom ye wora fili ye.

english_verse: Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River.
translation_verse: Afoɛ nyɔ mumua si, Faro hyene laleɛ kyɛ ogyi asue Naele noa.

english_verse: Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank.
translation_verse: Mvum nu, onwuni kyɛ nandwie mmeleɛ branoa nzoo bɔ bɛ nwonaen tua bɛ ɔ fili asue Naele nu beedidili ngyɛngyɛma ne anu.

english_verse: ate the fat, healthy cows. When this happened, the king woke up.
translation_verse: Na nandwie bɔ bɛ nwo yɛ tɛ na bafofɔ ne, bɛmemene nandwie branoa anwonyemene nemɔ. Afei Faro fili nnaa nu tingyele.

english_verse: The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk.
translation_verse: Osa fale nu lale. Ɔhyene laleɛ bieku, na onwuni kyɛ aburoo nzoo bɔ bahyẽ na bati paa wɔ bakaa ko aso.

english_verse: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Mvum nu, onwuni kyɛ aburoo nzoo bɔ bangye na eyia afiteleɛ mvrama akese bɛ ɔ afifi.

english_verse: The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
translation_verse: Na aburoo kesenewaa nemɔ memene aburoo nzoo bɔ bahyẽ nemɔ. Afei Faro nye tele, na onwuni kyɛ laleɛ yeɛ wahye ɔ.

english_verse: The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
translation_verse: Yiti aleɛ hyene ngyerɛmɔ ne, Faro yɛle basaa. Na ɔsomane maa bɛɛfrɛle Misraim ngonyaayelɛfoɛ amukoraa ne mmenia bɔ bɛse ase amukoraa bɛmane ye. Ɔhane ye laleɛ ne anu dwirɛ hyirele bɛ, nakoso bɛ nu biala angora ye bo kyire.

english_verse: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Yeɛ nzaasulɛfoɛ so panyi ne sele Faro kyɛ, “Makaye me mvomsoɛ ɛnɛ.

english_verse: When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard.
translation_verse: Nana, mmerɛ bɔ ɛfɛle wɔ ngoaa so yaa, na ɛhyele me ne paanootonɛfoɛ so panyi ne guale kuku nu wɔ angɔbeahene awuro ne,

english_verse: One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning.
translation_verse: ɛlɛho bie kɔngɔen, yɛ munyɔ yɛhyene laleɛ. Asora ebiala laleɛ ɔne kyɛbɔ laleɛ ne bo kyire ɔ.

english_verse: A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant,
translation_verse: Né Hebriniɛ aberandeɛ bie bɔ ɔte angɔbeahene akoaa boka yɛ so wɔ berɛ; na yɛhane yɛ laleɛ ne yɛhyirele ye ne, ohyirele yɛ laleɛ ne abo. Ohyirele yɛ bo kyɛbɔ ebiala laleɛ si te ɔ.

english_verse: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
translation_verse: Na nikyee biala wale nu kyɛbɔ ohyirele ne ala: esa fale me dibea wurale me sa, na paanootonɛniɛ ne de, bɛbɔle ye kɔme.”

english_verse: The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
translation_verse: Yiti Faro somane maa bɛɛfrɛle Yosef bɛmane ye. Bɛyele ye befili kumaa nu kuku nu berɛ ndɛndɛ. Na Yosef poane ye kanza na ɔsesane ye ndaadeɛ yiele ne, ɔwale oogyinane Faro nyunu.

english_verse: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
translation_verse: Na Faro sele Yosef kyɛ, “Mahye laleɛ bie, nakoso ebiala ngora ye bo kyire. Mate kyɛ wɔ de sɛ ebie ka ye laleɛ kyire wɔ a, ɛkora kyire ye bo.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
translation_verse: Yosef buale Faro kyɛ, “Nana, me de mengora ye bo kyire, na mmom Nyameɛ yeɛ ɔkɔma Faro nyeanoɛ paa ɔ.”

english_verse: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Faro ha hyirele Yosef kyɛ, “Tie, laleɛ ne anu, né ngyi asue Naele noa.

english_verse: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
translation_verse: Na nwuni kyɛ nandwie mmeleɛ branoa nzoo bɔ bɛ nwo yɛ nyemene fili asue Naele nu beedidili ngyɛngyɛma ne anu.

english_verse: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ye si ye, nandwie nzoo foforɛ bɔ bɛ nwo yɛ tɛ na bafɔ nyangenaen lili bɛ si wale. Nnwuni bɛ sɛso le wɔ Misraim aseɛ so nekaa biala.

english_verse: The skinny cows ate the fat ones.
translation_verse: Na nandwie tɛɛtɛɛ nyangenaen nemɔ memene branoa nzoo bɔ belili moa bɛwale ne.

english_verse: But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
translation_verse: Nakoso bɛmemene bɛ beyiele ne, né hwee ngyire kyɛ bameme bɛ, ofikyɛ né bɛtɛte nyangenaen kyɛbɔ daa né bɛte ne ala. Na ndingyele.

english_verse: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
translation_verse: Nza ngyene laleɛ nwuni aburoo nzoo bɔ bahyẽ paa, na bɛwɔ bakaa ko aso ɔ.

english_verse: Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Na ɛhe asi ne, nwuni kyɛ aburoo nzoo bɔ bangye, na eyia afiteleɛ mvrama amaa bakese ɔ afifi.

english_verse: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
translation_verse: Aburoo kesenewaa nemɔ memene aburoo nzoo bɔ bahyẽ paa nemɔ. Ngane laleɛ ye anu dwirɛ ngyirele ngonyaayelɛfoɛ nemɔ, nakoso bɛ nu biala wangora wangyire me ye bo.”

english_verse: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yosef sele Faro kyɛ, “Nana, laleɛ ne amunyɔ kyire nikyee ko. Nyameɛ aye bɔ ɔbaayɔ ɔ wahyire Faro.

english_verse: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
translation_verse: Nandwie branoa nzoo ne kyire afoɛ nzoo, yeɛ aburoo nzoo bɔ wahyẽ ne kyire afoɛ nzoo; laleɛ ne te ko.

english_verse: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
translation_verse: Nandwie tɛɛtɛɛ nyangenaen nzoo bɔ ye si ye bɛwale ne kyire afoɛ nzoo, aburoo tohwire tohwire bɔ eyia afiteleɛ mvrama amaa bakese ne koso kyire afoɛ nzoo bɔ ɛhɔen pohonandafe bie kɔwa ɔ.

english_verse: It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do.
translation_verse: Na kyɛbɔ mahã mahyire Faro nen, Nyameɛ aye bɔ ɔbaayɔ wahyire Faro.

english_verse: For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain,
translation_verse: Afoɛ nzoo kɔwa bɔ yeɛ aleɛ kobu wɔ Misraim aseɛ ye aso mukoraa ɔ.

english_verse: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
translation_verse: Na ɔnate ɛhɔen piri bɔ ɔkɔwa ne ati, bɛngɔkaye aleɛ bɔ né wabu so wɔ maen ne anu po; ɛhɔen piri ne anu kɔyɛ se paa.

english_verse: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
translation_verse: Faro hyene laleɛ mmɔhoɛ nyɔ. Ɛhe kyire kyɛ Nyameɛ ahyehyɛ ye sɔ amba, na ɔngɔhyɛ biala ɔkɔwa nu.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt.
translation_verse: Yiti Nana, neanea nu ye sona ko bɔ ye nye la ase na ɔse nworɛ ɔ, na maa oli Misraim maen ne aso.

english_verse: Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty.
translation_verse: Nana, sisi mbanyi hwɛsofoɛ mɔ wɔ maen ye anu, na afoɛ nzoo bɔ aleɛ kobu ne, maa bɛhyɛ Misraim fieso nningyein nu nnu, ná betu ko.

english_verse: Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities.
translation_verse: Maa bɛboaboa sɔ afoɛ bɔ aleɛ kobu ne anu aleɛ mukoraa noa. Nana, ma bɛ tumi maa bɛ́fa aburoo ne bégua pata so besie wɔ nguro nemɔ anu, na bɛ́bɔ ye nwo waen.

english_verse: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
translation_verse: Sɔ aburoo ne kɔyɛ aleɛ bɔ bɛ́fa bésie bɛnwondɛ ɛhɔen piri bɔ ɔkɔwa Misraim maen ne anu afoɛ nzoo ne, amaa ɔnate ɛhɔen piri ne ati maen ne ammɔ.” Bɛbɔ Yosef amrado wɔ Misraim

english_verse: The king and his officials liked this plan.
translation_verse: Faro ne ye mbanyi amu nwuni kyɛ sɔ nzusuleɛ ne te paa.

english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Faro bisale ye mbanyi nemɔ kyɛ, “Aso yɛkonya sona bɔ ɔte sɔa bɔ Nyameɛ Sunzum te ye nu ɔ?”

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: Yiti Faro sele Yosef kyɛ, “Ɔnate kyɛ Nyameɛ aye ɛhe amu wahyire wɔ ne ati, ebiala nne berɛ bɔ ole nimdeɛ na ɔse nworɛ kyɛ wɔ ɔ;

english_verse: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
translation_verse: Wɔ yeɛ ɛkɔnea nikyee biala so wɔ m’ahemvie wa ɔ, na wɔ noa dwirɛ yeɛ me mmenia amukoraa koli so ɔ, sana bia bɔ nde so ye ala yeɛ ngɔfa ngɔtra wɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: You are now governor of all Egypt!”
translation_verse: Na Faro sele Yosef kyɛ, “Nea, mafa Misraim maen ye amukoraa mawura wɔ sa.”

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Faro yele ye nzɔanoɛ pɛteaa fili ye sa, ɔfa wurale Yosef, ɔfale kende herale ye, na ɔfale sikaa kɔkorɛ atweaban yale ye.

english_verse: He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ɔfale ye tenane ye teaseɛnam bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ne anu, na bɛteane nu belili ye nyunu kyɛ, “Ebiala koto ye oo!” Na ɔnate so fale Misraim maen ne amukoraa bewurale ye sa.

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”
translation_verse: Afei Faro sele Yosef kyɛ, “Me yeɛ nde Faro ɔ; ebiala ngɔhora ngɔyɔ hwee wɔ Misraim aseɛ so, sana ama ye ate.”

english_verse: He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
translation_verse: Faro tole Yosef dumaa Safenate Panea, na ɔfale On sɔfo Pɔtifɛra awa brasua Asenate maa ogyale. Na Yosef neane aseɛ ne aso amukoraa.

english_verse: For seven years there were big harvests of grain.
translation_verse: Aseɛ ne hyene aleɛ paa wɔ sɔ afoɛ nzoo bɔ aleɛ buli ne anu.

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Na Yosef boaboale aburoo pee bɔ ye somaa te kyɛ mboanoa anweaa noa, kɔpem kyɛ bɛyakyili ye halɛ ɔ, ofikyɛ né ɔsone soma.

english_verse: Joseph and his wife had two sons before the famine began.
translation_verse: Yosef ne On sɔfo Pɔtifɛra awa Asenate bɛwole mmaa mmienzua nyɔ koraka yeɛ ɛhɔen piri ne ɔ́hyɛ ye bo ɔ.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: Yosef tole bamuɛbaa ne dumaa Manase, ofikyɛ ɔnwa, “Nyameɛ ama me wora afi me yealɛ amukoraa, ɔne me se awuro ama mu.”

english_verse: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
translation_verse: Ɔtole bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ne dumaa Efraim, ofikyɛ ɔnwa, “Nyameɛ amaa manya mmaa wɔ aseɛ bɔ amaneɛnwunɛ wɔ so ye aso.”

english_verse: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
translation_verse: Afoɛ nzoo bɔ aleɛ buli wɔ Misraim aseɛ so ne wale ayieleɛ,

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: na afoɛ nzoo bɔ ɛhɔen piri wɔ nu paa ne hyɛle ye bo, kyɛbɔ Yosef hane ne. Ɛhɔen piri wale aseɛ mukoraa so, nakoso Misraim aseɛ so amukoraa de, né bele aleɛ.

english_verse: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
translation_verse: Ɛhɔen ne dwuli Misraim nekaa biala, na mmenia beesuni ɛhɔen behyirele Faro. Na Faro sele Misraimfoɛ ne amu kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhɔ Yosef berɛ, na bɔ okose ɛmɔ ne biala, ɛ́mɔyɔ.”

english_verse: The famine became bad everywhere in Egypt, so Joseph opened the storehouses and sold the grain to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Ɛhɔen piri ne trɛle hɔle maen ne nekaa biala, yiti Yosef bukyebukyele pata mbiri nemɔ, na ɔtɔnene aburoo ne bie mane Misraimfoɛ nemɔ, ofikyɛ né ɛhɔen piri ne noa yɛ se paa wɔ Misraim aseɛ so.

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Na ewiase mmenia mukoraa wale Yosef berɛ wɔ Misraim bɛɛtɔle aburoo, ofikyɛ né ɛhɔen piri ne noa yɛ se paa wɔ aseɛ ne aso nekaa biala.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Yakob tele kyɛ aleɛ wɔ Misraim ne, obisale ye mma nemɔ kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔtete berɛ ná ɛmɔnyɔ ɛhɔen ye anwo hwee ye?”

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: Na ɔtoale so sele bɛ kyɛ, “Mate kyɛ aburoo wɔ Misraim; ɛmɔhɔ dɔ bɛɛtɔ bie bɛbrɛ yɛ maa yɛli yɛnya ngoa na yanwuwu.”

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: Yiti Yosef aliɛma mmienzua buru sili nu bɛhɔle Misraim kyɛ bɛkwaatɔ aburoo.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yakob amma Yosef aliɛma Benyamin wammoka oliɛma nemɔ aso ɔne bɛ angɔ, ofikyɛ né osuro kyɛ anyɔ a, nikyee bie ayɔ ye.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
translation_verse: Yiti mmenia bɔ bɛhɔle aburoo atɔ wɔ Misraim ne, né Yisrael mma nemɔ boka so, ofikyɛ né ɛhɔen piri ne awa Kanaan aseɛ so.

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: Né Yosef yeɛ ɔte amrado wɔ maen ne anu ɔ. Né ye yeɛ ɔtɔne aleɛ ma maen ne anu ama mukoraa ɔ. Yosef aliɛma mɔ wale, na bɛfale bɛ nyunu bebutubutuli ase bɛkotole ye.

english_verse: Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Yosef kayele laleɛ mɔ bɔ ɔhyehyene fale bɛ nwo ne, na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔte maentetɛlɛfoɛ! Ɛmɔawa kyɛ ɛmɔbaaneanea maen ye anu na bɛpena nekaa bɔ yɛtɔ si ɔ.”

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: Na bebuale kyɛ, “Daabi, yɛ mene. Wɔ ngoaa awa atɔ.

english_verse: We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
translation_verse: Yɛ mukoraa yɛte seɛ ko mma, yɛdi nahorɛ, wɔ ngoaa mɔ yɛtte maentetɛlɛfoɛ.”

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Osa sele bɛ kyɛ “Ɛmɔlaka, maen ye siitɔlɛ yeɛ ɛmɔbaatetɛ bɛnea ɔ.”

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: Na besili so kyɛ, “Wɔ ngoaa, yɛte aliɛmaa buru ne nyɔ, biaa bie bɔ ɔwɔ Kanaan aseɛ so mma. Kasiɛ ne ɔne yɛ baba wɔ awuro kyɛbɔ yɛdwudwo ye, na ko de, ɔbboka yɛ so ko.”

english_verse: Joseph replied: It's like I said. You're spies,
translation_verse: Nakoso Yosef sá sele bɛ kyɛ, “Ye ala yeɛ mahã ne, ɛmɔte maentetɛlɛfoɛ.

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: Méfa ɛhe méso ɛmɔ menea: Meta Faro ndaen kyɛ, mengɔma ɛmɔngofi wa bɛngɔhɔ, sana ɛmɔ aliɛma kãa paa ne awa wa koraka.

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Yiti ɛ́mɔsoma ɛmɔ nu ko maa ɔɔfa ɛmɔ aliɛma ne ɔbra; ɛmɔ ngaa ne de ɛmɔkogua kuku nu na yaneanea ɛmɔ dwirɛ ne anu yanea sɛ ɔte nahorɛ a. Wanyɔ sɔ de a, meta Faro ndaen kyɛ ɛmɔte maentetɛlɛfoɛ!”

english_verse: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
translation_verse: Na ɔfale bɛ mukoraati guale kuku nu ɛlɛsa.

english_verse: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
translation_verse: Ɛlɛsa ne aso, Yosef sele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔyɔ ɛhe na ɛmɔanya bɛ ti badidi nu, ofikyɛ mesuro Nyameɛ:

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: sɛ ɛmɔdi nahorɛ amba a, ɛ́mɔma ɛmɔ nu ko ɔha kuku nu wa, na ɛmɔ ngaa ne de, ɔnate ɛhɔen piri ne ati, memaa ɛmɔfa aburoo bɛkɔma ɛmɔ awuro ama.

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: Na ɛmɔɔfa ɛmɔ aliɛma kasiɛ ne bɛbrɛ me wa, amaa manwu kyɛ ɛmɔ dwirɛ ne te nahorɛ, ná ɛmɔanya bɛ ti badidi nu.” Na bɛyɔle ye sɔ ala.

english_verse: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ besisele bɛ nwo kyɛ, “Nahorɛ nu, yɛdi y’eliɛma ne anwo fɔ, ofikyɛ yɛnwuni kyɛbɔ né ye wora asi abɔ ɔ; ɔsrɛle yɛ, nakoso yandie; ɛhe ati yeɛ edwirɛ he ato yɛ ye.”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
translation_verse: Na Ruben sele bɛ kyɛ, “Manga mangyerɛ ɛmɔ kyɛ nnɛma ɛmɔyɔ abɛɛmaa ne tɛɛ biala? Nakoso ɛmɔandɛ me so. Yiti kekesaala ye, ye mogya nwo akatuaa yeɛ yɛnya ye ye.”

english_verse: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
translation_verse: Né bɛnze kyɛ Yosef te edwirɛ bɔ bɛka ne abo ɔ, ofikyɛ né sona bie wɔ berɛ bɔ okyire bɛ dwudwolɛ ne abo ɔ.

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
translation_verse: Na Yosef hwene ye nwo hɔle ahameɛ oosuni, na osa wale bɛ nwo berɛ ɔne bɛ beedwudwole. Ɔyele Simeon fili bɛ nu, na ɔmaa bɛkyekyele ye bɛ nyunu berɛ ala.

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Na Yosef hyɛle ye mmenia kyɛ bewura oliɛma nemɔ bɔtɔ aburoo tɛkyɛtɛkyɛɛ, ná besa bɛ́fa ebiala sikaa béwura ye bɔtɔ ne anu, ná bɛma bɛ aleɛ bɔ bekoli ye atunu ɔ. Na bɛyɔle ye sɔ bɛmane bɛ.

english_verse: they each loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
translation_verse: Bɛfale b’aburoo ne bɛsoale b’afunum nemɔ, na bɛpene atee so.

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: Beedwuli asikyeleɛ, na bɛ nu ko sangyele ye bɔtɔ anoa kyɛ ɔma ye afunum aleɛ nen, onwuni kyɛ ye sikaa ne wura aburoo ne anu wɔ ye bɔtɔ ne anoa ɔ.

english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: Yiti ɔbɔle oliɛma nemɔ amaneɛ kyɛ, “Basa bafa me sikaa ne bama me. Ɛ́mɔnea, owura me bɔtɔ ne anu.” Ɛhe mane bɛ kunu tele bɛ, na bele anwopopolɛ besisele bɛ nwo kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ dwirɛ yeɛ Nyameɛ amaa wato yɛ ye?”

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: Na beedwuli bɛ baba Yakob berɛ wɔ Kanaan maen nu nen, bɛhane bɔ wato bɛ amu behyirele ye kyɛ,

english_verse: The governor of Egypt was rude and treated us like spies.
translation_verse: “Maen ne anu amrado le anwunanwuna yeɛ odwudwole hyirele yɛ ɔ; ɔnwa yɛte maentetɛlɛfoɛ po.

english_verse: But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies.
translation_verse: Nakoso yɛsele ye kyɛ, ‘Yɛdi nahorɛ, na yɛtte maentetɛlɛfoɛ.

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: Yɛte aliɛmaa mmienzua buru ne nyɔ, seɛ ko ama; ko de ɔbboka yɛ so ko, na kekesaala ye bɔ yɛdwudwo ye, kasiɛ ne ne yɛ baba wɔ Kanaan aseɛ so.

english_verse: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
translation_verse: Na biaa ne bɔ ɔte maen ne aso amrado ne sele yɛ kyɛ, Bɔ ɔkɔmaa ngonwu kyɛ ɛmɔdi nahorɛ ɛhe: ɛ́mɔma ɛmɔ aliɛmaa ne ko ha wa; na ɛmɔ ngaa ne de, ɛhɔen piri ne ati ɛ́mɔfa aburoo bɛɛma ɛmɔ awuro ama.

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
translation_verse: Ɛmɔɔfa ɛmɔ aliɛma kasiɛ ne bɛbrɛ me, amaa manwu kyɛ ɛmɔdi nahorɛ, na mmom ɛmɔtte maentetɛlɛfoɛ. Sɛ ɛmɔyɔ sɔ a, ngɔye ɛmɔ aliɛma ne ngɔma ɛmɔ, na ɛmɔatena maen ye anu bayɔ b’adwuma.”

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: Bɛwɔ so behwiehwie bɛ mmɔtɔ ne anu nningyein nen, benwuni kyɛ ebiala sikaa borɛ wɔ ye bɔtɔ ne anu. Na bɛ ne bɛ baba nwuni bɛ sikaa borɛ nemɔ nen, ɔyɛle bɛ suro.

english_verse: who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
translation_verse: Na bɛ baba Yakob sele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔamaa me mma mɔ afi me sa: Yosef afi me sa, Simeon afi me sa, yeɛ ɛmɔbaafa Benyamin koso bɛkɔ. Me yeɛ ménwu sɔ amaneɛ ye amukoraa.”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Ruben sele ye baba kyɛ, “Fa ye wura me sa, na ngosa ngɔfa ye ngɔbrɛ wɔ. Sɛ mamva ye manza mammrɛ wɔ a, ku me mma mmienzua nyɔ ne.”

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: Na Yakob sele kyɛ, “Mengɔmaa ɛne mma ne ngɔhɔ, ofikyɛ oliɛma awu maa waha ye ngome. Sɛ edwirɛ tɛɛ bie to ye atee bɔ ɛmɔbaatu ye anu a, ye de ɛmɔkɔmaa nne aworabɔlɛ ngɔfa me gyein ye ngɔhɔ ɛborɔ.”

english_verse: The famine in Canaan got worse,
translation_verse: Ɛhɔen ne anu yɛle se maen ne anu.

english_verse: until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
translation_verse: Na belili aleɛ bɔ bɛ ne ye fili Misraim bɛwale beyiele ne, bɛ baba sele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔsa bɛɛtɔ aleɛ kãa bɛbra.”

english_verse: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
translation_verse: nakoso sɛ amma wangɔ bie de a, yɛngɔhɔ, ofikyɛ biaa ne sele yɛ kyɛ, ‘Sɛ ɛmɔ aliɛma ne ɔbboka ɛmɔ so a, nnɛma ɛmɔpe me nyunu wa.’ ”

english_verse: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
translation_verse: Na Yisrael sele kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔyɔle me tɛɛ sɔa ɔ, kyɛ ɛmɔhã behyirele biaa ne kyɛ ɛmɔle aliɛmaa bieku ɔ?”

english_verse: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
translation_verse: Bebuale ye kyɛ, “Biaa ne tole ye bo ase bisale yɛ ne y’abusua nwo dwirɛ. Obisale kyɛ, ‘Ɛmɔ ase te ase? Ɛmɔle aliɛmaa bieku anaa?’ Edwirɛ bɔ yɛhã yɛhyirele ye ne, ɔte ye adwobisa ne nwo nyeanoɛ. Yɛyɛ sɛɛ né yanwu kyɛ saa okose yɛ kyɛ, ‘Ɛ́mɔfa ɛmɔ aliɛma ne bɛbra’?”

english_verse: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.
translation_verse: Na Yuda sele ye baba kyɛ, “Ma ate maa me ne abɛɛmaa ne yɛhɔ, na yɛkɔhɔ kekesaala ye, amaa yɛ ne wɔ ne yɛ mma mɔ, yanya ngoa na yanwu.

english_verse: I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live.
translation_verse: Ngoli ye nwo agyinamuɛ; sɛ ɛpena ye a, bisa ye ti me berɛ. Sɛ mamva ye manza mammrɛ wɔ asomdwee nu a, ye de maa nni fɔ wɔ wɔ nyunu daa.

english_verse: If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ sɛ yanyɛ ngyɛkyerɛ a, ahaa yahɔ dɔ pɛen nyɔ yawa.”

english_verse: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
translation_verse: Na bɛ baba Yisrael sele bɛ kyɛ, “Sɛ sɔ ala yeɛ odi kyɛ yɛyɔ de a, nzaade ɛ́mɔfa yɛ wa mmakaammaa paa ne bie begua ɛmɔ bɔtɔ nu, na ɛ́mɔfa sakyeɛ kãa, woɛ kãa, pɔweɛ, asãa, ngateɛ ɔne atonwaa bɛɛhyɛ biaa ne.

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔfa sikaa ne mmɔhoɛ nyɔ, na ɛ́mɔsa bɛfa sikaa bɔ bɛfa bewurale ɛmɔ bɔtɔ ne anu bɛhɔ; ebiaa ɔte anyefasoɛ.

english_verse: Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔfa ɛmɔ aliɛma ne bɛboka so, na ɛ́mɔdwɔso besa bɛhɔ biaa ne dɔ.

english_verse: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
translation_verse: Ɛdangama Nyameɛ ɔ́ma biaa ne ónwu ɛmɔ anwumvoin, na ɔ́ma ɛmɔ aliɛma ko ne, ɔne Benyamin besa bɛbra. Sɛ ɔba kyɛ odi kyɛ mma mɔ befi me sa a, ɔyɛ sɔ.”

english_verse: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,
translation_verse: Yiti ye mma nemɔ fale akyɛdeɛ ne, besa bɛfale sikaa ne mmɔhoɛ nyɔ, ɔne Benyamin bɛbokale so, na besili nu bɛhɔle Yosef berɛ wɔ Misraim.

english_verse: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
translation_verse: Na Yosef nwuni kyɛ Benyamin ɔboka bɛ so ne, osele ye awuro neafoɛ ne kyɛ, “Fa biaa nemɔ kɔ m’awuro, na ku kaka yɛ aleɛ, na me ne bɛ kodidi eyia ye.”

english_verse: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
translation_verse: Yiti Yosef awuro neafoɛ ne yɔle kyɛbɔ Yosef hyɛle ye ne, na ɔfale biaa nemɔ hɔle Yosef awuro.

english_verse: But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
translation_verse: Né Yakob mma nemɔ suro, ɔnate Yosef awuro bɔ bɛfale bɛ bɛhɔle ne ati, na besele kyɛ, “Sikaa bɔ bɛfa bewurale yɛ mmɔtɔ nemɔ anu mmerɛ bɔ yɛlili moa yɛwale wa ne, yiti yeɛ bafa yɛ bawa wa ye, amaa wanya atee wahye yɛ nnure wafa yɛ wayɛ ngoaa, na wafa y’afunum nemɔ.”

english_verse: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
translation_verse: Yiti bɛhɔle Yosef awuro so neafoɛ ne berɛ wɔ awuro ne anoa nu, na behyirele edwirɛ ne anu

english_verse: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
translation_verse: kyɛ, “Me mene, yali moa yawa ko yaatɔ aleɛ.

english_verse: But when we stopped for the night, we each found in our grain sacks the exact amount we had paid. We have brought that money back,
translation_verse: Na yɛɛdwuli asikyeleɛ na yɛsangyele yɛ mmɔtɔ nemɔ anu ne, yɛnwuni kyɛ ebiala sikaa ne noa pɛpɛɛpɛ wura ye bɔtɔ ne anu. Yiti yasa yafa yawa.

english_verse: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
translation_verse: Na yasa yafa sikaa foforɛ bɔ yɛbaafa yɛtɔ aleɛ ne bie ɔ. Yɛnze sona horɛ bɔ ɔfale yɛ sikaa ne wuralɛ yɛ mmɔtɔ nemɔ anu ɔ.”

english_verse: “It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
translation_verse: Awuro berɛ neafoɛ ne buale bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔhã ɛmɔ ahone bɛto ɛmɔ kunu, nnɛma ɛmɔsuro, ebiaa ɛmɔ Nyameɛ, ɛmɔ baba ye Nyameɛ ne, ye yeɛ wafa agyapadeɛ wawura ɛmɔ mmɔtɔ nemɔ anu ɔ. Ɛmɔ sikaa ne de, me sa hane ye.” Na ɔyele Simeon brɛle bɛ.

english_verse: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
translation_verse: Biaa ne fale Yakob mma nemɔ wale Yosef awuro nen, ɔmane bɛ nzue maa benwunzini bɛ gya bo, na ɔmane b’afunum nemɔ aleɛ.

english_verse: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
translation_verse: Besiesiele b’akyɛdeɛ ne bɛfa bɛnwondɛle Yosef. Né ɔba awuro berɛ eyia ne, ofikyɛ né bate kyɛ bekodidi wɔ berɛ.

english_verse: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him.
translation_verse: Yosef wale awuro nen, bɛfale akyɛdeɛ bɔ bɛ ne ye wale ne bɛmane ye wɔ awuro berɛ, na bɛbɔle bɛ nu ase bɛkotole ye.

english_verse: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
translation_verse: Obisale b’aporɛ nu, yeɛ osa bisale bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔ ase, biaa aworowaa bɔ ɛmɔhane ye nwo dwirɛ ne, ye nwo te paa? Ɔtɛ te ase?”

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
translation_verse: Bebuale ye kyɛ, “Yoo, w’akoaa bɔ ɔte yɛ baba ne, ye nwo te paa, na ɔtɛ te ase.” Na bɛbɔle bɛ ti ase bɛkotole ye.

english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: Ɔmane ye ti so, na onwuni oni awa bienzua Benyamin, na obisale kyɛ, “Ɛmɔ kasiɛ bɔ ɛmɔhane ye nwo dwirɛ behyirele me ne, ye ɛhe?” Osele ye kyɛ, “Mma, Nyameɛ yira wɔ!”

english_verse: Then, because of his love for Benjamin, he rushed off to his room and cried.
translation_verse: Na Yosef yɛle ndɛ fitele, ofikyɛ né ye wora adɔ oliɛma ne, na ɔɔpenane nekaa bɔ ɔkwaasu ɔ. Oowurale ye pumbu nu suni.

english_verse: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
translation_verse: Onwunzini ye nyunu, na ofili berɛ fitele; ɔhyɛle ye nwo so, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔfa aleɛ ne bɛbra.”

english_verse: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
translation_verse: Bɛtole ye poen deɛ ngome, yeɛ bɛtole oliɛma nemɔ poen deɛ, na bɛtole Misraimfoɛ bɔ bɛ ne ye didi nemɔ koso bɛ poen deɛ ngome; ofikyɛ né Misraimfoɛ ne Hebrifoɛ bɛndo asaa nnidi, ɔte akyiwadeɛ ma Misraimfoɛ.

english_verse: To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest.
translation_verse: Na bɛtenatenane ye nyunu, bamuɛbaa ne kyɛbɔ ye panyi diberɛ te ɔ, yeɛ kasiɛ ne kyɛbɔ ye ngwadaa diberɛ te ɔ; na ɔyɛle Yakob mma nemɔ nwanwa maa bɛtotole bɛ nye bɛneaneane bɛ nyunu.

english_verse: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_verse: Bɛfale aleɛ ne bie befili Yosef poen ne aso bɛbrɛle bɛ, nakoso Benyamin de, né ye deɛ te bɛ ngaa ne deɛ mmɔhoɛ nnu. Yiti bɛnone nzaa, na bɛ ne Yosef bɛ mukoraa bɛ nye gyele.

english_verse: Later, Joseph told the servant in charge of his house, “Fill the men's grain sacks with as much as they can hold and put their money in the sacks. Also put my silver cup in the sack of the youngest brother.” The servant did as he was told.
translation_verse: Fa me kulie ne, ɛdwetɛ kulie ne wura bɛ kasiɛ ne bɔtɔ ne anu, na fa ye sikaa bɔ ɔbaafa tɔ aburoo ne boka so.” Na ɔyɔle kyɛbɔ Yosef ha hyirele ye ne.

english_verse: Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene pɛ, beguale Yakob mma nemɔ ne b’afunum nemɔ ate.

english_verse: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
translation_verse: Bɛtrale kuro ne bɛhɔle moa kãa nen, Yosef sele ye awuro neafoɛ ne kyɛ, “Ka wɔ nwo foa mmenia nemɔ, na sɛ ɛkɔto bɛ a, bisa bɛ kyɛ, ‘Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔafa tɛɛ batua paa so ɔ? Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔawua me mene ɛdwetɛ kulie ne ɔ?

english_verse: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
translation_verse: Aso ná sɔ kulie ne yeɛ me mene no nu, na afei ɔnea nu ɔfa onwu bɔ ɔbaasi ɔ. Nikyee bɔ ɛmɔayɔ ye de, ɔtte mayee koraa.’ ”

english_verse: When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say.
translation_verse: Ɔɔtole bɛ ne, ɔfale sɔ dwirɛ ne tole bɛ nyunu.

english_verse: But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!
translation_verse: Na besele ye kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ dwirɛ yeɛ me mene ɔne yɛ ka ye? Wɔ ngoaa ngɔhora sɔ nikyee ne yɔ le!

english_verse: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
translation_verse: Esikaa bɔ yɛnwuni ye wɔ yɛ bɔtɔ ne anu ne, yɛsa yɛfa yɛfili Kanaan aseɛ so yɛbrɛle wɔ. Nzu ati yeɛ yɛ́wua ɛdwetɛ anaa sikaa kɔkorɛ yɛ́fi wɔ mene awuro ɔ?

english_verse: If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
translation_verse: Sɛ enwu kulie ne wɔ yɛ nu biala berɛ a, maa behũ ye, na yɛ ngaa ne koso yɛkɔyɛ yɛ mene ngoaa.”

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
translation_verse: Awuro neafoɛ ne sele kyɛ, “Yoo, mepene so, sona bɔ ngonwu kulie ne wɔ ye berɛ ne, ɔkɔyɛ m’akoaa, nakoso ɛmɔ ngaa ne de, ɛmɔkɔfa bɛ nwo bekoli.”

english_verse: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
translation_verse: Yiti ebiala tole ye bɔtɔ ne ase ndɛndɛ, na ebiala sangyele ye bɔtɔ deɛ noa.

english_verse: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
translation_verse: Na awuro neafoɛ ne neaneane nu; ɔhyɛle ye bo fili bamuɛbaa ne deɛ so oodwuli kasiɛ ne aso. Na onwuni kulie ne Benyamin bɔtɔ deɛ ne anu.

english_verse: This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
translation_verse: Ɔwale ye sɔ nen, besunzuale bɛ ndaadeɛ nu, na ebiala sá sesale ye nningyein guale ye afunum so, na besale bɛ si bɛhɔle kuro ne aso.

english_verse: When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph,
translation_verse: Yuda ne oliɛma mɔ beedwuli Yosef awuro nen, né ɔtɛwɔ berɛ, na bɛlelale aseɛnwo wɔ ye nyunu.

english_verse: who asked them, “What have you done? Didn't you know I could find out?”
translation_verse: Yosef bisale bɛ kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ nikyee yeɛ ɛmɔayɔ ye? Anaa ɛmɔnze kyɛ sona bɔ ɔte kyɛ me de, ɔse ase ɔ?”

english_verse: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
translation_verse: Na Yuda buale kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ yeɛ yɛkã yɛkyire me mene ɔ? Nzikyɛ dwirɛ yeɛ yɛkã ɔ? Yɛyɛ sɛɛ né yasa yɛ nwo? Nyameɛ ama wɔ ngoaa nwo ala so; yayɛ me mene ngoaa, yɛ ne sona bɔ benwuni kulie ne wɔ ye dɔ ne yeɛ yayɛ ngoaa ɔ.”

english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Nakoso Yosef sele bɛ kyɛ, “Daabi, mengɔyɔ ye sɔ le! Sona bɔ benwuni kulie ne wɔ ye dɔ ne angome yeɛ ɔkɔyɛ m’akoaa ɔ; ɛmɔ ngaa ne de, ɛ́mɔsa bɛhɔ ɛmɔ ase dɔ asomdwee nu.” Yuda serɛ ma Benyamin

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Na Yuda hɔle Yosef nwo berɛ oosele ye kyɛ, “Me mene, mesrɛ wɔ, ma w’akoaa osusu edwirɛ kãa nwo ohyire ye mene; nnɛfɛ w’akoaa so yaa, ofikyɛ wɔ de wɔ diberɛ te kyɛ Faro bɔbɔ deinn.

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: Me mene bisale ye ngoaa kyɛ, ‘Aso ɛmɔ ase tɛ te ase, na ɛmɔle aliɛmaa bieku’?

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Na yɛbuale yɛ mene kyɛ, ‘Yoo, yɛ baba tɛ wɔ berɛ, wayɛ aworowaa. Yɛle aliɛmaa kãa ko wɔ berɛ, yɛ baba ye aworowaa nu baa ɛne; oni awa deɛ awu maa waha ye ngome, na ye baba kuro ye dwirɛ paa.

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: Yeɛ esele wɔ ngoaa kyɛ, ‘Ɛ́mɔfa ye bɛ́brɛ me maa nwu ye.’

english_verse: We told you that our father would die if Benjamin left him.
translation_verse: Na yɛsele me mene kyɛ, ‘Abɛɛmaa ne ngɔhora ye baba anwo fi, ofikyɛ sɛ ofi ɔse anwo a, ɔse kowu.’

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Yeɛ ɛha hyirele wɔ ngoaa kyɛ, ‘Sɛ ɛmɔamva ɛmɔ aliɛma kasiɛ ne bamma a, mengɔnea ɛmɔ nyunu ko.’

english_verse: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
translation_verse: Yɛsa yɛhɔle w’akoaa me baba dɔ nen, yɛfale yɛ mene noa dwirɛ yɛɛbɔle ye amaneɛ.

english_verse: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
translation_verse: Na yɛ baba sele yɛ kyɛ, ‘Ɛ́mɔsa bɛhɔ bɛɛtɔ aleɛ kãa bɛbrɛ yɛ’ nen,

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: yɛbuale kyɛ, ‘Yɛngɔhora kɔ. Sɛ y’eliɛma kãa ne ɔne yɛ kɔ de a, ye de yɛkɔhɔ; ofikyɛ sɛ y’eliɛma kãa ne ɔbboka yɛ so a, biaa ne ngɔnea yɛ nyunu po.’

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: Yeɛ w’akoaa, bɔ ɔte me baba ne, osele yɛ kyɛ, ‘Ɛ́mɔse kyɛ me ne me ye ne yɛwole mma mmienzua nyɔ;

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: bɛ nu ko afi me sa, na ngane kyɛ, amba kaka bie atete ye pasapasa, na ofi berɛ ne, mannwu ye ko.

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛmɔfa ɛhe koso bɛkɔ ná nikyee bie yɛ ye a, ɛmɔkɔmaa nne aworabɔlɛ ngɔfa me gyein ngɔhɔ ɛborɔ.’

english_verse: That's why Benjamin must be with us when I go back to my father. He loves him so much
translation_verse: Yiti kekesaala ye, sɛ mesa mekɔ w’akoaa me baba dɔ, na sɛ abɛɛmaa ne ɔbboka yɛ so a, ye de kyɛbɔ ɔne abɛɛmaa ne besi bɛte ko nen,

english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Na me, w’akoaa, nnili abɛɛmaa ne anwo agyinamuɛ wɔ me baba nyunu kyɛ, ‘Sɛ manza mamva ye mammrɛ wɔ a, ye de ngoli fɔ wɔ me baba nyunu me ngyẽa bɔ ngoli ye aseɛ ye aso amukoraa.’

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: Yiti afei, mesrɛ wɔ, maa w’akoaa, nzi abɛɛmaa ne gya nu na nyɛ me mene akoaa; na mmom abɛɛmaa ne de, maa ɔne oliɛma mɔ besa bɛhɔ.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Méyɛ sɛɛ né masa mahɔ me baba berɛ wɔ aberɛ bɔ abɛɛmaa ne ɔbboka me so ɔ? Membena kyɛ menwu kyɛ edwirɛ tɛɛ bie kɔto me baba ɔ.”

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Afei Yosef angora anhyɛ ye nwo so wɔ ye somvoɛ amukoraa bɔ bɛwɔ berɛ ne anyunu, yiti ɔteane nu sele bɛ kyɛ, “Ebiala ófi wa fite!” Na Yosef yele ye nwo ali hyirele oliɛma nemɔ nen, né sona foforɛ biala ɔnne berɛ.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Na Yosef teateane nu suni maa Misraimfoɛ nemɔ ne Faro awuro ama tele.

english_verse: Joseph asked his brothers if his father was still alive, but they were too frightened to answer.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yosef sele oliɛma nemɔ kyɛ, “Me ole Yosef; aso me baba tɛ te ase?” Nakoso oliɛma nemɔ angora ye noa ye, ofikyɛ bɛ nwo dwirili bɛ kyɛ banwu ye ɔ.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Yosef sele oliɛma nemɔ kyɛ, “Mesrɛ ɛmɔ, ɛ́mɔpingye me nwo wa.” Yiti bepingyele ye. Na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔ aliɛma Yosef bɔ ɛmɔtɔnene ye maa oofitele Misraim ne, ye ole me.

english_verse: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
translation_verse: Na afei nnɛmɔma ɛmɔ wora bɔ, yeɛ nnɛma ɛmɔfu bɛ nwo kyɛ ɛmɔtɔnene me maa mmamvitele ɛwa ɔ; ofikyɛ Nyameɛ somane me kyɛ nni ɛmɔ nyunu na nne mmenia ngoa.

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Ɛhɔen piri ne wale maen ye anu ɔ, afoɛ nyɔ ɛhe; nakoso waha afoɛ nnu bɔ yeɛ bɛngɔyɔ eboo na banya aleɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ somane me maa nnili ɛmɔ nyunu kyɛbɔ ɛmɔ boso ngonua wɔ aseɛ ye aso ɔ, amaa ɛmɔ bosofoɛ pee anya ngoa.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: Yiti nna ɛmɔ yeɛ ɛmɔfale me bɛwale wa ɔ, na mmom Nyameɛ ɔ; na wamaa maayɛ Faro foɛtulɛfoɛ panyi, ɔne ye awuro amukoraa so meneɛ, na nza nde Misraim maen mukoraa so hene.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: Yiti ɛ́mɔhã bɛ nwo bɛhɔ me baba berɛ beese ye kyɛ, Ɛwa Yosef nwa: Nyameɛ ayɛ me Misraim amukoraa so meneɛ; yiti ma wɔ nwo yɛ nyera na bra me nwo wa.

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Ɛkɔɔtena Gosen mbɔtam, ɛkɔtena kopingye me, ɛne wɔ mma ne wɔ nnomaa mɔ, ɔne wɔ mmoaen ne wɔ nandwie mɔ, ɔne wɔ nningyein amukoraa.

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Mengɔma hwee ngohia wɔ wɔ berɛ, ofikyɛ ɛhɔen piri ne, waha afoɛ nnu. Anyɔ a, ɛne w’awuro ama, ɔne bɔ ele ye amukoraa nwo kɔhyere bɛ.”

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: Ɔtoale so sele oliɛma nemɔ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔ nye tua, yeɛ nniɛma Benyamin koso nye tua kyɛ me bɔbɔ deinn yeɛ me ne ɛmɔ yɛdwudwo ye.

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔhã me diberɛ bɔ nne ye wɔ Misraim ɔne bɔ ɛmɔanwu ye amu behyire me baba. Ɛ́mɔhã bɛ nwo bɛɛfa me baba bɛbra wa.”

english_verse: Joseph and Benjamin hugged each other and started crying.
translation_verse: Afei ɔto brale oliɛma Benyamin osuni, na Benyamin koso to brale ye suni.

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: Na ɔfele oliɛma nemɔ amukoraa bɛ noa, na ɔtotɔle bɛ nu suni. Ye si ye, oliɛma nemɔ ne ye belili ngɔmɔ.

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Na Faro awuro ama tele kyɛ, “Yosef aliɛma mɔ awa” nen, ɔyɛle Faro ne ye mbanyi mɔ fɛ paa.

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Faro sele Yosef kyɛ, “Ka kyire eliɛma nemɔ kyɛ, ‘Ɛ́mɔwura aleɛ bɛsoasoa ɛmɔ ngaka nemɔ na ɛmɔsa bɛhɔ Kanaan aseɛ so;

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
translation_verse: na ɛmɔɔfa ɛmɔ ase ne ɛmɔ awuro ama mɔ bɛbra me wa. Na Misraim aseɛ ne, ngɔma ɛmɔ nekaa bɔ ɔte paa paa ɔ, ná ɛmɔanya aseɛ ne aso aleɛ paa bali.’

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: Na sá hyɛ bɛ kyɛ, ‘Ɛ́mɔfa teaseɛnam mɔ béfi Misraim maen nu na ɛmɔɔfa ɛmɔ mma ne ɛmɔ aye mɔ, na ɛ́mɔfa ɛmɔ ase bɛbra.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: Nnɛma ɛmɔdwene ɛmɔ agyapadeɛ bɔ ɔkɔha dɔ nwo, ofikyɛ Misraim aseɛ so nningyein paa amu te ɛmɔ deɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Yisrael mma nemɔ yɔle sɔ. Yosef mane bɛ teaseɛnam mɔ kyɛbɔ Faro hyɛle ne, na ɔmane bɛ aleɛ bɔ bekoli ye atunu ɔ.

english_verse: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
translation_verse: Ɔmane ebiala ataadeɛ bɔ ɔyɛ nyemene ko, nakoso Benyamin de, ɔmane ye ɛdwetɛ kɔyɛ kilo nza ne ndaadeɛ nyemene ahoroɔ nnu.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Na ɔfale nningyein hemɔ manene ye baba: afunum nyii buru bɔ bafa Misraim nningyein paa basoa bɛ, afunum mmeleɛ buru bɔ basoa bɛ aburoo, paanoo, ɔne aleɛ bɔ ye baba koli ye atee nu ɔ.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: Oguale oliɛma nemɔ ate, na besi nu nen, osele bɛ kyɛ, “Nnɛma ɛmɔkɔko atee nu oo.”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Yiti befili Misraim, na beedwuli bɛ se Yakob berɛ wɔ Kanaan aseɛ so.

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: Na bɛbɔle ye amaneɛ kyɛ, “Yosef tɛ te ase, na odi hene wɔ Misraim aseɛ mukoraa so.” Na ye ti anu yɛle ye nnaa, ofikyɛ wanne bɛ wanni.

english_verse: Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better
translation_verse: Nakoso bɛhane bɔ Yosef aha ahyire bɛ ne amu behyirele Yakob. Na Yakob nwuni teaseɛnam mɔ bɔ Yosef asoma kyɛ bɛfa bɛɛfa ye nen, ye kra wale ye nwo.

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: Na Yisrael sele kyɛ, “Ɔte nahorɛ, mma Yosef tɛ te ase; ngɔhɔ ngoonwu ye koraka né mawu.”

english_verse: Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Yiti Yisrael, bɛ besa bɛfrɛ ye Yakob ne sesale ye nwo nningyein amu, na ɔpene atee so. Oodwuli Beɛ Hyeba, na ɔbɔle afɔleɛ mane ye baba Yisake Nyameɛ.

english_verse: That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ dwudwo hyirele Yisrael kɔngɔen ne wɔ nyekyire nu. Ɔfrɛle ye: “Yakob, Yakob,” na osurole kyɛ, “Me ɛhe.”

english_verse: God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation.
translation_verse: Na osele kyɛ, “Me ole Nyameɛ, wɔ baba ye Nyameɛ, nnɛsuro kyɛ ɛkɔhɔ Misraim, ofikyɛ ngɔma wɔ bosofoɛ kɔyɛ maen kandinga wɔ dɔ.”

english_verse: I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
translation_verse: Me bɔbɔ me ne wɔ kɔhɔ Misraim, na ngosa ngɔfa wɔ bosofoɛ ngɔwa sɔ aseɛ ye aso; na Yosef yeɛ okogua wɔ noa nu nzue ɔ.”

english_verse: The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living.
translation_verse: Sɛ Faro frɛ ɛmɔ na obisa kyɛ, ‘Nzikyɛ adwuma yeɛ ɛmɔyɔ ɔ?’ a,

english_verse: Jacob had sent his son Judah ahead of him to ask Joseph to meet them in Goshen.
translation_verse: Yakob somane Yuda maa olili ye nyunu moa hɔle Yosef berɛ kyɛ Yosef ohyire ye Gosen atee, na bɛwale Gosen mbɔtam.

english_verse: So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time.
translation_verse: Yosef siesiele ye teaseɛnam na ɔfole ooyiale ye baba Yisrael wɔ Gosen. Ɔfale ye nwo hyirele ɔse; ɔtɔle ye nu, na ɔfale ye ti tole ye kɔme anwo suni hyɛle paa.

english_verse: Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
translation_verse: Na Yisrael sele Yosef kyɛ, “Afei de mewu po a, mekuro, ɔnate kyɛ manwu wɔ nyunu, na manwu kyɛ ɛte ase.”

english_verse: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them: I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan.
translation_verse: Na Yosef sele oliɛma mɔ ne ɔse awuro ama nemɔ kyɛ, “Ngɔhɔ Faro berɛ ngɔɔbɔ ye amaneɛ kyɛ, ‘Nniɛma mɔ ne me baba awuro ama bɔ né bɛwɔ Kanaan aseɛ so ne, bawa me wa.

english_verse: I will tell him that you are shepherds and that you have brought your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Bɛte mmoaenneafoɛ, ofikyɛ besie ngaka; na bafa bɛ mmoaen ne bɛ nandwie mɔ ne bɛ nwo nningyein mukoraa bawa wa.’

english_verse: When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen. Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
translation_verse: ɛ́mɔbua ye kyɛ, ‘Ofi yɛ ngwadaa nu bɔ ɔbaadwu ɛnɛ ye, wɔ ngoaa mɔ de, yɛte mmoaenneafoɛ kyɛ yɛ nana mɔ ala.’ Sɛ ɔba ye sɔ a, ɔkɔmaa ɛmɔkɔtena Gosen mbɔtam, ofikyɛ Misraimfoɛ kyi mmoaenneafoɛ kɔkɔkɔkɔ.”

english_verse: who asked them, “What do you do for a living?” “Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep.
translation_verse: Na Faro bisale oliɛma nemɔ kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ adwuma yeɛ ɛmɔyɔ ɔ?” Na bebuale Faro kyɛ, “Wɔ ngoaa mɔ te mmoaenneafoɛ kyɛ yɛ nana mɔ ala.”

english_verse: But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
translation_verse: Bɛtoale so besele Faro kyɛ, “Yawa kyɛ yɛbaatena maen ye anu, ofikyɛ wɔ ngoaa mɔ, yɛnnya aleɛ yɛmma yɛ ngaka mɔ. Ɛhɔen piri bɔ ɔwɔ Kanaan aseɛ so ne noa yɛ se paa. Yiti kekesaala ye, yɛsrɛ wɔ, maa wɔ ngoaa mɔ yɛtena Gosen mbɔtam.”

english_verse: The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Faro sele Yosef kyɛ, “Wɔ baba ne eliɛma mɔ bawa baaboka wɔ so wɔ wa.

english_verse: I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Misraim aseɛ ne wura wɔ sa, ma wɔ baba ne eliɛma mɔ bɛtena aseɛ ne nekaa bɔ ɔkye aleɛ paa ɔ. Maa bɛtena Gosen mbɔtam, na sɛ ɛse bɛ nu biemɔ bɔ bɛkɔhora a, maa bɛnea me nyɛmmoa deɛ mɔ bɛma me.”

english_verse: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing,
translation_verse: Afei Yosef mane ye baba Yakob wale oosomane Faro, na Yakob yirale Faro.

english_verse: and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
translation_verse: Na Faro bisale Yakob kyɛ, “Ali afoɛ nyɛɛ?”

english_verse: Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left.
translation_verse: Yakob yirale Faro, na ofili Faro nyunu berɛ ɔhɔle.

english_verse: Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yosef bɔle ɔse ne oliɛma mɔ atenaseɛ, na ɔmane bɛ aseɛ bɔ ɔkye aleɛ paa wɔ Ramese mbɔtam wɔ Misraim maen nu, kyɛbɔ Faro hyɛle ne.

english_verse: The famine was bad everywhere in Egypt and Canaan, and the people were suffering terribly.
translation_verse: Né aleɛ nne aseɛ ne aso nekaa biala; ofikyɛ ɛhɔen piri ne anu yɛle se paa, ɔnate sɔ ati né Misraim maen ne Kanaan maen nu mmenia mukoraa bɛ́teetee.

english_verse: So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury.
translation_verse: Né Misraim aseɛ so ne Kanaan aseɛ so sikaa mukoraa waali Yosef berɛ, ɔnate aburoo bɔ bɛtɔle befili ye berɛ ne ati, na Yosef fale esikaa ne hɔle Faro awuro.

english_verse: But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Misraimfoɛ ne Kanaanfoɛ bɛ sikaa amu yiele ne, Misraimfoɛ amukoraa wale Yosef berɛ beesele ye kyɛ, “Ma yɛ aleɛ; aso odi kyɛ yɛwuwu wɔ wɔ nyunu wa? Yɛ sikaa mukoraa ayie.”

english_verse: “If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yosef sele bɛ kyɛ, “Sɛ ɛmɔ sikaa amu ayie a, nzaade ɛ́mɔfa ɛmɔ nyɛmmoa mɔ bɛbra maa mva nzesã aleɛ mma ɛmɔ.”

english_verse: Then the people came to him and said: Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land.
translation_verse: Na sɔ afoɛ ne sone nen, ye afoɛ bieku besa bɛwale ye berɛ beesele ye kyɛ, “Yɛngɔfa ngɔfea me mene kyɛ yɛ sikaa mukoraa ayie, na nandwie nemɔ baali yɛ mene sa nu, na ɛhwee nne berɛ bɔ yɛkɔfa yɛkɔbrɛ me mene ɔ, sana yɛ nipadua ɔne y’aseɛ ala.

english_verse: Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
translation_verse: Nzu ati yeɛ odi kyɛ yɛwuwu wɔ wɔ nyunu wa ma y’aseɛ mɔ ka berɛ ɔ? Tɔ yɛ ne y’aseɛ ná ma yɛ aleɛ, na yɛkɔyɛ Faro ngoaa, na yɛ aseɛ ayɛ ye deɛ. Ma yɛ aburoo bɔ yɛkolua ɔ, amaa yanwuwu, na mmom yanya yɛ ti yadidi nu, na aseɛ ne koso wanna berɛ mbaen.”

english_verse: The famine became so severe that Joseph finally bought every piece of land in Egypt for the king
translation_verse: Yiti Yosef tɔle Misraim aseɛ ne amu mane Faro. Ɔnate ɛhɔen piri bɔ né ɔdosa mmenia ne ati, Misraimfoɛ amukoraa tɔnetɔnene b’aseɛ. Aseɛ ne ɔɔyɛle Faro deɛ,

english_verse: except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land.
translation_verse: Asɔfo nemɔ aseɛ angome yeɛ wandɔ ɔ; ofikyɛ asɔfo nemɔ de, né Faro tua bɛ kerɛ, na bɛfale sɔ akatuaa ne bɛneane bɛ nwo, yiti bandɔne b’aseɛ deɛ mɔ.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant,
translation_verse: Yiti Yosef sele mmenia nemɔ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔtie, ɛnɛ kyẽa ye, matɔ ɛmɔ ne ɛmɔ aseɛ mama Faro. Aburoo bɔ bedua ɛhe. Ɛ́mɔlua ye wɔ aseɛ ne aso.

english_verse: but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
translation_verse: Sɛ buberɛ dwu a, ɛmɔkɔhyɛ fieso aleɛ ne anu nnu: ko kɔyɛ Faro deɛ na nna ayɛ ɛmɔ deɛ. Ɛmɔkolua bie fieso, na ɛmɔ ne ɛmɔ awuro ama ne ɛmɔ mma mɔ bali bie.”

english_verse: “Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.”
translation_verse: Na besele ye kyɛ, “Ale yɛ ngoa, maa me mene ɔpene so, na yɛkɔyɛ Faro ngoaa.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land. Jacob Becomes an Old Man
translation_verse: Yiti Yosef hyɛle mmeraa fale Misraim aseɛ nwo, bɔ ɔtɛwɔ berɛ ɔbaadwu ɛnɛ ɔ, kyɛ fieso nningyein biala bɛkyɛ nu kure nnu a, ko te Faro deɛ; asɔfo nemɔ aseɛ ngome yeɛ wanyɛ Faro deɛ ɔ. Yakob nzamanzeɛ

english_verse: The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families.
translation_verse: Yiti Yisrael tenane Gosen mbɔtam wɔ Misraim maen nu. Benyane agyapadeɛ wɔ berɛ, na bɛwowole bɛyɛle pee.

english_verse: When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Yisrael wue pingyele ne, ɔfrɛle ɔwa Yosef sele ye kyɛ, “Sɛ anya alo me a, ye de fa wɔ sa bawura me sɔ abo, na hyɛ ɛbɔ kitii kyɛ ekoli nahorɛ kɔma me: Sɛ mewu a, nnɛsie me wɔ Misraim.

english_verse: Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.” “I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Na mmom maa ngɔnna nekaa bɔ me mbanyi mɔ la ɔ; fa me fi Misraim na kosie me wɔ me mbanyi mɔ asieleɛ.” Na Yosef buale ye kyɛ, “Yoo, ngɔyɔ ye kyɛbɔ aha ne ala.”

english_verse: “Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked. “Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
translation_verse: Yakob toale so kyɛ, “Ta ndaen kyire me.” Na Yosef tale ndaen hyirele ye. Na Yisrael bɔle ye nu ase fale ye ti kisale mba ne sorɔ.

english_verse: Joseph was told that his father Jacob had become very sick. So Joseph went to see him and took along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Na ɛhe asi ne, bɛɛbɔle Yosef amaneɛ kyɛ, “Wɔ baba nde apɔ.” Yiti ɔfale Manase ne Efraim bɔ bɛte ye mma nyɔ ne bokale ye nwo so.

english_verse: When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
translation_verse: Na ebie sele Yakob kyɛ, “Ɛwa Yosef awa wɔ wa.” Yiti Yisrael kendene ye nwo tenane ye mba ne aso.

english_verse: Jacob told Joseph: God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing
translation_verse: Na Yakob sele Yosef kyɛ, “Ɛdangama Nyameɛ yele ye nwo ali hyirele me wɔ Luse bɔ ɔwɔ Kanaan aseɛ so. Oyirale me,

english_verse: and promised, “I will give you a large family with many descendants that will grow into a nation. And I am giving you this land that will belong to you and your family forever.”
translation_verse: na osele me kyɛ, ‘Ngɔmaa ɛkɔwo na wɔ boso atrɛ; ngɔma wɔ boso ama kɔyɛ mmeni kure pee, na ngɔfa aseɛ he ngɔhyɛ wɔ ne wɔ boso ama afebɔɔ.’

english_verse: Then Jacob went on to say: Joseph, your two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, but I accept them as my own, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
translation_verse: Na afei wɔ mma mmienzua nyɔ nemɔ bɔ ɛwole bɛ wɔ Misraim koraka yeɛ meba wɔ wa wɔ Misraim nen, mekyire Efraim ɔne Manase, bɛte me deɛ; bɛkɔyɛ me mma kyɛbɔ Ruben ne Simeon bɛte ne ala.

english_verse: Any children you have later will be considered yours, but their inheritance will come from Ephraim and Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ngwadaa bɔ ɛkɔwo bɛ nziɛ ye de, bɛte wɔ deɛ; na sɛ ɔba agyapadeɛ hyɛlɛ nu a, b’eliɛma nemɔ dumaa yeɛ ɔkɔla bɛ deɛ so ɔ.

english_verse: Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ mvi Padan méba ne, atee nu, ɔhale kãa maa yɛdwu Efrate ne, Rahɛl wuli Kanaan aseɛ so mane me wora bɔle, na nziele ye wɔ Efrate atee nu.”

english_verse: Jacob turned to Joseph and told him, “For many years I thought you were dead and that I would never see you again. But now God has even let me live to see your children.”
translation_verse: Yisrael sele Yosef kyɛ, “Mandwene kyɛ ngonwu wɔ nyunu ko le, nakoso nea kyɛ Nyameɛ amaa manwu wɔ mma mɔ koso po ɔ.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made his sons move away from Jacob's knees, and Joseph bowed down in front of him with his face to the ground.
translation_verse: Yosef pagyale ngwadaa nemɔ fili Yisrael gya so, na Yosef kunduni fale ye nyunu butuli berɛ.

english_verse: After Joseph got up, he brought his two sons over to Jacob again. He led his younger son Ephraim to the left side of Jacob and his older son Manasseh to the right.
translation_verse: Na Yosef fale bɛ munyɔ pingyele ɔse. Ɔfale ye sa famaa sɔle Efraim nu maa oolili Yisrael sa bɛen so, yeɛ ɔfale ye sa bɛen sɔle Manase nu maa oolili Yisrael sa famaa so.

english_verse: But before Jacob gave them his blessing, he crossed his arms, putting his right hand on the head of Ephraim and his left hand on the head of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Yisrael tengyɛle ye sa famaa fa tole Efraim bɔ yeɛ ɔte kãa ne ti so, na ɔfale ye sa beale nu fale bɛen ne tole Manase so, ɔwɔ nu kyɛ né Manase yeɛ ɔte bamuɛbaa ɔ de.

english_verse: Then he gave Joseph his blessing and said: My grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac worshiped the Lord God. He has been with me all my life,
translation_verse: Na oyirale Yosef kyɛ, “Nyameɛ bɔ me mbanyi mɔ Abraham ne Yisake bɛsole ye ne, Nyameɛ bɔ wagyina me si me wiase bɔ mmale maa waadwu ɛne ye,

english_verse: and his angel has kept me safe. Now I pray that he will bless these boys and that my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac will live on because of them. I ask God to give them many children and many descendants as well.
translation_verse: abɔfo bɔ aye me afi musue mukoraa nu ɔ, yira mmɛɛmaa ye; maa ɔnate bɛ so, me dumaa, ɔne me mbanyi mɔ Abraham ne Yisake dumaa otira ndii; ma bɛ boso ama bɛsone na bɛyɛ pee wɔ aseɛ ye aso.”

english_verse: Joseph did not like it when he saw his father place his right hand on the head of the younger son. So he tried to move his father's right hand from Ephraim's head and place it on Manasseh.
translation_verse: Na Yosef nwuni kyɛ ye baba afa ye sa famaa wato Efraim ti so nen, wanyɛ ye fɛ; yiti ɔyele ye baba sa fili Efraim ti so fa tole Manase ti so.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Father, you have made a mistake. This is the older boy. Put your right hand on him.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yosef sele ye baba kyɛ, “Daabi, baba, ɛhe yeɛ ɔte bamuɛbaa ɔ, yiti fa wɔ sa famaa ne to ye ti so.”

english_verse: But his father said, “Son, I know what I am doing. It's true that Manasseh's family will someday become a great nation. But Ephraim will be even greater than Manasseh, because his descendants will become many great nations.”
translation_verse: Nakoso ye baba ambene, na osele kyɛ, “Mese, mma mese, ɛhe koso kɔyɛ maen, ye koso ɔkɔyɛ sona titire, nakoso oliɛma kãa ne koli mu kɔtra ye, na ye bosofoɛ kɔyɛ maen maen pee.”

english_verse: Jacob told him that in the future the people of Israel would ask God's blessings on one another by saying, “I pray for God to bless you as much as he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.” Jacob put Ephraim's name first to show that he would be greater than Manasseh.
translation_verse: Yiti oyirale bɛ sɔ kyẽa ne, na osele kyɛ, “Ɔnate wɔ so yeɛ maen Yisrael kɔha sɔ saleɛ dwirɛ he ɔ: ‘Nyameɛ ma ɛyɛ kyɛ Efraim, na ɔ́ma ɛyɛ kyɛ Manase.’ ” Yiti Yakob nate sɔ atee he aso bɔle Efraim panyi wɔ Manase so.

english_verse: After that, Jacob said, “Joseph, you can see that I won't live much longer. But God will be with you and will lead you back to the land he promised our family long ago.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yisrael sele Yosef kyɛ, “Mebaawu, nakoso Nyameɛ kogyina ɛmɔ si, na okosa kɔfa ɛmɔ kɔhɔ ɛmɔ nana mɔ aseɛ so.

english_verse: Jacob called his sons together and said: My sons, I am Jacob, your father Israel.
translation_verse: Yakob frɛfrɛle ye mma mɔ, na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔboaboa ɛmɔ noa ma nga bɔ kyẽa bie okosi ɛmɔ bra nu ɔ ngyire ɛmɔ.

english_verse: Come, gather around, as I tell your future.
translation_verse: “O Yakob mma, ɛ́mɔyia na ɛ́mɔtie, ɛ́mɔtie ɛmɔ ase Yisrael.

english_verse: Reuben, you are my oldest, born at the peak of my powers; you were an honored leader.
translation_verse: Ruben, wɔ yeɛ ɛte me bamuɛbaa ɔ, m’anwoserɛ, me sɛngyerɛnneɛ bɔ oli moa bɔ okyire kyɛ nde bienzua ɔ, w’anidie tra so, yeɛ wɔ tumi koso tra so.

english_verse: Uncontrollable as a flood, you slept with my wife and disgraced my bed. And so you no longer deserve the place of honor.
translation_verse: Ɛwosowoso kyɛ nzue, yiti wɔ panyililɛ ne kɔbɔ wɔ, ofikyɛ ɛne ɛse aye bɛlale; ɛɛlale me bɛen so, eguale ye nwo fiɛ.

english_verse: Simeon and Levi, you are brothers, each a gruesome sword.
translation_verse: Simeon ne Lewi te aliɛmaa, bɛ ngrandɛ mɔ te nzɛmmɔne akodeɛ

english_verse: I never want to take part in your plans or deeds. You slaughtered people in your anger, and you crippled cattle for no reason.
translation_verse: Ao me kra, nnɛne bɛ fa adwene; Ao me sunzum, nnɛne bɛ bɔ afɛ; ofikyɛ sɛ bɛfɛ yaa a, bedi awue, na bɛgye bɛ nye a, bɛpepɛ nandwie mɔ gya ndii nu.

english_verse: Now I place a curse on you because of your fierce anger. Your descendants will be scattered among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Musue to b’ɛyaafɛlɛ ne, ofikyɛ ye noa yɛ hye; ɔ́hã b’ɛyaafɛlɛ piri ne koso, ofikyɛ atianuserɛ wɔ nu! Ngɔhyehyɛ bɛ bosofoɛ nu wɔ Yakob maen ne anu, na mato bɛ mapete Yisrael maen nu.

english_verse: Judah, you will be praised by your brothers; they will bow down to you, as you defeat your enemies.
translation_verse: Yuda, eliɛma mɔ kɔkamvo wɔ, na ɛkɔfo kɔtena wɔ pɔfoɛ mɔ kɔme so; ɛse amma mmienzua mɔ kɔkoto wɔ.

english_verse: My son, you are a lion ready to eat your victim! You are terribly fierce; no one will bother you.
translation_verse: Yuda te gyata akrɔngrɔma, bɔ eku ngaka di ná esa bada wɔ boso ɔ. Okunduni, na obutuli berɛ kyɛ gyata, ɔte kyɛ gyata beleɛ; nwa yeɛ onzuro bɔ okotingye ye ɔ?

english_verse: You will tie your donkey to a choice grapevine and wash your clothes in wine from those grapes.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔmenda ye pɔngɔ akrɔngrɔma kɔbɔ bobe nu, na wamenda ye afunum ba wabɔ bobe paa nu, na ɔpo ye ndaadeɛ wɔ nzaa nu, na wapo ye tena wɔ bobe nzaa bɔ ɔyɛ fɛ nu;

english_verse: Your eyes are darker than wine, your teeth whiter than milk.
translation_verse: Ɔkɔno nzaa somaa biala bɔ okuro ɔ, ná nyɔfonesue ama ye gye ayɛ hyɛnn.

english_verse: Zebulun, you will settle along the seashore and provide safe harbors as far north as Sidon.
translation_verse: Sebulɔn kɔtena mboanoa, ɔkɔyɛ ɛlɛen mɔ agyinaleɛ, na ɔne Sidon bɛkɔbɔ ɛwɛen.

english_verse: Issachar, you are a strong donkey resting in the meadows.
translation_verse: Yisaka te afunum anwoserɛniɛ, obutu mmoaen kure mɔ afia;

english_verse: Dan, you are the tribe that will bring justice to Israel.
translation_verse: Dan kobua ye mmenia ndɛen, kyɛbɔ Yisrael mmusua kure ngaa nemɔ yɔ ne ala.
