english_verse: You are a snake that bites the heel of a horse, making its rider fall.
translation_verse: Dan kɔyɛ atunu ewoo, na wayɛ atimbire so ɛbɔnaa, bɔ ɔkeka pɔngɔ gya ndii nu ɔ, maa pɔngɔhanɛniɛ ne ɔte tɔ ye si ɔ.

english_verse: Our Lord, I am waiting for you to save us.
translation_verse: Ao AWURADE, wɔ ngoalelɛ yeɛ menea ye ate ɔ.

english_verse: Gad, you will be attacked, then attack your attackers.
translation_verse: Apaabɔlɛfoɛ kure kohwi kɔfa Gade so, nakoso ɔkɔkakyi ye nwo kɔbɔ bɛ so apaa.

english_verse: Asher, you will eat food fancy enough for a king.
translation_verse: Asɛ aleɛ kɔyɛ bɔ ɔte aleɛ paa ɔ, na ɔkɔma mmenia sa kɔha aleɛ bɔ ɔfata ɛhene mɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Naphtali, you are a wild deer with lovely fawns.
translation_verse: Nafetali te wanzane beleɛ bɔ basangye ye ɔ, bɔ ofifi mmɛen nyemene ɔ.

english_verse: Joseph, you are a fruitful vine growing near a stream and climbing a wall.
translation_verse: Yosef te bakaa mmaen frɔmfrɔm bɔ osu ɔ, bakaa mmaen frɔmfrɔm bɔ osu ná opingye asue ti ɔ; ye mmaen bua kogua fasue so.

english_verse: Enemies attacked with arrows, refusing to show mercy.
translation_verse: Agyaentolɛfoɛ dwɔsole tiale ye serɛserɛ, bɛfale agyaen bɛneane ye so bɛtole, na bɛtanene ye nye paa;

english_verse: But you stood your ground, swiftly shooting back with the help of Jacob's God, the All-Powerful One— his name is the Shepherd, Israel's mighty rock.
translation_verse: nakoso wando ye agyaen ne, Ɔnate Yakob ye Tuminiɛ ne ye anwoserɛ ti, ye abasa nu kɔyɛ se. .

english_verse: Your help came from the God your father worshiped, from God All-Powerful. God will bless you with rain and streams from the earth; he will bless you with many descendants.
translation_verse: Wɔ baba ye Nyameɛ yeɛ ɔkɔboka wɔ ɔ, Ɛdangama Nyameɛ yeɛ okoyira wɔ ɔ, ɔkɔfa nyameɛso anwuro anwuro saleɛ yeɛ okoyira wɔ ɔ; aseɛ bo dɔ saleɛ buma bɔ ɔtrɛ ɔ, nyɔfone ne aworɛ nu saleɛ yeɛ ɔkɔfa koyira wɔ ɔ.

english_verse: My son, the blessings I give are better than the promise of ancient mountains or eternal hills. Joseph, I pray these blessings will come to you, because you are the leader of your brothers.
translation_verse: Saleɛ bɔ ofi ɛse berɛ ne, ɔtra saleɛ bɔ ofi mmokaa mbiri bɔ otimu berɛ daa nu ɔ. Ɔtra nningyein paa bɔ bɛwɔ daa tete mmokaa bɔ bɛwɔ berɛ afebɔɔ nu ɔ; ma sɔ saleɛ ne ɔ́bra Yosef so, ye bɔ baye ye basie ahameɛ bafi oliɛma nemɔ anu.

english_verse: Benjamin, you are a fierce wolf, destroying your enemies morning and evening.
translation_verse: Benyamin te pataku bɔ ɔkye ngaka di ɔ, ngyerɛmɔ odi naen bɔ ye sa kɔsɔ ye nu ɔ, na nɔsoa ɔkyekyɛ koɛ nu nzesadeɛ.”

english_verse: These are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is how Jacob gave each of them their proper blessings. Jacob's Death
translation_verse: Yisrael mmusua kure buru ne nyɔ nemɔ ɛne. Na mmerɛ bɔ né bɛ baba óyira bɛ ne, edwirɛ bɔ ɔha hyirele bɛ hɔ ɛne; ɔfale saleɛ bɔ ɔfata bɛ nu biala yirale ye.

english_verse: Both the cave and the land that goes with it were bought from the Hittites.
translation_verse: Aseɛ ne ɔne nu nyɔboɛ bɔ wasi sua ne, bɛtɔle befili Hitifoɛ sa nu.”

english_verse: When Jacob had finished giving these instructions to his sons, he lay down on his bed and died.
translation_verse: Na Yakob hane sɔ dwirɛ ne kitii hyirele ye mma nemɔ yiele ne, ɔpagyale ye gya guale mba ne aso, olele ye nwomeɛ bɔ ɔpɛ ye bo ɔ, na ɔhale nu.

english_verse: Joseph started crying, then leaned over to hug and kiss his father.
translation_verse: Yosef yakyili ye nwo tole ye baba so, ɔfele ye noa na osuni ye.

english_verse: When the time of mourning was over, Joseph said to the Egyptian leaders, “If you consider me your friend, please speak to the king for me.
translation_verse: Na ngyẽa bɔ bɛfa besuni ye ne pɛle nu ne, Yosef sele Faro mbanyi kyɛ, “Sɛ ɛmɔanya baboka me sɔa de a, ye de mesrɛ ɛmɔ, ɛ́mɔfa bɛto Faro nyunu bɛma me kyɛ,

english_verse: Just before my father died, he made me promise to bury him in his burial cave in Canaan. If the king will give me permission to go, I will come back here.”
translation_verse: me baba maa ndale ndaen na ɔhane kyɛ, ‘Mebaawu, na kosie me wɔ Kanaan aseɛ so, wɔ asieleɛ bɔ mbɛ ndole berɛ kyɛ besie me wɔ nu ne anu.’ Yiti mesrɛ wɔ, maa ngonzie me baba na nza mmra.”

english_verse: The king answered, “Go to Canaan and keep your promise to your father.”
translation_verse: Na Faro buale kyɛ, “Kɔ na kosie ɛse, kyɛbɔ ɔmaa ɛtale ndaen ne.”

english_verse: After crossing the Jordan River, Joseph stopped at Atad's threshing place, where they all mourned and wept seven days for Jacob.
translation_verse: Beedwuli nekaa bɔ bɛboro aburoo wɔ Atade bɔ ɔwɔ asue Yɔɔdan asi dɔ ne, bɛbɔle awuye serɛserɛ bɔ ɔyɛ aworabɔ paa ɔ; na Yosef yɔle ɔse sɛen ɛlɛsoo.

english_verse: The Canaanites saw this and said, “The Egyptians are in great sorrow.” Then they named the place “Egypt in Sorrow.”
translation_verse: Na Kanaanfoɛ bɔ bɛte aseɛ ne asofoɛ nwuni ɛsɛen bɔ né bɛyɔ wɔ nekaa bɔ bɛboro aburoo wɔ Atade nen, bɛhane kyɛ, “Misraimfoɛ ɛsɛen piri paa ɛhe!” Yiti bɛfrɛle berɛ Abel Misraim. Ɔwɔ Yɔɔdan asi dɔ.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons did just as their father had instructed.
translation_verse: Yiti Yakob mma mɔ yɔle kyɛbɔ ɔhyɛle bɛ ne ala mane ye;

english_verse: They took him to Mamre in Canaan and buried him in Machpelah Cave, the burial place Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite.
translation_verse: ofikyɛ ye mma nemɔ soale ye hɔle Kanaan aseɛ so, na besiele ye wɔ Makepɛla aseɛ so nyɔboɛ bɔ wasi sua nu wɔ Mamre eyia afiteleɛ. Abraham tɔle sɔ nyɔboɛ ne ɔne aseɛ ne fili Hitiniɛ Efron berɛ kyɛ ɔfa yɛ ye asieleɛ.

english_verse: After the funeral, Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else returned to Egypt. Joseph's Promise to His Brothers
translation_verse: Na Yosef siele ye baba yiele nen, ɔne oliɛma mmienzua nemɔ, yeɛ bɛ bɔ beesomane ye maa osiele ye baba ne amukoraa, besa bɛwale Misraim. Yosef sá hyɛ oliɛma mɔ bɔ

english_verse: After Jacob died, Joseph's brothers said to each other, “What if Joseph still hates us and wants to get even with us for all the cruel things we did to him?”
translation_verse: Na Yosef aliɛma nemɔ nwuni kyɛ bɛ baba awu ne, besusuli ye nwo kyɛ, “Anyɔ a, né Yosef atu ye nye wasie yɛ so na watua yɛ bɔne bɔ yayɔ ye ne amu so kerɛ.”

english_verse: So they sent this message to Joseph: Before our father died,
translation_verse: Yiti bɛmaa bɛɛhã behyirele Yosef kyɛ, “Wɔ baba hane sɔ dwirɛ ye kitii koraka yeɛ owu ɔ kyɛ,

english_verse: he told us, “You did some cruel and terrible things to Joseph, but you must ask him to forgive you.” Now we ask you to please forgive the terrible things we did. After all, we serve the same God that your father worshiped. When Joseph heard this, he started crying.
translation_verse: ‘Ɛ́mɔhã behyire Yosef kyɛ, mesrɛ wɔ, fa eliɛma mɔ amumuyɛɛ ne bɛ bɔne kyɛ bɛ, ofikyɛ bɛyɔle wɔ tɛɛ paa.’ Yiti afei, yɛsrɛ wɔ, fa wɔ baba ye Nyameɛ ngoaa mɔ b’amumuyɛɛ kyɛ bɛ.” Na bɛhane ɛhe behyirele Yosef ne, osuni.

english_verse: Right then, Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to the ground in front of him and said, “We are your slaves.”
translation_verse: Oliɛma nemɔ koso wale beebutubutuli ye nyunu na besele kyɛ, “Yɛte wɔ ngoaa.”

english_verse: But Joseph told them, “Don't be afraid! I have no right to change what God has decided.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yosef sele bɛ kyɛ, “Nnɛma ɛmɔsuro. Aso ngɔhora ngole Nyameɛ adwuma ngɔyɔ anaa?

english_verse: You tried to harm me, but God made it turn out for the best, so that he could save all these people, as he is now doing.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ de, ɛmɔambena me ne paa, nakoso Nyameɛ nhyehyɛleɛ maa ɔkakyili paa; kyɛ ɔnate so okole mmeni pee ngoa, kyɛbɔ afei wala ali ye.

english_verse: Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better. Joseph's Death
translation_verse: Yiti nnɛma ɛmɔsuro, na ngɔnea ɛmɔ ne ɛmɔ mma mɔ.” Yiti ɔkyekyele bɛ wora mane bɛ kunu tɔle bɛ fɔnwoo. Yosef wue

english_verse: Joseph lived in Egypt with his brothers until he died at the age of
translation_verse: Yosef ne ɔse awuro ama bɛtenane Misraim, na Yosef lili afoɛ ɛyaa ko ne buru.

english_verse: Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family.
translation_verse: Yosef nwuni Efraim ye nana nganzowa mɔ po, na bɛwole Manase awa Makyiri mma bɛtole Yosef gya so.

english_verse: Before Joseph died, he told his brothers, “I won't live much longer. But God will take care of you and lead you out of Egypt to the land he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yosef sele oliɛma nemɔ kyɛ, “Mebaawu, nakoso Nyameɛ kɔɔnea ɛmɔ. Na aseɛ bɔ ɔtale ye nwo ndaen hyirele Abraham ne Yisake ne Yakob ne, ɔkɔye ɛmɔ kofi aseɛ he aso ɔkɔfa ɛmɔ kɔhɔ so.”

english_verse: Now promise me that you will take my body with you when God leads you to that land.”
translation_verse: Yosef mane Yisrael mma nemɔ tale ndaen hyirele ye, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Nyameɛ kɔɔye ɛmɔ kofi wa. Na sɛ ɔba ye sɔ a, ɛ́mɔsoa me mmowue béfi wa bɛhɔ.”

english_verse: After Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else in that generation had died,
translation_verse: Afei Yosef wuli, na oliɛma nemɔ amukoraa ne sɔ aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ ne amukoraa bewuli.

english_verse: the people of Israel became so numerous that the whole region of Goshen was full of them.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yisrael boso ama nemɔ wowole, bɛ boso trɛle, na bɛ nwo yɛle se. Yiti beyili maen ne anu tɛkyɛ.

english_verse: Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt,
translation_verse: Na ɛhene foforɛ bie bɔ né ɔnze Yosef oolili Misraim bia ne.

english_verse: and he told the Egyptians: There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are.
translation_verse: Na osele ye mmenia nemɔ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔnea, Yisraelfoɛ nemɔ asone soma, na b’anwoserɛ bo yɛ so.

english_verse: If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔma yɛfa bɛ yɛfa nworɛ atee bie aso. Anyɔ a bɛkɔsone pee, na sɛ koɛ bie ba a, bɛkɔɔboka yɛ pɔfoɛ mɔ ná baho batia yɛ, ná banya atee banwati bafi maen ye anu.”

english_verse: The Egyptians put slave bosses in charge of the people of Israel and tried to wear them down with hard work. Those bosses forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses, where the king could store his supplies.
translation_verse: Yiti bɛyeyele adwumayɔlɛfoɛ so mbanyi maa belili bɛ so, kyɛ bɛhyɛ bɛ ma bɛyɔ adwuma bɔ ɔbo bɛ so ɔ. Na bɛkyekyele nguro Pitom ne Ramese maa Faro fa yɛle nekaa bɔ osie ye nningyein ɔ.

english_verse: But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before
translation_verse: Nakoso bɛwɔ so bɛ́hyɛ bɛ anyeborolɛ maa ɔbo so nen, bekye po yeɛ né bɛ́kɔ so bɛsone ná bɛtrɛ ɔ. Na Misraimfoɛ surole Yisraelfoɛ paa.

english_verse: and made them work so hard
translation_verse: Yiti bɛhyɛle Yisraelfoɛ anyeborolɛ maa bɛyɔle adwuma serɛ paa bɛmane bɛ.

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: Bɛmane bɛ wora bɔle, ofikyɛ bɛhyɛle bɛ maa bɛyɔle adwuma bɔ ɔbo bɛ so wɔ nnɛterɛ ne mmerekese pɛlɛ nu, fieso adwuma ahoroɔ nu; na bɛhyɛle bɛ anyeborolɛ paa wɔ adwuma biala nu.

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
translation_verse: Afei Misraim hene sele Hebri mmrasua bɔ bede aworɛ, bɔ bɛ nu ko li Sifra, ná ko wora li Pua ne kyɛ,

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: “Sɛ ɛmɔde Hebri mmrasua aworɛ, ná awoleɛ nu berɛ, ɛmɔnwu kyɛ adɔma ne te bienzua a, odi kyɛ ɛmɔku ye. Sɛ ɔte brasua de a, nnɛma ɛmɔku ye.”

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Nakoso né mmrasua bɔ bede aworɛ ne suro Nyameɛ, yiti banyɔ bɔ Misraim hene hyɛle bɛ kyɛ bɛyɔ ne, na mmom bɛmane mmienzua nemɔ nyane bɛ ti didili nu.

english_verse: The king called them in again and asked, “Why are you letting those baby boys live?”
translation_verse: Yiti Misraim hene frɛle mmrasua bɔ bede aworɛ ne, na obisale bɛ kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔayɔ sɔ ye, bɔ ɛmɔama mmienzua nemɔ anya bɛ ti badidi nu ye?”

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Na mmrasua bɔ bede aworɛ ne buale Faro kyɛ, “Hebri mmrasua nemɔ de, bɛtte kyɛ Misraim mmrasua nemɔ; ofikyɛ bɛ nwo te kyerekyerɛɛ, na bɛwo koraka né sona bɔ ode aworɛ ne adwu berɛ.”

english_verse: God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own. The Hebrews kept increasing
translation_verse: Na ɔnate kyɛ mmrasua bɔ bede aworɛ ne besuro Nyameɛ ne ati, ɔmaa bɛ koso bɛbɔle taen.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Na Faro hyɛle ye mmenia ne amukoraa kyɛ, “Bienzua biala bɔ Hebrifoɛ kɔwo ye ne, ɛ́mɔgyi ye bɛto asue Naele nu, nakoso brasua biala de, ɛ́mɔma onya ngoa.”

english_verse: A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe,
translation_verse: Biaa bie bɔ ofi Lewi abusua nu oogyale Lewi abusua nu braa.

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: Braa ne nwonzɛle, na ɔwole baa bienzua. Na onwuni kyɛ ye nwo yɛ nyemene nen, ɔfale ye feale toonn bosome nza.

english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Afei de, né ɔfa ye fea a ɔnyɛ yee ko, yiti ɔfale elemmire kɛndɛen, ɔfale pɔweɛ nzue ne ehwaa fale ye nwo, ɔfale adɔma ne tole nu, na ɔɔfale ye siele ngyɛngyɛma nu wɔ asue Naele noa.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Na adɔma n’aliɛma brasua oogyinane dedeede neane bɔ ɔkɔto adɔma ne ɔ.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: Faro awa brasua wale kyɛ ɔbaabia asue ne anu. Né ye abaawa nemɔ natenate asue ne noa. Onwuni kyɛ kɛndɛen ne gyi ngyɛngyɛma ne anu, na ɔsomane ye abaawa ne ko kyɛ ɔɔfa bra.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: Obukyele so nen, onwuni adɔma bienzua bɔ osũ ɔ. Ɔyɛle ye anwumvo, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Hebrifoɛ mma ne bie ɛne.”

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Na adɔma n’aliɛma brasua ne bisale Faro awa brasua ne kyɛ, “Ngɔmvrɛ Hebri mmrasua nemɔ ko mmrɛ wɔ ma ɔma adɔma ne nyɔfone ma wɔ anaa?”

english_verse: “Yes,” the king's daughter answered. So the girl brought the baby's mother,
translation_verse: Na Faro awa brasua ne buale ye kyɛ, “Yoo, kɔ.” Na abaayaa ne ɔɔfrɛle adɔma ne maame wale.

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Na Faro awa brasua ne sele ye kyɛ, “Fa adɔma ne kɔma ye nyɔfone ma me, na ngotua wɔ kerɛ.” Yiti braa ne fale ye hɔle ɔɔmane ye nyɔfone.

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: Akwadaa ne nyini, na ɔɔfale ye mane Faro awa brasua ne. Ɔfale ye yɛle ɔwa, na ɔtole ye dumaa Mose, ofikyɛ ɔhane kyɛ, “Nzue nu yeɛ nyele ye mvili ɔ.” Mose nwati kɔ Midian

english_verse: After Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were hard at work, and he saw an Egyptian beating one of them.
translation_verse: Mose nyini ne, ɛlɛho bie ɔɔpasale oliɛma mɔ Hebrifoɛ nwo, na onwuni adwuma serɛ bɔ né bɛ́hyɛ bɛ maa bɛyɔ ɔ. Na onwuni kyɛ Misraimniɛ bie ɔ́bo oliɛma Hebrifoɛ nemɔ anu ko ɔ.

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: Ɔtotole ye nye bra yiale, na onwuni kyɛ sona biala nne berɛ nen, ohuni Misraimniɛ ne, na ɔfale ye feale anweaa nu.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, ofitele, edwirɛ nwanwa, onwuni Hebrifoɛ nyɔ kyɛ bɛ́ko ɔ. Na obisale bɔ ye dwirɛ nyɛ fɛ ne kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛ́bo eliɛngo ɔ?”

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Na obuale kyɛ, “Nwa yeɛ ɔyɛle wɔ yɛ so panyi ne ndɛenbualɛniɛ ɔ? Ɛpena kyɛ eku me kyɛbɔ ehuni Misraimniɛ ne anaa?” Yiti edwirɛ ne mane Mose surole, na ɔhane ye ye ti anu kyɛ, “Eh, edwirɛ ne afite amba!”

english_verse: When the king heard what Moses had done, he wanted to kill him. But Moses escaped and went to the land of Midian. One day, when Moses was sitting by a well,
translation_verse: Na Faro tele sɔ dwirɛ nen, ɔyɛle kyɛ okohu Mose. Nakoso Mose nwatili Faro, na ɔɔtenane Midian maen nu wɔ abura bie anwo.

english_verse: the seven daughters of Jethro, the priest of Midian, came up to water their father's sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Né Midian sɔfo le mmaa mmrasua nzoo, na bɛwale berɛ kyɛ bɛbaato nzue begua nningyein bɔ bɛ baba nyɛmmoa no nu nzue ne anu.

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Mmoaenneafoɛ biemɔ wale bɛɛfoane bɛ, nakoso Mose dwɔsole, ohuru gyinane bɛ si, na ɔmane mmoaen nemɔ nzue.

english_verse: When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
translation_verse: Na besa bɛwale bɛ baba Rewel berɛ nen, obisale bɛ kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛnɛ de ɛmɔawa ndɛ sɔa ye?”

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Bebuale kyɛ, “Misraimniɛ bie lele yɛ fili mmoaenneafoɛ nemɔ sa nu, ɔtole nzue mane yɛ po, na ɔmane yɛ mmoaen nemɔ nzue.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Na obisale ye mma mmrasua nemɔ kyɛ, “Ɔwɔ nisua? Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔayakyi biaa ne dɔ ɔ? Ɛmɔɔfrɛ ye ma oodidi.”

english_verse: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.
translation_verse: Mose penene so ɔne biaa ne bɛtenane, na ɔfale ɔwa brasua Sipora mane Mose gyale.

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Sipora wole baa bienzua, na Mose tole ye dumaa Gɛsɔm, ɔnate kyɛ Mose hane kyɛ, “Maayɛ ɛwɔfoɛ wɔ amanvrafoɛ aseɛ so.”

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: Afoɛ pee pɛle nu, na Misraim hene wuli. Afei Yisraelfoɛ nwuni ngoaasolɛ nu amaneɛ piri paa; bɛbɔle awuye, na bɛ suɛ wɔ ngoaasolɛ nu ne dwuli Nyameɛ nyunu.

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Nyameɛ tele b’awuyebɔlɛ ne, na ɔkayele apam bɔ ɔne Abraham, Yisake ne Yakob bɛyɛle ne.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ neane Yisraelfoɛ nemɔ, na bɛyɛle ye anwumvo.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
translation_verse: Né Mose yeɛ ɔnea ye sia Yɛtro, bɔ ɔte Midian sɔfo ne mmoaen so ɔ. Ɛlɛho bie, ɔhane mmoaen ne hɔle dedeede wɔ ɛserɛ ne noa dɔ paa, na oodwuli Nyameɛ bokaa Horebo nye abo.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE abɔfo yele ye nwo ali hyirele ye wɔ ngyɛkyerɛ bie bɔ né ogye wuronyiwuronyi nu. Mose neane, edwirɛ nwanwa, onwuni kyɛ ngyɛkyerɛ ne ogye de, nakoso né ɔnyera.

english_verse: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
translation_verse: Na Mose hane kyɛ, “Edwirɛ nwanwa he de, mémakye mékɔ dɔ mekɔnea nikyee ti bɔ ɔmma ngyɛkyerɛ ne nyera ne.”

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE nwuni kyɛ wamakye wafa dɔ ɔkwaanea nen, ɔfrɛle ye fili ngyɛkyerɛ ne anu kyɛ, “Mose! Mose! Na osurole kyɛ, “Me ɛhe.”

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE hane kyɛ, “Nnɛpingye wa! Puropuro wɔ gya nu mbaboa ne, ofikyɛ nekaa bɔ egyi ne te aseɛ krongron.”

english_verse: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
translation_verse: Na ɔfa sɔle so kyɛ, “Me ole wɔ baba Nyameɛ ne, Abraham Nyameɛ ne, Yisake Nyameɛ ne Yakob Nyameɛ ne. Na Mose fale ye nyunu feale, ofikyɛ né osuro kyɛ ɔkɔnea Nyameɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE hane kyɛ, “Me mmenia bɔ bɛwɔ Misraim ne, manwu b’amaneɛnwunɛ ne, na mate awuye bɔ b’adwuma so mbanyi mɔ maa bɛbɔ ne. Manwu b’amaneɛnwunɛ ne.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Na madwu mawa ase kyɛ mebaale bɛ mefi Misraimfoɛ sa nu, ná meye bɛ mefi sɔ aseɛ ne aso mekɔ aseɛ paa bɔ ɔtrɛ ɔ so, aseɛ bɔ nyɔfonesue ne woɛ tengyɛ wɔ so ne: Kanaanfoɛ, Hitifoɛ, Amorifoɛ, Perisifoɛ, Hiwifoɛ ne Yebusifoɛ maen ne.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Afei de, awuye bɔ Yisraelfoɛ bɛbɔ ne wadwu me nyunu, na manwu ɛhyɛlɛ bɔ Misraimfoɛ bɛhyɛ bɛ ne.

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: Yiti bra. Mésoma wɔ maa ɛkɔ Faro berɛ ɛkɔye me mmenia Yisraelfoɛ efi Misraim!”

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Nakoso Mose bisale Nyameɛ kyɛ, “Me ole nwa bɔ mékɔ Faro berɛ mekɔye Yisraelfoɛ mefi Misraim ɔ?”

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ sele ye kyɛ, “Ngoli wɔ si. Na bɔ okohyire kyɛ me yeɛ mésoma wɔ ɛhe: sɛ ɛye maen ne fi Misraim ba a, sɔ bokaa he aso yeɛ ɛmɔkɔsɔne Nyameɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Na Mose bisale Nyameɛ kyɛ, “Sɛ mekɔ Yisraelfoɛ berɛ, ná mekã mekyire bɛ kyɛ, ‘Ɛmɔ nana mɔ Nyameɛ yeɛ wasoma me ɔ,’ ná bɛ wora bebisa me kyɛ, ‘Ye dumaa li sɛɛ’ a, nzikyɛ dwirɛ yeɛ nga ngyire bɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ sa sele Mose kyɛ, “Kã kyire Yisraelfoɛ kyɛ, ‘AWURADE ɛmɔ nana mɔ Nyameɛ ne, Abraham Nyameɛ ne, Yisake Nyameɛ ne, Yakob Nyameɛ ne yeɛ wasoma me ɛmɔ berɛ ɔ.’ Me dumaa bɔ ɔwɔ berɛ afebɔɔ hɔ ɛne, na ɛhe yeɛ aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ mukoraa bɛkɔfa bɛkɔfrɛ me ɔ.

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Kɔ! Kɔboaboa Yisrael mbanyi mɔ noa, ná kã kyire bɛ kyɛ, ‘AWURADE ɛmɔ nana mɔ Nyameɛ ne, Abraham Nyameɛ ne, Yisake Nyameɛ ne, Yakob Nyameɛ ne, waye ye nwo ali wahyire me. Ɔnwa: ‘Maanea ɛmɔ, na manwu nikyee bɔ bɛfa bɛyɔ ɛmɔ wɔ Misraim ne.

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Na mayɛ m’adwene kyɛ ngɔye ɛmɔ ngofi Misraim amaneɛnwunɛ nu, ná mafa ɛmɔ mahɔ Kanaanfoɛ, Hitifoɛ, Amorifoɛ, Perisifoɛ, Hiwifoɛ ne Yebusifoɛ aseɛ ne aso, aseɛ bɔ nyɔfonesue ne woɛ tengyɛ wɔ so ne.

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: “Bekotie wɔ dwirɛ, na ɛne Yisrael mbanyi bɛhɔ Misraim hene berɛ beese ye kyɛ, ‘AWURADE, Hebrifoɛ Nyameɛ ne, ɔne yɛ ayia. Yiti yɛsrɛ wɔ, ma yɛ ate ma yɛhɔ atee bɔ bɛfa ɛlɛsa bɛpɛ ɔ wɔ ɛserɛ so, ná yɛɛbɔ afɔleɛ yɛma AWURADE yɛ Nyameɛ ne.’

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: Me de, mese kyɛ Misraim hene ngɔma ɛmɔ ate ma ɛmɔngɔhɔ, sana tumi piri bie hyɛ ye so koraka.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: Yiti ngɔtengyɛ me sa ngɔfa anwanwadeɛ mukoraati bɔ ngɔyɔ ye Misraim ne ngotia Misraim, na ɛhe asi ne, ɔkɔma ɛmɔ kɔhɔ.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: Yisrael brasua biala kobisa ɛdwetɛ ne sikaa kɔkorɛ mbembenanneɛ ne ndena kofi Misraim brasua bɔ ɔne ye bɛte bepingye ɔ berɛ, ɔne Misraim brasua biala bɔ ɔte ye awuro ɔ berɛ, na ɛmɔkɔfa sɔ nningyein ne bekosiesie ɛmɔ mma mmienzua ne mmrasua mɔ nwo. Na ɛhe kɔmaa ɛmɔkonya koɛ nu nzesadeɛ bekofi Misraimfoɛ berɛ.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Na Mose buale kyɛ, “Sɛ banne me banni, anaakyɛ bandie me dwirɛ, ná bɛka kyɛ, ‘AWURADE anye ye nwo ali wangyire wɔ huu’ ɛ?’ ”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bisale ye kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ yeɛ otira wɔ sa nu ye?” Obuale kyɛ, “Pɔmaa ɔ.”

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele kyɛ, “Gyi to aseɛnwo berɛ!” Ogyi tole berɛ, na ɔkakyili ewoo. Na Mose pimbini ye si fili ye nwo.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Tengyɛ wɔ sa sɔ ye dua ne anu.” Ɔtengyɛle ye sa sɔle ye nu, na ɔkakyili pɔmaa wɔ ye sa nu.

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele kyɛ, “Ɛhe kɔmaa bekole bekoli kyɛ AWURADE, bɛ nana mɔ Nyameɛ ne, Abraham Nyameɛ ne, Yisake Nyameɛ ne, Yakob Nyameɛ ne yeɛ waye ye nwo ali wahyire wɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sá sele ye kyɛ, “Fa wɔ sa wura wɔ hue so.” Ɔfale ye sa wurale ye hue so, na ɔyele ye sa fili ye hue so nen, né kwata ayɛ ye sa ne amaa wayɛ fufue kyɛ asukɔtwea.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele ye kyɛ, “Fa wɔ sa wura wɔ hue so bieku.” Ɔfale ye sa wurale ye hue so bieku, na ɔyele ye sa ne fitele nen, né wasa wakakyi kyɛ ye nwonaen ngaa ne ala.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ banne sɔ nzɛngyerɛnneɛ nyɔ ne po banni, anaa bandie wɔ dwirɛ a, ye de sa asue Naele nzue ne bie, ná hwie gua aseɛ wosee so. Na Naele nu nzue bɔ ɛkɔsa ne kɔkakyi mogya wɔ aseɛ wosee ne aso.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Na Mose sele AWURADE kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, AWURADE. Ofi me tetetete bɔ ɔbaadwu ɛnɛ bɔ ɛne w’akoaa bedwudwo ye, nnde sona bɔ ye noa ate ɔ; me dwudwolɛ te nyaanyaa, na me temverema abutu.”

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bisale ye kyɛ, “Nwa yeɛ ɔyɔle kuro sona noa ɔ? Nwa yeɛ ɔmaa ɔyɛ emumu anaa asotiniwaaniɛ, ɔmaa onwu nikye anaa ɔyɛ ye anyesiniwaaniɛ ɔ? Yiti nna me AWURADE ɔ?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: Yiti kɔ, na ngɔma wɔ noa kɔte ná mahyire wɔ bɔ ɛha ɔ.”

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Mose sele kyɛ, “Yieee! AWURADE, mesrɛ wɔ ala, soma sona foforɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Afei AWURADE fɛle Mose so yaa maa ɔhane kyɛ, “Eliɛma Aarɔn, bɔ ɔte Lewiniɛ ne, ɔnne berɛ hɔ ɔ? Mese kyɛ ye noa ate. Tie, wasi nu ɔbaayia wɔ, na sɛ onwu wɔ a, ɔkɔyɛ ye fɛ soma.

english_verse: Aaron will speak to the people for you, and you will be like me, telling Aaron what to say. I will be with both of you as you speak, and I will tell each of you what to do.
translation_verse: Okogyina wɔ gya nu kodwudwo kohyire mmenia ne, wɔ noa dwirɛ kotua ye noa, ná wɔ wora ayɛ kyɛ Nyameɛ ama ye.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Fa pɔmaa he tira, na ye yeɛ ɛkɔfa kɔyɔ nzɛngyerɛnneɛ ɔ.” Mose sá kɔ Misraim

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Mose sá hɔle ye sia Yɛtro berɛ, na osele ye kyɛ; “Mesrɛ wɔ, maa nza ngɔ nniɛma mɔ berɛ wɔ Misraim, ná ngɔnea sɛ bɛtɛ te ase a.” Na Yɛtro sele Mose kyɛ, “Kɔ asomdwee nu oo.”

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose wɔ Midian kyɛ, “Sá kɔ Misraim, ofikyɛ bɛ bɔ né bɛpena wɔ beku wɔ ne, bɛ mukoraa bawu.”

english_verse: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
translation_verse: Yiti Mose fale ɔye ne ye mma mmienzua nyɔ ne tenatenane afunum so, na osa hɔle Misraim aseɛ so. Na ɔfale Nyameɛ pɔmaa ne tirale.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Sɛ esa kɔ Misraim a, nea kyɛ anwanwadeɛ mukoraa bɔ mama wɔ tumi kyɛ ɛyɔ ne, ɛkɔyɔ ye Faro nyunu. Nakoso ngɔma ye so kɔyɛ se, bɔ ɔnate so ɔngɔma me mmenia nemɔ ngɔhɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Afei ka kyire Faro kyɛ, ‘AWURADE nwa: Yisrael te me bamuɛbaa bienzua.

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: Na mekã mekyire wɔ kyɛ, “Ma mma ne ɔhɔ ɔɔsɔne me.” Na sɛ amma ye ate ma wangɔ a, ngohũ wɔ bamuɛbaa bienzua.’ ”

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: Na Mose sili nu ne, AWURADE yiale ye wɔ asikyeleɛ bie anu wɔ atunu, na ɔyɛle kyɛ okohu Mose.

english_verse: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Sipora fale twerɛboɛ bie pɛle ɔwa ne bienzua, ɔfa hane Mose gya, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Amba, ɔnate sɔ amaneɛ he aso, aayɛ me bɔbɔ deinn me busuaniɛ!”

english_verse: So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.” Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE yakyili ye. Na ɔnate bienzuapɛlɛ ne ati, Sipora sele kyɛ, “Ɛte mogya nu atɔmvorɛ biaa.”

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: AWURADE sele Aarɔn kyɛ, “Kɔ ɛserɛ so dɔ koyia Mose.” Yiti ɔhɔle, oyiale ye wɔ Nyameɛ bokaa ne anwo, na ɔfele ye noa.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Mose fale AWURADE dwirɛ bɔ wafa wasoma ye ne amukoraa, ɔne nzɛngyerɛnneɛ bɔ wahyɛ ye kyɛ ɔyɔ ne nwo amaneɛ bɔle Aarɔn.

english_verse: Later they brought together the leaders of Israel,
translation_verse: Afei Mose ne Aarɔn hɔle bɛɛboaboale Yisrael mbanyi mukoraa noa.

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: Aarɔn fale edwirɛ amukoraa bɔ Nyameɛ aha ahyire Mose ne tole dwaa, na ɔyɔle nzɛngyerɛnneɛ ne wɔ mmenia ne nyunu berɛ.

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: Mmenia ne le lili. Na bɛtele kyɛ AWURADE aapasa Yisraelfoɛ nwo, ná wanwu b’amaneɛnwunɛ nen, bɛbɔle bɛ ti ase bɛsɔnene ye.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: Nziɛ ye, Mose ne Aarɔn hɔle Faro berɛ beesele ye kyɛ, “AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa: ‘Ma me mmenia nemɔ bɛhɔ, ná beeli aluolue bɛma me wɔ ɛserɛ so.’ ”

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Nakoso Faro buale kyɛ, “AWURADE ne ole nwa bɔ ɔsɛ kyɛ metie ye ná mema Yisraelfoɛ bɛkɔ ɔ? Menze sɔ AWURADE ne, yeɛ Yisraelfoɛ koso mengɔma bɛngɔhɔ!”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Na besele kyɛ, “Hebrifoɛ Nyameɛ ne ɔne yɛ ayia, yiti yɛsrɛ wɔ, ma yɛ ate ma yɛhɔ atee bɔ bɛfa ɛlɛsa bɛpɛ ɔ wɔ ɛserɛ so, ná yɛɛbɔ afɔleɛ yɛma AWURADE yɛ Nyameɛ ne; na anyɔ a né wafa ewue anwonyerɛ anaa ngrandɛ wawa yɛ so.”

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: Na Faro sá sele kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔtie, afei bɔ maen ne anu mmenia asone pee ne yeɛ ɛmɔmaa bɛyakyi adwumayɔlɛ ɔ!”

english_verse: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne ala, Faro hyɛle maen adwumayɔlɛfoɛ mɔ so mbanyi, yeɛ adwumayɔlɛfoɛ mɔ so neafoɛ mɔ kyɛ,

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: “Nnɛmɔma mmenia nemɔ ɛserɛ ko maa bɛpɛ mmerekese kyɛbɔ daa ne ɛmɔyɔle ne, na mmom ɛ́mɔma bɛ bɔbɔ bɛɛpena ɛserɛ ne.

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: Mmerekese somaa bɔ né bɛpɛ ye daa ne, ɛ́mɔma bɛ́pɛ sɔ ala. Nnɛma ɛmɔte so, ofikyɛ bɛte foen, na ɛhe ati yeɛ ɔmaa besu kyɛ, ‘Maa yɛhɔ yɛɛbɔ afɔleɛ yɛma yɛ Nyameɛ ne.’

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔma mmenia nemɔ adwuma bɔ ɔyɛ se paa ma bɛyɔ, amaa bandie nnakannaka dwirɛ biala.

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Yiti maen adwumayɔlɛfoɛ mɔ so mbanyi, yeɛ adwumayɔlɛfoɛ mɔ so neafoɛ mɔ hɔle beesele mmenia ne kyɛ, “Faro nwa: ‘Mengɔma ɛmɔ ɛserɛ ko.’

english_verse: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ bɔbɔ bɛɛpena ɛserɛ wɔ nekaa biala bɔ ɛmɔkonya bie ɔ; nakoso ɛmɔ adwuma ne de, yɛngɔte so kaala.

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Adwumayɔlɛfoɛ so mbanyi nemɔ hane bɛ bo kyɛ, “Odi kyɛ ɛmɔyie ɛmɔ daa daa adwuma ne, kyɛbɔ ɛserɛ wɔ berɛ ne ɛmɔyɔle ne ala!”

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Bɛbole Yisrael mbanyi bɔ Faro adwumayɔlɛfoɛ mɔ so mbanyi afa adwuma ne awura bɛ sa ne, na bebisale bɛ kyɛ, “Mmerekese somaa bɔ ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛmɔpɛ ye anoma ne ɛnɛ ne, nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔambɛ ye mu, kyɛbɔ dáa ɛmɔpɛ ne?”

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Afei Yisrael mbanyi bɔ bafa adwuma ne bawura bɛ sa ne wale Faro berɛ beesuni behyirele ye kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛfa sɔ dwirɛ he di wɔ ngoaa ɔ?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: Bɛmma wɔ ngoaa ɛserɛ biala, nakoso bese yɛ kyɛ, ‘Ɛ́mɔpɛ mmerekese!’ Bɛbo wɔ ngoaa, nakoso mvomsoɛ ne fi wɔ mmenia ne.”

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Na Faro buale kyɛ, “Ɛmɔte foen, ɛmɔte foen soma! Sɔ ati yeɛ ɛmɔnwa: ‘Ma yɛ ate ma yɛɛbɔ afɔleɛ yɛma AWURADE’ ne.

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Ɛmɔhã bɛ nwo bɛɛyɔ adwuma! Bɛngɔma ɛmɔ ɛserɛ biala, nakoso mmerekese somaa bɔ ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛmɔpɛ ne ala yeɛ ɛmɔkɔpɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Yisrael mbanyi bɔ adwuma ne wura bɛ sa nwuni kyɛ edwirɛ ato bɛ, wɔ mmerɛ bɔ bɛha behyirele bɛ kyɛ, “Mmerekese somaa bɔ ɛlɛho biala ɛmɔpɛ ne, ɛmɔngɔte so.”

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Befili Faro berɛ bɛ́ba nen, bɛɛtole Mose ne Aarɔn kyɛ bɛnwondɛ bɛ.

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: Na besele bɛ kyɛ, “Nyameɛ ɔ́nea ɛmɔ na óbua ɛmɔ ndɛen, ofikyɛ ɛmɔamaa yayɛ tɛɛ wɔ Faro ne ye mbanyi nyunu, na ɛmɔafa ngrandɛ bawura bɛ sa nu kyɛ behũ yɛ.” Mose bɔ Nyameɛ somoɛ

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Afei Mose sá sele AWURADE kyɛ, “Oo AWURADE, nzu ati yeɛ ama edwirɛ sɔaa ato mmenia ye mɔ ɔ? Nzu ati yeɛ ɛsomane me ɔ?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Ofi mmerɛ bɔ mmale Faro berɛ, ná ndwudwole wɔ dumaa nu ɔ, ɛhalɛ alaa yeɛ ɔha mmenia ye mɔ ɔ, nakoso ɛyyɔle wɔ mmenia ye mɔ bɛ lelɛ nwo hwee.”

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE buale Mose kyɛ, “Afei de, ɛbaanwu nikyee bɔ ngɔfa ngɔyɔ Faro ɔ. Ofikyɛ, tumi piri kɔha ye kɔme asi maa ɔkɔyakyi bɛ maa bɛkɔhɔ; tumi piri kɔha ye kɔme asi maa ɔkɔfoa bɛ kofi ye aseɛ so.” Mose frɛlɛ nwo dwirɛ bieku

english_verse: My name is the Lord.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ sele Mose kyɛ, “Me ole AWURADE.

english_verse: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
translation_verse: Nyele me nwo ali ngyirele Abraham, Yisake ne Yakob kyɛ nde Tuminiɛ Nyameɛ. Nakoso me dumaa YAHWE ne de, mamma bangyina so bannwu me.

english_verse: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
translation_verse: Mene bɛ koso yɛyɛle m’apam, kyɛ ngɔfa Kanaan aseɛ bɔ bɛɛtenane so bɛyɛle ɛwɔfoɛ ne ngɔma bɛ.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: Asa koso, Yisraelfoɛ bɔ Misraimfoɛ afa bɛ ayɛ nganga ne, mate awuye bɔ bɛbɔ ne, na makaye m’apam ne.

english_verse: Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery.
translation_verse: Yiti ka kyire Yisraelfoɛ kyɛ, “Me ole AWURADE, na ngɔye ɛmɔ ngofi Misraim amaneɛnwunɛ nu, ná male ɛmɔ mafi bɛ ngoaasolɛ nu. Na ɔnate tumi asaa ne asohwenɛ mbiri mbiri so yeɛ ngɔfa ngole ɛmɔ ɔ.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Ngɔfa ɛmɔ ngɔyɛ me mmenia, ná me wora ngɔyɛ ɛmɔ Nyameɛ. Na ɛmɔkonwu ye kyɛ me ole AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ bɔ olele ɛmɔ fili Misraim amaneɛnwunɛ nu ne.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: Aseɛ bɔ mata ndaen kyɛ ngɔfa ngɔma Abraham, Yisake ne Yakob nen, ngɔfa ɛmɔ ngɔhɔ so. Ngɔfa ngɔma ɛmɔ maa ɔkɔyɛ ɛmɔ deɛ. Me ole AWURADE.’ ”

english_verse: When Moses told this to the Israelites, they were too discouraged and mistreated to believe him.
translation_verse: Mose hane sɔ dwirɛ ne hyirele Yisraelfoɛ nemɔ, nakoso ɔnate b’aba nu bɔ né wabu, ɔne ngoaasolɛ serɛserɛ bɔ né bɛwɔ nu ne ati, bandɛ ye so.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ,

english_verse: to demand that the king of Egypt let the Israelites leave.
translation_verse: “Kɔ, kɔha kyire Misraim hene Faro kyɛ ɔyakyi Yisraelfoɛ mɔ ma befi ye aseɛ so bɛhɔ.”

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Nakoso Mose buale AWURADE kyɛ, “Yisraelfoɛ po bandie me, ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ né Faro atie me, me bɔ me noa ɔttele ɔ?”

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
translation_verse: AWURADE ne Mose ne Aarɔn dwudwole, na ɔhyɛle bɛ kyɛ bɛɛhã sɔ dwirɛ ne behyire Yisraelfoɛ, ɔne Misraim hene Faro, ná bɛ́ye Yisraelfoɛ béfi Misraim aseɛ so.

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Mbanyi bɔ né bɛlela b’abusua nemɔ noa ɛhe: Yisrael bamuɛbaa Ruben ye mma mɔ: Hanoke, Palu, Hesron ne Karemi. Ruben abusua mɔ ɛne.

english_verse: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation_verse: Simeon mma mɔ: Yemuel, Yamin, Ohade, Yakin, Soha, yeɛ Sɔɔlo bɔ oni te Kanaanniɛ ne. Simeon abusua mɔ ɛne.

english_verse: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
translation_verse: Gɛsɔn mma mɔ ɛhe: Libini ne Simei, bɛ ne b’abusua mɔ.

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Merari mma mɔ ɛhe: Maheli ne Musi. Lewi abusua nemɔ, kyɛbɔ b’aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ te ɛne.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Yisare mma mɔ ɛhe: Kora, Nefege ne Sikri.

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Yusiɛl mma mɔ ɛhe: Misael, Elsafan ne Sitri.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Aarɔn gyale Aminadabo awa brasua Elihyeba bɔ oliɛma ole Nason ne. Na ɔne ye bɛwole Nadabo, Abihu, Eleasa ne Yitama.

english_verse: Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph.
translation_verse: Kora mma mɔ ɛhe: Asire, Ɛlkana ne Abiasafe. Kora abusua mɔ ɛne.

english_verse: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Aarɔn awa Eleasa gyale Putiel mma mmrasua nemɔ ko, na ɔne ye bɛwole Finehase. Lewi abusua kure ne, nu abusua mbanyi bɔ bɛlela ye noa ɛne.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
translation_verse: Aarɔn ne Mose ole mmenia bɔ AWURADE ha hyirele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔye Yisraelfoɛ béfi Misraim aseɛ so, kyɛbɔ bɛ kure kure si te ɔ.”

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: Mose ne Aarɔn komapɛ ne ala yeɛ bɛfa bɛtole Misraim hene Faro nyunu kyɛ ɔ́ma Yisraelfoɛ bétu béfi Misraim ɔ. Nyameɛ sá hyɛ Mose bɔ

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Kyẽa bɔ AWURADE ne Mose dwudwole wɔ Misraim aseɛ so ne,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Me ole AWURADE. Kã edwirɛ bɔ mekã mekyire wɔ ne amukoraa kyire Misraim hene Faro.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Mose buale AWURADE wɔ ye nyunu berɛ kyɛ, “Yieee! Me noa ɔttele, ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ né Faro atie me dwirɛ?”

english_verse: The Lord said: I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Tie, mayɛ wɔ kyɛ Nyameɛ wɔ Faro nye so, na eliɛma Aarɔn kɔyɛ wɔ ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ.

english_verse: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
translation_verse: Ka bɔ mahyɛ wɔ kyɛ ɛha ne amukoraati; na eliɛma Aarɔn kɔha kohyire Faro kyɛ ɔyakyi Yisraelfoɛ ate ma befi ye aseɛ so bɛhɔ.

english_verse: But I will make the king so stubborn that he won't listen to you. He won't listen even when I do many terrible things to him and his nation. Then I will bring a final punishment on Egypt, and the king will let Israel's families and tribes go.
translation_verse: nakoso Faro ngɔtɛ ɛmɔ so. Ngɔfa me tumi ngɔhwe Misraim so, na ngɔfa asohwenɛ piri so ngɔye me lɔen, me mmenia Yisraelfoɛ, ngofi Misraim aseɛ so.

english_verse: When this happens, the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Na sɛ metengyɛ me sa wɔ Misraim so, ná meye Yisraelfoɛ mefi bɛ nu a, Misraimfoɛ konwu kyɛ me ole AWURADE.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
translation_verse: “Sɛ Faro ka kyire ɛmɔ kyɛ, ‘Ɛ́mɔyɔ sɛngyerɛnneɛ bie behyire a, ye de ka kyire Aarɔn kyɛ, ‘Gyi wɔ pɔmaa ne to Faro nyunu berɛ ma ɔkakyi ewoo.’ ”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: Yiti Mose ne Aarɔn hɔle Faro berɛ bɛɛyɔle kyɛbɔ AWURADE hyɛle bɛ ne. Aarɔn gyili ye pɔmaa ne tole Faro ne ye mbanyi mɔ nyunu berɛ, na ɔkakyili ewoo.

english_verse: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
translation_verse: Faro koso frɛfrɛle mmenia bɔ bɛse ase, ɔne musueyelɛfoɛ maa bɛwale, na sɔ Misraim ngonyaayelɛfoɛ nemɔ koso yele ngonyaa yɔle sɔ ala.

english_verse: they threw down sticks that turned into snakes. But Aaron's snake swallowed theirs.
translation_verse: Bɛ mukoraa begyili bɛ mbɔmaa nemɔ beguale aseɛnwo berɛ, na bɛkakyilikakyili ewoo mɔ. Nakoso Aarɔn pɔmaa ne memene bɛ mbɔmaa nemɔ.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Bekye po yeɛ Faro bubuli mmakaa tuale ye so ɔ, na wandɛ bɛ so, kyɛbɔ AWURADE hane ne ala. Nzue kakyi mogya

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Afei AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Faro abubu mmakaa watua ye so, na ɔngɔpene ma mmenia ne ngɔhɔ.

english_verse: Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king.
translation_verse: Kɔ Faro berɛ ngyerɛmɔ, mmerɛ bɔ ófite kɔ asue Naele noa ɔ. Kogyina asue ne noa berɛ nwondɛ ye, ná fa wɔ pɔmaa bɔ ɔkakyili ewoo ne tira.

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: Na ka kyire ye kyɛ, AWURADE, Hebrifoɛ Nyameɛ ne asoma me kyɛ mmanga ngyire wɔ kyɛ, ‘Ma me mmenia nemɔ bɛhɔ bɛɛsɔne me wɔ ɛserɛ so, nakoso abubu mmakaa atua wɔ so maa waadwu bekye.’

english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: AWURADE nwa nyoo, ‘Bɔ ɔkɔmaa ekonwu ye kyɛ nde AWURADE ɛhe: Tie, ngɔfa pɔmaa bɔ otira me sa nu ne ngofĩ asue Naele nu, na nzue ne kɔkakyi mogya.

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Naen bɔ bɛwɔ asue Naele nu kowuwu, nzue ne kɔbo mvamva, na Misraimfoɛ ngɔhora ngɔno Naele nzue.’ ”

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Ka kyire Aarɔn kyɛ, ‘Fa wɔ pɔmaa ne, ná tengyɛ wɔ sa wɔ Misraim nzue mɔ so: b’asue mbiri mɔ, Naele sa mɔ, b’abura mɔ ne b’ɛkwaa mukoraa so ma bɛkakyi mogya. Misraim aseɛ ne aso mukoraa kɔyɛ mogya, bua ne angora mɔ anu po.’ ”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
translation_verse: Mose ne Aarɔn yɔle kyɛbɔ AWURADE hyɛle bɛ ne ala. Aarɔn mane ye pɔmaa ne aso hɔle anwuro wɔ Faro ne ye mbanyi mɔ nyunu berɛ, ɔfa fini asue Naele nu, na Naele nzue amukoraa kakyili mogya.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Nzue ne anu naen wuwuli, na Naele nzue bone mvamvamvamva bɔ Misraimfoɛ angora bie no ɔ. Na Misraim aseɛ ne aso amukoraa yɛle mogya.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Nakoso Misraim ngonyaayelɛfoɛ koso yele ngonyaa yɔle sɔ ala. Yiti Faro bubuli mmakaa tuale ye so, na wandɛ bɛ so, kyɛbɔ AWURADE hane ne ala.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: Faro sá hɔle ye awuro, na wamva ɛhe po wanyɛ dwirɛ.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Na Misraimfoɛ amukoraa tutuli abura wɔ asue Naele noa bɛpenane nzue bɔ bɛkɔno ɔ, ofikyɛ bangora Naele nzue no.

english_verse: Seven days after the Lord had struck the Nile,
translation_verse: AWURADE sɛkyele asue Naele nen, ngyẽa ɛlɛsoo pɛle nu.

english_verse: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Kɔ Faro berɛ kose ye kyɛ, ‘AWURADE nwa nyoo: Ma me mmenia nemɔ ate ma bɛhɔ, ná bɛɛsɔne me.

english_verse: If he refuses, I will cover his entire country with frogs.
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ amma bɛ ate ma bangɔ a, ngɔma mborohyɛen kɔto kɔpete maen ne anu amukoraa.

english_verse: Warn the king that the Nile will be full of frogs, and from there they will spread into the royal palace, including the king's bedroom and even his bed. Frogs will enter the homes of his officials and will find their way into ovens and into the bowls of bread dough.
translation_verse: Mborohyɛen koyi asue Naele nu to, bekofi nu bɛkɔwa w’awuro, bɛkɔwa wɔ sua nu ne wɔ bɛen so, wɔ mbanyi mɔ ne wɔ mmenia awuro, wɔ bokyea mɔ ne wɔ ngukue mɔ nu.

english_verse: Frogs will be crawling on everyone—the king, his officials, and every citizen of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na mborohyɛen nemɔ kɔwa wɔ so, wɔ mmenia ne wɔ mbanyi mukoraa so.’ ”

english_verse: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Ka kyire Aarɔn kyɛ, ‘Tengyɛ wɔ sa, ná fa wɔ pɔmaa ne kyire asue mbiri mɔ so, asue Naele sa mɔ so, ɔne ɛkwaa mɔ so, ná ma mborohyɛen yɛ Misraim aseɛ so amukoraa manyamanya!’ ”

english_verse: But the magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing.
translation_verse: Nakoso Misraim ngonyaayelɛfoɛ koso yele ngonyaa yɔle sɔ ala, na bɛmane mborohyɛen wale Misraim aseɛ so.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Afei Faro frɛle Mose ne Aarɔn sele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔserɛ AWURADE bɛma ɔye mborohyɛen nemɔ ofi me ne me mmenia so, na ngɔma Yisraelfoɛ kɔhɔ ná baabɔ afɔleɛ bama AWURADE.”

english_verse: “All right,” Moses answered. “You choose the time when I am to pray for the frogs to stop bothering you, your officials, and your people, and for them to leave your houses and be found only in the river.”
translation_verse: Na Mose sele Faro kyɛ, “Wɔ adaworoma, maa nwu mmerɛ horɛ bɔ nzrɛ ma wɔ, ɛne wɔ mbanyi mɔ ne wɔ mmenia, kyɛbɔ ɔkɔyɛ ná mborohyɛen nemɔ awuwu afi wɔ ne w’awuro mɔ so ɔ; asue Naele nu deɛ angome yeɛ ɔkɔha ɔ.”

english_verse: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
translation_verse: Na obuale kyɛ, “Ɛhema.” Na Mose koso hane kyɛ, “Ɔ́yɛ sɔ ala, kyɛbɔ aha ne, amaa ɔnate so anwu ye kyɛ ebiala nne berɛ bɔ ɔte kyɛ AWURADE yɛ Nyameɛ ne ɔ.

english_verse: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
translation_verse: Yiti Mose ne Aarɔn fili Faro nyunu berɛ bɛhɔle. Na Mose srɛle AWURADE fale mborohyɛen bɔ wafa wawa Faro so ne nwo dwirɛ tole ye nyunu.

english_verse: The Lord listened to Moses, and the frogs died everywhere—in houses, yards, and fields.
translation_verse: AWURADE yɔle bɔ Mose srɛle ye ne; mborohyɛen nemɔ wuwuli wɔ awuro nemɔ anu, aluo ne fieso.

english_verse: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
translation_verse: Bɛboaboale bɛ noa kure kure, na maen ne anu bone mvamvamvamva.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
translation_verse: Faro nwuni kyɛ bɛ nwo atɔ bɛ kãa, yiti obubuli mmakaa tuale ye so, na wandɛ bɛ so, kyɛbɔ AWURADE hane ne ala. Mvuture kakyi ngondia

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Ka kyire Aarɔn kyɛ, ‘Tengyɛ wɔ pɔmaa ne, ná fa fĩ aseɛnwo mvuture nu ma ɔkakyi ngondia wɔ Misraim aseɛ so amukoraa.’ ”

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
translation_verse: Bɛyɔle sɔ. Aarɔn tengyɛle ye sa nu fale pɔmaa ne fini aseɛnwo mvuture nu, na ngondia te guale mmenia ne ngaka so. Na aseɛnwo mvuture amukoraa bɔ ɔwɔ Misraim kakyili ngondia.

english_verse: When the magicians tried to use their secret powers to do this, they failed, and gnats stayed on people and animals.
translation_verse: Ngonyaayelɛfoɛ nemɔ bɔle mmɔden kyɛ bɛkɔma ngondia kɔwa ɔ, nakoso bangora. Yiti ngondia kekale mmenia ne ngaka.

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Na ngonyaayelɛfoɛ nemɔ sele Faro kyɛ, “Ɛhe de, Nyameɛ sa wɔ nu! Nakoso Faro bubuli mmakaa tuale ye so, na wandɛ bɛ so, kyɛbɔ AWURADE hane ne ala. Nwɔsea pembepembe

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Dwɔso ngyerɛmɔ tutuutu kɔ Faro berɛ, wɔ mmerɛ bɔ ófite kɔ nzue ne anu ɔ, ná ka kyire ye kyɛ, ‘AWURADE nwa nyoo: Ma me mmenia nemɔ ate ma bɛhɔ, ná bɛɛso me.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
translation_verse: Na sɛ amma me mmenia nemɔ ate ma bangɔ a, ngɔsoma nwɔsea pembepembe paa maa bɛkɔwa wɔ ne wɔ mbanyi ne wɔ mmenia so, ɔne w’awuro mɔ nu. Nwɔsea koyi Misraimfoɛ awuro mɔ nu tɛkyɛ, ɔne aseɛ bɔ bɛ gya gyi so ne po.

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: AWURADE yɔle sɔ koso amba. Nwɔsea pembepembe paa wale beeyili Faro awuro ne ye mbanyi mɔ awuro tɛkyɛ. Na nwɔsea lele Misraim aseɛ ne aso amukoraa fale.

english_verse: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Afei Faro frɛle Mose ne Aarɔn, na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhɔ bɛɛbɔ afɔleɛ bɛma ɛmɔ Nyameɛ ne wɔ maen he anu ala.”

english_verse: “That's impossible!” Moses replied. “Any sacrifices we offer to the Lord our God would disgust the Egyptians, and they would stone us to death.
translation_verse: Na Mose buale kyɛ, “Ɔtte mayee kyɛ yɛkɔyɔ sɔ ɔ; ofikyɛ afɔleɛ bɔ yɛkɔbɔ kɔma AWURADE yɛ Nyameɛ nen, Misraimfoɛ bekyi. Na sɛ yɛfa nningyein bɔ Misraimfoɛ bekyi yɛbɔ afɔleɛ wɔ bɛ nyunu wa a, aso bɛngɔboro yɛ nyɔboɛ?

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: Ɔsɛ kyɛ yɛpɛ atee bɔ bɛfa ɛlɛsa bɛpɛ ɔ wɔ ɛserɛ so yɛkɔbɔ afɔleɛ yɛma AWURADE yɛ Nyameɛ ne, kyɛbɔ wahyɛ yɛ ne ala.”

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Na Faro sele kyɛ, “Ngɔmaa ɛmɔkɔɔbɔ afɔleɛ bɛkɔma AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ ne wɔ ɛserɛ so, nakoso nnɛma ɛmɔkɔ dedeede. Ɛ́mɔli me ti dwirɛ bɛma me.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Moses replied, “I'll pray for you as soon as I leave, and by tomorrow the flies will stop bothering you, your officials, and the citizens of your country. Only make sure that you're telling the truth this time and that you really intend to let our people offer sacrifices to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na Mose buale kyɛ, “Mefi wɔ wa mekɔ ala a, ngɔsrɛ AWURADE. Na nwɔsea pembepembe paa ne kofi Faro ne ye mbanyi ne ye mmenia so kɔhɔ ɛhema. Nakoso nnɛma Faro yɛ nnakannaka ko kyɛ ɔngɔma mmenia ne ngɔɔbɔ afɔleɛ ngɔma AWURADE.”

english_verse: After leaving the palace, Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Yiti Mose fili Faro nwo berɛ hɔle ɔɔsrɛle AWURADE.

english_verse: and the Lord answered his prayer. Not a fly was left to pester the king, his officials, or anyone else in Egypt.
translation_verse: AWURADE yɔle bɔ Mose srɛle ye ne. Ɔmane nwɔsea pembepembe paa ne fili Faro ne ye mbanyi ne ye mmenia so hɔle, bɔ ko po anga berɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But the king turned stubborn again and would not let the people go.
translation_verse: Nakoso Faro sá bubuli mmakaa tuale ye so sɔ mmerɛ ne, na wamma mmenia ne ate ma bangɔ.

english_verse: The Lord sent Moses with this message for the king of Egypt: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Afei AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Kɔ Faro berɛ kose ye kyɛ, ‘AWURADE, Hebrifoɛ Nyameɛ ne nwa nyoo: Ma me mmenia nemɔ ate ma bɛhɔ, ná bɛɛsɔne me.

english_verse: he will bring a terrible disease on your horses and donkeys, your camels and cattle, and your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: AWURADE tumi kɔma ngaka wue bɔ ye noa yɛ hye kɔha wɔ ngaka bɔ bahɔ adidie ɔ, wɔ mbɔngɔ mɔ, afunum mɔ, afupɔngɔ mɔ ne wɔ nyɛmmoa mɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord will protect the animals that belong to the people of Israel, and none of theirs will die.
translation_verse: Nakoso AWURADE kɔfa ɛwɛen kɔto Yisrael ngaka ne Misraim ngaka b’afia, amaa ɔnate so Yisraelfoɛ ngaka nemɔ nu biala anwu.’ ”

english_verse: Tomorrow is the day the Lord has set to do this.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE hyɛle kyẽa kyɛ, “Ɛhema yeɛ AWURADE kɔyɔ sɔ nikyee ne wɔ aseɛ ne aso ɔ.”

english_verse: It happened the next day—all of the animals belonging to the Egyptians died, but the Israelites did not lose even one.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, AWURADE yɔle sɔ ala. Misraimfoɛ nyɛmmoa mukoraa wuwuli, nakoso Yisraelfoɛ nyɛmmoa de, ko po anwu.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take a few handfuls of ashes from a stove and you, Moses, throw them into the air. Be sure the king is watching.
translation_verse: AWURADE sele Mose ne Aarɔn kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔfura foonoo nu nzoen bɛ sa bum ngoko, ná ma Mose ɔ́to hɔ anwuro wɔ Faro nyunu.

english_verse: The ashes will blow across the land of Egypt, causing sores to break out on people and animals.
translation_verse: Ɔkɔkakyi mvuture muhumuhu kotu kɔfa Misraim aseɛ so amukoraa; na ɔkɔkakyi mbɔmbɔ kotutu mmenia ne ngaka nwo ngena wɔ Misraim aseɛ so amukoraa.”

english_verse: So they took a few handfuls of ashes and went to the king. Moses threw them into the air, and sores immediately broke out on the Egyptians and their animals.
translation_verse: Yiti befurale foonoo nu nzoen, beegyinane Faro nyunu, Mose to hɔle anwuro, na ɔkakyili mbɔmbɔ tutuli mmenia ne ngaka nwo ngena.

english_verse: The magicians were suffering so much from the sores, that they could not even come to Moses.
translation_verse: Ɔnate mbɔmbɔ ne ati, ngonyaayelɛfoɛ nemɔ angora Mose nyunu gyina, ofikyɛ né mbɔmbɔ abobɔ ngonyaayelɛfoɛ nemɔ ne Misraimfoɛ amukoraa.

english_verse: Everything happened just as the Lord had told Moses—he made the king too stubborn to listen to Moses and Aaron. Hailstones
translation_verse: Nakoso AWURADE mane Faro bubuli mmakaa tuale ye so, na wandɛ bɛ so, kyɛbɔ AWURADE ha hyirele Mose ne ala. Asukɔtwea nyɔboɛ

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to get up early the next morning and say to the king: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him!
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Pɛ aleɛ dwɔso ná kɔ Faro berɛ kose ye kyɛ, ‘AWURADE, Hebrifoɛ Nyameɛ ne nwa nyoo: Ma me mmenia nemɔ ate ma bɛhɔ, na bɛɛsɔne me.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send his worst plagues to strike you, your officials, and everyone else in your country. Then you will find out that no one can oppose the Lord.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ afei de, mebaama me hawo amukoraa ba wɔ bɔbɔ wɔ so, wɔ somvoɛ mɔ ne wɔ maen so, amaa ɔnate so anwu ye kyɛ ebiala nne berɛ bɔ ɔte kyɛ me ɔ wɔ aseɛ so amukoraa.

english_verse: In fact, he could already have sent a terrible disease and wiped you from the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Na sɛ matengyɛ me sa mama ewue anwonyerɛ abɔ wɔ ne wɔ mmenia a, ahaa bekye awu afi aseɛ ye aso.

english_verse: But he has kept you alive, just to show you his power and to bring honor to himself everywhere in the world.
translation_verse: Nakoso mamaa anya wɔ ti adidi nu, kyɛ ngɔye me tumi ali ngohyire wɔ ɔ, amaa ɔnate so me dumaa atrɛ ahɔ aseɛ ye aso amukoraa.

english_verse: You are still determined not to let the Lord's people go.
translation_verse: Nakoso bekye po yeɛ adwɔso atia me mmenia, bɔ ɛngɔma bɛngɔhɔ ɔ.

english_verse: All right. At this time tomorrow, he will bring on Egypt the worst hailstorm in its history.
translation_verse: Tie, ɛhema bekye sɔa ala, ngɔma asukɔtwea nyɔboɛ kɔtete kogua, bɔ ye sɛso ɔwwale Misraim le fite mmerɛ bɔ bɛkyekyele maen ne bɔ ɔbaadwu ɛnɛ ɔ.

english_verse: You had better give orders for every person and every animal in Egypt to take shelter. If they don't, they will die.
translation_verse: Yiti ma wɔ nyɛmmoa ne wɔ nikyee biala bɔ ɔwɔ buro bɛbra awuro bɛɛbɔ bɛ nwo waen, ofikyɛ asukɔtwea nyɔboɛ ne kɔtɔ kogua sona ne kaka bɔ ɔwɔ buro, bɔ wamma awuro so, na bekowuwu.’ ”

english_verse: Some of the king's officials were frightened by what the Lord had said, and they hurried off to make sure their slaves and animals were safe.
translation_verse: Na Faro mbanyi nemɔ nu biala bɔ osuro AWURADE dwirɛ nen, ɔmane ye ngoaa ne ye nyɛmmoa nwatili wale awuro.

english_verse: But others paid no attention to his threats and left their slaves and animals out in the open.
translation_verse: Nakoso bɛ nu biemɔ bɔ bemmu AWURADE dwirɛ ne de, bɛyakyili bɛ ngoaa ne bɛ nyɛmmoa mɔ wɔ eburo.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, so that hailstones will fall on people, animals, and crops in the land of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Tengyɛ wɔ sa fa kyire anwuro ma asukɔtwea nyɔboɛ tɔ gua Misraim aseɛ so amukoraa, ma ogua sona ne ngaka ne eburo mmakaa mukoraa so wɔ Misraim aseɛ so.”

english_verse: Moses pointed his walking stick toward the sky, and hailstones started falling everywhere. Thunder roared, and lightning flashed back and forth, striking the ground. This was the worst storm in the history of Egypt.
translation_verse: Asukɔtwea nyɔboɛ ne agralaa bɔ ɔ́tete see yerɛmyerɛm lili afra. Na kyɛbɔ ye suronyi si te ne, ofite kyɛ Misraim yɛle maen ɔ, ye sɛso ɔwwale Misraim aseɛ ne amukoraa so le.

english_verse: People, animals, and crops were pounded by the hailstones, and bark was stripped from trees.
translation_verse: Asukɔtwea nyɔboɛ ne sɛkyele nikyee biala bɔ ɔwɔ buro wɔ Misraim aseɛ so amukoraa, fite mmenia so kodwu ngaka so; ɔsɛkyele eburo nningyein amukoraati, na ɔpombale eburo mmakaa mukoraati.

english_verse: Only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was safe from the storm.
translation_verse: Sana Gosen aseɛ so, nekaa bɔ né Yisraelfoɛ te ne, yeɛ asukɔtwea nyɔboɛ ne bie andɔ berɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Now I have really sinned! My people and I are guilty, and the Lord is right.
translation_verse: Afei Faro somane maa bɛɛfrɛle Mose ne Aarɔn bɛwale, na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛhe de, mayɛ bɔne, AWURADE di be, na me ne me mmenia mukoraa yɛdi fɔ.

english_verse: We can't stand any more of this thunder and hail. Please ask the Lord to make it stop. Your people can go—you don't have to stay in Egypt any longer.”
translation_verse: Yiti ɛ́mɔsrɛ AWURADE bɛma ɔyakyi, ofikyɛ agralaa ne asukɔtwea nyɔboɛ sɔa de, ɔbo yɛ so. Ngɔma ɛmɔ kɔhɔ, na ɛmɔngɔtena wa ko.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my arms in prayer. When the thunder and hail stop, you will know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Mose sele ye kyɛ, “Sɛ mefi kuro ye anu mefite pɛ a, ngɔtrɛ me sa nu ngɔsrɛ AWURADE, na agralaa ne kɔyakyi, yeɛ asukɔtwea nyɔboɛ ne koso ngɔte ngogua ko, amaa ɔnate so anwu ye kyɛ aseɛ ye te AWURADE deɛ.

english_verse: But I am certain that neither you nor your officials really fear the Lord God.”
translation_verse: Nakoso ɛne wɔ mbanyi mɔ de, mese kyɛ ɛmɔnnya bessurole AWURADE Nyameɛ.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the flax and barley crops had been destroyed by the storm because they were ready to ripen.
translation_verse: (Gyese ne ayuo sɛkyele, ofikyɛ né ayuo afa mmaa, yeɛ né gyese koso abɔ nyerɛen.

english_verse: But the wheat crops ripen later, and they were not damaged.
translation_verse: Nakoso ɛmo ahoroɔ mɔ bɔ bannua bɛ ndɛ ne de, banzɛkye.)

english_verse: After Moses left the royal palace and the city, he lifted his arms in prayer to the Lord, and the thunder, hail, and drenching rain stopped.
translation_verse: Mose fili Faro awuro berɛ, ofili kuro ne anu, ɔtrɛle ye sa nu srɛle AWURADE, na agralaa ne asukɔtwea nyɔboɛ ne yakyili, na esue ne andɔ angua aseɛ ne aso ko.

english_verse: When the king realized that the storm was over, he disobeyed once more. He and his officials were so stubborn
translation_verse: Nakoso Faro nwuni kyɛ esue ne asukɔtwea nyɔboɛ ne agralaa ne ayakyi nen, ɔhɔle so yɔle bɔne, na ɔne ye mbanyi mɔ bebubuli mmakaa betuatuale bɛ so.

english_verse: that he refused to let the Israelites go. This was exactly what the Lord had said would happen.
translation_verse: Yiti Faro bubuli mmakaa tuale ye so, na wamma Yisraelfoɛ nemɔ ate maa bangɔ, kyɛbɔ AWURADE nate Mose so hane ne ala.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Go back to the king. I have made him and his officials stubborn, so that I could work these miracles.
translation_verse: Afei AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Kɔ Faro berɛ, ofikyɛ me yeɛ mamaa ɔne ye mbanyi mɔ babubu mmakaa batuatua bɛ so ɔ, amaa ɔnate so mala me nzɛngyerɛnneɛ hemɔ ali wɔ bɛ berɛ.

english_verse: I did this because I want you to tell your children and your grandchildren about my miracles and about my harsh treatment of the Egyptians. Then all of you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Na ɔnate so ɛkɔha kyɛbɔ masi magoro Misraimfoɛ nwo, ɔne nzɛngyerɛnneɛ bɔ mayɔ ye bɛ berɛ kohyire ɛwa ne w’anomaa. Na ɛhe kɔmaa ekonwu ye kyɛ me ole AWURADE.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and told him that the Lord God of the Hebrews had said: How long will you stubbornly refuse to obey? Release my people so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Yiti Mose ne Aarɔn bɛhɔle Faro berɛ beesele ye kyɛ, “AWURADE, Hebrifoɛ Nyameɛ ne nwa nyoo, ‘Ɛkɔpo kyɛ ɛkɔbrɛ wɔ nwo ase wɔ me nyunu maa okoodwu kyinzu? Ma me mmenia nemɔ ate ma bɛhɔ, ná bɛɛsɔne me.

english_verse: Do this by tomorrow, or I will cover your country with so many locusts
translation_verse: Na sɛ ampene amma me mmenia nemɔ angɔ a, ɛhema ngɔma mmɛbɛ kɔwa wɔ maen ye anu,

english_verse: that you won't be able to see the ground. Most of your crops were ruined by the hailstones, but these locusts will destroy what little is left, including the trees.
translation_verse: na bekoyi bɛkɔfa aseɛ ne, bɔ sona biala ngonwu aseɛ ne ɔ. Na nikyee biala bɔ ɔhale berɛ mane ɛmɔ, bɔ asukɔtwea nyɔboɛ ne anzɛkye ye ne, bekoli; yeɛ ɛmɔ mmakaa mukoraa bɔ begyigyi buro koso, bekoli.

english_verse: Your palace, the homes of your officials, and all the other houses in Egypt will overflow with more locusts than have ever been seen in this country. After Moses left the palace,
translation_verse: Bekoyi w’awuro mɔ nu tɛkyɛ, wɔ mbanyi mɔ awuro amukoraa, ɔne Misraimfoɛ awuro amukoraa nu tɛkyɛ; bɔ wɔ baba mɔ ne wɔ nana mɔ bennwuni bie le, fite kyɛ bɛwale aseɛ ye aso bɔ ɔbaadwu ɛnɛ ɔ.’ ” Afei ɔkakyili ye nwo yakyili Faro berɛ hɔle.

english_verse: the king's officials asked, “Your Majesty, how much longer is this man going to be a troublemaker? Why don't you let the people leave, so they can worship the Lord their God? Don't you know that Egypt is a disaster?”
translation_verse: Na Faro mbanyi mɔ sele ye kyɛ, “Kyinzu koraa yeɛ biaa he kosua yɛ ngaen maa ɔkɔɔpem ɔ? Ma mmienzua ne bɛhɔ bɛɛsɔne AWURADE bɛ Nyameɛ ne. Aso ennwu ye kyɛ Misraim abɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: The king had Moses and Aaron brought back, and he said, “All right, you may go and worship the Lord your God. But first tell me who will be going.”
translation_verse: Yiti bɛmane Mose ne Aarɔn sá wale Faro berɛ, na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhɔ bɛɛsɔne AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ ne. Nakoso ɛmɔ nu nwa mɔ yeɛ bɛkɔhɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: “Everyone, young and old,” Moses answered. “We will even take our sheep, goats, and cattle, because we want to hold a celebration in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na Mose sele kyɛ, “Yɛ ne yɛ ngwadaa ne yɛ mbanyi, yɛ mma mmienzua ne mmrasua, yɛ mmoaen ne yɛ nandwie mɔ yeɛ yɛkɔhɔ ɔ, ofikyɛ, ɔsɛ kyɛ yɛdi aluolue yɛhyɛ AWURADE animnyam.”

english_verse: The king replied, “The Lord had better watch over you on the day I let you leave with your families! You're up to no good.
translation_verse: Na Faro sele bɛ kyɛ, “AWURADE óli ɛmɔ si, sɛ ɔba ye kyɛ mema ate maa ɛmɔ ne ɛmɔ mma mɔ bɛkɔ a! Yeɛ ɛmɔanwu ye kyɛ ɛmɔle adwene tɛɛ ɔ!

english_verse: Do you want to worship the Lord? All right, take only the men and go.” Then Moses and Aaron were chased out of the palace.
translation_verse: Ɔngɔyɛ yee! Ɛ́mɔma mmienzua nemɔ angome bɛhɔ bɛɛsɔne AWURADE, ofikyɛ bɔ ɛmɔpena hɔ ɛne.” Yiti bɛfoane Mose ne Aarɔn befili Faro nyunu.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward Egypt. Swarms of locusts will come and eat everything left by the hail.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Ma wɔ sa so kyire Misraim aseɛ ne ma mmɛbɛ beyi bɛfa aseɛ ne, ná beli aseɛ ne aso nyaanyaa mukoraa bɔ asukɔtwea akungumaboɔ ne anzɛkye ye ne.”

english_verse: Moses held out his walking stick, and the Lord sent an east wind that blew across Egypt the rest of the day and all that night. By morning, locusts
translation_verse: Yiti Mose mane ye pɔmaa ne aso hyirele Misraim aseɛ ne. Na AWURADE mane eyia afiteleɛ mvrama tuli aseɛ ne aso sɔ kyẽa ne eyia ne kɔngɔen amukoraa. Na aleɛ hyene ngyerɛmɔ nen, né eyia afiteleɛ mvrama ne afa mmɛbɛ nemɔ wawa.

english_verse: were swarming everywhere. Never before had there been so many locusts in Egypt, and never again will there be so many.
translation_verse: Mmɛbɛ nemɔ wale Misraim aseɛ so amu, na beyi bɛfale Misraim maen ne amu. Na kyɛbɔ besi bɛyɛle manyamanya nen, ebie ɔwwale le, yeɛ ebie koso ngɔwa le.

english_verse: The ground was black with locusts, and they ate everything left on the trees and in the fields. Nothing green remained in Egypt—not a tree or a plant.
translation_verse: Beyili bɛfale aseɛ ne aso amukoraa mane aseɛ ne aso yɛle tunn. Na aseɛ ne aso nyaa mukoraa ne mmakaammaa mukoraa bɔ asukɔtwea akungumaboɔ ne anzɛkye bɛ ne, belili. Nikyee monɛ ko po anga wɔ eburo mmakaa ne ndire mɔ so, wɔ Misraim aseɛ so amukoraa.

english_verse: At once the king sent for Moses and Aaron. He told them, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.
translation_verse: Afei Faro hane ye nwo tole ye sa frɛle Mose ne Aarɔn maa bɛwale, na osele kyɛ, “Mayɛ bɔne matia AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ ne, ɔne ɛmɔ.

english_verse: Forgive me one more time and ask the Lord to stop these insects from killing every living plant.”
translation_verse: Yiti mesrɛ wɔ, ɛhe angome de, fa me bɔne kyɛ me; na ɛ́mɔsrɛ AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ ne ma ɔye ewue he fi me so.”

english_verse: Moses left the palace and prayed.
translation_verse: Yiti Mose fili Faro nwo berɛ hɔle ɔɔsrɛle AWURADE.

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a strong west wind that swept the locusts into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE mane eyia atɔleɛ mvrama piri bie tuli, na opiane mmɛbɛ nemɔ ooguale Ɛpo Kɔkorɛ nu. Abɛbɛ ko po anga berɛ wɔ Misraim aseɛ so nekaa biala.

english_verse: but the Lord made the king so stubborn that he still refused to let the Israelites go. Darkness
translation_verse: Nakoso AWURADE mane Faro bubuli mmakaa tuale ye so, na wamma Yisraelfoɛ ate ma bangɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, and everything will be covered with darkness thick enough to touch.”
translation_verse: Afei AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Tengyɛ wɔ sa fa kyire anwuro ma awosii bra Misraim aseɛ so, awosii bɔ sana bɛfa bɛ sa befuafua ɔ.”

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days.
translation_verse: Yiti Mose tengyɛle ye sa hyirele anwuro, na awosii kabii wale Misraim aseɛ so amukoraa ɛlɛsa.

english_verse: During that time, the Egyptians could not see each other or leave their homes, but there was light where the Israelites lived.
translation_verse: Ɛlɛsa mumua, ebiala annwu obiɛngo, anaakyɛ wandu ye gya; nakoso nekaa bɔ né Yisraelfoɛ bɛte ne de, ewienu yɛle hyireinn.
