english_verse: The king sent for Moses and told him, “Go worship the Lord! And take your families with you. Just leave your sheep, goats, and cattle.”
translation_verse: Afei Faro frɛle Mose, na osele ye kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhɔ bɛɛsɔne AWURADE ɛmɔ ne ɛmɔ mma mɔ bɛhɔ; nakoso ɛmɔ mmoaen ne nandwie mɔ de, odi kyɛ bɛka wa.”

english_verse: “No!” Moses replied. “You must let us offer sacrifices to the Lord our God,
translation_verse: Nakoso Mose sele kyɛ, “Odi kyɛ ɛma yɛ sa ka nningyein bɔ yɛkɔfa kɔbɔ afɔleɛ ɔne naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ yɛkɔma AWURADE yɛ Nyameɛ ne ɔ.

english_verse: and we won't know which animals we will need until we get there. That's why we can't leave even one of them here.”
translation_verse: Odi kyɛ yɛfa yɛ nyɛmmoa koso yɛkɔ; bɛ gya mbaboa ko po ngɔha wa, ofikyɛ bɛ nu bie yeɛ yɛkwaafa yɛsɔne AWURADE yɛ Nyameɛ ɔ. Na yɛngɔhora ngonwu nikyee bɔ yɛkɔfa yɛkɔsɔne AWURADE ɔ, sana yadwu dɔ koraka.”

english_verse: This time the Lord made the king so stubborn
translation_verse: Nakoso AWURADE mane Faro bubuli mmakaa tuale ye so, na wamma bɛ ate maa bangɔ.

english_verse: that he said to Moses, “Get out and stay out! If you ever come back, you're dead!”
translation_verse: Na Faro sele Mose kyɛ, “Fi me nyunu wa kɔ! Nea wɔ nwo yé, na nnɛmaa menwu wɔ nyunu ko; ofikyɛ kyẽa bɔ ɛkɔwa me nyunu ne, ngɔmaa bekohu wɔ.”

english_verse: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_verse: Na Mose buale kyɛ, “Yoo, ɛnwa nnɛmaa meba wɔ nyunu ko a, mate!”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
translation_verse: AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Waha amaneɛ pirikua ko bɔ mebaafa meto Faro ne Misraim so ɔ. Ɛhe asi ye, ɔkɔmaa ɛmɔkofi wa bɛkɔhɔ, na sɛ ɔma ɛmɔ ate a, ɔkɔfoa ɛmɔ maa ɛmɔkofi wa.

english_verse: Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
translation_verse: Afei, bɔ wɔ mmenia nemɔ amaneɛ kyɛ, ɔsɛ kyɛ bienzua biala ne brasua biala obisa ɛdwetɛ ne sikaa kɔkorɛ mbembenanneɛ ofi obiɛngo Misraimniɛ berɛ.”

english_verse: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
translation_verse: AWURADE mane Misraimfoɛ lole Yisraelfoɛ. Asa koso, né Mose te sona bɔ odi mu wɔ Misraim aseɛ so, wɔ Faro mbanyi mɔ ne maen ne nyunu.

english_verse: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
translation_verse: na bamuɛbaa bienzua biala bɔ ɔwɔ Misraim aseɛ so kowu, fite Faro bamuɛbaa bienzua bɔ ɔtena ye bia so ɔ so, kodwu afaneɛ bɔ osi aburoo ɔ ɔwa so, ɔne nyɛmmoa mɔ bɛ bamuɛbaa mɔ so.

english_verse: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
translation_verse: Na awuye piri paa bɔ bɛkɔbɔ ye wɔ Misraim aseɛ mukoraa so ne, ebie ossili le, yeɛ ebie koso ngosi ko.

english_verse: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yisraelfoɛ mɔ de, kyea po ongopo sona anaa kaka biala; amaa ɔnate so ɛmɔanwu ye kyɛ AWURADE ma nzonzoleɛ da Misraim ne Yisrael nu.

english_verse: Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave. Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
translation_verse: Na wɔ mbanyi hemɔ amukoraa bɛkɔwa me nyunu bekoobu ndwerɛ bɛkɔhã kyɛ, ‘Fi wa kɔ, ɛne wɔ mmenia bɔ beli wɔ si amukoraa!’ Na ɛhe asi ne, ngofi wa ngɔhɔ.” Afei Mose fɛle ɛyaa hahii fili Faro nyunu berɛ hɔle.

english_verse: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Faro ngɔtɛ ɛmɔ so, na ɔnate so m’anwanwadeɛ kɔsone pee wɔ Misraim aseɛ so.”

english_verse: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
translation_verse: Mose ne Aarɔn yɔle anwanwadeɛ he amukoraa wɔ Faro nyunu; AWURADE mane Faro bubuli mmakaa tuale ye so, na wamma Yisraelfoɛ ate ma bamvi ye aseɛ so bangɔ.

english_verse: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: AWURADE sele Mose ne Aarɔn wɔ Misraim aseɛ so kyɛ,

english_verse: This month is to be the first month of the year for you.
translation_verse: “Bosome he yeɛ ɔkɔyɛ ɛmɔ bosome bɔ oli moa ɔ; ɔkɔyɛ afoɛ ne anu bosome bɔ oli moa kɔma ɛmɔ.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
translation_verse: Ka kyire Yisrael maen ne amukoraa kyɛ, bosome he anu kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne, ɔsɛ kyɛ bienzua biala pena boaen akrɔngrɔma ko ma ye awuro ama, awuro biala nu kohia boaen akrɔngrɔma ko.

english_verse: If any family is too small to eat the whole animal, they must share it with their next-door neighbors. Choose either a sheep or a goat, but it must be a one-year-old male that has nothing wrong with it. And it must be large enough for everyone to have some of the meat.
translation_verse: Ɔsɛ kyɛ boaen akrɔngrɔma ne yɛ nyii bɔ wali afoɛ ko, bɔ ollili nnɛen ɔ. Ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛmɔsa nu bɛye bɛ befi mmoaen anaa mbɔngye nemɔ anu.

english_verse: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔfa ye bésie toonn ma odwu bosome he anu kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nna ne, na afei Yisrael maen ne amukoraa behũhũ bɛ mmoaen ne nɔsoa.

english_verse: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
translation_verse: Awuro bɔ bekoli naen ne wɔ nu nen, ɔsɛ kyɛ bɛfa mogya ne bie bɛkeka aponnwaa nyɔ ne, ɔne sua ne ye bati so.

english_verse: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Ɔsɛ kyɛ bɛtoto naen ne bedi ye sɔ kɔngɔen ne, ná bɛfa paanoo kabrɛdi ne awɔwee nyaa bɛboka so.

english_verse: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
translation_verse: Nnɛma ɛmɔdi ye monɛ, yeɛ nnɛma ɛmɔfa nzue bɛto, na mmom ɛ́mɔtoto: ye ti, ye gya ne ye kunu nningyein ne boka so.

english_verse: Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left.
translation_verse: Nnɛma ɛmɔfa ebie besie ma aleɛ kye so; na sɛ ebie ka ma aleɛ kye so a, odi kyɛ ɛmɔyera ye.

english_verse: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
translation_verse: Atee he aso yeɛ ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛmɔpe so bedi ɔ: ɛ́mɔbɔ ɛmɔ abɔsoɛ, ɛ́mɔwura ɛmɔ mbaboa, ɛ́mɔfa ɛmɔ pɔmaa nemɔ bétiratira, ná ɛ́mɔli ye ndɛndɛ. AWURADE Abɔtra ne ɛne.

english_verse: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ngɔɔpɛ nu Misraim aseɛ so sɔ kyẽa ne kɔngɔen, na ngohũ Misraim aseɛ so bamuɛbaa mukoraa, fite mmenia so kodwu ngaka so; na ngobua Misraim mmosoen amukoraa ndɛen. Me ole AWURADE.

english_verse: The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
translation_verse: Mogya ne yeɛ ɔkɔhyɛ ɛmɔ nzorɛ, wɔ awuro mɔ bɔ ɛmɔtete nu ne anu ɔ. Na sɛ menwu mogya ne a, ngɔbɔ ngɔtra ɛmɔ, amaa sɛ mébɔ Misraim maen ne a, amaneɛ ne bie ando ɛmɔ.

english_verse: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: “Ɛmɔkoli paanoo kabrɛdi ɛlɛsoo. Kyẽa bɔ oli moa ne, ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛmɔye mɔle harewaa biala befi ɛmɔ awuro mɔ nu, ofikyɛ ofi kyẽa bɔ oli moa ne alaa bɔ ɔkwaadwu kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nzoo nen, sona biala bɔ okoli mɔle harewaa ne, bɛkɔpɛ ye asue bekofi Yisraelfoɛ nu.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
translation_verse: Ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛmɔyɛ nyianu krongron wɔ kyẽa bɔ oli moa ne, yeɛ kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nzoo ne koso ɛ́mɔyɛ nyianu krongron. Nnɛma ɛmɔyɔ adwuma wɔ sɔ ngyẽa ne; sana aleɛ bɔ ebiala koli angome yeɛ ɛ́mɔyɔ ye nwo adwuma ɔ.

english_verse: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.
translation_verse: Ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛmɔdi Paanoo Kabrɛdi aluolue ne, ofikyɛ sɔ kyẽa ne yeɛ nyele ɛmɔ amukoraati mvili Misraim aseɛ so ɔ. Yiti ɛ́mɔtu sɔ kyẽa ne besie berɛ beli sɔ aluolue ne afebɔɔ wɔ ɛmɔ aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ mukoraa nu.

english_verse: Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day.
translation_verse: Bosome bɔ oli moa ne anu, kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nna ne ye nɔsoa, bɔ ɔkwaadwu kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so aburanyɔ ne ko ne ye nɔsoa, ɛ́mɔli paanoo kabrɛdi.

english_verse: During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Ɛlɛsoo ne anu, ɔnzɛ kyɛ benwu mɔle harewaa wɔ ɛmɔ awuro; ofikyɛ ebiala bɔ okoli mɔle harewaa nen, sɛ ɛwɔfoɛ ahɔ oo, anaa bɛwole ye maen ne anu oo, bɛkɔpɛ sɔ sona ne asue bekofi Yisraelfoɛ nu.

english_verse: Stay away from yeast, no matter where you live. No one is allowed to eat anything made with yeast!
translation_verse: Nnɛma ɛmɔdi nikyee harewaa biala. Ɛ́mɔli paanoo kabrɛdi wɔ nekaa biala bɔ ɛmɔkɔtena ɔ.” Abɔtra Aluolue bɔ oli moa

english_verse: Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said: Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover.
translation_verse: Afei Mose frɛle Yisrael mbanyi amukoraa, na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ebiala ɔɔhye boaen ko ma ye awuro ama, ná ohu ye fa yɛ Abɔtra boaen ne.

english_verse: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔfa sufiɛ, ná ɛ́mɔfa bɛbɔ mogya bɔ ɔwɔ ayaa ne anu, ná ɛ́mɔfa mogya bɔ ɔwɔ nu ne bɛ́keka sua ne bati so ɔne aponnwaa nyɔ ne. Nnɛma ɛmɔ nu biala fi ye awuro fite maa okodwu ngyerɛmɔ.

english_verse: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ AWURADE kɔɔpɛ nu kohũhũ Misraimfoɛ; na sɛ AWURADE nwu mogya bɔ ɔwɔ sua ne ye bati so, ɔne aponnwaa nyɔ nemɔ nwo a, okosã sɔ anoa ne anwo, na ɔngɔma sɛkyelɛniɛ ne ate ma ɔngɔwa ɛmɔ awuro berɛ ongohũhũ ɛmɔ.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɛmɔdwu aseɛ bɔ AWURADE baafa ma ɛmɔ ne aso, kyɛbɔ wahyɛ ye nwo bɔ ne a, ɛmɔhɔ so beli sɔ aluolue he.

english_verse: Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?”
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɛmɔ mma mɔ bisa ɛmɔ kyɛ, ‘Ɛmɔ aluolue he, ye bo ole sɛɛ?’ a

english_verse: And you will answer, “The Passover animal is killed to honor the Lord. We do these things because on that night long ago the Lord passed over the homes of our people in Egypt. He killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, but he spared our children from death.” After Moses finished speaking, the people of Israel knelt down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔhã kyɛ, ‘Ɔte Abɔtra afɔleɛ bɔ yɛbɔ yɛma AWURADE bɔ ohuhuni Misraimfoɛ ne. Nakoso odwuli Yisraelfoɛ awuro mɔ nwo wɔ Misraim nen, ɔpɛle nu hɔle maa yɛnyane yɛ ti yɛdidili nu.’ ” Na mmenia ne bɔle bɛ ti ase bɛsɔne .

english_verse: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
translation_verse: Na Yisraelfoɛ mɔ hɔle bɛɛyɔle sɔ, kyɛbɔ AWURADE hyɛle Mose ne Aarɔn ne ala. Misraim bamuɛbaa mmienzua wuwu

english_verse: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Ye abunnamu ne, AWURADE huhuni Misraim aseɛ so bamuɛbaa mmienzua mukoraati, fite Faro bamuɛbaa bienzua bɔ ɔtena ye bia so ɔ so, kodwu sona bɔ bahye ye nnure bawura kuku nu ye bamuɛbaa so, ɔne nyɛmmoa mɔ bɛ bamuɛbaa mɔ so.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Yeɛ Faro dwɔsole kɔngɔen ne, ɔne ye mbanyi mɔ amukoraa ne Misraimfoɛ amukoraa, na awuyebɔlɛ piri paa wale Misraim, ofikyɛ awuro biala nne berɛ bɔ sona anwu nu ɔ.

english_verse: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
translation_verse: Na Faro tole ye sa frɛle Mose ne Aarɔn kɔngɔen ne sele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔ ne Yisraelfoɛ, ɛmɔhã bɛ nwo befi me maen ye anu bɛhɔ! Ɛmɔhɔ bɛɛsɔne AWURADE, kyɛbɔ ɛmɔaha ne.

english_verse: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔfa ɛmɔ mmoaen ne ɛmɔ nandwie mɔ, ná ɛ́mɔfi wa bɛhɔ, kyɛbɔ ɛmɔhane nen, ná ɛ́mɔyira me koso.

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Misraimfoɛ hane Yisraelfoɛ bo kyɛ bɛha bɛ nwo befi aseɛ ne aso; ofikyɛ bɛhane kyɛ, “Yɛ mukoraa yawu yayie.”

english_verse: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Yiti Yisraelfoɛ tetele bɛ mɔle wɔ mmerɛ bɔ né ɔngeka ɔ. Bɛfale bɛ ndena bɛkyekyele ye nwo wɔ ngukue nu, na bɛfa bɛtole bɛ kɔme anwo.

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ yɔle kyɛbɔ Mose ha hyirele bɛ ne, ofikyɛ né badide ɛdwetɛ ne sikaa kɔkorɛ mbembenanneɛ ne ɛtena bafi Misraimfoɛ berɛ.

english_verse: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Né AWURADE ama Misraimfoɛ alo Yisraelfoɛ dada; yiti bɛ sa hane bɔ bebisale befili bɛ berɛ amukoraati. Bɛyɛle Misraimfoɛ dosodoso. Yisraelfoɛ tu fi Misraim

english_verse: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ tu fili Ramese bɛhɔle Sukote. Mmienzua kɔyɛ apee ɛyaa nzia yeɛ bɛfale ase bɛhɔle ɔ; banga mmrasua ne ngwadaa bammoka so.

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Mmenia mvrafra pee koso ne bɛ hɔle, na nyɛmmoa pee paa boka so: mmoaen ne nandwie.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Na mɔle kabrɛdi bɔ bɛ ne ye fili Misraim wale ne, bɛfa bɛyɔle taterɛ. Nna mɔle harewaa ɔ. Na ɔnate kyɛ betuli bɛ apereapereɛ so befili Misraim ne ati, bannya atee banyɔ aleɛ bɔ bekoli ye atunu ɔ.

english_verse: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
translation_verse: Sɔ kɔngɔen ne, AWURADE lili Yisraelfoɛ nwo afofi, kyɛbɔ ɔkɔyɛ bɔ ɔkɔye bɛ kofi Misraim aseɛ so ɔ. Yiti odwu sɔ kyẽa ne kɔngɔen a, Yisraelfoɛ aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ amukoraa besili pɛ bɛfa bɛye AWURADE ayɛ. Abɔtra ne nwo nhyehyɛleɛ

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose ne Aarɔn kyɛ, “Abɔtra ne nwo nhyehyɛleɛ ɛhe: amanvraniɛ biala nni ye aleɛ ne bie.

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: Nakoso kanganiɛ biala bɔ afa sikaa atɔ ye ne, ɛpɛ ye bienzua de a, ɔkora di bie.

english_verse: but no foreigners who work for you are allowed to have any.
translation_verse: Ɛwɔfoɛ bɔ ɔne ɛmɔ baatena anaa paaniɛ biala nni bie.

english_verse: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
translation_verse: Awuro ko anu ala yeɛ odi kyɛ ɛmɔtena bedi ɔ; nnɛma ɛmɔfa naen ne bie befite aluo, yeɛ nnɛma ɛmɔbɔ ye bowue nu.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: Ɔsɛ kyɛ Yisraelfoɛ mukoraati bedi sɔ aluolue ne.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɛwɔfoɛ bie ɔne wɔ yeɛ bɛte ɔ, ná okuro kyɛ odi Abɔtra aluolue ne ɔye AWURADE ayɛ a, ye de maa bɛpɛ ye nwo ama mmienzua mukoraa bɛ bienzua, amaa wanya ye nwo ate wali bie. Ɛhe kɔmaa ɔkɔyɛ kyɛ maen ne anu niɛ; nakoso bɔ bɛppɛle ye bienzua ne de, ɔnzɛ kyɛ odi bie.

english_verse: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: Mmeraa komapɛ bɔ ɔwɔ berɛ ma maen mmaa ne, ye ala yeɛ ɔwɔ berɛ ma ɛwɔfoɛ bɔ ɔne ɛmɔ baatena ɔ.”

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Yiti Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa yɔle kyɛbɔ AWURADE hyɛle Mose ne Aarɔn ne ala.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE yele Yisraelfoɛ ɛlɔen kure kure ne fili Misraim aseɛ so sɔ kyẽa ne.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ,

english_verse: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
translation_verse: “Tu bamuɛbaa mukoraa sie berɛ ma me; ebiala bɔ okoli moa kofi koɛsɛen nu kɔwa wɔ Yisraelfoɛ nu ne, sona oo, ayɛmmoa oo, ɔte me deɛ.” Paanoo Kabrɛdi aluolue

english_verse: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
translation_verse: Na sɛ AWURADE fa wɔ kodwu Kanaanfoɛ, Hitifoɛ, Amorifoɛ, Hiwifoɛ ne Yebusifoɛ aseɛ bɔ ɔtale ndaen hyirele wɔ nana mɔ kyɛ ɔkɔfa kɔma wɔ ne aso, aseɛ bɔ nyɔfonesue ne woɛ tengyɛ wɔ so ne aso a, di aluolue he wɔ ɛsraen he anu.

english_verse: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Di paanoo kabrɛdi ɛlɛsoo, ná di aluolue ne fa ye AWURADE ayɛ wɔ ye ɛlɛsoo ne aso.

english_verse: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
translation_verse: Ɛlɛsoo yeɛ ɛ́mɔli paanoo kabrɛdi ɔ; ɔnzɛ kyɛ benwu paanoo harewaa biala wɔ ɛmɔ berɛ, anaa mɔle harewaa wɔ ɛmɔ aseɛ so nekaa biala.

english_verse: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na sɔ kyẽa ne, kyire nu kyire ɛwa kyɛ, ‘Ɔnate nikyee bɔ AWURADE yɔ mane me wɔ mmerɛ bɔ mvili Misraim ne ati ɔ.’

english_verse: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na ɛhe kɔyɛ kyɛ sɛngyerɛnneɛ bɔ ɔwɔ wɔ sa nwo, ná wayɛ ngayeɛ wɔ wɔ nwoma so wama wɔ, amaa ɔnate so AWURADE mmeraa ne ala wɔ noa; ofikyɛ AWURADE nate tumi piri so yeɛ ɔyele wɔ fili Misraim ɔ.

english_verse: Celebrate this festival each year at the same time.
translation_verse: Yiti di sɔ nhyehyɛleɛ he aso wɔ ye mmerɛ so afoɛnoa biala. Bamuɛbaa bienzua

english_verse: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Na sɛ AWURADE fa wɔ kodwu Kanaanfoɛ aseɛ so, ná ɔfa ma wɔ, kyɛbɔ ɔtale ndaen hyirele wɔ ne wɔ nana mɔ ne a,

english_verse: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
translation_verse: tu abɔdeɛ biala bɔ okoli moa kofi koɛsɛen nu kɔwa ne sie berɛ ma AWURADE. Wɔ nyɛmmoa mɔ bɛ bamuɛbaa bienzua mukoraa te AWURADE deɛ.

english_verse: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
translation_verse: Fa boaen ba sesã afunum bamuɛbaa biala, nakoso sɛ anzesã ye de a, ye de bu afunum ne kɔme anu. Yeɛ wɔ mma mɔ bɛ nu bamuɛbaa bienzua biala koso, odi kyɛ ɛpɔ ye fi AWURADE berɛ.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na sɛ kyẽa bie ɛwa bisa wɔ kyɛ, “Ɛhe bo kyire sɛɛ’ a, wɔ koso abua ye kyɛ, ‘AWURADE nate ye tumi piri so yeɛ ɔyele yɛ fili Misraim ngoaasolɛ nu ɔ.

english_verse: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ mmerɛ bɔ Faro bubuli mmakaa tuale ye so kyɛ ɔngɔma yɛngɔhɔ nen, AWURADE huhuni Misraim aseɛ so bamuɛbaa mukoraati, fite mmenia bamuɛbaa mɔ so, maa oodwuli nyɛmmoa bamuɛbaa mɔ so. Na ɔnate sɔ ati yeɛ mefa kaka bamuɛbaa bienzua biala mebɔ afɔleɛ mema AWURADE ɔ. Nakoso me mma mɔ bɛ nu bamuɛbaa bienzua biala de, mepɔ ye .’

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Na ɛhe kɔyɛ kyɛ sɛngyerɛnneɛ bɔ ɔwɔ wɔ sa nwo, anaa ngayeɛ wɔ wɔ nwoma so, ofikyɛ AWURADE nate tumi piri so yeɛ ɔyele yɛ fili Misraim ɔ.” Munungum ningɔnn ne see ningɔnn

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Faro mane mmenia ne ate kyɛ bɛhɔ nen, Nyameɛ amva bɛ amva Filistifoɛ aseɛ so, ɔwɔ nu kyɛ né berɛ yeɛ ɔte tika ɔ. Ofikyɛ Nyameɛ hane kyɛ, “Sɛ mmenia ne kɔtɔ koɛ nu a, annea a né banu bɛ nwo, ná basa bahɔ Misraim.”

english_verse: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
translation_verse: Yiti ɛserɛ so atee bɔ ɔkɔ Ɛpo Kɔkorɛ nwo ne, Nyameɛ mane mmenia ne makye fale so. Na Yisraelfoɛ tu fili Misraim aseɛ so bɛhɔle kyɛ mmenia bɔ bɛ́kɔ koɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
translation_verse: Mose sesale Yosef mmowue ne hɔle; ofikyɛ né Yosef ama Yisrael mma nemɔ ata ndaen. Osele kyɛ, “Nyameɛ koogyina ɛmɔ si, na ɔyɛ a, ɛ́mɔfa me mmowue ne béfi wa bɛhɔ.”

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Betuli bɛ bo befili Sukote, na beesikyele Etam, wɔ ɛserɛ ne noa.

english_verse: During the day the Lord went ahead of his people in a thick cloud, and during the night he went ahead of them in a flaming fire. That way the Lord could lead them at all times, whether day or night.
translation_verse: Munungum ningɔnn bɔ né oli bɛ nyunu ne, wanyakyi bɛ nu eyia; yeɛ see ningɔnn ne koso wanyakyi bɛ nu kɔngɔen.

english_verse: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Afei AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ,

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
translation_verse: “Ka kyire Yisraelfoɛ kyɛ besa bɛ si beesi asikyeleɛ wɔ Pi Hahirote nyunu, wɔ Migidol ne ɛpo ne b’afia, wɔ Baal Sefon nyunu. Ye ndendeneɛ so yeɛ ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛmɔsi asikyeleɛ ne ɔ, wɔ ɛpo ne anoa.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ Faro kɔha kɔfa Yisraelfoɛ nwo kyɛ, ‘Baaha aseɛ ne aso, na ɛserɛ ne amaa basota berɛ.’

english_verse: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
translation_verse: Ngɔma Faro kobubu mmakaa kotua ye so. Ɔkɔpo bɛ so, nakoso ɔnate Faro ne ye lɔen amukoraa so ngɔhyɛ me nwo animnyam; na Misraimfoɛ konwu ye kyɛ me ole AWURADE.” Na sɔ ala yeɛ Yisraelfoɛ yɔle ɔ.

english_verse: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ bɛha behyirele Misraim hene kyɛ mmenia nemɔ anwati nen, ɔne ye mbanyi mɔ benyane adwene foforɛ wɔ mmenia nemɔ anwo, na besele kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ nikye yeɛ yayɔ ye, bɔ yama Yisraelfoɛ ayakyi yɛ solɛ ná bahɔ ye?”

english_verse: The king got his war chariot and army ready.
translation_verse: Yiti osiesiele ye teaseɛnam, na ɔfale ye asraafoɛ bokale ye nwo so.

english_verse: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE mane Misraim hene Faro bubuli mmakaa tuale ye so, yiti ɔpole Yisraelfoɛ so, wɔ mmerɛ bɔ né Yisraelfoɛ nate atunu bɛ́kɔ ngonimlilɛ so ɔ.

english_verse: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
translation_verse: Misraimfoɛ pole bɛ so: Faro mbɔngɔ mɔ ne teaseɛnam amukoraa, ye pɔngɔhanɛfoɛ ne ye asraafoɛ amukoraa, na bɛɛtole bɛ kyɛ basi asikyeleɛ wɔ ɛpo ne noa wɔ Pi Hahirote, wɔ Baal Sefon nyunu.

english_verse: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Faro pingyele bɛ ne, Yisraelfoɛ mane bɛ nye so, na benwuni kyɛ Misraimfoɛ bɛ́po bɛ so; yiti ɛserɛ piri hane Yisraelfoɛ nemɔ, na besu bɛfrɛle AWURADE.

english_verse: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
translation_verse: Na besele Mose kyɛ, “Asieleɛ mɔ nne Misraim hɔ ɔ, bɔ yiti yeɛ afa yɛ awa kyɛ yɛɛwuwu yɛgua ɛserɛ ye aso ye? Ɛɛyele yɛ fili Misraim ne, bɔ amaa wato yɛ hɔ ɛne?

english_verse: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
translation_verse: Anaa yanga yangyire wɔ wɔ Misraim kyɛ, “Yakyi yɛ konn ma yɛso Misraimfoɛ’? Ofikyɛ, sɛ yɛso Misraimfoɛ mmom a, ahaa ɔte paa tra kyɛ yɛkowuwu ɛserɛ so ɔ!”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
translation_verse: Na Mose sele mmenia ne kyɛ, “Nnɛma ɛmɔsuro, ɛ́mɔgyina pindinn, ná ɛ́mɔnea ngoalelɛ bɔ AWURADE kole ɛmɔ ɛnɛ ɔ; ofikyɛ Misraimfoɛ bɔ ɛmɔnwu bɛ ɛnɛ ye, ɛmɔngonwu bɛ ko le.

english_verse: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
translation_verse: AWURADE kɔho kɔma ɛmɔ, yiti ɛmɔ de, ɛ́mɔyɛ konn.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ esu frɛ me ye? Ka kyire Yisraelfoɛ kyɛ bɛhɔ bɛ nyunu.

english_verse: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Ma wɔ pɔmaa ne aso, ná tengyɛ wɔ sa ɛpo ne aso ma nu hyɛ nyɔ, amaa ɔnate so Yisraelfoɛ afa aseɛ wosee so bapɛ ɛpo ne.

english_verse: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
translation_verse: Me de, ngɔma Misraimfoɛ kobubu mmakaa kotua bɛ so, amaa ɔnate so bapo Yisraelfoɛ so. Na ɔnate Faro ne ye asraafoɛ amukoraa so, ye teaseɛnam mɔ ne ye pɔngɔhanɛfoɛ so, ngɔhyɛ me nwo animnyam.

english_verse: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
translation_verse: Afei Nyameɛ abɔfo bɔ né oli Yisrael ɛlɔen ne nyunu ne, ɔse oolili bɛ si. Na munungum ningɔnn ne fili bɛ nyunu oolili bɛ si,

english_verse: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
translation_verse: na oogyinane Misraim ɛlɔen ne Yisrael ɛlɔen b’afia. Na kɔngɔen ne amukoraa, munungum ne yɛle awosii mane bue ko, yeɛ ɔtale mane bue ko; yiti bue ko ne angora ambingye obiɛngo kɔngɔen ne.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
translation_verse: Afei Mose tengyɛle ye sa ɛpo ne aso. Na AWURADE mane eyia afiteleɛ mvrama piri bie tuli, na oopiane ɛpo ne sale nziɛ kɔngɔen ne. Ɔmane ɛpo ne kakyili aseɛ wosee, na nzue ne anu hyɛle.

english_verse: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
translation_verse: Na Yisraelfoɛ fale aseɛ wosee so pɛle ɛpo ne; na nzue ne yɛle ɛwaen mane bɛ wɔ bɛ famaa so ne bɛ bɛen so.

english_verse: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
translation_verse: Na alebahyene ne, AWURADE tole ye nye fale see ningɔnn ne munungum ne anu neane Misraim asraafoɛ ne, na ɔmane Misraim asraafoɛ nemɔ nye so tanene bɛ.

english_verse: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
translation_verse: Ɔmane bɛ teaseɛnam nemɔ gya sɛkyesɛkyele bɔ né bɛngora ndɛ kɔ ɔ. Yiti Misraimfoɛ sele kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔma yɛ́nwati yɛ́fi Yisraelfoɛ mɔ nwo wa, ofikyɛ AWURADE gyi bɛ si ɔko tia Misraim.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Tengyɛ wɔ sa wɔ ɛpo ne aso ma nzue ne sá ha bɔ nu, ná obu fa Misraimfoɛ ne bɛ teaseɛnam mɔ ne bɛ pɔngɔhanɛfoɛ so.”

english_verse: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
translation_verse: Yiti Mose tengyɛle ye sa wɔ ɛpo ne aso, na aleɛ baahye ne, ɛpo nzue ne sá wale ye boso. Na Misraimfoɛ bɛ́nwati bɛ́kɔ nen, AWURADE hane bɛ guale ɛpo ne anu wɔ asufia.

english_verse: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
translation_verse: Nzue ne ha tuale, na ɔfale teaseɛnam nemɔ, pɔngɔhanɛfoɛ nemɔ, ɔne Faro ɛlɔen amukoraa bɔ bɛpole Yisraelfoɛ so wɔ ɛpo ne anu ne. Bɛ nu ko po anga.

english_verse: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yisraelfoɛ de, bɛfale aseɛ wosee so bɛpɛle ɛpo ne wɔ ye afia; na nzue ne yɛle ɛwaen mane bɛ wɔ bɛ famaa so ne bɛ bɛen so.

english_verse: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE lele Yisraelfoɛ fili Misraimfoɛ sa nu sɔ kyẽa ne; na Yisraelfoɛ nwuni Misraimfoɛ kyɛ bawuwu bagua mboanoa berɛ.

english_verse: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ nwuni tumi piri bɔ AWURADE fa ho tiale Misraimfoɛ ne. Yiti Yisraelfoɛ surole AWURADE, na belele AWURADE ne ye somvoɛ Mose belili.

english_verse: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
translation_verse: Afei Mose ne Yisraelfoɛ tole edwein he yele AWURADE ayɛ kyɛ, “Ngɔto dwein ngɔye AWURADE ayɛ, ofikyɛ wama ye nwo so ngonim nu; wagyi pɔngɔ ne pɔngɔhanɛniɛ ne wagua ɛpo nu.

english_verse: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
translation_verse: AWURADE te m’anwoserɛ ne me dwein, na wayɛ me ngoadefoɛ. Ɔte me Nyameɛ, na ngɔye ye ayɛ, me baba Nyameɛ ɛne, na ngɔma ye so.

english_verse: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
translation_verse: AWURADE te koɛhonɛniɛ; ye dumaa li AWURADE.

english_verse: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
translation_verse: Ogyili Faro teaseɛnam mɔ ne ye asraafoɛ guale ɛpo nu; na Ɛpo Kɔkorɛ afa ye koɛhonɛfoɛ atitire nemɔ.

english_verse: They sank to the bottom just like stones.
translation_verse: Buma ne akata bɛ so, na bamono bahɔ ye bo kyɛ nyɔboɛ.

english_verse: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
translation_verse: O AWURADE, wɔ sa famaa ne te ngonim ne tumi, O AWURADE, wɔ sa famaa ne dworɔm pɔfoɛ ne.

english_verse: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
translation_verse: Ɛnate wɔ tumi piri ne aso ɛkã bɛ bɔ bɛko betia wɔ ɔ gua; Ɛsoma wɔ yaa piri ne, na ɔyera bɛ kyɛ ngyɛngyɛma.

english_verse: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
translation_verse: Wɔ bonyi anu nwomeɛ mane nzue ne boaboale ye noa, asorɔkye ne gyinane berɛ kyɛ ɛwaen; na buma ne bɔle kunguma wɔ ɛpo afia.

english_verse: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
translation_verse: Pɔfoɛ ne hane kyɛ, ‘Ngɔpo bɛ so, ngɔɔto bɛ, ngɔhyɛ koɛ nu nzesadeɛ ne, na me kra ko koyi. Ngɔhwe me ngrandɛ, na me sa kɔma bɛ boso konua.’

english_verse: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
translation_verse: Ɛmane wɔ nwomeɛ tuli mvrama, na ɛpo ne fale bɛ; na bɛmonone kyɛ kungumaboɔ wɔ buma ne anu.

english_verse: When you signaled with your right hand, your enemies were swallowed deep into the earth.
translation_verse: Ɛtengyɛle wɔ sa famaa nu, na aseɛ memene bɛ.

english_verse: The people you rescued were led by your powerful love to your holy place.
translation_verse: Ɛnate w’anwumvoinnwunɛ so ɛyɛle mmenia bɔ ale bɛ ne taataa, na ɛnate w’anwoserɛ so ehyirele bɛ atee maa bɛhɔle nekaa krongron bɔ ɛte ne.

english_verse: Nations learned of this and trembled— Philistines shook with horror.
translation_verse: Maen maen ate, na bɛ nwo wosowoso bɛ; na bɛ bɔ bɛte Filistia ne, ahunundetelɛ atɔ bɛ so.

english_verse: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
translation_verse: Afei Edom ahemvo mɔ babɔ fuin; ɛserɛ aha Moabo atitirefoɛ; na bɛ bɔ bɛte Kanaan amukoraa b’ahone atu.

english_verse: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
translation_verse: Ahunundetelɛ ne ɛserɛ atɔ bɛ so; ɔnate wɔ tumi asaa ne ati, bayɛ dinn kyɛ nyɔboɛ, kɔpem kyɛ, O AWURADE, wɔ mmenia kɔpɛ nu kɔhɔ ɔ, kɔpem kyɛ mmenia bɔ ale bɛ ne kɔpɛ nu kɔhɔ ɔ.

english_verse: You will let your people settle on your own mountain, where you chose to live and to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Ɛkɔfa bɛ kɔwa, ná aabɔ bɛ atenaseɛ wɔ wɔ bɔbɔ wɔ bokaa ne aso, nekaa bɔ afa ayɛ w’atenaleɛ ne, O AWURADE, nekaa krongron bɔ afa wɔ sa asiesie ne, O AWURADE.

english_verse: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
translation_verse: AWURADE koli hene afebɔɔ.” Miriam edwein ne

english_verse: The Lord covered the royal Egyptian cavalry and chariots with the sea, after the Israelites had walked safely through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Faro mbɔngɔ mɔ, ye teaseɛnam mɔ ne ye pɔngɔhanɛfoɛ hɔle ɛpo ne anu nen, AWURADE mane ɛpo nzue ne sale ye si oobu fale bɛ so; nakoso Yisraelfoɛ de, bɛfale aseɛ wosee so wɔ ɛpo ne afia.

english_verse: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
translation_verse: Afei ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ Miriam bɔ ɔte Aarɔn aliɛma brasua ne, ɔfale akasaa tirale, na mmrasua ne amukoraa bɛwosole akasaa begole abilie befitele belili ye si.

english_verse: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
translation_verse: Na Miriam surole so kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔto dwein bɛ́ye AWURADE ayɛ, ofikyɛ wama ye nwo so ngonim nu; wagyi pɔngɔ ne pɔngɔhanɛniɛ ne wagua ɛpo nu.” Mara nzue weewee ne

english_verse: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
translation_verse: Afei Mose mane Yisraelfoɛ tuli bɛ bo befili Ɛpo Kɔkorɛ ne anwo, na bɛfale bɛ nye behyirele Sure ɛserɛ ne aso. Bɛnatele ɛserɛ ne aso ɛlɛsa mumua bɔ bannwu nzue ɔ.

english_verse: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
translation_verse: Na beedwuli Mara nen, bangora Mara nzue ne no, ofikyɛ né ɔyɛ wee. Yiti bɛfrɛle berɛ Mara.

english_verse: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
translation_verse: Na mmenia ne penepenene bɛ komvi beguale Mose so kyɛ, “Nzue beni yeɛ yɛ́nya ye yɛ́no ɔ?”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Yiti Mose sũ frɛle AWURADE, na AWURADE hyirele ye bakaa bie. Ogyili bakaa ne tole nzue ne anu, na nzue ne yɛle fɛ. AWURADE yɛle ahyɛdeɛ ne nhyehyɛleɛ mane bɛ wɔ berɛ, na osole bɛ neane wɔ berɛ.

english_verse: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
translation_verse: Na Mose hane kyɛ, “Sɛ ekotie AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ dwirɛ, ná ayɔ bɔ ɔsɔ ye nye, ná ali ye mmeraa dwirɛ ne ye ahyɛdeɛ mukoraati so a, ye de anwonyerɛ bɔ nde nguale Misraimfoɛ so ne, mengɔte nu biala ngogua wɔ so; ofikyɛ me ole AWURADE, wɔ safoɛ ne.”

english_verse: Later the Israelites came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and
translation_verse: Afei beedwuli Elim, nekaa bɔ asue ti buru ne nyɔ ɔne ayee aburasoo wɔ ne, na bɛkyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ nzue ne noa.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ tuli bɛ bo befili Elim, na Yisrael ɛlɔen ne amukoraa wale Sin ɛserɛ bɔ ɔla Elim ne Sinai b’afia ne aso. Betu befili Misraim aseɛ so ne, bosome bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ne anu, kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nnu ne aso yeɛ bedwuli Sin ɛserɛ ne aso ɔ.

english_verse: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Na Yisrael ɛlɔen ne amukoraa penepenene bɛ komvi beguale Mose ne Aarɔn so wɔ ɛserɛ ne aso.

english_verse: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
translation_verse: Besele Mose ne Aarɔn kyɛ, “Sɛ AWURADE tumi maa yɛwuwuli Misraim aseɛ so a, ahaa ɔte paa. Berɛ de, yɛtenatenane naen kukue nwo yɛdidili yɛtele naen mane yɛ ko yili pambee. Nakoso ɛmɔafa yɛ baagua ɛserɛ so wa kyɛ bɛbaama ɛhɔen ku maen ye amukoraa.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔtie, ngɔma aleɛ kɔtɔ kofi anwuro kogua ase kɔma ɛmɔ. Ɛlɛho biala mmenia ne kofite kɔɔsesa bɔ ɔkɔso bɛ di sɔ kyẽa ne ɔ. Na ɛhe kɔmaa ngonwu ye sɛ bekoli me mmeraa so anaakyɛ bengoli so a.

english_verse: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
translation_verse: Na kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nzia ne, sɛ bɛboaboa bɔ bɛkɔsesa ne noa a, ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔyɛ ɛlɛho biala deɛ bɔ bɛsesa ne ye faa nyɔ.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: Yiti Mose ne Aarɔn sele Yisraelfoɛ ne kyɛ, “Ɛnɛ nɔsoa, ɛmɔkonwu ye kyɛ AWURADE yeɛ ɔyele ɛmɔ fili Misraim aseɛ so ɔ.

english_verse: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
translation_verse: Na ngyerɛmɔ koso ɛmɔkonwu AWURADE animnyam, ofikyɛ AWURADE anwu kyɛ ɛmɔpenepene bɛ komvi begua ye so. Na yɛ de, yɛ ole nwa bɔ ɛmɔpenepene bɛ komvi begua yɛ so ɔ?”

english_verse: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
translation_verse: Na Mose sele kyɛ, “Nɔsoa biala, AWURADE kɔma ɛmɔ naen ma ɛmɔkoli, na ngyerɛmɔ koso, ɔkɔma ɛmɔ aleɛ ma ɛmɔ ko koyi; ofikyɛ AWURADE ate kyɛ ɛmɔpenepene bɛ komvi begua ye so. Na yɛ de, yɛ ole nwa? Nna yɛ yeɛ ɛmɔpenepene bɛ komvi begua yɛ so ɔ, na mmom AWURADE.”

english_verse: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
translation_verse: Na Mose sele Aarɔn kyɛ, “Ka kyire Yisrael ɛlɔen ne amukoraa kyɛ, ‘Ɛmɔhwe bepingye AWURADE, ofikyɛ wate kyɛ ɛmɔpenepene bɛ komvi.’ ”

english_verse: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
translation_verse: Na Aarɔn noa wɔ so bɔ odwudwo kyire Yisrael ɛlɔen nen, bɛtole bɛ nye bɛneane ɛserɛ ne aso dɔ, na mvum nu, AWURADE animnyam yele ye nwo ali wɔ munungum ne anu.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ,

english_verse: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
translation_verse: “Mate Yisraelfoɛ bɛ komvi bɔ bɛpenepene ne. Yiti ka kyire bɛ kyɛ, ‘Nɔsoa ɛmɔkoli naen, ná ngyerɛmɔ wora ɛmɔali aleɛ ama ɛmɔ ko ayi; amaa ɔnate so ɛmɔanwu kyɛ me ole AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ ne.’ ”

english_verse: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
translation_verse: Odwuli nɔsoa ne, ayenzii mɔ tuli bi beeyi bɛfale asikyeleɛ ne; na aleɛ hyene ngyerɛmɔ nen, ɛborɔ guale asikyeleɛ ne anu nekaa biala.

english_verse: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
translation_verse: Na ɛborɔ ne yakyili gualɛ nen, mvum nu, nikyee mmaa mmaa taataa bie bɔ ye hatahata te kyɛ asukɔtwea guaguale ɛserɛ ne aso.

english_verse: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
translation_verse: Na Yisraelfoɛ nwuni ye sɔ nen, bebisabisale bɛ nwo ngoko ngoko kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ nikyee ɛhe?” Ofikyɛ né bɛnze nikye horɛ. Na Mose sele bɛ kyɛ, “Aleɛ bɔ AWURADE afa ama ɛmɔ kyɛ ɛmɔli hɔ ɛne.

english_verse: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
translation_verse: Bɔ AWURADE ahyɛ hɔ ɛhe: ‘Ɔsɛ kyɛ ebiala sesa somaa bɔ ɔkɔso ye di ɔ; olonka ngoko ngoko. Ɔsɛ kyɛ ebiala nea mmenia somaa bɔ bɛwɔ ye ɛtena sua nu ɔ ná ɔsesa.’ ”

english_verse: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
translation_verse: Sɔ ala yeɛ Yisraelfoɛ yɔle ɔ; ebiemɔ sesale pee, yeɛ ebiemɔ wora bɛsesale kãa bie.

english_verse: Moses told them not to keep any overnight.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Mose sele bɛ kyɛ, “Nnɛma ebiala yakyi bie ma aleɛ kye so.”

english_verse: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
translation_verse: Nakoso bandɛ Mose so. Ebiemɔ yakyili bie ma aleɛ hyene so, na ngaka wale nu maa ɔbone mvii. Na Mose fɛle bɛ so yaa.

english_verse: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
translation_verse: Ngyerɛmɔ biala, ebiala sesale bɔ ɔkɔso ye di ɔ; nakoso sɛ eyia bɔ a, né wahuro.

english_verse: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
translation_verse: Kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nzia ne, bɛsesale aleɛ ne mmɔhoɛ nyɔ; ebiala sesale olonka nyɔ. Mbanyi amukoraa bɔ bɛlela ɛlɔen ne noa ne, bɛwale Mose berɛ bɛɛbɔle ye amaneɛ,

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
translation_verse: na Mose buale bɛ kyɛ, “Bɔ AWURADE ahyɛ hɔ ɛne: ‘Ɛhema te nwomelelɛ kyẽa bɔkɔɔ, afofikyẽa krongron ma AWURADE. Yiti bɔ ɛmɔkɔtoto ne, ɛ́mɔtoto, yeɛ bɔ ɛmɔkɔto ne koso, ɛ́mɔto. Na bɔ ɔkɔha ne, odi kyɛ ɛmɔfa besie maa odwu ɛhema ngyerɛmɔ.’ ”

english_verse: The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms.
translation_verse: Yiti bɛfale bie besiele mane aleɛ hyene so, kyɛbɔ Mose ha hyirele bɛ ne; wammo mvii, yeɛ ngaka koso amma nu.

english_verse: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
translation_verse: Na Mose sele kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔli ye ɛnɛ, ofikyɛ ɛnɛ te afofikyẽa ma AWURADE. Ɛmɔngonwu bie wɔ buro ɛnɛ.

english_verse: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Elesia yeɛ ɛmɔfa bɛsesa ɔ; nakoso kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nzoo, bɔ ɔte afofikyẽa ne de, ebie ngɔte ngogua.”

english_verse: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
translation_verse: Kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nzoo ne, mmenia ne biemɔ hɔle kyɛ bɛkwaapena bie bɛsesa, nakoso bannya bie.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Kyinzu koraa yeɛ ɛmɔkɔpo me mmeraa dwirɛ ne me mmeraa maa okoodwu ɔ?

english_verse: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Ɛmɔanwu ye kyɛ, AWURADE ama ɛmɔ afofikyẽa, na ye sɔ ati yeɛ kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nzia ne, ɔma ɛmɔ elenyɔ aleɛ ɔ. Yiti ɔsɛ kyɛ ebiala tena ye awuro; nnɛma ebiala tu ye gya baa fite fi ye awuro kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nzoo ne.”

english_verse: And so they rested on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Yiti mmenia ne lele bɛ nwome kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nzoo ne.

english_verse: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ frɛle aleɛ ne mana. Né ɔte kyɛ mviɛlɛ, fitaa, na ye fɛɛ te kyɛ apiti bɔ woɛ wɔ nu ɔ.

english_verse: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na Mose sele kyɛ, “Edwirɛ bɔ AWURADE aha ato berɛ hɔ ɛhe: ‘Ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛmɔfa mana olonka ko besie berɛ bɛma ɛmɔ si ama mukoraa bɔ bɛkɔwa ɔ, amaa ɔnate so banwu aleɛ bɔ mva mane ɛmɔ lili wɔ ɛserɛ so, mmerɛ bɔ nyele ɛmɔ mvili Misraim aseɛ so ne.’ ”

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
translation_verse: Na Mose sele Aarɔn kyɛ, “Fa talie, ná fa mana olonka ko gua nu; ná fa sie AWURADE nyunu, maa bɛ́fa bésie wɔ ɛmɔ aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ amukoraa nu.”

english_verse: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
translation_verse: Na kyɛbɔ AWURADE hyɛle Mose nen, sɔ ala yeɛ Aarɔn fa siele Adanzeɛ ne anu, kyɛ bɛ́fa bésie ɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
translation_verse: Yisrael ɛlɔen ne amukoraa tuli bɛ bo befili Sin ɛserɛ ne aso, na belili tutena, kyɛbɔ AWURADE mmeraa dwirɛ te ne; na bɛkyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ Refidim. Nakoso né nzue bɔ bɛkɔno ɔ nne berɛ.

english_verse: The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!” Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
translation_verse: Yiti ɛlɔen ne ne Mose nyane dwudwolɛ, na besele kyɛ, “Ma yɛ nzue ma yɛno.” Na Mose buale bɛ kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔbɔ me somoɛ ɔ? Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔso AWURADE bɛnea ɔ?”

english_verse: But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
translation_verse: Nakoso nzuhɔen huni mmenia ne wɔ berɛ, na bɛpenepenene bɛ komvi beguale Mose so. Bɛhane kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛɛyele yɛ fili Misraim ɔ, kyɛ ɛbaama nzuhɔen ku yɛ ne yɛ mma ne yɛ ngaka ɔ?”

english_verse: Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
translation_verse: Yiti Mose sũ frɛle AWURADE kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ yeɛ nyɔ mma mmenia ye mɔ ɔ? Bɛ́pena bɛboro me nyɔboɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE buale Mose kyɛ, “Fa Yisrael mbanyi nemɔ bie boka wɔ nwo so, ná se di mmenia ne nyunu. Fa pɔmaa bɔ ɛfa fini asue Naele nu ne tira, ná kɔ.

english_verse: When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
translation_verse: Tie, ngoogyina wɔ nyunu wɔ dɔ, wɔ nyɔbotaen ne aso wɔ Horebo. Fa fĩ nyɔbotaen ne aso, na nzue kofi nu kɔwa kɔma mmenia ne konya bie kɔno.” Na Mose yɔle sɔ wɔ Yisrael mbanyi nemɔ nyunu.

english_verse: The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.” Israel Defeats the Amalekites
translation_verse: Ɔfrɛle berɛ Masa ne Meriba, ɔnate kyɛ Yisraelfoɛ bɔle somoɛ, na besole AWURADE bɛneane. Bɛhane kyɛ, “Aso AWURADE wɔ yɛ nu wa, anaakyɛ ɔnne yɛ nu wa?” Bedi Amalɛkefoɛ so ngonim

english_verse: When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Afei Amalɛkefoɛ wale bɛ ne Yisraelfoɛ bɛɛhone wɔ Refidim.

english_verse: So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
translation_verse: Na Mose sele Yosua kyɛ, “Yeye yɛ nu mmienzua ne bie, ná ɛne Amalɛkefoɛ bɛɛho. Ngɔfa Nyameɛ pɔmaa ne ngotira ɛhema, na ngɔhɔ ngoogyina bokaa ne ti afia.”

english_verse: Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop.
translation_verse: Yiti Yosua ne Amalɛkefoɛ mɔ bɛɛhone, kyɛbɔ Mose ha hyirele ye ne ala. Na Mose, Aarɔn ne Hure bɛfo bɛhɔle bokaa ne ti afia.

english_verse: The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them.
translation_verse: Na sɛ Mose ma ye sa so a, né Yisraelfoɛ bédi ngonim; yeɛ sɛ ɔka ye sa ase a, né Amalɛkefoɛ bédi ngonim.

english_verse: After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset.
translation_verse: Nakoso Mose sa nyane; yiti bɛfale nyɔboɛ bie bɛtole ye gya si berɛ deinn, na ɔtenane so. Na Aarɔn ne Hure pagyale ye sa ne hɔle anwuro, ko gyinane ye bue faen, yeɛ ko wora gyinane ye bue dɔ. Yiti ye sa ne hora gyinane berɛ toonn mane eyia tɔle.

english_verse: That's how Joshua defeated the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Na Yosua mane Amalɛke ne ye mmenia bɛtotɔle ngrandɛ noa.

english_verse: Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Kyerɛ he wɔ nwomaa bie aso ma ɔyɛ ngayeɛ nikye, ná kenga kyire Yosua kyɛ, ngonua Amalɛke ye boso ngofi aseɛ ye aso.”

english_verse: Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Mose sili afɔleɛ bokyea, na ɔtole ye dumaa: AWURADE te me frangaa.

english_verse: Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhane kyɛ, “Odi kyɛ ebiala ma AWURADE frangaa ne aso, ofikyɛ AWURADE ne Amalɛke bɛkɔho koɛ wɔ aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ mukoraati nu.”

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
translation_verse: Na ɔmaa bɛɛbɔle Mose amaneɛ kyɛ, “Me, Yɛtro bɔ nde wɔ sia bienzua, me ne ɛye ne ye mma mmienzua nyɔ ne yɛ́ba wɔ berɛ.”

english_verse: When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent,
translation_verse: Yiti Mose fitele ooyiale ye sia bienzua ne, obuli ndwerɛ wɔ ye nyunu, na afei ɔtɔle ye nu. Bebisabisale kyɛbɔ ebiala aporɛ nu si te ɔ, na bɛɛworole ɛtena sua nu.

english_verse: where Moses told him everything the Lord had done to protect Israel against the Egyptians and their king. He also told him how the Lord had helped them in all of their troubles.
translation_verse: Na Mose fale ɛhemɔ nwo amaneɛ bɔle ye sia bienzua ne: nningyein mukoraa bɔ ɔnate Yisrael ti AWURADE afa ayɔ Faro ne Misraimfoɛ, ɔne amaneɛ mukoraa bɔ Yisraelfoɛ nwuni ye wɔ atunu, yeɛ afei kyɛbɔ AWURADE si yele bɛ fili nu ɔ.

english_verse: Now I know that the Lord is the greatest God, because he has rescued Israel from their arrogant enemies.”
translation_verse: Na afei de, manwu ye kyɛ AWURADE te piri tra bosoen biala, ofikyɛ olele mmenia ne fili Misraimfoɛ sa nu, mmerɛ bɔ né bɛ́hyɛ bɛ anyeborolɛ ne.”

english_verse: Jethro offered sacrifices to God. Then Aaron and Israel's leaders came to eat with Jethro there at the place of worship. Judges Are Appointed (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Na Yɛtro, bɔ ɔte Mose sia bienzua ne, ɔfale naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne afɔleɛ ahoroɔ brɛle Nyameɛ. Na Aarɔn ne Yisrael mbanyi amukoraa wale, na bɛ ne Mose sia bienzua ne bedidili wɔ Nyameɛ nyunu. Bɛye maenbulɛfoɛ (Deuteronomi

english_verse: You and the people who come to you will soon be worn out. The job is too much for one person; you can't do it alone.
translation_verse: Ɛfɛɛ paa yeɛ ɛne mmenia bɔ bɛboka wɔ so ne bɛkɔfɛ ɔ; ofikyɛ adwuma ne ɔbo wɔ so, na wɔ ngome twe ɛngɔhora ye yɔ.

english_verse: The next morning Moses sat down at the place where he decided legal cases for the people, and everyone crowded around him until evening.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, Mose tenane ase kyɛ osiesie mmenia afia dwirɛ, na mmenia gyinane ye so ndende toonn fite ngyerɛmɔ maa aleɛ dwole.

english_verse: Jethro saw how much Moses had to do for the people, and he asked, “Why are you the only judge? Why do you let these people crowd around you from morning till evening?”
translation_verse: Na Mose sia bienzua ne nwuni bɔ Mose ɔ́yɔ amukoraa ma mmenia nemɔ nen, osele kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ yeɛ ɛ́yɔ ma mmenia ye mɔ ye? Nzu ati yeɛ wɔ ngome twe esiesie dwirɛ, bɔ mmenia gyigyi wɔ so ndende fite ngyerɛmɔ ma aleɛ dwo ye?”

english_verse: Moses answered, “Because they come here to find out what God wants them to do.
translation_verse: Na Mose buale ye sia ne kyɛ, “Ɔnate kyɛ mmenia ne ba me berɛ maa mebisa Nyameɛ apɛdeɛ mema bɛ.

english_verse: They bring their complaints to me, and I make decisions on the basis of God's laws.”
translation_verse: Sɛ ebie ne obiɛngo benya dwirɛ a, bɛba me berɛ maa mesiesie b’afia, na mekyire bɛ Nyameɛ ahyɛdeɛ ne ye mmeraa.”

english_verse: Jethro replied: That isn't the best way to do it.
translation_verse: Na Mose sia ne buale ye kyɛ, “Bɔ ɛyɔ ye, ɔtte mayee.

english_verse: God will help you if you follow my advice. You should be the one to speak to God for the people,
translation_verse: Yiti tie bɔ meka ye: métu wɔ foɛ, na mesrɛ kyɛ Nyameɛ oli wɔ si. Odi kyɛ egyina mmenia ne gya nu wɔ Nyameɛ nyunu, ná ɛfa bɛ dwirɛ to Nyameɛ nyunu.

english_verse: and you should teach them God's laws and show them what they must do to live right.
translation_verse: Kyirekyire bɛ ahyɛdeɛ ne mmeraa ahoroɔ ne, ná maa benwu brabɔlɛ nu atee bɔ odi kyɛ bɛfa so ɔ, ɔne bɔ odi kyɛ bɛyɔ ɔ.

english_verse: You will need to appoint some competent leaders who respect God and are trustworthy and honest. Then put them over groups of
translation_verse: Afei koso, neanea mmenia ne amukoraa nu, ná ye mmenia bɔ bɛfata, bɔ besuro Nyameɛ, bɔ bedi nahorɛ, bɔ bekyi fea-ase-ma, ná maa bɛlela mmenia apee apee, ɛyaa ɛyaa, aburannu aburannu ne buru buru noa.

english_verse: These judges can handle the ordinary cases and bring the more difficult ones to you. Having them to share the load will make your work easier.
translation_verse: Maa besiesie mmenia nemɔ afia mmerɛ biala. Edwirɛ biala bɔ ɔbo bɛ so ne, maa bɛfa bɛbra wɔ gya so. Nakoso edwirɛ mmaa mmaa mɔ de, maa bɛ bɔbɔ beli. Ɛhe kɔte wɔ fɛɛ ne aso, ná bɛ wora baboka wɔ maa ayɔ sɔ adwuma ne.

english_verse: This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɛyɔ he kyɛbɔ Nyameɛ hyɛ wɔ ne a, ɛkɔhora kogyina ye noa, ná mmenia ne amukoraa koso bahɔ b’awuro asomdwee nu.”

english_verse: He chose some competent leaders from every tribe in Israel and put them over groups of
translation_verse: Mose neaneane Yisraelfoɛ amukoraati nu yeyele bɛ bɔ bɛfata ɔ, na ɔbɔle bɛ panyi wɔ mmenia ne aso maa bɛlelale mmenia apee apee, ɛyaa ɛyaa, aburannu aburannu ne buru buru noa.

english_verse: They served as judges, deciding the easy cases themselves, but bringing the more difficult ones to Moses.
translation_verse: Na besiesiele mmenia nemɔ afia mmerɛ biala. Bɛfale edwirɛ bɔ ɔyɛ se nemɔ bɛwale Mose gya so, nakoso edwirɛ mmaa mmaa nemɔ de, bɛ bɔbɔ belili.

english_verse: After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
translation_verse: Afei Mose guale ye sia ne ate, na ye sia ne hɔle ye bɔbɔ ye maen nu.

english_verse: The Israelites left Rephidim and arrived at the desert. Then two months after leaving Egypt, they arrived at the desert near Mount Sinai, where they set up camp at the foot of the mountain. This was two months after they had left Egypt.
translation_verse: Betuli bɛ bo befili Refidim nen, beedwuli Sinai ɛserɛ ne aso, na bɛkyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ berɛ; na Yisrael kyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ bokaa ne nyunu.

english_verse: Moses went up the mountain to meet with the Lord God, who told him to say to the people:
translation_verse: Mose fo hɔle Nyameɛ berɛ. AWURADE frɛle ye fili bokaa ne aso sele ye kyɛ, “Edwirɛ he yeɛ ka kyire Yakob bosofoɛ ɔ. Ka kyire Yisraelfoɛ kyɛ,

english_verse: You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ bɔbɔ ɛmɔanwu bɔ mva nyɔle Misraimfoɛ ɔ, ɔne kyɛbɔ nnodole ɛmɔ wɔ kɔleɛ ndaa so, ná mvale ɛmɔ mmale me berɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Now if you will faithfully obey me, you will be my very own people. The whole world is mine,
translation_verse: Na afei de, sɛ ɛmɔkoli me dwirɛ so, ná ɛmɔali m’apam ne aso a, ye de, ɛmɔkɔyɛ me bɔbɔ deinn me deɛ wɔ mmenia mukoraati nu, ofikyɛ aseɛ mukoraati te me deɛ.

english_verse: but you will be my holy nation and serve me as priests. Moses, that is what you must tell the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔkɔyɛ m’asɔfo ahennie maen ɔne maen krongron. Na edwirɛ bɔ ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛkã kyire Yisraelfoɛ hɔ ɛne.”

english_verse: After Moses went back, he reported to the leaders what the Lord had said,
translation_verse: Yiti Mose wale ɔɔfrɛfrɛle Yisrael mbanyi, na ɔfale edwirɛ amukoraa bɔ AWURADE ahyɛ ye kyɛ ɔha ne tole bɛ nyunu.

english_verse: and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa bɛ noa yɛle ko, na bebuale kyɛ, “Bɔ AWURADE aha ne amukoraa, yɛkɔyɔ.” Na Mose fale mmenia nemɔ mmuayɛɛ ne tole AWURADE nyunu.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud and let the people hear me speak to you. Then they will always trust you.” Again Moses reported to the Lord what the people had said.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Tie, mebaafa munungum kumɔnn nu meba wɔ berɛ, amaa sɛ me ne wɔ dwudwo a, mmenia ne ate, ná daa biala bale wɔ bali.” Afei Mose hane mmenia nemɔ noa dwirɛ hyirele AWURADE.

english_verse: Once more the Lord spoke to Moses: Go back and tell the people that today and tomorrow they must get themselves ready to meet me. They must wash their clothes
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Kɔ mmenia nemɔ berɛ, ná pete bɛ nwo ɛnɛ ne ɛhema. Maa bɛpo bɛ nwo nningyein,

english_verse: and be ready by the day after tomorrow, when I will come down to Mount Sinai, where all of them can see me.
translation_verse: ná bɛboaboa bɛ nwo besie ɛhema si, ofikyɛ AWURADE kodwu kɔwa Sinai bokaa ne aso ɛhema si, bɔ mmenia ne amukoraa bɛ nye tua ɔ.

english_verse: Warn the people that they are forbidden to touch any part of the mountain. Anyone who does will be put to death,
translation_verse: To ɛwɛen fa bokaa ne anwo bɔ mmenia ne ngɔbɔ ngɔtra ɔ, ná ka kyɛ, ‘Ɛ́mɔnea yé ná ɛmɔamvo bangɔ bokaa ne aso, anaakyɛ ɛmɔandra ɛwɛen ne. Ebiala bɔ ɔkɔfa ye nwo kɔha bokaa ne nen, ɔsɛ kyɛ beku ye.

english_verse: either with stones or arrows, and no one must touch the body of the person being put to death in this way. Even an animal that touches this mountain must be put to death. You may go up the mountain only after a signal is given on the trumpet.
translation_verse: Nnɛma ebiala fa ye sa ka sɔ sona ne; bɛkɔboro ye nyɔboɛ anaa bɛkɔto agyaen bɛkɔwɔ ye. Kaka oo, sona oo, ɔsɛ kyɛ beku ye.’ Na sɛ behu totorobɛndo ne anu tendetende a, ye de ɔsɛ kyɛ bɛfo bokaa ne aso.”

english_verse: After Moses went down the mountain, he gave orders for the people to wash their clothes and make themselves acceptable to worship God.
translation_verse: Yiti Mose fili bokaa ne aso dwu hɔle mmenia nemɔ anwo berɛ, ɔpetene bɛ nwo, na bɛpole bɛ nwo nningyein.

english_verse: He told them to be ready in three days and not to have sex in the meantime. The Lord Comes to Mount Sinai
translation_verse: Na osele mmenia ne kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔboaboa bɛ nwo bésie ɛhema si, nnɛma ɛmɔfa bɛ nwo bɛka brasua.”

english_verse: On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, a loud trumpet blast was heard, and everyone in camp trembled with fear.
translation_verse: Ye ɛlɛsa ne aso, ngyerɛmɔ, wɔ bokaa ne aso: agralaa tetele, Nyameɛ ne bobɔle nu kurudududu, munungum kumɔnn wale, na totorobɛndo ne teane nu serɛserɛ. Yiti mmenia mukoraati bɔ né bɛwɔ asikyeleɛ berɛ ne, bɛ nwo wosowosole bɛ.

english_verse: Moses led them out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
translation_verse: Afei Mose fale mmenia ne fili asikyeleɛ berɛ fitele kyɛ bɛkwaayia Nyameɛ; na beegyinagyinane bokaa ne nye abo berɛ.

english_verse: Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the Lord had come down in a flaming fire. Smoke poured out of the mountain just like a furnace, and the whole mountain shook.
translation_verse: Nwosina katale Sinai bokaa ne aso amukoraati, ofikyɛ AWURADE natele see nu dwu wale so. So nwosina ne tu hɔle anwuro kyɛ foonoo nu nwosina, na bokaa ne amukoraa wosole kikikikikiki.

english_verse: The trumpet blew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ totorobɛndo hulɛ ne noa yɛle se nen, Mose dwudwole, na Nyameɛ buale ye wɔ agralaa nu

english_verse: The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and told Moses to meet him there.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE dwu wale Sinai bokaa ne aso, wɔ bokaa ne ti afia. AWURADE frɛle Mose kyɛ ɔbra bokaa ne ti afia, na Mose fo hɔle.

english_verse: Then he said, “Moses, go and warn the people not to cross the boundary that you set at the foot of the mountain. They must not cross it to come and look at me, because if they do, many of them will die.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Dwu kɔ aseɛnwo dɔ kɔbɔ mmenia ne kɔkɔ, ná bandra ɛwɛen ne bamma kyɛ bɛbaanea AWURADE, ná bɛ nu pee anwuwu.

english_verse: Only the priests may come near me, and they must obey strict rules before I let them. If they don't, they will be punished.”
translation_verse: Asɔfo mɔ po bɔ bɛba AWURADE nyunu ne, maa bɛte bɛ nwo, ná AWURADE andete bɛ nu pasapasa.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “The people cannot come up the mountain. You warned us to stay away because it is holy.”
translation_verse: Na Mose buale AWURADE kyɛ, “Mmenia ne ngɔhora bokaa ne aso dɔ ba, ofikyɛ wɔ bɔbɔ deinn abɔ yɛ kɔkɔ kyɛ, ‘To ɛwɛen fa bokaa ne anwo, ná maa ɔyɛ krongron.’ ”

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Go down and bring Aaron back here with you. But the priests and people must not try to push their way through, or I will rush at them like a flood!”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele ye kyɛ, “Dwu kɔ aseɛnwo dɔ, ná ɛne Aarɔn bɛfo bɛbra. Nakoso asɔfo nemɔ ne mmenia ne de, nnɛmaa bɛtra ɛwɛen ne bɛfo bɛba AWURADE berɛ, ná wamvɛ bɛ so yaa.”

english_verse: After Moses had gone back down, he told the people what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Yiti Mose dwu hɔle mmenia ne berɛ ɔɔbɔle bɛ amaneɛ.

english_verse: God said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: Afei Nyameɛ hane sɔ dwirɛ he amukoraa. Ɔnwa:

english_verse: But when Moses went near the thick cloud where God was, the people stayed a long way off. Idols and Altars
translation_verse: Mmenia ne gyinane dedeede, nakoso Mose de opingyele awosii kabii bɔ né Nyameɛ wɔ nu ne. Afɔleɛ bokyea nwo mmeraa

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
translation_verse: “Me ole AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ bɔ nyele wɔ mvili Misraim aseɛ so, fili ngoaasolɛ nu ne.

english_verse: Do not worship any god except me.
translation_verse: “Nnɛnya nyameɛ foforɛ biala ɛboka me so.

english_verse: Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth.
translation_verse: “Nnɛyɔ amoen biala ɛso ye, anaa nikyee biala bɔ ye sue te kyɛ ewienu anwuro anwuro nikye, anaa aseɛ so nikye, anaa aseɛ bo dɔ nzue nu nikye.

english_verse: But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
translation_verse: Nakoso bɛ bɔ bekuro me dwirɛ, ná bedi me mmeraa dwirɛ so ne de, mekuro bɛ dwirɛ maa okodwu aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ apee apee so.

english_verse: Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
translation_verse: “Nnɛbɔ AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ dumaa mbaen mbaen; ofikyɛ ebiala bɔ ɔkɔbɔ AWURADE dumaa mbaen mbaen ne, ɔngɔma ɔngɔfa ye nwo ngoli tɔtorɔtɔɔ.

english_verse: Remember that the Sabbath Day belongs to me.
translation_verse: “Kaye afofikyẽa ne, ná di ye krongron.

english_verse: You have six days when you can do your work,
translation_verse: Elesia yeɛ fa yɔ adwuma, ná yɔ wɔ nningyein mukoraati ɔ.

english_verse: but the seventh day of each week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your slaves, your animals, or the foreigners who live in your towns.
translation_verse: Nakoso kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nzoo ne de, ɔte afofikyẽa ma AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ. Nnɛyɔ adwuma biala sɔ kyẽa ne: wɔ oo, ɛwa bienzua oo, ɛwa brasua oo, w’akoaa oo, w’afaneɛ oo, w’ayɛmmoa oo, anaa ɛwɔfoɛ bɔ ɔte wɔ kuro ɔ.

english_verse: In six days I made the sky, the earth, the oceans, and everything in them, but on the seventh day I rested. That's why I made the Sabbath a special day that belongs to me.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ elesia yeɛ AWURADE fa bɔle anwuro ne aseɛ, ɛpo ne bɛ nu nningyein amukoraati ɔ, nakoso olele ye nwome kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nzoo ne. Yiti AWURADE yirale afofikyẽa ne, na ɔyɛle ye krongron.

english_verse: Respect your father and your mother, and you will live a long time in the land I am giving you.
translation_verse: “Di ɛse ne eni ni, amaa ɔnate so anya ngoa tendenn wɔ aseɛ bɔ AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ ɔ́fa ma wɔ ne aso.

english_verse: Do not murder.
translation_verse: “Nnɛdi awue.

english_verse: Be faithful in marriage.
translation_verse: “Nnɛsɛkye agyaa.

english_verse: Do not tell lies about others.
translation_verse: “Nnɛdi adanzewia tia ebiɛngo.

english_verse: Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else. The People Are Afraid (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: “Nnɛma wɔ nye yɛ eliɛngo awuro nwo koakoa. Nnɛma wɔ nye yɛ eliɛngo aye nwo koakoa, anaa ye akoaa, ye afaneɛ, ye nandwie, ye afunum, anaa nikyee biala bɔ eliɛngo deɛ ahɔ ɔ.” Ɛserɛ hane mmenia ne (Deuteronomi

english_verse: So you must never make idols of silver or gold to worship in place of me.
translation_verse: Nnɛma ɛmɔfa ɛdwetɛ bɛyɛ nyameɛ foforɛ mɔ bɛboka me so, anaa sikaa kɔkorɛ bɛyɛ nyameɛ foforɛ mɔ bɛfa.

english_verse: The people trembled with fear when they heard the thunder and the trumpet and saw the lightning and the smoke coming from the mountain. They stood a long way off
translation_verse: Na mmenia ne amukoraa nwuni agralaa bɔ né ɔ́tete, ɔne bokaa bɔ né ótu nwosina ne, ná besa bɛtele agralaa bɔ né ɔ́bobɔ nu ne, ɔne totorobɛndo hulɛ nen, ɛserɛ mane bɛ nwo wosowosole bɛ, na beegyinane dedeede.

english_verse: and said to Moses, “If you speak to us, we will listen. But don't let God speak to us, or we will die!”
translation_verse: Na besele Mose kyɛ, “Wɔ bɔbɔ dwudwo kyire yɛ, na yɛkotie. Nnɛma Nyameɛ dwudwo kyire yɛ, ná yanwuwu.”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid!” Moses replied. “God has come only to test you, so that by obeying him you won't sin.”
translation_verse: Na Mose buale mmenia ne kyɛ, “Nnɛma ɛmɔsuro, ofikyɛ Nyameɛ awa kyɛ ɔbaaso ɛmɔ nea, amaa ɔnate so ye nwo suronyi atena ɛmɔ nu, ná ɛmɔanyɔ bɔne.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to the people of Israel: With your own eyes you saw me speak to you from heaven.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Edwirɛ he yeɛ ka kyire Yisraelfoɛ ɔ: ‘Ɛmɔ bɔbɔ ɛmɔanwu ye kyɛ me ne ɛmɔ yadwudwo fi nyameɛso.

english_verse: Build an altar out of earth, and offer on it your sacrifices of sheep, goats, and cattle. Wherever I choose to be worshiped, I will come down to bless you.
translation_verse: Wɔ de, si nnɛterɛ afɔleɛ bokyea ma me, na so yeɛ fa wɔ mmoaen ne wɔ nandwie bɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ, ɔne w’asomdwee afɔleɛ ɔ. Na nekaa biala bɔ ngɔmaa ɛkɔkaye me dumaa nen, ngɔwa wɔ berɛ ngooyira wɔ.

english_verse: If you ever build an altar for me out of stones, do not use any tools to chisel the stones, because that would make the altar unfit for use in worship.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɛfa nyɔboɛ si afɔleɛ bokyea ma me a, nnɛfa nyɔboɛ bɔ base ɔ si, ofikyɛ sɛ ɛfa pɛwaa di adwii wɔ so a, né agua ye nwo fiɛ.

english_verse: And don't build an altar that requires steps; you might expose yourself when you climb up.
translation_verse: Nnɛfo simbini so kɔ m’afɔleɛ bokyea nwo, ná wɔ nwo angua berɛ wɔ so.’

english_verse: Death is the punishment for attacking your father or mother.

translation_verse: Sɛ ɛtɔ kanganiɛ bɔ ɔte Hebriniɛ a, ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔso wɔ afoɛ nzia. Nakoso afoɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so nzoo ne de, maa ɔfa ye nwo li tɔtorɔtɔɔ ɔhɔ.

english_verse: If he was single at the time you bought him, he alone must be set free. But if he was married at the time, both he and his wife must be given their freedom.
translation_verse: Sɛ ye ngome twe yeɛ ɔwale hɔ a, ye ngome yeɛ ɔkɔhɔ ɔ. Nakoso sɛ ɔne ɔye yeɛ bɛwale de a, ye de ɔne ɔye yeɛ bɛkɔhɔ ɔ.

translation_verse: Na ye mene bɔ ɔtɔle ye ne, sɛ ye nye ngye ye nwo a, ye de ɔma bɛɛpɔ ye. Atee nne berɛ kyɛ ɔyɛ ye atɔen ma amanvrafoɛ ɔ, ofikyɛ wali ye ngasi.

english_verse: If he selects her as a wife for his son, he must treat her as his own daughter.
translation_verse: Sɛ ogya ye ma ɔwa bienzua a, ye de ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔyɛ ye kyɛbɔ ɔyɛ ɔwa brasua ne ala.

english_verse: Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve.
translation_verse: “Sɛ mmienzua bɛ́ko, ná bepura pemvoɛ maa ɔpɔ baa, ná edwirɛ tɛɛ bie amma ye si ko a, ye de kerɛ biala bɔ braa ne ahu ɔkɔbɔ sɔ sona bɔ opurale braa nen, sɛ ndɛenbualɛfoɛ de to nu a, ɔsɛ kyɛ otua.

english_verse: pieces of silver for the loss of the slave, and the bull must be killed by stoning.
translation_verse: Sɛ bekole ye mbata a, ye de ɔkɔhora kotua mbata biala bɔ bede ye ɔ, ná wafa wale ye ti ngoa.

english_verse: This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter.
translation_verse: Sɛ osi ebie awa bienzua anaa brasua a, mmeraa komapɛ ne ala yeɛ bɛ́fa beli ye ɔ.

english_verse: Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property.

english_verse: If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
translation_verse: “Sɛ ebie nandwie pura sona foforɛ nandwie maa owu a, ɔsɛ kyɛ bɛtɔne nandwie bɔ ɔte ase ne, ná bɛkyɛ sikaa ne ɔne kaka fuin ne koso.

english_verse: If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ benwu kyɛ nandwie ne taa si, nakoso ye mene nga ye ndo tuin nu a, ye de ɔsɛ kyɛ ye mene fa nandwie si nandwie gya nu, ná ɔfa ye kaka fuin ne.

english_verse: If you steal an ox and slaughter or sell it, you must replace it with five oxen; if you steal a sheep and slaughter it or sell it, you must replace it with four sheep.
translation_verse: “Sɛ ebie wua nandwie anaa boaen, ná oku ye, anaa ɔyɛ ye atɔen a, ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔfa nandwie nnu tua nandwie ko ne kerɛ, ná ɔfa mmoaen nna tua boaen ko ne kerɛ. Ɔsɛ kyɛ awueniɛ ne tua mbata, nakoso sɛ wangora ye tua a, ye de ɔsɛ kyɛ bɛyɛ ye atɔen betua kerɛ.

english_verse: If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
translation_verse: “Sɛ ebie fa ye ngaka kɔ adidie wɔ fieso anaa bobe boo nu, ná ɔyakyi ngaka nemɔ maa bekodi ebie boo a, ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔfa ye bɔbɔ ye boo nu aleɛ paa, anaa ye bobe mmaa paa tua kerɛ.

translation_verse: “Sɛ see tɔ nekaa bie, ná ɔkɔsɔ ngyɛngyɛma nu, ná ɔkɔyera pata so aburoo, anaa fieso aburoo, anaa aburoo boo a, ɔsɛ kyɛ sona bɔ ɔtole see ne tua kerɛ.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double.
translation_verse: “Sɛ ebie fa ye sikaa anaa nningyein ma obiɛngo sie, ná bewua ye wɔ sɔ sona ne awuro a, sɛ bɛkye awueniɛ ne a, ɔsɛ kyɛ awueniɛ ne tua ye mmɔhoɛ nyɔ.
