Ehud said, “Your Majesty, I need to talk with you in private.” Eglon replied, “Don't say anything yet!” His officials left the room, and Eglon stood up as Ehud came closer. “Yes,” Ehud said, “I have a message for you from God!”
translation_verse: Ehude hɔle ye nwo berɛ wɔ mmerɛ bɔ né ye ngome ɔwɔ ye aborɔsaen so pumbu nu dɔ ode mvrama ɔ. Na Ehude hane kyɛ, “Nyameɛ nwa nga ngraa bie ngyire wɔ.” Yiti Eglon dwɔso fili ye bia ne aso.

english_verse: Ehud pulled out the dagger with his left hand and shoved it so far into Eglon's stomach
translation_verse: Yeɛ Ehude fale ye sa bɛen yele sɛpɔ ne fili ye sɔ famaa ne anwo, na ɔfa wɔle Eglon kunu.

english_verse: that even the handle was buried in his fat. Ehud left the dagger there. Then after closing and locking the doors to the room, he climbed through a window onto the porch
translation_verse: Afei Ehude fite hɔle abrannaa ne aso dɔ, na ɔtotole aborɔsaen so pumbu anoa nemɔ anu nzafoaa.

english_verse: and left. When the king's officials came back and saw that the doors were locked, they said, “The king is probably inside relieving himself.”
translation_verse: Ehude hɔle ne, ye si ye, Eglon somvoɛ nemɔ sa hɔle dɔ. Na benwuni kyɛ batoto aborɔsaen so dɔ anoa nemɔ anu nen, bɛdwenene kyɛ, “Ebiaa, ɔ́kɔ bakaa so wɔ aborɔsaen ne aso dɔ.”

english_verse: They stood there waiting until they felt foolish, but Eglon still didn't open the doors. Finally, they unlocked the doors and found King Eglon lying dead on the floor.
translation_verse: Bɛnwondɛle bɛhyɛle maa oodwuli kyɛ ɔyɛle bɛ ahomete. Benwuni kyɛ Eglon ommukye aborɔsaen so dɔ anoa nemɔ nen, bɛfale nzafoaa nemɔ bebukyebukyele. Na benwuni kyɛ bɛ mene wawu la aseɛnwo berɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But by that time, Ehud had already escaped past the statues. Ehud went to the town of Seirah
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ né bɛnwondɛ ne, Ehude nwatili ɔɔpɛle nu wɔ nyɔboɛ amoen ne anwo hɔle Seyira.

english_verse: in the hill country of Ephraim and started blowing a trumpet as a signal to call the Israelites together. When they came, he shouted, “Follow me! The Lord will help us defeat the Moabites.” The Israelites followed Ehud down to the Jordan valley, and they captured the places where people cross the river on the way to Moab. They would not let anyone go across,
translation_verse: Osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔli me si, ofikyɛ AWURADE afa ɛmɔ pɔfoɛ Moabofoɛ wawura ɛmɔ sa.” Yiti belili ye si, na beetuale Yɔɔdan apɛleɛ nemɔ bɔ bamma Moaboniɛ biala wambɛ ye wangɔ ye si dɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Moab was so badly defeated that it was a long time before they were strong enough to attack Israel again. And Israel was at peace for
translation_verse: Yiti sɔ kyẽa ne, Moabo lili ngoguo wɔ Yisrael sa nu. Na asomdwee wale aseɛ ne aso afoɛ aburawɔtwɛ. Samega

english_verse: Shamgar the son of Anath was the next to rescue Israel. In one battle, he used a sharp wooden pole to kill
translation_verse: Ehude ewue asi ne, Anate awa Samega dwɔsole, ná ɔfale pɔmaa bɔ bɛfa bɛka nandwie huni Filistifoɛ ɛyaa nzia. Ye koso ɔɔpepɛ lele Yisrael.

english_verse: After the death of Ehud, the Israelites again started disobeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Ehude wue asi ne, Yisraelfoɛ sa yɔle bɔ ɔte bɔne wɔ AWURADE nyunu ɔ.

english_verse: So the Lord let the Canaanite King Jabin of Hazor conquer Israel. Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, lived in Harosheth-Ha-Goiim.
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE fale bɛ wurale Kanaan hene Yabin bɔ né odi hene wɔ Hasɔ ne sa. Ye safohene ole Sisera bɔ né ɔte Harosete Hagoyim ne.

english_verse: “Stand at the entrance to the tent,” Sisera told her. “If someone comes by and asks if anyone is inside, tell them ‘No.’ ”
translation_verse: Sisera sele ye kyɛ, “Ɛtena sua ne, gyina ye anoa nu berɛ. Na sɛ ebie ba bisa wɔ kyɛ, ‘Aso ebie awa wa’ a, bua ye kyɛ, ‘Daabi.’ ”

english_verse: Deborah the wife of Lappidoth was a prophet and a leader of Israel during those days.
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ brasua Debora bɔ ohu ole Lapidote ne, ye yeɛ né ɔla Yisrael noa ɔ.

english_verse: She would sit under Deborah's Palm Tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where Israelites would come and ask her to settle their legal cases.
translation_verse: Né ɔtaa tena Debora ayee bɔ ɔwɔ Rama ne Betel b’afia ne abo, wɔ Efraim mmokaa aseɛ ne aso. Berɛ yeɛ né Yisraelfoɛ fa b’edwirɛ bɛbato ye nyunu maa odi ɔ.

english_verse: One day, Barak the son of Abinoam was in Kedesh in Naphtali, and Deborah sent word for him to come and talk with her. When he arrived, she said: I have a message for you from the Lord God of Israel! You are to get together an army of
translation_verse: Debora somane maa bɛɛfrɛle Abinoam awa bienzua Barake befili Kedese bɔ ɔwɔ Nafetali ne bɛbrɛle ye. Na osele ye kyɛ, “AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ ahyɛdeɛ bɔ ɔfa ma wɔ ɛhe: ‘Yeye koɛhonɛfoɛ apee buru fi Nafetali ne Sebulɔn mmusua kure nu, ná di bɛ nyunu fa bɛ kɔ Tabɔ bokaa ne aso.

english_verse: The Lord will trick Sisera into coming out to fight you at the Kishon River. Sisera will be leading King Jabin's army as usual, and they will have their chariots, but the Lord has promised to help you defeat them.
translation_verse: Na ngɔtwetwe Yabin ye safohene Sisera maa ɔne ye teaseɛnam mɔ ne ye koɛhonɛfoɛ mɔ bekooyia wɔ wɔ Kison bɔnza ne anu; afei ngɔfa ye ngowura wɔ sa.’ ”

english_verse: “All right, I'll go!” she replied. “But I'm warning you that the Lord is going to let a woman defeat Sisera, and no one will honor you for winning the battle.” Deborah and Barak left for Kedesh,
translation_verse: Yeɛ Debora buale kyɛ, “Amba me ne wɔ kɔhɔ; nakoso atee bɔ ɛkɔ ye, ye nwo animnyam ngɔyɛ wɔ deɛ, ofikyɛ AWURADE kɔfa Sisera kowura brasua bie sa.” Na Debora dwɔsole ɔne Barake bɛhɔle Kedese.

english_verse: At this time, Heber of the Kenite clan was living near the village of Oak in Zaanannim, not far from Kedesh. The Kenites were descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, but Heber had moved and had set up his tents away from the rest of the clan.
translation_verse: Né Keniniɛ Heberi wate ye nwo wafi Kenifoɛ ngaa nemɔ anwo. Kenifoɛ bɛte Mose sia bienzua Hobabo ye boso ama, na né bakyekye b’asikyeleɛ maa waadwu Elon Besananim, bɔ opingye Kedese ne.

english_verse: When Sisera learned that Barak had led an army to Mount Tabor,
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ bɛbɔle Sisera amaneɛ kyɛ Abinoam awa Barake wafa koɛhonɛfoɛ wahɔ Tabɔ bokaa ne aso ne,

english_verse: Deborah shouted, “Barak, it's time to attack Sisera! Because today the Lord is going to help you defeat him. In fact, the Lord has already gone on ahead to fight for you.” Barak led his
translation_verse: Yeɛ Debora sele Barake kyɛ, “Dwɔso ɛne ye bɛɛho! Ofikyɛ ɛnɛ kyẽa ye yeɛ AWURADE afa Sisera wawura wɔ sa ɔ! Amba AWURADE li wɔ nyunu.” Yiti Barake torole Tabɔ bokaa ne, na né koɛhonɛfoɛ apee buru ne beli ye si.

english_verse: And during the battle, the Lord confused Sisera, his chariot drivers, and his whole army. Everyone was so afraid of Barak and his army, that even Sisera jumped down from his chariot and tried to escape.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE mane ahunundetelɛ tɔle Sisera so, ɔne ye teaseɛnamhanɛfoɛ amukoraa so, yeɛ ye koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa so wɔ Barake nyunu. Sisera dwu fili ye teaseɛnam ne aso nwatili ye gya kunu.

english_verse: Barak's forces went after Sisera's chariots and army as far as Harosheth-Ha-Goiim. Sisera's entire army was wiped out.
translation_verse: Barake foane teaseɛnam nemɔ ne koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ alaa oodwuli Harosete Hagoyim. Sisera koɛhonɛfoɛ ne amukoraa bɛtotɔle ngrandɛ noa bɔ komapɛ po anga ɔ.

english_verse: Only Sisera escaped. He ran to Heber's camp, because Heber and his family had a peace treaty with the king of Hazor. Sisera went to the tent that belonged to Jael, Heber's wife.
translation_verse: Né Sisera anwati ye gya kunu, na ɔhɔle Keniniɛ Heberi ɔye Yaele ye ɛtena sua nu; ofikyɛ Hasɔ hene Yabin ɔne Keniniɛ Heberi abusuafoɛ, b’afia te wosee.

english_verse: She came out to greet him and said, “Come in, sir! Please come on in. Don't be afraid.” After they had gone inside, Sisera lay down, and Jael covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Yaele fite ooyiale Sisera, na osele Sisera kyɛ, “Me mene, baafea wa. Baafea me nwo wa. Nnɛsuro.” Yiti Sisera ɔɔfeale Yaele berɛ wɔ Yaele ye ɛtena sua nu, na Yaele fale ɛtena katale ye so.

english_verse: “Could I have a little water?” he asked. “I'm thirsty.” Jael opened a leather bottle and poured him some milk, then she covered him back up.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sisera sele ye kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, ma me nzue kãa maa nno, na nzuhɔen ku me.” Yiti Yaele tuli nandwie nyɔfonesue towaa so, ɔmane Sisera bie maa ɔnone, na osa katale ye nwo.

english_verse: Sisera was exhausted and soon fell fast asleep. Jael took a hammer and drove a tent-peg through his head into the ground, and he died.
translation_verse: Nakoso Heberi aye Yaele fale ɛtena sua pɛmbɛen ɔne bɔsobaka otirale. Ɔyɛle nwaa hɔle Sisera nwo berɛ, na ɔbɔle pɛmbɛen ne aso wurale ye so taa nu maa pɛmbɛen ne oowurale ase. Né Sisera afɛ paa, yiti né walafe hatee, na ɔfale nu wuli.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Barak had been following Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. “The man you're looking for is inside,” she said. “Come in and I'll show him to you.” They went inside, and there was Sisera—dead and stretched out with a tent-peg through his skull.
translation_verse: Na Barake gu so ɔpena Sisera ne, Yaele fitele ooyiale ye sele ye kyɛ, “Bra maa ngyire wɔ biaa bɔ ɛpena ye ne.” Yiti Barake wurale Yaele ɛtena sua ne anu, na onwuni kyɛ Sisera wawu la berɛ, bɔ ɛtena sua pɛmbɛen ne wura ye so taa nu ɔ.

english_verse: That same day God defeated the Canaanite King Jabin while the Israelites looked on, and his army was no longer powerful enough to attack the Israelites.
translation_verse: Yiti sɔ kyẽa ne, Nyameɛ lili Kaanan hene Yabin so ngonim mane Yisraelfoɛ.

english_verse: Jabin grew weaker while the Israelites kept growing stronger, until at last the Israelites destroyed him.
translation_verse: Na Yisraelfoɛ hɔle so benyane Kaanan hene Yabin so tumi, kɔpem kyɛ behuni ye ɔ.

english_verse: After the battle was over that day, Deborah and Barak sang this song:
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne, Debora ne Abinoam awa Barake bɛtole edwein kyɛ,

english_verse: We praise you, Lord! Our soldiers volunteered, ready to follow you.
translation_verse: “Sɛ Yisrael nu koɛhonɛfoɛ di ye nyunu a, sɛ mmenia ne tu bɛ nwo sie berɛ a, ɛ́mɔye AWURADE ayɛ!

english_verse: Listen, kings and rulers, while I sing for the Lord, the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ahemvo, ɛ́mɔtie. Atitire, ɛ́mɔma ɛmɔ so bra wa; AWURADE yeɛ ngɔto dwein ngɔye ye ayɛ ɔ, ngɔto anigye dwein ngɔye AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ ayɛ.

english_verse: Our Lord, God of Israel, when you came from Seir, where the Edomites live,
translation_verse: AWURADE, mmerɛ bɔ etuli wɔ bo fili Sɛre ne, mmerɛ bɔ ɛpɛle nu wɔ Edom mbɔtam ne, aseɛ wosole, nyameɛso tɔle nzue, yeɛ munungum tɔle nzue paa.

english_verse: rain poured from the sky, the earth trembled, and mountains shook.
translation_verse: Mmokaa wosole serɛserɛ wɔ AWURADE Sinai Nyameɛ ne nyunu, bɛwosole wɔ AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ nyunu.

english_verse: In the time of Shamgar son of Anath, and now again in Jael's time, roads were too dangerous for caravans. Travelers had to take the back roads,
translation_verse: Anate awa Samega mmerɛ so, Yaele mmerɛ so, atimbire so yɛle bɔfonn; na akwandufoɛ makyele bɛɛfale eburo atee mɔ so.

english_verse: and villagers couldn't work in their fields. Then Deborah took command, protecting Israel as a mother protects her children.
translation_verse: Yisrael namue mɔ kakyili kurofoen, nguro nemɔ bɔle, kɔpem kyɛ Debora dwɔsole ɔ; odwɔsole kyɛ brataen wɔ Yisrael.

english_verse: The Israelites worshiped other gods, and the gates of their towns were then attacked. But they had no shields or spears to fight with.
translation_verse: Beelili nyameɛ foforɛ mɔ si, maa ɔnate so koɛ ɔɔtoale bɛ wɔ kuro berɛ pambim nu. Aso benwuni akokyɛm ne pealɛɛ wɔ Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ apee aburanna nemɔ nwo?

english_verse: I praise you, Lord, and I am grateful for those leaders and soldiers who volunteered.
translation_verse: M’ahone la Yisrael safohene mɔ anwo, bɔ betuli bɛ nwo besiele berɛ ne. Ɛ́mɔye AWURADE ayɛ.

english_verse: Listen, everyone! Whether you ride a donkey with a padded saddle or have to walk.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ bɔ ɛmɔtete afunum fufue mɔ so ɔ, ɛmɔ bɔ ɛmɔtete bɛen paa so ɔ, ɔne ɛmɔ bɔ ɛmɔnate atee noa ɔ, ɛ́mɔto ye nwo dwein.

english_verse: Even those who carry water to the animals will tell you, “The Lord has won victories, and so has Israel.” Then the Lord's people marched down to the town gates
translation_verse: Edwein bɔ edweintolɛfoɛ bɛto wɔ asaleɛ berɛ ne, berɛ yeɛ bɛto AWURADE ayɛyelɛ dwein ɔ, bɛto ayɛyelɛ dwein wɔ Yisrael. Yeɛ AWURADE mmenia torotorole hɔle pambim nemɔ anwo.

english_verse: and said, “Deborah, let's go! Let's sing as we march. Barak, capture our enemies.”
translation_verse: Dwɔso, Debora dwɔso e! Dwɔso, dwɔso to dwein! Barake, dwɔso ná di mmenia bɔ ahye bɛ nnure ne nyunu, O Abinoam awa.

english_verse: The Lord's people who were left joined with their leaders and fought at my side.
translation_verse: Afei atitire bɔ baha ne bedwɔsole betiale anwoserɛfoɛ. AWURADE mmenia dwɔsole betiale anwoserɛfoɛ bɛmane ye.

english_verse: Troops came from Ephraim, where Amalekites once lived. Others came from Benjamin; officers and leaders came from Machir and Zebulun.
translation_verse: Besili nu befili Efraim bɛhɔle Amalɛke bɔnza ne anu. Belili wɔ Benyamin, ne wɔ nwo ama si; Safohene nemɔ tuli bɛ bo befili Makyiri, yeɛ bɛ bɔ betira safohene pɔmaa mɔ koso, betuli bɛ bo befili Sebulɔn.

english_verse: The rulers of Issachar came along with Deborah, and Issachar followed Barak into the valley. But the tribe of Reuben was no help at all!
translation_verse: Yisaka safohene mɔ bɛ ne Debora yeɛ bɛwale ɔ, yeɛ Yisaka lili nahorɛ mane Barake; belili ye si bɛhɔle bɔnza ne anu. Ruben mmusua mmusua nemɔ, b’adwene anyɛ ko.

english_verse: Reuben, why did you stay among your sheep pens? Was it to listen to shepherds whistling for their sheep? No one could figure out why Reuben wouldn't come.
translation_verse: Nzu ati yeɛ ɛhale nziɛ wɔ mmoaen kure nemɔ anu ɔ? Kyɛ ɛkɔte ɛfrɛlɛ bɔ bɛfrɛ mmoaen nemɔ ti anaa? Ruben mmusua mmusua nemɔ, b’adwene anyɛ ko.

english_verse: The people of Gilead stayed across the Jordan. Why did the tribe of Dan remain on their ships and the tribe of Asher stay along the coast near the harbors?
translation_verse: Gileade hale asue Yɔɔdan asi; na Dan de, nzu ati yeɛ ɔtenane ɛlɛen nemɔ anwo ɔ? Asɛ tenane konn wɔ mboanoa, na ɔbɔle ye atenaleɛ wɔ etii so.

english_verse: But soldiers of Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives to attack the enemy.
translation_verse: Sebulɔnfoɛ fale bɛ ngoa tole serewa; sɔ ala yeɛ Nafetali koso yɔle ɔ, wɔ aseɛ pralaa mmokaa ne aso.

english_verse: Canaanite kings fought us at Taanach by the stream near Megiddo— but they couldn't rob us of our silver.
translation_verse: Ahemvo mɔ wale, na bɛhone; yeɛ Kanaan ahemvo koso bɛhone, wɔ Taanake bɔ opingye Megido nzue noa; bannya koɛ nu nzesadeɛ bɔ ɔte ɛdwetɛ ɔ.

english_verse: From their pathways in the sky the stars fought Sisera,
translation_verse: Nzramaa mɔ fili nyameɛso bɛɛhone; bɛnate b’atee so bɛhone betiale Sisera.

english_verse: and his soldiers were swept away by the ancient Kishon River. I will march on and be brave.
translation_verse: Kison asue piane bɛ hɔle, Kison asue bɔ ɔse worɔworɔ ne. Me kra, tu agyirɛ anwoserɛ nu kɔ wɔ nyunu!

english_verse: Sisera's horses galloped off, their hoofs thundering in retreat.
translation_verse: Mbɔngɔ gya mbaboa bobɔle ase, ofikyɛ behuruhuruli fɛen fɛen betuli amirika.

english_verse: The Lord's angel said, “Put a curse on Meroz Town! Its people refused to help the Lord fight his powerful enemies.”
translation_verse: AWURADE abɔfo nwa: Ɛ́mɔnoma Merose, ɛ́mɔnoma nu ama paa, ofikyɛ bamma ammoka AWURADE, bamma ammoka AWURADE maa wango wandia anwoserɛfoɛ nemɔ.

english_verse: But honor Jael, the wife of Heber from the Kenite clan. Give more honor to her than to any other woman who lives in tents. Yes, give more honor to her than to any other woman.
translation_verse: Wɔ Yaele bɔ anya saleɛ atra mmrasua amukoraa ɔ, Keniniɛ Heberi aye, mmrasua bɔ bɛtete ɛtena sua nu ne, anya saleɛ atra bɛ mukoraa.

english_verse: Sisera asked for water, but Jael gave him milk— cream in a fancy cup.
translation_verse: Sisera srɛle nzue, nakoso Yaele mane ye nandwie nyɔfonesue, ɔfale nandwie nyɔfonesue nye loe guale ahemvo kulie nu brɛle ye.

english_verse: She reached for a tent-peg and held a hammer in her right hand. And with a blow to the head, she crushed his skull.
translation_verse: Ɔtengyɛle ye sa fale ɛtena sua pɛmbɛen, ole ye sa famaa fale adwumayɔlɛfoɛ bɔsobaka; ɔfa bɔle Sisera, ɔfa bɔle ye ti pɛkyɛle ye, ɔfa bɔle ye so taa nu maa omi hɔle nu.

english_verse: Sisera's mother looked out through her window. “Why is he taking so long?” she asked. “Why haven't we heard his chariots coming?”
translation_verse: Sisera oni fale ye ti tɛle mboma nu neane, mboma nu yeɛ ɔfale ye nye tɛle bɔle awuye kyɛ, ‘Nzu ati yeɛ dadaada ye, ye teaseɛnam ɔmma ye? Nzu ati yeɛ ye teaseɛnam mɔ ahyɛ bɔ yɛnde bɛ gya boso ye?’

english_verse: Our Lord, we pray that all your enemies will die like Sisera. But let everyone who loves you shine brightly like the sun at dawn. Midian Steals Everything from Israel There was peace in Israel for about
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE, ma wɔ pɔfoɛ amukoraa, bɛ boso ónua! Nakoso bɛ bɔ bekuro wɔ dwirɛ de, maa bɛyɛ kyɛ eyia bɔ ɔbɔ gyireingyirein ɔ.” Na asomdwee wale aseɛ ne aso afoɛ aburanna.

english_verse: Then once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord, so he let the nation of Midian control Israel for seven years.
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ yɔle bɔ ɔte bɔne wɔ AWURADE nyunu ɔ, na AWURADE fale bɛ wurale Midian sa afoɛ nzoo.

english_verse: The Midianites were so cruel that many Israelites ran to the mountains and hid in caves.
translation_verse: Midian lili Yisrael so, na ɔnate Midian ti, Yisraelfoɛ bɔle bɛ nwo adwaa wɔ mmokaa so, nyɔboɛ bɔ wasi sua mɔ nu, ɔne anwoserɛ afealeɛ mɔ nu.

english_verse: Every time the Israelites planted crops, the Midianites invaded Israel together with the Amalekites and other eastern nations.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ mmerɛ biala bɔ Yisraelfoɛ kɔyɔ eboo ne, né Midianfoɛ ne Amalɛkefoɛ ne eyia afiteleɛfoɛ bafa ngondii baateta bɛ.

english_verse: They rode in on their camels, set up their tents, and then let their livestock eat the crops as far as the town of Gaza. The Midianites stole food, sheep, cattle, and donkeys. Like a swarm of locusts, they could not be counted, and they ruined the land wherever they went.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ Midianfoɛ ne bɛ nyɛmmoa mɔ bagua berɛ mitimiti kyɛ ngyein, na bɛfa b’ɛtena sua mɔ po bɛboka so bɛba. Bɛ ne b’afupɔngɔ mɔ, sɛ ɛka bɛ po a, ennwu bɛ noa. Yiti bɛba a, bɛsɛkye aseɛ ne aso nningyein amukoraa.

english_verse: I am your God, and I told you not to worship Amorite gods, even though you are living in the land of the Amorites. But you refused to listen. The Lord Chooses Gideon
translation_verse: Na nga ngyirele ɛmɔ kyɛ, ‘Me ole AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ; Amorifoɛ bɔ ɛmɔte b’aseɛ so ne, nnɛma ɛmɔsɔne bɛ nyameɛ mɔ.’ Nakoso ɛmɔandie me dwirɛ.” Gideon

english_verse: One day an angel from the Lord went to the town of Ophrah and sat down under the big tree that belonged to Joash, a member of the Abiezer clan. Joash's son Gideon was nearby, threshing grain in a shallow pit, where he could not be seen by the Midianites.
translation_verse: AWURADE abɔfo hɔle ɔɔtenane Abieseniɛ Yoase eluii ne abo wɔ Ofra. Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Yoase awa Gideon ɔboro atokoɔ wɔ kumaa bɔ betwi nzaa nu ɔ nu, ofikyɛ né ɔfa fea Midianfoɛ.

english_verse: The angel appeared and spoke to Gideon, “The Lord is helping you, and you are a strong warrior.”
translation_verse: AWURADE abɔfo ne yele ye nwo ali hyirele Gideon, na osele ye kyɛ, “Koɛhonɛniɛ ahoneserɛniɛ, AWURADE gyi wɔ si.”

english_verse: Gideon answered, “Please don't take this wrong, but if the Lord is helping us, then why have all of these awful things happened? We've heard how the Lord performed miracles and rescued our ancestors from Egypt. But those things happened long ago. Now the Lord has abandoned us to the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Gideon buale ye kyɛ, “Me mene, sɛ AWURADE gyi yɛ si a, nzu ati yeɛ amaneɛ he amukoraa atoto yɛ ye? Ye anwanwadeɛ mbiri mbiri bɔ yɛ nana mɔ hane ye nwo dwirɛ hyirele yɛ kyɛ, ‘Aso nna AWURADE yeɛ ɔyele yɛ fili Misraim’ ne, bɛ wɔ ni? Kekesaala ye de, AWURADE aye ye sa yɛ bo, na wafa yɛ wawura Midian sa.”

english_verse: Then the Lord himself said, “Gideon, you will be strong, because I am giving you the power to rescue Israel from the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE pɛle ye nye neane ye sele kyɛ, “Anwoserɛ bɔ ele ye ne, fa kɔ kole Yisraelfoɛ fi Midian sa nu. Me yeɛ masoma wɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: Gideon replied, “But how can I rescue Israel? My clan is the weakest one in Manasseh, and everyone else in my family is more important than I am.”
translation_verse: Gideon buale kyɛ, “Me mene, me yeɛ nne nwa bɔ mekora mepepɛ mede Yisrael ɔ? Manase abusua kure nu, m’abusua yeɛ yɛte awiɛmvoɛ koraa ɔ, na m’abusua nu koso, me yeɛ nde kãa paa ɔ.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “It's hard to believe that I'm actually talking to the Lord. Please do something so I'll know that you really are the Lord.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Gideon sele AWURADE kyɛ, “Sɛ anya alo me de a, né nzaade maa nwu sɛngyerɛnneɛ bɔ okyire kyɛ wɔ yeɛ ɛne me dwudwo ye.

english_verse: And wait here until I bring you an offering.” “All right, I'll wait,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Mesrɛ wɔ ala, nnɛfi wa kɔ, kɔpem kyɛ ngɔwa wɔ nyunu, na ngɔfa m’afɔleɛ ngoosie wɔ nyunu ɔ.” Yeɛ AWURADE sele ye kyɛ, “Ngɔnwondɛ wa maa okoodwu kyɛ ekosa kɔwa ɔ.”

english_verse: Gideon went home and killed a young goat, then started boiling the meat. Next, he opened a big sack of flour and made it into thin bread. When the meat was done, he put it in a basket and poured the broth into a clay cooking pot. He took the meat, the broth, and the bread and placed them under the big tree.
translation_verse: Yiti Gideon hɔle ye awuro oohuni abɔngye akrɔngrɔma ko tone, na ɔfale esam olonka buru yɔle taterɛ kabrɛdi. Ɔfale naen ne guale kɛndɛen nu, yeɛ ɔfale turoo ne guale kukue nu, na ɔfa brɛle ye wɔ eluii ne abo.

english_verse: God's angel said, “Gideon, put the meat and the bread on this rock, and pour the broth over them.” Gideon did as he was told.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE abɔfo sele Gideon kyɛ, “Fa naen ne ne taterɛ kabrɛdi ne gua nyɔbotaen he aso na hwie turoo ne gua so.” Na ɔyɔle sɔ.

english_verse: The angel was holding a walking stick, and he touched the meat and the bread with the end of the stick. Flames jumped from the rock and burned up the meat and the bread. When Gideon looked, the angel was gone.
translation_verse: Yeɛ AWURADE abɔfo ne, pɔmaa bɔ otira ye ne, ɔfale ye noa ne hane naen ne ɔne taterɛ kabrɛdi ne. Na see gye fili nyɔbotaen ne anu ɔɔyerale naen ne ɔne taterɛ kabrɛdi ne. Na AWURADE abɔfo ne, otu minini fili Gideon nyunu.

english_verse: Gideon realized that he had seen one of the Lord's angels. “Oh!” he moaned. “Now I'm going to die.”
translation_verse: Afei Gideon nwuni kyɛ AWURADE abɔfo ɔ; na Gideon sele kyɛ, “Dé me oo, AWURADE Nyameɛ! Ofikyɛ magyina AWURADE abɔfo nyunu manwu ye nyunu.”

english_verse: “Calm down!” the Lord told Gideon. “There's nothing to be afraid of. You're not going to die.”
translation_verse: Nakoso AWURADE sele ye kyɛ, “Asomdwee ha wɔ. Nnɛsuro, na engowu.”

english_verse: Gideon built an altar for worshiping the Lord and called it “The Lord Calms Our Fears.” It still stands there in Ophrah, a town in the territory of the Abiezer clan. Gideon Tears Down Baal's Altar
translation_verse: Gideon sili afɔleɛ bokyea mane AWURADE wɔ berɛ, na ɔtole afɔleɛ bokyea ne dumaa AWURADE te Asomdwee. Afɔleɛ bokyea ne tɛ gyi Abiesefoɛ kuro Ofra nu maa waadwu ɛnɛ.

english_verse: That night the Lord spoke to Gideon again: Get your father's second-best bull, the one that's seven years old. Use it to pull down the altar where your father worships Baal and cut down the sacred pole next to the altar.
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne kɔngɔen, AWURADE sele Gideon kyɛ, “Fa wɔ baba nandwie nyii bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ, bɔ wali afoɛ nzoo ne. Bubu wɔ baba ye Baal afɔleɛ bokyea ne gua, ná pɛ bosoen Asera dosii bɔ ɔwɔ ye ngyɛnu berɛ ne to.

english_verse: Then build an altar for worshiping me on the highest part of the hill where your town is built. Use layers of stones for my altar, not just a pile of rocks. Cut up the wood from the pole, make a fire, kill the bull, and burn it as a sacrifice to me.
translation_verse: Si afɔleɛ bokyea ma AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ wɔ bokaa he ti afia, ná hyehyɛ afɔleɛ bokyea nyɔboɛ ne pɛpɛɛpɛ. Afei fa nandwie nyii bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ne, ná fa bosoen Asera dosii bɔ ɛkɔpɛ ne boka so bɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ.”

english_verse: Gideon chose ten of his servants to help him, and they did everything God had said. But since Gideon was afraid of his family and the other people in Ophrah, he did it all at night.
translation_verse: Yiti Gideon fale ye somvoɛ nemɔ anu buru, na ɔyɔle kyɛbɔ AWURADE sele ye ne ala. Nakoso né osuro ye abusuafoɛ ɔne kuro berɛ ama, yiti wanyɔ ye eyia na mmom ɔyɔle ye kɔngɔen. Gideon bubu Baal afɔleɛ bokyea

english_verse: When the people of the town got up the next morning, they saw that Baal's altar had been knocked over, and the sacred pole next to it had been cut down. Then they noticed the new altar covered with the remains of the sacrificed bull.
translation_verse: Kuro berɛ ama dwɔsole ngyerɛmɔ tutuutu ne, benwuni kyɛ ebie abubu Baal afɔleɛ bokyea ne, ebie apɛ bosoen Asera dosii bɔ ogyi ye ngyɛnu berɛ ne wato ase, na ebie afa nandwie nyii bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ne wabɔ afɔleɛ wɔ afɔleɛ bokyea bɔ basi ne aso.

english_verse: “Who could have done such a thing?” they asked. And they kept on asking, until finally someone told them, “Gideon the son of Joash did it.”
translation_verse: Yiti bebisabisale bɛ nwo kyɛ, “Nwa yeɛ wayɔ sɔ nikyee ye?” Bebisabisale nu dee ne, bɛtele kyɛ Yoase awa Gideon yeɛ wayɔ sɔ nikyee ne ɔ.

english_verse: The men of the town went to Joash and said, “Your son Gideon knocked over Baal's altar and cut down the sacred pole next to it. Hand him over, so we can kill him!”
translation_verse: Yiti kuro berɛ ama sele Yoase kyɛ, “Ye ɛwa ne bra wa maa yɛhu ye, ofikyɛ wabubu Baal afɔleɛ bokyea ne, yeɛ bosoen Asera dosii bɔ ogyi afɔleɛ bokyea ne ngyɛnu ne koso, wapɛ wato.”

english_verse: The crowd pushed closer and closer, but Joash replied, “Are you trying to take revenge for Baal? Are you trying to rescue Baal? If you are, you will be the ones who are put to death, and it will happen before another day dawns. If Baal really is a god, let him take his own revenge on someone who tears down his altar.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Yoase sele mmenia bɔ bedwɔso betiale ye ne amukoraa kyɛ, “Aso ɛmɔ yeɛ odi kyɛ ɛmɔko bɛma Baal ɔ? Anaa ɛmɔ yeɛ odi kyɛ ɛmɔko ye ti ngondii ɔ? Ebiala bɔ ɔkɔho kɔma Baal ne, kyɛ odwu ɛhema ngyerɛmɔ ne, odi kyɛ beku ye. Sɛ Baal te nyameɛ a, ɛ́mɔma ye bɔbɔ ɔho ye ngondii, ofikyɛ ye afɔleɛ bokyea yeɛ babubu ye ɔ.”

english_verse: That same day, Joash changed Gideon's name to Jerubbaal, explaining, “He tore down Baal's altar, so let Baal take revenge himself.” Gideon Defeats the Midianites
translation_verse: Yiti sɔ kyẽa ne, bɛtole Gideon dumaa Yerubaal, bɔ ye bo ole: “Maa Baal ɔne ye beli,” ofikyɛ wabubu ye afɔleɛ bokyea.

english_verse: All the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations got together and crossed the Jordan River. Then they invaded the land of Israel and set up camp in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: Afei Midianfoɛ, Amalɛkefoɛ ɔne eyia afiteleɛfoɛ amukoraa bɛboale bɛ noa, bɛpɛle asue Yɔɔdan, na bɛɛkyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ Yesreel bɔnza ne anu dɔ.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of Gideon, and Gideon blew a trumpet as a signal for the men in the Abiezer clan to follow him.
translation_verse: Nakoso AWURADE Sunzum wale Gideon so, na ohuli totorobɛndo ne fa frɛle Abiesefoɛ amukoraa maa belili ye si.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, telling the men of these tribes to come and join his army. Then they set out toward the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Gideon tuli ɛbɔfoɛ maa bɛhɔle Manase aseɛ so amukoraa, na bɛbɔle bɛ amaneɛ maa bɛ koso beelili ye si. Osa tuli ɛbɔfoɛ maa bɛhɔle Asɛ, Sebulɔn ne Nafetali aseɛ so, na bɛ koso bɛɛbokale ye so. Nyameɛ ma Gideon sɛngyerɛnneɛ

english_verse: Gideon prayed to God, “I know that you promised to help me rescue Israel, but I need proof. Tonight I'll spread a sheep skin on the stone floor of that threshing-place over there. If you really will help me rescue Israel, then tomorrow morning let there be dew on the skin, but let the stone floor be dry.”
translation_verse: mekwaafa gyese meto nekaa bɔ bɛboro aburoo ne. Sɛ bosue gua gyese ne angome so, ná sɛ aseɛnwo berɛ amukoraa te wosee a, ye de ngole ngoli kyɛ ɛkɔfa me so kole Yisrael, kyɛbɔ aha ne.”

english_verse: And that's just what happened. Early the next morning, Gideon got up and checked the sheep skin. He squeezed out enough water to fill a bowl.
translation_verse: Na ɔwale nu sɔ. Odwɔsole ngyerɛmɔ tutuutu, ná ohwini gyese ne anu ne, bosue bɔ oguale gyese ne aso ne, onyane nzue komiti ko.

english_verse: But Gideon prayed to God again. “Don't be angry with me,” Gideon said. “Let me try this just one more time, so I'll really be sure you'll help me. Only this time, let the skin be dry and the stone floor be wet.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Gideon sele Nyameɛ kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, nnɛfɛ me so yaa. Maa mva edwirɛ bieku ndo wɔ nyunu. Ma nza mva gyese ne nzo nnea. Ma gyese ne angome ɔ́yɛ wosee, ná ma bosue ógua aseɛnwo berɛ amukoraa.”

english_verse: That night, God made the stone floor wet with dew, but he kept the sheep skin dry.
translation_verse: Na sɔ kyẽa ne kɔngɔen, Nyameɛ yɔle ye sɔ ala. Gyese ne angome yɛle wosee, na bosue guale aseɛnwo berɛ amukoraa.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Gideon and his army got up and moved their camp to Fear Spring. The Midianite camp was to the north, in the valley at the foot of Moreh Hill.
translation_verse: Yerubaal ɔne koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛboka ye so ne amukoraati, bedwɔsole ngyerɛmɔ tutuutu bɛɛkyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ Harode mbombonzue ne anwo. Né Midian asikyeleɛ wɔ bɛ sorɔ wɔ More bokaa ne anwo, wɔ bɔnza ne anu.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army is too big. I can't let you win with this many soldiers. The Israelites would think that they had won the battle all by themselves and that I didn't have anything to do with it.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Gideon kyɛ, “Koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛboka wɔ so bɔ mepena kyɛ mefa Midianfoɛ mewura bɛ sa ne, bɛsone soma. Ɔba ye sɔ a, Yisrael kɔhoahoa ye nwo kohyire me, ná waha kyɛ, ‘Me bɔbɔ m’anwoserɛ yeɛ wapepɛ wale me ɔ.’

english_verse: So call your troops together and tell them that anyone who is really afraid can leave Mount Gilead and go home.” Twenty-two thousand men returned home, leaving Gideon with only
translation_verse: Yiti bɔ ye dawure ma koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bɛte kyɛ, ‘Ebiala bɔ osuro ná ye kra anwati ne, osa ɔhɔ awuro.’ ” Na Gideon sale bɛ nu: bɛ nu apee aburanyɔ ne nyɔ sa hɔle, na apee buru de, bɛhale berɛ.

english_verse: but if you're still afraid, you and your servant Purah should sneak down to their camp.
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ esuro kyɛ ɛkɔfa koɛ kɔɔteta asikyeleɛ ne a, ye de ma wɔ somvoɛ Pura ɔne wɔ bɛhɔ.

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord said, “you still have too many soldiers. Take them down to the spring and I'll test them. I'll tell you which ones can go along with you and which ones must go back home.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ AWURADE sele Gideon kyɛ, “Koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bɛtɛ sone. Fa bɛ torotoro kɔ asue ne noa, ná ngɔsa bɛ nu wɔ dɔ ngɔma wɔ. Sɛ meka kyɛ, ‘Ɛne ɛhesɔa bɛhɔ’ a, ye de ɛne ye bɛhɔ. Yeɛ sɛ meka kyɛ ‘Nnɛma ɛne ɛhesɔa bɛkɔ’ a, onni kyɛ ɛne ye bɛkɔ.”

english_verse: When Gideon led his army down to the spring, the Lord told him, “Watch how each man gets a drink of water. Then divide them into two groups—those who lap the water like a dog and those who kneel down to drink.”
translation_verse: Yiti Gideon fale koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ torotoro hɔle asue ne noa; na AWURADE sele ye kyɛ, “Ebiala bɔ ɔkɔfa ye temverema kɔno nzue ne bie, kyɛbɔ kyẽa no nzue ne, maa ogyina bue ko. Yeɛ ebiala bɔ okobu ndwerɛ kɔfa ye noa kɔbɔ nzue ne anu kɔno bie ne, maa ye koso ogyina bue ko.”

english_verse: Three hundred men scooped up water in their hands and lapped it, and the rest knelt to get a drink.
translation_verse: Bɛ bɔ bele bɛ temverema bɛnone nzue ne bie ne, bɛ somaa te ɛyaa nza. Nakoso koɛhonɛfoɛ ngaa nemɔ de, bebuli ndwerɛ yeɛ bɛnone nzue ne bie ɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army will be made up of everyone who lapped the water from their hands. Send the others home. I'm going to rescue Israel by helping you and your army of
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Gideon kyɛ, “Mmenia ɛyaa nza bɔ bele bɛ temverema bɛnone nzue ne, ngɔfa bɛ so ngole ɛmɔ, ná mafa Midianfoɛ mawura wɔ sa. Ma bɛ ngaa ne amukoraa besa bɛ́hɔ b’awuro.”

english_verse: That night, the Lord said to Gideon. “Get up! Attack the Midianite camp. I am going to let you defeat them,
translation_verse: Sɔ kɔngɔen ne ala, AWURADE sele Gideon kyɛ, “Dwɔso, na fa koɛ kɔteta asikyeleɛ ne; ofikyɛ mafa mawura wɔ sa.”

english_verse: When you hear what the Midianites are saying, you'll be brave enough to attack.” Gideon and Purah worked their way to the edge of the enemy camp, where soldiers were on guard duty.
translation_verse: Kotie edwirɛ bɔ bɛkeka ɔ, na afei wɔ hue kɔyɛ se maa ɛkɔfa koɛ kɔɔteta asikyeleɛ ne.” Yeɛ Gideon ne ye somvoɛ Pura bɛhɔle beedwuli koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ b’asikyeleɛ ne tiwaa.

english_verse: The camp was huge. The Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations covered the valley like a swarm of locusts. And it would be easier to count the grains of sand on a beach than to count their camels.
translation_verse: Né Midianfoɛ, Amalɛkefoɛ ɔne eyia afiteleɛfoɛ nemɔ bayɛ bɔnza ne anu mitimiti kyɛ ngyein. B’afupɔngɔ mɔ de, bɛka a bennwu ye noa; ne bɛ somaa te kyɛ mboanoa anweaa.

english_verse: Gideon overheard one enemy guard telling another, “I had a dream about a flat loaf of barley bread that came tumbling into our camp. It hit the headquarters tent, and the tent flipped over and fell to the ground.”
translation_verse: Gideon oodwuli berɛ ne, né biaa bie ɔka ye laleɛ nu dwirɛ kyire obiɛngo kyɛ, “Ngyene laleɛ, nwuni kyɛ ayuo paanoo mumua ko amunu waatɔ Midian asikyeleɛ ne anu. Na oodwuli ɛtena sua ne anwo ne, ɔpemone ye maa otu tɔle; ɛtena sua ne gya tuatuale anwuro na ɔsɛkyele bɔkɔɔ.”

english_verse: The other soldier answered, “Your dream must have been about Gideon, the Israelite commander. It means God will let him and his army defeat the Midianite army and everyone else in our camp.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ obiɛngo ne buale kyɛ, “Laleɛ he de nna hwee ɔ; Yoase awa Yisraelniɛ Gideon, ye ngrandɛ ne ɔ. Nyameɛ afa Midian ne koɛhonɛfoɛ ne amukoraa wawura ye sa.”

english_verse: As soon as Gideon heard about the dream and what it meant, he bowed down to praise God. Then he went back to the Israelite camp and shouted, “Let's go! The Lord is going to let us defeat the Midianite army.”
translation_verse: Gideon tele kyɛ ɔka laleɛ ne anu dwirɛ ná okyire ye bo ne, ɔsɔnene AWURADE; na osa wale Yisrael asikyeleɛ ne anu oosele kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔdwɔso, ofikyɛ AWURADE afa Midian koɛhonɛfoɛ ne wawura ɛmɔ sa.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “When we get to the enemy camp, spread out and surround it. Then wait for me to blow a signal on my trumpet. As soon as you hear it, blow your trumpets and shout, ‘Fight for the Lord! Fight for Gideon!’ ”
translation_verse: Sɛ me ne koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa bɔ bɛboka me so ne, yɛhu totorobɛndo nemɔ a, ɛmɔ koso ɛ́mɔhu totorobɛndo nemɔ bɛfa asikyeleɛ ne anwo amukoraa bɛ́bra béyia, ná ɛ́mɔtea nu kyɛ, Yɛwɔ AWURADE ne Gideon bue nu!”

english_verse: Gideon and his group reached the edge of the enemy camp a few hours after dark, just after the new guards had come on duty. Gideon and his soldiers blew their trumpets and smashed the clay jars that were hiding the torches.
translation_verse: Abunnamu bɔ bɛsesane kuro berɛ awɛmvoɛ nemɔ nen, Gideon ne koɛhonɛfoɛ ɛyaa ko bɔ bɛboka ye so ne, bɛwale asikyeleɛ ne tiwaa. Behuli totorobɛndo nemɔ, na bɛbobɔle kwangoa bɔ né otiratira bɛ nemɔ.

english_verse: The rest of Gideon's soldiers blew the trumpets they were holding in their right hands. Then they smashed the jars and held the burning torches in their left hands. Everyone shouted, “Fight with your swords for the Lord and for Gideon!”
translation_verse: Na koɛhonɛfoɛ kure nza ne, behuli bɛ totorobɛndo nemɔ, na bɛbobɔle bɛ kwangoa nemɔ. Betiratirale ɛtɛen ne wɔ bɛ sa bɛen nu, yeɛ totorobɛndo bɔ behu ne koso wɔ bɛ sa famaa nu; na bɛteateane nu kyɛ, “AWURADE ne Gideon ngrandɛ!”

english_verse: The enemy soldiers started yelling and tried to run away. Gideon's troops stayed in their positions surrounding the camp
translation_verse: Koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ, bɛ mukoraa begyinagyinane Midian asikyeleɛ ne anwo bɛbra beyiale. Asikyeleɛ ne anu mmenia amukoraa bɛnwatili, na bɛnwati ne, né bɛbɔ awuye.

english_verse: and blew their trumpets again. As they did, the Lord made the enemy soldiers pull out their swords and start fighting each other. The enemy army tried to escape from the camp. They ran to Acacia Tree Town, toward Zeredah, and as far as the edge of the land that belonged to the town of Abel-Meholah near Tabbath.
translation_verse: Behuli totorobɛndo ɛyaa nza nemɔ nen, AWURADE mane Midian koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bɔbɔ bɛpɛle bɛ nwo bɛfale ngrandɛ behuhuni bɛ nwo. Na bɛnwatili toonn beedwuli Bete Sita. Bɛfale bɛ nye behyirele Serera beedwuli Abel Melola wɛen so, bɔ opingye Tabate ne.

english_verse: Gideon sent word for more Israelite soldiers to come from the tribes of Naphtali, Asher, and both halves of Manasseh to help fight the Midianites.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yisraelfoɛ frɛfrɛle bɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ befili Nafetali, Asɛ ɔne Manase amukoraa, na bɛpole Midianfoɛ nemɔ so.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to tell all the men who lived in the hill country of Ephraim, “Come and help us fight the Midianites! Put guards at every spring, stream, and well, as far as Beth-Barah before the Midianites can get to them. And guard the Jordan River.” Troops from Ephraim did exactly what Gideon had asked,
translation_verse: Gideon somane mmenia maa bɛhɔle Efraim mmokaa aseɛ ne amukoraa so beesele berɛ ama kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔtorotoro beeyia Midianfoɛ nemɔ, ná ɛ́mɔle asue Yɔɔdan befi bɛ sa nu maa oodwu Bete Bara.” Yiti Efraim mmienzua amukoraati boale bɛ noa, na beelele asue Yɔɔdan befili bɛ sa nu alaa maa oodwuli Bete Bara.

english_verse: and they even helped chase the Midianites on the east side of the Jordan River. These troops captured Raven and Wolf, the two Midianite leaders. They killed Raven at a large rock that has come to be known as Raven Rock, and they killed Wolf near a wine-pit that has come to be called Wolf Wine-Pit. The men of Ephraim brought the heads of the two Midianite leaders to Gideon.
translation_verse: Bɛpole Midianfoɛ so, na Midianfoɛ safohene nyɔ nemɔ bɔ bɛ ole Orebo ne Seebo ne, bɛhyele bɛ. Behuni Orebo wɔ Orebo nyɔbotaen ne anwo, yeɛ Seebo koso behuni ye wɔ Seebo nekaa bɔ betwi nzaa ne. Bɛpepɛle bɛ ti bɛfa bɛbrɛle Gideon wɔ asue Yɔɔdan si dɔ.

english_verse: But the men were really upset with Gideon and complained, “When you went to war with Midian, you didn't ask us to help! Why did you treat us like that?”
translation_verse: Afei Efraimfoɛ sele Gideon kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ dwirɛ yeɛ afa ali yɛ ye? Nzu ati yeɛ ɛne Midianfoɛ bɛkwaaho ne, amvrɛ yɛ ɔ?” Na behwili ye nyunu ɛyaa so.

english_verse: Gideon answered: Don't be upset! Even though you came later, you were able to do much more than I did. It's just like the grape harvest: The grapes your tribe doesn't even bother to pick are better than the best grapes my family can grow.
translation_verse: Yiti Gideon buale bɛ kyɛ, “Nikyee titire beni yeɛ mayɔ bɔ odwu bɔ ɛmɔayɔ ye ɔ? Aso Efraim bobe bɔ wate maa waha ye si ne, ɔnzone ɔndera Abiesa bobe abiribira?

english_verse: Besides, God chose you to capture Raven and Wolf. I didn't do a thing compared to you. By the time Gideon had finished talking, the men of Ephraim had calmed down and were no longer angry with him. Gideon Finishes Destroying the Midianite Army
translation_verse: Nyameɛ afa Midian safohene Orebo ne Seebo wawura ɛmɔ sa. Nikyee titire beni yeɛ mahora mayɔ bɔ odwu bɔ ɛmɔayɔ ye ɔ?” Ɔhane sɔ ne, b’ahone bɔ wahu ne tɔle nzue nu.

english_verse: The town of Succoth was nearby, so he went there and asked, “Please give my troops some food. They are worn out, but we have to keep chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the two Midianite kings.”
translation_verse: Yiti Gideon srɛle Sukotefoɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔma me mmenia bɔ beli me si ye aleɛ kãa. Ɛhɔen apɛ bɛ, na mefoa Midian ahemvo Seba ne Samuna mekɔkye bɛ.”

english_verse: The town leaders of Succoth answered, “Why should we feed your army? We don't know if you really will defeat Zebah and Zalmunna.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Sukote mbanyi buale kyɛ, “Aso wɔ sa anya aha Seba ne Samuna, bɔ yɛma wɔ lɔen ne aleɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: “Just wait!” Gideon said. “After the Lord helps me defeat them, I'm coming back here. I'll make a whip out of thorns and rip the flesh from your bones.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Gideon sele kyɛ, “Yoo, mate. Sɛ AWURADE fa Seba ne Samuna wura me sa a, ngɔfa ɛserɛ so agurɛ ne ɛfone ngofi ɛmɔ ma ɛmɔ nwonaen kɔtete.”

english_verse: After leaving Succoth, Gideon went to Penuel and asked the leaders there for some food. But he got the same answer as he did at Succoth.
translation_verse: Gideon fili berɛ ne, ɔhɔle Penuel, na ɔɔsrɛle bɛ sɔ ala. Na Penuelfoɛ buale ye kyɛbɔ Sukotefoɛ buale ye ne ala.

english_verse: “I'll come back safe and sound,” Gideon said, “but when I do, I'm going to tear down your tower!”
translation_verse: Yiti osele Penuelfoɛ kyɛ, “Sɛ medi ngonim ná mesa meba a, ngobubu abandenden he ngogua.”

english_verse: Gideon went to the town officials and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna. Remember how you made fun of me? You said, ‘We don't know if you really will defeat those two Midianite kings. So why should we feed your worn-out army?’ ”
translation_verse: Afei Gideon hɔle Sukotefoɛ berɛ, na osele kyɛ, “Seba ne Samuna bɛ ɛhe. Bɛ nwo ti yeɛ ɛmɔhane me ayinga kyɛ, ‘Aso wɔ sa anya aha Seba ne Samuna, bɔ yiti wɔ koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bafɛ ye, yɛma bɛ aleɛ ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Gideon reached the enemy camp by going east along Nomad Road past Nobah and Jogbehah. He made a surprise attack,
translation_verse: Yiti Gideon fale teaseɛnam atee bɔ ɔla Noba ne Yobeha eyia afiteleɛ so ne aso, na oofuni koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ anu fale koɛ tetale bɛ.

english_verse: and the enemy panicked. Zebah and Zalmunna tried to escape, but Gideon chased and captured them.
translation_verse: Midian ahemvo nyɔ bɔ bɛ ole Seba ne Samuna ne, bɛnwatili. Gideon foane bɛ ɔɔhyele bɛ, na ɔmane bɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ ne amukoraati bɛbɔle aya.

english_verse: After the battle, Gideon set out for home. As he was going through Heres Pass,
translation_verse: Yoase awa Gideon fi koɛ noa ɔba ne, ɔfale Herese pambaa ne aso.

english_verse: he caught a young man who lived in Succoth. Gideon asked him who the town officials of Succoth were, and the young man wrote down
translation_verse: Ɔhyele Sukote aberandeɛ ko, na ɔmaa ɔhyerɛle Sukote atitire ne mbanyi mɔ dumaa mane ye. Né bɛte aburasoo ne nzoo.

english_verse: Gideon made a whip from thorn plants and used it to beat the town officials.
translation_verse: Yiti Gideon hyele kuro berɛ mbanyi, na ɔfale ɛserɛ so agurɛ ne ɛfone bole kuro berɛ ama hyirele bɛ nworɛ.

english_verse: Afterwards he went to Penuel, where he tore down the tower and killed all the town officials.
translation_verse: Obubuli Penuel abandenden ne guale ase, na ohuhuni kuro berɛ mmienzua nemɔ.

english_verse: Then Gideon said, “Zebah and Zalmunna, tell me about the men you killed at Tabor.” “They were a lot like you,” the two kings answered. “They were dignified, almost like royalty.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ obisale Seba ne Samuna kyɛ, “Mmienzua bɔ ɛmɔhuhuni bɛ wɔ Tabɔ ne, bɛ sue te sɛɛ?” Bebuale kyɛ, “Bɛ nu biala te kyɛ wɔ ala; besoma mmenia bɔ bɛ se te ɛhene ɔ.”

english_verse: “They were my very own brothers!” Gideon said. “I swear by the living Lord that if you had let them live, I would let you live.”
translation_verse: Na Gideon buale kyɛ, “Nniɛma mɔ ɛne, me ne bɛ yɛfi niɛ. Kyɛ AWURADE te ase ye, sɛ ɛmɔyakyili bɛ maa benyane bɛ ti bedidili nu a, ahaa mengohu ɛmɔ.

english_verse: kilograms. In addition, there was the gold from the camels' ornaments and from the beautiful jewelry worn by the Midianite kings. Gideon also took their purple robes.
translation_verse: Yiti osele ye bamuɛbaa Yeta kyɛ, “Kɔ kohũ bɛ!” Nakoso aberandeɛ ne andwe ye ngrandɛ. Né osuro, ofikyɛ né ɔtɛ te abɛɛmaa.

english_verse: “What's the matter, Gideon?” Zebah and Zalmunna asked. “Do it yourself, if you're not too much of a coward!” Gideon jumped up and killed them both. Then he took the gold ornaments from the necks of their camels. The Israelites Ask Gideon To Be Their King
translation_verse: Yeɛ Seba ne Samuna hane kyɛ, “Bra na baahu yɛ, na kyɛ bɔ sona te ne, sɔ ala yeɛ ye anwoserɛ te ɔ.” Yiti Gideon dwɔsole oohuni Seba ne Samuna; na ɔyeyele mbembenanneɛ bɔ ɔya b’afupɔngɔ nemɔ ne. Gideon yɔ amoen

english_verse: After the battle with the Midianites, the Israelites said, “Gideon, you rescued us! Now we want you to be our king. Then after your death, your son and then your grandson will rule.”
translation_verse: Na Yisraelfoɛ sele Gideon kyɛ, “Di yɛ so hene, ɛne ɛwa ne w’anomaa koso; ofikyɛ ale yɛ afi Midian sa nu.”

english_verse: “No,” Gideon replied, “I won't be your king, and my son won't be king either. Only the Lord is your ruler.
translation_verse: Gideon buale bɛ kyɛ, “Me de mengoli ɛmɔ so hene, yeɛ mma koso ngoli ɛmɔ so hene; mmom AWURADE yeɛ okoli ɛmɔ so hene ɔ.”

english_verse: But I will ask you to do one thing: Give me all the earrings you took from the enemy.” The enemy soldiers had been Ishmaelites, and they wore gold earrings.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Gideon toale so sele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔma nzrɛ ɛmɔ nikyee ko: Koɛ nu nzesadeɛ asomade bɔ ebiala wanya ye ne, ɔ́ma me ko.”

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers replied, “Of course we will give you the earrings.” Then they spread out a robe on the ground and tossed the earrings on it.
translation_verse: Na bebuale ye kyɛ, “Yɛkofia yɛ kunu yɛkɔfa yɛkɔma wɔ.” Yiti bɛfale ɛtena bɛsɛle berɛ, na bɛ nu biala fale koɛ nzesadeɛ asomade bɔ wanya ye ne anu ko tole so.

english_verse: The total weight of this gold was nearly
translation_verse: Esikaa kɔkorɛ asomade bɔ bɛfa bɛmane Gideon ne, nu nonɛ te kilo buru ne ngona .

english_verse: Gideon had many wives and
translation_verse: Gideon wole mma mmienzua aburasoo, ofikyɛ ogyale mmraa pee.

english_verse: He even had a wife who lived at Shechem. They had a son, and Gideon named him Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ɔne ye sómaa bɔ ɔwɔ Sɛkem ne koso bɛwole baa bienzua, na ɔtole ye dumaa Abimɛlɛke.

english_verse: Gideon lived to be an old man. And when he died, he was buried in the family tomb in his hometown of Ophrah, which belonged to the Abiezer clan.
translation_verse: Yoase awa Gideon nyini yɛle aworowaa posoposo koraka yeɛ owu ɔ, na besiele ye wɔ ɔse Yoase ye nyɔboɛ sua nu wɔ Abiesefoɛ kuro Ofra.

english_verse: Soon after Gideon's death, the Israelites turned their backs on God again. They set up idols of Baal and worshiped Baal Berith as their god.
translation_verse: Gideon wuli pɛ yeɛ Yisraelfoɛ hyɛle ye bo besa bɛɛsɔnene Baal mɔ ɔ, na bɛfale Baal Berite bɛkakyili bɛ nyameɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites forgot that the Lord was their God, and that he had rescued them from the enemies who lived around them.
translation_verse: AWURADE bɛ Nyameɛ bɔ olele bɛ fili bɛ pɔfoɛ amukoraa sa nu wɔ nekaa biala ne de, Yisraelfoɛ mane bɛ wora fili ye.

english_verse: Besides all that, the Israelites were unkind to Gideon's family, even though Gideon had done so much for Israel.
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ Yerubaal , ɔyɔle nningyein paa pee mane Yisrael de, nakoso bɛyele ye awuro ama boniayɛ.

english_verse: Abimelech's uncles talked it over with the leaders of Shechem who agreed, “Yes, it would be better for one of our relatives to be king.”
translation_verse: Yiti oni awuro ama nemɔ gyinane ye gya nu bɛtole sɔ dwirɛ ne amukoraa beguale Sɛkem mbanyi amukoraa bɛ so anu, na mbanyi nemɔ lele Abimɛlɛke bɛtole nu, ofikyɛ bɛhane kyɛ, “Abimɛlɛke de, yɛ bɔbɔ yɛ deɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Abimelech and his soldiers went to his father's home in Ophrah and brought out Gideon's other sons to a large rock, where they murdered all
translation_verse: Ɔhɔle ɔse awuro berɛ wɔ Ofra, na oliɛma mmienzua mɔ bɔ bɛ ole Yerubaal mma aburasoo ne, ohuhuni bɛ wɔ nyɔboɛ komapɛ aso. Nakoso Yotam bɔ ɔte Yerubaal kasiɛ ne de, onyane ye ti didili nu, ofikyɛ ɔnwatili ɔɔfeale.

english_verse: The leaders of Shechem, including the priests and the military officers, met at the tree next to the sacred rock in Shechem to crown Abimelech king.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sɛkem ne Bete Milo mbanyi amukoraati bɛbɔle nu, na bɛhɔle beesili Abimɛlɛke ɛhene wɔ eluii ne abo. Eluii ne pingye bonima bɔ ɔwɔ Sɛkem ne. Yotam bu mmakaa nwo anyandera

english_verse: Jotham heard what they were doing. So he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim and shouted down to the people who were there at the meeting: Leaders of Shechem, listen to me, and maybe God will listen to you.
translation_verse: Bɛfale edwirɛ bɔ wasi ne nwo amaneɛ bɛbɔle Yotam nen, oogyinane Gerisim bokaa ne ti afia, na ɔteane nu sele bɛ kyɛ, “Sɛkem mbanyi, ɛ́mɔtie me, amaa Nyameɛ koso watie ɛmɔ.”

english_verse: Once the trees searched for someone to be king; they asked the olive tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Mmakaa mɔ sili nu, kyɛ bɛkwaapopa bɛ nu ko ngoo ma odi bɛ so hene. Yiti besele olive kyɛ, ‘Di yɛ so hene.’

english_verse: But the olive tree replied, “My oil brings honor to people and gods. I won't stop making oil, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Na olive buale bɛ kyɛ, ‘Aso me ngoo paa, bɔ bɛfa so bɛhyɛ nyameɛ mɔ ne adasa animnyam ne, nyakyi ye yɔlɛ, ná ngongyini mmakaa mɔ so anaa?’

english_verse: Then they asked the fig tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Yeɛ mmakaa nemɔ sele borɔdoma kyɛ, ‘Bra na baali yɛ so hene.’

english_verse: But the fig tree replied, “I won't stop growing my delicious fruit, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Nakoso borɔdoma buale bɛ kyɛ, ‘Aso me mma menemene ne, ɔne me mmaa fɛɛfɛɛ ne, nyakyi bɛ sulɛ, ná ngongyini mmakaa mɔ so anaa?’

english_verse: Next they asked the grape vine, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Na mmakaa nemɔ sele bobe kyɛ, ‘Bra na baali yɛ so hene.’

english_verse: But the grape vine replied, “My wine brings cheer to people and gods. I won't stop making wine, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Nakoso bobe buale bɛ kyɛ, ‘Aso me nzaa, bɔ ɔma nyameɛ mɔ ne adasa bɛ nye gye ne, nyakyi ye yɔlɛ, ná ngongyini mmakaa mɔ so anaa?’

english_verse: Finally, they went to the thornbush and asked, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Yiti mmakaa ne amu besele ɛfone kyɛ, ‘Bra ná baali yɛ so hene.’

english_verse: The thornbush replied, “If you really want me to be your king, then come into my shade and I will protect you. But if you're deceiving me, I'll start a fire that will spread out and destroy the cedars of Lebanon.” After Jotham had finished telling this story, he said:
translation_verse: Yeɛ ɛfone buale mmakaa nemɔ kyɛ, ‘Sɛ ɛmɔ kunu fitaa yeɛ ɛmɔpopa me ngoo bɛfa me bedi ɛmɔ so hene ne a, ye de ɛmɔbra bɛɛfea me nyaa abo fɔnwoo ne anu. Nakoso sɛ nna ɛmɔ kunu fitaa de a, ye de see ófi ɛfone nu, ná ɔɔyera Lebanon sida mmakaa nemɔ.’

english_verse: My father Gideon risked his life for you when he fought to rescue you from the Midianites. Did you reward Gideon by being kind to his family? No, you did not! You attacked his family and killed all
translation_verse: Nakoso ɛnɛ ye de, ɛmɔayɛ me baba awuro ama nwo lɔen. Ɛmɔahu ye mma mmienzua aburasoo wɔ nyɔboɛ komapɛ aso, na Abimɛlɛke bɔ ɔte ye afaneɛ awa ne, ɛmɔafa ye bali Sɛkem mbanyi so hene, ɔnate kyɛ ɔte ɛmɔ abusuaniɛ ne ati.

english_verse: So, you leaders of Shechem, if you treated Gideon and his family the way you should have, then I hope you and Abimelech will make each other very happy.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɛnɛ ɛmɔ ne Yerubaal ne ye awuro ama bali ye yé wɔ adwene paa nu ne animnyam nu a, ye de ɔnate Abimɛlɛke ti, ɛ́mɔma ɛmɔ nye gye, ná ye koso ɔnate ɛmɔ ti, ɔ́ma ye nye gye.

english_verse: But if it was wrong to treat Gideon and his family the way you did, then I pray that Abimelech will destroy you with fire, and I pray that you will do the same to him.
translation_verse: Na sɛ nna sɔ yeɛ ɔte hɔ a, ye de see ófi Abimɛlɛke nu ɔɔyera Sɛkem ne Bete Milo mbanyi; ná see ófi Sɛkem ne Bete Milo mbanyi mɔ nu ɔɔyera Abimɛlɛke.”

english_verse: Jotham ran off and went to live in the town of Beer, where he could be safe from his brother Abimelech. Abimelech Destroys Shechem
translation_verse: Afei Yotam nwati hɔle Beɛ ɔɔtenane berɛ; ofikyɛ né osuro oliɛma Abimɛlɛke. Sɛkemfoɛ yɛ Abimɛlɛke nwo lɔen

english_verse: Abimelech had been a military commander of Israel for three years,
translation_verse: Abimɛlɛke lili Yisrael so afoɛ nza.

english_verse: Then they sent some men to hide on the hilltops and watch for Abimelech and his troops, while they sent others to rob everyone that went by on the road. But Abimelech found out what they were doing.
translation_verse: Yiti Sɛkem mbanyi mane mmenia bɛɛtetɛle Abimɛlɛke wɔ mmokaa nemɔ ati afia. Na ebiala bɔ ɔfale atee ne aso ɔɔpɛle nu bɛ nwo berɛ ne, belele ye nwo nningyein. Na ebiemɔ bɛɛbɔle Abimɛlɛke amaneɛ.

english_verse: One day, Gaal son of Ebed went to live in Shechem. His brothers moved there too, and soon the leaders of Shechem started trusting him.
translation_verse: Ebede awa Gaal ne ye awuro ama betu bɛwale Sɛkem, na Sɛkem mbanyi fale bɛ wora wurale ye nu.

english_verse: The time came for the grape harvest, and the people of Shechem went into their vineyards and picked the grapes. They gathered the grapes and made wine. Then they went into the temple of their god and threw a big party. There was a lot of eating and drinking, and before long they were cursing Abimelech.
translation_verse: Bɛhɔle fieso, na bɛɛtetele bobe befili bɛ bobe boo mɔ nu. Behwini bɛyɛle nzaa, na bɛfa bɛgyele bɛ nye. Yeɛ bɛhɔle bɛ bosoen asɔneyɛɛ sua nu. Bedidili bɛnone, na bɛgorole Abimɛlɛke nwo.

english_verse: Gaal said: Hamor was the founder of Shechem, and one of his descendants should be our ruler. But Abimelech's father was Gideon, so Abimelech isn't really one of us. He shouldn't be our king, and we shouldn't have to obey him or Zebul, who rules Shechem for him.
translation_verse: Na Ebede awa Gaal sele kyɛ, “Abimɛlɛke te nzu bɔ yɛ Sɛkemfoɛ odi kyɛ yɛso ye ɔ? Sɔ Yerubaal awa ne, ɔne ye safohene Sebul, aso banzo Sɛkem ɔse Hamɔ ye mmenia? Nzu ati yeɛ odi kyɛ yɛso ye ɔ?

english_verse: If I were the ruler of Shechem, I'd get rid of that Abimelech. I'd tell him, “Get yourself an even bigger army, and we will still defeat you.”
translation_verse: Sɛ me yeɛ ndua mmenia ye noa a, ahaa matu Abimɛlɛke mafi bia so; ahaa mahã mahyire ye kyɛ, Fa mmenia bieku boka wɔ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ aso, ná bra maa yɛho.”

english_verse: Zebul was angry when he found out what Gaal had said.
translation_verse: Kuro berɛ odikro Sebul tele edwirɛ bɔ Ebede awa Gaal hane ne, ɔfɛle yaa paa.

english_verse: And so he sent some messengers to Abimelech. But they had to pretend to be doing something else, or they would not have been allowed to leave Shechem. Zebul told the messengers to say: Gaal the son of Ebed has come to Shechem along with his brothers, and they have persuaded the people to let Gaal rule Shechem instead of you.
translation_verse: Otuli ɛbɔfoɛ maa bɛhɔle Abimɛlɛke berɛ wɔ Aruma beesele ye kyɛ, “Edwirɛ asi. Ebede awa Gaal ne ye awuro ama bawa Sɛkem, na bɛto begua kuro berɛ ama so anu maa bɛyɛ wɔ nwo lɔen.

english_verse: This is what I think you should do. Lead your army here during the night and hide in the fields.
translation_verse: Yiti ɛne koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛboka wɔ so ne, ɛmɔhɔ bɛɛtetɛ eburo dɔ kɔngɔen.

english_verse: Get up the next morning at sunrise and rush out of your hiding places to attack the town. Gaal and his followers will come out to fight you, but you will easily defeat them.
translation_verse: Na ngyerɛmɔ tutuutu, eyia pukye pɛ, kɔfa koɛ toa kuro ne. Na sɛ Gaal ne koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛboka ye so ne, bɛfa koɛ bɛbayia wɔ a, ɛne bɛ ho pasaa kyɛ bɔ ɛkɔhora ɔ.”

english_verse: So one night, Abimelech led his soldiers to Shechem. He divided them into four groups, and they all hid near the town.
translation_verse: Yiti Abimɛlɛke ne ye koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa bedwɔsole kɔngɔen na bɛhyɛle bɛ nu kure nna bɛɛtetɛle Sɛkem kuro ne anwo.

english_verse: The next morning, Gaal went out and stood in the opening of the town gate. Abimelech and his soldiers left their hiding places,
translation_verse: Ebede awa Gaal fitele oogyinane kuro berɛ pambim ne anyunu, na Abimɛlɛke ne ye koɛhonɛfoɛ, befili nekaa bɔ bɛɛtetɛle ne befitele.

english_verse: and Gaal saw them. Zebul was standing there with Gaal, and Gaal remarked, “Zebul, that looks like a crowd of people coming down from the mountaintops.” “No,” Zebul answered, “it's just the shadows of the mountains. It only looks like people moving.”
translation_verse: Na Gaal nwuni bɛ ne, osele Sebul kyɛ, “Nea, mmenia biemɔ bɛtorotoro bokaa ne bɛba! Sebul buale ye kyɛ, “Bokaa ne aso wawoɛ mɔ yeɛ bayɛ wɔ nye so kyɛ mmenia ne.”

english_verse: “But Zebul, look over there,” Gaal said. “There's a crowd coming down from the sacred mountain, and another group is coming along the road from the tree where people talk with the spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Gaal sa sele kyɛ, “Nea, mmenia nemɔ befi Tabure Erese yeɛ bɛba ɔ, na kure ko fi Elon Meonenim bue nu dɔ yeɛ bɛba ɔ.”

english_verse: Then Zebul replied, “What good is all of your bragging now? You were the one who said Abimelech shouldn't be the ruler of Shechem. Out there is the army that you made fun of. So go out and fight them!”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sebul bisale ye kyɛ, “Wɔ noa nu dwirɛ mbiri ne, afei de ayakyi ye hanɛ? Ná wɔ yeɛ ɛhane kyɛ, ‘Abimɛlɛke te nzu bɔ odi kyɛ yɛso ye ɔ’ ne?” Koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ ɛgorole bɛ nwo ne, bɛ ɛhe. Afei kɔ na ɛne bɛ bɛɛho.”

english_verse: Gaal and the leaders of Shechem went out and fought Abimelech.
translation_verse: Yiti Gaal lili Sɛkem mbanyi nemɔ nyunu, na ɔne Abimɛlɛke bɛɛhone.

english_verse: Soon the people of Shechem turned and ran back into the town. However, Abimelech and his troops were close behind and killed many of them along the way.
translation_verse: Abimɛlɛke foane Gaal, na ɔnwati fili ye nyunu. Mmenia pee totɔle, na bɛsamone berɛ maa oodwuli kuro berɛ pambim ne.

english_verse: Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul forced Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
translation_verse: Yiti Abimɛlɛke tenane Aruma; na Sebul foane Gaal ne ye awuro ama bɔ wamma bandena Sɛkem ko ɔ.

english_verse: The next morning, the people of Shechem were getting ready to work in their fields as usual, but someone told Abimelech about it.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, Sɛkemfoɛ fale bɛ nye hyirele eburo. Na Abimɛlɛke tele ne,

english_verse: Abimelech divided his army into three groups and set up an ambush in the fields near Shechem. When the people came out of the town, he and his army rushed out from their hiding places and attacked.
translation_verse: ɔboaboale ye koɛhonɛfoɛ noa. Ɔhyɛle bɛ nu kure nza maa bɛɛtetɛle eburo dɔ. Abimɛlɛke nwuni kyɛ mmenia nemɔ fi kuro ne anu bɛba ne, ɔfale koɛ tetale bɛ huhuni bɛ.

english_verse: Abimelech and the troops with him ran to the town gate and took control of it, while two other groups attacked and killed the people who were in the fields.
translation_verse: Abimɛlɛke ne koɛhonɛfoɛ kure bɔ né bɛboka ye so ne, bɛbɔle hwii beegyinane kuro berɛ pambim ne anyunu. Yeɛ kure nyɔ bɔ baha ne, bɛ koso bɛfale koɛ bɛɛtetale mmenia bɔ bɛwɔ eburo dɔ ne amukoraa behuhuni bɛ.

english_verse: He and his troops fought in Shechem all day, until they had killed everyone in town. Then he and his men tore down the houses and buildings and scattered salt everywhere.
translation_verse: Abimɛlɛke ne kuro berɛ ama bɛhone sɔ kyẽa ne amukoraa. Olili kuro ne aso ngonim, na ohuhuni nu ama. Odwirili kuro ne guale ase bɔle ye tɔɔ, na ɔtole ngyee petene so.

english_verse: Earlier that day, the leaders of the temple of El Berith at Shechem had heard about the attack. So they went into the temple fortress,
translation_verse: Sɛkem abandenden nwo mbanyi amukoraa, bɛtele edwirɛ ne pɛ, beewurale Ɛl Berite asɔneyɛɛ sua anwoserɛ afealeɛ ne anu.

english_verse: but Abimelech found out where they were.
translation_verse: Abimɛlɛke tele kyɛ Sɛkem abandenden nwo mbanyi amukoraa baaboa bɛ noa.

english_verse: He led his troops to Mount Zalmon, where he took an ax and chopped off a tree branch. He lifted the branch onto his shoulder and shouted, “Hurry! Cut off a branch just as I did.”
translation_verse: Yiti Abimɛlɛke ne koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛboka ye so ne amukoraa, bɛhɔle Salmon bokaa ne aso. Ɔfale akumaa pepɛle bakaa bie mmaen, na ɔpagya tole ye kɔme anwo. Afei osele ye koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “Nikyee bɔ ɛmɔanwu kyɛ mayɔ ne, ɛmɔ koso ɛ́mɔhã bɛ nwo bɛyɔ bie.”

english_verse: When they all had branches, they followed Abimelech back to Shechem. They piled the branches against the fortress and set them on fire, burning down the fortress and killing about
translation_verse: Yiti koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ anu biala pɛle bakaa mmaen kyɛbɔ Abimɛlɛke yɔle ne ala, na ɔfa ookisale anwoserɛ afealeɛ ne. Bɛtole afealeɛ ne anu see bɔ né mmenia ne tɛ wɔ nu ɔ. Sɛkem abandenden ne anu mmenia amukoraa wuwuli. Bɛte mmienzua ne mmrasua kɔyɛ apee ko.

english_verse: After destroying Shechem, Abimelech went to Thebez. He surrounded the town and captured it.
translation_verse: Afei Abimɛlɛke hɔle Tebese ootuale kuro ne, na olili so ngonim.

english_verse: But there was a tall fortress in the middle of the town, and the town leaders and everyone else went inside. Then they barred the gates and went up to the flat roof.
translation_verse: Nakoso né abandenden pindinn bie wɔ kuro ne aso. Kuro ne aso mmienzua ne mmrasua amukoraa, ɔne berɛ mbanyi amukoraa bɛnwatili bɛɛfeale nu bɛtole bɛ nwo anoa nu. Bɛfo bɛhɔle abandenden ne aso anwuro nekaa bɔ basamo so ne.

english_verse: Abimelech and his army rushed to the fortress and tried to force their way inside. Abimelech himself was about to set the heavy wooden doors on fire,
translation_verse: Abimɛlɛke oodwuli abandenden ne anwo. Ɔfale koɛ tetale abandenden ne alaa oodwuli abandenden ye anoa nu, kyɛ ɔfa see to nu.

english_verse: when a woman on the roof dropped a large rock on his head and cracked his skull.
translation_verse: Nakoso braa bie yakyili nyɔkoa nu maa ɔɔbɔle Abimɛlɛke ti anu, na ɔpakyele ye ti kwangoa.

english_verse: The soldier who carried his weapons was nearby, and Abimelech told him, “Take out your sword and kill me. I don't want people to say that I was killed by a woman!” So the soldier ran his sword through Abimelech.
translation_verse: Berɛ ne ala, Abimɛlɛke frɛle aberandeɛ bɔ otira ye akodeɛ ne sele ye kyɛ, “Twe wɔ ngrandɛ ná ku me, amaa mmenia banga bamva me nwo kyɛ, ‘Brasua yeɛ ohuni ye ɔ.’ ” Yiti aberandeɛ ne hwene ye ngrandɛ fa wɔle ye maa owuli.

english_verse: And when the Israelite soldiers saw that their leader was dead, they went back home.
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ nwuni kyɛ Abimɛlɛke awu ne, bɛ mukoraa bɛhɔle awuro.

english_verse: That's how God punished Abimelech for killing his brothers and bringing shame on his father's family.
translation_verse: Yiti bɔne bɔ Abimɛlɛke yɔ tiale ye baba, kyɛ ohuhuni oliɛma mmienzua aburasoo ne, Nyameɛ tuale ye so kerɛ.

english_verse: God also punished the people of Shechem for helping Abimelech. Everything happened just as Jotham's curse said it would.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ mane Sɛkemfoɛ bɛ bɔne amukoraa bɔle bɛ ti so, na Yerubaal awa Yotam ɛnomalɛ ne wale bɛ so.

english_verse: Tola was the next person to rescue Israel. He belonged to the Issachar tribe, but he lived in Shamir, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His father was Puah, and his grandfather was Dodo.
translation_verse: Abimɛlɛke wue asi ne, Tola bɔ ɔse ole Pua bɔ ye koso ɔse ole Dodo bɔ ofi Yisaka abusua kure nu ne, otuli ye nwo siele berɛ kyɛ ɔkɔpepɛ kole Yisrael. Samiri bɔ ɔwɔ Efraim mmokaa aseɛ so ne, berɛ yeɛ né Tola te ɔ.

english_verse: The next leader of Israel was Jair, who lived in Gilead. He was a leader for
translation_verse: Tola wue asi ne, Gileadeniɛ Yari tuli ye nwo siele berɛ buli Yisrael maen ne afoɛ aburanyɔ ne nyɔ.

english_verse: When he died, he was buried in the town of Kamon. Israel Is Unfaithful to God
translation_verse: Yari wuli na besiele ye wɔ Kamon. Yisrael wura Amonfoɛ bo

english_verse: Before long, the Israelites began disobeying the Lord by worshiping Baal, Astarte, and gods from Syria, Sidon, Moab, Ammon, and Philistia.
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ sa yɔle bɔ ɔte bɔne wɔ AWURADE nyunu ɔ. Bɛsɔnene Baal ne Astarote mɔ, Siria nyameɛ mɔ, Sidon nyameɛ mɔ, Moabo nyameɛ mɔ, Amonfoɛ nyameɛ mɔ, yeɛ Filistifoɛ nyameɛ mɔ. Yiti bɛyakyili AWURADE si lilɛ, na banzɔne ye.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and decided to let Philistia and Ammon conquer them.
translation_verse: Ɔnate so ma AWURADE fɛle Yisrael so yaa paa, na ɔfale bɛ wurale Filistifoɛ ɔne Amonfoɛ sa.

english_verse: The leaders of Gilead asked each other, “Who can lead an attack on the Ammonites?” Then they agreed, “If we find someone who can lead the attack, we'll make him the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Na Gileadefoɛ bɛ safohene nemɔ sisele bɛ nwo kyɛ, “Nwa yeɛ okoli moa kɔfa koɛ kɔɔteta Amonfoɛ ɔ? Sɔ sona ne yeɛ ɔkɔla Gileadefoɛ amukoraa bɛ noa ɔ.”

english_verse: Then the Ammonites began crossing the Jordan and attacking the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Life was miserable for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Amonfoɛ koso pɛle asue Yɔɔdan bɛhɔle ye si, na bɛfale koɛ bɛɛtetale Yuda, Benyamin yeɛ Efraim boso ama; na ɛhe mane Yisrael nwo hyerele ye paa.

english_verse: They begged the Lord for help and confessed, “We were unfaithful to you, our Lord. We stopped worshiping you and started worshiping idols of Baal.”
translation_verse: Yiti Yisraelfoɛ sũ frɛle AWURADE kyɛ, “Yayɔ bɔne yatia wɔ, ofikyɛ wɔ bɔ ɛte yɛ Nyameɛ ne, yayakyi wɔ si lilɛ yaaso Baal mɔ.”

english_verse: But I'm not going to rescue you any more! You've left me and gone off to worship other gods. If you're in such big trouble, go and cry to them for help!
translation_verse: Nyameɛ mɔ bɔ ɛmɔafa ɛmɔ ti baawura bɛ bo ne, ɛmɔɔsu behyire bɛ maa bele ɛmɔ wɔ ɛmɔ anwokyere mmerɛ ye anu.”

english_verse: “We have been unfaithful to you,” the Israelites admitted. “If we must be punished, do it yourself, but please rescue us from the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Na Yisraelfoɛ sele AWURADE kyɛ, “Yayɔ bɔne, yiti bɔ wɔ bɔbɔ ekuro biala, fa di yɛ. Nakoso, pepɛ de yɛ kekesaala ye!”

english_verse: Then the Israelites got rid of the idols of the foreign gods, and they began worshiping only the Lord. Finally, there came a time when the Lord could no longer stand to see them suffer. The Ammonites Invade Gilead
translation_verse: Yiti begyili Amaenmaensofoɛ nyameɛ mɔ bɔ bɛwɔ bɛ berɛ ne beguale, na bɛsole AWURADE. Na Yisrael amaneɛnwunɛ ne yɛle AWURADE ahomete.

english_verse: The rulers of Ammon called their soldiers together and led them to Gilead, where they set up camp. The Israelites gathered at Mizpah and set up camp there.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Amonfoɛ yɛle koɛ nwo anwoboa, na bɛɛkyekyele b’asikyeleɛ wɔ Gileade. Yisraelfoɛ koso boale bɛ noa, na bɛɛkyekyele b’asikyeleɛ wɔ Misepa.

english_verse: “Please come back to Gilead! If you lead our army, we will be able to fight off the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Besele Yɛfeta kyɛ, “Bra baayɛ yɛ safohene, maa yɛ ne Amonfoɛ yɛho.”

english_verse: “Didn't you hate me?” Jephthah replied. “Weren't you the ones who forced me to leave my family? You're only coming to me now because you're in trouble.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Yɛfeta buale Gileade mbanyi nemɔ kyɛ, “Aso nna ɛmɔ komapɛ ye ala yeɛ ɛmɔpole me, ná ɛmɔfoane me befili me baba awuro ɔ? Nzu ati yeɛ ɛnɛ bɔ ɛmɔ nwo ahyere ɛmɔ ye, ɛmɔba me berɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: “But we do want you to come back,” the leaders said. “And if you lead us in battle against the Ammonites, we will make you the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Na Gileade mbanyi sele Yɛfeta kyɛ, “Ɛhe ati yeɛ yasa yawa wɔ gya so ɔ, kyɛ ɛne yɛ hɔ ma yɛne Amonfoɛ yɛɛho, ná da yɛ Gileadefoɛ amukoraa yɛ noa.”

english_verse: “All right,” Jephthah said. “If I go back with you and the Lord lets me defeat the Ammonites, will you really make me your ruler?”
translation_verse: Yɛfeta buale Gileade mbanyi nemɔ kyɛ, “Sɛ ɛmɔsa bɛfa me bɛkɔ me kuro maa me ne Amonfoɛ yɛkɔko, ná sɛ AWURADE fa bɛ wura me sa a, ye de ngɔla ɛmɔ noa.”

english_verse: “You have our word,” the leaders answered. “And the Lord is a witness to what we have said.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Gileade mbanyi sele Yɛfeta kyɛ, “AWURADE yeɛ ɔte yɛ ne wɔ adanzeɛ ɔ: yɛkoli bɔ aha ne aso pɛpɛɛpɛ.”

english_verse: So Jephthah went back to Mizpah with the leaders of Gilead. The people of Gilead gathered at the place of worship and made Jephthah their ruler. Jephthah also made promises to them.
translation_verse: Yiti Yɛfeta ne Gileade mbanyi nemɔ sili nu bɛhɔle, na Gileadefoɛ bɔle ye bɛ so panyi ne safohene. Na Yɛfeta fale ye dwirɛ amukoraa tole AWURADE nyunu wɔ Misepa.

english_verse: After the ceremony, Jephthah sent messengers to say to the king of Ammon, “Are you trying to start a war? You have invaded my country, and I want to know why!”
translation_verse: Afei Yɛfeta tuli ɛbɔfoɛ maa bɛhɔle Amonfoɛ hene berɛ beesele ye kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ dwirɛ yeɛ ɔwɔ me ne wɔ yɛ afia bɔ ye ti yeɛ ɛbaafa koɛ ɛtoa me maen ye?”

english_verse: The king of Ammon replied, “Tell Jephthah that the land really belongs to me, all the way from the Arnon River in the south, to the Jabbok River in the north, and west to the Jordan River. When the Israelites came out of Egypt, they stole it. Tell Jephthah to return it to me, and there won't be any war.”
translation_verse: Na Amonfoɛ hene buale Yɛfeta ɛbɔfoɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “Ofikyɛ Yisrael fili Misraim wale ne, oolele m’aseɛ bɔ ofi asue Anɔn ɔkwaadwu asue Yabɔko ɔne asue Yɔɔdan noa fili me sa nu. Yiti sɛ enguro wɔ nwo dwirɛ a, sa fa me nikyee ma me.”

english_verse: Jephthah sent the messengers back to the king of Ammon,
translation_verse: Yɛfeta sa tuli ɛbɔfoɛ maa bɛhɔle Amonfoɛ hene gya so

english_verse: and they told him that Jephthah had said: Israel hasn't taken any territory from Moab or Ammon.
translation_verse: beesele ye kyɛ, “Yɛfeta nwa nyoo: Yisrael amva Moabo aseɛ anaakyɛ Amonfoɛ aseɛ,

english_verse: When the Israelites came from Egypt, they traveled across the desert to the Red Sea and then to Kadesh.
translation_verse: na mmom Yisraelfoɛ fili Misraim bɛwale ne, bɛfale ɛserɛ ne aso beedwuli Ɛpo Kɔkorɛ ne noa, na bɛtoale so beedwuli Kadese.

english_verse: They sent messengers to the king of Edom and said, “Please, let us go through your country.” But the king of Edom refused. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he wouldn't let them cross his country either. And so the Israelites stayed at Kadesh.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yisrael tuli ɛbɔfoɛ maa bɛhɔle Edom hene berɛ beesele ye kyɛ, ‘Maa yɛfa w’aseɛ ye aso yɛpɛ nu yɛhɔ’; nakoso Edom hene ambene so. Yisrael sa tuli ɛbɔfoɛ maa bɛhɔle Moabo hene berɛ, nakoso wambene so. Yiti Yisrael tenane Kadese.

english_verse: A little later, the Israelites set out into the desert, going east of Edom and Moab, and camping on the eastern side of the Arnon River gorge. The Arnon is the eastern border of Moab, and since the Israelites didn't cross it, they didn't even set foot in Moab.
translation_verse: Afei bɛtoale so bɛfale ɛserɛ ne aso, na bɛkondone bɛɛfale Edom aseɛ ne noa ɔne Moabo aseɛ ne noa. Beedwuli Moabo aseɛ ne eyia afiteleɛ so, na bɛkyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ asue Anɔn si dɔ. Bamva Moabo aseɛ ne aso, ofikyɛ né asue Anɔn yeɛ ɔte Moabo ɛwɛen ɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites sent messengers to the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon. “Please,” they said, “let our people go through your country to get to our own land.”
translation_verse: Afei Yisrael tuli ɛbɔfoɛ maa bɛhɔle Amorifoɛ hene Sihon bɔ né odi hene Hesebon ne berɛ; na Yisrael srɛle ye kyɛ, ‘Maa yɛfa w’aseɛ ye aso yɛpɛ nu yɛhɔ yɛ maen deɛ so.’

english_verse: towns between Aroer and Minnith, and others as far as Abel-Keramim. After that, the Ammonites could not invade Israel any more. Jephthah's Daughter
translation_verse: Nakoso Sihon wanne Yisrael wanni, yiti wamma ye ate maa wamva ye aseɛ ne aso. Na Sihon boaboale ye koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraati noa. Bɛkyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ Yahase, na bɛ ne Yisrael hone.

english_verse: But the Lord God helped Israel defeat Sihon and his army. Israel took over all of the Amorite land where Sihon's people had lived,
translation_verse: Yeɛ AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ fale Sihon ne ye mmenia amukoraa wurale Yisrael sa, na Yisraelfoɛ lili bɛ so ngonim. Yiti Amorifoɛ bɔ bɛ yeɛ né bɛte maen ne anu ne, Yisrael fale b’aseɛ amukoraa.

english_verse: from the Arnon River in the south to the Jabbok River in the north, and from the desert in the east to the Jordan River in the west.
translation_verse: Bɛtenane Amorifoɛ aseɛ ne amukoraati so fi asue Anɔn kɔpem asue Yabɔko, yeɛ afei fi ɛserɛ ne aso kɔpem asue Yɔɔdan.

english_verse: The messengers also told the king of Ammon that Jephthah had said: The Lord God of Israel helped his nation get rid of the Amorites and take their land. Now do you think you're going to take over that same territory?
translation_verse: Na afei, AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ ne lele aseɛ ne fili Amorifoɛ sa nu fa mane ye maen Yisrael. Aso ɛpena kyɛ ede aseɛ ne fi Yisraelfoɛ sa nu anaa?

english_verse: If Chemosh your god takes over a country and gives it to you, don't you have a right to it? And if the Lord takes over a country and gives it to us, the land is ours!
translation_verse: Aso nna nikyee bɔ wɔ nyameɛ Kemose wafa wama wɔ ne yeɛ odi kyɛ ɛfa ɔ? Nikyee biala bɔ AWURADE yɛ Nyameɛ wali so ngonim wafa wama yɛ ne, aso nna yɛ yeɛ odi kyɛ yɛfa ɔ?

english_verse: Are you better than Balak the son of Zippor? He was the king of Moab, but he didn't quarrel with Israel or start a war with us.
translation_verse: Sipore awa Balake bɔ né ɔte Moabo hene ne, aso ɛte paa tra ye? Aso ɔfale ye dwirɛ wale Yisrael so le, anaa ɔfale koɛ ɔtoale Yisrael le?

english_verse: I haven't done anything to you, but it's certainly wrong of you to start a war. I pray that the Lord will show whether Israel or Ammon is in the right.
translation_verse: Nna me yeɛ mayɔ wɔ tɛɛ ɔ, na mmom wɔ yeɛ ayɔ me tɛɛ bɔ ɛfa koɛ batoa me ɔ. AWURADE bɔ ɔte ndɛenbualɛniɛ ne, ɛnɛ okohyire Yisraelfoɛ ne Amonfoɛ bɛ nu horɛ bɔ ye dwirɛ yɛ fɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: But the king of Ammon paid no attention to Jephthah's message.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yɛfeta ngraa bɔ ɔmaa bɛfa bɛɛmane Amonfoɛ hene ne, wamva wanyɛ dwirɛ. Yɛfeta hyɛ bɔ

english_verse: Then the Lord's Spirit took control of Jephthah, and Jephthah went through Gilead and Manasseh, raising an army. Finally, he arrived at Mizpah in Gilead, where
translation_verse: Yeɛ AWURADE Sunzum kanyane Yɛfeta, na Yɛfeta ɔɔpɛle nu Gileade ne Manase. Ɔtoale so hɔle Misepa bɔ ɔwɔ Gileade ne. Ofili Misepa bɔ ɔwɔ Gileade, na ɔpɛle nu fale koɛ ɔɔtoale Amonfoɛ.

english_verse: he promised the Lord, “If you will let me defeat the Ammonites
translation_verse: Na Yɛfeta hyɛle AWURADE bɔ kyɛ, “Sɛ ɛfa Amonfoɛ wura me sa a,

english_verse: and come home safely, I will sacrifice to you whoever comes out to meet me first.”
translation_verse: ye de sɛ medi Amonfoɛ so ngonim meyie ná mesa meba a, sona bɔ okofi m’awuro kofite kooyia me ne, ɔkɔyɛ AWURADE deɛ, na ngɔfa ye ngɔbɔ ɛyeralɛ afɔleɛ.”

english_verse: From Mizpah, Jephthah attacked the Ammonites, and the Lord helped him defeat them.
translation_verse: Yiti Yɛfeta pɛle nu hɔle Amonfoɛ berɛ ɔfale koɛ ɔɔtetale bɛ, na AWURADE fale bɛ wurale ye sa.

english_verse: When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, the first one to meet him was his daughter. She was playing a tambourine and dancing to celebrate his victory, and she was his only child.
translation_verse: Afei Yɛfeta sa wale ye awuro wɔ Misepa. Na edwirɛ nwanwa! Ɔwa brasua ne le akasaa ne abilie fitele kyɛ ɔbaayia ye! Né odi ye bahorɛ. Né olle baa bienzua anaa baa brasua ko boka ye so.

english_verse: “Oh no!” Jephthah cried. Then he tore his clothes in sorrow and said to his daughter, “I made a sacred promise to the Lord, and I must keep it. Your coming out to meet me has broken my heart.”
translation_verse: Yɛfeta nwuni ye pɛ, osunzuale ye bɔbɔ ye ndaadeɛ nu, na osele kyɛ, Yieee, mma, ate m’ahone! Afa edwirɛ awura me paa! Ofikyɛ mahyɛ AWURADE bɔ, na mengɔhora mengɔhwe mengosa.”

english_verse: “Father,” she said, “you made a sacred promise to the Lord, and he let you defeat the Ammonites. Now, you must do what you promised, even if it means I must die.
translation_verse: Na osele ɔse kyɛ, “Baba, sɛ ahyɛ AWURADE bɔ de a, ye de kekesaala ye bɔ AWURADE amaa atɔ wɔ pɔfoɛ Amonfoɛ so wereɛ ye, kyɛbɔ ato wɔ noa nu tui aha ne, fa sɔ ala yɔ me.”

english_verse: But first, please let me spend two months, wandering in the hill country with my friends. We will cry together, because I can never get married and have children.”
translation_verse: Na ɔtoale so sele ɔse kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ nikyee ko, na yɔ ma me: Ma me ate bosome nyɔ maa ngongyini mmokaa nemɔ aso, ná me ne me mmango mɔ yɛɛbɔ awuye, ofikyɛ mékɔ wue bɔ ndɛte ababunu bɔ onnwuni biaa le ɔ.”

english_verse: “Yes, you may have two months,” Jephthah said. She and some other girls left, and for two months they wandered in the hill country, crying because she could never get married and have children.
translation_verse: Yɛfeta buale ye kyɛ, “Atee la ase.” Na ɔmane ye ate bosome nyɔ. Yiti ɔne ye mmango mɔ bɛhɔle mmokaa nemɔ aso, na bɛɛbɔle awuye wɔ ye ababunuyɛlɛ, bɔ wannwu biaa le, bɔ ɔfa kɔ wue ne anwo.

english_verse: Then she went back to her father. He did what he had promised, and she never got married. That's why
translation_verse: Bosome nyɔ ne ayieleɛ, osa wale ye baba berɛ, na ye baba fale ye yɔle nikyee bɔ wahyɛ ye nwo bɔ ne. Né onnwuni biaa le. Yiti ɛhe mane amammerɛ bie ɔɔlale berɛ mane Yisraelfoɛ kyɛ,

english_verse: every year, Israelite girls walk around for four days, weeping for Jephthah's daughter.
translation_verse: afoɛ biala, Yisrael mmrasua betu ɛlɛnna besie berɛ bekosu Gileadeniɛ Yɛfeta ɔwa brasua ne.

english_verse: The men of the Ephraim tribe got together an army and went across the Jordan River to Zaphon to meet with Jephthah. They said, “Why did you go to war with the Ammonites without asking us to help? Just for that, we're going to burn down your house with you inside!”
translation_verse: Efraimfoɛ frɛfrɛle bɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ, na bɛpɛle nu bɛhɔle Safon beesele Yɛfeta kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛpɛle nu ɛne Amonfoɛ bɛɛhone, ná amvrɛ yɛ maa yɛne wɔ angɔ ɔ? Yɛkɔyera wɔ sua ne yɛkɔfra wɔ!”
