english_verse: “But I did ask for your help,” Jephthah answered. “That was back when the people of Gilead and I were having trouble with the Ammonites, and you wouldn't do a thing to help us.
translation_verse: Yɛfeta buale bɛ kyɛ, “Amonfoɛ bɔ né bɛhyɛ yɛ so yeayea ne, me ne me mmenia mɔ yɛne bɛ nyane ngondii. Nakoso mvrɛle ɛmɔ ne, ɛmɔambepɛ banne me bamvi bɛ sa nu.

english_verse: So when we realized you weren't coming, we risked our lives and attacked the Ammonites. And the Lord let us defeat them. There's no reason for you to come here today to attack me.”
translation_verse: Na nwuni kyɛ ɛmɔngɔpepɛ bengole me ne, mvale me ngoa ndole serewa, mbɛle ɛwɛen ne mvale koɛ ngɔndetale Amonfoɛ, na AWURADE fale bɛ wurale me sa. Nzu ati yeɛ ɛnɛ ye de ɛmɔawa me so bɔ ɛmɔ ne me baaho ye?”

english_verse: But the men from Ephraim said, “You people of Gilead are nothing more than refugees from Ephraim. You even live on land that belongs to the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh.” So Jephthah called together the army of Gilead, then they attacked and defeated the army from Ephraim.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yɛfeta boaboale Gileade koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa noa, na ɔne Efraim bɛɛhone, ofikyɛ Efraimfoɛ sele kyɛ, “Ɛmɔ Gileadefoɛ, ɛmɔte mmenia bɔ ɛmɔabɔ ko bafi Efraim ne Manase ɔ.” Na Gileadefoɛ lili Efraim so ngonim.

english_verse: The army of Gilead also posted guards at all the places where the soldiers from Ephraim could cross the Jordan River to return to their own land. Whenever one of the men from Ephraim would try to cross the river, the guards would say, “Are you from Ephraim?” “No,” the man would answer, “I'm not from Ephraim.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Gileadefoɛ hɔle asue Yɔɔdan apɛleɛ nemɔ beegyinagyinane berɛ, kyɛbɔ Efraimfoɛ bengonya ate bɛngɔnwati ɔ. Na Efraimfoɛ bɔ bɛnwati ne, sɛ bɛ nu bie ka kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔma mbɛ asue ne” a, né Gileadefoɛ babisa ye kyɛ, “Ɛte Efraimniɛ anaa?” Na sɛ obua kyɛ “Daabi” a,

english_verse: The guards would then tell them to say “Shibboleth,” because they knew that people of Ephraim could say “Sibboleth,” but not “Shibboleth.” If the man said “Sibboleth,” the guards would grab him and kill him right there. Altogether,
translation_verse: né base ye kyɛ, nzaade ka ‘Hyibolɛte’ maa yɛtie. Ɔnate kyɛ ɔngora nga ‘Hyibolɛte’ yé ne ati, ɔka ye ‘Sibolɛte’. Sɛ ɔba ye sɔ a, Gileadefoɛ kye sɔ sona ne beku ye wɔ asue Yɔɔdan apɛleɛ berɛ. Efraimfoɛ apee aburanna ne nyɔ yeɛ bɛtotɔle sɔ mmerɛ ne ɔ.

english_verse: Jephthah was a leader of Israel for six years, before he died and was buried in his hometown Mizpah in Gilead. Ibzan
translation_verse: Yɛfeta buli Yisrael maen ne afoɛ nzia. Afei Yɛfeta wuli, na besiele ye wɔ ye kuro wɔ Gileade. Yibesan, Elon, Abedon

english_verse: Ibzan, the next leader of Israel, came from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Yɛfeta wue asi ne, Yibesan bɔ ofi Betlehem yeɛ obuli Yisrael maen ne ɔ.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Bethlehem. Elon
translation_verse: Afei Yibesan wuli, na besiele ye wɔ Betlehem.

english_verse: Elon from the Zebulun tribe was the next leader of Israel. He was a leader for ten years,
translation_verse: Yibesan wue asi ne, Sebulɔnniɛ Elon yeɛ obuli Yisrael maen ne ɔ, na obuli Yisrael maen ne afoɛ buru.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Aijalon that belonged to the Zebulun tribe. Abdon
translation_verse: Afei Sebulɔnniɛ Elon wuli, na besiele ye wɔ Ayalɔn, wɔ Sebulɔn aseɛ so.

english_verse: Abdon the son of Hillel was the next leader of Israel. He had
translation_verse: Piratonniɛ Hilel awa Abedon wuli, na besiele ye wɔ Piraton, wɔ Efraim aseɛ so, wɔ Amalɛkefoɛ mmokaa aseɛ ne aso.

english_verse: Once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let the Philistines take control of Israel for
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ sa yɔle bɔ ɔte bɔne wɔ AWURADE nyunu ɔ, na AWURADE fale bɛ wurale Filistifoɛ sa afoɛ aburanna.

english_verse: Manoah from the tribe of Dan lived in the town of Zorah. His wife was not able to have children,
translation_verse: Né biaa bie wɔ berɛ bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Manoa. Ofi Dan abusua kure nu, na ye kuro ole Sora. Né ɔye te mmotaen bɔ ɔwwole baa le ɔ.

english_verse: She went to Manoah and said, “A prophet who looked like an angel of God came and talked to me. I was so frightened, that I didn't even ask where he was from. He didn't tell me his name,
translation_verse: Na braa ne hɔle ɔɔbɔle ohu amaneɛ kyɛ, “Nyameɛ sona bie wale me berɛ, na osoma Nyameɛ abɔfo. Ye nwo yɛ suro paa. Mammisa ye nekaa horɛ bɔ ofi wale ɔ, yeɛ ye koso wammɔ ye dumaa wangyire me.

english_verse: but he did say that I'm going to have a baby boy. I'm not supposed to drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Our son will belong to God for as long as he lives.”
translation_verse: Nakoso osele me kyɛ, ‘Ɛkɔnwonzɛ kɔwo baa bienzua. Yiti nnɛno bobe nzaa anaa nzaa serɛserɛ biala, yeɛ nnɛdi nikyee biala bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ, ofikyɛ akwadaa ne kɔyɛ nasiriteniɛ kɔma Nyameɛ fi ye aworɛ nu kɔpem kyẽa bɔ okowu ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Then Manoah prayed, “Our Lord, please send that prophet again and let him tell us what to do for the son we are going to have.”
translation_verse: Na Manoa srɛle AWURADE kyɛ, “O AWURADE, mesrɛ wɔ, Nyameɛ sona bɔ ɛsomane ye ne, maa osa bra yɛ wa, ná oohyire yɛ nikyee bɔ ɔsɛ kyɛ yɛyɔ yɛfa akwadaa bɔ yɛbaawo ye ne anwo ɔ.”

english_verse: God answered Manoah's prayer, and the angel went back to Manoah's wife while she was resting in the fields. Manoah wasn't there at the time,
translation_verse: Nyameɛ tiele Manoa mbaeɛ ne, na Nyameɛ abɔfo ne sa hɔle braa ne berɛ wɔ mmerɛ bɔ né ɔte berɛ wɔ fieso ɔ. Nakoso ohu Manoa de, né ɔnne ye nwo berɛ bie.

english_verse: so she found him and said, “That same man is here again! He's the one I saw the other day.”
translation_verse: Yiti braa ne tuli amirika oosele ohu kyɛ, “Biaa bɔ ɛlɛho ne ɔwale me wa ne, wasa waaye ye nwo ali wahyire me.”

english_verse: Manoah went with his wife and asked the man, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?” “Yes, I am,” he answered.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Manoa dwɔsole lili ɔye asi hɔle biaa ne berɛ, na obisale ye kyɛ, “Aso wɔ yeɛ ɛɛhane edwirɛ hyirele braa he ne?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Yoo, me ɔ.”

english_verse: Manoah then asked, “When your promise comes true, what rules must he obey and what will be his work?”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Manoa bisale kyɛ, “Sɛ wɔ dwirɛ ne ba nu a, nzikyɛ nhyehyɛleɛ yeɛ ɔfa akwadaa ne anwo ɔ? Nzikyɛ yeɛ odi kyɛ ɔyɔ ɔ?

english_verse: “Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her,” the Lord's angel answered.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE abɔfo ne sele Manoa kyɛ, “Odi kyɛ braa ne di edwirɛ bɔ mahã mahyire ye ne amukoraati so.

english_verse: “She must not eat or drink anything made from grapes. She must not drink wine or beer or eat anything forbidden by God's laws. I told her exactly what to do.”
translation_verse: Onni kyɛ odi nikyee biala bɔ ofi bobe nu ɔ. Onni kyɛ ɔno bobe nzaa anaa nzaa serɛserɛ biala, yeɛ onni kyɛ odi nikyee biala bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ. Ahyɛdeɛ bɔ mahyɛ mama ye ne amukoraati, odi kyɛ odi so.”

english_verse: “Please,” Manoah said, “stay here with us for just a little while, and we'll fix a young goat for you to eat.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Manoa sele AWURADE abɔfo ne kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, tena yɛ nwo wa kãa maa yɛhu abɔngye akrɔngrɔma ko maa eli.”

english_verse: Manoah didn't realize that he was really talking to one of the Lord's angels. The angel answered, “I can stay for a little while, although I won't eat any of your food. But if you would like to offer the goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, that would be fine.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE abɔfo ne buale Manoa kyɛ, “Sɛ ɛmaa metena wɔ nwo wa po a, mengoli w’aleɛ. Nakoso sɛ ekuro kyɛ ɛbɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ a, ye de bɔ ma AWURADE.”

english_verse: Manoah said, “Tell us your name, so we can honor you after our son is born.”
translation_verse: Afei Manoa bisale AWURADE abɔfo ne kyɛ, “Bɛfrɛ wɔ sɛ, amaa sɛ wɔ dwirɛ ne ba nu a, yahyɛ wɔ animnyam?”

english_verse: “No,” the angel replied. “You don't need to know my name. And if you did, you couldn't understand it.”
translation_verse: Nakoso AWURADE abɔfo ne buale ye kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ebisa me dumaa ɔ? Me dumaa ne te dumaa bɔ ɔyɛ nwanwa paa ɔ.”

english_verse: So Manoah took a young goat over to a large rock he had chosen for an altar, and he built a fire on the rock. Then he killed the goat, and offered it with some grain as a sacrifice to the Lord. But then an amazing thing happened.
translation_verse: Yiti Manoa fale abɔngye akrɔngrɔma ne, ɔne aburoo afɔleɛ ne, na ɔfa bɔle afɔleɛ wɔ nyɔbotaen ne aso mane AWURADE. Anwanwadeɛ bie sili bɔ né Manoa ne ɔye bɛ nye tua ɔ.

english_verse: The fire blazed up toward the sky, and the Lord's angel went up toward heaven in the fire. Manoah and his wife bowed down low when they saw what happened.
translation_verse: See gye fili afɔleɛ bokyea ne aso hɔle nyameɛso. Na AWURADE abɔfo ne fale afɔleɛ bokyea see bɔ ogye ne anu hɔle anwuro bɔ né Manoa ne ɔye bɛ nye tua ɔ. Na bɛfale bɛ nyunu bebutubutuli ase.

english_verse: Although the angel didn't appear to them again, they realized he was one of the Lord's angels.
translation_verse: AWURADE abɔfo ne wanye ye nwo ali wangyire Manoa ne ɔye ko. Ɛhe mane Manoa nwuni kyɛ AWURADE abɔfo ɔ.

english_verse: Manoah said, “We have seen an angel. Now we're going to die.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Manoa sele ɔye kyɛ, Ewue yeɛ yɛbaawu ɔ, ofikyɛ yanwu Nyameɛ.”

english_verse: “The Lord isn't going to kill us,” Manoah's wife responded. “The Lord accepted our sacrifice and grain offering, and he let us see something amazing. Besides, he told us that we're going to have a son.”
translation_verse: Nakoso ɔye sele ye kyɛ, “Sɛ AWURADE pena kyɛ oku yɛ a, ahaa ongole yɛ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ɔne yɛ aburoo afɔleɛ ne ngɔto nu. Ahaa ɔngɔye nningyein hemɔ amukoraa ngohyire yɛ, anaa ɔngɔhã edwirɛ sɔaa mɔ ngohyire yɛ.”

english_verse: Later, Manoah's wife did give birth to a son, and she named him Samson. As the boy grew, the Lord blessed him.
translation_verse: Braa ne wole bienzua na ɔtole ye dumaa Samson. Akwadaa ne nyini, na AWURADE yirale ye.

english_verse: Then, while Samson was staying at Dan's Camp between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol, the Spirit of the Lord took control of him.
translation_verse: AWURADE Sunzum hyɛle ye bo kanyane ye wɔ Mahane Dan bɔ ɔwɔ Sora ne Esetao b’afia ne.

english_verse: One day, Samson went to Timnah, where he saw a Philistine woman.
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, Samson hɔle Timina, na onwuni Filistiniɛ braa bie wɔ berɛ.

english_verse: When he got back home, he told his parents, “I saw a Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want to marry her. Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Yiti osa wale awuro ne, ɔfa tole ye baba ne ye maame nyunu kyɛ, “Manwu Filistiniɛ brasua bie wɔ Timina, yiti ɛmɔɔgya ye bɛma me.”

english_verse: His parents answered, “There are a lot of women in our clan and even more in the rest of Israel. Those Philistines are pagans. Why would you want to marry one of their women?” “She looks good to me,” Samson answered. “Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Nakoso ye baba ne ye maame buale ye kyɛ, “Aso w’abusua nu, anaakyɛ yɛ maen ye anu amukoraati, brasua biala ɔnne nu, bɔ yiti ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛkɔ Filistifoɛ bɔ bɛmbɛ bɛ bienzua ye mɔ anu ekogya braa ɔ?” Nakoso Samson sele ye baba kyɛ, “Kogya ye ma me, ofikyɛ ye yeɛ mekuro ye ɔ.”

english_verse: At that time, the Philistines were in control of Israel, and the Lord wanted to stir up trouble for them. That's why he made Samson desire that woman.
translation_verse: Né ye baba ne maame bɛnze kyɛ bɔ ɔkɔ so ne ofi AWURADE ɔ; ofikyɛ né AWURADE fa sɔ atee ne aso ɔfa koɛ kɔteta Filistifoɛ. Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Filistifoɛ di Yisrael so.

english_verse: As Samson and his parents reached the vineyards near Timnah, a fierce young lion suddenly roared and attacked Samson.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Samson ne ye baba ne ye maame bɛhɔle Timina. Na Samson dwuli Timina bobe boo nemɔ anu ne, mvum nu, gyata akrɔngrɔma bie pole, na ɔwale Samson so.

english_verse: But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and with his bare hands he tore the lion apart, as though it had been a young goat. His parents didn't know what he had done, and he didn't tell them.
translation_verse: AWURADE Sunzum wale ye so, na ole ye sa mbaen tetele gyata ne anu pasaa kyɛ wanya abɔngye ba bie bɔ ɔtete ye nu ɔ. Nakoso wanga bɔ wayɔ ne wangyire ye baba anaa ye maame.

english_verse: When they got to Timnah, Samson talked to the woman, and he was sure that she was the one for him.
translation_verse: Afei Samson hɔle ɔne braa ne beelili ngɔmɔ, na ye nye gyele braa ne anwo.

english_verse: Later, Samson returned to Timnah for the wedding. And when he came near the place where the lion had attacked, he left the road to see what was left of the lion. He was surprised to see that bees were living in the lion's skeleton, and that they had made some honey.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ kãa pɛle nu ne, Samson sa hɔle kyɛ ɔkwaagya braa ne. Atee nu, ɔmakyele ɔɔneane gyata ne fuin, na onwuni kyɛ gyata fuin ne alɔ woɛ, na né ɛwommaa wɔ nu mitimiti.

english_verse: He scooped up the honey in his hands and ate some of it as he walked along. When he got back to his parents, he gave them some of the honey, and they ate it too. But he didn't tell them he had found the honey in the skeleton of a lion.
translation_verse: Opiane woɛ ne guale ye sa nu, na ɔkɔ ne, né odi kɔ. Oodwuli ye baba ne ye maame nwo berɛ ne, ɔmane bɛ bie maa belili. Nakoso wanga wangyire bɛ kyɛ ɔnyene woɛ ne wɔ gyata fuin nu.

english_verse: While Samson's father went to make the final arrangements with the bride and her family, Samson threw a big party, as grooms usually did.
translation_verse: Ye baba hɔle braa ne awuro berɛ, na Samson tole poen wɔ berɛ kyɛbɔ kuro berɛ mmerandeɛ bɛyɔ ne ala.

english_verse: When the Philistines saw what Samson was like, they told
translation_verse: Mmenia ne nwuni ye ne, bɛmane mmerandeɛ aburasa bɛɛbokale ye so.

english_verse: But if you can't tell me the answer, then each of you will have to give me a shirt and a full change of clothing.” “It's a bet!” the Philistines said. “Tell us the riddle.”
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ ɛmɔangora bangyire me ye bo a, ye de ɛmɔ koso ɛmɔkɔma me nwera ndaadeɛ aburasa, ɔne ndaadeɛ bɔ bewura bɛkɔ dwaabɔlɛ bo aburasa.” Na besele ye kyɛ, “Fa w’anyandera ne to dwaa maa yɛtie.”

english_verse: Samson said: Once so strong and mighty— now so sweet and tasty! Three days went by, and the Philistine young men had not come up with the right answer.
translation_verse: Samson sele bɛ kyɛ, “Nana Nyameɛ abɔdeɛ bie bɔ ɔwɔ berɛ ɔ, ɔkye abɔdeɛ mɔ di, nakoso benyane nikyee bɔ bedi ɔ befili ye nu. Abɔdeɛ anwoserɛniɛ ne, benyane nikyee menemene befili ye nu. Nzikyɛ ɔ” Nakoso ɛlɛsa mumua, bangora bangyire anyandera ne abo.

english_verse: Finally, on the seventh day of the party they went to Samson's bride and said, “You had better trick your husband into telling you the answer to his riddle. Have you invited us here just to rob us? If you don't find out the answer, we will burn you and your family to death.”
translation_verse: Ye ɛlɛnna ne aso, besele Samson aye ne kyɛ, “Dɛfɛdɛfɛ ehu maa ohyire yɛ anyandera ne abo. Anyɔ sɔ a, yɛkɔfa see yɛkɔyera wɔ ne wɔ baba awuro. Ɛtole wɔ sa frɛle yɛ wa kyɛ ɛbaafa yɛ to kerɛ nu anaa?”

english_verse: Samson's bride went to him and started crying in his arms. “You must really hate me,” she sobbed. “If you loved me at all, you would have told me the answer to your riddle.” “But I haven't even told my parents the answer!” Samson replied. “Why should I tell you?”
translation_verse: Yiti Samson aye ne sũ guale ye so kyɛ, “Ɛpɔ me; enguro me koraa. Abu me mmenia mɔ anyandera, nakoso angyire me ye bo.” Na Samson buale ye kyɛ, “Nea, me baba ne me maame po, ngyirele bɛ ye bo. Nzu ati yeɛ odi kyɛ mekyire wɔ ye bo ɔ?

english_verse: For the entire seven days of the party, she had been whining and trying to get the answer from him. But that seventh day she put so much pressure on Samson that he finally gave in and told her the answer. She went straight to the young men and told them.
translation_verse: Braa ne sũ guale Samson so ɛlɛsoo bɔ bɛwɔ poentolɛ bo ne amukoraa. Na ɔnate kyɛ né odwane Samson nwo ne ati, ohyirele ye anyandera ne abo ɛlɛsoo ne aso. Braa ne hɔle oohyirele anyandera ne abo hyirele ye kuro ama nemɔ.

english_verse: Before sunset that day, the men of the town went to Samson with this answer: A lion is the strongest— honey is the sweetest! Samson replied, This answer you have given me doubtless came from my bride-to-be.
translation_verse: Yiti ye ɛlɛsoo ne aso, kuro berɛ mmienzua sele Samson koraka yeɛ eyia kwaatɔ ɔ kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ yeɛ ɔte menemene tra woɛ ɔ? Nzikyɛ yeɛ ye nwo yɛ se tra gyata ɔ?” Na Samson buale bɛ kyɛ, Sɛ ɛmɔamva me bɔbɔ me ye so a, ahaa ɛmɔande anyandera ne abo.”

english_verse: The father of the bride made Samson's wife marry one of the
translation_verse: Na bɛfale Samson aye ne bɛmane obiɛngo bɔ né ɔte ye agyaa nu adamvoa ne.

english_verse: “When you left the way you did, I thought you were divorcing her. So I arranged for her to marry one of the young men who were at your party. But my younger daughter is even prettier, and you can have her as your wife.”
translation_verse: Braa ne baba nwa, “Né mese kyɛ enguro ye ko, yiti mafa ye mama wɔ damvo ne. Oliɛma brasua kãa ne nwo yɛ nyemene tra ye. Nzu ati yeɛ engya ye mmom ɔ?”

english_verse: “This time,” Samson answered, “I have a good reason for really hurting some Philistines.” Samson Takes Revenge
translation_verse: Samson sele bɛ kyɛ, “Afei de, sɛ meyɔ nikyee tɛɛ biala metia Filistifoɛ a, menni fɔ.”

english_verse: Then Samson took the foxes into the Philistine wheat fields that were ready to be harvested. He set the rags on fire and let the foxes go. The wheat fields went up in flames, and so did the stacks of wheat that had already been cut. Even the Philistine vineyards and olive orchards burned.
translation_verse: Ɔfale see sosɔle ɛtɛen nemɔ anu, na ɔyakyili safuboa nemɔ maa bɛnwati bɛhɔle Filistifoɛ atokoɔ boo mɔ anu. See ne yerale b’atokoɔ bɔ bate baboa ye noa ɔne bɔ bennya bɛttele ne. Osa yerale bɛ bobe boo ne olive boo mɔ.

english_verse: Some of the Philistines started asking around, “Who could have done such a thing?” “It was Samson,” someone told them. “He married the daughter of that man in Timnah, but then the man gave Samson's wife to one of the men at the wedding.” The Philistine leaders went to Timnah and burned to death Samson's wife and her father.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Filistifoɛ bisale kyɛ, “Nwa yeɛ wayɔ sɔ amumuyɛɛ ye?” Na bɛtele kyɛ, “Timinaniɛ ne, ye sia bienzua Samson yeɛ wayɔ sɔ ne, ofikyɛ biaa ne ale Samson aye wafa ye wama Samson abiɛngo.” Yiti Filistifoɛ fale see bɛɛyerale braa ne ɔne ye baba.

english_verse: When Samson found out what they had done, he went to them and said, “You killed them! And I won't rest until I get even with you.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Samson sele bɛ kyɛ, “Sɛ sɔ yeɛ ɛmɔayɔ de a, ye de sana matɔ ɛmɔ so wereɛ koraka né m’ahone atɔ me kunu.”

english_verse: Then Samson started hacking them to pieces with his sword. Samson left Philistia and went to live in the cave at Etam Rock.
translation_verse: Yiti ɔfale koɛ tetale Filistifoɛ huhuni bɛ pasaa; na osili nu ɔɔtenane Etam nyɔbotaen ne anu nekaa bie bɔ nyɔboɛ ne asi sua ɔ.

english_verse: But it wasn't long before the Philistines invaded Judah and set up a huge army camp at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Afei Filistifoɛ hɔle bɛɛkyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ Yuda, na bɛɛbɔle apaa wɔ Lehi.

english_verse: The people of Judah asked, “Why have you invaded our land?” The Philistines answered, “We've come to get Samson. We're going to do the same things to him that he did to our people.”
translation_verse: Yudafoɛ bisale kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔafa koɛ baatoa yɛ ye?” Na Filistifoɛ buale kyɛ, “Yawa kyɛ yɛbaahye Samson ná yɛkɔfa bɔ ɔfa lili yɛ ne bie yɛdi ye.”

english_verse: Three thousand men from Judah went to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, “Don't you know that the Philistines rule us, and they will punish us for what you did?” “I was only getting even with them,” Samson replied. “They did the same things to me first.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yuda koɛhonɛfoɛ apee nza sili nu bɛhɔle nyɔboɛ bɔ wasi sua, bɔ ɔwɔ Etam nyɔbotaen anu ne, na besele Samson kyɛ, “Ɛnze kyɛ Filistifoɛ, yɛ mene mɔ ole bɛ ɔ? Nzikyɛ dwirɛ yeɛ aahwe aberɛ yɛ ye?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Nikyee bɔ bɛfa bɛyɔle me ne, sɔ ala yeɛ mafa mayɔ bɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: “We came here to tie you up and turn you over to them,” said the men of Judah. “I won't put up a fight,” Samson answered, “but you have to promise not to hurt me yourselves.”
translation_verse: Yudafoɛ sele ye kyɛ, “Yawa kyɛ yɛbaahye wɔ, ná yɛfa wɔ yɛkowura Filistifoɛ sa.” Na Samson buale bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔta ndaen kyɛ ɛmɔ bɔbɔ ɛmɔngohu me.”

english_verse: After the fighting was over, he made up this poem about what he had done to the Philistines: I used a donkey's jawbone to kill a thousand men; I beat them with this jawbone over and over again.
translation_verse: Na Samson sele kyɛ, “Mafa afunum awogyee, mamaa efuin mɔ ataataa so kure kure, mafa afunum awogyee mahu mmienzua apee ko.”

english_verse: Samson tossed the jawbone on the ground and decided to call the place Jawbone Hill. It is still called that today.
translation_verse: Odwudwo yiele ne, ogyili awogyee ne tole; na bɛfrɛle berɛ Ramate Lehi.

english_verse: Samson was so thirsty that he prayed, “Our Lord, you helped me win a battle against a whole army. Please don't let me die of thirst now. Those heathen Philistines will carry off my dead body.”
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né nzuhɔen ku Samson paa, yiti osũ frɛle AWURADE kyɛ, “Ɛnate w’akoaa so ali ngonim kandinga he. Aso nzuhɔen baahu me, maa mmenia bɔ bɛmbɛ bɛ bienzua nemɔ bɛ sa ka me anaa?”

english_verse: Samson was tired and weary, but God sent water gushing from a rock. Samson drank some and felt strong again. Samson named the place Caller Spring, because he had called out to God for help. The spring is still there at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Yiti kumaa bɔ ɔwɔ Lehi ne, Nyameɛ dwale nu, na nzue pu fili nu wale. Samson none nzue ne, onyane anwoserɛ, na osa kendene ye nwo. Yiti bɛfrɛle mbombonzue ne Ɛn Hakore, na ɔwɔ Lehi maa waadwu ɛnɛ.

english_verse: years, but the Philistines were still the rulers of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Samson buli Yisrael maen ne afoɛ aburanyɔ wɔ Filistifoɛ aberɛ so.

english_verse: The people who lived in Gaza found out he was there, and they decided to kill him at sunrise. So they went to the city gate and waited all night in the guardrooms on each side of the gate.
translation_verse: Bɛbɔle Gasafoɛ amaneɛ kyɛ, “Samson awa wa.” Yiti bɛpɛle sua ne anwo beyiale, yeɛ bɛtetɛle ye wɔ kuro berɛ pambim ne anu kɔngɔen ne amukoraa. Bɛyɛle konn kɔngɔen ne amukoraa na bɛdwenene ye nwo kyɛ, “Ɛmɔma yɛnwondɛ maa aleɛ hye, ná yahu ye.”

english_verse: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in Sorek Valley.
translation_verse: Ɛhe asi ne, oohurole braa bie bɔ ye kuro wɔ Soreke bɔnza ne anu ɔ. Bɛfrɛ ye Delila.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers went to Delilah and said, “Trick Samson into telling you what makes him so strong and what can make him weak. Then we can tie him up so he can't get away. If you find out his secret, we will each give you
translation_verse: Filistifoɛ mbanyi hɔle braa ne berɛ beesele ye kyɛ, “Dɛfɛdɛfɛ ye ná pena nikye horɛ bɔ ɔmaa ye nwo yɛ se sɔa ne, ɔne atee bɔ yɛkɔfa so yɛkoli ye so ngonim, amaa ɔnate so yafa nyamaa yakyekye ye yabrɛ ye ase. Sɛ ɛyɔ sɔ ma yɛ a, yɛ nu biala kɔma wɔ ɛdwetɛ apee ko ɛyaa ko.”

english_verse: The next time Samson was at Delilah's house, she asked, “Samson, what makes you so strong? How can I tie you up so you can't get away? Come on, you can tell me.”
translation_verse: Yiti Delila bisale Samson kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, nzikyɛ yeɛ ɔmaa wɔ nwo yɛ se paa sɔa ne? Ka kyire me. Ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ né ebie ahora afa nyamaa wakyekye wɔ, ná wabrɛ wɔ ase?”

english_verse: Samson answered, “If someone ties me up with seven new bowstrings that have never been dried, it will make me just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Samson buale ye kyɛ, “Sɛ bɛfa nyamaa monɛ nzoo bɔ ɔwwole bɛkyekye me a, ngɔyɛ mmerɛ ná mayɛ kyɛ kuro sona biala.”

english_verse: The Philistine rulers gave seven new bowstrings to Delilah. They also told some of their soldiers to go to Delilah's house and hide in the room where Samson and Delilah were. If the bowstrings made Samson weak, they would be able to capture him. Delilah tied up Samson with the bowstrings and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the bowstrings, as though they were pieces of scorched string. The Philistines had not found out why Samson was so strong.
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né mmenia nemɔ baatetɛ wɔ pumbu nu. Na Delila sele Samson kyɛ, “Samson, Filistifoɛ awa wɔ so oo!” Nakoso Samson tetele nyamaa ne anu kyɛ atendirehuo bɔ waha see ɔ. Yiti ye anwoserɛ anwo mvealeɛ dwirɛ ne, bannwu ye.

english_verse: “You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
translation_verse: Afei Delila sele Samson kyɛ, “Agoro me nwo, yeɛ apɛ ngondombo ahyire me. Mesrɛ wɔ, kyire me nikyee bɔ bɛkɔhora bɛkɔfa bɛkɔkyekye wɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Samson buale ye kyɛ, “Sɛ bɛfa findima monɛ bɔ bɛffa bɛyyɔle hwee le bɛkyekye me a, ye de ngɔyɛ mmerɛ, ná mayɛ kyɛ kuro sona biala.”

english_verse: Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
translation_verse: Yiti Delila fale findima monɛ kyekyele Samson, na osele ye kyɛ, “Samson, Filistifoɛ awa wɔ so oo!” Nakoso Samson tetele findima ne anu fili ye sa kyɛ gyese bie.

english_verse: “You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!” “My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Delila sele Samson kyɛ, “Agoro me nwo, yeɛ apɛ ngondombo ahyire me maa waadwu bekye. Kyire me nikyee bɔ bɛkɔhora bɛkɔfa bɛkɔkyekye wɔ ɔ.” Na obuale ye kyɛ, “Sɛ ɛfa me ti nwiaa mbɛsɛmbɛsɛ nzoo ne fra eduku ɛnwo, ná ɛfa buralɛ mia nu dweredwere a, ngɔyɛ mmerɛ ná mayɛ kyɛ kuro sona biala.”

english_verse: While Samson was asleep, Delilah wove his braids into the threads on a loom and nailed the loom to a wall. Then she shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson woke up and pulled the loom free from its posts in the ground and from the nails in the wall. Then he pulled his hair free from the woven cloth.
translation_verse: Samson lale, na Delila sɔle ye ti nwiaa mbɛsɛmbɛsɛ nzoo ne anu frale eduku nwone, na ɔfale buralɛ miane nu dweredwere. Na osele ye kyɛ, “Samson, Filistifoɛ awa wɔ so oo!” Nakoso Samson dwɔso fili nnaa nu, otuli buralɛ ne, na ɔsangyele eduku bɔ wafa wafra ye ti nwiaa mbɛsɛmbɛsɛ wanwo ne.

english_verse: “Samson,” Delilah said, “you claim to love me, but you don't mean it! You've made me look like a fool three times now, and you still haven't told me why you are so strong.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Delila sele ye kyɛ, “Aso ede di kyɛ ekuro me, wɔ aberɛ bɔ enguro me mvi w’ahone nu ɔ? Agoro me nwo pɛen nza ɛhe, na nikyee bɔ ɔmaa wɔ nwo yɛ se paa sɔa ne, anga angyire me.”

english_verse: Delilah started nagging and pestering him day after day, until he couldn't stand it any longer.
translation_verse: Delila fale edwirɛ ne dwanene Samson nwo daa biala, na ɔhɔle so hale ye adwene alaa maa yiti edwirɛ ne yɛle Samson ahomete.

english_verse: Finally, Samson told her the truth. “I have belonged to God ever since I was born, so my hair has never been cut. If it were ever cut off, my strength would leave me, and I would be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Na Samson hane ye mvealeɛ nu dwirɛ ne amu hyirele ye kyɛ, “Me ti ne, bɛttetele ye le, ofikyɛ nde nasiriteniɛ ma Nyameɛ fi me maame kunu. Sɛ bɛtete me ti a, m’anwoserɛ ne amukoraa kotu komini, ngɔyɛ mmerɛ ná mayɛ kyɛ kuro sona biala.”

english_verse: Delilah realized that he was telling the truth. So she sent someone to tell the Philistine rulers, “Come to my house one more time. Samson has finally told me the truth.” The Philistine rulers went to Delilah's house, and they brought along the silver they had promised her.
translation_verse: Delila nwuni kyɛ Samson aha ye mvealeɛ nu dwirɛ ne amukoraa wahyire ye ne, ɔsomane maa bɛɛfrɛle Filistifoɛ mbanyi nemɔ bɛbrɛle ye, na ɔbɔle bɛ amaneɛ kyɛ, “Afei de ɛmɔbra, ofikyɛ wabukye ye mvealeɛ nu dwirɛ ne amukoraa so wahyire me.” Yiti Filistifoɛ mbanyi ne amukoraati wale Delila berɛ, na né betiratira b’esikaa ne.

english_verse: Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up
translation_verse: Delila fale Samson ti tole ye sɔ so maa ɔlafele, na ɔfrɛle biaa bie maa ɔɔpoane ye ti nwiaa mbɛsɛmbɛsɛ nzoo ne. Na Samson hyɛle ye bo yɛle mmerɛ, na ye anwoserɛ tu minini.

english_verse: The Philistines grabbed Samson and poked out his eyes. They took him to the prison in Gaza and chained him up. Then they put him to work, turning a millstone to grind grain.
translation_verse: Yiti Filistifoɛ hyele ye, na betutuli ye nye. Bɛfale ye bɛhɔle Gasa, na bɛfale kɔɔbere ngɔnzɔngɔnzɔ beguale ye. Na ɔla kuku nu berɛ ne, né ye yeɛ opia ngaen bɔ bɛfa beti aburoo ɔ.

english_verse: But they didn't cut his hair any more, so it started growing back.
translation_verse: Nakoso ye ti nwiaa bɔ bɛpoane ne, osa hyele ye bo fuli. Samson wue

english_verse: The Philistine rulers threw a big party and sacrificed a lot of animals to their god Dagon. The rulers said: Samson was our enemy, but our god Dagon helped us capture him!
translation_verse: Afei Filistifoɛ mbanyi bɔle dwaa kyɛ bɛbɔ afɔleɛ kandinga bɛma bɛ nyameɛ Dagɔn, ná bɛgye bɛ nye; ofikyɛ bɛhane kyɛ, “Yɛ nyameɛ yeɛ wafa yɛ pɔfoɛ Samson wawura yɛ sa ɔ.”

english_verse: A young man was leading Samson by the hand, and Samson said to him, “I need to lean against something. Take me over to the columns that hold up the roof.”
translation_verse: na osele akwadaa bɔ otira ye sa okyire ye ate ne kyɛ, “Bonima mɔ bɔ betira sua ne anu ne, maa ngɔnzɔ nu ná ngisa bɛ.”

english_verse: Samson prayed, “Please remember me, Lord God. The Philistines poked out my eyes, but make me strong one last time, so I can take revenge for at least one of my eyes!”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Samson sũ frɛle AWURADE kyɛ, “AWURADE Nyameɛ, kaye me ná ma me anwoserɛ sɔ mmerɛ ye ala angome, O Nyameɛ; na mandɔ Filistifoɛ so wereɛ ɔnate me nye nyɔ bɔ batutu ne ati.”

english_verse: Samson was standing between the two middle columns that held up the roof. He felt around and found one column with his right hand, and the other with his left hand.
translation_verse: Yiti bonima nyɔ bɔ bɛwɔ afia paa bɔ betira sua ne anu ne, Samson le ye anwoserɛ amukoraa tirale nu. Ɔfale ye sa famaa fuale ko, yeɛ ɔfale bɛen ne koso fuale ko.

english_verse: Then he shouted, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed against the columns as hard as he could, and the temple collapsed with the Philistine rulers and everyone else still inside. Samson killed more Philistines when he died than he had killed during his entire life.
translation_verse: Na Samson sele kyɛ, “Maa me ne Filistifoɛ yɛwu!” Ole ye anwoserɛ amukoraati piane bonima nemɔ; na sua ne bu guale mbanyi ne mmenia bɔ né bayia berɛ ne amukoraati so. Yiti mmenia bɔ ohuni bɛ wɔ ye wue nu ne, bɛsone bɛtra mmenia bɔ ohuni bɛ mmerɛ bɔ né ɔte ase ɔ.

translation_verse: Na oliɛma mmienzua mɔ ne ye abusuafoɛ amukoraa bɛɛfale ye fuin beesiele ye wɔ ye baba Manoa asieleɛ nu, wɔ Sora ne Esetao b’afia. Samson buli Yisrael maen afoɛ aburanyɔ.

english_verse: Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she said, “I give this silver to the Lord, so my son can use it to make an idol.” Turning to her son, she said, “Micah, now the silver belongs to you.” But Micah handed it back to his mother. She took
translation_verse: Na osa fale ɛdwetɛ ne mane ye maame ne, braa ne yele nu ɛyaa nyɔ mane ɛdwetɛ dwumvoɛ maa ohurole ye yɔle buralɛ amoen. Né amoen ne gyi Mika awuro.

english_verse: He had a shrine for worshiping God there at his home, and he had made some idols and a sacred priestly vest. Micah chose one of his own sons to be the priest for his shrine.
translation_verse: Sɔ biaa Mika he, né ole amoen asɔneyɛɛ. Ɔpale ɔsɔfo ataadeɛ, na ɔyɔle abusua amoen. Ɔhyɛle ɔwa bienzua ko sɔfo maa ɔyɛle ye sɔfo.

english_verse: This was before kings ruled Israel, so all the Israelites did whatever they thought was right.
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né ɛhene biala nne Yisrael, yiti né ebiala yɔ bɔ okuro ɔ.

english_verse: One day a young Levite came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim. He had been staying with one of the clans of Judah in Bethlehem, but he had left Bethlehem to find a new place to live where he could be a priest.
translation_verse: Sɔ aberandeɛ ne tu fili Betlehem bɔ ɔwɔ Yuda, kyɛ kuro biala bɔ okonya ye ne, ɔkɔtena so. Ye ateetulɛ ne anu, oodwuli Mika awuro wɔ Efraim mmokaa aseɛ ne aso.

english_verse: “Where are you from?” Micah asked. “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” the man answered, “and I'm on my way to find a new place to live.”
translation_verse: Mika bisale ye kyɛ, “Efi ni yeɛ ɛba ye?” Obuale kyɛ, “Nde Lewiniɛ bɔ mvi Betlehem bɔ ɔwɔ Yuda, na kuro biala bɔ ngonya ye ne, ngɔtena so.”

english_verse: Micah said, “Why don't you stay here with me? You can be my priest and tell me what God wants me to do. Every year I'll give you ten pieces of silver and one complete set of clothes, and I'll provide all your food.” The young man went for a walk,
translation_verse: Yeɛ Mika sele ye kyɛ, “Tena m’awuro wa. Maa mva wɔ nyɛ me baba ne me sɔfo, na ngɔma wɔ ɛdwetɛ buru afoɛnoa biala, yeɛ ndaadeɛ ne wɔ noa aleɛ.”

english_verse: then he agreed to stay with Micah and be his priest. He lived in Micah's house, and Micah treated him like one of his own sons.
translation_verse: Yiti Mika hyɛle Lewiniɛ aberandeɛ ne sɔfo maa ɔɔyɛle ye sɔfo. Né ɔte Mika awuro berɛ.

english_verse: Micah said, “I have a Levite as my own priest. Now I know that the Lord will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Na Mika sele kyɛ, “Afei de, mese kyɛ AWURADE kɔmaa okoyie me yé, ofikyɛ manya Lewiniɛ maa waayɛ me sɔfo.”

english_verse: These things happened before kings ruled Israel. The Tribe of Dan Takes Micah's Priest and Idols About this time, the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to live. The other tribes had land, but the people of Dan did not really have any to call their own.
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né ɛhene biala nne Yisrael. Na sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Dan abusua kure ne bɛpena bɛ bɔbɔ b’aseɛ bɛtena so. Ofikyɛ ɔbaadwu sɔ mmerɛ ne, Yisrael mmusua kure ne anu, né bɛ de bɛmmane bɛ aseɛ biala.

english_verse: The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.” The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house,
translation_verse: Yiti Danfoɛ yele bɛ mmusua nemɔ anu mmienzua ahoneserɛfoɛ nnu, bɔ befi Sora ne Esetao, kyɛ bɛɛtetɛ aseɛ ne, ná bɛneanea so. Na besele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhɔ bɛɛneanea aseɛ ne aso.” Beedwuli Mika awuro wɔ Efraim mmokaa aseɛ ne aso ne, besikyele berɛ.

english_verse: because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
translation_verse: Bɛwɔ Mika awuro berɛ ne, bɛtele Lewiniɛ aberandeɛ ne komvi. Yiti bɛhɔle ye nwo berɛ beebisale ye kyɛ, “Nwa yeɛ ɔfale wɔ wale wa ɔ? Nzikyɛ yeɛ ɛyɔ ye wɔ wa ɔ? Ɛpena nzu wɔ wa?”

english_verse: The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
translation_verse: Obuale bɛ kyɛ, Bɔ Mika ayɔ ama me ɛhe: wafa me adwuma, na me yeɛ nde ye sɔfo ɔ.”

english_verse: “Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ besele ye kyɛ, “Bisa Nyameɛ ma yɛ maa yɛnwu ye sɛ atee bɔ yɛkɔ ye, okoyie yɛ yé a.”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔfo ne buale bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhɔ asomdwee nu. Atee bɔ ɛmɔkɔ ye, AWURADE gyi ɛmɔ si.”

english_verse: The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
translation_verse: Mmienzua nnu ne toale b’ateetulɛ ne aso, na beedwuli Layise ne, benwuni kyɛ berɛ ama te berɛ asomdwee nu kyɛ Sidonfoɛ nemɔ ala, bɔ bɛndwene kyɛ edwirɛ tɛɛ bie kɔto bɛ ɔ. Né banya bɛ nwo tam bɔ hwee nhia bɛ ɔ. Afei koso né bembingye Sidonfoɛ koraa, yeɛ né bɛ ne Siriafoɛ koso belle hwee bɛnyɔ.

english_verse: The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
translation_verse: Besale bɛ si bɛhɔle bɛ kuro ama berɛ wɔ Sora ne Esetao, na bebisale bɛ amaneɛ kyɛ, “Nekaa bɔ ɛmɔhɔle ɔ?”

english_verse: “Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛmɔkɔ dwu berɛ a, ɛmɔkɔɔto mmenia bie bɔ bɛndwene kyɛ edwirɛ tɛɛ bie po kɔto bɛ ɔ. Aseɛ ne terɛ, na wiase wa nikyee biala nhia bɛ wɔ berɛ. Aseɛ ne, Nyameɛ afa awura ɛmɔ sa.”

english_verse: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.
translation_verse: Dan abusua kure nu koɛhonɛfoɛ ɛyaa nzia bɔ betiratira akodeɛ ɔ, besili nu befili Sora ne Esetao,

english_verse: “Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do?
