translation_verse: Bebuale ye kyɛ, “Mua wɔ noa! Ka wɔ noa ne to nu di yɛ si, na maa yɛfa wɔ yɛyɛ yɛ baba ne yɛ sɔfo. Kyɛ ɛkɔyɛ sona horɛ awuro sɔfo, ɔne kyɛ ɛkɔyɛ abusua kure ne abusua sɔfo wɔ Yisrael ɔ, beni yeɛ ɔte paa ma wɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others
translation_verse: Ɔsɔfo ne penene b’edwirɛ ne aso. Ɔfale ɔsɔfo ataadeɛ ne, abusua amoen ne, ɔne amoen ne, na ɔne mmenia nemɔ sili nu bɛhɔle.

english_verse: from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
translation_verse: Yiti Danfoɛ bɛfale bɛ mma mɔ, bɛ nyɛmmoa ne bɛ nningyein belili bɛ nyunu moa, na besa bɛtoale b’ateetulɛ ne aso.

english_verse: They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan
translation_verse: Befili Mika awuro berɛ bɛhɔle moa kãa ne, Mika frɛfrɛle mmenia bɔ b’awuro mɔ pingye ye deɛ ne, na bɛpole Danfoɛ ne aso bɛɛtole bɛ.

english_verse: and shouted for them to stop. They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
translation_verse: Bɛteateane nu beguale Danfoɛ nemɔ aso, na Danfoɛ kakyili bɛ nye bebisale Mika kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ dwirɛ ti yeɛ afa ɛlɔen he ali wɔ si ye?”

english_verse: Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
translation_verse: Na Mika buale kyɛ, “Ɛmɔasesa me mmosoen bɔ mayɔ ɔ ɔne me sɔfo bahɔ, na beni yeɛ waha me sa nu ɔ? Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔbisa me kyɛ, ‘Nzikyɛ dwirɛ’ ahɔ ɔ?’ ”

english_verse: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”
translation_verse: Na Danfoɛ sele ye kyɛ, “Nnɛteatea nu gua yɛ so. Sɛ ɛyɔ sɔ a, mmenia bɔ bafɛ yaa paa kɔwa wɔ so, na ɛne w’awuro ama ɛmɔkɔhwere ɛmɔ ngoa.”

english_verse: After saying this, they turned and left. Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home. The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
translation_verse: Afei Danfoɛ sili nu bɛhɔle b’atee. Na Mika nwuni kyɛ bɛ nwo yɛ se tra ye ne, osale ye si hɔle ye awuro. Danfoɛ batena Layise

english_verse: But they named it Dan, after one of Israel's sons, who was the ancestor of their tribe.
translation_verse: Bɛfale kuro ne bɛtole bɛ nana Dan bɔ ɔte Yisrael awa ne. Nakoso daa ne, né kuro ne dumaa li Layise.

english_verse: Before kings ruled Israel, a Levite was living deep in the hill country of the Ephraim tribe. He married a woman from Bethlehem in Judah,
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ né ɛhene biala nne Yisrael nen, né Lewiniɛ bie te namue bie anu bɔ ɔwɔ dedeede wɔ Efraim mmokaa aseɛ ne aso. Ɔɔfale sómaa wɔ Betlehem bɔ ɔwɔ Yuda.

english_verse: but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem. Four months later
translation_verse: Nakoso ye sómaa ne fɛle ye so yaa. Braa ne fili ye berɛ sa hɔle ɔse awuro wɔ Betlehem bɔ ɔwɔ Yuda, na oolili kɔyɛ bosome nna.

english_verse: her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him
translation_verse: Yeɛ ohu ne pole ye so kyɛ ɔkwaagu se ye maa osa ba. Ɔne ye somvoɛ ne afunum nyɔ yeɛ bɛhɔle ɔ. Oodwuli braa ne baba awuro berɛ ne, taluwa ne baba nwuni ye, na ooyiale ye nyemene so.

english_verse: and did not want him to leave. So the man stayed three days, eating and drinking with his father-in-law.
translation_verse: Taluwa ne baba bɔ ɔte Lewiniɛ ne sia ne, ɔmaa Lewiniɛ ne sikyele ye awuro olili berɛ ɛlɛsa. Yiti bedidili bɛnone na ɔtenane berɛ.

english_verse: When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
translation_verse: Ye ɛlɛnna ne aso, bedwɔsole ngyerɛmɔ tutuutu, na Lewiniɛ ne boaboale ye nwo kyɛ ɔkɔ ye kuro. Nakoso ye sia bienzua ne sele ye kyɛ, “Didi kãa nya anwoserɛ koraka né ahɔ.”

english_verse: The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
translation_verse: Yiti mmienzua nyɔ nemɔ tenane poen nwo bedidili bɛnone, na taluwa ne baba sele Lewiniɛ ne kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛnna wa ɛnɛ ná ɛmma wɔ nye ngye ɔ?”

english_verse: The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there.
translation_verse: Lewiniɛ ne dwɔsole kyɛ ɔkɔ ne, ye sia ne hɔle so gu sele ye kɔpem kyɛ osa lale berɛ sɔ kyẽa ne koso ɔ.

english_verse: The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
translation_verse: Ye elennu ne aso, Lewiniɛ ne dwɔsole ngyerɛmɔ tutuutu kyɛ ɔkɔ; na taluwa ne baba sele ye kyɛ, “Didi koraka.” Yiti belele bɛ nwome maa oodwuli kyɛ aleɛ dwole ɔ, na bɛ munyɔ bedidili bɛnone.

english_verse: Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Lewiniɛ ne, ye sómaa ne, yeɛ ye somvoɛ ne bedwɔsole kyɛ bɛkɔ ne, taluwa ne baba bɔ ɔte Lewiniɛ ne sia ne, osele Lewiniɛ ne kyɛ, “Nea, mmerɛ ahɔ, aleɛ ayie sa. Ɛ́mɔla wa ɛnɛ, na aleɛ adwo. Ɛ́mɔla wa ɛnɛ, ná ma wɔ nye gye. Ɛhema ɛmɔkɔhora bekodwɔso ngyerɛmɔ tutuutu bekosi nu bɛkɔhɔ ɛmɔ kuro.”

english_verse: But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nakoso Lewiniɛ ne wambene so kyɛ ɔkɔla berɛ sɔ kyẽa ne. Osili nu, na oodwuli Yebusi ndendeneɛ so. Ɔne ye afunum nyɔ bɔ nningyein gua bɛ so, ɔne ye sómaa ne yeɛ bɛhɔle ɔ.

english_verse: It was beginning to get dark, and the man's servant said, “Let's stop and spend the night in this town where the Jebusites live.”
translation_verse: Ɔka kãa maa bedwu Yebusi ne, né aleɛ adwo. Na somvoɛ ne sele ye mene kyɛ, “Maa yɛmakye yɛhɔ Yebusifoɛ kuro ye aso na yɛɛla berɛ ɛnɛ kɔngɔen ye.”

english_verse: “No,” the Levite answered. “They aren't Israelites, and I refuse to spend the night there. We'll stop for the night at Gibeah,
translation_verse: Nakoso ye mene sele ye kyɛ, “Amanvorafoɛ mɔ bɔ nna Yisraelfoɛ ahɔ ɔ ne de, yɛngɔhɔ bɛ kuro so; na mmom yɛkɔtoa so yɛkɔhɔ Gibea.”

english_verse: They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset.
translation_verse: Yiti bɛtoale b’ateetulɛ ne aso; na eyia tɔle ne, né bapingye Gibea bɔ ɔte Benyamin kuro ne.

english_verse: They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
translation_verse: Bɛmakyele bɛhɔle Gibea kyɛ bɛkwaala berɛ. Lewiniɛ ne hɔle kuro ne anu ɔɔtenane kuro ne dwaaso, nakoso ebiala wamva bɛ wangɔ ye awuro kyɛ beesikye berɛ sɔ kɔngɔen ne.

english_verse: Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Aleɛ dwole ne, benwuni biaa aworowaa bie kyɛ ofi ye fieso ɔba. Biaa ne fi Efraim mmokaa aseɛ ne aso, na Gibea yeɛ né ɔte ɔ.

english_verse: He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
translation_verse: Biaa aworowaa ne pagyale ye ti so, na onwuni akwanduniɛ ne wɔ kuro ne dwaaso ne, obisale ye kyɛ, “Nisua yeɛ ɛkɔ ɔ, na efi ni po yeɛ ɛba ye?”

english_verse: “We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home.
translation_verse: Lewiniɛ ne buale ye kyɛ, “Yɛfi Betlehem bɔ ɔwɔ Yuda, na yɛsẽ yɛkɔ namue bie bɔ ɔwɔ dedeede anu wɔ Efraim mmokaa aseɛ ne aso. Berɛ yeɛ mvi ɔ. Ngɔle Betlehem bɔ ɔwɔ Yuda, na mesa mekɔ AWURADE awuro. Nakoso ebiala ɔmmane me nekaa maa nnzikyele.

english_verse: We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
translation_verse: Wɔ ngoaa mɔ, yɛle ɛserɛ ne nzenzaen bɔ yɛkɔfa yɛkɔma yɛ afunum mɔ ɔ, yeɛ me ne braa ye ne aberandeɛ bɔ ɔboka yɛ so ye, yɛle aleɛ ne nzaa. Yɛnhia hwee ko.”

english_verse: The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
translation_verse: Biaa aworowaa ne sele kyɛ, “Nyameɛ ɔma wɔ asomdwee. Ngɔma wɔ nikyee biala bɔ ekohia ɔ. Onhia kyɛ ɛkɔla dwaaso wa ɔ.”

english_verse: The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Yiti ɔfale ye hɔle ye awuro, na ɔmane afunum nemɔ aleɛ. Ɛwɔfoɛ nemɔ nwunzini bɛ gya bo, na bedidili bɛnone. Gibeafoɛ bɔ musue

english_verse: They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
translation_verse: Na begu so bɛgye bɛ nye ne, kuro berɛ mmienzua asanzafoɛ biemɔ bɛɛpɛle awuro ne anwo beyiale, na bɛhyɛle ye bo bɛborole anoa ne anu. Besele biaa aworowaa bɔ yeɛ ɔte awuro ne mene ne kyɛ, “Biaa bɔ wawa w’awuro wa ne, ye ye fite bra maa yɛne ye la.”

english_verse: The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house.
translation_verse: Yeɛ biaa ne bɔ ɔte awuro ne mene ne, ofite ooyiale bɛ, na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Daabi, daabi, nniɛma mɔ, nnɛma ɛmɔyɔ sɔ amumuyɛɛ he. Biaa he te me wɔfoɛ, yiti nnɛma ɛmɔyɔ sɔ nyanzoen nikyee he.

english_verse: Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
translation_verse: Mma brasua bɔ onwuni biaa le, yeɛ ɛwɔfoɛ ne sómaa ne, bɛwɔ wa. Ɛ́mɔma nye bɛ mvite kekesaala ye. Ɛmɔ ne bɛ la, na bɔ ɛmɔ kuro biala, ɛ́mɔfa bɛ́yɔ bɛ; na mmom biaa he de, nnɛma ɛmɔfa sɔ nyanzoen dwirɛ he bedi ye.”

english_verse: The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise,
translation_verse: Nakoso mmenia nemɔ bandie ye dwirɛ ne. Yiti Lewiniɛ ne sɔle ye sómaa ne anu, na ɔwɔle ye tole aluo dɔ mane bɛ. Bɛtole ye mmɔnaa pasaa, na bɛhyɛle ye bɛ ne ye lale kɔngɔen ne amukoraa mane aleɛ hyene. Na alebahyene ne, bɛyakyili ye kyɛ ɔhɔ.

english_verse: and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
translation_verse: Ewienu yɛle kyɛ ɔtete ne, braa ne hɔle ɔɔpɛ fini biaa n’awuro n’anoa nu berɛ, nekaa bɔ né ye somaa ne wɔ ne, na ɔlale berɛ toonn mane aleɛ hyene.

english_verse: About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, braa ne somaa ne dwɔsole, na obukyebukyele awuro berɛ anoa nemɔ. Na ofitele kyɛ ɔtoa ye ateetulɛ ne aso ne, onwuni kyɛ ye sómaa ne la awuro n’anoa nu berɛ, bɔ ye sa gua aponnwaa ne aso ɔ.

english_verse: “Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.” But his wife didn't move. He lifted her body onto his donkey and left.
translation_verse: Osele ye kyɛ, “Dwɔso maa yɛhɔ.” Nakoso braa ne andwudwo. Yeɛ ɔfale braa ne tole afunum ne aso, na osili nu hɔle ye kuro.

english_verse: When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel
translation_verse: Odwuli ye awuro ne, ɔfale dadeɛ ba. Ɔsɔle ye sómaa ne fuin ne anu, na ɔpepɛle nu ahuronzi ahuronzi buru ne nyɔ wɔ ye aporɛ aporɛ so, na ɔfa somane maa bɛhɔle Yisrael maen amukoraa nu.

english_verse: and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.” Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na ɔfale ngraa mane ɛbɔfoɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔbisa Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa sɔ dwirɛ he: ‘Ofi mmerɛ bɔ Yisraelfoɛ fili Misraim aseɛ so bɛwale bɔ ɔbaadwu ɛnɛ ɔ, aso sɔ dwirɛ he, ebie asi le? Ɛ́mɔdwene ye nwo, ɛmɔhɔ ye nwo agyina, ná ɛ́mɔbua ye nwo bie.’ ”

english_verse: The husband of the murdered woman answered: My wife and I went into the town of Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
translation_verse: Na Lewiniɛ bɔ ɔte braa bɔ behuni ye ne ahu ne, obuale kyɛ, “Mene me sómaa yɛhɔle Benyaminfoɛ kuro Gibea so yɛɛlale berɛ kɔngɔen.

english_verse: It was a terrible thing for Israelites to do! So I cut up her body and sent the pieces everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Yeɛ mvale me sómaa ne fuin mbepɛle nu ahuronzi ahuronzi maa bɛfa bɛhɔle Yisrael aseɛ so nekaa biala; ofikyɛ Gibeafoɛ babɔ musue ne nyanzoen bra wɔ Yisrael.

english_verse: You are the people of Israel, and you must decide today what to do about the men of Gibeah.
translation_verse: Yiti, ɛmɔ Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa, ɛ́mɔhyire ɛmɔ adwene, ná ɛmɔhã edwirɛ ne anwo bie.”

english_verse: The whole army was in agreement, and they said, “None of us will go home.
translation_verse: Mmenia ne amukoraa bɛbɔle nu bedwɔsole, na bɛhane kyɛ, “Yɛ nu biala ngɔhɔ ye ɛtena sua nu, yeɛ yɛ nu biala ngosa ngɔhɔ ye awuro.

english_verse: Everyone agreed that Gibeah had to be punished.
translation_verse: Yiti Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa, bɛbɔle nu kyɛ bɛfa koɛ bɛkɔteta kuro ne.

english_verse: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to every town and village in Benjamin. And wherever the messengers went, they said, “How could those worthless men in Gibeah do such a disgusting thing?
translation_verse: Yisrael mmusua kure nemɔ somane mmenia maa behyinini Benyamin abusua kure ne anu ama mukoraa so bebisale bɛ kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ nzɛmmɔne yeɛ ɛmɔali ye wɔ wa ye?

english_verse: We can't allow such a terrible crime to go unpunished in Israel! Hand the men over to us, and we will put them to death.” But the people of Benjamin refused to listen to the other Israelites.
translation_verse: Sɔ busuefoɛ bɔ bɛwɔ Gibea ye, ɛ́mɔye bɛ bɛma yɛ kekesaala ye maa yɛhu bɛ, ná yɛkyikyi bɔne ne yɛfi Yisrael.” Nakoso Benyaminfoɛ bandɛ b’eliɛma mɔ Yisraelfoɛ so.

english_verse: Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel.
translation_verse: Benyaminfoɛ fili bɛ nguro nemɔ aso bɛɛboale bɛ noa wɔ Gibea kyɛ bɛ ne Yisraelfoɛ bɛkwaaho.

english_verse: The other Israelite tribes organized their army and found they had
translation_verse: Na Yisraelfoɛ, sɛ ɛye Benyaminfoɛ fi nu a, bɛboaboale mmenia apee ɛyaa nna noa, bɔ bɛ mukoraa bɛte koɛhonɛfoɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yisraelfoɛ dwɔsole ngyerɛmɔ bɛɛkyekyele asikyeleɛ bepingyele Gibea.

english_verse: Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin. The War Between Israel and Benjamin
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ fale koɛ bɛɛtetale Benyaminfoɛ; bɛ ne Benyaminfoɛ bɛhone wɔ Gibea.

english_verse: Benjamin's soldiers came out of Gibeah and attacked, and when the day was over,
translation_verse: Benyaminfoɛ fili Gibea befitefitele, na sɔ kyẽa ne, behuhuni Yisraelfoɛ bɛ nu apee aburanyɔ ne nyɔ.

english_verse: The people of Israel went to the place of worship at Bethel, where the sacred chest was being kept. They sat on the ground, crying and not eating for the rest of the day. Then about sunset, they offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing. Phinehas the priest then prayed, “Our Lord, the people of Benjamin are our relatives. Should we stop fighting or attack them again?” “Attack!” the Lord answered. “Tomorrow I will let you defeat them.”
translation_verse: na Finehase bɔ ɔse ole Aarɔn awa Eleasa ne, ye yeɛ né ɔte sɔfo wɔ Nyameɛ alaka ne nyunu ɔ.) Bebisale AWURADE kyɛ, “Yɛfa koɛ yɛɛteta y’eliɛma mɔ Benyaminfoɛ bieku, anaakyɛ yɛyakyi?” Na AWURADE buale kyɛ, Ɛmɔɔho, ofikyɛ ɛhema ngɔfa bɛ ngowura ɛmɔ sa.”

english_verse: The Israelites surrounded Gibeah, but stayed where they could not be seen.
translation_verse: Yiti Yisrael mane koɛhonɛfoɛ bɛɛfeale bɛpɛle Gibea nwo beyiale.

english_verse: The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin,
translation_verse: Yiti Benyaminfoɛ kakyili bɛ nwo befili Yisraelfoɛ nyunu bɛfale bɛ nye behyirele ɛserɛ so atee ne aso; nakoso Yisraelfoɛ buale bɛ noa so, na Yisraelfoɛ bɔ né bɛwɔ kuro ne anu ne, bɛhane Benyaminfoɛ bemiane behuhuni bɛ.

english_verse: who were having to fight on all sides. The Israelite soldiers never let up their attack. They chased and killed the warriors of Benjamin as far as a place directly east of Gibeah,
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ pɛle Benyaminfoɛ nwo yiale. Bɛfoane bɛ befili Noha, na behuhuni bɛ alaa beedwuli Gibea eyia afiteleɛ so.

english_verse: Some other warriors of Benjamin turned and ran down the road toward Rimmon Rock in the desert. The Israelites killed
translation_verse: Bɛkakyili bɛ nwo bɛfale bɛ nye behyirele ɛserɛ so bɛhɔle Rimon nyɔbotaen ne anwo ne, Yisraelfoɛ huhuni bɛ nu apee nnu wɔ atimbire nemɔ aso. Bɛfoane bɛ alaa beedwuli Gidom, na behuhuni bɛ nu apee nyɔ.

english_verse: Twenty-five thousand soldiers of Benjamin died that day, all of them experienced warriors.
translation_verse: Yiti Benyamin koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa bɔ betiratira akodeɛ, bɔ bɛtotɔle sɔ kyẽa nen, bɛ somaa te apee aburanyɔ ne nnu; bɛ mukoraati bɛte koɛhonɛfoɛ ahoneserɛfoɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites turned back and went to every town in Benjamin's territory, killing all the people and animals, and setting the towns on fire.
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ sa kakyili bɛ nye besa bɛwale Benyaminfoɛ so. Bɛbɔle kuro ne, na bele ngrandɛ behuhuni mmenia amukoraa ne ngaka amukoraa. Na nguro bɔ baha nemɔ koso, bɛtole bɛ nu see.

english_verse: When the Israelites had met at Mizpah before the war with Benjamin, they had made this sacred promise: “None of us will ever let our daughters marry any man from Benjamin.”
translation_verse: Né Yisraelfoɛ ata ndaen wɔ Misepa kyɛ, “Yɛ nu biala ngɔfa ɔwa brasua ngɔma Benyaminniɛ agyaa.”

english_verse: After the war with Benjamin, the Israelites went to the place of worship at Bethel and sat there until sunset. They cried loudly and bitterly
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ hɔle Betel. Bɛtenane Nyameɛ nyunu wɔ berɛ maa oodwuli nɔsoa, na besuni hahii.

english_verse: and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”
translation_verse: Bɛhane kyɛ, “Ao AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ, ɔwale ye sɛ bɔ ɛnɛ ye de yɛpena abusua kure ko a, yɛnnwu ye wɔ Yisrael ɔ?”

english_verse: Early the next morning, the Israelites built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Ye alehyeleɛ ne, maen ne dwɔsole ngyerɛmɔ tutuutu. Besili afɔleɛ bokyea wɔ berɛ, na bɛbobɔle naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne asomdwee afɔleɛ.

english_verse: Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yisraelfoɛ bisale kyɛ, “Yisrael mmusua kure ne, bɛ nu beni yeɛ dwaa bɔ yɛbɔle wɔ AWURADE nyunu ne, wamma ye bo bie ɔ?” Ofikyɛ né bata ndaen bato berɛ kyɛ, ebiala bɔ wamma AWURADE nyunu wɔ Misepa ne, odi kyɛ beku ye.

english_verse: The Israelites were sad about what had happened to the Benjamin tribe, and they said, “One of our tribes was almost wiped out.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yisraelfoɛ nwuni b’eliɛma mɔ Benyaminfoɛ anwumvoin, na bɛhane kyɛ, “Abusua kure ko de, ɛnɛ wabɔ wɔ Yisrael.

english_verse: Only a few men of Benjamin weren't killed in the war. We need to get wives for them, so the tribe won't completely disappear. But how can we do that, after promising in the Lord's name that we wouldn't let them marry any of our daughters?”
translation_verse: Bɛbɔ baha ye, ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ né yanya mmraa yamaa bagyigya, wɔ aberɛ bɔ yafa AWURADE yata ndaen kyɛ yɛngɔfa yɛ mma mmrasua ngɔma Benyaminfoɛ agyaa ɔ?”

english_verse: Again the Israelites asked, “Did any of the tribes stay away from the meeting at Mizpah?” After asking around, they discovered that no one had come from Jabesh in Gilead.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ bɛhale mmenia bɔ bayia nu berɛ ne, né Yabese Gileadeniɛ biala nne berɛ bie.

english_verse: The warriors attacked Jabesh in Gilead, and returned to their camp at Shiloh in Canaan with
translation_verse: Benyane ndaluwa bɔ bennwuni biaa le ɔ ɛyaa nna wɔ Yabese Gileadefoɛ nu, na bɛfale bɛ bɛwale asikyeleɛ ne anu berɛ wɔ Silo, bɔ ɔwɔ Kanaan aseɛ so.

english_verse: The Israelites met and sent messengers to the men of Benjamin at Rimmon Rock, telling them that the Israelites were willing to make peace with them.
translation_verse: Afei Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa bɛfale ngraa bɛɛmane Benyaminfoɛ bɔ baatena Rimon nyɔbotaen ne anwo ne kyɛ, afei de bɛ ne bɛ kɔtena asomdwee nu.

english_verse: So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, Benyaminfoɛ sale bɛ si bɛwale, na Yabese Gileade mmrasua bɔ Yisraelfoɛ yakyili bɛ maa benyane bɛ ti bedidili nu ne, bɛfale bɛ bɛmane Benyaminfoɛ, nakoso banzo Benyaminfoɛ ti.

english_verse: The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes.
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ nwuni Benyaminfoɛ anwumvoin, ofikyɛ né AWURADE ama Yisrael mmusua kure nemɔ anu atete.

english_verse: Then their leaders said: All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left?
translation_verse: Yiti Yisrael mbanyi bisale kyɛ, “Benyaminfoɛ ngaa bɔ baha ye, yɛkɔyɛ sɛɛ né yanya mmraa maa bagya, ofikyɛ brasua biala wanga wɔ Benyaminfoɛ nu.”

english_verse: If they don't have children, one of the Israelite tribes will die out.
translation_verse: Na bebuale kyɛ, “Benyaminfoɛ bɔ banya bɛ ti badidi nu ne, odi kyɛ benya bɛ bosofoɛ, amaa ɔnate so abusua kure ko boso wannua wɔ Yisrael.

english_verse: But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
translation_verse: Nakoso yɛngɔhora yɛngɔfa yɛ mma mmrasua yɛngɔma bɛ agyaa.” Ofikyɛ né Yisraelfoɛ bali moa bata ndaen kyɛ, “Ebiala bɔ ɔkɔma Benyaminniɛ braa maa okogya ne, musue to ye.”

english_verse: Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
translation_verse: Yiti bɛhane kyɛ, “AWURADE afoɛnoa aluolue ne, bekoli ye wɔ Silo bɔ ɔwɔ Betel sorɔ dɔ ne. Atimbire bɔ ofi Betel kɔ Sɛkem ne, Silo wɔ ye eyia afiteleɛ so, na osa wɔ Lebona ngwaen.”

english_verse: Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife.
translation_verse: ná ɛ́mɔnea. Sɛ Silo ndaluwa nemɔ fite ba kyɛ bɛbaago b’abilie ne a, ɛ́mɔfi bobe boo nemɔ anu befite. Ɛmɔ anu biala ɔɔbɔ Silo brasua ko abum ɔfa ye yɛ ɔye, ná ɛmɔfa bɛ bɛhɔ Benyamin aseɛ so.

english_verse: If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ bɛ baba mɔ anaa b’eliɛma mmienzua mɔ fa ye nwo dwirɛ bato yɛ nyunu a, yɛkɔha yɛkohyire bɛ kyɛ, ‘Ɛ́mɔfa ɛmɔ nye bɛ́to yɛ, ná ɛmɔlo bɛ; ofikyɛ nna koɛ nu yeɛ yɛhyele braa yɛmane bɛ nu biala ɔ. Yeɛ ɛmɔ koso ɛmɔnni fɔ kyɛ ɛmɔafa ɛmɔ mma mmrasua bama bɛ agyaa ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
translation_verse: Benyaminfoɛ yɔle sɔ ala. Mmrasua bɔ bego abilie bɔ bɛbobɔle bɛ abum ne, ɔnate so mane bɛ nu biala nyane braa ogyale. Besa bɛhɔle b’aseɛ so, na besa bɛkyekyele bɛ nguro mɔ bɛtenane nu.

english_verse: Afterwards, the rest of the Israelites returned to their homes and families. Israel Was Not Ruled by a King
translation_verse: Afei Yisraelfoɛ fili berɛ mmusua kure mmusua kure ne mmusua mmusua, na besili nu bɛhɔle bɛ bɔbɔ b’aseɛ mɔ so.

english_verse: In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né ɛhene biala nne Yisrael, yiti né ebiala yɔ bɔ okuro ɔ.

english_verse: Before Israel was ruled by kings, Elimelech from the clan of Ephrath lived in the town of Bethlehem. His wife was named Naomi, and their two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. But when their crops failed in Israel, they moved to the country of Moab. And while they were there,
translation_verse: Biaa ne li Elimɛlɛke, yeɛ ɔye ne koso li Naomi. Ye mma mmienzua nemɔ li Malon ne Kilion. Bɛte Efratefoɛ bɔ befi Betlehem bɔ ɔwɔ Yuda, na betu bɛɛtenane Moabo aseɛ so.

english_verse: Elimelech died, leaving Naomi with only her two sons.
translation_verse: Nakoso Naomi ohu Elimɛlɛke wuli, maa ɔhale ye ne ye mma mmienzua nyɔ ne.

english_verse: Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later,
translation_verse: Begyigyale Moabo mmrasua; ko li Ɔpa, yeɛ ko koso li Rutu. Ye si ye, bɛtenane berɛ kɔyɛ afoɛ buru ne,

english_verse: When Naomi heard that the Lord had given his people a good harvest, she and her two daughters-in-law got ready to leave Moab and go to Judah. As they were on their way there,
translation_verse: Ɔne ye sia mmrasua nyɔ nemɔ betuli bɛ bo befili kuro bɔ né bɛte so ne aso, kyɛ besa bɛkɔ Yuda aseɛ so.

english_verse: Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you.
translation_verse: Nakoso Naomi sele ye sia mmrasua nyɔ nemɔ kyɛ, “Ebiala osa ɔhɔ ye maame awuro. AWURADE ɔlo ɛmɔ, kyɛbɔ ɛmɔ ne me, yeɛ bɛ bɔ bawu ne bɛtenane nyemene so ne.

english_verse: May he give each of you another husband and a home of your own.” Naomi kissed them. They cried
translation_verse: Mesrɛ kyɛ AWURADE ɔma ɛmɔ nu biala onya asetena paa wɔ ɛmɔ ahu mɔ awuro.” Afei ɔtɔle bɛ nu, na besuni hahii.

english_verse: and said, “We want to go with you and live among your people.”
translation_verse: Bebuale ye kyɛ, “Daabi, yɛne wɔ kosa kɔhɔ w’abusua nu.”

english_verse: But she replied, “My daughters, why don't you return home? What good will it do you to go with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry?
translation_verse: Nakoso Naomi sele kyɛ, “Me mma mɔ, ɛ́mɔsa, nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔpena kyɛ ɛmɔ ne me bɛkɔ ɔ? Aso ngɔhora ngosa ngɔwo mmaa mmienzua maa bekogya ɛmɔ anaa?

english_verse: You must go back home, because I am too old to marry again. Even if I got married tonight and later had more sons,
translation_verse: Me mma mɔ, ɛ́mɔsa bɛhɔ, ofikyɛ nekaa bɔ manyi madwu ye, bienzua biala ngogya me. Na sɛ manya anyelasoɛ po, ná sɛ ɛnɛ kɔngɔen ye ala menya biaa megya mewo mmaa mmienzua po a,

english_verse: would you wait for them to become old enough to marry? No, my daughters! Life is harder for me than it is for you, because the Lord has turned against me.”
translation_verse: aso ɛmɔkɔnwondɛ toonn maa bekonyi? Aso ɛmɔngogya biaa? Daabi, me mma mɔ, mali yealɛ matra ɛmɔ, ofikyɛ AWURADE ayakyi me nu amaa manwu amaneɛ.”

english_verse: They cried again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held on to her.
translation_verse: Yeɛ besa besuni hahii. Ɔpa tɔle ye sia brasua Naomi nu ɔne ye belili ngraa, nakoso Rutu de, ɔte matane ye.

english_verse: Naomi then said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and to her gods! Why don't you go with her?”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Naomi sele kyɛ, “Nea kyɛ ɛhora Ɔpa wasa ye si wahɔ ye abusua ne ye nyameɛ mɔ dɔ ɔ; di ɛhora ne asi.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “Please don't tell me to leave you and return home! I will go where you go, I will live where you live; your people will be my people, your God will be my God.
translation_verse: Nakoso Rutu buale kyɛ, “Nnɛhyɛ me kyɛ nyakyi wɔ nu ngɔ, anaakyɛ nyakyi wɔ si lilɛ! Nekaa bɔ ɛkɔhɔ ne, berɛ yeɛ ngɔhɔ ɔ; yeɛ nekaa bɔ ɛkɔtena ne, berɛ yeɛ ngɔtena ɔ; wɔ maen kɔyɛ me maen, yeɛ wɔ Nyameɛ kɔyɛ me Nyameɛ.

english_verse: I will die where you die and be buried beside you. May the Lord punish me if we are ever separated, even by death!”
translation_verse: Nekaa bɔ ekowu ne, berɛ yeɛ ngowu ɔ, na berɛ yeɛ bekosie me ɔ. AWURADE ɔne me li ye pasaa maa ɔbo so, sana ewue yeɛ ɔkɔtete me ne wɔ y’afia ɔ!”

english_verse: When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
translation_verse: Naomi nwuni kyɛ Rutu nye aboro kyɛ ɔne ye bɛkɔhɔ ne, wanga hwee wangyire ye ko.

english_verse: They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
translation_verse: Yiti bɛ munyɔ besili nu bɛhɔle beedwuli Betlehem. Na beedwuli Betlehem nen, ɔnate bɛ ti, kurotue ne amukoraa bɔle twi, na mmrasua nemɔ bisale kyɛ, “Yiti Naomi ɛhe?”

english_verse: Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter.
translation_verse: Na Naomi sele bɛ kyɛ, “Nnɛma ɛmɔfrɛ me Naomi ko, ɛ́mɔfrɛ me Mara, ofikyɛ Ɛdangama ama me bra ayɛ weewee.

english_verse: I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
translation_verse: Me sa bum yeɛ mva ngɔle ɔ, nakoso AWURADE amaa masa mawa nzanza; nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔfrɛ me Naomi, wɔ berɛ bɔ AWURADE ne me ali ye anyeborolɛ so, ná Ɛdangama amaa asane piri ato me ɔ?”

english_verse: The barley harvest was just beginning when Naomi and Ruth, her Moabite daughter-in-law, arrived in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Yiti Naomi ne ye sia brasua Moaboniɛ Rutu, bɔ ɔne ye befili Moabo aseɛ so besa bɛwale ne, bɛwale Betlehem mmerɛ bɔ né bɛ́hyɛ ye bo bɛte ayuo ɔ.

english_verse: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, Boase fili Betlehem wale. Ɔha hyirele ayuotelɛfoɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “AWURADE gyina ɛmɔ si oo.” Na bebuale ye kyɛ, “AWURADE yira wɔ oo.”

english_verse: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
translation_verse: Na Boase bisale ye somvoɛ bɔ ɔnea ayuotelɛfoɛ nemɔ aso ne kyɛ, “Sɔ taluwa he, ofi awuro beni anu?”

english_verse: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
translation_verse: Yeɛ somvoɛ bɔ ɔnea ayuotelɛfoɛ nemɔ aso ne buale kyɛ, “Moaboniɛ bɔ ɔne Naomi befili Moabo aseɛ so bɛwale ne, ye ɛne.

english_verse: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
translation_verse: Ɔsrɛle me kyɛ, ‘Maa nni ayuotelɛfoɛ nemɔ si ná nzesa bɔ basesa bahɔ maa waha berɛ ne bie.’ Na ɔwale ye, wagyina ye gya so fi ngyerɛmɔ maa waadwu bekye, bɔ ollele ye nwome koraa ɔ.”

english_verse: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
translation_verse: Yeɛ Boase sele Rutu kyɛ, “Mma, tie, nnɛfi fie he aso, yeɛ nnɛkɔ foforɛ so kɔsesa ayuo si bɔ bate maa waha berɛ ne bie, na mmom fa wɔ nwo bɔ me ndaluwa nemɔ.

english_verse: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
translation_verse: Ma wɔ nye sra nekaa bɔ bɛte ayuo ne, ná di bɛ si. Mahã mahyire mmerandeɛ nemɔ kyɛ nnɛmaa bɛha w’adwene. Sɛ nzuhɔen ku wɔ a, kɔ bua nemɔ anwo dɔ kɔno nzue bɔ mmerandeɛ nemɔ basa ne bie.”

english_verse: Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Rutu kotole aseɛnwo berɛ, ɔfale ye nye butuli berɛ, na obisale Boase kyɛ, “Ɔwale ye sɛ bɔ alo me sɔa ye, bɔ ayɛ me paa sɔaa ye, wɔ aberɛ bɔ nde ɛwɔfoɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
translation_verse: Nakoso Boase buale ye kyɛ, “Ofi mmerɛ bɔ ehu wuli ɔ, bɔ ayɔ ama wɔ sia brasua ne amukoraa, babɔ me amaneɛ: kyɛbɔ ɛyakyili wɔ baba ne wɔ maame ne wɔ bɔbɔ wɔ maen berɛ, ná ɛɛtoale mmenia bɔ né ɛnze bɛ ɔ ne.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
translation_verse: Bɔ ayɔ ye, mesrɛ kyɛ AWURADE ɔma wɔ ye nwo akatuaa. AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ, bɔ aabɔ wɔ nwo adwaa wɔ ye ndaa bo ne, mesrɛ kyɛ ɔma wɔ akatuaa mmorosoɛ.”

english_verse: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Rutu sele kyɛ, “Me mene, kɔ so do me sɔ ala, ofikyɛ akyekye me wora. Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ nna w’afaneɛ nemɔ bie ole me, nakoso ɛne w’afaneɛ adwudwo nyemene so.”

english_verse: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
translation_verse: Adidie mmerɛ sone ne, Boase sele ye kyɛ, “Bra baali aleɛ ye bie, ná fa wɔ paanoo ne bɔ nzaa kekarekekare ye anu bie.” Yiti Rutu tenane ayuotelɛfoɛ nemɔ anwo berɛ, na Boase mane ye ayuo bɔ bahye ne bie. Rutu lili mane ye ko yili maa ebie hale.

english_verse: When Ruth left to start picking up grain, Boaz told his men, “Don't stop her, even if she picks up grain from where it is stacked.
translation_verse: Rutu dwɔsole kyɛ ɔkwaasesa ayuo bɔ bate basesa maa waha berɛ ne bie nen, Boase sele ye mmerandeɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔma ɔsesa bɔ baboaboa ye noa ne bie, na nnɛma ɛmɔsi ye ate.

english_verse: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
translation_verse: Yiti Rutu boaboale ayuo ne noa wɔ fie ne aso toonn maa aleɛ dwole. Yeɛ ɔborole bɔ waboaboa ye noa ne, na onyane kɔyɛ olonka buru.

english_verse: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
translation_verse: Rutu soa wale kuro, na ye sia ne nwuni ayuo bɔ waasesa wawa ne. Afei aleɛ bɔ Rutu lili mane ye ko yili ne, ɔfale ye ngaa mane ye sia ne.

english_verse: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
translation_verse: Yeɛ ye sia bisale ye kyɛ, “Nisua yeɛ ɛnɛ ɛɛsesale ayuo ye? Fie beni aso yeɛ ɛhɔle ɔ? Nyameɛ yira sona bɔ wayɛ wɔ paa sɔaa ye.” Yeɛ Rutu hane sona bɔ ɔhɔle ye fieso adwuma ne nwo dwirɛ hyirele ye sia ne kyɛ, “Biaa bɔ ngɔnyɔle adwuma wɔ ye fieso ne, bɛfrɛ ye Boase.”

english_verse: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
translation_verse: Na Naomi sele ye sia ne kyɛ, “AWURADE bɔ daa ɔdo teasefoɛ ne awufoɛ ne, óyira sɔ sona ne!” Naomi sa sele ye kyɛ, “Sɔ biaa ne, ɔte yɛ abusuaniɛ, yɛ bɔbɔ yɛ nwoniɛ kaenn.”

english_verse: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Moaboniɛ Rutu hane kyɛ, “Ye po ɔha hyirele me kyɛ, Fa wɔ nwo bɔ m’adwumayɔlɛfoɛ nemɔ, kɔpem kyɛ bɛkɔte m’ayuo ne amukoraa bekoyie ɔ.”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
translation_verse: Na Naomi sele ye sia Rutu kyɛ, “Mma, ɔte paa kyɛ ɛkɔfa wɔ nwo kɔbɔ ye ndaluwa nemɔ ɔ; ebie mbaen fieso de, ebiaa né baha w’adwene.”

english_verse: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_verse: Yiti ɔfale ye nwo bɔle Boase ndaluwa nemɔ, na ɔsesale ayuo alaa kɔpem kyɛ ayuo ne atokoɔ telɛ pɛle nu ɔ. Na Rutu hɔle so ne ye sia bɛtenane.

english_verse: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, Rutu sia Naomi sele ye kyɛ, “Mma, aso onhia kyɛ memaa egyina wɔ gya so, amaa ɔnate so wayie wɔ yé?

english_verse: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
translation_verse: Yɛ nwoniɛ Boase wɔ berɛ. Ye yeɛ ɛne ye ndaluwa mɔ bɛyɔ adwuma ne. Tie, ɛnɛ kɔngɔen, okohuhu ayuo so wɔ nekaa bɔ bɛboro ayuo ne.

english_verse: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Yiti bia ná popa. Wura w’ataadeɛ bɔ ɔyɛ nyemene paa ná kɔ nekaa bɔ bɛboro ayuo ne. Nakoso nnɛye wɔ nwo ali kyire biaa ne kɔpem kyɛ okodidi ná ɔkɔno nzaa koyie ɔ.

english_verse: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɔda a, nea nekaa bɔ ɔkɔla ne yé. Kɔye ɛtena ne fi ye gya bo ná da berɛ; na ɔkɔha nikyee bɔ odi kyɛ ɛyɔ ɔ kohyire wɔ.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “I'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Na Rutu sele Naomi kyɛ, “Bɔ aha biala, ngɔyɔ.”

english_verse: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
translation_verse: Yiti Rutu hɔle nekaa bɔ bɛboro ayuo ne, na ɔɔyɔle kyɛbɔ ye sia hyirele ye ne ala.

english_verse: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
translation_verse: Boase didili ná ɔnone nzaa yiele bɔ ye nye agye ne, ɔɔlale atokoɔ kure ne anwo. Yeɛ Rutu yɛle kudɛɛ ɔɔyele Boase gya nwo tena ne, na ɔlale berɛ.

english_verse: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
translation_verse: Bebuli aleɛ nu ne, biaa ne bɔle pitiri, na ɔpɛnene ye nye ne, mvum nu, onwuni kyɛ brasua bie la ye gya ngwaen berɛ!

english_verse: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
translation_verse: Obisale kyɛ, “Wɔ nwa ɛne?” Yeɛ obuale ye kyɛ, “Me ɔ, w’afaneɛ Rutu; trɛ wɔ tena ne anu fa kata me nwo, ofikyɛ wɔ yeɛ ɛte koliagyaa ɔ.”

english_verse: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
translation_verse: Na Boase sele ye kyɛ, “Mma, AWURADE yira wɔ. Nahorɛ bɔ ali ye kekesaala ye ne, ɔtra nahorɛ bɔ ali moa ali ama wɔ sia ne. Ofikyɛ angɔanni mmerandeɛ mɔ si: kyɛ ehianiɛ oo, kyɛ sikaniɛ oo.

english_verse: Don't worry, I'll do what you have asked. You are respected by everyone in town.
translation_verse: Afei, mma, nnɛsuro. Nikyee bɔ ekobisa biala, ngɔyɔ ngɔma wɔ, ofikyɛ kuro wa ama mukoraa se ye kyɛ ɛte brasua bɔ wɔ suban te paa ɔ.

english_verse: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
translation_verse: Na ɔwɔ nu kyɛ nde abusuaniɛ kaenn de, nakoso abusuaniɛ foforɛ bie wɔ berɛ bɔ opingye wɔ sia abusua tra me ɔ.

english_verse: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
translation_verse: Da wa ɛnɛ kɔngɔen ye, na aleɛ kye ngyerɛmɔ, ná sɛ ode to nu kyɛ ɔkɔyɛ ehu koliagyaa kogya wɔ a, ye de ye paa nu ɔ. Na sɛ ɔngɔyɛ ehu koliagyaa ngogya wɔ de a, ye de, kyɛ AWURADE te ase ye, me yeɛ ngɔyɛ ehu koliagyaa ngogya wɔ ɔ. Da wa ma aleɛ hye.”

english_verse: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
translation_verse: Yiti Rutu lale ye gya ngwaen berɛ maa aleɛ hyene, nakoso odwɔsole mmerɛ bɔ né maen nu onnya ɔttetele ɔ, ofikyɛ Boase nyane adwene kyɛ, “Onni kyɛ ebiala nwu ye kyɛ braa ne wale nekaa bɔ bɛboro aburoo ne.”

english_verse: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
translation_verse: Boase sele ye kyɛ, “W’ataadeɛ aguasoɛ bɔ owura wɔ ne, trɛ nu.” Yiti ɔtrɛle nu, na Boase pɛle ayuo olonka nzia, na ɔfa soale Rutu. Na afei Boase sili nu hɔle kuro ne anu dɔ.

english_verse: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
translation_verse: kyɛ, “Ye yeɛ ɔmane me ayuo olonka nzia he ɔ, ofikyɛ ɔnwa: ‘Nnɛfa nzanza sa kɔ wɔ sia dɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Naomi buale kyɛ, “Mma, nya aboterɛ ná nea bɔ okofi edwirɛ ne anu kɔwa ɔ, ofikyɛ biaa ne ngɔhora tena, sana wabɔ edwirɛ ne porɛ ɛnɛ.”

english_verse: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
translation_verse: Boase hɔle kuro berɛ pambim ne anwo ɔɔtenane ase. Wangyɛ yeɛ busuaniɛ bɔ Boase hane ye dwirɛ ne koso ɔɔpɛle nu berɛ ɔ. Na Boase frɛle ye kyɛ, “Nniɛma, bra wa baatena ase.” Na opingyele ye ɔɔtenane ase.

english_verse: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
translation_verse: Yeɛ Boase frɛle kuro berɛ mbanyi nemɔ anu buru, na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔtena wa.” Na bɛtenatenane berɛ.

english_verse: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
translation_verse: Afei osele busuaniɛ ne kyɛ, “Naomi bɔ wafi Moabo aseɛ so wawa ne, ɔbaatɔne yɛ abusuaniɛ Elimɛlɛke ye aseɛ.

english_verse: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
translation_verse: Yiti mayɛ kyɛ meye w’asotire kyɛ, pɔ aseɛ ne wɔ mbanyi bɔ bayia wa ye, ɔne me maen mbanyi ye mɔ bɛ nyunu. Sɛ ɛkɔpɔ aseɛ ne a, pɔ ye; nakoso sɛ ɛngɔpɔ ye de a, ka kyire me maa nwu ye, ofikyɛ sona biala nne berɛ bɔ osã wɔ nwo ɔpɔ aseɛ ne a ɔyɛ yé ɔ. Sɛ ambɔ aseɛ ne a, yeɛ mekora mepɔ ye ɔ.” Na obuale kyɛ, “Ngɔpɔ aseɛ ne.”

english_verse: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Boase toale so hane kyɛ, “Kyẽa bɔ ɛkɔpɔ sɔ aseɛ ne wɔ Naomi sa nu ne, ye de Moaboniɛ Rutu, bɔ ɔte biaa bɔ wawu ne kunaniɛ ne, odi kyɛ egya ye, amaa ɔnate so biaa bɔ wawu ne, ye dumaa ahɔ so wala ye agyapadeɛ so.”

english_verse: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ abusuaniɛ ne tele sɔ dwirɛ nen, ɔhane kyɛ, “Sɛ mepɔ agyapadeɛ ye mefa a, me mma kɔhwere me bɔbɔ deinn m’agyapadeɛ deɛ. Agyapadeɛ bɔ ahaa me yeɛ odi kyɛ mepɔ ne, kɔpɔ fa, ofikyɛ mengɔhora ngɔpɔ ye.”

english_verse: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
translation_verse: Yiti mmerɛ bɔ abusuaniɛ ne sele Boase kyɛ, “Pɔ agyapadeɛ ne fa” ne, ɔyele ye mbaboa ko.

english_verse: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Boase sele mbanyi nemɔ ne mmenia nemɔ amukoraa kyɛ, “Ɛnɛ ɛmɔdi adanzeɛ, kyɛ Elimɛlɛke, Kilion ne Malon b’agyapadeɛ biala, mapɔ mafi Naomi sa nu.

english_verse: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
translation_verse: Afei koso, Moaboniɛ Rutu, bɔ né ɔte Malon aye ne, magya ye, amaa ɔnate so sona bɔ wawu ne, ye dumaa ahɔ so wala ye agyapadeɛ so; amaa ɔnate so sona bɔ wawu ne, ye dumaa angyikyi wamvi ye abusua ɔne ye kuro nu. Ɛnɛ, ɛmɔte m’adanzefoɛ.”

english_verse: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Yeɛ mmenia bɔ né baayia pambim ne anu berɛ ne amukoraa, bɛ ne mbanyi nemɔ bebuale kyɛ, “Yɛdi adanzeɛ. Braa ye bɔ ɛkwaagya ye ba w’awuro ne, AWURADE ma ɔyɛ kyɛ Rahɛl ne Lea, bɔ bɛ munyɔ yeɛ besuli Yisrael awuro ama nen. AWURADE ma wɔ boso trɛ wɔ Efrata, ná ɛyɛ sona titire wɔ Betlehem.

english_verse: May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
translation_verse: Na ngwadaa bɔ AWURADE kɔfa taluwa he aso ma wɔ sa kɔha bɛ ne, yɛsrɛ kyɛ AWURADE ɔfa bɛ so ma w’awuro ama bɛyɛ kyɛ Yuda ne Tamar bɛ wa Pɛrɛse ye awuro ama.” Dawide nana mɔ

english_verse: Boaz married Ruth, and the Lord blessed her with a son.
translation_verse: Yiti Boase gyale Rutu maa ɔɔyɛle ɔye, na ɔne ye bɛlale. Na AWURADE mane Rutu nwonzɛle, na ɔwole baa bienzua.

english_verse: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Yeɛ mmrasua nemɔ sele Naomi kyɛ, “Animnyam hã AWURADE bɔ ɛnɛ kyẽa ye wamaa anya koliagyaa wɔ w’awuro ɔ. AWURADE ɔma ɔyɛ sona titire wɔ Yisrael!

english_verse: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
translation_verse: Ɔkɔmaa ekonya wɔ boso ama, ná wama wɔ wɔ noa aleɛ wɔ wɔ nworowaa nu. Ofikyɛ wɔ sia bɔ okuro wɔ dwirɛ, bɔ yeɛ ɔtra mmaa mmienzua nzoo ma wɔ ne, ye yeɛ ɔwole ye ɔ.”

english_verse: Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Naomi mane akwadaa ne aso fale ye bɔle ye hue so, na ɔyɛle akwadaa ne neafoɛ.

english_verse: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
translation_verse: Mandamu berɛ mmrasua nemɔ tole akwadaa ne dumaa, na bɛhane kyɛ, “Bawo baa bienzua bama Naomi.” Bɛtole ye dumaa Obɛde; na ye yeɛ ɔwole Yese, bɔ yeɛ ɔte Dawide baba ne.

english_verse: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
translation_verse: Né biaa bie wɔ berɛ bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Ɛlkana. Ofi Ramatim Sofim bɔ ɔwɔ Efraim mmokaa aseɛ ne aso. Ɔse ole Yeroham bɔ ɔse ole Elihu bɔ ɔse ole Tohu bɔ ye koso ɔse ole Efraimniɛ Sufe ne.

english_verse: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
translation_verse: Né ɔye mɔ nyɔ. Ko li Hana, yeɛ ko wora li Penina. Né Penina le mmaa, nakoso Hana de, né olle ba.

english_verse: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
translation_verse: Afoɛ biala, né Ɛlkana fi ye kuro kɔ Silo kɔsɔne Asafo AWURADE ná ɔbɔ afɔleɛ ma ye wɔ berɛ. Hofini ne Finehase bɔ bɛte Eli mma mmienzua nyɔ ne, né bɛte AWURADE asɔfo wɔ Silo.

english_verse: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne dwu ná Ɛlkana bɔ afɔleɛ a, né ɔyɛ a ɔma ɔye Penina ne ye mma mmienzua ne mmrasua ne amukoraa afɔleɛ nningyein ne bie;

english_verse: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
translation_verse: nakoso Hana de, ɔma ye afɔleɛ nningyein ne mmɔhoɛ nyɔ, ofikyɛ né ɔte ye yɛyerɛ braa, ɔwɔ nu kyɛ né AWURADE amaa wayɛ mmotaen.

english_verse: Peninnah liked to make Hannah feel miserable about not having any children,
translation_verse: Né Hana ɔhora taa ka ye anyinga paa ma ye wora bɔ, ofikyɛ né AWURADE amaa wayɛ mmotaen.

english_verse: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
translation_verse: Sɔ dwirɛ ne hɔle so afoɛnoa biala; na mmerɛ biala bɔ bɛkɔhɔ AWURADE awuro ne, ɔyɛ a Penina ka ye anyinga. Yiti ɔyɛ a Hana sũ, na onnidi.

english_verse: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”

english_verse: When the sacrifice had been offered, and they had eaten the meal, Hannah got up and went to pray. Eli was sitting in his chair near the door to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Bedidili bɛnone beyiele wɔ Silo nen, Hana dwɔsole [ɔɔfale ye mbaeɛ tole AWURADE nyunu]. Né ɔsɔfo Eli te bia so wɔ AWURADE asɔneyɛɛ sua anoa nu berɛ.

english_verse: Hannah was heartbroken and was crying as she prayed,
translation_verse: Né Hana wora abɔ paa, na ole esuɛ hahii fale ye mbaeɛ tole AWURADE nyunu.

english_verse: “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
translation_verse: Na Hana hyɛle bɔ kyɛ, “O Asafo AWURADE, sɛ ahaa ɛkɔpɛ wɔ nye kɔnea w’afaneɛ aworabɔlɛ, ná ɛkɔkaye me, ná amma wɔ wora amvi w’afaneɛ, ná mmom ɛma w’afaneɛ baa bienzua a, ye de ngɔfa ye ngɔma wɔ AWURADE mmerɛ amukoraa bɔ ɔte ase ɔ; na dɛmaa biala ngɔtɔ ye ti so.”

english_verse: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
translation_verse: Né Hana bɔ mbaeɛ wɔ ye ti anu. Né ɔbesebese ye noa, nakoso edwirɛ bɔ ɔka de, ebiala ande. Na ɛhe mane Eli susuli kyɛ wano nzaa wabo.

english_verse: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
translation_verse: Yiti Eli sele ye kyɛ, “Kyinzu koraa yeɛ ɛkɔno nzaa kɔbo maa okoodwu ɔ? Yakyi wɔ nzaanonɛ ne!

english_verse: “Sir, please don't think I'm no good!” Hannah answered. “I'm not drunk, and I haven't been drinking. But I do feel miserable and terribly upset. I've been praying all this time, telling the Lord about my problems.”
translation_verse: Nnɛbu w’afaneɛ kyɛ nde brasua sanzaniɛ bie, ofikyɛ edwirɛ yealɛ ne aworabɔlɛ bɔ wato me yeɛ mabɔ ye nwo mbaeɛ maa waadwu bekye ye.”

english_verse: Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Eli sele kyɛ, “Fa asomdwee kɔ, na abisadeɛ bɔ afa ato Yisrael Nyameɛ nyunu ne, mesrɛ kyɛ ɔ́yɔ ma wɔ.”

english_verse: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
translation_verse: Na Hana sele kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, w’adaworoma, do w’afaneɛ sɔ ala.” Afei Hana fili berɛ hɔle, odidili, na aworabɔlɛ andira ye ko. Samuel aworɛ

english_verse: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, bedwɔsole ngyerɛmɔ tutuutu bɛsɔnene AWURADE, na afei besa bɛhɔle bɛ kuro Rama. Ɛlkana ne ɔye Hana bɛlale, na AWURADE kayele Hana.

english_verse: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
translation_verse: Hana nwonzɛle, na mmerɛ ne sone ne, ɔwole baa bienzua, na ɔtole ye dumaa Samuel, ofikyɛ ɔhane kyɛ, “Nzrɛle ye mvili AWURADE berɛ.”

english_verse: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɛlkana ne ye awuro ama mukoraati bɛhɔle Silo kyɛ ɔkwaabɔ afoɛnoa afɔleɛ ne ma AWURADE ná otua ye aboadeɛ.

english_verse: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Hana de wangɔ bie, na ɔha hyirele ohu kyɛ, “Sɛ akwadaa ne pɛ nyɔfone a, ngɔfa ye ngɔɔma AWURADE, na ɔkɔtena dɔ mmerɛ biala.”

english_verse: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
translation_verse: Na ohu Ɛlkana buale ye kyɛ, “Bɔ asusu ye nwo ne, yɔ sɔ ala. Nwondɛ maa oodwu mmerɛ bɔ ɛkɔpɛ ye nyɔfone koraka; na mesrɛ kyɛ AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɔ́bra nu.” Yiti Hana tenane awuro mane ɔwa ne nyɔfone kɔpem kyɛ ɔpɛle ye nyɔfone ɔ.

english_verse: “Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord
translation_verse: Na Hana sele kyɛ, “Me mene, w’adaworoma, me ole braa bɔ ogyinane wɔ nwo wa bɔle mbaeɛ hyirele AWURADE ne.

english_verse: to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for.
translation_verse: Akwadaa he yeɛ mmɔle mbaeɛ nzrɛle ne, na AWURADE ayɔ m’abisadeɛ bɔ mva ndole ye nyunu ne wama me.

english_verse: Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.” Hannah Prays Elkanah worshiped the Lord there at Shiloh, and
translation_verse: Yiti me koso, mafa ye mahyɛ AWURADE. Na mmerɛ amukoraa bɔ ɔte ase ne, mafa ye mama AWURADE.” Na bɛsɔnene AWURADE wɔ berɛ.

english_verse: Hannah prayed: You make me strong and happy, Lord. You rescued me. Now I can be glad and laugh at my enemies.
translation_verse: Afei Hana bɔle mbaeɛ kyɛ, “Me wora akyekye wɔ AWURADE nu; AWURADE nu yeɛ m’anwoserɛ wɔ ɔ. Mesere me pɔfoɛ mɔ, me nye gye, ofikyɛ ali ngonim ama me.

english_verse: No other god is like you. And with you we are safer than on a high mountain.
translation_verse: Ebiala nne berɛ bɔ ɔte krongron kyɛ AWURADE ɔ, amba, ebiala nne berɛ bɔ ɔte kyɛ wɔ ɔ; Nyɔbotaen biala nne berɛ bɔ ɔte kyɛ yɛ Nyameɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I can tell those proud people, “Stop your boasting! Nothing is hidden from the Lord, and he judges what we do.”
translation_verse: Nnɛma ɛmɔka nduhoɛ dwirɛ mbiri mbiri ko, nnɛmɔma anwomasoɛ dwirɛ fi ɛmɔ noa nu ba; ofikyɛ AWURADE te Nyameɛ bɔ onwu nikyee biala ɔ, na ye yeɛ obua ebiala yɔleɛ nwo ndɛen ɔ.

english_verse: Our Lord, you break the bows of warriors, but you give strength to everyone who stumbles.
translation_verse: Wama anwoserɛfoɛ agyaen mɔ nu abubu, nakoso bɛ bɔ bɛyɛ mmerɛ ne de, ɔmaa benya anwoserɛ.

english_verse: People who once had plenty to eat must now hire themselves out for only a piece of bread. But you give the hungry more than enough to eat. A woman did not have a child, and you gave her seven, but a woman who had many was left with none.
translation_verse: Bɛ bɔ né bɛ ko ayi ne, afei de bekoli paa koraka né banya aleɛ bali, nakoso bɛ bɔ né ɛhɔen apɛ bɛ ne, afei de aleɛ abu bɛ so. Mmotaen braa wawo nzoo, nakoso braa bɔ ye mma pee ne, afei de waha ye ngome.

english_verse: You take away life, and you give life. You send people down to the world of the dead and bring them back again.
translation_verse: AWURADE yeɛ oku, ná osa ma ngoa ɔ; ye yeɛ ɔmaa bɛkɔ ɛborɔ, ná osa maa bedwɔso befi dɔ bɛba ɔ.

english_verse: Our Lord, you are the one who makes us rich or poor. You put some in high positions and bring disgrace on others.
translation_verse: AWURADE yeɛ ɔma ebie di hiaa, ná osa ma ebie nya ye nwo ɔ; ye yeɛ ɔbrɛ sona ase, ná osa pagya sona ɔ.

english_verse: You lift the poor and homeless out of the garbage dump and give them places of honor in royal palaces. You set the world on foundations, and they belong to you.
translation_verse: Ɔma ehianiɛ so fi asefuo nu, na ɔma sona bɔ ɔyɛ anwumvo ɔ so fi fofoɛ so, maa ɔtena atitirefoɛ nu, na ɔmaa onya animnyam bia tena so. Ofikyɛ aseɛ nyinasoɛ nemɔ, AWURADE deɛ ɔ, na nyinasoɛ nemɔ so yeɛ wafa ewiase wasie ɔ.

english_verse: You protect your loyal people, but everyone who is evil will die in darkness. We cannot win a victory by our own strength.
translation_verse: Ɔbɔ ye anwoteefoɛ nwo waen wɔ atee biala so, nakoso amumuyɛɛfoɛ de, bewuwu aworabɔlɛ wue; ofikyɛ nna anwoserɛ yeɛ sona fa di ngonim ɔ.

english_verse: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
translation_verse: Okoyie AWURADE pɔfoɛ mɔ pasapasa, Anwuro Anwuro Nyameɛ kɔbɔ nu kurudududu kofi nyameɛso kogua bɛ so, AWURADE kobua aseɛ so amukoraa ndɛen, ɔkɔma ye hene ne anwoserɛ, na ɔkɔma bɔ wapopa ye ngoo ne konya tumi.”

english_verse: Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord. Eli's Sons
translation_verse: Afei Ɛlkana hɔle ye kuro Rama, nakoso akwadaa ne de, ɔhale ɔsɔfo Eli berɛ yɔle AWURADE adwuma. Eli mma mmienzua nemɔ

english_verse: Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork.
translation_verse: asɔfo asɛdeɛ bɔ bɛyɔ bɛma maen ne koso, né bɛtoto ye ase. Sɛ ebie ba bɔ afɔleɛ, ná naen ne gyi see so a, ɔyɛ a somvoɛ bɔ ɔso ɔsɔfo ne, ɔfa ateɛ anoa tworɔntworɔn bie tira ba,

english_verse: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
translation_verse: na ɔfa wura turonzemaa anaa dadesɛn anaa bua anaa kukue ne anu. Na naen biala bɔ ateɛ anoa tworɔntworɔn ne kɔye kɔwa ne, ɔsɔfo ne fa. Sɔ yeɛ né bɛfa bɛyɔ Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa bɔ bɛba Silo ɔ.

english_verse: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
translation_verse: Asa koso, anzana bɛkɔyera naen loe nen, ɔyɛ a somvoɛ bɔ ɔso ɔsɔfo ne bakã kyire sona bɔ ɔ́bɔ afɔleɛ ne kyɛ, “Ɔsɔfo ngole wɔ naen bɔ ato ne, naen monɛ yeɛ okole ɔ; yiti ma me naen monɛ ne bie ma ngɔma ye ma ɔtoto.”

english_verse: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ sona ne bua ye kyɛ, “Maa bɛyera ɛloe ne koraka né afa bɔ ekuro ɔ” a, ye koso obua kyɛ, “Daabi, fa ma me kekesaala ye. Anyɔ sɔ a, ngɔfa ye anyeborolɛ so!”

english_verse: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
translation_verse: Yiti mmerandeɛ nemɔ bɔne yɛle piri wɔ AWURADE nyunu, ofikyɛ bamva anidie bamma AWURADE afɔleɛ nemɔ. Samuel wɔ Silo

english_verse: The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment
translation_verse: Né Samuel de, ɔte akwadaa bɔ ɔso AWURADE ɔ. Né owura ɔsɔfo somvoɛ ataadeɛ bɔ ɔte nwera ɔ.

english_verse: and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Né ɔyɛ a, ye maame nwo ngwalaa ataadeɛ bie ma ye afoɛ biala. Sɛ ɔne ohu bɛkwaabɔ afoɛnoa afoɛnoa afɔleɛ ne wɔ Silo a, yeɛ né ɔfa kɔma ye ɔ.

english_verse: Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
translation_verse: Na ɔyɛ a Eli yira Ɛlkana ne ɔye kyɛ, “Mesrɛ kyɛ AWURADE ɔfa braa he aso ma enya mmaa bɔ bekosi bɔ wafa wahyɛ AWURADE ne gya nu ɔ.” Na ɛhe asi ne, besa bɛkɔ bɛ kuro.

english_verse: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
translation_verse: AWURADE lole Hana, ɔnwonzɛle, na osa wole mmienzua nza ne mmrasua nyɔ. Na akwadaa Samuel nyini wɔ AWURADE solɛ adwuma ne anu. Eli bɔ ye mma nemɔ kɔkɔ

english_verse: “Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Daabi, me mma, ɛ́mɔyakyi! Edwirɛ bɔ AWURADE mmenia bɛkeka maa mete ne, ɔtte mayee.

english_verse: If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!” But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father. A Prophet Speaks to Eli
translation_verse: Sɛ ebie yɔ bɔne tia obiɛngo a, ebie kɔpa kyerɛ kɔma ye wɔ Nyameɛ nyunu, nakoso sɛ ebie yɔ bɔne tia Nyameɛ a, nwa yeɛ ɔkɔpa kyerɛ kɔma ye ɔ?” Nakoso bandie bɛ se dwirɛ, ofikyɛ né AWURADE ayɛ kyɛ okohu bɛ.

english_verse: Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
translation_verse: Abɛɛmaa Samuel hɔle so nyini, na ɔsɔle AWURADE ne kuro sona nye. Eli abusua nwo ngɔmhyɛlɛ

english_verse: One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord: When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ sona bie wale Eli berɛ oosele ye kyɛ, “AWURADE nwa nyoo, ‘Mmerɛ bɔ né wɔ nana mɔ bɛte ngoaa bewura Faro bo wɔ Misraim ne, aso manye me nwo ali mangyire wɔ nana mɔ?

english_verse: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa nyoo, ‘Nhyɛle bɔ kyɛ w’abusua ne wɔ nana abusua bekoli sɔfo bɛkɔso me daa.’ Nakoso kekesaala ye de, AWURADE nwa: ‘Mengɔma sɔ dwirɛ ne ngɔyɛ adwuma! Ofikyɛ bɛ bɔ bedi me ni ne, me koso ngoli bɛ ni, yeɛ bɛ bɔ betiatia me nyunu ne, me koso mengɔfa bɛ ngɔyɛ huu.

english_verse: The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
translation_verse: Tie, mmerɛ bie ɔ́ba bɔ ngole wɔ sa nu tumi, ɔne wɔ nana abusua sa nu tumi, na ɔnate so w’awuro ama nu kobu gyeingyein bɔ ebiala ngonyi ngɔyɛ aworowaa ɔ.

english_verse: Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young.
translation_verse: Ekonwu kyɛbɔ Nyameɛ kɔmaa okoyie Yisrael yé ne amukoraa, na ɔkɔyɛ wɔ anyeboro; na w’awuro ama nu kobu gyeingyein bɔ ebiala ngonyi ngɔyɛ aworowaa ɔ.

english_verse: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
translation_verse: Nakoso wɔ bosoniɛ ko nya ye ti didi nu po, na memaa ɔyɔ m’afɔleɛ bokyea nwo adwuma po a, okosũ alaa kɔma ye wora kɔbɔ. Na w’awuro ama mukoraa kɔtotɔ ngrandɛ noa.

english_verse: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
translation_verse: Na bɔ ɔkɔto wɔ mma nyɔ Hofini ne Finehase ne de, ɔkɔyɛ sɛngyerɛnneɛ kɔma wɔ: bɛ munyɔ bekowu ɛlɛho.

english_verse: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
translation_verse: Me de, ngɔtete ɔsɔfo nahorɛniɛ ko ngɔma me bɔbɔ me nwo, na ye yeɛ okoli m’ahone nu dwirɛ ne me nhyehyɛleɛ so ɔ. Ngɔma ye bosofoɛ koli sɔfo kɔhyɛ, na okoli sɔfo afebɔɔ kɔso sona bɔ mapopa ye ngoo ne.

english_verse: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Na wɔ bosoniɛ biala bɔ ɔkɔha ne, ɔkɔhɔ ɔsɔfo ne berɛ kɔɔkoto kɔsrɛ ye sikaa ne aleɛ, na ɔkɔha kyɛ, Mesrɛ wɔ ala, fa ɔsɔfo adwuma ne ko maa nyɔ, ná nya aleɛ kãa nni.’ ”

english_verse: and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long
translation_verse: Né Nyameɛ kanea ne onnya nnuane. Né Samuel la AWURADE asɔneyɛɛ sua ne anu, wɔ nekaa bɔ Nyameɛ alaka ne gyi ne.

english_verse: when the Lord called out Samuel's name. “Here I am!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE frɛle Samuel kyɛ, “Samuel! Samuel!” Na osurole kyɛ, “Me ɛhe.”

english_verse: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” “I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.” Samuel went back.
translation_verse: Na ole amirika hɔle Eli berɛ oosele ye kyɛ, “Ɛfrɛle me, me ɛhe.” Nakoso Eli buale kyɛ, “Mmvrɛle wɔ, sa kɔla.” Yiti osa ɔɔlale.

english_verse: Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?” Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sa frɛle Samuel kyɛ, “Samuel!” Na Samuel dwɔsole hɔle Eli berɛ oosele ye kyɛ, “Ɛfrɛle me, me ɛhe.” Nakoso Eli buale kyɛ, “Mma, mmvrɛle wɔ, sa kɔla.”

english_verse: The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice.
translation_verse: Né AWURADE onnya ɔyyele ye nwo ali ohhyirele Samuel, yeɛ né onnya ɔttele AWURADE noa dwudwolɛ.

english_verse: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
translation_verse: AWURADE sa frɛle Samuel ye pɛen nza so. Na odwɔsole hɔle Eli berɛ ɔɔhane kyɛ, “Ɛfrɛle me, me ɛhe.” Na Eli nwuni kyɛ AWURADE yeɛ ɔ́frɛ abɛɛmaa ne ɔ.

english_verse: So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ” Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
translation_verse: Yiti Eli sele Samuel kyɛ, “Kɔ ná kɔla, na sɛ ɔfrɛ wɔ a, ka kyɛ, ‘AWURADE, dwudwo, na wɔ somvoɛ ótie.’ ” Na Samuel hɔle ɔɔlale nekaa bɔ né ɔla ne.

english_verse: The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!” “I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
translation_verse: AWURADE wale oogyinane berɛ. Na kyɛbɔ olili moa yɔle ne ala, ɔfrɛle kyɛ, “Samuel! Samuel!” Yeɛ Samuel surole kyɛ, “Dwudwo, na wɔ somvoɛ ótie.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it!
translation_verse: Na AWURADE sele Samuel kyɛ, “Tie, mebaayɔ nikyee bie wɔ Yisrael, na ebiala bɔ ɔkɔte sɔ dwirɛ nen, ye kunu kɔte ye.

english_verse: I will punish Eli and his family, just as I promised.
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne, edwirɛ biala bɔ mahã kyɛ ɔkɔto Eli abusua nen, ngɔmaa okosi fite ye bo koodwu ye ayieleɛ.

english_verse: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.
translation_verse: Mahã mahyire ye kyɛ mebaatua ye abusua so kerɛ afebɔɔ, ɔnate amumuyɛɛ bɔ ɔse ne ati; ofikyɛ ye mma nemɔ yɔle nningyein bɔ ɔte akyiwadeɛ wɔ AWURADE nyunu ne, wanyɔ bɛ huu.

english_verse: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
translation_verse: Na ɔnate sɔ ati, meta Eli abusua nwo ndaen kyɛ, kaka afɔleɛ anaa aleɛ afɔleɛ biala nne berɛ bɔ ɔkɔhora kɔpata kɔma Eli abusua amumuyɛɛ ɔ le.”

english_verse: The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Samuel lale mane aleɛ hyene ngyerɛmɔ; na afei obukyebukyele AWURADE awuro berɛ anoa nemɔ. Né Samuel suro kyɛ ɔkɔha nyekyire ne kohyire Eli ɔ.

english_verse: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Nakoso Eli frɛle Samuel kyɛ, “Mma Samuel.” Na osurole kyɛ, “Me ɛhe.”

english_verse: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
translation_verse: Na Eli bisale ye kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ dwirɛ yeɛ ɔha hyirele wɔ ne? Nnɛfa fea me. Edwirɛ amukoraa bɔ ɔha hyirele wɔ ne, sɛ ɛfa nu bie fea me a, Nyameɛ tua wɔ kerɛ maa ɔbo so!”

english_verse: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
translation_verse: Yiti Samuel fale ye mukoraa nwo amaneɛ bɔle Eli, na wamva bie wamvea ye. Na Eli sele kyɛ, “Ye yeɛ ɔte AWURADE ɔ, maa ɔyɔ bɔ okuro ɔ.”

english_verse: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
translation_verse: Na Samuel de onyi ne, AWURADE gyinane ye si, na edwirɛ biala bɔ Samuel hane ne, AWURADE maa ɔwale nu.

english_verse: From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: Na Yisrael amukoraati, fite Dan bɔ ɔkwaadwu Beɛ Hyeba, benwuni kyɛ Samuel te AWURADE ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ amba.

english_verse: The Lord often appeared to Samuel at Shiloh and told him what to say.
translation_verse: AWURADE hɔle so yele ye nwo ali wɔ Silo, ofikyɛ AWURADE nate ye bɔbɔ ye dwirɛ so yele ye nwo ali hyirele Samuel wɔ Silo.

english_verse: Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel. The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
translation_verse: Samuel noa dwirɛ dwuli Yisrael amukoraati. Filistifoɛ boaboale bɛ noa kyɛ bɛkwaafa koɛ bɛtoa Yisrael. Na Yisraelfoɛ tuli bi bɛhɔle kyɛ bɛ ne Filistifoɛ bɛkwaaho. Bɛkyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ Ebenesa, yeɛ Filistifoɛ koso kyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ Afeke.

english_verse: The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest. As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas,
translation_verse: Yiti maen ne tuli mmenia maa bɛhɔle Silo, na Asafo AWURADE bɔ ɔte kɛrubim nemɔ b’afia ne, bɛɛfale ye apam alaka ne befili dɔ bɛwale. Hofini ne Finehase bɔ bɛte Eli mma nyɔ ne, né bɛwɔ Nyameɛ apam alaka ne anwo.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ sa wale b’asikyeleɛ ne anu ne, bɛ mbanyi mɔ bisale kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ AWURADE amaa ɛnɛ yali ngoguo wɔ Filistifoɛ nyunu ye? Ɛ́mɔma yɛɛfa AWURADE apam alaka ne yɛfi Silo yɛbra, ná ɔɔtena yɛ nu ole yɛ fi yɛ pɔfoɛ mɔ sa nu.”

english_verse: brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ AWURADE apam alaka ne dwuli asikyeleɛ ne anu ne, Yisrael amukoraa bɔle ese mane aseɛ wosole.

english_verse: The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?” When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp,
translation_verse: Filistifoɛ tele esebɔlɛ nen, bɛhane kyɛ, “Esebɔlɛ bɔ ɔ́kɔ so wɔ Hebrifoɛ asikyeleɛ ye anu ye, ye bo ole sɛɛ?” Na Filistifoɛ tele kyɛ AWURADE alaka ne waadwu asikyeleɛ ne anu ne,

english_verse: they were scared to death and said: The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before.
translation_verse: ɛserɛ hane bɛ, na bɛhane kyɛ, “Nyameɛ bie awa b’asikyeleɛ ne anu.” Na besa bɛbɔle awuye kyɛ, “Yawu oo, yawu oo! Edwirɛ sɔa de, yɛnnwuni bie le.

english_verse: We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
translation_verse: “Yawu oo, yawu oo! Nwa yeɛ ɔkɔpepɛ kole yɛ kofi nyameɛ tumifoɛ hemɔ bɛ sa nu ɔ? Nyameɛ hemɔ yeɛ bɛpraprale amaneɛ ahoroɔ beguale Misraimfoɛ so wɔ ɛserɛ so ne.

english_verse: Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
translation_verse: Filistifoɛ, ɛ́mɔma yɛ ahone yɛ se, ná yɛhyire kyɛ yɛte mmienzua, ná yanyɛ Hebrifoɛ nganga, kyɛbɔ bɛte yɛ nganga ye. Ɛ́mɔma yɛhyire kyɛ yɛte mmienzua ná yɛho.”

english_verse: Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured. Eli Dies
translation_verse: Filistifoɛ lele Yisrael sa nu Nyameɛ alaka ne, na Hofini ne Finehase bɔ bɛte Eli mma nyɔ ne koso bɛtotɔle. Eli wue

english_verse: That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow.
translation_verse: Benyaminniɛ bie tuli amirika fili koɛ ne noa wale Silo sɔ kyẽa ne ala. Né wasunzua ye ndaadeɛ nu, yeɛ né wafa nnɛterɛ koso wagua ye ti so.

english_verse: He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying. Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ oodwuli ne, né Eli te ye bia nu wɔ atee noa ɔnea ate, ofikyɛ né ye kunu tete ye ma Nyameɛ apam alaka ne. Biaa ne wale kuro ne anu ɔɔbɔle amaneɛ, na kurotue ne amu sɔle awuyebɔlɛ nu.

english_verse: “Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_verse: Na bɔfoɛ ne buale kyɛ, “Yisrael anwati afi Filistifoɛ nyunu, ɛlɔen ne koso bɛ nu pee atotɔ, Hofini ne Finehase bɔ bɛte wɔ mma nyɔ ne koso bawu, yeɛ Nyameɛ apam alaka ne koso bale bafi Yisrael sa nu bahɔ.”

english_verse: Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Na ɔbɔle Nyameɛ apam alaka ne dumaa pɛ, Eli fili ye bia ne anu muni fale ye si ɔɔtɔle pambim ne anwo, ye kɔme anu buli, na owuli, ofikyɛ né wayɛ aworowaa, yeɛ afei né wayɛ piri paa. Né wabu Yisrael maen ne afoɛ aburanna. Finehase aye ne wue

english_verse: The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard,
translation_verse: Eli sia, bɔ ɔte Finehase aye ne, né ɔnwonzɛ bɔ waha kãa maa ɔwo ɔ. Mmerɛ bɔ ɔtele kyɛ bale Nyameɛ apam alaka ne bahɔ, ɔne kyɛ ye sia ne ohu koso bawu ne, ye ko hale ye mbendene so, na ɔkotole berɛ wole.

english_verse: and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!” She didn't pay any attention to them.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ ɔpena ka nu ne, mmrasua bɔ belele ye aworɛ ne sele ye kyɛ, “Nnɛsuro, ofikyɛ awo bienzua.” Nakoso wandɛ bɛ so, yeɛ wandie bɛ.

english_verse: The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Filistifoɛ lele Nyameɛ apam alaka ne fili Yisrael sa nu nen, bɛfa befili Ebenesa bɛhɔle Asedɔde.

english_verse: They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
translation_verse: Afei Filistifoɛ fale Nyameɛ apam alaka ne bɛhɔle bosoen Dagɔn sua nu, na bɛfa besiele Dagɔn nwo berɛ.

english_verse: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged.
translation_verse: Na ye alehyeleɛ nu ngyerɛmɔ tutututu bɔ Asedɔdefoɛ dwɔsole ne, benwuni kyɛ Dagɔn amunu afi, bɔ ye nyunu butu ase wɔ AWURADE alaka ne nyunu ɔ. Yiti bɛmane Dagɔn so besa besiele ye boso.

english_verse: But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway.
translation_verse: Nakoso ye alehyeleɛ nu bieku, ngyerɛmɔ tutututu bɔ bedwɔsole ne, né Dagɔn amunu afi, bɔ ye nyunu butu ase wɔ AWURADE alaka ne nyunu ɔ. Né ebie abu Dagɔn ti ne ye sa nyɔ nemɔ wafi so bɔ bɛlela simbini ne aso ɔ. Né waha ye kundunzii ne angome.

english_verse: This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
translation_verse: Na ɔnate sɔ ati, ɛnɛ ne ɛnɛ ye po, Dagɔn ahɔmeɛ ne sona biala bɔ ɔkɔ Dagɔn so ne, bendia Dagɔn simbini bɔ ɔwɔ Asedɔde ne aso.

english_verse: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.
