translation_verse: AWURADE tumi tuale Asedɔdefoɛ so kerɛ piri paa: ɔfale amaneɛ piri paa tole Asedɔde ne ye mbɔtam so, ɔmane mbɔmbɔ bobɔle bɛ.

english_verse: Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
translation_verse: Na Asedɔdefoɛ nwuni kyɛbɔ nningyein si sisi nen, bɛhane kyɛ, “Ɔnzɛ kyɛ yɛma Yisrael Nyameɛ apam alaka ne ɔka yɛ wa, ofikyɛ watua yɛ ne yɛ nyameɛ Dagɔn so kerɛ piri paa.”

english_verse: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
translation_verse: Yiti bɛsomane maa bɛɛfrɛfrɛle Filisti ahemvo amukoraa maa beyiale, na bebisale bɛ kyɛ, “Yisrael Nyameɛ apam alaka ne, yɛ́yɛ ye sɛ koraa?” Na bebuale kyɛ, “Ɔsɛ kyɛ yɛye Yisrael Nyameɛ apam alaka ne yɛfi wa yɛkɔ Gate.” Yiti bɛyele Yisrael Nyameɛ apam alaka ne befili berɛ bɛhɔle Gate.

english_verse: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
translation_verse: Yiti bɛmaa bɛfale Nyameɛ apam alaka ne bɛhɔle Ekron. Nakoso bɛfale Nyameɛ apam alaka ne bedwuli Ekron nen, Ekronfoɛ teateane nu kyɛ, “Bafa Yisrael Nyameɛ apam alaka ne bawa yɛ wa kyɛ bɛbaafa bekuku yɛ ne yɛ kuro ama.”

english_verse: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
translation_verse: Yeɛ bɛsomane maa bɛɛfrɛfrɛle Filisti ahemvo amukoraa maa beyiale, na besele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔye Yisrael Nyameɛ apam alaka ne béfi wa besa bɛɛfa besie ye boso, ná wangukũ yɛ ne yɛ kuro ama.” Ofikyɛ né ewue nwo ahunundetelɛ atɔ kuro ne aso amukoraa. Né Nyameɛ ama ɛhawo piri paa awa berɛ.

english_verse: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_verse: Na bɛ bɔ banwu ne, mbɔmbɔ bobɔle bɛ, na kuro berɛ ama hɔle so bɛbɔle awuye piri paa.

english_verse: After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months,
translation_verse: AWURADE alaka ne lili bosome nzoo wɔ Filistifoɛ aseɛ so.

english_verse: the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
translation_verse: Afei Filistifoɛ tole asaa bɛfrɛfrɛle b’ahɔmeɛ ne bɛ musueyelɛfoɛ, na bebisale bɛ kyɛ, “AWURADE alaka ne, yɛ́yɛ ye sɛ? Nikye horɛ bɔ ɔsɛ kyɛ yɛfa yɛboka so ná yafa yaasie ye boso ne, ɛmɔhã behyire yɛ.”

english_verse: “Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
translation_verse: Na bebuale kyɛ, “Sɛ ɛmɔye Yisrael Nyameɛ apam alaka ne befi wa bɛkɔ a, ye de nnɛma ɛmɔfa ye mbaen bɛkɔ, na mmom ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛmɔfa foɛlilɛ afɔleɛ bɛboka so bɛkɔma ye. Na ɛhe kɔma ɛmɔ anwonyerɛ ne kɔhɔ, na ɛmɔkonwu bɔ yiti yeɛ ɔmma ye amaneɛ piri paa he omvi ɛmɔ so ye.”

english_verse: “What should we send?” the Philistines asked. The priests and fortunetellers answered: There are five Philistine rulers, and they all have the same disease that you have.
translation_verse: Na Filistifoɛ bisale kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ foɛlilɛ afɔleɛ yeɛ yɛfa yɛɛma ye ɔ?” Bebuale kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔfa sikaa kɔkorɛ bɛ́yɔ mbɔmbɔ nnu ne mmurokuruwa nnu, kyɛbɔ Filisti ahemvo mɔ somaa te ɔ, ofikyɛ amaneɛ komapɛ ne ala yeɛ wawa ɛmɔ amukoraa ne ɛmɔ ahemvo mɔ so ɔ.

english_verse: So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops.
translation_verse: Yiti mbɔmbɔ ne mmurokuruwa mɔ bɔ bɛ́sɛkye ɛmɔ maen nen, ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛmɔyɛ bɛ sɛso, ná ɛmɔfa animnyam bɛma Yisrael Nyameɛ ne. Ebiaa amaneɛ piri paa bɔ wafa wato ɛmɔ ne ɛmɔ nyameɛ mɔ ɔne ɛmɔ aseɛ so ne, ɔkɔyakyi.

english_verse: Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
translation_verse: Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔyɛ asoserɛ kyɛbɔ Misraimfoɛ ne Faro yɛle asoserɛ ne? Oguale Misraimfoɛ nyunu ase yiele nen, aso bamma Yisraelfoɛ ate ma bangɔ?

english_verse: Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn.
translation_verse: Yiti ɛ́mɔyɔ teaseɛnam monɛ kamee ko, ná ɛmɔfa nandwie mmeleɛ nyɔ bɔ bɛma bɛ mma nyɔfone, bɔ bɛffale kɔnnua bɛttole bɛ kɔme le ɔ. Ɛ́mɔfa bakaa bɛ́sosɔ nandwie nemɔ bɛ́bɔ teaseɛnam ne, nakoso bɛ mma nemɔ de, ɛ́mɔte bɛ béfi bɛ ni mɔ anwo bɛɛfa bɛ begua tuin nu.

english_verse: Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔfa AWURADE alaka ne bésie teaseɛnam ne aso. Na sikaa kɔkorɛ nningyein bɔ ɛmɔfa bɛyɛ foɛlilɛ afɔleɛ bɛma ye ne de, ɛ́mɔfa bégua alaka bie anu bésie apam alaka ne anwo berɛ. Na afei ɛ́mɔyakyi ye ate ma ye bɔbɔ ɔhɔ ye atee.

english_verse: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
translation_verse: Afei ɛ́mɔfa ɛmɔ nye beli ye si. Sɛ ɔfa atee ne aso ɔkɔ Bete Semese ɔkɔ ye bɔbɔ ye maen nu a, ye de AWURADE yeɛ wafa amaneɛ piri he wato yɛ so ɔ. Nakoso sɛ wangɔ dɔ a, ye de yɛkonwu ye kyɛ nna AWURADE yeɛ wafa amaneɛ piri he wato yɛ so ɔ, na mmom asane bie mbaen yeɛ wato yɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
translation_verse: Filistifoɛ yɔle sɔ ala: bɛfale nandwie mmeleɛ nyɔ bɔ bɛma bɛ mma nyɔfone ne, bɛfale kɔnnua bɛsosɔle bɛ bɛbɔle teaseɛnam ne, na bɛhane bɛ mma nemɔ beguale tuin nu.

english_verse: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
translation_verse: Bɛfale AWURADE alaka ne besiele teaseɛnam ne aso. Na alaka baa bɔ sikaa kɔkorɛ mmurokuruwa ɔne Filistifoɛ mbɔmbɔ mɔ sɛso wɔ nu ne koso, bɛfa bɛbokale so.

english_verse: The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
translation_verse: Nandwie nemɔ hɔle bɛ nyunu tee bɛfale atimbire komapɛ aso bɛfale bɛ nye behyirele Bete Semese. Na nandwie nemɔ bɛkɔ ne, né besu. Bammakye bamva bɛen anaa famaa; na Filisti ahemvo nemɔ lili bɛ si toonn beedwuli Bete Semese ɛwɛen so.

english_verse: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Bete Semesefoɛ bɛ́te b’atokoɔ wɔ bɔnza ne anu. Bɛmane bɛ nye so ná benwuni alaka nen, ɔyɛle bɛ fɛ kyɛ banwu ye ɔ.

english_verse: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
translation_verse: Na Filisti ahemvo nnu ne nwuni bɔ wasi nen, besa bɛwale Ekron sɔ kyẽa ne.

english_verse: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
translation_verse: Esikaa kɔkorɛ mbɔmbɔ bɔ Filistifoɛ fa yɛle foɛlilɛ afɔleɛ bɛɛmane AWURADE ne, bɛ ɛhe: Asedɔde deɛ ko, Gasa deɛ ko, Asekelɔn deɛ ko, Gate deɛ ko, yeɛ Ekron deɛ ko.

english_verse: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
translation_verse: Yeɛ sikaa kɔkorɛ mmurokuruwa nemɔ koso, bɛ somaa ne Filisti ahemvo nnu nemɔ bɛ nguro nemɔ somaa pɛ: nguro bɔ bato bɛ nwo fasue ɔne namue mɔ bɔ fasue nne bɛ nwo ɔ. Na nyɔbotaen bɔ bɛfale AWURADE alaka ne besiele so, bɔ ɔwɔ Bete Semeseniɛ Yosua boo nu ne, ɔte adanzeɛ maa waadwu ɛnɛ. Kiriate Yearimfoɛ bɛɛfale apam alaka ne

english_verse: Some of the men of Beth-Shemesh looked inside the sacred chest, and the Lord God killed
translation_verse: Nyameɛ huni Bete Semesefoɛ nemɔ bie, ofikyɛ bɛneane AWURADE alaka ne anu. Ohuni maen ne anu mmenia aburasoo, na mmenia ne lili aworabɔlɛ, ofikyɛ AWURADE huni maen ne anu mmenia pee paa.

english_verse: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
translation_verse: Afei Bete Semesefoɛ hane kyɛ, “AWURADE, Krongronniɛ Nyameɛ he, nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora kogyina ye nyunu ɔ? Nwa berɛ koraa yeɛ yɛye AWURADE alaka ne yɛfi yɛ wa yɛkɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_verse: Yiti betuli ɛbɔfoɛ mɔ maa beesele Kiriate Yearimfoɛ kyɛ, “Filistifoɛ asa afa AWURADE alaka ne bawa. Ɛmɔbra bɛɛfa bɛhɔ ɛmɔ dɔ.”

english_verse: The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it,
translation_verse: Yiti Kiriate Yearimfoɛ wale bɛɛfale alaka ne bɛhɔle, na bɛfa bɛhɔle Abinadabo awuro wɔ bokaa ne aso. Na bɛtele ɔwa bienzua Eleasa nwo kyɛ ɔ́nea AWURADE alaka ne aso.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Afei Samuel sele Yisrael awuro ama amukoraati kyɛ, “Sɛ ɛmɔ ahone nu paa yeɛ ɛmɔsa bɛba AWURADE berɛ a, nzaade ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛmɔye Amaenmaensofoɛ nyameɛ mɔ ne mmosoen Astarote befi ɛmɔ nu begyi begua. Ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛmɔtu ɛmɔ nwo besie berɛ bɔkɔɔ bɛma AWURADE, ná ɛmɔso ye ngome, na okole ɛmɔ kofi Filistifoɛ sa nu.”

english_verse: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
translation_verse: Yiti Yisraelfoɛ gyili Baal mɔ ne Astarote mɔ beguale, na bɛsole AWURADE ngome.

english_verse: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
translation_verse: Na Samuel sele kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔma Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa béyia wɔ Misepa, na ngɔfa ɛmɔ mbaeɛ ngɔto AWURADE nyunu ngɔma ɛmɔ.”

english_verse: The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord. The Philistines Attack Israel
translation_verse: Yiti beeyiale nu wɔ Misepa, na bɛsale nzue behwie beguale ase bɛbɔle afɔleɛ bɛmane AWURADE. Bɛhyele hɔen sɔ kyẽa ne, na bɛhane kyɛ, “Yayɔ bɔne yatia AWURADE.” Na Samuel tenane Misepa buli Yisrael maen ne.

english_verse: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Filistifoɛ tele kyɛ Yisraelfoɛ baayia nu wɔ Misepa nen, Filisti ahemvo mɔ hɔle kyɛ bɛkwaafa koɛ bɛtoa Yisrael. Na Yisraelfoɛ tele sɔ dwirɛ nen, Filistifoɛ nwo suronyi tɔle bɛ so.

english_verse: “Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
translation_verse: Na Yisraelfoɛ sele Samuel kyɛ, “Esuɛ bɔ esu frɛ AWURADE yɛ Nyameɛ ma yɛ ne, nnɛyakyi; na srɛ kyɛ ole yɛ fi Filistifoɛ sa nu.”

english_verse: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
translation_verse: Na Samuel gu so ɔbɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ nen, Filistifoɛ pingyele Yisraelfoɛ kyɛ bɛ ne bɛ baaho. Nakoso AWURADE bɔle nu kurudududu serɛserɛ guale Filistifoɛ so sɔ kyẽa ne mane bɛ nye so tanene, na ɔmane Yisraelfoɛ huhuni bɛ.

english_verse: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ fili Misepa fitele bɛɛfoane Filistifoɛ, na behuhuni bɛ toonn beedwuli Bete Kare si dɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
translation_verse: Yisrael nguro bɔ Filistifoɛ le fili bɛ sa nu ne, AWURADE lele Yisrael nikyee mane ye, fite Ekron bɔ ɔkwaadwu Gate. Nguro nemɔ nwo aseɛ koso, Yisrael le fili Filistifoɛ sa nu. Na asomdwee koso wale Yisrael ne Amorifoɛ b’afia.

english_verse: Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life.
translation_verse: Samuel buli Yisrael maen ne mmerɛ amukoraa bɔ ɔtenane ase ɔ.

english_verse: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
translation_verse: Afoɛ biala, né ɔkɔ aporɔ wɔ Betel, Gilgal ne Misepa; na obuli Yisrael maen ne wɔ sɔ nguro nemɔ amukoraa so.

english_verse: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_verse: Né ɔyɛ a, osa ba Rama, ofikyɛ ye kuro ɛne, na né ɔte berɛ yeɛ obu Yisrael maen ne ɔ. Na osili afɔleɛ bokyea berɛ mane AWURADE.

english_verse: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
translation_verse: Ye bamuɛbaa bienzua ne li Yowel, yeɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ne li Abiya. Né bɛte maenbulɛfoɛ wɔ Beɛ Hyeba.

english_verse: But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
translation_verse: Nakoso ye mma nemɔ de, bamva ye suban, na mmom bɛmane bɛ nye borole nikye, belele fea-ase-ma, na bebuale ndɛengyea.

english_verse: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
translation_verse: Yiti Yisrael mbanyi mukoraati yiale, na bɛhɔle Samuel berɛ wɔ Rama

english_verse: and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
translation_verse: beesele ye kyɛ, “Ayɛ aworowaa, yeɛ wɔ mma nemɔ koso bamva wɔ suban, yiti ye ɛhene ma yɛ ma oli yɛ so, kyɛbɔ maen ngaa nemɔ bɛyɔ ne ala.”

english_verse: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
translation_verse: Nakoso bɛhane kyɛ, ‘Ma yɛ hene ma ɔla yɛ noa’ ne, wanyɛ Samuel fɛ. Yiti Samuel fa tole AWURADE nyunu,

english_verse: The Lord answered: Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king.
translation_verse: na AWURADE buale Samuel kyɛ, “Edwirɛ biala bɔ maen ne fa to wɔ nyunu ne, de to nu, ofikyɛ nna wɔ yeɛ bapo wɔ ɔ, na mmom me yeɛ bapo me kyɛ nnde bɛ so hene ko ɔ.

english_verse: Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you.
translation_verse: Na bɔ bafa bali me amukoraa, fite kyẽa bɔ nyele bɛ mvili Misraim mmale bɔ ɔbaadwu ɛnɛ, bɔ bayakyi me si lilɛ baaso nyameɛ foforɛ biemɔ ɔ, sɔ ala yeɛ bɛ́fa bédi wɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
translation_verse: Wɔ de, de b’edwirɛ ne to nu; nakoso kanzo bɛ kitii, ná maa benwu atee horɛ bɔ ɛhene ne kɔfa so koli bɛ so ɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Yiti Samuel hane AWURADE noa dwirɛ ne amukoraa hyirele mmenia bɔ bebisale ɛhene befili ye berɛ ne.

english_verse: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
translation_verse: Na osele kyɛ, “Ɛhene bɔ ɔbaali ɛmɔ so ne, sɔ atee he yeɛ ɔkɔfa ɛmɔ kɔfa so ɔ: ye koɛ teaseɛnam mɔ ne ye mbɔngɔ nemɔ, ɔkɔhyɛ ɛmɔ mma mmienzua maa bɛkɔhã, na ɔkɔmaa bekotu amirika bekoli koɛ teaseɛnam nemɔ nyunu bɛkɔbɔ ye nwo waen.

english_verse: Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
translation_verse: Ɔkɔhyɛ ɛmɔ mma mmrasua maa bɛkɔyɔ ye sakyeɛfona, bɛkɔto ye aleɛ, ná bato ye paanoo.

english_verse: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ boo, bobe boo, ɔne olive boo nemɔ, okole nu aleɛ paa ne kofi ɛmɔ sa nu kɔma ye somvoɛ mɔ.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ aburoo ne ɛmɔ bobe mma ne, okole buru nu ngyɛmuɛ ko kɔma ye mbanyi ne ye somvoɛ mɔ.

english_verse: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ nganga ne ɛmɔ afaneɛ nemɔ, yeɛ ɛmɔ nandwie ne ɛmɔ afunum paa nemɔ, ɔkɔhyɛ bɛ maa bɛkɔyɔ ye adwuma.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
translation_verse: Okole ɛmɔ mmoaen buru nu ngyɛmuɛ ko, na ɛmɔkɔyɛ ye nganga.

english_verse: and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Na sɔ mmerɛ ne, ɛmɔkosu, ɔnate ɛmɔ hene bɔ ɛmɔafa ye bali ɛmɔ so ne ati; nakoso AWURADE ngɔtɛ ɛmɔ so sɔ mmerɛ ne.”

english_verse: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
translation_verse: amaa ɔnate so yɛ koso yayɛ kyɛ maen ngaa nemɔ. Yɛ hene ne kɔla yɛ noa, na okoli yɛ nyunu maa yɛkɔhɔ yɛ koɛ mɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
translation_verse: Samuel tiele edwirɛ amukoraa bɔ mmenia ne hane ne, na ɔhane ye pɛpɛɛpɛ hyirele AWURADE.

english_verse: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE buale Samuel kyɛ, “De b’edwirɛ ne to nu, ná si hene ma bɛ.” Na Samuel sele maen ne kyɛ, “Ebiala osa hɔ ye kuro.”

english_verse: Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah.
translation_verse: Né biaa Benyaminniɛ bie wɔ berɛ bɔ oli Kise. Ɔse ole Abiɛl, bɔ ɔse ole Sero, bɔ ɔse ole Bekorate, bɔ ɔse ole Afia bɔ ɔte Benyamin bosoniɛ ɔ. Né Kise sa nu le bie.

english_verse: Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
translation_verse: Né ole baa bienzua aberandeɛ anwonyemene bie bɔ oli Sɔɔlo. Né sona biala nne Yisrael bɔ ye anwonyemene tra ye ɔ. Maen ne anu, ɔne sona biala gyi berɛ a, ɔwale tra ye.

english_verse: Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, Sɔɔlo baba Kise afunum mɔ minini. Yiti Kise sele ɔwa Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Fa somvoɛ nemɔ nu ko boka wɔ nwo so, ná kɔpena afunum nemɔ.”

english_verse: Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys.
translation_verse: Oohyinihyinini Efraim mmokaa aseɛ so ne Salisa aseɛ so, nakoso bannwu bɛ. Behyinihyinini Saalim aseɛ so, nakoso né afunum nemɔ bɛnne berɛ. Afei oohyinihyinini Benyamin aseɛ so, nakoso bannwu bɛ.

english_verse: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
translation_verse: Na beedwuli Sufe aseɛ so ne, Sɔɔlo sele somvoɛ bɔ ɔne ye nate ne kyɛ, “Maa yɛsa yɛhɔ. Anyɔ a, me baba kɔyakyi afunum nemɔ nwo adwenedwene, na ɔkɔma yɛ nwo adwenedwene kɔtɔ ye so.”

english_verse: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
translation_verse: Nakoso somvoɛ ne buale ye kyɛ, “Tie, Nyameɛ sona bie wɔ kuro he aso, na ɔte sona bɔ bebu ye ɔ. Bɔ ɔkɔha biala, ɔba nu. Maa yɛhɔ berɛ, na ebiaa ɔkɔha atee bɔ yawa ye nwo dwirɛ kohyire yɛ.”

english_verse: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo bisale somvoɛ ne kyɛ, “Sɛ yɛkɔ berɛ a, nzikyɛ yeɛ yɛkwaafa yɛma biaa ne ɔ? Aleɛ bɔ ɔwɔ yɛ bɔtɔ nu ne, wayie; na akyɛdeɛ biala nne berɛ bɔ yɛkonya ye yɛkɔma Nyameɛ sona ne ɔ. Nzikyɛ yeɛ yɛle ye wɔ berɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Na somvoɛ ne buale Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Nea, nne ɛdwetɛ sekel ngyɛmuɛ nna nu ko wɔ wa, ngɔfa ngɔma Nyameɛ sona ne, na okohyire yɛ nekaa bɔ odi kyɛ yɛkɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: “Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets. Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo sele ye somvoɛ ne kyɛ, “Bɔ aha ne ɔte paa, maa yɛhɔ.” Na besili nu bɛhɔle kuro bɔ Nyameɛ sona ne ɔwɔ so ne aso.

english_verse: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
translation_verse: Na bɛ́fo bokaa ne bɛ́kɔ kuro ne aso ne, beyiale mmaayaa biemɔ bɔ befi kuro ne anu befite bɛkɔ asue ɔ. Na bebisale mmaayaa nemɔ kyɛ, “Nyameɛ sona bɔ ɔse ase ne, aso ɔwɔ berɛ?”

english_verse: “Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry
translation_verse: Bebuale kyɛ, “Yoo, ɔwɔ berɛ, oli wɔ nyunu moa. Ma wɔ nwo yɛ nyera, na bekye ala yeɛ waadwu kuro wa ɔ, ofikyɛ maen ne baabɔ afɔleɛ ɛnɛ wɔ asɔneyɛɛ so berɛ.

english_verse: and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛmɔdwu kuro ne aso ala a, ɛmɔkonwu ye koraka né wafo wahɔ asɔneyɛɛ so berɛ waadidi. Sɛ ɔwwale a, mmenia nnidi, ofikyɛ ye yeɛ odi kyɛ oyira afɔleɛ ne aso koraka ɔ. Na ɛhe asi ne, mmenia bɔ bato bɛ sa bafrɛ bɛ ne, bedidi. Yiti ɛ́mɔfo bɛhɔ, na ɔngɔhyɛ biala ɛmɔkonwu ye.”

english_verse: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Bɛtoale so kyɛ bɛ́kɔ kuro berɛ. Na bɛyɛle kyɛ béwura kuro berɛ pambim ne anu ne, benwuni kyɛ Samuel fi kuro ne anu ɔ́ba. Né ye nye kyire bɛ dɔ, na né ɔse kɔ asɔneyɛɛ ne aso.

english_verse: The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel,
translation_verse: Ɔhale ɛlɛho ma Sɔɔlo ba ne, né AWURADE ali moa waye wahyire Samuel kyɛ,

english_verse: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
translation_verse: “Ɛhema, bekye sɔa ala, ngɔma biaa bie bɔ ofi Benyamin aseɛ so kɔwa wɔ berɛ, na fa ɛpopalɛ ngoo popa ye ma oli me maen Yisrael so hene. Ɔkɔpepɛ kole me maen kofi Filistifoɛ sa nu, ofikyɛ manwu amaneɛ bɔ me mmenia benwu ye ne, na bɛ suɛ adwu me nyunu.”

english_verse: Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
translation_verse: Na Samuel nye bɔle Sɔɔlo so nen, AWURADE sele ye kyɛ, “Biaa bɔ ngane ye nwo dwirɛ ngyirele wɔ ne, ye ɛne. Ye yeɛ okoli me maen ne nyunu ɔ.”

english_verse: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
translation_verse: Afei Sɔɔlo pingyele Samuel nwo berɛ wɔ pambim ne anu, na obisale ye kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ ala, Nyameɛ sona bɔ ɔse ase ne, ye awuro wɔ nisua?”

english_verse: “I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions.
translation_verse: Na Samuel buale Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Me ole Nyameɛ sona bɔ ɔse ase ne. Di me nyunu moa fo kɔ asɔneyɛɛ so dɔ, ofikyɛ ɛnɛ ɛmɔ ne me kodidi. Na edwirɛ bɔ ɔha wɔ ne, ngɔma wɔ ye nwo mmuayɛɛ ɛhema ngyerɛmɔ, ná afei mayakyi wɔ ate maa ahɔ.

english_verse: Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
translation_verse: W’afunum mɔ bɔ bamini ɛlɛsa ɛhe ne, nnɛdwene bɛ nwo ko, ofikyɛ banwu bɛ. Na nwa yeɛ Yisrael anwonyadeɛ amukoraa te ye deɛ ɔ? Ɛne wɔ baba abusua nu ama mukoraa, aso nna ɛmɔ deɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: “Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.” Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo buale kyɛ, “Nde Benyaminniɛ. Yisrael mmusua kure nemɔ, Benyamin yeɛ ɔte kãa paa wɔ nu ɔ. Na Benyamin abusua kure ne, m’abusua yeɛ ɔte awiɛmvoɛ paa wɔ mmusua ne amukoraa nu ɔ. Na nzu ati yeɛ aha sɔ dwirɛ he ahyire me ɔ?”

english_verse: Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.” The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.” After Saul and Samuel had finished eating,
translation_verse: Na sona bɔ ɔto aleɛ ne pagyale naen ne sɔ ne, ɔne bɔ ɔboka so ne, na ɔfa siele Sɔɔlo nyunu. Na Samuel hane kyɛ, “Nea, naen bɔ yɛfa yɛsiele ne, yeɛ bafa basie wɔ nyunu ne. Di, ofikyɛ mva nziele berɛ mane wɔ, kyɛ odwu sɔ mmerɛ ye a, ɛne mmenia bɔ mato asaa mafrɛ bɛ ne kodidi.” Yiti Sɔɔlo ne Samuel tole asaa didili sɔ kyẽa ne.

english_verse: they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house,
translation_verse: Na befili asɔneyɛɛ so dɔ bedwu bɛwale kuro ne anu ne, bɛtole Sɔɔlo mba wɔ sua ne aso nzamsoɛ ne aso maa ɔlale.

english_verse: and Saul slept there. About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.” Saul got up. He and Samuel left together
translation_verse: Alebahyene ne, né Sɔɔlo wɔ nzamsoɛ ne aso. Na Samuel frɛle ye sele ye kyɛ, “Dwɔso ma nzoma wɔ ate ma ɛhɔ.” Sɔɔlo dwɔsole, na ɔne Samuel befitele dwaaso dɔ.

english_verse: and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.” Samuel Tells Saul He Will Be King After the servant had gone,
translation_verse: Na bɛ́torotoro bɛ́kɔ kuro ne tiwaa nen, Samuel sele Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Ka kyire somvoɛ ne ma ɔɔse li yɛ nyunu moa. Na ɔse badi moa a, wɔ de gyina berɛ kãa ma nga Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ngyire wɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel took a small jar of olive oil and poured it on Saul's head. Then he kissed Saul and told him: The Lord has chosen you to be the leader and ruler of his people.
translation_verse: Afei Samuel fale ngoo towaa, otutu guale Sɔɔlo ti so, na ɔtɔle ye nu hane kyɛ, “AWURADE apopa wɔ ngoo wafa wɔ wali ye maen Yisrael so hene. Wɔ yeɛ ɛkɔla AWURADE maen ne noa ɔ, na bɛ pɔfoɛ mɔ bɔ bapɛ bɛ nwo bayia ne, wɔ yeɛ ɛkɔpepɛ kole bɛ kofi bɛ sa nu ɔ. Na bɔ okohyire kyɛ AWURADE afa wɔ wali ye agyapadeɛ so hene ɛhe:

english_verse: When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
translation_verse: Ɛnɛ sɛ efi me nwo wa ná ɛkɔ a, ekoyia mmienzua nyɔ wɔ Rahɛl asieleɛ ne anwo, wɔ Selsa, wɔ Benyamin aseɛ so. Na bekose wɔ kyɛ, ‘Afunum mɔ bɔ ɛhɔle bɛ penalɛ ne, banwu bɛ. Afei de, wɔ baba ndwene afunum nemɔ nwo ko, na mmom ɛmɔ nwo adwenedwene yeɛ watɔ ye so ɔ. Na ɔnwa: Yieee, mma ye, mekwaanwu ye ni?’

english_verse: Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine.
translation_verse: Efi berɛ toa so kɔ wɔ nyunu, ná ekodwu Tabɔ eluii ne anwo a, ekoyia mmienzua nza wɔ berɛ bɔ bɛkwaasɔne Nyameɛ wɔ Betel ɔ. Ko tira mbɔngye mmaa nza, ko tira paanoo mumua nza, yeɛ ko wora otira bobe nzaa ngomvo ko.

english_verse: After they greet you, they'll give you two loaves of bread.
translation_verse: Bekobisa wɔ ahye, na bɛkɔma wɔ paanoo mumua nyɔ bɔ odi kyɛ ede ɔ.

english_verse: Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
translation_verse: Na ɛhe asi ne, ekoodwu Gibeate Elohim, wɔ nekaa bɔ Filistifoɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ atenaleɛ wɔ ne. Na sɛ ɛkwaawura kuro ne anu a, ekoyia ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ kure bɔ befi asɔneyɛɛ so dɔ bɛ́torotoro bɛ́ba, bɔ adengum, akasaa, aweɛn ne sangoo angorɛ li bɛ nyunu ɔ. Na ekonwu kyɛ bɛ́hyɛ ngɔm ɔ.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them.
translation_verse: Afei AWURADE Sunzum kɔte kɔpe wɔ so, ɛne bɛ kɔbɔ nu kɔhyɛ ngɔm, na ɔkɔmaa ɛkɔsesã kɔyɛ sona foforɛ.

english_verse: After these things happen, do whatever you think is right! God will help you.
translation_verse: Na sɛ sɔ nningyein hemɔ ba nu ma wɔ a, yɔ nikyee biala bɔ ekuro ɔ, ofikyɛ Nyameɛ gyi wɔ si.

english_verse: Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next. Saul Goes Back Home
translation_verse: Na ɛhe asi ne, di me nyunu moa kɔ Gilgal, na ngooyia wɔ berɛ ngɔbɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne asomdwee afɔleɛ. Tena berɛ nwondɛ ɛlɛsoo, kɔpem kyɛ ngɔɔto wɔ berɛ ná ngohyire wɔ bɔ odi kyɛ ɛyɔ ɔ.” Sɔɔlo hyɛ ngɔm

english_verse: As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo kakyili ye nwo kyɛ ofi Samuel nwo berɛ kɔ ne, Nyameɛ sesane Sɔɔlo maa ɔyɛle sona foforɛ; na sɔ nzɛngyerɛnneɛ ne amukoraa wale nu sɔ kyẽa ne ala.

english_verse: When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
translation_verse: Na befili berɛ beedwuli Gibea nen, ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ kure wale beeyiale ye, na Nyameɛ sunzum wale ye so, na ɔhyɛle ye bo ɔne bɛ bɔle nu hyɛle ngɔm.

english_verse: Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Na mmenia bɔ bɛse ye daa amukoraa nwuni ye kyɛ ɔne ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ nemɔ bɛ́hyɛ ngɔm nen, bebisabisale bɛ nwo kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ nikye yeɛ wate wape Kise awa ye aso ye? Sɔɔlo koso boka ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ nemɔ so hɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Na biaa bie bɔ ofi kuro berɛ ala buale kyɛ, “Na nwa yeɛ ɔla bɛ noa ɔ?” Yiti ɔɔyɛle mbanyi mɔ dwirɛ bie bɔ ɔla berɛ kyɛ, “Sɔɔlo koso boka ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ nemɔ so hɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Na ngɔmhyɛlɛ ne fili ye nye so nen, ɔhɔle asɔneyɛɛ so berɛ.

english_verse: Later, Saul's uncle asked him, “Where have you been?” Saul answered, “Looking for the donkeys. We couldn't find them, so we went to talk with Samuel.”
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo baba aliɛma bienzua bisale ye ne somvoɛ ne kyɛ, “Nisua yeɛ ɛmɔhɔle ɔ?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Yɛhɔle afunum nemɔ penalɛ. Na yɛpenane bɛ dee bɔ yannwu bɛ ne, yɛhɔle Samuel berɛ.”

english_verse: “And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sɔɔlo baba aliɛma bienzua ne sele kyɛ, “Edwirɛ bɔ Samuel ha hyirele ɛmɔ ne, ka kyire me.”

english_verse: Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king. The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo buale ye baba aliɛma bienzua ne kyɛ, “Osele yɛ pefee kyɛ banwu afunum nemɔ.” Nakoso ahennie ne nwo dwirɛ bɔ Samuel ha hyirele Sɔɔlo ne de, wammɔ so wangyire ye. Bɛfale Sɔɔlo besili hene

english_verse: Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord.
translation_verse: Samuel tole asaa frɛle Yisrael maen ne maa bɛwale AWURADE nyunu wɔ Misepa,

english_verse: When everyone had arrived, Samuel said: The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
translation_verse: na osele bɛ kyɛ, “AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa nyoo, ‘Me yeɛ nyele Yisrael mvili Misraim ɔ. Mbepɛ nnele ɛmɔ mvili Misraimfoɛ sa nu, ɔne ahennie amukoraa bɔ né bɛhyɛ ɛmɔ so ne sa nu.’

english_verse: God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
translation_verse: Nakoso ɛnɛ de, ɛmɔapo ɛmɔ Nyameɛ bɔ ode ɛmɔ fi ɛmɔ amaneɛ mukoraa ne ɛmɔ anwokyere mukoraa nu ne, na ɛmɔaha bahyire ye kyɛ, ‘Daabi, si hene ma yɛ.’ Ye sɔ ne ati, ɛmɔbra beegyina AWURADE nyunu abusua kure abusua kure ne mmusua mmusua.”

english_verse: Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Afei Samuel mane Yisrael mmusua kure amukoraa beegyinane anyunu berɛ, na beguale serewa maa ɔyele Benyamin abusua kure ne.

english_verse: Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
translation_verse: Benyamin abusua kure ne, ɔmane nu mmusua mmusua ne beegyinane anyunu berɛ. Na beguale serewa maa ɔyele Matri abusua ne. Ɔmane Matri abusua nu ama beegyinane anyunu berɛ, na serewagualɛ ne yele Kise awa Sɔɔlo. Nakoso bɛpenane Sɔɔlo ne, bannwu ye.

english_verse: The people prayed, “Our Lord, is Saul here?” “Yes,” the Lord answered, “he is hiding behind the baggage.”
translation_verse: Yiti besa bebisale AWURADE kyɛ, “Sɔ sona ne, aso wamma wa bie anaa?” Na AWURADE buale kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔnea, waafea nningyein bɔ baboaboa ye noa ne anu.”

english_verse: The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else.
translation_verse: Na bele amirika bɛɛfale ye bɛwale. Oogyinane mmenia ne anu nen, né ɔne sona biala gyi berɛ a, ɔwale tra ye.

english_verse: “Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!” The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Na Samuel sele mmenia ne amukoraa kyɛ, “Ɛhe yeɛ AWURADE aneanea nu waye ye ɔ. Ebiala nne maen ye anu bɔ ɔte kyɛ ye ɔ.” Na mmenia ne amukoraa bɔ lele so kyɛ, “Nana, wɔ ngoa so oo!”

english_verse: Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
translation_verse: Samuel hane ahennie ne nwo nhyehyɛleɛ ne mmeraa hyirele maen ne. Ɔhyerɛle ye wɔ nwomaa nu, na ɔfale nwomaa ne tole AWURADE nyunu. Afei Samuel mane mmenia ne amukoraa betuli apo besa bɛhɔle b’awuro.

english_verse: God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo koso hɔle ye awuro wɔ Gibea, na koɛhonɛfoɛ biemɔ bɔ Nyameɛ kanyane bɛ ɔ yeɛ bɛfale ye bɛhɔle ɔ.

english_verse: But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_verse: Nakoso hohwifoɛ biemɔ sele kyɛ, “Ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ né akoaa he ahora ale yɛ?” Yiti bebuli ye animtia, na bamva akyɛdeɛ biala bammrɛ ye. Nakoso Sɔɔlo andɛ bɛ so.

english_verse: Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Amonniɛ Nahase buale bɛ kyɛ, “Sɛ ngɔpene so kyɛ me ne ɛmɔ kɔyɛ apam a, sana metu ebiala nye famaa ne, maa ɔyɛ animguaseɛ ka Yisrael amukoraati.”

english_verse: The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
translation_verse: Na Yabese mbanyi sele ye kyɛ, “Ma yɛ ɛlɛsoo maa yɛtu ɛbɔfoɛ ma behyini Yisrael amukoraati, na sɛ yannya defoɛ biala a, yɛkɔɔfa yɛ nwo yɛkowura wɔ sa.”

english_verse: Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying.
translation_verse: Ɛbɔfoɛ nemɔ dwuli Sɔɔlo kuro Gibea, na bɛfale edwirɛ ne nwo amaneɛ bɛbɔle berɛ ama nen, mmenia ne amukoraa bɛsɔle awuyebɔlɛ nu.

english_verse: Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen. “Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked. They told him what the men from Jabesh had said.
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Sɔɔlo ɔ́ka nandwie mɔ ofi eburo ba kuro, na obisale kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ dwirɛ yeɛ wato mmenia ye mɔ bɔ besu ye?” Na bɛfale Yabesefoɛ amaneɛ ne bɛbɔle ye.

english_verse: Then the Spirit of God suddenly took control of Saul and made him furious.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Sɔɔlo tele sɔ dwirɛ nen, Nyameɛ sunzum kanyane ye, na ɔfɛle yaa hahii.

english_verse: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
translation_verse: Ɔhyele nandwie nyii nyɔ bɔ bafa kɔnnua basosɔ bɛ babɔ nu ɔ, ɔpepɛle bɛ nu ahuronzi ahuronzi, na ɔfa somane ɛbɔfoɛ maa bɛhɔle Yisrael aseɛ so amukoraa beesele kyɛ, “Sona biala bɔ wanni Sɔɔlo ne Samuel si wangɔ koɛ ne, sɔ ala yeɛ bɛkɔpepɛ ye nandwie mɔ nu ɔ.” Afei AWURADE nwo suronyi tɔle maen ne aso, na mmenia ne amukoraa bɛbɔle nu befite bɛwale.

english_verse: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
translation_verse: Na besele ɛbɔfoɛ mɔ bɔ bɛwale ne kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhɔ beese Yabese Gileadefoɛ kyɛ, ‘Ɛhema, kyɛ odwu eyiagyina ne, né ɛmɔanya defoɛ.’ ” Na ɛbɔfoɛ nemɔ fale amaneɛ bɛɛbɔle Yabesefoɛ nen, ɔyɛle bɛ fɛ.

english_verse: So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
translation_verse: Na Yabesefoɛ sele Amonfoɛ kyɛ, “Ɛhema yɛkɔɔfa yɛ nwo yɛkowura ɛmɔ sa, na ɛmɔkɔhora kɔfa bɔ ɛmɔkuro biala bɛkɔyɛ yɛ.”

english_verse: The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, Sɔɔlo hyɛle ye lɔen ne anu kure nza. Na alebahyene, bɛhɔle Amonfoɛ asikyeleɛ ne anu, na behuhuni Amonfoɛ toonn maa oodwuli eyia ketee. Bɛ bɔ benyane bɛ ti bedidili nu ne, bɛbɔle aya, bɔ mmenia nyɔ po banga neka horɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
translation_verse: Afei Yisraelfoɛ bisale Samuel kyɛ, “Nwa mɔ yeɛ bɛhane kyɛ, ‘Aso Sɔɔlo yeɛ ɔbaali yɛ so hene anaa’ ne? Ɛ́mɔfa bɛ bɛbra ma yɛhu bɛ!”

english_verse: “No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.” Saul Is Accepted as King
translation_verse: Nakoso Sɔɔlo buale kyɛ, “Yɛngohu sona biala ɛnɛ kyẽa ye, ofikyɛ ɛnɛ te kyẽa bɔ AWURADE apepɛ ale Yisrael ɔ.”

english_verse: “Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
translation_verse: Na Samuel sele mmenia ne kyɛ, “Ɛmɔbra ma yɛhɔ Gilgal yɛɛbɔ ɛhene ne ohomoo bieku wɔ berɛ.”

english_verse: Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_verse: Yiti mmenia ne amukoraati hɔle Gilgal, na bɛbɔle Sɔɔlo ohomoo besili ye hene wɔ AWURADE nyunu wɔ Gilgal. Bɛbɔle asomdwee afɔleɛ berɛ wɔ AWURADE nyunu, na Sɔɔlo ne Yisraelfoɛ amukoraati nye gyele paa wɔ berɛ.

english_verse: Samuel told the Israelites: I have given you a king, just as you asked.
translation_verse: Afei Samuel sele Yisrael amukoraa kyɛ, “Matie edwirɛ bɔ ɛmɔaha bahyire me ne amukoraa, na masi ɛmɔ hene mama ɛmɔ.

english_verse: You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔtie, afei de, ɛhene ne yeɛ ɔla ɛmɔ noa ɔ. Me de, mayɛ aworowaa bɔ mafu gyein ɔ, nakoso me mma mmienzua nemɔ de, bɛboka ɛmɔ so. Mali ɛmɔ nyunu toonn fite me ngwadaa nu maa waadwu ɛnɛ kyẽa ye.

english_verse: Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
translation_verse: Ngyi ɛmɔ nyunu wa. Ɛ́mɔli me nwo adanzeɛ wɔ AWURADE nyunu, ɔne ye sona bɔ wapopa ye ngoo ne nyunu. Nwa nandwie yeɛ male ɔ? Nwa afunum yeɛ male ɔ? Anaakyɛ nwa yeɛ mali ye ndurum ɔ? Nwa yeɛ mahyɛ ye so ɔ? Nwa yeɛ male fea-ase-ma mafi ye berɛ, bɔ ɔnate so mabu me nye magua ndɛen turoloo so ɔ? Ɛ́mɔhã, na ngɔfa bie ngosi ye gya nu ngɔma ɛmɔ.”

english_verse: “No,” the Israelites answered. “You've never cheated us in any way!”
translation_verse: Na bebuale kyɛ, “Ellili yɛ ndurum, ɛhhyɛle yɛ so, yeɛ ellele ebiala nikye fee.”

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord and his chosen king are witnesses to what you have said.” “That's true,” they replied.
translation_verse: Yeɛ osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛnɛ kyẽa ye, AWURADE te ɛmɔ danzeniɛ, yeɛ ye sona bɔ wapopa ye ngoo ne koso ɔte ɛmɔ danzeniɛ, kyɛ ɛmɔ nikye fee oollili me berɛ.” Na bebuale kyɛ, “Ɔte danzeniɛ.”

english_verse: Then Samuel told them: The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Na Samuel sele mmenia ne kyɛ, “AWURADE bɔ ɔneaneane nu yele Mose ne Aarɔn, ná ɔfale ɛmɔ nana mɔ fili Misraim aseɛ so wale ne, ɔte danzeniɛ.

english_verse: Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
translation_verse: Yiti ɛmɔɔgyina wa, maa mmɔ ɛmɔ kwaadu wɔ AWURADE nyunu, wɔ paayɛlɛ mukoraa bɔ AWURADE ayɔ ama ɛmɔ ɔne ɛmɔ nana mɔ ne anwo.

english_verse: After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Yakob hɔle Misraim ne, [Misraimfoɛ hyɛle bɛ so] ɛmɔ nana mɔ sũ frɛle AWURADE, na AWURADE somane Mose ne Aarɔn maa bɛɛyele ɛmɔ nana mɔ befili Misraim, na ɔmaa bɛɛtenane wa.

english_verse: But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
translation_verse: Nakoso bɛmane bɛ wora fili AWURADE bɛ Nyameɛ; yiti ɔfale bɛ wurale Hasɔ safohene Sisera sa, Filistifoɛ sa, ɔne Moabo hene sa, na sɔ mmenia nemɔ ne bɛ hone koɛ.

english_verse: Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
translation_verse: Afei besu bɛfrɛle AWURADE kyɛ, “Yayɔ bɔne, ofikyɛ yayakyi AWURADE si lilɛ yaaso Baal mɔ ne Astarote mɔ. Nakoso, de yɛ fi yɛ pɔfoɛ mɔ sa nu, na yɛkɔso wɔ.’

english_verse: The Lord sent Gideon, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue you from your enemies, and you didn't have to worry about being attacked.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE somane Yerubaal, Bedan, Yɛfeta ne Samuel; na ɛmɔ pɔfoɛ mɔ bɔ bapɛ ɛmɔ nwo bayia ne, ɔpepɛ lele ɛmɔ fili bɛ sa nu maa ɛmɔtenane asomdwee nu.

english_verse: Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ yeɛ ɔte ɛmɔ hene ɔ, nakoso mmerɛ bɔ ɛmɔnwuni kyɛ Amonfoɛ hene Nahase ɔbaafa koɛ toa ɛmɔ ne, ɛmɔsele me kyɛ, ‘Daabi, ɔsɛ kyɛ yɛnya ɛhene maa odi yɛ so.’

english_verse: You asked for a king, and you chose one. Now he stands here where all of you can see him. But it was really the Lord who made him your king.
translation_verse: Afei, ɛ́mɔnea, ɛhene bɔ ɛmɔaneanea nu baye ye, bɔ ɛmɔsrɛle ne, ye ɛhe. Ɛ́mɔtie, AWURADE asi ɛmɔ hene wama ɛmɔ.

english_verse: If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn!
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛmɔkosuro AWURADE, ɛmɔkɔso ye, ɛmɔkotie ye dwirɛ, ná mmom ɛmɔandwi bamva AWURADE mmeraa dwirɛ so, ná ɛmɔ ne ɛhene bɔ odi ɛmɔ so ne bedi AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ si a, ye de okoyie ɛmɔ yé.

english_verse: If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ ɛmɔandie AWURADE dwirɛ, ná sɛ ɛmɔtwi bɛfa AWURADE mmeraa dwirɛ so de a, ye de AWURADE tumi kotua ɛmɔ so kerɛ, kyɛbɔ otuale ɛmɔ nana mɔ so kerɛ ne.

english_verse: Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power.
translation_verse: Yiti ɛmɔɔgyina wa bɛnea sɔ anwanwadeɛ he bɔ AWURADE baayɔ ma ɛmɔ nye nwu ye ɔ.

english_verse: Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
translation_verse: Aso nna atokoɔtelɛ mmerɛ ɛhe? Ngɔsrɛ AWURADE maa ɔkɔma agralaa kɔtete, ná wasa wama esue atɔ. Na ɛmɔkonwu ye, ná ɛmɔale bato nu kyɛ ɛmɔayɔ amumuyɛɛ piri wɔ AWURADE nyunu, kyɛ ɛmɔabisa maa wasi hene wama ɛmɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel.
translation_verse: Yiti Samuel srɛle AWURADE, na AWURADE mane agralaa tetele, yeɛ ɔmane esue koso tɔle sɔ kyẽa ne ala. Na maen ne amukoraati surole AWURADE ne Samuel paa.

english_verse: They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
translation_verse: Na maen ne mukoraa sele Samuel kyɛ, “Srɛ AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ ma wɔ ngoaa ná yanwuwu, ofikyɛ ɛhene bɔ yabisa yale nwo amumuyɛɛ ne, yafa yafoa yɛ bɔne amukoraa so.”

english_verse: Samuel answered: Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
translation_verse: Na Samuel sele maen ne kyɛ, “Nnɛma ɛmɔsuro. Ɛmɔayɔ amumuyɛɛ he amukoraa de, nakoso nnɛma ɛmɔyakyi AWURADE si lilɛ, na mmom odi kyɛ ɛmɔfa ɛmɔ ahone amukoraa bɛso AWURADE.

english_verse: Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble.
translation_verse: Yeɛ nningyein mbaen mbaen bɔ mvasoɛ nne so, anaa bɛngora benne ngoa ne, nnɛma ɛmɔdi makyebu bekodi bɛ si, ofikyɛ bɛte mbaen.

english_verse: But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
translation_verse: Na ɔnate AWURADE dumaa piri ne ati, ɔngɔye ye sa ngofi ye mmenia bo, ofikyɛ ɔyɛle AWURADE fɛ kyɛ ɔkɔfa ɛmɔ kɔyɛ ye mmenia ɔ.

english_verse: I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right.
translation_verse: Yeɛ me koso, ɔngɔwa ye sɔ le, kyɛ ngɔyakyi ɛmɔ nwo mbaeɛbɔlɛ maa ɔnate so ngɔyɔ bɔne ngotia AWURADE ɔ. Atee bɔ ɔte paa ná ɔtengyɛ ne yeɛ ngohyirehyire ɛmɔ ɔ.

english_verse: You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔnea nningyein mbiri mbiri bɔ wayɔ wama ɛmɔ ɔ. Esurolɛ mmom yeɛ ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛmɔsuro AWURADE, ná ɛmɔfa ɛmɔ ahone amukoraa bɛso ye nahorɛ nu ɔ.

english_verse: But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ ɛmɔtoa so bɛyɔ bɔne a, ye de, ɛmɔ ne ɛmɔ hene ne, ɛmɔ boso konua.”

english_verse: The messengers then said to the people of Israel, “Saul has destroyed the Philistine army camp at Geba. Now the Philistines really hate Israel, so every town and village must send men to join Saul's army at Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Yisrael amukoraa tele kyɛ Sɔɔlo ali Filistifoɛ bɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ atenaleɛ ne aso ngonim. Besa bɛtele kyɛ Filistifoɛ afɛ Yisrael so yaa paa, yiti Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bɛɛbokale Sɔɔlo so wɔ Gilgal.

english_verse: The Israelite army realized that they were outnumbered and were going to lose the battle. Some of the Israelite men hid in caves or in clumps of bushes, and some ran to places where they could hide among large rocks. Others hid in tombs or in deep dry pits.
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ nwuni kyɛ koɛ ne anu ayɛ se ama bɛ, . Na bɛɛfeafeale nyɔboɛ bɔ wasi sua nu, ngumaa nu, nyɔbotaen nu, asieleɛ ne abura mɔ nu.

english_verse: Still others went to Gad and Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River. Saul stayed at Gilgal. His soldiers were shaking with fear,
translation_verse: Hebrifoɛ biemɔ pɛle asue Yɔɔdan bɛhɔle Gade ne Gileade aseɛ so. Né Sɔɔlo tɛ wɔ Gilgal, na mmenia ne amukoraa bɛfale ahunundetelɛ belili ye si. Sɔɔlo di ye ti piri bɔ afɔleɛ

english_verse: and they were starting to run off and leave him. Saul waited there seven days, just as Samuel had ordered him to do, but Samuel did not come.
translation_verse: Kyɛbɔ Samuel hyɛle Sɔɔlo ne, Sɔɔlo nwondɛle ɛlɛsoo, nakoso Samuel amma Gilgal, na koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ hyɛle ye bo kyɛ bɛyakyi Sɔɔlo nu bɛkɔ.

english_verse: Finally, Saul commanded, “Bring me some animals, so we can offer sacrifices to please the Lord and ask for his help.” Saul killed one of the animals,
translation_verse: Yiti Sɔɔlo sele kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔfa naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne ɔne asomdwee afɔleɛ ne bɛbrɛ me.” Na ɔbɔle naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne.

english_verse: and just as he placed it on the altar, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to welcome him.
translation_verse: Ɔbɔle naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne yiele pɛ, berɛ ne ala, Samuel nyunu ɛhe. Na Sɔɔlo hɔle kyɛ ɔkwaayia ye yɛ ye akwaaba.

english_verse: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. Saul answered, “My soldiers were leaving in all directions, and you didn't come when you were supposed to. The Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
translation_verse: Yeɛ Samuel bisale ye kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ nikye yeɛ ayɔ ye?” Na Sɔɔlo buale kyɛ, “Nwuni kyɛ mmenia ne bɛ́yakyi me nu bɛ́kɔ. Wɔ koso mmerɛ bɔ ɛhyɛ tole berɛ ne, amma, yeɛ afei Filistifoɛ koso baboa bɛ noa wɔ Mikimase.

english_verse: and I was worried that they would attack me here at Gilgal. I hadn't offered a sacrifice to ask for the Lord's help, so I forced myself to offer a sacrifice on the altar fire.”
translation_verse: Yiti nzusuli kyɛ, ‘Afei de, Filistifoɛ kɔɔfa koɛ kɔtoa me wɔ Gilgal, yeɛ AWURADE berɛ mmokalɛ koso nnya nnzrɛle.’ Yiti ɔmaa nnili me bɔbɔ me ti piri mmɔle naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne.”

english_verse: “That was stupid!” Samuel said. “You didn't obey the Lord your God. If you had obeyed him, someone from your family would always have been king of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Samuel sele ye kyɛ, “Ali ngwaseasɛm! Anni AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ mmeraa bɔ ɔhyɛ mane wɔ ne aso. W’ahennie ne, ahaa AWURADE kɔma ye bo kotimu wɔ Yisrael daa,

english_verse: But no, you disobeyed, and so the Lord won't choose anyone else from your family to be king. In fact, he has already chosen the one he wants to be the next leader of his people.”
translation_verse: nakoso kekesaala ye de, w’ahennie ne ngogyina. AWURADE apena sona bɔ ɔla ye ahone nwo ɔ, na AWURADE afa ye ali ye maen so hene, ofikyɛ anni edwirɛ bɔ AWURADE hyɛle wɔ ne aso.”

english_verse: Then Samuel left Gilgal. Part of Saul's army had not deserted him, and he led them to Gibeah in Benjamin to join his other troops. Then he counted them and found that he still had
translation_verse: Na Samuel fili Gilgal sili nu hɔle. Afei koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ baha berɛ ne, belili Sɔɔlo si bɛɛbokale bɛ mmango nemɔ aso. Na befili Gilgal bɛhɔle Gibea bɔ ɔwɔ Benyamin. Sɔɔlo hale koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ baha ye nwo berɛ ne, na né bɛ somaa te mmienzua kɔyɛ ɛyaa nzia.

english_verse: Saul, Jonathan, and their army set up camp at Geba in Benjamin. Jonathan Attacks the Philistines The Philistine army was camped at Michmash.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo ne ɔwa Yonatan ne koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ baha bɛ nwo berɛ ne, bɛtenane Geba bɔ ɔwɔ Benyamin, yeɛ Filistifoɛ koso kyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ Mikimase.

english_verse: Each day they sent out patrols to attack and rob villages and then destroy them. One patrol would go north along the road to Ophrah in the region of Shual.
translation_verse: Mmenia bɔ bɛbɔ apaa kure nza fili Filistifoɛ asikyeleɛ ne anu dɔ wale: kure ko fale ye nye hyirele Ofra hɔle Soale aseɛ so;

english_verse: Another patrol would go west along the road to Beth-Horon. A third patrol would go east toward the desert on the road to the ridge that overlooks Zeboim Valley.
translation_verse: kure bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ne fale ye nye hyirele Bete Horon, yeɛ kure bɔ ɔtɔ so nza ne koso, ɔfale ye nye hyirele ɛwɛen bɔ ɔla Seboyim bɔnza ne anwuro dɔ ne, bɔ opingye ɛserɛ ne.

english_verse: The Philistines would not allow any Israelites to learn how to make iron tools. “If we allowed that,” they said, “those worthless Israelites would make swords and spears.”
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né buralɛ dwumvoɛ biala nne Yisrael aseɛ so nekaa biala, ofikyɛ Filistifoɛ hane kyɛ, “Yɛmbena kyɛ Hebrifoɛ bɛbɔ ngrandɛ anaa pealɛɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Whenever the Israelites wanted to get an iron point put on a cattle prod, they had to go to the Philistines. Even if they wanted to sharpen plow-blades, picks, axes, sickles, and pitchforks they still had to go to them. And the Philistines charged high prices.
translation_verse: Né sɛ besi kona ne esonyi biala a, bede ɛdwetɛ sekel nza nu ngyɛmuɛ nyɔ; yeɛ sɛ besi akumaa ne buralɛ bɔ bɛfa bɛka ngaka koso a, bede ɛdwetɛ sekel nza nu ngyɛmuɛ ko.

english_verse: So, whenever the Israelite soldiers had to go into battle, none of them had a sword or a spear except Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Yiti kyẽa bɔ koɛ ne sili ne, ɛlɔen bɔ né bɛwɔ Sɔɔlo ne Yonatan nwo berɛ ne, né bɛ nu biala nne berɛ bɔ ole ngrandɛ anaa pealɛɛ ɔ; sana Sɔɔlo ne Yonatan angome yeɛ né bele bie ɔ.

english_verse: The Philistines moved their camp to the pass at Michmash,
translation_verse: Na Filistifoɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ kure ko fale Mikimase atee ne aso bɛɛtɛle dɔ.

english_verse: Jonathan decided to get to the Philistine camp by going through the pass that led between Shiny Cliff and Michmash to the north and Thornbush Cliff and Geba to the south.
translation_verse: Nyɔbotaen ne ko wɔ atee ne sorɔ, wɔ Mikimase ndendeneɛ so, yeɛ ko wora wɔ ye ngwaen, wɔ Geba ndendeneɛ so.

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons talked as they went toward the Philistine camp. “It's just the two of us against all those godless men,” Jonathan said. “But the Lord can help a few soldiers win a battle just as easily as he can help a whole army. Maybe the Lord will help us win this battle.”
translation_verse: Na Yonatan sele ye somvoɛ bɔ otira ye akodeɛ ne kyɛ, “Sɔ bɛmbɛ-bɛ-bienzuafoɛ hemɔ, bɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ atenaleɛ ne, maa yɛpɛ bɔnza ne yɛhɔ dɔ. Ebiaa AWURADE kɔho kɔma yɛ, ofikyɛ nikye fee nzi AWURADE ate kyɛ ɔkɔfa mmenia pee anaa kãa bie so koli ngonim ɔ.”

english_verse: “Do whatever you want,” the soldier answered. “I'll be right there with you.”
translation_verse: Na somvoɛ bɔ otira ye akodeɛ ne buale kyɛ, “Bɔ adwene ye nwo biala, yɔ. Bɔ ɛkɔyɔ biala, mefoa so.”

english_verse: “This is what we will do,” Jonathan said. “We will go across and let them see us.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yonatan sele kyɛ, “Yɛkɔpɛ nu yɛkɔhɔ sɔ mmenia nemɔ dɔ maa bekonwu yɛ.

english_verse: If they agree to come down the hill and fight where we are, then we won't climb up to their camp.
translation_verse: Na sɛ bɛka bekyire yɛ kyɛ, ‘Ɛ́mɔgyina dɔ maa yɛɛto ɛmɔ berɛ’ a, ye de yɛkogyina yɛ boso berɛ, na yɛngɔfo ngɔhɔ bɛ dɔ.

english_verse: But we will go if they tell us to come up the hill and fight. That will mean the Lord is going to help us win.”
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ bɛka kyɛ, ‘Ɛ́mɔfo bɛbra yɛ wa’ a, ye de yɛkɔfo kɔhɔ, ofikyɛ okyire kyɛ AWURADE afa bɛ awura yɛ sa. Na ɛhe yeɛ ɔkɔyɛ sɛngyerɛnneɛ kɔma yɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier stood at the bottom of the hill where the Philistines could see them. The Philistines said, “Look! Those worthless Israelites have crawled out of the holes where they've been hiding.” Then they yelled down to Jonathan and the soldier, “Come up here, and we will teach you a thing or two!” Jonathan turned to the soldier and said, “Follow me! The Lord is going to let us win.”
translation_verse: Na koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛwɔ asikyeleɛ ne anu ne, bɛteane nu besele Yonatan ne ye somvoɛ bɔ otira ye akodeɛ ne kyɛ, “Ɛmɔ de, ɛ́mɔfo bɛbra wa, na yɛkohyire ɛmɔ nworɛ!” Na Yonatan sele ye somvoɛ bɔ otira ye akodeɛ ne kyɛ, “Di me si, ofikyɛ AWURADE afa bɛ awura Yisrael sa.”

english_verse: Jonathan crawled up the hillside with the soldier right behind him. When they got to the top, Jonathan killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind.
translation_verse: Afei Yonatan kongone fole bokaa ne, na ye somvoɛ bɔ otira ye akodeɛ ne koso lili ye si. Filistifoɛ totɔle wɔ Yonatan nyunu, na ye somvoɛ bɔ otira ye akodeɛ li ye si ne huhuni bɛ.

english_verse: I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
translation_verse: Koɛ nu nzesadeɛ bɔ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ nyane ye fili yɛ pɔfoɛ Filistifoɛ mɔ berɛ ne, sɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ belili bie ɛnɛ a, ahaa yahũhũ Filistifoɛ nemɔ pee yatra sɔaa.”

english_verse: Saul quickly called his army together, then led them to the Philistine camp. By this time the Philistines were so confused that they were killing each other.
translation_verse: Afei Sɔɔlo ne koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa bɔ bɛboka ye so ne, bɛboale bɛ noa, na bɛhɔle koɛ wɔ asikyeleɛ ne anu. Edwirɛ nwanwa! Né Filistifoɛ amukoraa bapɛ bɛ nwo bele ngrandɛ bɛ ne bɛ nwo bɛko, na ɛhe mane bagyabagya ne noa yɛle se paa.

english_verse: The whole Philistine army panicked—those in camp, those on guard duty, those in the fields, and those on raiding patrols. All of them were afraid and confused. Then God sent an earthquake, and the ground began to tremble. Israel Defeats the Philistines
translation_verse: Ahunundetelɛ tɔlɛ ɛlɔen ne amukoraa so wɔ asikyeleɛ ne anu, ɔne eburo. Ahunundetelɛ tɔle koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ ne bɛ bɔ bɛbɔ apaa ne aso, aseɛ wosole, na ɛserɛ piri paa hane bɛ. Yisrael di Filistifoɛ so ngonim

english_verse: Saul's lookouts at Geba saw that the Philistine army was running in every direction, like melted wax.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛwɔ Benyamin kuro Gibea, bɔ bɛtetɛ pɔfoɛ nemɔ ne, bɛtotole bɛ nye, na benwuni kyɛ Filistifoɛ ɛlɔen ne babɔ aya.

english_verse: Saul told his officers, “Call the roll and find out who left our camp.” When they had finished, they found out that Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons were missing.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo sele koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛboka ye so ne kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔha mmenia ne bɛnea sona bɔ ɔnne wa bie ɔ.” Bɛhale mmenia ne, na benwuni kyɛ Yonatan ne ye somvoɛ bɔ otira ye akodeɛ ne bɛnne berɛ bie.

english_verse: At that time, Ahijah was serving as priest for the army of Israel, and Saul told him, “Come over here! Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sɔɔlo sele Ahiya kyɛ, “Fa Nyameɛ alaka ne bra.” Ofikyɛ sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Nyameɛ alaka ne wɔ Yisraelfoɛ berɛ.

english_verse: Just as Saul finished saying this, he could see that the Philistine army camp was getting more and more confused, and he said, “Ahijah, never mind!”
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo noa wɔ so bɔ ɔne ɔsɔfo ne bedwudwo nen, bagyabagya bɔ né ɔ́kɔ so wɔ Filistifoɛ asikyeleɛ ne anu ne, ɔyɛle piri. Na Sɔɔlo sele ɔsɔfo ne kyɛ, “Alaka bɔ ɛfa bisa Nyameɛ berɛ dwirɛ ne, twe wɔ sa.”

english_verse: There were also some hired soldiers in the Philistine camp, who now switched to Israel's side and fought for Saul and Jonathan.
translation_verse: Né Hebrifoɛ biemɔ bafa bɛ nwo baabɔ Filistifoɛ dada, bɔ né bɛ ne bɛ wɔ b’asikyeleɛ ne anu berɛ ɔ. Na bɛ koso bɛpɛle bɛ nwo bɛɛfale bɛ nwo bɛbɔle Yisraelfoɛ bɔ bɛwɔ Sɔɔlo ne Yonatan bue nu ne.

english_verse: Many Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim. And when they heard that the Philistines were running away, they came out of hiding and joined in chasing the Philistines.
translation_verse: Sɔ ala yeɛ Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa bɔ né baafeafea Efraim mmokaa ne anu dɔ ne, bɛtele kyɛ Filistifoɛ bɛ́nwati nen, bɛ koso bɛfoane bɛ bɛɛfale koɛ bɛtoale bɛ ɔ.

english_verse: So the Lord helped Israel win the battle that day. Saul's Curse on Anyone Who Eats Saul had earlier told his soldiers, “I want to get even with those Philistines by sunset. If any of you eat before then, you will be under a curse!” So he made them swear not to eat. By the time the fighting moved past Beth-Aven, the Israelite troops were weak from hunger.
translation_verse: Yisraelfoɛ lili amia sɔ kyẽa ne, ofikyɛ Sɔɔlo tale ndaen guale koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ so kyɛ, “Ofi bekye bɔ ɔkwaadwu nɔsoa, kyɛ oodwu kyɛ ngɔtɔ me pɔfoɛ mɔ so wereɛ ne, ebiala bɔ okodidi ne, musue to ye.” Yiti koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ anu biala wamva aleɛ wanga ye noa.

english_verse: The army and the people who lived nearby had gone into a forest, and they came to a place where honey was dripping on the ground. But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
translation_verse: Bedwuli eburo berɛ nen, benwuni kyɛ woɛ pepe gua, nakoso ebiala amva bie wanga ye noa; ofikyɛ ndaen ne ati, né besuro.

english_verse: Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yonatan de, né onnya ɔttele kyɛ ye baba ata ndaen wagua koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ aso ɔ. Yiti ɔfale ye pɔmaa bɔ otira ye ne noa bɔle woɛ ne anu, ɔtafele, na ɔmaa onyane anwoserɛ.

english_verse: Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
translation_verse: Na koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ anu ko sele kyɛ, “Wɔ baba tale ndaen guale koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ aso kyɛ, ‘Musue to sona biala bɔ okodidi ɛnɛ ɔ.’ Ye sɔ ne ati, ɛhɔen apɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ.”

english_verse: Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert.
translation_verse: Na Yonatan sele kyɛ, “Me baba afa ɛhawo wato maen ye aso. Mvale woɛ he kãa ngane me noa ye, ɛ́mɔnea kyɛbɔ wamaa manya anwoserɛ ɔ.

english_verse: By evening the Israelite army was exhausted from killing Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon.
translation_verse: Na Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ huhuni Filistifoɛ sɔ kyẽa ne, fite Mikimase toonn beedwuli Ayalɔn nen, né ɛhɔen apɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ paa.

english_verse: They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood.
translation_verse: Yiti koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ te guale koɛ nu nzesadeɛ ne aso. Bɛhyele mmoaen, nandwie ne nandwie mmaa behuni bɛ wɔ aseɛnwo berɛ nekaa bɔ bɛhyele bɛ ne, na belili naen ne bɛfrale ye mogya.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.” “You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here.
translation_verse: Na ebie ɔɔbɔle Sɔɔlo amaneɛ kyɛ, “Tie, koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ gu so bɛ́yɔ bɔne bétia AWURADE, ofikyɛ begu so bédi naen bɛfra ye mogya.” Na Sɔɔlo sele kyɛ, “Ɛmɔali edwirɛ tɛɛ! Ɛ́mɔmunu nyɔbotaen bɛ́brɛ me wa kekesaala ye!”

english_verse: Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.” That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there.
translation_verse: Afei Sɔɔlo sele kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhɔ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ anu dɔ beese bɛ kyɛ, ‘Ɛwa yeɛ odi kyɛ ebiala fa ye nandwie anaa ye mmoaen baku ye di ɔ, na onni kyɛ ɛmɔdi naen ne bɛfra ye mogya bɛfa bɛyɔ bɔne betia AWURADE.’ ” Yiti sɔ kɔngɔen ne, koɛhonɛfoɛ ne anu biala fale ye nandwie wale oohuni ye wɔ berɛ.

english_verse: It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord. The Army Rescues Jonathan
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sɔɔlo sili afɔleɛ bokyea mane AWURADE. Ɛhe te afɔleɛ bokyea bɔ oli moa bɔ osi mane AWURADE ɔ.

english_verse: Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!” The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.” “Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Afei Sɔɔlo sele kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔma yɛtorotoro yɛpo Filistifoɛ so kɔngɔen ye, ná yɛhũhũ bɛ toonn ma oodwu ngyerɛmɔ. Yɛngɔma bɛ nu ko po ngonya ye ti ngodidi nu.” Na bebuale ye kyɛ, “Bɔ ekuro kyɛ ɛyɔ biala, yɔ.” Nakoso ɔsɔfo ne hane kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔma yɛfa edwirɛ ne yɛto Nyameɛ nyunu wɔ ɛwa yɛnea.”

english_verse: Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?” This time God did not answer.
translation_verse: Yiti Sɔɔlo bisale Nyameɛ kyɛ, “Yiti mva koɛ ngɔndoa Filistifoɛ anaa? Aso ɛkɔfa bɛ kowura Yisrael sa anaa?” Nakoso Nyameɛ andɛ ye so sɔ kyẽa ne.

english_verse: Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sɔɔlo sele kyɛ, “Safohene mɔ amukoraa, ɛmɔbra wa. Ɛ́mɔma yɛ́pena atee bɔ bɔne he nate so wale ɛnɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I swear by the living Lord that whoever sinned must die, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan.” No one said a word.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE teasefoɛ bɔ ɔko de Yisrael ne, ngyi ye nyunu meka kyɛ, sɛ mma Yonatan po yeɛ wayɔ sɔ bɔne ne a, odi kyɛ beku ye!” Nakoso koɛhonɛfoɛ ne anu biala wanga hwee wangyire Sɔɔlo.

english_verse: Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.” Everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo sele Yisrael amukoraa kyɛ, Ɛ́mɔgyina bue ko, maa me ne mma Yonatan koso yɛ́gyina bue ko.” Na koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ buale Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Bɔ ekuro kyɛ ɛyɔ biala, yɔ.”

english_verse: Then Saul prayed, “Our Lord, God of Israel, why haven't you answered me today? Please show us who sinned. Was it my son Jonathan and I, or was it your people Israel?” The answer came back that Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not the army.
translation_verse: Afei Sɔɔlo sele kyɛ, “Oo, AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ, nzu ati yeɛ ɛnɛ andɛ w’akoaa so ye? Sɛ sɔ mvomsoɛ he fi me anaa mma Yonatan a, oo AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ, ma serewa ne ɔye Yurim ne. Nakoso sɛ sɔ mvomsoɛ he fi wɔ mmenia Yisraelfoɛ a, ye de ma serewa ne ɔye Tumim ne.” Serewagualɛ ne yele Sɔɔlo ne Yonatan, na koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ nwo sale.

english_verse: Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.” The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo sele kyɛ, “Me ne mma Yonatan, ɛ́mɔgua yɛ so serewa.” Na serewa ne yele Yonatan.

english_verse: “Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!” “I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo sele Yonatan kyɛ, “Nikye horɛ bɔ ayɔ ne, ka kyire me.” Yeɛ Yonatan sele ye kyɛ, “Pɔmaa bɔ né otira me ne, mvale ye ti ne mɔle woɛ nu ndafele. Mepene so kyɛ beku me ɔ.”

english_verse: “Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo sele kyɛ, “Yonatan, Nyameɛ tua me kerɛ maa ɔbo so, sɛ mamma bangu wɔ a!”

english_verse: “No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
translation_verse: Na koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ sele Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Yonatan bɔ wali ngonim kandinga he wama Yisrael ye, yiti odi kyɛ beku ye anaa? Nyameɛ pa gua! Kyɛ AWURADE te ase ye, ye ti nwiaa ko po ngotu ngɔtɔ ase, ofikyɛ Nyameɛ yeɛ wagyina ye si maa wali ngonim ɛnɛ ɔ.” Yiti koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ pepɛ lele Yonatan maa onyane ye ti didili nu.

english_verse: Saul stopped hunting down the Philistines, and they went home. Saul Fights His Enemies
translation_verse: Afei Sɔɔlo ambo Filistifoɛ so ko, na Filistifoɛ hɔle bɛ maen nu. Sɔɔlo abusua

english_verse: Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo aberɛ so amukoraa, ɔne Filistifoɛ bɛhone koɛ bɔ nu yɛ se ɔ. Sɛ né onwu bienzua anwoserɛniɛ anaa koɛhonɛniɛ ahoneserɛniɛ biala a, ɔfa ye boka ye koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ aso.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told Saul: The Lord told me to choose you to be king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the Lord:
translation_verse: Samuel sele Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Me yeɛ AWURADE somane me maa mvale ɛpopalɛ ngoo mmanguale wɔ ti so nzili wɔ ye maen so hene ɔ. Afei, tie AWURADE noa dwirɛ.

english_verse: “When the Israelites were on their way out of Egypt, the nation of Amalek attacked them. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and now I am going to make Amalek pay!
translation_verse: Asafo AWURADE nwa nyoo, ‘Ngotua Amalɛkefoɛ so kerɛ, ɔnate kyɛ mmerɛ bɔ né Yisraelfoɛ béfi Misraim bɛ́ba ne, bɛɛtɛle bɛ atunu bɛ ne bɛ hone.

english_verse: “Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
translation_verse: Yiti kɔ na kohũ Amalɛkefoɛ, ná sɛkye bɔ bele ye amu bɔkɔɔ. Nnɛma ebiala nya ye ti didi nu, na mmom ku mmienzua ne mmrasua, ngwadaa ne nnɔma, nandwie ne mmoaen, afupɔngɔ ne afunum.’ ”

english_verse: Saul sent messengers who told every town and village to send men to join the army at Telaim. There were
translation_verse: Yiti Sɔɔlo tole ye sa frɛle koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ maa beyiale, na ɔhale bɛ wɔ Telaim. Né bɛ somaa te koɛhonɛfoɛ apee ɛyaa nyɔ bɔ bɛnate ase ɔ, ɔne Yuda koɛhonɛfoɛ apee buru.

english_verse: The Lord told Samuel,
translation_verse: AWURADE lale ye dwirɛ ali hyirele Samuel kyɛ,

english_verse: then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack.
translation_verse: Afei Sɔɔlo ne koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ hɔle beedwuli Amalɛke kuro piri ne aso, na bɛɛtɛle bɔnza ne anu dɔ.

english_verse: Some Kenites lived nearby, and Saul told them, “Your people were kind to our nation when we left Egypt, and I don't want you to get killed when I wipe out the Amalekites. So stay away from them.” The Kenites left,
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo sele Kenifoɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhɔ! Ɛ́mɔfi Amalɛkefoɛ mɔ nu bɛ́nwati bɛ́hɔ, ná mangu ɛmɔ mamvra bɛ. Ɔnate kyɛ, mmerɛ bɔ né Yisraelfoɛ befi Misraim bɛ́ba ne, ɛmɔyɔle bɛ mukoraa paa.” Yiti Kenifoɛ fili Amalɛkefoɛ nu bɛnwati bɛhɔle.

english_verse: and Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, which is just east of Egypt.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo lili Amalɛkefoɛ so ngonim fite Hawila toonn oodwuli Sure bɔ ɔwɔ Misraim eyia afiteleɛ ne.

english_verse: Saul and his army let Agag live, and they also spared the best sheep and cattle. They didn't want to destroy anything of value, so they only killed the animals that were worthless or weak. The Lord Rejects Saul
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo ne koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bangu Agage, mmoaen ne nandwie paa nemɔ, nandwie sayɛɛ nemɔ, ɔne mmoaen mmaa nemɔ, yeɛ banzɛkye nikyee biala bɔ ɔte paa ɔ. Banguro kyɛ bekohu bɛ ɔ. Nakoso nikyee biala bɔ bebuli ye kyɛ ɔtte mayee ná ye nwo olle mvasoɛ ne de, bɛsɛkyele ye bɔkɔɔ. Nyameɛ fɛ Sɔɔlo so yaa bieku

english_verse: “Saul has stopped obeying me, and I'm sorry that I made him king.” Samuel was angry, and he cried out in prayer to the Lord all night.
translation_verse: “Ɔyɛ me yea kyɛ mvale Sɔɔlo nzili hene ɔ, ofikyɛ wayakyi me si lilɛ, na onni me mmeraa so.” Sɔ dwirɛ ne hale Samuel, na osũ frɛle AWURADE kɔngɔen ne amukoraa.

english_verse: Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Samuel pɛle aleɛ dwɔsole kyɛ ɔkwaapena Sɔɔlo. Na bɛha behyirele Samuel kyɛ, “Sɔɔlo ahɔ Kamɛl, nekaa bɔ wasi ngayeɛ nikyee wafa wahyɛ ye nwo animnyam ne, na waase wapɛ nu wahɔ Gilgal.”

english_verse: Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
translation_verse: Na Samuel dwuli Sɔɔlo nwo berɛ ne, Sɔɔlo sele ye kyɛ, “AWURADE yira wɔ oo! Bɔ AWURADE hyɛle me kyɛ nyɔ ne, mayɔ.”

english_verse: “Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
translation_verse: Nakoso Samuel bisale kyɛ, “Mmoaen suɛ bɔ ogua me so anu ye, ɔne nandwie suɛ bɔ mete ye koso ɛ?

english_verse: “The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sɔɔlo buale kyɛ, “Amalɛkefoɛ mɔ dɔ yeɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bɛ ne bɛ fi wale ɔ, ofikyɛ bɛyakyili mmoaen paa ne nandwie paa nemɔ kyɛ bɛbaafa bɛbɔ afɔleɛ bɛma AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ. Nakoso bɛ ngaa nemɔ de, yahũhũ bɛ bɔkɔɔ.”

english_verse: “Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.” “All right,” Saul answered.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Samuel sele Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Pɛ so! Maa nga bɔ AWURADE ha hyirele me ɛnɛ kɔngɔen ye ngyire wɔ.” Na osele kyɛ, “Kã e.”

english_verse: Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Samuel sele kyɛ, “Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ ebu wɔ nwo kyɛ ɛte kwahweabaa bie de, nakoso aso nna wɔ yeɛ ɛla Yisrael mmusua kure nemɔ noa ɔ? AWURADE popale wɔ ngoo fale wɔ lili Yisrael so hene;

english_verse: When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites.
translation_verse: na AWURADE somane wɔ fale adwuma wurale wɔ sa kyɛ, ‘Sɔ Amalɛkefoɛ bɔnefoɛ nemɔ, kohũhũ bɛ bɔkɔɔ, na fa koɛ toa bɛ toonn kɔpem kyɛ bɛ boso konua ɔ.’

english_verse: Why didn't you listen to the Lord? Why did you keep the animals and make him angry?”
translation_verse: Nzu ati yeɛ anni AWURADE dwirɛ so ɔ? Nzu ati yeɛ ɛfene koɛ nu nzesadeɛ ne, maa ɔnate so ɛyɔle AWURADE nyunu bɔne ɔ?”

english_verse: “But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo buale Samuel kyɛ, “Mali AWURADE dwirɛ so. Adwuma bɔ AWURADE somane me fa wurale me sa ne, mayɔ. Mahye Amalɛke hene Agage mawa, na mahuhu Amalɛkefoɛ bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Nakoso koɛ nu nzesadeɛ ne, bɔ AWURADE atu asie berɛ kyɛ bɛsɛkye ye ne, koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ fale mmoaen paa ne nandwie paa ne bie, kyɛ bɛbaafa bɛbɔ afɔleɛ bɛma AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ wɔ Gilgal.”

english_verse: “Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him.
translation_verse: Nakoso Samuel hane kyɛ, “Aso AWURADE nye gye naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne afɔleɛ mɔ nwo tra kyɛ ekotie AWURADE dwirɛ ɔ? Nahorɛ nu, sotie te paa tra afɔleɛbɔlɛ, yeɛ asoɛ mmerɛlɛyɛlɛ te paa tra boaen nyii loe.

english_verse: Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ ɛlɔenyɛlɛ ɔte bɔne kyɛ ahɔenlilɛ ne ala, yeɛ asoserɛ te kyɛ amumuyɛɛ ne amoensɔlɛ. Na ɔnate kyɛ apo AWURADE dwirɛ ne ati, wɔ hene bɔ edi ne, ye koso waye ye sa wafi wɔ bo.”

english_verse: “I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sɔɔlo sele Samuel kyɛ, “Mayɔ bɔne kyɛ mabu AWURADE mmeraa ne wɔ noa dwirɛ so ɔ, ofikyɛ nzurole koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ, na ndiele bɛ dwirɛ.

english_verse: Please forgive me and come back with me so I can worship the Lord.”
translation_verse: Yiti mesrɛ wɔ ala, fa me bɔne kyɛ me, ná ɛne me sa hɔ ma ngɔnzɔne AWURADE.”
