english_verse: “No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
translation_verse: Na Samuel sele Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Me ne wɔ ngosa ngɔhɔ, ofikyɛ apo AWURADE dwirɛ. Na Yisrael so hene bɔ edi ne, AWURADE koso waye ye sa wafi wɔ bo.”

english_verse: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore!
translation_verse: Na Samuel kakyili ye nwo bɔ ɔkɔ nen, Sɔɔlo sɔle ye ataadeɛ tendenn ne noa, na nu suale.

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and he will give it to someone who is better than you.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Samuel sele ye kyɛ, “AWURADE ale Yisrael ahennie ne wafi wɔ sa nu ɛnɛ kyẽa ye, na wafa wama sona foforɛ bɔ ɔte paa tra wɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
translation_verse: Asa koso, Yisrael Animnyam ne, ɔtte nnakannakaniɛ, yeɛ ɔnzesã ye adwene, ofikyɛ ɔtte kuro sona ná wasesã ye adwene.”

english_verse: Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo buale ye kyɛ, “Mayɔ bɔne de, nakoso mesrɛ wɔ ala, nnɛgua me nyunu ase wɔ me maen mbanyi ne Yisrael nyunu. Ɛne me sa hɔ ma ngɔnzɔne AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ.”

english_verse: Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Yiti Samuel lili Sɔɔlo si ɔne ye bɛhɔle, na Sɔɔlo sɔnene AWURADE.

english_verse: Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!” Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
translation_verse: Afei Samuel sele kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔfa Amalɛkefoɛ hene Agage bɛ́brɛ me!” Na Agage wale ye nwo berɛ bɔ né ye gya to brabra nu ɔ. Yeɛ Agage hane kyɛ, “Amba, ewueyealɛ ato me.”

english_verse: But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
translation_verse: Na Samuel sele kyɛ, “Kyɛbɔ wɔ ngrandɛ ama mmrasua bafa bɛ sa bafi terɛ ne, sɔ ala yeɛ mmrasua mɔ nu wora, eni kɔfa ye sa kofi terɛ ɔ.” Na Samuel pepɛle Agage nu ahuronzi ahuronzi wɔ AWURADE nyunu wɔ Gilgal.

english_verse: Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah.
translation_verse: Afei Samuel hɔle Rama, yeɛ Sɔɔlo koso hɔle ye kuro Gibea.

english_verse: Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again. The Lord Chooses David To Be King The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Samuel nye ammɔ Sɔɔlo nyunu ko kɔpem kyɛ Samuel wuli ɔ, nakoso Samuel lili Sɔɔlo nwo aworabɔlɛ. Na ɔyɛle AWURADE yea kyɛ wafa Sɔɔlo wali Yisrael so hene ɔ.

english_verse: One day he said, “Samuel, I've rejected Saul, and I refuse to let him be king any longer. Stop feeling sad about him. Put some olive oil in a small container and go visit a man named Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I've chosen one of his sons to be my king.”
translation_verse: AWURADE bisale Samuel kyɛ, “Kyinzu koraa yeɛ ekoli Sɔɔlo nwo aworabɔlɛ maa okoodwu ɔ? Maye me sa mafi ye bo maa ye sɔ ati ɔtte Yisrael so hene ko. Fa ngoo gua wɔ towaa ne anu ná si nu kɔ. Mésoma wɔ Betlehemniɛ Yese berɛ, ofikyɛ ye mma nemɔ anu ko yeɛ me bɔbɔ maye ye kyɛ oli hene ɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel answered, “If I do that, Saul will find out and have me killed.” “Take a calf with you,” the Lord replied. “Tell everyone that you've come to offer it as a sacrifice to me,
translation_verse: Na Samuel bisale kyɛ, “Ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ né mahora mahɔ? Sɛ Sɔɔlo te sɔ dwirɛ ne a, okohu me.” Na AWURADE buale kyɛ, “Ɛkɔ a, fa nandwie beleɛ akrɔngrɔma ko kɔ, ná kɔha kyɛ, ‘Mawa kyɛ mebaabɔ afɔleɛ mema AWURADE.’

english_verse: then invite Jesse to the sacrifice. When I show you which one of his sons I have chosen, pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: To wɔ sa frɛ Yese maa ɔbra afɔleɛ ne abo, na me bɔbɔ ngohyire wɔ nikyee bɔ odi kyɛ ɛyɔ ɔ. Sona bɔ ngohyire wɔ ne, fa ɛpopalɛ ngoo gua ye ti so ma me.”

english_verse: Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
translation_verse: Samuel yɔle bɔ AWURADE hyɛle ye ne, na ɔhɔle Betlehem. Kuro berɛ mbanyi fale ahunundetelɛ beeyiale ye, na bebisale ye kyɛ, “W’atee so bɔkɔɔ de?”

english_verse: “Yes, it is!” Samuel answered. “I've come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get yourselves ready to take part in the sacrifice and come with me.” Samuel also invited Jesse and his sons to come to the sacrifice, and he got them ready to take part.
translation_verse: Na obuale kyɛ, “Bɔkɔɔ. Mawa kyɛ mebaabɔ afɔleɛ mema AWURADE. Ɛ́mɔpete ɛmɔ nwo ná ɛ́mɔma yɛhɔ afɔleɛ ne abo.” Ɔpetene Yese ne ye mma nemɔ anwo, na osele bɛ kyɛ bɛbra afɔleɛ ne abo.

english_verse: When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
translation_verse: Bedwuli berɛ ná Samuel nwuni Eliabo nen, ɔhane ye wɔ ye ti anu kyɛ, “Amba, sona bɔ AWURADE aneanea nu waye ye ne, ye yeɛ ogyi AWURADE nyunu ye.”

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “Samuel, don't think Eliab is the one just because he's tall and handsome. He isn't the one I've chosen. People judge others by what they look like, but I judge people by what is in their hearts.”
translation_verse: Nakoso AWURADE sele ye kyɛ, “Nnɛnea kyɛbɔ osi te ɔ anaa ye tendenn, ofikyɛ nna ye yeɛ mekuro ɔ. Na kyɛbɔ sona si nwu nikyee ne, nna sɔ yeɛ AWURADE nwu ye ɔ. Bɛ nye so nikye yeɛ sona nea ɔ, nakoso AWURADE de, ɔnea b’ahone nu.”

english_verse: Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yese frɛle Abinadabo maa ɔɔpɛle nu Samuel nyunu berɛ. Nakoso Samuel sele kyɛ, “Ɛhe koso, AWURADE nguro.”

english_verse: Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
translation_verse: Afei Yese mane Sama ɔɔpɛle nu, nakoso Samuel sele kyɛ, “Ɛhe koso, AWURADE nguro.”

english_verse: One by one, Jesse told all seven of his sons to go over to Samuel. Finally, Samuel said, “Jesse, the Lord hasn't chosen any of these young men.
translation_verse: Yiti Yese mane ye mma mmienzua nzoo nemɔ bɛɛpɛle nu wɔ Samuel nyunu, na Samuel sele Yese kyɛ, “AWURADE nguro ɛhemɔ nu biala.”

english_verse: Do you have any other sons?” “Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.” “Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
translation_verse: Afei Samuel bisale Yese kyɛ, “Wɔ mma mmienzua nemɔ, bɛ mu ɛhe?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Waha kãa paa ne, na ye de ɔ́nea mmoaen so.” Yeɛ Samuel sele Yese kyɛ, “Soma ma bɛɛfa ye bɛbra, ofikyɛ yɛngɔtena ase kyɛ yɛdidi, sana wawa wa koraka.”

english_verse: Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Yese somane maa bɛɛfale ye bɛwale. Né ɔte sona bɔ ɔte apɔ, ye nye mmaa dabadabaa, na ye nwo yɛ nyemene. Na AWURADE sele kyɛ, “Ɛhe ɛne, dwɔso fa ɛpopalɛ ngoo ne gua ye ti so!”

english_verse: Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on. Samuel returned home to Ramah. David Plays the Harp for Saul
translation_verse: Afei Samuel fale ɛpopalɛ ngoo towaa ne, na ohwiele ngoo ne guale Dawide ti so wɔ oliɛma nemɔ anyunu berɛ. Na ofi sɔ kyẽa ne bɔ ɔkɔ ne, AWURADE Sunzum kanyane Dawide paa. Afei Samuel sili nu hɔle Rama. Dawide wɔ Sɔɔlo ahemvie

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him.
translation_verse: AWURADE Sunzum hwene ye nwo fili Sɔɔlo nwo, na AWURADE somane sunzum tɛɛ bie maa ɔɔteetee ye.

english_verse: “It's an evil spirit from God that's frightening you,” Saul's officials told him.
translation_verse: Yiti Sɔɔlo somvoɛ nemɔ ha hyirele ye kyɛ, “Nana, sunzum tɛɛ bie bɔ ofi Nyameɛ berɛ yeɛ ɔteetee wɔ ɔ.

english_verse: “Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
translation_verse: Yɛ mene, wɔ somvoɛ mɔ yeɛ yɛwɔ wɔ nyunu wa ye. Ma ate ma yɛɛpena sona bɔ ɔse sangoo bɔ paa ɔ, na sɛ sunzum tɛɛ ne fi Nyameɛ berɛ te pe wɔ so a, wabɔ wama wɔ nwo asande wɔ.”

english_verse: “All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo sele ye somvoɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔɔpena sona bɔ ɔse ye bɔ paa bɛma me.”

english_verse: “A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
translation_verse: Na mmerandeɛ nemɔ anu ko buale kyɛ, “Manwu Betlehemniɛ Yese ɔwa bienzua bie kyɛ ɔse ye bɔ paa. Ɔte ahoneserɛniɛ, koɛhonɛniɛ, ye noa ate, ye nwo yɛ nyemene, na AWURADE gyi ye si.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
translation_verse: Yiti Sɔɔlo tuli bɔfoɛ maa bɛhɔle Yese berɛ beesele ye kyɛ, “Ɛwa Dawide bɔ ɔnea mmoaen so ne, maa ɔbra me wa.”

english_verse: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul.
translation_verse: Yese fale afunum, na ɔfale aleɛ, bobe nzaa ngomvo ko, ɔne abɔngye ba soale kaka ne, na ɔfa somane ɔwa Dawide maa ɔɔmane Sɔɔlo.

english_verse: David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons.
translation_verse: Na Dawide wale Sɔɔlo berɛ ɔɔyɛle ye somvoɛ. Sɔɔlo hurole Dawide dwirɛ paa, na ɔmane Dawide yɛle ye somvoɛ bɔ otira ye akodeɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
translation_verse: Afei Sɔɔlo somane maa beesele Yese kyɛ, “Ma Dawide tena me nwo wa ɔso me, ofikyɛ mekuro ye dwirɛ paa.”

english_verse: Whenever the evil spirit from God bothered Saul, David would play his harp. Saul would relax and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ biala, sɛ né Nyameɛ soma sunzum tɛɛ ne maa ɔte pe Sɔɔlo so a, ɔyɛ a Dawide bɔ sangoo ne ma Sɔɔlo nwo tɔ ye, ye nwo sande ye, na sunzum tɛɛ ne fi ye so kɔ.

english_verse: The Philistines got ready for war and brought their troops together to attack the town of Socoh in Judah. They set up camp at Ephes-Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.
translation_verse: Filistifoɛ boaboale bɛ noa kyɛ bɛkwaaho koɛ. Bɛɛboale bɛ noa wɔ Soko bɔ ɔwɔ Yuda, na bɛkyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ Efese Damim bɔ ɔwɔ Soko ne Aseka b’afia.

english_verse: King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
translation_verse: Filistifoɛ gyinagyinane bokaa ne bue ko, yeɛ Yisraelfoɛ koso begyinagyinane bokaa ne bue ko, na né bɔnza la b’afia.

english_verse: The Philistine army had a hero named Goliath who was from the town of Gath and was about three meters tall.
translation_verse: Na bienzua kwabranoa bie fili Filistifoɛ asikyeleɛ ne anu oogyinane anyunu. Oli Goliate, ofi Gate, na ye tendenn te agyirɛ ngona ne bɛ sa mmɛseka ko.

english_verse: He wore a bronze helmet and had bronze armor to protect his chest and legs. The chest armor alone weighed about
translation_verse: Né wafa kɔɔbere wadwura ye gya nwo, yeɛ né buralɛ tendenn tworɔntworɔn bie la ye kɔme anwo.

english_verse: When David came back from fighting Goliath, he was still carrying Goliath's head. Abner took David to Saul,
translation_verse: Dawide oohuni Filistiniɛ ne ná osa wale ne, Abenɛ fale ye hɔle Sɔɔlo nyunu. Né ɔtɛ tira Filistiniɛ ne ye ti ne.

english_verse: and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
translation_verse: Ye pealɛɛ ne, ɔte kyɛ mbuna bɔ bɛfa nyamaa bɛsosɔ nu bɛnwo ɛtena ɔ. Ye pealɛɛ ne noa ne, nu nonɛ kɔyɛ kilo nzoo; na né sona bɔ otira ye akokyɛm ne li ye nyunu.

english_verse: Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel: Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me!
translation_verse: Goliate oogyinane berɛ teane nu sele Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔawa kyɛ ɛmɔbaaho koɛ ɔ? Me, nde Filistiniɛ, yeɛ ɛmɔ koso ɛmɔte Sɔɔlo ngoaa. Ɛ́mɔye ɛmɔ nu bienzua ko ma odwu bra ma me ne ye yɛli ahoɛ.

english_verse: If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɔkora ɔne me ko ná oku me a, ye de yɛkɔyɛ ɛmɔ ngoaa; nakoso sɛ medi ye so ngonim ná meku ye a, ye de ɛmɔkɔyɛ yɛ ngoaa bɛkɔso yɛ.”

english_verse: Here and now I challenge Israel's whole army! Choose someone to fight me!
translation_verse: Na Filistiniɛ ne toale so sele kyɛ, “Ɛnɛ kyẽa ye, Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ, sɛ ɛmɔte mmienzua a, ɛ́mɔye sona ko ma me ne ye yɛli ahoɛ!”

english_verse: Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing. David Decides To Challenge Goliath
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo ne Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa tele sɔ dwirɛ bɔ Filistiniɛ ne hane nen, ɛserɛ hane bɛ, na besurole paa. Dawide kɔ Sɔɔlo asikyeleɛ nu

english_verse: David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons:
translation_verse: Dawide baba li Yese. Ɔte Efrateniɛ. Ofi Betlehem bɔ ɔwɔ Yudea. Né Yese le mmaa mmienzua mmɔtwɛ. Na Sɔɔlo aberɛ so ne, né sɔ biaa ne wanyi wayɛ aworowaa.

english_verse: He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
translation_verse: Nakoso Dawide de, né ɔyɛ a ofi Sɔɔlo nwo ɔkɔnea ɔse mmoaen so wɔ Betlehem osa ba.

english_verse: Goliath came out and gave his challenge every morning and every evening for
translation_verse: Ngyẽa eleburanna, ngyerɛmɔ ne nɔsoa biala, né Filistiniɛ ne bagyina berɛ fa ye nwo kyire.

english_verse: and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath. David Kills Goliath
translation_verse: Afei Dawide fale ye bɔbɔ ye pɔmaa ne tirale, ɔsesale kokwaboba nnu wɔ asue ba ne anu, na ɔfa guale bɔtɔ bɔ ɔwɔ ye mmoaenneafoɛ kotoku ne anu. Ɔfale ye taya ne tirale, na afei ɔbɔ pingyele Filistiniɛ ne. Dawide di Goliate so ngonim

english_verse: One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp.
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, Yese sele ɔwa Dawide kyɛ, “Ngyeweɛ graa ko he, ɔne paanoo buru he, fa kɔma eliɛma nemɔ. Ma wɔ nwo yɛ nyera ná kɔ asikyeleɛ ne anu fa kɔma eliɛma nemɔ.

english_verse: And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right.
translation_verse: Na nandwie nyɔfonesue bɔ babɔ ye kunguma buru he koso, fa kɔma bɛ safohene bɔ ɔla koɛhonɛfoɛ apee ko noa ne. Nea kyɛbɔ eliɛma nemɔ bɛ nwo si te ɔ, ná fa bɛ nwo nikyee bie baahyire me maa nwu kyɛ bɛte ase.”

english_verse: They're with Saul's army, fighting the Philistines in Elah Valley.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo ne Dawide aliɛma nemɔ ne Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ ne amu, né bɛwɔ Ela bɔnza ne anu bɛ ne Filistifoɛ bɛ́ko.

english_verse: David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry.
translation_verse: Dawide dwɔsole alebahyene, ɔfale mmoaen nemɔ wurale ebie sa kyɛ ɔnea bɛ so, na ɔfale aleɛ ne sili nu hɔle, kyɛbɔ Yese hyɛle ye ne. Mmerɛ bɔ oodwuli asikyeleɛ ne anu ne, né Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bétu bɛ bo bekogyina koɛ noa, bɔ né bɛteatea nu bɛ́to koɛ dwein ɔ.

english_verse: The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.
translation_verse: Né Yisrael ne Filistifoɛ bate bagyina kyɛ bɛkɔho, bɔ ɛlɔen ko gyi bue ko, ná ko koso gyi bue ko ɔ.

english_verse: David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well.
translation_verse: Dawide yakyili ye nningyein ne mane sona bɔ ɔnea nningyein so ne, na otuli amirika hɔle koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ nwo dɔ oobisale oliɛma nemɔ kyɛbɔ bɛ nwo si te ɔ.

english_verse: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off.
translation_verse: Na Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ ne amukoraa nye bɔle biaa ne aso nen, ɛserɛ hane bɛ maa bɛnwatili befili ye nyunu.

english_verse: They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ sisele kyɛ, “Yeɛ ɛmɔanwu biaa he bɔ ɔ́fo ba ye? Susu amba, wawa kyɛ ɔbaapɛ Yisrael poa. Sona bɔ okohu sɔ biaa he nen, Nana Sɔɔlo kɔbɔ ye aba so maa okonya ye nwo, ɔkɔfa ɔwa brasua maa okogya, na ɔkɔma ɔse awuro ama konya bɛ fawɔnwodi wɔ Yisrael.”

english_verse: David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
translation_verse: Na Dawide bisale mmenia bɔ begyigyi ye nwo berɛ ne kyɛ, “Sona bɔ okohu sɔ Filistiniɛ he, ná ɔkɔye animguaseɛ kofi Yisrael so ne, nzikyɛ yeɛ bɛkɔfa bɛkɔbɔ ye aba so ɔ? Sɔ Filistiniɛ he bɔ ɔmbɛ ye bienzua ye, ye ole nwa bɔ ɔpɛ Nyameɛ teasefoɛ ye koɛhonɛfoɛ poa ɔ?”

english_verse: The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
translation_verse: Na koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ mane Dawide mmuayɛɛ komapɛ ne ala kyɛ, “Nikyee bɔ bafa babɔ anohoba ne, yeɛ bɛkɔfa bɛkɔma sona bɔ okohu ye ɔ.”

english_verse: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
translation_verse: Dawide aliɛma panyi Eliabo tele kyɛ ɔ́ka edwirɛ kyire koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ nen, ɔfɛle Dawide so yaa, na ɔhane kyɛ, “W’amaneɛ wɔ wa? Mmoaen kãa bie ne, nwa yeɛ ɛfale bɛ yakyili ye wɔ ɛserɛ ne aso ɔ? Mese kyɛbɔ esi te dwɛɛ ɔne adwene tɛɛ bɔ ɔwɔ wɔ ti anu ɔ. Koɛ ne ala yeɛ ɛwale kyɛ ɛbaanea ɔ!”

english_verse: “Now what have I done?” David answered. “Can't I even ask a question?”
translation_verse: Na Dawide buale ye kyɛ, “Mayɔ nzu? Edwirɛ mbaen yeɛ mébisa ɔ.”

english_verse: Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
translation_verse: Dawide fili Eliabo nwo berɛ oobisale sona foforɛ edwirɛ komapɛ ne ala, na mmuayɛɛ komapɛ ne ala yeɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ sa fa mane ye ɔ.

english_verse: Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came.
translation_verse: Na bɛtele edwirɛ bɔ Dawide hane nen, bɛɛbɔle Sɔɔlo amaneɛ, na ɔmaa bɛɛfale Dawide bɛwale.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” he said, “this Philistine shouldn't turn us into cowards. I'll go out and fight him myself!”
translation_verse: Na Dawide ha hyirele Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Nnɛma ebiala suro ye. W’akoaa, me ne sɔ Filistiniɛ he yɛkɔɔho.”

english_verse: “You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sɔɔlo sele Dawide kyɛ, “Sɔ Filistiniɛ he, ɛngɔhora ngogyina ye nyunu ɛne ye bɛngɔho; ofikyɛ ɛte akwadaa, nakoso ye de waho koɛ toonn fite ye ngwadaa nu.”

english_verse: But David told him: Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear,
translation_verse: Nakoso Dawide buale Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “W’akoaa, me yeɛ menea me baba mmoaen so ɔ; na mmerɛ biala sɛ gyata anaa kwabrafo bakye boaen ba fi mmoaen kure ne anu a,

english_verse: I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
translation_verse: mefoa ye mepura ye, na mede boaen ne mefi ye noa nu. Na sɛ kaka ne ba me so kyɛ ɔbaahye me a, mesɔ ye awogyee nu mebɔ ye meku ye.

english_verse: Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God!
translation_verse: W’akoaa ahu gyata mɔ ne kwabrafo mɔ, na sɔ Filistiniɛ he bɔ ɔmbɛ ye bienzua ye de, ɔkɔyɛ kyɛ bɛ nu ko ala, ofikyɛ wapɛ Nyameɛ teasefoɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ poa.

english_verse: The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine. “All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
translation_verse: Na AWURADE bɔ olele me fili gyata sa nu, ɔne kwabrafo sa nu ne, okole me kofi sɔ Filistiniɛ he sa nu.” Yeɛ Sɔɔlo sele Dawide kyɛ, “Kɔ, na mesrɛ kyɛ AWURADE ogyina wɔ si!”

english_verse: Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo fale ye koɛ ataadeɛ ne wurale Dawide. Ɔfale kɔɔbere kyerɛ wurale ye, na ɔfale buralɛ katale ye hue so.

english_verse: David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things. “I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.” David took off the armor
translation_verse: Dawide fale Sɔɔlo ngrandɛ ne sinzele ye ataadeɛ ne aso. Ɔyɛle kyɛ ɔ́fa nate, nakoso né ɔffale bie owwurale le. Na Dawide sele Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Mengɔhora sɔ nningyein hemɔ fa nate, ofikyɛ mmvale bie nnwurale le.” Yiti Dawide puropurole bɛ fili ye nwo.

english_verse: Goliath came toward David, walking behind the soldier who was carrying his shield.
translation_verse: Né Filistiniɛ ne koso ɔ́bɔ pingye Dawide; na né sona bɔ otira Filistiniɛ n’akokyɛm ne, oli ye nyunu.

english_verse: When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him.
translation_verse: Na Filistiniɛ ne tole ye nye ná onwuni Dawide nen, wammu ye sona bie, ofikyɛ né ɔte akwadaa ba bie. Né ɔboro, yeɛ né ye nwo yɛ nyemene.

english_verse: “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods
translation_verse: Na Filistiniɛ ne sele Dawide kyɛ, “Mmokuroma yeɛ ɛfa ba me so ɔ, nde kyea hɔ ɔ?” Afei Filistiniɛ ne fale ye nyameɛ mɔ payele Dawide.

english_verse: and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
translation_verse: Na Filistiniɛ ne sele Dawide kyɛ, “Wɔ de bra me nyunu, na ngɔfa wɔ naen ngɔma ewienu nnomaa ne eburo ngaka.”

english_verse: David answered: You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
translation_verse: Nakoso Dawide buale Filistiniɛ ne kyɛ, “Wɔ de, ngrandɛ ne pealɛɛ ne buralɛ tendenn tworɔntworɔn yeɛ ɛ́fa ba me so ɔ; nakoso me de, Asafo AWURADE, Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ Nyameɛ bɔ apɛ ye poa ne, ye dumaa nu yeɛ méba wɔ so ɔ.

english_verse: Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God.
translation_verse: Ɛnɛ kyẽa ye, AWURADE kɔfa wɔ kowura me sa. Ngohũ wɔ ngɔpɛ wɔ ti. Ɛnɛ kyẽa ye, ngɔfa Filisti koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bɛ fuin ngɔma ewienu nnomaa ne aseɛ so ngaka. Na ɔnate so ewiase amukoraa konwu ye kyɛ Nyameɛ bie wɔ Yisrael.

english_verse: Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
translation_verse: Na mmenia bɔ bayia wa ye amukoraa konwu ye kyɛ, AWURADE mva ngrandɛ ne pealɛɛ yeɛ ode ye mmenia ɔ; ofikyɛ AWURADE yeɛ koɛ ne te ye koɛ ɔ, na ɔkɔfa ɛmɔ kowura yɛ sa.”

english_verse: He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground.
translation_verse: Dawide fale ye sa wurale ye bɔtɔ ne anu, ɔyele nyɔboɛ ko fili nu, ɔfa wurale ye taya ne anu, na ɔto bɔle Filistiniɛ ne nwoma so. Nyɔboɛ ne mi hɔle ye nwoma ne anu, na ɔpɛ fini aseɛnwo berɛ mane ye nyunu butuli ase.

english_verse: David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
translation_verse: Yiti taya ɔne nyɔboɛ yeɛ Dawide fa lili Filistiniɛ ne so ngonim ɔ. Ɔto bɔle Filistiniɛ ne huni ye. Né Dawide de ottira ngrandɛ biala.

english_verse: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
translation_verse: Afei Dawide tuli amirika oogyinane Filistiniɛ ne aso. Ɔsɔle sɔ Filistiniɛ ne ngrandɛ nu hwe fili ye bɔha nu, na ohuni ye. Afei ɔfa pɛle ye ti fili so. Na Filistifoɛ mɔ nwuni kyɛ bɛ sona bɔ ɔla bɛ noa ne wawu nen, bɛnwatili.

english_verse: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ ne Yuda koɛhonɛfoɛ hyɛle ye bo bɛbɔle ese, na bɛfoane Filistifoɛ toonn bedwuli Gate ne Ekron pambim nemɔ. Filistifoɛ bɔ bepurapurale ne, bɛtotɔle atee so fili Saaraim toonn beedwuli Gate ne Ekron.

english_verse: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Afei Yisraelfoɛ yakyili Filistifoɛ foalɛ, na besa bɛwale bɛɛfene Filistifoɛ asikyeleɛ ne anu nningyein.

english_verse: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
translation_verse: Dawide fale Filistiniɛ ne ti ne, ɔfa wale Yerusalem, nakoso Filistiniɛ n’akodeɛ ne de, ɔfa guale ye bɔbɔ ye tena sua nu.

english_verse: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Sɔɔlo nwuni Dawide kyɛ ɔkwaayia Filistiniɛ ne ɔne ye bɛko ne, obisale safohene Abenɛ kyɛ, “Sɔ aberandeɛ he, nwa awa ɛne?” Na Abenɛ buale kyɛ, “Nana, meta wɔ ndaen kyɛ menze.”

english_verse: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo bisale ye kyɛ, “Aberandeɛ, nwa awa ole wɔ?” Yeɛ Dawide buale kyɛ, “W’akoaa Yese, Betlehemniɛ ne, ɔwa ole me.”

english_verse: From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
translation_verse: Na ofi sɔ kyẽa ne, Sɔɔlo fale Dawide ɔne ye bɛtenane, na wamma wanza wangɔ ye baba awuro dɔ ko.

english_verse: Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends.
translation_verse: Afei Yonatan ne Dawide yɛle apam, ofikyɛ né okuro Dawide dwirɛ kyɛ ye bɔbɔ ye nwo.

english_verse: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
translation_verse: Yonatan purole ye ataadeɛ tendenn bɔ owurale ye ne mane Dawide, na ɔfale ye akodeɛ, ye ngrandɛ ne ye agyaen ne ye abɔsoɛ po bokale so.

english_verse: David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers. Saul Becomes David's Enemy
translation_verse: Koɛ biala bɔ Sɔɔlo somane Dawide maa ɔɔhone ne, olili ngonim, yiti Sɔɔlo maa ɔlale koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ noa. Na ɛhe yɛle koɛhonɛfoɛ ne amukoraa ne Sɔɔlo somvoɛ nemɔ po fɛ. Sɔɔlo nya Dawide nwo adwene tɛɛ

english_verse: David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Dawide huni Filistiniɛ ne, ná ɔne koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ besa bɛba nen, mmrasua fale edwein ne abilie befili Yisrael nguro ne amukoraa so beeyiale Nana Sɔɔlo. Né bele akasaa ne firikyiwa bɛ́to anigye dwein.

english_verse: They sang: Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!
translation_verse: Na mmrasua nemɔ gole abilie bɛtole dwein besurole so kyɛ, “Sɔɔlo ahu apee apee, yeɛ Dawide ahu apee buru apee buru.”

english_verse: This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.”
translation_verse: Sɔ dwirɛ ne anyɛ Sɔɔlo fɛ, yiti ɔfɛle yaa hahii. Na ɔhane kyɛ, “Bɛnwa Dawide ahu apee buru apee buru, yeɛ me wora mahu apee apee ɔ. Nzikyɛ bieku yeɛ waha bɔ ye sa kɔha ye ɔ? Ahennie ye ɔ!”

english_verse: The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, Nyameɛ somane sunzum tɛɛ bie maa ɔte pene Sɔɔlo so, na ye nye so yɛle ye krakra wɔ ye awuro berɛ. Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Dawide ɔbɔ sangoo ne, kyɛbɔ né ɔbɔ ye daa biala ne. Né Sɔɔlo tira ye pealɛɛ ne.

english_verse: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo tole pealɛɛ ne, ofikyɛ onyane adwene kyɛ, “Ngɔfa ngɔwɔ Dawide maa ɔkɔha terɛ ne anwo.” Nakoso Dawide hwene ye nwo pɛen nyɔ bɔ wanwɔ ye ɔ.

english_verse: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him.
translation_verse: Né Sɔɔlo suro Dawide, ofikyɛ né AWURADE gyi Dawide si; nakoso Sɔɔlo de, né AWURADE aye ye sa wafi ye bo.

english_verse: The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles.
translation_verse: Dawide nyane ngɔsoɛ wɔ bɔ ɔyɔle amukoraati nu, ofikyɛ AWURADE lili ye si.

english_verse: This made Saul even more afraid of David.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo nwuni kyɛ Dawide onya ngɔsoɛ wɔ nikyee biala nu nen, osurole ye paa.

english_verse: But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yisrael amukoraa ne Yuda amukoraa hurole Dawide dwirɛ, ofikyɛ né ye yeɛ odi bɛ nyunu ɔfa bɛ kɔ koɛ ɔ. Dawide gya Sɔɔlo awa brasua Mikal

english_verse: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
translation_verse: Afei Sɔɔlo sele Dawide kyɛ, “Nea, mma brasua panyi Merabo ɛhe. Ngɔfa ye ngɔmaa ekogya, nakoso sana etu wɔ nwo sie berɛ ma me, ná ɛko AWURADE koɛ ne.” Né Sɔɔlo adwene ole kyɛ, “Me de, mengɔfa me sa mengɔhã ye; Filistifoɛ yeɛ mekuro kyɛ beku ye ɔ.”

english_verse: David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide buale Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Me ole nwa? Me nwo ama gyi ye sɛ? Me se abusua gyi ye sɛ wɔ Yisrael, bɔ me, mebaayɛ Nana sia ɔ?”

english_verse: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
translation_verse: Nakoso mmerɛ dwuli bɔ odi kyɛ Sɔɔlo fa ɔwa brasua Merabo ma Dawide nen, ɔfale Merabo mane Meholateniɛ Adriɛl maa ogyale.

english_verse: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
translation_verse: Né Sɔɔlo awa brasua Mikal kuro Dawide. Na bɛbɔle Sɔɔlo amaneɛ nen, ɔyɛle Sɔɔlo fɛ.

english_verse: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sɔɔlo hane ye wɔ ye ti anu kyɛ, “Ngɔfa Mikal ngɔma ye ngɔfa ngosua ye ngaen, na ɔnate so Filistifoɛ konya ye kohũ ye.” Yiti Sɔɔlo sele Dawide ye pɛen nyɔ so kyɛ, “Afei de, ɛkɔyɛ me sia.”

english_verse: Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?” “I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo somvoɛ nemɔ feale ase hane sɔ dwirɛ ne behyirele Dawide. Na Dawide buale kyɛ, “Ɛmɔnwa nzɛ ɔte edwirɛ baa kyɛ ngɔyɛ Nana sia ɔ. Me, ehianiɛ baa, nnde huu.”

english_verse: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo somvoɛ nemɔ fale Dawide mmuayɛɛ ne nwo amaneɛ bɛɛbɔle ye.

english_verse: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sɔɔlo buale kyɛ, “Ɛmɔɔha behyire Dawide kyɛ, ‘Nana mbena kyɛ ɛyɛ braa ne nwo nningyein, na mmom ɔpena Filistifoɛ ɛyaa ko bɛ bienzua noa nwomaa, bɔ ɔkɔmaa Nana kɔtɔ ye pɔfoɛ mɔ so wereɛ ɔ.’ Né Sɔɔlo pena kyɛ Filistifoɛ beku Dawide.

english_verse: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo somvoɛ nemɔ bɛɛhane sɔ dwirɛ ne behyirele Dawide nen, ɔyɛle Dawide fɛ paa kyɛ ɔbaayɛ Nana sia ɔ. Na mmerɛ ne andwu po,

english_verse: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
translation_verse: Nakoso Sɔɔlo nwuni kyɛ AWURADE gyi Dawide si, ná ɔwa Mikal koso kuro Dawide nen,

english_verse: But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo hɔle so surole Dawide paa, na Sɔɔlo pɔle Dawide wɔ ye asetena nu amukoraa.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_verse: Né ɔyɛ a Filisti safohene nemɔ bɛba kyɛ bɛbaaho koɛ. Na mmerɛ biala bɔ bɛwale nen, Dawide lili bɛ so ngonim trale Sɔɔlo somvoɛ ngaa ne amukoraati. Na ɛhe mane Dawide lele dumaa paa.

english_verse: One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends,
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo ha hyirele ɔwa Yonatan ne ye somvoɛ amukoraati kyɛ benya Dawide a behũ ye. Nakoso né Sɔɔlo awa Yonatan kuro Dawide dwirɛ.

english_verse: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
translation_verse: Ngoogyina me baba anwo berɛ wɔ eburo dɔ, nekaa bɔ ɛkɔɔfea ne, na ngɔhã edwirɛ bɔ ɔfa wɔ nwo ngohyire me baba. Na sɛ mete edwirɛ ne anwo bie a, ngɔma wɔ so kɔte.”

english_verse: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ ɔfale ye ngoa tole serewa oohuni Filistiniɛ ne, na AWURADE lili ngonim pirikua mane Yisrael amukoraati. Enwuni ye, na ɔyɛle wɔ fɛ. Na nzu ati yeɛ ɛpena kyɛ eku Dawide mbaen, maa ɔnate so ɛkã sona bɔ odi be mogya gua ɔ?”

english_verse: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo lele bɔ Yonatan hane ne tole nu, na ɔtale ndaen kyɛ, “Kyɛ AWURADE te ase ye, mengɔma ebiala ngohũ Dawide.”

english_verse: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
translation_verse: Nziɛ ye, Yonatan frɛle Dawide, na ɔhane edwirɛ ne amukoraa hyirele ye. Afei Yonatan fale Dawide hɔle Sɔɔlo berɛ, na ɔtenane Sɔɔlo berɛ sole ye kyɛ daa ne ala.

english_verse: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Koɛ sili bieku, na Dawide ne Filistifoɛ bɛɛhone. Ohuhuni bɛ paa maa ɔnate so bɛnwati befili ye nyunu.

english_verse: One night, David was in Saul's home, playing the harp for him. Saul was sitting there, holding a spear, when an evil spirit from the Lord took control of him. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David dodged, and it stuck in the wall. David ran out of the house and escaped.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo tole ye pealɛɛ ne kyɛ ɔ́fa wɔ Dawide maa ɔka terɛ ne anwo, nakoso Dawide hwene ye nwo, na pealɛɛ ne wɔle terɛ ne anu. Dawide nyane ye ti didili nu, na ɔnwatili kɔngɔen ne. Mikal boka ma Dawide nwati

english_verse: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo tuli mmenia maa bɛhɔle Dawide awuro kyɛ bɛɛtɛ ye behũ ye ngyerɛmɔ. Nakoso Dawide tiale Mikal gya so kyɛ, “Sɛ annwati kɔngɔen ye a, ɛhema ngyerɛmɔ bekohu wɔ.”

english_verse: She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off,
translation_verse: Yiti Mikal dwurale Dawide fale mboma nu, na ɔnwatili nyane ye ti didili nu.

english_verse: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
translation_verse: Mikal fale abaduaba dedale ye wɔ mba ne aso, ɔfale abɔngye nwiaa tole abaduaba ne ti dɔ yɛle sumu, na ɔfale ɛtena gurɔle ye nwo.

english_verse: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo somane mmenia kyɛ bɛɛhye Dawide, nakoso Mikal hane kyɛ, “Ɔnde apɔ.”

english_verse: Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sɔɔlo sa somane ɛbɔfoɛ nemɔ kyɛ bɛ bɔbɔ bɛɛfa bɛ nye benwu Dawide. Na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔɔhye ye wɔ bɛen ne aso bɛbrɛ me ma ngu ye!”

english_verse: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
translation_verse: Na ɛbɔfoɛ nemɔ dwuli berɛ nen, benwuni abaduaba bɔ bafa abɔngye nwiaa bayɛ sumu bato ye ti dɔ ne kyɛ ɔla mba ne aso.

english_verse: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo bisale Mikal kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ alakalaka me sɔa ye, bɔ ama me pɔfoɛ anwati ahɔ, maa wanya ye ti wadidi nu ye?” Yeɛ Mikal buale Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Ɔha hyirele me kyɛ, ‘Yakyi me ma ngɔ; anyɔ sɔ a, ngohũ wɔ.’ ” Dawide nwati kɔ Samuel berɛ

english_verse: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
translation_verse: Dawide nwatili nyane ye ti didili nu, na ɔhɔle Samuel berɛ wɔ Rama. Ɔhane edwirɛ bɔ Sɔɔlo afa ali ye amukoraa hyirele Samuel. Na ɔne Samuel betu bɛɛtenane Nayote.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
translation_verse: Na bɛbɔle Sɔɔlo amaneɛ kyɛ, “Dawide wɔ Nayote bɔ ɔwɔ Rama.”

english_verse: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
translation_verse: Yiti Sɔɔlo somane mmenia kyɛ bɛɛhye Dawide bɛbra. Mmerɛ bɔ Sɔɔlo bɔfoɛ nemɔ nwuni ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ kure ne kyɛ begu so bɛhyɛ ngɔm, bɔ né Samuel gyi berɛ ɔ́nea bɛ so ne, Nyameɛ sunzum wale ɛbɔfoɛ nemɔ so mane bɛ koso bɛhyɛle ngɔm.

english_verse: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ ebie ɔɔbɔle Sɔɔlo amaneɛ nen, ɔsomane mmenia foforɛ, na bɛ koso bɛhyɛle ngɔm. Sɔɔlo somane mmenia bieku, ye pɛen nza so, na bɛ koso bɛhyɛle ngɔm sɔ ala.

english_verse: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
translation_verse: Afei ye bɔbɔ osili nu kyɛ ɔkɔ Rama. Oodwuli abura piri bɔ ɔwɔ Seku ne anwo, na obisale kyɛ, “Nisua yeɛ Samuel ne Dawide bɛwɔ ɔ?” Na bebuale ye kyɛ, “Bɛwɔ Nayote bɔ ɔwɔ Rama.”

english_verse: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
translation_verse: Osili nu bɔ ɔkɔ Nayote bɔ ɔwɔ Rama nen, ye koso Nyameɛ sunzum wale ye so. Na ɔkɔ ne, ɔhyɛle ngɔm toonn oodwuli Nayote bɔ ɔwɔ Rama.

english_verse: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_verse: Ye koso opuropurole ye ndaadeɛ, na ɔhyɛle ngɔm wɔ Samuel nyunu berɛ. Na ɔfale ye nwo tole so lale berɛ sɔ kyẽa ne, eyia ne kɔngɔen amukoraa. Yiti ɔɔyɛle edwirɛ bie bɔ ɔla berɛ kyɛ, “Sɔɔlo koso boka ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ nemɔ so hɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
translation_verse: Dawide nwatili fili Nayote bɔ ɔwɔ Rama, na ɔhɔle Yonatan berɛ oobisale ye kyɛ, “Mayɔ nzu? Nzikyɛ mvomsoɛ yeɛ mayɔ ɔ? Nzikyɛ bɔne yeɛ mayɔ matia wɔ baba bɔ yiti ɔpena me ku me ye?”

english_verse: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
translation_verse: Na Yonatan buale ye kyɛ, “Nyameɛ pa gua! Ongohu wɔ. Tie, me baba nyɔ nikye fee, kyɛ piri oo, kyɛ kãa oo, bɔ ɔmmɔ me amaneɛ ɔ. Ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ bɔ me baba kɔfa sɔ dwirɛ he kɔfea me ɔ? Menne menni!”

english_verse: “Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide koso buale kyɛ, “Wɔ baba se ye pefee kyɛ ekuro me dwirɛ, yiti wayɛ ye adwene kyɛ, ‘Mengɔma Yonatan ngɔte ye nwo bie, anyɔ a ɔkɔyɛ ye yea.’ Nakoso nahorɛ nu, kyɛ AWURADE te ase ye, ná wɔ kra koso te ase ye, ewue li me mvanvando.”

english_verse: Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
translation_verse: Na Yonatan sele Dawide kyɛ, “Bɔ ekuro kyɛ meyɔ mema wɔ biala, ngɔyɔ.”

english_verse: David answered: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide buale Yonatan kyɛ, “Ɛhema yeɛ ɛsraen kofi maa yɛkɔto poen ɔ. Na sɛ Nana to poen kyɛ odidi a, ɔnzɛ kyɛ meye me nwo mefi nu. Nakoso ma me ate ma ngɔmvea eburo toonn ma odwu ye ɛlɛsa ne aso nɔsoa.

english_verse: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
translation_verse: Sɛ wɔ baba bisa me boso a, ka kyɛ, ‘Dawide srɛle me ate serɛserɛ kyɛ ɔ́bɔ hwii kɔ ye kuro Betlehem, ofikyɛ ye abusua ne amukoraa bɛ́bɔ afoɛnoa afɔleɛ wɔ berɛ.’

english_verse: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
translation_verse: Sɛ ode to nu a, ye de w’akoaa ti ngoa; nakoso sɛ ɔfɛ yaa a, ye de nwu ye kyɛ adwene tɛɛ awa ye ti anu.

english_verse: Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
translation_verse: Nwu w’akoaa anwumvoin, ofikyɛ ama w’akoaa ne wɔ bayɛ apam wɔ AWURADE dumaa nu. Sɛ medi fɔ a, ye de wɔ bɔbɔ ku me. Nzu ati yeɛ ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛfa me kɔma wɔ baba ɔ?”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
translation_verse: Na Yonatan buale kyɛ, “Sɔ dwirɛ ne ngɔto wɔ le! Sɛ mese kyɛ me baba abɔ wɔ nwo porɛ kyɛ okohu wɔ a, aso ahaa mengɔhã mengohyire wɔ?”

english_verse: “Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered. When they got there,
translation_verse: Na Yonatan buale Dawide kyɛ, “Bra ma yɛhɔ eburo dɔ.” Yiti bɛ munyɔ bɛhɔle eburo dɔ.

english_verse: Jonathan said: I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you.
translation_verse: Afei Yonatan sele Dawide kyɛ, “AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ te danzeniɛ, kyɛ ɛhema anaa ɛhema si bekye sɔa ala, sɛ menwu me baba adwene, ná wɔ nwo adwene paa wɔ ye ti anu a, aso mengɔsoma ma bɛngɔɔye wɔ asotire anaa?

english_verse: But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise. I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father.
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ me baba anya adwene kyɛ okoli wɔ awue, ná sɛ manna ye ali mangyire wɔ ma angɔ asomdwee nu a, ye de AWURADE otua me Yonatan so kerɛ piri paa. Mesrɛ kyɛ AWURADE ogyina wɔ si, kyɛbɔ ogyi me baba si ne.

english_verse: Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
translation_verse: wɔ nahorɛ abiɛngoɛfalɛ ne, nnɛyakyi ye falɛ wɔ m’abusua nu. Na sɛ AWURADE ma Dawide pɔfoɛ mɔ bɛ boso nua fi aseɛ ye aso po a, m’abusua de, nnɛyakyi ye abiɛngoɛfalɛ le.”

english_verse: Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend.
translation_verse: Yonatan mane Dawide tale ndaen bieku kyɛ okuro ye dwirɛ; ofikyɛ né Yonatan kuro Dawide dwirɛ kyɛ ye bɔbɔ ye nwo.

english_verse: After this Jonathan said: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty.
translation_verse: Na Yonatan sele ye kyɛ, “Ɛhema yeɛ ɛsraen kofi maa yɛkɔto poen ɔ, na ebiala konwu ye kyɛ ɛnne berɛ bie, ofikyɛ wɔ bia ne kɔla berɛ mbaen.

english_verse: By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock.
translation_verse: Na ye ɛlɛsa ne aso, kɔ dedeede kɔfea nekaa bɔ ɛɛfeale daa ne, ná fea Esel nyɔboɛ ne asi.

english_verse: I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock,
translation_verse: Ngɔto agyaen nza ngɔwa ye nwo berɛ, kyɛ ebiaa méto méwɔ nikyee bie ne.

english_verse: and send my servant to find the arrows. You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!”
translation_verse: Na ngɔsoma me somvoɛ abɛɛmaa ne kyɛ, ‘Kɔ, kɔpena agyaen nemɔ!’ Sɛ mekã mekyire abɛɛmaa ne kyɛ, ‘Nea, agyaen nemɔ wɔ wɔ bue faen, sesa bra’ a, ye de fite bra. Kyɛ AWURADE te ase ye, ɔte asomdwee ma wɔ, na wɔ ti ngeka.

english_verse: But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go.
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ mekã mekyire abɛɛmaa ne kyɛ, ‘Nea, agyaen nemɔ wɔ wɔ nyunu moa dɔ’ a, ye de nwati kɔ, ofikyɛ okyire kyɛ AWURADE yeɛ wama wɔ ate kyɛ ɛhɔ ɔ.

english_verse: But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
translation_verse: Na apam bɔ me ne wɔ yayɛ ne de, AWURADE te yɛ munyɔ y’afia danzeniɛ afebɔɔ.”

english_verse: So David hid there in the field. During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide ɔɔfeale eburo dɔ. Na ɛsraen ne fili ne, Nana Sɔɔlo tenane ase wɔ poentolɛ bo kyɛ odidi.

english_verse: by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty.
translation_verse: Nana Sɔɔlo tenane ye bia so mane ye si hɔle terɛ ne anwo dɔ, kyɛbɔ ɔyɔ ye daa ne. Yonatan gyinane berɛ, na Abenɛ tenane Sɔɔlo nwo berɛ; nakoso né Dawide bia ne la berɛ mbaen.

english_verse: Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo anga hwee sɔ kyẽa ne, ofikyɛ osusuli kyɛ, “Nikyee bie asi ye ate, ye nwo agua fiɛ, amba ye nwo agua fiɛ.”

english_verse: The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
translation_verse: Nakoso ɛsraen ne fili ne, ye kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ne aso, né Dawide bia ne la berɛ mbaen. Na Sɔɔlo bisale ɔwa Yonatan kyɛ, “Yese awa ne, anoma ne ɛnɛ, nzu ati yeɛ wamma poentolɛ ye abo bie ye?”

english_verse: Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
translation_verse: Ɔnwa: ‘Mesrɛ wɔ ala, ma me ate ma ngɔ, ofikyɛ m’abusua kwaabɔ afɔleɛ wɔ kuro berɛ, na nniɛma ahyɛ me kyɛ mmra berɛ bie. Yiti mesrɛ wɔ ala, ma me ate ma ngonwu nniɛma nemɔ.’ Nana, ɛhe ati yeɛ wamma wɔ poentolɛ ye abo bie ɔ.”

english_verse: Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born.
translation_verse: Afei Sɔɔlo ahone huli Yonatan so, na osele ye kyɛ, “Wɔ, brasua sanzaniɛ sɛkyefoɛ awa! Ɛnwa nzɛ menze kyɛ afa wɔ nwo abɔ Yese awa ne, bɔ ɔnate so égua wɔ ne eni nyunu ase ɔ?

english_verse: You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Yese awa ne ɔtɛte ase ye de, wɔ anaa w’ahennie ngogyina. Maa bɛɛfa ye bɛbrɛ me kekesaala ye, ofikyɛ ɔfata kyɛ beku ye ɔ.”

english_verse: “Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
translation_verse: Na Yonatan bisale ye baba kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɔsɛ kyɛ beku ye ɔ? Nzikyɛ yeɛ wayɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo tole ye pealɛɛ ne kyɛ ɔfa ku Yonatan, na ɛhe mane Yonatan nwuni ye kyɛ ye baba asua Dawide so kyɛ okohu ye.

english_verse: Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
translation_verse: Yonatan fɛle yaa hahii dwɔso fili poentolɛ ne abo. Yiti ɛsraen fili ne, ye kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ne, wanni hwee; ofikyɛ olili Dawide nwo aworabɔlɛ, yeɛ afei koso né ye baba agua ye nyunu ase.

english_verse: In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ngyerɛmɔ ne, Yonatan hɔle eburo dɔ, nekaa bɔ ɔne Dawide beli besiele kyɛ ɔɔfea ne, na ɔfale somvoɛ abɛɛmaa bie bokale ye nwo so.

english_verse: and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.” The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him.
translation_verse: Osele abɛɛmaa ne kyɛ, “Tu amirika kɔpena agyaen bɔ mebaatoto megua dɔ ne.” Abɛɛmaa ne tuli amirika bɔ ɔkɔ nen, ɔtole agyaen nemɔ maa bɛtrale ye beeguale ye nyunu moa dɔ.

english_verse: When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?”
translation_verse: Na abɛɛmaa ne dwuli nekaa bɔ Yonatan agyaen nemɔ beeguale nen, Yonatan tole abɛɛmaa ne huuu kyɛ, “Nea! Aso nna wɔ nyunu moa dɔ yeɛ agyaen nemɔ wɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: Jonathan shouted to him again, “Hurry up! Don't stop!” The boy picked up the arrows and brought them back to Jonathan,
translation_verse: Yonatan tole abɛɛmaa ne huuu bieku kyɛ, “Ka wɔ nwo, ma wɔ nwo yɛ nyera, nnɛgyina berɛ!” Yiti Yonatan abɛɛmaa ne sesale agyaen nemɔ, na osa wale ye mene nwo berɛ.

english_verse: but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.
translation_verse: Nakoso né abɛɛmaa ne nze bɔ ɔ́kɔ so ɔ. Yonatan ne Dawide ngome yeɛ né bɛse bɔ ɔ́kɔ so ɔ.

english_verse: Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
translation_verse: Yonatan fale ye akodeɛ ne mane abɛɛmaa ne, na osele ye kyɛ, “Fa kɔ awuro.”

english_verse: After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder.
translation_verse: Abɛɛmaa ne fili berɛ hɔle pɛ yeɛ Dawide fili nyɔbotaen ne asi fitele ɔ. Ɔtole ye nwo yele aseɛnwo berɛ fale ye nyunu butuli berɛ, na ɔbɔle ye ti ase pɛen nza. Bɛtotɔle bɛ nwo nu, besuni, na Dawide aworabɔlɛ deɛ bole so.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.” David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_verse: Afei Yonatan sele Dawide kyɛ, “Kɔ asomdwee nu, ɔnate kyɛ yɛ munyɔ yata ndaen wɔ AWURADE dumaa nu, kyɛ, ‘AWURADE di yɛ munyɔ y’afia adanzeɛ, yeɛ odi me bosofoɛ ne wɔ bosofoɛ koso adanzeɛ daa.’ ” Yeɛ Dawide sili nu hɔle, na Yonatan de, osa hɔle awuro.

english_verse: David went to see Ahimelech, a priest who lived in the town of Nob. Ahimelech was trembling with fear as he came out to meet David. “Why are you alone?” Ahimelech asked. “Why isn't anyone else with you?”
translation_verse: Dawide hɔle ɔsɔfo Ahimɛlɛke berɛ wɔ Nɔbo. Ahimɛlɛke fale ahunundetelɛ ooyiale ye, na obisale ye kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ wɔ ngome twe ɛnate ɔ bɔ ebiala ɔbboka wɔ so ye?”

english_verse: “I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide buale ɔsɔfo Ahimɛlɛke kyɛ, “Nana Sɔɔlo asoma me wafa adwuma bie wawura me sa, na ɔnwa: ‘Ɛsomanɛ bɔ mésoma wɔ ye, nnɛma ebiala te ye nwo bie, yeɛ nnɛma ebiala te nikyee bɔ mahyɛ wɔ kyɛ ɛɛyɔ ne!’ ” Na Dawide toale so hane kyɛ, “Me mmerandeɛ nemɔ de, me ne bɛ yahyehyɛ nekaa bie bɔ beeyia me ɔ.

english_verse: Do you have any food you can give me? Could you spare five loaves of bread?”
translation_verse: Nzikyɛ aleɛ yeɛ ele ye wɔ berɛ kekesaala ye ɔ? Ma me paanoo nnu anaa aleɛ biala bɔ ele ye wɔ berɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: “The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔfo ne buale Dawide kyɛ, “Nnne paanoo mbaen biala wɔ wa, sana paanoo krongron ne ala. Nakoso sɛ mmerandeɛ nemɔ bɛffale bɛ nwo bɛhhane mmrasua ɛlɛsa ye de a, ye de bɛkora bedi bie.”

english_verse: “Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide buale ɔsɔfo ne kyɛ, “Nahorɛ nu, mmerɛ biala bɔ ngɔhɔ koɛ ne, yɛtwe yɛ nwo yɛfi mmrasua nwo. Sɛ yɛtu atee mbaen bie po a, mmerandeɛ nemɔ bɛngɔ mmrasua nwo. Ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ bɔ ɛnɛ ye de bekogua bɛ nwo fiɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
translation_verse: Yiti ɔsɔfo ne fale paanoo krongron ne mane ye, ofikyɛ né paanoo biala nne berɛ kyɛ paanoo bɔ bɛfa begua afɔleɛ poen so ne. Né sɛ bɛye befi AWURADE nyunu a, bɛfa paanoo hyerɛ besi bɛ gya nu sɔ kyẽa ne ala.

english_verse: It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne, né Sɔɔlo somvoɛ nemɔ ko wɔ Ahimɛlɛke berɛ, ofikyɛ né ole dwumadie bie di wɔ AWURADE nyunu. Oli Dɔɔgye, ɔte Edomniɛ, na né ɔte Sɔɔlo mmoaenneafoɛ nemɔ so panyi.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide bisale Ahimɛlɛke kyɛ, “Elle pealɛɛ anaa ngrandɛ biala wɔ wa? Mamva me ngrandɛ anaa m’akodeɛ mamma, ɔnate kyɛ Nana Sɔɔlo somanɛ ne, ɔyɛle mbendene so.”

english_verse: The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.” “It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!” David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
translation_verse: Yeɛ ɔsɔfo ne buale kyɛ, “Filistiniɛ Goliate bɔ ehuni ye wɔ Ela bɔnza ne anu ne, ye ngrandɛ ne wɔ wa. Bafa ɛtena bakyekye ye nwo, na ɔla ɔsɔfo ataadeɛ ne asi dɔ. Sɛ ekuro kyɛ ɛfa a, fa, ofikyɛ ngrandɛ biala nne wa ko, sana ɛhe ala.” Na Dawide buale kyɛ, “Ngrandɛ biala ne ye nzɛ, fa ma me.” Dawide nwati kɔ Gate

english_verse: David kept on running from Saul that day until he came to Gath, where he met with King Achish.
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne, Dawide toale so nwatili fili Sɔɔlo berɛ, na ɔhɔle Gate hene Akise berɛ.

english_verse: The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing, ‘Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand’?”
translation_verse: Na Akise somvoɛ nemɔ sele ye kyɛ, “Dawide bɔ ɔte hene wɔ ye aseɛ so ne, aso nna ye ɛhe? Aso nna ye yeɛ begole abilie bɛtole dwein bɛfrɛfrɛle ye kyɛ, ‘Sɔɔlo ahu apee apee, yeɛ Dawide ahu apee buru apee buru’ ne?”

english_verse: David thought about what they were saying, and it made him afraid of Achish.
translation_verse: Dawide dwenene sɔ dwirɛ ne anwo, na ɔmaa osurole Gate hene Akise.

english_verse: So right there in front of everyone, he pretended to be insane. He acted confused and started making scratches on the doors of the town gate, while drooling in his beard.
translation_verse: Yiti ɔmane ye yɔbea sesane wɔ bɛ nyunu berɛ, na ɔhyɛle da yɛle ye nwo kyɛ bɔnamvoɛ wɔ bɛ nyunu berɛ. Anoa bɔ ɔwɔ pambim ne anu ne, odwiridwirili ye nwo, na ɔmane ye noa nzue songyili ooguale ye kanza nu.

english_verse: “Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me?
translation_verse: Na Akise sele ye somvoɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔse kyɛ akoaa he abɔ laen. Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔafa ye babrɛ me ɔ?

english_verse: I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
translation_verse: Bɔnamvoɛ yɛ me nna, bɔ yeɛ ɛmɔafa akoaa he bawa me wa, kyɛ ɔɔma ye laen ne ogyina nu wɔ me nyunu ye? Ɔyɛle sɛɛ bɔ sɔ akoaa he nyane atee wale m’awuro ɔ?”

english_verse: When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there.
translation_verse: Dawide fili Gate, na ɔnwatili ɔɔfeale nyɔboɛ bɔ wasi sua wɔ Adulam ne anu. Na oliɛma mɔ ne ye baba abusuafoɛ tele sɔ dwirɛ nen, bɛɛtoale ye wɔ berɛ.

english_verse: A lot of other people joined him too. Some were in trouble, others were angry or in debt, and David was soon the leader of
translation_verse: Na ebiala bɔ né ɔwɔ anwokyere nu, anaa ɔma kerɛ, anaa ye kunu ndwo ne, bɛboale bɛ noa bɛɛtoale ye wɔ berɛ, na ɔyɛle bɛ so safohene. Mmienzua kɔyɛ ɛyaa nna yeɛ bɛɛtoale ye ɔ.

english_verse: David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.”
translation_verse: Dawide fili berɛ hɔle Misepe bɔ ɔwɔ Moabo. Na ɔfa tole Moabo hene nyunu kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ ala, ma me baba ne me maame bɛɛtena wɔ wa kɔpem kyɛ ngonwu bɔ Nyameɛ kɔyɔ kɔma me ɔ.”

english_verse: So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
translation_verse: Ɔɔfale bɛ wale Moabo hene berɛ, na bɛtenane ye berɛ mmerɛ amukoraa bɔ né Dawide wɔ anwoserɛ afealeɛ ne anu ne.

english_verse: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest. Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
translation_verse: Na ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ Gade sele Dawide kyɛ, “Nnɛtena anwoserɛ afealeɛ ne anu; fi nu kɔ Yuda aseɛ so.” Yiti Dawide fili berɛ, na osili nu hɔle Herete ɛhɔayeɛ nu. Sɔɔlo kuku asɔfo wɔ Nɔbo

english_verse: Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him.
translation_verse: Afei Sɔɔlo tele kyɛ banwu nekaa bɔ Dawide ne mmenia bɔ bɛboka ye so ne bɛwɔ ɔ. Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Sɔɔlo te akyea ne abo, wɔ pambaa bie aso wɔ Gibea. Né otira ye pealɛɛ, yeɛ afei né ye somvoɛ mɔ begyigyi ye nwo berɛ.

english_verse: He told them: Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo sele ye somvoɛ mɔ bɔ begyigyi ye nwo berɛ ne kyɛ, “Ɛmɔ Benyaminfoɛ, ɛmɔtie! Yese awa ne, aso ɔkɔma ɛmɔ nu biala eboo anaa bobe boo? Aso ɛmɔ amukoraa, ɔkɔbɔ ɛmɔ koɛhonɛfoɛ apee apee so safohene, anaa ɛyaa ɛyaa so safohene?

english_verse: But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
translation_verse: Yiti ɛhe ati yeɛ ɛmɔ amukoraa bayɛ me nwo lɔen ye? Me kunu ba ne Yese awa bayɛ apam a, ɛmɔ nu biala ndia me gya so. Ɛmɔ nu biala ndwene me nwo, anaakyɛ ondia me gya so, kyɛ mma apesa awura me somvoɛ kyɛ ɔho tia me, kyɛ ɔtɛ me hu me, kyɛbɔ kekesaala ye ɔyɔ ye.”

english_verse: Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
translation_verse: Na Edomniɛ Dɔɔgye bɔ né ogyi Sɔɔlo somvoɛ nemɔ nwo berɛ ne, obuale kyɛ, “Nwuni Yese awa ne kyɛ ɔ́ba Ahitubo awa Ahimɛlɛke berɛ wɔ Nɔbo.

english_verse: Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
translation_verse: Obisale AWURADE berɛ dwirɛ mane ye. Ɔmane ye aleɛ bɔ okoli ye atee so ɔ, na ɔfale Filistiniɛ Goliate ngrandɛ ne mane ye.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came,
translation_verse: Afei Nana Sɔɔlo somane maa bɛɛfale Ahitubo awa ɔsɔfo Ahimɛlɛke ne ɔse abusuafoɛ amukoraa bɔ bɛte asɔfo bɔ bɛwɔ Nɔbo bɛwale, na bɛ mukoraa bɛwale Sɔɔlo berɛ.

english_verse: Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.” “Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo sele kyɛ, “Wɔ, Ahitubo awa, tie! Na obuale kyɛ, “Me mene, métie.”

english_verse: Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo bisale ye kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛne Yese awa ne bayɛ me nwo lɔen, bɔ ama ye aleɛ ne ngrandɛ, abisa Nyameɛ berɛ dwirɛ ama ye, maa ɔnate so ɔko tia me, bɔ ɔtɛ me ku me, kyɛbɔ kekesaala ye ɔyɔ ye?”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, none of your officers is more loyal than David!” Ahimelech replied. “He's your son-in-law and the captain of your bodyguard. Everyone in your family respects him.
translation_verse: Na Ahimɛlɛke buale Nana Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Wɔ somvoɛ nemɔ amukoraa, bɛ nu nwa yeɛ odi nahorɛ kyɛ Dawide ɔ? Nana, ɔte wɔ sia, otie wɔ dwirɛ, na bebu ye wɔ w’awuro berɛ.

english_verse: This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
translation_verse: Aso ɛnɛ angome yeɛ mabisa Nyameɛ berɛ dwirɛ mama ye ɔ? Daabi, nna ɛnɛ angome ɔ. Nana, ɛhe de, nnɛfa edwirɛ he susu wɔ somvoɛ, anaa me se abusuaniɛ biala. Ofikyɛ, né wɔ somvoɛ nze edwirɛ he anwo hwee, kyɛ ɔte edwirɛ piri oo, anaa kaaba bie oo.”

english_verse: “Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
translation_verse: Na Nana Sɔɔlo sele kyɛ, “Wɔ Ahimɛlɛke, ɔsɛ kyɛ beku wɔ, ɛne ɛse abusuafoɛ amukoraa.”

english_verse: Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!” But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Nana Sɔɔlo sele awɛmvoɛ bɔ begyigyi ye nwo berɛ ne kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhɔ AWURADE asɔfo nemɔ so beehuhu bɛ, ofikyɛ bɛ koso bɛwɔ Dawide bue nu. Né bɛse kyɛ wanwati, nakoso bandia me gya so.” Nakoso né Nana Sɔɔlo somvoɛ nemɔ benguro kyɛ bɛkɔfa bɛ sa bɛkɔhã AWURADE asɔfo nemɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep. Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
translation_verse: Na asɔfo nemɔ bɛ kuro Nɔbo koso, ɔfale ngrandɛ huhuni berɛ ama mukoraa: mmienzua ne mmrasua, ngwadaa ne nnɔma, nandwie, afunum ne mmoaen.

english_verse: Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David
translation_verse: Nakoso Ahitubo awa Ahimɛlɛke ɔwa bienzua ko bɔ oli Abiata ne, onyane atee nwatili, na ɔhɔle Dawide berɛ.

english_verse: and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
translation_verse: Abiata bɔle Dawide amaneɛ kyɛ Sɔɔlo ahũhũ AWURADE asɔfo nemɔ.

english_verse: David answered, “That day when I saw Doeg, I knew he would tell Saul! Your family died because of me.
translation_verse: Na Dawide sele Abiata kyɛ, “Sɔ kyẽa ne bɔ nwuni Edomniɛ Dɔɔgye wɔ berɛ ne, né mese kyɛ, kyɛ ɔkɔyɛ biala ɔkɔɔhã kohyire Sɔɔlo. Ɔnate me ti yeɛ bahu ɛse abusuafoɛ amukoraati ɔ.

english_verse: Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_verse: Maa yɛtena wa, na nnɛsuro, ofikyɛ sona bɔ ɔpena me ku me ne, wɔ koso ɔpena wɔ ku wɔ. Na ɛwɔ me wa de a, ngɔbɔ wɔ nwo waen.”

english_verse: One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
translation_verse: Nziɛ ye, bɛbɔle Dawide amaneɛ kyɛ, “Filistifoɛ afa koɛ baateta Keila kuro ne, na begu so bɛfẽ aburoo bɔ ɔwɔ nekaa bɔ bɛboro aburoo ne.”

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack these Philistines?” “Yes,” the Lord answered. “Attack them and rescue Keilah.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide bisale AWURADE kyɛ, “Me ne Filistifoɛ hemɔ yɛɛho anaa?” Yeɛ AWURADE buale Dawide kyɛ, “Ɛne bɛ bɛɛho na de Keila kuro ne.”

english_verse: But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
translation_verse: Nakoso Dawide mmenia nemɔ sele ye kyɛ, “Tie, Yuda wa po yeɛ yɛsuro ye, ná ye de yɛkɔhɔ Keila kyɛ yɛne Filisti koɛhonɛfoɛ yɛkwaaho ɔ!”

english_verse: David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
translation_verse: Dawide bisale AWURADE bieku. Na AWURADE buale ye kyɛ, “Kɔ. Kɔ Keila, na ngɔfa Filistifoɛ ngowura wɔ sa.”

english_verse: David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide ne ye mmenia nemɔ hɔle Keila, ɔne Filistifoɛ bɛhone, ohuhuni bɛ paa, na ɔfale bɛ nyɛmmoa nemɔ wale. Sɔ yeɛ Dawide yɔle lele Keilafoɛ ngoa ɔ.

english_verse: David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide tele kyɛ Sɔɔlo abɔ ye ti so porɛ nen, osele ɔsɔfo Abiata kyɛ, “Fa ɔsɔfo ataadeɛ ne bra.”

english_verse: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
translation_verse: Na Dawide hane kyɛ, “O, AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ, wɔ somvoɛ ate kyɛ Sɔɔlo pena kyɛ ɔba Keila, kyɛ ɔnate me ti ɔbaabɔ kuro ne.

english_verse: Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.” “Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Aso Keilafoɛ kɔfa me kowura ye sa anaa? Sɔɔlo kɔwa kyɛbɔ wɔ somvoɛ ate ne ala anaa? O, AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ, mesrɛ wɔ ala, ka kyire wɔ somvoɛ.” Na AWURADE buale kyɛ, “Yoo, ɔkɔwa.”

english_verse: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide bisale kyɛ, “Aso Keilafoɛ kɔfa me ne me mmenia nemɔ bekowura Sɔɔlo sa anaa?” Na AWURADE buale kyɛ, “Yoo, bɛkɔye ɛmɔ bɛkɔma ye.”

english_verse: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
translation_verse: Dawide tenane ɛserɛ so anwoserɛ afealeɛ nemɔ anu, wɔ mmokaa aseɛ bɔ ɔwɔ Sife ɛserɛ ne aso. Sɔɔlo hɔle so penane ye mmerɛ biala, nakoso Nyameɛ amva ye wanwura ye sa.

english_verse: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
translation_verse: Né Dawide wɔ Sife ɛserɛ so nekaa bie bɔ bɛfrɛ berɛ Horese, na ɔtele kyɛ Sɔɔlo asi nu kyɛ ɔbaapena ye ku ye.

english_verse: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sɔɔlo awa Yonatan sili nu hɔle Dawide berɛ wɔ Horese, na ɔkyekyele Dawide wora kyɛ Nyameɛ kɔbɔ ye nwo waen.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
translation_verse: Ɔha hyirele ye kyɛ, “Nnɛsuro, ofikyɛ me baba Sɔɔlo ye sa ngɔhã wɔ. Ekoli Yisrael so hene, bɔ yeɛ ɛnne berɛ a, me yeɛ nwɔ berɛ ɔ; na me baba Sɔɔlo se ye sɔ.”

english_verse: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul
translation_verse: Afei bɛ munyɔ bɛyɛle apam wɔ AWURADE nyunu. Dawide tenane Horese berɛ, yeɛ Yonatan koso osa hɔle ye awuro.

english_verse: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
translation_verse: Na Sifefoɛ hɔle Sɔɔlo berɛ wɔ Gibea bɛɛbɔle ye amaneɛ kyɛ, “Dawide aafea yɛ berɛ wɔ anwoserɛ afealeɛ bɔ ɔwɔ Horese ne anu, wɔ Hakila pambaa bɔ ɔwɔ Yesimɔn ngwaen dɔ ne aso.

english_verse: Saul told them: You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo buale kyɛ, “AWURADE yira ɛmɔ kyɛ ɛmɔanwu me anwumvoin ɔ!

english_verse: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔhɔ bɛɛneanea nu yé bieku, ná ɛ́mɔpena nekaa pɔtee bɔ ɔwɔ ɔ, ɔne sona bɔ ye nye apɛ ye so wɔ berɛ ɔ, ofikyɛ mate kyɛ ɔte sona bɔ ye nwo yɛ ndono ɔ.

english_verse: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔɔpena benwu ye afealeɛ ne amukoraa, ná ɛ́mɔfa ye nwo amaneɛ pɔtee bɛɛbɔ me. Ɔba ye sɔ a, me ne ɛmɔ yɛkɔhɔ. Na sɛ ɔwɔ mbɔtam berɛ angome de a, ye de ngɔpena ye wɔ Yuda mmusua amukoraa nu.”

english_verse: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
translation_verse: Yiti Sifefoɛ nemɔ lili Sɔɔlo nyunu moa bɛhɔle Sife. Né Dawide ne ye mmenia nemɔ bɛwɔ Mayɔn ɛserɛ bɔ ɔwɔ aseɛ frɛtɛɛ, bɔ ɔwɔ Yesimɔn ngwaen dɔ ne aso.

english_verse: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo ne ye mmenia sili nu hɔle kyɛ bɛkwaapena Dawide. Ebie bɔle Dawide amaneɛ, na ɔtorotorole hɔle nyɔbotaen nemɔ anu dɔ ɔɔtenane Mayɔn ɛserɛ ne aso. Sɔɔlo tele sɔ dwirɛ nen, ɔpole Dawide so hɔle Mayɔn ɛserɛ ne aso.

english_verse: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
translation_verse: Né Sɔɔlo nate bokaa ne bue ko, yeɛ né Dawide ne ye mmenia koso bɛnate bokaa ne bue ko. Dawide mane ye nwo yɛle nyera kyɛ ɔkɔnwati bɔ Sɔɔlo ngonwu ye ɔ. Nakoso Sɔɔlo ne ye mmenia nemɔ, né bɛpena kyɛ bɛpɛ Dawide ne ye mmenia nemɔ nwo beyia bɛkye bɛ.

english_verse: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
translation_verse: Na sɔ mmerɛ ne ala, ɛbɔfoɛ bie wale Sɔɔlo berɛ oosele ye kyɛ, “Sa bra ndɛndɛ, ofikyɛ Filistifoɛ bawa baabɔ aseɛ ne aso apaa.”

english_verse: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
translation_verse: Yiti Sɔɔlo yakyili Dawide foalɛ, na ɔne Filistifoɛ bɛɛhone. Yiti bɛfrɛle nekaa bɔ ɔyakyili Dawide foalɛ ne Ɛnwatilɛ Nyɔbotaen.

english_verse: David left and went to live in the hideouts at En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Afei Dawide fili berɛ, na ɔhɔle Ɛn Gedi ɔɔtenane anwoserɛ afealeɛ nemɔ anu.

english_verse: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo ne Filistifoɛ bɛɛhone koɛ, na osa wale ne, bɛbɔle ye amaneɛ kyɛ, “Dawide wɔ Ɛn Gedi ɛserɛ ne aso.”

english_verse: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo oodwuli mmoaennduin biemɔ anwo wɔ atee ne noa. Né nyɔboɛ bie asi sua wɔ berɛ, na owurale nu kyɛ ɔkɔ bakaa so. Nyɔbotaen bɔ wasi sua ne, né Dawide ne ye mmenia nemɔ baawurawura ye kunu dɔ paa.

english_verse: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
translation_verse: Na Dawide mmenia nemɔ sele ye kyɛ, “Ɛnɛ kyẽa ye yeɛ AWURADE hane ye nwo dwirɛ hyirele wɔ kyɛ, ‘Ngɔfa wɔ pɔfoɛ ngowura wɔ sa maa ɛkɔfa bɔ ekuro biala kɔyɛ ye.’ ” Na Dawide yɛle kudɛɛ ɔɔpɛle Sɔɔlo ataadeɛ tendenn ne noa.

english_verse: Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that,
translation_verse: Na ɛhe asi ne, Dawide tiboa buale ye fɔ, kyɛ wapɛ Sɔɔlo ataadeɛ tendenn ne noa ɔ.

english_verse: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide hwili ye mmenia nemɔ nyunu, na wamma bɛ ate ma banyɔ Sɔɔlo nikyee fee. Afei Sɔɔlo dwɔsole, na ofili nyɔboɛ bɔ wasi sua ne anu sili nu kyɛ ɔkɔ.

english_verse: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
translation_verse: Ye si ye, Dawide koso fili nyɔboɛ bɔ wasi sua ne anu fitele, na ɔtole Sɔɔlo huuu kyɛ, “Nana, me mene ee!” Sɔɔlo pɛle ye nye neane nziɛ, na Dawide fale ye nyunu butuli berɛ anidie nu.

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
translation_verse: Na Dawide sele Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Bɛ bɔ bɛkeka kyɛ, ‘Dawide pena wɔ ku wɔ’ ne, nzu ati yeɛ etie bɛ dwirɛ ye?

english_verse: You can see for yourself that the Lord gave me the chance to catch you in the cave today. Some of my men wanted to kill you, but I wouldn't let them do it. I told them, “I will not harm the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Tie, ɛnɛ kyẽa ye, wɔ nye tua kyɛbɔ AWURADE fale wɔ wurale me sa, wɔ nyɔboɛ bɔ wasi sua ne anu ɔ. Ebiemɔ sele me kyɛ ngu wɔ, nakoso mamaa anya wɔ ti adidi nu. Na ngane kyɛ, ‘Mengɔfa me sa ngɔhã me mene, ofikyɛ AWURADE apopa ye ngoo.’

english_verse: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
translation_verse: Oo me baba, nea kyɛ ndira w’ataadeɛ tendenn ne noa ɔ. Sɛ mapɛ w’ataadeɛ tendenn ne noa, ná mangu wɔ a, ye de odi kyɛ ɛte ye bo kyɛ, wɔ nwo adwene tɛɛ biala nne me ti anu, anaa nnyɔle wɔ nwo lɔen. Nnyɔle wɔ bɔne biala, nakoso ɛpena me ku me.

english_verse: I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you.
translation_verse: Me ne wɔ yɛ munyɔ, AWURADE yeɛ okohyire bɔ odi fɔ ɔ! AWURADE yeɛ ɔkɔtɔ wɔ so wereɛ kɔma me ɔ. Nakoso me de, mengɔfa me sa ngɔhã wɔ.

english_verse: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
translation_verse: Na mbanyi mɔ bu anyandera kyɛ, ‘Sona bɔ ɔtte mayee ne, ye yɔleɛ koso ɔtte mayee.’ Nakoso me de, mengɔfa me sa ngɔhã wɔ.
