english_verse: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
translation_verse: Nwa koraa yeɛ Yisrael hene kyini pena ye ku ye ye? Nwa yeɛ ɛfoa ye ye? Aso nna kyea fuin yeɛ ɛfoa ye ɔ? Aso nna sosoa ko yeɛ ɛfoa ye ye?

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will help me escape and show that I am in the right.
translation_verse: AWURADE te ndɛenbualɛniɛ, na yɛ nu ko bɔ odi fɔ ne, okobua ye fɔ. Mesrɛ kyɛ ɔneanea nu, oli me dwirɛ ma me, ná ole me fi wɔ sa nu.”

english_verse: “David, my son—is that you?” Saul asked. Then he started crying
translation_verse: Dawide hane sɔ dwirɛ ne hyirele Sɔɔlo yiele nen, Sɔɔlo sele kyɛ, “Mma Dawide, wɔ yeɛ edwudwo ye?” Na Sɔɔlo suni hahii.

english_verse: and said: David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you.
translation_verse: Na osele Dawide kyɛ, “Ɛtengyɛ tra me; ofikyɛ paa ala yeɛ ayɛ me ɔ, nakoso me de, bɔne yeɛ mafa matua wɔ kerɛ ɔ.

english_verse: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
translation_verse: Ɛnɛ amaa manwu kyɛbɔ asi alo me ɔ, ofikyɛ mmerɛ bɔ AWURADE fale me wurale wɔ sa ne, angu me.

english_verse: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
translation_verse: Nwa yeɛ ɔkɔto ye pɔfoɛ a, ɔmaa ɔfa ye nwo di tɔtorɔtɔɔ ɔkɔ ɔ? Paa bɔ afa ayɛ me ɛnɛ ye, mesrɛ kyɛ AWURADE ɔma wɔ ye nwo akatuaa paa.

english_verse: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
translation_verse: Afei de, mese kyɛ ekoli hene amba, na Yisrael ahennie ne, wɔ sa nu yeɛ ye bo kotimu ɔ.

english_verse: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
translation_verse: Fa AWURADE ta ndaen kyire me, kyɛ me boso ama mɔ, engonua bɛ boso, kyɛ ɛngɔkyikyi me dumaa ngofi me se awuro.”

english_verse: So David promised, and Saul went home. David and his men returned to their hideout.
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide tale sɔ ndaen ne hyirele Sɔɔlo. Afei Sɔɔlo sili nu hɔle awuro, na Dawide ne ye mmenia nemɔ koso bɛfo bɛhɔle anwoserɛ afealeɛ ne anu.

english_verse: One day, Nabal was in Carmel where his servants were cutting the wool from his sheep. David was in the desert when he heard about it.
translation_verse: Dawide tele ye wɔ ɛserɛ ne aso kyɛ Nabal gu so ɔpepɛ ye mmoaen nwo nwiaa.

english_verse: So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal: I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔhã behyire ye bɛma me kyɛ, ‘Asomdwee ha wɔ, asomdwee ha w’awuro ama, asomdwee ha bɔ ele ye amukoraati.

english_verse: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
translation_verse: Mate kyɛ wɔ mmenia nemɔ begu so bɛpepɛ wɔ mmoaen nemɔ nwo nwiaa. Na mmerɛ bɔ né wɔ mmoaenneafoɛ nemɔ bɛwɔ yɛ wa ne, yanyɔ bɛ tɛɛ biala, yeɛ bɛ nikye fee wammini wɔ mmerɛ bɔ né bɛwɔ Kamɛl ne.

english_verse: Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing. My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
translation_verse: Wɔ de, bisa wɔ mmerandeɛ nemɔ, na bɛkɔhã bekohyire wɔ. Yiti de me mmerandeɛ nemɔ nyemene so, ofikyɛ ɛnɛ bɔ yawa ye, ɔte anigye kyẽa. Yɛsrɛ wɔ ala, nikyee biala bɔ wɔ sa kɔsõ so ne, fa ma wɔ ngoaa ne ɛwa Dawide.’ ”

english_verse: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
translation_verse: Dawide mmerandeɛ nemɔ hɔle ne, bɛhane Dawide ngraa ne amukoraa behyirele Nabal, na bɛnwondɛle.

english_verse: This is what he said: Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days.
translation_verse: Nakoso Nabal buale Dawide somvoɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “Nwa ole sɔ Dawide ne? Nwa ole sɔ Yese awa ne? Ngoaa mɔ bɔ ɛlɛsa ye bɛnwati befi bɛ mene mɔ nwo ne, bɛsone pee.

english_verse: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
translation_verse: Mmenia bɔ bɛ́pepɛ me mmoaen nwo nwiaa ne, m’aleɛ ne me nzue bɔ mefa mema bɛ, ɔne me naen bɔ mahu ye mama bɛ ne, me yeɛ mva ma mmenia bɔ menze nekaa bɔ befi ɔ?”

english_verse: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide mmerandeɛ nemɔ sale bɛ si bɛhɔle, na bɛfale mmuayɛɛ ne amukoraa bɛbɔle Dawide amaneɛ.

english_verse: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
translation_verse: Yiti tie ná dwene bɔ ɛkɔyɔ ɔ nwo, ofikyɛ babɔ yɛ mene ne ye awuro ama mukoraa nwo porɛ. Na ɔnate ye suban bɔ ɔtte mayee ne ati, ebie ngora ndu ye foɛ.”

english_verse: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
translation_verse: Na Abigail sele ye mmerandeɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔli me nyunu moa bɛhɔ, na me koso médi ɛmɔ si méba.” Nakoso wammɔ ohu Nabal amaneɛ.

english_verse: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
translation_verse: Né ɔte afunum ne aso ɔkɔ. Na oodwuli bokaa ne nye abo nen, né Dawide ne ye mmenia nemɔ koso bɛ́torotoro bokaa ne bɔ bɛ nye kyire ye dɔ ɔ, na Abigail ne bɛ yiale.

english_verse: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
translation_verse: Né Dawide ali moa waha kyɛ, “Sɔ akoaa he, mabɔ ye nningyein amukoraa nwo waen mbaen wɔ ɛserɛ so, bɔ mamva ye nikyee fee ɔ. Nakoso bɔne yeɛ wafa watua me kerɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
translation_verse: Kyɛ odwu ɛhema ngyerɛmɔ ne, sɛ mema ye nwo ama bienzua ko po nya ye ti didi nu a, Nyameɛ tua me Dawide kerɛ maa ɔbo so.”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Abigail nwuni Dawide nen, ofili afunum ne aso dwuli ase ndɛndɛ, ɔbɔle ye nu ase, na ɔfale ye nyunu butuli ase wɔ Dawide nyunu.

english_verse: Don't pay any attention to that good-for-nothing Nabal. His name means “fool,” and it really fits him! I didn't see the men you sent,
translation_verse: Me mene, sɔ Nabal he bɔ ye suban ɔtte mayee he, nnɛfa ye dwirɛ yɛ dwirɛ; ofikyɛ ye suban te kyɛ ye dumaa ne ala. Ye dumaa li Egyiminɛ, na egyiminɛ bata ye. Nakoso me mene, w’afaneɛ de, wɔ mmerandeɛ bɔ ɛsomane bɛ ne, mannwu bɛ.

english_verse: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
translation_verse: Mesrɛ wɔ ala, fa w’afaneɛ mvomsoɛ kyɛ ye. AWURADE kɔma me mene ne ye boso ama bekoli hene afebɔɔ amba, ofikyɛ AWURADE koɛ yeɛ me mene ɔko ɔ. Na edwirɛ tɛɛ biala ngɔto wɔ wɔ mmerɛ biala bɔ ɛte ase ɔ.

english_verse: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
translation_verse: Me mene, sɛ ebie yɛ kyɛ ɔfoa wɔ pena wɔ ku wɔ a, ye de AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ kɔbɔ wɔ ngoa nwo waen maa ɛkɔboka ateasefoɛ so. Nakoso wɔ pɔfoɛ mɔ bɛ ngoa de, okofindi bɛ kogua kyɛbɔ bɛfa taya befindi nyɔboɛ ne ala.

english_verse: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
translation_verse: Paa mukoraa bɔ AWURADE aha afa me mene nwo ne, sɛ ɔmaa ɔba nu, ná ɔmaa edi Yisrael so hene a,

english_verse: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
translation_verse: ye de me mene ngonu ye nwo, anaa ye tiboa ngobua ye fɔ, kyɛ aha mogya agua mbaen, anaakyɛ wɔ bɔbɔ atɔ mmenia so wereɛ ɔ. Me mene, sɛ AWURADE maa oyie wɔ yé a, ye de kaye w’afaneɛ.”

english_verse: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
translation_verse: Na Dawide sele Abigail kyɛ, “Animnyam hã AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ bɔ ɔsomane wɔ maa eeyiale me ɛnɛ ɔ!

english_verse: And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people.
translation_verse: Adwene paa bɔ anya ye ne, Nyameɛ yira so, na oyira wɔ, kyɛ ɛnɛ amma manga mogya mangua manni ye nwo fɔ, kyɛ amma me bɔbɔ mandɔ mmenia so wereɛ ɔ.

english_verse: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
translation_verse: Na AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ bɔ wamma mamva edwirɛ tɛɛ manni wɔ ne, meta ye ndaen kyɛ, sɛ anga wɔ nwo ammanyia me a, ahaa kyɛ odwu ɛhema ngyerɛmɔ ne, né Nabal nwoniɛ bienzua ko po nne berɛ bɔ okonya ye ti kodidi nu ɔ.”

english_verse: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
translation_verse: Afei Dawide lele nningyein bɔ Abigail fa brɛle ye ne, na osele Abigail kyɛ, “Kɔ w’awuro asomdwee nu. Tie, bɔ aha ne, mate, na mapene edwirɛ bɔ afa ato me nyunu ne aso.”

english_verse: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
translation_verse: Na Abigail sa hɔle awuro wɔ Nabal berɛ ne, né Nabal ato poen wɔ ye awuro berɛ kyɛ ahemvo poentolɛ. Né ɔgye ye nye, ofikyɛ né wabo sram; yiti Abigail anga hwee wangyire ye kɔpem kyɛ aleɛ hyene ɔ.

english_verse: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene bɔ nzaa ne tetele Nabal nye so ne, ɔye hane edwirɛ ne amukoraa hyirele ye, na ye ahone bɔle ye palipali mane ye nwo yɛle ye hodwoo kyɛ wawu ne.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Na ngyẽa kɔyɛ eleburu asi ne, AWURADE huni Nabal.

english_verse: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
translation_verse: Na berɛ ne ala, ɔbɔle ye ti ase kotole, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Me mene, wɔ somvoɛ te afaneɛ bɔ wasiesie ye nwo kyɛ okonwunzi wɔ somvoɛ mɔ bɛ gya bo ɔ.”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
translation_verse: Na Abigail yɛle ndɛndɛ fo tenane afunum so hɔle. Ye abaawa mɔ nnu lili ye si, na olili Dawide bɔfoɛ nemɔ si ɔne bɛ hɔle ɔɔyɛle ɔye.

english_verse: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
translation_verse: Né Dawide agya Ahinoam koso bɔ ofi Yesreel, na bɛ munyɔ bɛyɛle ɔye mɔ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_verse: Né Sɔɔlo afa ɔwa Mikal, bɔ ɔte Dawide aye ne, wama Layise awa Palti bɔ ofi Galim ne maa wagya.

english_verse: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
translation_verse: Afei Sifefoɛ wale Sɔɔlo berɛ wɔ Gibea bɛɛhane kyɛ, “Dawide aafea Hakila bokaa bɔ ɔwɔ Yesimɔn ndendeneɛ so ne aso.”

english_verse: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo kyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ Hakila bokaa bɔ ɔwɔ Yesimɔn ndendeneɛ so ne aso, wɔ atee ne anoa. Nakoso Dawide de, ɔhale ɛserɛ ne aso, na ɔtele kyɛ Sɔɔlo awa kyɛ ɔbaapena ye ku ye.

english_verse: he sent some spies to find out if it was true.
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide somane mmenia maa bɛɛtetɛle, na benwuni kyɛ Sɔɔlo awa berɛ amba.

english_verse: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
translation_verse: Afei Dawide sili nu hɔle nekaa bɔ né Sɔɔlo akyekye asikyeleɛ ne. Onwuni nekaa bɔ Sɔɔlo ne ye safohene Abenɛ, bɔ ɔte Nɛɛ awa ne bɛla ɔ. Né Sɔɔlo alafe wɔ asikyeleɛ ne afia, bɔ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bapɛ ye nwo bayia ɔ.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?” “I will!” Abishai answered.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide bisale Hitiniɛ Ahimɛlɛke, ɔne Yoabo aliɛma Abisae bɔ oni ole Seruya ne kyɛ, “Nwa yeɛ ɔne me kɔhɔ Sɔɔlo nwo dɔ wɔ asikyeleɛ ne anu ɔ?” Na Abisae buale kyɛ, “Me ne wɔ kɔhɔ.”

english_verse: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide ne Abisae bɛhɔle koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ anwo dɔ kɔngɔen. Benwuni kyɛ Sɔɔlo alafe wɔ asikyeleɛ ne afia berɛ, bɔ ye pealɛɛ ne pena ye ti sorɔ ɔ. Né Abenɛ ne koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ koso balafe bapɛ ye nwo bayia.

english_verse: Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
translation_verse: Na Abisae sele Dawide kyɛ, “Nyameɛ afa wɔ pɔfoɛ wawura wɔ sa ɛnɛ, yiti maa mva pealɛɛ ne nwɔ ye komapɛ twe ma ɔha aseɛnwo berɛ; mengɔwɔ ye nyɔ koraa.”

english_verse: “Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king.
translation_verse: Nakoso Dawide sele Abisae kyɛ, “Nnɛku ye! Nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora kɔfa ye sa kɔha sona bɔ AWURADE apopa ye ngoo, bɔ ongoli fɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide toale so sele kyɛ, “Kyɛ AWURADE te ase ye, AWURADE yeɛ okohu ye ɔ. Sɛ wanwu ye Ɛdangama wue a, bekohu ye wɔ koɛ nu.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
translation_verse: AWURADE pa gua kyɛ ngɔfa me sa ngɔhã sona bɔ AWURADE apopa ye ngoo ɔ. Nakoso tu pealɛɛ bɔ ɔpena ye ti sorɔ berɛ ne, ná fa nzue ngomvo ne boka so ma yɛhɔ.”

english_verse: David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide fale pealɛɛ bɔ ɔpena Sɔɔlo ti sorɔ berɛ ne, ɔne nzue ngomvo ne, na besili nu bɛhɔle. Ebiala nye ambɛ so, anaa ebiala ande, yeɛ ebiala andingye. Né bɛ mukoraa balafe, ofikyɛ né AWURADE ama nnafelɛ hatee atɔ bɛ so.

english_verse: David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance.
translation_verse: Afei Dawide trale bɔnza ne hɔle ye si dɔ, na oogyinane bokaa ne ti afia wɔ dedeede. Né ɔne nekaa bɔ Sɔɔlo wɔ ne, nu twe.

english_verse: “Abner!” David shouted toward Saul's army. “Can you hear me?” Abner shouted back. “Who dares disturb the king?”
translation_verse: Na Dawide tole koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ ne Nɛɛ awa Abenɛ huuu kyɛ, “Abenɛ ee! Engosuro hɔ ɔ?” Yeɛ Abenɛ teane nu bisale kyɛ, “Wɔ nwa ɛne, bɔ ɛ́to Nana Sɔɔlo huuu ne?”

english_verse: “Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight.
translation_verse: Na Dawide buale Abenɛ kyɛ, “Saa ɛtte bienzua! Nwa yeɛ ɔne wɔ bɛte pɛ wɔ Yisrael ɔ? Nzu ati yeɛ ammɔ wɔ mene Nana Sɔɔlo nwo waen ɔ? Koɛhonɛfoɛ ne, ko wale asikyeleɛ ne anu kyɛ ahaa ɔbaahu wɔ mene Nana Sɔɔlo.

english_verse: You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
translation_verse: Sɔ nikyee he bɔ ayɔ ye, ɔtte mayee. Na kyɛ AWURADE te ase ye, odi kyɛ beku ɛmɔ, ofikyɛ ɛmɔammɔ ɛmɔ mene bɔ AWURADE apopa ye ngoo ne nwo waen. Nea, Nana Sɔɔlo pealɛɛ ne, ɔne nzue ngomvo bɔ ogyi ye ti sorɔ berɛ ne, bɛwɔ nisua?”

english_verse: Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?” “Yes it is, Your Majesty.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo tele kyɛ Dawide komvi ɔ, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Mma Dawide, wɔ yeɛ édwudwo ye anaa?” Na Dawide buale kyɛ, “Me mene, Nana Sɔɔlo, me yeɛ médwudwo ye.”

english_verse: Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime?
translation_verse: Na Dawide fa sɔle so kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ me mene ɔfoa ye somvoɛ ɔ? Mayɔ nzu? Bɔne beni yeɛ mayɔ ɔ?

english_verse: Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods.
translation_verse: Nana, me mene, tie wɔ somvoɛ noa dwirɛ. Sɛ AWURADE yeɛ wamaa atu me anyeɛ a, ye de mesrɛ kyɛ ole afɔleɛ ná ɔyakyi. Nakoso sɛ kuro mmenia ahɔ de a, ye de AWURADE tua bɛ kerɛ, ofikyɛ ɛnɛ bafoa me bafi AWURADE agyapadeɛ ne anwo bɔ mengonya bie ɔ. Na bɛnwa: ‘Kɔso nyameɛ foforɛ biemɔ.’

english_verse: Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
translation_verse: Yiti aseɛ bɔ so ama nze AWURADE ne, nnɛkã me mogya gua wɔ so. Sosoa komapɛ yeɛ Yisrael hene asi nu wawa kyɛ ɔbaahye ye ɔ, kyɛbɔ sona foa akɔkɔhwereɛ wɔ mmokaa so ɔ.”

english_verse: “David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sɔɔlo sele kyɛ, “Mayɔ bɔne, mma Dawide, sa bra, na mengotu me nye ngosie wɔ so ko, ofikyɛ ɛnɛ ahyire kyɛ me ngoa nwo hia wɔ. Mali ngwaseasɛm, na mali edwirɛ tɛɛ piri paa.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it.
translation_verse: Na Dawide buale kyɛ, “Nana, wɔ pealɛɛ ne ɛhe. Ma wɔ mmerandeɛ nemɔ ko bra ɔɔfa.

english_verse: The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right.
translation_verse: Sona biala ye tengyɛlɛ ne ye nahorɛlilɛ, yeɛ AWURADE gyina so ɔma ye nwo akatuaa ɔ. AWURADE fale wɔ wurale me sa ɛnɛ kyẽa ye, nakoso né menguro kyɛ ngɔfa me sa ngɔhã sona bɔ AWURADE apopa ye ngoo ne ɔ.

english_verse: I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
translation_verse: Na kyɛbɔ mama wɔ ngoa nwo ahia me ɛnɛ ne, sɔ ala yeɛ mesrɛ AWURADE kyɛ, ɔ́ma me ngoa nwo hia ye, ná ole me fi amaneɛ mukoraati nu ɔ.”

english_verse: “David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!” David in Philistia Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo buale Dawide kyɛ, “Nyameɛ yira wɔ, mma Dawide. Ɛkɔyɔ nningyein pee, na ekoli nu ngonim.” Afei Dawide sili nu hɔle, na Sɔɔlo koso sa hɔle ye awuro.

english_verse: but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
translation_verse: Dawide hane ye wɔ ye ti anu kyɛ, “Annea a, ɛlɛho Sɔɔlo konya me kohũ me. Bɔ ɔsɛ kyɛ meyɔ ala ole kyɛ ngɔnwati ngɔhɔ Filistifoɛ aseɛ so. Ɔba ye sɔ a, Sɔɔlo kɔpa aba, bɔ ɔngɔpena me ko wɔ Yisrael aseɛ so ɔ, na ngɔnwati ngofi ye sa nu.”

english_verse: When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo tele kyɛ Dawide anwati wahɔ Gate nen, ɔyakyili ye penalɛ.

english_verse: One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide sele Akise kyɛ, “Sɛ anya alo me de a, ye de maa bɛma me nekaa wɔ nguraa nemɔ ko aso ma ngɔndena dɔ. Nzu ati yeɛ ɔsɛ kyɛ w’akoaa ne wɔ bɛtena ahenguro wa ɔ?”

english_verse: Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
translation_verse: Na sɔ kyẽa ne ala, Akise fale akuraa bɔ oli Siklage mane ye. Na ɔnate sɔ ati, Siklage ɔɔyɛle Yuda ahemvo mɔ deɛ maa waadwu ɛnɛ.

english_verse: David was in Philistia for a year and four months.
translation_verse: Dawide lili afoɛ ko ne bosome nna wɔ Filistifoɛ maen ne anu.

english_verse: The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns.
translation_verse: Dawide ne ye mmenia nemɔ beetuale Gesurefoɛ, Gisifoɛ ne Amalɛkefoɛ, ofikyɛ Sure atee ne aso bɔ ɛfa kɔ Misraim aseɛ so ne, sɔ mmenia nemɔ yeɛ né ofi tetetete bɛte berɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there. After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish,
translation_verse: Sɛ né Dawide fa koɛ kɔtoa mbɔtam bie a, okũkũ berɛ ama, na ɔmma bienzua anaa brasua ko po nnya ye ti nnidi nu. Nakoso berɛ mmoaen, nandwie, afunum, afupɔngɔ ne ndaadeɛ mɔ de, né ɔsesa, na osa ba nekaa bɔ Akise wɔ ne.

english_verse: who would ask, “Where did you attack today?” David would answer, “Oh, we attacked some desert town that belonged to the Judah tribe.” Sometimes David would say, “Oh, we attacked a town in the desert where the Jerahmeel clan lives” or “We attacked a town in the desert where the Kenites live.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ Akise bisa ye kyɛ, “Nisua yeɛ ɛmɔahɔ baabɔ apaa ɛnɛ ye” a, ɔyɛ a Dawide bua ye kyɛ, “Yɛɛbɔle apaa ne wɔ Yuda aseɛ ne ngwaen dɔ”, anaa “Yerameelfoɛ aseɛ ne ngwaen dɔ”, anaa “Kenifoɛ aseɛ ne ngwaen dɔ.”

english_verse: That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.” David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia.
translation_verse: Dawide anyakyi bienzua anaa brasua ko po ma wannya ye ti wannidi nu, kyɛ ɔ́fa ye ba Gate, ofikyɛ osusuli kyɛ, “Annea a, né baahã yɛ nwo dwirɛ kyɛ, ‘Bra bɔ Dawide abɔ hɔ ɛhe.’ ” Mmerɛ bɔ Dawide lili ye wɔ Filistifoɛ aseɛ so ne amukoraa, sɔ nikyee ne yeɛ ɔyɔle ɔ.

english_verse: But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
translation_verse: Akise lele Dawide lili, na Akise dwenene kyɛ, “Wama ye nwo ayɛ ye bɔbɔ ye mmenia Yisraelfoɛ ahi paa, yiti ɔkɔyɛ me somvoɛ daa.”

english_verse: The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa.
translation_verse: Filistifoɛ boaboale bɛ noa, na bɛɛkyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ Sunem. Sɔɔlo boaboale Yisrael ɛlɔen ne amukoraa noa, na bɛkyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ Gilboa.

english_verse: Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Sɔɔlo nwuni Filisti koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ nen, ɛserɛ hane ye, na ɔbɔle fuin.

english_verse: So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo bisale AWURADE, nakoso laleɛ nu oo, Yurim so oo, anaa ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ so oo, AWURADE andɛ ye so.

english_verse: Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.” His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Afei Sɔɔlo sele ye somvoɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔɔpena brasua nzamangɔmhyɛlɛniɛ bɛma me maa ngɔ ye berɛ abisa.” Na ye somvoɛ nemɔ buale ye kyɛ, “Nzamangɔmhyɛlɛniɛ bie wɔ Ɛndɔɔ.”

english_verse: That night, Saul put on different clothing so nobody would recognize him. Then he and two of his men went to the woman, and asked, “Will you bring up the ghost of someone for us?”
translation_verse: Yiti Sɔɔlo sakyerale ye nwo, owurale ndaadeɛ mbaen biemɔ, na osili nu ɔne mmenia nyɔ bɛhɔle berɛ. Beedwuli braa ne berɛ kɔngɔen. Na osele braa ne kyɛ, “Fa ngɔndwemahwenɛ so kɔ abisa ma me, na frɛ bɔ ngɔbɔ ye dumaa ngohyire wɔ ne fi ɛborɔ dɔ ma me.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
translation_verse: Na braa ne buale ye kyɛ, “Wɔ bɔbɔ ɛse bɔ Sɔɔlo ayɔ ɔ, kyɛ watu nzamangɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ ne musueyelɛfoɛ wafi aseɛ ye aso. Nzu ati yeɛ ɛpena kyɛ esua me ngaen maa beku me ee?”

english_verse: Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Sɔɔlo fale AWURADE tale ndaen hyirele ye kyɛ, “Kyɛ AWURADE te ase ye, engonya ɛhe anwo asohwenɛ biala.”

english_verse: “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked. “Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
translation_verse: Yeɛ braa ne bisale ye kyɛ, “Nwa yeɛ mvrɛ ye mvi ɛborɔ dɔ mmrɛ wɔ ɔ?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Frɛ Samuel fi dɔ ma me.”

english_verse: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
translation_verse: Na braa ne nwuni Samuel nen, braa ne teane nu serɛserɛ sele Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ alakalaka me ee? Wɔ ole Sɔɔlo!”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.” She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
translation_verse: Na Nana Sɔɔlo sele ye kyɛ, “Nnɛsuro, nzikyɛ yeɛ enwu ye ɔ?” Na braa ne buale Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Menwu sunzum bie kyɛ ofi aseɛ bo dɔ ofite ba.”

english_verse: “What does it look like?” “It looks like an old man wearing a robe.” Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo bisale braa ne kyɛ, “Ye sue te sɛɛ?” Obuale kyɛ, “Biaa aworowaa bie yeɛ ófite ba ɔ, na owura ataadeɛ tendenn bie.” Yiti Sɔɔlo nwuni kyɛ Samuel ɔ, na Sɔɔlo fale ye nyunu butuli ase kotole ye.

english_verse: “Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked. “I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
translation_verse: Afei Samuel bisale Sɔɔlo kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ agyegye me amaa mafi ɛborɔ dɔ mawa ɔ”? Na Sɔɔlo buale kyɛ, “Edwirɛ piri paa ato me, ofikyɛ Filistifoɛ afa koɛ batoa me. Nakoso Nyameɛ ayakyi me nu, na ɔmva ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ so anaa laleɛ nu mmua me ko. Yiti yeɛ mafrɛ wɔ kyɛ eehyire me bɔ nyɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel said: If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do.
translation_verse: Na Samuel bisale kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ebisa me bɔ odi kyɛ ɛyɔ ɔ, wɔ aberɛ bɔ ɛse kyɛ AWURADE ayakyi wɔ nu, ná wayɛ wɔ pɔfoɛ ɔ?

english_verse: I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing!
translation_verse: Bɔ AWURADE nate me so hane ne ala yeɛ wamaa wato wɔ ɔ, ofikyɛ AWURADE ale ahennie ne wafi wɔ sa nu, na wafa wama ebiɛngo Dawide.

english_verse: When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you.
translation_verse: Andie AWURADE dwirɛ, yeɛ ye yaa hahii bɔ wafɛ Amalɛkefoɛ so ne, angyina so annua bɛ boso, yiti yeɛ AWURADE ama edwirɛ he ato wɔ ɛnɛ ye.

english_verse: Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Asa koso, AWURADE kɔfa Yisrael ne wɔ kowura Filistifoɛ sa; na ɛhema ɛne wɔ mma mmienzua mɔ bɛkɔɔboka me so. Na AWURADE kɔfa Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ koso kowura Filistifoɛ sa.”

english_verse: At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
translation_verse: Berɛ ne ala, Sɔɔlo tu tɔle aseɛnwo berɛ, ɔlale berɛ bangwaa, ofikyɛ Samuel noa dwirɛ ne mane ɛserɛ hane ye. Ye nwo yɛle ye hodwoo, ofikyɛ né ollili hwee sɔ kyẽa ne amukoraa ne sɔ kɔngɔen ne amukoraa.

english_verse: The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked.
translation_verse: Braa ne hɔle Sɔɔlo nwo berɛ, na onwuni kyɛ waboto paa ne, osele ye kyɛ, “W’afaneɛ atie wɔ dwirɛ. Mafa me ngoa mato serewa mayɔ bɔ ɛha hyirele me ne.

english_verse: Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
translation_verse: Yiti wɔ koso tie bɔ w’afaneɛ ka ye. Maa mbena nikyee kãa ma ɛha wɔ noa. Didi ná nya anwoserɛ bɔ ɛkɔfa kosi nu kɔhɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: “No, I won't eat!” But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo ambene, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Mengoli.” Nakoso ye somvoɛ nemɔ ne braa ne hɔle so srɛle ye, na ɔpenene bɛ dwirɛ ne aso. Yiti odwɔsole fili aseɛnwo berɛ tenane mba ne aso.

english_verse: At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread.
translation_verse: Né braa ne le nandwie ba bɔ walɔ ɔ wɔ awuro berɛ. Ɔyɛle ndɛndɛ huni ye, ɔfale esam fofale ye nwo, na ɔfa yɛle taterɛ kabrɛdi.

english_verse: Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_verse: Ɔfa siele Sɔɔlo ne ye somvoɛ nemɔ nyunu, na belili. Na besili nu bɛhɔle kɔngɔen ne ala.

english_verse: The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted: Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers.
translation_verse: Nakoso Filistifoɛ safohene nemɔ fɛle Akise so yaa, na besele ye kyɛ, “Ma akoaa he osa hɔ nekaa bɔ afa ama ye kyɛ ɔtena ne. Ɔnzɛ kyɛ yɛne ye bɔ nu yɛkɔ koɛ ne. Anyɔ a né wapɛ ye nwo ɔne yɛ aho. Nzikyɛ yeɛ sɔ akoaa he kɔfa kɔpata ye mene ɔ? Mmenia bɔ yɛwɔ wa ye, aso nna yɛ ti yeɛ ɔkɔfa kɔpata ye ɔ?

english_verse: The Israelites even dance and sing, “Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!”
translation_verse: Aso nna Dawide he yeɛ bɛfale ye dumaa bɛtole dwein begole abilie kyɛ, ‘Sɔɔlo ahu apee apee, yeɛ Dawide ahu apee buru apee buru’ ne?”

english_verse: Achish called David over and said: I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along.
translation_verse: Afei Akise frɛle Dawide sele ye kyɛ, “Kyɛ AWURADE te ase ye, edi nahorɛ. Ɔhale me ngome a, ahaa ɛne me yeɛ yɛkɔhɔ koɛ ne ɔ; ofikyɛ, ofi kyẽa bɔ ɛɛfale wɔ nwo bɔle me bɔ ɔbaadwu ɛnɛ ɔ, nnwuni wɔ nwo dwirɛ tɛɛ biala. Nakoso ahemvo ngaa nemɔ bɛmbene so kyɛ ɛne yɛ kɔhɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Go on back home and try not to upset them.
translation_verse: Yiti sa kɔ. Kɔ asomdwee nu, na nnɛma Filistifoɛ ahemvo nemɔ bɛfɛ wɔ so yaa.”

english_verse: “But what have I done?” David asked. “Do you know of anything I've ever done that would keep me from fighting the enemies of my king?”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide sele Akise kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ yeɛ mayɔ ɔ? Ofi kyẽa bɔ nhyɛle ye bo nzole wɔ, bɔ ɔbaadwu ɛnɛ ɔ, Nana, me mene, nzikyɛ mvomsoɛ yeɛ anwu ye wɔ wɔ somvoɛ nwo ɔ, bɔ yiti ɔnzɛ kyɛ me ne wɔ pɔfoɛ mɔ yɛkɔko ɔ.”

english_verse: Achish said: I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle.
translation_verse: Na Akise buale Dawide kyɛ, “Me ngome de, mese kyɛ wɔ nwo sannwuu kyɛ Nyameɛ abɔfo, nakoso Filistifoɛ safohene mɔ nwa: ‘Yɛ ne ye ngɔhɔ koɛ ne.’

english_verse: You and your troops will have to go back to the town I gave you. Get up and leave tomorrow morning as soon as it's light. I'm pleased with you, so don't let any of this bother you.
translation_verse: Yiti ɛne wɔ mene somvoɛ mɔ bɔ bɛ ne wɔ wale ne, ɛ́mɔpɛ aleɛ bedwɔso. [Wɔ nwo dwirɛ tɛɛ bɔ baha ne, nnɛmaa ɔha wɔ, ofikyɛ me nye asɔ bɔ ayɔ ne.] Ɔsɛ kyɛ alebahyene ɛmɔdwɔso, na sɛ maen nu tete ala a, ɛ́mɔsi nu bɛhɔ nekaa bɔ mama ɛmɔaatena ne.”

english_verse: David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide ne ye mmenia nemɔ sili nu alebahyene kyɛ besa bɛkɔ Filistifoɛ aseɛ so. Nakoso Filistifoɛ nemɔ de, bɛhɔle Yesreel.

english_verse: It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground,
translation_verse: Ye ɛlɛsa ne aso, bɔ Dawide ne ye mmenia nemɔ beedwuli Siklage nen, né Amalɛkefoɛ baabɔ apaa wɔ Yuda ngwaen dɔ ne Siklage. Né bafa koɛ baatoa Siklage bato nu see.

english_verse: When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Dawide ne ye mmenia nemɔ beedwuli kuro ne aso ne, benwuni kyɛ bayera kuro ne. Afei koso, né bahye bɛ ye mɔ ne bɛ mma mmienzua ne mmrasua mɔ nnure bahɔ.

english_verse: They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more.
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide ne mmenia bɔ bɛboka ye so ne betikyele esuɛ nu, na besuni toonn mane b’anwoserɛ bɔ bɛfa besu ne yiele.

english_verse: David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength,
translation_verse: Edwirɛ piri tole Dawide, ofikyɛ ye mmenia nemɔ yɛle kyɛ bɛkɔboro ye nyɔboɛ. Ebiala ahone huli, ofikyɛ né bahye bɛ mma mmienzua ne mmrasua nnure bahɔ. Nakoso Dawide fale ye nye tole AWURADE ye Nyameɛ, na ogyinane pindinn.

english_verse: and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.” Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide sele Ahimɛlɛke awa ɔsɔfo Abiata kyɛ, “Fa ɔsɔfo ataadeɛ ne brɛ me.” Na Abiata fale ɔsɔfo ataadeɛ ne brɛle ye.

english_verse: Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?” “Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide bisale AWURADE kyɛ, “Mbo apaabɔlɛfoɛ hemɔ so anaa? Ngɔto bɛ anaa?” Na AWURADE buale ye kyɛ, “Po bɛ so, ɛkɔto bɛ, na mekã mekyire wɔ kyɛ, mmenia bɔ bahye bɛ nnure ne, ekole bɛ.”

english_verse: Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water,
translation_verse: Mmenia ɛyaa nna ne nwuni Misraimniɛ bie wɔ eburo berɛ, na bɛfale ye bɛbrɛle Dawide. Bɛmane ye aleɛ maa olili, ɔne nzue maa ɔnone.

english_verse: some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
translation_verse: Besa bɛmane ye borɔdoma taterɛ, ɔne bobe bɔ babobɔ ye kunguma nyɔ. Oli yiele nen, ye nwo yɛle ye se, ofikyɛ ɛlɛsa mumua, eyia ne kɔngɔen, né onnyane aleɛ anaa nzue biala ɔhhane ye noa.

english_verse: “Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?” “I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick.
translation_verse: Na Dawide bisale ye kyɛ, “Wɔ mene ole nwa? Efi nisua?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Nde Misraimniɛ aberandeɛ, nde Amalɛkeniɛ bie kanganiɛ. Me mene ahɔ ayakyi me, ofikyɛ anwonyerɛ bɔle me ɔ ɛnɛ te ɛlɛsa.

english_verse: We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
translation_verse: Yɛɛbɔle apaa wɔ Keretifoɛ ngwaen dɔ, Yuda ngwaen dɔ, yeɛ Kalebo ngwaen dɔ, na yɛtole Siklage nu see.”

english_verse: “Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked. “Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide bisale ye kyɛ, “Ekoohyire me nekaa bɔ apaabɔlɛfoɛ nemɔ wɔ ne anaa?” Yeɛ obuale kyɛ, “Fa Nyameɛ ta ndaen kyire me kyɛ engohu me, anaakyɛ ɛngɔfa me ngowura me mene sa, na ngoohyire wɔ nekaa bɔ apaabɔlɛfoɛ nemɔ bɛwɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: He led David to the Amalekites. They were eating and drinking everywhere, celebrating because of what they had taken from Philistia and Judah.
translation_verse: Misraimniɛ ne fale Dawide hɔle apaabɔlɛfoɛ nemɔ dɔ. Né bayɛ berɛ amukoraa birikabirika. Né begu so bedidi, bɛno, bego abilie, ɔnate koɛ nu nzesadeɛ worawora bɔ baafa ye Filistifoɛ aseɛ so ne Yuda aseɛ so ne ati.

english_verse: David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
translation_verse: Dawide huhuni bɛ fite alebahyene maa oodwuli kyẽa bɔ ɔtoa so ne ye nɔsoa. Bɛ nu biala annya ye ti wannidi nu, sana mmerandeɛ ɛyaa nna yeɛ bɛfole afupɔngɔ mɔ so bɛnwati bɛhɔle ɔ.

english_verse: David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag.
translation_verse: Nikyee biala bɔ Amalɛkefoɛ fale ne, Dawide lele, na ye sa hane ɔye nyɔ nemɔ koso.

english_verse: No one was missing—young or old, sons or daughters. David brought back everything that had been stolen,
translation_verse: Bɛ nikye fee amvi bɛ sa, ngwadaa oo, mbanyi oo, mmaa mmienzua oo, mmaa mmrasua oo, koɛ nu nzesadeɛ oo, anaa nikyee biala bɔ Amalɛkefoɛ fa hɔle oo. Dawide fale ye mukoraa sa wale.

english_verse: including their livestock. David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
translation_verse: Dawide fale mmoaen ne nandwie amukoraa koso wale. Ye mmenia nemɔ hane mmoaen ne nandwie nemɔ lili nyɛmmoa ngaa ne anyunu, na besele kyɛ, “Ɛhe te Dawide koɛ nu nzesadeɛ.”

english_verse: Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
translation_verse: Yeɛ mmenia bɔ bɛ ne Dawide hɔle ne, bɛ nu atianuserɛfoɛ ne ammɔbrafoɛ biemɔ sele kyɛ, “Bɛ ne yɛ angɔ, yiti koɛ nu nzesadeɛ bɔ yaale ne, yɛngɔma bɛ bie. Bɛ ye mɔ ne bɛ mma mɔ ala, yeɛ bɛ nu biala ye sa kɔha ye ɔ.”

english_verse: But David said: My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked.
translation_verse: Nakoso Dawide sele kyɛ, “Aliɛmaa mɔ, nikyee bɔ AWURADE afa ama yɛ ne, ɔnzɛ kyɛ ɛmɔfa bɛbɔ atianuserɛ. Wabɔ yɛ nwo waen, na wafa mmenia bɔ bɛɛbɔle yɛ so apaa ne wawura yɛ sa.

english_verse: Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
translation_verse: Bɔ ɛmɔaha ne, ebiala ne ɛmɔ nyɛ adwene. Ofikyɛ, sona bɔ ogyina koɛ noa ne, ye koɛ nu nzesadeɛ bue deɛ ne, sɔ ala yeɛ sona bɔ ɔneane nningyein ne koso, ɔsɛ kyɛ onya ɔ. Bɛkyɛ ye pɛ.”

english_verse: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
translation_verse: Na ofi sɔ kyẽa ne, Dawide fa yɛle ahyɛdeɛ ne nhyehyɛleɛ tole berɛ mane Yisrael, na ɔtɛwɔ berɛ maa waadwu ɛnɛ.

english_verse: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
translation_verse: Dawide sa wale Siklage nen, ɔsomane maa bɛfale koɛ nu nzesadeɛ ne bie bɛɛmane Yuda mbanyi mɔ. Bɛte ye damvo mɔ, na ɔtole bɛ ngraa kyɛ, “Koɛ nu nzesadeɛ bɔ yanya yafi AWURADE pɔfoɛ mɔ berɛ ne, ɛmɔ deɛ ɛne.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
translation_verse: Afei Filistifoɛ fale koɛ bɛɛtetale Yisrael. Yisrael mmienzua nwati fili Filistifoɛ nyunu, na bɛ nu pee totɔle wɔ Gilboa bokaa ne aso.

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Filistifoɛ pole Sɔɔlo ne ye mma mmienzua nemɔ aso, na behuhuni Sɔɔlo mma mmienzua Yonatan, Abinadabo ne Malkisua.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Koɛ ne anu yɛle se mane Sɔɔlo. Filisti agyaentolɛfoɛ nemɔ nwuni ye, na bɛtole agyaen besinane ye maa opurale paa.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo sele ye somvoɛ bɔ otira ye akodeɛ ne kyɛ, “Twe wɔ ngrandɛ ne fa wɔ me. Anyɔ a, mmenia hemɔ bɔ bɛmbɛ bɛ bienzua ye, bɛkɔɔfa bie bɛkɔwɔ me ná bagoro me nwo.” Nakoso ye somvoɛ bɔ otira ye akodeɛ ne ambene so kyɛ ɔkɔyɔ sɔ ɔ, ofikyɛ ɛserɛ piri hane ye. Yiti Sɔɔlo fale ye bɔbɔ ye ngrandɛ ne, na ɔtole ye nwo yele so huni ye nwo.

english_verse: When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Sɔɔlo somvoɛ bɔ otira ye akodeɛ ne nwuni kyɛ Sɔɔlo awu nen, ye koso ɔtole ye nwo yele ye ngrandɛ so ɔne Sɔɔlo bewuli.

english_verse: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
translation_verse: Yiti Sɔɔlo ne ye mma mmienzua nza ne, ye somvoɛ bɔ otira ye akodeɛ ne, yeɛ ye koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛtotɔle ne, bɛ mukoraa bɛtotɔle ɛlɛho.

english_verse: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
translation_verse: Na Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ né bɛwɔ bɔnza ne asi dɔ ne, ɔne bɛ bɔ né bɛwɔ asue Yɔɔdan si dɔ ne, mmerɛ bɔ benwuni kyɛ Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ banwati, ná Sɔɔlo ne ye mma mmienzua nemɔ koso bawuwu nen, bɛnwatili befili bɛ nguro nemɔ aso, na Filistifoɛ wale bɛɛfale nguro nemɔ bɛtenane so.

english_verse: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, Filistifoɛ hɔle kyɛ bɛkwaayeye Yisraelfoɛ bɔ bawuwu nemɔ bɛ nwo nningyein, na benwuni kyɛ Sɔɔlo ne ye mma mmienzua nza nemɔ batotɔ wɔ Gilboa bokaa ne aso.

english_verse: The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Yabese Gileadefoɛ tele nikyee bɔ Filistifoɛ afa ayɛ Sɔɔlo nen,

english_verse: So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them.
translation_verse: bɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ ahoneserɛfoɛ nemɔ penene atee so. Bɛnatele kɔngɔen ne toonn, na bɛɛyele Sɔɔlo ne ye mma nemɔ fuin befili Bete San fasue ne anwo. Na bɛfale bɛ bɛwale Yabese bɛɛyerale bɛ wɔ berɛ.

english_verse: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Afei bɛsesale bɛ mmowue nemɔ besiele bɛ wɔ akyea ne abo wɔ Yabese, na bebua bɛlale ɛlɛsoo.

english_verse: Saul was dead. Meanwhile, David had defeated the Amalekites and returned to Ziklag.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo wue asi ne, mmerɛ bɔ né Dawide waali Amalɛkefoɛ so ngonim wawa ne, Dawide lili elenyɔ wɔ Siklage.

english_verse: Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
translation_verse: Ye ɛlɛsa ne aso, biaa bie fili Sɔɔlo asikyeleɛ ne anu dɔ wale. Né ye ndaadeɛ nu asunzua, yeɛ né nnɛterɛ wɔ ye ti so. Oodwuli Dawide nyunu berɛ ne, ɔbɔle ye ti ase kotole ye.

english_verse: David asked, “Where did you come from?” The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide bisale ye kyɛ, “Nisua yeɛ efi bɔ ɛ́ba ye?” Yeɛ obuale ye kyɛ, “Manwati mafi Yisrael asikyeleɛ ne anu.”

english_verse: “Who won the battle?” David asked. The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide bisale ye kyɛ, “Sɛɛ yeɛ koɛ ne ooyiele ɔ? Ka kyire me!” Na obuale kyɛ, “Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bangora koɛ ne noa gyina, banwati; na koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ pee baho batɔ. Sɔɔlo ne ɔwa Yonatan koso bawu.”

english_verse: The young man replied: I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him.
translation_verse: Na aberandeɛ bɔ ɔɔbɔle amaneɛ ne buale kyɛ, “Ngɔ mvitele Gilboa bokaa ne aso, na mvum nu, nwuni kyɛ Sɔɔlo kisa ye pealɛɛ ne. Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né teaseɛnam mɔ ne pɔngɔhanɛfoɛ mɔ bafoa ye bapingye ye.

english_verse: When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
translation_verse: Ɔpɛle ye nye neane nziɛ, onwuni me, na ɔfrɛle me. Na nzurole kyɛ, ‘Me ɛhe’.

english_verse: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
translation_verse: Na obisale me kyɛ, ‘Wɔ nwa ɛne’? Na mmuale ye kyɛ, ‘Nde Amalɛkeniɛ.’

english_verse: Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ osele me kyɛ, ‘Bra me nwo wa baahu me; ofikyɛ m’ahone te, nakoso mennwu.’

english_verse: So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
translation_verse: Yiti ngɔle ye nwo berɛ ngɔ nguni ye, ofikyɛ, kyɛbɔ né osi la berɛ ne, nwuni kyɛ ongonya ngoa. Me mene, nduli ye abotire ne, yeɛ nyele ye bati kaa ne, na mafa mawa wa kyɛ méfa mebrɛ wɔ.”

english_verse: They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
translation_verse: Bɛbɔle awuye besuni, na bɛhyele hɔen toonn maa oodwuli nɔsoa, ɔnate Sɔɔlo ne ɔwa Yonatan wue, ɔne AWURADE koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ wue ti, yeɛ Yisrael awuro ama ti, ofikyɛ batotɔ ngrandɛ noa.

english_verse: David asked the young man, “Where is your home?” The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide sele aberandeɛ bɔ ɔɔbɔle ye amaneɛ ne kyɛ, “Efi nisua?” Obuale kyɛ, “Amalɛkeniɛ ɛwɔfoɛ bie bɔ ɔne Yisraelfoɛ baatena ɔ, ɔwa ole me.”

english_verse: David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!” Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!” David Sings in Memory of Saul
translation_verse: Na Dawide sele ye kyɛ, “Wɔ mogya kɔbɔ wɔ bɔbɔ wɔ ti so, ofikyɛ wɔ bɔbɔ ato wɔ noa nu tui aha abua wɔ nwo fɔ kyɛ, ‘Me yeɛ nguni sona bɔ AWURADE apopa ye ngoo ne ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
translation_verse: Na Dawide tole aworabɔlɛ dwein he fa suni Sɔɔlo ne ɔwa Yonatan.

english_verse: and he ordered his men to teach the song to everyone in Judah. He called it “The Song of the Bow,” and it can be found in The Book of Jashar. This is the song:
translation_verse: Ɔhyɛle kyɛ edwein bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Agyaen nwo Dwein ne, behyire Yudafoɛ. Na bahyerɛ ye wɔ Yasa Nwomaa ne anu kyɛ,

english_verse: Israel, your famous hero lies dead on the hills, and your mighty warriors have fallen!
translation_verse: “O Yisrael, w’animnyam mɔ yeɛ bahu bɛ bagua asɔneyɛɛ mɔ so dɔ ye! Yieee, katakyie mɔ baho batɔ!

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
translation_verse: Nnɛma ɛmɔbɔ so wɔ Gate, nnɛma ɛmɔbɔ ye nwo dawure wɔ Asekelɔn dwaaso; ɛmɔbɔ so a, Filisti mmrasua koli ahurusi, na mmenia bɔ bɛmbɛ bɛ bienzua ne, bɛ mmrasua nye kɔgye.

english_verse: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
translation_verse: “Ao, Gilboa mmokaa, ɛmɔ, esue ngɔtɔ anaa bosue ngogua ɛmɔ so ko, yeɛ ndire ngofifi ɛmɔ so! Ofikyɛ bagua anwoserɛfoɛ akokyɛm nyunu ase wɔ berɛ. Yieee, bɛngɔpopa Sɔɔlo akokyɛm ngoo ko.

english_verse: The arrows of Jonathan struck, and warriors died. The sword of Saul cut the enemy apart.
translation_verse: “Me ngome oo! Yonatan agyaen anza amma mbaen, bɔ yeɛ ɔngɔma mmenia ngɔtotɔ ɔ, bɔ ongohwi anwoserɛfoɛ bɛ loe ngogua ɔ; yieee, Sɔɔlo ngrandɛ anza amma nzanza.

english_verse: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
translation_verse: “Sɔɔlo ne Yonatan, anwonyemenefoɛ bɔ mmenia kuro bɛ dwirɛ ɔ! Bɛ ngoa nu oo, bɛ wue nu oo, b’afia andete. Né bɛ nwo yɛ nyera tra kɔleɛ, bɛ nwo yɛ se tra gyata.

english_verse: Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He brought you fine red cloth and jewelry made of gold.
translation_verse: “O Yisrael mmrasua, ɛ́mɔsu Sɔɔlo! Ye yeɛ ɔmane ɛmɔ kende kɔkorɛ nyemenenyemene maa ɛmɔherale ɔ, bɔ ɔfale sikaa kɔkorɛ mbembenanneɛ maa ɛmɔsiesiele ɛmɔ nwo ɔ.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
translation_verse: “Yieee, katakyie mɔ baho batɔ wɔ koɛ nu! Me ngome oo! Yonatan aho atɔ wɔ w’asɔneyɛɛ mɔ so.

english_verse: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
translation_verse: O, nniɛma Yonatan, wɔ ti me wora abɔ; né mekuro wɔ dwirɛ paa, kyɛbɔ esi hurole me dwirɛ ne ɔyɛ nwanwa, na ɔtra ehurolɛ bɔ ofi mmrasua berɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen, and their weapons are destroyed.
translation_verse: “Yieee, katakyie mɔ baho batɔ, na akodeɛ mɔ asɛkye!”

english_verse: Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?” The Lord answered, “Yes.” David asked, “Which town should I go to?” “Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
translation_verse: Ɛhe asi ne, Dawide bisale AWURADE kyɛ, “Aso ngɔ Yuda nguro nemɔ ko aso anaa?” Na AWURADE buale ye kyɛ, “Yoo, kɔ.” Yeɛ Dawide sa bisale kyɛ, “Bɛ nu beni yeɛ ngɔ so ɔ?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Hebron.”

english_verse: David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide ne ɔye nyɔ nemɔ bɛhɔle berɛ. Bɛ ole Ahinoam bɔ ofi Yesreel, yeɛ Abigail bɔ ofi Kamɛl bɔ ɔte Nabal kunaniɛ ne.

english_verse: David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
translation_verse: Dawide fale mmienzua bɔ ɔne bɛ nate ne koso bokale ye nwo so; bɛ nu biala ne ye awuro ama, na bɛɛtenane Hebron nwo nguro nemɔ anu.

english_verse: The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
translation_verse: Afei Yuda mmienzua wale bɛɛpopale Dawide ngoo, na bɛfale ye besili Yuda awuro ama so hene wɔ berɛ. Mmerɛ bɔ bɛbɔle Dawide amaneɛ kyɛ Yabese Gileadefoɛ yeɛ besiele Sɔɔlo nen,

english_verse: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
translation_verse: Dawide tuli ɛbɔfoɛ mɔ maa bɛhɔle Yabese Gileadefoɛ berɛ beesele bɛ kyɛ, “AWURADE yira ɛmɔ, kyɛ ɛmɔahyire ɔdɔ bama ɛmɔ mene Sɔɔlo, ná ɛmɔasie ye ɔ.

english_verse: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
translation_verse: Mesrɛ kyɛ, AWURADE ɔye ye ɔdɔ pindinn ne ye nahorɛlilɛ ali ohyire ɛmɔ. Na me koso, bɔ ɛmɔayɔ ye, ngɔfa ye nwo akatuaa ngɔma ɛmɔ.

english_verse: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
translation_verse: Yiti ɛ́mɔgyina pindinn ná ɛ́mɔmia ɛmɔ nye; ofikyɛ ɛmɔ mene Sɔɔlo awu, na Yuda awuro ama bapopa me ngoo bafa me bali bɛ so hene.” Abenɛ fa Yisbosɛte di Yisrael so hene

english_verse: Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim
translation_verse: Nakoso Sɔɔlo safohene Abenɛ, bɔ ɔse ole Nɛɛ ne, ɔfale Sɔɔlo awa Yisbosɛte wale Mahanaim.

english_verse: and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin.
translation_verse: Ɔfale ye sili Gileade, Asurifoɛ, Yesreel, Efraim, Benyamin ne Yisrael mukoraa so hene.

english_verse: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
translation_verse: Na Dawide lili Yuda awuro ama so hene wɔ Hebron afoɛ nzoo ne bue. Koɛ tɔ Yisrael ne Yuda b’afia

english_verse: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
translation_verse: Nɛɛ awa Abenɛ ne Sɔɔlo awa Yisbosɛte ye somvoɛ mɔ befili Mahanaim bɛhɔle Gibeon.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Seruya awa Yoabo ne Dawide somvoɛ mɔ koso bɛboaboale bɛ noa beeyiale bɛ wɔ Gibeon ɛkwaa ne anwo. Abenɛ ne ye lɔen begyinane ɛkwaa ne bue ko, yeɛ Yoabo ne ye lɔen koso begyinane ɛkwaa ne bue ko.

english_verse: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
translation_verse: Na Abenɛ to manene Yoabo kyɛ, “Ma mmerandeɛ nemɔ bedwɔso bɛho wɔ yɛ nyunu wa.” Yeɛ Yoabo buale kyɛ, “Maa bɛfa bɛbɔ so e!”

english_verse: and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men.
translation_verse: Yiti bedwɔsole maa bɛhale bɛ. Benyamin abusua ne Sɔɔlo awa Yisbosɛte bɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ ne, bɛte buru ne nyɔ, yeɛ Dawide mmenia mɔ koso bɛ deɛ buru ne nyɔ.

english_verse: They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.”
translation_verse: Bɛfa bɛbɔle so, na bɛ nu ko biala sɔle obiɛngo ti mane ye wora ɔsɔle ye deɛ. Na ebiala fale ngrandɛ wɔle obiɛngo mvenu mane ye wora ɔwɔle ye bie. Na bɛ mukoraa bɛte beguale aseɛnwo berɛ bewuwuli. Yiti nekaa bɔ ɛhe sili wɔ Gibeon ne, bɛfrɛ berɛ Helkate Hasurim.

english_verse: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
translation_verse: Koɛ ne noa yɛle se sɔ kyẽa ne, na Dawide mmenia nemɔ lili Abenɛ ne Yisrael mmenia ne aso ngonim.

english_verse: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
translation_verse: Seruya mma mmienzua nza nemɔ, bɔ bɛ ole Yoabo, Abisae ne Asahel ne, né bɛwɔ berɛ bie. Né Asahel tu amirika te kyɛ ɛwanzane.

english_verse: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Abenɛ pɛle ye nye nziɛ sele kyɛ, “Asahel, wɔ ɛne?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Yoo, me ɔ.”

english_verse: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
translation_verse: Na Abenɛ sele ye kyɛ, “Yakyi me foalɛ. Fa wɔ nye kyire famaa so anaa bɛen so, ná kye mmerandeɛ nemɔ nu ko de ye nwo koɛ nu nzesadeɛ ne.” Nakoso Asahel anyakyi ye foalɛ.

english_verse: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Abenɛ sele Asahel bieku kyɛ, “Yakyi me foalɛ. Nzu ati yeɛ ɛpena kyɛ meku wɔ ɔ? Sɛ meku wɔ a, aso ngɔhora eliɛma Yoabo nyunu nea?”

english_verse: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
translation_verse: Nakoso Asahel anyakyi ye foalɛ. Yiti Abenɛ fale ye pealɛɛ ne bo wɔle Asahel kunu maa ofitele ye si. Na owu tɔle berɛ ala. Na ebiala bɔ oodwuli nekaa bɔ Asahel ho tɔle ne, ogyinane berɛ konn.

english_verse: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yoabo ne Abisae hɔle so foane Abenɛ. Na eyia kwaatɔ ne, beedwuli Amma pambaa bɔ ɔwɔ Gia ndendeneɛ so ne aso. Ɔwɔ Gibeon ɛserɛ so atee ne aso.

english_verse: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
translation_verse: Benyaminfoɛ nemɔ boale bɛ noa beegyinane Abenɛ si bɛyɛle fekue ko, na beegyinane pambaa bie ti afia.

english_verse: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Abenɛ teane nu sele Yoabo kyɛ, “Aso odi kyɛ yɛkɔ so yɛfa ngrandɛ yɛdi yɛ nwo awue anaa? Aso ɛnze kyɛ ɔkɔfa ɛpɔen kɔwa ɔ? Ɛkɔmaa okoodwu kyinzu koraka né ama wɔ lɔen ne bayakyi b’eliɛma mɔ foalɛ?”

english_verse: Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!”
translation_verse: Na Yoabo buale kyɛ, “Meta AWURADE ndaen kyɛ, sɛ anga sɔ dwirɛ ne a, ahaa koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ kɔhɔ so kɔfoa b’eliɛma nemɔ toonn kɔma aleɛ kɔhye.”

english_verse: Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
translation_verse: Yiti Yoabo huli totorobɛndo ne, na koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ gyinane. Bamvoa Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ ko, yeɛ bɛ ne bɛ ango ko.

english_verse: Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Abenɛ ne ye lɔen ne natele sɔ kɔngɔen ne toonn wɔ Yɔɔdan bɔnza ne anu. Bɛpɛle asue Yɔɔdan, na bɛfale Bitron amukoraa kɔpem kyɛ beedwuli Mahanaim ɔ.

english_verse: As soon as Joab stopped chasing Abner, he got David's troops together and counted them. There were
translation_verse: Yoabo yakyili Abenɛ foalɛ sale ye si. Na ɔmane ye koɛhonɛfoɛ ne amukoraa bɛboale bɛ noa nen, onwuni kyɛ Dawide koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ, asora Asahel wue ne, bɛ nu buru ne ngona bɛnne berɛ bie.

english_verse: Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_verse: Na Yoabo ne koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bɛɛfale Asahel besiele ye wɔ ye baba asieleɛ ne anu wɔ Betlehem. Bɛnatele kɔngɔen ne toonn, na beedwuli Hebron ne, né aleɛ ahye.

english_verse: As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ koɛ tɔle Sɔɔlo awuro ama ne Dawide awuro ama b’afia ne, Abenɛ mane ye dibea wɔ Sɔɔlo sasofoɛ nu hɔle anwuro.

english_verse: He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo te ase ne, né ye sómaa bie dumaa li Risipa. Ɔte Aya awa brasua. Na Yisbosɛte fa sili Abenɛ nyunu kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛne me baba sómaa ne bala ɔ?”

english_verse: Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth: Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
translation_verse: Yisbosɛte noa dwirɛ ne mane Abenɛ ahone huli paa maa ɔhane kyɛ, “Ɛnwa nzɛ nde kyea hɔ ɔ, bɔ mefa me ngoa meto serewa wɔ Yuda sa nu ɔ? Ɔbaadwu ɛnɛ ye, mali nahorɛ mama wɔ baba Sɔɔlo sasofoɛ, oliɛma mɔ ne ye damvo mɔ. Manye wɔ mamma Dawide. Nakoso afei de, braa he anwo kwaadu yeɛ ɛfa bɔ me ɔ.

english_verse: I ask God to punish me if I don't help David get what the Lord promised him!
translation_verse: Nea, ndaen bɔ AWURADE ta hyirele Dawide nen, sɛ manyɔ sɔ ala mamma Dawide a, Nyameɛ otua me Abenɛ so kerɛ piri paa!

english_verse: God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
translation_verse: Ɔtale ndaen kyɛ, ɔkɔye ahennie ne kofi Sɔɔlo awuro, ná wama Dawide ali Yisrael ne Yuda so hene, fite Dan bɔ ɔkwaadwu Beɛ Hyeba.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
translation_verse: Né Yisbosɛte suro Abenɛ, yiti wangora wanga sɔ edwirɛ ne anwo hwee ko.

english_verse: Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
translation_verse: Afei Abenɛ tuli ɛbɔfoɛ mɔ maa bɛhɔle Dawide berɛ wɔ Hebron beesele ye kyɛ, “Nwa yeɛ maen ye wura ye bo ɔ? Maa yɛyɛ apam, na ngɔboka wɔ maa Yisrael amukoraa bɛkɔwa wɔ bue nu.”

english_verse: David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide buale kyɛ, “Yoo, mate; me ne wɔ yɛkɔyɛ apam. Nakoso nikyee ko yeɛ mepena kyɛ ɛyɔ ma me ɔ. Ye ole kyɛ, nnɛba me nyunu, sɛ ɛ́ba me nyunu a, sana ɛfa Sɔɔlo awa brasua Mikal ɛboka wɔ nwo so ɛne ye bɛba.”

english_verse: David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed
translation_verse: Na Dawide tuli mmenia maa bɛhɔle Sɔɔlo awa Yisbosɛte berɛ beesele ye kyɛ, “Me ye Mikal bɔ mvale Filistifoɛ ɛyaa ko bɛ bienzua noa nwomaa nyɛle ye nwo nningyein ne, fa me nikyee ma me.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth sent some of his men to take Michal away from her new husband, Paltiel the son of Laish.
translation_verse: Na Yisbosɛte tuli mmenia maa beelele Mikal befili ohu Paltiɛl bɔ ɔse ole Layise ne berɛ bɛwale.

english_verse: Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
translation_verse: Nakoso ohu Paltiɛl fale esuɛ natele lili ye si toonn oodwuli Bahurim. Yeɛ Abenɛ sele ye kyɛ, “Sa wɔ si kɔ!” Na osale ye si.

english_verse: Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now.
translation_verse: Na Abenɛ ne Yisrael mbanyi belili ngitahoɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔyɛle kyɛ ɛmɔpena Dawide maa odi ɛmɔ so hene ɔ wahyɛ.

english_verse: So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Bekye yeɛ mmerɛ ne adwu ɔ, ofikyɛ AWURADE ahyɛ Dawide bɔ kyɛ, ‘Ngɔfa me somvoɛ Dawide so yeɛ ngole me mmenia Yisrael ngofi Filistifoɛ sa nu, ɔne bɛ pɔfoɛ amukoraa bɛ sa nu ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Finally, Abner talked with the tribe of Benjamin. Then he left for Hebron to tell David everything that the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the people of Israel wanted to do.
translation_verse: Abenɛ ne Benyaminfoɛ koso belili ngitahoɛ. Afei Abenɛ hɔle Hebron, kyɛ nikyee biala bɔ Yisrael ne Benyamin sasofoɛ amukoraa bale bato nu kyɛ bɛkɔyɔ ne, ɔkwaafa ye nwo amaneɛ ɔbɔ Dawide.

english_verse: soldiers with him, and when they got to Hebron, David gave a big feast for them.
translation_verse: Abenɛ ne mmenia aburanyɔ wale Dawide berɛ wɔ Hebron, na Dawide tole poen mane Abenɛ ne mmenia bɔ bɛboka ye so ne.

english_verse: After the feast, Abner said, “Your Majesty, let me leave now and bring Israel here to make an agreement with you. You'll be king of the whole nation, just as you've been wanting.” David told Abner he could leave, and he left without causing any trouble. Joab Kills Abner
translation_verse: Na Abenɛ sele Dawide kyɛ, “Nana, me mene, maa ngɔmmoaboa Yisrael amukoraa bɛ noa ma wɔ. Bɛ ne wɔ kɔyɛ apam, na ekoli ebiala so hene kyɛbɔ ɛpena ɔ.” Na Dawide ne Abenɛ lili ngraa maa osili nu hɔle asomdwee nu. Yoabo ku Abenɛ

english_verse: Soon after Abner had left Hebron, Joab and some of David's soldiers came back, bringing a lot of things they had taken from an enemy village.
translation_verse: Wangyɛ biala, Dawide koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ ne Yoabo befili apaabɔlɛ nu wale, na bɛfale koɛ nu nzesadeɛ pee bɛwale. Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Abenɛ ɔnne Dawide berɛ wɔ Hebron, ofikyɛ Dawide ne ye lili ngraa maa ɔhɔle asomdwee nu.

english_verse: Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
translation_verse: Yoabo ne koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa bɔ bɛboka ye so ne, bɛwale ne, ebie bɔle Yoabo amaneɛ kyɛ, “Nɛɛ awa Abenɛ wale Nana Dawide berɛ, na ɔne ye bali ngraa maa wahɔ asomdwee nu.”

english_verse: Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone!
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yoabo hɔle Nana Dawide berɛ oobisale ye kyɛ, “Nana, nzikyɛ dwirɛ yeɛ ali ye sɔa ye? Abenɛ wale wɔ wa. Nzu ati yeɛ ama ye ate maa wafa ye nwo wali wahɔ ye?

english_verse: You know Abner—he came to trick you. He wants to find out how strong your army is and to know everything you're doing.”
translation_verse: Ɛnze kyɛ Nɛɛ awa Abenɛ wale kyɛ ɔbaato wɔ kanda onwu wɔ koɛhonɛ nwo nhyehyɛleɛ, ɔne bɔ ɛyɔ amukoraa ɔ?”

english_verse: Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it.
translation_verse: Yoabo fili Dawide nwo berɛ fitele ne, otuli ɛbɔfoɛ mɔ maa bɛpole Abenɛ so, na bɛɛfale ye befili Sira abura nwo bɛwale; nakoso né Dawide nze ye nwo huu.

english_verse: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel. Abner's Funeral
translation_verse: Abenɛ sa wale Hebron nen, Yoabo ne ye bɛhɔle kuro berɛ pambim ne ahameɛ, kyɛ ɔne ye bɛkwaatu asure. Na Yoabo wɔle Abenɛ kunu dadeɛ huni ye, ɔnate kyɛ né Abenɛ aha Yoabo aliɛma Asahel mogya wagua.

english_verse: David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death!
translation_verse: Nziɛ ye bɔ Dawide tele sɔ dwirɛ nen, ɔhane kyɛ, “Nɛɛ awa Abenɛ mogya ne, me ne m’ahennie yɛdi ye nwo be afebɔɔ wɔ AWURADE nyunu.

english_verse: Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
translation_verse: Ye nwo foɛlilɛ kɔbɔ Yoabo ti so, ɔne ɔse abusuafoɛ bɛ ti so. Sona bɔ ye bienzua fiti, anaa kwataniɛ, anaa sayɛɛ, anaa bɔ ɔtɔ ngrandɛ noa, anaa bɔ ye noa aleɛ abɔ ye ne, ebie ngɔpa Yoabo awuro le!”

english_verse: Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Yoabo ne oliɛma Abisae behuni Abenɛ, ofikyɛ ohuni b’eliɛma Asahel wɔ Gibeon koɛ ne anu.

english_verse: David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!” David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide sele Yoabo ne koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa bɔ bɛboka ye so ne kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔsunzua ɛmɔ ndaadeɛ nu, ɛ́mɔfa ɛsɛen tena bɛhera, ná ɛ́mɔsu Abenɛ.” Na Nana Dawide lili efuin alaka ne asi.

english_verse: Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly.
translation_verse: Besiele Abenɛ wɔ Hebron. Nana Dawide tikyele esuɛ nu wɔ Abenɛ asieleɛ ne aso, na mmenia ne amukoraa besuni.

english_verse: Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner: Abner, why should you have died like an outlaw?
translation_verse: Nana Dawide suni Abenɛ kyɛ, “Ao, aso ngwaseaa wue yeɛ odi kyɛ Abenɛ wu ɔ?

english_verse: No one tied your hands or chained your feet, yet you died as a victim of murderers. Everyone started crying again.
translation_verse: Bangyekye wɔ sa bangua wɔ nwo, yeɛ bammɔ wɔ panwu. Na kyɛbɔ sona si wu wɔ amumuyɛɛfoɛ bɛ sa nu ne, ao, sɔ ala yeɛ awu ɔ.” Na koɛhonɛfoɛ ne amukoraa besuni Abenɛ bieku.

english_verse: Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
translation_verse: Afei mmenia ne amukoraa bɛwale Dawide berɛ bɛɛsrɛle ye kyɛ ɔpena nikyee kãa li, wɔ mmerɛ bɔ né eyia gyi so ɔ. Nakoso Dawide tale ndaen kyɛ, “Sɛ mefa aleɛ anaa nikyee biala meka me noa koraka né eyia atɔ a, Nyameɛ otua me so kerɛ piri paa!”

english_verse: Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did.
translation_verse: Mmenia ne amu tele Dawide noa dwirɛ nen, ɔyɛle bɛ fɛ, kyɛbɔ nikyee biala bɔ Nana Dawide yɔle ne, bɛ mukoraa bɛ nye gyele ye nwo ne.

english_verse: Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
translation_verse: Yiti sɔ kyẽa ne, mmenia ne amukoraa ne Yisrael amukoraa, benwuni ye kyɛ, Nana Dawide nze Nɛɛ awa Abenɛ wue ne nwo hwee.

english_verse: David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died?
translation_verse: Na Nana Dawide sele ye mbanyi mɔ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔnze kyɛ sona titire bɔ ɔte safohene ɔ wawu ɛnɛ wɔ Yisrael ɔ?

english_verse: I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ bapopa me ngoo bafa me basi hene de, nakoso ɛnɛ de, Seruya mma nemɔ bama me nwo ahyere me. Sɔ mmenia hemɔ, mebɔ bɛ kyɛnn so a ɔmmɔ. Na sona bɔ ɔyɔ bɔne ne, AWURADE kotua ye kerɛ kyɛbɔ ye bɔne yɔleɛ te ɔ!”

english_verse: Ishbosheth felt like giving up after he heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Everyone in Israel was terrified.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo awa Yisbosɛte tele kyɛ bahu Abenɛ wɔ Hebron nen, ye aba nu buli, na ɛserɛ tɔle Yisrael amukoraa so.

english_verse: Ishbosheth had put the two brothers Baanah and Rechab in charge of the soldiers who raided enemy villages. Rimmon was their father, and they were from the town of Beeroth, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo awa ne, ye mmenia bɔ bɛbɔ apaa ne, né ole mmenia nyɔ bɔ bɛla bɛ noa ɔ. Ko dumaa li Baana, yeɛ ko wora li Rekabo. Bɛte Benyaminniɛ Rimon bɔ ofi Beerote ne ye mma. Né mmenia bu Beerote kyɛ ɔte Benyaminfoɛ kuro.

english_verse: Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who had not been able to walk since he was five years old. It happened when someone from Jezreel told his nurse that Saul and Jonathan had died. She hurried off with the boy in her arms, but he fell and injured his legs.
translation_verse: Né Sɔɔlo awa Yonatan le baa bienzua bubuaniɛ bie. Oli Mefibosɛte. Mmenia fili Yesreel bɛɛbɔle amaneɛ kyɛ Sɔɔlo ne Yonatan bawu nen, né Mefibosɛte ali afoɛ nnu. Baanealɛniɛ bɔ ɔnea ye ne pagyale ye nwatili. Na ndɛndɛ so bɔ ɔnwati nen, Mefibosɛte te tɔle, na ɔyɛle bubuaniɛ.

english_verse: One day about noon, Rechab and Baanah went to Ishbosheth's house. It was a hot day, and he was resting
translation_verse: Beeroteniɛ Rimon ye mma Rekabo ne Baana besili nu, na beedwuli Yisbosɛte awuro eyia ketee, wɔ mmerɛ bɔ né ɔda eyia ɔ.

english_verse: in his bedroom. The two brothers went into the house, pretending to get some flour. But once they were inside, they stabbed Ishbosheth in the stomach and killed him. Then they cut off his head and took it with them. Rechab and Baanah walked through the Jordan River valley all night long.
translation_verse: Bɛhɔle awuro berɛ nen, né Yisbosɛte alafe wɔ ye mba so wɔ ye sua nu, na bɛwɔle ye dadeɛ behuni ye. Bɛpɛle ye ti, na bɛfale tire ne bɛnatele bɛɛfale Yɔɔdan bɔnza ne anu toonn kɔngɔen ne.

english_verse: Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
translation_verse: Bɛfale Yisbosɛte ti ne bɛbrɛle Nana Dawide wɔ Hebron, na bɛhane kyɛ, “Wɔ pɔfoɛ Sɔɔlo bɔ né ɔpena wɔ ku wɔ ne, ɔwa Yisbosɛte ye ti ɛhe. Nana, me mene, AWURADE atɔ Sɔɔlo ne ye boso ama so wereɛ wama wɔ.”

english_verse: When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
translation_verse: sona bɔ ɔɔbɔle me amaneɛ kyɛ Sɔɔlo awu ne, né ye adwene yɛ ye kyɛ ndɛenvɛen yeɛ ɔfa brɛ me ɔ. Nakoso ngyele ye nguni ye wɔ Siklage. Amaneɛ bɔ ɔɔbɔle ne, bɔ mva nduale ye so kerɛ hɔ ɛne.

english_verse: You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
translation_verse: Na sɛ nzɛmmɔnefoɛ ahu sona bɔ ɔtengyɛ, wɔ ye bɔbɔ ye awuro, wɔ ye mba so a, ye de ngotua bɛ so kerɛ piri paa! Ɔnate ehunɛ bɔ ɛmɔahu ye ne ati, ngotua ɛmɔ so kerɛ, na ngɔye ɛmɔ ngofi aseɛ ye aso.”

english_verse: Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide mane ye mmerandeɛ nemɔ huni bɛ. Bɛpepɛle bɛ gya ne bɛ sa befili so. Na bɛ kundunzii ne, besinzele bɛ wɔ ɛkwaa bɔ ɔwɔ Hebron ne anwo. Nakoso Yisbosɛte ti ne de, besiele ye wɔ Abenɛ asieleɛ ne anu wɔ Hebron.

translation_verse: Aberɛso Dwirɛ

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.
translation_verse: Tiro hene Hiram tuli mmenia maa bɛhɔle Dawide berɛ. Bɛfale sida mmakaa bɛɛmane ye. Bakaa dwumvoɛ mɔ ne suasilɛfoɛ boka so yeɛ bɛhɔle ɔ, na besili awuro bɛmane Dawide.

english_verse: He lived in Hebron for the first seven and a half years and ruled only Judah. Then he moved to Jerusalem, where he ruled both Israel and Judah for
translation_verse: Olili Yuda so hene wɔ Hebron afoɛ nzoo ne bue; yeɛ olili Yisrael amukoraa ne Yuda so hene wɔ Yerusalem afoɛ aburasa ne nza. Dawide ko fa Yerusalem

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and David led his army there to attack them. The Jebusites did not think he could get in, so they told him, “You can't get in here! We could keep you out, even if we couldn't see or walk!”
translation_verse: Yebusifoɛ bɔ né bɛte aseɛ ne aso ne, Nana Dawide ne ye koɛhonɛfoɛ sili nu hɔle Yerusalem bɛɛfale koɛ bɛtoale bɛ. Na Yebusifoɛ sele Dawide kyɛ, “Ɛngɔhora wa ba, ofikyɛ anyesiniwaafoɛ ne mmubuafoɛ mɔ po bɛkɔfoa wɔ maa ekosa.” Besusuli kyɛ Dawide ngɔhora ngowura kuro ne anu.

english_verse: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
translation_verse: Dawide hɔle so nyane ngɔsoɛ, ofikyɛ AWURADE, Asafo Nyameɛ gyinane ye si.

english_verse: David knew that the Lord had made him king of Israel and that he had made him a powerful ruler for the good of his people. David's Sons Born in Jerusalem (
translation_verse: Afei Dawide nwuni ye kyɛ AWURADE afa ye asi Yisrael so hene, na ɔnate AWURADE maen Yisrael ti, AWURADE apagya ye Dawide ahennie ne.

english_verse: After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he married many women from Jerusalem, and he had a lot of children.
translation_verse: Dawide tu fili Hebron wale nen, ye si ye ɔfale sómaa pee, na ogyale mmraa koso pee wɔ Yerusalem. Dawide wole mmaa mmienzua ne mmrasua pee.
