translation_verse: Yibare, Elisua, Nefege, Yafia,

english_verse: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet. David Fights the Philistines (
translation_verse: Elisama, Eliada, yeɛ Elifɛlɛte. Dawide di Filistifoɛ so ngonim (

english_verse: The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress.
translation_verse: Filistifoɛ tele kyɛ bapopa Dawide ngoo bafa ye bali Yisrael so hene ne, Filisti koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa hɔle kyɛ bɛkwaapena Dawide bɛkye ye. Nakoso Dawide tele sɔ dwirɛ nen, oowurale anwoserɛ afealeɛ ne anu.

english_verse: So the Philistines camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Filistifoɛ nemɔ wale bɛɛyɛle Refaim bɔnza ne anu mitimiti.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you let me win?” The Lord told David, “Attack! I will let you win.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide bisale AWURADE kyɛ, “Mva koɛ ngɔndoa Filistifoɛ anaa? Ɛkɔfa bɛ kowura me sa anaa?” Yeɛ AWURADE buale Dawide kyɛ, “Kɔ, ngɔfa Filistifoɛ ngowura wɔ sa amba.”

english_verse: David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide hɔle Baal Perasim, na olili bɛ so ngonim wɔ berɛ. Na ɔhane kyɛ, “AWURADE ahwi afa me pɔfoɛ mɔ so wɔ me nyunu kyɛbɔ asue yi twi fa nningyein so ɔ.” Yiti bɛfrɛle berɛ Baal Perasim.

english_verse: David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Filistifoɛ nwatili bɛyakyili bɛ mmosoen berɛ, na Dawide ne ye koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ sesale bɛ hɔle.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Filistifoɛ sa hɔle bieku bɛɛyɛle Refaim bɔnza ne anu mitimiti.

english_verse: David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered: Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees.
translation_verse: Dawide bisale AWURADE, na obuale kyɛ, “Nnɛkɔ wɔ nyunu tee, na mmom kakyi wɔ nwo kɔfa bɛ si. Kɔ bɛ so wɔ mmakaa bɔ bɛfrɛ ye basam ne ndendeneɛ so.

english_verse: Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛte mmenia gya boso nga wɔ basam mmakaa nemɔ aso a, ye de kɔ Filistifoɛ so. Na ɛhe kyire kyɛ AWURADE ali wɔ nyunu moa okũkũ Filisti koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ.”

english_verse: David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: Dawide yɔle kyɛbɔ AWURADE hyɛle ye ne ala, na ohuhuni Filistifoɛ nemɔ toonn fite Geba oodwuli Gɛsɛre.

english_verse: The people carrying the chest walked six steps, then David sacrificed an ox and a choice cow.
translation_verse: Na bɛ bɔ bɛsõ AWURADE alaka ne, betuli bɛ gya nzia ne, Dawide fale nandwie ne nandwie sayɛɛ bɔle afɔleɛ.

english_verse: He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth.
translation_verse: Dawide fale ye anwoserɛ amukoraa gole abilie wɔ AWURADE nyunu. Né Dawide afa ɔsɔfo ataadeɛ bɔ ɔte nwera ɔ wapɛ ye bo.

english_verse: He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
translation_verse: Na Dawide ne Yisrael awuro ama amukoraa bɛbɔle ese behuli totorobɛndo bɛfale AWURADE alaka ne bɛwale Yerusalem.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ AWURADE alaka ne oodwuli Dawide kuro berɛ nen, Sɔɔlo awa brasua Mikal tole ye nye neane mboma nu. Onwuni kyɛ Nana Dawide ohuru pepe go abilie wɔ AWURADE nyunu ɔ, na obuli Dawide animtia wɔ ye ti anu.

english_verse: They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart,
translation_verse: Bɛfale Nyameɛ alaka ne besiele teaseɛnam monɛ kamee so, na bɛye befili Abinadabo awuro bɔ ogyi pambaa so ne anu. Teaseɛnam monɛ kamee bɔ Nyameɛ apam alaka ne gyi so ne, Abinadabo mma Yusa ne Ahio yeɛ bɛfa bɛhɔle ɔ.

english_verse: led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
translation_verse: Dawide ne koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛboka ye so ne amukoraa besili nu befili Baale Yuda, kyɛ bɛkwaafa Nyameɛ apam alaka ne bɛba. Alaka ne, Asafo AWURADE bɔ ye ahennie bia wɔ kɛrubim nemɔ afia ne, ye dumaa la so.

english_verse: with Ahio walking in front of it.
translation_verse: Né Ahio li Nyameɛ alaka ne nyunu.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
translation_verse: Na Dawide ne Yisrael awuro ama amukoraa bɛfale sangoo, adengum, akasaa, donno ne firikyiwa bɛfale b’anwoserɛ mu bɛtole dwein begole abilie wɔ AWURADE nyunu.

english_verse: But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Na beedwuli Nakɔn ye nekaa bɔ bɛboro aburoo nen, nandwie nemɔ sotili, yiti Yusa tengyɛle ye sa sɔle Nyameɛ alaka ne anu.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: AWURADE fɛle Yusa so yaa, ofikyɛ ɔtengyɛle ye sa sɔle alaka ne anu. Nyameɛ bɔle ye tole ase wɔ berɛ, na owuli tɔle Nyameɛ alaka ne anwo berɛ.

english_verse: David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
translation_verse: Dawide fɛle yaa, ɔnate kyɛ AWURADE fɛle yaa tuale Yusa so kerɛ. Yiti bafrɛ berɛ Pɛrɛse Yusa maa waadwu ɛnɛ.

english_verse: David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?”
translation_verse: Dawide surole AWURADE sɔ kyẽa ne, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ né mahora mafa AWURADE alaka ne mahɔ m’awuro?”

english_verse: He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide anguro kyɛ ɔkɔfa AWURADE alaka ne ɔkɔ ye awuro wɔ Dawide kuro ne anu, na mmom Dawide makye fale alaka ne hɔle Gitiniɛ Obɛde Edom awuro.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.” At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating.
translation_verse: Na ebiemɔ bɛbɔle Nana Dawide amaneɛ kyɛ, “Ɔnate Nyameɛ alaka ne ati, AWURADE ayira Obɛde Edom awuro ama, ɔne bɔ ole ye amukoraa.” Yiti Dawide hɔle anigye so ɔɔfale Nyameɛ alaka ne fili Obɛde Edom awuro wale Dawide kuro ne anu.

english_verse: They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar,
translation_verse: Bɛfale AWURADE alaka ne beesiele nekaa bɔ basiesie bama ye ne, wɔ ɛtena sua bɔ Dawide si siele berɛ mane ye ne anu. Na Dawide bɔle naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne asomdwee afɔleɛ wɔ AWURADE nyunu.

english_verse: then he blessed the people in the name of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Dawide bɔle naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne asomdwee afɔleɛ yiele ne, ɔsrɛle Asafo AWURADE saleɛ mane maen ne.

english_verse: He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home. Michal Talks to David
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛle aleɛ mane Yisrael maen ne anu mmienzua ne mmrasua mukoraa. Ebiala nyane paanoo mumua ko, naen porɛ ko ne bobe taterɛ ko. Na afei ebiala hɔle ye awuro.

english_verse: David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
translation_verse: Nziɛ ye, Dawide sa hɔle kyɛ ɔkwaasrɛ Nyameɛ saleɛ ma ye awuro ama. Yeɛ Sɔɔlo awa Mikal fitele ooyiale Dawide, na osele Dawide kyɛ, “Ɛnɛ de, Yisrael hene ayɛ ye nwo bie paa! Wapa ye nwo ɛnɛ wɔ ye somvoɛ mɔ b’afaneɛ mɔ nyunu, kyɛbɔ sona bɔ ɔnze nyanzoen si pa ye nwo ɔ!”

english_verse: David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him.
translation_verse: Na Dawide buale Mikal kyɛ, “AWURADE bɔ ɔyele wɔ baba ne ye awuro ama mukoraa siele ahameɛ, ná ɔneaneane nu yele me sili me hene wɔ ye maen Yisrael so ne, ye nyunu yeɛ ngole abilie ne ɔ.

english_verse: I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
translation_verse: Ngɔyɔ bɔ ɔtra sɔ koraa, maa ekobu me kyɛ magua me nyunu ase. Nakoso afaneɛ mɔ bɔ ɛkã bɛ nwo dwirɛ ne, bɛ yeɛ bɛkɔhyɛ me animnyam ɔ.”

english_verse: Michal never had any children.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo awa Mikal wanwo ba le ɔfa hɔle wue.

english_verse: Chronicles
translation_verse: Aberɛso Dwirɛ

english_verse: But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Nakoso me dɔ pindinn ne de, mengɔye ngofi ye so, kyɛbɔ nyele ɔdɔ ne mvili Sɔɔlo so ne. Ye yeɛ nduli ye mvili bia so mvale wɔ nziele so ɔ.

english_verse: Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
translation_verse: Nana Dawide sele Ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ Natan kyɛ, “Nea, nde awuro bɔ bafa sida basi ɔ nu, nakoso Nyameɛ alaka ne de, ogyi ɛtena sua nu.”

english_verse: Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
translation_verse: Na Natan buale Nana Dawide kyɛ, “Bɔ adwene ye nwo kyɛ ɛkɔyɔ ne, yɔ, ofikyɛ AWURADE gyi wɔ si.”

english_verse: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
translation_verse: “Kɔha kyire me somvoɛ Dawide kyɛ, AWURADE nwa nyoo: Wɔ yeɛ ɛbaasi sua maa metena nu anaa?

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Ofi kyẽa bɔ nyele Yisraelfoɛ mvili Misraim mmale bɔ ɔbaadwu ɛnɛ ɔ, nndenane awuro nu le; na mmom medi tutena wɔ ɛtena sua ne nyianu sua nu.

english_verse: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Nekaa biala bɔ mali tutena me ne Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa yahɔ ne, Yisrael mbanyi bɔ maye bɛ kyɛ bɛnea me maen Yisrael so ne, aso mabɔ bɛ nu bie somoɛ kyɛ, ‘Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔamva sida banzi awuro bamma me ɔ?’

english_verse: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
translation_verse: “Yiti ka kyire me somvoɛ Dawide kyɛ, Asafo AWURADE nwa nyoo: Me yeɛ nyele wɔ mvili mmoaen nealɛ nu, ɔne mmoaen si lilɛ nu, ná mvale wɔ nduale me maen Yisrael noa ɔ.

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: Magyina wɔ si wɔ nekaa biala bɔ ɛhɔle ɔ, maprapra wɔ pɔfoɛ amukoraa mafi w’atee nu, na mapagya wɔ dumaa maa wayɛ kyɛ aseɛ ye aso atitirefoɛ bɛ dumaa.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: Asa koso, ngɔma me maen Yisrael nekaa maa ɔkɔtena. Ngɔbɔ bɛ atenaseɛ wɔ bɛ bɔbɔ b’aseɛ so, bɔ ebiala ngɔha bɛ ko, bɔ amumuyɛɛfoɛ ngɔhyɛ bɛ so ko, kyɛbɔ bɛyɔle ye daa

english_verse: when I let judges rule my people. And I have kept your enemies from attacking you. Now I promise that you and your descendants will be kings.
translation_verse: fite mmerɛ bɔ nyele maenbulɛfoɛ maa beelili me maen Yisrael so ne ala. Ngɔma wɔ asomdwee ngofi wɔ pɔfoɛ amukoraa bɛ sa nu. Asa koso, AWURADE ka kyire wɔ kyɛ, ɔkɔma wɔ boso ama kɔhɔ so koli hene.

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Sɛ wɔ mmerɛ so ná ɛtoa wɔ mbanyi mɔ a, ngɔpagya wɔ bosofoɛ nemɔ ko, bɔ ɔte wɔ kunu ba, na ngɔma ye ahennie kotindim.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Ye yeɛ okosi sua kɔfa me dumaa kɔto so ɔ, na ngɔma ye ahennie kotindim afebɔɔ.

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: Ngɔyɛ ye baba, ná ye wora wayɛ mma. Sɛ ɔyɔ mvomsoɛ a, ngɔfa bakaa ne mbire ngɔtea ye, kyɛbɔ kuro sona tea ɔwa ɔ.

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ wɔ, Asafo AWURADE, Yisrael Nyameɛ, aye wɔ somvoɛ asotire kyɛ, ‘Ngɔma wɔ boso ama kɔhɔ so koli hene.’ Na ɛhe yeɛ wahyɛ wɔ somvoɛ nguraen bɔ ɔmaa ɔbɔ sɔ mbaeɛ he kyire wɔ ye.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Afei Nana Dawide ɔɔtenane AWURADE nyunu, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Ao, AWURADE Nyameɛ, me ole nwa, yeɛ m’abusua gyi ye sɛ, bɔ apagya me amaa manya dibea sɔa ye?

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: Nzikyɛ dwirɛ bieku koraa yeɛ nga ngyire wɔ ɔ? Ofikyɛ, AWURADE Nyameɛ, wɔ yeɛ ɛse wɔ somvoɛ ɔ.

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: Ɔnate wɔ bɔhyɛ ne, ɔne wɔ ti anu dwirɛ ne ati, yeɛ ayɔ nikyee piri he ɔ, kyɛ ɛkɔma wɔ somvoɛ konwu ye ɔ.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: O, AWURADE Nyameɛ, ɛte piri. Edwirɛ amukoraa bɔ yate ye wɔ yɛ so anu ne, okyire kyɛ ebiala nne berɛ bɔ ɔte kyɛ wɔ ɔ, yeɛ nyameɛ biala nne berɛ kyɛ wɔ.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Maen beni yeɛ ɔwɔ aseɛ ye aso bɔ ɔte kyɛ wɔ maen Yisrael ɔ? Yisrael bɔ Nyameɛ ɔɔpɔle ye fa yɛle ye maen, bɔ ɔnate so Nyameɛ dumaa trɛle, bɔ yiti Nyameɛ foane maen maen mɔ ne bɛ nyameɛ mɔ fili ye mmenia nyunu, ná ɔyɔle nningyein mbiri mbiri ne anwanwadeɛ mane bɛ ne.

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Afa wɔ maen Yisrael ayɛ wɔ bɔbɔ deinn wɔ maen afebɔɔ, na wɔ, AWURADE, ayɛ bɛ Nyameɛ.

english_verse: And now, Lord God, please do what you have promised me and my descendants.
translation_verse: Afei, ao, AWURADE Nyameɛ, kyɛbɔ aha afa wɔ somvoɛ ne ye boso ama nwo ne, maa ɔbra nu afebɔɔ. Kyɛbɔ ahyɛ bɔ ne, yɔ sɔ ala.

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.”
translation_verse: Na bɛkɔbɔ wɔ dumaa bɛkɔkamvo wɔ daa kyɛ, ‘Asafo AWURADE te Nyameɛ bɔ odi Yisrael so ɔ.’ Na wɔ somvoɛ Dawide boso ama bekogyina pindinn wɔ wɔ nyunu.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
translation_verse: O, AWURADE Nyameɛ, wɔ yeɛ ɛte Nyameɛ ɔ, wɔ dwirɛ te nahorɛ, na afa sɔ ndɛenvɛen he ahyɛ wɔ somvoɛ bɔ.

english_verse: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_verse: Yiti mesrɛ wɔ ala, yira wɔ somvoɛ boso ama, ná maa bɛhɔ so betindim wɔ wɔ nyunu afebɔɔ. Ofikyɛ, AWURADE Nyameɛ, wɔ yeɛ aha sɔ dwirɛ ye ɔ, na wɔ yeɛ ɛkɔma wɔ somvoɛ boso ama bekonya wɔ saleɛ ne afebɔɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were priests.
translation_verse: Né Yehoada awa Benaya ɔte Keretifoɛ ne Peletifoɛ so safohene; yeɛ né Dawide mma mmienzua nemɔ bɛte maen mbanyi.

english_verse: David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
translation_verse: Dawide lili Moabofoɛ koso so ngonim. Ɔmaa bɛlelale aseɛnwo berɛ fekue fekue nza. Ohuni fekue nyɔ, na ɔmane fekue ko nyane ye ti didili nu. Yiti Moabofoɛ bɛɛyɛle Dawide ngoaa bɔ né betua ɛtoɔ bɛma ye ɔ.

english_verse: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
translation_verse: Soba hene Hadadesa bɔ ɔse ole Rehobo ne, ye koso Dawide lili ye so ngonim, wɔ mmerɛ bɔ né ɔkwaaho trɛ ye ahennie ne anu wɔ asue Yufreti noa ɔ.

english_verse: When troops from the Aramean kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed
translation_verse: Na Siriafoɛ bɔ bɛwɔ Damasko ne, bɛwale kyɛ bɛbaaboka Soba hene Hadadesa nen, Dawide huni Siriafoɛ nemɔ anu apee aburanyɔ ne nyɔ.

english_verse: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Afei Dawide ɔɔkyekyele koɛhonɛfoɛ asikyeleɛ mɔ wɔ Damasko bɔ ɔwɔ Siria. Na Siriafoɛ bɛɛyɛle Dawide ngoaa bɔ né betua ɛtoɔ bɛma ye ɔ. Na AWURADE mane Dawide lili ngonim wɔ koɛ biala bɔ ɔhone ɔ nu.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Sikaa kɔkorɛ akokyɛm bɔ né Hadadesa mbanyi mɔ betiratira ne, Dawide lele bɛ sa nu fa wale Yerusalem.

english_verse: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
translation_verse: Nana Dawide fale kɔɔbere pee fili Hadadesa nguro Beta ne Berotae so.

english_verse: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
translation_verse: Toyi somane ɔwa bienzua Yoram wɔ Nana Dawide berɛ maa oobisale ye ahye yɛle ye mmo, kyɛ wali Hadadesa so ngonim ɔ, ofikyɛ né Hadadesa ne Toyi bɛtaa bɛko koɛ. Yoram ɔkɔ Dawide berɛ ne, ɔfale mbembenanneɛ bɔ bafa ɛdwetɛ, esikaa kɔkorɛ ne kɔɔbere bayɔ yeɛ ɔhɔle ɔ.

english_verse: David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from
translation_verse: Na Nana Dawide tuli sɔ nningyein nemɔ koso siele berɛ mane AWURADE sɔnenɛ, kyɛbɔ maen mɔ bɔ olili bɛ so ngonim ne, otuli b’ɛdwetɛ ne sikaa kɔkorɛ siele berɛ mane AWURADE sɔnenɛ ne.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.
translation_verse: né Ahitubo awa Sadoke ne Abiata awa Ahimɛlɛke bɛte asɔfo; yeɛ né Seraya te ahemvie berɛ ahyerɛlɛniɛ.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Né Seruya awa Yoabo ɔte koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ so safohene; né Ahilude awa Yehosafate ɔte maen ne anu abakɔsɛm ahyerɛlɛniɛ;

english_verse: One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.”
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, Dawide bisale kyɛ, “Sɔɔlo boso ama ne, aso ebie tɛ wɔ berɛ bɔ ɔnate Yonatan ti ɔsɛ kyɛ meyɛ ye paa ɔ?”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.” “Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
translation_verse: Né Sɔɔlo awuro somvoɛ bie wɔ berɛ. Oli Siba. Bɛɛfrɛle ye bɛbrɛle Nana Dawide, na Dawide bisale ye kyɛ, “Wɔ yeɛ eli Siba ne?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Nana, w’akoaa, me ɔ.”

english_verse: David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.” Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
translation_verse: Na Nana Dawide bisale ye kyɛ, “Aso Sɔɔlo bosoniɛ bie tɛ wɔ berɛ bɔ ngɔhora ngɔfa me nye ngɔto Nyameɛ anwumvoinnwunɛ so ngɔboka ye ɔ?” Na Siba buale Nana Dawide kyɛ, “Waha Yonatan awa bienzua ko; ɔte bubuaniɛ.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” David asked. Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Dawide bisale Siba kyɛ, “Ɔwɔ nisua?” Na obuale Nana kyɛ, “Ɔwɔ Amiɛl awa Makyiri awuro wɔ Lodeba.”

english_verse: David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down. David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?” “Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo awa Yonatan ɔwa Mefibosɛte oodwuli Dawide nyunu berɛ ne, ɔfale ye nyunu butuli berɛ anidie nu. Yeɛ Dawide frɛle ye kyɛ, “Mefibosɛte!” Na osurole kyɛ, “Nana, w’akoaa, me ɛhe.”

english_verse: David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide sele ye kyɛ, “Nnɛsuro, na ɔnate wɔ baba Yonatan ti ngɔyɛ wɔ paa. Wɔ nana Sɔɔlo aseɛ ne, ngɔfa ye mukoraa ngɔma wɔ, na ɛne me kɔtena ɛpoen ko anwo yɛkodidi daa.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Mefibosɛte fale ye nyunu butuli berɛ sele kyɛ, “W’akoaa, kyea fuin bɔ ɔte kyɛ me ɔ, nde nzu bɔ alo me sɔa ɔ?”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family.
translation_verse: Afei Nana Dawide maa bɛɛfrɛle Siba bɛwale, na osele ye kyɛ, “Nikyee biala bɔ ɔte Sɔɔlo ne ye abusua deɛ ne, mafa mama wɔ mene Sɔɔlo anomaa ne.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
translation_verse: Na ahemvo amukoraa bɔ né bewura Hadadesa bo ne, benwuni kyɛ Yisrael ali bɛ so ngonim ne, bɛ ne Yisrael yɛle asomdwee apam, na bɛsole Yisrael. Na Siriafoɛ surole kyɛ bɛkɔɔboka Amonfoɛ bieku ɔ.

english_verse: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, and I will be kind to his son.” So he sent some officials to the country of Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
translation_verse: Na Dawide sele kyɛ, “Hanun baba Nahase wayɔ me paa, yiti me koso ngɔyɔ Hanun paa ne bie.” Yiti Dawide tuli ɛbɔfoɛ mɔ kyɛ bɛɛyɛ ye yaakɔ, ɔnate ɔse wue ne ati. Nakoso Dawide bɔfoɛ nemɔ beedwuli Amonfoɛ aseɛ so ne,

english_verse: But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.”
translation_verse: Amon mbanyi sele bɛ mene Hanun kyɛ, “Dawide somanɛ bɔ wasoma mmenia kyɛ bɛɛyɛ wɔ yaakɔ ye, ɛnwa nzɛ anidie yeɛ ɔfa ma wɔ baba ɔ? Aso nna kuro ye anu neanealɛ, ye sralɛ, ɔne so ngonimlilɛ ti yeɛ Dawide atu ɛbɔfoɛ maa bawa wɔ wa ye?”

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Yiti Hanun hyele Dawide bɔfoɛ nemɔ, ɔpoane ebiala kanza bue, ɔpepɛle bɛ ndaadeɛ ne nekaa bɔ ɔkata bɛ bo ne guale, na ɔfoane bɛ maa bɛhɔle.

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message and told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: Na Nana Dawide tele edwirɛ bɔ wasi nen, ɔsomane mmenia maa beeyiale bɛ bɛha behyirele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔtena Yeriko ma ɛmɔ kanza ne ofu koraka né ɛmɔasa bawa.” Ofikyɛ né Hanun agua bɛ nyunu ase paa.

english_verse: The Ammonites realized that they had made David very angry, so they hired more foreign soldiers. Twenty thousand of them were foot soldiers from the Aramean cities of Beth-Rehob and Zobah,
translation_verse: Amonfoɛ nwuni kyɛ bama Dawide ahone ahu bɛ so paa, yiti betuli ɛbɔfoɛ mɔ maa bɛɛbɔle sɔ mmenia hemɔ paa: Siriafoɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ apee aburanyɔ bɔ bɛnate ase ɔ, bɔ befi Bete Rehobo ne Soba, Maaka hene berɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ apee ko, yeɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ apee buru ne nyɔ bɔ befi Tobo aseɛ so.

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. I pray that the Lord will do whatever pleases him.”
translation_verse: Gyina pindinn. Na ɔnate yɛ maen, ɔne yɛ Nyameɛ nguro nemɔ ati, maa yɛhyire yɛ bienzua. Mesrɛ kyɛ AWURADE ɔyɔ bɔ okuro ɔ.”

english_verse: David heard what they had done, and he sent out Joab with all of his well-trained soldiers.
translation_verse: Na Dawide tele porɛ bɔ babɔ nen, ɔmane Yoabo ne koɛhonɛfoɛ ne amukoraa bɛhɔle kyɛ bɛ ne bɛ bɛɛho.

english_verse: The Ammonite troops came out and got ready to fight in front of the gate to their city. The Arameans from Zobah and Rehob and the soldiers from Tob and Maacah formed a separate group in the nearby fields.
translation_verse: Amonfoɛ fili bɛ kuro ne anu fitele beegyinagyinane kuro berɛ pambim ne anyunu. Nakoso Siriafoɛ bɔ befi Soba ne Rehobo, yeɛ Tobo ne Maaka koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ de, beegyinagyinane eburo.

english_verse: Joab saw that he had to fight in front and behind at the same time, and he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Arameans.
translation_verse: Yoabo nwuni kyɛ koɛ ne afite ye nyunu ne ye si, yiti ɔyele Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ paa paa nemɔ nu bie, kyɛ ɔkwaafa bɛ toa Siriafoɛ ɔne bɛ ko.

english_verse: He put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and gave them orders to fight the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Ɔmane oliɛma Abisae lale ye koɛhonɛfoɛ ngaa nemɔ noa, kyɛ ɔɔfa bɛ toa Amonfoɛ ɔne bɛ ho.

english_verse: Joab told his brother, “If the Arameans are too much for me to handle, you can come and help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
translation_verse: Na Yoabo sele kyɛ, “Sɛ Siriafoɛ b’anwoserɛ bo me so a, baaboka me; yeɛ sɛ Amonfoɛ koso b’anwoserɛ bo wɔ so a, ngɔɔboka wɔ.

english_verse: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Arameans, and the Arameans ran from them.
translation_verse: Afei Yoabo ne ye koɛhonɛfoɛ hɔle bɛ nyunu bɛ ne Siriafoɛ bɛɛfa bɛtetale so, na Siriafoɛ nwati fili ye nyunu.

english_verse: When the Ammonite soldiers saw that the Arameans had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Amonfoɛ nwuni kyɛ Siriafoɛ anwati nen, bɛ koso bɛnwati befili Abisae nyunu, na beewurale kuro ne anu. Yoabo ne Amonfoɛ bɛɛhone koɛ beyiele ne, afei osa wale Yerusalem.

english_verse: The Arameans realized they had lost the battle, so they brought all their troops together again.
translation_verse: Siriafoɛ nwuni kyɛ Yisrael ali bɛ so ngonim, yiti bɛboaboale bɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ noa bieku.

english_verse: Hadadezer sent messengers to call in the Arameans who were on the other side of the Euphrates River. Then Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them to the town of Helam.
translation_verse: Siriafoɛ bɔ bɛwɔ asue Yufreti si dɔ ne, Hadadesa somane maa bɛɛfale bɛ bɛwale. Bɛwale Helam. Né Hadadesa safohene Sobake yeɛ ɔla bɛ noa ɔ.

english_verse: David found out what the Arameans were doing, and he brought Israel's whole army together. They crossed the Jordan River and went to Helam, where the Arameans were ready to meet them.
translation_verse: Dawide tele sɔ dwirɛ nen, ɔboaboale Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa noa, na ɔɔpɛle asue Yɔɔdan hɔle Helam. Siria koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ te gyinane, na bɛ ne Dawide fale koɛ tetale so.

english_verse: It was now spring, the time when kings go to war. David sent out the whole Israelite army under the command of Joab and his officers. They destroyed the Ammonite army and surrounded the capital city of Rabbah, but David stayed in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Bɛhyɛ afoɛ bo bieku nen, mmerɛ bɔ ɔyɛ a ahemvo mɔ bɛkɔ koɛ ne, Dawide somane Yoabo ne ye koɛhonɛfoɛ mbanyi ne Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa kyɛ bɛhɔ koɛ. Behuhuni Amonfoɛ pasaa, na betuale Raba kuro ne. Nakoso Dawide de, ɔhale Yerusalem.

english_verse: David sent a message to Joab: “Send Uriah the Hittite to me.” Joab sent Uriah
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide tole Yoabo ngraa kyɛ, “Ma Hitiniɛ Yuria ɔbra me wa.” Na Yoabo mane Yuria hɔle Dawide berɛ.

english_verse: to David's palace, and David asked him, “Is Joab well? How is the army doing? And how about the war?”
translation_verse: Yuria oodwuli Dawide berɛ ne, Dawide bisale ye kyɛbɔ Yoabo ne koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bɛ nwo si te ɔ, ɔne kyɛbɔ koɛ ne osi kɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Then David told Uriah, “Go home and clean up.” Uriah left the king's palace, and David had dinner sent to Uriah's house.
translation_verse: Afei Dawide sele Yuria kyɛ, “Kɔ awuro kɔpena nzue bie bia.” Yeɛ Yuria fili ahemvie berɛ fitele, na Nana Dawide maa bɛfale akyɛdeɛ bɛɛmane ye.

english_verse: But Uriah didn't go home. Instead, he slept outside the entrance to the royal palace, where the king's guards slept.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yuria angɔ ye awuro. Ɔlale ahemvie anoa nu berɛ, ɔne ye mene Dawide somvoɛ amukoraa yeɛ bɛlale berɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Someone told David that Uriah had not gone home. So the next morning David asked him, “Why didn't you go home? Haven't you been away for a long time?”
translation_verse: Na bɛbɔle Dawide amaneɛ kyɛ Yuria angɔ ye awuro nen, Dawide sele Yuria kyɛ, “Bekye ala yeɛ efi atee awa ɔ. Nzu ati yeɛ angɔ w’awuro ye?”

english_verse: Uriah answered, “The sacred chest and the armies of Israel and Judah are camping out somewhere in the fields with our commander Joab and his officers and troops. Do you really think I would go home to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? I swear by your life that I would not!”
translation_verse: Na Yuria buale Dawide kyɛ, “Me mene, Nyameɛ alaka ne ɔne Yisrael ne Yuda koɛhonɛfoɛ bɛwɔ asese nu, yeɛ me mene Yoabo ne wɔ somvoɛ mɔ koso bakyekye asikyeleɛ wɔ eburo. Aso ngɔhora ngɔhɔ awuro ngoodidi ngɔno, ná me ne me ye yala anaa? Nana, mesrɛ meta wɔ ndaen kyɛ, sɔ nikyee de, mengɔyɔ.”

english_verse: Then David said, “Stay here in Jerusalem today, and I will send you back tomorrow.” Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day. Then the next day,
translation_verse: Na Dawide sele Yuria kyɛ, “Nzaade da kuro wa ɛnɛ koso, na ɛhema ngɔmaa ekosa kɔhɔ.” Yiti Yuria tenane Yerusalem sɔ kyẽa ne. Na aleɛ hyene ne,

english_verse: David invited him for dinner. Uriah ate with David, who gave him so much to drink that he got drunk. But Uriah still did not go home. He went out and slept on his mat near the palace guards.
translation_verse: Dawide tole ye sa frɛle ye maa bedidili bɛnone, na Dawide maa ɔbole. Odwuli nɔsoa ne, Yuria angɔ ye awuro. Ɔne ye mene Dawide somvoɛ nemɔ yeɛ bɛlale ahemvie anoa nu berɛ ɔ. Dawide maa beku Yuria

english_verse: Early the next morning, David wrote a letter and told Uriah to deliver it to Joab.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, Dawide hyerɛle Yoabo krataa, na ɔfa wurale Yuria sa nu kyɛ ɔɔfa ma ye.

english_verse: The letter said: “Put Uriah on the front line where the fighting is the worst. Then pull the troops back from him, so that he will be wounded and die.”
translation_verse: Krataa ne anu dwirɛ ɛhe: “Nekaa bɔ koɛ ne noa yɛ se paa ne, ma Yuria oogyina ye noa. Afei ɛ́mɔyakyi ye ngome nu ma bepura ye behũ ye.”

english_verse: Joab had been carefully watching the city of Rabbah, and he put Uriah in a place where he knew there were some of the enemy's best soldiers.
translation_verse: Na Yoabo gu so bɔ otua kuro ne nen, ɔfale Yuria oogyinane nekaa bɔ Amonfoɛ bɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ ahoneserɛfoɛ paa wɔ ne.

english_verse: When the men of the city came out, they fought and killed some of David's soldiers—Uriah the Hittite was one of them.
translation_verse: Kuro berɛ ama fite wale bɛɛfale koɛ bɛtoale Yoabo. Behuni Dawide koɛhonɛfoɛ mbanyi ne biemɔ, na behuni Hitiniɛ Yuria koso.

english_verse: Joab sent a messenger to tell David everything that was happening in the war.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yoabo tuli bɔfoɛ maa ɔɔfale koɛ ne anu amaneɛ amukoraa bɔle Dawide.

english_verse: He gave the messenger these orders: When you finish telling the king everything that has happened,
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛle bɔfoɛ ne kyɛ, “Sɛ ɛkã koɛ ne anu dwirɛ amukoraa kyire Nana Dawide yie,

english_verse: Don't you know how Abimelech the son of Gideon was killed at Thebez? Didn't a woman kill him by dropping a large rock from the top of the city wall? Why did you go so close to the city walls?” Then tell him, “One of your soldiers who was killed was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Nwa yeɛ ohuni Yerubaal awa Abimɛlɛke ɔ? Aso nna braa bie yeɛ ɔyakyili nyɔkoa nu fili fasue so maa ɔɔbɔle ye huni ye wɔ Tebese ɔ? Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔhɔle fasue ne anwo berɛ pɛɛ ɔ?’ a, ye de ka kyɛ, ‘Wɔ somvoɛ Hitiniɛ Yuria koso bahu ye.’ ”

english_verse: The messenger went to David and reported everything Joab had told him.
translation_verse: Yiti ɛbɔfoɛ ne sili nu hɔle, na ɔfale Yoabo ngraa ne amu bɔle Dawide amaneɛ.

english_verse: He added, “The enemy chased us from the wall and out into the open fields. But we pushed them back as far as the city gate.
translation_verse: Ɛbɔfoɛ ne bɔle Dawide amaneɛ kyɛ, “Amonfoɛ b’anwoserɛ bole yɛ deɛ so. Befili kuro ne anu befitele, bɛfale koɛ bɛɛtoale yɛ wɔ eburo, nakoso yɛfoane bɛ alaa yɛɛdwuli kuro berɛ pambim ne anyunu.

english_verse: Then they shot arrows at us from the top of the wall. Some of your soldiers were killed, and one of them was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Afei b’agyaentolɛfoɛ nemɔ totole agyaen fale fasue ne aso wowɔle wɔ somvoɛ mɔ. Nana, wɔ somvoɛ nemɔ bie awuwu, na wɔ somvoɛ Hitiniɛ Yuria koso wawu.”

english_verse: David replied, “Tell Joab to cheer up and not to be upset about what happened. You never know who will be killed in a war. Tell him to strengthen his attack against the city and break through its walls.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide sele ɛbɔfoɛ ne kyɛ, “Kose Yoabo kyɛ, ‘Nnɛdi edwirɛ he anwo yealɛ, ofikyɛ koɛ nu de, ɔyɛ sɛɛ ala a, mmenia totɔ wɔ bue ne amunyɔ nu. Yiti mia wɔ nye tua kuro ne ná di so ngonim.’ Afei hyɛ ye nguraen.”

english_verse: When Bathsheba heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
translation_verse: Na Yuria aye ne tele kyɛ ohu Yuria awu nen, osuni ohu ne.

english_verse: Then after the time for mourning was over, David sent someone to bring her to the palace. She became David's wife, and they had a son. The Lord's Message for David The Lord was angry because of what David had done,
translation_verse: Olili ye kuna yiele nen, Dawide somane maa bɛɛfale ye bɛwale ye ahemvie berɛ. Ɔyɛle ɔye, na ɔne ye bɛwole baa bienzua. Nakoso AWURADE nye angye nikyee bɔ Dawide yɔle ne anwo.

english_verse: The rich man owned a lot of sheep and cattle,
translation_verse: Né sikaniɛ ne le mmoaen ne nandwie pee;

english_verse: One day someone came to visit the rich man, but the rich man didn't want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle and serve it to the visitor. So he stole the poor man's lamb and served it instead.
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, sikaniɛ ne nyane ɛwɔfoɛ. Nakoso sikaniɛ ne anguro kyɛ ye mmoaen anaa nandwie nemɔ, okohu nu ko kɔfa kɔyɛ aleɛ kɔma ɛwɔfoɛ bɔ waasikye ye awuro ne ɔ. Yiti ɔɔhyele ehianiɛ ne boaen deɛ ne, na ohuni ye fa yɛle aleɛ mane ɛwɔfoɛ bɔ wawa ye berɛ ne.”

english_verse: David was furious with the rich man and said to Nathan, “I swear by the living Lord that the man who did this deserves to die!
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide fɛle sikaniɛ ne so yaa hahii, na osele Natan kyɛ, “Kyɛ AWURADE te ase ye, sona bɔ wabɔ sɔ bra ne, ehunɛ yeɛ ɔsɛ kyɛ beku ye ɔ!

english_verse: And because he didn't have pity on the poor man, he will have to pay four times what the lamb was worth.”
translation_verse: Odi kyɛ ɔfa boaen ne bie si ye gya nu pɛen nna, ɔnate sɔ nikyee bɔ wayɔ ne ati, yeɛ afei ɔnate kyɛ ɔnze anwumvoin.”

english_verse: Then Nathan told David: You are that rich man! Now listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you: “I chose you to be the king of Israel. I kept you safe from Saul
translation_verse: Yeɛ Natan sele Dawide kyɛ, “Wɔ yeɛ abɔ sɔ bra ne! Na AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Me yeɛ mbopale wɔ ngoo mvale wɔ nzili Yisrael so hene ɔ, me yeɛ nnele wɔ mvili Sɔɔlo sa nu ɔ.

english_verse: and even gave you his house and his wives. I let you rule Israel and Judah, and if that had not been enough, I would have given you much more.
translation_verse: Me yeɛ mmaa enyane wɔ mene Sɔɔlo awuro ama so tumi, ná nza mvale ɔye mɔ koso nwurale wɔ sa ɔ, yeɛ mafa Yisrael ne Yuda awuro ama koso mama wɔ. Na sɛ ɛhe te kãa po a, ahaa ngɔfa ye mmɔhoɛ ngɔboka wɔ so.

english_verse: Why did you disobey me and do such a horrible thing? You murdered Uriah the Hittite by letting the Ammonites kill him, so you could take his wife.
translation_verse: Nzu ati yeɛ ahwi afa AWURADE dwirɛ so aayɔ bɔ ɔte bɔne wɔ ye nyunu ɔ? Ahu Hitiniɛ Yuria, na afa ɔye agya. Amonfoɛ ngrandɛ yeɛ afa ahu ye ɔ.

english_verse: “Because you wouldn't obey me and took Uriah's wife for yourself, your family will never live in peace.
translation_verse: Yiti ngrandɛ noa wue ngofi w’awuro le, ofikyɛ ahwi afa me dwirɛ so, yeɛ ale Hitiniɛ Yuria ɔye afa ye ayɛ ɛye.

english_verse: Someone from your own family will cause you a lot of trouble, and I will take your wives and give them to another man before your very eyes. He will go to bed with them while everyone looks on.
translation_verse: AWURADE nwa nyoo: Ngɔma wɔ bɔbɔ w’awuroniɛ kodwɔso kotia wɔ serɛserɛ. Ngole ɛye mɔ ngofi wɔ sa nu bɔ wɔ nye tua ɔ, ngɔfa bɛ ngɔma ebiɛngo bienzua, na ɔne ɛye mɔ kɔla pandann nu eyia ketee.

english_verse: What you did was in secret, but I will do this in the open for everyone in Israel to see.”
translation_verse: Ɛyɔle wɔ deɛ mvealeɛ nu, nakoso me de, ngɔmaa okosi Yisrael amukoraa nyunu eyia ketee.” Dawide de ye bɔne to nu

english_verse: David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.” “Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.”
translation_verse: Nakoso sɔ bra he bɔ abɔ, bɔ ɔnate so ama AWURADE pɔfoɛ mɔ banya ate baha musue dwirɛ batia ye ne ati, akwadaa bɔ awo ye ne okowu.”

english_verse: Then Nathan went back home. David's Young Son Dies The Lord made David's young son very sick.
translation_verse: Afei Natan hɔle ye awuro. Na akwadaa bɔ Yuria aye ne ɔne Dawide bɛwole ye ne, AWURADE mane anwonyerɛ kandinga bie bɔle ye.

english_verse: So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor.
translation_verse: Dawide srɛle AWURADE kyɛ ɔma akwadaa ne nya ngoa; Dawide yɔle akɔngyere, na ɔhɔle sua nu ɔɔlale aseɛnwo berɛ kɔngɔen ne amukoraa.

english_verse: His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
translation_verse: Afei ye ahemvie berɛ mbanyi wale ye nwo berɛ, bɛsrɛle ye kyɛ odwɔso fi aseɛnwo berɛ, nakoso wandwɔso, yeɛ ɔne bɛ angɔannidi.

english_verse: After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
translation_verse: Na ye ɛlɛsoo ne aso, akwadaa ne wuli. Né Dawide somvoɛ nemɔ besuro kyɛ bɛkɔbɔ ye amaneɛ kyɛ akwadaa ne awu ɔ; ofikyɛ bɛhane kyɛ, “Akwadaa ne te ase ne po, wandie bɔ yɛhã yɛhyirele ye ne, ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ né yahora yahã yahyire ye kyɛ akwadaa ne awu. Ebiaa né wayɔ ye nwo nikye.”

english_verse: David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants. “Yes, he did,” they answered.
translation_verse: Nakoso Dawide nwuni kyɛ ye somvoɛ nemɔ bɛ́wɔ bɛ noa ase bedi ngɔmɔ nen, onyane adwene kyɛ akwadaa ne awu. Yiti obisale ye somvoɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “Akwadaa ne awu hɔ ɔ?” Na bebuale kyɛ, “Yoo, wawu.”

english_verse: His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
translation_verse: Afei ye somvoɛ nemɔ sele ye kyɛ, “Nana, na nzikyɛ yeɛ ɛyɔ ye? Akwadaa ne te ase ne, ebualale, yeɛ esuni; nakoso akwadaa ne wuli ye de, adwɔso adidi.”

english_verse: David answered: While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide buale bɛ kyɛ, “Mmerɛ bɔ né akwadaa ne te ase ne, nzuni nyɔle akɔngyere, ofikyɛ nyane adwene kyɛ, ‘Ebie nze, ebiaa né AWURADE alo me ama akwadaa ne anya ngoa.’

english_verse: But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me. Solomon Is Born
translation_verse: Nakoso kekesaala ye bɔ wanya wawu ye de, nzu ati yeɛ ɔsɛ kyɛ mebua meda ɔ? Ngɔhora maa okosa kɔwa ngoa nu anaa? Me yeɛ ngɔɔtoa ye ɔ, nna ye mmom yeɛ okosa kɔwa kɔɔtoa me ɔ.” Bahyeba wo Solomon

english_verse: David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon
translation_verse: Afei Dawide kyekyele ɔye Bahyeba wora, ɔne ye bɛlale, ɔwole baa bienzua, na bɛtole ye dumaa Solomon. AWURADE hurole akwadaa ne dwirɛ,

english_verse: and sent Nathan the prophet to tell David, “The Lord will call him Jedidiah.” The End of the War with Ammon (

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab had been in the country of Ammon, attacking the city of Rabbah. He captured the royal fortress
translation_verse: Yoabo fale koɛ ɔtetale Amonfoɛ ahenguro Raba, na olili so ngonim.

english_verse: and sent a messenger to tell David: I have attacked Rabbah and captured the fortress guarding the city water supply.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yoabo tuli ɛbɔfoɛ mɔ maa bɛwale Dawide berɛ beesele ye kyɛ, “Mafa koɛ mateta Raba, na maho mafa nekaa bɔ benya bɛ nzue ne.

english_verse: Call the rest of the army together. Then surround the city, and capture it yourself. If you don't, everyone will remember that I captured the city.
translation_verse: Yiti boaboa koɛhonɛfoɛ ngaa nemɔ noa, ná baatua kuro ne di so ngonim. Ofikyɛ membena kyɛ me bɔbɔ medi kuro ne aso ngonim ma me dumaa da so.”

english_verse: David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide boaboale koɛhonɛfoɛ ne amukoraa noa, ɔfale bɛ hɔle Raba, na ɔfale koɛ tetale kuro ne lili so ngonim.

english_verse: David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities. David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_verse: Dawide sesale kuro berɛ ama hɔle, na ɔmaa bɛfale sralaa, kona ne akumaa bɛyɔle adwuma, na ɔmaa bɛpɛle mmerekese koso. Sɔ yeɛ ɔyɔle ye wɔ Amonfoɛ nguro ne amukoraa so ɔ. Afei Dawide ne koɛhonɛfoɛ ne amu besa bɛhɔle Yerusalem.

english_verse: David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her.
translation_verse: Né Dawide awa Absalom ole aliɛmaa brasua anwonyemene bie bɔ oli Tamar. Na né Dawide awa bienzua Amnɔn kuro ye.

english_verse: But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
translation_verse: Amnɔn hurolɛ bɔ né okuro oliɛma Tamar ne, né ode ye nwo a onne, maa yiti ɔpati fokyɛle. Né Tamar te taluwa bɔ onnwuni biaa le ɔ, yiti Amnɔn nwuni kyɛ ɔkɔyɛ se kyɛ okonya ye ɔne ye bɛkɔla ɔ.

english_verse: Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted,
translation_verse: Né Amnɔn le obiɛngo bie bɔ oli Yonadabo. Ɔse ole Dawide aliɛma Simea. Né Yonadabo te kanda sona paa.

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: Na Yonadabo sele Amnɔn kyɛ, “Wɔ baba te hene. Nakoso nzu ati yeɛ alehyeleɛ biala ɛma aworabɔlɛ tira wɔ sɔa ye? Nikyee bɔ ɔha wɔ ne, ka kyire me.” Na Amnɔn buale ye kyɛ, “Nniɛma brasua Tamar bɔ ɔte Absalom aliɛma ne, mekuro ye.”

english_verse: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yonadabo sele ye kyɛ, “Kɔla wɔ mba ne aso, ná pati yɛ kyɛ ɛnde apɔ. Na sɛ wɔ baba banea wɔ a, ka kyire ye kyɛ, ‘Ma nniɛma Tamar bra ɔɔpena nikyee ma nni. Maa ɔɔyɛ aleɛ ne wɔ me nyunu wa, bɔ me nye tua ɔ, ná ɔtete ma me.’ ”

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Yiti Amnɔn ɔɔlale berɛ, na ɔpati yɛle kyɛ ɔnde apɔ. Na Nana Dawide wale kyɛ ɔbaanea ye nen, Amnɔn sele ye kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, ma nniɛma Tamar ɔbra ɔɔyɛ taterɛ kɔyɛ nyɔ bie ma me wɔ me nyunu wa, ná ɔtete ma me.”

english_verse: David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide somane maa bɛhɔle ahemvie berɛ beesele Tamar kyɛ, “Kɔ eliɛma Amnɔn awuro kɔyɛ aleɛ ma ye.”

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: Yiti Tamar hɔle oliɛma Amnɔn awuro, wɔ nekaa bɔ né ɔla ne. Ɔfale mɔle, ɔfetele, ɔyɛle taterɛ wɔ ye nyunu berɛ, na ɔhyele taterɛ ne.

english_verse: Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it. Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone,
translation_verse: Afei osikyele kukue ne, na ɔfale taterɛ ne siele Amnɔn nyunu, nakoso wanni. Yeɛ Amnɔn sele kyɛ, “Ebiala ofite hɔ!” Yiti ebiala fili ye nwo berɛ fitele.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Na Amnɔn sele Tamar kyɛ, “Fa aleɛ ne bra pumbu nu faen baatete ma me.” Yiti Tamar fale taterɛ bɔ wahye ne ɔɔmane oliɛma Amnɔn wɔ pumbu nu dɔ.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: Ɔfale aleɛ ne pingyele ye kyɛ oli pɛ, yeɛ Amnɔn yerele ye ɔ, na osele Tamar kyɛ, “Nniɛma brasua, maa me ne wɔ yɛla.”

english_verse: She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting!
translation_verse: Nakoso obuale ye kyɛ, “Daabi, nniɛma bienzua, nnɛyere me, ofikyɛ bɛnyɔ sɔ nikyee ne wɔ Yisrael maen nu; nnɛbɔ sɔ musue ne!

english_verse: Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
translation_verse: Me de, m’animguaseɛ ne, nisua yeɛ mefa mefa ɔ? Wɔ de, busuefoɛ mmenia bɔ bɛwɔ Yisrael ne, ɛkɔyɛ kyɛ bɛ nu ko. Yiti mesrɛ wɔ ala, fa to Nana nyunu, na ɔkɔfa me kɔma wɔ.”

english_verse: But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her.
translation_verse: Nakoso Amnɔn andɛ ye so. Na ɔnate kyɛ ye nwo yɛ se tra Tamar ne ati, ɔyerele ye ɔne ye bɛlale.

english_verse: Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
translation_verse: Afei Amnɔn hyɛle ye bo ɔpɔle Tamar paa trale ehurolɛ bɔ né okuro ye daa ne. Yiti Amnɔn sele ye kyɛ, “Dwɔso fi wa kɔ!”

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Na Tamar sele ye kyɛ, “Daabi, nniɛma, ɛfoanɛ bɔ ɛfoa me ne, ɔte bɔne piri paa tra bɔ ali moa afa ayɛ me ne.” Nakoso Amnɔn andɛ ye so.

english_verse: He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
translation_verse: Amnɔn frɛle ye somvoɛ aberandeɛ ne sele ye kyɛ, “Foa sɔ braa he ma ofi me nye so wa hɔ, ná to anoa ne asi.”

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: Né Tamar wura ataadeɛ tendenn bie, ofikyɛ sɔ mmerɛ ne, ɛhene mma mmrasua bɔ bennwuni biaa le ne, sɔ ndaadeɛ ne yeɛ né bewura ɔ. Ye somvoɛ ne foane ye maa ofitele, na ɔtole anoa ne asi.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Yeɛ Tamar fale nzoen guale ye ti so, osunzuale ataadeɛ tendenn bɔ owura ye ne anu, na ɔfale ye sa guale ye ti so bɔle awuye fili berɛ hɔle.

english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: Na oliɛma Absalom bisale ye kyɛ, “Eliɛma Amnɔn ɔne wɔ bala hɔ ɔ? Nniɛma, wɔ de nnɛbɔ so. Eliɛma ɔ. Nnɛdi ɛhe anwo aworabɔlɛ.” Na ofi sɔ mmerɛ ne, Tamar fale aworabɔlɛ tenane oliɛma Absalom awuro berɛ.

english_verse: When David heard what had happened to Tamar, he was very angry. But Amnon was his oldest son and also his favorite, and David would not do anything to make Amnon unhappy.
translation_verse: Na Nana Dawide tele sɔ dwirɛ hemɔ amukoraa nen, ɔfɛle yaa paa. [Nakoso wandwe ɔwa Amnɔn so, ofikyɛ né okuro ye dwirɛ, né ye bamuɛbaa ɛne.]

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Nakoso Absalom anga edwirɛ biala wangyire Amnɔn, kyɛ edwirɛ paa oo, anaa tɛɛ oo. Absalom pɔle Amnɔn, ofikyɛ né wato oliɛma Tamar mmɔnaa. Absalom tɔ Amnɔn so wereɛ

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Afoɛ nyɔ asi ne, mmerɛ bie, né Absalom ɔmaa bɛpepɛ ye mmoaen nwo nwiaa wɔ Baal Hasɔ bɔ opingye Efraim. Na Absalom tole poen tole ye sa frɛle Nana Dawide mma mmienzua ne amukoraa.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: Absalom hɔle Nana Dawide berɛ oosele ye kyɛ, “Nana, w’akoaa, me mmoaen nwo nwiaa bɔ begu so bɛpepɛ ne, mato ye nwo poen. Yiti mesrɛ wɔ, ɛne wɔ mbanyi mɔ, kyɛ ɛ́mɔma yɛhɔ w’akoaa poentolɛ ne abo.”

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: Nakoso Nana Dawide buale Absalom kyɛ, “Daabi, mma, ɔnzɛ kyɛ yɛ mu yɛkɔ; anyɔ a, wɔ nwo kɔhyere wɔ.” Absalom hɔle so srɛle ye, nakoso wangɔ, na mmom ɔhane kyɛ ɔne Nyameɛ bɛhɔ.

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Absalom sele kyɛ, “Sɛ engonya ye nwo a, ye de mesrɛ wɔ, ma nniɛma Amnɔn ɔne yɛ hɔ.” Na Nana Dawide bisale ye kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛpena kyɛ ɔne wɔ bɛkɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Nakoso Absalom hɔle so srɛle Nana Dawide. Na afei ɔmane Amnɔn, yeɛ ye mma mmienzua ngaa ne amu bɛ ne Absalom hɔle. [Absalom poen bɔ ɔtole ne, ɔte kyɛ ahemvo poentolɛ.]

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: Né Absalom ali moa waha wahyire ye somvoɛ nemɔ kitii kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔfa bɛ nye bɛ́sra Amnɔn, na sɛ ɛmɔnwu kyɛ nzaa ne abo ye, ná mekã mekyire ɛmɔ kyɛ, ‘Ɛ́mɔhu Amnɔn!’ a, ɛ́mɔhu ye. Nnɛma ɛmɔsuro. Me yeɛ mahyɛ ɛmɔ kyɛ ɛ́mɔyɔ sɔ ɔ. Ɛ́mɔsi ɛmɔ ahone bɛyɛ mmienzua.”

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Yiti Absalom somvoɛ nemɔ huni Amnɔn kyɛbɔ Absalom hyɛle bɛ ne. Na Dawide mma ngaa ne amu bɛfo bɛtenatenane b’afunum mɔ so bɛnwati bɛhɔle.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: Na bɛnate atee so bɔ bɛnwati bɛkɔ nen, ebie ɔɔbɔle Dawide amaneɛ kyɛ Absalom ahũhũ Dawide mma mmienzua ne amukoraa, bɔ ko po anga ɔ.

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Yiti Nana Dawide dwɔsole, osunzuale ye ndaadeɛ nu, na ɔtole ye nwo yele aseɛnwo berɛ. Na ye somvoɛ mɔ bɔ né begyigyi ye nwo berɛ ne, bɛ koso besunzuale bɛ ndaadeɛ nu.

english_verse: Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yonadabo, bɔ ɔte Dawide aliɛma Simea awa ne, ɔhane kyɛ, “Nana, me mene, nnɛdwene kyɛ bahu wɔ mma mmerandeɛ ne amukoraa. Amnɔn angome yeɛ bahu ye ɔ. Ofi kyẽa bɔ Amnɔn tole Absalom aliɛma Tamar mmɔnaa ne, yeɛ Absalom bɔle sɔ porɛ ne ɔ.

english_verse: Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead,
translation_verse: Yiti Nana, me mene, nnɛdi edwirɛ he anwo aworabɔlɛ, kyɛ ebiaa wɔ mma ne amukoraa yeɛ bahu bɛ ɔ; ofikyɛ Amnɔn ngome yeɛ bahu ye ɔ.”

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Absalom de wanwati. Biaa bɔ ɔwɛne kuro ne tole ye nye, na onwuni kyɛ ɛlɔen bie fi ye si dɔ bɛtorotoro bokaa ne bɛba ɔ.

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Na Yonadabo sele Nana Dawide kyɛ, “Nana, kyɛbɔ wɔ somvoɛ ngane ne, sɔ ala yeɛ ɔte ɔ. Wɔ mma nemɔ yeɛ bɛ́ba ne.”

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: Ye noa pene pɛ, yeɛ Nana Dawide mma nemɔ wale ɔ. Besuni bɛbɔle awuye, na Dawide ne ye somvoɛ ne amukoraa koso besuni hahii.

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: Afei Nana Dawide wora lɔle Absalom, ofikyɛ Amnɔn wue asi ne, nziɛ ye Dawide wora kyekyele.

english_verse: Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom,
translation_verse: Seruya awa Yoabo nwuni kyɛ Absalom nwo adwenedwene atɔ Nana Dawide so.

english_verse: The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
translation_verse: Braa bɔ ofi Tekoa ne wale Nana Dawide berɛ nen, ɔbɔle ye ti ase kotole ye, na osele kyɛ, “Nana, mesrɛ wɔ, boka me!”

english_verse: David asked, “What's the matter?” She replied: My husband is dead, and I'm a widow.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Dawide bisale ye kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ yeɛ ehia ɔ?” Obuale kyɛ, “Nana, nde kunaniɛ, me hu awu.

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: W’afaneɛ, né nne mmaa mmienzua nyɔ. Bɛɛhone ngondii wɔ eburo. Né ebiala nne berɛ bɔ ɔkɔpata bɛ ɔ, na ko bɔle obiɛngo maa owuli.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Na abusua ne amukoraa badwɔso w’afaneɛ so kyɛ, ‘Ko bɔ wabɔ oliɛma wahũ ye ne, ye ye bra ma yɛhu ye bie yɛtua kerɛ, ɔmva ye nwo kyɛ koliagyaa ne yeɛ yɛku ye yɛfi berɛ ɔ.’ Nana, bɛpena kyɛ benua me gyetia ko bɔ waha ne, na ɛhe kɔma me hu dumaa anaa ye boso konunu kofi aseɛ ye aso.”

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Na Nana Dawide sele braa ne kyɛ, “Wɔ de, kɔ w’awuro, na ngɔnea ngosiesie edwirɛ ne ngɔma wɔ.”

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ braa bɔ ofi Tekoa ne sele Nana Dawide kyɛ, “Nana, me mene, mede meto nu kyɛ, me ne me baba abusuafoɛ yeɛ yɛdi edwirɛ he anwo fɔ ɔ. Nakoso Nana, ɛne wɔ bia de, ɛmɔdi ye nwo be.”

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Dawide buale kyɛ, “Sɛ ebie ha wɔ a, fa ye brɛ me, na ɔngɔha wɔ ko.”

english_verse: “Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!” He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
translation_verse: Na braa ne sele kyɛ, “Nana, fa AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ ta ndaen, bɔ ɔnate so wereɛtɔlɛniɛ ne ɔngɔhã mogya ko ngogua ɔ, amaa ɔnate so mma ne anya ye ti wadidi nu.” Na Dawide sele kyɛ, “Kyɛ AWURADE te ase ye, ɛwa ne, ye ti nwiaa ko po ngotu ngɔtɔ ase.”

english_verse: Then she asked, “Your Majesty, may I say something?” “Yes,” he answered.
translation_verse: Afei braa ne sele kyɛ, “Nana, me mene, mesrɛ wɔ ala, ma w’afaneɛ ɔha edwirɛ kãa hyire wɔ.” Na Dawide sele kyɛ, “Kɔ so.”

english_verse: The woman said: Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back.
translation_verse: Yeɛ braa ne sele kyɛ, “Né nzaade, nzu ati yeɛ abɔ Nyameɛ mmenia nwo porɛ sɔa ɔ? Nana, wɔ bɔbɔ wɔ noa dwirɛ abua wɔ fɔ, ofikyɛ ɛwa bɔ afoa ye afi wɔ nwo ne, ɛmbena kyɛ esa fa ye ba awuro.

english_verse: We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
translation_verse: Ewue de, yɛ mukoraa yɛkowu. Yɛte kyɛ nzue bɔ bahwie bagua ase, bɔ bɛsesa a ɔnyɛ yé ɔ. Nyameɛ de, ɔnga mogya ngua, na mmom ebiala bɔ ɔne ye b’afia atete ne, ole nhyehyɛleɛ bɔ ɔnate so osa twe ye bata ye nwo ɔ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: Yiti Nana, me mene, mawa kyɛ mebaaha sɔ dwirɛ he mekyire wɔ, ofikyɛ mmenia amaa masuro. W’afaneɛ, nzusuli kyɛ, ‘Ngɔɔfa edwirɛ ne ngɔto Nana nyunu; ebiaa Nana kɔyɔ ye afaneɛ abisadeɛ kɔma ye.

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: Mese kyɛ Nana kotie me, na sona bɔ ɔpena kyɛ oku me ne mma, ná ɔye yɛ fi Nyameɛ agyapadeɛ nu ne, Nana kole ye afaneɛ kofi ye sa nu.’

english_verse: I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
translation_verse: Nana, me mene, w’afaneɛ susuli kyɛ, ‘Wɔ noa dwirɛ kɔma me soa nu kɔtɔ me.’ Ofikyɛ Nana, me mene, ɛte kyɛ Nyameɛ abɔfo, na ɛse paa ne bɔne nu nzonzoleɛ. AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ ne, ogyina wɔ si.”

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Na Nana Dawide buale braa ne kyɛ, “Edwirɛ bɔ mebaabisa wɔ ye, ka nu nahorɛ.” Na braa ne sele kyɛ, “Nana, me mene, bisa.”

english_verse: David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?” The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say,
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Dawide bisale ye kyɛ, “Sɔ dwirɛ he, aso nna Yoabo yeɛ wapesa wawura wɔ ɔ?” Na braa ne buale kyɛ, “Nana, me mene, aha ato me deɛ ne aso. Bɔ aha ne te nahorɛ turoloo. Amba, wɔ somvoɛ Yoabo yeɛ ohyirele me kyɛ nyɔ sɔ ɔ. Ye yeɛ ɔfale edwirɛ he amukoraa tuale w’afaneɛ noa ɔ.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: Wɔ somvoɛ Yoabo yɔle sɔ, kyɛbɔ engonwu edwirɛ ne asi ɔ. Nakoso me mene, ɛse nworɛ kyɛ Nyameɛ abɔfo ala, bɔ ɔmaa enwu aseɛ ye aso dwirɛ amukoraa ɔ.”

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: Afei Nana Dawide sele Yoabo kyɛ, “Mate, mepene wɔ nzusuleɛ ne aso. Kɔfa aberandeɛ Absalom maa osa bra.”

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Yiti Yoabo sili nu hɔle Gesure ɔɔfale Absalom wale Yerusalem.

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: Nakoso Nana Dawide sele kyɛ, “Maa ɔɔtena ye bɔbɔ ye awuro. Membena kyɛ menwu ye nyunu.” Yiti Absalom ɔɔtenane ye bɔbɔ ye awuro, na wambe Nana Dawide nyunu. Dawide fa Absalom nwo kyɛ ye

english_verse: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
translation_verse: Sɛ né ɔtete ye ti a, ɔkari enwiaa ne, na nu nonɛ te kilo nyɔ ne bue, kyɛbɔ ahemvie berɛ kilo nu nonɛ te ɔ.

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: Absalom wole mmaa mmienzua nza ne brasua ko. Brasua ne li Tamar. Ɔte brasua bɔ ye nwo yɛ nyemene ɔ.

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Absalom lili afoɛ nyɔ mumua wɔ Yerusalem, bɔ wannwu Nana Dawide nyunu ɔ.

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Absalom somane kyɛ bɛɛfrɛ Yoabo bɛbrɛ ye ma ɔsoma ye Nana Dawide berɛ, nakoso Yoabo amma. Ɔsomane maa bɛhɔle Yoabo berɛ ye pɛen nyɔ so, nakoso wamma.

english_verse: Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
translation_verse: Yiti Absalom sele ye somvoɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔtie, Yoabo boo bɔ ɔne me deɛ bɛbɔ wɛen ne, ayuo wɔ nu. Ɛmɔhɔ bɛɛto nu see.” Na Absalom somvoɛ nemɔ bɛɛtole eboo ne anu see.

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yoabo sili nu hɔle Absalom berɛ wɔ ye awuro oobisale ye kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ wɔ somvoɛ nemɔ baato me boo ne anu see ɔ?”

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Na Absalom buale Yoabo kyɛ, “Tie, ndole wɔ ngraa kyɛ ɛbra wa maa mva ngraa nzoma wɔ Nana Dawide berɛ kyɛ, ‘Ɛwa bɔ mvili Gesure mmale ye, ye nwo mvasoɛ ole sɛɛ? Sɛ ndɛ wɔ dɔ po a, ahaa ɔte paa.’ Afei de, maa ngɔ Nana nyunu, na sɛ medi fɔ a, ohu me!”

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Yiti Yoabo hɔle Nana Dawide berɛ ɔɔbɔle ye amaneɛ. Dawide maa bɛɛfrɛle Absalom. Absalom wale Nana Dawide berɛ, na ɔtole ye nwo yele berɛ fale ye nyunu butuli berɛ wɔ Dawide nyunu, na Nana Dawide tɔle ye nu.

english_verse: Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had
translation_verse: Ɛhe asi ye, Absalom fale teaseɛnam ne mbɔngɔ, ɔne mmienzua aburannu bɔ bɛkɔbɔ ye nwo waen ɔ.

english_verse: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
translation_verse: Alebahyene biala, atee bɔ ɔkɔ kuro berɛ pambim ne anu ne, ɔyɛ a né Absalom dwɔso kogyina so. Na sɛ ebie ɔ́fa ye dwirɛ ba Nana Dawide gya so maa odi a, ɔyɛ a Absalom frɛ ye bisa ye kyɛ, “Efi kuro beni aso?” Na sɛ sɔ sona ne bua ye kyɛ, “W’akoaa, mvi sɔ abusua kure he anu,” a,

english_verse: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
translation_verse: ɔyɛ a Absalom ka kyire ye kyɛ, “Nea, wɔ dwirɛ yɛ fɛ paa, nakoso ebiala nne berɛ bɔ okogyina Nana gya nu okoli wɔ dwirɛ ne ɔ.”

english_verse: I wish someone would make me the judge around here! I would be fair to everyone.”
translation_verse: Osa toa so ka kyɛ, “Ɔhale me ngome a, ahaa nde ndɛenbualɛniɛ wɔ maen ye anu. Ahaa ebiala bɔ ole nguro bɔ ne, ɔkɔwa me berɛ maa ngoli ye dwirɛ ngɔma ye.”

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Né sɛ ebie ba Absalom berɛ kyɛ ɔbaabɔ ye ti ase koto ye a, ɔyɛ a Absalom tɔ ye nu yɛ ye atuu.

english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Na Yisraelniɛ biala bɔ ɔwale Nana Dawide berɛ kyɛ ɔbaafa ye dwirɛ to ye nyunu ne, sɔ ala yeɛ Absalom yɛle ye ɔ. Yiti Absalom yɔle sɔ hwene mmenia ne wale ye bue nu.

english_verse: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
translation_verse: Afoɛ nna asi ne, Absalom sele Nana Dawide kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, mahyɛ AWURADE bɔ, yiti ma me ate ma ngɔ Hebron ngondua ye aboadeɛ ne.

english_verse: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ, wɔ somvoɛ, mmerɛ bɔ né nwɔ Gesure bɔ ɔwɔ Siria ne, nhyɛle bɔ kyɛ, ‘Sɛ AWURADE sa fa me kɔ Yerusalem a, ye de ngɔsɔne AWURADE [wɔ Hebron].’ ”

english_verse: David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron.
translation_verse: Na Nana Dawide sele ye kyɛ, “Kɔ asomdwee nu.” Yiti osili nu hɔle Hebron.

english_verse: A messenger came and told David, “Everyone in Israel is on Absalom's side!”
translation_verse: Ɛbɔfoɛ bie wale Dawide berɛ ɔɔbɔle ye amaneɛ kyɛ, “Yisraelfoɛ ayakyi wɔ si lilɛ bahɔ Absalom bue nu.”

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide sele ye mbanyi amukoraa bɔ bɛ ne ye wɔ Yerusalem berɛ ne kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔhã bɛ nwo! Ɛ́mɔma yɛnwati, anyɔ a Absalom ngɔmma yɛngonya yɛ ti ngodidi nu. Ɛ́mɔhã bɛ nwo. Sɛ ɔbato yɛ a, okohũhũ yɛ, na ɔkɔfa ngrandɛ kohũhũ kuro wa ama.”

english_verse: The officials said, “Your Majesty, we'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Na Nana Dawide mbanyi nemɔ sele ye kyɛ, “Nana, yɛ mene, bɔ ɛkɔha kyɛ wɔ ngoaa yɛyɔ biala, yɛkɔyɔ.”

english_verse: David left behind ten of his wives to take care of the palace, but the rest of his family and his officials and soldiers went with him. They stopped at the last house at the edge of the city.
translation_verse: Nana Dawide sili nu, bɔ né mmenia ne amukoraa beli ye si ɔ, na beegyinane kuro tiwaa sua bie anwo.

english_verse: Then David stood there and watched while his regular troops and his bodyguards marched past. The last group was the
translation_verse: Ye mbanyi ne amu bɛɛse bɛpɛle nu wɔ ye nyunu. Na Keretifoɛ amu, Peletifoɛ amu, yeɛ Gitifoɛ ɛyaa nzia amu bɔ belili ye si befili Gate ne, bɛ koso bɛɛpɛle nu wɔ ye nyunu.

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Dawide bisale Gitiniɛ Yitae kyɛ, “Wɔ koso, nzu ati yeɛ ɛboka yɛ so ɛne yɛ kɔ ɔ? Sa kɔ, ná kɔtena bɔ wasi ye nwo hene ne anwo; ofikyɛ ɛte amanvraniɛ, na basa bapɛ wɔ asue bafi wɔ maen nu.

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: Anomasi wa ala yeɛ ɛwale ɔ. Aso ɔfata kyɛ kekesaala ye memaa ɛne yɛ kokyinikyini anaa, wɔ aberɛ bɔ menze nekaa po bɔ mékɔ ɔ? Fa w’abusuafoɛ nemɔ boka wɔ nwo so ná sa kɔ. Mesrɛ kyɛ AWURADE ma enwu ye nahorɛlilɛ ne ye anwumvoinnwunɛ ne.”

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Yitae buale Nana Dawide kyɛ, “Kyɛ AWURADE te ase ye, ɔne kyɛ Nana, me mene, wɔ koso ɛte ase ye, nekaa biala bɔ Nana, me mene, ɛkɔhɔ ne, ewue nu oo, ngoa nu oo, berɛ yeɛ wɔ somvoɛ me koso ngɔhɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide sele Yitae kyɛ, “Nzaade, baasẽ ma yɛhɔ.” Yiti Gitiniɛ Yitae ne ye mmienzua mukoraa ne ye abusua mukoraa bɔ bɛboka ye so ne, bɛɛse bɛhɔle.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: Dawide ne ye mmenia ne amukoraa, mmerɛ bɔ né bɛse bɛkɔ ne, Yerusalem kurotue ne amu besuni bɛbɔle awuye. Nana Dawide pɛle Kidron bɔnza ne. Na mmenia bɔ bɛboka ye so ne amukoraa pɛle bɔnza ne bɛfale bɛ nye behyirele ɛserɛ ne aso.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Né Abiata, Sadoke, ɔne Lewifoɛ amukoraa bɔ bɛso Nyameɛ apam alaka ne, bɛ koso bɛboka bɛ so. Na besikyele alaka ne besiele berɛ toonn maa oodwuli kyɛ mmenia ne amu befili kuro ne anu bɛse bɛhɔle ɔ.

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: Na Nana Dawide sele Sadoke kyɛ, “Fa Nyameɛ alaka ne sa kɔ kuro ne anu. Sɛ ebiaa AWURADE nwu me anwumvoin a, ɔkɔmaa ngosa ngɔwa ngoonwu alaka ne, ɔne nekaa bɔ ogyi ɔ.

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ ɔka kyɛ, ‘Ɛnzɔ me nye’ a, mepene so. Bɔ okuro biala, maa ɔfa yɛ me.”

english_verse: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
translation_verse: Na Nana Dawide sa sele Sadoke kyɛ, “Aso nna wɔ yeɛ ɛte Nyameɛ sona bɔ ɛse ase ɔ. Sa kɔ kuro nu dɔ asomdwee nu; ɛne ɛwa Ahimaase, yeɛ Abiata ne ɔwa Yonatan, ɛmɔ mma nyɔ nemɔ.

english_verse: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔtie, mékɔ ɛserɛ so apɛleɛ berɛ, na ngɔnwondɛ kɔpem kyɛ me sa kɔhã ɛmɔ ngraa ɔ.”

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: Yiti Sadoke ne Abiata fale Nyameɛ alaka ne besa bɛhɔle Yerusalem, na bɛtenane berɛ.

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: Dawide fo hɔle Olive bokaa ne aso. Ɔfo kɔ ne, né osũ, né wakata ye ti so, yeɛ né ye gya gua ase. Mmenia bɔ bɛboka ye so ne amu bɛkatale bɛ ti so, na bɛfale esuɛ yeɛ bɛfo bɛhɔle ɔ.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: Yeɛ ebie bɔle Dawide amaneɛ kyɛ, mmenia bɔ bɛ ne Absalom babɔ ye ti so porɛ ne, Ahitofel boka so. Na Dawide sele kyɛ, “AWURADE, mesrɛ wɔ, ma Ahitofel foɛtulɛ ne ɔyɛ ngwaseaa foɛtulɛ.”

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: Dawide dwuli bokaa ne ti afia, wɔ nekaa bɔ mmenia sɔne Nyameɛ ne. Na mvum nu, Akiniɛ Husae wale ooyiale ye. Né wasunzua ye ndaadeɛ nu, na né wafa nnɛterɛ koso wayɛ ye ti so.

english_verse: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
translation_verse: Na Dawide sele ye kyɛ, “Sɛ ɛne me kɔ a, ɛkɔyɛ me so tɔsom.

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ esa kɔ kuro nu dɔ, ná ɛkã kyire Absalom kyɛ, ‘Nana Absalom, ngɔyɛ wɔ somvoɛ, kyɛbɔ mmerɛ bie bɔ wapɛ nu ɔ nyɛle wɔ baba somvoɛ nen, sɔ ala yeɛ ngɔyɛ wɔ somvoɛ ɔ’ a, ye de ɛkɔbɔ Ahitofel foɛtulɛ ne kogua kɔma me.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Asɔfo Sadoke ne Abiata bɛwɔ dɔ bɔ bɛkɔboka wɔ so ɔ. Na edwirɛ biala bɔ ɛkɔte ye wɔ ɛhene n’ahemvie berɛ ne, ma Sadoke ne Abiata bɛ so te.

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: Yiti Dawide adamvo Husae sa hɔle Yerusalem, wɔ mmerɛ bɔ né Absalom ɔkwaawura kuro ne anu ɔ.

english_verse: David had started down the other side of the Mount of Olives, when he was met by Ziba, the chief servant of Mephibosheth. Ziba had two donkeys that were carrying
translation_verse: Dawide trale bokaa ne ti afia hɔle ye nyunu kãa ne, mvum nu, Mefibosɛte somvoɛ Siba wale ooyiale ye. Ɔfale afunum nyɔ wale. Né bɛso paanoo ɛyaa nyɔ, bobe bɔ babobɔ ye kunguma ɛyaa ko, borɔdoma ɛyaa ko, yeɛ bobe nzaa kɔndoa ko.

english_verse: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Dawide bisale Siba kyɛ, “Sɔ nningyein hemɔ, ɛfa bayɔ nzu?” Na Siba buale kyɛ, “Afunum nemɔ, méfa mebrɛ Nana awuro ama maa bɛtena so. Paanoo ne ɔne borɔdoma ne, bɛte mmerandeɛ nemɔ deɛ bɔ bekoli ɔ, yeɛ nzaa ne koso ɔte bɛ bɔ bɛ nwo kɔyɛ bɛ hodwoo wɔ ɛserɛ so ne deɛ.”

english_verse: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
translation_verse: Na Nana Dawide bisale ye kyɛ, “Wɔ mene awa bienzua ne, ɔwɔ ni?” Yeɛ Siba buale Nana Dawide kyɛ, “Ɔwɔ Yerusalem, na ɔnwa: ‘Ɛnɛ kyẽa ye, Yisrael awuro ama kosa kɔfa me nana ahennie ne kɔma me.’ ”

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Dawide sele Siba kyɛ, “Ofi ɛnɛ bɔ ɔkɔ ɔ, Mefibosɛte nikyee biala bɔ ole ye ne, wayɛ wɔ deɛ.” Na Siba sele kyɛ, “Nana, me mene, mekoto wɔ. W’adaworoma, do me.” Simei boro Dawide amoen

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Nana Dawide oodwuli Bahurim nen, mvum nu, biaa bie bɔ oli Simei bɔ ofi Sɔɔlo abusua nu wale berɛ. Ye baba ole Gera. Ɔ́ba ne, né ɔ́boro amoen.

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: Simei borole Nana Dawide ne ye somvoɛ amukoraa nyɔboɛ. Né Dawide mmenia ne amu ne koɛhonɛfoɛ ne amu begua ye bɛen ne ye famaa.

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: Amoen bɔ Simei borole ne ɛhe: “Fi wa kɔ! Fi wa kɔ! Wudiniɛ! Ɛte busueniɛ!

english_verse: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
