translation_verse: Sɔɔlo bɔ atu ye ali ye bia ne, ye abusuafoɛ mogya mukoraa bɔ aha agua ne, AWURADE atua wɔ so kerɛ! AWURADE ale ahennie ne wafi wɔ sa nu wama ɛwa Absalom. Abue yeɛ wabu wɔ ɔ, ofikyɛ ɛte kodiawuniɛ!”

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Na Seruya awa Abisae sele Nana Dawide kyɛ, “Me mene, ɔwale ye sɛ bɔ sɔ kyea fuin he ɔboro wɔ amoen ɔ? Nana, maa ngɔnde ye ti mvi so.”

english_verse: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
translation_verse: Nakoso Nana Dawide buale ye kyɛ, “Ɛmɔ Seruya mma ye mɔ, me dwirɛ fa ɛmɔ nwo nzu? Amoen bɔ ɔ́boro ye, sɛ AWURADE yeɛ waha wahyire ye kyɛ, ‘Boro Dawide amoen,’ a, nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora kobisa ye kyɛ, ‘Nzu ati yeɛ ɛ́yɔ sɔ ɔ?’ ”

english_verse: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
translation_verse: Na Dawide sele Abisae ne somvoɛ ne amu kyɛ, “Sɛ me kunu ba po ɔpena me ku me a; nzaade bɔ Benyaminniɛ he ɔ́yɔ ye, ɔnyɛ nwanwa! Ɛ́mɔyakyi ye ma ɔboro amoen ne. Ebiaa AWURADE yeɛ waha wahyire ye kyɛ ɔyɔ sɔ ɔ.

english_verse: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
translation_verse: Ebiaa AWURADE kɔnea m’amaneɛnwunɛ ye, na ɔkɔkakyi amoen bɔ baboro me ɛnɛ ye maa ngonya saleɛ.”

english_verse: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
translation_verse: Afei Dawide ne ye mmenia nemɔ toale so bɛfale atee ne aso, yeɛ Simei koso fale bokaa ne ngyɛnu dɔ lili bɛ mvanvando. Ɔ́kɔ ne, né ogu so ɔboro Dawide amoen, ɔboro ye nyɔboɛ, ná osa tu mvuture gua ye so.

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Nana Dawide ne ye mmenia ne amukoraa beedwuli asue Yɔɔdan noa nen, né bafɛ, na olele ye nwome wɔ berɛ. Ahitofel tu Absalom foɛ tɛɛ

english_verse: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Absalom ne Yisrael mmienzua mukoraa bɛwale Yerusalem, bɔ né Ahitofel boka ye so ɔ.

english_verse: David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Akiniɛ Husae bɔ ɔte Dawide adamvo ne, ɔwale Absalom berɛ, na obisale Absalom ahye kyɛ, “Nana, wɔ ngoa so oo! Nana, wɔ ngoa so oo!”

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Na Absalom bisale ye kyɛ, “Eh, wɔ nahorɛ bɔ édi ma wɔ damvo ɛhe? Nzu ati yeɛ ɛne wɔ damvo bangɔ ɔ”

english_verse: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
translation_verse: Na Husae buale Absalom kyɛ, “Daabi oo, sona bɔ AWURADE ne mmenia bɔ bayia wa ye, ɔne Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa baneanea nu baye ye ne, ye yeɛ ngyi ye si ɔ, na ye bue nu yeɛ nwɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.” Ahithophel's Advice
translation_verse: Asa koso, sɛ manzo Dawide awa ne a, né nwa yeɛ ngɔnzo ye ɔ? Na kyɛbɔ nzole wɔ baba ne, sɔ ala yeɛ ngɔso wɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Absalom sele Ahitofel kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔhyire ɛmɔ adwene; nzu yeɛ ɔsɛ kyɛ yɛyɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
translation_verse: Na Ahitofel buale Absalom kyɛ, “Wɔ baba sómaa mɔ bɔ wayakyi bɛ berɛ kyɛ bɛnea awuro berɛ ne, ɛne bɛ bɛɛla. Na sɛ Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa bɛte kyɛ agua ɛse anyunu ase pɔtɔɔ a, ɔkɔhyɛ mmenia bɔ begyi wɔ si ne nguraen.”

english_verse: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
translation_verse: Yiti besili ɛtena sua wɔ sua ne aso anwuro nekaa bɔ basamo ne, na Absalom ne ɔse sómaa nemɔ bɛɛlale bɔ Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa bɛ nye tua ɔ.

english_verse: Ahithophel gave such good advice in those days that both Absalom and David thought it came straight from God.
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Ahitofel foɛ biala bɔ otu ne, né ɛnwa nzɛ ɔte Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ. Yiti né Dawide ne Absalom bɛndoto Ahitofel foɛtulɛ biala ase koraa.

english_verse: and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die!
translation_verse: Nekaa biala bɔ waafea ne, yɛkoofite ye so. Na kyɛbɔ bosue gua doadoa aseɛnwo amukoraa ne, sɔ ala yeɛ yɛkɔhɔ ye so yɛkohu ye ɔ. Ɔne ye koɛhonɛfoɛ ne, bɛ nu ko po ngonya ye ti ngodidi nu.

english_verse: while he is tired and discouraged. He will panic, and everyone with him will run away. I won't kill anyone except David,
translation_verse: Ngɔhɔ ye so wɔ mmerɛ bɔ wafɛ ná ye aba nu bu ɔ. Ngɔma ye nye so kɔtane ye maa mmenia bɔ bɛboka ye so ne amu kɔnwati. Ngohũ Dawide angome,

english_verse: since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war. Hushai Fools Absalom
translation_verse: na ngɔfa mmenia bɔ beli ye si ne amu ngosa ngɔbrɛ wɔ. Sɛ bɛ mukoraa besa bɛba, bɔ sona bɔ ɛpena ye ku ye ne, ye de ɔbboka bɛ so bie a, ye de mmenia ne amukoraa bɛkɔwa asomdwee nu.”

english_verse: Absalom and all the leaders of the tribes of Israel agreed that Ahithophel had a good plan.
translation_verse: Na Absalom ne Yisrael mbanyi amukoraa belele sɔ foɛtulɛ ne bɛtole nu. Husae bɔ Ahitofel foɛtulɛ ne gua

english_verse: Then Absalom said, “Bring in Hushai the Archite. Let's hear what he has to say.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Absalom hane kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔfrɛ Akiniɛ Husae koso bɛbra ma yɛtie bɔ ole ye ka ɔ.”

english_verse: Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
translation_verse: Na Husae oodwuli Absalom nwo berɛ nen, Absalom sele ye kyɛ, “Bɔ Ahitofel aha hɔ ɛhe. Ɛnea a, ɔte paa kyɛ yɛkɔfa ye foɛtulɛ ne anaa? Sɛ ɔtte mayee a, wɔ koso kyire w’adwene.”

english_verse: Hushai said: This time Ahithophel's advice isn't so good.
translation_verse: Na Husae buale Absalom kyɛ, “Foɛ bɔ Ahitofel atu ye kekesaala ye de, ɔtte mayee.”

english_verse: You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others.
translation_verse: Na Husae toale so sele kyɛ, “Ɛse kyɛ wɔ baba ne ye mmenia nemɔ bɛte koɛhonɛfoɛ, na bɛ nye aboro kyɛ kwabrafo bɔ ebie ahye ye mma wɔ eburo ɔ. Asa koso, wɔ baba se koɛ ko paa, na ɔne koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bɛngɔla neka horɛ kɔngɔen.

english_verse: He has probably already found a hiding place in a cave or somewhere else. As soon as anyone hears that some of your soldiers have been killed, everyone will think your whole army has been destroyed.
translation_verse: Na kekesaala ye po, waafea kumaa bie anu, anaa nekaa bie. Sɛ yɛfa koɛ yɛkɔɔtoa bɛ, ná yɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bie totɔ a, ye de ebiala bɔ ɔkɔte ne, ɔkɔha kyɛ, ‘Mmenia bɔ beli Absalom si ne, batotɔ.’

english_verse: Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɔba ye sɔ a, koɛhonɛniɛ bɔ ye ahone yɛ se te kyɛ gyata ne po, ɔkɔbɔ fuin. Ofikyɛ Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa bɛse kyɛ wɔ baba te koɛhonɛniɛ, yeɛ ye mmenia nemɔ koso bɛte koɛhonɛfoɛ ahoneserɛfoɛ.

english_verse: My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself,
translation_verse: Me de, métu wɔ foɛ kyɛ, ma Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa, ofi Dan bɔ ɔkwaadwu Beɛ Hyeba, bɔ bɛ somaa te kyɛ mboanoa anweaa, bɛɛboa bɛ noa wɔ wɔ nyunu, ná wɔ bɔbɔ di bɛ nyunu kɔ koɛ ne.

english_verse: If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɔnwati kɔfea kuro bie anu a, Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa kɔfa nyamaa kɔsosɔ sɔ kuro ne, na yɛkɔhwe kuro ne ase yɛkɔɔto bɔnza nu, kɔpem kyɛ nyɔboɛ ko po ngɔha berɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Absalom and the others liked Hushai's plan better than Ahithophel's plan. This was because the Lord had decided to keep Ahithophel's plan from working and to cause trouble for Absalom. Jonathan and Ahimaaz Tell David the News
translation_verse: Yeɛ Absalom ne Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa besele kyɛ, “Akiniɛ Husae foɛ ne, ɔte paa tra Ahitofel deɛ ne.” Ofikyɛ né AWURADE ahyehyɛ kyɛ ɔkɔma Ahitofel foɛ bɔ ɔte paa ne kɔyɛ mbaen, amaa ɔnate so AWURADE aprapra amaneɛ wagua Absalom so. Husae tia Dawide gya so

english_verse: At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Husae hã hyirele asɔfo Sadoke ne Abiata kyɛ, “Foɛ bɔ Ahitofel atu Absalom ne Yisrael mbanyi hɔ ɛne; yeɛ me koso foɛ bɔ matu hɔ ɛhe.

english_verse: Then he said, “Hurry! Send someone to warn David not to spend the night on this side of the Jordan. He must get across the river, so he and the others won't be wiped out!”
translation_verse: Yiti ɛ́mɔsoma ma beese Dawide ndɛndɛ kyɛ, ‘Nnɛtena ɛserɛ so apɛleɛ berɛ ɛnɛ kɔngɔen, na mmom pɛ nu kɔ ndɛndɛ. Nana, sɛ anyɔ sɔ a, ɛne wɔ koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa ɛmɔ boso konua.’ ”

english_verse: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David.
translation_verse: Né Yonatan ne Ahimaase baatetɛ wɔ Ɛn Rogyel, ofikyɛ né bɛmbena kyɛ bɛkɔ kuro ne anu dɔ maa benwu bɛ. Yiti né afaneɛ abaayaa bie yeɛ ɔfa ngraa ne kɔma bɛ maa bɛkɔbɔ Nana Dawide amaneɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Nakoso abɛɛmaa bie nye pɛle bɛ so, na ɔɔbɔle Absalom amaneɛ. Yiti bɛ munyɔ befili berɛ bɛnwatili ndɛndɛ, na bɛhɔle biaa bie awuro wɔ Bahurim. Né ole abura wɔ ye awuro berɛ, na bedwuli nu.

english_verse: The man's wife put the cover on the well and poured grain on top of it, so the well could not be seen.
translation_verse: Biaa n’aye fale nikyee katale abura ne aso, na ɔfale aburoo guale so trɛtrɛle nu. Yiti ebiala adwene angɔ so.

english_verse: Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered, “They went across that stream.” The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Absalom somvoɛ nemɔ bɛɛtole braa ne wɔ awuro berɛ ne, bebisale ye kyɛ, “Ahimaase ne Yonatan bɛwɔ nisua?” Na braa ne buale bɛ kyɛ, “Bapɛ asue ne bahɔ.” Bɛpenane bɛ alaa, nakoso bannwu bɛ, yiti besa bɛhɔle Yerusalem.

english_verse: After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
translation_verse: Nziɛ ye bɔ Absalom somvoɛ nemɔ besa bɛhɔle ne, Ahimaase ne Yonatan fili abura ne anu fitele, na bɛɛbɔle Nana Dawide amaneɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔdwɔso bɛɛpɛ asue ne ndɛndɛ, ofikyɛ ɛmɔ nwo foɛ tɛɛ bɔ Ahitofel atu hɔ ɛhe.”

english_verse: David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side. Ahithophel Kills Himself
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide ne ɛlɔen amukoraa bɔ bɛboka ye so ne, besili nu bɛɛpɛle asue Yɔɔdan. Na aleɛ hyene ne, né bɛ nu biala apɛ asue Yɔɔdan.

english_verse: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom and the leaders of Israel were not going to follow his advice, he saddled his donkey and rode back to his home in Gilo. He told his family and servants what to do. Then he hanged himself, and they buried him in his family's burial place. Absalom Puts Amasa in Charge of the Army
translation_verse: Na Ahitofel nwuni kyɛ bamva ye foɛ bɔ watu nen, ɔfale ye nningyein tale ye afunum si, na osili nu hɔle ye awuro wɔ ye kuro. Ɔtotole ye si yé, na afei ɔɔbɔle ye kɔme. Owuli, na besiele ye wɔ ye baba asieleɛ nu.

english_verse: David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel.
translation_verse: Afei Dawide oodwuli Mahanaim, na Absalom ne Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa bɛɛpɛle asue Yɔɔdan.

english_verse: Absalom put Amasa in Joab's place as commander of the army. Amasa's father was Ithra from the family of Ishmael, and his mother was Abigal, the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah.
translation_verse: Absalom bɔle Amasa safohene maa ɔlale ye lɔen ne noa sili Yoabo gya nu. Né Amasa te Yisraelniɛ biaa bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Yitra ɔwa. Sɔ biaa ne, ogyale Nahase awa Abigail bɔ ɔte Yoabo maame Seruya aliɛma brasua ne.

english_verse: The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead. Friends Bring Supplies to David
translation_verse: Absalom ne Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ kyekyele asikyeleɛ wɔ Gileade aseɛ so.

english_verse: After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Dawide oodwuli Mahanaim nen, Nahase bɔ ofi Amonfoɛ kuro Raba ne, ɔwa Sobi, ɔne Amiɛl bɔ ofi Lodeba ɔwa Makyiri, yeɛ Gileadeniɛ Basilae bɔ ofi Rogelim,

english_verse: Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese. They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_verse: woɛ, nandwie nyɔfonesue nye loe, mmoaen, ɔne nandwie nyɔfonesue bɔ babobɔ ye kunguma bɛbrɛle Dawide ne koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛboka ye so ne kyɛ beli. Ofikyɛ bɛhane kyɛ, “Ɛhɔen ne nzuhɔen ahu koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ wɔ ɛserɛ ye aso maa bayɛ bohoo.”

english_verse: He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
translation_verse: Dawide hyɛle koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ nu kure nza: ɔfale ko wurale Yoabo sa, ɔfale ko wurale Yoabo aliɛma Abisae bɔ oni ole Seruya ne sa, yeɛ ɔfale ko wora wurale Gitiniɛ Yitae sa. Na Nana Dawide sele koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “Me bɔbɔ me ne ɛmɔ yɛkɔhɔ koɛ ne.”

english_verse: But the soldiers said, “No, don't go into battle with us! It won't matter to our enemies if they make us all run away, or even if they kill half of us. But you are worth
translation_verse: Nakoso koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ sele kyɛ, “Daabi, yɛsrɛ wɔ, ɛngɔ bie. Ofikyɛ sɛ yɛnwati a, pɔfoɛ nemɔ ngobu ye nikyee titire bie. Yeɛ sɛ yɛ mmenia ne bue totɔ po a, ye koso bengobu ye nikyee titire bie. Nakoso wɔ de, wɔ nwo hia te kyɛ yɛ nu mmenia apee buru. Yiti sɛ ɛtena kuro wa, ná ɛsoma maa bɛfa nningyein bɔ yɛhia ɔ bɛbrɛ yɛ a, ɔte paa.”

english_verse: and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
translation_verse: Biaa bie nwuni ye, na ɔɔbɔle Yoabo amaneɛ kyɛ, “Baanea! Manwu kyɛ Absalom sinze eluii bie aso ɔ.”

english_verse: Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
translation_verse: Koɛ ne trɛ hɔle porɛ ne anu amukoraa. Na mmenia bɔ bewuwuli ɛhɔayeɛ ne anu sɔ kyẽa nen, bɛsone bɛtra bɛ bɔ bɛtotɔle ngrandɛ noa ɔ.

english_verse: Absalom was riding his mule under a huge tree when his head caught in the branches. The mule ran off and left Absalom hanging in midair. Some of David's soldiers happened by,
translation_verse: Mvum nu, Absalom ne Dawide koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bɔle numbunumbu. Né Absalom te ye afunum so. Afunum ne fale ye ɔɔfale eluii bie bɔ ye mmaen ayɛ sesakaa ɔ bo. Absalom ti nwiaa sotale bakaa mmaen ne anu maa osinzele berɛ bɔ né ye gya nga ase ɔ. Nakoso afunum bɔ ɔte ye so ne de, ɔtoale so hɔle.

english_verse: Joab said, “You saw Absalom? Why didn't you kill him? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a special belt.”
translation_verse: Na Yoabo sele biaa bɔ ɔɔbɔle ye amaneɛ ne kyɛ, “Aaah! Anwu ye! Nzu ati yeɛ angu ye wɔ berɛ ɔ? Ahaa ngɔfa ɛdwetɛ buru ne abɔsoɛ ngɔbɔ wɔ aba so.”

english_verse: He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
translation_verse: Nana de, edwirɛ biala mvea ye. Sɛ ɔwale kyɛ nguni ye po a, ahaa wɔ bɔbɔ po yeɛ ɛkɔpɛ wɔ nwo ɛkɔye me kɔma ɔ.”

english_verse: Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!” Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest.
translation_verse: Na Yoabo sele kyɛ, “Mengɔma ɛngɔsɛkye me mmerɛ sɔ.” Yiti ɔfale pealɛɛ nza tirale, na ɔɔfa wowɔle Absalom ahone so anyekaenn so, wɔ mmerɛ bɔ né Absalom tɛ sinze bakaa ne aso ɔ.

english_verse: Ten of Joab's bodyguards came over and finished him off.
translation_verse: Yeɛ mmerandeɛ buru bɔ betiratira Yoabo akodeɛ ne, bɛpɛle Absalom nwo beyiale, na behuni ye.

english_verse: Then Joab blew a trumpet to signal his troops to stop chasing Israel's soldiers.
translation_verse: Afei Yoabo huli totorobɛndo ne anu, na koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ sale bɛ si bɔ bamvoa Yisraelfoɛ ko ɔ, ofikyɛ Yoabo maa bɛyakyili Yisraelfoɛ foalɛ.

english_verse: They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and put a big pile of rocks over it. Meanwhile, the people of Israel had all run back to their own homes.
translation_verse: Bɛyele Absalom, befindini ye bɛtole ɛhɔayeɛ ne anu kumaa piri bie anu, na bɛboaboale nyɔboɛ kure kandinga paa beguale ye so. Na Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa bɛnwati bɛhɔle b’awuro.

english_verse: When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today. Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ né Absalom te ase ne, nyɔboɛ bɔ ɔwɔ Ɛhene Bɔnza ne anu ne, ɔfa penane berɛ yɛle ye bɔbɔ ye nwo ngayeɛ, ofikyɛ ɔhane kyɛ, “Nnne baa bienzua biala bɔ ɔnate ye so bɛkɔkaye me dumaa ɔ.” Ɔfale ye dumaa tole ngayeɛ nyɔboɛ ne aso, na bɛfrɛ ye Absalom ngayeɛ maa waadwu ɛnɛ. Dawide te Absalom wue

english_verse: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sadoke awa Ahimaase sele kyɛ, “Maa ndu amirika mva ndɛenvɛen he ngɔmɔ Nana Dawide amaneɛ, kyɛ AWURADE ale ye wafi ye pɔfoɛ mɔ sa nu.”

english_verse: Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Yoabo sele ye kyɛ, “Ɛmva ndɛenvɛen ɛngɔ ɛnɛ biala! Maa ɔyɛ kyẽa foforɛ né afa ndɛenvɛen ne ahɔ. Ɛnɛ de, nnɛkɔ, ofikyɛ Nana awa yeɛ wawu ɔ.”

english_verse: Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
translation_verse: Afei Yoabo sele Kuseniɛ bie kyɛ, “Kɔ Nana Dawide berɛ kɔha bɔ anwu ye ɔ kyire ye.” Kuseniɛ ne bɔle ye ti ase wɔ Yoabo nyunu, na afei ɔsɔle amirika tulɛ nu.

english_verse: Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.” Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sadoke awa Ahimaase sele Yoabo bieku kyɛ, “Bɔ okosi biala, osi. Ma me koso ndu amirika nni Kuseniɛ ne asi.” Na Yoabo bisale ye kyɛ, “Mma, nzu ati yeɛ ɛpena kyɛ etu amirika po ye ɔ? Ɛse kyɛ amaneɛ bɔ ɛkwaabɔ ye, mvasoɛ biala ngɔwa so ngɔma wɔ.”

english_verse: “I'll run no matter what!” Ahimaaz insisted. “All right then, run!” Joab said. Ahimaaz took the road through the Jordan Valley and outran the Ethiopian.
translation_verse: Na Ahimaase buale kyɛ, “Bɔ okosi biala, osi. Ngotu amirika ngɔhɔ.” Yiti Yoabo sele ye kyɛ, “Tu amirika kɔ e.” Na Ahimaase tuli amirika ɔɔfale Yɔɔdan noa aseɛ frɛtɛɛ ne aso dɔ sane Kuseniɛ ne anwo.

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Dawide te kuro berɛ pambim nyɔ nemɔ b’afia. Wɛmvoɛ ne fole fasue ne aso hɔle pambim ne ti afia. Ɔtole ye nye, na onwuni kyɛ biaa bie ngome ole amirika ɔba ɔ.

english_verse: and shouted down to tell David. David answered, “If he's alone, he must have some news.” The runner was getting closer,
translation_verse: Wɛmvoɛ ne teane nu bɔle Nana Dawide amaneɛ. Na Nana sele kyɛ, “Sɛ ye ngome yeɛ ɔ́ba de a, ye de ɔso ngraa.” Ɔwale alaa, na opingyele bɛ.

english_verse: when the soldier saw someone else running. He shouted down to the gate, “Look! There's another runner!” David said, “He must have some news too.”
translation_verse: Afei wɛmvoɛ ne nwuni kyɛ biaa bieku le amirika ɔba ɔ. Na ɔteane nu sele pambim wɛmvoɛ ne kyɛ, “Nea kyɛ biaa bie koso otu amirika ba ɔ!” Na Nana Dawide sele kyɛ, “Ye koso ɔso ngraa.”

english_verse: The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ wɛmvoɛ ne sele kyɛ, “Ko bɔ oli moa ne, ye amirikatulɛ soma Sadoke awa Ahimaase.” Na Nana Dawide sele kyɛ, “Ɔte sona paa, yiti ɔso ndɛenvɛen.”

english_verse: Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
translation_verse: Afei Ahimaase teane nu sele Nana Dawide kyɛ, “Ɔte bɔkɔɔ!” Ɔfale ye nyunu butuli ase wɔ Nana Dawide nyunu berɛ, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Nana, me mene, mmenia bɔ bedwɔso betiale wɔ ne, animnyam hã AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ kyɛ wafa bɛ wawura wɔ sa ɔ.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Dawide bisale kyɛ, “Aberandeɛ Absalom, ye nwo te paa anaa?” Na Ahimaase buale kyɛ, “Nana, w’akoaa, mmerɛ bɔ Yoabo ɔ́soma me ne, nwuni kyɛ mmenia ayɛ berɛ bagyabagya, nakoso mannwu nikye horɛ.”

english_verse: David told him, “Stand over there and wait.” Ahimaaz went over and stood there.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Dawide sele kyɛ, “Twe wɔ nwo gyina ahameɛ!” Yiti ɔhwene ye nwo gyinane ahameɛ konn.

english_verse: The Ethiopian came and said, “Your Majesty, today I have good news! The Lord has rescued you from all your enemies!”
translation_verse: Afei Kuseniɛ ne oodwuli berɛ; na osele kyɛ, “Nana, me mene, ndɛenvɛen yeɛ mafa mabrɛ wɔ ɔ. Ofikyɛ ɛnɛ AWURADE ali wɔ dwirɛ wama wɔ, na mmenia mukoraa bɔ bedwɔso betiale wɔ ne, wale wɔ wafi bɛ sa nu.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!” David Cries for Absalom
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Dawide buale Kuseniɛ ne kyɛ, “Aberandeɛ Absalom, ye nwo te paa anaa?” Na Kuseniɛ ne buale kyɛ, “Nana, me mene, wɔ pɔfoɛ mɔ ne ebiala bɔ okodwɔso kotia wɔ kyɛ ɔmbena wɔ paa ne, b’ayieleɛ óyie bɛ kyɛ sɔ aberandeɛ ne.”

english_verse: David started trembling. Then he went up to the room above the city gate to cry. As he went, he kept saying, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I could have died instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Edwirɛ ne mane Nana Dawide wora bɔle. Na sua bɔ ogyi pambim ne aso ne, ɔfo hɔle nu oosuni. Ɔkɔ ne, né osũ kyɛ, “Yieee, mma Absalom, mma ye, mma Absalom! Ahaa maa nwu ma ɛtena ase e! Ao Absalom, mma ye, mma ye!”

english_verse: Someone told Joab, “The king is crying because Absalom is dead.”
translation_verse: Bɛɛbɔle Yoabo amaneɛ kyɛ, “Nana Dawide ósu Absalom, na ódi ye wue nwo aworabɔlɛ.”

english_verse: David's army found out he was crying because his son had died, and their day of victory suddenly turned into a day of sadness.
translation_verse: Yiti sɔ kyẽa ne, koɛhonɛfoɛ ne amukoraa bɛ ngonim bɔ bali ne, ɔkakyili aworabɔlɛ, ofikyɛ sɔ kyẽa ne, koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ tele kyɛ Dawide ódi ɔwa ne wue nwo aworabɔlɛ.

english_verse: The troops were sneaking into Mahanaim, just as if they had run away from a battle and were ashamed.
translation_verse: Na sɔ kyẽa ne, koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ yɛle kudɛɛ bɛwale kuro ne anu, kyɛbɔ koɛhonɛfoɛ bɛnwati befi koɛ nu a, bɛfa ɛfɛrelɛ bewuawua bɛ nwo bɛba ne ala.

english_verse: David covered his face with his hands and kept on crying loudly, “My son, Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Nana Dawide katale ye nyunu, na ɔteane nu suni kyɛ, “Yieee, mma Absalom, Ao Absalom, mma ye, mma ye!”

english_verse: Joab went to the house where David was staying and told him: You've made your soldiers ashamed! Not only did they save your life, they saved your sons and daughters and wives as well.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yoabo wale Nana Dawide berɛ wɔ sua nu, na osele kyɛ, “Wɔ somvoɛ mɔ bɔ ɛnɛ bale wɔ ne wɔ mma mmienzua, wɔ mma mmrasua, ɛye mɔ ne wɔ sómaa mɔ ngoa ne, agua bɛ mukoraa bɛ nyunu ase ɛnɛ.

english_verse: You're more loyal to your enemies than to your friends. What you've done today has shown your officers and soldiers that they don't mean a thing to you. You would be happy if Absalom was still alive, even if the rest of us were dead.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ ahyire kyɛ ekuro wɔ pɔfoɛ mɔ dwirɛ, na bɛ bɔ bekuro wɔ dwirɛ ne de, ɛpɔ bɛ. Ɛnɛ amaa wala ali pefee kyɛ, safohene mɔ ne somvoɛ mɔ de, bɛ nwo nhia wɔ. Manwu ye kyɛ, ɛnɛ sɛ Absalom tɛ te ase, bɔ yɛ mukoraa yawuwu a, ahaa ekuro.

english_verse: Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
translation_verse: Yiti dwɔso kodwudwo kyire wɔ somvoɛ nemɔ ma b’ahone tɔ nzue nu. Na meta AWURADE ndaen kyɛ, sɛ angɔ a, sona ko po ngɔha wɔ nwo wa ɛnɛ kɔngɔen ye. Na ɛhe kɔyɛ edwirɛ piri paa kɔtra edwirɛ biala bɔ wato wɔ ɔ, fite wɔ mmerandeɛ nu bɔ ɔbaadwu ɛnɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him. Israel and Judah Want David Back After Israel's soldiers had all returned home,
translation_verse: Yiti Nana Dawide dwɔsole ɔɔtenane ase wɔ kuro berɛ pambim ne anwo. Yeɛ bɛɛbɔle mmenia ne amukoraa amaneɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔtie, Nana aatena kuro wa pambim ne anwo.” Na mmenia ne amukoraa bɛhɔle Nana Dawide berɛ. Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa banwati bahɔ b’awuro. Dawide sa ba Yerusalem

english_verse: When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said: Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home?
translation_verse: Yiti Nana Dawide fale ngraa he somane maa beesele asɔfo Sadoke ne Abiata kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔfa bɛ́to Yuda mbanyi nyunu kyɛ, ‘Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔtena berɛ ma ebiemɔ bedi ɛmɔ nyunu moa bɛkɔɔfa Nana Dawide bɛba ye awuro ɔ? Ofikyɛ edwirɛ bɔ bɛ́keka ye wɔ Yisrael amukoraa ne, mate.

english_verse: He is your brother, your own relative! Why haven't you done anything to bring him back?”
translation_verse: Me deɛ ole ɛmɔ, ɛmɔte me nnehyeɛ kaenn. Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔtena berɛ ma ebiemɔ di ɛmɔ nyunu moa bɛkɔfa Nana Dawide bɛba ɔ?’

english_verse: And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔsa bɛha behyire Amasa koso kyɛ, ‘Ɛte me dehyeɛ kaenn. Ofi ɛnɛ bɔ ɔkɔ ɔ, sɛ mamva wɔ manzi Yoabo gya nu mammɔ wɔ safohene wɔ me koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ aso a, Nyameɛ tua me kerɛ piri paa.’ ”

english_verse: Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.” David Starts Back for Jerusalem
translation_verse: Dawide noa dwirɛ ne hane mmenia bɔ bɛwɔ Yuda amukoraa bɔle nu maa bɛyɛle ko, na bɛmaa beesele Nana Dawide kyɛ, “Sa bra, ɛne wɔ somvoɛ amukoraa.”

english_verse: Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and
translation_verse: Na Benyaminniɛ Gera ɔwa Simei bɔ ofi Bahurim ne, ɔyɛle ndɛndɛ ɔne Yudafoɛ bɛhɔle beeyiale Nana Dawide.

english_verse: I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
translation_verse: W’akoaa, mese kyɛ mayɔ bɔne. Yiti Nana, me mene, mesrɛ wɔ, Yosef awuro ama amukoraa, me yeɛ mali moa mawa kyɛ mebaayia wɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne ala, mmenia fale Nana Dawide awuro ama beguale ɛlɛen nu kyɛ bɛfa bɛ bɛpɛ asue ne, ná besa bɛyɔ nikyee biala bɔ okuro ɔ bɛma ye. Na mmerɛ bɔ Nana Dawide yɛle kyɛ ɔpɛ asue Yɔɔdan nen, Gera awa Simei oobutuli ye nyunu berɛ,

english_verse: He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it.
translation_verse: na osele Nana Dawide kyɛ, “Me mene, mesrɛ wɔ ala, nnɛnea me bɔne bɔ mayɔ ɔ. Nana, me mene, mvomsoɛ bɔ w’akoaa nyɔle ye kyẽa bɔ efili Yerusalem ne, mesrɛ wɔ, bu wɔ nye gua so. Nana, nnɛfa sie wɔ ti anu.

english_verse: But Abishai shouted, “You should be killed for cursing the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Na Seruya awa Abisae buale kyɛ, “Aso ɔnzɛ kyɛ beku Simei anaa? Ofikyɛ ɔborole sona bɔ AWURADE apopa ye ngoo ne amoen.”

english_verse: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
translation_verse: Nakoso Dawide buale kyɛ, “Ɛmɔ Seruya mma ye mɔ, me dwirɛ fa ɛmɔ nwo nzu, bɔ ɛnɛ ɛmɔayɛ me pɔfoɛ ye? Aso ɛnɛ ɔsɛ kyɛ beku sona wɔ Yisrael anaa? Aso menze kyɛ ɛnɛ me yeɛ nde Yisrael so hene ɔ.”

english_verse: Then David promised Shimei that he would not be killed. Mephibosheth Meets with David
translation_verse: Na Nana Dawide tale ndaen foale so sele Simei kyɛ, “Ebiala ngohũ wɔ.” Dawide nwu Mefibosɛte anwumvoin bieku

english_verse: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
translation_verse: Na obuale kyɛ, “O Nana, me mene, me somvoɛ ne lakalakale me. Nana, wɔ somvoɛ, nga ngyirele ye kyɛ osiesie afunum ma ndena so ma me ne wɔ yɛhɔ, ofikyɛ wɔ somvoɛ, nde bubuaniɛ.

english_verse: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
translation_verse: Nana, me mene, waatoatoa me wahyire wɔ. Nakoso Nana, me mene, wɔ de ɛte kyɛ Nyameɛ abɔfo, yiti bɔ ekuro kyɛ ɛyɔ biala, yɔ.

english_verse: After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
translation_verse: Nana, me mene, ahaa me baba abusuafoɛ mukoraa, ehunɛ yeɛ yɛfata kyɛ eku yɛ ɔ. Nakoso amaa me, wɔ somvoɛ, maboka mmenia bɔ bedidi wɔ poen so ne aso. Nana, nzikyɛ bieku yeɛ ngɔhora ngobisa ngofi wɔ berɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: David answered, “You've said enough! I've decided to divide the property between you and Ziba.”
translation_verse: Na Nana Dawide sele ye kyɛ, “Onhia kyɛ ɛkɔha wɔ nwo kodwudwo ko. Mahã kyɛ, ɛne Siba bɛkɔhyɛ aseɛ ne.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
translation_verse: Yeɛ Mefibosɛte sele Nana Dawide kyɛ, “Nana, me mene, awuro bɔ asa awa asomdwee nu ne yeɛ ohia ɔ, yiti maa ɔfa ye mukoraa.” Dawide yɛ Basilae paa

english_verse: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
translation_verse: Gileadeniɛ Basilae fili Rogelim wale, na ɔne Nana Dawide bɛhɔle asue Yɔɔdan noa dɔ, kyɛ ɔkwaasoma ye dwu asue ne asi dɔ.

english_verse: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
translation_verse: Nana Dawide sele ye kyɛ, “Maa yɛpɛ asue ne yɛhɔ Yerusalem kɔtena nekaa bɔ nde ne, na ngɔnea wɔ.”

english_verse: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
translation_verse: Nakoso Basilae buale Nana Dawide kyɛ, “Waha m’afoɛ nyɛɛ wɔ aseɛ ye aso, bɔ me ne Nana yɛkɔ Yerusalem ɔ?

english_verse: I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me.
translation_verse: Nana, wɔ somvoɛ, me ne wɔ yɛkɔpɛ asue ne yɛkɔhɔ ye si dɔ kãa. Nana, nzu ati yeɛ ɛbɔ me aba so sɔa ɔ?

english_verse: Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
translation_verse: Mesrɛ wɔ ala, wɔ somvoɛ, maa nza ngɔ ngonwu wɔ me kuro, wɔ nekaa bɔ me ni ne me se asieleɛ wɔ ɔ. Nakoso Nana, me mene, wɔ somvoɛ Kimham ɛhe. Maa ɔne wɔ bɛpɛ asue ne bɛhɔ, na paa biala bɔ ekuro ne, fa yɛ ye.”

english_verse: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Dawide buale kyɛ, “Me ne Kimham yɛkɔpɛ asue ne yɛkɔhɔ, na paa biala bɔ ekuro kyɛ mefa meyɛ ye ne, ngɔfa ngɔyɛ ye; yeɛ nikyee biala bɔ ekobisa me ne koso, ngɔyɔ ngɔma wɔ.”

english_verse: David's soldiers went on across the river, while he stayed behind to tell Barzillai goodbye and to wish him well. Barzillai returned home, but
translation_verse: Afei koɛhonɛfoɛ ne amukoraa bɛ ne Nana Dawide bɛpɛle asue ne. Na anzana Nana Dawide baapɛ asue ne nen, ɔtɔle Basilae nu yɛle ye atuu, oyirale ye, na Basilae sa hɔle ye kuro.

english_verse: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
translation_verse: Nana Dawide toale so hɔle Gilgal, na Kimham ne ye hɔle. Na Yuda koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa, bɛ ne Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ ne bue bɛfale Nana Dawide bɛhɔle.

english_verse: The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
translation_verse: Afei Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa wale Nana Dawide berɛ beebisale ye kyɛ, “Nana Dawide, nzu ati yeɛ y’eliɛma mɔ bɔ befi Yuda ne, bale wɔ bafi yɛ sa nu, bɔ bafa wɔ ne w’awuro ama, ɔne bɛ bɔ bɛboka wɔ so amukoraa bapɛ asue Yɔɔdan ɔ?”

english_verse: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yuda koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa buale Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “Nana Dawide te yɛ nwoniɛ kaenn ti ɔ. Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔafɛ edwirɛ he anwo yaa ɔ? Aleɛ bɔ yali ne, Nana yeɛ ɔfa mane yɛ hɔ ɔ, anaakyɛ wahyɛ yɛ nikyee bie hɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ buale Yuda koɛhonɛfoɛ kyɛ, “Yɛ bue deɛ bɔ ɔwɔ ɛhene ne anu ne, ɔtra ɛmɔ bue deɛ sɔ alaa buru. Yɛ bue deɛ bɔ ɔwɔ Dawide nu ne, ɔtra ɛmɔ bue deɛ. Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔmmu yɛ sɔa ye? Aso nna yɛ yeɛ yɛlili moa yɛhane kyɛ yɛkwaafa yɛ hene yɛsa yɛba ɔ?” Nakoso Yudafoɛ mane bɛ noa yɛle se trale Yisraelfoɛ.

english_verse: A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
translation_verse: Biaa bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Hyeba, bɔ onni dwirɛ ngɔ kuro so ɔ, né ɔwɔ berɛ bie. Ɔse ole Benyaminniɛ Bikri. Ohuli totorobɛndo teane nu sele kyɛ, “Yɛ ne Dawide yɛlle hwee yɛnyɔ oo! Yese awa ne, yɛlle agyapadeɛ biala wɔ ye nu oo! Yisraelfoɛ ee, ebiala hɔ ye awuro!”

english_verse: So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. David's Ten Wives
translation_verse: Yiti Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa yakyili Dawide si lilɛ beelili Bikri awa Hyeba si. Nakoso Yudafoɛ de, begyinane bɛ hene ne asi fite asue Yɔɔdan noa beedwuli Yerusalem.

english_verse: David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. He gave them whatever they needed, but he never slept with any of them again. They had to live there for the rest of their lives as if they were widows. The Army Goes after Sheba
translation_verse: Nana Dawide wale ye ahemvie berɛ wɔ Yerusalem. Ye sómaa buru bɔ ɔyakyili bɛ berɛ kyɛ bɛnea awuro berɛ ne, ɔmaa bɛɛtenane awuro bie anu. Ɔmaa bɛwɛnene bɛ, na ɔbɔle bɛ akɔhoma. Nakoso wamva ye nwo wanga bɛ. Yiti bɛ ngome bɛtenane dɔ alaa kyɛ akunafoɛ maa oodwuli bɛ wue.

english_verse: David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
translation_verse: Afei Nana Dawide sele Amasa kyɛ, “Mema wɔ ɛlɛsa. Fa boaboa Yudafoɛ noa maa bɛbra me wa, na wɔ koso bra bie.”

english_verse: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
translation_verse: Yiti Amasa hɔle kyɛ ɔkwaafrɛfrɛ Yudafoɛ, nakoso ɔmane ɛlɛsa bɔ Dawide ahyɛ ye ne pale ye nwo.

english_verse: So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.” Joab Kills Amasa
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide sele Abisae kyɛ, “Afei de, nikyee bɔ Bikri awa Hyeba kɔfa kɔyɛ yɛ ne, ɔkɔtra Absalom deɛ ne po. Yiti fa me koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ ná po ye so. Anyɔ a, ɔkɔɔfea nguro bɔ bato bɛ nwo fasue ne bie anu, bɔ yɛ sa ngɔhã ye ɔ.”

english_verse: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yoabo mmenia nemɔ, Keretifoɛ, Peletifoɛ ne koɛhonɛfoɛ ne amukoraa belili Abisae si, na besili nu befili Yerusalem kyɛ bɛpo Bikri awa Hyeba so.

english_verse: They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.
translation_verse: Na beedwuli nyɔboɛ piri ne anwo wɔ Gibeon nen, Amasa wale ooyiale bɛ. Né Yoabo wura koɛ ataadeɛ. Na abɔsoɛ bɔ ɔbɔ so ne, né wafa ngrandɛ bɔ owura bɔha nu wawura nu. Mmerɛ bɔ Yoabo ɔ́kɔ ye nyunu moa nen, ngrandɛ ne ye fili bɔha ne anu.

english_verse: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Na Yoabo sele Amasa kyɛ, “Nniɛma, wɔ nwo te sɛɛ?” Afei Yoabo le ye sa famaa sɔle Amasa kanza nu kyɛ ɔkwaatɔ ye nu yɛ ye atuu.

english_verse: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
translation_verse: Nakoso Amasa annwu kyɛ Yoabo tira ngrandɛ ɔ. Yoabo fa wɔle Amasa kunu mane ye nyaa tu guale, na owuli. Wanwɔ ye pɛen nyɔ. Afei Yoabo ne oliɛma Abisae bɛpole Bikri awa Hyeba so.

english_verse: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
translation_verse: Na Yoabo mmenia nemɔ nu ko oogyinane Amasa fuin ne anwo berɛ teane nu sele kyɛ, “Wɔ biala bɔ ekuro Yoabo dwirɛ, ɔne wɔ biala bɔ ɛwɔ Dawide bue nu ne, di Yoabo si.”

english_verse: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Amasa fuin bɔ mogya abia ye takaa ne, né ɔla atimbire ne anu. Sɔ biaa ne nwuni kyɛ, ebiala dwu berɛ ná onwu Amasa a, né wagyina. Onwuni kyɛ ebiala dwu ye nwo berɛ a ogyina ne ati, ɔmane Amasa so fili atimbire ne anu ɔɔtole buro, na ɔfale ɛtena katale ye so.

english_verse: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
translation_verse: Ɔyele ye fili atimbire ne anu nen, afei ebiala lili Yoabo si maa bɛpole Bikri awa Hyeba so

english_verse: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
translation_verse: Hyeba hyinihyini Yisrael mmusua kure amukoraa nu oodwuli Abel Bete Maaka, na Bikrifoɛ amukoraa boale bɛ noa bɛ ne ye hɔle kuro ne anu.

english_verse: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
translation_verse: Mmenia bɔ beli Yoabo si ne, bɛhane Bikri bepuane wɔ Abel Bete Maaka. Afei kuro berɛ fasue ne, bɛboaboale nyɔboɛ noa wɔ ye si maa ɔhɔle anwuro. Na bɛhyɛle ye bo kyɛ bedwiri fasue ne begua.

english_verse: A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!”
translation_verse: Yeɛ braa nworɛniɛ bie teane nu fili kuro ne anu kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔtie oo! Ɛ́mɔtie oo! Ɛ́mɔhã behyire Yoabo kyɛ ɔbra wa ma nga dwirɛ ngyire ye.”

english_verse: When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?” “Yes, I am,” he answered. She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.” “All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
translation_verse: Opingyele braa ne anwo berɛ, na braa ne bisale ye kyɛ, “Aso wɔ ole Yoabo anaa?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Yoo, me ɔ.” Yeɛ osele Yoabo kyɛ, “Ma w’afaneɛ ɔha dwirɛ kãa hyire wɔ.” Na obuale kyɛ, “Métie.”

english_verse: She said, “Long ago people used to say, ‘If you want good advice, go to the town of Abel to get it.’ The answers they got here were all that was needed to settle any problem.
translation_verse: Afei braa ne sele kyɛ, “Daa ne, né bɛtaa bɛka kyɛ, ‘Ɛmɔhɔ Abel bɛɛpena foɛtulɛ, na ɔnate so edwirɛ ne aso kɔpɛ.’

english_verse: We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
translation_verse: Asomdwee mmenia ne mmenia bɔ bedi nahorɛ wɔ Yisrael ne, bɛ nu ko ole me. Kuro bɔ ye nwo hia paa wɔ Yisrael yeɛ ɛpena kyɛ ɛbɔ ye ɔ. Nzu ati yeɛ ɛpena kyɛ enua AWURADE agyapadeɛ boso ɔ.”

english_verse: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yoabo buale kyɛ, “Ɔngɔwa ye sɔ le, ɔngɔwa ye sɔ le kyɛ ngɔbɔ kuro ne anaakyɛ ngɔma ye boso konua ɔ!

english_verse: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
translation_verse: Edwirɛ ne, nna sɔ yeɛ ɔte ɔ! Bɔ ɔte ole kyɛ, biaa bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Hyeba, bɔ ɔse ole Bikri bɔ ofi Efraim mmokaa aseɛ ne aso ne, wayɛ Nana Dawide nwo lɔen. Ɛ́mɔye ye ngome bɛbra, na ngɔyakyi kuro ne tualɛ.” Na braa ne buale kyɛ, “Nzaade yɛkofindi ye ti yɛkɔfa fasue ne aso yɛkɔma wɔ.”

english_verse: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
translation_verse: Afei braa ne fale ye nworɛ adwene ne ɔɔbɔle kuro berɛ ama mukoraa amaneɛ. Bɛpɛle Bikri awa Hyeba ti, na befindini bɛtole dɔ bɛmane Yoabo. Yiti Yoabo huli totorobɛndo ne, na bɛ mukoraa befili kuro ne anwo bɛhɔle b’awuro. Nakoso Yoabo de, osa hɔle Nana Dawide berɛ wɔ Yerusalem.

english_verse: Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
translation_verse: Yoabo yeɛ né ɔla Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa noa ɔ; Yehoada awa Benaya yeɛ né ɔla Keretifoɛ ne Peletifoɛ noa ɔ;

english_verse: Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
translation_verse: Adoram yeɛ né ɔnea mmenia bɔ bɛhyɛ bɛ maa bɛyɔ adwuma ne aso ɔ; Ahilude awa Yehosafate yeɛ né ɔte maen ne anu abakɔsɛm ahyerɛlɛniɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
translation_verse: Né Sewa yeɛ ɔte ahemvie berɛ ahyerɛlɛniɛ ɔ; yeɛ né Sadoke ne Abiata bɛte asɔfo.

english_verse: Ira from Jair was David's priest.
translation_verse: Né Yariniɛ Yira koso ɔte Dawide sɔfo.

translation_verse: Aberɛso Dwirɛ

english_verse: He said, “What can I do to make up for what Saul did, so that you'll ask the Lord to be kind to his people again?”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide bisale Gibeonfoɛ kyɛ, “Nzu yeɛ ɛmɔkuro kyɛ meyɔ mema ɛmɔ ɔ? Nzikyɛ yeɛ ɛmɔkuro kyɛ mefa mepata ɛmɔ ɔ, bɔ ɔnate so ɛmɔkoyira AWURADE mmenia ɔ?”

english_verse: They replied, “Saul tried to kill all our people so that none of us would be left in the land of Israel.
translation_verse: Na bebuale Nana Dawide kyɛ, “Biaa bɔ ohuhuni yɛ, bɔ ahaa ɔpena kyɛ yɛ boso nua, ná ɔye yɛ fi Yisrael aseɛ so nekaa biala ne,

english_verse: Give us seven of his descendants. We will hang these men near the place where the Lord is worshiped in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, the Lord's chosen king.” “I'll give them to you,” David said.
translation_verse: maa bɛfa ye boso ama mmienzua nzoo bewura yɛ sa, ná yɛɛbɔ bɛ kɔme wɔ AWURADE nyunu, wɔ Sɔɔlo bɔ AWURADE neaneane nu yele ye ne ye kuro Gibea.” Na Nana Dawide hane kyɛ, “Ngɔfa bɛ ngɔma ɛmɔ.”

english_verse: David had made a promise to Jonathan with the Lord as his witness, so he spared Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul.
translation_verse: Nakoso Sɔɔlo anomaa Mefibosɛte bɔ ɔte Yonatan awa ne de, Nana Dawide maa onyane ye ti didili nu, ɔnate kyɛ né Dawide ne Sɔɔlo awa Yonatan bɛ munyɔ bafa AWURADE bata bɛ nwo ndaen.

english_verse: turned them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged all seven of them on the mountain near the place where the Lord was worshiped. This happened right at the beginning of the barley harvest. Rizpah Takes Care of the Bodies
translation_verse: na ɔfale bɛ wurale Gibeonfoɛ sa. Na Gibeonfoɛ bɔle mmenia nzoo ne bɛ kɔme wɔ bokaa ne aso wɔ AWURADE nyunu. Mmenia nzoo ne amukoraa, bewu bɛbɔle nu. Ayuo telɛ dwuli ne, bɛhyɛle ye bo kyɛ bɛte ne ala yeɛ behuni bɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Rizpah spread out some sackcloth on a nearby rock. She wouldn't let the birds land on the bodies during the day, and she kept the wild animals away at night. She stayed there from the beginning of the harvest until it started to rain. The Burial of Saul and His Descendants
translation_verse: Afei Aya awa brasua Risipa fale ɛsɛen tena sɛle nyɔboɛ so wɔ nekaa bɔ efuin nemɔ gua ne. Na ɔtenane berɛ toonn fite mmerɛ bɔ bɛhyɛle ayuotelɛ bo maa oodwuli kyɛ esue tɔ guale efuin nemɔ so ɔ. Alehyeleɛ nu, wamma nnomaa ate ma banzuso efuin nemɔ. Yeɛ alesaleɛ nu koso, wamma ngaka aboyaa ate ma banni.

english_verse: Earlier the Philistines had killed Saul and Jonathan on Mount Gilboa and had hung their bodies in the town square at Beth-Shan. The people of Jabesh in Gilead had secretly taken the bodies away, but David found out what Saul's wife Rizpah had done, and he went to the leaders of Jabesh to get the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Na ɛhe mane Dawide hɔle Yabese Gileadefoɛ berɛ oolele Sɔɔlo ne ɔwa Yonatan mmowue ne fili bɛ berɛ. Né Yabese Gileadefoɛ bali moa baawua mmowue ne bafi Bete San dwaa ne aso. Kyẽa bɔ Filistifoɛ huni Sɔɔlo wɔ Gilboa ne, Bete San dwaa ne aso yeɛ bɛfale efuin nemɔ besinzele ɔ.

english_verse: David had their bones taken to the land of Benjamin and buried in a side room in Saul's family burial place. Then he gave orders for the bones of the men who had been hanged to be buried there. It was done, and God answered prayers to bless the land. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
translation_verse: Na besiele Sɔɔlo ne ɔwa Yonatan bɛ mmowue ne wɔ Sɔɔlo baba Kise asieleɛ nu, wɔ Sela, wɔ Benyamin aseɛ so. Bɛyɔle bɔ Nana Dawide ha hyirele bɛ ne amukoraa. Na ye si ye, Nyameɛ tiele aseɛ ne anwo mbaeɛ bɔ bɛbɔle ne. Yisraelfoɛ ku Filisti kwabranoa mɔ (

english_verse: There was another war, this time in Gath. One of the enemy soldiers was a descendant of the Rephaim. He was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.
translation_verse: Besa bɛ ne Filistifoɛ hone koɛ wɔ Gate. Gate berɛ, né Filistiniɛ bienzua tendenn guraen bie wɔ berɛ. Ye sa ne ye gya mmɛseka nemɔ te nzia nzia, na ye mu ka bɔ nu a, ɔte aburanyɔ ne nna. Ye koso ɔte kwabranoa nemɔ bosoniɛ.

english_verse: One time David got very tired when he and his soldiers were fighting the Philistines.
translation_verse: Filistifoɛ ne Yisrael sa fale koɛ tetale so. Dawide ne ye koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ yeɛ bɛhɔle koɛ ne ɔ. Bɛ ne Filistifoɛ hone, na nziɛ ye, né Dawide afɛ paa.

english_verse: One of the Philistine warriors was Ishbibenob, who was a descendant of the Rephaim, and he tried to kill David. Ishbibenob was armed with a new sword, and his bronze spearhead alone weighed about three and a half kilograms.
translation_verse: Na Filisti kwabranoa nemɔ, bɛ bosoniɛ ko bie bɔ oli Yisibi Benobo ne, ɔbɔle mmɔden kyɛ okohu Dawide. Né ye pealɛɛ ne anu nonɛ te kilo nza ne bue, na né ye akodeɛ nemɔ te monɛ.

english_verse: But Abishai came to the rescue and killed the Philistine. David's soldiers told him, “We can't let you risk your life in battle anymore! You give light to our nation, and we want that flame to keep burning.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Abisae bɔ oni ole Seruya ne, ɔpepɛ lele Dawide, na ɔhɔle Filistiniɛ ne so ohuni ye. Na ɛhe mane Dawide mmenia nemɔ tale ndaen tole ye so kyɛ, “Yɛkɔ koɛ bieku a, ɛngɔhɔ bie, anyɔ a ekonua Yisrael kanea ne.”

english_verse: There was another battle with the Philistines at Gob, where Sibbecai from Hushah killed a descendant of the Rephaim named Saph.
translation_verse: Ɛhe asi ye, bɛ ne Filistifoɛ hone koɛ bieku wɔ Gɔbo. Koɛ ne anu, Husaniɛ Sibekae huni kwabranoa nemɔ bosoniɛ ko bɔ oli Safe.

english_verse: There was still another battle with the Philistines at Gob. A soldier named Elhanan killed Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. Elhanan's father was Jari from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Besa bɛ ne Filistifoɛ hone koɛ bieku wɔ Gɔbo. Na Betlehemniɛ Yaare Oregim ɔwa Ɛlhanan ohuni Gitiniɛ Goliate. Goliate pealɛɛ ne, ɔte kyɛ mbuna bɔ bɛfa nyamaa bɛsosɔ nu bɛnwo ɛtena ɔ.

english_verse: But when he made fun of Israel, David's nephew Jonathan killed him. Jonathan was the son of David's brother Shimei.
translation_verse: Ɔpɛle Yisrael poa, na Dawide aliɛma Simei ɔwa Yonatan huni ye.

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these four men who were descendants of the Rephaim from Gath.
translation_verse: Sɔ mmenia nna ne, bɛte Gate kwabranoa nemɔ bɛ bosofoɛ nemɔ bie. Na Dawide ne ye mmenia nemɔ huhuni bɛ.

english_verse: You rescued me from enemies who were hateful and too powerful for me.
translation_verse: Olele me fili me pɔfoɛ anwoserɛniɛ sa nu, ɔne bɛ bɔ bekyi me ɔ bɛ sa nu; ofikyɛ né bɛ nwo yɛ se tra me koraa.

english_verse: David sang a song to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, especially Saul. These are the words to David's song:
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ AWURADE lele Dawide fili ye pɔfoɛ amukoraa sa nu ne Sɔɔlo sa nu ne, Dawide tole dwein he yele AWURADE ayɛ.

english_verse: I will praise you, Lord, and I will honor you among the nations.
translation_verse: Yiti, O AWURADE, ngɔkamvo wɔ wɔ maen maen mɔ so, ná mabɔ wɔ dumaa mato ayɛyelɛ dwein.

english_verse: Our Lord and our God, you are my mighty rock, my fortress, my protector.
translation_verse: Ɔtole ye kyɛ, “AWURADE te me nyɔbotaen, m’anwoserɛ afealeɛ ne me defoɛ,

english_verse: You are the rock where I am safe. You are my shield, my powerful weapon, and my place of shelter. You rescue me and keep me safe from violence.
translation_verse: me Nyameɛ, me nyɔbotaen bɔ mebɔ me nwo waen wɔ nu ɔ, m’akokyɛm ne me ngoalelɛ anwoserɛ, m’anwoserɛ afealeɛ ne me nwo adwaa, me defoɛ bɔ ode me fi basabasayɔlɛ nu ɔ.

english_verse: I praise you, our Lord! I prayed to you, and you rescued me from my enemies.
translation_verse: AWURADE bɔ ɔfata ayɛyelɛ ne, ye yeɛ mesu mefrɛ ye ɔ, na ode me fi me pɔfoɛ mɔ sa nu.

english_verse: Death, like ocean waves, surrounded me, and I was almost swallowed by its flooding waters.
translation_verse: Ewue asorɔkye pɛle me nwo yiale, na ewue bu fale me so kyɛ asue.

english_verse: Ropes from the world of the dead had coiled around me, and death had set a trap in my path.
translation_verse: Ɛborɔ dɔ nyamaa mendale me, na ewue ngaen wale me so kyɛ ɔbaahye me.

english_verse: I was in terrible trouble when I called out to you, but from your temple you heard me and answered my prayer.
translation_verse: Nzu mvrɛle AWURADE wɔ m’amaneɛ nu, na ndeane nu mvrɛle me Nyameɛ kyɛ ɔboka me. Ɔwɔ ye asɔneyɛɛ sua nu yeɛ ɔtele me mbaeɛ ɔ, na me sufrɛ dwuli ye so anu.

english_verse: Earth shook and shivered! The columns supporting the sky rocked back and forth. You were angry
translation_verse: Yeɛ aseɛ pusuli, na ɔwosole; nyameɛso nyinasoɛ ye bo kekane, na ɔwosole, ɔnate kyɛ Nyameɛ ahone huli.

english_verse: and breathed out smoke. Scorching heat and fiery flames spewed from your mouth.
translation_verse: Nwosina fili ye bonyi anu pu wale, see wuronyiwuronyi fili ye noa nu wale; na see bɔ wasɔ gonn fili ye nwo tutu guale.

english_verse: You opened the heavens like curtains, and you came down with storm clouds under your feet.
translation_verse: Ɔmoamoane ewienu, na odwuli ase, na né awosii kabii wɔ ye gya bo.

english_verse: You rode on the backs of flying creatures. You appeared with the wind as wings.
translation_verse: Ɔtenane kɛrubo so tuli, na benwuni ye wɔ mvrama ye ndaa so.

english_verse: Darkness was your tent! Thunderclouds filled the sky, hiding you from sight.
translation_verse: Ɔfale awosii munduni ye nwo, ɔfale munungum kusuu, bɔ ɔte esue bɔ wamuna ɔ katale ye nwo.

english_verse: Fiery coals lit up the sky in front of you.
translation_verse: Kanea hyireinn bɔ oli ye nyunu ne, see gonn fili nu tutu guale.

english_verse: Lord Most High, your voice thundered from the heavens.
translation_verse: AWURADE bɔle nu kurudududu fili nyameɛso, na Anwuro Anwuro Nyameɛ ne dwudwole.

english_verse: You scattered your enemies with arrows of lightning.
translation_verse: Ɔtotole agyaen mane ye pɔfoɛ mɔ bɔle aya, ye agralaa ne mane bɛ nye so tanene.

english_verse: You roared at the sea, and its deepest channels could be seen. You snorted, and the earth shook to its foundations.
translation_verse: Afei AWURADE hane bɛ nyunu, nwomeɛ fili ye bonyi anu tu wale, yiti ɛpo ye bo dɔ aseɛ yele ye nwo ali, na aseɛ nyinasoɛ nwo lale berɛ.

english_verse: You reached down from heaven, and you lifted me from deep in the ocean.
translation_verse: Ɔtengyɛle ye sa fili anwuro ɔɔsɔle me nu, na ɔyele me fili buma nu.

english_verse: On the day disaster struck, they came and attacked, but you defended me.
translation_verse: M’amaneɛnwunɛ mmerɛ nu yeɛ bɛwale me so ɔ, nakoso AWURADE gyinane me si.

english_verse: When I was fenced in, you freed and rescued me because you love me.
translation_verse: Ɔfale me hɔle nekaa bɔ berɛ te pandann ɔ, ɔpepɛ lele me, ofikyɛ okuro me dwirɛ.

english_verse: You are good to me, Lord, because I do right, and you reward me because I am innocent.
translation_verse: “AWURADE neane kyɛbɔ mesi metengyɛ ɔ so mane me ye nwo akatuaa, ogyinane kyɛbɔ me bra si te sannwuu ɔ so mane me ye nwo akatuaa.

english_verse: I do what you want and never turn to do evil.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ mali AWURADE dwirɛ so, na nnyɔle bɔne nngakyili me si mmmane Nyameɛ.

english_verse: I keep your laws in mind and never turn away from your teachings.
translation_verse: Mali ye nhyehyɛleɛ amukoraa so, yeɛ ye ahyɛdeɛ koso, nndwene me nwo mmvili ye nwo.

english_verse: I obey you completely and guard against sin.
translation_verse: M’atee tengyɛ wɔ ye nyunu, na mate me nwo mafi bɔne nwo.

english_verse: You have been good to me because I do right; you have rewarded me for being innocent by your standards.
translation_verse: Ye sɔ ne ati, AWURADE agyina me tengyɛlɛ so wama me ye nwo akatuaa, wagyina kyɛbɔ me bra te sannwuu wɔ ye nyunu ɔ so.

english_verse: You are always loyal to your loyal people, and you are faithful to the faithful.
translation_verse: Sona bɔ odi nahorɛ ma wɔ ne, wɔ wora edi nahorɛ ma ye, yeɛ bɔ mvomsoɛ nne ye nwo ne, wɔ wora ɛmaa onwu kyɛ mvomsoɛ nne wɔ nwo.

english_verse: With all who are sincere you are sincere, but you treat the unfaithful as their deeds deserve.
translation_verse: Bɔ ye nwo te ne, wɔ wora ɛmaa onwu kyɛ wɔ nwo te, nakoso sona bɔ ɔte kanda de, ɛmaa onwu kyɛ ɛse nworɛ tra ye.

english_verse: You rescue the humble, but you look for ways to put down the proud.
translation_verse: Ɛpepɛ de anwobrɛaseɛfoɛ, nakoso anwomasoɛfoɛ de, wɔ nye sa bɛ maa ɛbrɛ bɛ ase.

english_verse: Our Lord and God, you are my lamp. You turn darkness to light.
translation_verse: O AWURADE, wɔ yeɛ ɛte me kanea ɔ, AWURADE, ɔta maa menya kanea wɔ m’awosii nu.

english_verse: Your way is perfect, Lord, and your word is correct. You are a shield for those who run to you for help.
translation_verse: Sɔ Nyameɛ he, ye atee tengyɛ, AWURADE bɔhyɛ te nahorɛ, na ebiala bɔ ɔbɔ ye nwo waen wɔ Nyameɛ nu ne, Nyameɛ te ye akokyɛm.

english_verse: You alone are God! Only you are a mighty rock.
translation_verse: “Nwa yeɛ ɔte Nyameɛ ɔ? Sana AWURADE angome. Nwa yeɛ ɔte nyɔbotaen ɔ? Sana yɛ Nyameɛ angome.

english_verse: You are my strong fortress, and you set me free.
translation_verse: Sɔ Nyameɛ he bɔ ɔma me anwoserɛ ne, ɔbɔ asomdwee atee pralaa to berɛ ma me.

english_verse: You make my feet run as fast as those of a deer, and you help me stand on the mountains.
translation_verse: Ɔma me gya boso yɛ nyera kyɛ kɛtɛbɔɔ, na ɔmaa megyina pindinn wɔ mmokaa so.

english_verse: You teach my hands to fight and my arms to use a bow of bronze.
translation_verse: Okyire me koɛhonɛ, amaa ɔnate so mekora mekondo kɔɔbere agyaen nu.

english_verse: You alone are my shield, and by coming to help me, you have made me famous.
translation_verse: Afa wɔ ngoalelɛ akokyɛm ne ama me, na wɔ mmokalɛ amaa mayɛ sona titire.

english_verse: You clear the way for me, and now I won't stumble.
translation_verse: Ɛbɔ atee pralaa maa mefa so bɔ ɔmaa menzoti ɔ.

english_verse: I kept chasing my enemies until I caught them and destroyed them.
translation_verse: Mvoane me pɔfoɛ mɔ ngukuni bɛ, na manza me si kɔpem kyɛ ngukuni bɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I destroyed them! I stuck my sword through my enemies, and they were crushed under my feet.
translation_verse: Nnili bɛ so ngonim, mmobɔle bɛ nguale berɛ bɔ bangora dwɔso ko ɔ, na bɛtotɔle beguale me gya bo.

english_verse: You helped me win victories and forced my attackers to fall victim to me.
translation_verse: Ɛmane me koɛ nu anwoserɛ, na ɛmane me pɔfoɛ mɔ lili ngoguo wɔ me nyunu.

english_verse: You made my enemies run, and I killed them.
translation_verse: Ɛmane me pɔfoɛ mɔ nwati fili me nyunu, bɛ bɔ bekyi me ne, nnuane bɛ boso.

english_verse: They cried out for help, but no one saved them; they called out to you, but there was no answer.
translation_verse: Bɛtotole bɛ nye, nakoso bannya defoɛ biala, besu bɛfrɛle AWURADE, nakoso wandɛ bɛ so.

english_verse: I ground them to dust, and I squashed them like mud in the streets.
translation_verse: Ndini bɛ muhumuhu kyɛ aseɛnwo mvuture, na ndiatiale bɛ so nwɔle bɛ kyɛ dwaaso nnɛterɛ.

english_verse: You rescued me from my stubborn people and made me the leader of foreign nations, who are now my slaves.
translation_verse: Me mmenia bɔ bɛyɔle me nwo lɔen ne, ɛpepɛ lele me fili bɛ sa nu. Ɛfale me tuale maen maen noa, na mmenia bɔ né menze bɛ ɔ bɛsole me.

english_verse: They have lost all courage and from their fortresses they come trembling.
translation_verse: Ahunundetelɛ tɔle maen maen so ama so, na bɛfale anwopopolɛ befili b’anwoserɛ afealeɛ mɔ nu befite bɛwale.

english_verse: You are the living Lord! I will praise you! You are a mighty rock. I will honor you for keeping me safe.
translation_verse: AWURADE te ase! Me nyɔbotaen, meye wɔ ayɛ! Me Nyameɛ, bɔ ɛte me ngoalelɛ Nyɔbotaen, mekamvo wɔ!

english_verse: You took revenge for me, and you put nations in my power.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ bɔ ɔtɔ me pɔfoɛ so wereɛ ma me ɔ, ye bɔ ɔbrɛ maen maen mɔ ase wura me bo ɔ,

english_verse: You give glorious victories to your chosen king. Your faithful love for David and for his descendants will never end.
translation_verse: Odi ngonim piri paa ma ye hene ne, ɔye ɔdɔ onni ngasi ali kyire sona bɔ wapopa ye ngoo ne, ɔye ye ali kyire Dawide ne ye boso ama afebɔɔ.”

english_verse: Chronicles
translation_verse: Aberɛso Dwirɛ

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord has told me what to say.
translation_verse: AWURADE Sunzum fa me so dwudwo, ye noa dwirɛ wɔ me temverema so.

english_verse: Our Mighty Rock, the God of Jacob, told me, “A ruler who obeys God and does right
translation_verse: Yisrael Nyameɛ adwudwo, Yisrael Nyɔbotaen ne sele me kyɛ, ‘Sona bɔ ɔfa pɛpɛɛpɛyɛlɛ da mmenia noa ne, bɔ ɔfa Nyameɛ surolɛ da bɛ noa ne,

english_verse: is like the sunrise on a cloudless day, or like rain that sparkles on the grass.”
translation_verse: ɔte hyireinn kyɛ eyia bɔ wapukye ngyerɛmɔ ɔ, bɔ munungum nne ye nyunu ɔ, ɔte kyɛ eyia bɔ esue tɔ gua ndire so a, ɔbɔ so ɔ.

english_verse: I have ruled this way, and God will never break his promise to me. God's promise is complete and unchanging; he will always help me and give me what I hope for.
translation_verse: Aso nna sɔ yeɛ m’abusua ɔte wɔ Nyameɛ nyunu anaa? Ofikyɛ ɔne me ayɛ apam afebɔɔ, ɔte apam bɔ wahyehyɛ ye pɛpɛɛpɛ bɔ onni ngasi ɔ. Na m’anyelasoɛ amukoraa, ɔne bɔ mepena amukoraa, aso ɔngɔboka me ma me sa ngɔhã ye anaa?

english_verse: But evil people are pulled up like thornbushes. They are not dug up by hand,
translation_verse: Nakoso amumuyɛɛfoɛ de, bɛ mukoraa bɛte kyɛ mmowue bɔ begyi begua ɔ, ofikyɛ ɛngɔhora ngɔfa wɔ sa ngɔsesa.

english_verse: except Eleazar. He killed Philistines until his hand was cramped, and he couldn't let go of his sword. When Eleazar finished, all the Israelite troops had to do was come back and take the enemies' weapons and armor. The Lord gave Israel a great victory that day.
translation_verse: nakoso Eleasa de ogyinane pindinn. Ohuhuni Filistifoɛ alaa mane ye sa nyane, nakoso né ɔngora ye ngrandɛ ne anu yakyi. Na AWURADE maa olili ngonim kandinga sɔ kyẽa ne. Afei Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ sa wale ye nwo berɛ, nakoso efuin nemɔ yeɛ beepuropurole bɛ nwo nningyein ɔ.

english_verse: and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was the commander of the Thirty Warriors, but he still did not become one of the Three Warriors.
translation_verse: Koɛhonɛfoɛ ahoneserɛfoɛ aburasa ne, ye yeɛ olele dumaa piri paa ɔ. Ɔyɛle bɛ so safohene, nakoso wando koɛhonɛfoɛ ahoneserɛfoɛ nza nemɔ.

english_verse: These are the names of David's warriors: Ishbosheth the son of Hachmon was the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle, he killed
translation_verse: Dawide koɛhonɛfoɛ ahoneserɛfoɛ nemɔ, bɛ dumaa ɛhe: Takemoniniɛ Yosebo Basebete bɔ né ɔla koɛhonɛfoɛ ahoneserɛfoɛ nza nemɔ noa ne. Ɔhwene ye pealɛɛ wɔ mmenia ɛyaa mmɔtwɛ so huhuni bɛ wɔ koɛ komapɛ anu.

english_verse: The next one of the Three Warriors was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite. One time when the Philistines were at war with Israel, he and David dared the Philistines to fight them. Every one of the Israelite soldiers turned and ran,
translation_verse: Sɛ Yosebo Basebete nne berɛ a, Eleasa bɔ ɔse ole Dodo, bɔ ye koso ɔse ole Ahohi ne, ye yeɛ ɔwɔ berɛ ɔ. Eleasa boka koɛhonɛfoɛ ahoneserɛfoɛ nza ne aso. Mmerɛ bɔ Filistifoɛ boale bɛ noa kyɛ bɛ ne Yisraelfoɛ bɛbaaho ne, né Eleasa boka Dawide so. Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ nwatili,

english_verse: but Shammah stood in the middle of the field and killed the Philistines. The crops were saved, and the Lord gave Israel a great victory.
translation_verse: Nakoso Sama de, oogyinane eboo ne afia bɔle eboo ne nwo waen, na ohuhuni Filistifoɛ nemɔ. Na AWURADE maa olili ngonim kandinga.

english_verse: One year at harvest time, the Three Warriors went to meet David at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley
translation_verse: Na atokoɔ telɛ mmerɛ dwuli ne, koɛhonɛfoɛ atitire aburasa ne, bɛ nu nza hɔle Dawide berɛ wɔ nyɔboɛ bɔ wasi sua wɔ Adulam ne anu. Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Filistifoɛ fekue bie baakyekye asikyeleɛ wɔ Refaim bɔnza ne anu.

english_verse: and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in his fortress,
translation_verse: Né Dawide wɔ anwoserɛ afealeɛ ne anu; yeɛ né Filistifoɛ kure ne koso bɛwɔ Betlehem.

english_verse: and he was very thirsty. He said, “I wish I had a drink from the well by the gate at Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Na Dawide le aworadɔlɛ hane kyɛ, “Abura bɔ ɔwɔ Betlehem kuro berɛ pambim ne anwo ne, sɛ ebie sa nu nzue brɛ me maa meno a, ahaa mekuro.”

english_verse: The Three Warriors sneaked into the Philistine camp and got some water from the well near Bethlehem's gate. But after they brought the water back to David, he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as a sacrifice
translation_verse: Yiti koɛhonɛfoɛ ahoneserɛfoɛ nza nemɔ sili bɛ hue bɛhɔle Filistifoɛ asikyeleɛ ne anu. Na abura bɔ ɔwɔ Betlehem kuro berɛ pambim ne anwo ne, bɛsale nu nzue ne bie bɛbrɛle Dawide. Nakoso wanno, na mmom ohwie guale mane AWURADE;

english_verse: and said to the Lord, “I can't drink this water! It's like the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it for me.” The Three Warriors did these brave deeds. The Thirty Warriors (
translation_verse: ofikyɛ ɔhane kyɛ, “Daabi, AWURADE pa gua kyɛ ngɔno nzue ne ɔ! Sɛ meno a, mmenia bɔ bɛfale bɛ ngoa bɛtole serewa bɛɛsale nzue ne bɛwale ne, né mano bɛ mogya!” Yiti wanno. Sɔ koɛhonɛfoɛ ahoneserɛfoɛ nza nemɔ yeɛ bɛyɔle sɔ nikyee ne ɔ.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. He killed two of Moab's best fighters, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
translation_verse: Yehoada awa Benaya bɔ ofi Kabeseel ne, né ɔte koɛhonɛniɛ ahoneserɛniɛ bɔ ye hue yɛ se paa wɔ nningyein pee anu ɔ. Ohuni Moabofoɛ nyɔ bɔ b’ahone yɛ se te kyɛ gyata ɔ. Asa koso, oohuni gyata wɔ abura bie anu ɛlɛho bie bɔ né asukɔtwea tɔ gua ɔ.

english_verse: Another time, he killed an Egyptian, as big as a giant. The Egyptian was armed with a spear, but Benaiah only had a club. Benaiah grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it.
translation_verse: Osa huni Misraimniɛ branoa bie. Né Misraimniɛ ne tira pealɛɛ, nakoso Benaya fale abopura hɔle ye so. Ofotili pealɛɛ ne fili Misraimniɛ ne sa nu, na ɔfale Misraimniɛ ne bɔbɔ ye pealɛɛ ne huni ye.

english_verse: Benaiah did these things. He never became one of the Three Warriors, but he was just as famous as they were and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. David made him the leader of his bodyguard.
translation_verse: Olele dumaa paa wɔ koɛhonɛfoɛ ahoneserɛfoɛ aburasa nemɔ anu, nakoso wando koɛhonɛfoɛ ahoneserɛfoɛ nza nemɔ. Na Dawide nwo ɛwaenbɔlɛfoɛ nemɔ, ɔbɔle ye bɛ so panyi.

english_verse: and said, “Your Majesty! Why have you come to see me?” David answered, “I've come to buy your threshing place. I have to build the Lord an altar here, so this disease will stop killing the people.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Arayuna bisale kyɛ, “Nana, me mene, nzu ati yeɛ awa w’akoaa berɛ ɔ?” Na Dawide buale kyɛ, “Nekaa bɔ bɛboro aburoo ne, mebaatɔ mefi wɔ berɛ mefa mesi afɔleɛ bokyea mema AWURADE, amaa ɔnate so waye amaneɛ ne wafi maen ne aso.”

english_verse: They went to Gilead and to Kadesh in Syria. Then they went to Dan, Ijon, and on toward Sidon.
translation_verse: Afei beedwuli Gileade, yeɛ Kadese bɔ ɔwɔ Hitifoɛ aseɛ so. Befili berɛ bɛhɔle Dan, na bɛtoale so bɛhɔle Sidon.

english_verse: So David told Joab and the army officers, “Go to every tribe in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north all the way south to Beersheba, and count everyone who can serve in the army. I want to know how many there are.”
translation_verse: Yiti Nana Dawide sele Yoabo ne safohene nemɔ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔɔhyini Yisrael mmusua kure amukoraa nu, fite Dan bɔ ɔkwaadwu Beɛ Hyeba, ná ɛ́mɔha mmenia ne ma nwu bɛ somaa.”

english_verse: But when David refused to change his mind, Joab and the army officers went out and started counting the people.
translation_verse: Nakoso Nana Dawide tuli Yoabo ne safohene nemɔ bɛ dwirɛ deɛ guale. Yiti Yoabo ne safohene nemɔ fili Nana Dawide nyunu berɛ, na besili nu bɛhɔle kyɛ bɛkwaaha Yisraelfoɛ.

english_verse: They crossed the Jordan River and began with Aroer and the town in the middle of the river valley. From there they went toward Gad and on as far as Jazer.
translation_verse: Bɛɛpɛle asue Yɔɔdan, na besikyele wɔ Aroye, wɔ kuro ne ngwaen dɔ wɔ bɔnza ne anu, wɔ Gade ndendeneɛ so, na bɛtoale so bɛhɔle Yasere.

english_verse: After they had gone through the whole land, they went back to Jerusalem. It had taken them
translation_verse: Bɛfale bosome ngona ne eleburanyɔ yeɛ behyinini aseɛ ne aso amukoraa beyiele ɔ, na besa bɛwale Yerusalem.

english_verse: Araunah looked and saw David and his soldiers coming up toward him. He went over to David, bowed down low,
translation_verse: Arayuna tole ye nye, na onwuni Nana Dawide ne ye mbanyi mɔ kyɛ bɛba ye nwo berɛ. Arayuna ooyiale bɛ, na ɔlale aseɛnwo berɛ fale ye nyunu butuli ase wɔ Nana Dawide nyunu.

english_verse: David saw the angel killing everyone and told the Lord, “These people are like sheep with me as their shepherd. I have sinned terribly, but they have done nothing wrong. Please, punish me and my family instead of them!” David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place (
translation_verse: Na Dawide nwuni abɔfo bɔ ogu so oku mmenia nemɔ nen, osele AWURADE kyɛ, “Bɔne ne, me ngome yeɛ mayɔ ɔ, mvomsoɛ ne, me ngome yeɛ mayɔ ɔ. english_verse: After everyone had been counted, David realized he had done wrong. He told the Lord, “What I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Lord, please forgive me.”
translation_verse: Dawide maa bɛhale mmenia ne beyiele nen, nziɛ ye, ye tiboa buale ye fɔ. Na Dawide fa tole AWURADE nyunu kyɛ, “Bɔ mayɔ ye, mayɔ bɔne paa. Nakoso AWURADE, mesrɛ wɔ ala, fa w’akoaa amumuyɛɛ kyɛ ye, ofikyɛ mali ngwaseasɛm paa.”

english_verse: to take a message to David. Gad went to David and told him: You must choose one of three ways for the Lord to punish you: Will there be seven years when the land won't grow enough food for your people? Or will your enemies chase you and make you run from them for three months? Or will there be three days of horrible disease in your land? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God, who sent me.
translation_verse: Yiti Gade wale Dawide berɛ ɔɔbɔle ye amaneɛ. Obisale ye kyɛ, “Beni yeɛ ekuro ɔ? Kyɛ ɛhɔen kɔpe wɔ maen nu afoɛ nzoo, anaakyɛ ɛkɔnwati kofi wɔ pɔfoɛ mɔ bɔ bɛ́fõa wɔ ɔ nyunu bosome nza, anaakyɛ anwonyerɛ tɛɛ kɔte kɔpe wɔ maen nu ɛlɛsa. english_verse: David was really frightened and said, “It's a terrible choice to make! But the Lord is kind, and I'd rather be punished by him than by anyone else.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Dawide buale Gade kyɛ, “Yieee, edwirɛ piri paa yeɛ wato me e! Kyɛ kuro sona kɔhwe me so de, ye de ma AWURADE mmom ɔhwe yɛ so, ofikyɛ ye de, ye anwumvoinnwunɛ te piri.”

english_verse: Araunah said, “Take whatever you want and offer your sacrifice. Here are some oxen for the sacrifice. You can use the threshing-boards and the wooden yokes for the fire.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Arayuna sele Dawide kyɛ, “Nana, me mene, fa, fa aseɛ ne, ná bɔ afɔleɛ biala bɔ ekuro ɔ. Nandwie mɔ bɔ ɛkɔfa kɔbɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ɛhe, yeɛ ndaboa bɔ bɛboro so aburoo, ɔne nandwie kɔme anu mmakaa bɔ ɛkɔfa kɔsɔ see ɛhe.

english_verse: That same day the prophet Gad came and told David, “Go to the threshing place that belongs to Araunah and build an altar there for the Lord.” So David went.
translation_verse: Dawide lili Gade dwirɛ ne aso, na ɔfo hɔle berɛ, kyɛbɔ AWURADE hyɛle ne ala.

english_verse: Take them—they're yours! I hope the Lord your God will be pleased with you.”
translation_verse: Nana, me mene, me Arayuna, mefa sɔ nningyein ne amukoraa mema wɔ.” Yeɛ Arayuna toale so sele kyɛ, “Mesrɛ kyɛ AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ ole w’afɔleɛ ne ɔto nu.”

english_verse: But David answered, “No! I have to pay you what they're worth. I can't offer the Lord my God a sacrifice that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing place and the oxen for
translation_verse: Nakoso Nana Dawide buale Arayuna kyɛ, “Daabi! Ɛtɔlɛ yeɛ ngɔtɔ ngofi wɔ berɛ ɔ. Ngotua ye kerɛ, kyɛbɔ bɛ nyɔboɛ te ɔ.
