english_verse: For many years the country of Moab had been controlled by Israel and was forced to pay taxes to the kings of Israel. King Mesha of Moab raised sheep, so he paid the king of Israel
translation_verse: Né Moabo hene Mesa osie mmoaen. Na ɔyɛ a, né ɔfa mmoaen akrɔngrɔma apee ɛyaa ko otua toɔ ma Yisrael hene. Né osa ɔfa mmoaen nyii apee ɛyaa ko bɛ nwo nwiaa otua toɔ ma ye.

english_verse: But soon after the death of Ahab, Mesha rebelled against Israel.
translation_verse: Nakoso Ahabo wuli ne, Moabo hene yɛle Yisrael hene nwo lɔen.

english_verse: One day, Joram left Samaria and called together Israel's army.
translation_verse: Yiti sɔ mmerɛ ne, Nana Yehoram sili nu fili Samaria ɔɔboaboale Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa noa.

english_verse: He sent this message to King Jehoshaphat of Judah, “The king of Moab has rebelled. Will you go with me to attack him?” “Yes, I will,” Jehoshaphat answered. “I'm on your side, and my soldiers and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Ɔkɔ ne, ɔmaa bɛɛbɔle Yuda hene Yehosafate amaneɛ kyɛ, “Moabo hene ayɛ me nwo lɔen. Ɛkɔɔboka me maa me ne Moabo yɛkɔho anaa?” Yehosafate buale kyɛ, “Ngɔhɔ, ngyi wɔ si. Me lɔen te wɔ lɔen, yeɛ me mbɔngɔ te wɔ deɛ.”

english_verse: But which way should we go?” “We will march through Edom Desert,” Joram replied.
translation_verse: Osa bisale kyɛ, “Nisua atee yeɛ yɛfa so yɛkɔ ɔ?” Na Yehoram buale kyɛ, “Yɛkɔfa Edom ɛserɛ so atee ne aso.”

english_verse: So Joram, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom led their troops out. But seven days later, there was no drinking water left for them or their animals.
translation_verse: Yiti Yisrael hene, Yuda hene yeɛ Edom hene besili nu. Na bɛpɛle atee bɔ ɔkondo ɔ ɛlɛsoo ne, né bennya nzue bɛmma koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ ne bɛ ngaka bɔ bɛboka bɛ so ne.

english_verse: Joram cried out, “This is terrible! The Lord must have led us out here to be captured by Moab's army.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yisrael hene sele kyɛ, “Aworabɔlɛ dwirɛ! Eh, ahemvo nza ye, aso AWURADE aboaboa yɛ noa, kyɛ ɔbaafa yɛ wura Moabo hene sa anaa!”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat said, “Which of the Lord's prophets is with us? We can find out from him what the Lord wants us to do.” One of Joram's officers answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He was one of Elijah's closest followers.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Yehosafate bisale kyɛ, “Aso AWURADE ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ nne wa, bɔ yɛkɔhora yɛkɔfa ye so yɛkobisa AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɔ?” Yeɛ Yisrael hene somvoɛ nemɔ nu ko buale kyɛ, “Safate awa Elisa bɔ né ɔte Elia somvoɛ ne, ɔwɔ berɛ.”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat replied, “He can give us the Lord's message.” The three kings went over to Elisha,
translation_verse: Yehosafate sele kyɛ, “Amba AWURADE fa ye so dwudwo.” Yiti Yisrael hene ne Yehosafate ne Edom hene besili nu bɛhɔle Elisa berɛ.

english_verse: and he asked Joram, “Why did you come to me? Go talk to the prophets of the foreign gods your parents worshiped.” “No,” Joram answered. “It was the Lord who led us out here, so that Moab's army could capture us.”
translation_verse: Elisa sele Yisrael hene kyɛ, “Ɛpena nzu me dɔ? Kɔ ɛse ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ ne eni ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ nemɔ dɔ.” Nakoso Yisrael hene buale ye kyɛ, “Daabi, ɔyɛ me kyɛ AWURADE yeɛ waboa yɛ ahemvo nza ye yɛ noa kyɛ ɔbaafa yɛ wura Moabo sa ɔ.”

english_verse: Elisha said to him, “I serve the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as he lives, I swear I wouldn't even look at you if I didn't respect King Jehoshaphat.”
translation_verse: Elisa sele kyɛ, “Kyɛbɔ Asafo AWURADE bɔ ngyi ye nyunu ye ɔte ase ye, sɛ nna Yuda hene Yehosafate yeɛ mefa me nye meto ye a, ahaa mengɔnea wɔ nyunu po anaa mengɔtɛ wɔ so.

english_verse: Then Elisha said, “Send for someone who can play the harp.” The harpist began playing, and the Lord gave Elisha this message for Joram:
translation_verse: Nakoso ɛ́mɔpena edweintolɛniɛ bɛ́ma me.” Na edweintolɛniɛ ne gu so ɔto dwein ne, AWURADE tumi wale Elisa so.

english_verse: The Lord says that this dry riverbed will be filled with water.
translation_verse: Na osele kyɛ, “AWURADE nwa, ‘Sɔ bɔnza bɔ nu ayɛ wosee ye, ngɔmaa nzue koyi nu.’

english_verse: You won't feel any wind or see any rain, but there will be plenty of water for you and your animals.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ AWURADE nwa, ‘Ɛmɔngonwu kyɛ mvrama tu ɔ, yeɛ ɛmɔngonwu kyɛ esue tɔ ɔ, nakoso nzue koyi bɔnza ne anu tɛkyɛ, amaa ɔnate so ɛmɔ ne ɛmɔ nyɛmmoa ne ɛmɔ ngaka banya bie bano.’

english_verse: That simple thing isn't all the Lord is going to do. He will also help you defeat Moab's army.
translation_verse: Ɛhe te nikyee kaaba koraa wɔ AWURADE nye so, ofikyɛ ɔkɔfa Moabo kowura ɛmɔ sa koso.

english_verse: You will capture all their walled cities and important towns. You will chop down every good tree and stop up every spring of water, then ruin their fertile fields by covering them with rocks.
translation_verse: Kuro biala bɔ bato ye nwo fasue, ɔne kuro titire biala, ɛmɔkoli so ngonim. Bakaa bɔ bedi ye mma biala ɛmɔkobu ye bɛkɔto ase. Mbombonzue biala, ɛmɔkotua nekaa bɔ nzue ne ofi opu ba ɔ, na aseɛ bɔ ɔkye aleɛ biala, ɛmɔkɔhwe nyɔboɛ bekogua so bɛkɔsɛkye ye.”

english_verse: The next morning, while the sacrifice was being offered, water suddenly started flowing from the direction of Edom, and it flooded the land.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, ngyerɛmɔ afɔleɛbɔlɛ mmerɛ dwuli ne, mvum nu, nzue fi Edom bue nu dɔ pu wale alaa, kɔpem kyɛ nzue buli aseɛ ne aso nekaa biala ɔ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Moab had heard that the three kings were coming to attack them. They had called together all of their fighting men, from the youngest to the oldest, and these troops were now standing at their border, ready for battle.
translation_verse: Moabofoɛ amukoraa bɛtele kyɛ ahemvo nemɔ bafa koɛ batoa bɛ ne, bɛfrɛfrɛle bɛ mmenia bɔ baso koɛhonɛ amukoraa, fi mmerandeɛ so kɔpem mbanyi so maa bɛboale bɛ noa wɔ ɛwɛen ne aso.

english_verse: When they got up that morning, the sun was shining across the water, making it look red. The Moabite troops took one look
translation_verse: Moabo koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ dwɔsole ngyerɛmɔ tutuutu, na eyia bɔle nzue ne aso ne, benwuni nzue bɔ ɔwɔ bɛ ndendeneɛ so ne kyɛ ɔte kɔɔ kyɛ mogya.

english_verse: and shouted, “Look at that blood! The armies of those kings must have fought and killed each other. Come on, let's go take what's left in their camp.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ bɛteanene nu kyɛ, “Mogya ɛne! Bekye ahemvo nemɔ bapɛ bɛ nwo baho bahũhũ bɛ nwo. Moabofoɛ ee, ɛ́mɔma yɛɛsesa koɛ nu nzesadeɛ ne!”

english_verse: But when they arrived at Israel's camp, the Israelite soldiers came out and attacked them, until they turned and ran away. Israel's army chased them all the way back to Moab, and even there they kept up the attack.
translation_verse: Nakoso Moabo koɛhonɛfoɛ beedwuli Yisrael koɛhonɛfoɛ asikyeleɛ ne anwo ne, Yisraelfoɛ dwɔsole bɛfale koɛ bɛtetale bɛ. Moabofoɛ nwatili fili Yisraelfoɛ nyunu. Na Yisraelfoɛ foane Moabofoɛ behuhuni bɛ toonn wɔ Moabo aseɛ so.

english_verse: The Israelites destroyed the Moabite towns. They chopped down the good trees and stopped up the springs of water, then covered the fertile fields with rocks. Finally, the only city left standing was Kir-Hareseth, but soldiers armed with slings surrounded and attacked it.
translation_verse: Bɛsɛkyele nguro nemɔ anu nningyein pasaa, na aseɛ bɔ ɔkye aleɛ biala koso bɛ nu biala gyili nyɔboɛ tole so, kɔpem kyɛ nyɔboɛ katale aseɛ ne aso amukoraa ɔ. Mbombonzue biala, nekaa bɔ ye nzue ne ofi opu ɔba ne, betuale ye, na bakaa bɔ bedi ye mma biala koso, bebu bɛtole ase. Kire Haresete angome yeɛ ɔte kuro bɔ bammubu ye nyɔboɛ fasue ɔ, kɔpem kyɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛto nyɔboɛ ne, bɛɛpɛle ye nwo beyiale bɛfale koɛ bɛtetale ye ɔ.

english_verse: King Mesha of Moab saw that he was about to be defeated. So he took along
translation_verse: Moabo hene nwuni kyɛ ɔpena di ngoguo ne, ɔfale koɛhonɛfoɛ ɛyaa nzoo bɔ betiratira ngrandɛ, kyɛ bɛkwaatutu bɛfa Edom hene ndendeneɛ so dɔ bɛnwati bɛkɔ, nakoso bangora.

english_verse: He then grabbed his oldest son who was to be the next king and sacrificed him as an offering on the city wall. The Israelite troops were so horrified that they left the city and went back home.
translation_verse: Yiti Moabo hene hyele ye bamuɛbaa bienzua bɔ kyẽa bie okoli ye bia ɔ, na ɔfale ye bɔle naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ wɔ fasue ne aso. Na ɛyaafɛlɛ piri wale Yisrael so. Yiti bandoa koɛ ne aso ko, na besale bɛ si bɛhɔle bɛ bɔbɔ bɛ maen nu.

english_verse: One day the widow of one of the Lord's prophets said to Elisha, “You know that before my husband died, he was a follower of yours and a worshiper of the Lord. But he owed a man some money, and now that man is on his way to take my two sons as his slaves.”
translation_verse: Ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ fekue ne, bɛ nu ko aye oosuni hyirele Elisa kyɛ, “Me hu, bɔ ɔte wɔ somvoɛ ne, wawu. Ɛse kyɛ wɔ somvoɛ, né osuro AWURADE. Nakoso ebie bɔ yɛma ye kerɛ ɔ, wawa kyɛ ɔbaafa me mma nyɔ nemɔ yɛ nganga sie kerɛ ne anoa.”

english_verse: “Maybe there's something I can do to help,” Elisha said. “What do you have in your house?” “Sir, I have nothing but a small bottle of olive oil.”
translation_verse: Elisa bisale ye kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ yeɛ nyɔ mma wɔ ɔ? Ka kyire me, nzikyɛ yeɛ ele ye wɔ awuro ɔ.” Braa ne buale kyɛ, “W’afaneɛ, nnne nikye fee wɔ awuro, sana ngoo bua ko ala.”

english_verse: Elisha told her, “Ask your neighbors for their empty jars. And after you've borrowed as many as you can,
translation_verse: Na Elisa sele ye kyɛ, ‘‘Fite kɔsrɛsrɛ bua fi wɔ mmango mɔ amukoraa bɛ berɛ. De bua bɔ hwee nne nu ɔ; pena pee.

english_verse: go home and shut the door behind you and your sons. Then begin filling the jars with oil and set each one aside as you fill it.”
translation_verse: Afei ɛne wɔ mma mɔ, ɛmɔhɔ sua nu ná ɛ́mɔto ɛmɔ nwo anoa nu. Hwiehwie ngoo ne gua bua nemɔ amukoraa nu. Bɔ okoyi biala, fa sie ahameɛ.”

english_verse: The woman left. Later, when she and her sons were back inside their house, the two sons brought her the jars, and she began filling them.
translation_verse: Yiti braa ne fili Elisa nwo berɛ hɔle, na ɔne ye mma mɔ bɛɛtole bɛ nwo anoa nu. Bɛhɔle so bɛsesale bua bɛmane ye, na ye koso ɔhɔle so ohwiehwiele ngoo ne guaguale nu.

english_verse: At last, she said to one of her sons, “Bring me another jar.” “We don't have any more,” he answered, and the oil stopped flowing from the small bottle.
translation_verse: Bua nemɔ yiyili ne, osele ɔwa ne ko kyɛ, “Fa bua bieku brɛ me.” Nakoso obuale ye kyɛ, “Bua ko nne berɛ.” Yeɛ ngoo bɔ ohwie ne ɔpɛle ɔ.

english_verse: After she told Elisha what had happened, he said, “Sell the oil and use part of the money to pay what you owe the man. You and your sons can live on what is left.” Elisha Brings a Rich Woman's Son Back to Life
translation_verse: Braa ne ɔɔbɔle Nyameɛ sona ne amaneɛ, na osele braa ne kyɛ, “Kɔtɔne ngoo ne fa tuatua wɔ nwo kerɛ. Na bɔ ɔkɔha ne, ɛne wɔ mma mɔ, ɛ́mɔfa bɛnea bɛ nwo.” Elisa ne Sunamniɛ braa ne

english_verse: Once, while Elisha was in the town of Shunem, he met a rich woman who invited him to her home for dinner. After that, whenever he was in Shunem, he would have a meal there with her and her husband.
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, né Elisa ɔpɛ nu wɔ Sunem. Né braa sikaniɛ bie te kuro berɛ. Ɔtole ye sa frɛle Elisa srɛle ye maa oodidili. Yiti mmerɛ biala, sɛ Elisa ɔpɛ nu kuro berɛ a, né wafa braa ne berɛ waadidi.

english_verse: Some time later the woman said to her husband, “I'm sure the man who comes here so often is a prophet of God.
translation_verse: Nziɛ ye, braa ne sele ohu kyɛ, “Tie, mede medi kyɛ biaa ye bɔ ɔtaa ba yɛ wa ye, ɔte Nyameɛ sona krongron.

english_verse: Why don't we build him a small room on the flat roof of our house? We can put a bed, a table and chair, and an oil lamp in it. Then whenever he comes, he can stay with us.”
translation_verse: Mesrɛ wɔ, sua bɔ yasamo so ne, maa yɛsi sua kaaba ko yɛsie so yɛma ye, ná yɛfa mba, ɛpoen, bia ne kanea yɛsiesie nu, amaa mmerɛ biala bɔ ɔkɔwa yɛ wa ne, né waala nu.”

english_verse: The next time Elisha was in Shunem, he stopped at their house and went up to his room to rest.
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, Elisa hɔle kuro berɛ, na ɔhɔle aborɔsaen ne aso ɔɔlale sua ne anu.

english_verse: He said to his servant Gehazi, “This woman has been very helpful. Have her come up here to the roof for a moment.” She came, and Elisha told Gehazi to say to her, “You've gone to a lot of trouble for us, and we want to help you. Is there something we can request the king or army commander to do?” The woman answered, “With my relatives nearby, I have everything I need.”
translation_verse: Elisa sele Gehasi kyɛ, “Bisa ye ma yɛ kyɛ, ‘Ɛfɛɛ wora bɔ afɛ yɛ nwo ye, nzikyɛ yeɛ ekuro kyɛ yɛyɔ yɛma wɔ ɔ? Yɛɛfa wɔ dwirɛ yɛto nana anaa koɛhonɛfoɛ safohene nyunu yɛma wɔ anaa?’ ” Na braa ne buale ye kyɛ, “Nde me bɔbɔ me maen nu.”

english_verse: “Then what can we do for her?” Elisha asked Gehazi. Gehazi replied, “I do know that her husband is old, and that she doesn't have a son.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Elisa bisale kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ yeɛ yɛkɔyɔ yɛkɔma braa ye ɔ?” Na Gehasi buale kyɛ, “Braa ne olle ba, yeɛ ohu koso wayɛ aworowaa.”

english_verse: “Ask her to come here again,” Elisha told his servant. He called for her, and she came and stood in the doorway of Elisha's room.
translation_verse: Elisa sele kyɛ, “Frɛ ye bra.” Na Gehasi frɛle braa ne maa oogyinane anoa ne anyunu berɛ.

english_verse: Elisha said to her, “Next year at this time, you'll be holding your own baby son in your arms.” “You're a man of God,” the woman replied. “Please don't lie to me.”
translation_verse: Na Elisa sele kyɛ, “Afoɛ bieku bekye sua, ɛkɔfa ɛwa kɔto wɔ gya so.” Yeɛ braa ne buale kyɛ, “Daabi, me mene, Nyameɛ sona, nnɛlakalaka w’afaneɛ.”

english_verse: But a few months later, the woman got pregnant. She gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had promised.
translation_verse: Braa ne nwonzɛle, na mmerɛ ne dwuli ne, ɔwole baa bienzua, kyɛbɔ Elisa hã hyirele ye ne ala.

english_verse: One day while the boy was still young, he was out in the fields with his father, where the workers were harvesting the crops.
translation_verse: Akwadaa ne nyini, na ɛlɛho bie, ɔpole ye baba so wɔ nekaa bɔ biaa ne ɔne mmenia bɛte ayuo ɔ.

english_verse: Suddenly he shouted, “My head hurts. It hurts a lot!” “Carry him back to his mother,” the father said to his servant.
translation_verse: Ɔhã hyirele ye baba kyɛ, “Aa, me ti pakye me, me ti pakye me!” Na biaa ne sele ye bɔbɔ ye somvoɛ kyɛ, “Pagya ye kɔma ye maame.”

english_verse: loaves of bread made from the first barley that was harvested. Elisha said, “Give it to the people so they can eat.”
translation_verse: Ɔpagyale ye ɔɔmane ye maame. Akwadaa ne lale ye maame gya so toonn maa oodwuli eyia, na owuli.

english_verse: She carried him upstairs to Elisha's room and laid him across the bed. Then she walked out and shut the door behind her.
translation_verse: Braa ne fole aborɔsaen ne na ɔɔfale akwadaa ne tole Nyameɛ sona ne mba so. Ɔtole ye anoa nu, na ɔyakyili ye berɛ hɔle.

english_verse: The woman called to her husband, “I need to see the prophet. Let me use one of the donkeys. Send a servant along with me, and let me leave now, so I can get back quickly.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ braa ne somane ma beesele ohu kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, ma somvoɛ nemɔ anu ko ɔfa afunum beleɛ nemɔ anu ko ɔbrɛ me, na ngɔ Nyameɛ sona ne berɛ kekesaala ye nza mmra.”

english_verse: “Why do you need to see him today?” her husband asked. “It's not the Sabbath or time for the New Moon Festival.” “That's all right,” she answered.
translation_verse: Ohu bisale kyɛ, “Ɛnɛ kyẽa ye, nna ɛsraen foforɛ aluolue kyẽa ɔ, yeɛ nna afofikyẽa ɔ, nzu ati yeɛ ɛkɔ ye berɛ ɔ? Na braa ne buale kyɛ, “Ɔte bɔkɔɔ”

english_verse: She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Let's go. And don't slow down unless I tell you to.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ braa ne siesiele afunum ne, na ɔhã hyirele ye somvoɛ ne kyɛ, “Ma kaka ne ɔhã ye nwo; nnɛmaa ogyina, sana mahã mahyire wɔ kyɛ maa ogyina.”

english_verse: She left at once for Mount Carmel to talk with Elisha. When Elisha saw her coming, he said, “Gehazi, look! It's the woman from Shunem.
translation_verse: Yiti osili nu hɔle Nyameɛ sona ne berɛ wɔ Kamɛl bokaa ne anwo. Nyameɛ sona ne nwuni kyɛ braa ne ba ne, osele ye somvoɛ Gehasi kyɛ, “Nea, Sunamniɛ braa ne yeɛ ɔba ne.

english_verse: Run and meet her. And ask her if everything is all right with her and her family.” “Everything is fine,” she answered Gehazi.
translation_verse: Tu amirika koyia ye, na bisa ye kyɛ, “Wɔ nwo te paa? Ehu nwo te paa? Akwadaa ne nwo te paa? Na braa ne buale kyɛ, “Yɛ nwo te paa.”

english_verse: But as soon as she got to the top of the mountain, she went over and grabbed Elisha by the feet. Gehazi started toward her to push her away, when Elisha said, “Leave her alone! Don't you see how sad she is? But the Lord hasn't told me why.”
translation_verse: Braa ne oodwuli Nyameɛ sona ne anwo berɛ wɔ bokaa ne aso ne, ɔkotole sɔle ye gya. Gehasi hɔle braa ne anwo berɛ kyɛ ɔkwaapia ye fi berɛ. Nakoso Nyameɛ sona ne sele kyɛ, “Yakyi ye, ofikyɛ odi aworabɔlɛ piri; AWURADE afa afea me bɔ wanga wangyire me ɔ.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Sir, I begged you not to get my hopes up, and I didn't even ask you for a son.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ braa ne nwa, “Me mene, aso nzrɛle wɔ dɔ baa anaa? Manga kyɛ nnɛlakalaka me?”

english_verse: “Gehazi, get ready and go to her house,” Elisha said. “Take along my walking stick, and when you get there, lay it on the boy's face. Don't stop to talk to anyone, even if they try to talk to you.”
translation_verse: Na Elisa sele Gehasi kyɛ, “Bɔ w’abɔsoɛ, fa me pɔmaa ne tira, na si nu kɔ. Sɛ eyia ebiala wɔ atunu a, nnebisa ye ahye; na sɛ ebiala bisa wɔ ahye a, nnesuro. Fa me pɔmaa ne kɔto akwadaa ne aso.”

english_verse: But the boy's mother said to Elisha, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I won't leave without you.” So Elisha got up and went with them.
translation_verse: Yeɛ akwadaa ne maame sele kyɛ, “Kyɛ AWURADE te ase ye, ɔne kyɛ wɔ koso ɛte ase ye, sɛ ɛne me angɔ a, mengɔhɔ.” Yiti Elisa dwɔsole lili braa ne asi.

english_verse: Gehazi ran on ahead and laid Elisha's walking stick on the boy's face, but the boy didn't move or make a sound. Gehazi ran back to Elisha and said, “The boy didn't wake up.”
translation_verse: Gehasi lili bɛ nyunu moa, na ɔɔfale pɔmaa ne tole akwadaa ne aso, nakoso akwadaa ne wangekã ye nwo. Gehasi sa ooyiale Elisa, na ɔbɔle ye amaneɛ kyɛ, “Akwadaa ne andingye.”

english_verse: Elisha arrived at the woman's house and went straight to his room, where he saw the boy's body on his bed.
translation_verse: Elisa wurale awuro berɛ ne, onwuni kyɛ akwadaa ne wawu. Né ɔla Elisa mba ne aso.

english_verse: He walked in, shut the door, and prayed to the Lord.
translation_verse: Yiti ɔworole sua nu berɛ, na ɔtole ye nwo ne akwadaa ne anoa nu, na ɔbɔle mbaeɛ hyirele AWURADE.

english_verse: Then he got on the bed and stretched out over the dead body, with his mouth on the boy's mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hand on his hands. As he lay there, the boy's body became warm.
translation_verse: Ɔfole mba ne aso, na obutuli akwadaa ne aso. Ɔmane ye noa hane akwadaa ne noa, ye nye hane akwadaa ne nye, yeɛ ye sa fuafuale akwadaa ne asa nu. Na ɔtɛ butu akwadaa ne aso ne, akwadaa ne anwo yɛle hye.

english_verse: Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the room, then he went back and leaned over the boy's body. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
translation_verse: Elisa dwɔsole, ɔhɔle sua ne ti wale ye ti, na osa fole mba ne oobutuli akwadaa ne aso. Akwadaa ne pɛle yaen pɛen nzoo, na ɔtetele ye nye.

english_verse: Elisha called out to Gehazi, “Ask the boy's mother to come here.” Gehazi did, and when she was at the door, Elisha said, “You can take your son.”
translation_verse: Elisa frɛle Gehasi na osele ye kyɛ, “Frɛ Sunamniɛ braa ne maa ɔbra.” Yiti ɔfrɛle ye. Braa ne wale Elisa nwo berɛ, na Elisa sele ye kyɛ, “De ɛwa ne.”

english_verse: She came in and bowed down at Elisha's feet. Then she picked up her son and left. Elisha Makes Some Stew Taste Better
translation_verse: Braa ne wurale nu, ɔtole ye nwo yele Elisa gya bo, ɔfale ye nyunu butuli ase, na afei ɔfale ɔwa ne fitele. Elisa ma ɛborɔ fi aleɛ nu

english_verse: Later, Elisha went back to Gilgal, where there was almost nothing to eat, because the crops had failed. One day while the prophets who lived there were meeting with Elisha, he said to his servant, “Prepare a big pot of stew for these prophets.”
translation_verse: Elisa sa wale Gilgal. Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né ɛhɔen ape maen ne anu. Mmerɛ bɔ ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ fekue ne bɛtete Elisa nyunu berɛ ne, osele ye somvoɛ ne kyɛ, “Fa turonzemaa piri ne sie see so, na yɛ turoo ma ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ fekue ne.”

english_verse: One of them went out into the woods to gather some herbs. He found a wild vine and picked as much of its fruit as he could carry, but he didn't know that the fruit was very sour. When he got back, he cut up the fruit and put it in the stew.
translation_verse: Bɛ nu ko hɔle buro kyɛ ɔkwaatete kwaanzusuaa. Onwuni eburo nyamaa bie, na ɔtetele ye mma ne bie guale ye tena nu maa oyili. Osa wale ɔɔpepɛle guale turo ne anu, wɔ aberɛ bɔ né ɔnze nikye horɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The stew was served, and when the prophets started eating it, they shouted, “Elisha, this stew tastes terrible! We can't eat it.”
translation_verse: Bɛsale bie bɛmane ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ nemɔ kyɛ beli. Nakoso begu so bedidi ne, bɛteane nu kyɛ, “O Nyameɛ sona, ɛborɔ wɔ turo ne anu!” Na bangora ye di.

english_verse: “Bring me some flour,” Elisha said. He sprinkled the flour in the stew and said, “Now serve it to them.” And the stew tasted fine. Elisha Feeds One Hundred People
translation_verse: Yeɛ Elisa sele kyɛ, “Nzaade ɛ́mɔma me esam kãa.” Ɔfa guale turonzemaa ne anu, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Sa bie maa beli.” Na turoo bɔ ɔwɔ turonzemaa ne anu ne, ɛborɔ ne fili nu. Elisa ma mmenia ɛyaa ko aleɛ

english_verse: So the servant served the bread and grain to the people. They ate and still had some left over, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Ɔfa siele bɛ nyunu, na belili maa ebie hale, kyɛbɔ AWURADE hane ne ala.

english_verse: Naaman was the commander of the Syrian army. The Lord had helped him and his troops defeat their enemies, so the king of Syria respected Naaman very much. Naaman was a brave soldier, but he had leprosy.
translation_verse: Naaman te Siria hene ye koɛhonɛfoɛ so safohene. Né ɔte sona titire bɔ ye mene Siria hene kuro ye dwirɛ ɔ, ofikyɛ ɔnate ye so, AWURADE mane Siria lili ngonim wɔ koɛ nu. Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ né biaa ne te koɛhonɛniɛ titire paa de, nakoso né kwata anwonyerɛ ayɛ ye.

english_verse: One day while the Syrian troops were raiding Israel, they captured a girl, and she became a servant of Naaman's wife.
translation_verse: Siriafoɛ bɛbɔle apaa na bɛhyele Yisrael abaayaa bie nnure befili Yisrael aseɛ so bɛhɔle. Né sɔ abaayaa ne, ɔso Naaman aye.

english_verse: the king replied, “Go ahead! I will give you a letter to take to the king of Israel.” Naaman left and took along
translation_verse: Yeɛ Siria hene buale kyɛ, “Nzaade a kɔ, na ngɔhyerɛ krataa ngɔboka wɔ so ngɔɔma Yisrael hene.” Na Naaman fale ɛdwetɛ talɛnde buru, esikaa kɔkorɛ sekel apee nzia ne ndaadeɛ faa buru, na osili nu hɔle.

english_verse: He also carried the letter to the king of Israel. It said, “I am sending my servant Naaman to you. Would you cure him of his leprosy?”
translation_verse: Ɔfale krataa ne ɔɔmane Yisrael hene. Nu dwirɛ ole kyɛ, “Mefa sɔ krataa he mebrɛ wɔ mekã mekyire wɔ kyɛ, mama me somvoɛ Naaman wawa wɔ berɛ kyɛ ɛsa ye kwata anwonyerɛ ne.”

english_verse: Elisha sent someone outside to say to him, “Go wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you'll be completely cured.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Elisa somane sona maa ɔɔhã hyirele ye kyɛ, “Kɔ na kobia asue Yɔɔdan nu pɛen nzoo, na wɔ nwonaen kosa kɔyɛ kyɛ ye daa ne ala, na wɔ nwo kɔte.”

english_verse: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes in fear and shouted, “That Syrian king believes I can cure this man of leprosy! Does he think I'm God with power over life and death? He must be trying to pick a fight with me.”
translation_verse: Yisrael hene kengale krataa ne yiele pɛ, osunzuale ye bɔbɔ ye ndaadeɛ nu, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Aso nde Nyameɛ né mahora mama ewue anaa ngoa, bɔ yeɛ biaa ye ato me ngraa kyɛ nza biaa he kwata anwonyerɛ ɔ! Aso ɛmɔnea a, ɔmbena me ne ngondii!”

english_verse: As soon as Elisha the prophet heard what had happened, he sent the Israelite king this message: “Why are you so afraid? Send the man to me, so that he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Nyameɛ sona Elisa tele kyɛ Yisrael hene asunzua ye ndaadeɛ nu ne, ɔmaa beesele ye kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ asunzua wɔ ndaadeɛ nu ɔ? Ma ɔbra me wa, amaa ɔnate so wanwu kyɛ ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ wɔ Yisrael.”

english_verse: Naaman left with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
translation_verse: Yiti Naaman ne ye mbɔngɔ ne teaseɛnam mɔ bɛwale, na beegyinane Elisa awuro anoa nu berɛ.

english_verse: But Naaman stormed off, grumbling, “Why couldn't he come out and talk to me? I thought for sure he would stand in front of me and pray to the Lord his God, then wave his hand over my skin and cure me.
translation_verse: Nakoso Naaman fɛle yaa, ofili berɛ hɔle, na osele kyɛ, “Me de menwa nzɛ okofite kɔwa, ná waagyina wa wabɔ AWURADE ye Nyameɛ ne dumaa, ná wanwaha ye sa wɔ nekaa bɔ anwonyerɛ ne wɔ ne aso, ná wasa kwata anwonyerɛ ne!

english_verse: What about the Abana River or the Pharpar River? Those rivers in Damascus are just as good as any river in Israel. I could have washed in them and been cured.”
translation_verse: Damasko asue mɔ Abana ne Faapa, aso benni mu bɛndra Yisrael asue biala? Ahaa ye de mengomia bɛ nu ma me nwo nde?” Yiti ole ɛyaa kakyili ye nwo sili nu kyɛ ɔkɔ.

english_verse: His servants went over to him and said, “Sir, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, you would have done it. So why don't you do what he said? Go wash and be cured.”
translation_verse: Nakoso ye somvoɛ nemɔ hɔle ye nwo berɛ beesele ye kyɛ, “Yɛ mene, sɛ ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ ne, ɔhane kyɛ ɛyɔ nikyee serɛ bie po a, ahaa ɛngɔyɔ anaa? Na sɛ wahã wahyire wɔ kyɛ, ‘Kɔ bia asue nu ma wɔ nwo te’ a, nzu ati yeɛ ɛngɔyɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: Naaman walked down to the Jordan; he waded out into the water and stooped down in it seven times, just as Elisha had told him. At once, he was cured, and his skin became as smooth as a child's.
translation_verse: Yiti osili nu hɔle asue Yɔɔdan nu ɔɔtɔle nu pɛen nzoo, kyɛbɔ Nyameɛ sona ne hane ne ala. Na ye nwonaen sa tɔle so kyɛ akwadaa kaaba deɛ, na ye nwo tele.

english_verse: Naaman and his officials went back to Elisha. Naaman stood in front of him and announced, “Now I know that the God of Israel is the only God in the whole world. Sir, would you please accept a gift from me?”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Naaman, ɔne ye lɔen bɔ bɛboka ye so amukoraa, besa bɛhɔle Nyameɛ sona ne berɛ. Naaman oogyinane ye nyunu berɛ, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Afei de manwu kyɛ aseɛ ye aso amukoraa, Nyameɛ biala ɔnne neka fee sana Yisrael angome. Mesrɛ wɔ, de w’akoaa sa nu akyɛdeɛ ye.”

english_verse: “I am a servant of the living Lord,” Elisha answered, “and I swear that I will not take anything from you.” Naaman kept begging, but Elisha kept refusing.
translation_verse: Nakoso Elisa buale kyɛ, “Kyɛbɔ AWURADE bɔ ngyi ye nyunu ye ɔte ase ye, mengole hwee!” Naaman hɔle so srɛle Elisa kyɛ ole ye akyɛdeɛ ne, nakoso wanne.

english_verse: Finally Naaman said, “If you won't accept a gift, then please let me take home as much soil as two mules can pull in a wagon. Sir, from now on I will offer sacrifices only to the Lord.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Naaman hane kyɛ, “Sɛ engole m’akyɛdeɛ ne po a, mesrɛ wɔ, maa bɛsa ɛwa nnɛterɛ somaa bɔ afunum nyɔ kɔhora ye soa ɔ bɛma w’akoaa. Ofikyɛ w’akoaa, mengɔbɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ anaakyɛ afɔleɛ biala mengɔma nyameɛ foforɛ biala ko, sana AWURADE angome.

english_verse: “Go on home, and don't worry about that,” Elisha replied. Then Naaman left. Elisha Places a Curse on Gehazi After Naaman had gone only a short distance,
translation_verse: Na Elisa sele Naaman kyɛ, “Fa asomdwee kɔ.” Gehasi nye boro nikye Nakoso Naaman fili Elisa nyunu berɛ hɔle moa kãa ne,

english_verse: Gehazi said to himself, “Elisha let that Syrian off too easy. He should have taken Naaman's gift. I swear by the living Lord that I will talk to Naaman myself and get something from him.”
translation_verse: Gehasi bɔ ɔte Nyameɛ sona Elisa somvoɛ ne, osusuli kyɛ, “Me mene ama sɔ Sirianiɛ Naaman ne, wafa ye nwo wali, ofikyɛ wanne akyɛdeɛ bɔ wafa wabrɛ ye ne. Kyɛ AWURADE te ase ye, ngɔpo ye so ngɔɔpena nikyee bie ngole ngofi ye dɔ.”

english_verse: So he hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw Gehazi running after him, he got out of his chariot to meet him. Naaman asked, “Is everything all right?”
translation_verse: Yiti Gehasi pole Naaman so. Naaman nwuni kyɛ biaa bie le amirika oli ye si nen, odwu fili teaseɛnam ne anu ooyiale ye, na obisale ye kyɛ, “Ɔte bɔkɔɔ de?”

english_verse: “Yes,” Gehazi answered. “But my master has sent me to tell you about two young prophets from the hills of Ephraim. They came asking for help, and now Elisha wants to know if you would give them
translation_verse: Na obuale ye kyɛ, “Ɔte bɔkɔɔ, na mmom me mene afa ngraa wasoma me wɔ berɛ kyɛ, ‘Ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ fekue ne anu mmenia nyɔ, befi Efraim mmokaa aseɛ ne aso dɔ bawa me wa kekesaala ye. Mesrɛ wɔ, ma bɛ ɛdwetɛ talɛnde ko ne ndaadeɛ faa nyɔ.’ ”

english_verse: “Sure,” Naaman replied. “But why don't you take twice that amount of silver?” He convinced Gehazi to take it all, then put the silver in two bags. He handed the bags and the clothes to his two servants, and they carried them for Gehazi.
translation_verse: Naaman buale kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, maa mma wɔ talɛnde nyɔ.” Naaman srɛle Gehasi, na ɔkyekyele ɛdwetɛ talɛnde nyɔ wɔ bɔtɔ nyɔ nu. Ɔfale ndaadeɛ faa nyɔ bokale so, na ɔfa mane ye somvoɛ nemɔ anu nyɔ maa bɛsoale belili Gehasi nyunu.

english_verse: When they reached the hill where Gehazi lived, he took the bags from the servants and placed them in his house, then sent the men away. After they had gone,
translation_verse: Gehasi oodwuli bokaa ne aso ne, olele bɔtɔ nemɔ fili somvoɛ nemɔ berɛ ɔfa oosiele sua nu. Afei ɔmane bɛ ate maa bɛhɔle.

english_verse: Gehazi went in and stood in front of Elisha, who asked, “Gehazi, where have you been?” “Nowhere, sir,” Gehazi answered.
translation_verse: Gehasi oogyinane ye mene Elisa nyunu, na Elisa bisale ye kyɛ, “Gehasi, ɛhɔle ni?” Obuale kyɛ, “Wɔ somvoɛ, nngɔle neka fee.”

english_verse: Elisha asked, “Don't you know that my spirit was there when Naaman got out of his chariot to talk with you? Gehazi, you have no right to accept money or clothes, olive orchards or vineyards, sheep or cattle, or servants.
translation_verse: Nakoso Elisa sele ye kyɛ, “Mmerɛ bɔ biaa bie huru fili ye teaseɛnam nu ooyiale wɔ ne, aso nna me sunzum ɔne wɔ yeɛ bɛhɔle ɔ? Aso sɔ mmerɛ ye yeɛ odi kyɛ ede esikaa ne ndaadeɛ, olive boo ne bobe boo, mmoaen ne nandwie mɔ, ngoaa ne afaneɛ mɔ ɔ?

english_verse: Because of what you've done, Naaman's leprosy will now be on you and your descendants forever!” Suddenly, Gehazi's skin became white with leprosy, and he left.
translation_verse: Ɔnate ye sɔ ti, Naaman kwata anwonyerɛ ne kɔte kɔha wɔ ne wɔ boso ama so afebɔɔ.” Yiti Gehasi fili Elisa nyunu berɛ hɔle bɔ né kwata anwonyerɛ ayɛ ye ma ye nwo ayɛ horaenn kyɛ asukɔtwea ɔ.

english_verse: One day the prophets said to Elisha, “The place where we meet with you is too small.
translation_verse: Afei ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ fekue ne, besele Elisa kyɛ, “Kyɛbɔ wɔ bɔbɔ anwu ye ne, nekaa bɔ yɛte maa ɛnea yɛ so ne, ɔte kãa ma yɛ.

english_verse: Why don't we build a new meeting place near the Jordan River? Each of us could get some wood, then we could build it.” “That's a good idea,” Elisha replied, “get started.”
translation_verse: Yiti yɛsrɛ wɔ, maa yɛhɔ asue Yɔɔdan noa, na yɛ nu biala ɔpɛ bakaa ko, na yɛɛsi sua wɔ dɔ yɛtena nu.” Na Elisa buale kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhɔ.”

english_verse: “Aren't you going with us?” one of the prophets asked. “Yes, I'll go,” Elisha answered,
translation_verse: Yeɛ bɛ nu ko hane kyɛ, “Wɔ somvoɛ mɔ, yɛsrɛ wɔ, ɛne yɛ hɔ.” Na obuale kyɛ, “Yoo, me ne ɛmɔ yɛkɔhɔ.”

english_verse: and he left with them. They went to the Jordan River and began chopping down trees.
translation_verse: Yiti ɔne bɛ hɔle. Beedwuli asue Yɔɔdan noa ne, bɛhyɛle ye bo bɛpepɛle mmakaa.

english_verse: “Where did it fall in?” Elisha asked. The prophet pointed to the place, and Elisha cut a stick and threw it into the water at that spot. The ax head floated to the top of the water.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nyameɛ sona ne bisale kyɛ, “Nisua yeɛ ɔɔtɔle ɔ?” Ohyirele Elisa nekaa bɔ ɔtɔle ɔ. Elisa pɛle bakaa ofindini tole nekaa bɔ ɔtɔle ne, na ɔmane akumaa ne turuli asue ne anye.

english_verse: “Now get it,” Elisha told him. And the prophet reached in and grabbed it. Elisha Stops an Invasion of the Syrian Army
translation_verse: Elisa sele kyɛ, “Ma so.” Yiti ɔtengyɛle ye sa fale. Elisa ma Yisrael di Siriafoɛ so ngonim

english_verse: Time after time, when the king of Syria was at war against the Israelites, he met with his officers and announced, “I've decided where we will set up camp.”
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bie bɔ Siria hene fale koɛ ɔɔtetale Yisrael ne, Siria hene ne ye mbanyi mɔ bɛbɔle porɛ, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Sɔ nekaa he yeɛ ngɔkyekye me koɛ asikyeleɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Each time, Elisha would send this warning to the king of Israel: “Don't go near there. That's where the Syrian troops have set up camp.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Nyameɛ sona ne fale ngraa ɔɔmane Yisrael hene kyɛ, “Nea yé né angɔamva dɔ, ofikyɛ Siriafoɛ kɔɔkyekye asikyeleɛ wɔ dɔ.”

english_verse: The king of Syria was furious when he found out what was happening. He called in his officers and asked, “Which one of you has been telling the king of Israel our plans?”
translation_verse: Nikyee bɔ né ɔkɔ so ne, ɔhale Siria hene adwene paa. Yiti ɔfrɛle ye mbanyi nemɔ bisale bɛ kyɛ, “Yɛ nu nwa yeɛ ɔyɛ a, ɔkɔte yɛ bo kyire Yisrael hene ye?”

english_verse: “None of us, Your Majesty,” one of them answered. “It's an Israelite named Elisha. He's a prophet, so he can tell his king everything—even what you say in your own room.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ ye mbanyi nemɔ ko buale kyɛ, “Me mene, Nana, nna yɛ nu biala ɔ, na mmom Yisrael ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ Elisa ɔ. Ye yeɛ edwirɛ bɔ ekosusu ye nwo wɔ wɔ pumbu nu ne, ɔkã kyire Yisrael hene ɔ.”

english_verse: “Find out where he is!” the king ordered. “I'll send soldiers to bring him here.” They learned that Elisha was in the town of Dothan and reported it to the king.
translation_verse: Na Siria hene sele kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhɔ bɛɛpena nekaa bɔ Elisa wɔ ɔ, na ngɔsoma maa bɛkɔɔhye ye.” Bebuale kyɛ, “Ɔwɔ Dotan.”

english_verse: He ordered his best troops to go there with horses and chariots. They marched out during the night and surrounded the town.
translation_verse: Yiti Siria hene somane koɛhonɛfoɛ pee maa bɛfale mbɔngɔ ne teaseɛnam mɔ bɛhɔle dɔ. Beedwuli kɔngɔen, na bɛpɛle kuro ne anwo beyiale.

english_verse: When Elisha's servant got up the next morning, he saw that Syrian troops had the town surrounded. “Sir, what are we going to do?” he asked.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ sona ne, ye somvoɛ ne dwɔsole ngyerɛmɔ tutuutu. Na ofitele ne, onwuni kyɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛtete mbɔngɔ so ne teaseɛnam mɔ nu ɔ bapɛ kuro ne anwo bayia ɔ. Ye somvoɛ ne hane kyɛ, “Me mene, yawu oo! Ɛhe de, yɛyɛ ye sɛ?”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Elisha answered. “There are more troops on our side than on theirs.”
translation_verse: Elisa buale kyɛ, “Nnesuro, ofikyɛ yɛ lɔen bɔ begyi yɛ si ne, bɛsone bɛtra bɛ lɔen deɛ ne.”

english_verse: Then he prayed, “Lord, please help him to see.” And the Lord let the servant see that the hill was covered with fiery horses and flaming chariots all around Elisha.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Elisa bɔle mbaeɛ kyɛ, “Ao AWURADE, mesrɛ wɔ, te ye nye maa onwu nikye bɔ ɔkɔ so ɔ.” Yiti AWURADE tele somvoɛ ne nye. Na onwuni kyɛ mbɔngɔ ne see teaseɛnam mɔ bayɛ mitimiti wɔ bokaa ne aso bapɛ Elisa nwo amukoraa bayia ɔ.

english_verse: As the Syrian army came closer, Elisha prayed, “Lord, make those soldiers blind!” And the Lord blinded them with a bright light.
translation_verse: Siriafoɛ nemɔ hɔle Elisa so ne, Elisa bɔle mbaeɛ hyirele AWURADE kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, ma mmenia hemɔ bɛ nye osi.” Yiti Nyameɛ mane bɛ nye sini kyɛbɔ Elisa srɛle ne ala.

english_verse: Elisha told the enemy troops, “You've taken the wrong road and are in the wrong town. Follow me. I'll lead you to the man you're looking for.” Elisha led them straight to the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Na Elisa sele bɛ kyɛ, “Nna atee ne ɛhe, yeɛ nna kuro ne ɛhe. Ɛ́mɔli me si maa mva ɛmɔ ngɔ sona bɔ ɛmɔpena ye ne berɛ.” Yiti olili bɛ nyunu fale bɛ hɔle Samaria.

english_verse: When all the soldiers were inside the city, Elisha prayed, “Lord, now let them see again.” The Lord let them see that they were standing in the middle of Samaria.
translation_verse: Beedwuli Samaria pɛ, Elisa bɔle mbaeɛ kyɛ, “Ao AWURADE, te mmenia ye mɔ anye maa benwu bɔ ɔkɔ so ɔ.” Yiti AWURADE tele bɛ nye, na benwuni kyɛ saa bɛwɔ Samaria.

english_verse: The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, “Should I kill them, sir?”
translation_verse: Yisrael hene nwuni Siriafoɛ nemɔ nen, obisale Elisa kyɛ, “Me baba, ngukũ bɛ anaa? Ngukũ bɛ anaa?”

english_verse: “No!” Elisha answered. “You didn't capture these troops in battle, so you have no right to kill them. Instead, give them something to eat and drink and let them return to their leader.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Elisa buale kyɛ, “Daabi, nnɛkũkũ bɛ. Aso mmenia bɔ ɛkɔfa wɔ ngrandɛ ne w’agyaen kɔhye bɛ nnure ne, odi kyɛ ekũkũ bɛ anaa? Brɛ bɛ aleɛ ne nzue maa bedidi na bɛno, na maa besa bɛhɔ bɛ mene dɔ.”

english_verse: The king ordered a huge meal to be prepared for Syria's army, and when they finished eating, he let them go. For a while, the Syrian troops stopped invading Israel's territory. King Benhadad of Syria Attacks Samaria
translation_verse: Yiti Yisrael hene tole poen kandinga mane bɛ, na bedidili bɛnone beyiele ne, ɔmane bɛ ate, na besa bɛhɔle bɛ mene dɔ. Na Siriafoɛ bamma kyɛ bɛbaabɔ apaa wɔ Yisrael aseɛ so ko. Ben Hadade tua Samaria

english_verse: Some time later, King Benhadad of Syria called his entire army together, then they marched to Samaria and attacked.
translation_verse: Ɛhe asi ne, Siria hene Ben Hadade boaboale ye koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa noa. Ɔfale koɛ ɔɔtetale Samaria, na otuale kuro ne.

english_verse: They kept up the attack until there was nothing to eat in the city. In fact, a donkey's head cost
translation_verse: Ɔnate kyɛ ɔhɔle so tuale Samaria ne ati, ɛhɔen pohonandafe bie wale kuro ne aso. Ɔnate so, né bɛfa afunum ti ko bede ɛdwetɛ sekel aburawɔtwɛ, yeɛ né bɛfa abubure ye bondua kongo bue bede ɛdwetɛ sekel nnu.

english_verse: One day as the king of Israel was walking along the top of the city wall, a woman shouted to him, “Please, Your Majesty, help me!”
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, né Yisrael hene nate kuro berɛ fasue ne aso. Na braa bie teane nu sele ye kyɛ, “Nana, me mene, boka me ee!”

english_verse: “Let the Lord help you!” the king said. “Do you think I have grain or wine to give you?”
translation_verse: Na obuale kyɛ, “Sɛ AWURADE ammoka wɔ a, nisua yeɛ mekwaanya mmokalɛ mefa meboka wɔ ɔ: nekaa bɔ bɛboro aburoo anaa nekaa bɔ betwi nzaa hɔ anaa?”

english_verse: Then he asked, “What's the matter anyway?” The woman answered, “Another woman and I were so hungry that we agreed to eat our sons. She said if we ate my son one day, we could eat hers the next day.
translation_verse: Afei Yisrael hene bisale braa ne kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ dwirɛ ɔ?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Braa he hã hyirele me kyɛ, ‘Fa ɛwa bienzua ne maa yɛhu ye yɛto ye yɛli ɛnɛ, na ɛhema né mafa me deɛ maa yahu ye yato yali.’

english_verse: So yesterday we cooked my son and ate him. But today when I went to her house to eat her son, she had hidden him.”
translation_verse: Yiti yɛhuni mma bienzua ne yɛtone ye yɛlili. Aleɛ hyene ne, nga ngyirele ye kyɛ, ‘Fa ɛwa bienzua ne maa yɛhu ye yɛto ye yɛli.’ Nakoso ye de, wafa ɔwa deɛ ne wafea.”

english_verse: The king tore off his clothes in sorrow, and since he was on top of the city wall, the people saw that he was wearing sackcloth underneath.
translation_verse: Yisrael hene tele braa ne dwirɛ nen, osunzuale ye bɔbɔ ye ndaadeɛ nu. Ɔnate kyɛ né ɔnate kuro berɛ fasue ne aso ne ati, berɛ ama nwuni kyɛ ataadeɛ bɔ ɔwɔ ko bɔ wasunzua nu ne abo ne, ɔte ɛsɛen tena ataadeɛ.

english_verse: He said, “I pray that God will punish me terribly, if Elisha's head is still on his shoulders by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhane kyɛ, “Safate awa Elisa, sɛ ɛnɛ mande ye ti mamvi so a, Nyameɛ otua me kerɛ maa ɔbo so.”

english_verse: Then he sent a messenger to Elisha. Elisha was home at the time, and the important leaders of Israel were meeting with him. Even before the king's messenger arrived, Elisha told the leaders, “That murderer is sending someone to cut off my head. When you see him coming, shut the door and don't let him in. I'm sure the king himself will be right behind him.”
translation_verse: Yiti ɔsomane sona kyɛ ɔhɔ Elisa berɛ. Né Elisa te ye awuro, bɔ né mbanyi mɔ tete ye nwo berɛ ɔ. Anzana bɔfoɛ ne baadwu berɛ ne, Elisa hã hyirele mbanyi nemɔ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔse kyɛ kodiawuniɛ ne, wasoma sona kyɛ ɔɔpɛ me ti ɔ? Sɛ bɔfoɛ ne badwu wa a, ɛmɔnea kyɛ ɛmɔkɔto anoa ne asi bɔ ongonya ate ngowura nu ɔ. Mete ye mene Yisrael hene ye gya bo so kyɛ oli ye si ɔba.”

english_verse: Before Elisha finished talking, the messenger came up and said, “The Lord has made all these terrible things happen to us. Why should I think he will help us now?”
translation_verse: Na ogu so ɔne bɛ dwudwo ne, ɛbɔfoɛ ne wale ye berɛ osele kyɛ, “AWURADE yeɛ wama amaneɛ he awa ɔ! Nzu ati yeɛ odi kyɛ mekɔ so mefa me nwo meto ye so ɔ?”

english_verse: Elisha answered, “I have a message for you. The Lord promises that tomorrow here in Samaria, you will be able to buy a large sack of flour or two large sacks of barley for almost nothing.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Elisa buale kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔtie AWURADE noa dwirɛ: AWURADE nwa nyoo, ‘Ɛhema bekye sɔa, bɛkɔfa esam paa kilo buru ne nyɔ bekole sekel ko, ná bafa ayuo kilo aburanyɔ ne nna bale sekel ko, wɔ Samaria dwaa nu.’ ”

english_verse: The chief officer there with the king replied, “I don't believe it! Even if the Lord sent a rainstorm, it couldn't produce that much grain by tomorrow.” “You will see it happen, but you won't eat any of the food,” Elisha warned him. The Syrian Army Stops Its Attack
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yisrael hene safohene bɔ ode ye di paa ne sele Nyameɛ sona ne kyɛ, “Sɛ AWURADE tofitofi ewienu po a, aso ɛhe kɔhora kosi?” Nakoso Elisa buale ye kyɛ, “Ɛkɔfa wɔ nye konwu ye, nakoso engoli bie.” Kwatafoɛ biemɔ ma Siriafoɛ nwati

english_verse: About the same time, four men with leprosy were just outside the gate of Samaria. They said to each other, “Why should we sit here, waiting to die?
translation_verse: Mmienzua kwatafoɛ nna biemɔ, bɔ né bɛte kuro berɛ pambim ne asi dɔ ɔ, besisele bɛ nwo kyɛ, “Nzu ati yeɛ odi kyɛ yɛtena wa ma ɛhɔen ku yɛ maa yɛwu ɔ?

english_verse: There's nothing to eat in the city, so we would starve if we went inside. But if we stay out here, we will die for sure. Let's sneak over to the Syrian army camp and surrender. They might kill us, but they might not.”
translation_verse: Sɛ yɛkã kyɛ yɛkɔ kuro ne aso dɔ a, ɛhɔen wɔ dɔ, na ɛhɔen kɔmaa yɛkowu dɔ. Nakoso sɛ yɛtena wa a, ye koso ɛhɔen kɔmaa yɛkowuwu. Yiti ɛ́mɔma yɛhɔ Siriafoɛ b’asikyeleɛ ne anu dɔ. Sɛ bɛyakyi yɛ maa yɛnya yɛ ti yɛdidi nu a, ye de yɛ ti ngoa. Nakoso sɛ beku yɛ koso a, ewue komapɛ ne ala ɔ.”

english_verse: They said to each other, “This isn't right. Today is a day to celebrate, and we haven't told anyone else what has happened. If we wait until morning, we will be punished. Let's go to the king's palace at once and tell the good news.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ besisele bɛ nwo kyɛ, “Nikyee bɔ yɛyɔ ye, ɔtte mayee. Ɛnɛ te ndɛenvɛen kyẽa. Sɛ yammɔ so ná yɛtena berɛ ma aleɛ kye a, yɛkoli ye nwo fɔ. Yiti ɛ́mɔma yɛhɔ ahemvie yɛɛbɔ amaneɛ.”

english_verse: They went back to Samaria and shouted up to the guards at the gate, “We've just come from the Syrian army camp, and all the soldiers are gone! The tents are empty, and the horses and donkeys are still tied up. We didn't see or hear anybody.”
translation_verse: Yiti bɛɛfrɛfrɛle kuro berɛ pambim awɛmvoɛ nemɔ bɛbɔle bɛ amaneɛ kyɛ, “Yɛhɔle Siriafoɛ asikyeleɛ ne anu, nakoso yannwu sona fee, yeɛ yande sona fee nga wɔ dɔ. Bɔ yɛnwuni ala yeɛ ole mbɔngɔ ne afunum mɔ bɔ bamendamenda bɛ ɔ, ɔne b’ɛtena sua mɔ kyɛbɔ bɛyakyili bɛ berɛ bɛhɔle ne ala.”

english_verse: The guards reported the news to the king's palace.
translation_verse: Na pambim awɛmvoɛ nemɔ teateane nu bɛbɔle ahemvie berɛ ama amaneɛ.

english_verse: The king got out of bed and said to his officers, “I know what those Syrians are doing. They know we're starving, so they're hiding in the fields, hoping we will go out to look for food. When we do, they can capture us and take over our city.”
translation_verse: Yisrael hene dwɔsole kɔngɔen ne ala, na osele ye mbanyi mɔ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔma ngyire ɛmɔ ngaen bɔ Siriafoɛ basua yɛ ɔ. Bɛse ye kyɛ ɛhɔen ku yɛ, yiti bafi b’asikyeleɛ ne anu baafeafea eburo, na b’adwene ole kyɛ, ‘Sɛ Yisraelfoɛ befi bɛ kuro ne anu befite a, yɛkɔhyehye bɛ anyekaenn so, ná yanya ate yawura kuro ne anu.’ ”

english_verse: One of his officers replied, “We have a few horses left—why don't we let some men take five of them and go to the Syrian camp and see what's happening? We're going to die anyway like those who have already died.”
translation_verse: Ye mbanyi nemɔ ko buale kyɛ, “Ma mmenia ne bie bɛfa mbɔngɔ bɔ baha nemɔ anu nnu ná ɛ́mɔma yɛsoma bɛ maa bɛɛnea. Ofikyɛ mbɔngɔ bɔ baha wa ne, bekowuwu kyɛ Yisrael ɛlɔen bɔ bawuwu ne ala.”

english_verse: They found two chariots, and the king commanded the men to find out what had happened to the Syrian troops.
translation_verse: Yiti betuli mmenia, na Yisrael hene somane bɛ maa bɛfale teaseɛnam nyɔ bɔ mbɔngɔ sosɔ bɛ ɔ bɛpole Siria koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ aso kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhɔ bɛɛnea bɔ wasi ɔ.”

english_verse: The men rode as far as the Jordan River. All along the way they saw clothes and equipment that the Syrians had thrown away as they escaped. Then they went back to the king and told him what they had seen.
translation_verse: Bɛpole Siriafoɛ so alaa beedwuli asue Yɔɔdan noa. Mmerɛ bɔ Siriafoɛ bɛnwati, bɔ né bɛ nwo kã bɛ tɛtɛtɛtɛ ne, bɛ ndaadeɛ ne akodeɛ bɔ befindini beguale ne, ɛbɔfoɛ nemɔ nwuni bɛ wɔ atee ne aso. Yiti ɛbɔfoɛ nemɔ besa bɛwale bɛɛbɔle Yisrael hene amaneɛ.

english_verse: At once the people went to the Syrian camp and carried off what was left. They took so much that a large sack of flour and two large sacks of barley sold for almost nothing, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Samariafoɛ fitele bɛɛfene Siriafoɛ asikyeleɛ ne anu nningyein. Ɔnate so, bɛfale esam paa kilo buru ne nyɔ belele sekel ko, yeɛ bɛfale ayuo kilo aburanyɔ ne nna belele sekel ko, kyɛbɔ AWURADE hane ne ala.

english_verse: The king of Israel had put his chief officer in charge of the gate, but he died when the people trampled him as they rushed out of the city.
translation_verse: Na Yisrael hene tuli ye safohene bɔ ode ye di paa ne kyɛ oogyina pambim ne anyunu berɛ ɔɔtoto nningyein yé. Na ɛlɔen ne tiatiale ye so behuni ye wɔ pambim ne anyunu berɛ, kyɛbɔ Nyameɛ sona ne hane ala, wɔ mmerɛ bɔ Yisrael hene hɔle ye berɛ ne.

translation_verse: Ofikyɛ mmerɛ bɔ Nyameɛ sona ne hã hyirele Yisrael hene kyɛ, “Ɛhema bekye sɔa, bɛkɔfa ayuo kilo aburanyɔ ne nna bekole sekel ko, ná bafa esam paa kilo buru ne nyɔ bale sekel ko, wɔ Samaria dwaa nu” ne,

english_verse: Then she returned to Israel and immediately begged the king to give back her house and property.

translation_verse: Yisrael hene ne Gehasi, bɔ ɔte Nyameɛ sona ne somvoɛ ne, né bedi ngɔmɔ. Na osele Gehasi kyɛ, “Kekã anwanwadeɛ amukoraa bɔ Elisa wayɔ ne kyire me.”

Na Gehasi sele kyɛ, “Nana, me mene, braa ne, ɔne ɔwa bɔ Elisa tingyele ye wale ngoa nu ne, bɛ ɛhe.”

english_verse: Some time later Elisha went to the capital city of Damascus to visit King Benhadad of Syria, who was sick. And when Benhadad was told he was there,
translation_verse: Elisa hɔle Damasko wɔ mmerɛ bɔ né anwonyerɛ abɔ Siria hene Ben Hadade ɔ. Bɛbɔle ye amaneɛ kyɛ, “Nyameɛ sona ne, wawa wa” nen,

english_verse: Hazael left with forty camel loads of the best things made in Damascus as a gift for Elisha. He found the prophet and said, “Your servant, King Benhadad, wants to know if he will get well.”
translation_verse: Yiti Hasael fale akyɛdeɛ, ɔne Damasko nningyein paa ahoroɔ soale afupɔngɔ aburanna, na ɔhɔle Elisa berɛ. Hasael oogyinane ye nyunu ne, Hasael sele kyɛ, “W’akoaa Siria hene Ben Hadade wasoma me wɔ berɛ kyɛ mmamisa wɔ kyɛ, ‘Aso sɔ anwonyerɛ bɔ wabɔ me ye, ngɔte apɔ anaa?’ ”

english_verse: “Tell him he will,” Elisha said to Hazael. “But the Lord has already told me that Benhadad will definitely die.”
translation_verse: Elisa buale ye kyɛ, “Kɔhã kyire ye kyɛ, ‘Hmmm, ɛkɔte apɔ amba’, nakoso AWURADE aye ahyire me kyɛ nahorɛ nu okowu.”

english_verse: Elisha stared at him until Hazael was embarrassed, then Elisha began crying.
translation_verse: Ɔneane ye nyunu haa kɔpem kyɛ afei de ye nyunu yɛle basaa. Afei, Nyameɛ sona ne suni.

english_verse: “Sir, why are you crying?” Hazael asked. Elisha answered, “Because I know the terrible things you will do to the people of Israel. You will burn down their walled cities and slaughter their young men. You will even crush the heads of their babies and rip open their pregnant women.”
translation_verse: Na Hasael bisale kyɛ, “Me mene, nzu ati yeɛ esu ye?” Na Elisa buale kyɛ, “Ofikyɛ mese bɔne bɔ ɛkɔfa koli Yisraelfoɛ ɔ. english_verse: “How could I ever do anything like that?” Hazael replied. “I'm only a servant and don't have that kind of power.” “Hazael, the Lord has told me that you will be the next king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Hasael buale kyɛ, “W’akoaa, kyea ba bɔ ɔte kyɛ me ɔ, me yeɛ nne nwa bɔ ngɔhora ngɔbɔ sɔ musue piri he ɔ?” Na Elisa buale kyɛ, “AWURADE aye ahyire me kyɛ wɔ yeɛ ɛbaali Siria so hene ɔ.”

translation_verse: Yehoram mmerɛ so, Edom yɛle Yuda nwo lɔen, na besili bɛ bɔbɔ bɛ hene.

translation_verse: Yisrael hene Ahabo ɔwa Yoram lili hene ne, ye afoɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so nnu ne anu, Yuda hene Yehosafate ɔwa Yehoram lili Yuda so hene.

translation_verse: Ɔyɔle bɔne bɔ Yisrael ahemvo bɛyɔle ne bie, kyɛbɔ Ahabo boso ama bɔ belili bia ne, bɛyɔle ne ala, ofikyɛ ogyale Ahabo awa brasua. Ɔyɔle bɔ ɔte bɔne wɔ AWURADE nyunu ɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord refused to destroy Judah, because he had promised his servant David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Nakoso AWURADE anzɛkye Yuda, ɔnate ye somvoɛ Dawide ti. Ofikyɛ né wahyɛ Dawide bɔ kyɛ ye boso ama koli bia afebɔɔ.

translation_verse: Yiti Yehu dwɔso hɔle sua nu. Ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ aberandeɛ ne hwiele ngoo ne guale ye ti so, na osele ye kyɛ, “AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa: Mapopa wɔ ngoo mafa wɔ masie AWURADE maen Yisrael so hene.
