translation_verse: Mmrasua mukoraa bɛkɔte Nana hemmaa yɔleɛ tɛɛ he, na ɔnate so bengobu bɛ hu mɔ. Ofikyɛ bɛkɔhã kyɛ, ‘Nana Ahasuro po hane kyɛ bɛɛfa Nana hemmaa Wasiti ma ɔbra ye nyunu, nakoso Nana hemmaa andɛ ye so.’

english_verse: Before this day is over, the wives of the officials of Persia and Media will find out what Queen Vashti has done, and they will refuse to obey their husbands. They won't respect their husbands, and their husbands will be angry with them.
translation_verse: Ɛnɛ kyẽa ye ala, Pɛsia ne Media nnehyeɛ mmrasua bɔ bate nana hemmaa yɔleɛ tɛɛ he nen, bɛkɔhyɛ ye bo bekohyire sɔ suban ne bie bekohyire bɛ hu mɔ, na ɛhe ngɔma animtia ne ahonehulɛ bo ngɔpɛ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
translation_verse: Nana, sɛ ɛkɔpene so a, hyɛ mmeraa, ná maa bɛhyerɛ bɛboka Pɛsia ne Medese mmeraa bɔ bɛngora ye sesã ne aso, kyɛ, Onni kyɛ Nana Wasiti ba Nana Ahasuro nyunu le ko. Afei koso, Nana, fa Wasiti hemmaa dibea ne ma brasua foforɛ bɔ ɔte paa tra Wasiti ɔ.

english_verse: When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
translation_verse: Nana, sɛ bɛbɔ sɔ mmeraa bɔ ɛkɔhyɛ ne dawure wɔ w’ahennie tɛtrɛtɛɛ ye amukoraa nu a, mmrasua amukoraa kɔfa anidie bɛkɔma bɛ hu mɔ, fite mmienzua atitirefoɛ so kodwu kwahweabaa mɔ so.”

english_verse: King Xerxes and his officials liked what Memucan had said,
translation_verse: Sɔ foɛtulɛ ne yɛle Nana Ahasuro ne ye mbanyi amukoraa fɛ, na Nana Ahasuro yɔle kyɛbɔ Memukan susuli ne ala.

english_verse: and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
translation_verse: Nana Ahasuro maa bɛfale ngrataa bɛhɔle ye manzini ne amukoraa nu. Manzini biala, kyɛbɔ ye ahyerɛlɛ ɔte ne, yeɛ mmenia biala, kyɛbɔ bɛ dwudwolɛ ɔte ne, sɔ ala yeɛ bɛhyerɛle krataa ne ɔ; kyɛ, bienzua biala yeɛ tumi wura ye sa wɔ ye awuro ɔ, na ɔnzɛ kyɛ betu ye noa dwirɛ begua.

english_verse: After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her.
translation_verse: Sɔ dwirɛ nemɔ asi ne, bɔ Nana Ahasuro ahone tɔle nzue nu ne, ɔkayele Wasiti ne nikyee bɔ wayɔ ne, ɔne mmeraa bɔ wahyɛ wafa ye nwo ne.

english_verse: Then the king's personal servants said: Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women.
translation_verse: Na Nana Ahasuro somvoɛ mɔ bɔ bepingye ye paa ne sele ye kyɛ, “Nana, maa bɛpena mmabunu bɔ bɛ nwo yɛ nyemene ɔ bɛma wɔ.

english_verse: You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments.
translation_verse: Nana, manzini amukoraa bɔ bɛwɔ w’ahennie nu ne, tu mbanyi sie berɛ maa bɛboaboa mmabunu anwonyemene amukoraa noa. Maa bɛfa bɛ bɛbra Susa ahemvie mmraanu berɛ. Nana, wɔ sayɛɛ Hegae bɔ ɔnea mmrasua so ne, maa bɛfa bɛ bewura ye sa, ná maa ɔma bɛ sakyeɛ mɔ bɔ bɛkɔfa bɛkɔpopa ɔ.

english_verse: Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen. King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
translation_verse: Nana, taluwa bɔ ye nwo kɔyɛ wɔ nyemene paa ne, maa oli hemmaa osi Wasiti gya nu.” Sɔ nzusuleɛ ne yɛle Nana Ahasuro fɛ, na ɔyɔle sɔ ala.

english_verse: At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Né Yudaniɛ bie wɔ Susa ahenguro berɛ. Ɔte Benyaminniɛ bɔ ye dumaa li Modekae. Ɔse ole Yari bɔ ofi Simei abusua nu, bɔ ye koso ofi Kise abusua nu ne.

english_verse: Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Babilɔn hene Nebukadenesa ɔhyele Yuda hene Yekonia nnure, ná ɔsesale ye ne mmenia bɔ wahye bɛ nnure ne fili Yerusalem hɔle ne, né Modekae boka so.

english_verse: Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died.
translation_verse: Modekae yeɛ ɔtetele ye baba aliɛma awa brasua Hadasa bɔ osa li Ɛseta ne ɔ, ofikyɛ né sɔ taluwa ne olle niɛ ne seɛ. Né anwonyemene abia ye. Oni ne ɔse bewuli ne yeɛ Modekae fale ye yɛle ɔwa ɔ.

english_verse: When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them. Hegai was put in charge of all the women,
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ bɛbɔle Nana Ahasuro noa dwirɛ ne ye mmeraa nwo dawure, bɔ bɛboaboale ndaluwa pee noa wɔ Susa ahemvie bɛfale bɛ bewurale Hegae sa ne, Ɛseta koso bɛfale ye bɛhɔle Nana Ahasuro ahemvie berɛ bie, na bɛfale ye bewurale Hegae bɔ ɔnea mmrasua so ne sa.

english_verse: and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
translation_verse: Taluwa Ɛseta sɔle Hegae nye, na Hegae lole ye. Ɔyɛle ndɛndɛ fale Ɛseta sakyeɛ mɔ bɔ ɔfa popa ɔ ɔne ye aleɛ mane ye. Osa neaneane Nana Ahasuro abaawa nemɔ nu yele nu nzoo kyɛ bɛso Ɛseta, na ɔmaa ɔne ye abaawa nemɔ bɛɛtenane nekaa paa paa wɔ mmraanu berɛ.

english_verse: Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him.
translation_verse: Ɛseta anna ye maen anaa ye abusua ali wangyire ebiala, ofikyɛ né Modekae abɔ ye noa kyɛ nnɛmaa ɔka.

english_verse: He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
translation_verse: Alehyeleɛ biala, né ɔyɛ a Modekae di mmraanu anyunu berɛ akɔneaba ɔnea kyɛbɔ Ɛseta nwo si te ɔ, ɔne sɛ ebiaa edwirɛ bie ato ye a.

english_verse: The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes.
translation_verse: Bosome buru ne nyɔ ne sone, kyɛbɔ mmrasua nemɔ bɛ nwo siesielɛ amammerɛ ɔte ne. Mmerɛ somaa bɔ né bɛfa besiesie bɛ nwo hɔ ɛne. Bɛbobɔ bɛ korobo bosome nzia, yeɛ bɛfa mmrasua sakyeɛfona bɛyɛ bɛ nwo bosome nzia. Sɔ mmerɛ ne sone ne, odwuli taluwa biala so kyɛ odi kyɛ ɔfa ye anwonyemene kokyire Nana Ahasuro.

english_verse: When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters.
translation_verse: Sɛ odwu taluwa biala so kyɛ ɔkɔ Nana Ahasuro nyunu a, nikyee biala bɔ okuro kyɛ ɔfa siesie ye nwo ofi mmraanu berɛ ɔkɔ Nana ahemvie berɛ ne, bɛfa bɛma ye.

english_verse: In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
translation_verse: Nɔsoa yeɛ ɔkɔ dɔ ɔ, na aleɛ kye ngyerɛmɔ a, osa ba mmraanu bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ne anu. Bɛfa ye bewura Nana Ahasuro sayɛɛ Saasegase sa wɔ berɛ. Ye yeɛ ɔnea Nana sómaa nemɔ so ɔ. Taluwa ne onza ngɔ Nana Ahasuro dɔ ko, sana ye nye gye taluwa ne anwo. Na ɔba ye sɔ a, ɔbɔ ye dumaa maa bɛkɔfa ye bɛba.

english_verse: Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti.
translation_verse: Na Nana Ahasuro hurole Ɛseta trale mmrasua ngaa ne amu. Ohurole ye dwirɛ, na ye nye gyele ye nwo trale mmabunu ne amu, yiti ɔfale ɛhemmaa kyerɛ ne wurale ye, na ɔfale ye sili hemmaa sili Wasiti gya nu.

english_verse: In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts. Mordecai Saves the King's Life
translation_verse: Afei Nana Ahasuro tole poen kandinga mane ye mbanyi ne ye somvoɛ amukoraa fa hyɛle Ɛseta animnyam. Ɔmaa bɛyakyili manzini toɔdidelɛ ne mmerɛ kãa, na ɔyele ye kunu hyɛle bɛ nningyein. Modekae de Nana Ahasuro ngoa

english_verse: When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ bɛboaboale mmabunu nemɔ noa ye pɛen nyɔ so ne, né Modekae waatena ahemvie anoa nu berɛ.

english_verse: He had told Esther never to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him, just as she had always done.
translation_verse: Né Ɛseta ɔllale ye abusua anaa ye maen ali, kyɛbɔ Modekae bɔle ye noa ne ala, ofikyɛ Ɛseta lili Modekae dwirɛ so, kyɛbɔ ɔyɔle ye mmerɛ bɔ né ɔtete ye ne ala.

english_verse: Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, né Modekae te ahemvie anoa nu berɛ. Sɔ mmerɛ ne, Bigitan ne Terese, bɔ bɛte Nana Ahasuro sayɛɛ nemɔ anu nyɔ bɔ bɛwɛne Nana pumbu nu anoa nemɔ nen, bɛfɛle yaa, na bɛbɔle porɛ kyɛ bekohu Nana Ahasuro.

english_verse: Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out.
translation_verse: Nakoso edwirɛ ne pɛle Modekae so anu, na ɔɔbɔle Nana hemmaa Ɛseta amaneɛ. Na Ɛseta koso bɔle Nana Ahasuro amaneɛ hane kyɛ Modekae yeɛ ɔtele ɔ.

english_verse: King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
translation_verse: Bɛneaneane edwirɛ ne anu, na benwuni kyɛ ɔte nahorɛ nen, bɛbɔle sɔ mmienzua nyɔ ne kɔme wɔ bakaa so. Na bɛhyerɛ bewurale aberɛso dwirɛ nwomaa ne anu wɔ Nana Ahasuro nyunu berɛ.

english_verse: Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag,
translation_verse: Nziɛ ye, Nana Ahasuro bɔle Agaginiɛ Hamedata ɔwa Haman aba so. Ɔbɔle ye panyi, na ɔpagyale ye dibea maa ɔtrale ye mmango mbanyi ne amukoraa.

english_verse: and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai.
translation_verse: Nana Ahasuro somvoɛ amukoraa bɔ bɛwɔ ahemvie anoa nu berɛ ne, né ɔyɛ a bɛkoto Haman bɛfa anidie bɛma ye, ofikyɛ né Nana Ahasuro ahyɛ kyɛ bɛyɔ sɔ bɛma ye. Nakoso Modekae de, wangoto ye, yeɛ wammɔ ye ti ase wamma ye.

english_verse: he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
translation_verse: Bebisale ye daa biala, nakoso ɔyɛle ye adwene kyɛ ɔngɔyɔ bɔ bɛka ne. Yiti bɛbɔle Haman amaneɛ bɛneane, sɛ Modekae kɔhɔ so kɔyɔ sɔ a, ofikyɛ né Modekae aha ahyire bɛ kyɛ ɔte Yudaniɛ.

english_verse: Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him.
translation_verse: Haman nwuni kyɛ Modekae ngoto ye mmɔ ye ti ase mma ye nen, Haman ahone huli.

english_verse: And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
translation_verse: Né baha maen horɛ bɔ Modekae fi nu ɔ bahyire Haman, yiti Haman anguro kyɛ okohu ye ngome ɔ. Na mmom Haman bɔle porɛ kyɛ, Modekae aliɛma mɔ Yudafoɛ amukoraa bɔ bɛwɔ Ahasuro ahennie nu ne, okonua bɛ boso.

english_verse: It was now the twelfth year of the rule of King Xerxes. During Nisan, the first month of the year, Haman said, “Find out the best time for me to do this.” The time chosen was Adar, the twelfth month.
translation_verse: Nana Ahasuro lili bia ne, ye afoɛ buru ne nyɔ ne anu, bosome bɔ oli moa, bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Nisan ne anu, beguale serewa wɔ Haman nyunu. Bɛfrɛ serewagualɛ ne Pure. Bɛfa bɛpenane kyẽa ne bosome bɔ ɔkɔfa konua Yudafoɛ boso ɔ. Na serewagualɛ ne yele kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nza wɔ bosome bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nyɔ bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Ada ne.

english_verse: Then Haman went to the king and said: Your Majesty, there are some people who live all over your kingdom and won't have a thing to do with anyone else. They have customs that are different from everyone else's, and they refuse to obey your laws. We would be better off to get rid of them!
translation_verse: Yeɛ Haman sele Nana Ahasuro kyɛ, “Manzini amukoraa bɔ bɛwɔ w’ahennie ye anu ye, nu mmenia ne, bɛ nu biemɔ wɔ nu bɔ bɛwɔ manzini nemɔ nu nekaa biala, bɔ bɛ suban te sonongo ɔ. Asora bɛ mmeraa, yeɛ asora mmenia ngaa nemɔ koso bɛ deɛ. Nana, benni wɔ mmeraa so. Nana, ɔtte mayee kyɛ ɛkɔyakyi bɛ maa bɛkɔyɔ sɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Why not give orders for all of them to be killed? I can promise that you will get tons of silver for your treasury.
translation_verse: Nana, sɛ ɛkɔpene so a, maa bɛhyɛ mmeraa kyɛ odi kyɛ benua bɛ boso; na Nana, ngotua ɛdwetɛ talɛnde apee buru ngɔma bɛ bɔ bɛnea w’adwuma so ne maa bɛkɔfa bekogua wɔ fotoɛ nu.”

english_verse: The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him,
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Ahasuro yele ye nzɔanoɛ pɛteaa fili ye sa, na ɔfa mane Agaginiɛ Hamedata ɔwa Haman bɔ ɔpɔ Yudafoɛ ne.

english_verse: “Do what you want with those people! You can keep their money.”
translation_verse: Na Nana Ahasuro sele Haman kyɛ, “Sikaa ne wura wɔ sa, yeɛ mmenia ne koso bewura wɔ sa. Bɔ ekuro biala, fa yɔ bɛ.”

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Nisan, Haman called in the king's secretaries and ordered them to write letters in every language used in the kingdom. The letters were written in the name of the king and sealed by using the king's own ring. At once they were sent to the king's highest officials, the governors of each province, and the leaders of the different nations in the kingdom of Xerxes.
translation_verse: Bosome bɔ oli moa ne, ye kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nza ne, bɛfrɛfrɛle Nana Ahasuro ahyerɛlɛfoɛ amukoraa maa beyiale, na bɛhyerɛle maa ɔyɛle mmeraa, kyɛbɔ Haman hyɛle kyɛ bɛyɔ ne ala. Na bɛfa bɛɛmane Nana Ahasuro mbɔtam mbanyi mɔ, amrado mɔ, maen maen nemɔ so mbanyi mɔ, manzini biala, kyɛbɔ ye ahyerɛlɛ ne nu mmenia dwudwolɛ si te ne, sɔ ala yeɛ bɛhyerɛle ye ɔ. Bɛhyerɛle ye Nana Ahasuro dumaa nu, na bɛfale ye nzɔanoɛ pɛteaa bɛsɔle ye noa.

english_verse: The letters were taken by messengers to every part of the kingdom, and this is what was said in the letters: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, all Jewish men, women, and children are to be killed. And their property is to be taken.
translation_verse: Bɛfale ngrataa nemɔ bɛsomane mmenia bɔ bɛ nwo yɛ nyera ɔ maa bɛfa bɛhɔle Nana Ahasuro manzini ne amukoraa nu. Nu dwirɛ kyire kyɛ, beli Yudafoɛ awue, behũ bɛ ná benua bɛ mukoraa bɛ boso: mmerandeɛ ne mbanyi, mmrasua ne ngwadaa ɛlɛhomapɛ, bɔ sɔ kyẽa ne te kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nza wɔ bosome buru ne nyɔ, bɔ ye ole Ada ne anu. Osa ka kyɛ bɛfẽ bɛ nningyein bɛfa.

english_verse: King Xerxes gave orders for these letters to be posted where they could be seen by everyone all over the kingdom. The king's command was obeyed, and one of the letters was read aloud to the people in the walled city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink together, but no one in the city could figure out what was going on.
translation_verse: Kyɛbɔ Nana Ahasuro hyɛle mmeraa nen, ɛbɔfoɛ nemɔ hane bɛ nwo bɛhɔle ndɛndɛ; yeɛ mmeraa nemɔ koso bɛbɔle ye nwo dawure wɔ Susa ahenguro. Afei Nana Ahasuro ne Haman bɛtenane ase bɛnone nzaa, wɔ aberɛ bɔ né Susa kuro ne anu ama bɛ nwo adwiri bɛ ɔ.

english_verse: When Mordecai heard about the letter, he tore his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he covered his head with ashes and went through the city, crying and weeping.
translation_verse: Modekae tele edwirɛ bɔ wasi ne amukoraa nen, osunzuale ye ndaadeɛ nu, ɔherale ɛsɛen tena, ɔfale nzoen yɛle ye nwo, na ole esuɛ ne awuyebɔlɛ hyinini kuro ne anu.

english_verse: But he could go only as far as the palace gate, because no one wearing sackcloth was allowed inside the palace.
translation_verse: Ɔhɔle alaa oodwuli ahemvie anoa nu berɛ, ofikyɛ né mmeraa mma ate mma ebiala ngera ɛsɛen tena onwura ahemvie berɛ.

english_verse: In every province where the king's orders were read, the Jews cried and mourned, and they went without eating. Many of them even put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.
translation_verse: Manzini ne amukoraa nu, nekaa biala bɔ Nana Ahasuro mmeraa bɔ wahyɛ ne oodwuli ne, Yudafoɛ nemɔ bɔle awuye belili aworabɔlɛ ne mmuadaa, na bɛ nu pee herale ɛsɛen tena bɛfale nzoen bɛyɛle bɛ nwo.

english_verse: When Esther's servant girls and her other servants told her what Mordecai was doing, she became very upset and sent Mordecai some clothes to wear in place of the sackcloth. But he refused to take them.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana hemmaa Ɛseta abaawa nemɔ ne ye sayɛɛ nemɔ bɛɛbɔle ye amaneɛ, na edwirɛ ne hale Ɛseta paa. Yiti ɔmaa bɛfale ndaadeɛ bɛɛmane Modekae, kyɛ ɔpa ɛsɛen tena ne ogua dɔ, ná ɔfa ndaadeɛ ne owura, nakoso wanne ndaadeɛ ne.

english_verse: Esther had a servant named Hathach, who had been given to her by the king. So she called him in and said, “Find out what's wrong with Mordecai and why he's acting this way.”
translation_verse: Afei Ɛseta maa bɛɛfrɛle Hatake bɛbrɛle ye. Ɔte Nana Ahasuro sayɛɛ nemɔ ko bɔ baye ye kyɛ ɔso Ɛseta ɔ. Na Ɛseta somane ye kyɛ ɔhɔ Modekae berɛ oobisa ye edwirɛ horɛ bɔ wasi ɔ, ɔne kyɛbɔ ɔyɛle bɔ osili ɔ.

english_verse: Hathach went to Mordecai in the city square in front of the palace gate,
translation_verse: Hatake hɔle Modekae berɛ wɔ kuro berɛ dwaa ne aso, wɔ ahemvie anyunu berɛ.

english_verse: and Mordecai told him everything that had happened. He also told him how much money Haman had promised to add to the king's treasury, if all the Jews were killed.
translation_verse: Na Modekae hane edwirɛ bɔ wato ye amukoraa hyirele ye. Yeɛ sikaa somaa bɔ Haman ahyɛ ye nwo bɔ kyɛ okotua kɔto Nana Ahasuro fotoɛ nu maa bekonua Yudafoɛ boso ne koso, ɔha hyirele ye.

english_verse: Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the orders for the murder of the Jews and told him that these had been read in Susa. He said, “Show this to Esther and explain what it means. Ask her to go to the king and beg him to have pity on her people, the Jews!”
translation_verse: Mmeraa bɔ bɛhyɛle, bɔ bɛhyerɛle ye wɔ Susa kyɛ begyina so behũhũ Yudafoɛ ne, Modekae fale sɔ krataa ne bie mane Hatake. Ɔnwa ɔɔfa hyire Ɛseta, ohyirehyire edwirɛ ne anu hyire ye, ná ɔha hyire ye kyɛ ɔhɔ Nana Ahasuro berɛ ɔɔpa ye kyerɛ, ná ɔsrɛ ma ye, Ɛseta ye mmenia.

english_verse: Hathach went back to Esther and told her what Mordecai had said.
translation_verse: Hatake fale bɔ Modekae hane ne ɔɔbɔle Ɛseta amaneɛ.

english_verse: there is a law about going in to see the king, and all his officials and his people know about this law. Anyone who goes in to see the king without being invited by him will be put to death. The only way that anyone can be saved is for the king to hold out the gold scepter to that person. And it's been thirty days since he has asked for me.”
translation_verse: “Nana somvoɛ amukoraa, yeɛ ye manzini nemɔ nu ama bɛse kyɛ, sɛ Nana wando ye sa wamvrɛ wɔ, ná ɛkɔ ye nyunu wɔ ahemvie ne akunu dɔ a, kyɛ bienzua oo, anaa brasua oo, ye nwo mmeraa te komapɛ, bekohu sɔ sona ne. Sana sona bɔ Nana konwu ye anwumvoin kɔfa ye sikaa kɔkorɛ hɔtɔ kɔtengyɛ ye so ne, ye yeɛ okonya ye ti okodidi nu ɔ. Eleburasa ɛhe, ɔffrɛle me kyɛ mmra ye nyunu.”

english_verse: When Mordecai was told what Esther had said,
translation_verse: Bɛfale bɔ Ɛseta hane ne bɛɛbɔle Modekae amaneɛ nen,

english_verse: he sent back this reply, “Don't think that you will escape being killed with the rest of the Jews, just because you live in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Modekae koso fale ngraa maa bɛɛmane Ɛseta kyɛ, “Nnɛdwene kyɛ ɛwɔ ahemvie berɛ ne ati, sɛ beku Yudafoɛ amukoraa a, wɔ de ekonya wɔ ti kodidi nu.

english_verse: If you don't speak up now, we will somehow get help, but you and your family will be killed. It could be that you were made queen for a time like this!”
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ sɛ ɛkã wɔ noa to nu wɔ mmerɛ bɔ ɔte sɔaa nu a, mmokalɛ ne ngoalelɛ kofi neka foforɛ kɔwa kɔma Yudafoɛ, nakoso ɛne ɛse abusuafoɛ de, ɛmɔ boso konua. Nwa yeɛ ɔse ɔ? Ebiaa mmerɛ bɔ ɔte sɔaa ati yeɛ anya ɛhemmaa dibea ye ɔ.”

english_verse: Esther sent a message to Mordecai, saying,
translation_verse: Na Ɛseta fale mmuayɛɛ maa bɛɛmane Modekae kyɛ,

english_verse: “Bring together all the Jews in Susa and tell them to go without eating for my sake! Don't eat or drink for three days and nights. My servant girls and I will do the same. Then I will go in to see the king, even if it means I must die.”
translation_verse: “Kɔboaboa Yudafoɛ bɔ bɛwɔ Susa mukoraa noa, ná ɛ́mɔgyina me gya nu bɛyɛ akɔngyere. Nnɛma ɛmɔdidi, yeɛ nnɛma ɛmɔno hwee, eyia ne kɔngɔen sɔ alaa ɛlɛsa. Me koso, me ne m’abaawa nemɔ yɛkɔyɔ sɔ ala. Ye si ye, ngɔhɔ Nana nyunu, ɔwɔ nu kyɛ otia mmeraa de, na sɛ ɔba kyɛ nwu a, maa nwu.”

english_verse: Mordecai did everything Esther told him to do.
translation_verse: Na Modekae hɔle ɔɔyɔle nikyee biala, kyɛbɔ Ɛseta hane kyɛ ɔyɔ ne ala.

english_verse: Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway.
translation_verse: Ye ɛlɛsa ne aso, Ɛseta wurale ye ɛhemmaa ndaadeɛ, na oogyinane ahemvie ne akunu dɔ, wɔ Nana Ahasuro asaso ndendeneɛ so. Né Nana Ahasuro ɔte ye ahennie bia so wɔ ahemvie berɛ, wɔ ahemvie anoa ne ndendeneɛ so.

english_verse: He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her. When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter,
translation_verse: Nana Ahasuro nwuni Nana hemmaa Ɛseta kyɛ ogyi ahemvie ne akunu berɛ pɛ, ye nwo yɛle ye ahomeka, na ɔtengyɛle sikaa kɔkorɛ hɔtɔ bɔ otira ye ne wɔ Ɛseta so. Ɛseta pingyele ye nwo berɛ, na ɔfale ye sa hane ɛhɔtɔ ne ti.

english_verse: the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Ahasuro bisale ye kyɛ, “Nana hemmaa Ɛseta, nzu ɔ? Nzikyɛ yeɛ ɛpena ɔ? Sɛ m’ahennie ye bue po a, ngɔfa ngɔma wɔ.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛseta buale kyɛ, “Nana, mato poen mama wɔ, na sɛ ɛkɔpene so a, Nana, ɛne Haman bɛbra ye bo ɛnɛ.”

english_verse: The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.” The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner,
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Ahasuro sele kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhã bɛ nwo bɛɛfa Haman bɛbra ma yɛyɔ Ɛseta apɛdeɛ yɛma ye.” Yiti Nana Ahasuro ne Haman bɛhɔle ɛpoen bɔ Ɛseta ato ne abo.

english_verse: and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Bɛwɔ so bɛno nzaa nen, Nana Ahasuro bisale Ɛseta kyɛ, “W’abisadeɛ ne ole nzu? Ka, na ngɔfa ngɔma wɔ. Nzu yeɛ ɛpena ɔ? Sɛ m’ahennie ye bue po a, wɔ sa kɔha ye.”

english_verse: Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.” Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
translation_verse: Nana, sɛ anwu me anwumvoin a, yeɛ sɛ ɛpene so kyɛ ɛkɔyɔ m’abisadeɛ kɔma me, ɔne kyɛ ɛkɔma me sa kɔha bɔ mepena ɔ de a, ye de, Nana, ɛpoen bieku bɔ ɛhema ngɔto ngɔma wɔ ne Haman ne, mesrɛ wɔ ala, ɛmɔbra ye bo, na ngɔfa me dwirɛ ne ngɔto wɔ nyunu.” Haman bɔ Modekae ti so porɛ

english_verse: Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry,
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne, Haman fili ɛpoentolɛ ne abo bɔ né ye nye agye, bɔ ye ti anu ayɛ ye fɛfɛɛfɛ ɔ. Nakoso Haman oonwuni Modekae wɔ ahemvie anyunu berɛ, bɔ Modekae wandwɔso, ná afei koso wangyire kyɛ osuro Haman nen, ye ahone huli Modekae paa.

english_verse: but he did not say a thing. When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh
translation_verse: Nakoso Haman hyɛle ye nwo so, na osili nu hɔle ye awuro. Yeɛ ɔsomane maa bɛɛfrɛfrɛle ye damvo mɔ ne ɔye Sɛrese bɛwale.

english_verse: and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him.
translation_verse: Haman hane sɔ dwirɛ hemɔ hyirele bɛ: ye nwo bɔ wanya ye paa ɔ, ye mma somaa bɔ wawo bɛ ɔ, ye aba so bɔ Nana Ahasuro wabɔ amukoraa, ɔne kyɛbɔ Nana Ahasuro wasi wapagya ye dibea maa watra ye mbanyi mɔ ne ye somvoɛ mɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow.
translation_verse: Haman toale so hane kyɛ, “Nna ye mu ɛne. Nana hemmaa Ɛseta ɛpoen bɔ ɔtole ne po, wamma ebiala ammoka Nana Ahasuro so ɔne ye bangɔ ye bo, sana me ngome. Wasa wato ye sa wafrɛ me ne Nana Ahasuro kyɛ yɛbra ɛpoentolɛ bo ɛhema koso.

english_verse: But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
translation_verse: Nakoso ɛhe amukoraa ɔnyɛ me fɛ, wɔ mmerɛ biala bɔ menwu Yudaniɛ Modekae kyɛ ɔte ahemvie anoa nu berɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king.
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne kɔngɔen, Nana Ahasuro angora da. Yiti ɔhyɛle kyɛ bɛfa abakɔsɛm nwomaa bɔ ɔte aberɛso dwirɛ ne bɛbra. Na bɛkengale behyirele ye.

english_verse: the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?” “Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Ahasuro bisale kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ yeɛ yafa yabɔ Modekae aba so anaa yafa yahyɛ ye animnyam wɔ ɛhe anwo ɔ?” Na Nana Ahasuro somvoɛ nemɔ buale ye kyɛ, “Yɛyyɔle hwee yɛmmane ye.”

english_verse: About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
translation_verse: Na Nana Ahasuro bisale kyɛ, “Nwa yeɛ ɔwɔ ahemvie ne akunu berɛ ne?” Sɔ mmerɛ ne, né Haman adwu ahemvie aluo berɛ pato nu berɛ, kyɛ ɔbaahã kyire Nana kyɛ ɔ́pene so ma bɛbɔ Modekae kɔme wɔ bakaa bɔ wafa wapena berɛ wama Modekae ne aso.

english_verse: The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.” “Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
translation_verse: Yiti Nana Ahasuro somvoɛ nemɔ sele ye kyɛ, “Haman yeɛ waagyina ahemvie ne akunu berɛ ɔ?” Yeɛ Nana sele kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔma ɔbra nu!”

english_verse: When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?” Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor.
translation_verse: Yiti Haman wale nu, na Nana Ahasuro bisale ye kyɛ, “Sona bɔ me nye kɔgye kyɛ ngɔbɔ ye aba so ne, nzikyɛ yeɛ nyɔ ma ye ɔ?” Yeɛ Haman hane ye wɔ ye ti anu kyɛ, “Nwa koraa yeɛ Nana kɔbɔ ye aba so kɔtra me ɔ?”

english_verse: So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man,
translation_verse: Na Haman sele Nana Ahasuro kyɛ, “Nana, sona bɔ ekuro kyɛ ɛbɔ ye aba so ne,

english_verse: get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress.
translation_verse: maa bɛfa ahennie ataadeɛ bɔ awura ye le ɔ bɛbra, ɔne pɔngɔ bɔ atena ye so le ɔ, bɔ ahennie abotire bɔ ye ɔ bɛbra.

english_verse: The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Ahasuro sele Haman kyɛ, “Ka wɔ nwo kɔfa ataadeɛ ne pɔngɔ ne, kyɛbɔ aha ne ala, ná yɔ sɔ ma Modekae bɔ ɔtena ahemvie anoa nu berɛ ne. Edwirɛ biala bɔ aha ne, nnɛyɔ nu bie yakyi bie.”

english_verse: Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
translation_verse: Yiti Haman ɔɔfale ataadeɛ ne wurale Modekae, ɔfale ye tenane pɔngɔ ne aso, olili ye nyunu fale ye fale kuro ne dwaaso, na ɔbɔle ye dawure kyɛ, “Sona bɔ Nana kuro kyɛ ɔbɔ ye aba so ne, sɔaa yeɛ odi kyɛ bɛyɛ ye hɔ oo.”

english_verse: Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame.
translation_verse: Na ɛhe asi ne, Modekae sa wale ahemvie anoa nu berɛ, nakoso Haman de, ɔfale aworabɔlɛ ne animguaseɛ hane ye nwo hɔle ye awuro.

english_verse: Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.”
translation_verse: Edwirɛ bɔ wato Haman ne, ɔfale ye mukoraa bɔle ɔye Sɛrese ne ye damvo nemɔ amukoraa amaneɛ. Na ye foɛtulɛfoɛ nemɔ ne ɔye Sɛrese besele ye kyɛ, “Modekae bɔ ahyɛ ye bo agua wɔ nyunu ase wɔ ye nyunu ne, sɛ ɔte Yudaniɛ de a, ye de ɛngɔhora ye nyunu gyina, ekoli ngoguo wɔ ye nyunu.”

english_verse: They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_verse: Bɛ noa wɔ so bɔ bɛ ne ye bedwudwo ne, Nana Ahasuro sayɛɛ nemɔ wale berɛ, na bɛfale Haman ndɛndɛ so bɛhɔle ɛpoen bɔ Ɛseta ato ne abo.

english_verse: The king and Haman were dining with Esther
translation_verse: Nana Ahasuro ne Haman bɛhɔle Nana hemmaa Ɛseta ɛpoentolɛ ne abo kyɛ bɛ ne ye bɛkwaadidi.

english_verse: and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
translation_verse: Ye elenyɔ ne aso, bɛwɔ ɛpoentolɛ ne abo ne, Nana Ahasuro bisale Ɛseta bieku kyɛ, “Nana hemmaa Ɛseta, w’abisadeɛ ne ole nzu? Ka, na ngɔfa ngɔma wɔ. Nzu yeɛ ɛpena ɔ? Sɛ m’ahennie ye bue po a, wɔ sa kɔha ye.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want,
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana hemmaa Ɛseta buale kyɛ, “O, Nana, sɛ anwu me anwumvoin, yeɛ sɛ ɛpene so a, maa nya me ti nnidi nu. M’abisadeɛ ne, ye ɛne; yeɛ bɔ mepena koso ole kyɛ, me mmenia konya bɛ ti bekodidi nu ɔ.

english_verse: because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ bayɛ me ne me mmenia atɔen kyɛ beli yɛ awue, behũ yɛ, ná benua yɛ boso. Na sɛ bɛtɔnene yɛ maa yɛyɛle ngoaa ne afaneɛ mɔ po a, ahaa mengɔtɛ me noa nu, ofikyɛ ahaa ye nwo ngohia kyɛ ngɔfa sɔ dwirɛ kaaba he ngɔha Nana adwene ɔ.

english_verse: “Who would dare to do such a thing?” the king asked.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Ahasuro bisale Nana hemmaa Ɛseta kyɛ, “Sona beni ɛne, ɔwɔ nisua, nwa yeɛ wabɔ sɔ porɛ he ne?”

english_verse: Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!” Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
translation_verse: Na Ɛseta buale kyɛ, “Sɔ Haman he, ɔte busueniɛ, okyi yɛ, na osa te yɛ pɔfoɛ.” Na sɔ dwirɛ ne mane Haman kunu tele ye wɔ Nana Ahasuro ne Nana hemmaa Ɛseta bɛ nyunu berɛ.

english_verse: The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden. Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Ahasuro le ɛyaa dwɔsole fili ɛpoentolɛ ne abo, na ɔhɔle ahemvie turo ne anu, nakoso Haman de, ɔhale berɛ srɛle Nana hemmaa Ɛseta kyɛ onwu ye anwumvoin ole ye ngoa, ofikyɛ onwuni kyɛ Nana Ahasuro wayɛ ye adwene kyɛ ɔkɔma edwirɛ piri paa kɔto ye.

english_verse: Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!” As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Nana Ahasuro fili ahemvie turo ne anu sa wale ɛpoentolɛ ne abo nen, né Haman ato ye nwo waatɔ nnamu bɔ Ɛseta la nu ne aso, na Nana Ahasuro sele kyɛ, “Eh, me nyunu wa po, wɔ m’awuro wa, yeɛ ɛbaato Nana hemmaa mmɔnaa ye!” Na Nana Ahasuro noa ambe, yeɛ bɛkyekyele Haman nye ɔ.

english_verse: At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_verse: Yiti bakaa bɔ Haman fa penane berɛ kyɛ bɛbaabɔ Modekae kɔme wɔ so ne, so yeɛ bɛbɔle Haman kɔme ɔ. Na afei Nana Ahasuro ahone tɔle nzue nu.

english_verse: Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne ala, Yudafoɛ bɛ pɔfoɛ Haman ye awuro ne, Nana Ahasuro fa mane Nana hemmaa Ɛseta. Na Modekae wale Nana nyunu, ofikyɛ né Ɛseta aha ahyire Nana kyɛ ye nwoniɛ ɛne.

english_verse: and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
translation_verse: Afei Nana Ahasuro ye nzɔanoɛ pɛteaa bɔ ole fili Haman berɛ ne, ɔye fili ye bɔbɔ ye sa, na ɔfa mane Modekae. Na Ɛseta bɔle Modekae panyi wɔ Haman awuro ne aso.

english_verse: Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!”
translation_verse: Afei Ɛseta hɔle Nana Ahasuro nyunu bieku, ɔtole ye nwo yele ye gya bo, na ole esuɛ ɔkotole ye ɔfa tole ye nyunu kyɛ, Yudafoɛ nwo adwene tɛɛ bɔ Agaginiɛ Haman nyane ye, ɔne bɛ ti so porɛ bɔ ɔbɔle ne, ɔsrɛ ye ala, ɔ́pɛ nu.

english_verse: King Xerxes held out the golden scepter to Esther,
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Ahasuro tengyɛle sikaa kɔkorɛ hɔtɔ ne wɔ Ɛseta so. Ɛseta dwɔso gyinane Nana Ahasuro nyunu berɛ,

english_verse: and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed,
translation_verse: na ɔhane kyɛ, “Nana, sɛ ɛpene so, sɛ anwu me anwumvoin a, Nana, sɛ ɛnea ná ɔte paa a, yeɛ sɛ masɔ wɔ nye a, ye de ngrataa bɔ Agaginiɛ Hamedata ɔwa Haman nyane adwene tɛɛ hyerɛle fa hyɛle mmeraa kyɛ behũ Yudafoɛ bɔ bɛwɔ wɔ manzini amukoraa nu ne, hyɛ mmeraa maa bɛpɛ nu.

english_verse: King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Ahasuro sele Nana hemmaa Ɛseta ne Yudaniɛ Modekae kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔtie! Mafa Haman awuro mama Ɛseta, na babɔ ye kɔme wɔ bakaa ne aso, ofikyɛ ɔbɔle Yudafoɛ bɛ ti so porɛ kyɛ okohu bɛ.

english_verse: I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
translation_verse: Bɔ ɛmɔkuro biala, ɛmɔhyerɛ bɛfa Yudafoɛ nwo wɔ me, Nana Ahasuro me dumaa nu, ná ɛ́mɔfa me nzɔanoɛ kaa ne bɛsɔ krataa ne noa, ofikyɛ mmeraa bɔ bahyerɛ ye wɔ me, Nana Ahasuro me dumaa nu, bɔ bafa me nzɔanoɛ kaa basɔ ye noa ne, bɛkakyi ye a ɔnyɛ yé.”

english_verse: They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
translation_verse: Modekae maa bɛhyerɛle ngrataa nemɔ Nana Ahasuro dumaa nu, ɔfale Nana Ahasuro nzɔanoɛ kaa sosɔle bɛ noa, ɔfa somane mmenia bɔ bɛ nwo yɛ nyera, bɔ bɛtenatenane mbɔngɔ bɔ bɛ nwo yɛ nyera ɔ so. Né ahemvie adwuma ti yeɛ bɛhyɛ da besie sɔ mbɔngɔ nemɔ ɔ.

english_verse: In these letters the king said: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, the Jews in every city and province will be allowed to get together and defend themselves. They may destroy any army that attacks them, and they may kill all of their enemies, including women and children. They may also take everything that belongs to their enemies. A copy of this law is to be posted in every province and read by everyone.
translation_verse: Sɔ krataa ne mane Yudafoɛ ate kyɛ bɛkora bɛfa nu dwirɛ bɛhyɛ mmeraa wɔ manzini amukoraa nu, ɔne kyɛ bɛkora bɛbɔ ye nwo dawure bekyire maen maen amukoraa so mmenia. Osa ma Yudafoɛ ate kyɛ bɛboaboa bɛ nwo bɛtɔ bɛ pɔfoɛ mɔ so wereɛ sɔ kyẽa ne.

english_verse: Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth. After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered,
translation_verse: Afei Modekae fili Nana Ahasuro berɛ fitele. Né owura ahemvo ataadeɛ bɔ ɔte bibire ne fufue, nwera ne koogyan aguasoɛ, na né ɔbɔ sikaa kɔkorɛ abotire. Na Susa kuro berɛ ama bɔle ese belili ahurusi.

english_verse: and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
translation_verse: Na ɛhe yɛle Yudafoɛ bɛ ti ngoa, anwosɛpɛ, anigye ne animnyam.

english_verse: In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_verse: Manzini biala nu ne kuro biala so bɔ Nana Ahasuro mmeraa ne ahyɛdeɛ ne oodwuli ne, Yudafoɛ nyane anwosɛpɛ ne anigye, bɛtole poen, na belili afofi. Yeɛ maen maen mɔ bɔ bɛwɔ aseɛ ne aso ne, Yudafoɛ nwo suronyi tɔle bɛ nu pee so, yiti bɛ nu pee bɛɛyɛle Yudafoɛ.

english_verse: The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around,
translation_verse: Bosome bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nyɔ, bɔ oli Ada ne, ye kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nza ne aso, bɔ né bɛbaafa Nana Ahasuro mmeraa ne ye krataa ne bɛyɔ adwuma ne, sɔ kyẽa ne ala yeɛ né Yudafoɛ bɛ pɔfoɛ mɔ batu basie berɛ kyɛ bekohũhũ Yudafoɛ ɔ. Nakoso wamma ye sɔ. Ɔyɛle kyẽa bɔ Yudafoɛ belili bɛ pɔfoɛ mɔ so ngonim ɔ.

english_verse: and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
translation_verse: Yudafoɛ boaboale bɛ noa wɔ bɛ nguro nemɔ aso, wɔ Nana Ahasuro manzini ne amukoraa nu, kyɛ ebiala bɔ ɔkɔwa kyɛ ɔbaahu bɛ ne, bɛ koso bekohu ye. Na ebiala angora wangyina bɛ nyunu, ofikyɛ bɛ nwo suronyi tɔle amaen maen nemɔ nu mmenia so.

english_verse: The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews.
translation_verse: Manzini nemɔ anu mbanyi ne mbɔtam mbanyi ne amrado mɔ ne ahemvie mbanyi gyinane Yudafoɛ si, ofikyɛ Modekae nwo suronyi tɔle bɛ so.

english_verse: Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
translation_verse: Ɔwale ye sɔ, ofikyɛ Modekae nyane tumi wɔ ahemvie berɛ, ye dumaa trɛle hɔle manzini ne amukoraa nu, na ɔhɔle so nyane tumi.

english_verse: The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy.
translation_verse: Yiti Yudafoɛ fale ngrandɛ behuhuni bɛ pɔfoɛ mɔ amukoraa, bɛpepɛle bɛ, benuane bɛ boso, na bɔ bekuro biala, bɛfa bɛyɔle bɛ pɔfoɛ mɔ.

english_verse: Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa.
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne, mmenia somaa bɔ behuni bɛ wɔ Susa ahenguro berɛ ne, bɛfale ye nwo amaneɛ bɛɛbɔle Nana Ahasuro.

english_verse: Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
translation_verse: Na Nana Ahasuro sele Nana hemmaa Ɛseta kyɛ, “Susa ahenguro wa, Yudafoɛ bahuhu mmienzua ɛyaa nnu, yeɛ basa bahu Haman mma mmienzua buru nemɔ. Né nzaade bɔ bayɔ ye wɔ me manzini ngaa nemɔ anu ne, ɔkɔtra so. Kekesaala ye, nzikyɛ yeɛ ɔte w’abisadeɛ ɔ? Ka, na ngɔfa ngɔma wɔ. Nzikyɛ bieku yeɛ ɛpena ɔ? Wɔ sa kɔha ye.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛseta buale kyɛ, “Nana, sɛ ɛkɔpene a, Yudafoɛ bɔ bɛwɔ Susa ne, ɛhema koso ma bɛ ate ma besa bɛyɔ bɔ bagyina mmeraa ne aso bayɔ ye ɛnɛ ne. Haman mma mmienzua buru nemɔ koso, maa besinze bɛ fuin nemɔ wɔ bakaa so.”

english_verse: King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa.
translation_verse: Na Nana Ahasuro fale ahyɛdeɛ mane kyɛ bɛyɔ sɔ. Ɔhyɛle mmeraa wɔ Susa, na besinzele Haman mma mmienzua buru nemɔ bɛ fuin.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yudafoɛ bɔ bɛwɔ Susa ne de, kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nza, ɔne bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nna ne yeɛ bɛboaboale bɛ noa ɔ. Belele bɛ nwome kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nnu ne, na bɛfa bɛkakyili ɛpoentolɛ ne anigye kyẽa.

english_verse: This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other. The Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Ye sɔ ne ati, Yudafoɛ bɔ bɛwɔ namue nemɔ anu, bɔ fasue nne bɛ nguro nemɔ anwo ne, batu bosome Ada, ye kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nna ne basie berɛ kyɛ ɔte anigye ne ɛpoentolɛ kyẽa, na ɔte nwomelelɛ kyẽa bɔ bɛkyekyɛ bɛ nwo bɛ nwo aleɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces
translation_verse: Modekae hyerɛle edwirɛ bɔ osisili ne, na ɔmaa bɛfale ngrataa bɛɛmane Yudafoɛ amukoraa bɔ bepingye, ɔne bɛ bɔ bɛwɔ dedeede, bɔ bɛwɔ Nana Ahasuro manzini amukoraa nu ɔ.

english_verse: and told them: Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar,
translation_verse: Ɔnwa, odi kyɛ betu bosome Ada, ye kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nna, ɔne bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne nnu ne besie berɛ afoɛnoa biala,

english_verse: the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
translation_verse: kyɛ bɛte ngyẽa bɔ Yudafoɛ bɛperele benyane asomdwee befili bɛ pɔfoɛ mɔ sa nu ɔ, kyɛ ɔte bosome bɔ b’aworabɔlɛ kakyili anigye, bɔ b’esuɛ kakyili nwomelelɛ ɔ. Ɔnwa, odi kyɛ betu besie berɛ bɛfa bɛyɛ ɛpoentolɛ ne anigye ngyẽa, ngyẽa bɔ bɛkɔhyehyɛ bɛ nwo bɛ nwo aleɛ, ná bahyɛ ehiafoɛ mɔ koso nningyein ɔ.

english_verse: They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration. The Reason for the Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Yiti Modekae nhyehyɛleɛ bɔ ɔhyerɛ ɔɔmane Yudafoɛ ne, bɛfa bɛfoale bɔ né bahyɛ ye bo bɛyɔ ne aso maa ɔɔyɛle b’amammerɛ.

english_verse: Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
translation_verse: Ɔhyerɛle kyɛ, Agaginiɛ Hamedata ɔwa Haman bɔ ɔpɔ Yudafoɛ amukoraa ne, ɔbɔle porɛ kyɛ okonua Yudafoɛ bɛ boso. Oguale serewa bɔ bɛfrɛ ye ‘Pure’ ne, kyɛ okoli bɛ so ngonim ná wanua bɛ boso.

english_verse: Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged.
translation_verse: Nakoso mmerɛ bɔ Ɛseta hɔle Nana Ahasuro nyunu nen, Nana Ahasuro hyɛle mmeraa maa bɛhyerɛle, kyɛ Yudafoɛ ti so porɛ bɔ Haman wabɔ ne, odi kyɛ ɔbɔ ye bɔbɔ ye ti so. Na odi kyɛ besinze ye ne ye mma mmienzua nemɔ wɔ bakaa so.

english_verse: Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast.
translation_verse: Ye sɔ ne ati, bɛfrɛ sɔ ngyẽa ne Purim, bɔ benya befili edwofua Pure nu ɔ. Ɔnate Modekae krataa ne anu dwirɛ amukoraa so, yeɛ tebea bɔ bɛhɔle nu wɔ sɔ dwirɛ ye anwo, ɔne edwirɛ bɔ ɔtole bɛ ne ati,

english_verse: Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast.
translation_verse: Nana hemmaa Ɛseta bɔ ɔse ole Abihail ne, ogyinane tumi so hyerɛle krataa bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ɔ, kyɛ odi kyɛ bedi Purim aluolue ne, na ɔfa foale Yudaniɛ Modekae krataa ne aso.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
translation_verse: Na ngrataa ne hyɛle bɛ kyɛ, odi kyɛ bedi Purim ngyẽa ne wɔ mmerɛ bɔ bahyehyɛ bato berɛ ɔ nu, kyɛbɔ Yudaniɛ Modekae ne Nana hemmaa Ɛseta bɛhyɛle Yudafoɛ kyɛ bɛyɔ ne ala, kyɛbɔ bale bato nu kyɛ bɛ ne bɛ bosofoɛ bekoli mmuadaa ne awuyebɔlɛ mmerɛ nwo nhyehyɛleɛ ne aso ne.

english_verse: These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_verse: Na mmeraa bɔ Nana hemmaa Ɛseta hyɛle ne, ɔmane Purim nwo nhyehyɛleɛ ne timuni, na bɛhyerɛ bɛtole berɛ.

english_verse: King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea.
translation_verse: Afei Nana Ahasuro pɛle ɛtoɔ kyɛ maen ne anu ama, ɔne bɛ bɔ bɛwɔ supɔ nemɔ aso ne betua.

english_verse: All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai.
translation_verse: Nana Ahasuro tumi ne ye koɛ nu anwoserɛ amukoraa, yeɛ panyi bɔ ɔbɔle Modekae maa onyane animnyam kandinga ne, ye nwo dwirɛ amukoraa, bahyerɛ ye wɔ Media ne Pɛsia ahemvo b’aberɛ so dwirɛ nwomaa ne anu.

english_verse: Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_verse: Na Yudaniɛ Modekae ye dibea ne, sɛ né Nana Ahasuro nne berɛ a, ye yeɛ ɔwɔ berɛ ɔ. Onyane animnyam wɔ Yudafoɛ nyunu, na ye mmango Yudafoɛ hurole ye dwirɛ, ofikyɛ né ɔpena ye mmenia paa, na ɔfale ye boso ama bɛ yeeyɛlɛ nwo dwirɛ tole ye nwo so, na ɔhane asomdwee dwirɛ hyirele ye mmenia amukoraa.

english_verse: Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
translation_verse: Né biaa bie te Yuse aseɛ so. Ye dumaa li Yob. Sɔ biaa ne, né ye bra te sannwuu, na ɔtengyɛ. Ɔte sona bɔ né osuro Nyameɛ ɔ, na ɔhwene ye nwo fili bɔne nwo.

english_verse: the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ AWURADE bisale Satan kyɛ, “Nisua yeɛ efi wale ɔ?” Na Satan buale AWURADE kyɛ, “Aseɛ so bɔ mekyinikyini, bɔ medi so akɔneaba ne yeɛ mvi so mmale ɔ.”

english_verse: Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Ye mma mmienzua nemɔ, né ɔyɛ a, bɛkɔ ebiala awuro ngoko ngoko bɛkɔto poen, na né ɔyɛ a bɛto bɛ sa bɛfrɛ b’eliɛma mmrasua nza nemɔ maa bɛ ne bɛ babɔ nu bedidi bɛno.

english_verse: After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God. Angels, the Lord, and Satan
translation_verse: Sɛ bɛto poen ne alaa maa oyia bɛ ti a, ɔyɛ a Yob soma maa bɛkɔfrɛ bɛ bɛba, na ɔpete bɛ nwo. Né ɔyɛ a ɔpɛ aleɛ odwɔso gyina bɛ nu biala ye gya nu ɔbɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ. Ofikyɛ Yob susuli kyɛ, “Me mma ye mɔ, ebiaa bayɔ bɔne, ebiaa badwudwo batia Nyameɛ wɔ bɛ nzusuleɛ nu.” Na sɔ ala yeɛ né ɔyɛ a Yob yɔ ɔ. Nyameɛ di Yob nwo adanzeɛ paa

english_verse: One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, Nyameɛ mma mɔ wale beegyinagyinane AWURADE nyunu, na Satan koso ɔfrale bɛ nu hɔle berɛ bie.

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ AWURADE bisale Satan kyɛ, “Aso asusu m’akoaa Yob nwo? Kyɛ sona biala nne berɛ bɔ ɔte kyɛ ye ɔ wɔ aseɛ so; kyɛ ɔte sona bɔ ye bra te sannwuu, ná ɔtengyɛ ɔ; kyɛ osuro Nyameɛ, na ɔtwe ye nwo fi bɔne nwo ɔ?”

english_verse: “You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere.
translation_verse: Ye nwo waen, ye abusua nwo waen, ɔne nikyee biala bɔ ole ye ɔ nwo waen bɔ abɔ abra ayia ne, aso nna ye ti ɔ? Ayira ye sa noa adwuma so, na ye nyɛmmoa bata pee wɔ aseɛ ne aso.

english_verse: Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Nakoso wɔ de, tengyɛ wɔ sa de bɔ ole ye amukoraa fi ye sa nu nea, sɛ ɔngɔkekã musue dwirɛ ngotia wɔ a!”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.” Then Satan left. Job Loses Everything
translation_verse: Yeɛ AWURADE sele Satan kyɛ, “Nea, nikyee biala bɔ ole ye ne, owura wɔ sa. Nakoso ye ngoa de, nnɛfa wɔ sa ka ye!” Yiti Satan fili AWURADE nyunu berɛ hɔle. Yob agyapadeɛ ne ye mma fi ye sa

english_verse: Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son,
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, Yob mma mmienzua ne mmrasua nemɔ tole poen bɔ né bedidi bɛno wɔ b’eliɛma bienzua panyi paa n’awuro ɔ.

english_verse: when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass,
translation_verse: Na ɛbɔfoɛ wale Yob berɛ ɔɔbɔle ye amaneɛ kyɛ, “Nandwie nemɔ, mmerɛ bɔ né begu so befundam aseɛ, bɔ né afunum mmeleɛ nemɔ koso bedidi wɔ bɛ nwo berɛ ne,

english_verse: a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: mvum nu, Sabeafoɛ wale bɛɛhyehyele bɛ bɛhɔle, na bafa ngrandɛ bahuhu somvoɛ nemɔ. Me ngome twe yeɛ manya me ti madidi nu bɔ mebaabɔ wɔ amaneɛ ye.”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Ye noa wɔ so bɔ odwudwo ne, sona foforɛ wale ɔɔbɔle amaneɛ kyɛ, “Nyameɛ see afi nyameɛso watete wagua wayera mmoaen ne somvoɛ nemɔ wahũ bɛ. Me ngome twe yeɛ manya me ti madidi nu bɔ mebaabɔ wɔ amaneɛ ye.”

english_verse: Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Ye noa wɔ so bɔ odwudwo ne, sona foforɛ wale ɔɔbɔle amaneɛ kyɛ, “Kaldeafoɛ hyɛle bɛ nu kure nza, babɔ afupɔngɔ nemɔ so apaa bahyehye bɛ bahɔ, na bafa ngrandɛ bahuhu somvoɛ nemɔ. Me ngome twe yeɛ manya me ti madidi nu bɔ mebaabɔ wɔ amaneɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son,
translation_verse: Ye noa wɔ so bɔ odwudwo ne, sona foforɛ wale ɔɔbɔle amaneɛ kyɛ, “Wɔ mma mmienzua ne mmrasua nemɔ, né bedidi bɛno wɔ b’eliɛma bienzua panyi paa n’awuro.

english_verse: when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Na mvum nu, mvrama piri bie tu fili ɛserɛ ne aso dɔ, oofini awuro ne ndweasoɛ nna nemɔ, na wabu wagua mmerandeɛ ne ndaluwa nemɔ aso maa bawuwu. Me ngome twe yeɛ manya me ti madidi nu bɔ mebaabɔ wɔ amaneɛ ye.”

english_verse: When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yob dwɔsole, osunzuale ye bɔbɔ ye ndaadeɛ nu, ɔpoane ye ti, na ɔtole ye nwo yele aseɛnwo berɛ sɔnene .

english_verse: and said: “We bring nothing at birth; we take nothing with us at death. The Lord alone gives and takes. Praise the name of the Lord!”
translation_verse: Na ɔhane kyɛ, “Mvi me ni akunu méba ne, né me nwo la so, na ye sɔ ala yeɛ ngosa ngɔfa ngɔhɔ ɔ. AWURADE yeɛ ɔfa mane me ɔ, yeɛ AWURADE asa ale ɔ. Animnyam hã AWURADE dumaa.”

english_verse: In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_verse: Na ɛhe amukoraa nu ne, Yob anyɔ bɔne, yeɛ wammɔ Nyameɛ somoɛ.

english_verse: When the angels gathered around the Lord again, Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Ɛlɛho bie, Nyameɛ mma mɔ wale beegyinagyinane AWURADE nyunu bieku, na Satan koso ɔfrale bɛ nu hɔle berɛ kyɛ ɔkwaagyina AWURADE nyunu.

english_verse: and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ AWURADE bisale Satan kyɛ, “Nisua yeɛ efi wale ɔ?” Na Satan buale AWURADE kyɛ, “Aseɛ so bɔ mekyinikyini, bɔ medi so akɔneaba ne yeɛ mvi so mmale ɔ.”

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ AWURADE bisale Satan kyɛ, “Aso asusu m’akoaa Yob nwo? Kyɛ sona biala nne berɛ bɔ ɔte kyɛ ye ɔ wɔ aseɛ so; kyɛ ɔte sona bɔ ye bra te sannwuu, ná ɔtengyɛ ɔ; kyɛ osuro Nyameɛ, na ɔtwe ye nwo fi bɔne nwo ɔ?” Ɔtɛ gyi ye gya nu wɔ ye nahorɛlilɛ nu, ɔwɔ nu kyɛ awurawura me amaa mafa ye nwo dwirɛ, kyɛ mbrapra amaneɛ ngua ye so wɔ aberɛ bɔ ɔyyɔle bɔne biala ɔ.”

english_verse: Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive.
translation_verse: Na Satan buale AWURADE kyɛ, “Na ye nwonaen koso ɛ! Bɔ sona le ye amukoraa, okuro kyɛ ɔkɔmaa ɔkɔhwere ye, ná wanya ngoa.

english_verse: Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Nakoso wɔ de, tengyɛ wɔ sa ka ye ma anwonyerɛ ɔbɔ ye nea, sɛ ɔngɔkekã musue dwirɛ ngotia wɔ a!”

english_verse: “All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ AWURADE sele Satan kyɛ, “Nea, owura wɔ sa. Nakoso ye ngoa de, nnɛfa wɔ sa ka ye!”

english_verse: Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
translation_verse: Yiti Satan fili AWURADE nyunu berɛ hɔle, na ɔpraprale ngena mbiri guale Yob so mane ye nwo tutuli ngena fite ye ti so kɔka ye gya bo.

english_verse: Then Job sat on the ash-heap to show his sorrow. And while he was scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery,
translation_verse: Afei Yob ɔɔtenane nzoen nu, na ɔfale nyangaa bue bie dwirili ye nwo.

english_verse: his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
translation_verse: Yeɛ ɔye sele ye kyɛ, “Yiti ɛtɛ gyi wɔ gya nu wɔ wɔ nahorɛlilɛ nu! Ka musue dwirɛ tia Nyameɛ, ná wu!”

english_verse: Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God. Job's Three Friends
translation_verse: Nakoso obuale ye kyɛ, “Edwudwo kyɛbɔ brasua kwaseaa biala odwudwo ɔ. Nzu ɔ? Nyameɛ ma yɛ nikye paa a, yɛde; nzu ati yeɛ sɛ ɔma yɛ bɔ ɔtte mayee a, ɔnzɛ kyɛ yɛde ɔ?” Na ɛhemɔ amukoraa nu ne, Yob amma ye noa andia Nyameɛ. Yob abiɛngo nza nemɔ

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him.
translation_verse: Né Yob le ye mmango nza biemɔ. Bɛ ole Temanniɛ Elifase, Suhiniɛ Bildade, yeɛ Naamaniɛ Sofa. Bɛtele amaneɛ amukoraa bɔ wato ye nen, bɛ nu biala fili ye kuro wale, na beeyiale bɛfale adwene kyɛ bɛkɔ Yob berɛ bɛkɔyɛ ye yaakɔ ná bɛkyekye ye wora.

english_verse: When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly.
translation_verse: Bɛwɔ dedeede ná bɛtole bɛ nye bɛneane ye nen, bannwu ye sona horɛ. Yiti besuni hahii, besunzuale bɛ ndaadeɛ nu, na betuli mvuture bɛhɔle anwuro beguale bɛ ti so.

english_verse: For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_verse: Bɛ ne ye tenatenane asefuo nu berɛ ɛlɛsoo, eyia ne kɔngɔen. Na bɛ nu biala ne ye andwudwo, ofikyɛ benwuni kyɛ né onwu amaneɛ paa.

english_verse: Finally, Job cursed the day of his birth
translation_verse: Ɛhe asi ne, Yob bukyele ye noa nomale ye krakyẽa.

english_verse: by saying to God:
translation_verse: Yob hane kyɛ,

english_verse: Blot out the day of my birth and the night when my parents created a son.
translation_verse: “Kyẽa bɔ bɛwole me ne, sɔ kyẽa ne ótu mini, ɔne kɔngɔen bɔ bɛhane kyɛ, ‘Banwonzɛ baa bienzua’ ɔ.

english_verse: Forget about that day, cover it with darkness,
translation_verse: Awosii to sɔ kyẽa ne! Nnɛma Nyameɛ fi anwuro kaye ye, yeɛ nnɛma kanea ta so.

english_verse: and send thick, gloomy shadows to fill it with dread.
translation_verse: Awosii tunn ne awosii kabii ómundu so. Munungum ɔ́kata so, alehyeleɛ bɔ ɔkakyi awosii ne, ówunanwuna ye.

english_verse: Don't let children be created or joyful shouts be heard ever again in that night.
translation_verse: Sɔ kɔngɔen ne, ɔyɛ bɔfonn, nnɛmaa bɛte komviɛ bɔ ɔte anigye wɔ nu.

english_verse: Let those with magic powers place a curse on that day.
translation_verse: Bɛ bɔ bɛnoma alehyeleɛ ne, maa bɛnoma ye, bɛ yeɛ bɛnoma ɛlɛngyɛen suronyisuronyi maa odwɔso ɔ.

english_verse: Darken its morning stars and remove all hope of light,
translation_verse: Awosii to ye alebahyene nzramaa mɔ, ɔkɔpena kanea si atee, nakoso ongonya bie, nnɛma ye nye nwu ngyerɛmɔ kanea,

english_verse: because it let me be born into a world of trouble. Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
translation_verse: ofikyɛ wandua me ni awodeɛ ye noa ate, bɔ ɔnate so wamaa menwu amaneɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Why was I accepted and allowed to nurse at my mother's breast?
translation_verse: Nzu ati yeɛ nangoroma ebie maa bɛwole me bɛtole so ɔ? Nzu ati yeɛ nyane nyɔfone nnone ɔ?

english_verse: Now I would be at peace in the silent world below
translation_verse: Sɛ nwuli a, ahaa mala berɛ konn, ah, ahaa malafe, bɔ mede me nwome ɔ;

english_verse: with kings and their advisors whose palaces lie in ruins,
translation_verse: ahaa me ne ɛhemɔ: ewiase ahemvo ne foɛtulɛfoɛ, bɔ besisili sua maa wabubu wagua ɔ,

english_verse: I wish I had been born dead and then buried, never to see the light of day.
translation_verse: Anaakyɛ, nzu ati yeɛ banzie me kyɛ baa bɔ bapɔ ye ɔ, kyɛ baa bɔ wawu oni akunu ɔ?

english_verse: In the world of the dead, the wicked and the weary rest without a worry. *
translation_verse: Ɛborɔ dɔ de, amumuyɛɛfoɛ bɛnha ebiala ko, na dɔ de, bɛ bɔ bafɛ ne bede bɛ nwome.

english_verse: where captives and slaves are free at last. Why Does God Let Me Live?
translation_verse: Berɛ de, atitirefoɛ ne kwahweabaa mɔ bɛwɔ berɛ, na ngangafoɛ banya fawɔnwodi bafi bɛ mene mɔ sa nu.

english_verse: Why does God let me live when life is miserable and so bitter?
translation_verse: “Sona bɔ ɔyɛ anwumvo ne, nzu ati yeɛ ɛma ye kanea, ná ɛma bɔ odi aworabɔlɛ onya ngoa ɔ?

english_verse: I keep longing for death more than I would seek a valuable treasure.
translation_verse: Bɛ yeɛ bɛnwondɛ ewue, nakoso ɔmma ɔ, bɛ yeɛ bɛpena ewue bɛtra agyapadeɛ bɔ bafa bafea ɔ,

english_verse: Nothing could make me happier than to be in the grave.
translation_verse: bɛ yeɛ bewu a bɛ nye gye paa ɔ, bɛ yeɛ besie bɛ a, benya anika ɔ.

english_verse: Why do I go on living when God has me surrounded, and I can't see the road?
translation_verse: Sona bɔ ye atee amini ne, nzu ati yeɛ ɛma ye kanea ɔ, mekyire sona bɔ Nyameɛ amaa wali amia ne?

english_verse: Moaning and groaning are my food and drink,
translation_verse: Me suɛ akakyi m’aleɛ, yeɛ me penelɛ wayɛ kyɛ nzue bɔ behwie begua ɔ.

english_verse: I have no peace or rest— only troubles and worries.
translation_verse: Me nwo ndɔ me, mennya asomdwee, mennya me nwome menne, na mmom amaneɛ yeɛ ɔto me ɔ.”

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman said:
translation_verse: Yeɛ Temanniɛ Elifase buale kyɛ,

english_verse: Please be patient and listen to what I have to say. *
translation_verse: “Sɛ ebie ka edwirɛ he anwo bie kyire wɔ a, ɔkɔha wɔ anaa? Nakoso nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora komua ye noa ɔ?

english_verse: In my experience, only those who plant seeds of evil harvest trouble,
translation_verse: Bɔ mese ole kyɛ, bɛ bɔ betutu amumuyɛɛ bɛtɛ, ná bedua amaneɛ ne, bɔ batɛ ne bɔ balua ne ala yeɛ bɛtete ɔ.

english_verse: and then they are swept away by the angry breath of God.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ ye nwomeɛ yeɛ oku bɛ ɔ, na ye ɛyaafɛlɛ noa hyerɛ ma bɛ boso nua.

english_verse: They may roar and growl like powerful lions. But when God breaks their teeth,
translation_verse: Gyata polɛ ne gyata bɔ ye nye aboro ɔ ye suɛ bo apɛ, yeɛ gyata akrɔngrɔma mɔ koso bɛ gye atutu.

english_verse: they starve, and their children are scattered. A Secret Was Told to Me
translation_verse: Sɛ gyata onnya naen ngye ye nni a, owu, na gyata beleɛ ye mma nemɔ bɛbɔ aya.

english_verse: A secret was told to me in a faint whisper—
translation_verse: “Ebie hane edwirɛ bie hyirele me kudɛɛ, otuli me asure.

english_verse: I was overcome by sleep, but disturbed by dreams;
translation_verse: Kɔngɔen laleɛ bie anu yeɛ ndele ɔ, mmerɛ bɔ adasa bɛda hatee ne.

english_verse: and my hair stood on end, as a wind blew past my face.
translation_verse: Sunzum bie pɛle nu wɔ me nye so, na me nwo yɛle me nyininini.

english_verse: It stopped and stood still. Then a form appeared— a shapeless form. And from the silence, I heard a voice say,
translation_verse: Ogyinane berɛ konn, nakoso mannwu kyɛbɔ ye sue osi te ɔ. Nikyee bie ye sue gyinagyinane me nye so, berɛ yɛle dinn, na ndele komviɛ bie kyɛ,

english_verse: “No humans are innocent in the eyes of God their Creator.
translation_verse: ‘Aso dasaniɛ kɔhora kɔtengyɛ kɔtra Nyameɛ? Aso dasaniɛ kɔhora kɔtengyɛ kɔtra Nyameɛ bɔ ɔbɔle ye ɔ?

english_verse: He finds fault with his servants and even with his angels.
translation_verse: Sɛ Nyameɛ somvoɛ mɔ po, ɔmva ye nwo ndo bɛ so, ná osa nwu ye abɔfo mɔ bɛ nwo mvomsoɛ a,

english_verse: Humans are formed from clay and are fragile as moths, so what chance do you have?
translation_verse: né nzaade, dasaniɛ bɔ bɛfale nnɛterɛ bɛnwone ye, bɔ ofi mvuture nu, bɔ betia ye so bɛbɛtɛ ye kyɛ mvrɔlɔ ne, ye de ogyi ye sɛ?

english_verse: Your tent pegs are pulled up, and you leave this life, having gained no wisdom.”
translation_verse: Ɛtena sua bɔ odwira bɛ nwo ne, ye nyamaa ne abo tutu, na bewu bɔ bennwu nworɛ biala ɔ.’

english_verse: Envy and jealousy will kill a stupid fool.
translation_verse: Susu amba kyɛ, ɛyaafɛlɛ ku ngwaseafoɛ, yeɛ anyeboroborolɛ koso oku bɛ bɔ bagyimi ɔ.

english_verse: I have seen fools take root. But God sends a curse, suddenly uprooting them
translation_verse: Manwu kwaseaa bɔ ye bra ayie ye yé ɔ, nakoso mvum nu, mbayele ye awuro.

english_verse: Our suffering isn't caused by the failure of crops;
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ, musue mvi nnɛterɛ nu yeɛ ɔba ɔ, yeɛ amaneɛ koso mvifi mvi aseɛnwo.

english_verse: it's all part of life, like sparks shooting skyward.
translation_verse: Na mmom, bɛwo sona bɛto amaneɛ nu, kyɛbɔ kobogya tu kɔ anwuro ne ala.

english_verse: Job, if I were you, I would ask God for help.
translation_verse: “Sɛ me ahɔ a, ahaa ngɔpena Nyameɛ si atee, na Nyameɛ yeɛ ngɔfa me dwirɛ ngowura ye sa ɔ.

english_verse: God sends showers on earth and waters the fields.
translation_verse: Ye bɔ ɔma esue tɔ gua aseɛ so, ná oguagua fieso so nzue ne,

english_verse: He protects the sorrowful and lifts up those who have been disgraced. *
translation_verse: ɔma anwobrɛaseɛfoɛ so, na ɔma bɛ bɔ bedi aworabɔlɛ so ɔkɔ anigye nu.

english_verse: Darkness is their only companion, hiding their path at noon.
translation_verse: Awosii to bɛ alehyeleɛ nu, na befuafua eyia ketee kyɛ kɔngɔen ahɔ ne.

english_verse: God rescues the needy from the words of the wicked and the fist of the mighty.
translation_verse: Nakoso Nyameɛ ode sona bɔ ɔyɛ anwumvo ɔ ofi bɛ noa dwirɛ bɔ odi awue ne anu, ɔne tumifoɛ bɛ sa nu.

english_verse: The poor are filled with hope, and injustice is silenced. Consider Yourself Fortunate
translation_verse: Yiti anyelasoɛ wɔ berɛ ma sona bɔ ɔyɛ anwumvo ɔ, na Nyameɛ ka amumuyɛɛfoɛ bɛ noa to nu.

english_verse: He may cause injury and pain, but he will bandage and heal your cuts and bruises.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ Nyameɛ bɔ opura sona nen, ye ala yeɛ ɔbɔ so borɛ ɔ; ye bɔ ɔbɔ fɛɛ ne, ye sa yeɛ ɔsa anwonyerɛ ɔ.

english_verse: God will protect you from harm, no matter how often trouble may strike.
translation_verse: Ɔkɔye wɔ kofi amaneɛ sɔ alaa nzia nu, yoo, na bɔ ɔtɔ so nzoo ne anu, edwirɛ biala ngɔto wɔ.

english_verse: In times of war and famine, God will keep you safe.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛhɔen pe a, okole wɔ kofi ewue nu, yeɛ koɛ nu koso, okole wɔ kofi ngrandɛ noa.

english_verse: You will be sheltered, without fear of hurtful words or any other weapon.
translation_verse: Okole wɔ kofi kuro sona noa bɔ odi awue nu, na sɛ musue ba a, engosuro.

english_verse: You will laugh at the threat of destruction and famine. And you won't be afraid of wild animals—
translation_verse: Ɛkɔsere musue ne ne ɛhɔen, na aseɛ so ngaka aboyaa koso, engosuro bɛ.

english_verse: they will no longer be fierce, and your rocky fields will become friendly.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ ɛne eburo nyɔboɛ mɔ bɛkɔyɛ apam, na eburo ngaka mɔ bɛ ne wɔ kɔtena asomdwee nu.

english_verse: Your home will be secure, and your sheep will be safe.
translation_verse: Ekonwu kyɛ asomdwee wɔ w’awuro, na sɛ ɛneanea w’agyapadeɛ nu a, ekonwu kyɛ nikye fee nne berɛ bɔ wamini ɔ.

english_verse: You will have more descendants than there are blades of grass on the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Ekonwu ye koso kyɛ wɔ boso ama bata pee, na wɔ kunu mmaa kɔyɛ pee kyɛ aseɛ so ndire.

english_verse: You will live a very long life, and your body will be strong until the day you die.
translation_verse: Ekonyi kɔyɛ posoposo koraka né awu, kyɛbɔ bebu aburoo worowaa wɔ ye mmerɛ nu ne.

english_verse: Our experience has proven these things to be true, so listen and learn.
translation_verse: Nea, yafeefee ɛhe anu, na yanwu kyɛ ɔte nahorɛ. Yiti tie, ná fa to wɔ ti anu.”

english_verse: They outweigh the sand along the beach, and that's why I have spoken without thinking first.
translation_verse: Ahaa nu nonɛ kɔtra mboanoa anweaa; ye sɔ ati, ɔmaa ngane edwirɛ fumfum.

english_verse: The fearsome arrows of God All-Powerful have filled my soul with their poison.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ Ɛdangama Nyameɛ ato ye agyaen mɔ wawowɔ me, me sunzum ɔno bɛ noa borɔ ne, na Nyameɛ ɛyaafɛlɛ ne ɔko tia me.

english_verse: Do oxen and wild donkeys cry out in distress unless they are hungry?
translation_verse: Sɛ eburo afunum nya ɛserɛ ná odi a, aso osũ? Yeɛ sɛ nandwie koso nya aleɛ a, aso osũ?

english_verse: What is food without salt? What is more tasteless than the white of an egg?
translation_verse: Aleɛ bɔ ɔte bitaa ne, ngyee nne nu a, aso bedi a odi? Kyiremvua si fufue ne, aso ɔyɛ fɛ?

english_verse: That's how my food tastes, and my appetite is gone. *
translation_verse: Me komvi nne sɔ aleɛ nemɔ aso, bɛte aleɛ bɔ bɛma me noa nu sa ɔ.

english_verse: How I wish that God would answer my prayer
translation_verse: “O, m’abisadeɛ ne, sɛ ahaa me sa ka ye a, m’anyelasoɛ ne, sɛ Nyameɛ maa menya ye a,

english_verse: Then I would be comforted, knowing that in all of my pain I have never disobeyed God.
translation_verse: Ahaa ewue ne kɔyɛ m’aworakyekyerɛ, bɔ m’amaneɛnwunɛ nu po, ahaa me nye kɔgye ɔ, ofikyɛ Krongronniɛ ne, ye noa dwirɛ ne, nndwi mmvale so.

english_verse: I am not strong as stone or bronze,
translation_verse: M’anwoserɛ ne, aso ɔte kyɛ nyɔboɛ anwoserɛ anaa? Me nwonaen ne, aso ɔte kɔɔbere anaa?

english_verse: and I have finally reached the end of my rope. My Friends, I Am Desperate
translation_verse: Nahorɛ nu, mengora ye noa gyina ko, yeɛ mmokalɛ biala mvi neka fee mma.

english_verse: My friends, I am desperate, and you should help me, even if I no longer respect God All-Powerful. *
translation_verse: “Sona bɔ wali amia ne, sɛ obiɛngo annwu ye anwumvoin a, ye de né obiɛngo ne apo kyɛ okosuro Ɛdangama Nyameɛ ɔ.

english_verse: like streams that swell with melting snow,
translation_verse: bɔ asukɔtwea akata ye nye, bɔ asue ne ɔtengyɛ wɔ ye bo ɔ.

english_verse: I am like a caravan, lost in the desert while searching for water.
translation_verse: Dwadifoɛ bɔ bɛtete afupɔngɔ so ne, bɛmakye befi b’atee so, na bɛkɔ ɛserɛ so bekowuwu.

english_verse: just as I am with you. Only one look at my suffering, and you run away scared. What Have I Done Wrong?
translation_verse: Sɔ ala yeɛ kekesaala ye ɛmɔ koso ɛmɔmmoka me ɔ; ɛmɔanwu amaneɛ bɔ wato me ɔ, na wama ɛserɛ aha ɛmɔ.

english_verse: Have I ever asked any of you to give me a gift
translation_verse: Mahã kyɛ mepena akyɛdeɛ mefi ɛmɔ berɛ anaa, anaakyɛ ɛmɔfa ɛmɔ sikaa betua fea-ase-ma bele me anaa,

english_verse: What have I done wrong? Show me, and I will keep quiet.
translation_verse: “Ɛmɔhyirehyire me e, na ngomua me noa, bɔ mayɔ bɔ ɔtte mayee ne, ɛ́mɔma nwu ye.

english_verse: The truth is always painful, but your arguments prove nothing.
translation_verse: Edwirɛ nahorɛ ye hanɛ yɛ se! Nakoso me nyunu bɔ ɛmɔtwi ye, nzikyɛ paa yeɛ okyire ɔ?

english_verse: Here I am desperate, and you consider my words as worthless as wind.
translation_verse: Me dwirɛ deɛ ne, ɛmɔbu ye animtia hɔ ɔ? Ɛmɔdwene kyɛ sona bɔ ɔyɛ anwumvo ne, odwudwo gua mvrama nu anaa?

english_verse: Why, you would sell an orphan or your own neighbor!
translation_verse: Ayisiaaniɛ po, ɛmɔgua ye nwo serewa, yeɛ ɛmɔ adamvo koso, ɛmɔdi ye noa bɛtɔne ye.

english_verse: Look me straight in the eye; I won't lie to you.
translation_verse: “Afei de, mepena kyɛ ɛmɔnea me nyunu, ofikyɛ mengɔpɛ anoanu wɔ ɛmɔ nyunu.

english_verse: Stop accusing me falsely; my reputation is at stake.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔyakyi, nnɛma ɛmɔbua me ndɛengyea, ɛ́mɔyakyi, na medi be.

english_verse: I know right from wrong, and I am not telling lies.
translation_verse: Aso nnakannaka dwirɛ wɔ me noa nu anaa, anaakyɛ mende yealɛ anaa?

english_verse: We are slaves in search of shade; we are laborers longing for our wages.
translation_verse: Ɔte kyɛ kanganiɛ bɔ ɔpena fɔnwoo nu tena ɔ, ɔte kyɛ paaniɛ bɔ ɔnwondɛ ye akatuaa ɔ.

english_verse: God has made my days drag on and my nights miserable.
translation_verse: Yiti bosome pee yeɛ nningyein ayɛ basaa wɔ m’asetena nu ɔ, ɔne aworabɔlɛ kɔngɔen mɔ yeɛ bakyekye basoa me ɔ.

english_verse: My parched skin is covered with worms, dirt, and sores,
translation_verse: Me nwonaen alɔ nnɔboakoma, na wayɛ fiɛ betɔɔ, me wereɛ apakyepakye, na otwi nzue.

english_verse: and my days are running out quicker than the thread of a fast-moving needle. Don't Forget!
translation_verse: Me mmerɛ se kɔ ndɛndɛ tra akurokurowa, na ɔba ayieleɛ bɔ anyelasoɛ biala nne nu ɔ.

english_verse: I beg you, God, don't forget! My life is just a breath, and trouble lies ahead.
translation_verse: “Kaye kyɛ me ngoa te mvrama, me nye ngɔgye ko.

english_verse: I will vanish from sight, and no one, including you, will ever see me again.
translation_verse: Anyeɛ bɔ onwu me ne, ongonwu me ko, wɔ nye kotua me, nakoso né matu mamini.

english_verse: I will disappear in the grave or vanish from sight like a passing cloud.
translation_verse: Na kyɛbɔ munungum se kɔ ná otu mini ne, sɔ ala yeɛ ebiala bɔ ɔkɔ ɛborɔ dɔ ne, onza mma ko ɔ.

english_verse: Never will I return home; soon I will be forgotten.
translation_verse: Onza mma ye awuro berɛ ko, na nekaa bɔ ɔte ne, berɛ ama ngonwu ye ko.

english_verse: And so, I cry out to you in agony and distress.
translation_verse: “Yiti mengomua me noa, ngɔhã yealɛ bɔ me sunzum onwu ye ɔ, na ngɔbɔ aworabɔlɛ bɔ me kra di ɔ nwo somoɛ.

english_verse: Am I the sea or a sea monster? Is that why you imprison me?
translation_verse: Aso nde ɛpo anaa ɛpo nu sasrabɔnzam, bɔ ɛma awɛmvoɛ bɛ nye li me si ɔ?

english_verse: but you torture me with terrible dreams. *
translation_verse: né afa laleɛ anwunanwuna me, né afa nyekyire aha me serɛ.

english_verse: I'd rather choke to death than live in this body.
translation_verse: Ah! me kra kuro kyɛ bekomia me kɔme maa ngowu mmom tra kyɛ ngɔfɔ maa ɔkɔha me mmowue ɔ.

english_verse: Leave me alone and let me die; my life has no meaning.
translation_verse: Afei de, ewiase afono me. Mengɔtena ngoa nu daa. Yakyi me, ofikyɛ me ngoa te mbaen.

english_verse: Why do you test us from sunrise to sunset?
translation_verse: bɔ ɛkɔpasa ye nwo ngyerɛmɔ biala ɔ, bɔ mmerɛ biala eso ye nea enwu kyɛbɔ osi te ɔ?

english_verse: Why do you watch us so closely? What's it to you, if I sin? Why am I your target and such a heavy burden?
translation_verse: Wɔ bɔ esisa adasa ɔ, sɛ mayɔ bɔne po a, ahaa ɔfa wɔ nwo nzu? Nzu ati yeɛ atu wɔ nye asie me so ɔ? Nzu ati yeɛ amaa mayɛ wɔ so tɔsom ɔ?

english_verse: Bildad from Shuah said:
translation_verse: Yeɛ Suhiniɛ Bildade buale kyɛ,

english_verse: How long will you talk and keep saying nothing?
translation_verse: “Kyinzu koraa yeɛ ɛkɔkeka sɔ dwirɛ hemɔ maa okoodwu ɔ, bɔ ekodwudwo kogua mvrama nu mbaen ɔ?

english_verse: Does God All-Powerful stand in the way of justice?
translation_verse: Aso Nyameɛ obua ndɛengyea, anaa Tuminiɛ ne, aso obua ndɛen mundumundu so?

english_verse: He made your children pay for their sins.
translation_verse: Sɛ wɔ mma nemɔ bɛyɔle ye bɔne a, wamaa banya bɛ mmeraatolɛ nwo akatuaa.

english_verse: So why don't you turn to him
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛkɔpena Nyameɛ si atee, ná ɛkɔsrɛ Tuminiɛ ne maa okonwu wɔ anwumvoin a,

english_verse: and start living right? Then he will decide to rescue and restore you to your place of honor.
translation_verse: sɛ wɔ nwo te ná ɛtengyɛ a, susu amba kyɛ, ɔkɔkanyane ye nwo ɔkɔboka wɔ, na ɔkɔma wɔ sa kɔha bɔ ahwere biala.

english_verse: Your future will be brighter by far than your past. Our Ancestors Were Wise
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ ɛhyɛle ye bo kaaba bie de, nakoso w’ayieleɛ nu kɔyɛ piri paa.

english_verse: Our own time has been short, like a fading shadow, and we know very little.
translation_verse: Yɛ de, anomasi wa ala yeɛ bɛwo yɛ ɔ, na yɛnze huu, ofikyɛ aseɛ ye aso, yɛ ngoa otu mini te kyɛ wawoɛ.

english_verse: and if the water dries up, they die sooner than grass.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ ɔte frɔmfrɔm bɔ bennya bɛppɛle ne, bɛkese ndɛndɛ bɛtra ndire biala.

english_verse: and trust in something as frail as a spider's web—
translation_verse: Bɔ wafa ye nwo wato so ne, ɔsɛkye, yeɛ ye anyelasoɛ koso ɔyɛ mmerɛ kyɛ ananze ndendaen.

english_verse: Sinful people are like plants with spreading roots and plenty of sun and water.
translation_verse: Sɔ sona ne te kyɛ bakaa bɔ onyi frɔmfrɔm wɔ eyia nu ɔ, na ye mmaen nemɔ nu trɛtrɛ wɔ eboo ne anu.

english_verse: They wrap their roots tightly around rocks.
translation_verse: Ye ndii mendamenda nyɔboɛ nyɔboɛ, na nyɔboɛ nyɔboɛ nemɔ afia yeɛ owura ɔ.

english_verse: their life slips away, and other plants grow there.
translation_verse: Yoo, ye anigye atee bɔ ɔnate so ɛne, na mmakaa foforɛ koso fifi wɔ ye boso berɛ.

english_verse: We know God doesn't reject an innocent person or help a sinner.
translation_verse: “Daabi, sona bɔ ɔtengyɛ ne, Nyameɛ mbo ye, yeɛ ɔmmoka bɔnefoɛ.

english_verse: And so, he will make you happy and give you something to smile about.
translation_verse: Ɔkɔmaa ɛkɔseresere bieku, ná wama wɔ noa ali ahurusi.

english_verse: But your evil enemies will be put to shame and disappear forever.
translation_verse: Animguaseɛ kɔmata wɔ pɔfoɛ mɔ, na amumuyɛɛfoɛ awuro kɔbɔ tɔɔ.”

english_verse: What you say is true. No human is innocent in the sight of God.
translation_verse: “Nahorɛ nu, mese kyɛ ɔte sɔ, nakoso ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ né dasaniɛ watengyɛ wɔ Nyameɛ nyunu?

english_verse: Not once in a thousand times could we win our case if we took him to court.
translation_verse: Sɛ ebie kuro kyɛ ɔne ye bɛbɔ kuro a, edwirɛ apee ko bɔ Nyameɛ kobisa ne, ɔngɔhora nu ko po noa ye.

english_verse: God is wise and powerful— who could possibly oppose him and win?
translation_verse: Ye nworɛ ne ye tumi te totohyia, nwa yeɛ wadwɔso watia ye bɔ wafa ye nwo wali tɔtorɔtɔɔ ɔ?

english_verse: When God becomes angry, he can move mountains before they even know it.
translation_verse: Ye bɔ otutu mmokaa bo gua bɔ ɔmmɔ bɛ kɔkɔ ɔ, ye bɔ ɔfɛ yaa dwiri bɛ gua ɔ,

english_verse: God can shake the earth loose from its foundations
translation_verse: ye bɔ ɔwoso aseɛ fi ye boso, ná ɔma aseɛ nyinasoɛ mɔ bɛwoso ɔ.

english_verse: or command the sun and stars to hold back their light.
translation_verse: Ye bɔ ɔhyɛ eyia kyɛ nnɛmaa opukye a ombukye ɔ, ye bɔ omundu nzramaa mɔ nyunu mma bɛ nda ɔ.

english_verse: God alone stretched out the sky, stepped on the sea,
translation_verse: Ye bɔ ye ngome yeɛ ɔtrɛtrɛle ewienu nu ɔ, ye bɔ otiatia ɛpo asorɔkye so ɔ.

english_verse: and set the stars in place— the Big Dipper and Orion, the Pleiades and the stars in the southern sky.
translation_verse: Ye bɔ ɔyɔle nzramaa kure bɔ ɔwɔ ewienu sorɔ, ɔne ewienu afia, Akɔtaen-ne-ye-mma, yeɛ nzramaa kure bɔ ɔwɔ ewienu ngwaen.

english_verse: Of all the miracles God works, we cannot understand a one.
translation_verse: Ye bɔ ɔyɔ nningyein mbiri mbiri bɔ ɔbo sona ndeaseɛ so ɔ, anwanwadeɛ bɔ ɛka a ennwu ye noa ɔ.

english_verse: God walks right past me, without making a sound.
translation_verse: Eh, ɔpɛ nu me nwo wa, nakoso mennwu ye; ɔsẽ kɔ, nakoso me nye mbɛ ye so.

english_verse: And if he grabs something, who can stop him or raise a question?
translation_verse: Sɛ ofoti nikyee kɔ a, nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora kosi ye atee ɔ? Nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora kobisa ye kyɛ, ‘Nzikyɛ yeɛ ɛ́yɔ e?’

english_verse: When God showed his anger, the servants of the sea monster fell at his feet.
translation_verse: “Nyameɛ ngɔhwe ye yaafɛlɛ ne ngosa, na bɛ bɔ bɛboka Rahabo ne, Nyameɛ abrɛ bɛ ase maa bawura ye bɔbɔ ye bo.

english_verse: How, then, could I possibly argue my case with God? Though I Am Innocent
translation_verse: Yiti, me ole nwa bɔ mekora meye me noa mekyire ye ɔ, anaa, ngɔyɛ sɛɛ né mahora masa me nwo mahyire ye?

english_verse: Even though I am innocent, I can only beg for mercy.
