translation_verse: Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ bɔnefoɛ ɔyɔ bɔne yɔleɛ sɔ alaa ɛyaa, ná onya ngoa tendenn de; nakoso nahorɛ nu, me de mese kyɛ bɛ bɔ besuro Nyameɛ ná bebu ye ne yeɛ okoyie bɛ yé ɔ.

english_verse: but no one who sins and rejects God will prosper or live very long.
translation_verse: Bɔnefoɛ de, ongoyie ye yé, yeɛ ye ngoa bɔ ɔte kyɛ wawoɛ ne, ɔngɔyɛ tendenn, ɔnate kyɛ onzuro Nyameɛ.

english_verse: There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens.
translation_verse: Nikyee mbaen bie ɔkɔ so wɔ aseɛ so. Edwirɛ bɔ ɔfata bɔnefoɛ ne yeɛ bɛfa bedi teneneefoɛ ɔ; yeɛ bɔ ɔfata teneneefoɛ ne yeɛ bɛfa bedi bɔnefoɛ ɔ. Na ngane kyɛ, ɛhe koso te mbaen.

english_verse: So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
translation_verse: Yiti me de, menwu ye kyɛ anigye te paa, ofikyɛ nikye paa biala nne berɛ mma sona wɔ wiase ndra kyɛ okodidi, ɔkɔno, ná ɔkɔgye ye nye ɔ. Ye ngoa bɔ Nyameɛ afa ama ye wɔ wiase ne, ɛfɛɛ bɔ ɔfɛ wɔ nu ne, bɔ odi kyɛ ɔfa bata ye nwo hɔ ɛne.

english_verse: Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world.
translation_verse: Yiti mva nziele me nye so kyɛ ngɔpena nworɛ si atee, ɔne kyɛ ngonwu ɛfɛɛ adwuma bɔ ɔkɔ so wɔ aseɛ so ɔ, kyɛbɔ sona onnya nnaa nna eyia ne kɔngɔen ne;

english_verse: I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
translation_verse: na nwuni Nyameɛ adwuma bɔ ɔyɔ amukoraa, kyɛ sona biala ngɔte bɔ ɔkɔ so wɔ wiase ɔ bo. Sona kɔfɛ ye nwo kyɛ ɔkɔfeefee nu, nakoso ɔngɔte ye bo. Nworɛfoɛ nwa nzɛ bɛse, nakoso bɛngɔhora bengonwu ye.

english_verse: I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad.
translation_verse: Ɛhe amukoraa, madwene ye nwo, mapɛnzɛpɛnzɛ ye mukoraa nu manea, na manwu ye kyɛ, teneneefoɛ ne nworɛfoɛ, yeɛ afei bɔ bɛyɔ ne, owura Nyameɛ sa nu: kyɛ ɔdɔ oo, kyɛ ɛpɔen oo, sona biala nze bɔ ɔkɔto ye ɔ;

english_verse: But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
translation_verse: ofikyɛ ayieleɛ komapɛ ne ala yeɛ ɔla berɛ ma bɛ mukoraa ɔ: teneneeniɛ ne bɔnefoɛ, sona paa ne sona bɔ ɔtte mayee ɔ, sona bɔ ye nwo te ne bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ, bɔ ɔbɔ afɔleɛ ne bɔ ɔmmɔ afɔleɛ ɔ. Sona paa ne amumuyɛɛniɛ b’ayieleɛ te ko, yeɛ bɔ ɔta ndaen ne bɔ osuro ndaentalɛ koso b’ayieleɛ te ko.

english_verse: As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion.
translation_verse: Nakoso sona biala bɔ ɔboka ateasefoɛ so ne, anyelasoɛ wɔ berɛ ma ye, ofikyɛ kyea bɔ ɔte ngoa nu ne, ɔte paa tra gyata bɔ wawu ɔ.

english_verse: We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ ateasefoɛ bɛse kyɛ bekowu, nakoso awufoɛ de, bɛnze huu; belle akatuaa biala ko, na bɛ nwo ngayeɛ atu amini.

english_verse: Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
translation_verse: Ɔdɔ bɔ benyane ye oo, ɛpɔen bɔ bɛpɔle oo, b’anyeboro oo, watu wamini dadadada, na nikyee biala bɔ ɔkɔ so wɔ wiase ne, belle kyɛfa biala wɔ nu ko.

english_verse: So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do.
translation_verse: Yiti kɔ so, di w’aleɛ wɔ anigye nu, ná fa anwosɛpɛ no wɔ nzaa, ofikyɛ bɔ ɛyɔ ne, Nyameɛ ale ato nu dadadada.

english_verse: Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ biala, wura anigye ataadeɛ, yeɛ nnɛma sakyeɛfona pa wɔ ti so.

english_verse: Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth.
translation_verse: Wɔ ngoa amukoraa bɔ ɔte mbaen bɔ Nyameɛ afa ama wɔ wɔ wiase ne, ɛne ɛye bɔ ekuro yeɛ ɔ ɛmɔtena anigye so, ofikyɛ ɛfɛɛ bɔ ɛfɛ wiase ne, wɔ bue nu deɛ bɔ anya ye hɔ ɛne.

english_verse: Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
translation_verse: Adwuma biala bɔ wɔ sa kɔsɔ nu kyɛ ɛyɔ ne, fa w’anwoserɛ yɔ, ofikyɛ ɛborɔ dɔ bɔ ɛbaahɔ ne, adwuma anaa adwene anaa nimdeɛ anaa nworɛ nne dɔ.

english_verse: Here is something else I have learned: The fastest runners and the greatest heroes don't always win races and battles. Wisdom, intelligence, and skill don't always make you healthy, rich, or popular. We each have our own share of misfortune.
translation_verse: Nza nwuni kyɛ ewiase wa, nna bɛ bɔ bɛ nwo yɛ nyera ɔ yeɛ bedi amirikatulɛ nu ngonim ɔ; nna anwoserɛfoɛ yeɛ bedi koɛ nu ngonim ɔ; nna nworɛfoɛ yeɛ benya bɛ noa aleɛ ɔ, nna badwemma mɔ yeɛ benya bɛ nwo ɔ; yeɛ nna nimdeɛfoɛ yeɛ benya animnyam ɔ; nakoso mmerɛ ne mmerɛ tɛɛ la berɛ ma bɛ mukoraa.

english_verse: None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap. Better To Be Wise than Foolish
translation_verse: Sona biala nze ye mmerɛ deɛ. Na kyɛbɔ bɛfa asawu atianuserɛserɛ bɛkye egyein, ná besua ngaen bɛkye nnomaa ne, sɔ ala yeɛ mmerɛ tɛɛ te ngaen bɔ ɔkye adasa mvum nu ɔ.

english_verse: Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me.
translation_verse: Masa manwu sɔ nworɛ he koso wɔ wiase, na ɔte nikyee bɔ ɔte piri wɔ me nye so ɔ.

english_verse: It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls.
translation_verse: Né kuro kaaba bie wɔ berɛ bɔ mmenia kaaba bie wɔ so ɔ. Yeɛ ɛhene tuminiɛ bie hɔle ootuale kuro ne, na ɔkyekyele nyinasoɛ bɔ okogyina so kɔfo fasue ne ɔkɔhɔ kuro ne anu ɔ.

english_verse: But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten.
translation_verse: Né biaa ehianiɛ nworɛniɛ bie wɔ kuro ne anu, na ɔfale ye nworɛ pepɛ lele kuro ne. Nakoso ebiala ngaye sɔ ehianiɛ ne.

english_verse: So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
translation_verse: Na ye sɔ ne ati, ngane kyɛ, “Nworɛ nwo hia tra anwoserɛ, nakoso bemmu ehianiɛ nworɛ, yeɛ ɔkã dwirɛ a bɛmva.”

english_verse: Words of wisdom spoken softly make much more sense than the shouts of a ruler to a crowd of fools.
translation_verse: Nworɛfoɛ bɛ noa dwirɛ bɔ mmenia tie ye konn ne, bede bɛto nu bɛtra ngwaseafoɛ hene ye ndeateamuɛ.

english_verse: Wisdom is more powerful than weapons, yet one mistake can destroy all the good you have done.
translation_verse: Nworɛ nwo hia tra akodeɛ, nakoso bɔnefoɛ komapɛ sɛkye paa pee.

english_verse: A few dead flies in perfume make all of it stink, and a little foolishness outweighs a lot of wisdom.
translation_verse: Kyɛbɔ nwɔsea fuin ma sona bɔ ɔyɔ sakyeɛfona ye sakyeɛ ne bo mvamva ne, sɔ ala yeɛ ngwaseasɛm kãa bie sɛkye nworɛ ne animnyam ɔ.

english_verse: Sensible thoughts lead you to do right; foolish thoughts lead you to do wrong.
translation_verse: Nworɛniɛ adwene maa ɔyɔ bɔ ɔte paa ɔ, nakoso kwaseaa adwene de, ɔmaa ɔyɔ bɔ ɔtte mayee ɔ.

english_verse: Fools show their stupidity by the way they live; it's easy to see they have no sense.
translation_verse: Sɛ kwaseaa nate atee so po a, nworɛ bɔ ye, na ye yɔleɛ ma ebiala nwu ye kyɛ ɔte kwaseaa.

english_verse: Don't give up your job when your boss gets angry. If you stay calm, you'll be forgiven.
translation_verse: Sɛ wɔ hene fɛ wɔ so yaa a, nnɛfi ye nyunu berɛ, ofikyɛ sɛ ɛbrɛ wɔ nwo ase a, ɔmaa bɛfa wɔ bɔne mbiri mbiri bɛkyɛ wɔ.

english_verse: They honor fools, but dishonor the rich;
translation_verse: bama ngwaseasɛm dibea maa wanya animnyam piri, na sikafoɛ dibea de, wahɔ ase.

english_verse: they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
translation_verse: Manwu nganga bɔ bɛtete mbɔngɔ so ɔ, wɔ aberɛ bɔ nnehyeɛ bɛnate ase kyɛ nganga ɔ.

english_verse: If you dig a pit, you might fall in; if you break down a wall, a snake might bite you.
translation_verse: Sona biala bɔ ofu kumaa ne, ye bɔbɔ ɔkɔtɔ nu, yeɛ bɔ okodwiri ɛwaen kogua ne, ewoo kɔha ye.

english_verse: You could even get hurt by chiseling a stone or chopping a log.
translation_verse: Ebiala bɔ odwa nyɔboɛ ne, nyɔboɛ pura ye; yeɛ bɔ ɔpakye mmakaa ne wora, nu yeɛ opura ɔ.

english_verse: If you don't sharpen your ax, it will be harder to use; if you are wise, you'll know what to do.
translation_verse: Sɛ ebie dadeɛ tiri ná wanzi a, ye de sana ɔfa anwoserɛ pee ɔyɔ adwuma, yiti nworɛ yeɛ ɔma sona adwuma yɛ yé ɔ.

english_verse: The power to charm a snake does you no good if it bites you anyway.
translation_verse: Sona bɔ ole ewoo ayire ne, sɛ ɔma ewoo ka ebie yie koraka né wahye ye a, ye de mvasoɛ biala nne bɔ ole ewoo ayire ne aso.

english_verse: If you talk sensibly, you will have friends; if you talk foolishly, you will destroy yourself.
translation_verse: Nworɛniɛ noa dwirɛ maa onya animnyam, nakoso kwaseaa de, ye noa dwirɛ maa onya dwirɛ.

english_verse: Fools begin with nonsense, and their stupid chatter ends with disaster.
translation_verse: Ngwaseasɛm yeɛ ɔfa hyɛ ye dwirɛ bo ɔ, na ye dwirɛ n’ayieleɛ te gyimikekã.

english_verse: They never tire of talking, but none of us really know what the future will bring.
translation_verse: Kwaseaa dwudwo pee bɔ ye noa mbe ɔ, nakoso sona nze bɔ ɔbaasi ɔ, bɔ kyẽa bie okosi wɔ ye si ne, nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora kɔla ye ali kohyire ye ɔ?

english_verse: Fools wear themselves out— they don't know enough to find their way home.
translation_verse: Adwuma bɔ kwaseaa yɔ ne, ɔmaa ɔfɛ, na ɔnze atee po bɔ ɔfa so kɔ kuro nu ɔ.

english_verse: A country is in for trouble when its ruler is childish, and its leaders party all day long.
translation_verse: Maen bɔ wɔ hene adwene te ngwadaa adwene ɔ, bɔ wɔ nnehyeɛ bɛto poen ngyerɛmɔ ɔ, wɔ yaakɔ o!

english_verse: But a nation will prosper when its ruler is mature, and its leaders don't party too much.
translation_verse: Ɔte saleɛ ma wɔ, maen bɔ wɔ hene te dehyeɛ baa ɔ, bɔ wɔ nnehyeɛ bɛto poen wɔ mmerɛ bɔ ɔsɛ ɔ nu ɔ, kyɛ bɛfa bɛpena anwoserɛ, ná mmom bɛnno bɛmmo ɔ!

english_verse: Some people are too lazy to fix a leaky roof— then the house collapses.
translation_verse: Ɔnate ɛfoen ti sua kwatena bu gua nu, yeɛ anyeɛhalɛ ma sua nwi.

english_verse: Eating and drinking make you feel happy, and money can buy everything you need.
translation_verse: Ɛpoentolɛ ma sona sere, nzaa ma sona nye gye, na sikaa yeɛ ɔyɔ nikyee biala ɔ.

english_verse: Don't let yourself think about cursing the king; don't curse the rich, not even in secret. A little bird might hear and tell everything.
translation_verse: Ɛhene ne, wɔ ti anu po, nnɛnoma ye, yeɛ nnɛfea wɔ pumbu nu noma sikafoɛ, ofikyɛ ewienu anomaa bie kɔfa wɔ noa dwirɛ ne kɔhɔ, anaa kaka bie bɔ ole ndaa ɔ kɔɔbɔ amaneɛ.

english_verse: Be generous, and someday you will be rewarded.
translation_verse: Gyi wɔ paanoo gua nzue nye, na kyẽa bie wɔ sa kɔhã ye.

english_verse: Share what you have with seven or eight others, because you never know when disaster may strike.
translation_verse: Kyekyɛ nu ma nzoo anaa mmɔtwɛ po, ofikyɛ ɛnze edwirɛ tɛɛ bɔ ebiaa ɔbaasi aseɛ ye aso ɔ.

english_verse: If you worry about the weather and don't plant seeds, you won't harvest a crop.
translation_verse: Sona bɔ ɔnea kyɛbɔ mvrama si bɔ ne, ongolua ye nningyein; yeɛ bɔ ɔnea kyɛbɔ ewienu ayɛ kusuu ne koso, ɔngɔfa ye fieso aleɛ.

english_verse: No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
translation_verse: Kyɛbɔ ɛnze mvrama atee, anaa kyɛbɔ mmowue si nyi wɔ pemvoɛ kunu ne, sɔ ala yeɛ Nyameɛ bɔ ɔyɔ nikyee biala ne, ɛnze atee bɔ ɔpe so yɔ ye adwuma ɔ.

english_verse: Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce. Youth and Old Age
translation_verse: Dua wɔ fieso nningyein ngyerɛmɔ, yeɛ nnɛte wɔ sa fi ye lualɛ nwo nɔsoa, ofikyɛ ɛnze bɛ nu horɛ bɔ ɔkɔyɛ paa ɔ; kyɛ ɛhe anaa ɛhene, anaakyɛ bɛ munyɔ bɛkɔyɛ paa ɔ. Ngwadaa nu ne mmerandeɛ nu

english_verse: Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun.
translation_verse: Hyireinn yɛ ahomeka, na anyeɛ nye gye kyɛ onwu eyia ɔ.

english_verse: Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
translation_verse: Yiti sɛ sona di afoɛ pee a, odi kyɛ ɔma ye nye gye wɔ ye mukoraa nu. Nakoso odi kyɛ osa kaye kyɛ, awosii ngyẽa bɔ bɛbaawa ne, ɔsone pee. Bɔ ɔkɔwa ne amukoraa te mbaen.

english_verse: Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
translation_verse: Aberandeɛ, ma wɔ nye gye wɔ wɔ mmerandeɛ nu, nya anigye wɔ wɔ nu wɔ wɔ mmerandeɛ nu. Yɔ bɔ wɔ nye gye ye nwo ɔ ɔne bɔ ɔte wɔ nye so akɔnnɔ ɔ, nakoso nwu ye kyɛ, Nyameɛ kobua wɔ ndɛen wɔ bɔ ɛkɔyɔ amukoraa nwo.

english_verse: Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
translation_verse: Ye aworabɔlɛ fi w’ahone nu, ná ye anwoɔnaen nu ateetee fi wɔ so, ofikyɛ ngwadaa nu ne mmerandeɛ nu po te mbaen.

english_verse: Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
translation_verse: Kaye Nyameɛ bɔ ɔbɔle wɔ ne wɔ wɔ mmerandeɛ nu koraka né mmerɛ tɛɛ ne awa; anyɔ sɔ ná afoɛ nemɔ pingye a, ɛkɔhã kyɛ, “Mennya bɛ nu anigye biala”;

english_verse: Someday the light of the sun and the moon and the stars will all seem dim to you. Rain clouds will remain over your head.
translation_verse: koraka né eyia, hyireinn, ɛsraen ne nzramaa bakakyi awosii, ɔne kyɛ esue tɔ a osa muna ɔ;

english_verse: The noisy grinding of grain and the voices of singers will be shut out by your deaf ears, but even the song of a bird will keep you awake.
translation_verse: kyẽa bɔ bɛkɔtoto mmorɔnoɛ mɔ so anoa nemɔ anu, bɔ bɛngɔte aburoo silɛ nga ɔ, bɔ anomaa suɛ maa ekotingye kofi nnaa nu ɔ, bɔ edweintolɛfoɛ amukoraa bɛ bo kɔpɛ ɔ;

english_verse: You will be afraid to climb up a hill or walk down a road. Your hair will turn as white as almond blossoms. You will feel lifeless and drag along like an old grasshopper. We each go to our eternal home, and the streets here are filled with those who mourn.
translation_verse: kyẽa bɔ sona kosuro nningyein bɔ so kɔ anwuro ɔ, bɔ atee so kɔyɛ suro ɔ, bɔ atonwaa kɔbɔ nyerɛen ɔ, bɔ torɔka kɔhwe ye nwo ase ɔ, bɔ akɔnnɔ bo kɔpɛ ɔ; ofikyɛ sona kɔ ye awuro afebɔɔ ne anu, bɔ ɛsɛenvoɛ bekyinikyini mmorɔnoɛ so ɔ;

english_verse: The silver cord snaps, the golden bowl breaks; the water pitcher is smashed, and the pulley at the well is shattered.
translation_verse: koraka né ɛdwetɛ nyamaa ne ate, koraka né sikaa kɔkorɛ talie ne abɔ, koraka né bua ne abɔ wɔ asue noa, koraka né nyamaa bɔ bɛfa bɛto nzue ne ate;

english_verse: So our bodies return to the earth, and the life-giving breath returns to God.
translation_verse: koraka né nnɛterɛ asa ahɔ nnɛterɛ nu kyɛbɔ né ɔte daa ne ala, koraka né nwomeɛ wasa wahɔ Nyameɛ bɔ ɔfa mane ne berɛ.

english_verse: Nothing makes sense. I have seen it all— nothing makes sense. Respect and Obey God
translation_verse: “Mbaen nu mbaen.” Nworɛ Dwirɛhanɛniɛ ne nwa nyoo, “Ye mukoraa te mbaen!” Edwirɛ n’ayieleɛ

english_verse: I was a wise teacher with much understanding, and I collected a number of proverbs that I had carefully studied.
translation_verse: Nworɛ Dwirɛhanɛniɛ ne, nna nworɛ angome yeɛ ɔse ɔ, na mmom ohyirehyirele mmenia nimdeɛ bokale so. Otiele anyandera pee, ɔpɛnzɛpɛnzɛle nu, na obuli anyandera pee.

english_verse: Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
translation_verse: Nworɛ Dwirɛhanɛniɛ ne, ɔbɔle mmɔden kyɛ ɔkɔpena edwirɛ mɔ bɔ bɛtɔ asoɛ nu ɔ, na edwirɛ bɔ wahyerɛ wato berɛ ne, ɔte nahorɛ ne turoloo.

english_verse: Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together.
translation_verse: Nworɛniɛ ye noa dwirɛ ɔte kyɛ nandwiehanɛniɛ ye pɔmaa noa buralɛ; yeɛ ye anyandera bɔ waboaboa ye noa ne koso, ɔte kyɛ mberɛgoo bɔ mmoaenneafoɛ komapɛ wafa wabɔ berɛ pindinn ɔ.

english_verse: My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these. There is no end to books, and too much study will wear you out.
translation_verse: Mma, bɔ waha wɔ ɛhemɔ asi ne, mebɔ wɔ kɔkɔ kyɛ, nwomaa pembepembe hyerɛlɛ olle ayieleɛ, yeɛ nikyeesualɛ pee koso fa ɛfɛɛ wura sona nwonaen nu.

english_verse: Everything you were taught can be put into a few words: Respect and obey God! This is what life is all about.
translation_verse: Edwirɛ amukoraa bɔ yate ne, sɔa yeɛ yɛbɔ ye porɛ ɔ: Suro Nyameɛ ná di ye mmeraa dwirɛ so, ofikyɛ bɔ odi kyɛ kuro sona biala ɔyɔ hɔ ɛne.

english_verse: God will judge everything we do, even what is done in secret, whether good or bad.
translation_verse: Ɔnate kyɛ, Nyameɛ kobua yɔleɛ biala nwo ndɛen, bɔ yayɔ ye mvealeɛ nu boka so, kyɛ paa oo, kyɛ tɛɛ oo, okobua ye nwo ndɛen.

english_verse: This is Solomon's most beautiful song. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Edwein nu dwein bɔ ɔte Solomon deɛ ne. Braa ne dwein deɛ

english_verse: Kiss me tenderly! Your love is better than wine,
translation_verse: Maa ɔfa ye noa ɔfe me noa! Ofikyɛ wɔ hurolɛ ne, ɔyɛ fɛ tra bobe nzaa.

english_verse: and you smell so sweet. All the young women adore you; the very mention of your name is like spreading perfume. *
translation_verse: Wɔ sakyeɛ ne bo fona paa, yeɛ wɔ dumaa te kyɛ sakyeɛfona bɔ béhwie ɔ; ye sɔ ati yeɛ ndaluwa kuro wɔ ye.

english_verse: Hurry, my king! Let's hurry. Take me to your home. The Young Women Speak: We are happy for you! And we praise your love even more than wine. She Speaks: Young women of Jerusalem, it is only right that you should adore him.
translation_verse: Twetwe me bra wɔ nwo, ma yɛ nwo ɔyɛ nyera. Ao, ɛhene ne afa me awa ye pumbu nu. Yɛ nye kɔhã, ná yali wɔ nwo ahurusi, wɔ hurolɛ ne, yɛkɔkamvo ye yɛkɔtra bobe nzaa. Ɔnyɛ nwanwa kyɛ bekuro wɔ ɔ.

english_verse: My skin is dark and beautiful, like a tent in the desert or like Solomon's curtains.
translation_verse: O Yerusalem ndaluwa, nde bire, na me nwo yɛ nyemene kyɛ Kedare ɛtena sua mɔ, kyɛ Solomon mbɛmuɛ tena.

english_verse: Don't stare at me just because the sun has darkened my skin. My brothers were angry with me; they made me work in the vineyard, and so I neglected my complexion.
translation_verse: Nnɛma ɛmɔnea me haa, kyɛ nde bire ne ati, ofikyɛ eyia yeɛ wapini me sɔ ɔ. Me ni mma mmienzua mɔ fɛle me so yaa, bɛmaa nneane bobe boo nemɔ aso, nakoso me bɔbɔ me bobe boo deɛ de, mayakyi mato berɛ.

english_verse: My darling, I love you! Where do you feed your sheep and let them rest at noon? Don't let the other shepherds think badly of me. I'm not one of those women who shamelessly follow after shepherds. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Ao, wɔ bɔ me kra kuro wɔ ɔ, kã kyire me, nisua yeɛ ɛfa wɔ mmoaen kɔ adidie ɔ, nisua yeɛ eyia bɔ a ɛmaa bede bɛ nwome ɔ? Ofikyɛ, nzu ati yeɛ odi kyɛ meyɛ kyɛ ebie bɔ okyinikyini wɔ wɔ mmango mɔ bɛ mmoaen so ɔ? Biaa ne dwein deɛ

english_verse: My dearest, if you don't know, just follow the path of the sheep. Then feed your young goats near the shepherds' tents.
translation_verse: O, wɔ bɔ ɛtra mmrasua mukoraa b’anwonyemene ɔ, sɛ ɛnze berɛ a, fa mmoaen nemɔ bɛ gya bo so, ná ma wɔ mbɔngye nemɔ bedidi wɔ mmoaenneafoɛ mɔ bɛ tena sua nemɔ anwo.

english_verse: You move as gracefully as the pony that leads the chariot of the king.
translation_verse: O wɔ bɔ mekuro wɔ ɔ, mefa wɔ metoto Faro teaseɛnam mbɔngɔ nemɔ anwo.

english_verse: Earrings add to your beauty, and you wear a necklace of precious stones.
translation_verse: Mbembenanneɛ fata wɔ so taa nu, yeɛ sikaa kɔkorɛ akomuade fata wɔ kɔme.

english_verse: Let's make you some jewelry of gold, woven with silver. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Yɛkɔyɔ sikaa kɔkorɛ asomade bɔ ɛdwetɛ tuatua nu ɔ yɛkɔma wɔ. Braa ne dwein deɛ

english_verse: My king, while you were on your couch, my aroma was a magic charm.
translation_verse: Me hene ne, mmerɛ bɔ ɔwɔ ye didipono nwo ne, me nwo sakyeɛfona lele berɛ.

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— your eyes are those of a dove. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Ah, me kurofoɛ, wɔ nwo yɛ nyemene, ah, wɔ nwo yɛ nyemene! Wɔ nye mmaa dabadabaa kyɛ abubure nye!

english_verse: My love, you are handsome, truly handsome— the fresh green grass will be our wedding bed
translation_verse: Ah, me kurofoɛ, wɔ nwo yɛ nyemene, nahorɛ nu, anwonyemene ɛhe! Yɛ bɛen ne, ye anwosue te nyaa monɛ,

english_verse: in the shade of cedar and cypress trees.
translation_verse: yɛ sua mbuna te sida, na yɛ nzenyene bɔ ɔbɔ so ne te ɛtena bakaa.

english_verse: I am merely a rose from the land of Sharon, a lily from the valley. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Nde Saron nyerɛen, bɔnza nu sukooko. Biaa ne dwein deɛ

english_verse: My darling, when compared with other young women, you are a lily among thorns. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Kyɛbɔ sukooko te wɔ ɛfone mɔ nu ne, sɔ yeɛ me kurofoɛ ne ɔte wɔ ndaluwa mɔ nu ɔ. Braa ne dwein deɛ

english_verse: And you, my love, are an apple tree among trees of the forest. Your shade brought me pleasure; your fruit was sweet.
translation_verse: Kyɛbɔ aprɛ te wɔ eburo mmakaa mɔ nu ne, sɔ ala yeɛ me kurofoɛ ne ɔte wɔ mmerandeɛ mɔ nu ɔ. Ndenane ye bo fɔnwoo ne anu wɔ anika nu, na ye mma ne, wabie wagua me gye abo.

english_verse: You led me to your banquet room and showered me with love.
translation_verse: Wafa me wawa ɛpoentolɛ sua ne anu, na ye frangaa bɔ ogyi me so ne ɔte ehurolɛ.

english_verse: Refresh and strengthen me with raisins and apples. I am hungry for love!
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔma me bobe mmaa taterɛ ma nya anwoserɛ, ɛ́mɔma me aprɛ maa me nwo sande me, ofikyɛ ehurolɛ abɔ me anwonyerɛ.

english_verse: Put your left hand under my head and embrace me with your right arm.
translation_verse: Me ti la ye sa bɛen so,, wafa ye sa famaa wato wabra me.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles never to awaken love before it is ready. Winter Is Past She Speaks:
translation_verse: O Yerusalem ndaluwa, mesrɛ ɛmɔ kitii, mefa ɛwanzane mɔ ne dabɔɔ meta ndaen kyɛ, nnɛma ɛmɔtingye ehurolɛ, yeɛ nnɛma ɛmɔperepere ye nwo kɔpem mmerɛ bɔ ye bɔbɔ okuro ɔ.

english_verse: I hear the voice of the one I love, as he comes leaping over mountains and hills
translation_verse: Me kurofoɛ ne, ye komvi ɛhe! Nea, ye yeɛ ɔba ye, ohuruhuru wɔ mmokaa nemɔ aso, ɔbɔ apendengwa wɔ pambaa nemɔ so.

english_verse: and speaking to me. He Speaks: My darling, I love you! Let's go away together.
translation_verse: Me kurofoɛ ne, odwudwole me nwo kyɛ, “Dwɔso, me kurofoɛ, me kurofoɛ anwonyemene, bra e!

english_verse: Winter is past, the rain has stopped;
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ prakasua ne apɛ nu, yeɛ asuso ne ayakyi, na wapɛ nu.

english_verse: flowers cover the earth, it's time to sing. The cooing of doves is heard in our land.
translation_verse: Nyerɛen awa aseɛ ne aso, edweintolɛ mmerɛ ne adwu, na yɛte aborɔma suɛ wɔ yɛ aseɛ ye aso.

english_verse: Fig trees are bearing fruit, while blossoms on grapevines fill the air with perfume. My darling, I love you! Let's go away together.
translation_verse: Borɔdoma ahyɛ ye bo osu, bobe nemɔ abɔ nyerɛen, bɛbo fonafona. Dwɔso, me kurofoɛ, me kurofoɛ anwonyemene, bra e!

english_verse: You are my dove hiding among the rocks on the side of a cliff. Let me see how lovely you are! Let me hear the sound of your melodious voice.
translation_verse: O m’abubure bɔ ɛwɔ tokuro bɔ ɔla nyɔbotaen nu ɔ, bɔ aafea nyɔbotaen si ɔ, maa nwu wɔ nyunu e, maa nde wɔ komvi e, ofikyɛ wɔ komvi yɛ fɛ, na wɔ nyunu yɛ nyemene.

english_verse: Our vineyards are in blossom; we must catch the little foxes that destroy the vineyards. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔhyehye safuboa nemɔ bɛ́ma yɛ, safuboa mmaa mmaa mɔ bɔ bɛsɛkye bobe boo ne, ofikyɛ yɛ bobe nemɔ asu.”

english_verse: My darling, I am yours, and you are mine, as you feed your sheep among the lilies.
translation_verse: Me kurofoɛ ne, ɔte me deɛ, yeɛ me wora nde ye deɛ, ɔfa ye mmoaen kɔ adidie wɔ sukooko mɔ nu.

english_verse: Pretend to be a young deer dancing on mountain slopes until daylight comes and shadows fade away.
translation_verse: Me kurofoɛ, sa wɔ si bra e, yɛ kyɛ ɛwanzane anaa mmokaa so dabɔɔ akrɔngrɔma, kɔpem kyɛ aleɛ kodwo ná wawoɛ komini ɔ.

english_verse: While in bed at night, I reached for the one I love with heart and soul. I looked for him, but he wasn't there.
translation_verse: Kɔngɔen bɔ nna me bɛen so ne, me wora lɔle me kurofoɛ bɔ me kra kuro ye paa ne, me wora lɔle ye, nakoso mannwu ye, [mvrɛle ye, nakoso wanzuro.]

english_verse: So I searched through the town for the one I love. I looked on every street, but he wasn't there.
translation_verse: Nzaade, ngodwɔso ngoohyinihyini kuro nu dɔ, wɔ dwaaso ne mmorɔnoɛ nemɔ aso, ngɔɔpena me kurofoɛ bɔ me kra kuro ye ne; mbenane ye, nakoso mannwu ye.

english_verse: I even asked the guards patrolling the town, “Have you seen the one I love so much?”
translation_verse: Awɛmvoɛ bɔ bekyinikyini bɛwɛne kuro berɛ ne, beyiale me. “Aso ɛmɔanwu biaa bɔ me kra kuro ye ne?”

english_verse: Right after that, I found him. I held him and would not let go until I had taken him to the home of my mother.
translation_verse: Nzane bɛ nwo ne ala, yeɛ nwuni bɔ me kra kuro ye ne ɔ. Ndo mmrale ye, kyɛ mengɔma ɔngɔhɔ, kɔpem kyɛ mvale ye mmale me ni awuro, sona bɔ ɔnwonzɛle me ne, ye pumbu ne anu ɔ.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles, never to awaken love before it is ready. The Groom and the Wedding Party Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: O Yerusalem ndaluwa, mesrɛ ɛmɔ kitii, mefa ɛwanzane mɔ ne dabɔɔ mɔ meta ndaen kyɛ, nnɛma ɛmɔtingye ehurolɛ, yeɛ nnɛma ɛmɔperepere ye nwo kɔpem mmerɛ bɔ ye bɔbɔ okuro ɔ.

english_verse: What do we see approaching from the desert like a cloud of smoke? With it comes the sweet smell of spices, including myrrh and frankincense.
translation_verse: Nwa yeɛ ofi ɛserɛ so dɔ ɔba ye, bɔ ɔba kyɛ nwosina ningɔnn ye, bɔ korobo ne ɛyɛɛ ayɛ ye nwo fonafona ye, bɔ watutu dwadifoɛ sakyeɛfona amukoraa wagua ye nwo ye?

english_verse: It is King Solomon carried on a throne, surrounded by sixty of Israel's best soldiers.
translation_verse: Nea ye sɛko ne, Solomon deɛ ne ɔ! Mmienzua anwoserɛfoɛ aburasia yeɛ bapɛ ye nwo bayia ɔ, befi Yisrael mmienzua anwoserɛfoɛ nu.

english_verse: Each of them wears a sword. They are experts at fighting, even in the dark.
translation_verse: Bɛ mukoraa betiratira ngrandɛ, bɛse koɛ ko paa, ebiala ngrandɛ wura ye taku so, ɔnate esurolɛ bɔ besuro kɔngɔen ti.

english_verse: The throne is made of trees from Lebanon.
translation_verse: Nana Solomon fale Lebanon mmakaa yɔle ye bɔbɔ ye sɛko.

english_verse: Its posts are silver, the back is gold, and the seat is covered with purple cloth. You women of Jerusalem have taken great care to furnish the inside.
translation_verse: Ɔfale ɛdwetɛ yɔle ye mbuna nemɔ, ye si ne te sikaa kɔkorɛ, ye bia ne te koogyan, na ye kunu ne koso, Yerusalem ndaluwa mɔ bɛ hurolɛ yeɛ bafa badwura nu ɔ.

english_verse: Now come and see the crown given to Solomon by his mother on his happy wedding day.
translation_verse: O Sion mma mmrasua, ɛ́mɔfite bɛbra bɛɛnea Nana Solomon, kyɛ owura abotire bɔ ye maame fa bɔle ye wɔ kyẽa bɔ ɔfale atɔmvorɛ ne, ɔne kyẽa bɔ ye nye gyele paa ne.

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— as you look through your veil, your eyes are those of a dove. Your hair tosses about as gracefully as goats coming down from Gilead.
translation_verse: Ah, me kurofoɛ, wɔ nwo yɛ nyemene, ah, wɔ nwo yɛ nyemene! Wɔ nye mmaa bɔ owura wɔ ngatanyunu nu ne, ɔte kyɛ abubure nye! Wɔ ti nwiaa te kyɛ mbɔngye kure bɔ bɛtorotoro Gileade bokaa ɔ.

english_verse: Your teeth are whiter than sheep freshly washed; they match perfectly, not one is missing.
translation_verse: Wɔ gye te kyɛ mmoaen mmeleɛ bɔ bekye ala yeɛ babia bɛ ɔ bɛ nwo, bɔ bɛ mukoraa bawo ndaa, bɔ ko po nne bɛ nu bɔ ɔnwo ɔ.

english_verse: Your lips are crimson cords, your mouth is shapely; behind your veil are hidden beautiful rosy cheeks.
translation_verse: Wɔ noa te kyɛ nyamaa kɔkorɛ, wɔ noa dwudwolɛ yeɛ oku me ye, wɔ mvoka bɔ ɔtetɛ berɛ wɔ wɔ ngatanyunu nu ne, ɔte kyɛ akengaa bɔ bapakye nu nyɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Your neck is more graceful than the tower of David, decorated with thousands of warriors' shields.
translation_verse: Wɔ kɔme te kyɛ Dawide abandenden ne, bɔ besili ye kyɛ bɛfa akodeɛ begua nu, bɔ akokyɛm apee ko sinzesinze so, bɔ bɛ mukoraa bɛte koɛhonɛfoɛ b’akokyɛm ɔ.

english_verse: Your breasts are perfect; they are twin deer feeding among lilies.
translation_verse: Wɔ nyɔfone nyɔ ne, bɛte kyɛ dabɔɔ akrɔngrɔma nyɔ bɔ bɛte ndaa ɔ, bɔ bedidi wɔ sukooko mɔ nu ɔ.

english_verse: I will hasten to those hills sprinkled with sweet perfume and stay there till sunrise.
translation_verse: Ngɔhɔ korobo bokaa ne aso, ɔne ɛyɛɛ pambaa ne aso, kɔpem kyɛ aleɛ kodwo ná wawoɛ komini ɔ.

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely in every way.
translation_verse: Me kurofoɛ, anwonyemene abia wɔ, na ɛndɔ sii wɔ wɔ neka fee.

english_verse: My bride, together we will leave Lebanon! We will say goodbye to the peaks of Mount Amana, Senir, and Hermon, where lions and leopards live in the caves.
translation_verse: M’atɔmvorɛ braa, maa yɛfi Lebanon yɛhɔ, maa yɛfi Lebanon yɛhɔ. Fi Amana bokaa ti afia dwu bra, fi Seniri ne Hɛmɔn bokaa ti afia dwu bra, fi gyata mɔ bɛ bue nu bra, fi aboa mmokaa ne aso dwu bra.

english_verse: My bride, my very own, you have stolen my heart! With one glance from your eyes and the glow of your necklace, you have stolen my heart.
translation_verse: Nniɛma brasua, m’atɔmvorɛ braa, amaa mede me nwo a onne, wɔ nye bɔ afa anea me ne, yeɛ akomuade ko bɔ ɔla wɔ kɔme ne, amaa mede me nwo a onne.

english_verse: Your love is sweeter than wine; the smell of your perfume is more fragrant than spices.
translation_verse: Ao, nniɛma brasua, m’atɔmvorɛ braa, wɔ hurolɛ ne, kyɛbɔ ye fɛɛ osi te ne, wɔ hurolɛ yɛ fɛ tra nzaa, na wɔ nwo sakyeɛfona ne, ɔbo fona tra ayirefona biala.

english_verse: Your lips are a honeycomb; milk and honey flow from your tongue. Your dress has the aroma of cedar trees from Lebanon.
translation_verse: M’atɔmvorɛ braa, wɔ noa pepe woɛ, woɛ ne nyɔfonesue wɔ wɔ temverema bo, wɔ tena nu fona te kyɛ Lebanon fona.

english_verse: My bride, my very own, you are a garden, a fountain closed off to all others.
translation_verse: Nniɛma brasua ne, m’atɔmvorɛ braa ne, ɔte turo bɔ bato ye nwo waen ɔ, mbombonzue bɔ bato ye nwo waen ɔ, abura bɔ bafa nzɔanoɛ basɔ ye noa ɔ.

english_verse: Your arms are vines, covered with delicious fruits and all sorts of spices— henna, nard,
translation_verse: Wɔ mmaen nemɔ, bɛte turo bɔ akengaa wɔ nu, bɔ mmakaammaa paa wɔ nu ɔ, kandanguru ne mmakaa fonafona,

english_verse: saffron, calamus, cinnamon, frankincense, myrrh, and aloes —all the finest spices.
translation_verse: mmakaa fonafona ne ɛsaa, hwendea ne ɛmanyire ne ɛyɛɛ mmakaa mukoraa, korobo ne pɛprɛ ne ayirefona paapaa mukoraa.

english_verse: You are a spring in the garden, a fountain of pure water, and a refreshing stream from Mount Lebanon. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Ɛte turo nu abura, mbombonzue ne asue mmaa mmaa bɔ bɛtengyɛ befi Lebanon so ɔ. Braa ne dwein deɛ

english_verse: Let the north wind blow, the south wind too! Let them spread the aroma of my garden, so the one I love may enter and taste its delicious fruits.
translation_verse: O, sorɔ dɔ mvrama, dwɔso, O, ngwaen dɔ mvrama, bra e! Baatu fa me turo ye anu ma ye fona ne ɔto pete. Me kurofoɛ ne, mepena kyɛ ɔba ye turo ne anu ɔbadi nu mmakaammaa paapaa ne.

english_verse: My bride, my very own, I come to my garden and enjoy its spices. I eat my honeycomb and honey; I drink my wine and milk. Their Friends Speak: Eat and drink until you are drunk with love. Another Dream She Speaks:
translation_verse: Nniɛma brasua, m’atɔmvorɛ braa, mawa me turo ne anu, méboaboa me korobo ne m’ayirefona ne noa, médi me woɛ bɔ ɔwɔ ye nzasameɛ nu ɔne me woɛ ne, méno me nzaa ne me nyɔfonesue ne. Me mmango mɔ, ɛ́mɔdidi ná ɛ́mɔno, adɔfo mɔ, ɛ́mɔno ma ɛmɔ ko yi. Braa ne dwein deɛ

english_verse: I was asleep, but dreaming: The one I love was at the door, knocking and saying, “My darling, my very own, my flawless dove, open the door for me! My head is drenched with evening dew.”
translation_verse: Nnale, nakoso m’ahone nu de, né nnnale. Ndele kyɛ me kurofoɛ ne ɔbɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ kyɛ, “Bukye me, nniɛma brasua, me kurofoɛ, m’abubure, me kurofoɛ bɔ odi mu ɔ, ofikyɛ ebosue aloaloa me ti so, ɛborɔ bɔ ogua kɔngɔen ne, waloa me ti nwiaa mbɛsɛmbɛsɛ ne.” Braa ne dwein deɛ

english_verse: But I had already undressed and bathed my feet. Should I dress again and get my feet dirty?
translation_verse: Mapuro m’ataadeɛ magua berɛ dadadada, ngɔyɛ sɛɛ né mawura? Manwunzi me gya bo, ngɔyɛ sɛɛ né mayɛ ye fiɛ?

english_verse: Then my darling's hand reached to open the latch, and my heart stood still.
translation_verse: Me kurofoɛ ne sɔle daakoo ne anu, na me kunu yɛle me nufaa.

english_verse: When I rose to open the door, my hands and my fingers dripped with perfume.
translation_verse: Yeɛ ndwɔsole kyɛ mekwaabukye me kurofoɛ ne, na me sa nwo korobo ne, ɔpepe guale, me sa mmɛseka nwo korobo nzue ne, ɔpepe guale, bɛpepe beguale daakoo ne aso.

english_verse: And I yearned for him while he spoke to me, but when I opened the door, my darling had disappeared. I searched and shouted, but I could not find him— there was no answer.
translation_verse: Mmukyele me kurofoɛ ne, nakoso né me kurofoɛ ne akakyi ye nwo wasa wahɔ. Me wora bɔle kyɛ wahɔ ɔ, mbenane ye, nakoso mannwu ye, mvrɛle ye, nakoso wanzuro.

english_verse: Then I was found by the guards patrolling the town and guarding the wall. They beat me up and stripped off my robe.
translation_verse: Awɛmvoɛ mɔ bɔ bekyinikyini bɛwɛne kuro berɛ ne, beyiale me, bedufudufuli me, bepurale me; na sɔ awɛmvoɛ mɔ bɔ bɛwɛne fasue ne, belele me ngatanyunu ne.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, if you find the one I love, please say to him, “She is weak with desire.” Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: O Yerusalem ndaluwa, mesrɛ ɛmɔ kitii, sɛ ɛmɔnwu me kurofoɛ ne a, ɛmɔhã behyire ye kyɛ, ehurolɛ abɔ me anwonyerɛ. Yerusalem ndaluwa suro edwein ne aso

english_verse: Most beautiful of women, why is the one you love more special than others? Why do you ask us to tell him how you feel? She Speaks:
translation_verse: O, wɔ bɔ w’anwonyemene tra mmrasua mukoraa ɔ, nzu yeɛ wɔ kurofoɛ ne ɔfa tra kurofoɛ biemɔ, bɔ ɔmaa ɛsrɛ yɛ kitii sɔa ɔ? Braa ne dwein deɛ

translation_verse: Me kunu a, ahaa ɛte nniɛma bienzua, bɔ ɔnone me ni nyɔfone ɔ! Sɛ meyia wɔ dwaaso a, ahaa ngɔfe wɔ noa, bɔ ebiala ngosobi ye noa ngogua me so ɔ.

english_verse: I could take you to the home of my mother, who taught me all I know. I would give you delicious wine and fruit juice as well.
translation_verse: Ahaa ngoli wɔ nyunu ngɔfa wɔ ngɔwa me ni awuro maa ekohyire me ehurolɛ. Ahaa ngɔmaa ɛkɔno nzaa bɔ nningyein fonafona wɔ nu ɔ bɔ ɔte m’akengaa nzue bɔ bahwi ɔ.

english_verse: Put your left hand under my head and embrace me with your right arm.
translation_verse: Me ti la ye sa bɛen so, wafa ye sa famaa wato wabra me.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me never to awaken love before it is ready. Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: O Yerusalem ndaluwa, mesrɛ ɛmɔ kitii, kyɛ nnɛma ɛmɔtingye ehurolɛ, yeɛ nnɛma ɛmɔperepere ye nwo kɔpem mmerɛ bɔ ye bɔbɔ okuro ɔ. Yerusalem ndaluwa suro edwein ne aso

english_verse: Who is this young woman coming in from the desert and leaning on the shoulder of the one she loves? She Speaks: I stirred up your passions under the apple tree where you were born.
translation_verse: Brasua beni yeɛ ofi ɛserɛ so dɔ ɔba e, bɔ wate wamata ye kurofoɛ ye? Ndingyele wɔ wɔ aprɛ ne abo, nekaa bɔ wɔ maame wole wɔ ne, bɔ ɔwole wɔ ne, berɛ yeɛ aworɛ hane ye ɔ. Braa ne dwein deɛ

english_verse: Always keep me in your heart and wear this bracelet to remember me by. The passion of love bursting into flame is more powerful than death, stronger than the grave.
translation_verse: Fa me yɛ w’ahone nwo nzɔanoɛ, fa me yɛ wɔ sa nwo nzɔanoɛ, ofikyɛ ehurolɛ nu yɛ se te kyɛ ewue, nungunɛ ti anu yɛ se te kyɛ asieleɛ kumaa. Ehurolɛ nzramaa te see nzramaa bɔ ɔsɔ wuronyiwuronyi ɔ.

english_verse: Love cannot be drowned by oceans or floods. It cannot be bought— any offer would be scorned no matter how great. Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Nzue pee ngɔhora ngonua ehurolɛ, yeɛ asue mɔ ngɔhora ngɔma ɔngɔmono. Sɛ sona fa ye anwonya mukoraa po kyɛ ɔfa tɔ ehurolɛ a, bekosobi bɛ noa bekogua ye so. Braa n’aliɛma mmienzua mɔ dwein

english_verse: We have a little sister whose breasts are not yet formed. If someone asks to marry her, what should we do?
translation_verse: Yɛle aliɛmaa brasua bie bɔ ɔte kãa ɔ, onnya ɔbbobɔle nyɔfone. Kyẽa bɔ bienzua bie kɔɔsrɛ ye agyaa ne, nzu yeɛ yɛkɔyɔ yɛkɔma y’eliɛma brasua ye ɔ?

english_verse: She isn't a wall that we can defend behind a silver shield. Neither is she a room that we can protect behind a wooden door. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Sɛ y’eliɛma ne ɔte fasue a, ahaa yɛkɔto ɛdwetɛ abandenden yɛkosie so, yeɛ sɛ ɔte anoa a, ahaa yɛkɔfa sida yɛkɔma ye nwo yɛkoyia. Braa ne dwein deɛ

english_verse: I am a wall around a city, my breasts are towers, and just looking at me brings him great pleasure.
translation_verse: Nde fasue, na me nyɔfone te kyɛ abandenden, na mayɛ kyɛ sona bɔ ɔne asomdwee yeɛ bɛnate ɔ wɔ me kurofoɛ n’anye so.

english_verse: Solomon has a vineyard at Baal-Hamon, which he rents to others for a thousand pieces of silver each.
translation_verse: Né Solomon le bobe boo wɔ Baal Hamon; ɔfale bobe boo ne wurale hwɛsofoɛ sa, bɛ nu biala te bobe mmaa ne a, né odi kyɛ ɔbrɛ ye ɛdwetɛ apee ko.

english_verse: My vineyard is mine alone! Solomon can keep his silver and the others can keep their share of the profits. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Me bobe boo bɔ me bɔbɔ me deɛ ahɔ ne, me bɔbɔ yeɛ menea so ɔ. O Solomon, ɛdwetɛ apee ko ne, ɔte wɔ deɛ, yeɛ bobe mmaa so hwɛsofoɛ nemɔ bɛ deɛ ɛyaa nyɔ.

english_verse: You are in the garden with friends all around. Let me hear your voice! She Speaks:
translation_verse: O, wɔ bɔ ɛte turo nemɔ anu ɔ, wɔ mmango mɔ bɛnwondɛ kyɛ bɛkɔte wɔ komvi ɔ, maa nde wɔ komvi e.

english_verse: Hurry to me, my darling! Run faster than a deer to mountains of spices.
translation_verse: Me kurofoɛ, bra ndɛndɛ, yɛ kyɛ ɛwanzane, anaakyɛ dabɔɔ akrɔngrɔma wɔ ayirefona mmokaa nemɔ aso.

english_verse: I am Isaiah, the son of Amoz. And this is the message that I was given about Judah and Jerusalem when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah: A Guilty Nation
translation_verse: Nyekyire he yeɛ Amoso awa Yesaya onwuni ye fale Yuda ne Yerusalem nwo wɔ Yuda ahemvo Yusia, Yotam, Ahase ne Hesekia b’aberɛ so ɔ. Yuda bɔne nwo asotwe

english_verse: The Lord has said, “Listen, heaven and earth! The children I raised have turned against me.
translation_verse: O nyameɛso, ɛ́mɔtie, O aseɛ, ma wɔ so bra wa! Ofikyɛ AWURADE nwa nyoo: “Matete ngwadaa manea bɛ so maa banyi, nakoso bayɛ me nwo lɔen.

english_verse: Oxen and donkeys know who owns and feeds them, but my people won't ever learn.”
translation_verse: Nandwie se ye mene, yeɛ afunum se nekaa bɔ ye mene ma ye aleɛ ɔ, nakoso Yisrael de, ɔnze, me maen ne ɔnde ye bo.”

english_verse: Israel, you are a sinful nation loaded down with guilt. You are wicked and corrupt and have turned from the Lord, the holy God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ao, maen bɔ bɔne ayi nu tɛkyɛ ɔ! Mmenia bɔ amumuyɛɛ ali bɛ ti ɔ! Bɔnefoɛ mɔ bɛ bosofoɛ! Mmaa bɔ basɛkye ɔ! Bɔ bapo AWURADE, bɔ babu Yisrael Krongronniɛ ne animtia, ná bakakyi bɛ si bama ye ɔ!

english_verse: Why be punished more? Why not give up your sin? Your head is badly bruised, and you are weak all over.
translation_verse: Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔkuro kyɛ mekɔ so mebo ɛmɔ ɔ? Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔtɛyɛ lɔen ye? Tire ne amukoraa nde apɔ, yeɛ ahone ne amukoraa ayɛ hodwoo.

english_verse: From your head to your toes there isn't a healthy spot. Bruises, cuts, and open sores go without care or oil to ease the pain. A Country in Ruins
translation_verse: Ofi ɛmɔ gya kunu kɔkã ɛmɔ ti so, nekaa biala nde apɔ, wapepɛ wapuropuro wayɛ ngenangena bɔ otu mogya ɔ; ngena bɔ bemmia, bɔ bɛngyekye so, bɔ bɛmva ayire bɛnda nu ɔ.

english_verse: Your country lies in ruins; your towns are in ashes. Foreigners and strangers take and destroy your land while you watch.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ maen ne abɔ, bafa see bayera ɛmɔ nguro nemɔ, amanvrafoɛ bɛfẽ ɛmɔ fieso aleɛ bɛfa bɔ ɛmɔ nye tua ɔ; wabɔ, kyɛbɔ ɛwɔfoɛ mɔ basɛkye ye ne.

english_verse: Enemies surround Jerusalem, alone like a hut in a vineyard or in a cucumber field.
translation_verse: Waha Sion awa brasua ne angome berɛ, kyɛ bobe boo nu asese, kyɛ ferɛ eboo nu pata, kyɛ kuro bɔ batua ye ɔ.

english_verse: Zion would have disappeared like Sodom and Gomorrah, if the Lord All-Powerful had not let a few of its people survive. Justice, Not Sacrifices
translation_verse: Sɛ Asafo AWURADE anyakyi yɛ mmenia kãa bie ma bannya bɛ ti bannidi nu a, ahaa yayɛ kyɛ Sodom, ahaa yakakyi kyɛ Gomora.

english_verse: You are no better than the leaders and people of Sodom and Gomorrah! So listen to the Lord God:
translation_verse: Mbanyi bɔ bedi Sodom so ɔ, ɛ́mɔtie AWURADE noa dwirɛ! Ɛmɔ Gomorafoɛ, ɛ́mɔyɛ asoɛ bétie yɛ Nyameɛ ngyerɛkyerɛ!

english_verse: “Your sacrifices mean nothing to me. I am sick of your offerings of rams and choice cattle; I don't like the blood of bulls or lambs or goats.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ afɔleɛ worawora ne, mefa meyɛ nzu? AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne. Mmoaen nyii naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ɔne nyɛmmoa mɔ bɛ loe ne, mali maa wabɔ me; yeɛ nandwie mogya anaa mmoaen mogya, anaa mbɔngye mogya ɔnzɔ me nye.

english_verse: “Who asked you to bring all this when you come to worship me? Stay out of my temple!
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛmɔba me nyunu a, nwa yeɛ osele ɛmɔ kyɛ ɛmɔyɔ sɔ ɔ, kyɛ ɛ́mɔtiatia m’aluo berɛ basabasa ɔ?

english_verse: Your sacrifices are worthless, and your incense disgusting. I can't stand the evil you do on your New Moon Festivals or on your Sabbaths and other times of worship.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ afɔleɛ mbaen mbaen ne, nnɛma ɛmɔfa bɛba ko, ɛyɛɛ ne te m’akyiwadeɛ. Ɛsraen foforɛ ne afofikyẽa aluolue ne, ɔne ɛmɔ dwaabɔlɛ ne, nyianu krongron ne po, ɔte amumuyɛɛ, mengɔhora ngɔgyegye so.

english_verse: I hate your New Moon Festivals and all others as well. They are a heavy burden I am tired of carrying.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ ɛsraen foforɛ aluolue ne aluolue nemɔ, me kra kyi, ɔte ɛhawo ma me, bɔ bayɛ me so adesoa ɔ.

english_verse: “No matter how much you pray, I won't listen. You are too violent.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛmɔtrɛtrɛ ɛmɔ sa nu ngɔye me nye ngɔto buro bɔ mengɔtɛ ɛmɔ so ɔ. Ɛmɔbɔ mbaeɛ pee de, nakoso mengotie, ofikyɛ ɛmɔahã mogya bagua paa.

english_verse: Wash yourselves clean! I hate your filthy deeds. Stop doing wrong
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔnwunzi ɛmɔ nwo, ɛ́mɔpete ɛmɔ nwo, ɛ́mɔye ɛmɔ bɔne yɔleɛ ne béfi me nye so, ɛ́mɔyakyi bɔne yɔlɛ.

english_verse: and learn to live right. See that justice is done. Defend widows and orphans and help the oppressed.” An Invitation from the Lord
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔsua bɔ ɔte paa ɔ bɛyɔ, ɛ́mɔpena pɛpɛɛpɛyɛlɛ si atee, ɛ́mɔpepɛ bele bɛ bɔ bɛyɛ anwumvo ɔ, ɛ́mɔhã bie bɛma nyisiaafoɛ, ná ɛmɔgyina akunafoɛ mmrasua si.

english_verse: I, the Lord, invite you to come and talk it over. Your sins are scarlet red, but they will be whiter than snow or wool.
translation_verse: AWURADE nwa nyoo: “Ɛmɔbra ma yɛsiesie yɛ afia. Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ ɛmɔ bɔne te kyɛ adaabene de, nakoso bɛkɔyɛ fufue kyɛ nwera, ɔwɔ nu kyɛ bɛboro kyɛ koogyan, nakoso bɛkɔyɛ kyɛ gyese.

english_verse: If you willingly obey me, the best crops in the land will be yours.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛmɔpene so ná ɛmɔyɛ sotie a, ye de aseɛ ne aso nikye paa yeɛ ɛmɔkoli ɔ.

english_verse: But if you turn against me, your enemies will kill you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Condemns Jerusalem
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ ɛmɔtwi bɛfa so, ná ɛmɔyɛ lɔen a, ye de ɛmɔkɔtotɔ ngrandɛ noa, ofikyɛ AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.” Yerusalem

english_verse: Jerusalem, you are like an unfaithful wife. Once your judges were honest and your people lived right; now you are a city full of murderers.
translation_verse: Kuro bɔ né odi nahorɛ ne, nea kyɛbɔ wasi wakakyi gyanderaniɛ ɔ! Ye bɔ ahaa né pɛpɛɛpɛyɛlɛ wayi ye nu tɛkyɛ ne, bɔ ahaa né ɔte tenenee kuro ne, afei de kodiawufoɛ yeɛ bɛwɔ nu ɔ!

english_verse: Your silver is fake, and your wine is watered down.
translation_verse: Wɔ dwetɛ ne akakyi nikyee fiɛ, wɔ nzaa paa ne, bafa nzue bayuro ye.

english_verse: Your leaders have rejected me to become friends of crooks; your rulers are looking for gifts and bribes. Widows and orphans never get a fair trial.
translation_verse: Wɔ mbanyi ayɛ lɔen, na bafa awuefoɛ abiɛngoɛ. Bɛ mukoraa bɛ nye gye fea-ase-ma nwo, na bɛpere bɛpena akyɛdeɛ. Bɛnga bie bɛmma nyisiaafoɛ, na akunafoɛ mmrasua dwirɛ ba bɛ nyunu a bɛmvrɛ.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the mighty ruler of Israel, and I make you a promise: You are now my enemy, and I will show my anger by taking revenge on you.
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE, Asafo AWURADE, Yisrael Tuminiɛ ne, ɔnwa nyoo: Aa, bɛ bɔ bekyi me ne, ngɔfɛ bɛ so yaa piri paa, yeɛ ngɔtɔ me pɔfoɛ mɔ bɛ so wereɛ!

english_verse: I will punish you terribly and burn away everything that makes you unfit to worship me.
translation_verse: Ngɔfa me tumi ngɔhwe wɔ so, ngohuro wɔ ngɔye wɔ nwo fiɛ ne, ná maye wɔ nwo wohyee ne amukoraa magua.

english_verse: Jerusalem, I will choose judges and advisors like those you had before. Your new name will be “Justice and Faithfulness.” The Lord Will Save Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ngosa ngɔma wɔ maenbulɛfoɛ kyɛ daa ne ala, yeɛ foɛtulɛfoɛ koso, kyɛbɔ ahyɛaseɛ ne né ɔte ne ala. Na ɛhe asi ne, bɛkɔfrɛ wɔ tenenee kuro ne nahorɛlilɛ kuro.

english_verse: Jerusalem, you will be saved by showing justice; Zion's people who turn to me will be saved by doing right.
translation_verse: Ɔnate ndɛenbualɛ turoloo so ngole Sion, yeɛ ɔnate pɛpɛɛpɛyɛlɛ so ngole nu mmenia bɔ basakyera b’adwene ɔ.

english_verse: But those rebellious sinners who turn against me, the Lord, will all disappear.
translation_verse: Nakoso mmeraatolɛfoɛ ne bɔnefoɛ de, ngohũ bɛ ngɔbɔ nu, na bɛ bɔ bɛpo AWURADE ne wora, ngohũhũ bɛ.

english_verse: You will be like a grove of trees dying in a drought.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔkɔyɛ kyɛ eluii bɔ ye nyaa kese, anaakyɛ turo bɔ nzue ngua so ɔ.

english_verse: Your strongest leaders will be like dry wood set on fire by their idols. No one will be able to help, as they all go up in flames.
translation_verse: Anwoserɛniɛ kɔyɛ kyɛ mmɛyeram worowaa, ye sa noa adwuma kɔyɛ kyɛ see nzramaa, na ɔne ye sa noa adwuma ne bɛkɔyera bɛkɔbɔ nu, bɔ ebiala nne berɛ bɔ okonua ye ɔ.

english_verse: This is the message I was given about Judah and Jerusalem:
translation_verse: Nyekyire he yeɛ Amoso awa Yesaya nwuni ye fale Yuda ne Yerusalem nwo ɔ:

english_verse: In the future, the mountain with the Lord's temple will be the highest of all. It will reach above the hills; every nation will rush to it.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔwa kyɛ, mmerɛ bɔ oli nziɛ ne, bokaa bɔ AWURADE awuro ne gyi so ne, ye bo kotimu maa ɔkɔware kɔtra bokaa biala, ɔkɔyɛ tendenn kɔtra pambaa biala, na maen maen mukoraa bekobiri bɛkɔwa so.

english_verse: Many people will come and say, “Let's go to the mountain of the Lord God of Jacob and worship in his temple.” The Lord will teach us his Law from Jerusalem, and we will obey him.
translation_verse: Na mmenia pee bɛkɔwa bɛkɔɔhã kyɛ, “Ɛmɔbra ma yɛfo yɛhɔ AWURADE bokaa ne aso, ɛ́mɔma yɛhɔ Yakob Nyameɛ awuro ne anu, amaa ɔnate so wahyirehyire yɛ ye atee ne, ná yanate ye atimbire ne aso.” Ofikyɛ Sion yeɛ mmeraa ne kofi kɔwa ɔ, na Yerusalem yeɛ AWURADE dwirɛ ne kofi kɔwa ɔ.

english_verse: He will settle arguments between nations. They will pound their swords and their spears into rakes and shovels; they will never make war or attack one another.
translation_verse: Okoli maen maen mɔ so, okosiesie mmenia pee b’afia, bɛkɔboro bɛ ngrandɛ bɛkɔfa bɛkɔbɔ kona, ná baboro bɛ pealɛɛ bafa babɔ asɔsɔaa. Maen bie ngɔhwe obiɛngo maen so ngrandɛ, na bengosua koɛhonɛ ko.

english_verse: People of Israel, let's live by the light of the Lord. Following Sinful Customs
translation_verse: O, Yakob awuro ama, ɛmɔbra ma yɛnate AWURADE kanea ne anu! AWURADE kyẽa ne

english_verse: Our Lord, you have deserted your people, Israel, because they follow customs of nations from the east. They worship Philistine gods and are close friends of foreigners.
translation_verse: Amba, apo wɔ mmenia, Yakob boso ama nemɔ, ofikyɛ eyia afiteleɛ ahɔmeɛ bɛ ne Filisti ngonyaayelɛfoɛ bayi maen ne anu tɛkyɛ, na Yakob boso ama nemɔ, bɛ ne maen maen mɔ nu ama yeɛ bɛbɔ afɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Everywhere in the country they worship the idols they have made.
translation_verse: Mmosoen ayi b’aseɛ ne aso tɛkyɛ; bɛsɔne bɛ sa noa adwuma, nningyein bɔ bafa bɛ bɔbɔ bɛ sa bayɔ ɔ.

english_verse: And so, all of them will be ashamed and disgraced. Don't forgive them! A Day of Judgment
translation_verse: Ye sɔ ne ati, adasa mmaa nyunu agua ase, na kuro sona asopa ye nwo. O, nnɛfa bɛ bɔne kyɛ bɛ!

english_verse: Every one of you, go hide among the rocks and in the ground, because the Lord is fearsome, marvelous, and glorious.
translation_verse: Na ɔnate AWURADE nwo suronyi, ɔne ye animnyam totohyia ne ati, kowura nyɔbotaen nu, fa wɔ nwo kɔfea mvuture nu.

english_verse: When the Lord comes, everyone who is proud will be made humble, and the Lord alone will be honored.
translation_verse: Bɛkɔbrɛ ahandaen anyeɛ ase, yeɛ bekogua mmenia b’anwomasoɛ nyunu ase, na AWURADE angome yeɛ bɛkɔma ye so sɔ kyẽa ne ɔ.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful has chosen a day when those who are proud and conceited will be put down.
translation_verse: Na Asafo AWURADE ole ye kyẽa bɔ ɔkɔwa ebiala bɔ ɔte anwomasoɛ ne ahandaen ɔ so, ɔne ebiala bɔ wama ye nye atra ye ndo nwiaa ɔ so, na ɔkɔbrɛ ye ase;

english_verse: The tall and towering cedars of Lebanon will be destroyed. So will the oak trees of Bashan,
translation_verse: ɔkɔwa Lebanon sida mukoraa bɔ bahɔ anwuro tendetende ɔ so, ɔne Basan eluii amukoraa so;

english_verse: all the seagoing ships, and every beautiful boat.
translation_verse: ɔkɔwa Tasise ɛlɛen amukoraa so, ɔne nu nningyein bɔ bali adwii bayɔ ye nyemene amukoraa so.

english_verse: When that day comes, everyone who is proud will be put down. Only the Lord will be honored.
translation_verse: Bɛkɔbrɛ sona ye ahandaen ase, yeɛ bekogua mmenia b’anwomasoɛ nyunu ase, na AWURADE angome yeɛ bɛkɔma ye so sɔ kyẽa ne ɔ.

english_verse: Idols will be gone for good.
translation_verse: Amoen amukoraa bɛ boso komini.

english_verse: You had better hide in caves and holes— the Lord will be fearsome, marvelous, and glorious when he comes to terrify people on earth.
translation_verse: Na sɛ AWURADE dwɔso woso aseɛ serɛserɛ a, ɔnate AWURADE nwo suronyi, ɔne ye animnyam totohyia ne ati, mmenia koowurawura nyɔbotaen ndokuro nu, ɔne aseɛnwo ngumaa nu.

english_verse: On that day everyone will throw to the moles and bats their idols of silver and gold they made to worship.
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne, mmenia b’ɛdwetɛ amoen ne bɛ sikaa kɔkorɛ amoen bɔ bayɔ bama bɛ nwo, bɔ bɛsɔne bɛ ne, bekogyi bekogua bɛkɔma mmurokuruwa ne mbena.

english_verse: The Lord will be fearsome, marvelous, and glorious when he comes to terrify people on earth— they will hide in caves and in the hills.
translation_verse: Na sɛ AWURADE dwɔso woso aseɛ serɛserɛ a, bekoowurawura nyɔbotaen ndokuro nu, ɔne mmokaa so bɔen mɔ nu, ɔnate AWURADE nwo suronyi, ɔne ye animnyam totohyia ne ati.

english_verse: Stop trusting the power of humans. They are all going to die, so how can they help?
translation_verse: Kuro sona bɔ ode nwomeɛ fa ye bonyi anu ne, nnɛma ɛmɔfa bɛ nwo bɛto ye so. Kuro sona te nzu?

english_verse: The mighty Lord All-Powerful is going to take away from Jerusalem and Judah everything you need— your bread and water, *
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔtie! AWURADE, Asafo AWURADE ɔbaaye ɛhemɔ fi Yerusalem ne Yuda: pɔmaa ne bakaa biala bɔ bekisa ye ɔ, aleɛ biala ne nzue biala,

english_verse: soldiers and heroes, judges and prophets, leaders and army officers,
translation_verse: katakyie ne koɛhonɛniɛ, ndɛenbualɛniɛ ne ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ, nworɛniɛ ne panyi,

english_verse: officials and advisors, fortunetellers and others who tell the future.
translation_verse: aburannu so safohene ne animnyamniɛ, foɛtulɛniɛ ne ngonyaayelɛniɛ bɔ wabe, yeɛ ndafowayelɛniɛ.

english_verse: He will let children and babies become your rulers.
translation_verse: Ngɔmaa mmɛɛmaa koli bɛ so mbanyi, na nnɔma koli bɛ so.

english_verse: You will each be cruel to friends and neighbors. Young people will insult their elders; no one will show respect to those who deserve it.
translation_verse: Mmenia kɔhyɛ bɛ mmango so, bɛkɔhyɛ bɛ biɛngo so, ebiala kɔhyɛ obiɛngo so. Mmerandeɛ ne ndaluwa bɛ nye ngɔsɔ mbanyi, yeɛ kwahweabaa koso ye nye ngɔsɔ animnyamniɛ.

english_verse: Some of you will grab hold of a relative and say, “You still have a coat. Be our leader and rule this pile of ruins.”
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne, ebie kɔsɔ oliɛma bɔ ofi ɔse abusua nu ɔ nu, na okose ye kyɛ, “Wɔ yeɛ ele tena ɔ, yiti da yɛ noa yɛ yɛ so panyi, ná fa sɔ anwokyere kandinga he to wɔ nwo so.”

english_verse: But the answer will be, “I can't do you any good. Don't make me your leader. There's no food or clothing left in my house.”
translation_verse: Nakoso ko ne kɔtea nu sɔ kyẽa ne kose kyɛ, “Daabi, mengonya ɛhawo he anwo sɔbea oo, aleɛ anaa ɛtena biala nne m’awuro, yiti nnɛma ɛmɔfa me bedi mmenia ne aso panyi.”

english_verse: Jerusalem and Judah, you rebelled against your glorious Lord— your words and your actions, made you stumble and fall.
translation_verse: Yerusalem asoti, yeɛ Yuda afi ase, ofikyɛ bɛfa bɛ dwudwolɛ ne bɛ yɔleɛ bedwɔso betia AWURADE, kyɛ bɛfa bebu ye animnyam anyunuɛ ne animtia.

english_verse: The look on your faces shows that you are sinful as Sodom, and you don't try to hide it. You are in for trouble, and you have brought it all on yourselves. The Wrong Kind of Leaders
translation_verse: Kyɛbɔ basi bayɛ bɛ nyunu ne, odi adanzeɛ tia bɛ, bɛbɔ bɛ bɔne nwo dawure kyɛ Sodom, bɛmva bɛmvea. Bɛ kra yaakɔ! Ofikyɛ bahwehwe musue babrɛ bɛ nwo.

english_verse: Tell those who obey God, “You're very fortunate— you will be rewarded for what you have done.”
translation_verse: Ɛmɔhã behyire teneneefoɛ kyɛ okoyie bɛ yé, ofikyɛ bɛ sa kɔhã bɛ yɔleɛ paa nwo akatuaa.

english_verse: Tell those who disobey, “You're in big trouble— what you did to others will come back to you.”
translation_verse: Nakoso bɔnefoɛ de, ye yaakɔ! Ye ayieleɛ te musue, ofikyɛ ye bɔne yɔleɛ ne, bɛkɔyɔ bie bekotua ye so kerɛ.

english_verse: Though you are God's people, you are ruled and abused by women and children. You are confused by leaders who guide you down the wrong path.
translation_verse: Ngwadaa yeɛ bɛhyɛ me maen so ɔ, na mmrasua yeɛ bedi bɛ so panyi ɔ. O me maen, wɔ mbanyi mɔ lakalaka wɔ maa edi makyebu fi w’atimbire so.

english_verse: The Lord is ready to accuse and judge all nations.
translation_verse: AWURADE adwɔso bɔ ɔbɔ kwaadu, wagyina berɛ obua maen ne ndɛen.

english_verse: He will even judge you rulers and leaders of his own nation. You destroyed his vineyard and filled your houses by robbing the poor.
translation_verse: AWURADE baabua ye maen mbanyi ne ahemvo ndɛen, kyɛ, “Ɛmɔ, ɛmɔ yeɛ ɛmɔali bobe boo ne ɔ, ehiafoɛ nningyein bɔ ɛmɔasisi bɛ bale ne, ogua ɛmɔ awuro.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful says, “You have crushed my people and rubbed in the dirt the faces of the poor.” The Women of Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ɔwale ye sɛ bɔ ɛmɔadufudufu me mmenia sɔa, bɔ ɛmɔadwiridwiri ehiafoɛ bɛ nyunu sɔa e?” AWURADE, Asafo NYAMEƐ ne, ye noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: The Lord says: The women of Jerusalem are proud and strut around, winking shamelessly. They wear anklets that jingle and call attention to the way they walk.
translation_verse: Asa koso, AWURADE hane kyɛ, Ɔnate kyɛ Sion mma mmrasua te ahandaen, bɛ kɔme la bɛ nwo, bɛtwetwe bɛ nye asi bɛnate, bɛyeye bɛ gya ngoko ngoko, ná bɛma ngaa bɔ ogua bɛ gya wosowoso ne ati,

english_verse: But I, the Lord, will cover their heads with sores, and I will uncover their private parts.
translation_verse: AWURADE kɔma Sion mma mmrasua bɛ ti so kotutu ngena, na AWURADE kɔpa bɛ nwo.

english_verse: In place of perfume, there will be a stink; in place of belts, there will be ropes; in place of fancy hairdos, they will have bald heads. Instead of expensive clothes, they will wear sackcloth; instead of beauty, they will have ugly scars.
translation_verse: Na ɔkɔwa kyɛ, bɛ nwo fona ne kɔkakyi mvamva, bɛkɔfa nyamaa bɛkɔkakyi b’abɔsoɛ, bɛ ti bɔ babɔ ye nyemenenyemene ne, ɔkɔkakyi tikwa, bɛ kende ne kɔkakyi ɛsɛen tena, na bɛ nwonaen nyemene ne, okotwindwam.

english_verse: The fighting men of Jerusalem will be killed in battle.
translation_verse: Wɔ mmienzua kɔtotɔ ngrandɛ noa, yeɛ wɔ mmienzua ahoneserɛfoɛ kɔtotɔ wɔ koɛ nu.

english_verse: The city will mourn and sit in the dirt, emptied of its people.
translation_verse: Ye pambim nemɔ kosũ kɔbɔ awuye, bɛkɔla berɛ too, na kuro ne kɔtɔ ase.

english_verse: When this happens, seven women will grab the same man, and each of them will say, “I'll buy my own food and clothes! Just marry me and take away my disgrace.” The Lord Will Bless His People Who Survive
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne, mmrasua nzoo kɔte kɔmata bienzua ko, na bekose kyɛ, “Yɛkɔpena yɛ bɔbɔ yɛ noa aleɛ ɔne ɛtena bɔ yɛkɔhera ɔ. Wɔ de, fa wɔ dumaa to yɛ so, ná ye yɛ animguaseɛ ne fi yɛ so.” Yerusalem kosa kosi ye gya nu

english_verse: The time is coming when the Lord will make his land fruitful and glorious again, and the people of Israel who survive will take great pride in what the land produces.
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne, AWURADE mmaen ne kɔyɛ nyemene, okonya animnyam, na aseɛ ne aso mmakaammaa kɔyɛ anwohoahoa nikyee ne animnyam kɔma Yisrael mmenia bɔ banya bɛ ti badidi nu ne.

english_verse: after the Lord sends a fiery judgment to clean the city and its people of their violent deeds.
translation_verse: mmerɛ bɔ AWURADE kɔfa ndɛenbualɛ sunzum so ne ɛyeralɛ sunzum so kobia Sion mma mmrasua nwo fiɛ kogua, ná wanwunzi mogya bɔ Yerusalem ahã agua ne.

english_verse: Then the Lord will cover the whole city and its meeting places with a thick cloud each day and with a flaming fire each night. God's own glory will be like a huge tent that covers everything.
translation_verse: Na afei Sion bokaa ne, ye nekaa biala, ɔne mmenia bɔ beyia berɛ ne, AWURADE kɔyɛ munungum eyia, ɔne nwosina ne see gonn kɔngɔen komundu bɛ so. Ofikyɛ animnyam ne kɔyɛ ngatasoɛ kɔkata bɛ mukoraa bɛ so.

english_verse: It will provide shade from the heat of the sun and a place of shelter and protection from storms and rain.
translation_verse: Ɔkɔyɛ ɛtena sua bɔ eyia bɔ a nu te fɔnwoo ɔ, afealeɛ ne nekaa bɔ bɛbɔ bɛ nwo waen bɔ ɔmma mvrama piri ne esue nga bɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I will sing a song about my friend's vineyard that was on the side of a fertile hill.
translation_verse: Maa ndo me dɔfo nwo dwein, me dɔfo dwein bɔ ɔfa ye bobe boo nwo ɔ: Né me dɔfo ne ole bobe boo wɔ bokaa bie bɔ ɔkye aleɛ ɔ so.

english_verse: My friend dug the ground, removed the stones, and planted the best vines. He built a watchtower and dug a pit in rocky ground for pressing the grapes. He hoped they would be sweet, but bitter grapes were all it produced.
translation_verse: Olele ye nwo waen, ɔyeyele so nyɔboɛ ne, oluale bobe mmaa paa wɔ nu, osili abandenden siele eboo n’afia, otuli nu kumaa bɔ okohwi bobe mmaa ne anu kɔyɔ nzaa ɔ, ɔnwondɛle kyɛ bobe ne kosu mmaa paa ɔ, nakoso ye mma bɔ osuli ne te bisii.

english_verse: Listen, people of Jerusalem and of Judah! You be the judge of me and my vineyard.
translation_verse: Afei, ɛmɔ bɔ ɛmɔte Yerusalem, yeɛ Yudafoɛ, mesrɛ ɛmɔ, me ne me bobe boo dwirɛ ne, ɛ́mɔbua.

english_verse: What more could I have done for my vineyard? I hoped for sweet grapes, but bitter grapes were all that grew.
translation_verse: Nzikyɛ bieku yeɛ ahaa odi kyɛ meyɔ ye me bobe boo ne anu bɔ manyɔ ɔ? Mvale me nye ndole so kyɛ okosu mmaa paa, nzu ati yeɛ wasu mmaa bisii ɔ?

english_verse: Now I will let you know what I am going to do. I will cut down the hedge and tear down the wall. My vineyard will be trampled and left in ruins.
translation_verse: Afei de, bɔ ngɔfa ngɔyɔ me bobe boo ne, mebaahã mekyire ɛmɔ. Ngotutu ye nwo waen ne maa ngaka kooli; ngodwiri ye nwo fasue ne ngogua maa bekotiatia bobe ne aso.

english_verse: It will turn into a desert, neither pruned nor hoed; it will be covered with thorns and briars. I will command the clouds not to send rain.
translation_verse: Ngɔmaa ɔkɔkakyi adangasa, mengɔdwaadwaa ye nwo, yeɛ mengɔbɔ ye nwo, nu kofu agurɛ ne mmowue. Asa koso, ngɔhyɛ munungum kyɛ nnɛmaa ɔtɔ esue gua so.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful! Israel is the vineyard, and Judah is the garden I tended with care. I had hoped for honesty and for justice, but dishonesty and cries for mercy were all I found. Isaiah Condemns Social Injustice
translation_verse: Hmmm, Asafo AWURADE bobe boo ne, ye ole Yisrael awuro ama, yeɛ Yudafoɛ wora bɛte ye boo bɔ ɔyɛ ye nyemene ɔ. Ahaa né ɔpena kyɛ onwu ndɛenbualɛ turoloo, nakoso onwu aminɛlilɛ, ahaa né ɔpena kyɛ onwu tenenee, nakoso awuyebɔlɛ yeɛ ɔte ɔ! AWURADE dwudwo tia asisie

english_verse: You are in for trouble! You take over house after house and field after field, until there is no room left for anyone else in all the land.
translation_verse: Bɛ yaakɔ! Bɛ bɔ basesa sua mɔ babɔ so, bɔ basesa eboo mɔ babɔ so, kɔpem kyɛ bɛkɔkandam ye mukoraa so, kɔpem kyɛ bɛ ngome bɛkɔha wɔ aseɛ ne aso ɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful has made this promise to me: Those large and beautiful homes will be left empty, with no one to take care of them.
translation_verse: Asafo AWURADE ahã agua me so anu kyɛ, “Nahorɛ nu, awuro pee kɔbɔ, awuro mbiri mbiri nyemenenyemene mɔ kɔkakyi dandue.

english_verse: None of them are tired. They don't sleep or get drowsy, and they run without stumbling. Their belts don't come loose; their sandal straps don't break.
translation_verse: B’ɛlɔen ne, bɛ nu biala mvɛ, ebiala nzoti, ebiala ndɔ ngosie anaa ɔnnafe, b’abɔsoɛ nu ngoho, yeɛ bɛ mbaboa nyamaa ndete;

english_verse: You are in for trouble! The lies you tell are like ropes by which you drag along sin and evil.
translation_verse: Bɛ yaakɔ! Bɛ bɔ bɛfa nnakannaka nyamaa bɛtwetwe amumuyɛɛ ɔ, bɛ bɔ bɛtwetwe bɔne kyɛ teaseɛnam nyamaa yeɛ bɛfa bɛtwe ne,

english_verse: You are in for trouble! You get up early to start drinking, and you keep it up late into the night.
translation_verse: Bɛ yaakɔ! Bɛ bɔ bɛpɛ aleɛ bedwɔso bekodi nzaa serɛ si, bɛ bɔ besiri pɛ bɛno nzaa toonn bɛbo ɔ!

english_verse: At your drinking parties you have the music of stringed instruments, tambourines, and flutes. But you never even think about all the Lord has done,
translation_verse: Bɛ yeɛ bɛfa sangoo, adengum, akasaa, awɛen ne nzaa bɛkɔ bɛ poentolɛ bo ɔ, nakoso bɛmva nningyein bɔ AWURADE yɔ ɔ bɛnyɔ huu ɔ, yeɛ ye sa noa adwuma koso bennwu ye.

english_verse: and so his people know nothing about him. That's why many of you will be dragged off to foreign lands. Your leaders will starve to death, and everyone else will suffer from thirst.
translation_verse: Ye sɔ ne ati, bɛkɔhye me maen nnure bɛkɔhɔ, ɔnate nimdeɛ bɔ belle bie ti; ɛhɔen kohũ b’atitirefoɛ maa bekowu, yeɛ nzuhɔen kohũ mmenia wora ne maa bekowu.

english_verse: The world of the dead has opened its mouth wide and is eagerly waiting for the leaders of Jerusalem and for its noisy crowds, especially for those who take pride in that city.
translation_verse: Ye sɔ ne ati, ɛborɔ ye komvi ode ye tekɔtekɔ paa, wabukye ye noa nu fakaa, na Yerusalem animnyamfoɛ ne ye mmenia worawora ne ye lɔen ne bɛ bɔ bɛ nye gye ye nu ne, bekoowura nu.

english_verse: Its citizens have been put down, and its proud people have been brought to shame.
translation_verse: Babrɛ kuro sona ase, adasa nyunu agua ase, babrɛ mmenia b’anwomasoɛ ase.

english_verse: But the holy Lord God All-Powerful is praised, because he has shown who he is by bringing justice.
translation_verse: Nakoso Asafo AWURADE de, bɛma ye so wɔ ye ndɛenbualɛ turoloo nu, na Krongronniɛ Nyameɛ ɔda ye krongronyɛlɛ ali wɔ tenenee nu.

english_verse: His people will be like sheep grazing in their own pasture, and they will take off what was left by others.
translation_verse: Afei mmoaen mmaa konya aleɛ bekoli, kyɛ bedidi eburo ne ala, na ɛwɔfoɛ mɔ konya aleɛ bekoli wɔ kuro bɔ wabɔ ne anu.

english_verse: And you say, “Let the holy God of Israel hurry up and do what he has promised, so we can see it for ourselves.”
translation_verse: bɛ bɔ bɛnwa, “Ma ye nwo yɛ nyera e, maa ɔyɔ ye adwuma ne ndɛndɛ ma yɛnea e; Yisrael Krongronniɛ ne, ma ye botaeɛ ne opingye ma yɛnea e!”

english_verse: You think you are clever and smart.
translation_verse: Bɛ yaakɔ! Bɛ bɔ bɛdwene kyɛ bɛte nworɛfoɛ, ná bɛdwene kyɛ bɛte badwemma ɔ!

english_verse: And you are great at drinking and mixing drinks. But you are in for trouble.
translation_verse: Bɛ yaakɔ! Bɛ bɔ bale dumaa wɔ nzaanonɛ nu ɔ, ɔne bɛ bɔ bɛbɔ mmɔden wɔ nzaa serɛ frafralɛ nu ɔ.

english_verse: You accept bribes to let the guilty go free, and you cheat the innocent out of a fair trial.
translation_verse: Bɛ yaakɔ! Bɛ bɔ bede fea-ase-ma bebua sona bɔ odi fɔ be ɔ, ɔne bɛ bɔ bebua sona bɔ odi be ndɛengyea ɔ!

english_verse: You will go up in flames like straw and hay! You have rejected the teaching of the holy Lord God All-Powerful of Israel. Now your roots will rot, and your blossoms will turn to dust.
translation_verse: Yiti kyɛbɔ see osi yera ngyɛngyɛma motoo, ɔne kyɛbɔ see wuronyiwuronyi osi yera ndire worowaa ne, sɔ ala yeɛ sɔ mmenia nemɔ bɛ ndii kɔporɔ ɔ, na mvrama kɔporo bɛ nyerɛen kogua kyɛ mvuture, ofikyɛ bapo Asafo AWURADE mmeraa ne, na babu Yisrael Krongronniɛ ne dwirɛ animtia.

english_verse: You are the Lord's people, but you made him terribly angry, and he struck you with his mighty arm. Mountains shook, and dead bodies covered the streets like garbage. The Lord is still angry, and he is ready to strike you again. Foreign Nations Will Attack
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE fɛle ye maen so yaa piri paa, odwɔso tiale bɛ huhuni bɛ, mmokaa mɔ wosole, na bɛ fuin mɔ to petene kyɛ fofoɛ bɔ ogua dwaaso ɔ. Na ɛhemɔ amukoraa nu po ne, wanyakyi bɛ so yaafɛlɛ, na ɔtɛ dwɔso tia bɛ.

english_verse: The Lord has signaled for the foreign nations to come and attack you. He has already whistled, and they are coming as fast as they can.
translation_verse: AWURADE kɔpagya frangaa kohyire dedeede maen maen mɔ, ɔkɔbɔ mvrɛma kɔfrɛ bɛ kofi aseɛ noa dɔ; na nea, bele amirika bɛkɔwa ndɛndɛ!

english_verse: Their arrows are sharp, and their bows are ready. The hoofs of their horses are hard as flint; the wheels of their war chariots turn as fast as a whirlwind.
translation_verse: b’agyaen mɔ yɛ nna, basinasina b’agyaen ne amukoraati, bɛ mbɔngɔ nemɔ gya boen te kyɛ twerɛboɛ, na bɛ teaseɛnam nemɔ betu amirika kyɛ mvrama bɔ ɔpɛ ye nwo ɔ.

english_verse: They roar and growl like fierce young lions as they grab their victims and drag them off where no one can rescue them.
translation_verse: Kyɛbɔ besi bɛbobɔ nu ne, ɔte kyɛ gyata deɛ, na bepo kyɛ gyata akrɔngrɔma mɔ, bɛyɛ bɛ komvi hooo bɛkye bɛ naen, na bɛfa bɛkɔ bɔ ebiala ngora nnne mvi bɛ sa nu ɔ.

english_verse: On the day they attack, they will roar like the ocean. And across the land you will see nothing but darkness and trouble, because the light of day will be covered by thick clouds.
translation_verse: Bekopo bɛ sɔ kyẽa ne, kyɛbɔ ɛpo yɛ wuruwuru ɔ. Na sɛ ɛto wɔ nye nea aseɛ a, awosii ne aworabɔlɛ yeɛ ekonwu ye ɔ, na munungum komundu hyireinn so maa ɔkɔyɛ tunn.

english_verse: In the year that King Uzziah died, I had a vision of the Lord. He was on his throne high above, and his robe filled the temple.
translation_verse: Afoɛ bɔ Nana Yusia wuli ne anu, nwuni AWURADE kyɛ ɔte ahennie bia bɔ so ma paa ɔ so. Né ye ataadeɛ ne noa wayi asɔneyɛɛ sua ne anu tɛkyɛ.

english_verse: Flaming creatures with six wings each were flying over him. They covered their faces with two of their wings and their bodies with two more. They used the other two wings for flying,
translation_verse: Né Serafim mɔ bɛwɔ ye ti so anwuro. Bɛ nu biala le ndaa nzia: bɛ nu biala fa nyɔ kata ye nyunu, ɔfa nyɔ kata ye gya nwo, yeɛ ɔfa nyɔ tu.

english_verse: as they shouted, “Holy, holy, holy, Lord All-Powerful! The earth is filled with your glory.”
translation_verse: Na ebiala tea nu se obiɛngo kyɛ, “Krongron, krongron, Asafo AWURADE te krongron; ye animnyam ayi aseɛ so amukoraa tɛkyɛ.”

english_verse: As they shouted, the doorposts of the temple shook, and the temple was filled with smoke.
translation_verse: Bɛ komvi bɔ bɛfa bɛteane nu ne, ɔmane anoa nemɔ bɛ nyinasoɛ ne wosole, na nwosina yili sua ne anu tɛkyɛ.

english_verse: Then I cried out, “I'm doomed! Everything I say is sinful, and so are the words of everyone around me. Yet I have seen the King, the Lord All-Powerful.”
translation_verse: Na ngane kyɛ, “Edwirɛ ato me oo! Mawu oo! Ofikyɛ nde sona bɔ me noa kekã amumuyɛɛ dwirɛ, yeɛ nde maen bɔ nu ama kekã amumuyɛɛ dwirɛ ɔ nu; ɔnate kyɛ me nye anwu Ɛhene ne, bɔ ye ole Asafo AWURADE!”

english_verse: One of the flaming creatures flew over to me with a burning coal that it had taken from the altar with a pair of metal tongs.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Serafim nemɔ anu ko tu wale me nwo berɛ. Né otira see bɔ ogye bɔ wafa akapɛ waye wafi afɔleɛ bokyea ne aso ɔ.

english_verse: It touched my lips with the hot coal and said, “This has touched your lips. Your sins are forgiven, and you are no longer guilty.”
translation_verse: Ɔfa hane me noa, na osele kyɛ, “Tie, sɔ nikyee ye ahã wɔ noa; baye w’amumuyɛɛ ne bafi wɔ so, na bate wɔ nwo bafi wɔ bɔne nwo.”

english_verse: After this, I heard the Lord ask, “Is there anyone I can send? Will someone speak for us?” “I'll go,” I answered. “Send me!”
translation_verse: Na ndele AWURADE komvi kyɛ obisa kyɛ, “Nwa yeɛ nzoma yeɛ ɔ, nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhɔ kɔma yɛ ɔ?” Na nzele kyɛ, “Me ɛhe, soma me.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to go and speak this message to the people: “You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.” The Lord also said,
translation_verse: Na osele kyɛ, “Kɔ, kɔhã kyire maen he kyɛ, “ ‘Etielɛ de ɛmɔtie, nakoso ɛmɔnde ye bo; ɛnealɛ de ɛmɔnea, nakoso ɛmɔnnwu ye.’

english_verse: “Make these people stubborn! Make them stop up their ears, cover their eyes, and fail to understand. Don't let them turn to me and be healed.”
translation_verse: Ma maen he b’adwene ɔla, ma bɛ so anu yɛ se, ná ma bɛ nye si; wamma ye sɔ a, bɛkɔfa bɛ nye bekonwu nikye, bɛkɔfa bɛ so bɛkɔte dwirɛ, bɛkɔfa b’adwene bɛkɔte dwirɛ bo, ná basakyera maa masa bɛ anwonyerɛ.”

english_verse: Then I asked the Lord, “How long will this last?” The Lord answered: Until their towns are destroyed and their houses are deserted, until their fields are empty,
translation_verse: Yeɛ mmisale kyɛ, “O AWURADE, ɛhe kɔhɔ so alaa maa okoodwu kyinzu?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Kɔpem kyɛ nguro kɔkakyi kurofoen bɔ sona nne so ɔ, ɔne kyɛ awuro mɔ kɔkakyi dandue bɔ sona nne nu ɔ, ɔne kyɛ aseɛ ne kɔsɛkye bɔkɔɔ kɔla berɛ mbaen ɔ,

english_verse: and I have sent them far away, leaving their land in ruins.
translation_verse: kɔpem kyɛ AWURADE kɔpɛ mmenia ne asue kɔhɔ dedeede maa kurofoen nemɔ kɔyɛ pee wɔ aseɛ ne aso ɔ.

english_verse: If only a tenth of the people are left, even they will be destroyed. But just as stumps remain after trees have been cut down, some of my chosen ones will be left.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɔka buru nu ngyɛmuɛ ko wɔ nu po a, bekosa bekowuwu, kyɛ esaa anaa eluii bɔ babu ye bato, bɔ ye dosii tɛ gyi berɛ ɔ.” Bɛ bosofoɛ krongron ne ole dosii ne.

english_verse: When news reached the royal palace that Syria had joined forces with Israel, King Ahaz and everyone in Judah were so terrified that they shook like trees in a windstorm.
translation_verse: Na bɛbɔle Dawide awuro ama mɔ amaneɛ kyɛ, “Siria ne Efraim bayɛ apam” nen, Yuda hene Ahase ne ye mmenia bɛ nwo wosole bɛ tɛtɛtɛtɛ kyɛ ɛhɔayeɛ nu mmakaa bɔ mvrama woso bɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said to me: Take your son Shearjashub and go see King Ahaz. You will find him on the road near the cloth makers' shops at the end of the canal that brings water from the upper pool.
translation_verse: Nakoso AWURADE sele Yesaya kyɛ, “Kɔ ná koyia Ahase, ɛne ɛwa Sea-Yasubo wɔ anwuro dɔ ɛkwaa ne noa, wɔ atapoɛ atee ne aso dɔ,

english_verse: Tell Ahaz to stop worrying. There's no need for him to be afraid of King Rezin and King Pekah. They are very angry, but they are nothing more than a dying fire. Ahaz doesn't need to fear
translation_verse: ná se ye kyɛ, Gyina pindinn, yɛ konn, nnɛsuro, yeɛ nnɛma wɔ kunu tete wɔ wɔ gyetia nyɔ hemɔ bɔ begye monɛɛmonɛɛ ne anwo, bɔ bɛ ole Sirianiɛ Resin ɔne Remalia awa ne bɛ yaa hahii bɔ bafɛ ne.

english_verse: to invade and defeat Judah and Jerusalem and to let the son of Tabeel be king in his place.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔma yɛɛtua Yuda ma ahunundetelɛ tɔ ye so, ná yɛli so ngonim, ná yɛfa Tabeel awa bienzua ne yɛli so hene.”

english_verse: I, the Lord, promise that this will never happen.
translation_verse: Ye sɔ ne ati, AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Sɔ porɛ ne ngogyina, yeɛ ɔngɔyɔ adwuma.

english_verse: Damascus is just the capital of Syria, and King Rezin rules only in Damascus. Samaria is just the capital of Israel, and King Pekah rules only in Samaria. But in less than
translation_verse: Efraim ahenguro ole Samaria, yeɛ Remalia awa ne yeɛ ɔla Samaria noa ɔ. Na sɛ ɛmɔanne banni a, nahorɛ nu, ɛmɔngɔhora ɛmɔ gya nu gyina.” Yimanuel ne te sɛngyerɛnneɛ

english_verse: “Ask me for proof that my promise will come true. Ask for something to happen deep in the world of the dead or high in the heavens above.”
translation_verse: “Bisa sɛngyerɛnneɛ bie fi AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ berɛ; kyɛ ɔkɔ kuronn kyɛ ɛborɔ dɔ oo, anaa ɔkɔ anwuro anwuro kyɛ nyameɛso oo.”

english_verse: “No, Lord,” Ahaz answered. “I won't test you!”
translation_verse: Nakoso Ahase buale kyɛ, “Mengobisa, yeɛ mengoso AWURADE mengɔnea.”

english_verse: Then I said: Listen, every one of you in the royal family of David. You have already tried my patience. Now you are trying God's patience by refusing to ask for proof.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yesaya sele kyɛ, “O Dawide awuro ama, ɛ́mɔtie! Ɛmɔnwa nzɛ ɔte edwirɛ baa kyɛ ɛmɔma ɛmɔ nwo yɛ mmenia ahi, bɔ yeɛ ɛmɔama ɛmɔ nwo ayɛ me Nyameɛ koso ahi ye?

english_verse: But the Lord will still give you proof. A virgin is pregnant; she will have a son and will name him Immanuel.
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE bɔbɔ kɔma ɛmɔ sɛngyerɛnneɛ. Ɛ́mɔtie! taluwa bie kɔnwonzɛ kɔwo baa bienzua, na ɔkɔto ye dumaa Yimanuel.

english_verse: Even before the boy is old enough to know how to choose between right and wrong, he will eat yogurt and honey, and the countries of the two kings you fear will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ, aseɛ bɔ so ahemvo nyɔ bama ahunundetelɛ atɔ wɔ so ne, ɔkɔkakyi kurofoen koraka né akwadaa ne anwu kyɛ ɔkɔpo bɔne, ɔne kyɛ ɔkɔfa paa ɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord will make more trouble for your people and your kingdom than any of you have known since Israel broke away from Judah. He will even bring the king of Assyria to attack you. The Threat of an Invasion
translation_verse: “AWURADE kɔma mmerɛ bie kɔto wɔ ne wɔ maen ne wɔ baba awuro ama, bɔ sɔ mmerɛ ne ɔttole ɛmɔ le, ofi mmerɛ bɔ Efraim tele ye nwo fili Yuda nwo ɔ. Ɔkɔfa Asiria hene so.

english_verse: When that time comes, the Lord will whistle, and armies will come from Egypt like flies and from Assyria like bees.
translation_verse: “Sɔ mmerɛ ne, AWURADE kɔbɔ mvrɛma kɔfrɛ nwɔsea bɔ bɛwɔ Misraim asue mɔ bɛ sorɔ dɔ, ɔne ɛwommaa bɔ bɛwɔ Asiria aseɛ so ɔ.

english_verse: They will settle everywhere—in the deep valleys and between the rocks, on every thornbush and all over the pastureland.
translation_verse: Bɛ mukoraa bɛkɔwa bɛkɔɔtenatena kongonyi nemɔ anu, nyɔbotaen ndokuro nemɔ anu, ndire mmowue mmowue ne nzenzaen amukoraa so.

english_verse: The Lord will pay the king of Assyria to bring a razor from across the Euphrates River and shave your head and every hair on your body, including your beard.
translation_verse: “Sɔ mmerɛ ne, dɛmaa bɔ AWURADE abɔ ye paa wafi asue Yufreti si dɔ, bɔ ye ole Asiria hene ne, ɔkɔfa kopia ɛmɔ ti nwiaa ne ɛmɔ nwo nwiaa, na ɔkɔye ɛmɔ kanza koso.

english_verse: Anyone who is able to save only one young cow and two sheep,
translation_verse: “Na ɔkɔwa kyɛ, sɔ mmerɛ ne, sona kosie nandwie beleɛ akrɔngrɔma ko ne mmoaen nyɔ,

english_verse: will have enough milk to make yogurt. In fact, everyone left in the land will eat yogurt and honey.
translation_verse: na ɔnate nyɔfonesue pee bɔ okonya ye ne ati, okoli nandwie nyɔfonesue nye loe; ofikyɛ ebiala bɔ ɔkɔha aseɛ ne aso ne, nandwie nyɔfonesue nye loe ne woɛ yeɛ okoli ɔ.

english_verse: You will go there to hunt with your bow and arrows, because the whole country will be covered with thornbushes.
translation_verse: Agyaen ne agyaen mmakaa yeɛ mmenia kɔfa kɔwa berɛ ɔ, ofikyɛ aseɛ ne amukoraa kɔkakyi agurɛ ne mmowue.

english_verse: The hills where you once planted crops will be overgrown with thorns and thistles. You will be afraid to go there, and your cattle, sheep, and goats will be turned loose on those hills.
translation_verse: Na pambaa amukoraa bɔ né bɛfa kona bɛyɔ so boo ne, agurɛ ne mmowue nemɔ ati ebiala ngɔhɔ berɛ; na mmom bɛkɔkakyi nekaa bɔ bɛyakyi nandwie ne mmoaen maa bɛkɔ adidie ɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Isaiah, get something to write on. Then write in big clear letters the name, MAHER-SHALAL-HASH-BAZ.
translation_verse: Afei AWURADE sele me kyɛ, “Fa nyɔboɛ pirikua taataa bɔ bɛkyerɛ so ɔ, ná twerɛ bɔ sona kɔkenga kɔte ye bo ɔ, kyɛ, ‘Maheri Sala Hasibase’.

english_verse: I will tell Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah to serve as witnesses to this.”
translation_verse: Na mmane ɔsɔfo Yuria ne Yeberekia awa Sakaria bɛhyerɛ bɛmane me bɛyɛle ye nwo adanzefoɛ nahorɛfoɛ.”

english_verse: Sometime later, my wife and I had a son, and the Lord said, “Name him Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz.
translation_verse: Afei me ne ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ braa ne yɛlale, ɔnwonzɛle, na ɔwole bienzua. Na AWURADE sele me kyɛ, “To ye dumaa Maheri Sala Hasibase,

english_verse: Because before he can say ‘Mommy’ or ‘Daddy,’ the king of Assyria will attack and take everything of value from Damascus and Samaria.”
translation_verse: ofikyɛ, anzana akwadaa ne konwu ‘Baba anaa Mooni’ kã ne, né Asiria hene wasoa Damasko anwonya ne Samaria koɛ nu nzesadeɛ wahɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord spoke to me again and said:
translation_verse: Yeɛ AWURADE sa sele me kyɛ,
