translation_verse: Na mvale akotokyiwa mɔ bɔ nzaa ayiyi bɛ tɛkyɛtɛkyɛɛ ɔ ne awaa mɔ nziesiele Rekabofoɛ nemɔ nyunu, na nzele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔno nzaa ne.”

english_verse: But they answered: No! The ancestor of our clan, Jonadab son of Rechab, made a rule that we must obey. He said, “Don't ever drink wine
translation_verse: Nakoso bebuale kyɛ, “Yɛngɔno nzaa biala, ofikyɛ yɛ nana Yonadabo bɔ ye baba ole Rekabo ne, ɔfale ahyɛdeɛ mane yɛ kyɛ, ‘Nnɛma ɛmɔno nzaa kyẽa biala le, ɛmɔ ne ɛmɔ boso ama mɔ;

english_verse: or build houses or plant crops and vineyards. Instead, you must always live in tents and move from place to place. If you obey this command, you will live a long time.”
translation_verse: onni kyɛ ɛmɔsi sua anaa ɛmɔdua nikyee anaa ɛmɔyɛ bobe boo, yeɛ onni kyɛ ɛmɔnya nu biala, na mmom odi kyɛ ɛmɔtena ɛtena sua nu ɛmɔ ngoa amukoraa, amaa ɔnate so ɛmɔatena ase bahyɛ wɔ aseɛ bɔ ɛmɔayɛ ɛwɔfoɛ wɔ so ne aso.’

english_verse: Our clan has always obeyed Jonadab's command. To this very day, we and our wives and sons and daughters don't drink wine or build houses or plant vineyards or crops. And we have lived in tents,
translation_verse: na mmom yatena ɛtena sua nu, na yatie ahyɛdeɛ bɔ yɛ nana Yonadabo fa mane yɛ ne amukoraa yali so.

english_verse: except now we have to live inside Jerusalem because Nebuchadnezzar has taken over the countryside with his army from Babylonia and Syria.
translation_verse: Nakoso mmerɛ bɔ Babilɔn hene Nebukadenesa fale koɛ ɔɔtoale maen ne nen, yɛhane kyɛ, ‘Ɛmɔbra maa yɛhɔ Yerusalem, ɔnate Kaldeafoɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ ne Siriafoɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ bɛ nwo suronyi ti.’ Na ɛhe ati yeɛ ɔmaa yɛte Yerusalem ɔ.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, want you to learn a lesson
translation_verse: “Asafo AWURADE, Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Kɔhã kyire Yudafoɛ ne Yerusalemfoɛ kyɛ, Aso ɛmɔngole foɛtulɛ bɛngɔto nu ná ɛmɔngotie me dwirɛ anaa? AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: from the Rechabite clan. Their ancestor Jonadab told his descendants never to drink wine, and to this very day they have obeyed him. But I have spoken to you over and over, and you haven't obeyed me!
translation_verse: Ahyɛdeɛ bɔ Rekabo awa Yonadabo ɔfa mane ye boso ama kyɛ nnɛmaa bɛno nzaa ne, bali so, na ɔbaadwu ɛnɛ ye, bɛnno nzaa biala, na mmom bedi bɛ nana ahyɛdeɛ so. Na ɛmɔ de, madwudwo mahyire ɛmɔ alaa, nakoso ɛmɔandie me dwirɛ.

english_verse: You refused to listen to my prophets, who kept telling you, “Stop doing evil and worshiping other gods! Start obeying the Lord, and he will let you live in this land he gave your ancestors.”
translation_verse: Mahɔ so masoma me somvoɛ ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ amukoraa wɔ ɛmɔ berɛ dee kyɛ, ‘Odi kyɛ ɛmɔ anu biala sakyera ye adwene wɔ ye bɔne atee nwo, ná ɔbɔ bra paa; na nnɛma ɛmɔkodi nyameɛ foforɛ mɔ si bɛso bɛ, amaa ɔnate so ɛmɔatena aseɛ bɔ mva mane ɛmɔ ne ɛmɔ nana mɔ ne aso. Nakoso ɛmɔanyɛ asoɛ bandie me dwirɛ.

english_verse: The Rechabites have obeyed the command of their ancestor Jonadab, but you have not obeyed me,
translation_verse: Rekabo awa Yonadabo ye boso ama bali ahyɛdeɛ bɔ bɛ nana fa mane bɛ ne aso, nakoso maen he de, bandie me dwirɛ.

english_verse: your God. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warned you about the terrible things that would happen to you if you did not listen to me. But you have ignored me, so now disaster will strike you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to the Rechabites
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE, Asafo Nyameɛ, Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Ɛ́mɔtie, musue amukoraa bɔ ngane kyɛ ngɔmaa ɔkɔwa Yuda ne Yerusalemfoɛ amukoraa bɛ so ne, ngɔprapra ngogua bɛ so; ofikyɛ madwudwo mahyire bɛ, nakoso bandie; mafrɛ bɛ, nakoso bandɛ me so.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to the Rechabite clan: “I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You have obeyed your ancestor Jonadab,
translation_verse: Na Rekabofoɛ nemɔ de, Yeremia sele bɛ kyɛ, “Asafo AWURADE, Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa: Ɔnate kyɛ ɛmɔali ɛmɔ nana Yonadabo ahyɛdeɛ so, ná ɛmɔali ye nhyehyɛleɛ amukoraa so, ná ɛmɔayɔ bɔ wahyɛ ɛmɔ ne amukoraa ne ati,

english_verse: so I promise that your clan will be my servants and will never die out.”
translation_verse: yiti Asafo AWURADE, Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Sona bɔ okogyina me nyunu ɔ, ɔngɔbɔ Rekabo awa Yonadabo le.”

english_verse: During the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, the Lord said to me, “Jeremiah,
translation_verse: Yuda hene Yehoakim bɔ ye baba ole Yosia ne, ye ahennie afoɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so nna ne anu, AWURADE dwirɛ bɔ ɔlale ye ali hyirele Yeremia ole kyɛ,

english_verse: since the time Josiah was king, I have been speaking to you about Israel, Judah, and the other nations. Now, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you,
translation_verse: “Fa nwomaa bɔ babobɔ ɔ, na nikyee amukoraa bɔ mahã mahyire wɔ kyɛ ngɔyɔ ngotia Yisrael ne Yuda ne maen maen amukoraa, ofi kyẽa bɔ ndwudwo ngyirele wɔ, ofi Yosia aberɛ so bɔ ɔbaadwu ɛnɛ ne, kyerɛ gua nu.

english_verse: then read it to the people of Judah. Maybe they will stop sinning when they hear what terrible things I plan for them. And if they turn back to me, I will forgive them.”
translation_verse: Ebiaa Yuda awuro ama bɛkɔte musue amukoraa bɔ mayɛ m’adwene kyɛ ngɔprapra ngogua bɛ so ne, amaa ɔnate so ebiala asakyera ye adwene wafi ye bɔne atee nwo, ná mafa b’amumuyɛɛ ne bɛ bɔne mahyɛ bɛ.”

english_verse: I sent for Baruch son of Neriah and asked him to help me. I repeated everything the Lord had told me, and Baruch wrote it all down on a scroll.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yeremia frɛle Baruku bɔ ye baba ole Neria ne, na AWURADE dwirɛ amukoraa bɔ ɔhã hyirele Yeremia ne, Yeremia hã mane Baruku hyerɛ guale nwomaa bɔ babobɔ ɔ bie anu.

english_verse: Then I said, Baruch, the officials refuse to let me go into the Lord's temple,
translation_verse: Na Yeremia fale ahyɛdeɛ mane Baruku kyɛ, “Me de, bato me nu bɔ mengɔhora mengɔhɔ AWURADE awuro berɛ ɔ;

english_verse: so you must go instead. Wait for the next holy day when the people of Judah come to the temple to pray and to go without eating. Then take this scroll to the temple and read it aloud.
translation_verse: yiti kɔ AWURADE awuro berɛ akɔngyere kyẽa, na AWURADE dwirɛ bɔ nga maa ɛhyerɛle ne, kenga fi nwomaa bɔ babobɔ ne anu maa maen ne bɛte. Afei koso, kenga ma Yudafoɛ amukoraa bɔ befi bɛ nguro mɔ so bawa ne bɛte.

english_verse: The Lord is furious, and if the people hear how he is going to punish them, maybe they will ask to be forgiven.
translation_verse: Ebiaa bɛkɔfa bɛ sufrɛ bɛkɔto AWURADE nyunu, na bɛ nu biala kɔsakyera ye adwene kofi ye bɔne atee nwo, ofikyɛ AWURADE ɛyaafɛlɛ ne ahonehulɛ bɔ wahã kyɛ ɔkɔmaa ɔkɔwa maen he aso ne, ɔte piri.”

english_verse: In the ninth month of the fifth year that Jehoiakim was king, the leaders set a day when everyone who lived in Jerusalem or who was visiting there had to pray and go without eating. So Baruch took the scroll to the upper courtyard of the temple. He went over to the side of the courtyard and stood in a covered area near New Gate, where he read the scroll aloud. This covered area belonged to Gemariah, one of the king's highest officials.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Baruku kengale Yeremia noa dwirɛ fili nwomaa ne anu wɔ AWURADE awuro berɛ hyirele maen ne amukoraa maa bɛtele. Ɔkengale ye wɔ Gemaria bɔ ye baba ole ahyerɛlɛniɛ Safan ye pumbu bɔ ɔwɔ aborɔsaen so, bɔ ɔwɔ AWURADE awuro berɛ Anoa Foforɛ ne anu berɛ ne.

english_verse: Gemariah's son Micaiah was there and heard Baruch read what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Makaya bɔ ye baba ole Gemaria bɔ ye baba ole Safan ne, ɔtele AWURADE dwirɛ amukoraa bɔ ofi nwomaa ne anu ne,

english_verse: When Baruch finished reading, Micaiah went down to the palace. His father Gemariah was in the officials' room, meeting with the rest of the king's officials, including Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, and Zedekiah.
translation_verse: ɔhɔle ahyerɛlɛniɛ ne pumbu ne anu wɔ ahemvie berɛ. Né atitirefoɛ nemɔ amukoraa bɛtete berɛ. Bɛ ole ahyerɛlɛniɛ Elisama, Delaya bɔ ye baba ole Semaya ne, Elnatan bɔ ye baba ole Akibɔ ne, Gemaria bɔ ye baba ole Safan ne, Sedekia bɔ ye baba ole Hanania ne, yeɛ atitirefoɛ nemɔ amukoraa.

english_verse: Micaiah told them what he had heard Baruch read to the people.
translation_verse: Na Makaya hane edwirɛ amukoraa bɔ ɔtele mmerɛ bɔ Baruku kengale nwomaa ne hyirele maen ne ne.

english_verse: the officials said, “Please sit down and read it to us,” which he did.
translation_verse: Na besele ye kyɛ, “Tena ase ná kenga maa yɛtie.” Yiti Baruku kengale maa betiele.

english_verse: After they heard what was written on the scroll, they were worried and said to each other, “The king needs to hear this!” Turning to Baruch, they asked,
translation_verse: Na ɔwale kyɛ, bɛtele sɔ dwirɛ ne amukoraa nen, bɛ nwo dwirili bɛ maa ebiala neane obiɛngo nyunu, na besele Baruku kyɛ, “Odi kyɛ yɛfa edwirɛ he amukoraa yɛkɔbɔ Nana amaneɛ.”

english_verse: “Did someone tell you what to write on this scroll?”
translation_verse: Yeɛ bebisale Baruku kyɛ, “Kã kyire yɛ, ɛyɛle sɛɛ yeɛ ɛhyerɛle ye noa dwirɛ he amukoraa ɔ?”

english_verse: The officials said, “You and Jeremiah must go into hiding, and don't tell anyone where you are going.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ atitire nemɔ sele Baruku kyɛ, “Ɛne Yeremia, ɛmɔɔfea, na nnɛmɔma ebiala nwu ɛmɔ si atee.” Nana Yehoakim yera nwomaa ne

english_verse: The king told his son Jerahmeel to take Seraiah and Shelemiah and to go arrest Baruch and me. But the Lord kept them from finding us. Jeremiah's Second Scroll
translation_verse: Yeɛ ɛhene ne fale ahyɛdeɛ mane ɔwa bienzua Yerameel ne Seraya bɔ ye baba ole Asriɛl ne Selemia bɔ ye baba ole Abideel ne kyɛ bɛɛhye ahyerɛlɛniɛ Baruku ne ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ Yeremia bɛbra, nakoso AWURADE fale bɛ feale.

english_verse: I had told Baruch what to write on that first scroll, but King Jehoiakim had burned it. So the Lord told me
translation_verse: Na ɛhene ne yerale nwomaa ne anu dwirɛ bɔ Yeremia hane ma Baruku hyerɛle ne yiele nen, afei AWURADE lale ye dwirɛ ali hyirele Yeremia kyɛ,

english_verse: Then he told me to say to King Jehoiakim: Not only did you burn Jeremiah's scroll, you had the nerve to ask why he had written that the king of Babylonia would attack and ruin the land, killing all the people and even the animals.
translation_verse: Na Yuda hene Yehoakim de, se ye kyɛ, ‘AWURADE nwa nyoo: Ayera nwomaa he, na ɛnwa, “Nzu ati yeɛ ahyerɛ ye wɔ nu kyɛ, amba, Babilɔn hene kɔwa kɔɔsɛkye maen he, ná okonua mmenia ne ngaka bɛ boso kofi so ɔ?”

english_verse: So I, the Lord, promise that you will be killed and your body thrown out on the ground. The sun will beat down on it during the day, and the frost will settle on it at night. And none of your descendants will ever be king of Judah.
translation_verse: Yiti bɔ AWURADE ɔkã fa Yuda hene Yehoakim nwo ɛhe: Ongonya koliagyaa maa ɔngɔtena Dawide ahennie bia ne aso, na bekogyi ye fuin bɛkɔto maa eyia kɔbɔ ye eyia, ná ɛyerɛ ahu ye kɔngɔen.

english_verse: You, your children, and your servants are evil, and I will punish everyone of you. I warned you and the people of Judah and Jerusalem that I would bring disaster, but none of you have listened. So now you are doomed!
translation_verse: Na ngɔhwe ye ne ye boso ama ne ye somvoɛ mɔ bɛ so, ɔnate b’amumuyɛɛ ti. Na bɛ ne Yerusalemfoɛ ne Yudafoɛ, musue amukoraa bɔ ngane kyɛ ngɔmaa ɔkɔto bɛ ne, ngɔprapra ngogua bɛ so, nakoso bengotie.’ ”

english_verse: After the Lord finished speaking to me, I got another scroll and gave it to Baruch. Then I told him what to write, so this second scroll would contain even more than was on the scroll Jehoiakim had burned.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yeremia fale nwomaa bɔ babobɔ ɔ foforɛ, na ɔfa mane ahyerɛlɛniɛ Baruku bɔ ye baba ole Neria ne. Ye yeɛ Yeremia hane nwomaa ko bɔ Yuda hene Yehoakim fale see yerale ye ne anu dwirɛ amukoraa maa ɔhyerɛle ɔ, na ɔfale edwirɛ bɔ ɔte kyɛ sɔ dwirɛ nemɔ ɔ pee bokale so.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead.
translation_verse: Sedekia bɔ ye baba ole Yosia ne, Babilɔn hene Nebukadenesa fale ye lili Yuda maen so hene, na osili Yehoakim awa Konia gya nu lili hene.

english_verse: But Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Judah ignored everything the Lord had told me.
translation_verse: Nakoso ye oo, ye somvoɛ mɔ oo, aseɛ ne aso ama oo, bandie AWURADE dwirɛ bɔ ɔnate ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ Yeremia so hane ne.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to send them back to Zedekiah with this message: Zedekiah, you wanted Jeremiah to ask me, the Lord God of Israel, what is going to happen. So I will tell you. The king of Egypt and his army came to your rescue, but soon they will go back to Egypt.
translation_verse: “AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Yuda hene bɔ ɔsomane ɛmɔ me berɛ kyɛ ɛmɔɔbisa me noa dwirɛ ne, ɛmɔhã behyire ye kyɛ, ‘Tie, Faro koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛɛbokale wɔ ne, bekosa bɛkɔhɔ Misraim, bɛ bɔbɔ bɛ maen nu.

english_verse: Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire.
translation_verse: Na Kaldeafoɛ nemɔ bekosa bɛkɔwa bɛkɔfa koɛ bɛkɔɔtoa kuro he. Bekoli so ngonim, na bɛkɔto nu see.

english_verse: Don't fool yourselves into thinking that the Babylonians will leave as they did before.
translation_verse: AWURADE nwa nyoo: Nnɛma ɛmɔlakalaka ɛmɔ nwo bɛkã kyɛ, “Kaldeafoɛ nemɔ bekofi yɛ nwo wa bɛkɔhɔ,” ofikyɛ bengofi wa bɛngɔhɔ.

english_verse: Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire. Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ Kaldeafoɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa bɔ bafa koɛ baatoa ɛmɔ ne, sɛ ɛmɔdi bɛ so ngonim, ná ɔka bɛ mmenia bɔ bapurapura angome twe po a, bɛ nu biala kodwɔso kofi ye tena sua nu, na bɛkɔfa see bɛkɔɔyera kuro he.’ ” Besa bɛto Yeremia kuku nu

english_verse: The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us.
translation_verse: Na ɔwale kyɛ, mmerɛ bɔ Kaldeafoɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ befili Yerusalem, ɔnate Faro koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ né bɛ́ba ne ati nen,

english_verse: So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land.
translation_verse: Yeremia sili nu fili Yerusalem kyɛ ɔkɔ Benyamin aseɛ so okode ye aseɛ deɛ ofi berɛ ama nemɔ, bɛ dɔ.

english_verse: I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
translation_verse: Odwuli Benyamin pambim ne anu ne, né wɛmvoɛ mɔ so panyi bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Yiriya, bɔ ye baba ole Selemia bɔ ye baba ole Hanania ne, ɔwɔ berɛ. Ɔhyele ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ Yeremia, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Wɔ, ɛnwati fa wɔ nwo kɔbɔ Kaldeafoɛ!”

english_verse: “I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yeremia buale kyɛ, “Daabi, ɔtte nahorɛ. Mennwati memva me nwo mengɔmmɔ Kaldeafoɛ.” Nakoso Yiriya wandie bɔ Yeremia kã ne, na ɔhyele ye fale ye hɔle mbanyi mɔ nyunu.

english_verse: King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?” “Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
translation_verse: Afei Nana Sedekia somane maa bɛɛfale ye bɛwale ye nyunu. Na Nana bisale ye mvealeɛ nu wɔ ye awuro berɛ kyɛ, “Aso AWURADE ala edwirɛ bie ali wahyire wɔ anaa?” Yeɛ Yeremia buale kyɛ, “Yoo, edwirɛ wɔ berɛ.” Afei Yeremia toale so kyɛ, “Bɛkɔfa wɔ bekowura Babilɔn hene sa.”

english_verse: Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation?
translation_verse: Yeremia sa bisale Nana Sedekia kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ tɛɛ yeɛ mayɔ wɔ anaa wɔ mbanyi anaa maen he bɔ ɛmɔafa me bato kuku nu ye?

english_verse: Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem?
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ bɔ bɛhyɛle ɛmɔ ngɔm kyɛ, ‘Babilɔn hene ɔngɔfa koɛ ngɔtoa ɛmɔ ne maen he’ ne, bɛwɔ nisua?

english_verse: Please, don't send me back to that prison at Jonathan's house. If you do, I will die there.”
translation_verse: Ao Nana, me mene, mesrɛ wɔ, tie m’abisadeɛ bɔ méfa méto wɔ nyunu ye, na nnɛmaa besa bɛfa me bɛkɔto ahyerɛlɛniɛ Yonatan awuro dɔ, ná mangɔanwu dɔ.”

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
translation_verse: Yiti Nana Sedekia hyɛle maa bɛfale Yeremia bɛɛtole kuku nu aluo berɛ, na daa biala né bɛma ye paanoo mumua ko fi paanootonɛfoɛ borɔnoɛ so kɔpem kyɛ kuro berɛ paanoo amukoraa yiele ɔ. Yiti Yeremia hale kuku nu aluo berɛ.

english_verse: So the four of them went to the king and said, “You should put Jeremiah to death, because he is making the soldiers and everyone else lose hope. He isn't trying to help our people; he's trying to harm them.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ mbanyi nemɔ hã hyirele ɛhene ne kyɛ, “Yɛsrɛ wɔ, maa behũ akoaa he, ofikyɛ ɔnate ye dwirɛ bɔ ɔkekã kyire bɛ ne aso, obu koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ baha kuro ye anu, ɔne maen ne amukoraa b’abasa nu. Ofikyɛ akoaa he ɔmbena maen he yé, na mmom ɔpena ye ne tɛɛ.”

english_verse: Zedekiah replied, “Do what you want with him. I can't stop you.”
translation_verse: Na Nana Sedekia sele kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔtie, ɔwɔ ɛmɔ sa nu, ofikyɛ me bɔ nde ɛhene ne, mengɔhora mengotu ɛmɔ noa dwirɛ mengogua.”

english_verse: Then they took me back to the courtyard of the palace guards and let me down with ropes into the well that belonged to Malchiah, the king's son. There was no water in the well, but I sank down in the mud.
translation_verse: Yiti bɛhyele Yeremia, na beegyili ye bɛtole Nana awa Malkiya ye abura bɔ ɔwɔ kuku nu aluo berɛ ne anu. Bɛfale nyamaa yeɛ bedwurale Yeremia bɛtole nu ɔ. Né nzue nne abura ne anu, na mmom asaa ngome, na Yeremia mene wɔ asaa ne anu. Yitiopianiɛ bie pepɛ de Yeremia

english_verse: Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
translation_verse: “Nana, me mene, bɔ mmenia hemɔ bafa bali ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ Yeremia ne amukoraa, bayɔ bɔne. Bafa ye bato kumaa nu kuku nu kyɛ ɛhɔen hu ye maa owu wɔ nekaa bɔ ɔwɔ ne, ofikyɛ aleɛ biala nne kuro ye anu.”

english_verse: Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well.
translation_verse: Yiti Ebede Meleke fale mmenia ne bokale ye nwo so, na ɔhɔle ahemvie berɛ nekaa bɔ bɛfa nningyein besie ne. Ɔɔfale ndangurɛ ne ndaadeɛ teterewaa, na ɔfale nyamaa dwurale sɔ nningyein ne ase mane Yeremia wɔ abura ne anu.

english_verse: Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did,
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yitiopianiɛ Ebede Meleke sele Yeremia kyɛ, “Fa ndangurɛ ne, ɔne ndaadeɛ teterewaa nemɔ wura wɔ mvorɔma nu wɔ nyamaa ne abo.” Na Yeremia yɔle sɔ.

english_verse: the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards. King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
translation_verse: Yeɛ bɛfale nyamaa ne bɛtwetwene Yeremia bɛyele ye befili abura ne anu. Na Yeremia hale kuku nu aluo berɛ. Sedekia ne Yeremia mvealeɛ nu ngɔmɔ

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me brought to his private entrance to the temple, and he said, “I'm going to ask you something, and I want to know the truth.”
translation_verse: Nana Sedekia somane maa bɛɛfale ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ Yeremia bɛbrɛle ye wɔ AWURADE awuro berɛ anoa bɔ ɔtɔ so nza ne anyunu berɛ. Yeɛ ɛhene ne sele Yeremia kyɛ, “Mebaabisa wɔ dwirɛ; nnɛfa hwee fea me.”

english_verse: He said, “I swear in the name of the living Lord our Creator that I won't have you killed. No one else can hear what we say, and I won't let anyone kill you.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Sedekia feale ye nwo tale ndaen hyirele Yeremia kyɛ, “Kyɛ AWURADE bɔ ɔbɔle yɛ kra ɔte ase ye, mengohu wɔ, yeɛ mengɔfa wɔ mengowura bɛ bɔ bɛpena wɔ beku wɔ nemɔ bɛ sa.”

english_verse: Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yeremia sele Sedekia kyɛ, AWURADE Asafo Nyameɛ, Yisrael Nyameɛ ne, ɔnwa nyoo: Sɛ ekofite kɔfa wɔ nwo kɔɔma Babilɔn hene mbanyi nemɔ a, ye de ekonya wɔ ti kodidi nu, bɛngɔfa see bɛngɔyera kuro ye, yeɛ ɛne wɔ awuro ama ɛmɔkonya ngoa.

english_verse: But if you don't surrender, I will let the Babylonian army capture Jerusalem and burn it down, and you will be taken prisoner.”
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ amvite amva wɔ nwo angɔamma Babilɔn hene mbanyi nemɔ a, ye de, kuro ye koowura Kaldeafoɛ bɛ sa, na bɛkɔfa see bɛkɔto nu bɛkɔyera ye, na engonya wɔ ti ngodidi nu ngofi bɛ sa nu.”

english_verse: Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Nana Sedekia sele Yeremia kyɛ, “Mesuro Yudafoɛ bɔ baafa bɛ nwo bama Kaldeafoɛ ne. Annea a, né Kaldeafoɛ bafa me bawura bɛ sa maa bagoro me nwo.”

english_verse: I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yeremia buale kyɛ, Bɛngɔfa wɔ bengowura bɛ sa. Mesrɛ wɔ, tie AWURADE noa dwirɛ bɔ mekã mekyire wɔ ye, na okoyie wɔ yé, na wɔ kra konya ye ti kodidi nu.

english_verse: But the Lord has shown me that if you refuse to obey,
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ ambene so amvite a, ye de, edwirɛ bɔ AWURADE ala ye ali wahyire me ole kyɛ,

english_verse: then the women of your palace will be taken prisoner by Nebuchadnezzar's officials. And those women will say to you: Friends you trusted led you astray. Now you're trapped in mud, and those friends you trusted have all turned away.
translation_verse: Tie, mmrasua amukoraa bɔ baha wɔ Yuda hene ahemvie ne, bɛkɔfa bɛ bekofite bɛkɔɔma Babilɔn hene mbanyi mɔ, na mmrasua nemɔ kɔhã kyɛ, ‘Wɔ mmango mɔ balakalaka wɔ bali wɔ so ngonim; afei bɔ wɔ gya atimu asaa nu ye, bakakyi bɛ si bama wɔ.’

english_verse: The Babylonian army will take your wives and children captive, you will be taken as a prisoner to the King of Babylonia, and Jerusalem will be burned down.”
translation_verse: Bɛkɔfa ɛye mɔ amukoraa ne wɔ mma mɔ bekofite bɛkɔɔma Kaldeafoɛ. Wɔ wora, engonya wɔ ti ngodidi nu ngofi bɛ sa nu, na mmom Babilɔn hene kɔhye wɔ, na kuro he de, bɛkɔfa see bɛkɔto nu bɛkɔyera ye.”

english_verse: Zedekiah said, “Jeremiah, if you tell anyone what we have talked about, you might lose your life.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Sedekia sele Yeremia kyɛ, “Nnɛbɔ edwirɛ he aso kyire ebiala, na bengohu wɔ.

english_verse: And I'm sure that if my officials hear about our meeting, they will ask you what we said to each other. They might even threaten to kill you if you don't tell them.
translation_verse: Sɛ mbanyi nemɔ bɛte kyɛ me ne wɔ yali ngɔmɔ, ná bɛba wɔ berɛ bɛbase wɔ kyɛ, ‘Edwirɛ bɔ ɛhã hyirele Nana, ɔne bɔ Nana ɔhã hyirele wɔ ne, kã kyire yɛ; nnɛfa hwee fea yɛ, na yɛngohu wɔ’ a,

english_verse: So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
translation_verse: ye de kã kyire bɛ kyɛ, ‘Mvale me dwirɛ ndole Nana nyunu kyɛ nnɛmaa ɔmaa besa bɛfa me bɛkɔ Yonatan awuro maa mekowu dɔ.’ ”

english_verse: The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.
translation_verse: Yeɛ mbanyi nemɔ amukoraa bɛwale Yeremia berɛ beebisale ye, na ɔhane edwirɛ amukoraa bɔ ɛhene ne hyɛle ye kyɛ ɔhã ne hyirele bɛ. Yiti bɛpɛle edwirɛ ne aso, ofikyɛ né ebiala ɔttele edwirɛ ne.

english_verse: I was held in the courtyard of the palace guards until the day Jerusalem was captured.
translation_verse: Na Yeremia hale kuku nu aluo berɛ kɔpem kyẽa bɔ belili Yerusalem so ngonim ɔ. [Na belili Yerusalem so ngonim ne, né ɔtɛ wɔ berɛ.]

english_verse: When King Zedekiah and his troops saw that Jerusalem had been captured, they tried to escape from the city that same night. They went to the king's garden, where they slipped through the gate between the two city walls and headed toward the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Na ɔwale kyɛ, mmerɛ bɔ Yuda hene Sedekia ne koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ amukoraa benwuni bɛ ne, bɛnwatili. Bɛfale ɛhene turo ne anu bɛɛfale pambim bɔ ɔla fasue nyɔ nemɔ b’afia ne anu befili kuro berɛ kɔngɔen, na bɛfale bɛ nye behyirele aseɛ pralaa ne aso.

english_verse: to Ebedmelech from Ethiopia: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I warned everyone that I would bring disaster, not prosperity, to this city. Now very soon I will do what I said, and you will see it happen.
translation_verse: “Kɔ ná kɔhã kyire Yitiopianiɛ Ebede Meleke kyɛ, ‘Asafo AWURADE, Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Tie, me dwirɛ bɔ mahã mafa kuro he anwo, kyɛ ngɔfa bɔ ɔtte mayee ngoli ye, na mmom nna paa ahɔ nen, ɔkɔwa nu wɔ wɔ nyunu sɔ kyẽa ne.

english_verse: “Find Jeremiah and keep him safe. Take good care of him and do whatever he asks.”
translation_verse: “Fa ye, te wɔ nye nea ye, nnɛyɔ ye tɛɛ biala, na bɔ ɔkɔhã kohyire wɔ biala, yɔ ma ye.”

english_verse: But the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah and took him to the town of Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial, then found him guilty,
translation_verse: Nakoso Kaldea koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ pole bɛ so, na bɛɛtole Sedekia wɔ Yeriko aseɛ frɛtɛɛ ne aso. Na bɛhyele ye nen, bɛfale ye bɛbrɛle Babilɔn hene Nebukadenesa wɔ Ribla bɔ ɔwɔ Hamate aseɛ so ne, na obuale ye ndɛen wɔ berɛ.

english_verse: and gave orders for him to be punished. Zedekiah's sons were killed there in front of him, and so were the leaders of Judah's ruling families.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Babilɔn hene huhuni Sedekia mma mmienzua nemɔ wɔ Ribla bɔ ye nye tua ɔ. Asa koso, Babilɔn hene huhuni Yuda atitire amukoraa.

english_verse: Then his eyes were poked out, and he was put in chains, so he could be dragged off to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Otutuli Sedekia nye, na oguale ye ngɔnzɔngɔnzɔ kyɛ ɔfa ye ɔkɔ Babilɔn.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Babylonian army had burned the houses in Jerusalem, including the royal palace, and they had broken down the city walls.
translation_verse: Kaldeafoɛ nemɔ fale see bɛyerale ahemvie ne, ɔne amanvoɛ awuro mɔ, na bedwirili Yerusalem fasue ne beguale ase.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guards, led away everyone from the city as prisoners, even those who had deserted to Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Yeɛ awɛmvoɛ nemɔ aso safohene Nebusaradan, ɔhyele mmenia ngaa bɔ baha kuro berɛ ne, bɛ bɔ bɛfale bɛ nwo bɛɛmane ye ne, yeɛ maen ne anu ama ngaa ne nnure hɔle Babilɔn.

english_verse: Only the poorest people who owned no land were left behind in Judah, and Nebuzaradan gave them fields and vineyards.
translation_verse: Nakoso ehiafoɛ nemɔ bie bɔ belle hwee ne, awɛmvoɛ nemɔ aso safohene Nebusaradan yakyili bɛ wɔ Yuda aseɛ so, na osa mane bɛ bobe boo mɔ ne eboo mɔ sɔ mmerɛ ne ala. Nebukadenesa pepɛ de Yeremia

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar had given the following orders to Nebuzaradan:
translation_verse: Babilɔn hene Nebukadenesa fale Yeremia nwo ahyɛdeɛ mane awɛmvoɛ nemɔ aso safohene Nebusaradan kyɛ,

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, Nebushazban, Nergal Sharezer, and the other officers of King Nebuchadnezzar
translation_verse: Yiti awɛmvoɛ nemɔ aso safohene Nebusaradan, Nebusaseban, Rabosari, Negal Saresa, Rabomago ɔne Babilɔn hene mbanyi nemɔ amukoraa

english_verse: sent some of their troops to bring me from the courtyard of the royal palace guards. They put me in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam and told him to take me to my home. And so I was allowed to stay with the people who remained in Judah. The Lord Promises To Protect Ebedmelech
translation_verse: bɛsomane maa bɛɛfale Yeremia befili kuku nu aluo dɔ bɛwale. Bɛfale ye bewurale Gedalia bɔ ye baba ole Ahikam, bɔ ye baba ole Safan ne sa, kyɛ ɔfa ye ɔhɔ awuro. Yiti Yeremia ne maen anu ama bɛɛtenane. AWURADE to Ebede Meleke ngraa

english_verse: While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ né bato Yeremia nu wɔ kuku nu aluo berɛ nen, AWURADE lale ye dwirɛ ali hyirele ye kyɛ,

english_verse: But because you trusted me, I will protect you from the officials of Judah, and when Judah is struck by disaster, I will rescue you and keep you alive. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ ngɔpepɛ ngole wɔ amba, na ɛngɔtɔ ngrandɛ noa, na mmom ekonya wɔ ti kodidi nu kyɛ koɛ nu nzesadeɛ, ɔnate kyɛ afa wɔ wora awura me nu ne ati, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.’ ”

english_verse: I was led away in chains along with the people of Judah and Jerusalem who were being taken to Babylonia. Nebuzaradan was the officer in charge of the guard, and while we were stopped at Ramah, the Lord caused him to set me free.
translation_verse: Awɛmvoɛ nemɔ aso safohene Nebusaradan, onwuni Yeremia kyɛ bagua ye ngɔnzɔngɔnzɔ bɔ ɔboka mmenia amukoraa bɔ bahye bɛ nnure bafi Yerusalem ne Yuda bɔ bɛ́fa bɛ bɛ́kɔ Babilɔn ne aso. Nebusaradan sangyele Yeremia wɔ Rama, na ye si ye, AWURADE lale ye dwirɛ ali hyirele Yeremia.

english_verse: But they continued to rebel against him, and now he has punished them just as he threatened.
translation_verse: Na afei, AWURADE amaa wawa nu, na wayɔ kyɛbɔ ɔhane ne ala: ofikyɛ ɛmɔayɔ bɔne batia AWURADE, na ɛmɔandie ye dwirɛ, yiti yeɛ sɔ amaneɛ he wato ɛmɔ ye.

english_verse: Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish.
translation_verse: Afei, tie, ɛnɛ kyẽa ye, mesangye ngɔnzɔngɔnzɔ bɔ ogua wɔ sa ne. Sɛ ekuro a, ɛne me hɔ Babilɔn, na ngɔte me nye ngɔnea wɔ. Nakoso sɛ enguro kyɛ ɛne me kɔhɔ Babilɔn a, ye de nnɛkɔ. Nea, aseɛ ye amukoraa yeɛ ɔla wɔ nyunu tɛtrɛtɛɛ ye; nekaa biala bɔ ɔte paa ma wɔ bɔ ekuro kyɛ ɛkɔ ne, kɔ.”

english_verse: I decided to stay with the people of Judah, and I went to live near Gedaliah in Mizpah. The Harvest Is Brought In
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yeremia hɔle Ahikam awa Gedalia berɛ wɔ Misepa, na ɔne ye bɛɛtenane wɔ mmenia bɔ bayakyi bɛ wɔ aseɛ ne aso nemɔ anu.

english_verse: Gedaliah told them, “There's no need to be afraid of the Babylonians. Everything will be fine, if we live peacefully and obey King Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Gedalia bɔ ye baba ole Ahikam, bɔ ye baba ole Safan ne, ɔtale ndaen hyirele bɛ ne bɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ kyɛ, “Nnɛma ɛmɔsuro kyɛ ɛmɔkɔso Kaldeafoɛ nemɔ ɔ. Ɛ́mɔtena aseɛ ye aso, ná ɛ́mɔso Babilɔn hene, na okoyie ɛmɔ yé.”

english_verse: I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔtie, me de ngɔtena Misepa ngɔso Kaldeafoɛ bɔ bɛkɔwa yɛ wa ne, na ɛmɔ de, ɛ́mɔboaboa nzaa ne borɔdoma ne ngoo noa. Ɛ́mɔfa bégua ɛmɔ nningyein nu, ná ɛ́mɔtena ɛmɔ nguro bɔ ɛmɔatena so nemɔ aso.”

english_verse: One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Afei Kerea awa Yohanan ne koɛhonɛfoɛ so safohene mɔ bɔ né bɛwowɔ eburo ne, bɛwale Gedalia berɛ wɔ Misepa,

english_verse: They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!” Gedaliah refused to believe them,
translation_verse: na bebisale ye kyɛ, “Aso ɛse kyɛ Amonfoɛ hene Baalise wasoma Netania awa Yismael kyɛ oohu wɔ ɔ?” Nakoso Ahikam awa Gedalia wanne bɛ dwirɛ ne wanni.

english_verse: so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Kerea awa Yohanan hane ye ahameɛ hyirele Gedalia wɔ Misepa kyɛ, “Mesrɛ wɔ, maa ngɔ ngongu Netania awa Yismael, na ebiala ngonwu sona bɔ ohuni ye ɔ. Nzu ati yeɛ odi kyɛ oku wɔ maa Yudafoɛ amukoraa bɔ bapɛ wɔ nwo bayia ne bɛbɔ aya, ma Yuda ngaa ne bɛ boso nua ɔ?”

english_verse: Gedaliah answered, “Don't kill Ishmael! What you've said about him can't be true.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Ahikam awa Gedalia buale Karea awa Yohanan kyɛ, “Nnɛyɔ sɔ nikyee ne, ofikyɛ bɔ ɛkã fa Yismael nwo ne, ɔtte nahorɛ.”

english_verse: But in the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah with ten of his soldiers. He had been one of the king's officials and was a member of the royal family. Ishmael and his men were invited to eat with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Na ɔwale kyɛ, bosome nzoo ne anu, Yismael bɔ ye baba ole Netania, bɔ ye baba ole Elisama bɔ ofi nnehyeɛ abusua nu ne, ɔne ɛhene ye mbanyi nemɔ buru bɛhɔle Ahikam awa Gedalia berɛ wɔ Misepa. Na mmerɛ bɔ bɛte aleɛ nwo bedidi ne,

english_verse: During the meal, Ishmael and his soldiers killed Gedaliah, the man chosen as ruler of Judah by the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Netania awa Yismael ne mmienzua buru bɔ bɛboka ye so ne, bedwɔsole bɛfale ngrandɛ behuni Gedalia bɔ ye baba ole Ahikam, bɔ ye baba ole Safan, bɔ Babilɔn hene wafa ye wali aseɛ ne aso amrado ne.

english_verse: Then they killed the Jews who were with Gedaliah, and they also killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
translation_verse: Asa koso, Yismael huhuni Yudafoɛ amukoraa bɔ né bɛ ne Gedalia wɔ Misepa ne, yeɛ Kaldea koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ né bɛwɔ berɛ ne.

english_verse: The next day, the murders had still not been discovered,
translation_verse: Ohuni Gedalia ne, ye elenyɔ ne aso bɔ né ebiala onnya ɔttele edwirɛ ne anwo bie ne,

english_verse: Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah.
translation_verse: Na Netania awa Yismael le esuɛ alaa fili Misepa ooyiale bɛ. Oyiale bɛ ne, osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔbra Ahikam awa Gedalia berɛ.”

english_verse: But after they were inside the town, Ishmael ordered his soldiers to kill them and throw their bodies into a well.
translation_verse: Bewurale kuro ne anu nen, Netania awa Yismael ɔne mmienzua bɔ bɛboka ye so ne, behuhuni bɛ begyili bɛ beguale abura bie anu.

english_verse: He let ten of the men live, because they offered to give him supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey they had hidden in a field.
translation_verse: Nakoso bɛ nu mmienzua buru biemɔ hã hyirele Yismael kyɛ, “Nnɛku yɛ, ofikyɛ yɛle atokoɔ, ayuo, ngoo ne woɛ wɔ fieso.” Yiti ɔyakyili, na wangu bɛ wammoka bɛ mmango nemɔ aso.

english_verse: The well that he filled with bodies had been dug by King Asa of Judah to store rainwater, because he was afraid that King Baasha of Israel might surround Mizpah and keep the people from getting to their water supply.
translation_verse: Mmienzua amukoraa bɔ ɔnate Gedalia ti Yismael huhuni bɛ ne, abura bɔ ogyili bɛ fuin nemɔ guale nu ne, ye ole abura bɔ Yisrael hene Baasa nwo suronyi ti Nana Asa tuli ne. Na Netania awa Yismael fale bɛ bɔ ohuni bɛ ne yili ye to.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Yismael hyele ɛhemɔ nnure: mmenia ngaa bɔ baha Misepa ne amukoraa, ɛhene mma mmrasua, yeɛ mmenia ngaa amukoraa bɔ baha Misepa bɔ awɛmvoɛ nemɔ aso safohene Nebusaradan wafa bɛ wawura Ahikam awa Gedalia sa ne. Netania awa Yismael hyele bɛ nnure, na osili nu kyɛ ɔfa bɛ kɔ Amonfoɛ mɔ dɔ.

english_verse: So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon.
translation_verse: bɛfale bɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa kyɛ bɛkwaafa koɛ bɛtoa Netania awa Yismael. Bɛɛtole ye wɔ ɛkwaa piri bɔ ɔwɔ Gibeon ne anwo.

english_verse: But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon. Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
translation_verse: Nakoso Netania awa Yismael ne mmenia mmɔtwɛ bɛnwatili befili Yohanan sa nu bɛhɔle Amonfoɛ dɔ.

english_verse: Johanan, Jezaniah, the other army officers, and everyone else in the group, came to me
translation_verse: Yeɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ so safohene nemɔ amukoraa, Karea awa Yohanan, Hosaya awa Yesania, ɔne mmenia ne amukoraa, ofi kwahweabaa mɔ so bɔ ɔkwaadwu atitire mɔ so ɔ, bɛbɔ bepingyele,

english_verse: and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left.
translation_verse: na besele ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ Yeremia kyɛ, “Yɛsrɛ wɔ ala, tie yɛ sufrɛ, ná bɔ mbaeɛ kyire AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ ma yɛ, yɛ mmenia ngaa bɔ yaha ye ,

english_verse: Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
translation_verse: amaa ɔnate so AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ wahyire yɛ atee bɔ yɛ́fa so ɔ, ɔne nikye horɛ bɔ yɛ́yɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord himself will be our witness that we promise to do whatever he says,
translation_verse: Yeɛ besele Yeremia kyɛ, “AWURADE ɔ́yɛ y’afia danzeniɛ nahorɛniɛ turoloo, sɛ AWURADE wɔ Nyameɛ dwirɛ amukoraa bɔ wafa wasoma wɔ kyɛ ɛhã hyire yɛ ne, sɛ yanni so pɛpɛɛpɛ a.

english_verse: even if it isn't what we want to do. We will obey the Lord so that all will go well for us.”
translation_verse: Kyɛ ɔte paa oo, kyɛ ɔtte mayee oo, yɛkotie AWURADE yɛ Nyameɛ bɔ yɛ́soma wɔ ye berɛ ne dwirɛ, amaa ɔnate so, sɛ yɛtie AWURADE yɛ Nyameɛ dwirɛ a, wayie yɛ yé.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord gave me an answer for
translation_verse: Na ɔwale kyɛ, ye eleburu ne asi, AWURADE lale ye dwirɛ ali hyirele Yeremia.

english_verse: and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said: You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do.
translation_verse: na osele bɛ kyɛ, “AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ bɔ ɛmɔsomane me ye berɛ kyɛ mva ɛmɔ abisadeɛ ngɔndo ye nyunu ne, ɔnwa nyoo:

english_verse: I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛmɔkɔhɔ so bɛkɔtena aseɛ he aso a, ye de ngɔma ɛmɔ bo kotimu, na mengodwiri ɛmɔ mengogua ase; ngolua ɛmɔ na mengotutu ɛmɔ bo, ofikyɛ manu me nwo wɔ musue bɔ mbraprale nguale ɛmɔ so ne anwo.

english_verse: and I will even force him to have mercy on you and give back your farms.
translation_verse: Na ngonwu ɛmɔ anwumvoin, amaa ɔnate so ye koso wanwu ɛmɔ anwumvoin, na ɔkɔmaa ɛmɔkosa bɛkɔwa ɛmɔ bɔbɔ ɛmɔ aseɛ so.

english_verse: But you might keep on saying, “We won't stay here in Judah, and we won't obey the Lord our God.
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ ɛmɔkã kyɛ, ‘Yɛngɔtena aseɛ he aso’, ná sɛ ɛmɔyɛ AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ dwirɛ nwo asoserɛ

english_verse: We are going to Egypt, where there is plenty of food and no danger of war.”
translation_verse: bɛkã kyɛ, ‘Daabi, Misraim aseɛ so mmom yeɛ yɛkɔhɔ ɔ, na dɔ de, koɛ ngɔto yɛ, yɛngɔte totorobɛndo nga, yeɛ aleɛ nwo hɔen ngohũ yɛ, na dɔ yeɛ yɛkɔɔtena ɔ’ a,

english_verse: People of Judah, you survived when the Babylonian army attacked. Now you are planning to move to Egypt, and if you do go, this is what will happen.
translation_verse: ye de ɛmɔ Yudafoɛ ngaa ne, afei ɛ́mɔtie AWURADE noa dwirɛ. Asafo AWURADE, Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Sɛ ɛmɔfa besie ɛmɔ nye so kyɛ ɛmɔkɔhɔ Misraim bɛkɔɔtena dɔ a,

english_verse: You are afraid of war, starvation, and disease here in Judah, but they will follow you to Egypt and kill you there. None of you will survive the disasters I will send.
translation_verse: Na mmenia amukoraa bɔ bɛkɔfa bekosie bɛ nye so kyɛ bɛkɔhɔ Misraim bɛkɔɔtena dɔ ne, bɛkɔtotɔ ngrandɛ noa, ɛhɔen ne ewue anwonyerɛ kohũhũ bɛ, na musue bɔ ngɔprapra ngogua bɛ so ne, bɛ nu biala ngɔha, anaa ongonya ye ti ngodidi nu ngofi nu.

english_verse: I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word. Jeremiah Gives a Warning
translation_verse: “Ofikyɛ Asafo AWURADE, Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Kyɛbɔ me yaafɛlɛ ne m’ahonehulɛ wale Yerusalemfoɛ so ne, sɔ ala yeɛ sɛ ɛmɔkɔ Misraim a, m’ahonehulɛ kɔwa ɛmɔ so ɔ. Ɛmɔkɔkakyi musue nikye, anwodwiri nikye, ɛnomalɛ nikye ne ngorohoɛ nikye; na ɛmɔ nye ngonwu wa ko.

english_verse: I told the people: You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ, Yudafoɛ bɔ ɛmɔaha ɔ, AWURADE ahã ahyire ɛmɔ kyɛ, ‘Nnɛma ɛmɔkɔ Misraim!’ Ɛ́mɔkaye kyɛ ɛnɛ kyẽa ye, mabɔ ɛmɔ kɔkɔ.

english_verse: You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake,
translation_verse: Ɛmɔlakalakale ɛmɔ bɔbɔ ɛmɔ kra. Ofikyɛ ɛmɔsomane me wɔ AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ berɛ kyɛ, ‘Bɔ mbaeɛ kyire AWURADE yɛ Nyameɛ ma yɛ, na bɔ AWURADE yɛ Nyameɛ kɔhã biala, fa to yɛ nyunu, na yɛkoli so.’

english_verse: because now that I have given you the Lord's answer, you refuse to obey him.
translation_verse: Na ɛnɛ kyẽa ye, mafa mato ɛmɔ nyunu, nakoso ɛmɔandie AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ, anaa bɔ ɔfa somane me kyɛ nga ngyire ɛmɔ ne anu biala.

english_verse: But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt.
translation_verse: Hosaya awa Asaria ne Karea awa Yohanan ne mmienzua anwomasoɛfoɛ nemɔ amukoraa besele Yeremia kyɛ, “Ɛlaka, AWURADE yɛ Nyameɛ wanzoma wɔ kyɛ ɛɛhã kyɛ, ‘Nnɛma ɛmɔkɔ Misraim bɛkɔtena dɔ.’

english_verse: Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Neria awa Baruku yeɛ opiapia wɔ maa ɛyɔ bɔ otia yɛ ɔ, kyɛbɔ ɔkɔyɛ bɔ ɔkɔfa yɛ kowura Kaldeafoɛ nemɔ sa, amaa ɔnate so bahũhũ yɛ anaa bahye yɛ nnure bafa yɛ bahɔ Babilɔn ɔ.”

english_verse: Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command.
translation_verse: Yiti Karea awa Yohanan, koɛhonɛfoɛ so safohene nemɔ amukoraa ne maen ne amukoraa bandie AWURADE noa dwirɛ, kyɛ bɛkɔtena Yuda aseɛ so ɔ.

english_verse: So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yudafoɛ ngaa amukoraa bɔ bɛfoane bɛ maa bɛbɔle aya bɛhɔle maen maen amukoraa so, bɔ né bafi dɔ basa bawa baatena Yuda aseɛ so ne, Karea awa Yohanan ne koɛhonɛfoɛ so safohene nemɔ amukoraa, bɛsesale bɛ:

english_verse: Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
translation_verse: mmienzua, mmrasua, ngwadaa, ɛhene mma mmrasua, yeɛ sona biala bɔ awɛmvoɛ nemɔ aso safohene Nebusaradan yakyili ye berɛ fa wurale Safan awa Ahikam awa Gedalia sa ne, yeɛ afei ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ Yeremia ne Neria awa Baruku,

english_verse: The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes,
translation_verse: na bɛ ne bɛ hɔle Misraim aseɛ so, ofikyɛ bandie AWURADE noa dwirɛ; na beedwuli Tapenese.

english_verse: Jeremiah, carry some large stones to the entrance of the government building in Tahpanhes. Bury the stones underneath the brick pavement and be sure the Jews are watching.
translation_verse: “Fa nyɔboɛ mbiri mbiri tira wɔ sa nu, na atee bɔ bafa mmerekese bahyehyɛ bɔ ɔwɔ Faro ahemvie anoanu berɛ wɔ Tapenese ne, fa nyɔboɛ nemɔ fea nnɛterɛ nu bɔ Yudafoɛ bɛ nye tua ɔ.

english_verse: Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury.
translation_verse: Na kã kyire bɛ kyɛ, ‘Asafo AWURADE, Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Ɛ́mɔtie, ngɔsoma ngɔɔfa me somvoɛ Babilɔn hene Nebukadenesa, na ngɔfa ye ahennie bia ngosie nyɔboɛ hemɔ bɔ mafa mafea ne aso, na ɔkɔfa ye ahennie akyiniwaa kɔkata bɛ so.

english_verse: He will attack Egypt and kill many of its people; others will die of disease or be dragged away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Ɔkɔwa kɔɔsɛkye Misraim maen ne, na bɛ bɔ bɛfata ewue ne, ɛhunɛ yeɛ bekohu bɛ ɔ, bɛ bɔ bɛfata nnurehyelɛ ne, bɛkɔhye bɛ nnure, bɛ bɔ bɛfata ngrandɛ ne, bɛkɔtɔ ngrandɛ noa.

english_verse: The Lord told me to speak with the Jews who were living in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis in northern Egypt, and also to those living in southern Egypt. He told me to tell them:
translation_verse: Yudafoɛ amukoraa bɔ né bɛtete Misraim aseɛ so wɔ Migidol, Tapenese, Memfise, yeɛ Patrose aseɛ so ne, AWURADE dwirɛ bɔ ɔlale ye ali hyirele Yeremia fale bɛ nwo ne, ye ɛhe.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You saw how I destroyed Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. They lie empty and in ruins today,
translation_verse: “Bɔ Asafo AWURADE, Yisrael Nyameɛ kã ɛhe: Ɛmɔanwu musue amukoraa bɔ maprapra magua Yerusalem ne Yuda nguro amukoraa so ne. Na ɛ́mɔnea, ɛnɛ bayɛ kurofoen bɔ ebiala nne berɛ bɔ ɔte so ɔ,

english_verse: because the people of Judah made me angry by worshiping gods that had never helped them or their ancestors.
translation_verse: ɔnate bɛ bɔne bɔ bayɔ bafa bawura me apue ne ati, ofikyɛ bɛhɔle bɛɛyerale ayirefona bɛsole nyameɛ foforɛ mɔ bɛ bɛnze bɛ ɔ: bɔ bɛ oo, ɛmɔ oo, ɛmɔ nana mɔ oo, ɛmɔnze bɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning,
translation_verse: Nakoso ndoale so nzomane me somvoɛ ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ amukoraa wɔ ɛmɔ berɛ kyɛ beese ɛmɔ kyɛ, ‘Ao, nnɛma ɛ́mɔyɔ musue nikye he bɔ mekyi ne!’

english_verse: but they refused to listen and would not stop worshiping other gods.
translation_verse: Nakoso bandie, yeɛ banyɛ asoɛ bamma me kyɛ bɛkɔsakyera b’adwene bekofi bɛ bɔne nwo, ɔne kyɛ bɛngɔyera ɛyɛɛ bɛngɔma nyameɛ foforɛ mɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Finally, my anger struck like a raging flood, and today Jerusalem and the towns of Judah are nothing but empty ruins.
translation_verse: Yiti me yaafɛlɛ ne m’ahonehulɛ wale, na begyele wɔ Yuda nguro mɔ ne Yerusalem mmorɔnoɛ mɔ so maa babɔ bakakyi kurofoen, kyɛbɔ ɔte ɛnɛ ye.

english_verse: Why do you now insist on heading for another disaster? A disaster that will destroy not only you, but also your children and babies.
translation_verse: Na afei, AWURADE Asafo Nyameɛ, Yisrael Nyameɛ bisa kyɛ: Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔyɔ bɔne piri he betia ɛmɔ kra, bɔ ɛmɔnua mmienzua ne mmrasua bɛ boso, yeɛ nnɔma ne ngwadaa bɛ boso befi Yuda, bɔ ɛmɔ nu ko po wanga ye?

english_verse: You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔfa ɛmɔ sa noa nnwumaa bewura me apue, bɔ ɛmɔyera ɛyɛɛ bɛma nyameɛ foforɛ mɔ wɔ Misraim aseɛ bɔ ɛmɔatena so ne aso, bɔ ɔnate ye sɔ ati ɛmɔ boso kɔnnua, ná ɛmɔayɛ ɛnomalɛ nikye ne ngorohoɛ nikye wɔ aseɛ ye aso maen amukoraa nu ɔ?

english_verse: When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens.
translation_verse: Aso ɛmɔ wora afi ɛmɔ nana mɔ bɛ bɔne, Yuda ahemvo mɔ bɛ bɔne, bɛ ye mɔ bɛ bɔne, ɛmɔ bɔbɔ ɛmɔ bɔne, yeɛ ɛmɔ aye mɔ bɔne bɔ bayɔ ye wɔ Yuda aseɛ so, ɔne Yerusalem mmorɔnoɛ so ne?

english_verse: Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Bammrɛ bɛ nwo ase maa waadwu ɛnɛ ye, banzuro me, yeɛ banni me mmeraa ne m’ahyɛdeɛ bɔ mva mane ɛmɔ ne ɛmɔ nana mɔ ne aso.

english_verse: There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Ngɔfa Yudafoɛ ngaa bɔ bayɛ b’adwene kyɛ bɛkɔ Misraim aseɛ so bɛkɔtena dɔ ne, ngɔhwe bɛ so, na bɛ mukoraa bekowuwu; bɛkɔtotɔ wɔ Misraim aseɛ so. Bɛkɔtotɔ ngrandɛ noa, na ɛhɔen kohũ bɛ maa bekowuwu, ofi kwahweabaa mɔ so bɔ ɔkwaadwu atitire mɔ so; bɛkɔtotɔ ngrandɛ noa, na ɛhɔen kohũ bɛ maa bekowuwu, na bɛkɔyɛ musue nikye, anwodwiri nikye, ɛnomalɛ nikye ne ngorohoɛ nikye.

english_verse: I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you.
translation_verse: Na bɛ bɔ bɛkɔtena Misraim aseɛ so ne, ngɔfa ngrandɛ, ɛhɔen ne ewue anwonyerɛ ngɔhwe bɛ so, kyɛbɔ mahwe Yerusalem so ne,

english_verse: None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back. The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
translation_verse: amaa ɔnate so, Yudafoɛ ngaa bɔ baatena Misraim aseɛ so ne, bɛ nu biala wannwati anaa wannya ye ti wannidi nu, ná wanza wangɔ Yuda aseɛ bɔ bɛpena kyɛ besa bɛkɔtena so ne aso; ofikyɛ bengosa bɛngɔwa, sana kãa bie bɔ bɛkɔnwati ɔ.”

english_verse: A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
translation_verse: Yeɛ mmienzua amukoraa bɔ bɛse kyɛ bɛ ye mɔ bayera ayirefona bama nyameɛ foforɛ mɔ ne, bɛ ne mmrasua amukoraa bɔ né begyigyi berɛ, ɛlɔen kandinga ne, mmenia amukoraa bɔ né bɛte Patrose wɔ Misraim aseɛ so ne, bebuale Yeremia kyɛ,

english_verse: Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen!
translation_verse: “Edwirɛ bɔ ahã ahyire yɛ wɔ AWURADE dumaa nu ne, yɛngotie wɔ dwirɛ ne.

english_verse: We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us.
translation_verse: Na mmom yɛkɔhɔ so yɛkɔyɔ nikyee biala bɔ yahã kyɛ yɛkɔyɔ ɔ: yɛkɔyera ayirefona yɛkɔma nyameɛso hemmaa, ná yabɔ anonneɛ afɔleɛ yama ye kyɛbɔ yɛ ne yɛ nana mɔ, y’ahemvo mɔ ne y’atitire mɔ yɛyɔle ye wɔ Yuda nguro ne Yerusalem mmorɔnoɛ mɔ so ne; ofikyɛ sɔ mmerɛ ne, né yɛnya aleɛ pee yɛdi, yɛnya ngɔsoɛ, na yande edwirɛ tɛɛ biala.”

english_verse: But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
translation_verse: Nakoso ofi mmerɛ bɔ yɛyakyili kyɛ yɛyera ɛyɛɛ yɛma nyameɛso hemmaa, ɔne kyɛ yɛyakyili kyɛ yɛbɔ anonneɛ afɔleɛ yɛma ye ne, nikyee biala nwo ahia yɛ, yatotɔ ngrandɛ noa, na ɛhɔen ku yɛ maa yɛwuwu.”

english_verse: Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
translation_verse: [Yeɛ mmrasua nemɔ sele kyɛ,] “Mmerɛ bɔ yɛyerale ɛyɛɛ yɛmane nyameɛso hemmaa, ná yɛbɔle anonneɛ afɔleɛ yɛmane ye ne, aso yɛtone taterɛ yɛfa yɛsɔnene ye, yeɛ yɛbɔle anonneɛ afɔleɛ yɛmane ye bɔ yɛ hu mɔ bɛmbene so ɔ? Yeremia ma Yudafoɛ mmuayɛɛ

english_verse: Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah?
translation_verse: “Ɛyɛɛ bɔ ɛmɔ ne ɛmɔ nana mɔ, ɛmɔ ahemvo mɔ, ɛmɔ atitire mɔ ne aseɛ ne aso ama ɛmɔyerale ye wɔ Yuda nguro nemɔ aso ne Yerusalem mmorɔnoɛ nemɔ aso ne, aso AWURADE ɔngaye? Aso ɔnne ye ti anu?

english_verse: And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today.
translation_verse: AWURADE wangora wammu ye nye wangua ɛmɔ bɔne yɔleɛ, ɔne akyiwadeɛ bɔ ɛmɔyɔle ne aso. Yiti ɛmɔ maen akakyi kurofoen, anwodwiri nikye ɔne ɛnomalɛ nikye bɔ sona fee ɔtte so ɔ, kyɛbɔ ɔte ɛnɛ ye.

english_verse: This disaster happened because you worshiped other gods and rebelled against the Lord by refusing to obey him or follow his laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Ɔnate kyɛ ɛmɔayera ɛyɛɛ, ɔne kyɛ ɛmɔayɔ bɔne batia AWURADE, ná ɛmɔandie AWURADE noa dwirɛ, yeɛ ɛmɔanni ye mmeraa, ye ahyɛdeɛ ne ye nhyehyɛleɛ so ne ati, yeɛ sɔ amaneɛ he wato ɛmɔ kyɛbɔ ɔte ɛnɛ ye.”

english_verse: Then I told the men and their wives, that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: Here in Egypt you still keep your promises to burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to the so-called Queen of Heaven.
translation_verse: Asafo AWURADE, Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Ɛmɔ ne ɛmɔ aye mɔ, ɛmɔate ɛmɔ noa bahã, yeɛ ɛmɔayɔ bafa bafoa so kyɛ, ‘Amba, aboadeɛ bɔ yaboa kyɛ yɛkɔyera ɛyɛɛ yɛkɔma nyameɛso hemmaa, ɔne kyɛ yɛkɔbɔ anonneɛ afɔleɛ yɛkɔma ye ne, yɛkoli so.’ Nzaade, ɛ́mɔsi ɛmɔ aboadeɛ ne agyinayɛɛ amba ee, ná ɛmɔtua ɛmɔ aboadeɛ nemɔ amba ee!

english_verse: Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name.
translation_verse: Yiti, Yudafoɛ bɔ ɛmɔte Misraim aseɛ so amukoraa, ɛ́mɔtie AWURADE noa dwirɛ: Ɛ́mɔtie, mafa me dumaa kandinga ne mata ndaen kyɛ, Yudaniɛ biala ngɔbɔ me dumaa ngɔta ndaen wɔ Misraim aseɛ amukoraa so ko kyɛ, ‘Kyɛ AWURADE Nyameɛ te ase ye,’ AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne’.

english_verse: Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔtie, ngotu me nye ngosie bɛ so ngɔfa bɔ ɔtte mayee ɔ ngoli bɛ, na mmom nna paa ɔ; na Yuda mmienzua amukoraa bɔ bɛwɔ Misraim aseɛ so ne, bɛkɔtotɔ wɔ ngrandɛ noa, na ɛhɔen kohũhũ bɛ maa bekowuwu, kɔpem kyɛ bɛ boso konua ɔ.

english_verse: Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
translation_verse: Na bɛ nu kãa bie bɔ bɛkɔnwati bekofi ngrandɛ noa ne, bekosa bekofi Misraim aseɛ so bɛkɔwa Yuda aseɛ so. Na Yudafoɛ ngaa amukoraa bɔ bɛhɔle Misraim aseɛ so bɛɛtenane dɔ ne, bekonwu bɔ ye noa dwirɛ kɔyɛ adwuma ɔ: kyɛ me deɛ oo, anaa bɛ deɛ oo.

english_verse: And here is how you will know that I will keep my threats to punish you in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na ɛhe kɔyɛ sɛngyerɛnneɛ kɔma ɛmɔ, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne, kyɛ ngɔhwe ɛmɔ so wɔ wa, amaa ɔnate so ɛmɔanwu kyɛ amba, me noa dwirɛ kɔwa nu kɔprapra amaneɛ kogua ɛmɔ so.

english_verse: I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
translation_verse: AWURADE nwa nyoo: Ɛ́mɔtie, ngɔfa Misraim hene Faro Hofra ngowura ye pɔfoɛ ne bɛ bɔ bɛpena ye beku ye nemɔ bɛ sa, kyɛbɔ mvale Yuda hene Sedekia nwurale Babilɔn hene Nebukadenesa bɔ ɔte ye pɔfoɛ, ná ɔpena ye ku ye ne, ye sa ne.”

english_verse: Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
translation_verse: “Ao Baruku, AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ ose wɔ kyɛ,

english_verse: You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest.
translation_verse: Ɛnwa, ‘Edwirɛ ato me oo! Ofikyɛ AWURADE wafa aworabɔlɛ waboka me yealɛ so; mapene mafɛ, na mennya me nwome menne.’

english_verse: But all over the earth I am tearing down what I built and pulling up what I planted.
translation_verse: Kã kyire ye kyɛ, AWURADE nwa nyoo: Tie, bɔ masi ne, ngobubu ye, yeɛ bɔ malua ne, ngotutu ye bo. Na ngɔyɛ ɛhe wɔ aseɛ ye amukoraa so.

english_verse: I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Na wɔ, aso nningyein mbiri mbiri yeɛ ɛpena mma wɔ nwo ɔ? Nnɛpena, ofikyɛ ngɔprapra musue ngogua anwoɔnaen amukoraa so, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne. Nakoso wɔ de, ekonya wɔ ti kodidi nu kyɛ koɛ nu nzesadeɛ wɔ nekaa biala bɔ ɛkɔhɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord often told me what to say about the different nations of the world. What the Lord Says about Egypt
translation_verse: AWURADE dwirɛ bɔ ɔlale ye ali hyirele ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ Yeremia fale maen maen mɔ nwo ne, ye ɛhe:

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
translation_verse: Misraim deɛ ɛhe: Ɔfa Misraim hene Faro Neko ye koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ né bɛwɔ asue Yufreti noa wɔ Kakemise, bɔ Babilɔn hene Nebukadenesa lili bɛ so ngonim ne anwo. Ɛhe sili wɔ Yuda hene Yehoakim bɔ ye baba ole Yosia ne, ye ahennie afoɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so nna ne anu. :

english_verse: It's time to go into battle! So grab your shields,
translation_verse: “Ɛ́mɔfa buralɛ ataadeɛ ne akokyɛm, ná ɛmɔhɔ koɛ!

english_verse: saddle your horses, and polish your spears. Put on your helmets and armor, then take your positions.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔfa teaseɛnam mɔ bɛsosɔ mbɔngɔ mɔ; pɔngɔhanɛfoɛ, ɛ́mɔtenatena bɛ so! Ɛ́mɔfa ɛmɔ buralɛ kyerɛ bɛte begyina, ɛ́mɔsi ɛmɔ ngrandɛ mɔ, ɛ́mɔwurawura ɛmɔ buralɛ ngatasoɛ nemɔ!

english_verse: I can see the battle now— you are defeated and running away, never once looking back. Terror is all around.
translation_verse: Nzu ati yeɛ manwu bɛ kyɛ ahunundetelɛ atɔ bɛ so bɔ basa bɛ si ye? Babo bɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ, maa banwati bahɔ ndɛndɛ; bannea bɛ si, ofikyɛ ɛserɛ akyekye bɛ, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: You are strong and run fast, but you can't escape. You fall in battle near the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Bɛ bɔ bɛ nwo yɛ nyera ne, bɛngɔhora bɛngɔnwati bɛngɔhɔ, yeɛ koɛhonɛniɛ ngonya ye ti ngodidi nu. Bekosoti, ná bafifi ase wɔ sorɔ dɔ, wɔ asue Yufreti noa.

english_verse: What nation is this, that rises like the Nile River overflowing its banks?
translation_verse: Nwa yeɛ ɔ́ba kyɛ asue Naele, bɔ ye nzue bu fa so kyɛ asue mɔ ye?

english_verse: It is Egypt, rising with a roar like a raging river and saying, “I'll flood the earth, destroying cities, and killing everyone in them.”
translation_verse: Misraim ma ye nwo so kyɛ Naele, kyɛ asue mɔ bɔ bayi bebu bɛfa so ɔ. Ɔnwa: Ngoyi ngɔkata aseɛ so; ngɔsɛkye kuro ne, ɔne nu ama mɔ.

english_verse: Go ahead, Egypt. Tell your chariots and cavalry to attack and fight hard. Order your troops to march out, with Ethiopians and Libyans carrying shields, and the Lydians armed with bows and arrows.
translation_verse: Mbɔngɔ, ɛ́mɔdwɔso! Ao teaseɛnam mɔ, ɛ́mɔkekã ɛmɔ anwo! Koɛhonɛfoɛ, ɛmɔhɔ ɛmɔ nyunu: Yitiopiafoɛ ne Libiafoɛ bɔ ɛmɔtira akokyɛm ɔ, Lidiafoɛ bɔ ɛmɔse agyaen to paa ɔ. AWURADE kyẽa ne

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful will win this battle and take revenge on his enemies. His sword will eat them and drink their blood until it is full. They will be killed in the north near the Euphrates River, as a sacrifice to the Lord.
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne te AWURADE Asafo Nyameɛ ye kyẽa, ɔte wereɛtɔlɛ kyẽa bɔ ɔkɔtɔ ye pɔfoɛ mɔ so wereɛ ɔ. Ngrandɛ ne kohũhũ kɔma ye ko koyi, ná wano bɛ mogya wabo. Ofikyɛ AWURADE Asafo Nyameɛ asiesie afɔleɛ wɔ sorɔ dɔ maen ne anu, wɔ asue Yufreti noa.

english_verse: Egypt, no medicine can heal you, not even the soothing lotion from Gilead.
translation_verse: Ao ababunu, Misraim awa brasua, kɔ Gileade ná kɔpena ayire, ayɛ ayire pee, nakoso mbaen ɔ; ɛngɔte apɔ.

english_verse: All nations have heard you weep; you are disgraced, and they know it. Your troops fall to the ground, stumbling over each other. A Warning for Egypt
translation_verse: Maen maen mɔ bate w’animguaseɛ ne, na wɔ suɛ ayi aseɛ ye aso tɛkyɛ, ofikyɛ koɛhonɛniɛ afĩ ase atɔ koɛhonɛniɛ so, na bɛ munyɔ babɔ nu batotɔ.” Nebukadenesa kɔfa koɛ kɔɔtoa Misraim

english_verse: When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them: Prepare to defend yourselves! Everywhere in your nation, people are dying in war.
translation_verse: “Ɛ́mɔbɔ ye dawure wɔ Misraim, ná ɛ́mɔfa bɛto dwaa wɔ Migidol; ɛ́mɔfa bɛto dwaa wɔ Memfise ne Tapenese. Ɛmɔhã kyɛ, ‘Gyina berɛ pindinn, ná boaboa wɔ nwo, ofikyɛ ngrandɛ ne kohũhũ kɔpɛ wɔ nwo kɔbra koyia.’

english_verse: I have struck down your mighty god Apis and chased him away.
translation_verse: Ɔyɛle sɛɛ bɔ w’anwoserɛfoɛ batete bagua ye? Bangora gyina, ofikyɛ AWURADE foane bɛ.

english_verse: Your soldiers stumble over each other and say, “Get up! The enemy will kill us, unless we can escape to our own land.”
translation_verse: Amba, ɔmane bɛ nu pee bɛtete beguale, ko te tɔle ko aso. Na besisele bɛ nwo kyɛ, ‘Dwɔso maa yɛsa yɛhɔ yɛ bɔbɔ yɛ mmenia mɔ dɔ, yɛ bɔbɔ yɛ maen bɔ nu yeɛ bɛwole yɛ ɔ, ná yɛnwati yɛfi ndaneanyeɛfoɛ ngrandɛ noa.’

english_verse: Egypt, I am the true king, the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as I live, those enemies who attack will tower over you like Mount Tabor among the hills or Mount Carmel by the sea.
translation_verse: “Ɛhene bɔ ye dumaa ole Asafo AWURADE ne, ɔnwa: Kyɛ nde ase ye, amba, kyɛ Tabɔ ɔte wɔ mmokaa mɔ nu, ɔne kyɛ Kamɛl ɔla mboanoa ne, sɔ ala yeɛ ɔkɔwa ɔ.

english_verse: You will be led away captive, so pack a few things to bring with you. Your capital, Memphis, will lie empty and in ruins.
translation_verse: Ao, wɔ, baa brasua bɔ ɛte Misraim ɔ, boaboa wɔ nwo kyɛ bɛkɔhye wɔ nnure bɛkɔhɔ ɔ; ofikyɛ Memfise kɔyɛ kurofoen ne aseɛ mbaen bɔ sona fee ɔtte so ɔ.

english_verse: An enemy from the north will attack you, beautiful Egypt, like a fly biting a cow.
translation_verse: Misraim te nandwie beleɛ akrɔngrɔma anwonyemene, nakoso atuin fi sorɔ dɔ ɔ́ba, ɔ́ba ye so.

english_verse: The foreign soldiers you hired will turn and run. But they are doomed, like well-fed calves being led to the butcher. *
translation_verse: Ye koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ wabɔ bɛ paa ne, bɛwɔ ye nu, bɛte kyɛ nandwie mɔ bɔ balɔ ɔ; ofikyɛ bɛ koso basa bɛ si, na babɔ nu banwati bahɔ. Bangora gyina, ofikyɛ b’amaneɛnwunɛ kyẽa ne b’asohwenɛ mmerɛ ne, wawa bɛ so.

english_verse: The enemy army will go forward like a swarm of locusts. Your troops will feel helpless, like a snake in a forest
translation_verse: “Dede bɔ ɔyɔ ne, ɔte kyɛ ewoo bɔ ɔtwe ye nwo ase ɔ, ofikyɛ ye pɔfoɛ nemɔ batu bi bɛba; na bele akumaa mɔ bɛ́ba ye so kyɛ mmenia bɔ bebu mmakaa ɔ.

english_verse: when men with axes start chopping down trees. It can only hiss and try to escape.
translation_verse: Bekobu ye hɔayeɛ mɔ bekogua ase, ɔwɔ nu kyɛ nu falɛ yɛ se de, ofikyɛ bɛsone bɛtra mmɛbɛ bɔ bɛka a, bennwu bɛ noa ɔ, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Your people will be disgraced and captured by the enemy from the north.
translation_verse: Bekogua Misraim awa brasua ne nyunu ase, na bɛkɔfa ye bekowura sorɔ dɔ maen ne sa.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power.
translation_verse: Asafo AWURADE, Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa nyoo, “Ɛ́mɔtie, ngɔhwe Amon bɔ ɔwɔ Tebese, Faro, yeɛ Misraim ne ye nyameɛ mɔ ne ye ahemvo mɔ bɛ so, yeɛ Faro ne mmenia bɔ bɛfa bɛ wora bewura ye nu ɔ.

english_verse: I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Bring Israel Home The Lord said:
translation_verse: Na ngɔfa bɛ ngowura bɛ bɔ bɛpena bɛ beku bɛ ɔ nemɔ sa, yeɛ Babilɔn hene Nebukadenesa ne ye somvoɛ mɔ sa. Na ye si ye, mmenia kɔtena Misraim kyɛ daa ne ala, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Israel, don't be afraid. Someday I will bring you home from foreign lands. You and your descendants will live in peace and safety, with nothing to fear.
translation_verse: “Nakoso wɔ, me somvoɛ Yakob, nnɛsuro, wɔ, Yisrael, nnɛma wɔ kunu tete wɔ; ofikyɛ tie, ngɔpepɛ ngole wɔ ngofi dedeede, ɔne wɔ boso ama ngofi aseɛ bɔ bahye bɛ nnure bahɔ so ne aso. Yakob kosa kɔwa kɔɔtena anwotɔ ne asomdwee nu, na ebiala ngonwunanwuna ye.

english_verse: So don't be afraid, even though now you deserve to be punished and have been scattered among other nations. But when I destroy them, I will protect you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ao me somvoɛ Yakob, nnɛsuro ofikyɛ ngyi wɔ si, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne. Maen maen amukoraa bɔ mafoa wɔ mahɔ so ne, ngonua bɛ boso. Nakoso wɔ de, mengonua wɔ boso, na mmom ngɔhwe wɔ so kyɛbɔ ɔfata ɔ, na mengɔyakyi wɔ maa ɛngɔfa wɔ nwo ngoli tɔtorɔtɔɔ.”

english_verse: Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
translation_verse: AWURADE dwirɛ bɔ ɔlale ye ali hyirele ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ Yeremia fale Filistifoɛ nwo, koraka yeɛ Faro ɔkwaali Gasa so ngonim ne, ye ɛhe:

english_verse: I, the Lord, tell you that your land will be flooded with an army from the north. It will destroy your towns and sweep you away, moaning and screaming.
translation_verse: “AWURADE nwa nyoo: Tie, nzue ma ye nwo so fi sorɔ dɔ, na ɔkɔyɛ asue bɔ oyi bu fa so ɔ; na okobu kɔfa aseɛ ne aso nningyein amukoraa so, kuro ne, ɔne nu ama. Mmenia kɔteatea nu, na aseɛ ne aso ama amukoraa bɛkɔbɔ awuye.

english_verse: You refugees from Crete, your time has now come, and I will destroy you. None of you will be left to help the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
translation_verse: ɔnate kyẽa bɔ ɔbaahũhũ Filistifoɛ amukoraa ne ati, ɔne kyɛ ɔbaanua bokafoɛ biala bɔ waha wɔ Tiro ne Sidon ɔ, bɛ bo. Ofikyɛ AWURADE kohũhũ Filistifoɛ bɔ bɛ ole Kafito supɔ ngaa nemɔ ne.

english_verse: The Anakim who survive in Gaza and Ashkelon will mourn for you by shaving their heads and sitting in silence.
translation_verse: Gasa ti so apa, Asekelɔn abɔ. Wɔ bɔ aha bɔnza ne anu ɔ, ɛkɔtete wɔ nwonaen maa okoodwu kyinzu?

english_verse: You ask how long will I continue to attack you with my sword, then you tell me to put it away and leave you alone.
translation_verse: Ao, AWURADE ngrandɛ, kyinzu yeɛ ɛkɔyɛ konn ɔ? Kowura wɔ bɔha nu, de wɔ nwome ná yɛ konn!

english_verse: But how can my sword rest, when I have commanded it to attack Ashkelon and the seacoast?
translation_verse: Ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ né wayɛ konn, wɔ aberɛ bɔ AWURADE ama ye ahyɛdeɛ kyɛ ɔfa koɛ ɔteta Asekelɔn ne mboanoa ne ɔ? Berɛ yeɛ wafa wawura ye sa ɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab: The town of Nebo is doomed; Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced, and even its fortress will be left in ruins.
translation_verse: Bɔ Asafo AWURADE, Yisrael Nyameɛ kã fa Moabo nwo ɛhe: Nebo, wɔ yaakɔ oo! Ofikyɛ wabɔ! Kiriatim nyunu agua ase, na bahye ye bahɔ, anwoserɛ afealeɛ ne nyunu agua ase, na badwiri bagua.

english_verse: No one honors you, Moab. In Heshbon, enemies make plans to end your life. My sword will leave only silence in your town named “Quiet.”
translation_verse: Bɛngɔkamvo Moabo ko. Bɛbɔle ye nwo porɛ wɔ Hesebon kyɛ, ‘Ɛmɔbra maa yɛnua ye boso, bɔ ɔngɔyɛ maen ko ɔ!’ Wɔ, kuro bɔ bɛfrɛ wɔ Mademen koso, bɛkɔmaa ɛkɔhã wɔ noa kɔto nu, na ngrandɛ ne kɔfoa wɔ.

english_verse: The people of Horonaim will cry for help, as their town is attacked and destroyed.
translation_verse: Tie, komviɛ bie tea nu fi Horonaim kyɛ, ‘Ɛsɛkyelɛ ne kurobɔlɛ piri!’

english_verse: Moab will be shattered! Your children will sob
translation_verse: Moabo abɔ; ye mma mmaa mmaa bɛteatea nu maa bate bɛ komvi.

english_verse: and cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they will tell of disasters.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ Luhite pambaa ne, bele esuɛ yeɛ bɛkɔfo ɔ, na Horonaim nekaa bɔ bɛtorotoro ne, pɔfoɛ nemɔ ate awuyebɔlɛ serɛserɛ.

english_verse: Run for your lives! Head into the desert like a wild donkey.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔnwati, ɛ́mɔpena ɛmɔ ti bédidi nu, ná ɛ́mɔyɛ kyɛ ɛserɛ so afunum.

english_verse: You thought you could be saved by your power and wealth, but you will be captured along with your god Chemosh, his priests, and officials.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ, ɔnate kyɛ afa wɔ nwo ato wɔ nnwumaa ne wɔ anwonyadeɛ so ne ati, wɔ koso bɛkɔhye wɔ bɛkɔhɔ; na bɛkɔhye Kemose nnure bɛkɔhɔ, ɔne ye asɔfo mɔ ne ye atitire mɔ bɔ bɛboka ye so ɔ.

english_verse: Not one of your towns will escape destruction. I have told your enemies, “Wipe out the valley and the flatlands of Moab.
translation_verse: Sɛkyefoɛ ne kɔwa kuro biala so, kuro biala ngonya ye nwo ngɔtete; bɔnza ne kɔbɔ tɔɔ, na bɛkɔsɛkye aseɛ pralaa ne, kyɛbɔ AWURADE ahã ne ala.

english_verse: Spread salt on the ground to kill the crops. Leave its towns in ruins, with no one living there.
translation_verse: “Ɛ́mɔma Moabo ndaa maa otu ɔnwati hɔ, ofikyɛ ye nguro nemɔ kɔyɛ kurofoen, bɔ sona fee ɔtte so ɔ.

english_verse: I want you to kill the Moabites, and if you let them escape, I will put a curse on you.”
translation_verse: Ebiala bɔ ɔnde ye nye nyɔ AWURADE adwuma ne, ɛnomalɛ bra ye so, na ebiala bɔ ɔtwe ye ngrandɛ sa, bɔ ɔmva nga mogya ngua ne, ɛnomalɛ bra ye so.

english_verse: Moab, you are like wine left to settle undisturbed, never poured from jar to jar. And so, your nation continues to prosper and improve.
translation_verse: “Moabo atena asomdwee nu fi ye ngwadaa nu, wayɛ kyɛ nzaa bɔ ye pue ne la ye bo ɔ; banhwie ye bamvi akotokyiwa ko anu bangua foforɛ nu, yeɛ bangye ye nnure bangɔ. Yiti ye fɛɛ ne tɛgyi ye nu, na ye fona ne, ɔssesane.

english_verse: Then you will be ashamed, because your god Chemosh cannot save you, just as Bethel could not help the Israelites.
translation_verse: Afei Kemose nwo kɔyɛ Moabo nya, kyɛbɔ Betel bɔ ɔte Yisrael awuro ama mɔ b’anyelasoɛ ne, ye nwo yɛle Yisrael awuro ama mɔ nya ne.

english_verse: You claim that your soldiers are strong and brave.
translation_verse: “Ɔyɛ sɛɛ bɔ ɛmɔkekã kyɛ, ‘Yɛte katakyiefoɛ ne koɛhonɛfoɛ ahoneserɛfoɛ’ ɔ?

english_verse: But I am the Lord, the all-powerful King, and I promise that enemies will overpower your towns. Even your best warriors will die in the battle.
translation_verse: Moabo abɔ, na sɛkyefoɛ ne wafo wahɔ ye nguro nemɔ anu, na ye mmerandeɛ bɔ baneanea nu baye bɛ nemɔ, baahu bɛ wɔ akumyɛɛ, Ɛhene ne, bɔ ye dumaa ole Asafo AWURADE ne, ye noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: It won't be long now— disaster will hit Moab!
translation_verse: Moabo sɛkyelɛ ne wapingye, na ye amaneɛnwunɛ ne, ɔba ndɛndɛ.

english_verse: I will order the nearby nations to mourn for you and say, “Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others, but now its glorious power has been shattered.”
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ bɔ ɛmɔpingye ye amukoraa, ɛ́mɔsu ye, ɛmɔ bɔ ɛmɔse ye dumaa ɔ amukoraa, ɛmɔhã kyɛ, ‘Ɔwale ye sɛ bɔ ɛhɔtɔ serɛserɛ bɔ ɔte pɔmaa nyemene ne, nu abubu ye?’

english_verse: People in the town of Dibon, you will be honored no more, so have a seat in the dust. Your walls will be torn down when the enemies attack.
translation_verse: “Wɔ, baa brasua bɔ ɛte Dibɔn ɔ, fi w’animnyam ne anu dwu bra, ná baatena aseɛ katerepee so! Ofikyɛ Moabo sɛkyefoɛ ne kɔwa wɔ so, na ɔkɔsɛkye w’anwoserɛ afealeɛ mɔ.

english_verse: You people of Aroer, go wait beside the road, and when refugees run by, ask them, “What happened?”
translation_verse: Wɔ bɔ ɛte Aroye ɔ, gyina atee ne anoa ná tetɛ; bisa bienzua bɔ ɔnwati ne brasua bɔ ɔnwati pena ye ti didi nu ne kyɛ, ‘Nzikyɛ dwirɛ yeɛ wasi ɔ?’

english_verse: They will answer, “Moab has been defeated! Weep with us in shame. Tell everyone at the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Moabo nyunu agua ase, ofikyɛ badwiri ye bagua ase: ɛ́mɔbɔ awuye ná ɛ́mɔsu! Ɛ́mɔbɔ ye dawure wɔ Anɔn kyɛ Moabo abɔ.

english_verse: I will punish every town that belongs to Moab, but especially Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath,
translation_verse: Babua aseɛ pralaa ne, ɔne nguro hemɔ ndɛen: Holon, Yahasa, Mefaate,

english_verse: Dibon, Nebo, Beth-Diblathaim,
translation_verse: Dibɔn, Nebo, Bete Diblatayim,

english_verse: Kiriathaim, Beth-Gamul, Beth-Meon,
translation_verse: Kiriatim, Bete Gamul, Bete Meon,

english_verse: My decision is final— your army will be crushed, and your power broken.
translation_verse: Bapɛ Moabo mmɛen ne bafi berɛ, yeɛ babu ye sa nu, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: People of Moab, you claim to be stronger than I am. Now I will tell other nations to make you drunk and to laugh while you collapse in your own vomit.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔma ɔbo , ofikyɛ ɔmomane ye nwo so hyirele AWURADE. Yiti Moabo kɔla ye feɛ nu, na ye koso bɛkɔgoro ye nwo.

english_verse: You made fun of my people and treated them like criminals caught in the act.
translation_verse: Aso Yisrael nwo anyɛ wɔ sere? Aso enwuni ye wɔ awuefoɛ nu, bɔ daa biala ɛkã ye dwirɛ a, né ɛwosowoso wɔ ti ye?

english_verse: Now you must leave your towns and live like doves in the shelter of cliffs and canyons.
translation_verse: “Ɛmɔ bɔ ɛmɔtete Moabo, ɛ́mɔtu béfi nguro nemɔ aso bɛɛtena nyɔbotaen nemɔ anu, ɛ́mɔyɛ kyɛ abubure bɔ ɔnwo ye saen wɔ kumaa noa ye ngyɛnu ɔ.

english_verse: I know about your pride, and how you strut and boast.
translation_verse: Yate Moabo anwomasoɛ , ye dwɛɛ, ye ahandaen, ye anwomasoɛ, ɔne ye ahone nu aniammɔwoho nwo dwirɛ.

english_verse: So I will cry and mourn for Moab and its town of Kir-Heres.
translation_verse: Yiti ngɔbɔ Moabo nwo awuye, na ngosu Moabo amukoraa, m’ahone kɔbɔ Kire Heresefoɛ nwo awuye.

english_verse: People of Sibmah, you were like a vineyard heavy with grapes, and with branches reaching north to the town of Jazer and west to the Dead Sea. But you have been destroyed, and so I will weep for you, as the people of Jazer weep for the vineyards.
translation_verse: Ao Sibima bobe, ngosu wɔ kyɛ mesu Yasere ɔ! Wɔ mmaen trɛtrɛle fale ɛpo so, bɛtrɛ bekodwu Yasere ɛpo ne po; sɛkyefoɛ ne, watu ye nye wasie wɔ borɔdoma mma ne wɔ bobe mma so.

english_verse: Harvest celebrations are gone from the orchards and farms of Moab. I have silenced the shouts of people making wine.
translation_verse: Baye anika ne anigye bafi aseɛ bɔ ɔkye aleɛ ne aso, ɔne Moabo aseɛ so, na mama nzaa bo apɛ wɔ nekaa bɔ betwi nzaa nemɔ. Ebiala ngohwi nzaa ngɔbɔ ese, na bɛ ndeateamuɛ ne ngɔyɛ esebɔlɛ.

english_verse: Weeping from Heshbon can be heard as far as Elealeh and Jahaz; cries from Zoar are heard in Horonaim and Eglath-Shelishiyah. And Nimrim Creek has run dry.
translation_verse: “Bɛteatea nu befi Hesebon bekodwu Eleale ne Yahase. Bɛteatea nu befi Soa bekodwu Horonaim ne Eglate Selisiya, ofikyɛ Nimrim nzue po wawewe.

english_verse: I will get rid of anyone who burns incense to the gods of Moab or offers sacrifices at their shrines. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Afei koso, ebiala bɔ ɔbɔ afɔleɛ wɔ asɔneyɛɛ mɔ so, ɔne ebiala bɔ ɔyera ɛyɛɛ ma ye nyameɛ mɔ ne, ngonua ye boso wɔ Moabo, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: In my heart I moan for Moab, like a funeral song played on a flute. I mourn for the people of the town of Kir-Heres, because their wealth is gone. *
translation_verse: Yiti m’ahone koli Moabo nwo aworabɔlɛ kyɛ atɛndɛbɛn nu dwein, na m’ahone koli Kire Heresefoɛ nwo aworabɔlɛ kyɛ atɛndɛbɛn nu dwein, ofikyɛ anwonyadeɛ bɔ wanya ye ne, watu wamini.

english_verse: The people of Moab mourn on the rooftops and in the streets. Men cut off their beards, people shave their heads; they make cuts on their hands and wear sackcloth. And it's all because I, the Lord, have shattered Moab like a jar that no one wants.
translation_verse: Na awuyebɔlɛ ngome yeɛ bɛkɔte ye wɔ Moabo sua amukoraa so, ɔne mmorɔnoɛ mɔ so ɔ, ofikyɛ mabɔ Moabo kyɛ kukue bɔ ebiala nye ngye ye nwo ɔ, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Moab lies broken! Listen to its people cry as they turn away in shame. Other nations are horrified at what happened, but still they mock her.
translation_verse: Nea kyɛbɔ basi badwiri ye bagua ase ɔ! Nea kyɛbɔ besi bɛbɔ awuye ɔ! Nea kyɛbɔ Moabo le animguaseɛ wakakyi ye kɔme asi ɔ! Yiti Moabo ayɛ ngorohoɛ nikye ne anwodwiri nikye wɔ bɛ bɔ bapɛ ye nwo bayia amukoraa bɛ nye so.

english_verse: Moab, an enemy swoops down like an eagle spreading its wings over your land.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ AWURADE nwa nyoo: “Tie, okotu kyɛ kɔleɛ, ná watrɛ ye ndaa nu wɔ Moabo so.

english_verse: Your cities and fortresses will be captured, and your warriors as fearful as women giving birth.
translation_verse: Bali Keriote so ngonim, yeɛ bale anwoserɛ afealeɛ nemɔ, na sɔ kyẽa ne, Moabo anwoserɛfoɛ bɛ kra kɔnwati kofi bɛ nwo, kyɛ brasua bɔ wafo aworɛ so ɔ ye deɛ.

english_verse: You are finished as a nation, because you dared oppose me, the Lord.
translation_verse: Na bɛkɔbɔ Moabo bɔ ɔngɔyɛ maen ko ɔ, ofikyɛ wama ye nwo so watia AWURADE.

english_verse: Terror, pits, and traps are waiting for you.
translation_verse: Wɔ, Moaboniɛ, ahunundetelɛ, kumaa ne ngaen la berɛ ɔnwondɛ ɔ! AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; and if you crawl out of the pit, you'll get caught in a trap. The time has come for you to be punished. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Bɔ ɔkɔnwati ahunundetelɛ ne, ɔkɔtɔ kumaa ne anu, yeɛ bɔ ɔkɔfo kofi kumaa ne anu ne, ngaen ne kɔhye ye. Ofikyɛ ngɔma sɔ nningyein nemɔ kɔwa Moabo so, wɔ b’asohwenɛ afoɛ ne anu, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Near the city of Heshbon, where Sihon once ruled, tired refugees stand in shadows cast by the flames of their burning city. Soon, the towns on other hilltops, where those warlike people live, will also go up in smoke.
translation_verse: “Bɛ bɔ bɛnwatili ne, bɛɛbɔle bɛ nwo adwaa wɔ Hesebon fɔnwoo nu, ɔnate b’anwoserɛ bɔ wayie ne ati. Nakoso see kofi Hesebon kɔwa, na see bɔ ogye kofi Sihon kɔwa kɔɔyera Moabo ye nwoma so, ɔne basabasayɔlɛfoɛ bɛ ti afia.

english_verse: People of Moab, you worshiped Chemosh, your god, but now you are done for, and your children are prisoners in a foreign country.
translation_verse: Ao Moabo, wɔ yaakɔ! Kemose maen ne wabɔ, ofikyɛ bahye wɔ mma mmienzua mɔ nnure bahɔ, yeɛ bahye wɔ mma mmrasua mɔ nnure bahɔ.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Nakoso ngyẽa bɔ oli nziɛ ne, ngɔfa Moabo ngofi nnurehyelɛ nu ngosa ngɔwa, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.” Moabo ndɛenbualɛ ne, ye ayieleɛ ɛne.

english_verse: The Lord has this to say about the nation of Ammon: The people of Israel have plenty of children to inherit their lands. So why have you worshipers of the god Milcom taken over towns and land belonging to the tribe of Gad?
translation_verse: Bɔ AWURADE kã fa Amonfoɛ nwo ole kyɛ, “Aso Yisrael olle mmaa mmienzua anaa? Olle sona bɔ okoli ye bia anaa? Ɔyɛle sɛɛ bɔ bɛ hene yeɛ odi Gade so, bɔ ye mmenia tete ye nguro mɔ so ye?
