english_verse: Someday I will send an army to attack you in Rabbah, your capital city. It will be left in ruins, and the surrounding villages will lie in ashes. You took some of Israel's land, but on that day Israel will take yours!
translation_verse: Yiti ɛ́mɔtie, mmerɛ bie ɔ́ba, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne, bɔ ngɔmaa bɛkɔte koɛ nwo ngunga wɔ Amonfoɛ kuro Raba; ɔkɔkakyi kurofoen so sire, na bɛkɔfa see bɛkɔyera ye nwo nguraa mɔ. Na bɛ bɔ Yisrael agyapadeɛ oolili bɛ dɔ ne, Yisrael kosa kole ye nikye, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Cry, people of Heshbon; your town will become a pile of rubble. You will turn here and there, but your path will be blocked. Put on sackcloth and mourn, you citizens of Rabbah, because the idol you worship will be taken to a foreign country, along with its priests and temple officials.
translation_verse: “Hesebon, bɔ awuye, ofikyɛ Aye abɔ! Raba mma mmrasua mɔ, ɛ́mɔsu. Ɛ́mɔfa ɛsɛen tena bɛhera, ɛ́mɔbɔ awuye ná ɛmɔli akɔneaba wɔ fasue nemɔ afia! Ofikyɛ bɛkɔhye bɛ hene ne nnure bɛkɔhɔ, bɔ ye asɔfo ne atitire mɔ bɛboka so ɔ.

english_verse: You rebellious Ammonites trust your wealth and ask, “Who could attack us?” But I warn you not to boast when your strength is fading.
translation_verse: Wɔ, baa brasua bɔ ayɛ lɔen ɔ, Nzu ati yeɛ ɛfa wɔ bɔnza nemɔ hoahoa wɔ nwo ɔ, wɔ bɔnza bɔ ɔkye aleɛ ne, wɔ bɔ ɛfale wɔ nwo tole w’anwonyadeɛ so hane kyɛ, ‘Nwa yeɛ okodwɔso kotia me ɔ?’

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will send neighboring nations to strike you with terror. You will be scattered, with no one to care for your refugees.
translation_verse: Tie, bɛ bɔ bapɛ wɔ nwo bayia amukoraa, ngɔfa bɛ nwo suronyi ngɔto wɔ so, Asafo AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne. Na bɛkɔfoa ɛmɔ ngoko ngoko bɔ sona li ebiala si ɔ, na bɛ bɔ banwati nemɔ, ebiala ngɔhora bɛ noa boaboa.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Edom
translation_verse: Na ye si ye, ngosa ngɔfa Amonfoɛ ngofi nnurehyelɛ nu ngɔwa, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.” Nyameɛ bua Edom ndɛen

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful says about Edom: Wisdom and common sense have vanished from Teman.
translation_verse: Bɔ Asafo AWURADE kã fa Edom nwo ole kyɛ, “Aso nworɛ nne Teman ko? Aso nworɛfoɛ bendu foɛ ko anaa? Aso bɛ nworɛ atu amini anaa?

english_verse: I will send disaster to punish you descendants of Esau, so anyone from Dedan had better turn around and run back home.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ, Dedanfoɛ, ɛ́mɔnwati, ɛ́mɔsa ɛmɔ si, ɛ́mɔfeafea ngumaa nemɔ anu, ofikyɛ ngɔprapra Yisɔ amaneɛnwunɛ ngogua ye so wɔ mmerɛ bɔ ngɔɔhwe ye so ne.

english_verse: People who harvest grapes leave some for the poor. Thieves who break in at night take only what they want.
translation_verse: Sɛ bobetelɛfoɛ bɛba wɔ berɛ a, aso bɛngɔyakyi bobe mmaa ne kãa wɔ so? Sɛ awuefoɛ bɛba kɔngɔen a, aso nna bɔ bekuro ɔ yeɛ bekowua ɔ?

english_verse: But I will take everything that belongs to you, people of Edom, and I will uncover every place where you try to hide. Then you will die, and so will your children, relatives, and neighbors.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yisɔ de, mabɔ ye kwaterekwa, mama ye afealeɛ mɔ nwo alela berɛ, na ɔngora mva ye nwo mvea. Bahũhũ ye boso ama mɔ, oliɛma mɔ ne ye mmango mɔ, na ye boso anua.

english_verse: But I can be trusted to care for your orphans and widows.
translation_verse: Yakyi wɔ nyisiaa nemɔ berɛ, na ngɔmaa bɛkɔtena ngoa nu; na odi kyɛ wɔ kunafoɛ nemɔ, bɛfa bɛ wora bewura me nu.”

english_verse: Even those nations that don't deserve to be punished will have to drink from the cup of my anger. So how can you possibly hope to escape?
translation_verse: Na AWURADE nwa nyoo, “Tie, sɛ bɛ bɔ ahaa onni kyɛ bɛno sɔ kwangoa ne po bano amba a, né aso wɔ de ɛkɔfa wɔ nwo koli anaa? Ɛngɔfa wɔ nwo ngoli, na mmom amba, ɛkɔno kwangoa ne .

english_verse: I, the Lord, swear in my own name that your city of Bozrah and all your towns will suffer a horrible fate. They will lie in ruins forever, and people will use the name “Bozrah” as a curse word.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ mata me bɔbɔ me nwo ndaen kyɛ Bosra kɔyɛ kurofoen, ngorohoɛ nikye, kuro bɔ wabɔ ɔ, ɔne ɛnomalɛ nikye, na ye nwo nguro amukoraa kɔyɛ nguro bɔ babɔ ɔ afebɔɔ, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.”

english_verse: I have sent a messenger to command the nations to prepare for war against you people of Edom.
translation_verse: Mate edwirɛ bie mafi AWURADE berɛ, na basoma ɛbɔfoɛ wɔ maenmaensofoɛ nemɔ berɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔboaboa ɛmɔ noa, ɛ́mɔdwɔso bɛɛfa koɛ bɛtoa ye, ɛ́mɔdwɔso bɛhɔ koɛ ne!”

english_verse: Your nation will be small, yet hated by other nations.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ tie, ngɔmaa ɛkɔyɛ kãa wɔ maen maen mɔ nu bɔ bebu wɔ animtia wɔ mmenia nu ɔ.

english_verse: Pride tricks you into thinking that other nations look at you with fear. You live along the cliffs and high in the mountains like the eagles, but I am the Lord, and I will bring you down.
translation_verse: Wɔ nwo suronyi ne w’ahone nu anwomasoɛ ne, balakalaka wɔ. Wɔ bɔ ɛte nyɔbotaen bɔen mɔ nu, ɔne bokaa ti afia paa ɔ, ɔwɔ nu kyɛ ɛnwo wɔ saen anwuro anwuro kyɛ kɔleɛ deɛ de, nakoso ngɔhwe wɔ ngofi dɔ ngɔto ase, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: as bad as the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah and towns nearby. The towns of Edom will be empty.
translation_verse: Na kyɛbɔ bɛsɛkyele Sodom ne Gomora ne nguro bɔ bepingyepingye bɛ nemɔ nen, kuro sona biala ngɔtena berɛ, yeɛ dasaniɛ biala ngotu ngɔtena nu, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔtie, ɔkɔwa kyɛ gyata bɔ ofi Yɔɔdan ɛhɔayeɛ nu, bɔ ɔba bako tia anwoserɛfoɛ atenaleɛ ne ɔ, nakoso mvum nu, ngɔma Edom kofi berɛ kɔnwati. Na sona bɔ maneanea nu maye ne, ngɔfa berɛ ngowura ye sa. Na nwa yeɛ ɔte kyɛ me ɔ? Nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora kobisa me dwirɛ ɔ? Na mmoaenneafoɛ beni yeɛ ɔkɔhora me nyunu gyina ɔ?

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will reach the Red Sea and cause the earth to shake.
translation_verse: B’asefinɛ nwo dede ne kɔma aseɛ kɔwoso, na awuye bɔ bɛbɔ ne, bɛkɔte ye wɔ Ɛpo Kɔkorɛ noa dɔ paa.

english_verse: An enemy will swoop down to attack you, like an eagle spreading its wings and circling over Bozrah. Your warriors will be as fearful as women giving birth. What the Lord Says about Damascus
translation_verse: Tie, ɔkɔfo ná watu kyɛ kɔleɛ, na ɔkɔtrɛtrɛ ye ndaa nu wɔ Bosra so. Na sɔ kyẽa ne, Edom anwoserɛfoɛ bɛ kra kɔnwati kofi bɛ nwo, kyɛ brasua bɔ wafo aworɛ so ɔ ye deɛ. Nyameɛ bua Damasko ndɛen

english_verse: The Lord says about Damascus: The towns of Hamath and Arpad have heard your bad news. They have lost hope, and worries roll over them like ocean waves.
translation_verse: Bɔ ɔfa Damasko nwo ɛhe: Hamate ne Apade nyunu agua ase, ofikyɛ bate edwirɛ bɔ ɔnyɛ fɛ ɔ; ahunundetelɛ atɔ bɛ so, aworabɔlɛ wɔ ɛpo so, ɔngora nyɛ konn.

english_verse: You people of Damascus have lost your courage, and in panic you turn to run, gripped by fear and pain.
translation_verse: Damasko ayɛ hodwoo, wakakyi ye nwo kyɛ ɔnwati, ahunundetelɛ atɔ ye so, yealɛ ne aworabɔlɛ ato ye kyɛ brasua bɔ wafo aworɛ so ɔ.

english_verse: Once I was pleased with your famous city. But now I warn you, “Escape while you still can!”
translation_verse: Ayɛyelɛ kuro ne, m’anika kuro ne! Nea kyɛbɔ banyakyi ye ɔ!

english_verse: Soon, even your best soldiers will lie dead in your streets. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken.
translation_verse: Yiti ye mmerandeɛ nemɔ kɔtotɔ wɔ ye mmorɔnoɛ nemɔ aso, na bekohũhũ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ amukoraa sɔ kyẽa ne, Asafo AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: I will set fire to your city walls and burn down the fortresses King Benhadad built. Nebuchadnezzar and the People of the Desert
translation_verse: Na ngɔto Damasko fasue ne anu see, na ɔkɔyera Ben Hadade anwoserɛ afealeɛ nemɔ. Nyameɛ bua Arabia mmusua kure ndɛen

english_verse: Here is what the Lord says about the Kedar tribe and the desert villages that were conquered by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia: Listen, you people of Kedar and the other tribes of the eastern desert. I have told Nebuchadnezzar to attack and destroy you.
translation_verse: Kedare ne Hasɔ ahennie mɔ bɔ Babilɔn hene Nebukadenesa kɔbɔ bɛ ne, bɔ AWURADE kã fa bɛ nwo ɛhe: “Ɛ́mɔdwɔso bɛfa koɛ bɛɛtoa Kedare, ná ɛ́mɔnua eyia afiteleɛfoɛ nemɔ boso.

english_verse: Run and hide, you people of the desert who live in villages! Nebuchadnezzar has big plans for you.
translation_verse: Ao Hasɔfoɛ, ɛ́mɔnwati, ɛmɔhɔ dedeede, ɛmɔɔfeafea ngumaa nemɔ anu, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne. Ofikyɛ Babilɔn hene Nebukadenesa wabɔ ɛmɔ nwo porɛ, na wafa ɛmɔ nwo adwene tɛɛ.

english_verse: You have no city walls and no neighbors to help, yet you think you're safe— so I told him to attack.
translation_verse: “Ɛ́mɔdwɔso, ɛ́mɔfa koɛ bɛɛtoa maen bɔ ye nwo atɔ ye, bɔ ɔte asomdwee nu, bɔ olle pambim mɔ anaa buralɛ bɔ ɔbeabea pambim mɔ si, maen bɔ ye ngome yeɛ ɔte berɛ ne, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Then your camels and large herds will be yours no longer. People of the Arabian Desert, disaster will strike you from every side, and you will be scattered everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Bɛ mbɔngɔ kɔyɛ koɛ nu nzesadeɛ, yeɛ bɛ nyɛmmoa kɔyɛ nikyee bɔ bɛfẽ bɛfa ɔ. Na bɛ bɔ bepiapia bɛ ti angyɛnu ne, ngɔbɔ bɛ ngɔsande ngogua nekaa amukoraa; ngɔmaa b’amaneɛnwunɛ kofi nekaa biala kɔɔto bɛ, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Only jackals will live where your villages once stood. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Elam
translation_verse: Hasɔ kɔyɛ ɛserɛ so ngyea b’atenaleɛ ne kurofoen afebɔɔ; sona biala ngɔtena berɛ, dasaniɛ biala ngɔtena nu.” Nyameɛ bua Elam ndɛen

english_verse: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me to say: People of Elam, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will kill the archers who make your army strong.
translation_verse: Asafo AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛhe: “Tie, Elam agyaen bɔ yeɛ ɔte b’anwoserɛ titire ne, ngobubu nu,

english_verse: Your king and his officials will die, and I will rule in their place. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ngɔfa m’ahennie bia ngosie Elam, na ngohũhũ b’ɛhene ne b’atitire nemɔ, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: But I promise that someday I will bring your people back to their land.
translation_verse: Nakoso ngyẽa bɔ oli nziɛ ne anu, ngosa ngɔfa Elam ngofi nnurehyelɛ nu ngɔwa, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: The Lord told me to say: Announce what will happen and don't leave anything out.
translation_verse: AWURADE dwirɛ bɔ ɔnate ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ Yeremia so lale ye ali fale Babilɔn ne Kaldea aseɛ nwo ne, ye ɛhe:

english_verse: Raise the signal flags; shout so all nations can hear— Babylon will be captured! Marduk, Babylon's god, will be ashamed and terrified, and his idols broken.
translation_verse: “Ɛ́mɔbɔ ye dawure wɔ maen maen mɔ so, ɛ́mɔfa bɛto dwaa, ɛ́mɔfa frangaa bɛpena berɛ, ɛ́mɔfa bɛto dwaa; nnɛma ɛmɔkata so, na mmom ɛmɔhã kyɛ, ‘Bali Babilɔn so ngonim, Bel nyunu agua ase, babubu Merodake nu pasapasa, ye mmosoen mɔ nyunu agua ase, babubu ye amoen mɔ nu pasapasa.’

english_verse: The attack on the Babylonians will come from the north; they and their animals will run, leaving the land empty. Israel and Judah Will Return to Their Land
translation_verse: “Ofikyɛ maen bie kofi sorɔ dɔ kɔfa koɛ kɔɔteta ye, na ɔkɔma ye maen ne kɔbɔ. Sona ne kaka biala ngɔtena nu, bekotu bekofi berɛ bɛkɔhɔ.

english_verse: The Lord said: People of Israel and Judah, when these things happen you will weep, and together you will return to your land and worship me, the Lord your God.
translation_verse: “Sɔ ngyẽa nemɔ anu, sɔ mmerɛ ne, Yisraelfoɛ ne Yudafoɛ bele esuɛ bɛkɔbɔ nu bɛkɔwa, na bɛkɔwa bɛkɔɔpena AWURADE bɛ Nyameɛ si atee, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: You will ask the way to Zion and then come and join with me in making an agreement you won't break or forget.
translation_verse: Bekobisa atee bɔ ɔkɔ Sion, bɔ bɛ nye kyire dɔ ɔ. Na bɛkɔhã kyɛ, ‘Ɛmɔbra maa yɛfa yɛ nwo yɛɛbata AWURADE, wɔ apam bɔ ɔwɔ berɛ afebɔɔ, bɔ yɛ wora ngofi ye le ɔ nu.’

english_verse: My people, you are lost sheep abandoned in the mountains by their shepherds. You don't even remember your resting place.
translation_verse: “Me maen akakyi mmoaen bɔ bamini ɔ; bɛ neafoɛ nemɔ amaa bali makyebu. Bɛmaa behyinini wɔ mmokaa nemɔ aso; bafi mmokaa so bahɔ pambaa mɔ so, bɛ wora afi bɛ dabea.

english_verse: I am your true pastureland, the one who gave hope to your ancestors. But you abandoned me, so when your enemies found you, they felt no guilt as they gobbled you up.
translation_verse: Bɛ bɔ benwuni bɛ ne amukoraa bahye bɛ bali, na bɛ pɔfoɛ mɔ nwa, ‘Yɛnni fɔ, ofikyɛ bayɔ bɔne batia AWURADE, bɛ tenenee atenaleɛ, AWURADE bɔ ɔte bɛ nana mɔ anyelasoɛ ne.’

english_verse: Escape from Babylonia, my people. Get out of that country! Don't wait for anyone else.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔnwati béfi Babilɔn, ná ɛ́mɔfi Kaldeafoɛ aseɛ ne aso bɛhɔ, na ɛ́mɔyɛ kyɛ mbɔngye nyii bɔ beli mmoaen kure nemɔ nyunu ɔ.

english_verse: In the north I am bringing great nations together. They will attack Babylon and capture it. The arrows they shoot are like the best soldiers, always finding their target.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ, tie, mebaakanyane maen maen mbiri mbiri fekue bɔ befi sorɔ dɔ maa bedwɔso bɛfa koɛ bɛbatoa Babilɔn. Bekotu bɛ nye bekosie ye so, na berɛ yeɛ bɛkɔɔfa ye bekofi bɛkɔhɔ ɔ. B’agyaen mɔ te kyɛ koɛhonɛniɛ bɔ ye nye gyene, bɔ ɔndo mvo ɔ.

english_verse: Babylonia will be conquered, and its enemies will carry off everything they want. Babylon Will Be Disgraced The Lord said:
translation_verse: Kaldea kɔkakyi koɛ nu nzesadeɛ, na bɛ bɔ bɛfẽ ye nningyein bɛfa amukoraa b’ahone kɔtɔ bɛ kunu, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: People of Babylonia, you were glad to rob my people. You had a good time, making more noise than horses and jumping around like calves threshing grain.
translation_verse: “Ao, ɛmɔ bɔ ɛmɔfẽ m’agyapadeɛ ne ɔ, ɔnate kyɛ ɛmɔ nye gyele, ɔnate kyɛ ɛmɔlili ahurusi ne ati, ɛmɔayɛ mbiri mbiri kyɛ nandwie beleɛ akrɔngrɔma bɔ ɛserɛ apɛ ye nwo ayia ɔ, yeɛ ɛmɔsu kyɛ nandwie nyii’.

english_verse: The city of Babylon was like a mother to you. But it will be disgraced and become nothing but a barren desert.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ ani ye nyunu kogua ase paa, bɔ ɔwole ɛmɔ ne, ɔkɔfɛre. Ɛ́mɔtie, ɔkɔyɛ maen bɔ animnyam abɔ ye koraa wɔ maen maen mɔ nu ɔ, ɔkɔyɛ aseɛ pralaa, aseɛ katerepee ne ɛserɛ.

english_verse: My anger will destroy Babylon, and no one will live there. Everyone who passes by will be shocked to see what has happened.
translation_verse: Ɔnate AWURADE yaafɛlɛ piri ne ati, ebiala ngɔtena so, na mmom ɔkɔyɛ kurofoen bɔkɔɔ. Ebiala bɔ ɔpɛ nu wɔ Babilɔn ne, ye nwo kodwiri ye, na okosobi ye noa, ɔnate amaneɛ amukoraa bɔ wato Babilɔn ne ati.

english_verse: Babylon has rebelled against me. Archers, take your places. Shoot all your arrows at Babylon.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ bɔ ɛmɔse agyaen to amukoraa, ɛ́mɔgyina bɛfa koɛ bɛɛtoa Babilɔn bɛbra ye nwo beyia; ɛ́mɔto besina ye, nnɛma ɛmɔyakyi agyaen ko po, ofikyɛ wayɔ bɔne watia AWURADE.

english_verse: Attack from every side! Babylon surrenders! The enemy tears down its walls and towers. I am taking my revenge by doing to Babylon what it did to other cities.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔtea nu bégua ye so bɛbra beyia. Wama ye sa so kyɛ ɔngɔhora koɛ ne aso toa, ye nyinasoɛ adwiri agua, babubu ye fasue nemɔ; ofikyɛ AWURADE wereɛtɔlɛ ne ɛne. Ɛ́mɔtɔ ye so wereɛ, bɔ wayɔ ne ala bie yeɛ ɛ́mɔfa beli ye ɔ.

english_verse: There is no one in Babylonia to plant or harvest crops. Even foreigners who lived there have left for their homelands, afraid of the enemy armies.
translation_verse: Kuaniɛ ne, ɔne bɔ otira dadeɛ koateɛ wɔ mmakaammaa telɛ mmerɛ ne, ɛ́mɔnua bɛ boso béfi Babilɔn. Na ɔnate nhyɛsoɛ ngrandɛ ne anwo suronyi ti, ebiala kosa kɔhɔ ye maen nu, na ebiala kɔnwati kɔhɔ ye bɔbɔ ye aseɛ so.

english_verse: Israel is a flock of sheep scattered by hungry lions. The king of Assyria first gobbled Israel up. Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylonia, crunched on Israel's bones.
translation_verse: Yisrael te mmoaen kure bɔ babɔ ye basande ɔ; gyata mɔ afoa ye maa wanwati wahɔ. Bɔ oli moa ɔ, Asiria hene ahu ye, na bɔ ɔpɛ ye bo ɔ, Babilɔn hene Nebukadenesa abubu ye mmowue nu.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, punished the king of Assyria, and I will also punish the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Yiti, Asafo AWURADE, Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Ɛ́mɔtie, ngɔhwe Babilɔn hene ne ye maen so, kyɛbɔ ndwene Asiria hene so nen.

english_verse: But I will bring Israel back to its own land. The people will be like sheep eating their fill on Mount Carmel and in Bashan, in the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead.
translation_verse: Ngosa ngɔfa Yisrael ngɔhɔ ye atenaleɛ, na okodidi wɔ Kamɛl ne Basan’. Ye kra ko koyi wɔ Efraim bokaa ne Gileade bokaa so.

english_verse: I will rescue a few people from Israel and Judah. I will forgive them so completely that their sin and guilt will disappear, never to be found. The Lord's Commands to the Enemies of Babylonia
translation_verse: Na sɔ ngyẽa ne anu, sɔ mmerɛ ne, bɛkɔpena Yisrael amumuyɛɛ, nakoso bengonya bie; yeɛ bɛkɔpena Yuda ye bɔne, nakoso bengonwu bie, ofikyɛ bɛ bɔ ngɔmaa bɛkɔha wa ne, ngɔfa bɛ bɔne ngɔhyɛ bɛ, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have told the enemies of Babylonia, “Attack the people of Merathaim and Pekod. Kill them all! Destroy their possessions!”
translation_verse: Fa koɛ kɔteta Meratayim maen ne, yeɛ bɛ bɔ bɛte Pekode ɔ. Kuku bɛ, ná nua bɛ boso, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne, na yɔ kyɛbɔ ahyɛdeɛ amukoraa bɔ mafa mama wɔ ne, ɔte ne ala.

english_verse: Sounds of war and the noise of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Koɛ nwo dede wɔ aseɛ ne aso, yeɛ ɛsɛkyelɛ kandinga paa koso!

english_verse: Babylonia was a hammer pounding every country, but now it lies broken. What a shock to the nations of the world!
translation_verse: Aseɛ ye amukoraa so bɔsobaka ne, nea kyɛbɔ basi bapepɛ nu babubu nu ɔ! Nea kyɛbɔ Babilɔn wayɛ maen maen mɔ nu kurofoen ɔ!

english_verse: Babylonia challenged me, the Lord God All-Powerful, but that nation doesn't know it is caught in a trap that I set.
translation_verse: Ao Babilɔn, masua wɔ ngaen, mahye wɔ, na wɔ de annwu ye; banwu wɔ, yeɛ bahye wɔ, ofikyɛ adwɔso atia AWURADE.

english_verse: I've brought out my weapons, and with them I will put a curse on Babylonia.
translation_verse: AWURADE abukye ye akodeɛ sua ne, na waye ye ɛyaafɛlɛ akodeɛ nemɔ wafite, ofikyɛ Asafo AWURADE Nyameɛ ole adwuma ɔyɔ wɔ Kaldeafoɛ aseɛ so.

english_verse: Come from far away, you enemies of Babylon! Pile up the grain from its storehouses, and destroy it completely, along with everything else.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔfi aseɛ noa dɔ dedeede bɛbra ye so, ɛ́mɔbukyebukye nekaa bɔ osie ye nningyein ne, ɛ́mɔboaboa ye noa kyɛ aburoo, na ɛ́mɔsɛkye ye bɔkɔɔ; nnɛmɔma ye nwo hwee ka berɛ.

english_verse: Kill the soldiers of Babylonia, because the time has come for them to be punished.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔhũhũ ye nandwie nyii nemɔ amukoraa, ɛ́mɔma bɛtorotoro bɛhɔ akumyɛɛ. Bɛ yaakɔ, ofikyɛ bɛ kyẽa ne adwu, b’asohwenɛ mmerɛ ne ɛne.

english_verse: The Babylonian army destroyed my temple, but soon I will take revenge. Then refugees from Babylon will tell about it in Zion.
translation_verse: “Ɛ́mɔtie oo, kyɛ, bɛ bɔ bɛ́nwati bɛpena bɛ ti bedidi nu befi Babilɔn aseɛ so ne, bɛ́ba bɛbabɔ AWURADE yɛ Nyameɛ wereɛtɔlɛ, ye asɔneyɛɛ sua nwo wereɛtɔlɛ nwo dawure wɔ Sion ɔ.

english_verse: Attack Babylon, enemy archers; set up camp around the city, and don't let anyone escape. It challenged me, the holy God, so do to it what it did to other cities. Proud Babylon Will Fall
translation_verse: “Ɛ́mɔboaboa agyaentolɛfoɛ noa maa bɛfa koɛ bɛɛtoa Babilɔn: ɛmɔ amukoraa bɔ ɛmɔto agyaen ɔ, ɛ́mɔkyekye asikyeleɛ bɛbra ye nwo beyia; nnɛmɔma bɛ nu biala nwati’. Ɛ́mɔtua ye kerɛ kyɛbɔ ye yɔleɛ te ɔ. Bɔ wayɔ amukoraa, ɛ́mɔyɔ ye bie betua ye so, ofikyɛ wayɛ AWURADE, Yisrael Krongronniɛ ne aso anwomasoɛ.

english_verse: People of Babylon, I, the Lord, promise that even your best soldiers will lie dead in the streets.
translation_verse: Yiti ye mmerandeɛ mɔ kowuwu kogua mmorɔnoɛ nemɔ aso, na bekonua ye koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ amukoraa bɛ boso sɔ kyẽa ne, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Babylon, you should be named, “The Proud One.” But the time has come when I, the Lord All-Powerful, will punish you.
translation_verse: Wɔ, anwomasoɛniɛ, tie, meko metia wɔ, ofikyɛ wɔ kyẽa ne adwu, mmerɛ bɔ ngɔhwe wɔ so ne ɛne, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: You are proud, but you will stumble and fall, and no one will help you up. I will set your villages on fire, and everything around you will go up in flames.
translation_verse: Na anwomasoɛniɛ paa ne, okosoti kofĩ ase, na ebiala ngɔma ye so; ngɔto ye nguro nemɔ anu see, na ɔkɔyera nikyee biala bɔ wapɛ ye nwo wayia ɔ.

english_verse: You Babylonians were cruel to Israel and Judah. You took them captive, and now you refuse to let them go.
translation_verse: “AWURADE nwa nyoo: Bɛhyɛle Yisraelfoɛ so, yeɛ bɛhyɛle Yudafoɛ koso so, na bɛ bɔ bɛhyele bɛ nnure ne amukoraa, bɛwɛnene bɛ anyeserɛ so paa, na bambene so kyɛ bɛkɔyakyi bɛ maa bɛkɔhɔ ɔ.

english_verse: But I, the Lord All-Powerful, will rescue and protect them. I will bring peace to their land and trouble to yours.
translation_verse: Nakoso bɛ Defoɛ ne nwo yɛ se; ye dumaa ole Asafo AWURADE. Okoli bɛ dwirɛ kɔma bɛ amba, amaa ɔnate so wama aseɛ ye ale ye nwome, ná wama basabasa ato Babilɔnfoɛ.

english_verse: I have declared war on you, your officials, and advisors.
translation_verse: “Ngrandɛ gyi Kaldeafoɛ so, yeɛ Babilɔnfoɛ ne b’atitire ne bɛ nworɛfoɛ so! AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: This war will prove that your prophets are liars and fools. And it will frighten your warriors.
translation_verse: Ngrandɛ gyi ngɔndorɔfoɛ mɔ so, maa ɔnate so bayɛ ngwaseafoɛ; ngrandɛ gyi bɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ so, amaa ɔnate so ahunundetelɛ atɔ bɛ so!

english_verse: Then your chariot horses and the foreigners in your army will refuse to go into battle, and the enemy will carry away everything you treasure.
translation_verse: Ngrandɛ gyi bɛ mbɔngɔ ne bɛ teaseɛnam mɔ so, yeɛ ogyi koɛhonɛfoɛ ɛwɔfoɛ amukoraa bɔ baatena bɛ nu nemɔ aso, na bɛkɔyɛ kyɛ mmrasua. Ngrandɛ gyi b’anwonyadeɛ so, na bɛkɔfẽ sɔ nningyein nemɔ bɛkɔfa.

english_verse: Your rivers and canals will dry up. All of this will happen, because your land is full of idols, and they have made fools of you.
translation_verse: Wawa ape b’asue mɔ aso, na bɛkɔwewe, ofikyɛ ɔte aseɛ bɔ amoen mɔ bayi so to, na babobɔ bɛ mmosoen mɔ nwo laen.

english_verse: I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the nearby towns, and I will destroy Babylon just as completely. No one will live there again. Babylonia Is Invaded The Lord said:
translation_verse: Na kyɛbɔ Nyameɛ sɛkyele Sodom ne Gomora ne nguro bɔ bepingyepingye bɛ nemɔ nen, kuro sona biala ngɔtena berɛ, yeɛ dasaniɛ biala ngotu ngɔtena nu, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Far to the north, a nation and its allies have been awakened. They are powerful and ready for war.
translation_verse: “Tie, maen bie kofi sorɔ dɔ kɔwa, ɔte maen piri, na ahemvo pee bɛkɔma bɛ nwo so bekofi aseɛ ne noa dɔ paa.

english_verse: Bows and arrows and swords are in their hands. The soldiers are cruel and show no pity. The hoofbeats of their horses echo like ocean waves crashing against the shore. The army has lined up for battle and is coming to attack you, people of Babylonia!
translation_verse: Betiratira agyaen ne pealɛɛ, bɛ ti anu yɛ se, na bɛnze anwumvoin. Bɛ ndeateamuɛ te kyɛ ɛpo bɔ obu fa so ɔ; bɛtete mbɔngɔ so, basiesie bɛ nwo kyɛ sona bɔ ɔkɔ koɛ ɔ, na wɔ, Babilɔn awa brasua, wɔ yeɛ bɛfa koɛ bɛbatoa wɔ ɔ!

english_verse: Ever since your king heard about this army, he has been weak with fear; he twists and turns in pain like a woman giving birth.
translation_verse: “Babilɔn hene ate bɛ nga, na ye abasa nu ayɛ hodwoo; ahunundetelɛ atɔ ye so, ɔte yealɛ kyɛ brasua bɔ wafo aworɛ so ɔ.

english_verse: Babylonia, I will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: “Tie, ɔ́ba kyɛ gyata bɔ ofi asue Yɔɔdan noa ɛhɔayeɛ nu bɔ ɔfa koɛ kɔteta anwoserɛfoɛ atenaleɛ ɔ, nakoso ngɔmaa bɛkɔnwati bekofi ye nwo mvum nu, na ngɔma bɔ maneanea nu maye ye ne koli ye so. Ofikyɛ nwa yeɛ ɔte kyɛ me ɔ? Nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora kobisa me dwirɛ ɔ? Na mmoaenneafoɛ beni yeɛ ɔkɔhora me nyunu gyina ɔ?

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will be heard among the nations, and the earth will shake.
translation_verse: Ese bɔ bɛkɔbɔ ye wɔ Babilɔn so ngonimlilɛ nwo ne, ɔkɔmaa aseɛ kɔwoso, na bɛkɔte ye awuyebɔlɛ wɔ maen maen mɔ so.

english_verse: I, the Lord, am sending a wind to destroy the people of Babylonia and Babylon, its capital.
translation_verse: AWURADE nwa nyoo: “Tie, ngɔkanyane sɛkyefoɛ sunzum bie ngotia Babilɔn, yeɛ bɛ bɔ baatena mmenia bɔ bɛko betia me nemɔ anu ne.

english_verse: Foreign soldiers will come from every direction, and when the disaster is over, Babylonia will be empty and worthless.
translation_verse: Ngɔsoma mmenia bɔ behuhu so ɔ maa bɛkɔhɔ Babilɔn, na bekohuhu ye so, ná babɔ ye maen ne tɔɔ, ofikyɛ amaneɛnwunɛ kyẽa ne, bɛkɔfa koɛ bɛkɔteta ye bɛkɔbra bekoyia.

english_verse: I will tell these soldiers, “Attack quickly, before the Babylonians can string their bows or put on their armor. Kill their best soldiers and destroy their army!”
translation_verse: Ma agyaentolɛniɛ ɔto ye agyaen ɔfa koɛ teta sona bɔ okundu ye agyaen nu ne, ɔne bɔ ɔfa ye buralɛ akokyɛm hoahoa ye nwo ne. Nnɛmɔma ye mmerandeɛ nemɔ bɛfa bɛ nwo bedi, na ɛ́mɔnua ye lɔen ne amukoraa bɛ boso bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel and Judah is guilty. But I, the Lord All-Powerful, their holy God, have not abandoned them.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ Yisrael ne Yuda bɛ Nyameɛ Asafo AWURADE ne, ɔppole bɛ, ɔwɔ nu kyɛ bɛ bɔne bɔ bayɔ batia Yisrael Krongronniɛ ne, wayi b’aseɛ ne aso to de.

english_verse: Get out of Babylon! Run for your lives! If you stay, you will be killed when I take revenge on the city and punish it for its sins.
translation_verse: “Ɛ́mɔnwati béfi Babilɔn, ɛ́mɔma ebiala ɔpepɛ ole ye kra; nnɛmɔmaa ɔnate ye amumuyɛɛ ti ɛmɔ boso nua, ofikyɛ AWURADE ye wereɛtɔlɛ mmerɛ ne ɛhe, na okotua ye so kerɛ.

english_verse: Babylon was my golden cup, filled with the wine of my anger. The nations of the world got drunk on this wine and went insane.
translation_verse: Né Babilɔn te AWURADE sa nu esikaa kɔkorɛ kulie bɔ ɔmane aseɛ amukoraa bole ɔ; maen maen mɔ bano ye nzaa ne bie, yiti maen maen mɔ babobɔ laen.

english_verse: But suddenly, Babylon will fall and be destroyed. I, the Lord, told the foreigners who lived there, “Weep for the city! Get medicine for its wounds; maybe they will heal.”
translation_verse: Mvum nu, Babilɔn afi ase, na wabɔ, ɛ́mɔsu ye! Ɛ́mɔfa ayire bɛwasa ye nwo bɔ otutu ye ne aso, ebiaa ye nwo kɔsande ye.

english_verse: The foreigners answered, “We have already tried to treat Babylon's wounds, but they would not heal. Come on, let's all go home to our own countries. Nothing is left in Babylonia; everything is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Ahaa yɛpena kyɛ yɛsa Babilɔn anwonyerɛ, nakoso wande apɔ. Ɛ́mɔpo ye, ná ɛ́mɔma yɛ nu biala ɔhɔ ye bɔbɔ ye maen nu, ofikyɛ ye ndɛen bɔ babua ye ne, wafo wadwu nyameɛso, na bama so baadwu ewienu dɔ.

english_verse: I, the Lord, want Babylon destroyed, because its army destroyed my temple. So, you kings of Media, sharpen your arrows and pick up your shields.
translation_verse: “Ɛ́mɔsi agyaen nemɔ noa! Ɛ́mɔma akokyɛm nemɔ aso! AWURADE akanyane Medese ahemvo mɔ sunzum, ofikyɛ wanya Babilɔn nwo adwene kyɛ ɔkɔsɛkye ye, AWURADE wereɛtɔlɛ ne, ye ɛne; ye asɔneyɛɛ sua nwo wereɛtɔlɛ ne, yɛ ɛne.

english_verse: People of Babylon, you live along the Euphrates River and are surrounded by canals. You are rich, but now the time has come for you to die.
translation_verse: Ao, wɔ bɔ ɛte asue pee noa, bɔ anwonyadeɛ abu wɔ so ɔ, w’ayieleɛ awa, na wɔ ngoa nyamaa nu ate.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, swear by my own life that enemy soldiers will fill your streets like a swarm of locusts. They will shout and celebrate their victory. A Hymn of Praise (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Asafo AWURADE ata ye bɔbɔ ye nwo ndaen kyɛ: Amba, ngɔma mmenia koyi wɔ nu mitimiti kyɛ mmɛbɛ, na bɛkɔbɔ wɔ nwo ese.

english_verse: The waters in the heavens roar at his command. He makes clouds appear; he sends the wind from his storehouse and makes lightning flash in the rain.
translation_verse: Ɔbɔ nu kurudududu a, nzue pee ba ewienu, ɔma tutue fi aseɛ noa dɔ tu kɔ anwuro; esue tɔ a, ɔma agralaa tete, na ɔma mvrama tu fi nekaa bɔ osie ye nningyein ne.

english_verse: God used his wisdom and power to create the earth and spread out the heavens.
translation_verse: “Ye yeɛ ole ye tumi ɔbɔle aseɛ ɔ, ye nworɛ yeɛ ɔnate so fale wiase tindimuni berɛ ɔ, na ye nimdeɛ yeɛ ɔfa trɛtrɛle ewienu nu ɔ.

english_verse: People who make idols are stupid! They will be disappointed, because their false gods cannot breathe.
translation_verse: Sona biala te kwaseaa bɔ olle nimdeɛ ɔ; esikaa kɔkorɛ dwumvoɛ biala, ye mmosoen yeɛ begua ye nyunu ase ɔ; ye amoen nemɔ te nnakannaka, na nwomeɛ biala ɔnne bɛ nu.

english_verse: Idols are merely a joke, and when the time is right, they will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Bɛte nningyein mbaen, bɛte ngorohoɛ nikye, na b’asohwenɛ mmerɛ ne anu, bɛ boso konua.

english_verse: But the Lord, Israel's God, is all-powerful. He created everything, and he chose Israel to be his very own. God's Hammer The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yakob ye bue deɛ de, ɔtte kyɛ sɔ nningyein nemɔ, ofikyɛ ye de, ye yeɛ ɔyɔle nningyein amukoraa ɔ. Yisrael te abusua kure bɔ ɔte ye agyapadeɛ ɔ, na ye dumaa ole Asafo AWURADE. Babilɔn te Nyameɛ abopura

english_verse: Babylonia, you were my hammer; I used you to pound nations and break kingdoms,
translation_verse: Wɔ yeɛ ɛte m’abopura ne koɛ nu akodeɛ ɔ, mefa wɔ yeɛ mebubu maen maen mɔ nu ɔ, na mefa wɔ yeɛ mesɛkye ahennie mɔ ɔ;

english_verse: But now, my people will watch, while I repay you for what you did to Zion.
translation_verse: “Na ngotua Babilɔn ne Kaldeafoɛ amukoraa bɛ so kerɛ, ɔnate b’amumuyɛɛ amukoraa bɔ bayɔ ye wɔ Sion bɔ ɛmɔ nye tua ne ati, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: You destroyed the nations and seem strong as a mountain, but I am your enemy. I might even grab you and roll you off a cliff. When I am finished, you'll only be a pile of scorched bricks.
translation_verse: “Tie, wɔ, bokaa sɛkyefoɛ bɔ ɛsɛkye aseɛ ye amukoraa ɔ, meko metia wɔ, na ngɔtengyɛ me sa ngɔhwe wɔ so; ngomunu wɔ ngofi nyɔbotaen nemɔ aso ngɔto ase, na ngɔmaa ɛkɔyɛ bokaa bɔ wayera ɔ, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Your stone blocks won't be reused for cornerstones or foundations, and I promise that forever you will be a desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Nations Will Attack Babylon The Lord said:
translation_verse: Bɛngɔfa nyɔboɛ biala bengofi wɔ so bɛngɔyɛ ndweasoɛ, yeɛ bɛngɔfa wɔ nyɔboɛ bɛngɔyɛ nyinasoɛ, na mmom ɛkɔyɛ kurofoen afebɔɔ, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Signal the nations to get ready to attack. Raise a flag and blow a trumpet. Send for the armies of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Choose a commander; let the cavalry attack like a swarm of locusts.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔfa frangaa bɛpena aseɛ ne aso, ɛ́mɔhu totorobɛndo wɔ maen maen mɔ nu; ɛ́mɔboaboa maen maen mɔ noa maa bɛɛfa koɛ bɛtoa ye, ɛ́mɔfrɛfrɛ ahennie hemɔ maa bɛɛfa koɛ bɛtoa ye: Ararate, Mini ne Asekenase; ɛ́mɔye safohene maa ɔfa koɛ ɔtoa ye, ɛ́mɔma mbɔngɔ bɛbra maa bɛyɛ mitimiti kyɛ mmɛbɛ.

english_verse: Tell the kings and governors, the leaders and the people of the kingdoms of the Medes to prepare for war!
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔsiesie maen maen mɔ maa bɛɛfa koɛ bɛɛtoa ye, mekyire Medese ahemvo, bɛ safohene mɔ, bɛ mbanyi amukoraa, ɔne maen biala bɔ owura bɛ bo ɔ.

english_verse: The earth twists and turns in torment, because I have decided to make Babylonia a desert where no one can live, and I won't change my mind.
translation_verse: Na aseɛ ne woso di aworabɔlɛ, ofikyɛ AWURADE nhyehyɛleɛ biala bɔ ɔfa Babilɔn nwo ne, wawa nu, kyɛ ɔkɔmaa Babilɔn aseɛ ne kɔyɛ kurofoen, bɔ sona fee ɔtte so ɔ.

english_verse: The Babylonian soldiers have lost their strength and courage. They stay in their fortresses, unable to fight, while the enemy breaks through the city gates, then sets their homes on fire.
translation_verse: Babilɔn koɛhonɛfoɛ bayakyi koɛhonɛ, baafeafea b’anwoserɛ afealeɛ mɔ nu. B’anwoserɛ ayie, bakakyi mmrasua; mmenia ato ye atenaleɛ mɔ nu see, mmuralɛ bɔ ɔbeabea ye pambim mɔ asi ne, babubu nu.

english_verse: The enemy now controls the river crossings! The marshes are on fire! Your army has panicked!”
translation_verse: batua asue apɛleɛ nemɔ, bafa see bayerayera elemmire nemɔ, na ahunundetelɛ atɔ koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ aso.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I make this promise— “Soon Babylon will be leveled and packed down like a threshing place at harvest time.” Babylonia Will Pay!
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ Asafo AWURADE Yisrael Nyameɛ nwa: Babilɔn awa brasua te kyɛ nekaa bɔ bɛboro aburoo ɔ, mmerɛ bɔ betiatia ye so ɔ, nakoso ɔngɔhyɛ biala, né ye buberɛ ne wadwu.”

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem say, “King Nebuchadnezzar made us panic. That monster stuffed himself with us and our treasures, leaving us empty— he gobbled up what he wanted and spit out the rest.
translation_verse: “Babilɔn hene Nebukadenesa wapura me, wapɛkyɛ me; wayɛ me tondura too, wame me kyɛ sasrabɔnzam yeɛ wame me ɔ; wafa me kunu nningyein fɛɛ wayi ye ko, na wafe me wato ase.

english_verse: The people of Babylonia harmed some of us and killed others. Now, Lord, make them pay!” The Lord Will Take Revenge on Babylon
translation_verse: Odi kyɛ Sionfoɛ bɛkã kyɛ, Amaneɛ bɔ me ne me nwonaen yanwu ye ne, ɔkɔbɔ Babilɔn ti so.” Yeɛ odi kyɛ Yerusalem kã kyɛ, “Me mogya kɔbɔ Kaldeafoɛ bɛ ti so.”

english_verse: My people, I am on your side, and I will take revenge on Babylon. I will cut off its water supply, and its stream will dry up.
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE nwa nyoo: “Tie, ngoli wɔ dwirɛ ngɔma wɔ, ná matɔ ye so wereɛ mama wɔ. Ngɔma ye ɛpo ne kɔwewe, ná mama ye asue mɔ bawewe.

english_verse: Babylon will be a pile of rubble where only jackals live, and everyone will be afraid to walk among the ruins.
translation_verse: Na Babilɔn kɔkakyi esire, ɛserɛ so ngyea atenaleɛ, anwodwiri nikye ne ngorohoɛ nikye bɔ sona fee ɔtte berɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The Babylonians roar and growl like young lions.
translation_verse: “Bɛkɔbɔ nu bɛkɔbobɔ nu kyɛ gyata mɔ, na bekopo kyɛ gyata mmaa.

english_verse: And since they are hungry, I will give them a banquet. They will celebrate, get drunk, then fall asleep, never to wake up!
translation_verse: Sɛ benya akɔnnɔ ná bɛsɔ a, ngɔto bɛ poen, na ngɔmaa bɛkɔbo, kɔpem kyɛ bɛ nye kɔgye ɔ, bɛkɔla nnaa afebɔɔ, na bengotingye, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: I will lead them away to die, like sheep, lambs, and goats being led to the butcher.
translation_verse: Ngɔfa bɛ ngɔtorotoro ngɔhɔ kyɛ mmoaen akrɔngrɔma bɔ bɛfa bɛ bɛkɔ akumyɛɛ ɔ, kyɛ mmoaen nyii ne mbɔngye nyii.

english_verse: All nations now praise Babylon, but when it is captured, those same nations will be horrified.
translation_verse: Nea kyɛbɔ basi bali Sesake so ngonim ɔ, nea kyɛbɔ wiase amukoraa anwohoahoa ne, basi babɔ ye tɔɔ ɔ! Nea kyɛbɔ Babilɔn asi akakyi anwodwiri nikye wɔ maen maen mɔ nu ɔ!

english_verse: Babylon's enemies will rise like ocean waves and flood the city.
translation_verse: Ɛpo ayi afa Babilɔn; ye asorɔkye wuruwuru ne abu afa ye so.

english_verse: Horrible destruction will strike the nearby towns. The land will become a barren desert, where no one can live or even travel.
translation_verse: Ye nguro mɔ akakyi kurofoen, aseɛ katerepee ne ɛserɛ, aseɛ bɔ sona fee ɔtte so ɔ, bɔ dasaniɛ biala ɔmva so ɔ.

english_verse: I will punish Marduk, the god of Babylon, and make him vomit out everything he gobbled up. Then nations will no longer bring him gifts, and Babylon's walls will crumble. The Lord Offers Hope to His People
translation_verse: Ngɔhwe Bel so wɔ Babilɔn, ná ngɔye bɔ wame ne ngofi ye noa nu. Maen maen ngobiri ngɔwa ye berɛ ko, amba, Babilɔn fasue ne adwiri agua ase.

english_verse: Get out of Babylon, my people, and run for your lives, before I strike the city in my anger!
translation_verse: “Me maen, ɛ́mɔfi ye nu befite! Odi kyɛ ebiala ɔpepɛ de ye kra fi AWURADE yaafɛlɛ piri ne anu.

english_verse: The time will come when I will punish Babylon's false gods. Everyone there will die, and the whole nation will be disgraced,
translation_verse: Yiti, tie, mmerɛ bie ɔ́ba, bɔ ngɔhwe Babilɔn amoen mɔ bɛ so ɔ, ye maen ne amukoraa nyunu kogua ase, na ye mmenia bɔ bahũhũ bɛ ne, bɛkɔbeabea berɛ wɔ ye nu.

english_verse: when an army attacks from the north and brings destruction. Then the earth and the heavens and everything in them will celebrate.
translation_verse: Yeɛ anwuro ne aseɛ, ɔne bɛ nu nningyein amukoraa, bɛkɔtea nu bekɔbɔ Babilɔn nwo ese, ofikyɛ sɛkyefoɛ mɔ kofi sorɔ dɔ bɛkɔfa koɛ bɛkɔɔteta ye, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Babylon must be overthrown, because it slaughtered the people of Israel and of many other nations.
translation_verse: Kyɛbɔ Babilɔn ama Yisraelfoɛ bɔ bahũhũ bɛ nemɔ bɛbeabea berɛ ne, sɔ ala yeɛ aseɛ so mmenia amukoraa bɔ bahũhũ bɛ ne, bɛkɔbeabea berɛ wɔ Babilɔn ɔ.

english_verse: My people, you escaped death when Jerusalem fell. Now you live far from home, but you should trust me and think about Jerusalem. Leave Babylon! Don't stay!
translation_verse: “Ɛmɔ bɔ ɛmɔanya ɛmɔ ti badidi nu bafi ngrandɛ noa ɔ, ɛ́mɔfi wa bɛhɔ, nnɛma ɛmɔgyina! Odi kyɛ ɛmɔkaye AWURADE wɔ dedeede dɔ, ná ɛ́mɔkaye Yerusalem koso.

english_verse: You feel ashamed and disgraced, because foreigners have entered my sacred temple.
translation_verse: ‘Yɛ nyunu agua ase, ofikyɛ yate nzoaa pepɛlɛ, animguaseɛ abia yɛ, ofikyɛ ɛwɔfoɛ mɔ bawa AWURADE awuro berɛ nekaa krongron nemɔ anu.’

english_verse: Soon I will send a war to punish Babylon's idols and leave its wounded people moaning everywhere.
translation_verse: “Yiti, tie, mmerɛ bie ɔ́ba, bɔ ngɔhwe ye amoen mɔ so, na ye aseɛ ne aso amukoraa, bɛ bɔ bapurapura ne, bɛkɔpenepene, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Although Babylon's walls reach to the sky, the army I send will destroy that city. I, the Lord, have spoken. Babylon Will Be Destroyed The Lord said:
translation_verse: Sɛ Babilɔn fo kɔ anwuro anwuro, ná omiamia ye anwoserɛ abandenden ne anu po a, sɛkyefoɛ kofi me berɛ kɔhɔ ye so, AWURADE noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Listen to the cries for help coming from Babylon. Everywhere in the country the sounds of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: “Tie, awuye bie fi Babilɔn! Ɛsɛkyelɛ kandinga nwo ndeateamuɛ fi Kaldeafoɛ aseɛ ne aso dɔ!

english_verse: The shouts of the enemy, like crashing ocean waves, will drown out Babylon's cries as I level the city.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ AWURADE asɛkye Babilɔn, na wamaa wahã ye noa serɛserɛ ne wato nu. Ye asorɔkye mɔ bɛsẽ wuruwuru kyɛ asue mbiri, na dede bɔ bɛyɔ, ne ɔgyegye;

english_verse: An enemy will attack and destroy Babylon. Its soldiers will be captured and their weapons broken, because I am a God who takes revenge against nations for what they do.
translation_verse: ofikyɛ sɛkyefoɛ ne awa ye so, wawa Babilɔn so; bahyehye ye koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ, babubu b’agyaen nemɔ anu, ofikyɛ AWURADE Nyameɛ bɔ otua kerɛ ne, okotua kerɛ amba.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the true King, promise that the officials and advisors, the governors and leaders, and the soldiers of Babylon will get drunk, fall asleep, and never wake up.
translation_verse: Na ngɔma ye atitire mɔ, ye nworɛfoɛ, ye safohene mɔ, ye maen mbanyi mɔ ne ye koɛhonɛfoɛ mɔ bɛkɔbobo, bɛkɔla nnaa afebɔɔ, na bengotingye. Ɛhene bɔ ye dumaa ole Asafo AWURADE ne, ye noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: The thick walls of that city will be torn down, and its huge gates burned. Everything that nation worked so hard to gain will go up in smoke. Jeremiah Gives Seraiah a Scroll
translation_verse: “Yiti Asafo AWURADE nwa nyoo: Bekodwiri Babilɔn fasue tɛtrɛtɛɛ nemɔ bekogua ase, na ye pambim ndendenn nemɔ, bɛkɔfa see bɛkɔyera bɛ; mmenia kɔfɛ kogua mbaen, na nningyein bɔ maen maen mɔ bafɛ banya ye ne, see yeɛ ɔkɔyera ye ɔ.”

english_verse: During Zedekiah's fourth year as king of Judah, he went to Babylon. And Baruch's brother Seraiah went along as the officer in charge of arranging for places to stay overnight.
translation_verse: Seraya bɔ ye baba ole Neria, bɔ ye baba ole Maaseya ne, ɔne Yuda hene Sedekia bɛhɔle Babilɔn wɔ Sedekia ye ahennie afoɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so nna ne anu nen, edwirɛ bɔ ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ Yeremia fa tuale Seraya noa ne, ye ɛne. Né Seraya te sanaahene.

english_verse: Before they left, I wrote on a scroll all the terrible things that would happen to Babylon.
translation_verse: Yiti musue amukoraa bɔ ɔkɔto Babilɔn ne, edwirɛ he amukoraa bɔ bahyerɛ bafa Babilɔn nwo ne, Yeremia hyerɛle guale nwomaa bie anu.

english_verse: I gave the scroll to Seraiah and said: When you get to Babylon, read this scroll aloud,
translation_verse: Na Yeremia sele Seraya kyɛ, “Sɛ ekodwu Babilɔn a, nea kyɛ ɛkɔkenga edwirɛ he amukoraa ɔ;

english_verse: then pray, “Our Lord, you promised to destroy this place and make it into a desert where no people or animals will ever live.”
translation_verse: ná kã kyɛ, ‘Ao AWURADE, wɔ yeɛ ahã musue dwirɛ bɔ ɔfa ɛwa sɔa nwo ɔ, kyɛ ɛkɔsɛkye ye bɔkɔɔ bɔ ebiala ngɔtena wa ɔ, kyɛ sona oo, kyɛ kaka oo, na mmom ɔkɔkakyi kurofoen afebɔɔ ɔ.’

english_verse: When you finish praying, tie the scroll to a rock and throw it in the Euphrates River. Then say,
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɛkenga nwomaa he yie a, kyekye nyɔboɛ bata ye, findi to asue Yufreti nu,

english_verse: “This is how Babylon will sink when the Lord destroys it. Everyone in the city will die, and it won't have the strength to rise again.” The End of Jeremiah's Writing Jeremiah's writing ends here.
translation_verse: ná kã kyɛ, ‘Sɔ ala yeɛ Babilɔn kɔmono, bɔ ongodwɔso ko ngofi musue bɔ ngɔprapra ngogua ye so ne anu ɔ.’ ” Na b’ayieleɛ koyie bɛ. Yeremia noa dwirɛ n’ayieleɛ ɛne.

english_verse: then his eyes were poked out. He was put in chains, then dragged off to Babylon and kept in prison until he died.
translation_verse: Babilɔn hene tutuli Sedekia nye, oguale ye ngɔnzɔngɔnzɔ fale ye hɔle Babilɔn, na ɔfale Sedekia tole kuku nu alaa kɔpem kyẽa bɔ Sedekia wuli ɔ. Babilɔnfoɛ bubu asɔneyɛɛ sua ne (

english_verse: meters around. They were hollow, but the bronze was about
translation_verse: Yiti betuale kuro ne alaa maa oodwuli Nana Sedekia ye ahennie afoɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne ko ne anu.

english_verse: After a year and a half, all the food in Jerusalem was gone. Then on the ninth day of the fourth month,
translation_verse: Na bosome nna ne anu, ye ɛlɛhona ne aso, ɛhɔen ne noa yɛle hye paa wɔ kuro ne anu bɔ né aseɛ ne aso ama bennya aleɛ benni koraa ɔ.

english_verse: the Babylonian troops broke through the city wall. That same night, Zedekiah and his soldiers tried to escape through the gate near the royal garden, even though they knew the enemy had the city surrounded. They headed toward the Jordan River valley,
translation_verse: Na bɛbɔngyebɔngyele kuro berɛ fasue ne anu tokuro. Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ né Kaldeafoɛ bapɛ kuro ne anwo bayia de, nakoso kɔngɔen, koɛhonɛfoɛ nemɔ amukoraa bɛnwati bɛfale pambim bɔ ɔwɔ fasue bɔ ɔbɔ ye nwo nyɔ ne anu befili kuro berɛ bɛhɔle. Sɔ pambim ne, opingye ɛhene turo ne. Bɛfale bɛ nye behyirele asue Yɔɔdan bɔnza ne anu dɔ.

english_verse: Zedekiah was taken to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial and found him guilty.
translation_verse: Yeɛ bɛhyele Nana Sedekia bɛfale ye bɛbrɛle Babilɔn hene wɔ Ribla wɔ Hamate aseɛ so, na obuale ye foɛ.

english_verse: Zedekiah's sons and the officials of Judah were killed while he watched,
translation_verse: Babilɔn hene huhuni Sedekia mma mmienzua bɔ ye nye tua ɔ, na osa huhuni Yuda atitirefoɛ amukoraa wɔ Ribla.

english_verse: Jerusalem was captured during Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year as king of Babylonia. About a month later, Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guards arrived in Jerusalem. His name was Nebuzaradan,
translation_verse: Babilɔn hene Nebukadenesa ye ahennie afoɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne ngona ne, bosome bɔ ɔtɔ so nnu ne, ye eleburu ne aso, awɛmvoɛ nemɔ aso safohene Nebusaradan bɔ osa te Babilɔn hene ye mbanyi nemɔ anu ko ne, ɔhɔle Yerusalem.

english_verse: and he burned down the Lord's temple, the king's palace, and every important building in the city, as well as all the houses.
translation_verse: Ɔyerale AWURADE awuro ne, ahemvie ne, ɔne Yerusalem sua amukoraa, na atitire nemɔ sua ne koso, ɔtole bɛ nu see yerale bɛ.

english_verse: Then he ordered the Babylonian soldiers to break down the walls around Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Kaldeafoɛ koɛhonɛfoɛ amukoraa bɔ né bɛboka awɛmvoɛ nemɔ aso safohene ne aso ne, bebubuli Yerusalem nwo fasue ne amukoraa bɛbra beyiale.

english_verse: He led away the people left in the city, including everyone who had become loyal to Nebuchadnezzar, the rest of the skilled workers, and even some of the poor people of Judah.
translation_verse: Mmenia bɔ bɛ nwo yɛ anwumvo nemɔ bie, mmenia ngaa bɔ baha kuro ne aso, ɔne koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛnwatili bɛɛfale bɛ nwo bɛɛmane Babilɔn hene ne, yeɛ mmenia ne amukoraa, awɛmvoɛ nemɔ aso safohene Nebusaradan hyele bɛ nnure fale bɛ hɔle.

english_verse: Evil Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there.
translation_verse: Ɔne Yehoakyin belili ngitahoɛ paa, na ahemvo mɔ bɔ né bɛ ne ye wɔ Babilɔn ne, ɔmane ye dibea bɔ ɔtra bɛ deɛ ne ɔ.

english_verse: Jehoiachin was allowed to wear regular clothes instead of a prison uniform, and he even ate at the king's table every day.
translation_verse: Yiti Yehoakyin puropurole ye kuku nu ndaadeɛ ne guale, na mmerɛ amukoraa bɔ né ɔte ase ne, né ɔne Ewile Merodake yeɛ bɛtena poen nwo bedidi ɔ.

english_verse: As long as Jehoiachin lived, he was paid a daily allowance to buy whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Na nningyein bɔ Yehoakyin hia ye daa biala ne wora, Babilɔn hene hɔle so fa mane ye mmerɛ bɔ ɔte ase ne, kɔpem kyɛ owuli ɔ.

english_verse: Jerusalem, once so crowded, lies deserted and lonely. This city that was known all over the world is now like a widow. This queen of the nations has been made a slave.
translation_verse: Ao, kuro bɔ né mmenia ayɛ nu mitimiti ne, ye yeɛ afei waha ye ngome e! Kuro bɔ né odi mu wɔ maen maen mɔ nu ne, ye yeɛ afei wakakyi kyɛ kunaniɛ ye! Kuro bɔ né odi maen maen mɔ so hemmaa ne, ye yeɛ afei de bede ye ndɔ e!

english_verse: Each night, bitter tears flood her cheeks. None of her former lovers are there to offer comfort; her friends have betrayed her and are now her enemies.
translation_verse: Osũ hahii kɔngɔen, ɛmoen songyi ye nye abo, na bɛ bɔ bekuro ye ne amukoraa, onnya bɛ nu ko po mma ɔngyekye ye wora; ye mmango amukoraa bali ye ngasi, na bakakyi ye pɔfoɛ mɔ.

english_verse: The people of Judah are slaves, suffering in a foreign land, with no rest from sorrow. Their enemies captured them and were terribly cruel.
translation_verse: Amaneɛnwunɛ ne nhyɛsoɛ kandinga nu yeɛ bahye Yuda nnure bahɔ ɔ. Waatena amaen maen mɔ nu, na onnya nekaa bɔ ɔkɔtena kole ye nwome ɔ, bɛ bɔ bɛfoa ye ne amukoraa baato ye, bahã ye bapua wɔ atee kyenɔnn bie aso.

english_verse: The roads to Zion mourn because no one travels there to celebrate the festivals. The city gates are deserted; priests are weeping. Young women are raped; Zion is in sorrow!
translation_verse: Sion atimbire nemɔ bedi aworabɔlɛ, ofikyɛ sona biala mma aluolue nemɔ abo, ye pambim amukoraa bɛlela berɛ too, ye asɔfo mɔ bedi yealɛ, ye mmabunu mɔ bayɛ anwumvoin anwumvoin, na ye bɔbɔ wora onwu amaneɛ paa.

english_verse: Enemies now rule the city and live as they please. The Lord has punished Jerusalem because of her awful sins; he has let her people be dragged away.
translation_verse: Bɛbɔ bekyi ye ne, bakakyi ye mene mɔ, wayie ye pɔfoɛ mɔ yé, ofikyɛ AWURADE aprapra amaneɛ wagua ye so. Na ɔnate ye mmeraatolɛ worawora ne ati, ye pɔfoɛ mɔ bahye ye mma mɔ nnure, na bafa bɛ bahɔ.

english_verse: Zion's glory has disappeared. Her leaders are like deer that cannot find pasture; they are hunted down till their strength is gone.
translation_verse: Sion awa brasua ne, ye anwonyemene amukoraa atu amini; ye atitire mɔ bayɛ kyɛ dabɔɔ bɔ bennya aleɛ benni ɔ, na banwati bɔ b’anwoserɛ ayie, wɔ bɛ bɔ bɛfoa bɛ nemɔ bɛ nyunu.

english_verse: Her people recall the good life that once was theirs; now they suffer and are scattered. No one was there to protect them from their enemies who sneered when their city was taken.
translation_verse: Na Yerusalem ye anwokyere ne aworabɔlɛ mmerɛ nu, ɔkayele ye nningyein nyemene amukoraa, bɔ mmerɛ bie né ole ye ne. Mmerɛ bɔ ye mmenia beelili pɔfoɛ ne sa nu, bɔ wannya ebiala maa wammoka ye ne, bɛ bɔ bekyi ye nemɔ benwuni ye, na bɛgorole ye nwo, ɔnate ye asefinɛ ne ati.

english_verse: Jerusalem's horrible sins have made the city a joke. Those who once admired her now hate her instead— she has been disgraced; she groans and turns away.
translation_verse: Yerusalem ayɔ bɔne paa, yiti ye nwo agua fiɛ. Bɛ bɔ né bebu ye ne amukoraa, bebu ye animtia, ofikyɛ banwu ye nwo; amba ye bɔbɔ deinn ogua anwongokoɔ, na wakakyi ye si.

english_verse: Her sins had made her filthy, but she wasn't worried about what could happen. And when Jerusalem fell, it was so tragic. No one gave her comfort when she cried out, “Help! I'm in trouble, Lord! The enemy has won.”
translation_verse: Ye nwo bɔ wagua fiɛ ne, wayɛ ye ataadeɛ ne anu; wangaye ye ayieleɛ, yiti wafi ase buramm, na olle aworakyekyerɛniɛ biala. “Ao AWURADE, nea m’amaneɛnwunɛ, ofikyɛ pɔfoɛ ne, wali ngonim.”

english_verse: Zion's treasures were stolen. Jerusalem saw foreigners enter her place of worship, though the Lord had forbidden them to belong to his people.
translation_verse: Pɔfoɛ ne, watengyɛ ye sa wɔ ye nningyein nyemene ne amukoraa so, na wanwu kyɛ maenmaensofoɛ nemɔ, bɔ ahyɛ bɛ kyɛ nnɛmaa bɛkɔ wɔ badwa ne anu ne, bahɔ ye nekaa krongron ne anu.

english_verse: Everyone in the city groans while searching for food; they trade their valuables for barely enough scraps to stay alive. Jerusalem Speaks: Jerusalem shouts to the Lord, “Please look and see how miserable I am!”
translation_verse: Ye mmenia amukoraa bedi yealɛ, bɛpena aleɛ; bafa bɛ nningyein nyemenenyemene ne basesã aleɛ bama bɛ kra nwo atɔ ye. “Ao AWURADE, nea ná nwu ye, ofikyɛ bebu me animtia.”

english_verse: No passerby even cares. Why doesn't someone notice my terrible sufferings? You were fiercely angry, Lord, and you punished me worst of all.
translation_verse: “Ɛmɔ bɔ ɛmɔpɛ nu wa amukoraa, aso ɔmva ɛmɔ nwo? Ɛ́mɔnea ná ɛ́mɔnwu ye, sɛ aworabɔlɛ bie wɔ berɛ, bɔ ɔte kyɛ m’aworabɔlɛ bɔ wato me ye, bɔ AWURADE aprapra wagua me so, wɔ ye yaafɛlɛ piri kyẽa ne anu ye.

english_verse: From heaven you sent a fire that burned in my bones; you set a trap for my feet and made me turn back. All day long you leave me in shock from constant pain.
translation_verse: “Wasoma see wafi anwuro maa waawura me mmowue nu, na ɔyerayera nu; wasua me gya ngaen, wamaa masa me si, wamaa waha me ngome oo, na meyɛ hodwoo daa biala.

english_verse: You have tied my sins around my neck, and they weigh so heavily that my strength is gone. You have put me in the power of enemies too strong for me.
translation_verse: “Wafa ye sa wakyekye me mmeraatolɛ ne maa wakakyi kɔnnua. Basina baya me kɔme anu, wama m’anwoserɛ ayie. Bɛ bɔ mengora bɛ nyunu gyina ne, AWURADE afa me wawura bɛ sa.

english_verse: You, Lord, have turned back my warriors and crushed my young heroes. Judah was a woman untouched, but you let her be trampled like grapes in a wine pit.
translation_verse: “M’anwoserɛfoɛ amukoraa bɔ bɛwɔ me nu ne, AWURADE atiatia bɛ so. Wafrɛfrɛ mmenia pee maa babɔ dwaa batia me, kyɛ behũhũ me mmerandeɛ mɔ. AWURADE atiatia Yuda awa brasua ababunu ne aso, kyɛbɔ bɛyɔ ye wɔ kumaa bɔ betwi nu nzaa ne anu ne ala.

english_verse: Because of this, I mourn, and tears flood my eyes. No one is here to comfort or to encourage me; we have lost the war— my people are suffering. The Prophet Speaks:
translation_verse: “Sɔ nningyein nemɔ ati yeɛ mesu ye; me nye moen poro nzue, ofikyɛ aworakyekyerɛniɛ bɔ odi kyɛ ɔkyekye me kra wora ne, ɔwɔ dedeede.” Waha me mma mɔ angome oo, ofikyɛ pɔfoɛ ne ali ngonim.

english_verse: Zion reaches out her hands, but no one offers comfort. The Lord has turned the neighboring nations against Jacob's descendants. Jerusalem is merely a filthy rag to her neighbors. Jerusalem Speaks:
translation_verse: Sion atrɛtrɛ ye sa nu, na olle ebiala maa ɔngyekye ye wora. AWURADE ama Yakob nwo ahyɛdeɛ, kyɛ ye pɔfoɛ mɔ bɛpɛ ye nwo beyia. Yerusalem akakyi kyɛ nikyee bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ wɔ bɛ nu.

english_verse: The Lord was right, but I refused to obey him. Now I ask all of you to look at my sufferings— even my young people have been dragged away.
translation_verse: “AWURADE di be, ofikyɛ mayɛ ye mmeraa nwo lɔen. Maen maen amukoraa, mesrɛ ɛmɔ, ɛ́mɔtie, ná ɛ́mɔnea m’aworabɔlɛ ye. Bahye me ndaluwa mɔ ne me mmerandeɛ mɔ nnure bahɔ.

english_verse: I called out to my lovers, but they betrayed me. My priests and my leaders died while searching the city for scraps of food.
translation_verse: “Mvrɛfrɛle bɛ bɔ mekuro bɛ nemɔ, nakoso bɛlakalakale me. M’asɔfo ne me mbanyi mɔ, bɛtotɔle wɔ kuro ne anu, mmerɛ bɔ né bɛpena bɛ noa aleɛ ma bɛ kra mɔ nwo tɔ bɛ ne.

english_verse: Won't you look and see how upset I am, our Lord? My stomach is in knots, and my heart is broken because I betrayed you. In the streets and at home, my people are slaughtered.
translation_verse: “Ao AWURADE, nea, na edwirɛ ato me, me kunu tete me; me wora abɔ, ofikyɛ mayɛ ɛlɔen kandinga paa. Ngrandɛ ne kũkũ me mma wɔ dwaaso, yeɛ ewue koso kũkũ bɛ wɔ awuro.

english_verse: Everyone heard my groaning, but no one offered comfort. My enemies know of the trouble that you have brought on me, and it makes them glad. Hurry and punish them, as you have promised.
translation_verse: “Bate kyɛ medi yealɛ, na ebiala nne berɛ bɔ ɔkyekye me wora ɔ. Me pɔfoɛ mɔ amukoraa bate m’amaneɛnwunɛ ne, na bɛ nye agye kyɛ ayɔ sɔ ɔ. Kyẽa bɔ ahyehyɛ ato berɛ ne, ɛkɔmaa ɔkɔwa nu, na bɛkɔyɛ kyɛ me ala.

english_verse: Don't let their evil deeds escape your sight. Punish them as much as you have punished me because of my sins. I never stop groaning— I've lost all hope!
translation_verse: “Ma b’amumuyɛɛ amukoraa oodwu wɔ nyunu, na ɛne bɛ li kyɛbɔ ɔnate m’amumuyɛɛ amukoraa ne ati, ɛne me ali ne. Ofikyɛ me yealɛlilɛ ne wasone, na ahunundetelɛ atɔ me so.

english_verse: The Lord was angry! So he disgraced Zion though it was Israel's pride and his own place of rest. In his anger he threw Zion down from heaven to earth.
translation_verse: Nea kyɛbɔ AWURADE ole yaa, wafa munungum wamundu Sion awa brasua ne aso ɔ! ná wagyi Yisrael anwonyemene wafi nyameɛso waato ase, bɔ wangaye ye gya bo ndiasoɛ, wɔ ye ɛyaafɛlɛ kyẽa ne anu ɔ.

english_verse: The Lord had no mercy! He destroyed the homes of Jacob's descendants. In his anger he tore down every walled city in Judah; he toppled the nation together with its leaders, leaving them in shame.
translation_verse: AWURADE asɛkye Yakob atenaleɛ amukoraa, na wannwu bɛ anwumvoin. Ye yaafɛlɛ nu, wadwiri Yuda awa brasua n’anwoserɛ afealeɛ mɔ wagua ase. Wahã bɛ wagua ase, wagua ahennie ne, ɔne nu mbanyi mɔ nwo fiɛ.

english_verse: The Lord was so furiously angry that he wiped out the whole army of Israel by not supporting them when the enemy attacked. He was like a raging fire that swallowed up the descendants of Jacob.
translation_verse: Wapepɛ Yisrael mmɛen amukoraa wɔ ye yaafɛlɛ piri ne anu. Ye tumi asaa ne, wahwe wasa wɔ mmerɛ bɔ pɔfoɛ ne ɔ́ba bɛ so ɔ. Na ogyele kyɛ see bɔ ɔyera bra yia ɔ yerale Yakob.

english_verse: He attacked like an enemy with a bow and arrows, killing our loved ones. He has burned to the ground the homes on Mount Zion.
translation_verse: Wakondo ye agyaen nu kyɛ pɔfoɛ, wagyina watengyɛ ye sa famaa kyɛ ebie bɔ okyi bɛ ɔ. Ohuhuni bɔ ɔyɛ yɛ nye so nyemene amukoraa, wɔ Sion awa brasua ɛtena sua ne anu. Ohwiele ye yaa bɔ wafɛ ye hahii ne kyɛ see.

english_verse: The Lord was like an enemy! He left Israel in ruins with its palaces and fortresses destroyed, and with everyone in Judah moaning and weeping.
translation_verse: AWURADE akakyi kyɛ pɔfoɛ, wasɛkye Yisrael. Wasɛkye ye ahemvie mɔ amukoraa, wasɛkye ye anwoserɛ afealeɛ mɔ, na wamaa esuɛ ne awuyebɔlɛ basone wɔ Yuda awa brasua ne anu.

english_verse: He shattered his temple like a hut in a garden; he completely wiped out his meeting place, and did away with festivals and Sabbaths in the city of Zion. In his fierce anger he rejected our king and priests.
translation_verse: Ole anyeborolɛ ɔsɛkyele ye ɛtena sua kyɛ ɔsɛkye eboo ɔ. Wasɛkye ye nekaa mɔ bɔ beyia nu ne; AWURADE ama bɛ wora afi, aluolue ne afofingyẽa nemɔ wɔ Sion, na ye ahone bɔ wahu ne, wabu ɛhene ne ɔsɔfo animtia.

english_verse: The Lord abandoned his altar and his temple; he let Zion's enemies capture her fortresses. Noisy shouts were heard from the temple, as if it were a time of celebration.
translation_verse: AWURADE agyi ye afɔleɛ bokyea ne wato, okyi ye nekaa krongron ne. Ye ahemvie nemɔ, wafa bɛ fasue nemɔ wawura pɔfoɛ ne sa. Babɔ ese wɔ AWURADE awuro berɛ, kyɛ kyẽa bɔ bedi aluolue ɔ.

english_verse: The Lord had decided to tear down the walls of Zion stone by stone. So he started destroying and did not stop until walls and fortresses mourned and trembled.
translation_verse: AWURADE ayɛ ye adwene kyɛ ɔkɔsɛkye Sion awa brasua fasue ne, wasa nyamaa wafa wasusu, na wanyakyi ye sɛkyelɛ bɔ ɔsɛkye ye ne. Yiti ɔmane ɛwaen ne fasue belili aworabɔlɛ, bɛbɔle nu belili yealɛ.

english_verse: Zion's gates have fallen facedown on the ground; the bars that locked the gates are smashed to pieces. Her king and royal family are prisoners in foreign lands. Her priests don't teach, and her prophets don't have a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Ye pambim nemɔ bamimi bahɔ ase, wasɛkye mmuralɛ bɔ ɔbrambram ye si nemɔ, na wabubu nu; ye hene ne ye mbanyi mɔ baali maen maensofoɛ mɔ nu. Mmeraa ne, ɔnne berɛ ko. Ye ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ koso, bennya nyekyire bemvi AWURADE berɛ.

english_verse: Zion's leaders are silent. They just sit on the ground, tossing dirt on their heads and wearing sackcloth. Her young women can do nothing but stare at the ground.
translation_verse: Sion awa brasua ye mbanyi mɔ bɛtete ase, na bayɛ konn. Bafa mvuture bagua bɛ ti so, na baherahera ɛsɛen tena. Yerusalem ababunu nemɔ, basisi bɛ ti ase.

english_verse: My eyes are red from crying, my stomach is in knots, and I feel sick all over. My people are being wiped out, and children lie helpless in the streets of the city.
translation_verse: Ɛmoen ama me nye ayie bɔ, me kunu tete me. ‘Aworabɔlɛ atira me ɔnate me maen awa brasua bɔ basɛkye ye ne ati, ofikyɛ ngwadaa ne nnɔma mɔ bɛ nye so aburu bɛ wɔ kuro berɛ dwaa nemɔ aso.

english_verse: A child begs its mother for food and drink, then blacks out like a wounded soldier lying in the street. The child slowly dies in its mother's arms.
translation_verse: Bebisa bɛ maame mɔ kyɛ, “Nisua yeɛ aleɛ ne nzaa wɔ ɔ?” Mmerɛ bɔ bɛ nye so buruli bɛ kyɛ mmenia bɔ bapura wɔ kuro berɛ dwaa nemɔ aso; mmerɛ bɔ bɛka nu wɔ bɛ ni mɔ sa so ne.

english_verse: Zion, how can I comfort you? How great is your pain? Lovely city of Jerusalem, how can I heal your wounds, gaping as wide as the sea?
translation_verse: Ao Yerusalem awa brasua, nzikyɛ yeɛ nga mva nni wɔ nwo adanzeɛ ɔ? Nzikyɛ yeɛ mva ndoto wɔ nwo ɔ? Ao Sion awa brasua ababunu, nzikyɛ yeɛ mma ɛne ye bɛsɛ ɔ, amaa ɔnate so makyekye wɔ wora ɔ? Ofikyɛ w’asefinɛ ne te piri kyɛ ɛpo, na nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora kɔsa wɔ anwonyerɛ ɔ?

english_verse: Your prophets deceived you with false visions and lying messages— they should have warned you to leave your sins and be saved from disaster.
translation_verse: Nningyein mbaen mbaen ne nnakannaka yeɛ wɔ ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ banwu bama wɔ ɔ; na banna w’amumuyɛɛ ali bɔ ɔnate so kɔmaa bɛkɔye wɔ bekofi nnurehyelɛ nu ɔ. Na mmom ngondombo ne nnakannaka nyekyire yeɛ banwu ye bama wɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Those who pass by shake their heads and sneer as they make fun and shout, “What a lovely city you were, the happiest on earth, but look at you now!”
translation_verse: Bɛ bɔ bɛpɛ nu amukoraa bɛbɔ bɛ sa nu bɛgoro wɔ nwo. Besobi bɛ noa bɛwoso bɛ ti begua Yerusalem awa brasua ne aso kyɛ, “Kuro bɔ bɛfrɛ ye: Kuro bɔ ye anwonyemene di mu, aseɛ amukoraa anika ne, aso ye ɛhe?”

english_verse: Zion, your enemies curse you and snarl like wild animals, while shouting, “This is the day we've waited for! At last, we've got you!”
translation_verse: Wɔ pɔfoɛ mɔ amukoraa, batu bɛ noa bagua wɔ so. Besobi bɛ noa bɛnwose bɛ gye. Na bɛnwa, “Yasɛkye ye bɔkɔɔ. Amba, kyẽa bɔ yɛnea ye ate ne, ye ɛne; yɛ sa ahã ye, na yanwu ye!”

english_verse: The Lord has done everything that he had planned and threatened long ago. He destroyed you without mercy and let your enemies boast about their powerful forces.
translation_verse: Bɔ AWURADE yɛle ye adwene kyɛ ɔkɔyɔ ne, wayɔ, wama ye dwirɛ ne awa nu, Ahyɛdeɛ bɔ ɔhyɛ tole berɛ tete mmerɛ nu ne, ye ɛne: wadwiri wagua, na wannwu anwumvoin. Na wama wɔ pɔfoɛ ali wɔ nwo ahurusi, wama bɛ bɔ bekyi wɔ ɔ b’anwoserɛ agyina so.

english_verse: Zion, deep in your heart you cried out to the Lord. Now let your tears overflow your walls day and night. Don't ever lose hope or let your tears stop.
translation_verse: B’ahone sũ frɛle AWURADE. Ao Sion awa brasua fasue, ma wɔ nye moen poro gua kyɛ asue eyia ne kɔngɔen. Nnɛde wɔ nwome, yeɛ nnɛma wɔ nye kyiremvua yakyi suɛ.

english_verse: Get up and pray for help all through the night. Pour out your feelings to the Lord, as you would pour water out of a jug. Beg him to save your people, who are starving to death at every street crossing. Jerusalem Speaks:
translation_verse: Dwɔso, tea nu kɔngɔen: abunnamu ahyɛaseɛ, hwie wɔ sufrɛ ne kyɛ nzue fa to AWURADE nyunu. Ma wɔ sa so kyire ye, ɔnate wɔ mma mmaa mmaa mɔ bɛ ngoa ti; bɛ yeɛ ɛhɔen apɛ bɛ wɔ borɔnoɛ biala ngwandaa ɔ.

english_verse: Think about it, Lord! Have you ever been this cruel to anyone before? Is it right for mothers to eat their children, or for priests and prophets to be killed in your temple?
translation_verse: Ao AWURADE, tie, ná dwene bɔ afa ɛhe ali ye ne anwo. Aso odi kyɛ mmrasua beku bɛ kunu mmaa bɛto bedi anaa, bɛ mma bɔ badodo bɛ ɔ? Aso odi kyɛ beku ɔsɔfo ne ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ wɔ AWURADE nekaa krongron berɛ anaa?

english_verse: My people, both young and old, lie dead in the streets. Because you were angry, my young men and women were brutally slaughtered.
translation_verse: Ngwadaa ne mbanyi, bɛlela aseɛnwo wɔ dwaa nemɔ aso. Me ndaluwa mɔ ne me mmerandeɛ mɔ, batotɔ ngrandɛ noa. Ahũhũ bɛ wɔ wɔ yaafɛlɛ kyẽa ne anu; ahũhũ bɛ, na annwu bɛ anwumvoin.

english_verse: When you were angry, Lord, you invited my enemies like guests for a party. No one survived that day; enemies killed my children, my own little ones.
translation_verse: Ato wɔ sa afrɛ m’amaneɛnwunɛ afi nekaa biala, kyɛ aluolue kyẽa ne ala, na ye sɔ ti AWURADE yaafɛlɛ kyẽa ne, ebiala wannya ye ti wannidi nu, yeɛ ebiala wanga. Bɛ bɔ magyi bɛ matete bɛ ne, me pɔfoɛ mɔ ahũhũ bɛ.

english_verse: I have suffered much because God was angry.
translation_verse: Me ole sona bɔ manwu amaneɛ wɔ ye yaafɛlɛ mbire ne anoa ne.

english_verse: He chased me into a dark place, where no light could enter.
translation_verse: Wahwe me wafa me wahɔ awosii nu, na mmom nna hyireinn nu ɔ.

english_verse: I am the only one he punishes over and over again, without ever stopping.
translation_verse: Amba, me ngome yeɛ watu ye nye wasie me so ɔ, na ɔfa ye sa ogyina me nwo daa biala.

english_verse: God caused my skin and flesh to waste away, and he crushed my bones.
translation_verse: Wama me nwonaen ne me wereɛ atwindwam; wabubu me mmowue nu.

english_verse: He attacked and surrounded me with hardships and trouble;
translation_verse: Wafa abɔwee ne amaneɛnwunɛ wato me nwo fasue wabra wayia.

english_verse: he forced me to sit in the dark like someone long dead.
translation_verse: Wafa me watena awosii nu kyɛ daa tete awufoɛ nemɔ ala.

english_verse: God built a fence around me that I cannot climb over, and he chained me down.
translation_verse: Wayɔ aberedwaa wafa me nwo bɔ mengora memvite ɔ, wagua me ngɔnzɔngɔnzɔ nonɛnonɛ.

english_verse: Even when I shouted and prayed for help, he refused to listen.
translation_verse: Yeɛ sɛ mebɔ awuye metea nu koso a, osi me mbaeɛ nwo ate.

english_verse: God put big rocks in my way and made me follow a crooked path.
translation_verse: Wafa nyɔboɛ bɔ badwa ɔ watua m’atimbire, wakondokondo m’atee.

english_verse: God was like a bear or a lion waiting in ambush for me;
translation_verse: Ɔte kyɛ kwabrafo bɔ ɔtetɛ ɔ ma me, kyɛ gyata bɔ ɔwɔ mvealeɛ nu ɔ.

english_verse: he dragged me from the road, then tore me to shreds.
translation_verse: Wamaa mali makyebu, na watete me nu pasapasa: wamaa waha me ngome oo.

english_verse: God took careful aim and shot his arrows
translation_verse: Wasina ye agyaen, na wafa agyaen ne wahyire me so.

english_verse: I am a joke to everyone— no one ever stops making fun of me.
translation_verse: Ngakyili ngorohoɛ nikyee mane me maen amukoraa, ngakyili bɛ noa nu dwein daa biala.

english_verse: He made me eat gravel and rubbed me in the dirt.
translation_verse: Wamaa mafa me gye mapesa nyɔboseka; wafa nzoen wagua me nwo amukoraa.

english_verse: I tell myself, “I am finished! I can't count on the Lord to do anything for me.”
translation_verse: Na ngane kyɛ, “M’anwoserɛ ne m’anyelasoɛ atu amini afi AWURADE nu.”

english_verse: Just thinking of my troubles and my lonely wandering makes me miserable.
translation_verse: Kaye m’amaneɛnwunɛ ne m’anwokyere, ɔte awɔwee ne abɔwee.

english_verse: That's all I ever think about, and I am depressed.
translation_verse: Me kra tɛ kaye bɛ, na wabrɛ ye nwo ase wɔ me nu.

english_verse: Then I remember something that fills me with hope.
translation_verse: Nakoso ɛhe yeɛ mekaye wɔ me ti anu ɔ, yiti anyelasoɛ wɔ berɛ ma me.

english_verse: The Lord's kindness never fails! If he had not been merciful, we would have been destroyed.
translation_verse: AWURADE adaworoma yeɛ yɛ boso wannua ɔ, ofikyɛ ye anwumvoinnwunɛ ye bo ngɔpɛ le.

english_verse: The Lord can always be trusted to show mercy each morning.
translation_verse: Ngyerɛmɔ biala ɔte foforɛ, wɔ nahorɛlilɛ te piri.

english_verse: Deep in my heart I say, “The Lord is all I need; I can depend on him!”
translation_verse: Me kra nwa, “AWURADE yeɛ ɔte me bue deɛ ɔ, yiti ngɔfa me wora ngowura ye nu.”

english_verse: The Lord is kind to everyone who trusts and obeys him.
translation_verse: AWURADE te paa ma bɛ bɔ bɛ nye la ye ate ɔ, ɔte paa ma ɛkra bɔ ɔpena ye si atee ɔ.

english_verse: It is good to wait patiently for the Lord to save us.
translation_verse: Ɔte paa kyɛ ɛkɔyɛ konn anyelasoɛ nu kɔnwondɛ AWURADE ngoalelɛ ne ɔ.

english_verse: When we are young, it is good to struggle hard
translation_verse: Ɔte paa ma sona kyɛ ɔkɔfa kɔnnua ne kɔto ye kɔme nu wɔ ye mmerandeɛ nu ɔ.

english_verse: and to sit silently alone, if this is what the Lord intends.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɔfa to sona ne kɔme anu a, odi kyɛ ye ngome ɔtena berɛ ɔyɛ konn.

english_verse: Being rubbed in the dirt can teach us a lesson;
translation_verse: Odi kyɛ ɔfa ye noa butu nnɛterɛ nu, ebiaa né anyelasoɛ wɔ berɛ ma ye.

english_verse: The Lord won't always reject us!
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ AWURADE ngɔpo sona afebɔɔ.

english_verse: He causes a lot of suffering, but he also has pity because of his great love.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɔma ebie wora bɔ po a, okonwu ye anwumvoin kyɛbɔ ye anwumvoinnwunɛ ne, ye piri ɔte ne.

english_verse: or cheat anyone out of what is rightfully theirs. God Most High sees everything,
translation_verse: sɛ obua ebie ndɛengyea wɔ Anwuro Anwuroniɛ ne nyunu a,

english_verse: and he knows when you refuse to give someone a fair trial.
translation_verse: sɛ bedi dwirɛ betia ebie a, AWURADE mbene so sɔ.

english_verse: No one can do anything without the Lord's approval.
translation_verse: Nwa yeɛ ɔkã maa ɔba nu wɔ aberɛ bɔ nna AWURADE yeɛ wahyehyɛ ye sɔ ɔ?

english_verse: Good and bad each happen at the command of God Most High.
translation_verse: Tɛɛ oo, paa oo, aso nna Anwuro Anwuroniɛ ne noa nu yeɛ befi bɛba ɔ?

english_verse: We're still alive! We shouldn't complain when we are being punished for our sins.
translation_verse: Nzu ati yeɛ odi kyɛ dasaniɛ ɔbɔ somoɛ wɔ ye bɔne nwo asohwenɛ nwo ɔ?

english_verse: Instead, we should think about the way we are living, and turn back to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔma yɛneanea y’atee nu ná yɛpɛnzɛpɛnzɛ nu, ná yɛsa yɛbra AWURADE berɛ!

english_verse: When we lift our hands in prayer to God in heaven, we should offer him our hearts and say,
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔma yɛfi y’ahone nu yɛma yɛ sa so yɛbɔ mbaeɛ yɛhyire Nyameɛ wɔ nyameɛso kyɛ,

english_verse: “We've sinned! We've rebelled against you, and you haven't forgiven us!
translation_verse: “Yayɛ amumuyɛɛ, yeɛ yayɛ lɔen, na amva angyɛ.

english_verse: Anger is written all over you, as you pursue and slaughter us without showing pity.
translation_verse: Afa ɛyaafɛlɛ amundu wɔ nwo, na atane yɛ nye: ahũhũ bɔ annwu anwumvoin ɔ.

english_verse: You are behind a wall of clouds that blocks out our prayers.
translation_verse: Afa munungum amundu wɔ nwo, kyɛbɔ ɔkɔyɛ bɔ yɛ mbaeɛ ngɔfa nu ngodwu wɔ berɛ ɔ.

english_verse: You allowed nations to treat us like garbage;
translation_verse: Amaa yakakyi kyɛ ewura ne fofoɛ wɔ maen maen mɔ b’afia.

english_verse: We are terrified and trapped, caught and crushed.”
translation_verse: Ahunundetelɛ, kumaa, ɛsɛkyelɛ ne amaneɛ yeɛ wawa yɛ so ɔ.

english_verse: until the Lord looks down from heaven and helps.
translation_verse: kɔpem kyɛ AWURADE kɔto ye nye kofi nyameɛso kɔnea ase ɔ.

english_verse: I am horrified when I see what enemies have done to the young women of our city.
translation_verse: Me nye ma me wora bɔ, ɔnate me kuro mma mmrasua amukoraa bɛ ti.

english_verse: No one had reason to hate me, but I was hunted down like a bird.
translation_verse: “Me pɔfoɛ mɔ bɛfoa me anyeborolɛ so mbaen kyɛ anomaa.

english_verse: Then they tried to kill me by tossing me into a pit and throwing stones at me.
translation_verse: Bafindi me bato kumaa nu anyekaenn so, na bahuru nyɔboɛ bagua me so.

english_verse: Water covered my head— I thought I was gone.
translation_verse: Nzue bu fale me ti so, na ngane kyɛ, ‘Mawu mayie oo!’

english_verse: From the bottom of the pit, I prayed to you, Lord.
translation_verse: “Ao AWURADE, mvi kumaa ne bo dɔ nzu mvrɛle wɔ dumaa.

english_verse: I begged you to listen. “Help!” I shouted. “Save me!” You answered my prayer
translation_verse: Atie me sufrɛ, nnɛtuatua wɔ so wɔ me mbaeɛ ne me suɛ nwo.

english_verse: and came when I was in need. You told me, “Don't worry!”
translation_verse: Kyẽa bɔ nzu mvrɛle wɔ ne, ɛhwe pingyele me, na ɛhane kyɛ, ‘Nnesuro!’

english_verse: You rescued me and saved my life.
translation_verse: “Ao AWURADE, ali me kra dwirɛ ama ye; apepɛ ale me ngoa.

english_verse: You saw them abuse me, Lord, so make things right.
translation_verse: Ao AWURADE, anwu edwirɛ tɛɛ bɔ bafa bali me ɔ, di me dwirɛ ma me.

english_verse: You know every plot they have made against me.
translation_verse: Anwu bɛ wereɛtɔlɛ amukoraa, ɔne me nwo porɛ bɔ babɔ amukoraa.

english_verse: Yes, you know their insults and their evil plans.
translation_verse: Ao AWURADE, ate ɛgorolɛ bɔ bɛgoro me nwo, ɔne me nwo porɛ bɔ babɔ amukoraa.

english_verse: No matter what they are doing, they keep on mocking me.
translation_verse: B’asetenalɛ nu oo, bɛ dwɔsolɛ nu oo, me yeɛ mayɛ bɛ ngorohoɛ dwein ɔ.

english_verse: Pay them back for everything they have done, Lord!
translation_verse: Ao AWURADE, tua bɛ so kerɛ kyɛbɔ bɛ yɔleɛ te ɔ.

english_verse: Put your curse on them and make them suffer.
translation_verse: Ma bɛ wora ɔbɔ, ná wɔ ɛnomalɛ ne ɔbra bɛ so.

english_verse: Get angry and go after them until not a trace is left under the heavens.
translation_verse: Ao AWURADE, fɛ yaa foa bɛ kũkũ bɛ fi wɔ nyameɛso ne abo.

english_verse: The purest gold is ruined and has lost its shine; jewels from the temple lie scattered in the streets.
translation_verse: Nea, kyɛbɔ esikaa kɔkorɛ wasi wapini ɔ! Kyɛbɔ esikaa kɔkorɛ paa wasi wakakyi ɔ! Bato nekaa krongron berɛ nyɔboɛ nemɔ bapanzam wɔ borɔnoɛ biala ngwandaa.

english_verse: These are Zion's people, worth more than purest gold; yet they are counted worthless like dishes of clay.
translation_verse: Sion mma mmienzua titire, bɔ bɛfa bɛ bɛtoto esikaa kɔkorɛ paa nwo ɔ, ɔwale ye sɛ bɔ bebu bɛ kyɛ ngukue bɔ bafa nnɛterɛ banwo ɔ, bɔ ɔte ngukuenwonɛniɛ ye sa noa adwuma ɔ!

english_verse: Even jackals nurse their young, but my people are like ostriches that abandon their own.
translation_verse: Ɛserɛ so ngyea mɔ po, bɛyeye bɛ nyɔfone bɛma bɛ mma mɔ bɛno; nakoso me maen awa brasua akakyi atianuserɛniɛ kyɛ ɛserɛ so soholi mɔ.

english_verse: Babies are so thirsty that their tongues are stuck to the roof of the mouth. Children go begging for food, but no one gives them any.
translation_verse: Nzuhɔen ti, adɔma temverema mata ye nnaalɔ. Ngwadaa mɔ bɛsrɛsrɛ aleɛ, nakoso ebiala mma bɛ bie.

english_verse: All who ate expensive foods lie starving in the streets; those who grew up in luxury now sit on trash heaps.
translation_verse: Bɛ bɔ bedi aleɛ fɛɛ ne, ɛhɔen apepɛ bɛ agua dwaaso; bɛ bɔ bɛtetele bɛ wɔ anwonya nu ne, fofoɛ so yeɛ bɛpena bɛ noa aleɛ ɔ.

english_verse: My nation was punished worse than the people of Sodom, whose city was destroyed in a flash without the help of human hands.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ me maen awa brasua, ye amumuyɛɛ nwo asohwenɛ ne, ɔte piri tra Sodom ye bɔne nwo asohwenɛ deɛ; Sodom bɔ bɛsɛkyele ye mvum nu, bɔ ebiala wandwe ye sa wɔ ye so ɔ.

english_verse: The leaders of Jerusalem were purer than snow and whiter than milk; their bodies were healthy and glowed like jewels.
translation_verse: Né ye mbanyi mɔ bɛ nwo te tra asukɔtwea, né bɛ fufue tra nyɔfonesue, bɛ nwonaen ne, né ɔboro tra mbaen, ná ne bɛ nwonaen atɔ so te kyɛ kokwaboba.

english_verse: Now they are blacker than tar, and no one recognizes them; their skin clings to their bones and is drier than firewood.
translation_verse: Nakoso kekesaala ye de, bɛ nyunu te bire tra ebunaen, na mmenia nwu bɛ wɔ dwaaso a, bennwu mmeni horɛ. Bɛ nwonaen amata bɛ mmowue, bafɔ bayɛ kangenaen.

english_verse: Life in the city is so bad that loving mothers have boiled and eaten their own children.
translation_verse: Mmrasua bɔ bɛ kunu tete bɛ ɔ, bafa bɛ sa batõ bɛ bɔbɔ bɛ kunu mmaa bafa bakakyi bɛ noa aleɛ, wɔ me maen awa brasua ye amaneɛnwunɛ mmerɛ ne anu.

english_verse: The Lord was so fiercely angry that he burned the city of Zion to the ground.
translation_verse: AWURADE ala ye ɛyaafɛlɛ ali wayie, wama ye ahone ahu kandinga paa. Yeɛ wasɔ see wɔ Sion, maa wayera ye fapem nemɔ.

english_verse: Not a king on this earth or the people of any nation believed enemies could break through her gates.
translation_verse: Ahaa aseɛ so ahemvo, yeɛ wiase ama amukoraa bengole bengoli, kyɛ ateeteefoɛ ne pɔfoɛ nemɔ bekoowura Yerusalem pambim nemɔ anu ɔ.

english_verse: Jerusalem was punished because her prophets and her priests had sinned and caused the death of innocent victims.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ ye ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ nemɔ bɛ bɔne, ɔne ye asɔfo nemɔ b’amumuyɛɛ ti yeɛ ɔwale ye sɔ ɔ. Bahã teneneefoɛ mogya bagua wɔ ye nu.

english_verse: Yes, her prophets and priests were covered with blood; no one would come near them, as they wandered from street to street.
translation_verse: Banate fofalifofali kyɛ anyesiniwaafoɛ wɔ dwaa nemɔ aso. Bafa mogya bagua bɛ nwo fiɛ maa ɔnate so mmenia ngora nzɔ bɛ ndaadeɛ nu.

english_verse: Instead, everyone shouted, “Go away! Don't touch us! You're filthy and unfit to belong to God's people!” So they had to leave and become refugees. But foreign nations told them, “You can't stay here!”
translation_verse: Mmenia teateane nu sisele bɛ mmango kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔfi wa bɛhɔ, na ye nwo nde, Ɛ́mɔfi wa bɛhɔ, ɛ́mɔfi wa bɛhɔ, nnɛmɔma ɛmɔ nwo kã bɛ!” Yiti bɛnwatili bɛbɔ bɛsandene, na mmenia kekane ye wɔ Amaenmaensofoɛ nemɔ anu kyɛ, “Yɛ ne bɛ ngɔtena wa ko.”

english_verse: The Lord is the one who sent them scattering, and he has forgotten them. No respect or kindness will be shown to the priests or leaders.
translation_verse: AWURADE ɛyaafɛlɛ ne abɔ bɛ asande; ɔngɔhɔ so ngɔnea bɛ so ko. Bammu asɔfo nemɔ bɛ dibea, na bamva anidie bamma mbanyi nemɔ.

english_verse: Our eyes became weary, hopelessly looking for help from a nation that could not save us.
translation_verse: Mmokalɛ bɔ yɛnnya ye ne, yɛ nye anea ye ate wafɛ. Yawɛne, yawɛne, kyɛ yɛnea maen bɔ ɔngɔhora ngɔpepɛ ngole yɛ ne ate.

english_verse: Enemies hunted us down on every public street. Our time was up; our doom was near.
translation_verse: Bɛtetɛ yɛ, yiti yɛngora yɛngɔ yɛ dwaa mɔ so: Y’ayieleɛ apingye, yɛ ngyẽa ayie, ofikyɛ y’ayieleɛ adwu.

english_verse: They swooped down faster than eagles from the sky. They hunted for us in the hills and set traps to catch us out in the desert.
translation_verse: Yɛ ndaneanyeɛfoɛ mɔ, bɛ nwo yɛ nyera tra ewienu kɔleɛ mɔ. Bɛfoane yɛ wɔ mmokaa nemɔ aso, bɛtetɛle yɛ wɔ ɛserɛ so.

english_verse: The Lord's chosen leader was our hope for survival! We thought he would keep us safe somewhere among the nations, but even he was caught in one of their traps.
translation_verse: Yɛ ngoa nwomeɛ, bɔ yeɛ ole bɔ AWURADE apopa ye ngoo ne, bɛhyele ye wɔ bɛ kumaa nemɔ anu. Ye yeɛ yɛhã yɛfale ye nwo kyɛ, “Ye fɔnwoo ne abo, yeɛ yɛkɔtena wɔ Amaenmaensofoɛ nemɔ anu ɔ.”

english_verse: You people of Edom can celebrate now! But your time will come to suffer and stagger around naked.
translation_verse: Ao Edom awa brasua, wɔ bɔ ɛte Yuse aseɛ so ɔ, di ahurusi, ná ma wɔ nye gye. Nakoso, wɔ koso, kulie ne kɔpɛ nu kɔwa wɔ so, ɛkɔbo, na ɛkɔye wɔ nwo kɔto so.

english_verse: The people of Zion have paid for their sins, and the Lord will soon let them return home. But, people of Edom, you will be punished, and your sins exposed.
translation_verse: Ao Sion awa brasua, w’amumuyɛɛ ne nwo akatuaa wawa ayieleɛ, na ɔngɔfa wɔ ngɔhɔ nnurehyelɛ nu ko. Nakoso wɔ, Edom awa brasua de, okootua w’amumuyɛɛ so kerɛ, na ɔkɔma wɔ bɔne kɔla ali.

english_verse: Our Lord, don't forget how we have suffered and been disgraced.
translation_verse: Ao AWURADE, kaye edwirɛ bɔ wato yɛ ye, fa wɔ nye to, ná nea y’animguaseɛ ye.

english_verse: Foreigners and strangers have taken our land and our homes.
translation_verse: Y’agyapadeɛ waali ɛwɔfoɛ mɔ bɛ sa nu, y’awuro mɔ baali amanvrafoɛ mɔ bɛ sa nu.

english_verse: We are like children whose mothers are widows.
translation_verse: Yakakyi nyisiaafoɛ bɔ belle seɛ ɔ, yɛ ni mɔ akakyi kunafoɛ.

english_verse: The water we drink and the wood we burn cost far too much.
translation_verse: Nzue bɔ yɛno ɔ, sana yɛtua ye kerɛ, na yɛ nwuaka koso, bɛtɔne ye bɛma yɛ.

english_verse: We are terribly mistreated; we are worn out and can find no rest.
translation_verse: Yɛ kɔme wura ndaneanyeɛ bo; yɛyɔ adwuma bɔ bɛmma yɛnne yɛ nwome ɔ.

english_verse: We had to surrender to Egypt and Assyria because we were hungry.
translation_verse: Yafa yɛ nwo yawura Misraimfoɛ ne Asiriafoɛ bɛ bo, kyɛbɔ ɔkɔyɛ bɔ yɛkonya aleɛ yɛkoli ɔ.
