translation_verse: “Sona awa, sɛ maen bie ɔyɔ bɔne tia me, bɔ wanni nahorɛ wamma me, ná sɛ metengyɛ me sa metwe ye so, ná mema aleɛ nwo yɛ se wɔ nu, ná mema ɛhɔen pe so, ná mekũkũ mmenia ne ngaka mefi nu,

english_verse: Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were living in that nation, their faithfulness would not save anyone but themselves.
translation_verse: ná sɛ sɔ mmenia nza hemɔ: Nowa, Daniel ne Yob po bɛwɔ nu a, bɛ tenenee yeɛ okole bɛ bɔbɔ bɛ kra ɔ, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Or suppose I punish a nation by sending wild animals to eat people and scare away every passerby, so that the land becomes a barren desert.
translation_verse: Yeɛ sɛ mema ngaka aboyaa bɛba aseɛ ne aso, bekũkũ so ama maa ɔyɛ kurofoen, bɔ ɔnate ngaka ne ati sona biala mbɛ nu berɛ a,

english_verse: As surely as I live, I promise that even if these three men lived in that nation, their own children would not be spared. The three men would live, but the land would be an empty desert.
translation_verse: sɛ sɔ mmenia nza ne po bɛwɔ so a, kyɛ nde ase ye de, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne, bengole mmaa mmienzua anaa mmaa mmrasua po ngoa; sana bɛ ngome yeɛ bekonya ngoa ɔ, nakoso aseɛ ne de, ɔkɔkakyi kurofoen.

english_verse: Or suppose I send an enemy to attack a sinful nation and kill its people and livestock.
translation_verse: “Anaakyɛ, sɛ metwe ngrandɛ metia sɔ maen ne, ná mekã kyɛ, ‘Ngrandɛ, fa aseɛ ne aso maa ngukũ mmenia ne ngaka mvi so a;

english_verse: If these three men were in that nation when I punished it, not even their children would be spared. Only the three men would live.
translation_verse: na sɛ sɔ mmenia nza ne po bɛwɔ so a, kyɛ nde ase ye de, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne, bengole mmaa mmienzua anaa mmaa mmrasua ngoa; sana bɛ ngome yeɛ bekonya ngoa ɔ.

english_verse: And suppose I am so angry that I send a deadly disease to wipe out the people and livestock of a sinful nation.
translation_verse: Yeɛ sɛ mema ewue anwonyerɛ pe aseɛ ne aso, ná mema m’ahone hu mede bɛ ngoa mefi bɛ sa nu, mekũkũ mmenia ne ngaka mefi so a,

english_verse: Again, even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were living there, I, the Lord, promise that the children of these faithful men would also die. Only the three of them would be spared.
translation_verse: sɛ Nowa ne Daniel ne Yob po bɛwɔ so a, kyɛ nde ase ye de, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne, bengole mmaa mmienzua anaa mmaa mmrasua ngoa; nakoso bɛ bɔbɔ de, bɛ tenenee yeɛ okole bɛ ngoa ɔ.

english_verse: I am the Lord God, and I promise to punish Jerusalem severely. I will send war, starvation, wild animals, and deadly disease to slaughter its people and livestock.
translation_verse: “AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Nzaade me ndɛenbualɛ suronyisuronyi nna, bɔ bɛ ole ngrandɛ, ɛhɔen, awerɔm ngaka aboyaa ne ewue anwonyerɛ ne, sɛ meprapra megua Yerusalem so mekũkũ so mmenia ne ngaka mefi so ɛ?

english_verse: And those who survive will be taken from their country and led here to Babylonia. Ezekiel, when you see how sinful they are, you will know why I did all these things to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nakoso mmaa mmienzua ne mmaa mmrasua bɔ bekonya bɛ ti bekodidi nu nen, bɛkɔfa bɛ bekofi nu bekofite. Ɛ́mɔtie, bɛkɔwa ɛmɔ berɛ, na sɛ ɛmɔnwu bɛ suban ne bɛ yɔleɛ a, ye de musue bɔ maprapra magua Yerusalem so, ɔne edwirɛ bɔ mamaa wato ye ne amukoraa, ɛmɔkonya nu aworakyekyerɛ.

english_verse: You will be convinced that I, the Lord God, was right in doing what I did.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɛmɔnwu bɛ suban ne bɛ yɔleɛ a, bɛkɔkyekye ɛmɔ wora, na ɛmɔkɔte ye bo kyɛ, bɔ mayɔ amukoraa wɔ Yerusalem ne, manyɔ ye mbaen, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.”

english_verse: Some time later, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Yeɛ AWURADE lale ye dwirɛ ali hyirele me kyɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, what happens to the wood of a grapevine after the grapes have been picked? It isn't like other trees in the forest,
translation_verse: “Sona awa, nzikyɛ yeɛ bobe bakaa fa tra bakaa biala ɔ, anaa nzikyɛ yeɛ bobe mmaen ɔfa tra ɛhɔayeɛ nu mmakaa mɔ ɔ?

english_verse: because the wood of a grapevine can't be used to make anything, not even a small peg to hang things on.

english_verse: I will forgive you, but you will think about your sins and be too ashamed to say a word. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: amaa ɔnate so sɛ mefa wɔ bɔne bɔ ayɔ amukoraa mekyɛ wɔ a, akaye, ná wayɛ wɔ nya, na w’animguaseɛ ne ati ɛngɔtɛ wɔ noa nu ko, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel the following story,
translation_verse: “Sona awa, kã Nana Nyameɛ nikyee bie bɔ ɔwɔ berɛ ɔ nwo dwirɛ, ná ka mvandoho dwirɛ kyire Yisraelfoɛ.

english_verse: so they will understand what I am saying to them: A large eagle with strong wings and beautiful feathers once flew to Lebanon. It broke the top branch off a cedar tree,
translation_verse: Kã kyɛ, AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Kɔleɛ kandinga bie, bɔ ole ndaa ngandinga ne ndɛkra ndendenn, bɔ ndɛkra woronworaen wɔ ye nwo amu ɔ ɔwale Lebanon. Obumane sida bakaa ne kɔme anu,

english_verse: then carried it to a nation of merchants and left it in one of their cities.
translation_verse: ɔpale ye mmaen bɔ ɔwɔ ye ti dɔ paa ne, ɔfa hɔle aseɛ bie bɔ bedi dwaa so ɔ so, na ooluale ye wɔ dwadifoɛ kuro bie aso.

english_verse: The eagle also took a seed from Israel and planted it in a fertile field with plenty of water, like a willow tree beside a stream.
translation_verse: Afei ɔfale aseɛ ne aso bakaa mmaa ne bie, na oluale ye wɔ aseɛ bɔ ɔkye aleɛ ɔ so maa opingyele nekaa bɔ nzue pee wɔ ɔ, kyɛ nzue noa bakaa bɔ walua ɔ.

english_verse: The seed sprouted and grew into a grapevine that spread over the ground. It had lots of leaves and strong, deep roots, and its branches grew upward toward the eagle.
translation_verse: Ofifili yɛle bobe bakaa, obuale bɔ wangɔ anwuro ɔ; ye mmaen nemɔ bɛtrɛtrɛle bɛhɔle kɔleɛ ne anwo, nakoso ye ndii nemɔ de, né bɛtɛwɔ bakaa ne abo. Yiti ɔyɛle bobe bakaa, onyane mmaen mɔ, na ɔfefɛle nyaa.

english_verse: There was another eagle with strong wings and thick feathers. The roots and branches of the grapevine soon turned toward this eagle, hoping it would bring water for the soil.
translation_verse: “Nakoso né kɔleɛ kandinga bieku koso wɔ berɛ, bɔ ole ndaa ngandinga ne ndɛkra pee ɔ. Na tie, bobe ne tengyɛle ye ndii ne anu fili nekaa bɔ beluale ye ne ɔhɔle kɔleɛ ne anwo berɛ; na ɔtrɛtrɛle ye mmaen nemɔ hɔle ye nwo berɛ, kyɛ kɔleɛ ne oguagua ye so nzue.

english_verse: But the vine was already growing in fertile soil, where there was plenty of water to produce healthy leaves and large grapes.
translation_verse: Oluale ye wɔ aseɛ paa so wɔ nzue pee noa, kyɛ óbua ná osu mmaa, ná ɔyɛ bobe bɔ ɔyɛ nyemene ɔ.

english_verse: Now tell me, Ezekiel, do you think this grapevine will live? Or will the first eagle pull it up by its roots and pluck off the grapes and let its new leaves die? The eagle could easily kill it without the help of a large and powerful army.
translation_verse: “Kã kyɛ, AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Aso bakaa ne kɔyɛ yee? Aso kɔleɛ ne ngotutu bakaa ne abo ndii ne ɔngɔma ye mma ne ngotwindwam ngɔsɛkye anaa? Aso ye nyaa bɔ wafefɛ ne, ɔngɔkese anaa? Na ongohia anwoserɛ piri biala anaa mmenia pee bɔ bɛkɔfa bekotutu ye ndii ne abo ɔ.

english_verse: The grapevine is strong and healthy, but as soon as the scorching desert wind blows, it will quickly wither. The Lord Explains the Story
translation_verse: Tie, sɛ betu bɛtɛ a, aso ɔkɔyɛ yee? Sɛ eyia afiteleɛ mvrama bɔ ye a, aso ɔngɔkese ngowu anaa? Ɔkɔkese wɔ ngofie bɔ ofifili so nemɔ aso anaa?”

english_verse: Ezekiel, ask the rebellious people of Israel if they know what this story means. Tell them that the king of Babylonia came to Jerusalem, then he captured the king of Judah and his officials, and took them back to Babylon as prisoners.
translation_verse: “Bisa ɛlɔenyɛlɛ abusua ne kyɛ, Aso ɛmɔnde ɛhemɔ abo hɔ ɔ? Kã kyɛ, Ɛ́mɔtie, Babilɔn hene wale Yerusalem, ɔhyehyele nu hene ne nu atitire, na ɔsesale bɛ hɔle Babilɔn.

english_verse: He chose someone from the family of Judah's king and signed a treaty with him, then made him swear to be loyal. He also led away other important citizens,
translation_verse: Ɔfale nnehyeɛ nemɔ nu ko ɔne ye bɛyɛle apam, na ɔmaa ɔtale ndaen foale so. (Né wahye aseɛ ne aso atitirefoɛ nnure wahɔ,

english_verse: so that the rest of the people of Judah would obey only him and never gain control of their own country again.
translation_verse: amaa ɔnate so wabrɛ maen ne ase bɔ ongodwɔso ko ɔ; na sɛ maen ne baahora gyina a, sana wali ye apam ne aso.)

english_verse: But this new king of Judah later rebelled against Babylonia and sent officials to Egypt to get horses and troops. Will this king be successful in breaking the treaty with Babylonia? Or will he be punished for what he's done?
translation_verse: Nakoso sɔ dehyeɛ ne yɛle ye nwo lɔen, na otuli ɛbɔfoɛ mɔ maa bɛhɔle Misraim, kyɛ Misraimfoɛ bɛma ye mbɔngɔ ne koɛhonɛfoɛ pee. Aso okoyie ye yé anaa? Sona bɔ ɔyɔ sɔ ne, aso ɔkɔfa ye nwo koli? Aso ɔkɔhora kobu apam ne aso ná wafa ye nwo wali anaa?

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I swear that the king of Judah will die in Babylon, because he broke the treaty with the king of Babylonia, who appointed him king.
translation_verse: Na kyɛ nde ase ye de, nahorɛ nu, sɔ hene bɔ ɔfale ye siele bia so, bɔ wabu ye ndaen animtia, bɔ wasa wabu ɔne ye b’apam ne aso ne, ye nekaa bɔ ɔte bɔ ye ole Babilɔn ne, berɛ yeɛ okowu ɔ.

english_verse: Even the king of Egypt and his powerful army will be useless to Judah when the Babylonians attack and build towers and dirt ramps to destroy the cities of Judah and its people.
translation_verse: Sɛ Pɔfoɛ ne yɔ anweaa sire, ɔne nyinasoɛ bɔ bɛkɔfo so bɛkɔhɔ kuro ne anu, kyɛ bɛkwaahũhũ mmenia pee a, Faro koɛhonɛfoɛ anwoserɛfoɛ ne ye lɔen worawora ne, bɛngɔɔboka sɔ hene ne.

english_verse: The king of Judah broke his own promises and ignored the treaty with Babylonia. And so he will be punished!
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ wabu ndaen ne animtia, yeɛ wabu apam ne aso. Ɔtale ndaen foale so, nakoso wayɔ sɔ nningyein nemɔ, yiti ongonya ye ti ngodidi nu.

english_verse: He made a promise in my name and swore to honor the treaty. And now that he has broken that promise, my name is disgraced. He must pay for what he's done.
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Kyɛ nde ase ye, nahorɛ nu, me ndaen bɔ wabu ye animtia, ɔne m’apam bɔ wabu so ne, ngɔmaa ɔkɔbɔ ye ti so.

english_verse: I will spread out a net to trap him. Then I will drag him to Babylon and see that he is punished for his unfaithfulness to me.
translation_verse: Ngɔtrɛtrɛ m’asawu nu ngogua ye so, na me ngaen kɔhye ye, na ngɔfa ye ngɔhɔ Babilɔn. Ngɔɔhwe ye so wɔ dɔ, ɔnate me nwo lɔen bɔ wayɔ ne ati.

english_verse: His best troops will be killed in battle, and the survivors will be scattered in every direction. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ye koɛhonɛfoɛ bɔ bɛkɔnwati ne amukoraa, bɛkɔtotɔ ngrandɛ noa, na bɛ bɔ bekonya bɛ ti bekodidi nu ne, bɛkɔbɔ bɛ bɛkɔsande bɛkɔhɔ nekaa bɔ mvrama bɔ kɔ biala, amaa ɔnate so ɛmɔanwu kyɛ me, AWURADE, yeɛ mahã sɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: Someday, I, the Lord, will cut a tender twig from the top of a cedar tree, then plant it on the peak of Israel's tallest mountain,
translation_verse: AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: “Me bɔbɔ ngobu sida bakaa ne ti anwuro dɔ paa mmaen ne ko ngoolua; ye ti dɔ paa mmaen lokoloko ne yeɛ ngɔpa ɔ. Na ngolua ye wɔ bokaa tendenn bɔ ɔkɔ anwuro ɔ so.

english_verse: where it will grow strong branches and produce large fruit. All kinds of birds will find shelter under the tree, and they will rest in the shade of its branches.
translation_verse: Yisrael bokaa tendenn ne aso yeɛ ngolua ye ɔ. Ɔkɔyeye mmaen frɔmfrɔm ná wasu mmaa, na ɔkɔyɛ sida bakaa nyemenenyemene. Nnomaa mukoraa bɛkɔtenatena ye bo, na ye mmaen fɔnwoo ne anu yeɛ kaka biala bɔ ole ndaa ɔ ɔkɔnwo ye saen ɔ.

english_verse: Every tree in the forest will know that I, the Lord, can bring down tall trees and help short ones grow. I dry up green trees and make dry ones green. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will keep my word.
translation_verse: Eburo mmakaa mukoraa bekonwu kyɛ me, AWURADE, me yeɛ mema bakaa tendenn yɛ tikaa, ná mesa mema bakaa tikaa yɛ tendenn ɔ; me yeɛ mema bakaa monɛ yɛ wuruwaa, ná mesa mema bakaa wuruwaa fefɛ ɔ. Me, AWURADE, me yeɛ mahã ɔ, na ngɔyɔ.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, I hear the people of Israel using the old saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
translation_verse: “Sɔ anyandera he bɔ ɛmɔtaa bebu bɛfa Yisrael maen nwo ne, sɛɛ yeɛ ɛmɔkyire ɔ? Ɛmɔnwa: ‘Seɛ mɔ bali abrɛbɛ bisii, na mmaa mɔ yeɛ bɛ gye anya ɔ.’

english_verse: Now tell them that I am the Lord God, and as surely as I live, that saying will no longer be used in Israel.
translation_verse: Susu amba, kyɛ nde ase ye, ɛmɔngobu sɔ anyandera ne ko wɔ Yisrael, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: The lives of all people belong to me—parents as well as children. However, only those who sin will be put to death.
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔtie, mmenia mukoraa bɛ kra te me deɛ. Na kyɛbɔ baba kra te me deɛ ne, sɔ ala yeɛ baa kra koso ɔte me deɛ ɔ: ɛkra bɔ ɔyɔ bɔne ne, ye yeɛ okowu ɔ.

english_verse: Suppose there is a truly good man who always does what is fair and right.
translation_verse: “Sɛ sona bie tengyɛ, ɔyɔ bɔ ɔte pɛpɛɛpɛ ne bɔ ɔtengyɛ,

english_verse: He refuses to eat meat sacrificed to foreign gods at local shrines or to worship Israel's idols. He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period.
translation_verse: ná onni mmokaa so asɔneyɛɛ so aleɛ, anaa ɔmma ye ti so mva ye nye ngyire Yisrael awuro ama bɛ mmosoen, anaa ɔne obiɛngo aye bɛnna, anaa ɔmva ye nwo nga brasua bɔ wabu ye sa,

english_verse: He never cheats or robs anyone and always returns anything taken as security for a loan; he gives food and clothes to the poor
translation_verse: ɔnhyɛ obiɛngo so; na mmom sɛ ebie fa nikyee si ye berɛ awowaa a, osa fa ye nikyee ma ye, ɔmva ebie nningyein patapaa so, na mmom ɔfa ye aleɛ ma bɔ ɛhɔen ku ye ɔ, ɔma bɔ ye nwo la so ɔ ɛtena,

english_verse: and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone
translation_verse: ɔmmɔ bosea mva nzihoɛ nzi ye nwo, anaa onne bie mva mmoka so, ɔtwe ye nwo fi amumuyɛɛ nwo, obua mmenia afia ndɛen bɔ ɔtengyɛ ɔ,

english_verse: and faithfully obeys my laws and teachings. This man is good, and I promise he will live.
translation_verse: odi me nhyehyɛleɛ so, ná odi m’ahyɛdeɛ so nahorɛ nu a, sɔ sona ne yeɛ ɔtengyɛ ɔ, na nahorɛ nu, okonya ngoa, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: But suppose this good man has an evil son who is violent and commits sins
translation_verse: “Na sɛ ɔwo baa bɔ ɔte awerɔm awueniɛ bɔ ɔkã mogya gua, anaa ɔyɔ sɔ nningyein nemɔ nu biala,

english_verse: his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife,
translation_verse: bɔ ɔnyɔ nningyein bɔ ye baba yɔle ne anu biala, na mmom odi mmokaa so asɔneyɛɛ so aleɛ, ɔne obiɛngo aye bɛda,

english_verse: cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things,
translation_verse: ɔhyɛ ehiafoɛ ne bɛ bɔ bɛyɛ anwumvo ɔ so, ɔfa ebie nningyein patapaa so, ebie fa nikyee si ye berɛ awowaa a onza mva ye nikyee mma ye, ɔma ye ti so ɔfa ye nye kyire mmosoen mɔ, ɔbɔ akyiwadeɛ bra,

english_verse: and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
translation_verse: ɔbɔ bosea fa nzihoɛ si ye nwo, anaa ode bie boka so a, aso okonya ngoa anaa? Ongonya ngoa. Wabɔ sɔ akyiwadeɛ bra ne amukoraa; ewue yeɛ okowu ɔ, na ye bɔbɔ ye mogya kɔbɔ ye ti so.

english_verse: But suppose this evil man has a son who sees his father do these things and refuses to act like him.
translation_verse: “Nakoso sɛ sɔ baa ne wo baa, ná ye de onwu ye baba bɔne bɔ wayɔ amukoraa, ná osuro, ná wanyɔ sɔ bie,

english_verse: He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife.
translation_verse: ná onni mmokaa so asɔneyɛɛ so aleɛ, anaa ɔmma ye ti so mva ye nye ngyire Yisrael awuro ama bɛ mmosoen, anaa ɔne obiɛngo aye bɛnna,

english_verse: He never cheats or robs anyone and doesn't even demand security for a loan. He gives food and clothes to the poor
translation_verse: onzisi ebie, ɔbɔ bosea a onne awowaa, ɔmva ebie nikyee patapaa so; na mmom ɔfa ye aleɛ ma bɔ ɛhɔen ku ye ɔ, ɔma bɔ ye nwo la so ɔ ɛtena,

english_verse: and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father.
translation_verse: onni ehiafoɛ aminɛ, ɔbɔ bosea a ɔmva nzihoɛ nzi ye nwo, anaa onne bie mmoka so; ná mmom odi me nhyehyɛleɛ ne m’ahyɛdeɛ so a, ye de, nna ye baba amumuyɛɛ ne ati yeɛ ɔbaamaa owu ɔ. Nahorɛ nu, okonya ngoa.

english_verse: You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws.
translation_verse: “Nakoso ɛmɔ de, ɛmɔnwa: ‘Nzu ati yeɛ baa onnya ye baba amumuyɛɛ nwo asohwenɛ ɔ?’ Sɛ baa ne ayɔ bɔ ɔte paa ne bɔ ɔtengyɛ, ná wali m’ahyɛdeɛ mukoraa so nahorɛ nu a, nahorɛ nu, okonya ngoa.

english_verse: Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
translation_verse: Ɛkra biala bɔ ɔyɔ bɔne ne, ye yeɛ okowu ɔ. Baa ngonya ye baba amumuyɛɛ nwo asohwenɛ, yeɛ baba ngonya ɔwa amumuyɛɛ nwo asohwenɛ. Sona bɔ ɔtengyɛ ne, okonya ye tengyɛlɛ nwo akatuaa, yeɛ bɔnefoɛ koso, okonya ye bɔne nwo akatuaa.

english_verse: Suppose wicked people stop sinning and start obeying my laws and doing right. They won't be put to death.
translation_verse: “Nakoso sɛ bɔnefoɛ twe ye nwo fi ye bɔne amukoraa bɔ wayɔ ɔ nwo, ná odi m’ahyɛdeɛ mukoraa so, ná ɔyɔ bɔ ɔte paa ne bɔ ɔtengyɛ a, nahorɛ nu, okonya ngoa, na ongowu.

english_verse: All their sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they did right.
translation_verse: Ye bɔne bɔ wayɔ amukoraa, mengobu ye nwo ngondaa mengogua ye so ko, na ɔnate tenenee bra bɔ wabɔ ne ati, okonya ngoa.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
translation_verse: Aso me nye gye bɔnefoɛ ye wue nwo anaa? AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne. Aso me nye ngye kyɛ ɔkɔhwe ye nwo kofi ye yɔleɛ nwo ná okonya ngoa ɔ?

english_verse: But when good people start sinning and doing disgusting things, will they live? No! All their good deeds will be forgotten, and they will be put to death because of their sins.
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ teneneeniɛ twe ye nwo fi ye tenenee nwo, ná ɔkɔbɔ amumuyɛɛ bra, ná ɔbɔ akyiwadeɛ bra mukoraa bɔ bɔnefoɛ bɛbɔ ne a, yiti okonya ngoa anaa? Ye tenenee bra bɔ wabɔ amukoraa, mengɔkaye. Na ɔnate ye nahorɛ bɔ wanni bɔ odi ye nwo foɛ, ɔne bɔne bɔ wayɔ ne ati, okowu.

english_verse: You people of Israel accuse me of being unfair! But listen—I'm not unfair; you are!
translation_verse: “Nakoso ɛmɔnwa: ‘AWURADE atee ndengyɛ.’ O Yisrael awuro ama, nzaade ɛ́mɔtie e: Aso m’atee ndengyɛ anaa? Aso nna ɛmɔ atee mmom yeɛ ɔndengyɛ ɔ?

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Sɛ teneneeniɛ twe ye nwo fi ye tenenee nwo ɔkɔbɔ amumuyɛɛ bra a, nu yeɛ okowu ɔ; na ɔnate amumuyɛɛ bra bɔ wabɔ ne ati, okowu.

english_verse: And if wicked people start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
translation_verse: Nakoso sɛ bɔnefoɛ twe ye nwo fi ye bɔne bɔ wayɔ ɔ nwo ɔkɔyɔ bɔ ɔte paa ne bɔ ɔtengyɛ a, okole ye kra ngoa.

english_verse: They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death.
translation_verse: Na ɔnate kyɛ wadwene ye nwo, ná wahwe ye nwo wafi ye mmeraatolɛ amukoraa bɔ wato nwo ne ati, nahorɛ nu, okonya ngoa, na ongowu.

english_verse: But you still say that I am unfair. You are the ones who have done wrong and are unfair!
translation_verse: Nakoso Yisrael awuro ama nwa: ‘AWURADE atee ndengyɛ.’ O Yisrael awuro ama, aso m’atee ndengyɛ anaa? Aso nna ɛmɔ atee mmom yeɛ ɔndengyɛ ɔ?

english_verse: I will judge each of you for what you've done. So stop sinning, or else you will certainly be punished.
translation_verse: “Yiti Yisrael awuro ama, ngobua ɛmɔ nu biala ye atee bɔ ɔnate so ɔ nwo ndɛen, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne. Ɛ́mɔsakyera ɛmɔ adwene, ná ɛmɔhwe ɛmɔ nwo béfi ɛmɔ mmeraatolɛ amukoraa nwo, ná amumuyɛɛ wanyɛ ɛmɔ so sundidua.

english_verse: Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins?
translation_verse: Mmeraatolɛ amukoraa bɔ ɛmɔato ne, ɛ́mɔgyi ye mukoraa béfi ɛmɔ so bégua, ná ɛmɔnya adwene foforɛ ne sunzum foforɛ. O Yisrael awuro ama, nzu ati yeɛ odi kyɛ ɛmɔwuwu ɔ?

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ me nye ngye ebiala ye wue nwo, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne, yiti ɛ́mɔsakyera, ná ɛmɔnya ngoa.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
translation_verse: Na wɔ, bɔ Yisrael atitirefoɛ nwo awuye,

english_verse: Your mother was a brave lioness who raised her cubs among lions.
translation_verse: ná kã kyɛ: Nwa yeɛ ɔte eni ɔ? Ɔte gyata beleɛ bɔ obutu gyata nyii mɔ nu, bɔ ɔtete ye mma mmaa mmaa ɔ.

english_verse: She taught one of them to hunt, and he learned to eat people.
translation_verse: Ɔtetele ye mma mmaa mmaa nemɔ nu ko maa ɔɔyɛle gyata akrɔngrɔma, osuane naenhyelɛ; na ɔhyehyele mmenia.

english_verse: When the nations heard of him, they trapped him in a pit, then they used hooks to drag him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Maen maen mɔ tele ye nga, besuale ye ngaen wɔ bɛ kumaa nu bɛhyele ye, na beguale ye ngɔnzɔngɔnzɔ bɛhwene ye bɛhɔle Misraim aseɛ so.

english_verse: His mother waited for him to return. But soon she lost all hope and raised another cub, who also became fierce.
translation_verse: Na oni nwuni kyɛ wanwondɛ tonn, nakoso ye anyelasoɛ ayie ne, osa fale ye mma mmaa mmaa nemɔ nu ko, na ɔyɛle ye gyata akrɔngrɔma.

english_verse: He hunted with other lions and learned to eat people.
translation_verse: Ohyinihyinini wɔ gyata nemɔ anu, ofikyɛ né wayɛ gyata akrɔngrɔma, osuane naenhyelɛ, na ɔhyehyele mmenia.

english_verse: Nations plotted to kill him, and people came from all over to spread out a net and catch him in a trap.
translation_verse: Yeɛ maen maen mɔ bɔ bɛwɔ mbɔtam berɛ ne, bedwɔso betiale ye, bɛtole b’asawu beguale ye so, na bɛhyele ye wɔ bɛ kumaa nu.

english_verse: They put him in a cage and took him to Babylonia. The lion was locked away, so that his mighty roar would never again be heard on Israel's hills.
translation_verse: Beguale ye ngɔnzɔngɔnzɔ, begyili ye bɛtole tuin nu, bɛfale ye bɛbrɛle Babilɔn hene, na bɛfale ye bɛtole kuku nu, kyɛbɔ ɔkɔyɛ bɔ bɛngɔte ye komvi ko wɔ Yisrael mmokaa nemɔ aso ɔ.

english_verse: Your mother was a vine like you, growing near a stream. There was plenty of water, so she was filled with branches and with lots of fruit.
translation_verse: Ahaa né wɔ maame te kyɛ bobe turo nu bobe bɔ balua ye nzue noa ɔ; na nzue somaa bɔ onyane ye ne ati, onyane mmaen pee, na osuli mmaa.

english_verse: Her strong branches became symbols of authority, and she was taller than all other trees— everyone could see how strong and healthy she was.
translation_verse: Ye mmaen nemɔ anu yɛle se, na ɔkakyili ahemvo mɔ bɛ hɔtɔ. Ɔyɛle tendenn paa trale mmaen frɔmfrɔm pusaa nemɔ, na ebiala nwuni ye tendenn ne ye mmaen pusaa ne.

english_verse: But in anger, I pulled her up by the roots and threw her to the ground, where the scorching desert wind dried out her fruit. Her strong branches wilted and burned up.
translation_verse: Nakoso betutuli bobe bakaa ne abo anyeborolɛ so, na begyili ye bɛtole ase. Eyia afiteleɛ mvrama kesene ye mma nemɔ, ye mmaen serɛserɛ nemɔ wuli, na see yerale bɛ.

english_verse: Then she was planted in a hot, dry desert,
translation_verse: Afei de, batu baalua ye wɔ ɛserɛ so, wɔ aseɛ wosee bɔ nzuhɔen ku ye ɔ so.

english_verse: where her stem caught fire, and flames burned her branches and fruit. Not one strong branch is left; she is stripped bare. This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
translation_verse: Na see afi bakaa ne anu, waatɔ ye mmaen nemɔ anu, ɔne ye mma ne anu wayera bɛ. Yiti mmaen serɛserɛ biala nne berɛ ko bɔ ɔkɔyɛ ahemvo mɔ bɛ hɔtɔ ɔ. Ɛhe te awuyebɔlɛ, na waayɛ awuyebɔlɛ.

english_verse: Seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, some of Israel's leaders came to me on the tenth day of the fifth month. They sat down and asked for a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Afoɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so nzoo ne, bosome nnu ne anu, ye eleburu ne aso, Yisrael mbanyi nemɔ anu biemɔ wale AWURADE berɛ kyɛ bɛbaabisa ye bɔ odi kyɛ bɛyɔ ɔ, na bɛtenatenane me nyunu.

english_verse: Just then, the Lord God said:
translation_verse: Na AWURADE lale ye dwirɛ ali hyirele me kyɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, these leaders have come to find out what I want them to do. As surely as I live, I will not give them an answer of any kind.
translation_verse: “Sona Awa, se Yisrael mbanyi nemɔ kyɛ, ‘AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Me berɛ abisa ti yeɛ ɛmɔwale hɔ anaa? Kyɛ nde ase ye de, mengɔma ɛmɔngɔfa ɛmɔ abisa ngɔto me nyunu, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Are you willing to warn them, Ezekiel? Then remind them of the disgusting sins of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Ekobua bɛ ndɛen anaa, Sona awa? Ekobua bɛ ndɛen anaa? Nzaade maa benwu bɛ nana mɔ b’akyiwadeɛ bra bɔ bɛbɔle ɔ;

english_verse: Tell them that long ago I, the Lord God, chose Israel to be my own. I appeared to their ancestors in Egypt and made a solemn promise that I would be their God and the God of their descendants.
translation_verse: ná se bɛ kyɛ, AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Kyẽa bɔ nneanea nu nyele Yisrael ne, ndale ndaen mvoale so ngyirele Yakob awuro ama, na nyele me nwo ali ngyirele bɛ wɔ Misraim aseɛ so. Na ndale ndaen ngyirele bɛ kyɛ, Me ole AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ ne.

english_verse: I swore that I would rescue them from Egypt and lead them to a land I had already chosen. This land was rich with milk and honey and was the most splendid land of all.
translation_verse: Na sɔ kyẽa ne, ndale ndaen ngyirele bɛ kyɛ ngɔye bɛ ngofi Misraim aseɛ so ngɔfa bɛ ngɔhɔ aseɛ bɔ mapena mato berɛ mama bɛ ne aso, aseɛ bɔ nyɔfonesue ne woɛ tengyɛ wɔ so, aseɛ bɔ ɔyɛ nyemene tra aseɛ biala ne.

english_verse: I told them to get rid of their disgusting idols and not to sin by worshiping the gods of Egypt. I reminded them that I was the Lord their God,
translation_verse: Na nzele bɛ kyɛ: Odi kyɛ ɛmɔ nu biala ogyi akyiwadeɛ nningyein bɔ ɛmɔ nye gye ye nwo ne ogua. Nnɛma ɛmɔfa Misraim mmosoen begua ɛmɔ nwo fiɛ. Me ole AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ ne.

english_verse: but they still rebelled against me. They refused to listen and kept on worshiping their idols and foreign gods. In my anger, I decided to punish the Israelites in Egypt.
translation_verse: Nakoso bɛyɛle me nwo lɔen, bɔ bandɛ me so ɔ. Bɛ nu biala wangyi akyiwadeɛ nningyein bɔ ye nye gye ye nwo ne wangua, yeɛ banyakyi Misraim mmosoen sɔnenɛ. Yiti ngane kyɛ ngɔma m’ahone kohu bɛ so, bɔ me yaafɛlɛ ne kɔyɔ bɛ nwo adwuma koyie ɔ, wɔ Misraim aseɛ so.

english_verse: But that would have made me look like a liar, because I had already promised in front of everyone that I would lead them out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Nakoso ɔnate me dumaa ti, ndwe nzale, amaa ɔnate so me dumaa nwo angua fiɛ wɔ maen maen bɔ bɛte so nemɔ anyunu; maen maen bɔ so ama bɛ nye tua kyɛbɔ nyele me nwo ali ngyirele bɛ, ná nyele bɛ mvili Misraim aseɛ so ne.

english_verse: So I brought them out and led them into the desert.
translation_verse: Yiti nyele bɛ mvili Misraim aseɛ so, na mvale bɛ male ɛserɛ ne aso.

english_verse: I gave them my laws and teachings, so they would know how to live right.
translation_verse: Yeɛ mvale m’ahyɛdeɛ mane bɛ, na ngyirele bɛ me mmeraa bɔ sɛ sona di so a onya ngoa ne.

english_verse: And I commanded them to respect the Sabbath as a way of showing that they were holy and belonged to me.
translation_verse: Asa koso, mvale m’afofingyẽa nemɔ mane bɛ, kyɛ ɔte sɛngyerɛnneɛ bɔ ɔla me ne bɛ y’afia ɔ, amaa ɔnate so banwu kyɛ me, AWURADE, me yeɛ mete bɛ nwo ɔ.

english_verse: But the Israelites rebelled against me in the desert. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath like any other day. Then in my anger, I decided to destroy the Israelites in the desert once and for all.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yisrael awuro ama yɛle me nwo lɔen wɔ ɛserɛ ne aso; banni m’ahyɛdeɛ so, na mmom bɛpole me mmeraa bɔ sɛ sona di so a onya ngoa ne; na beguale m’afofingyẽa nemɔ nwo fiɛ piri paa. “Yeɛ ngane kyɛ: Ngɔma m’ahone kohu bɛ so wɔ ɛserɛ ne aso, ná mahuhu bɛ.

english_verse: But that would have disgraced me, because many other nations had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Nakoso ɔnate me dumaa ti, ndwe nzale, amaa ɔnate so me dumaa nwo angua fiɛ wɔ maen maen nemɔ bɛ nyunu, maen maen bɔ bɛ nye tua kyɛ nyele bɛ mvili berɛ male ne.

english_verse: Instead, I told them in the desert that I would not lead them into the beautiful, fertile land I had promised.
translation_verse: Nza ndale ndaen ngyirele bɛ wɔ ɛserɛ ne aso, kyɛ mengɔfa bɛ ngɔhɔ aseɛ bɔ mva mane bɛ ne aso, aseɛ bɔ nyɔfonesue ne woɛ tengyɛ wɔ so, aseɛ bɔ ɔyɛ nyemene tra aseɛ biala ne;

english_verse: I said this because they had not only ignored my laws and teachings, but had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped idols.
translation_verse: ɔnate kyɛ, bɛpole me mmeraa, banni m’ahyɛdeɛ so, yeɛ beguale m’afofingyẽa nemɔ nwo fiɛ, ofikyɛ b’ahone oolili bɛ mmosoen nemɔ asi.

english_verse: Yet, I felt sorry for them and could not let them die in the desert.
translation_verse: Nakoso nwuni bɛ anwumvoin, bɔ mangũkũ bɛ, anaa mannua bɛ boso wɔ ɛserɛ ne aso ɔ.

english_verse: So I warned the children not to act like their parents or follow their evil ways or worship their idols.
translation_verse: “Na nzele bɛ mma mɔ wɔ ɛserɛ ne aso kyɛ, ‘Ɛmɔ nana mɔ yɔleɛ ne, nnɛma ɛmɔyɔ bie, nnɛma ɛmɔtu b’agyirɛ bɔ betuli ne bie, yeɛ nnɛma ɛmɔsɔne bɛ mmosoen nemɔ begua ɛmɔ nwo fiɛ.

english_verse: I reminded them that I was the Lord their God and that they should obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Me ole AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ ne; ɛ́mɔli m’ahyɛdeɛ so, ná ɛmɔli me mmeraa so nahorɛ nu;

english_verse: I told them to respect my Sabbath to show that they were my people and that I was the Lord their God.
translation_verse: ɛ́mɔyɛ m’afofingyẽa nemɔ krongron ma bɛyɛ sɛngyerɛnneɛ bɔ ɔla me ne ɛmɔ y’afia ɔ, amaa ɔnate so ɛmɔanwu kyɛ me ole AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ ne.

english_verse: But the children also rebelled against me. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath as any other day. I became angry and decided to punish them in the desert.
translation_verse: Nakoso mmaa nemɔ yɛle me nwo lɔen; banni m’ahyɛdeɛ so, yeɛ me mmeraa ne bɔ sona di so a onya ngoa ne, ye koso banni so; na m’afofingyẽa ne koso, beguale bɛ nwo fiɛ. Yiti ngane kyɛ: Ngɔma m’ahone kohu bɛ so, na ngɔma me yaafɛlɛ ne kɔyɔ bɛ nwo adwuma koyie wɔ ɛserɛ ne aso.

english_verse: But I did not. That would have disgraced me in front of the nations that had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Nakoso ɔnate me dumaa ti, ndwe nzale; nyɔle sɔ, amaa ɔnate so me dumaa nwo angua fiɛ wɔ maen maen nemɔ bɛ nyunu, maen maen bɔ bɛ nyunu yeɛ nyele bɛ mvili berɛ male ne.

english_verse: So I solemnly swore that I would scatter the people of Israel across the nations,
translation_verse: Nza ndale ndaen ngyirele bɛ wɔ ɛserɛ ne aso, kyɛ ngɔbɔ bɛ ngɔsande ngɔhɔ maen maen mɔ nu, ná mato bɛ mapete aseɛ mɔ so;

english_verse: because they had disobeyed my laws and ignored my teachings; they had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped the idols their ancestors had made.
translation_verse: ɔnate kyɛ banni me mmeraa so, na mmom bɛpole m’ahyɛdeɛ, beguale m’afofingyẽa nemɔ nwo fiɛ, yeɛ bɛ nye oolili bɛ nana mɔ mmosoen nemɔ asi.

english_verse: I gave them laws that bring punishment instead of life,
translation_verse: Afei de, nyele bɛ mane ahyɛdeɛ bɔ ɔtte mayee ɔ, ɔne mmeraa bɔ bengonya ngoa wɔ nu ɔ;

english_verse: and I let them offer me unacceptable sacrifices, including their first-born sons. I did this to horrify them and to let them know that I, the Lord, was punishing them.
translation_verse: na nguale bɛ nwo fiɛ wɔ b’ayɛyɛdeɛ nu, nyakyili bɛ maa bɛfale bɛ bamuɛbaa mɔ amukoraa bɛbɔle afɔleɛ wɔ see nu, amaa ɔnate so masɛkye bɛ pasapasa. Nyɔle sɔ, kyɛbɔ ɔkɔyɛ bɔ bekonwu kyɛ me ole AWURADE ɔ.

english_verse: by offering sacrifices, incense, and wine to gods on every hill and under every large tree. I was very angry, because they did these things in the land I had given them!
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ, aseɛ bɔ ndale ye nwo ndaen kyɛ ngɔfa ngɔma bɛ ne, mvale bɛ mmale so nen, nekaa biala bɔ benwuni pambaa tendenn biala, anaa bakaa pusaa biala nen, bɛbɔle b’afɔleɛ wɔ berɛ, na bɛfale b’ayɛyɛdeɛ bɔ bɛfa bɛba ne behuli m’ahone. Berɛ yeɛ bɛbɔle ɛyɛɛ fonafona afɔleɛ, ná bɛbɔle bɛ nzaa afɔleɛ ɔ.

english_verse: I asked them where they went to worship those gods, and they answered, “At the local shrines.” And those places of worship are still called shrines.
translation_verse: Na mmisale bɛ kyɛ, Asɔneyɛɛ so bɔ ɛmɔkɔ ne, ɔte nzu?’ ” Ye sɔ ne ati, bɛtɛfrɛ berɛ Bama maa waadwu ɛnɛ. Asohwenɛ ɔne bɔhyɛ

english_verse: by worshiping idols and by sacrificing their own children as offerings. They commit these sins and still think they can ask me for a message. As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will give them no answer.
translation_verse: Sɛ ɛmɔfa ɛmɔ ayɛyɛdeɛ ne bɛba, ná ɛmɔfa ɛmɔ mma mɔ bɛbɔ afɔleɛ wɔ see nu a, ɛhe kyire kyɛ ɛmɔkɔ so bɛfa ɛmɔ mmosoen begua ɛmɔ nwo fiɛ maa waadwu ɛnɛ. O Yisrael awuro ama, aso odi kyɛ mema ɛmɔba me berɛ abisa anaa? Kyɛ nde ase ye de, mengɔma ɛmɔngɔwa me berɛ abisa, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: They may think they can be like other nations and get away with worshiping idols made of wood and stone. But that will never happen! The Lord Promises To Restore Israel The Lord said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: “Bɔ ɔwɔ ɛmɔ adwene nu ne, ɔngɔwa nu le. Ɛmɔnwa: Ɛ́mɔma yɛyɛ kyɛ maen maen nemɔ, kyɛ aseɛ nemɔ aso mmusua nemɔ, ná yɛsɔne bakaa ne nyɔboɛ.

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will rule over you with my powerful arm. You will feel my fierce anger
translation_verse: “Kyɛ nde ase ye, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne, nahorɛ nu, tumi piri ne tumi asaa ne ahonehulɛ yeɛ ngɔfa ngoli ɛmɔ so hene ɔ.

english_verse: and lead you into a desert surrounded by nations. I will meet you there face to face. Then I will pass judgment on you
translation_verse: Ngɔfa ɛmɔ ngɔwa maen maen mɔ b’ɛserɛ so, na berɛ yeɛ me bɔbɔ ngɔwa ngoobua ɛmɔ ndɛen bɔ ɛmɔ nye tua ɔ.

english_verse: and punish you, just as I punished your ancestors in the desert near Egypt.
translation_verse: Na kyɛbɔ mmuale ɛmɔ nana mɔ ndɛen ɛserɛ so wɔ Misraim aseɛ so ne, sɔ ala yeɛ ngobua ɛmɔ ndɛen ɔ, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: I will force each of you to obey the regulations of our solemn agreement.
translation_verse: Ngɔmaa ɛmɔkɔsẽ bɛkɔfa pɔmaa ne abo, na ngɔmaa ɛmɔkoli apam ne aso.

english_verse: I will separate the sinful rebels from the rest of you, and even though I will bring them from the nations where they live in exile, they won't be allowed to return to Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Na mmenia bɔ bayɛ lɔen, ɔne bɛ bɔ bɛto me mmeraa ne, ngɔpa nu ngɔye bɛ ngofi ɛmɔ nu. Ngɔɔye bɛ ngofi aseɛ bɔ bɛtete so ne aso de, nakoso bɛ gya baa ngotia Yisrael aseɛ so. Na afei ɛmɔkonwu kyɛ me ole AWURADE.

english_verse: Go ahead and worship your idols for now, you Israelites, because soon I will no longer let you dishonor me by offering gifts to them. You will have no choice but to obey me!
translation_verse: “Na ɛmɔ, Yisrael awuro ama, AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Sɛ ɛmɔngotie me dwirɛ de a, nzaade afei ɛmɔ nu biala ɔhɔ ɔɔso ye mmosoen. Nakoso ye si ye, nnɛma ɛmɔfa ɛmɔ akyɛdeɛ ne ɛmɔ mmosoen ne begua me dumaa krongron ne nwo fiɛ ko.

english_verse: When that day comes, everyone in Israel will worship me on Mount Zion, my holy mountain in Jerusalem. I will once again call you my own, and I will accept your sacred offerings and sacrifices.
translation_verse: “Ofikyɛ me bokaa krongron ne aso, Yisrael bokaa tendenn ne aso, berɛ yeɛ Yisrael awuro ama amukoraa, bɛ mukoraa bɔ bɛwɔ aseɛ ne aso ɔ bɛkɔso me ɔ. AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne. Berɛ yeɛ ngole bɛ ngɔto nu ɔ, na berɛ yeɛ ngɔnea ate kyɛ ɛmɔkɔfa ɛmɔ ndoboa, ɛmɔ fieso aleɛ bɔ ɛmɔkoli moa bɛkɔfa ɔ, ɔne ɛmɔ afɔleɛ krongron bɛkɔbrɛ me ɔ.

english_verse: When I bring you home from the places where you are now scattered, I will be pleased with you, just as I am pleased with the smell of the smoke from your sacrifices. Every nation on earth will see that I am holy,
translation_verse: Ngole ɛmɔ ngɔto nu kyɛ ɛyɛɛ fonafona, mmerɛ bɔ ngɔye ɛmɔ ngofi maen maen mɔ so, bɔ ngɔboaboa ɛmɔ noa ngofi aseɛ mɔ bɔ mabɔ ɛmɔ masande maagua so ne aso ne. Na ɔnate ɛmɔ so, me krongronyɛlɛ kɔla ali wɔ maen maen nemɔ bɛ nyunu.

english_verse: and you will know that I, the Lord, am the one who brought you back to Israel, the land I promised your ancestors.
translation_verse: Na ɛmɔkonwu kyɛ me ole AWURADE, mmerɛ bɔ ngɔfa ɛmɔ ngɔwa Yisrael aseɛ so, aseɛ bɔ ndale ndaen kyɛ ngɔfa ngɔma ɛmɔ nana mɔ ne.

english_verse: Then you will remember your wicked sins, and you will hate yourselves for doing such horrible things. They have made you unacceptable to me,
translation_verse: Berɛ yeɛ ɛmɔkɔkaye atee bɔ ɛmɔnate so ɔ, ɔne bɔ ɛmɔayɔ amukoraa bafa bagua ɛmɔ nwo fiɛ ɔ; na ɔnate ɛmɔ bɔne amukoraa bɔ ɛmɔayɔ ne ati, ɛmɔ nwo kɔyɛ ɛmɔ tɛ.

english_verse: so you deserve to be punished. But I will treat you in a way that will bring honor to my name, and you will know that I am the Lord God. Fire from the South
translation_verse: O Yisrael awuro ama, sɛ me dumaa ti menwu ɛmɔ anwumvoin, ná mangyina ɛmɔ bɔne so, anaa ɛmɔ yɔleɛ tɛɛ so me ne ɛmɔ yanni ye weewee a, ye de ɛmɔkonwu kyɛ me ole AWURADE; AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.”

english_verse: “Ezekiel, son of man, turn toward the south and warn the forests
translation_verse: “Sona awa, fa wɔ nye kyire ngwaen dɔ, kã dwirɛ fa ngwaen dɔ nwo, hyɛ ngɔm tia ngwaen dɔ ɛhɔayeɛ aseɛ ne,

english_verse: that I, the Lord God, will start a fire that will burn up every tree, whether green or dry. Nothing will be able to put out the blaze of that fire as it spreads to the north and burns everything in its path.
translation_verse: ná se ngwaen dɔ ɛhɔayeɛ ne kyɛ, ‘Tie AWURADE noa dwirɛ. AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Tie, mebaato wɔ nu see, na ɔkɔyera bakaa monɛ ne bakaa wuruwaa biala bɔ ɔwɔ wɔ nu ɔ. Ɔte see bɔ ogye wuronyiwuronyi bɔ ongonua ɔ, na ofi ngwaen bɔ ɔkwaadwu sorɔ ne, ɔkɔyera bɔ ɔwɔ so amukoraa.

english_verse: Everyone will know that I started it, and that it cannot be stopped.”
translation_verse: Na anwoɔnaen mukoraa konwu kyɛ me, AWURADE yeɛ ndole nu see ɔ, na see ne ngonua.”

english_verse: But I complained, “Lord God, I don't want to do that! People already say I confuse them with my messages.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ nzele kyɛ, “Yieee, AWURADE Nyameɛ! Bɛkekã bɛfa me nwo kyɛ, ‘Aso nna anyandera nu yeɛ odwudwo e?’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the places in Jerusalem where people worship. Warn everyone in Israel
translation_verse: “Sona awa, fa wɔ nye kyire Yerusalem, ná kã dwirɛ fa nekaa krongron nemɔ anwo; hyɛ ngɔm tia Yisrael aseɛ ne,

english_verse: that I am about to punish them. I will pull out my sword and have it ready to kill everyone, whether good or evil.
translation_verse: ná se Yisrael aseɛ ne kyɛ, AWURADE nwa nyoo: Tie, meko metia wɔ, ngɔhwe me sɛpɔ ne ngofi ye bɔha nu, na teneneefoɛ oo, bɔnefoɛ oo, ngonua bɛ boso ngofi wɔ nu.

english_verse: Ezekiel, groan in sorrow and despair so that everyone can hear you.
translation_verse: “Na wɔ, Sona awa, fa aworabɔlɛ ne yealɛlilɛ gua anwongokoɔ bɔ bɛ nye tua ɔ.

english_verse: When they ask why you are groaning, tell them you have terrifying news that will make them faint and tremble in fear and lose all courage. These things will happen soon. I, the Lord God, make this promise! A Sword Is Ready To Attack Israel
translation_verse: Na sɛ bebisa wɔ kyɛ, ‘Nzu ati yeɛ egua anwongokoɔ e?’ a, bua kyɛ, ‘Edwirɛ bɔ ɔ́ba ne ati ɔ. Ɔba a, ahunundetelɛ kɔtɔ ebiala so, ebiala abasa nu kodwo, ebiala nwo ngaka kotu komini, na ebiala nangoroma nu kɔyɛ mmerɛ kyɛ nzue. Ɛ́mɔnea, ɔ́ba, na ɔkɔwa nu koso amba,’ ” AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Jerusalem: I have sharpened my sword to slaughter you; it is shiny and will flash like lightning! Don't celebrate— punishment is coming, because everyone has ignored my warnings.
translation_verse: bɔ basi kyɛ bɛfa bekũkũ ɔ, bɔ bahwi ye nwo maa ɔte yerɛmyerɛm kyɛ agralaa ɔ! Aso odi kyɛ yɛfa edwirɛ ne yɛdi angorɛ anaa? Mma, abu mbire ne ne asohwenɛ amukoraa animtia.

english_verse: Groan in sorrow, Ezekiel; the sword is drawn against my people and their leaders. They will die! So give up all hope.
translation_verse: Sona awa, sũ ná bɔ awuye, ofikyɛ sɔ dwirɛ ne kɔto me maen; ɔkɔto Yisrael mbanyi amukoraa; mafa bɛ ne me maen mawura ngrandɛ sa, yiti fa wɔ sa gua w’ahone so di aworabɔlɛ.

english_verse: I am testing my people, and they can do nothing to stop me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: “ ‘Ɛ́mɔdwene ye nwo: Sɛ ɛmɔbu mbire ne animtia a, aso edwirɛ ne ngosi anaa? AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.’

english_verse: Ezekiel, warn my people, then celebrate my victory by clapping your hands. My vicious sword will attack again and again, killing my people with every stroke.
translation_verse: “Na wɔ, Sona awa, hyɛ ngɔm ná bɔ wɔ sa nu. Ma ngrandɛ ne ohũhũ ye pɛen nyɔ so ɔne ye pɛen nza so. Mmenia huhunɛ ngrandɛ ne, ɔte ngrandɛ bɔ bɛbaafa bekũkũ mmenia pee bɔ wahã bɛ wapua ɔ.

english_verse: They will lose all courage and stumble with fear. My slaughtering sword is waiting at every gate, flashing and ready to kill.
translation_verse: Mafa ngrandɛ anoa nnaennaen magyinagyina bɛ pambim amukoraa nu, amaa ɔnate so ahunundetelɛ atɔ bɛ so, ná b’amaneɛnwunɛ ayɛ pee. Ah! ɔte yerɛmyerɛm kyɛ agralaa, na bahwi ye nwo bɔ bɛbaafa bekũkũ ɔ.

english_verse: It will slash right and left, wherever the blade is pointed.
translation_verse: O ngrandɛ, pɛ kɔ famaa so, pɛ kɔ bɛen so, pɛ kɔ nekaa biala bɔ bɛkɔfa wɔ nyunu bekohyire ne.

english_verse: Then I will stop being angry, and I will clap my hands in victory. I, the Lord, have spoken. The King of Babylonia and His Sword
translation_verse: Me koso ngɔbɔ me sa nu, ná afei mama m’ahone atɔ nzue nu. Me, AWURADE, me yeɛ mahã ɔ.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, mark two roads for the king of Babylonia to follow when he comes with his sword. The roads will begin at the same place, but be sure to put up a signpost where the two roads separate and go in different directions.
translation_verse: “Wɔ, Sona awa, atee nyɔ bɔ Babilɔn hene ngrandɛ ɔkɔfa so kɔwa ne, fa beabea berɛ. Ma bɛ munyɔ bɛhyɛ ye bo befi aseɛ komapɛ aso bɛbra. Na ngwandaa bɔ ɔkɔ kuro ne anu ne, fa frangaa bie pena berɛ bɔ okyire atee ne ɔ.

english_verse: Clearly mark where the two roads lead. One goes to Rabbah, the capital of Ammon, and the other goes to Jerusalem, the fortified capital of Judah.
translation_verse: Fa atee ko bea berɛ bɔ ngrandɛ ne kɔfa so kɔwa Amonfoɛ kuro Raba so ɔ, ɔne atee ko koso bɔ ɔkɔfa so kɔwa Yuda ɔ, mékyire Yerusalem bɔ bato ye nwo fasue ne.

english_verse: When the Babylonian king stands at that signpost, he will decide which way to go by shaking his arrows, by asking his idols, and by carefully looking at the liver of a sacrificed animal.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ Babilɔn hene waagyina ngwandaa ne aso, nekaa bɔ atee nyɔ nemɔ beyia ne, kyɛ ɔkɔ abisa. Ɔnwaha agyaen, obisa abusua amoen ne, na ɔnea brɛboɛ mɔ nu.

english_verse: His right hand will pull out the arrow marked “Jerusalem.” Then he will immediately give the signal to shout the battle cry, to build dirt ramps up to the top of the city walls, to break down its walls and gates with large wooden poles, and to kill the people.
translation_verse: Ye sa famaa ne anu serewagualɛ ne, waye Yerusalem. Wahyɛ kyɛ behũhũ mmenia, ɔ́bɔ ese, wayɔ nikyee bɔ bɛfa bebubu pambim ɔ, bɔ bɛfa betua kuro ɔ, ɔne atweleɛ mɔ bɔ begyina so betua kuro ɔ.

english_verse: Everyone in Jerusalem had promised to be loyal to Babylonia, and so none of them will believe that this could happen to them. But Babylonia's king will remind them of their sinful ways and warn them of their coming captivity.
translation_verse: Na bɛ bɔ bata ndaen ne de, bekobu sɔ dwirɛ ne kyɛ ngɔndorɔ bie ɔ. Nakoso ye de, ɔkɔkaye b’amumuyɛɛ ne, na ɔkɔhye bɛ nnure.

english_verse: Ezekiel, tell the people of Jerusalem and their ruler that I, the Lord God, am saying: Everything you do is wicked and shows how sinful you are. You are guilty and will be taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: “Yiti AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Ɛmɔ mmeraatolɛ ne, wala ali maa ɔnate so ɛmɔamaa wakaye ɛmɔ amumuyɛɛ, bɔ ɛmɔ bɔne da adi wɔ bɔ ɛmɔyɔ amukoraa nu ɔ. Na ɔnate kyɛ bɛkaye ɛmɔ ne ati, bɛkɔhye ɛmɔ nnure.

english_verse: And now, you evil and wicked ruler of Israel, your day of final punishment is almost here.
translation_verse: “ ‘Na wɔ, Yisrael panyi busueniɛ amumuyɛɛniɛ bɔ wɔ kyẽa ne adwu ɔ, wɔ so hwenɛ mmerɛ ne adwu bɔkɔɔ;

english_verse: I, the Lord God, command you to take off your royal turban and your crown, because everything will be different. Those who had no power will be put in charge, and those who now rule will become nobodies.
translation_verse: na AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Tu abotire ne, tu ɛhene abotire ne, na dibea ne ngɔyɛ kyɛ ye daa ne ala. Ma awiɛmvoɛ ne aso, ná brɛ anwomasoɛniɛ ne ase.

english_verse: I will leave Jerusalem in complete ruins like no one has ever seen until my chosen one comes to punish this city. Judgment against Ammon
translation_verse: Ngɔbɔ ye oo, ngɔbɔ ye oo, ngɔbɔ kuro ne, na ɛhe ngosi, kɔpem kyɛ bɔ ndɛenbualɛ wura ye sa ne kɔwa ɔ, na ye yeɛ ngɔfa ngowura ye sa ɔ.’

english_verse: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, the Ammonites have insulted Israel, so condemn them and tell them I am saying: A sword is drawn, ready to slaughter; it is polished and prepared to kill as fast as lightning.
translation_verse: “Na wɔ, Sona awa, hyɛ ngɔm ná kã kyɛ: Bɔ AWURADE Nyameɛ kã fa Amonfoɛ ne bɛ ngorohoɛ nwo ɛhe. Kã kyɛ, “ ‘Ngrandɛ, bahwe ngrandɛ kyɛ bɛ́fa behũhũ, bahwi ye nwo kyɛ oli awue, kyɛ ɔ́tete yerɛmyerɛm kyɛ agralaa;

english_verse: You wicked Ammonites see false visions and believe untrue messages. But your day of punishment is coming soon, and my sword will slaughter you!
translation_verse: wɔ aberɛ bɔ ngondombo nyekyire yeɛ benwu ye bɛma wɔ ɔ, bɛhyɛ wɔ ngɔm bɔ ɔtte nahorɛ ɔ, kyɛbɔ bɛkɔfa sɔ ngrandɛ ne bɛkɔpepɛ bɔnefoɛ bɛ ti ɔ, amumuyɛɛfoɛ bɔ bɛ kyẽa apingye, bɔ b’asohwenɛ mmerɛ adwu ne.

english_verse: Your days to punish others are over, so put your swords away. You will be punished in the land of your birth.
translation_verse: Sa fa wɔ ngrandɛ ne wura ye bɔha nu, nekaa bɔ bɛbɔle wɔ ne, aseɛ bɔ bɛwole wɔ bɛtole so ne aso, berɛ yeɛ ngobua wɔ ndɛen ɔ.

english_verse: My furious anger will scorch you like fire, and I will hand you over to cruel men who are experts in killing.
translation_verse: Ngɔfɛ wɔ so yaa piri paa, m’anyeborolɛ see ne, ngohu ngogua wɔ so; na ngɔfa wɔ ngowura atianuserɛfoɛ bɔ nzɛmmɔne ali bɛ ti ɔ bɛ sa.

english_verse: You will be burned and will die in your own land. Then you will be forgotten forever. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Bɛkɔfa wɔ bɛkɔkakyi eyein bekohua see, bɛkɔhã wɔ mogya bekogua wɔ aseɛ ne aso, na bɛngɔkaye wɔ ko, ofikyɛ me, AWURADE, me yeɛ mahã ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Some time later, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Na ɔwale kyɛ, AWURADE lale ye dwirɛ ali hyirele me bieku kyɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, are you ready to condemn Jerusalem? That city is filled with murderers, so remind the people of their sins
translation_verse: Wɔ, Sona awa, ekobua ndɛen anaa, ekobua awuelilɛ kuro ne ndɛen anaa? Nzaade maa onwu ye akyiwadeɛ bra bɔ wabɔ amukoraa.

english_verse: and tell them I am saying: Jerusalem, you have murdered many of your own people and have worshiped idols. You will soon be punished!
translation_verse: Kã kyɛ, ‘AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Kuro bɔ ɔkã mogya gua wɔ ye nu ɔ, ye ayieleɛ mmerɛ adwu, kuro bɔ ogyina mmosoen mɔ ɔfa gua ye nwo fiɛ ɔ!

english_verse: Those crimes have made you guilty, and the idols have made you unacceptable to me. So your final punishment is near. Other nations will laugh at you and make insulting remarks,
translation_verse: Ɔnate wɔ mogya bɔ ahã agua ne ati, edi fɔ; na afa wɔ mmosoen bɔ ayɔ ne agua wɔ nwo fiɛ. Ama wɔ kyẽa ne apingye, na w’afoɛ nemɔ b’ayieleɛ ne adwu. Yiti, mamaa ayɛ nyanzoen nikyee wɔ maen maen mɔ bɛ nyunu, ɔne ngorohoɛ nikyee wɔ aseɛ amukoraa so.

english_verse: None of you honor your parents, and you cheat foreigners, orphans, and widows.
translation_verse: Bebu seɛ ne niɛ animtia wɔ wɔ nu; bɛhyɛ ɛwɔfoɛ so wɔ wɔ nu; yeɛ besisi nyisiaa ne kunafoɛ mmrasua koso wɔ wɔ nu.

english_verse: You show no respect for my sacred places and treat the Sabbath just like any other day.
translation_verse: Abu me nningyein krongron nemɔ animtia, na agua m’afofingyẽa nemɔ nwo fiɛ.

english_verse: Some of your own people tell lies, so that others will be put to death. Some of you eat meat sacrificed to idols at local shrines, and others never stop doing vulgar things.
translation_verse: Wɔ nu mmenia bɛpɛ dwirɛ bɛto mmenia so beku bɛ; mmokaa so asɔneyɛɛ so yeɛ wɔ nu mmenia bedidi ɔ, na nyanzoen bra yeɛ bɛbɔ ye wɔ wɔ nu ɔ.

english_verse: Men have sex with their father's wife or with women who are having their monthly period
translation_verse: Wɔ nu yeɛ mmenia bɛye bɛ se mɔ b’adagya bɛto so ɔ; na wɔ nu mmrasua bɔ babu bɛ sa, bɔ bɛ nwo nde ne, yeɛ bɛ ne bɛ bɛda ɔ.

english_verse: or with someone else's wife. Some men even sleep with their own daughter-in-law or half sister.
translation_verse: Ebie ne obiɛngo aye bɛbɔ akyiwadeɛ bra; ebie ɔbɔ nyanzoen bra ɔfa ɔwa bienzua aye; na wɔ nu yeɛ ebie to oliɛma brasua bɔ ɔne ye bɛte seɛ mmaa mmɔnaa ɔ.

english_verse: Others of you accept money to murder someone. Your own people charge high interest when making a loan to other Israelites, and they get rich by cheating. Worst of all, you have forgotten me, the Lord God.
translation_verse: Mmenia wɔ wɔ nu bɔ bede fea-ase-ma beku mmenia ɔ. Ede nzihoɛ mbemanim, na esisi ebiɛngo enya wɔ nwo; nakoso me de, wɔ wora afi me, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: I will shake my fist in anger at your violent crimes.
translation_verse: “Yiti tie, mebɔ me sa nu metia mvasoɛ fiɛ bɔ anya ye ne, ɔne mogya bɔ ahã agua wɔ wɔ nu ne.

english_verse: When I'm finished with you, your courage will disappear, and you will be so weak that you won't be able to lift your hands. I, the Lord, have spoken and will not change my mind.
translation_verse: Kyẽa bɔ me ne wɔ yɛkoli ye weewee so ne, aso ɛkɔhora kosi wɔ hue, anaa ɛkɔhora kogyina ye noa’? Me, AWURADE, me yeɛ mahã ɔ, na ngɔyɔ koso.

english_verse: I will scatter you throughout every nation on earth and put a stop to your sinful ways.
translation_verse: Ngɔbɔ wɔ ngɔsande ngɔhɔ maen maen mɔ nu, ná mato wɔ mapete aseɛ mɔ so; na ngokyikyi wɔ yɔleɛ fiɛ ne ngofi wɔ nu bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: You will be humiliated in the eyes of other nations. Then you will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. Jerusalem Must Be Purified
translation_verse: Wɔ nwo kogua fiɛ wɔ maen maen mɔ bɛ nyunu, na ekonwu ye kyɛ me ole AWURADE.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I consider the people of Israel as worthless as the leftover metal in a furnace after silver has been purified.
translation_verse: “Sona awa, Yisrael awuro ama bayɛ me nye so ewura. Bɛ mukoraa bakakyi ɛdwetɛ, kɔɔbere, kyɛnzee, buralɛ ne sum bɔ bahuro bɛ wɔ afaa nu toonn maa bakakyi buralɛ ewura ɔ.

english_verse: So I am going to bring them together in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo, ‘Ɔnate kyɛ ɛmɔ amukoraa bakakyi buralɛ ewura ne ati, ɛ́mɔtie, ngɔboa ɛmɔ noa wɔ Yerusalem.

english_verse: like silver in a furnace. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them in my anger. Everyone in Jerusalem Is Guilty
translation_verse: Na kyɛbɔ behuro ɛdwetɛ wɔ afaa nu ne, sɔ ala yeɛ ɛmɔkohuro wɔ nu ɔ; na ɛmɔkonwu kyɛ me, AWURADE yeɛ m’ahone ahu ɛmɔ so serɛserɛ ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel that their country is full of sin, and that I, the Lord, am furious!
translation_verse: “Sona awa, kã kyire ye kyɛ, ‘Ɛte aseɛ bɔ bɛttele ye nwo, bɔ esue ɔttɔ ogguale so wɔ ahonehulɛ kyẽa ne ɔ.

english_verse: Their leaders are like roaring lions, tearing apart their victims. They put people to death, then steal everything of value. Husbands are killed, and many women are left as widows.
translation_verse: Aseɛ bɔ so ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ bɛbɔ porɛ, bɛte kyɛ gyata bɔ wahye naen ná opo ɔtete ye nu ɔ. Beku mmenia, bede anwonya ne mbembenanneɛ, na bama so akunafoɛ mmrasua basone pee.

english_verse: The priests of Israel ignore my Law! Not only do they refuse to respect any of my sacred things, but they don't even teach the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary or between what is clean and what is unclean. They treat my Sabbath like any other day, and so my own people no longer honor me.
translation_verse: Ye asɔfo mɔ babu me mmeraa so, bagua me nningyein krongron nemɔ anwo fiɛ; bɛmma nzonzoleɛ nna nningyein bɔ bɛte krongron ɔne bɔ bɛtte krongron ɔ b’afia; yeɛ bengyire nzonzoleɛ bɔ ɔla nikyee bɔ ye nwo te ɔ ɔne bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ b’afia, bɛmva m’afofingyẽa nemɔ bɛnyɛ huu, na bagua me nwo fiɛ wɔ bɛ nu.

english_verse: Israel's officials are like ferocious wolves, ripping their victims apart. They make a dishonest living by injuring and killing people.
translation_verse: Ye mbanyi bɔ bɛwɔ ye nu ne, bɛte kyɛ mbataku bɔ bɛtete naen bɔ bahye ye ɔ nu ɔ. Bɛkã mogya begua, na beku mmenia maa ɔnate so benya anwonyadeɛ fiɛ.

english_verse: And then the prophets in Israel cover up these sins by giving false visions. I have never spoken to them, but they lie and say they have a message from me.
translation_verse: Na ye ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ benwu ngondombo nyekyire bekyire bɛ, yeɛ bɛhyɛ ngɔndorɔ bekyire bɛ. Bɛkã kyɛ, ‘AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo,’ wɔ aberɛ bɔ nna AWURADE yeɛ wahã ɔ.

english_verse: The people themselves cheat and rob; they abuse the poor and take advantage of foreigners.
translation_verse: Aseɛ ne aso mmenia bɛhyɛ mmenia so, bedi aminɛ, besisi ehiafoɛ ne bɛ bɔ bɛyɛ anwumvo ɔ, na bebu mmeraa so bɛhyɛ ɛwɔfoɛ mɔ so.

english_verse: I looked for someone to defend the city and to protect it from my anger, as well as to stop me from destroying it. But I found no one.
translation_verse: Mbenane bɛ nu sona ko bɔ okosiesie ɛwaen ne, bɔ okogyina tokuro ne anu kɔma aseɛ ne wɔ me nyunu ɔ, amaa ɔnate so manzɛkye ye ɔ, nakoso mannwu bie.

english_verse: So in my fierce anger, I will punish the Israelites for what they have done, and they will know that I am furious. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Yiti mama m’ahone ahu bɛ so piri paa, mafa m’anyeborolɛ see ne mayera bɛ, na mama bɛ yɔleɛ abɔ bɛ bɔbɔ bɛ ti so, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, listen to this story about two sisters.
translation_verse: “Sona awa, né mmrasua nyɔ bie wɔ berɛ bɔ bɛte niwaa mmaa ɔ.

english_verse: The older one was named Oholah, which stands for Samaria; the younger one was Oholibah, which stands for Jerusalem. They became my wives and gave birth to my children.
translation_verse: Panyi ne dumaa li Ohola, yeɛ oliɛma brasua ne koso li Oholiba. Bɛɛyɛle me deɛ, na bɛwole mmaa mmienzua ne mmrasua. Bɛ dumaa ne, Ohola gyi berɛ ma Samaria, yeɛ Oholiba gyi berɛ ma Yerusalem.

english_verse: Even though Oholah was my wife, she continued to be a prostitute and chased after Assyrian lovers.
translation_verse: “Né Ohola te me deɛ de, nakoso ɔbɔle gyandera; ɔfale ye nwo mane bɛ bɔ yeɛ okuro bɛ ɔ, Asiriafoɛ bɔ bepingye ye ne.

english_verse: She offered herself to soldiers in purple uniforms: handsome, high-ranking officers and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: Bewurawura ndaadeɛ bibire, bɛte amrado ne safohene mɔ, bɛte mmerandeɛ bɔ bɛ mukoraa bɛ nwo yɛ nyemene ɔ, pɔngɔhanɛfoɛ bɔ bɛtete mbɔngɔ so ɔ.

english_verse: She had sex with all the important Assyrian officials and even worshiped their disgusting idols.
translation_verse: Ɔfale ye nwo mane bɛ ɔbɔle gyandera, Asiriafoɛ atitire amukoraa, na bɛ bɔ ɔfale ye nwo mane bɛ ne amukoraa, ɔfale bɛ mmosoen amukoraa guale ye nwo fiɛ.

english_verse: Once she started doing these things in Egypt, she never stopped. Men slept with her, and she was always ready for sex.
translation_verse: Ye gyandera bra bɔ ɔbɔle fili mmerɛ bɔ né ɔwɔ Misraim ne, wanyakyi; ofikyɛ ofi ye mmaayaa nu yeɛ mmienzua ne ye bala basosɔ ye ababunu nyɔfone nu, ná bɛ ne ye babɔ adwaman ɔ.

english_verse: So I gave Oholah to the Assyrian lovers she wanted so badly.
translation_verse: Yiti nyele ye nwurale bɛ bɔ okuro bɛ nemɔ sa, Asiriafoɛ bɔ ɔfale ye nwo mane bɛ nemɔ sa.

english_verse: They ripped off her clothes, then captured her children and killed her. Women everywhere talked about what had happened to Oholah.
translation_verse: Benwuni ye nwo, bɛhyele ye mma mmienzua ne mmrasua; na ye bɔbɔ de, bɛfale ngrandɛ behuni ye. Na bɛhwene ye so nen, mmrasua fale ye dwirɛ ne gorole ye nwo.

english_verse: Oholibah saw all this, but she was more sinful and wanted sex more than her sister Oholah ever did.
translation_verse: “Oliɛma Oholiba nye tua ɛhe, nakoso ɔlɔle asukɔ wɔ ye hurolɛ fiɛ ne anu, ɔne ye gyanderabɔlɛ ne anu trale bɔ oliɛma brasua ne yɔle ne.

english_verse: Just like her sister, she did vulgar things.
translation_verse: Nwuni kyɛ wagua ye nwo fiɛ; bɛ munyɔ bɛfale atee ko aso.

english_verse: But Oholibah behaved worse than her sister. Oholibah saw images of Babylonian men carved into walls and painted red.
translation_verse: Na ye de, ɔlɔle asukɔ paa wɔ ye gyanderabɔlɛ ne anu; onwuni mmienzua bɔ bakurukyire bɛ bagua fasue nwo ɔ, Kaldeafoɛ mvonini bɔ bafa adaabene bakurukyire ɔ,

english_verse: They had belts around their waists and large turbans on their heads, and they reminded her of Babylonian cavalry officers.
translation_verse: bɔ bafa abɔsoɛ babɔ bɛ yaase, bɔ abotire ndendenn bobɔ bɛ ti ɔ; bɔ bɛ mukoraa besoma Babilɔnfoɛ bɔ Kaldea aseɛ yeɛ ɔte bɛ maen ne.

english_verse: As soon as she looked at them, she wanted to have sex with them. And so, she sent messengers to bring them to her.
translation_verse: Na onwuni bɛ pɛ, ɔfale ye nwo mane bɛ, na otuli bɔfoɛ mɔ maa bɛhɔle bɛ berɛ wɔ Kaldea.

english_verse: Men from Babylonia came and had sex with her so many times that she got disgusted with them.
translation_verse: Yeɛ Babilɔnfoɛ wale ye berɛ bɛ ne ye bɛɛlale wɔ ehurolɛ nu, na bɛfale b’adwamanbɔlɛ ne beguale ye nwo fiɛ. Na beguale ye nwo fiɛ beyiele ne, bɛ nwo yɛle ye ahi maa ɔyakyili bɛ.

english_verse: She let everyone see her naked body and didn't care if they knew she was a prostitute. That's why I turned my back on her, just as I had done with her older sister.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ ɔyele ye nyunu bɔle gyandera, ná ɔpale ye nwo hyirele nen, ye nwo yɛle me ahi maa ndwene me nwo mvili ye nwo, kyɛbɔ oliɛma brasua ne nwo yɛle me ahi maa ndwene me nwo mvili ye nwo ne.

english_verse: Oholibah didn't stop there, but became even more immoral and acted as she had back in Egypt.
translation_verse: Nakoso ɔhɔle so lɔle asukɔ wɔ gyanderabɔlɛ nu, ɔkayele ye mmaayaa mmerɛ nu, mmerɛ bɔ né ɔbɔ gyandera wɔ Misraim aseɛ so ne.

english_verse: She eagerly wanted to go to bed with Egyptian men, who were famous for their sexual powers.

translation_verse: Ngɔhwe Moabo so, na bekonwu kyɛ me ole AWURADE.’ ” Edom nwo ngɔm

english_verse: The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah.
translation_verse: “AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo, ‘Ɔnate kyɛ Edom atɔ Yuda awuro ama so wereɛ, ná afei wali ye nwo foɛ paa kyɛ watɔ bɛ so wereɛ ne ati,

english_verse: So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan.
translation_verse: yiti AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Ngɔhwe Edom so, na ngohũhũ so mmenia ne ngaka. Ngɔbɔ maen ne, na bɛkɔtotɔ ngrandɛ noa bekofi Teman maa okoodwu Dedan.

english_verse: I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.” Judgment on Philistia
translation_verse: Ngɔfa me maen Yisrael so ngɔtɔ Edom so wereɛ. Bɛkɔhwe Edom so, kyɛbɔ me yaafɛlɛ ne m’ahonehulɛ osi te ɔ, na bekonwu me wereɛtɔlɛ ne, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne. Filistifoɛ nwo ngɔm

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The cruel Philistines have taken revenge on their enemies over and over and have tried to destroy them.
translation_verse: “AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo, ‘Ɔnate kyɛ Filistifoɛ batɔ ye so wereɛ, ná bafa atianuserɛ ɛpɔen batɔ ye so wereɛ, kyɛ bekonua ye boso ne ati;

english_verse: Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast.
translation_verse: yiti AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Tie, ngɔhwe Filistifoɛ bɛ so, ngonua Keretifoɛ bɛ boso, yeɛ ngohũhũ bɛ bɔ baha wɔ mboanoa ne.

english_verse: In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ngɔfɛ yaa piri paa ngɔtɔ bɛ so wereɛ piri; na sɛ metɔ bɛ so wereɛ a, yeɛ bekonwu kyɛ me ole AWURADE ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
translation_verse: Na ɔwale kyɛ, ye afoɛ buru ne ko ne anu, kyẽa bɔ oli moa wɔ bosome ne anu ne, AWURADE lale ye dwirɛ ali hyirele me kyɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing, “Jerusalem has fallen! It used to be powerful, a center of trade. Now the city is shattered, and we will take its place.”
translation_verse: “Sona awa, ɔnate kyɛ Tiro wahã wafa Yerusalem nwo kyɛ, ‘Ehee! Pambim bɔ né maen maen mɔ bɛfa nu bekodi dwaa ne, wabubu. Afei de, dwaa nningyein ne kɔkakyi kɔwa me berɛ; na kekesaala ye bɔ wabɔ ye de, ngonya me nwo,’ ne ati,

english_verse: Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore.
translation_verse: bɔ AWURADE Nyameɛ kã hɔ ɛhe: Tie, wɔ Tiro, meko metia wɔ, na ngɔma maen maen pee bɛkɔfa koɛ bɛkɔɔtoa wɔ, kyɛbɔ ɛpo ɔbɔ ye asorɔkye ba ne.

english_verse: They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock,
translation_verse: Bɛkɔɔsɛkye Tiro fasue nemɔ, na bekobubu ye abandenden nemɔ bekogua. Ngɔprapra so anweaa ne ngofi so, na ngɔmaa ɔkɔyɛ kyɛ nyɔbotaen wosee.

english_verse: where fishermen can dry their nets along the coast. I promise that you will be robbed
translation_verse: Ɔkɔyɛ nekaa bɔ bɛworɛ asawu nu ɔ wɔ ɛpo nu; ofikyɛ me yeɛ mahã ɔ, na ɔkɔyɛ maen maen mɔ bɛ koɛ nu nzesadeɛ, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ye mma mmrasua mɔ bɔ baha aseɛ ne aso ne, bɛkɔtotɔ ngrandɛ noa, na afei bekonwu kyɛ me ole AWURADE.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: “Ofikyɛ AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Tie, mebaafa Babilɔn hene Nebukadenesa bɔ ɔte ahemvo mɔ nu hene ne, ɔne mbɔngɔ, teaseɛnam mɔ, pɔngɔhanɛfoɛ ne koɛhonɛfoɛ ɛlɔen pee mefi sorɔ dɔ meba wɔ, Tiro so.

english_verse: First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you.
translation_verse: Ɔkɔfa ngrandɛ kohũhũ wɔ mma mmrasua bɔ bɛwɔ aseɛ ne aso ne; ɔkɔyɔ nyinasoɛ bɔ bɛkɔfo so bɛkɔwa wɔ nu ɔ, ɔkɔboaboa anweaa sire wɔ wɔ si, na ɔkɔfa akokyɛm mɔ kɔwa wɔ so.

english_verse: He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers.
translation_verse: Ɔkɔfa nikyee bɔ bɛfa bebubu fasue ɔ kɔwa wɔ so, na ɔkɔfa ye akodeɛ kobubu w’abandenden mɔ kogua.

english_verse: He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city.
translation_verse: Ye mbɔngɔ nemɔ somaa ne ati, bɛ si mvuture kɔkata wɔ so. Na pɔngɔhanɛfoɛ nemɔ, akodeɛ teaseɛnam mɔ ne teaseɛnam nemɔ, bɛ dede bɔ bɛkɔyɔ ne, ɔkɔwoso wɔ fasue nemɔ, wɔ mmerɛ bɔ ɔfa wɔ pambim nemɔ anu ɔba, kyɛbɔ mmenia wura kuro bɔ bɔen la ye fasue nu nen.

english_verse: His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground.
translation_verse: Ye mbɔngɔ nemɔ, ɔkɔfa bɛ gya mbaboa ne kotiatia wɔ mmorɔnoɛ ne amukoraa so; ɔkɔfa ye ngrandɛ kohũhũ wɔ mmenia, na okosumu wɔ bonima mbiri nemɔ kogua ase.

english_verse: The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea.
translation_verse: Bɛkɔfa w’anwonyadeɛ bɛkɔyɛ koɛ nu nzesadeɛ, ná bafẽ wɔ dwaa nningyein bafa. Bekobubu wɔ fasue nemɔ bekogua, ná basɛkye wɔ sua nyemenenyemene nemɔ. Na bekofindi wɔ nyɔboɛ mɔ ne wɔ mmakaa ne wɔ nnɛterɛ bekogua nzue ne anu.

english_verse: You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps,
translation_verse: Ngɔma w’anika dweintolɛ ne bo kɔpɛ, na wɔ sangoo ne nga koso, bɛngɔte ye ko.

english_verse: because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
translation_verse: Ngɔmaa ɛkɔkakyi nyɔbotaen wosee; ɛkɔyɛ nekaa bɔ bɛworɛ asawu nu ɔ; bɛngɔkyekye wɔ ko, ofikyɛ me, AWURADE, me yeɛ mahã ɔ. AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.

english_verse: The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death.
translation_verse: Bɔ AWURADE Nyameɛ ɔkã kyire Tiro ɛhe: W’asefinɛ ne, ye dede bɔ ɔkɔyɛ ne, mmerɛ bɔ mmenia bɔ bapura bɛbɔ awuye, bɔ ebiemɔ koso bekũkũ bɛ wɔ wɔ nu ne, aso ɔngɔma supɔ mɔ bɛngɔwoso?

english_verse: The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear
translation_verse: Na afei, ɛpo so ahemvo amukoraa bekodwu ase bekofi b’ahennie bia so, bekopuropuro bɛ ndaadeɛ aguasoɛ, na bekodwa bɛ ndena bɔ bali adwii bagua nu ɔ bekogua berɛ. Ahunundetelɛ kɔtɔ bɛ so, bekopofo aseɛnwo, bɛ nwo kɔwoso bɛ mmerɛ biala, na ɔnate wɔ ti, bɛ nwo kodwiri bɛ.

english_verse: But now Tyre is in ruins, and the people on the coast stare at it in horror and tremble in fear.”
translation_verse: Kekesaala ye de, supɔ nemɔ bɛ nwo wosowoso bɛ wɔ w’asefinɛ kyẽa ne; yieee, ɛpo nu supɔ nemɔ, bɛ nwo adwiri bɛ wɔ w’ayieleɛ bɔ wayie wɔ ne anwo.’

english_verse: I, the Lord God, will turn you into a ghost-town. The ocean depths will rise over you
translation_verse: “AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Sɛ memaa ɛkakyi kuro bɔ wabɔ, kyɛ nguro bɔ sona nne so ne, mmerɛ bɔ ngɔma ɛpo kohwi kɔfa wɔ so, bɔ nzue pee kɔkata wɔ so ne a,

english_verse: and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people.
translation_verse: ye de, ngɔfa wɔ ngɔboka bɛ bɔ ofi tetetete bedwu ase bɛkɔ ɛborɔ kumaa nu ne aso, na ngofindi wɔ ngɔto ase. Ngɔmaa ɛkɔtena aseɛ bo dɔ, nekaa bɔ berɛ te aworabɔlɛ fi tetetete ne, ɛne bɛ bɔ bedwu ase bɛkɔ ɛborɔ kumaa nu ne, amaa ɔnate so ebiala wandena wɔ nu ko, na ngɔma animnyam kɔwa ateasefoɛ aseɛ so.

english_verse: You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ngɔma w’ayieleɛ kɔyɛ suronyisuronyi, na wɔ boso komini. Bɛkɔpena wɔ boso de, nakoso bengonwu wɔ ko le, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre,
translation_verse: “Afei wɔ, Sona awa, bɔ Tiro nwo awuye,

english_verse: the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me: Tyre, you brag about your perfect beauty,
translation_verse: ná se Tiro kyɛ: Wɔ, kuro bɔ bɛkyekyele wɔ wɔ mboanoa, bɔ ɛne maen maen bedi dwaa wɔ supɔ pee so ɔ, AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: “O Tiro, wɔ de ɛnwa, ‘M’anwonyemene di mu bɔkɔɔ.’

english_verse: and your control of the sea. You are a ship built to perfection.
translation_verse: Wɔ wɛen nemɔ bɛwɔ ɛpo afia, na bɛ bɔ bɛkyekyele wɔ ne, bɛmane w’anwonyemene lili mu.

english_verse: Builders used cypress trees from Mount Hermon to make your planks and a cedar tree from Lebanon for your tall mast.
translation_verse: Wɔ lɛen ndaboa ne, bɛfale asia mmakaa bɔ ofi Seniri yeɛ bɛyɔle ɔ; sida bakaa bɔ ofi Lebanon yeɛ bɛfa bɛyɔle ɛlɛen frangaa bakaa bɛmane wɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Oak trees from Bashan were shaped into oars; pine trees from Cyprus were cut for your deck, which was then decorated with strips of ivory.
translation_verse: Basan eluii yeɛ bɛfa bɛyɔle wɔ tabɔnga ɔ; Kitim mboanoa sapele yeɛ bɛfa bɛyɔle wɔ kuku nzamsoɛ bɔ ɛsoen gye wɔ nu ɔ.

english_verse: The builders used fancy linen from Egypt for your sails, so everyone could see you. Blue and purple cloth from Cyprus was used to shade your deck.
translation_verse: Nwera bɔ ofi Misraim bɔ bali adwii bagua nu yeɛ ɔte wɔ lɛen mvrama tena bɔ ɔte wɔ frangaa ɔ, bibire ne koogyan bɔ ofi Elisa mboanoa yeɛ ɔte wɔ ngatasoɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Men from Sidon and Arvad did the rowing, and your own skilled workers were the captains.
translation_verse: Sidonfoɛ ne Arwadefoɛ yeɛ bɛte wɔ ɛlɛenhanɛfoɛ ɔ, O Tiro, wɔ nimdeɛfoɛ yeɛ bɛla wɔ ɛlɛenhanɛfoɛ nemɔ noa bekyire b’atee ɔ.

english_verse: Experienced men from Byblos repaired any damages. Sailors from all over shopped at the stores in your port.
translation_verse: Gebal mbanyi ne ye nimdeɛfoɛ bɛwɔ wɔ nu bɔ betuatua ɛlɛen ne abo ndokuro nemɔ ɔ. Ɛpo so ɛlɛen amukoraa ne nu ɛlɛenhanɛfoɛ bɛwɔ wɔ nu, kyɛ bɛ ne wɔ bɛbaali dwaa.

english_verse: Brave soldiers from Persia, Lydia, and Libya served in your navy, protecting you with shields and helmets, and making you famous.
translation_verse: “Pɛsia ne Lude ne Pute bɛte koɛhonɛfoɛ wɔ wɔ lɔen ne anu; bɛfa akokyɛm ne buralɛ kyerɛ besinzesinze wɔ nu, na bɛmaa ɛyɛ nyemene.

english_verse: Your guards came from Arvad and Cilicia, and men from Gamad stood watch in your towers. With their weapons hung on your walls, your beauty was complete.
translation_verse: Arwadefoɛ ne b’ɛlɔen bɛwɛne wɔ fasue nemɔ bɛbra beyia; Gamadefoɛ bɛwɔ w’abandenden nemɔ anu. Bɛfa b’akokyɛm mɔ besinzesinze wɔ fasue nwo bɛbra beyia, na bɛma w’anwonyemene di mu.

english_verse: Merchants from southern Spain traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products.
translation_verse: “W’anwonya pee amukoraa ne ati, Tasise ne wɔ belili dwaa. Bɛfale ɛdwetɛ, buralɛ, kyɛnzee ne sum yeɛ bɛsesane wɔ dwaa nningyein ɔ.

english_verse: The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze,
translation_verse: Yawan, Tubal ne Meseke bɛ ne wɔ lili dwaa; bɛfale kuro mmenia ne kɔɔbere nningyein yeɛ bɛsesane wɔ dwaa nningyein ɔ.

english_verse: and those from Beth-Togarmah traded work horses, war horses, and mules.
translation_verse: Bete Togamafoɛ fale mbɔngɔ, pɔngɔhanɛfoɛ ne afunum mɔ yeɛ bɛsesane wɔ dwaa nningyein ɔ.

english_verse: You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods.
translation_verse: Dedanfoɛ bɛ ne wɔ lili dwaa; mboanoa aseɛ pee aso yeɛ né ɛfa wɔ dwaa nningyein ɛkɔ ɔ, na bɛfale ɛsoen gye ne akumadua ndaboa yeɛ betuale wɔ kerɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise.
translation_verse: Yuda ne Yisrael maen bɛ ne wɔ lili dwaa. Bɛfale atokoɔ bɔ ofi Minite, ayuo, woɛ, ngoo ne sakyeɛ yeɛ bɛsesane wɔ dwaa nningyein ɔ.

english_verse: The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
translation_verse: Damasko ne wɔ belili dwaa, ɔnate wɔ dwaa nningyein pee ne, ɔne w’anwonya ahoroɔ mukoraa, Helebon nzaa ne mmoaen nwiaa fufue ne ati.

english_verse: The people of Dedan supplied you with saddle blankets,
translation_verse: Dedan ne wɔ belili ɛtena bɔ bɛfa bɛsɛ pɔngɔ so ɔ nwo dwaa.

english_verse: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products.
translation_verse: Hyeba ne Raama dwadifoɛ bɛ ne wɔ lili dwaa. Bɛfale ayirefona mukoraa nu paa, nyɔboɛ paa mukoraa ne sikaa kɔkorɛ bɛsesane wɔ dwaa nningyein.

english_verse: You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad,
translation_verse: Haran, Kanne, Eden, Hyeba dwadifoɛ, Asure ne Kilmade bɛ ne wɔ lili dwaa.

english_verse: and they gave you expensive clothing, purple and embroidered cloth, brightly colored rugs, and strong rope.
translation_verse: Bɛ ne wɔ lili nningyein hemɔ nwo dwaa: ɛtena paa, ɛtena bibire, ɔne bɔ bali adwii bagua nu ɔ, ɛtena ndiamuɛ bɔ banwo mmɛsa bafa banwo bamia nu ɔ.

english_verse: Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go. You were like a ship loaded with heavy cargo
translation_verse: Tasise ɛlɛen mɔ yeɛ né bɛsoa wɔ dwaa nningyein ɔ. “Yiti nningyein yili wɔ nu tɛkyɛ, wɔ ɛpo n’afia dɔ.

english_verse: and sailing across the sea, but you were wrecked by strong eastern winds.
translation_verse: Wɔ ɛlɛenhanɛfoɛ nemɔ, bɛfale wɔ bɛhɔle ɛpo ne aso dɔ moa moa paa, na eyia afiteleɛ mvrama ama wɔ ɛlɛen ne abutu wɔ ɛpo n’afia dɔ.

english_verse: The shouts of your drowning crew were heard on the shore.
translation_verse: Bɛ bɔ bɛla wɔ ɛlɛenhanɛfoɛ nemɔ noa bekyire b’atee ne, bɛtea nu a, ɔma mboanoa aseɛ woso,

english_verse: mourning for you. They show their sorrow by putting dust on their heads and rolling in ashes;
translation_verse: bɛteatea nu besu wɔ, na besu hahii. Betu mvuture begua bɛ ti so, na bemunumunu bɛ nwo wɔ nzoen nu.

english_verse: they shave their heads and dress in sackcloth as they cry in despair.
translation_verse: Ɔnate wɔ ti bɛbɔ tikwa, na bɛkera ɛsɛen tena, na bɛbɔ awuye bedi aworabɔlɛ besu wɔ hahii.

english_verse: In their grief they sing a funeral song for you: “Tyre, you were greater than all other cities. But now you lie in silence at the bottom of the sea.
translation_verse: Bɛ suɛ ne anu, bɛbɔ wɔ nwo awuye, na bɛbɔ wɔ nwo awuye kyɛ, ‘Kuro beni yeɛ né ɔte kyɛ Tiro bɔ afei de wayɛ pasaa wɔ ɛpo nu e?

english_verse: But now you are wrecked in the deep sea, with your cargo and crew scattered everywhere.
translation_verse: Na afei de, ɛpo ne abubu wɔ wɔ ɛpo buma ne anu, na wɔ dwaa nningyein ne wɔ nu mmenia amukoraa, bɛ ne wɔ amono bahɔ nzue ne abo.

english_verse: People living along the coast are shocked at the news. Their rulers are horrified, and terror is written across their faces.
translation_verse: Na ɔnate wɔ ti, mboanoafoɛ amukoraa bɛ nwo dwiri bɛ; ɛserɛ kandinga kã b’ahemvo mɔ, na bɛ nyunu yɛ bosaa.

english_verse: The merchants of the world can't believe what happened. Your death was gruesome, and you are gone forever.”
translation_verse: Maen maen mɔ nu dwadifoɛ mɔ, besobi bɛ noa begua wɔ so; w’ayieleɛ ayie wɔ pasaa, na engodwɔso ko le.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying: You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human.
translation_verse: “Sona awa, se Tiro maen panyi ne kyɛ, AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: “Ɔnate kyɛ ɛte anwomasoɛ, ná ahã kyɛ, ‘Nde nyameɛ, nde nyameɛ mɔ bɛ bia so wɔ ɛpo afia;’ nakoso ɛte kuro sona, ɛtte nyameɛ, na ɛyɛ wɔ nwo kyɛ ɛse nworɛ kyɛ Nyameɛ;

english_verse: You think you're wiser than Daniel and know everything.
translation_verse: kyɛ ɛse nworɛ tra Daniel, mvealeɛ nu dwirɛ biala mvea wɔ,

english_verse: Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver.
translation_verse: wɔ nworɛ ne wɔ nimdeɛ yeɛ afa anya wɔ nwo ɔ, na aboaboa sikaa kɔkorɛ ne ɛdwetɛ noa agua nekaa bɔ esie wɔ nningyein ɔ;

english_verse: You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
translation_verse: Wɔ dwaalilɛ nu nworɛ piri ne, ɛnate so ama w’anwonya asone pee, na w’anwonya ne ama anwomasoɛ awa wɔ nu.

english_verse: You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God,
translation_verse: Yiti AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: “Ɔnate kyɛ ebu wɔ nwo nworɛniɛ kyɛ Nyameɛ ne ati,

english_verse: will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get.
translation_verse: yiti, tie, ngɔfa ɛwɔfoɛ mɔ maa bɛkɔwa wɔ so, bɛte maen bɔ bɛ ti anu yɛ se paa wɔ maen maen mɔ nu ɔ; na bɛkɔhwe bɛ ngrandɛ wɔ w’anwonyemene ne wɔ nworɛ ne aso, na bekogua w’animnyam nwo fiɛ.

english_verse: Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
translation_verse: Bekofindi wɔ bɛkɔto ɛborɔ kumaa nu, na ekowu mmenia bɔ batotɔ ɔ b’ewue, wɔ ɛpo afia.

english_verse: When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human.
translation_verse: Aso ɛkɔhɔ so kɔhã kyɛ, ‘Nde Nyameɛ,’ wɔ bɛ bɔ beku wɔ ne anyunu? Ɛte sona, na mmom ɛtte Nyameɛ wɔ mmenia bɔ beku wɔ nemɔ bɛ sa nu.

english_verse: Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
translation_verse: Ekowu mmenia bɔ bɛmbɛ bɛ bienzua ɔ bɛ wue, wɔ ɛwɔfoɛ mɔ bɛ sa nu; ofikyɛ me yeɛ mahã ɔ, AWURADE Nyameɛ noa dwirɛ ɛne.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying: At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking.
translation_verse: “Sona awa, bɔ Tiro hene nwo awuye, ná se ye kyɛ, AWURADE Nyameɛ nwa nyoo: Né ɛte sona bɔ odi mu paa nwo nhwɛsoɛ, bɔ nworɛ ayi wɔ ti anu tɛkyɛ, ná w’anwonyemene di mu paa ɔ.

english_verse: You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born.
