english_verse: The Lord's power was with them, and many people turned to the Lord and put their faith in him.
translation_verse: Awurade gyinane bɛ si; na mmenia pee bɔ bele belili ne, bɛfale bɛ nwo bɛmane Awurade.

english_verse: News of what was happening reached the church in Jerusalem. Then they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
translation_verse: Na Yerusalem asɔre ne tele sɔ dwirɛ ne, yiti bɛsomane Banaba maa ɔhɔle Antiokia.

english_verse: When Barnabas got there and saw how God had blessed them with undeserved grace, he was very glad. So he begged them to remain faithful to the Lord with all their hearts.
translation_verse: Banaba hɔle oodwuli berɛ na onwuni kyɛbɔ Nyameɛ asi ayira asɔre nen, ye nye gyele, na ɔhyɛle bɛ nguraen kyɛ bɛfa b’ahone mukoraa bɛsɔ gyidie ne anu paa, na beli nahorɛ bɛma Awurade.

english_verse: Barnabas was a good man of great faith, and he was filled with the Holy Spirit. Many more people turned to the Lord.
translation_verse: Né Banaba te sona paa bɔ Sunzum Krongron ne gyidie ayi ye tɛkyɛ ɔ, na ɔhwene mmenia pee maa beelili Awurade si.

english_verse: Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul.
translation_verse: Banaba fili berɛ hɔle Taaso kyɛ ɔkwaapena Sɔɔlo.

english_verse: He found Saul and brought him to Antioch, where they met with the church for a whole year and taught many of its people. There in Antioch the Lord's followers were first called Christians.
translation_verse: Na onwuni Sɔɔlo nen, ɔfale ye wale Antiokia. Bɛ munyɔ bɛ ne Antiokia asɔremma ne bɛtenane afoɛ ko mumua, na bɛyɛle ngyerɛkyerɛ behyirele mmenia pee. Na Antiokia berɛ yeɛ belili moa bɛfrɛle agyidifoɛ nemɔ Akristofoɛ ɔ.

english_verse: During this time some prophets from Jerusalem came to Antioch.
translation_verse: Na sɔ mmerɛ ne anu, ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ biemɔ fili Yerusalem bɛwale Antiokia.

english_verse: One of them was Agabus. Then with the help of the Spirit, he told that there would be a terrible famine everywhere in the world. And it happened when Claudius was Emperor.
translation_verse: Bɛ nu ko bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Agabo fale Sunzum Krongron tumi so hyɛle ngɔm kyɛ ɛhɔen pirikua bie baawa ewiase amukoraa. Sɔ hɔen ne wale Klɔdio Kaesare aberɛ so.

english_verse: The followers in Antioch decided to send whatever help they could to the followers in Judea.
translation_verse: Yiti asuafoɛ nemɔ yɛle kyɛ bɛ nu biala ɔkekã ye sa ase kãa kyɛbɔ ɔkɔhora ɔ, ná bɛfa bɔ bekonya ye ne bɛɛboka aliɛmaa mɔ bɔ bɛwɔ Yudea ɔ.

english_verse: So they appointed Barnabas and Saul to take their gifts to the church leaders in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Bɛyɔle sɔ, na bɛfale akyɛdeɛ ne bɛsomane Banaba ne Sɔɔlo maa bɛɛmane Yerusalem asɔre ne mbanyi mɔ.

english_verse: At that time King Herod caused terrible suffering for some members of the church.
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne anu, Nana Herode tuli asɔre ne anu mmenia ne biemɔ anyeɛ.

english_verse: When Herod saw that this pleased the Jewish people, he had Peter arrested during the Festival of Thin Bread.
translation_verse: Na onwuni kyɛ bɔ wayɔ ne ayɛ Yudafoɛ nemɔ fɛ, yiti ɔtoale so hyele Petro koso.

english_verse: He put Peter in jail and ordered four squads of soldiers to guard him. Herod planned to put him on trial in public after the festival.
translation_verse: Ɔhyele Petro nen, ɔtole ye kuku nu, na ɔfale ye wurale asraafoɛ fekue faa nna sa kyɛ bɛwɛne ye. Né fekue ko biala tira mmenia nna. Na Herode yɛle kyɛ sɛ bedi Abɔtra aluolue ne beyie a, ɔkɔye ye koli ye dwirɛ wɔ badwa nu.

english_verse: While Peter was being kept in jail, the church never stopped praying to God for him. Peter Is Rescued
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Petro la kuku nu berɛ nen, asɔre mma ne mane bɛ nye borole hɔle so bɔle mbaeɛ mane ye. Nyameɛ abɔfo ye Petro fi kuku nu

english_verse: The night before Peter was to be put on trial, he was asleep and bound by two chains. A soldier was guarding him on each side, and two other soldiers were guarding the entrance to the jail.
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne kɔngɔen, bɔ Herode yɛle kyɛ aleɛ kye a ɔkɔye Petro kɔwa badwa nu ne, né Petro alafe wɔ asraafoɛ nyɔ afia. Né bafa ngɔnzɔngɔnzɔ nyɔ bagua ye ne asraafoɛ nyɔ ne; yeɛ afei né asraafoɛ ne bie koso gyigyi anoa ne si bɛwɛne kuku nu ne.

english_verse: Suddenly an angel from the Lord appeared, and light flashed around in the cell. The angel poked Peter in the side and woke him up. Then he said, “Quick! Get up!” The chains fell off his hands,
translation_verse: Aworafire nu, Awurade abɔfo wale kuku nu berɛ, na sua ne anu tale hyireinn. Abɔfo ne pusupusuli Petro maa otingyele, na osele ye kyɛ, “Dwɔso ndɛ!” Na berɛ ne ala ngɔnzɔngɔnzɔ ne fili ye sa puro guale.

english_verse: and the angel said, “Get dressed and put on your sandals.” Peter did what he was told. Then the angel said, “Now put on your coat and follow me.”
translation_verse: Na Abɔfo ne sele ye kyɛ, “Bɔ w’abɔsoɛ na wura wɔ mbaboa.” Petro yɔle sɔ, na abɔfo ne sa sele ye kyɛ, “Fa w’ataadeɛ aguasoɛ wura na di me si.”

english_verse: Peter left with the angel, but he thought everything was only a dream.
translation_verse: Na ofitele lili ye si; na né ɔnze kyɛ bɔ abɔfo ne yɔle ne ɔte edwirɛ bɔ osi amba, na né ɔdwene kyɛ onwu nyekyire.

english_verse: They went past the two groups of soldiers, and when they came to the iron gate to the city, it opened by itself. They went out and were going along the street, when all at once the angel disappeared.
translation_verse: Na bɛtrale awɛmvoɛ fekue bɔ oli moa ne ɔne bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ nen, bɛtole buralɛ anoa bɔ bɛfa nu bɛkɔ kuro ne anu ne. Anoa ne bɔbɔ bukyele mane bɛ, na bewurale nu befitele. Bɛpɛle nu borɔnoɛ ko aso, na berɛ ne ala, abɔfo ne yakyili ye berɛ.

english_verse: Peter now realized what had happened, and he said, “I am certain that the Lord sent his angel to rescue me from Herod and from everything the Jewish leaders planned to do to me.”
translation_verse: Na Petro nye wale ye nwo so ne, ɔhane kyɛ, “Afei de, manwu kyɛ ɔte nahorɛ kyɛ Awurade asoma ye abɔfo maa waaye me wafi Herode sa nu, ɔne nikyee biala bɔ Yudafoɛ nye la so kyɛ bɛkɔfa bɛkɔyɛ me ɔ nu.”

english_verse: Then Peter went to the house of Mary the mother of John whose other name was Mark. Many of the Lord's followers had come together there and were praying.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Petro nwuni ye sɔ ne, ɔhɔle Yohane bɔ besa bɛfrɛ ye Marko ne ye maame Maria awuro, nekaa bɔ né mmenia pee bayia bɛbɔ mbaeɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Peter knocked on the gate, and a servant named Rhoda came to answer.
translation_verse: Petro bɔle dwaaso anoa ne anu, na abaayaa somvoɛ bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Roda wale kyɛ ɔbaanea sona horɛ.

english_verse: When she heard Peter's voice, she was too excited to open the gate. She ran back into the house and said Peter was standing there.
translation_verse: Ɔtele Petro komvi, na ye fɛɛ bɔ ɔyɛ ye ne ati, wammukye anoa ne, na mmom otuli amirika ɔɔbɔle amaneɛ kyɛ Petro gyi dwaaso anoa ne asi dɔ.

english_verse: “You are crazy!” everyone told her. But she kept saying it was Peter. Then they said, “It must be his angel.”
translation_verse: Na besele abaawa ne kyɛ, “Gyamea nikyee bie yeɛ ɔyɛ wɔ ɔ!” Nakoso ɔhɔle so ɔhane ye anyeborolɛ so kyɛ ɔte nahorɛ. Na bɛhane kyɛ, “Nzaade ye abɔfo ɔ.”

english_verse: But Peter kept on knocking, until finally they opened the gate. They saw him and were completely amazed.
translation_verse: Né Petro gu so ɔ́bɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ. Nziɛ ye bebukyele anoa ne, na benwuni kyɛ ye ahɔ amba ne, bɛ nwo dwirili bɛ.

english_verse: Peter motioned for them to keep quiet. Then he told how the Lord had led him out of jail. He also said, “Tell James and the others what has happened.” After that, he left and went somewhere else.
translation_verse: Ɔfale ye sa nwahane bɛ kyɛ bemua bɛ noa, na ɔhane kyɛbɔ Awurade si yele ye fili kuku nu berɛ ne hyirele bɛ. Na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔhã edwirɛ he behyire Yakobo ne agyidifoɛ ngaa ne.” Na afei ofili berɛ hɔle neka foforɛ.

english_verse: The next morning the soldiers who had been on guard were terribly worried and wondered what had happened to Peter.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, edwirɛ piri tole asraafoɛ nemɔ, ofikyɛ né bɛngora bennwu nikyee bɔ wayɛ Petro ɔ.

english_verse: Herod ordered his own soldiers to search for him, but they could not find him. Then he questioned the guards and had them put to death. After this, Herod left Judea to stay in Caesarea for a while. Herod Dies
translation_verse: Herode hane bɛ so kyɛ bɛpena ye, nakoso bannwu ye. Yiti obisale awɛmvoɛ ne kyɛbɔ osi yɛle bɔ Petro nne berɛ ne, na ɔhyɛle kyɛ behũ bɛ. Ɛhe asi ne, Herode fili Yudea hɔle Kaesarea ɔɔtenane berɛ kãa. Herode Agripa wue

english_verse: Herod and the people of Tyre and Sidon were very angry with each other. But their country got its food supply from the region that he ruled. So a group of them went to see Blastus, who was one of Herod's high officials. They convinced Blastus that they wanted to make peace between their cities and Herod,
translation_verse: Né Herode afɛ Tirofoɛ ne Sidonfoɛ so yaa paa, yiti betuli mmenia kyɛ beenwu ye. Bɛfale bɛ dwirɛ bɛtole Blasto bɔ ɔnea ahemvie berɛ ne nyunu kyɛ ɔboka bɛ na ɔsrɛ ma bɛ, ɔnate kyɛ Herode maen nu yeɛ bɛ maen ne nya ye aleɛ fi ɔ.

english_verse: and a day was set for them to meet with him. Herod came dressed in his royal robes. He sat down on his throne and made a speech.
translation_verse: Betuli kyẽa ko besiele berɛ, na odwuli ne, Herode wurale ye ahemvo ndaadeɛ, ɔɔtenane ye ahennie bia so, na odwudwo hyirele bɛ.

english_verse: The people shouted, “You speak more like a god than a man!”
translation_verse: Na mmenia nemɔ bɛbɔ belele so kyɛ, “Ɛhe de, nyameɛ bie yeɛ odwudwo ne, na nna kuro sona ɔ!”

english_verse: At once an angel from the Lord struck him down because he took the honor that belonged to God. Later, Herod was eaten by worms and died.
translation_verse: Na aworafire nu, Awurade abɔfo ɔɔbɔle ye tole ase, ofikyɛ wamva animnyam wamma Nyameɛ; ɔlɔle nnɔboakoma na owuli.

english_verse: And after Barnabas and Saul had done the work they were sent to do, they went back to Jerusalem with John, whose other name was Mark.
translation_verse: Banaba ne Sɔɔlo yiele bɛ dwumadie ne Yerusalem. Na besa befi Yerusalem bɛkɔ ne, bɛfale Yohane bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Marko ne bɛbokale bɛ nwo so.

english_verse: The church at Antioch had several prophets and teachers. They were Barnabas, Simeon, also called Niger, Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen, who was Herod's close friend, and Saul.
translation_verse: Né ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ ne akyerɛkyerɛfoɛ biemɔ bɛwɔ Antiokia asɔre ne anu. Bɛ ole: Banaba, Simeon , Lukio , Manaen yeɛ Sɔɔlo.

english_verse: While they were worshiping the Lord and going without eating, the Holy Spirit told them, “Appoint Barnabas and Saul to do the work for which I have chosen them.”
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ bɛwɔ so bɛsɔne Awurade na bɛyɔ akɔngyere ne, Sunzum Krongron ne sele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔye Banaba ne Sɔɔlo bɛma me ma bɛɛyɔ adwuma bɔ yiti yeɛ mmvrɛle bɛ ne.”

english_verse: Everyone prayed and went without eating for a while longer. Next, they placed their hands on Barnabas and Saul to show that they had been appointed to do this work. Then everyone sent them on their way. Barnabas and Saul in Cyprus
translation_verse: Bɛyɔle akɔngyere, bɛbɔle mbaeɛ, bɛfale bɛ sa beguale Banaba ne Sɔɔlo so, na beguale bɛ ate. Banaba ne Sɔɔlo kɔ Kipro

english_verse: After Barnabas and Saul had been sent by the Holy Spirit, they went to Seleucia. From there they sailed to the island of Cyprus.
translation_verse: Sunzum Krongron ne somane Banaba ne Sɔɔlo nen, besili nu bɛhɔle Selukia, na bɛfale ɛlɛen befili berɛ bɛhɔle Kipro.

english_verse: They arrived at Salamis and began to preach God's message in the synagogues. They also had John as a helper.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ bedwuli Salami nen, bɛhane Nyameɛ dwirɛ ne wɔ Yudafoɛ nyianu sua nemɔ nu. Né Yohane boka bɛ ɔyɔ somvoɛ adwuma.

english_verse: Barnabas and Saul went all the way to the city of Paphos on the other end of the island, where they met a Jewish man named Bar-Jesus. He practiced witchcraft and was a false prophet.
translation_verse: Bɛpɛle nu supɔ ne aso beedwuli Pafɔso, na benwuni ngonyaayelɛniɛ bie bɔ ɔte Yudaniɛ ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ ngondomboniɛ, bɔ ye dumaa li Bar Yesu ɔ.

english_verse: He also worked for Sergius Paulus, who was very smart and was the governor of the island. Sergius Paulus wanted to hear God's message, and he sent for Barnabas and Saul.
translation_verse: Né sɔ biaa ne te supɔ ne aso amrado badwemaniɛ bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Sɛgio Pɔɔlu n’abiɛngo. Amrado ne somane maa bɛɛfale Banaba ne Sɔɔlo bɛwale berɛ, ɔnate kyɛ né okuro kyɛ otie Nyameɛ dwirɛ ne.

english_verse: But Bar-Jesus, whose other name was Elymas, was against them. He even tried to keep the governor from having faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Nakoso ngonyaayelɛniɛ Elima sili bɛ ate, na ɔbɔle mmɔden kyɛ ɔkɔhwe amrado ne kofi gyidie ne nwo.

english_verse: Then Saul, better known as Paul, was filled with the Holy Spirit. He looked straight at Elymas
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo, bɔ besa bɛfrɛ ye Pɔɔlo, bɔ Sunzum Krongron ayi ye tɛkyɛ ne, ɔneane ngonyaayelɛniɛ ne haa,

english_verse: and said, “You son of the devil! You are a liar, a crook, and an enemy of everything that is right. When will you stop speaking against the true ways of the Lord?
translation_verse: na osele ye kyɛ, “Ɛte abɔnzam sona! Ɛte tenenee mukoraa pɔfoɛ, nnakannaka ne amumuyɛɛ ayi wɔ ti anu tɛkyɛ, aso ɛngɔyakyi kyɛ ɛkɔhyea Awurade tenenee atee ne ɔ?

english_verse: The Lord is going to punish you by making you completely blind for a while.” Suddenly the man's eyes were covered by a dark mist, and he went around trying to get someone to lead him by the hand.
translation_verse: Tie, Awurade kotua wɔ kerɛ kekesaala ye; wɔ nye kosi, na engonwu eyia ko, sana mmerɛ kãa pɛ nu.” Na berɛ ne ala awosii ne ɛborɔ katale Elima nye so maa ofuafuale penane sona bɔ ɔkɔsɔ ye sa kohyire ye atee ɔ.

english_verse: When the governor saw what had happened, he was amazed at this teaching about the Lord. So he put his faith in the Lord. Paul and Barnabas in Antioch of Pisidia
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ amrado ne nwuni bɔ wasi nen, olelili, ɔnate kyɛ Awurade nwo ngyerɛkyerɛ ne yɛle ye nwanwa paa. Pɔɔlo ne Banaba wɔ Pisidia Antiokia

english_verse: Paul and the others left Paphos and sailed to Perga in Pamphylia. But John left them and went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo ne ye mmango nemɔ bɛfale ɛlɛen befili Pafɔso bɛwale Pɛɛga wɔ Pamfilia, na Yohane yakyili bɛ berɛ sa hɔle Yerusalem.

english_verse: The rest of them went on from Perga to Antioch in Pisidia. Then on the Sabbath they went to the synagogue and sat down.
translation_verse: Nakoso bɛ de, befili Pɛɛga, na bɛbɔle hwii bɛwale Antiokia bɔ ɔwɔ Pisidia; na afofikyẽa dwuli nen, bɛhɔ bɛɛtenane ase wɔ nyianu sua nu.

english_verse: After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the leaders sent someone over to tell Paul and Barnabas, “Friends, if you have anything to say that will help the people, please say it.”
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ ebie kengale Mose mmeraa ne ɔne ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ nwomaa ne yiele nen, nyianu sua ne anu mbanyi bisale Pɔɔlo ne Banaba kyɛ, “Aliɛmaa mɔ, sɛ ɛmɔle foɛtulɛ dwirɛ bie bɛma mmenia ne a, ɛmɔhã.”

english_verse: Paul got up. He motioned with his hand and said: People of Israel, and everyone else who worships God, listen!
translation_verse: Yiti Pɔɔlo dwɔso gyinane, ɔmane ye sa so hyirele kyɛ bɛyɛ dinn, na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Aliɛmaa mɔ Yisraelfoɛ ne Amaenmaensofoɛ mukoraa bɔ besuro Nyameɛ ɔ, ɛmɔyɛ asoɛ betie me!

english_verse: The God of Israel chose our ancestors, and he let our people prosper while they were living in Egypt. Then with his mighty power he led them out,
translation_verse: Yisrael Nyameɛ neaneane nu yele yɛ nana mɔ, na ɔyɛle bɛ mmeni titire wɔ mmerɛ bɔ né bɛte amanvrafoɛ wɔ Misraim aseɛ so ne. Nyameɛ nate ye tumi piri so yele bɛ fili Misraim,

english_verse: Make sure what the prophets have said doesn't happen to you. They said,
translation_verse: Yiti ɛ́mɔnea yé ná bɔ bahã ye wɔ ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ nwomaa ne anu ne wamma ɛmɔ so, kyɛ,

english_verse: He destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan and gave their land to our people.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ sɛkyele maen nzoo wɔ Kanaan aseɛ so, na ɔhyɛle b’aseɛ ne mane yɛ nana mɔ kyɛkyɛ.

english_verse: Later, God removed Saul and let David rule in his place. God said about him, “David the son of Jesse is the kind of person who pleases me most! He does everything I want him to do.”
translation_verse: Ɛhe asi ne, Nyameɛ tuli Sɔɔlo fili bia so, na ɔfale Dawide sili bɛ so hene. Na edwirɛ he yeɛ Nyameɛ ha fale ye nwo ɔ: ‘Manwu Yese awa Dawide kyɛ ɔte sona bɔ ɔsɔ me nye, na ye yeɛ ɔkɔyɔ m’apɛdeɛ mukoraa ɔ’

english_verse: God promised that someone from David's family would come to save the people of Israel, and this one is Jesus.
translation_verse: Sɔ biaa he, ye bosofoɛ nu yeɛ Nyameɛ yele Yisrael Ngoadefoɛ Yesu, kyɛbɔ ye bɔhyɛ te ne.

english_verse: But before Jesus came, John was telling everyone in Israel to turn back to God and be baptized.
translation_verse: Na anzana ɔbaahyɛ ye adwuma bo nen, Yohane lili moa hane adwenesakyera asubɔlɛ nwo nzɛmba hyirele Yisrael maen.

english_verse: Then, when John's work was almost done, he said, “Who do you people think I am? Do you think I am the Promised One? He will come later, and I am not good enough to untie his sandals.”
translation_verse: Na Yohane ɔbaayie ye adwuma nen, ɔhane kyɛ, ‘Ɛmɔnea a, nwa ole me? Nna me ole ye oo. Na ɛ́mɔtie, ebie li me si ɔ́ba, bɔ memvata kyɛ mesangye ye gya bo mbaboa nyamaa po ɔ.’

english_verse: Now listen, you descendants of Abraham! Pay attention, all of you Gentiles who are here to worship God! Listen to this message about how to be saved, because it is for everyone.
translation_verse: “Aliɛmaa mɔ, Abraham bosofoɛ ne Amaenmaensofoɛ mukoraa bɔ besuro Nyameɛ ɔ, yɛ berɛ yeɛ Nyameɛ somane ngoalelɛ dwirɛ ne ɔ.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem and their leaders didn't realize who Jesus was. And they didn't understand the words of the prophets they read each Sabbath. So they condemned Jesus just as the prophets had said.
translation_verse: Na ɔnate kyɛ bɛ bɔ bɛwɔ Yerusalem ne bɛ mbanyi mɔ bammu Yesu kyɛ ye ole Ngoadefoɛ ne, ná afei ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ dwirɛ bɔ bɛkenga ye afofikyẽa biala ne bande ye bo ne ati, bebuale ye ewue foɛ mane edwirɛ nemɔ wale nu.

english_verse: But God raised him from death!
translation_verse: Nakoso Nyameɛ tingyele ye fili awufoɛ nu,

english_verse: Then for many days Jesus appeared to his followers who had gone with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. Now they are telling our people about him.
translation_verse: na ɔfale ngyẽa pee yele ye nwo ali hyirele bɛ bɔ bɛne ye fili Galilea bɛwale Yerusalem ne. Na sɔ mmenia ne te ye adanzefoɛ ma Yisraelfoɛ.

english_verse: God made a promise to our ancestors. And we are here to tell you the good news
translation_verse: Na yɛ de, nzɛmba ne yeɛ yɛfa yɛbrɛ ɛmɔ ɔ,

english_verse: that he has kept this promise to us. It is just as the second Psalm says about Jesus, “You are my son because today I have become your Father.”
translation_verse: kyɛ anohoba bɔ Nyameɛ bɔle yɛ nana mɔ ne, ɔnate Yesu bɔ otingyele ye ne aso wamaa wawa nu wama yɛ mɔ bɔ yɛte bɛ bosofoɛ ne, kyɛbɔ bahyerɛ ye wɔ Edwein bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ ne anu kyɛ, ‘Ɛte Mma; ɛnɛ mayɛ wɔ Baba.’

english_verse: God raised Jesus from death and will never let his body decay. It is just as God said, “I will make to you the same holy promises that I made to David.”
translation_verse: Na ye tingyelɛ bɔ otingyele ye fili awufoɛ nu, bɔ ongosa ngɔhɔ porɔlowaa tebea nu ko ne, bɔ ɔhã fale ye nwo ɛhe: ‘Ngɔfa Dawide saleɛ krongron bɔ onni ngasi ne ngɔma ɛmɔ.’

english_verse: And in another psalm it says, “God will never let the body of his Holy One decay.”
translation_verse: Yiti osa kã ye Edwein foforɛ nu kyɛ, ‘Ɛngɔma wɔ Krongronniɛ ne ngɔhɔ porɔlowaa tebea nu.’

english_verse: When David was alive, he obeyed God. Then after he died, he was buried in the family grave, and his body decayed.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ, Dawide de, ɔsole Nyameɛ wɔ ye aberɛ so yiele nen, ɔlale, na besiele ye wɔ nekaa bɔ ye nana mɔ la ɔ, na ɔporɔle kumaa nu.

english_verse: But God raised Jesus from death, and his body did not decay.
translation_verse: Nakoso bɔ Nyameɛ tingyele ye fili ewue nu ne de wamborɔ.

english_verse: My friends, the message is that Jesus can forgive your sins! The Law of Moses could not set you free from all your sins.
translation_verse: Ɔnate sɔ ne ati, aliɛmaa mɔ, yɛma ɛmɔnwu ye kyɛ ɔnate Yesu so yeɛ bɛbɔ bɔnefakyɛ dwirɛ ne dawure bekyire ɛmɔ ye;

english_verse: “Look, you people who make fun of God! Be amazed and disappear. I will do something today that you won't believe, even if someone tells you about it!”
translation_verse: ‘Ɛmɔtie, ɛmɔ, ngorohoɛfoɛ, ɛ́mɔma ɔ́yɛ ɛmɔ nwanwa ná ɛ́mɔtu bemini; ɔnate kyɛ méyɔ adwuma bie wɔ ɛmɔ aberɛ so, adwuma bɔ sɛ ebie kã kyire ɛmɔ po a, ɛmɔngole bengoli ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people begged them to say more about these same things on the next Sabbath.
translation_verse: Na bɛyɛle kyɛ befi nyianu sua ne anu berɛ bɛkɔ nen, mmenia ne srɛle kyɛ bɛbra afofikyẽa bieku bɛɛhã sɔ dwirɛ nemɔ behyire bɛ bieku.

english_verse: After the service, many Jews and a lot of Gentiles who worshiped God went with them. Paul and Barnabas begged them all to remain faithful to God, who had treated them with undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Na mmenia bɔ bɛwɔ nyianu sua ne anu ne, bɛpɔnone ná bɛpakyepakyele nu ne, Yudafoɛ pee ne Amaenmaensofoɛ pee bɔ basɔ Yudasom nu ɔ belili Pɔɔlo ne Banaba si; na asuafoɛ nyɔ ne tuli bɛ foɛ kyɛ bɛhɔ so bɛfa bɛ nwo bɛto Nyameɛ adom ne aso.

english_verse: The next Sabbath almost everyone in town came to hear the message about the Lord.
translation_verse: Na afofikyẽa bieku dwuli ne, kurotue ne amukoraa bɛwale nyianu sua nu berɛ maa ɔhale mmenia kãa bie kyɛ bɛbaatie Nyameɛ dwirɛ ne.

english_verse: When the Jewish people saw the crowds, they were very jealous. They insulted Paul and spoke against everything he said.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Yudafoɛ nemɔ nwuni ɛlɔen ne nen, ɔyɛle bɛ anyeboro, yiti bɛne Pɔɔlo suli edwirɛ bɔ né ɔkã ne nwo aporowaa, na bɛpepɛle ye nzoaa.

english_verse: But Paul and Barnabas bravely said: We had to tell God's message to you before we told it to anyone else. But you rejected the message! This proves that you don't deserve eternal life. Now we are going to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo ne Banaba sili b’ahone besele kyɛ, “Né ohia kyɛ ɛmɔ, Yudafoɛ yeɛ yɛdi moa yɛkã Nyameɛ dwirɛ ne yɛkyire ɛmɔ ɔ. Nakoso ɔnate kyɛ ɛmɔpo edwirɛ ne, ná ɛmɔmmu bɛ nwo kyɛ ɛmɔfata daa ngoa ne ati, ɛ́mɔtie, yɛkɔyakyi yɛkɔhɔ Amaenmaensofoɛ mɔ berɛ.

english_verse: The Lord has given us this command, “I have placed you here as a light for the Gentiles. You are to take the saving power of God to people everywhere on earth.”
translation_verse: Ɔnate kyɛ ahyɛdeɛ bɔ Awurade afa ama yɛ hɔ ɛhe: ‘Mafa wɔ mayɛ kanea mama Amaenmaensofoɛ, amaa afa ngoalelɛ ahɔ aseɛ so nekaa biala.’ ”

english_verse: This message made the Gentiles glad, and they praised what they had heard about the Lord. Everyone who had been chosen for eternal life then put their faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Amaenmaensofoɛ nemɔ bɛtele sɔ dwirɛ nen, ɔyɛle bɛ fɛ, na bɛhyɛle Awurade dwirɛ ne animnyam. Na bɛ bɔ baneanea nu baye bɛ kyɛ benya daa ngoa ne, bele belili.

english_verse: The message about the Lord spread all over this region.
translation_verse: Awurade dwirɛ ne trɛle wɔ manzini ne anu amukoraa.

english_verse: But the Jewish leaders went to some of the important men in the town and to some respected women who were religious. They turned them against Paul and Barnabas and started making trouble for them. They even chased them out of this part of the country.
translation_verse: Nakoso mmrasua nyamesurofoɛ bɔ bɛ sa nu le bie, bɛne mmienzua atitire bɔ bɛwɔ kuro ne anu ne, Yudafoɛ nemɔ to guale bɛ so anu, na bɛmane mmenia tuli bɛ nye besiele Pɔɔlo ne Banaba so, na bɛfoane bɛ befili bɛ mbɔtam berɛ.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas shook the dust from that place off their feet and went on to the city of Iconium.
translation_verse: Na asomafoɛ nyɔ ne poroporole bɛ gya kunu mvuture beguale berɛ betiale bɛ, na besili nu bɛhɔle Yikoniom.

english_verse: But the Lord's followers in Antioch were very happy and were filled with the Holy Spirit.
translation_verse: Na asuafoɛ nemɔ de, bɛ nye gyele paa, na Sunzum Krongron yili bɛ tɛkyɛ.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas spoke in the synagogue in Iconium, just as they had done at Antioch, and many Jews and Gentiles put their faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Na ɔwale kyɛ Yikoniom koso, bɛ munyɔ bɛhɔle Yudafoɛ nyianu sua nu, na kyɛbɔ besi bedwudwole ne, ɔmane Yudafoɛ ne Helafoɛ pee bele belili.

english_verse: But the Jews who did not have faith in him made the other Gentiles angry and turned them against the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yudafoɛ bɔ banne dwirɛ ne banni ne, bɛsɛkyele Amaenmaensofoɛ nemɔ adwene, na bɛmaa benyane aliɛmaa nemɔ nwo adwene tɛɛ.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas stayed there for a while, having faith in the Lord and bravely speaking his message. The Lord gave them the power to work miracles and wonders, and he showed that their message about his gift of undeserved grace was true.
translation_verse: Nakoso bɛtenane berɛ bɛhyɛle; besili b’ahone bedwudwole wɔ Awurade nu, na ye koso olili ye adom dwirɛ ne nwo adanzeɛ, na ɔfale bɛ so yɔle nzɛngyerɛnneɛ ne anwanwadeɛ.

english_verse: The people of Iconium did not know what to think. Some of them believed the Jewish group, and others believed the apostles.
translation_verse: Nakoso kuro berɛ ama nu hyɛle nyɔ; bue ko gyi Yudafoɛ nemɔ si, yeɛ bue ko koso gyi asomafoɛ nemɔ si.

english_verse: Finally, some Gentiles and Jews, together with their leaders, decided to make trouble for Paul and Barnabas and to stone them to death.
translation_verse: Nziɛ ye, Helafoɛ ne Yudafoɛ biemɔ ne bɛ mbanyi mɔ yɛle adwene kyɛ bɛkɔhyɛ Pɔɔlo ne Banaba anyeborolɛ na baboro bɛ nyɔboɛ.

english_verse: In Lystra there was a man who had been born with paralyzed feet and had never been able to walk.
translation_verse: Né biaa bie wɔ Lisetra, opofo aseɛnwo, bɔ ɔngora ngyina ye gya so ɔ. Bɛwole ye bubuaniɛ, na né ɔnnatele le.

english_verse: The man was listening to Paul speak, when Paul saw that he had faith in Jesus and could be healed. So he looked straight at the man
translation_verse: Né otie edwirɛ bɔ Pɔɔlo ɔkã ne; na Pɔɔlo neane ye haa, na onwuni kyɛ biaa ne le gyidie kyɛ okonya ayaresa ɔ.

english_verse: and shouted, “Stand up!” The man jumped up and started walking around.
translation_verse: Yiti ɔteane nu sele ye kyɛ, “Dwɔso gyina wɔ gya so fɔngɔnn!” Na ohuru gyinane, na ɔnatele.

english_verse: When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they yelled out in the language of Lycaonia, “The gods have turned into humans and have come down to us!”
translation_verse: Na ɛlɔen ne nwuni nikyee bɔ Pɔɔlo ayɔ nen, bɛteateane nu wɔ Likaonia dwudwolɛ nu kyɛ, “Mmosoen nemɔ bayeyɛ bɛ nwo kyɛ mmenia badwu bawa yɛ wa!”

english_verse: The people then gave Barnabas the name Zeus, and they gave Paul the name Hermes, because he did the talking.
translation_verse: Yiti bɛfrɛle Banaba Seuse, yeɛ Pɔɔlo koso bɛfrɛle ye Hɛme, ɔnate kyɛ né Pɔɔlo yeɛ odwudwo ma bɛ ɔ.

english_verse: The temple of Zeus was near the entrance to the city. Its priest and the crowds wanted to offer a sacrifice to Barnabas and Paul. So the priest brought some bulls and flowers to the city gates.
translation_verse: Na bosoen Seuse bɔ ye asɔneyɛɛ sua wɔ kuro ne tiwaa ne, ye kɔmeɛ fale nandwie ne flawase wale kuro berɛ pambim ne anwo, na ɔyɛle kyɛ ɔne ɛlɔen ne bɛbaafa bɛbɔ afɔleɛ.

english_verse: When the two apostles found out about this, they tore their clothes in horror and ran to the crowd, shouting:
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Banaba ne Pɔɔlo tele sɔ dwirɛ nen, besunzuale bɛ ndaadeɛ nu; betuli amirika bɛhɔle mmenia ne anu, na bɛteateane nu kyɛ,

english_verse: Why are you doing this? We are humans just like you. Please give up all this foolishness. Turn to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
translation_verse: “Biamɔ, nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔyɔ sɔ ye? Yɛ koso yɛte mmenia kyɛ ɛmɔ ala! Yɛwale kyɛ yɛbaabɔ nzɛmba ne dawure yɛkyire ɛmɔ, kyɛ ɛ́mɔhwe ɛmɔ nwo befi sɔ nningyein mbaen mbaen hemɔ nwo, ná ɛ́mɔfa ɛmɔ nwo bɛma Nyameɛ teasefoɛ bɔ ɔbɔle nyameɛso ne aseɛ ne ɛpo ne bɔ ɔwɔ bɛ nu amukoraa ne.

english_verse: In times past, God let each nation go its own way.
translation_verse: Daa tete mmerɛ bɔ wapɛ nu ne de, ɔmane maen maen amukoraa ate maa bɛyɔle bɔ bekuro ɔ,

english_verse: But he showed he was there by the good things he did. God sends rain from heaven and makes your crops grow. He gives food to you and makes your hearts glad.
translation_verse: nakoso wanyakyi ye nwo adanzeɛlilɛ, ofikyɛ ɔyɛle paa, na ɔmane yɛ nzue fili nyameɛso, ɔne mmerɛ bɔ aleɛ ba ɔ, ɔmane ɛmɔ aleɛ, na ɔmaa yɛnya aleɛ ne anigye ma yɛ kunu dwo yɛ fɔnn.”

english_verse: Even after Paul and Barnabas had said all this, they could hardly keep the people from offering a sacrifice to them.
translation_verse: Na edwirɛ bɔ bɛhane ne mukoraa asi ne po, bɛhã bɛfɛle paa koraka yeɛ bɛkora bɛma mmenia ne yakyi afɔleɛ bɔ ahaa bɛbaabɔ bɛma bɛ ne ɔ. Bɛborole Pɔɔlo nyɔboɛ

english_verse: Some Jewish leaders from Antioch and Iconium came and turned the crowds against Paul. They hit him with stones and dragged him out of the city, thinking he was dead.
translation_verse: Na Yudafoɛ biemɔ fili Antiokia ne Yikoniom bɛwale berɛ; betuli mmenia ne foɛ tɛɛ, na bɛborole Pɔɔlo nyɔboɛ bɛhwene ye befili kuro ne anu; né besusuli kyɛ wawu.

english_verse: But when the Lord's followers gathered around Paul, he stood up and went back into the city. The next day he and Barnabas went to Derbe. Paul and Barnabas Return to Antioch in Syria
translation_verse: Nakoso mmerɛ bɔ asuafoɛ nemɔ pɛle ye nwo yiale ne, odwɔsole, na osa hɔle kuro ne anu. Na aleɛ hyene ne, ɔne Banaba befili berɛ bɛhɔle Dɛɛbi. Pɔɔlo ne Banaba sa kɔ Antiokia

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas preached the good news in Derbe and won some people to the Lord. Then they went back to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch in Pisidia.
translation_verse: Na bɛhane nzɛmba ne behyirele kuro berɛ ama, ná benyane asuafoɛ pee nen, afei besa bɛhɔle Lisetra, Yikoniom ne Antiokia,

english_verse: They encouraged the followers and begged them to remain faithful. They told them, “We have to suffer a lot before we can get into God's kingdom.”
translation_verse: na bɛhyɛle asuafoɛ nemɔ kra nguraen, betuli bɛ foɛ kyɛ bɛhɔ so begyina pindinn wɔ gyidie ne anu, na bɛhane kyɛ, ɔsɛ kyɛ yɛfa amaneɛnwunɛ pee nu yɛkɔ Nyameɛ ahennie nu.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas chose some leaders for each of the churches. Then they went without eating and prayed that the Lord would take good care of these leaders who had trusted in the Lord.
translation_verse: Na besili asɔre biala nu mbanyi bɛmane bɛ, na bɛfale mbaeɛbɔlɛ ne akɔngyere betuli bɛ bewurale Awurade bɔ bale ye bali ne sa.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas went on through Pisidia to Pamphylia,
translation_verse: Afei bɛɛpɛle nu Pisidia bɛwale Pamfilia.

english_verse: where they preached in the town of Perga. Then they went down to Attalia
translation_verse: Na bɛhane nzɛmba ne wɔ Pɛɛga nen, bɛtoale so bɛhɔle Atalia.

english_verse: and sailed to Antioch in Syria. It was there that they had been placed in God's care for the work they had now completed.
translation_verse: Na befili berɛ bɛfale ɛlɛen bɛwale Antiokia, nekaa bɔ bɛfale bɛ bewurale Nyameɛ adom ne sa bɛmane adwuma bɔ bayɔ bayie ne.

english_verse: After arriving in Antioch, they called the church together. They told the people what God had helped them do and how he had made it possible for the Gentiles to believe.
translation_verse: Beedwuli berɛ ne, bɛmane asɔre mma ne yiale, na bɛhane nikyee biala bɔ Nyameɛ afa bɛ so wayɔ ɔ behyirele bɛ, ɔne kyɛbɔ wasi wabukye gyidie anoa wama Amaenmaensofoɛ koso ɔ.

english_verse: Then they stayed there with the followers for a long time.
translation_verse: Na bɛne asuafoɛ nemɔ bɛtenane berɛ bɛhyɛle.

english_verse: Some people came from Judea and started teaching the Lord's followers that they could not be saved, unless they were circumcised as Moses had taught.
translation_verse: Mmenia biemɔ fili Yudea bɛwale Antiokia bɛɛyɛle ngyerɛkyerɛ behyirele agyidifoɛ ne kyɛ, “Sɛ ɛmɔambɛ ɛmɔ bienzua kyɛbɔ Mose amanneɛ ne te ne a, ɛmɔngɔhora ngonya daa ngoa.”

english_verse: This caused trouble, and Paul and Barnabas argued with them about this teaching. So it was decided to send Paul and Barnabas and a few others to Jerusalem to discuss this problem with the apostles and the church leaders. The Church Leaders Meet in Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ɛhe mane Pɔɔlo ne Banaba bɛne mmenia nemɔ benyane dwudwolɛ besuli aporowaa serɛserɛ wɔ sɔ dwirɛ he anwo. Yiti betuli mmenia kyɛ bɛboka Pɔɔlo ne Banaba so bɛhɔ Yerusalem beenwu asomafoɛ nemɔ ne mbanyi mɔ wɔ sɔ dwirɛ he anwo.

english_verse: The men who were sent by the church went through Phoenicia and Samaria, telling how the Gentiles had turned to God. This news made the Lord's followers very happy.
translation_verse: Antiokia asɔremma ne guale bɛ ate; na bɛkɔ nen, bɛfale Fonikia ne Samaria bɛhane kyɛbɔ Amaenmaensofoɛ asi afa bɛ nwo ama Nyameɛ, na edwirɛ he mane agyidifoɛ ne amukoraa bɛ nye gyele paa.

english_verse: When the men arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church, including the apostles and the leaders. They told them everything God had helped them do.
translation_verse: Na bedwuli Yerusalem nen, asɔre ne ne asomafoɛ nemɔ ne mbanyi nemɔ bɛyɛle bɛ awaawaatuu; na bɛhane bɔ Nyameɛ afa bɛ sɔ wayɔ amukoraa behyirele bɛ.

english_verse: But some Pharisees had become followers of the Lord. They stood up and said, “Gentiles who have faith in the Lord must be circumcised and told to obey the Law of Moses.”
translation_verse: Nakoso agyidifoɛ biemɔ bɔ befi Farasiifoɛ fekue ne anu bedwɔso begyinane, na bɛhane kyɛ, “Ɔsɛ kyɛ Amaenmaensofoɛ bɛpɛ bɛ bienzua, ná bɛhyɛ bɛ maa bedi Mose mmeraa ne aso.”

english_verse: The apostles and church leaders met to discuss this problem about Gentiles.
translation_verse: Na asomafoɛ nemɔ ne mbanyi nemɔ beyiale nu bɛfale edwirɛ he nwo adwene.

english_verse: They had talked it over for a long time, when Peter got up and said: My friends, you know that God decided long ago to let me be the one from your group to preach the good news to the Gentiles. God did this so they would hear and obey him.
translation_verse: Bɛkekane ye nwo bie dee, na Petro dwɔso sele bɛ kyɛ, “Aliɛmaa mɔ, ɛmɔse kyɛ mmerɛ bie bɔ wapɛ nu wahɔ ɔ, Nyameɛ neaneane nu yele me fili ɛmɔ nu, kyɛ nga nzɛmba ne ngyire Amaenmaensofoɛ maa bɛ koso bɛte dwirɛ ne na bele beli.

english_verse: He knows what is in everyone's heart. And he showed he had chosen the Gentiles, when he gave them the Holy Spirit, just as he had given his Spirit to us.
translation_verse: Na Nyameɛ bɔ ɔse angorangora biala ti anu adwene ne lili bɛ adanzeɛ, na ɔmane bɛ Sunzum Krongron ne kyɛbɔ ɔfa mane yɛ ne ala.

english_verse: God treated them in the same way that he treated us. They put their faith in him, and he made their hearts pure.
translation_verse: Wangyire kyɛ nzonzoleɛ biala wɔ yɛ ne bɛ nu, na mmom ɔnate gyidie so fale bɛ bɔne hyɛle bɛ.

english_verse: Now why are you trying to make God angry by placing a heavy burden on these followers? This burden was too heavy for us or our ancestors.
translation_verse: Na afei, nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔso Nyameɛ bɛnea na bɛfa nningyein bɔ yɛ ne yɛ nana mɔ yangora ye soa bɛsoa agyidifoɛ ne ɔ?

english_verse: But we believe that we will be saved by the gift of undeserved grace from our Lord Jesus Christ, just as the Gentiles are.
translation_verse: Na kyɛbɔ yɛde yɛdi kyɛ ɔnate Awurade Yesu adom so yɛkonya daa ngoa nen, sɔ ala koso yeɛ bɛ deɛ te ɔ.”

english_verse: Everyone kept quiet and listened as Barnabas and Paul told how God had given them the power to work a lot of miracles and wonders for the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Mmenia ne amukoraa bɛyɛle dinn, na betiele Banaba ne Pɔɔlo wɔ b’amaneɛ bɔ ɔfa nzɛngyerɛnneɛ ne anwanwadeɛ amukoraa bɔ Nyameɛ afa bɛ so wayɔ wɔ Amaenmaensofoɛ nu ne.

english_verse: After they had finished speaking, James said: My friends, listen to me!
translation_verse: Bɛ noa pene ne, Yakobo buale kyɛ, “Aliɛmaa mɔ, ɛmɔyɛ asoɛ betie me!

english_verse: Simon Peter has told how God first came to the Gentiles and made some of them his own people.
translation_verse: Simɔn aha kyɛbɔ osi yɛle bɔ Nyameɛ ɔɔneaneane Amaenmaensofoɛ nu yele mmenia bie fili bɛ nu kyɛ bɛyɛ ye deɛ bɔkɔɔ ɔ.

english_verse: This agrees with what the prophets wrote,
translation_verse: Na ɛhe ne ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ dwirɛ bɔ bɛhane ne te ko, kyɛbɔ bahyerɛ kyɛ,

english_verse: “I, the Lord, will return and rebuild David's fallen house. I will build it from its ruins and set it up again.
translation_verse: ‘Ɛhe asi ne, ngosa ngɔwa na mama Dawide ahennie bɔ ɔtɔle ase ne so bieku. Ngosi bɔ wabubu ne bieku ná mama so bieku;

english_verse: Then other nations will turn to me and be my chosen ones. I, the Lord, say this.
translation_verse: amaa ɔnate so mmenia bɔ baha ne, yeɛ Amaenmaensofoɛ bɔ mafrɛ bɛ kyɛ bɛyɛ me deɛ ne, bapena Awurade si atee.

english_verse: And so, my friends, I don't think we should place burdens on the Gentiles who are turning to God.
translation_verse: Na Yakobo toale so hane kyɛ, “Me de, mesusu kyɛ, ɔnzɛ kyɛ yɛha Amaenmaensofoɛ bɔ bafa bɛ nwo bama Nyameɛ nen.

english_verse: We should simply write and tell them not to eat anything that has been offered to idols. They should be told not to eat the meat of any animal that has been strangled or that still has blood in it. They must also not commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: Na mmom odi kyɛ yɛkyerɛ krataa yɛkɔma bɛ, kyɛ, onni kyɛ bedi aleɛ biala bɔ bafa babɔ afɔleɛ bama bosoen, bɛhwe bɛ nwo befi adwamanbɔlɛ nwo; yeɛ afei onni kyɛ bedi kaka biala bɔ wawu ye mogya nu, anaakyɛ mogya.

english_verse: We must remember that the Law of Moses has been preached in city after city for many years, and every Sabbath it is read in our synagogues. A Letter to Gentiles Who Had Faith in the Lord
translation_verse: Ɔnate kyɛ ofi tete yeɛ mmenia bɔ Mose mmeraa ne dawure wɔ nguro mukoraa so ɔ, na bɛkenga ye afofikyẽa biala wɔ nyianu sua nemɔ nu.” Bɛfa krataa bɔkɔma Antiokia asɔre ne

english_verse: The apostles, the leaders, and all the church members decided to send some men to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Silas and Judas Barsabbas, who were two leaders of the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Afei asomafoɛ ne, mbanyi nemɔ ne asɔremma ne amukoraa bɛyɛle adwene kyɛ bɛkɔye bɛ nu bie na basoma bɛ maa baboka Pɔɔlo ne Banaba so bahɔ Antiokia. Yiti betuli mmenia nyɔ: Yudase bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Basaba, ɔne Silase bɔ bebu bɛ wɔ agyidifoɛ nemɔ anu kyɛ bɛne bɛ hɔ,

english_verse: They wrote a letter that said: We apostles and leaders send friendly greetings to all of you Gentiles who are followers of the Lord in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.
translation_verse: na bɛhyerɛle krataa he bɛfa bɛsomane bɛ: “Yɛ asomafoɛ ne asɔre mbanyi mɔ, bɔ yɛte ɛmɔ aliɛma mɔ, yɛbisa y’eliɛma mɔ Amaenmaensofoɛ bɔ bɛwɔ Antiokia, Siria ne Kilikia ahye.

english_verse: We have heard that some people from here have terribly upset you by what they said. But we did not send them!
translation_verse: Yate kyɛ yɛ nu biemɔ bɔ nna yɛ yeɛ yɛsomane bɛ ɔ bawa ɛmɔ berɛ baahã edwirɛ bafa babiri ɛmɔ nye so bama ɛmɔ adwene ayɛ ɛmɔ naa.

english_verse: So we met together and decided to choose some men and to send them to you along with our good friends Barnabas and Paul.
translation_verse: Sɔ ne ati, wawa kyɛ yɛ mukoraa yahã yɛ ti yapura, na yatu mmenia kyɛ bɛne yɛ dɔfo Banaba Pɔɔlo,

english_verse: These men have risked their lives for our Lord Jesus Christ.
translation_verse: bɔ y’Awurade Yesu Kristo dumaa nu ti bafa bɛ ngoa babɔ afɔleɛ ne, kyɛ bɛbra ɛmɔ berɛ.

english_verse: We are also sending Judas and Silas, who will tell you in person the same things that we are writing.
translation_verse: Yiti yasoma Yudase ne Silase, na bɛ bɔbɔ bɛkɔhã edwirɛ biala bɔ ɔwɔ krataa ne anu bekohyire ɛmɔ.

english_verse: The Holy Spirit has shown us that we should not place any extra burden on you.
translation_verse: Na Sunzum Krongron ne yɛ yale yato nu kyɛ, ɔnzɛ kyɛ yɛfa adesoa biala ko yɛsoa ɛmɔ; sana sɔ nningyein hemɔ bɔ bɛ nwo hia ye:

english_verse: But you should not eat anything offered to idols. You should not eat any meat that still has the blood in it or any meat of any animal that has been strangled. You must also not commit any terrible sexual sins. If you follow these instructions, you will do well. We send our best wishes.
translation_verse: Nnɛma ɛmɔdi aleɛ biala bɔ bafa babɔ afɔleɛ bama bosoen; nnɛma ɛmɔdi mogya; nnɛma ɛmɔdi kaka biala bɔ wawu ye mogya nu; yeɛ afei ɛmɔhwe bɛ nwo befi adwamanbɔlɛ nwo. Na sɛ ɛmɔtwe bɛ nwo befi ɛhemɔ nwo a, ɔte paa. Yɛbisa bɛ.”

english_verse: The four men left Jerusalem and went to Antioch. Then they called the church members together and gave them the letter.
translation_verse: Bɛyakyili ɛbɔfoɛ nemɔ ate, na bedwuli Antiokia nen, bɛmane asɔremma ne amukoraa beyiale, na bɛfale krataa ne bɛmane bɛ.

english_verse: When the letter was read, everyone was pleased and greatly encouraged.
translation_verse: Na agyidifoɛ nemɔ kengale krataa ne nen, bɛ nye gyele, ɔnate kyɛ benyane aworakyekyerɛ befili nu.

english_verse: Judas and Silas were prophets, and they spoke a long time, encouraging and helping the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Na Yudase ne Silase bɔ bɛ koso bɛte ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ ne, bɛfale edwirɛ bɛtole dwirɛ nwo betuli bɛ foɛ maa benyane anwoserɛ.

english_verse: The men from Jerusalem stayed on in Antioch for a while. And when they left to return to the ones who had sent them, the followers wished them well.
translation_verse: Bɛhyɛle Antiokia berɛ kãa, na agyidifoɛ nemɔ yakyili bɛ ate asomdwee nu maa besa bɛhɔle bɛ bɔ bɛsomane bɛ ne berɛ. [

english_verse: But Paul and Barnabas stayed on in Antioch, where they and many others taught and preached about the Lord. Paul and Barnabas Go Their Separate Ways
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo ne Banaba tenane Antiokia hyɛle kãa; bɛ ne mmeni pee yɛle ngyerɛkyerɛ, na bɛhane Awurade nzɛmba ne. Pɔɔlo ne Banaba afia tetele

english_verse: Sometime later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let's go back and visit the Lord's followers in the cities where we preached his message. Then we will know how they are doing.”
translation_verse: Ngyẽa kãa asi ne, Pɔɔlo sele Banaba kyɛ, “Maa yɛsa yɛɛsra aliɛmaa mɔ bɔ bɛwɔ kuro biala bɔ yɛhane Awurade dwirɛ ne wɔ so ne, na yɛnea kyɛbɔ bɛ nwo si te ɔ.”

english_verse: Barnabas wanted to take along John, whose other name was Mark.
translation_verse: Né Banaba pena kyɛ bɛfa Yohane, bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Marko bɛboka bɛ nwo so,

english_verse: But Paul did not want to, because Mark had left them in Pamphylia and had stopped working with them.
translation_verse: nakoso Pɔɔlo susuli kyɛ ye nwo nhia kyɛ bɛkɔfa ye bɛkɔhɔ bie ɔ, ɔnate kyɛ ɔyakyili bɛ nu wɔ Pamfilia; na ɔne bɛ angɔanyɔ asɛmbatrɛ adwuma ne.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas argued, then each of them went his own way. Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus,
translation_verse: Na ɛhe nwo aporowaasulɛ yɛle kyengye paa mane bɛ munyɔ b’afia tetele: Banaba fale Yohane Marko bokale ye nwo so, na ɔne ye fale ɛlɛen hɔle Kipro,

english_verse: but Paul took Silas and left after the followers had placed them in God's care.
translation_verse: nakoso Pɔɔlo de, ɔfale Silase bokale ye nwo so. Agyidifoɛ ne fale Pɔɔlo wurale Awurade adom ne sa, na osili nu hɔle.

english_verse: They traveled through Syria and Cilicia, encouraging the churches.
translation_verse: Ɔɔpɛle nu wɔ Siria ne Kilikia na ɔhyɛle asɔremma nemɔ nguraen.

english_verse: Paul and Silas went back to Derbe and Lystra, where there was a follower named Timothy. His mother was also a follower. She was Jewish, and his father was Greek.
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo hɔle oodwuli Dɛɛbi ne Lisetra. Né gyidiniɛ bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Timoteo wɔ berɛ. Ye maame te Yudaniɛ gyidiniɛ, yeɛ ye baba koso te Helaniɛ.

english_verse: The Lord's followers in Lystra and Iconium said good things about Timothy,
translation_verse: Né agyidifoɛ amukoraa bɔ bɛwɔ Lisetra ne Yikoniom ɔ bedi Timoteo nwo adanzeɛ.

english_verse: and Paul wanted him to go with them. But Paul first had him circumcised, because all the Jewish people around there knew that Timothy's father was Greek.
translation_verse: Né Pɔɔlo kuro kyɛ ɔfa Timoteo boka ye nwo so ɔne ye bɛkɔ, yiti ɔpɛle ye bienzua, ɔnate kyɛ né Yudafoɛ bɔ bɛwɔ porɛ ne anu berɛ mukoraa se kyɛ ye baba te Helaniɛ.

english_verse: As Paul and the others went from city to city, they told the followers what the apostles and leaders in Jerusalem had decided, and they urged them to follow these instructions.
translation_verse: B’aporɔ bɔ bɛbɔle wɔ nguro nemɔ so ne, bɛfale asomafoɛ nemɔ ne Yerusalem mbanyi nemɔ nhyehyɛleɛ bɔ bɛnwa agyidifoɛ ne li so ne bɛtole bɛ nyunu.

english_verse: The churches became stronger in their faith, and each day more people put their faith in the Lord. Paul's Vision in Troas
translation_verse: Ɛhe mane asɔre nemɔ nyane anwoserɛ wɔ gyidie nu, na mmeni pee bokale bɛ so daa biala. Pɔɔlo nya nyekyire wɔ Troase

english_verse: Paul and his friends went through Phrygia and Galatia, but the Holy Spirit would not let them preach in Asia.
translation_verse: Bɛpɛle nu Frigyea ne Galatia aseɛ so, ofikyɛ Sunzum Krongron ne amma bɛ ate ma banga nzɛmba ne wɔ Asia mbɔtam.

english_verse: After they arrived in Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not let them.
translation_verse: Na bedwuli Misia manzini ndendeneɛ so ne, bɛyɛle kyɛ bɛkɔ Bitinia, nakoso Yesu Sunzum ne amma bɛ ate.

english_verse: So they went on through Mysia until they came to Troas.
translation_verse: Yiti besane Misia nwo bɛwale Troase.

english_verse: During the night, Paul had a vision of someone from Macedonia who was standing there and begging him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us!”
translation_verse: Sɔ kyẽa ne kɔngɔen, Pɔɔlo nyane nyekyire, na onwuni biaa bie bɔ ofi Makedonia kyɛ ogyi berɛ ná ɔpa ye kyerɛ kyɛ, “Bra Makedonia baaboka yɛ!”

english_verse: After Paul had seen the vision, we began looking for a way to go to Macedonia. We were sure that God had called us to preach the good news there. Lydia Becomes a Follower of the Lord
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Pɔɔlo nyane nyekyire ne pɛ, yɛboaboale yɛ nwo kyɛ yɛkɔ Makedonia, ofikyɛ yɛnyane adwene kyɛ amba Nyameɛ afrɛ yɛ kyɛ yɛɛbɔ nzɛmba ne dawure yɛhyire bɛ. Lidia yɛle gyidiniɛ wɔ Filipi

english_verse: We sailed straight from Troas to Samothrace, and the next day we arrived in Neapolis.
translation_verse: Yɛfale ɛlɛen yɛfili Troase na yɛhɔle yɛ nyunu ndendeneɛ so yɛɛdwuli supɔ Samotrake so. Na aleɛ hyene ne, yɛhɔle Neapoli.

english_verse: From there we went to Philippi, which is a Roman colony in the first district of Macedonia. We spent several days in Philippi.
translation_verse: Na yɛfili berɛ yɛhɔle Roman manzini Makedonia kuro piri Filipi so. Na yɛlili ngyẽa kãa wɔ sɔ kuro ne aso.

english_verse: Then on the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to a place by the river, where we thought there would be a Jewish meeting place for prayer. We sat down and talked with the women who came.
translation_verse: Afofikyẽa dwuli ne, yɛfili kuro berɛ yɛhɔle asue bie noa nekaa bie bɔ yɛsusuli kyɛ ɔyɛ a beyia bɛbɔ mbaeɛ ɔ. Yɛtenane ase, na yɛdwudwo yɛhyirele mmrasua bɔ beeyiale berɛ ne.

english_verse: One of them was Lydia, who was from the city of Thyatira and sold expensive purple cloth. She was a worshiper of the Lord God, and he made her willing to accept what Paul was saying.
translation_verse: Né mmrasua ne ko li Lidia; ofi Tiatira. Né ɔtɔne ago. Ɔte Nyamesomniɛ, na Awurade bukyele ye adwene nu maa ɔyɛle asoɛ mane Pɔɔlo.

english_verse: Then after she and her family were baptized, she kept on begging us, “If you think I really do have faith in the Lord, come stay in my home.” Finally, we accepted her invitation. Paul and Silas Are Put in Jail
translation_verse: Na ɔmaa bɛbɔle ye ne ye awuroama mukoraa asu beyiele nen, osele yɛ kyɛ, “Sɛ ɛmɔabu me kyɛ mede Awurade medi nahorɛ nu a, nzaade ɛmɔbra bɛɛtena m’awuro.” Na ɔhɔle so hane kyɛ yɛma yɛhɔ. Bɛto Pɔɔlo ne Silase kuku nu wɔ Filipi

english_verse: One day on our way to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl. She had a spirit in her that gave her the power to tell the future. By doing this she made a lot of money for her owners.
translation_verse: Né yɛkɔ nekaa bie bɔ mmenia bɛtaa beyia bɛbɔ mbaeɛ ɔ, na abaayaa bie bɔ ɔte afaneɛ bɔ odi ahɔen ɔ wale ooyiale yɛ. Ye ngɔmhyɛlɛ ne, né wama ye mene mɔ banya bɛ nwo tam.

english_verse: The girl followed Paul and the rest of us, and she kept yelling, “These men are servants of the Most High God! They are telling you how to be saved.”
translation_verse: Olili Pɔɔlo ne yɛ si teateane nu kyɛ, “Sɔ mmenia hemɔ bɛte Anwuro Anwuro Nyameɛ ne ngoaa bɔ bekyire ɛmɔ ngoalelɛ atee ne ɔ.”

english_verse: This went on for several days. Finally, Paul got so upset that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ, I order you to leave this girl alone!” At once the evil spirit left her.
translation_verse: Afaneɛ ne yɔle sɔ alaa ngyẽa pee maa oodwuli kyɛ ɔyɛle Pɔɔlo ahomete, yiti ɔkakyili ye nwo sele sunzummɔne ne kyɛ, “Mehyɛ wɔ wɔ Yesu Kristo dumaa nu kyɛ fi ye nu fite!” Na berɛ ne ala sunzummɔne ne fili ye nu.

english_verse: When the girl's owners realized they had lost all chances for making more money, they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them into court.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ ye mene mɔ nwuni kyɛ b’atee bɔ bɛfa so benya sikaa abɔ bɛ nen, bɛhyele Pɔɔlo ne Silase, na bɛhwene bɛ bɛhɔle mbanyi nyunu wɔ badwa nu.

english_verse: They are telling us to do things we Romans are not allowed to do.”
translation_verse: Bekyire amanneɛ bɔ otia yɛ Romanfoɛ mmeraa, bɔ ɔyɛ se kyɛ yɛkole yɛkɔto nu, anaakyɛ yɛkoli so ɔ.”

english_verse: The crowd joined in the attack on Paul and Silas. Then the officials tore the clothes off the two men and ordered them to be beaten with a whip.
translation_verse: Na ɛlɔen ne koso bedwɔso bɛhɔle bɛ so. Na ndɛenbualɛfoɛ nemɔ puropurole Pɔɔlo ne Silase ndaadeɛ, na bɛhyɛle kyɛ befi bɛ mbire.

english_verse: After they had been badly beaten, they were put in jail, and the jailer was told to guard them carefully.
translation_verse: Bɛbole bɛ botorɔ beyiele ne, bɛfale bɛ beguale kuku nu; na bɛfale ahyɛdeɛ bɛmane kukunu so neafoɛ ne kyɛ ɔ́fa bɛ sie paa.

english_verse: The jailer did as he was told. He put them deep inside the jail and chained their feet to heavy blocks of wood.
translation_verse: Na ye koso onyane sɔ ahyɛdeɛ nen, ɔfale bɛ hɔle kuku nu sua n’akunu dɔ ɔɔbɔle bɛ panwu.

english_verse: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing praises to God, while the other prisoners listened.
translation_verse: Kɔngɔen ne, kɔyɛ abunnamu, né Pɔɔlo ne Silase bɛbɔ mbaeɛ ná bɛto Nyameɛ ayɛyelɛ dwein, na kukunufoɛ ngaa ne tiele bɛ.

english_verse: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the jail to its foundations. The doors opened, and the chains fell from all the prisoners.
translation_verse: Mvum nu, aseɛ wosole serɛserɛ mane kuku nu sua ne nyinasoɛ ne wosole. Berɛ ne ala, anoa ne amukoraa bukyebukyele, na ebiala ngɔnzɔngɔnzɔ bɔ ɔsosɔ ye ne puropuro guale.

english_verse: When the jailer woke up and saw that the doors were open, he thought that the prisoners had escaped. He pulled out his sword and was about to kill himself.
translation_verse: Bɔ ɔnea kukunufoɛ so ne fili nnaa nu dwɔsole, na mmerɛ bɔ onwuni kyɛ kuku nu anoa nemɔ abukyebukye nen, ɔdwenene kyɛ kukunufoɛ ne anwati; yiti ɔhwene ye ngrandɛ kyɛ oku ye nwo.

english_verse: But Paul shouted, “Don't harm yourself! No one has escaped.”
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo teane nu serɛserɛ sele kyɛ, “Nnɛdi wɔ nwo awue, na yɛ mukoraa yɛwɔ wa!”

english_verse: The jailer asked for a torch and went into the jail. He was shaking all over as he knelt down in front of Paul and Silas.
translation_verse: Biaa ne maa bɛfale kanea bɛbrɛle ye, otuli amirika wale sua ne anu dɔ, na ɔfale anwopopolɛ tole ye nwo yele Pɔɔlo ne Silase gya bo.

english_verse: After he had led them out of the jail, he asked, “What must I do to be saved?”
translation_verse: Afei ɔyele bɛ fitele, na obisale bɛ kyɛ, “Me mene mɔ, nzu yeɛ nyɔ na manya daa ngoa ɔ?”

english_verse: They replied, “Have faith in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved! This is also true for everyone who lives in your home.”
translation_verse: Bebuale ye kyɛ, “Dé Awurade Yesu di na ɛne w’awuro ama konya daa ngoa.”

english_verse: Then Paul and Silas told him and everyone else in his house about the Lord.
translation_verse: Afei bɛhane Awurade nwo dwirɛ ne behyirele ye ne ye awuro ama mukoraa.

english_verse: While it was still night, the jailer took them to a place where he could wash their cuts and bruises. Then he and everyone in his home were baptized.
translation_verse: Sɔ dɔnhwere ne anu ala kɔngɔen ne, ɔfale Pɔɔlo ne Silase hɔle oomiane bɛ nwo apirakuro ne; na ɔmaa bɛbɔle ye ne ye awuro ama mukoraa asu berɛ ne ala.

english_verse: They were very glad they had put their faith in God. After this, the jailer took Paul and Silas to his home and gave them something to eat.
translation_verse: Afei ɔfale bɛ wale ye awuro ɔɔmane bɛ nikyee maa belili, na ɔne ye awuro ama mukoraa benyane anigye kyɛ banya gyidie wɔ Nyameɛ nu ɔ. Bɛyakyi Pɔɔlo ne Silase

english_verse: The next morning the officials sent some police with orders for the jailer to let Paul and Silas go.
translation_verse: Na aleɛ hyene nen, ndɛenbualɛfoɛ nemɔ somane polisifoɛ mɔ, na bɛfale edwirɛ he betuale bɛ noa: “Yakyi mmenia nemɔ ma bɛhɔ!”

english_verse: The jailer told Paul, “The officials have ordered me to set you free. Now you can leave in peace.”
translation_verse: Yiti biaa ne sele Pɔɔlo kyɛ, “Ndɛenbualɛfoɛ nemɔ asoma maa baase me kyɛ nyakyi ɛmɔ ma ɛmɔhɔ. Yiti ɛmɔfite bɛhɔ asomdwee nu.”

english_verse: But Paul told the police, “We are Roman citizens, and the Roman officials had us beaten in public without giving us a trial. They threw us into jail. Now do they think they can secretly send us away? No, they cannot! They will have to come here themselves and let us out.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Pɔɔlo sele bɛ kyɛ, “Bammua yɛ ndɛen wɔ bɔne biala nwo, yeɛ bafi yɛ mbire wɔ mmenia nu wɔ aberɛ bɔ yɛte Romanfoɛ ɔ, na bɛfale yɛ beguale kuku nu. Afei de, bɛ́fea bɛ nwo bɛye yɛ maa yɛkɔ anaa. Daabi, yɛngɔhɔ! Ma bɛ bɔbɔ bɛbra bɛɛye yɛ.”

english_verse: When the police told the officials that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, the officials were afraid.
translation_verse: Na polisifoɛ nemɔ hɔle bɛɛbɔle ndɛenbualɛfoɛ nemɔ amaneɛ, na bɛtele kyɛ Pɔɔlo ne Silase bɛte Romanfoɛ nen, besurole.

english_verse: So they came and apologized. They led them out of the jail and asked them to please leave town.
translation_verse: Yiti bɛɛyɛle bɛ dibem; bɛyele bɛ befili kuku nu, na bɛsrɛle bɛ kyɛ befi kuro berɛ bɛhɔ.

english_verse: But Paul and Silas went straight to the home of Lydia, where they saw the Lord's followers and encouraged them. Then they left.
translation_verse: Yiti befili kuku nu berɛ bɛhɔle Lidia awuro. Benwuni agyidifoɛ nemɔ berɛ; bɛhyɛle bɛ nguraen, na befili berɛ bɛhɔle.

english_verse: After Paul and his friends had traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they went on to Thessalonica. A synagogue was in that city.
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo ne Silase bɛpɛle nu wɔ Amfipoli ne Apolonia bɛwale Tɛsalonika, nekaa bɔ Yudafoɛ nyianu sua wɔ ɔ.

english_verse: So as usual, Paul went there to worship, and on three Sabbaths he spoke to the people. He used the Scriptures
translation_verse: Na kyɛbɔ né Pɔɔlo taa yɔ ne, ɔhɔle nyianu sua ne anu, na ɔne bɛ yɔle Ahyerɛlɛ ne anu ngyerɛkyerɛ afofikyẽa sɔ alaa pɛen nza.

english_verse: to show them that the Messiah had to suffer, but that he would rise from death. Paul also told them that Jesus is the Messiah he was preaching about.
translation_verse: Ohyirehyirele nu lili ye nwo adanzeɛ kyɛ, né ɔsɛ kyɛ Kristo ne nwu amaneɛ na odwɔso fi awufoɛ nu. Na ɔhane kyɛ, “Sɔ Yesu he bɔ mekã ye nwo dwirɛ mekyire ɛmɔ ne, ye ole Kristo ne.”

english_verse: Some of them believed what Paul had said, and they became followers with Paul and Silas. Some Gentiles and many important women also believed the message.
translation_verse: Bɛ nu biemɔ lele edwirɛ ne lili, na bɛfale bɛ nwo bɛbɔle Pɔɔlo ne Silase; sɔ ala yeɛ Helafoɛ nyamesurofoɛ pee ne mmrasua atitirefoɛ pee koso yɔle ɔ.

english_verse: The Jewish leaders were jealous and got some troublemakers who hung around the marketplace to start a riot in the city. They wanted to drag Paul and Silas out to the mob, and so they went straight to Jason's home.
translation_verse: Nakoso Yudafoɛ bɔ banne banni ne, bɛ nye borole, yiti bɛfale ammɔbrafoɛ kekakekafoɛ biemɔ bɛbokale bɛ nwo so, bɛmane ɛlɔen yiale, na bɛmane kuro berɛ yɛle basabasa. Bɛpɛle Yason sua nwo beyiale, bɔ né bɛpena kyɛ bɛtwe bɛ befite bɛbrɛ ɛlɔen ne ɔ.

english_verse: But when they did not find them there, they dragged out Jason and some of the Lord's followers. They took them to the city authorities and shouted, “Paul and Silas have been upsetting things everywhere. Now they have come here,
translation_verse: Na bannwu bɛ nen, bɛhwene Yason ne agyidifoɛ ne biemɔ bɛɛmane kuro ne anu mbanyi mɔ, na bɛteateane nu kyɛ, “Mmenia hemɔ bɔ bama ewiase amukoraa ayɛ basabasa ne, bawa wa koso,

english_verse: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. All of them break the laws of the Roman Emperor by claiming that someone named Jesus is king.”
translation_verse: na Yason asikye bɛ wɔ ye awuro. Bɛ mukoraa bebu Kaesare mmeraa so, na bɛnwa ɛhene bieku koso wɔ berɛ bɔ oli Yesu ɔ.”

english_verse: The officials and the people were upset when they heard this.
translation_verse: Na ɛlɔen ne ne kuro ne anu mbanyi nemɔ tele sɔ dwirɛ nen, ɔhale bɛ paa.

english_verse: So they made Jason and the other followers pay bail before letting them go. People in Berea Welcome the Message
translation_verse: Na bɛmane Yason ne bɛ ngaa nemɔ belili agyinamuɛ bɛmane bɛ, na bɛyakyili bɛ maa bɛhɔle. Pɔɔlo ne Silase wɔ Bɛrea

english_verse: That same night the Lord's followers sent Paul and Silas on to Berea, and after they arrived, they went to the synagogue.
translation_verse: Na aleɛ sane pɛ, aliɛmaa nemɔ mane Pɔɔlo ne Silase bɛhɔle Bɛrea. Beedwuli ne, bɛhɔle Yudafoɛ nyianu sua nu.

english_verse: The people in Berea were much nicer than those in Thessalonica, and they gladly accepted the message. Day after day they studied the Scriptures to see if these things were true.
translation_verse: Na sɔ Yudafoɛ nemɔ, né b’adwene nu api tra bɛ bɔ bɛwɔ Tɛsalonika ne, ɔnate kyɛ bɛyele bɛ kunu betiele edwirɛ ne; na daa biala bɛneaneane Ahyerɛlɛ ne anu kyɛ, aso edwirɛ ne, ye ala ɛne a.

english_verse: Many of them put their faith in the Lord, including some important Greek women and several men.
translation_verse: Yiti bɛ nu pee, yeɛ afei Hela mmrasua atitirefoɛ pee ne Hela mmienzua pee lele edwirɛ ne lili.

english_verse: When the Jewish leaders in Thessalonica heard that Paul had been preaching God's message in Berea, they went there and caused trouble by turning the crowds against Paul.
translation_verse: Nakoso mmerɛ bɔ Yudafoɛ bɔ bɛwɔ Tɛsalonika ne bɛtele kyɛ Pɔɔlo waahã Nyameɛ dwirɛ ne wɔ Bɛrea koso nen, bɛwale berɛ bɛɛto beguale mmenia nemɔ so anu bɛsɛkyele b’adwene.

english_verse: At once the followers sent Paul down to the coast, but Silas and Timothy stayed in Berea.
translation_verse: Na berɛ ne ala agyidifoɛ ne guale Pɔɔlo ate maa ɔhɔle mboanoa, nakoso Silase ne Timoteo de, bɛhale Bɛrea.

english_verse: Some men went with Paul as far as Athens, and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible. Paul in Athens
translation_verse: Na bɛ bɔ beesomane Pɔɔlo ate ne, bɛfale ye beedwuli Atense, na besa bɛkɔ nen, ɔfale ngraa maa bɛɛmane Silase ne Timoteo kyɛ bɛma bɛ nwo yɛ nyera bɛɛboka ye so. Pɔɔlo ka nzɛmba kyire Atensefoɛ

english_verse: While Paul was waiting in Athens, he was upset to see all the idols in the city.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ Pɔɔlo nwondɛ Silase ne Timoteo wɔ Atense nen, onwuni kyɛ bosoensolɛ ayi kuro ne anu tɛkyɛ; yiti ɔhale ye paa.

english_verse: He went to the synagogue to speak to the Jews and to anyone who worshiped with them. Day after day he also spoke to everyone he met in the market.
translation_verse: Yiti ɔne Yudafoɛ ne Amaenmaensofoɛ nyamesurofoɛ bɛyɛle mbɛnzɛmbɛnzɛmuɛ wɔ nyianu sua nu, na daa biala ɔne bɛ bɔ bɛwɔ dwaaso koso yɔle sɔ ala.

english_verse: Some of them were Epicureans and some were Stoics, and they started arguing with him. People were asking, “What is this know-it-all trying to say?” Some even said, “Paul must be preaching about foreign gods! That's what he means when he talks about Jesus and about people rising from death.”
translation_verse: Na nwomanimfoɛ fekue nyɔ bie bɔ bɛfrɛ bɛ Epikurofoɛ ne Setokifoɛ koso ne ye suli aporowaa. Ebiemɔ hane kyɛ, “Akoaa he bɔ ɔnze hwee ye, nzu yeɛ okyire ye?” Na biemɔ koso hane kyɛ, “Osoma kyɛ ɔ́ka mmosoen ɛwɔfoɛ biemɔ nwo dwirɛ.” Bɛhane sɔ, ɔnate kyɛ né Pɔɔlo ka Yesu ne ewutingyelɛ nwo dwirɛ.

english_verse: They brought Paul before a council called the Areopagus, and said, “Tell us what your new teaching is all about.
translation_verse: Yiti bɛ ne ye hɔle Areopago na bɛhane kyɛ, “Ɛkɔhora kohyire yɛ ngyerɛkyerɛ foforɛ bɔ ɛkã ye nwo dwirɛ ne bo?

english_verse: We have heard you say some strange things, and we want to know what you mean.”
translation_verse: Ɔnate kyɛ yɛttele edwirɛ bɔ ɛkã ne bie le, na yɛpena kyɛ ekyire yɛ ye bo.”

english_verse: More than anything else the people of Athens and the foreigners living there loved to hear and to talk about anything new.
translation_verse: Ɔnate kyɛ, Atensefoɛ ne ɛwɔfoɛ mɔ bɔ baatena berɛ ne amukoraa, né bɛmbena nikye fee bɛnyɔ te kyɛ edwirɛ foforɛ bɔ bekonya bekotie anaakyɛ bɔ bɛkɔhã ɔ. Pɔɔlo noa dwirɛ wɔ Areopago

english_verse: So Paul stood up in front of the council and said: People of Athens, I see that you are very religious.
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo dwɔso gyinane Areopago n’afia berɛ hane kyɛ, “Atensefoɛ, menwu kyɛ ɛmɔafa ɛmɔ gyidie bawura ɛsom ahoroɔ nu paa.

english_verse: As I was going through your city and looking at the things you worship, I found an altar with the words, “To an Unknown God.” You worship this God, but you don't really know him. So I want to tell you about him.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ manate kuro ye anu, na manwu nningyein ahoroɔ bɔ ɛmɔsɔne bɛ ɔ. Manwu afɔleɛ bokyea ko bɔ bahyerɛ so kyɛ, ‘Ɛhe te nyameɛ bɔ yɛnze ye ne deɛ.’ Na bɔ ɛmɔsɔne ye nakoso ɛmɔnze ye ne, ye nwo dwirɛ yeɛ mekã mekyire ɛmɔ ye.

english_verse: This God made the world and everything in it. He is Lord of heaven and earth, and he doesn't live in temples built by human hands.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ bɔ ɔbɔle wiase ne nu nningyein amukoraa ne, ye bɔ ɔte nyameɛso ne aseɛ Mene ne, nna asɔneyɛɛ sua mɔ bɔ bafa bɛ sa basi ɔ nu yeɛ ɔte ɔ,

english_verse: He doesn't need help from anyone. He gives life, breath, and everything else to all people.
translation_verse: yeɛ nna sona sa yeɛ bɛfa bɛsɔne ye ɔ, kyɛ ebiaa ohia nikyee bie ɔ; ofikyɛ ye bɔbɔ yeɛ ɔma sona biala ngoa ne nwomeɛ ne nikyee biala ɔ;

english_verse: From one person God made all nations who live on earth, and he decided when and where every nation would be.
translation_verse: na ɔbɔle mmenia bɔ bɛwɔ maen amukoraa nu fili sona komapɛ nu maa bɛtenane aseɛ ye aso amukoraa. Na ɔhyehyɛle mmerɛ ahoroɔ ne nekaa biala bɔ bɛkɔtena ɔ ye wɛen so tole berɛ mane bɛ,

english_verse: God has done all this, so that we will look for him and reach out and find him. He isn't far from any of us,
translation_verse: kyɛ bɛpena Awurade si atee, amaa sɛ bɛpena ye a, banwu ye; nakoso ɔne yɛ nu biala afia atee anwa.

english_verse: and he gives us the power to live, to move, and to be who we are. “We are his children,” just as some of your poets have said.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ, ‘Ye nu yeɛ yɛte ase, yɛkɔ yɛba, ná yɛnya ngoa ɔ’; kyɛbɔ ɛmɔ edweintolɛfoɛ ne biemɔ bahã kyɛ, ‘Ofikyɛ yɛ koso yɛte ye mma.’

english_verse: Since we are God's children, we must not think that he is like an idol made out of gold or silver or stone. He isn't like anything that humans have thought up and made.
translation_verse: Na ɔnate kyɛ yɛte Nyameɛ mma ne ati, ɔnzɛ kyɛ yɛdwene kyɛ Nyameɛ sue te kyɛ esikaa kɔkorɛ, anaa ɛdwetɛ, anaa nyɔboɛ bɔ kuro sona afa ye sa ne ye nworɛ wali adwii wayɔ ɔ.

english_verse: In the past, God forgave all this because people did not know what they were doing. But now he says that everyone everywhere must turn to him.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ né mmenia bennya bennwuni Nyameɛ yé nen, obuli ye nye guale so; nakoso kekesaala ye de, ɔhyɛ ebiala bɔ ɔwɔ nekaa biala ɔ kyɛ ɔsakyera ye adwene,

english_verse: He has set a day when he will judge the world's people with fairness. And he has chosen the man Jesus to do the judging for him. God has given proof of this to all of us by raising Jesus from death.
translation_verse: ofikyɛ watu kyẽa ko bie wasie berɛ, bɔ ɔkɔfa sona bie bɔ waneanea nu waye ye ɔ so kobua ewiase amukoraa ndɛen tenenee nu ɔ. Na wali ɛhe nwo adanzeɛ wahyire wɔ etingyɛlɛ bɔ otingyele ye fili awufoɛ nu ne, kyɛ mmenia amukoraa bele ye beli.”

english_verse: As soon as the people heard Paul say a man had been raised from death, some of them started laughing. Others said, “We will hear you talk about this some other time.”
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ bɛtele awufoɛ etingyelɛ nwo dwirɛ nen, bɛ nu biemɔ serele Pɔɔlo; na ebiemɔ koso hane kyɛ, “Yɛkuro kyɛ esa si dwirɛ he aso bieku mmerɛ foforɛ.”

english_verse: When Paul left the council meeting,
translation_verse: Yiti Pɔɔlo fili nyianu ne abo hɔle.

english_verse: some of the men put their faith in the Lord and went with Paul. One of them was a council member named Dionysius. A woman named Damaris and several others also put their faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Nakoso mmenia ne bie fale bɛ nwo bɛbɔle ye bɛyɛle agyidifoɛ; ebiemɔ ole Dionisio bɔ ɔboka Areopago fekue ne aso ne, yeɛ afei braa bie bɔ oli Damari, ɔne ebiemɔ bɔ bɛboka bɛ so ɔ.

english_verse: Paul left Athens and went to Corinth,
translation_verse: Ɛhe asi ne, Pɔɔlo fili Atense hɔle Korinto.

english_verse: where he met Aquila, a Jewish man from Pontus. Not long before this, Aquila had come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Emperor Claudius had ordered the Jewish people to leave Rome. Paul went to see Aquila and Priscilla
translation_verse: Na onwuni Yudaniɛ bie bɔ oli Akwila bɔ bɛwole ye Ponto ɔ. Né ɔne ɔye Prisila befili Yitalia bɛwale berɛ ɔ ɔhhyɛle biala, ofikyɛ né Klɔdio ahyɛ mmeraa kyɛ Yudafoɛ amukoraa bétu befi Rome bɛhɔ. Pɔɔlo hɔle bɛ berɛ,

english_verse: and found out they were tent makers. Paul was also a tent maker, so he stayed with them, and they worked together.
translation_verse: na kyɛbɔ ɛtena sua nwonɛ te bɛ mukoraa bɛ sa noa adwuma ne ati, ɔne bɛ tenane, na ɔne bɛ yɔle adwuma.

english_verse: Every Sabbath, Paul went to the synagogue. He spoke to Jews and Gentiles and tried to win them over.
translation_verse: Né afofikyẽa biala ɔkɔyɛ ngyerɛkyerɛ wɔ nyianu sua nu, na otuli Yudafoɛ ne Helafoɛ foɛ maa bele belili.

english_verse: But after Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia, he spent all his time preaching to the Jews about Jesus the Messiah.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Silase ne Timoteo befili Makedonia bɛwale ne, Pɔɔlo fale ye mmerɛ tole berɛ hane nzɛmba ne, na olili adanzeɛ hyirele Yudafoɛ nemɔ kyɛ Yesu ole Kristo ne.

english_verse: Finally, they turned against him and insulted him. So he shook the dust from his clothes and told them, “Whatever happens to you will be your own fault! I am not to blame. From now on I am going to preach to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ né Yudafoɛ nemɔ bedwɔso betia ye, ná bɛkã musue dwirɛ betia ye a, ye koso ɔporoporo ye ataadeɛ nu kã kyire bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔ bɔbɔ ɛmɔ mogya bɔ ɛmɔ ti so, ofikyɛ me de, menni ye nwo fɔ. Na ofi ɛnɛ bɔ ɔkɔ ɔ, ngɔhɔ Amaenmaensofoɛ mɔ dɔ.”

english_verse: Paul then moved into the house of a man named Titius Justus, who worshiped God and lived next door to the synagogue.
translation_verse: Yiti ɔyakyili bɛ berɛ ɔɔtenane biaa bie bɔ ye dumaa li Tito Yusto, bɔ ɔso Nyameɛ ɔ ye awuro. Né ye awuro ne pingye nyianu sua ne pɛɛ.

english_verse: Crispus was the leader of the synagogue. He and everyone in his family put their faith in the Lord. Many others in Corinth also heard the message, and all the people who had faith in the Lord were baptized.
translation_verse: Na Krispo, bɔ ɔte nyianu sua ne aso panyi ne, ɔne ye awuro ama mukoraa belele Awurade belili; yeɛ afei Korintofoɛ pee bɔ bɛtele Pɔɔlo dwirɛ ne koso, bele belili, na bɛ mukoraa bɛmaa bɛbɔle bɛ asu.

english_verse: One night, Paul had a vision, and in it the Lord said, “Don't be afraid to keep on preaching. Don't stop!
translation_verse: Na ɛlɛho bie kɔngɔen, Awurade hã hyirele Pɔɔlo wɔ nyekyire kyɛ, “Nnɛsuro, dwudwo, na nnɛmua wɔ noa,

english_verse: I am with you, and you won't be harmed. Many people in this city belong to me.”
translation_verse: ofikyɛ ngyi wɔ si, na ebiala ngɔwa wɔ so ngɔyɔ wɔ hwee, ɔnate kyɛ nne mmenia pee wɔ kuro ye anu.”

english_verse: Paul stayed on in Corinth for a year and a half, teaching God's message to the people.
translation_verse: Yiti Pɔɔlo lili berɛ afoɛ ko ne bosome nzia hane Nyameɛ dwirɛ ne hyirele berɛ ama. Yudafoɛ fa Pɔɔlo kɔ Galio nyunu

english_verse: While Gallio was governor of Achaia, some of the Jewish leaders got together and grabbed Paul. They brought him into court
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ né Galio te amrado wɔ Akaia nen, Yudafoɛ nemɔ yɛle ko, bɛhyele Pɔɔlo, na bɛhwene ye bɛhɔle badwafoɛ nyunu.

english_verse: and said, “This man is trying to make our people worship God in a way that is against our Law!”
translation_verse: Na besele Galio kyɛ, “Sɔ biaa he afa atee bɔ otia Yudafoɛ mmeraa so ɔma mmenia sɔne Nyameɛ.”

english_verse: Even before Paul could speak, Gallio said, “If you were charging this man with a crime or some other wrong, I would have to listen to you.
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo yɛle kyɛ ɔye ye noa pɛ yeɛ Galio sele Yudafoɛ ne kyɛ, “O Yudafoɛ, sɛ ɔyɛle nzɛmmɔnelilɛ anaakyɛ awuelilɛ dwirɛ bie de a, ahaa ngotie ɛmɔ.

english_verse: But since this concerns only words, names, and your own law, you will have to take care of it yourselves. I refuse to judge such matters.”
translation_verse: Nakoso kyɛbɔ waayɛ edwirɛ, ɔne dumaa ne ɛmɔ bɔbɔ ɛmɔ mmeraa nwo aporowaasulɛ ye de, ɛmɔ bɔbɔ beesiesie; na edwirɛ sɔaa mɔ de, mengɔyɛ ye nwo ndɛenbualɛniɛ!”

english_verse: Then he sent them out of the court.
translation_verse: Na ofoane bɛ fili nekaa bɔ bedi dwirɛ ne.

english_verse: The crowd grabbed Sosthenes, the Jewish leader, and beat him up in front of the court. But none of this mattered to Gallio. Paul Returns to Antioch in Syria
translation_verse: Yiti bɛ mukoraa bɛhyele nyianu sua ne aso panyi Sositene, na bɛbole ye wɔ nekaa bɔ bedi dwirɛ n’anyunu berɛ, nakoso Galio anga ye nwo bie. Pɔɔlo sa ba Antiokia

english_verse: After Paul had stayed for a while with the Lord's followers in Corinth, he told them goodbye and sailed on to Syria with Aquila and Priscilla. But before he left, he had his head shaved at Cenchreae because he had made a promise to God.
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo tenane berɛ hyɛle kãa, na nziɛ ye ɔne aliɛmaa nemɔ belili ngraa, na ofili berɛ fale ɛlɛen hɔle Siria. Prisila ne Akwila koso bokale ye so bɛne ye hɔle. Pɔɔlo bɔle tikwa, wɔ Kɛnkrea, ɔnate kyɛ né wabɔ anohoba.

english_verse: The three of them arrived in Ephesus, where Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He then went into the synagogue to talk with the people there.
translation_verse: Bedwuli Ɛfeso nen, ɔyakyili bɛ wɔ berɛ; na ye de, ɔhɔle nyianu sua nu ɔne Yudafoɛ bɛɛyɛle ngyerɛkyerɛ.

english_verse: They asked him to stay longer, but he refused.
translation_verse: Na bɛsrɛle ye kyɛ ɔne bɛ tena berɛ kãa, nakoso wambene.

english_verse: He told them goodbye and said, “If God lets me, I will come back.”
translation_verse: Na mmom ɔhrale bɛ kyɛ, “Sɛ Nyameɛ ma ate a, ngosa ngɔwa ɛmɔ wa.” Na ɔfale ɛlɛen fili Ɛfeso hɔle.

english_verse: Paul sailed to Caesarea, where he greeted the church. Then he went on to Antioch.
translation_verse: Na odwuli Kaesarea nen, ɔbɔle hwii hɔle Yerusalem oobisale asɔremma nemɔ ahye, na afei osili nu hɔle Antiokia.

english_verse: After staying there for a while, he left and visited several places in Galatia and Phrygia. He helped the followers there to become stronger in their faith. Apollos in Ephesus
translation_verse: Ɔhyɛle berɛ kãa, na afei ofili berɛ oohyinini Galatia ne Frigyea mbɔtam hyɛle asuafoɛ nemɔ amukoraa nguraen. Apolo ka nzɛmba wɔ Ɛfeso ne Korinto

english_verse: A Jewish man named Apollos came to Ephesus. Apollos had been born in the city of Alexandria. He was a very good speaker and knew a lot about the Scriptures.
translation_verse: Yudaniɛ bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Apolo, bɔ bɛwole ye Aleksandria ɔ, ɔwale Ɛfeso. Ɔte sona bɔ ye noa ate ná afei wasa wabe wɔ Ahyerɛlɛ ne anu paa.

english_verse: He also knew much about the Lord's Way, and he spoke about it with great excitement. What he taught about Jesus was right, but all he knew was John's message about baptism.
translation_verse: Bɛfale Awurade Atee so yeɛ behyirele ye nikye ɔ, na ɔnate kyɛ ɔyɛ se wɔ sunzum nu ne ati, odwudwole, na ohyirehyirele Yesu nwo dwirɛ turoloo; ɔwɔ nu kyɛ né Yohane asubɔlɛ ne angome yeɛ ɔse ɔ.

english_verse: Apollos started speaking bravely in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him to their home and helped him understand God's Way even better.
translation_verse: Ɔhyɛle ye bo sili ye ahone dwudwole wɔ nyianu sua nu; na mmerɛ bɔ Prisila ne Akwila nwuni ye ne, bɛ ne ye hɔle b’awuro, na behyirehyirele ye Nyameɛ Atee ne anu pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english_verse: Apollos decided to travel through Achaia. So the Lord's followers wrote letters, encouraging the followers there to welcome him. After Apollos arrived in Achaia, he was a great help to everyone who had put their faith in the Lord Jesus because of God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Na Apolo yɛle ye adwene kyɛ ɔkɔ Akaia nen, aliɛmaa nemɔ bɛhyɛle ye nguraen, na bɛhyerɛle krataa bɛɛmane asuafoɛ nemɔ kyɛ bele ye bɛto nu nyemene so. Oodwuli ne, ɔbokale bɛ bɔ bɛnate adom so bayɛ agyidifoɛ ne paa.

english_verse: He got into fierce arguments with the Jewish people, and in public he used the Scriptures to prove that Jesus is the Messiah.
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ ɔnate ye ngyerɛkyerɛ so lili Yudafoɛ so ngonim wɔ badwa nu, na ɔfale Ahyerɛlɛ ne hyirele nu pefee kyɛ Yesu ole Kristo ne.

english_verse: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled across the hill country to Ephesus, where he met some of the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ né Apolo wɔ Korinto nen, Pɔɔlo hyinini manzini ne anu tonn oofitele Ɛfeso. Onwuni agyidifoɛ biemɔ wɔ berɛ,

english_verse: He asked them, “When you put your faith in Jesus, were you given the Holy Spirit?” “No!” they answered. “We have never even heard of the Holy Spirit.”
translation_verse: na obisale bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔyɛle agyidifoɛ nen, aso ɛmɔnyane Sunzum Krongron ne?” Na bebuale kyɛ, “Daabi, yɛ de yɛttele ye le po kyɛ Sunzum Krongron bie wɔ berɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: “Then why were you baptized?” Paul asked. They answered, “Because of what John taught.”
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo bisale bɛ kyɛ, “Nzaade né nzikyɛ asubɔlɛ yeɛ bɛfa bɛbɔle ɛmɔ ɔ?” Na bebuale kyɛ, “Yohane asubɔlɛ ne.”

english_verse: Paul replied, “John baptized people so they would turn to God. But he also told them someone else was coming, and they should put their faith in him. Jesus is the one that John was talking about.”
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo sele kyɛ, “Nahorɛ nu, Yohane bɔle adwenesakyeralɛ asu, na ɔhã hyirele maen ne kyɛ béle bɔ oli ye si ɔ́ba, bɔ ye ole Yesu ne béli.”

english_verse: After the people heard Paul say this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Na bɛtele sɔ dwirɛ nen, bɛmaa bɛbɔle bɛ asu wɔ Awurade Yesu dumaa nu.

english_verse: Then Paul placed his hands on them. The Holy Spirit was given to them, and they spoke unknown languages and prophesied.
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo fale ye sa guale bɛ so ne, Sunzum Krongron wale bɛ so; bɛhane edwudwolɛ ahoroɔ, na bɛhyɛle ngɔm.

english_verse: There were about twelve men in this group.
translation_verse: Né bɛ mukoraa bɛkɔyɛ mmenia buru ne nyɔ.

english_verse: For three months Paul went to the synagogue and talked bravely with the people about God's kingdom. He tried to win them over,
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo hɔle nyianu sua nu tonn bosome nza. Osili ye ahone ɔne mmenia ne dwudwole, na ɔne bɛ yɛle ngyerɛkyerɛ fale Nyameɛ ahennie ne nwo.

english_verse: but some of them were stubborn and refused to believe. In front of everyone they said terrible things about God's Way. Paul left and took the followers with him to the lecture hall of Tyrannus. He spoke there every day
translation_verse: Nakoso ebiemɔ yɛle asoserɛ, banne dwirɛ ne banni, na bɛhane musue dwirɛ betiale Atee ne wɔ mmenia wora ne nyunu. Yiti ɔyakyili bɛ berɛ, ɔfale agyidifoɛ ne bokale ye nwo so; na daa biala ɔyɛle ngyerɛkyerɛ wɔ ebie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Tirano sukuu sua nu.

english_verse: for two years, until every Jew and Gentile in Asia had heard the Lord's message. The Sons of Sceva
translation_verse: Ɛhe hɔle so sɔ alaa afoɛ nyɔ, na ɔmane bɛ bɔ bɛwɔ Asia mbɔtam berɛ amukoraa, Yudafoɛ ne Helafoɛ, bɛtele Awurade nwo dwirɛ ne. Sekewa mma mmienzua nzoo nemɔ

english_verse: God gave Paul the power to work great miracles.
translation_verse: Nyameɛ fale Pɔɔlo so yɔle nzɛngyerɛnneɛ sonongo,

english_verse: People even took handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul's body, and they carried them to everyone who was sick. All of the sick people were healed, and the evil spirits went out.
translation_verse: na bɛfale ye nwo duku anaa ye ataadeɛ ngatanyunu po beguale ayarefoɛ so maa bɛtele apɔ, na sunzummɔne tutu fili bɛ nu.

english_verse: Some Jewish men started going around trying to force out evil spirits by using the name of the Lord Jesus. They said to the spirits, “Come out in the name of that same Jesus that Paul preaches about!”
translation_verse: Yiti Yudafoɛ ngonyaayelɛfoɛ biemɔ bɔ bekyini betutu sunzummɔne yɛle kyɛ bɛ koso bɛkɔfa Awurade Yesu dumaa bɛkɔyɔ bie, na besele sunzummɔne nemɔ kyɛ, “Yɛhyɛ wɔ wɔ Yesu bɔ Pɔɔlo di ye nwo adanzeɛ ne dumaa nu kyɛ, fi ye nu fite!”

english_verse: Seven sons of a high priest named Sceva were doing this,
translation_verse: Né Yuda sɔfo panyi paa Sekewa mma mmienzua nzoo yeɛ bɛyɔ sɔ nikyee ne ɔ.

english_verse: when an evil spirit said to them, “I know Jesus! And I have heard about Paul. But who are you?”
translation_verse: Nakoso sunzummɔne ne buale bɛ kyɛ, “Mese Yesu, yeɛ mese Pɔɔlo; na ɛmɔ koso, nwa ole ɛmɔ?”

english_verse: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and beat them up. They ran out of the house, naked and bruised.
translation_verse: Na biaa bɔ ole sunzummɔne ne te tɔle bɛ so bobɔle bɛ mukoraa pasaa maa bepurapurale, na bɛfale bɛ nwo bɛtole so bɛnwati befili sɔ awuro berɛ bɛhɔle.

english_verse: When the Jews and Gentiles in Ephesus heard about this, they were so frightened that they praised the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Yudafoɛ amukoraa ne Helafoɛ amukoraa bɔ bɛwɔ Ɛfeso bɛtele sɔ dwirɛ nen, bɛ mukoraa besurole, na bɛyele Awurade Yesu dumaa ayɛ piri paa.

english_verse: Many who were followers now started telling everyone about the evil things they had been doing.
