translation_verse: Na bɛ bɔ bele belili ne, bɛ nu pee bɛwale bɛɛtole bɛ noa nu tui bɛhane bɛ bɔne ne bɛ mvealeɛ nu dwirɛ mukoraa.

english_verse: Some who had been practicing witchcraft even brought their books and burned them in public. These books were worth about
translation_verse: Ngonyaayelɛfoɛ nemɔ anu pee fale b’adwuma mmukuu bɛwale bɛɛyerale bɛ bɔ ebiala nye tua ɔ, na bɛsesene bɛ nyɔboɛ benwuni kyɛ ɔte ɛdwetɛ apee aburannu.

english_verse: So the Lord's message spread and became even more powerful. The Riot in Ephesus
translation_verse: Yiti Awurade dwirɛ ne hɔle so trɛle na onyini ngonim nu. Ɛfesofoɛ yɔle basabasa

english_verse: After all this had happened, Paul decided to visit Macedonia and Achaia on his way to Jerusalem. Paul had said, “From there I will go on to Rome.”
translation_verse: Ɛhemɔ asi ne, Pɔɔlo nate Sunzum Krongron so yɛle ye adwene kyɛ ɔkwaapɛ nu Makedonia ne Akaia kɔ Yerusalem, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Sɛ medwu berɛ a, ɔsɛ kyɛ mekɔ Rome koso.”

english_verse: So he sent his two helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia. But he stayed on in Asia for a while.
translation_verse: Yiti ɔsomane ye bokafoɛ nyɔ, Timoteo ne Eraseto maa bɛhɔle Makedonia, na ye de, ɔtenane Asia mbɔtam hyɛle kãa.

english_verse: At that time there was serious trouble because of the Lord's Way.
translation_verse: Sɔ mmerɛ ne anu, Atee ne ati basabasayɔlɛ wale Ɛfeso.

english_verse: A silversmith named Demetrius had a business that made silver models of the temple of the goddess Artemis. Those who worked for him earned a lot of money.
translation_verse: Ɔwale kyɛ, ɛdwetɛ dwumvoɛ bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Demetrio fale ɛdwetɛ yɔle bosoen brasua Ateme asɔneyɛɛ sua sɛso pee, na sɔ dwumadie ne mane adwumvoɛ nemɔ benyane mvasoɛ paa.

english_verse: Demetrius brought together everyone who was in the same business and said: Friends, you know we make a good living at this.
translation_verse: Yiti Demetrio mane ye adwumayɔlɛfoɛ ne bɛ bɔ betira sɔ nzanodwuma ne amu beyiale, na ɔfa tole bɛ nyunu kyɛ, “Biamɔ, ɛmɔse kyɛ sɔ adwiililɛ he anu yeɛ yɛnya yɛ sikaa ɔ.

english_verse: But you have surely seen and heard how this man Paul is upsetting a lot of people, not only in Ephesus, but almost everywhere in Asia. He claims that the gods we humans make are not really gods at all.
translation_verse: Na ɛmɔnwu ye, yeɛ ɛmɔte kyɛ sɔ Pɔɔlo ne nwa, nyameɛ mɔ bɔ kuro sona afa ye sa wayɔ ne de bɛtte nyameɛ mɔ koraa; na watu mmeni pee foɛ wasesã b’adwene: nna Ɛfeso wa angome ɔ, na mmom Asia mbɔtam amukoraa.

english_verse: Everyone will start saying terrible things about our business. They will stop respecting the temple of the goddess Artemis, who is worshiped in Asia and all over the world. Our great goddess will be forgotten!
translation_verse: Na bɔ mesuro ole kyɛ, nna y’adwuma he angome yeɛ ɔbaasɛkye ɔ, na mmom bosoen kokuroko Ateme asɔneyɛɛ sua ne yeɛ mmenia mmamva nyɛ hwee ko ɔ. Afei koso bosoen n’animnyam bɔ Asia amukoraa ɔne ewiase amukoraa fa sɔne ye ne baabɔ ye.”

english_verse: When the workers heard this, they got angry and started shouting, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ bɛtele sɔ dwirɛ nen, b’ahone huli, na bɛteateane nu kyɛ, “Ɛfesofoɛ Ateme te kokuroko!”

english_verse: Soon the whole city was in a riot, and some men grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, who had come from Macedonia with Paul. Then everyone in the crowd rushed to the place where the town meetings were held.
translation_verse: Yiti kuro ne anu amu yɛle basabasa. Na ɛlɔen ne tuli bi bɛɛhyele Makedoniafoɛ nyɔ nemɔ: Gayɔso ne Aristako, na bɛhwene bɛ bɛhɔle badwa nyunu. Né bɛ munyɔ bɛboka Pɔɔlo so wɔ ye ateetulɛ ne anu.

english_verse: Paul wanted to go out and speak to the people, but the Lord's followers would not let him.
translation_verse: Ahaa Pɔɔlo pena kyɛ ɔkɔ ɛlɔen ne anu berɛ bie, nakoso agyidifoɛ nemɔ amma ye ate.

english_verse: A few of the local officials were friendly to Paul, and they sent someone to warn him not to go.
translation_verse: Na berɛ mbanyi nemɔ bie bɔ bɛte Pɔɔlo damvo mɔ ne, bɛtole ye ngraa kyɛ bɛsrɛ ye ala, nnɛmaa otu ye gya baa tia badwa ne anu.

english_verse: Some of the people in the meeting were shouting one thing, and others were shouting something else. Everyone was completely confused, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
translation_verse: Na nyianu ne bo yɛle basabasa: mmenia ne bie teatea nu kã edwirɛ he, né ebiemɔ koso bɛteatea nu bɛkã edwirɛ foforɛ; ɔnate kyɛ né bɛ nu pee ngora nwu nikye horɛ bɔ yiti yeɛ bayia nu berɛ ne.

english_verse: Several of the Jewish leaders pushed a man named Alexander to the front of the crowd and started telling him what to say. He motioned with his hand and tried to explain what was going on.
translation_verse: Na mmenia ne bie susuli kyɛ Aleksandro se edwirɛ ne nwo bie, ɔnate kyɛ né Yudafoɛ ne ahwe ye aagyina anyunu kyɛ ɔye dwirɛ ne noa. Aleksandro mane ye sa so hyirele mmenia ne kyɛ bɛyɛ dinn, na ɔyɛle kyɛ ɔye dwirɛ ne noa.

english_verse: But when the crowd saw that he was Jewish, they all shouted for two hours, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Nakoso ɛlɔen ne nwuni kyɛ ɔte Yudaniɛ nen, bɛ mukoraa bɛbɔle nu bɛteateane nu alaa kɔyɛ dɔnhwere nyɔ bɛhane kyɛ “Ɛfesofoɛ Ateme te kokuroko!”

english_verse: Finally, a town official made the crowd be quiet. Then he said: People of Ephesus, who in the world doesn't know that our city is the center for worshiping the great goddess Artemis? Who doesn't know that her image which fell from heaven is right here?
translation_verse: Afei kuro berɛ krakye panyi ne neane maa ɛlɔen ne yɛle dinn ne, osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛfesofoɛ, ɛmɔ nu nwa yeɛ ɔnze kyɛ Ɛfeso kuro ye yeɛ ɔbɔ Ateme kokuroko asɔneyɛɛ sua ɔne nyɔboɛ bɔ ofi anwuro wale ne nwo waen ɔ?

english_verse: No one can deny this, and so you should calm down and not do anything foolish.
translation_verse: Ɔnate kyɛ biala ngɔhora ngosu ɛhe nwo aporowaa ne ati, ɛmɔma b’ahone ɔ́tɔ nzue nu, na nnɛma ɛmɔyɔ basabasa biala.

english_verse: You have brought men in here who have not robbed temples or spoken against our goddess.
translation_verse: Sɔ mmenia hemɔ bewwuale asɔneyɛɛ sua nemɔ nu nikye fee, yeɛ bɛhhane musue dwirɛ biala bettiale ɛmɔ bosoen brasua ne, nakoso ɛmɔafa bɛ bawa wa.

english_verse: If Demetrius and his workers have a case against these men, we have courts and judges. Let them take their complaints there.
translation_verse: Na Demetrio ne adwiililɛfoɛ bɔ bɛboka ye so ne, sɛ bele kwaadu bie bɛbɔ bɛ nu biala a, kɔɔto ne amrado nemɔ wɔ berɛ; yiti bɛhɔ dɔ bɛɛbɔ nguro.

english_verse: But if you want to do more than that, the matter will have to be brought before the city council.
translation_verse: Na sɛ ɛmɔnea na edwirɛ bieku wɔ berɛ de a, ye de yɛkoli ye badwa nu kyɛbɔ mmeraa kyire ɔ.

english_verse: We could easily be accused of starting a riot today. There is no excuse for it! We cannot even give a reason for this uproar.
translation_verse: Na annea a, mbanyi mɔ kɔbɔ yɛ kwaadu wɔ ɛnɛ basabasayɔlɛ ye nwo. Yeɛ yɛngonya nyeanoɛ anaa edwirɛ paa biala ngɔhã wɔ sɔ basabasayɔlɛ he nwo.”

english_verse: After saying this, he told the people to leave.
translation_verse: Na ɔhane sɔ yiele nen, ɔmaa betuli apo.

english_verse: When the riot was over, Paul sent for the followers and encouraged them. He then told them goodbye and left for Macedonia.
translation_verse: Nziɛ ye bɔ basabasa ne noa dwole ase ne, Pɔɔlo frɛle agyidifoɛ nemɔ maa beyiale; otuli bɛ foɛ na ɔne bɛ lili ngraa, na afei ɔhɔle Makedonia.

english_verse: As he traveled from place to place, he encouraged the followers with many messages. Finally, he went to Greece
translation_verse: Ɔfale manzini nemɔ nu hyɛle agyidifoɛ nemɔ nguraen pee yiele ne, afei ɔwale Hela aseɛ so.

english_verse: and stayed there for three months. Paul was about to sail to Syria. But some of the Jewish leaders plotted against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.
translation_verse: Olili berɛ bosome nza. Na mmerɛ bɔ ɔboaboa ye nwo kɔfa ɛlɛen kɔ Siria nen, ɔtele kyɛ Yudafoɛ ne abɔ ye ti so porɛ bɛtɛ ye; yiti ɔyɛle kyɛ osa ye si fa ase kɔfa Makedonia kɔ.

english_verse: With him were Sopater, son of Pyrrhus from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica. Gaius from Derbe was also with him, and so were Timothy and the two Asians, Tychicus and Trophimus.
translation_verse: Ɔne ɛhemɔ yeɛ bɛhɔle ɔ: Piro awa Sopata bɔ ofi Bɛrea; Aristako ne Sekunduse bɔ befi Tɛsalonika; Gayɔso bɔ ofi Dɛɛbi, Timoteo yeɛ Asiafoɛ Tihiko ne Trofimo.

english_verse: They went on ahead to Troas and waited for us there.
translation_verse: Bɛ de belili moa bɛɛnwondɛle yɛ wɔ Troase,

english_verse: After the Festival of Thin Bread, we sailed from Philippi. Five days later we met them in Troas and stayed there for a week. Paul's Last Visit to Troas
translation_verse: na yɛ koso de, Paanoo kabrɛdi aluolue ne pɛle nu ne, yɛfale ɛlɛen yɛfili Filipi, na ye elennu ne aso yɛɛtole bɛ wɔ Troase, na yɛlili berɛ ɛlɛsoo. Pɔɔlo kɔ Troase

english_verse: On the first day of the week we met to break bread together. Paul spoke to the people until midnight because he was leaving the next morning.
translation_verse: Kyẽa bɔ oli moa wɔ dapɛn ne anu ne, mmerɛ bɔ yɛyiale nu kyɛ yɛdidi ne, Pɔɔlo yɛle ngyerɛkyerɛ hyirele bɛ, na ɔtoale so alaa maa oodwuli abunnamu; ofikyɛ né aleɛ kye a, ɔkɔ.

english_verse: In the upstairs room where we were meeting, there were a lot of lamps.
translation_verse: Né nganea pee wɔ aborɔsaen ne aso nekaa bɔ yɛyiale ne.

english_verse: A young man by the name of Eutychus was sitting on a window sill. While Paul was speaking, the young man got very sleepy. Finally, he went to sleep and fell three floors all the way down to the ground. When they picked him up, he was dead.
translation_verse: Né aberandeɛ bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Yutiko te mboma noa, na ɔnate kyɛ Pɔɔlo dwudwo hyɛle ne ati, Yutiko tɔle ngosie, na nziɛ ye ɔlafele hatee; na ofili aborɔsaen bɔ ɔtɔ so nza ne aso te tɔle ase, na bɛɛpagyale ye nen, né wawu.

english_verse: Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.”
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo dwuli ase oobutuli ye so; ɔto brale ye, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Nnɛma ɛmɔ kunu tete ɛmɔ, na owwuli.”

english_verse: After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left.
translation_verse: Afei Pɔɔlo sa hɔle aborɔsaen ne aso, ɔfale nikyee kãa hane ye noa; na ɔtoale so dwudwole tonn ma aleɛ hyene, na ofili berɛ hɔle.

english_verse: Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy. The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
translation_verse: Afei bɛ ne aberandeɛ ne hɔle awuro bɔ né ye nwo asande ye ɔ, na benyane aworakyekyerɛ somaa. Pɔɔlo fi Troase kɔ Mileto

english_verse: Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there.
translation_verse: Yɛfale ɛlɛen yɛlili moa yɛhɔle Asɔso kyɛ yɛkwaafa Pɔɔlo wɔ berɛ, ofikyɛ né ɔne yɛ ahyehyɛ kyɛ ɔfa ase odi moa kɔ dɔ.

english_verse: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
translation_verse: Oyiale yɛ wɔ Asɔso nen, ɔfole ɛlɛen ne anu, na yɛtoale so yɛhɔle Mitilene.

english_verse: The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus.
translation_verse: Yɛfili berɛ, na aleɛ hyene ne, yɛdwuli Kiose ndendeneɛ so. Aleɛ sa hyene ne, yɛdwuli Samo na ye alehyeleɛ nu bieku ne, yɛdwuli Mileto.

english_verse: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost. Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
translation_verse: Né Pɔɔlo ayɛ ye adwene kyɛ ongogyina Ɛfeso amaa wanzɛkye mmerɛ wɔ Asia mbɔtam, ofikyɛ né ɔpe ndɛen kyɛ sɛ ɔkɔyɛ yee a, okodwu Yerusalem wɔ Pɛntekɔso kyẽa ne. Pɔɔlo ne Ɛfeso asɔre mbanyi di ngraa

english_verse: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo tole Ɛfeso asɔre mbanyi ne ngraa fili Mileto kyɛ bɛbra bɛbra.

english_verse: When they got there, he said: You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia.
translation_verse: Bɛwale ne, osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛmɔ bɔbɔ ɛmɔse kyɛbɔ ofi kyẽa bɔ mmale Asia me ne ɛmɔ yɛɛtenane ye, nzi mmɔle me bra mmerɛ biala ɔ.

english_verse: Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble.
translation_verse: Na mmrɛle me nwo ase mvale me nye moen nyɔle m’adwuma wɔ amaneɛ bɔ Yudafoɛ biemɔ bɔle me ti so porɛ maa nwuni ye ne anu.

english_verse: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
translation_verse: Yeɛ dwaaso ne ɛmɔ awuro nu nzɛmbahanɛ ne ngyerɛkyerɛ bɔ nyɔle ne, mangata nikyee biala bɔ ɔkɔboka ɛmɔ ɔ so;

english_verse: I told Jews and Gentiles to turn to God and have faith in our Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: na nnili adanzeɛ ngyirele Yudafoɛ ne Amaenmaensofoɛ kyɛ benya Nyameɛ nyunu adwenesakyera ne y’Awurade Yesu Kristo nu gyidie.

english_verse: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
translation_verse: Na kekesaala ye, ɔnate kyɛ mayɛ asoɛmmerɛlɛ mama Sunzum Krongron ne ati, mekɔ Yerusalem, na menze nikyee bɔ ɔkɔto me dɔ ɔ;

english_verse: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: sana bɔ Sunzum Krongron ne ahã ahyire me wɔ kuro biala so kyɛ mmenia kɔto me kuku nu na bamaa manwu amaneɛ ɔ.

english_verse: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Nakoso me de, memva he menyɛ hwee, yeɛ me ngoa koso memva menyɛ hwee; amaa ɔnate so mahora mafa anigye mayie me natelɛ ne Awurade Yesu asɛmbatrɛ adwuma bɔ ɔfa mane me kyɛ nni Nyameɛ adom nzɛmba ne nwo adanzeɛ ne.

english_verse: I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again.
translation_verse: “Na afei, ɛ́mɔtie. Mahyini ɛmɔ amukoraa so mahã Nyameɛ ahennie ne nwo dwirɛ, na kekesaala ye de, mese kyɛ ɛmɔ nu biala ngonwu me ko.

english_verse: I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you!
translation_verse: Ɛhe ati ɛnɛ kyẽa ye mekã mekyire ɛmɔ kyɛ, menni ɛmɔ nu biala mogya nwo fɔ;

english_verse: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
translation_verse: ɔnate kyɛ mamva nikyee biala bɔ ɔfa Nyameɛ nhyehyɛleɛ ne nwo mamvea ɛmɔ.

english_verse: Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
translation_verse: Yiti ɛ́mɔnea ɛmɔ nwo ne mmoaen amukoraa bɔ Sunzum Krongron afa bɛ awura ɛmɔ sa ne aso yé. Ɛ́mɔyɛ Nyameɛ asɔre ne bɔ ɔnate ye bɔbɔ Ɔwa ne mogya so nyane ye ne neafoɛ.

english_verse: I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you.
translation_verse: Na mese kyɛ mefi wa mekɔ a, mbataku awerɔm koowura ɛmɔ nu, na bɛngɔyakyi mmoaen ne koraa.

english_verse: Some of your own people will tell lies to win over the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Asa koso, ɛmɔ bɔbɔ bɛ nu mmenia ne bie kodwɔso ná baha ngondombo dwirɛ bafa bahwe agyidifoɛ ne bie bali bɛ si.

english_verse: Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
translation_verse: Yiti ɛmɔla ɛmɔ nwo so, na ɛ́mɔkaye kyɛ mvale me nye moen eyia ne kɔngɔen nduli ɛmɔ nu biala foɛ sɔ alaa afoɛ nza.

english_verse: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
translation_verse: “Afei, mefa ɛmɔ mewura Nyameɛ sa, ɔne ye adom dwirɛ ne anu; na adom dwirɛ ne yeɛ ɔkɔhora kɔma ɛmɔkonyi ná wama ɛmɔ agyapadeɛ bɔ wahyehyɛ wato berɛ wama anwoteefoɛ mukoraa ne ɔ.

english_verse: I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes.
translation_verse: Me nye ammoro ebiala dwetɛ anaa sikaa kɔkorɛ anaa ataadeɛ.

english_verse: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
translation_verse: Ɛmɔ bɔbɔ ɛmɔse kyɛ me sa noa adwuma yeɛ mva neane me nwo ne bɛ bɔ bɛboka me so ne ɔ.

english_verse: By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
translation_verse: Mahyire ɛmɔ wɔ nikyee biala nu kyɛ ɔsɛ kyɛ ɛmɔyɔ adwuma sɔa bɛfa bɛboka ehiafoɛ, ná ɛmɔma yɛkaye Awurade Yesu dwirɛ bɔ ɔhane ne. Ɔnwa: ‘Ɔte saleɛ pee kyɛ ɛkɔma tra kyɛ ekole ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
translation_verse: Na ye noa pene ne, obuli ndwerɛ ɔne bɛ mukoraa bɛbɔle mbaeɛ.

english_verse: Everyone cried and hugged and kissed him.
translation_verse: Na bɛ mukoraa bɛfale esuɛ bɛtotɔle ye nu bɛ ne ye lili ngraa;

english_verse: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
translation_verse: na bɔ ɔmane bɛ wora bɔle koraa ole ye dwirɛ bɔ ɔhane kyɛ bengonwu ye ko ne. Na afei beesomane ye ate bedwuli ɛlɛen ne anwo.

english_verse: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
translation_verse: Yɛne bɛ pakyepakyele nu yiele nen, yɛsili nu yɛfale nzue so yɛhɔle yɛ nyunu tee yɛwale Kɔse; na aleɛ hyene ne, yɛdwuli Worode na yɛfili berɛ yɛhɔle Patara.

english_verse: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
translation_verse: Yɛnwuni kyɛ ɛlɛen bie pɛ nu kɔ Fonikia, yiti yɛfo yɛhɔle.

english_verse: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
translation_verse: Yɛdwuli nekaa bie bɔ né yɛ nye tua supɔ Kipro, na yɛyakyili ye yɛ sa bɛen so yɛhɔle Siria. Yɛdwu yɛwale etii so wɔ Tiro, ofikyɛ né bɛye ɛlɛen ne anu nningyein begua berɛ.

english_verse: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
translation_verse: Nakoso yɛ ngyẽa bɔ yɛdi ye berɛ ne sone nen, yɛfili berɛ yɛtoale yɛ ateetulɛ ne aso. Bɛ mukoraa bɛ ne bɛ ye mɔ ne bɛ mma mɔ beesomane yɛ ate maa yɛfili kuro ne anu, na yɛkotole mboanoa berɛ yɛbɔle mbaeɛ yɛ ne yɛ nwo yɛ nwo lili ngraa.

english_verse: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
translation_verse: Afei yɛne bɛ lili ngraa, yɛfole ɛlɛen ne anu, na bɛ koso besa bɛhɔle awuro. Pɔɔlo kɔ Kaesarea

english_verse: We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day.
translation_verse: Yɛtoale so yɛfale nzue so fili Tiro yɛwale Tolema; yɛɛbisale berɛ agyidifoɛ ne ahye na yɛlili bɛ nwo berɛ ɛlɛho.

english_verse: The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles,
translation_verse: Na aleɛ hyene ne, yɛfili berɛ yɛwale Kaesarea. Yɛɛsikyele nzɛmbahanɛniɛ Filipo awuro. Né Filipo boka mmenia nzoo ne aso.

english_verse: and he had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
translation_verse: Né ole mmaa mmrasua nna. Bɛte mmabunu bɔ bɛhyɛ ngɔm ɔ.

english_verse: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
translation_verse: Yɛlili ngyẽa kãa berɛ, na ngɔmhyɛlɛniɛ bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Agabo fili Yudea wale.

english_verse: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Na ɔwale yɛ nwo berɛ ne, ɔfale Pɔɔlo abɔsoɛ ne kyekyele ye bɔbɔ ye gya ne ye sa, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Kyɛ Sunzum Krongron ne kã hɔ ɛhe: ‘Sona bɔ ye abɔsoɛ ɛhe ne, sɔ ala yeɛ Yudafoɛ kɔkyekye ye wɔ Yerusalem ná bafa ye bawura Amaenmaensofoɛ sa ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na yɛtele sɔ dwirɛ nen, yɛne Kaesarea agyidifoɛ ne srɛle Pɔɔlo kyɛ nnɛmaa ɔkɔ Yerusalem.

english_verse: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
translation_verse: Nakoso obuale yɛ kyɛ, “Na esuɛ ye koso ɛ? Bɔ bɛyɔ sɔ bɛma m’aba nu bu ye! Me de, nna kuku nu nnaa ngome yeɛ masiesie me nwo mama ɔ, na mmom kyɛ Awurade Yesu dumaa ti ngowu wɔ Yerusalem ɔ.”

english_verse: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
translation_verse: Yɛhane de, nakoso wambene; yiti yɛyakyili, na yɛhane kyɛ, “Awurade pɛ yeɛ ɔyɛ berɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Then we got ready to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Yɛlili ngyẽa kãa berɛ, na yɛboaboale yɛ nwo yɛhɔle Yerusalem.

english_verse: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
translation_verse: Kaesarea agyidifoɛ ne bie ne yɛ hɔle, na beesikyele yɛ wɔ Menason bɔ né yɛkwaatena ye berɛ n’awuro; ofi Kipro na né ɔte gyidiniɛ dadaada. Pɔɔlo kɔsra Yakobo wɔ Yerusalem

english_verse: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
translation_verse: Yɛdwuli Yerusalem nen, agyidifoɛ ne lele yɛ nyemene so.

english_verse: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, Pɔɔlo ne yɛ hɔle Yakobo awuro, na yɛɛtole asɔre mbanyi ne amu berɛ.

english_verse: Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo bisale bɛ ahye, na ɔhane nikyee bɔ Nyameɛ nate ye asɛmbatrɛ adwuma ne aso wayɔ wɔ Amaenmaensofoɛ nu ngoko ngoko hyirele bɛ.

english_verse: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Na bɛtele sɔ ne, bɛyele Nyameɛ ayɛ; na besele ye kyɛ, “Aliɛmaa Pɔɔlo, tie yɛ e! Yudafoɛ pembepembe wɔ wa bɔ bayɛ agyidifoɛ ɔ, na bɛ mukoraa basɔ Mose mmeraa ne anu serɛserɛ.

english_verse: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
translation_verse: Na ebiemɔ ahã ahyire bɛ kyɛ ekyirekyire Yudafoɛ amu bɔ bɛwɔ amaenmaen so ne kyɛ nnɛma bedi Mose mmeraa so; ɛnwa nnɛma bɛpɛ bɛ mma bienzua anaakyɛ bedi Yudafoɛ amanneɛ so.

english_verse: What should we do now that our people have heard you are here?
translation_verse: Yiti yɛkɔyɛ ye sɛ? Susu amba, kyɛbɔ ɔkɔyɛ biala bɛkɔte kyɛ awa.

english_verse: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
translation_verse: Bɔ yɛpena kyɛ ɛyɔ hɔ ɛhe. Yɛle mmienzua nna wɔ wa bɔ bahyɛ Nyameɛ bɔ ɔ.

english_verse: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Ɛne bɛ hɔ ná ɛmɔɔpete ɛmɔ nwo, ná tua kerɛ ma bɛ, ná afei bahora babɔ tikwa. Na ɛhe kɔma ebiala konwu ye kyɛ nahorɛ nne edwirɛ bɔ mmenia aha afa wɔ nwo ahyire bɛ ne anu; na mmom wɔ bɔbɔ koraa edi Mose mmeraa so.

english_verse: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: Nakoso Amaenmaensofoɛ bɔ bayɛ agyidifoɛ ne de, yahyerɛ krataa yaama bɛ, na yahyire bɛ y’adwene kyɛ nnɛma bedi bosoen so aleɛ biala, anaakyɛ mogya, anaa kaka biala bɔ wawu ye mogya nu, na afei bɛhwe bɛ nwo befi adwamanbɔlɛ nwo.”

english_verse: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
translation_verse: Yiti Pɔɔlo ne mmienzua nna nemɔ bɛhɔle, na aleɛ hyene ne, ɔne bɛ petene bɛ nwo. Na ɔhɔle asɔneyɛɛ sua ne anu ɔɔlale kyẽa bɔ bɛkɔpete bɛ nwo koyie, ná afei babɔ afɔleɛ bama ebiala ngoko ngoko ɔ ali. Bɛhyele Pɔɔlo wɔ Nyameɛ asɔneyɛɛ sua nu

english_verse: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
translation_verse: Na ɛlɛsoo bɔ bɛfa bɛpete bɛ nwo ne baaso nen, Yudafoɛ biemɔ bɔ befi Asia maen nu nwuni Pɔɔlo wɔ asɔneyɛɛ sua nu; yiti bɛsɛkyele ɛlɔen bɔ bayia berɛ n’adwene maa bɛhyele Pɔɔlo,

english_verse: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
translation_verse: na bɛteane nu kyɛ, “Yisraelfoɛ ee, ɛmɔbra oo, na sona bɔ ɔnate ɔyɛ ngyerɛkyerɛ kyire mmenia wɔ nekaa biala fa tia Yisraelfoɛ ne Mose mmeraa ne asɔneyɛɛ sua ne ɛhe oo! Na wasa wafa Helafoɛ po wawa asɔneyɛɛ sua ne anu waagua Nekaa Krongron ne nwo fiɛ.”

english_verse: Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
translation_verse: Né bali moa banwu Trofimo bɔ ofi Ɛfeso kyɛ ɔboka Pɔɔlo so wɔ kuro ne anu, yiti besusuli kyɛ Pɔɔlo afa ye ahɔ asɔneyɛɛ sua ne anu.

english_verse: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
translation_verse: Afei kuro ne anu amukoraa yɛle basabasa, na mmenia ne amukoraa betuli bi bele amirika bɛɛhyele Pɔɔlo bɛhwene ye befili asɔneyɛɛ sua ne anu; na berɛ ne ala bɛtotole anoa nemɔ nu.

english_verse: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ bɛyɛle kyɛ beku ye nen, Roman asraafoɛ panyi ne tele kyɛ basabasa asi Yerusalem.

english_verse: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
translation_verse: Na berɛ ne ala, ɔfale asraafoɛ mbanyi ne asraafoɛ ne bie, na bɛhane bɛ nwo bɛhɔle ɛlɔen ne anu. Na benwuni asraafoɛ panyi ne ne asraafoɛ nen, bɛyakyili Pɔɔlo bolɛ.

english_verse: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
translation_verse: Asraafoɛ panyi ne ɔɔsɔle Pɔɔlo nu na ɔmaa bɛfale ngɔnzɔngɔnzɔ nyɔ beguale ye, na afei obisale bɛ kyɛ, “Na nwa ɛhe? Wayɔ nzu?”

english_verse: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
translation_verse: Na mmenia ne bie teane nu hane edwirɛ he, yeɛ ebiemɔ koso teane nu hane edwirɛ foforɛ. Na basabasa ne ati, asraafoɛ panyi ne angora annwu nikyee pɔtee bɔ wasi ɔ, yiti ɔhyɛle kyɛ asraafoɛ nemɔ befa Pɔɔlo beewura nu wɔ b’adwuma nu dɔ.

english_verse: As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ odwuli ndweleɛ ne aso nen, bɛpagyale ye bɛhɔle anwuro, ɔnate kyɛ né ɛlɔen ne nye aboro paa.

english_verse: The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!” Paul Speaks to the Crowd
translation_verse: Na ɛlɔen ne tu lili ye si bɛteateane nu kyɛ, “Behu ye befi berɛ!” Pɔɔlo ye ye noa fa sa ye nwo

english_verse: When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?” “How do you know Greek?” the commander asked.
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ asraafoɛ ne yɛle kyɛ bɛfa Pɔɔlo bɛkɔ b’adwuma nu dɔ nen, osele asraafoɛ panyi ne kyɛ, “Aso mekora mekã edwirɛ kãa mekyire wɔ?” Na obuale kyɛ, “Ɛka Hela dwudwolɛ hɔ ɔ?

english_verse: “Aren't you that Egyptian who started a riot not long ago and led
translation_verse: Yiti nna wɔ ole Misraimniɛ bie bɔ ɛlɛsa ye ɔyɔle basabasa na ɔfale awudifoɛ amammɔyɛfoɛ apee nna tɔle ɛserɛ so dɔ ne?”

english_verse: “No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo buale kyɛ, “Nde Yudaniɛ, mvi Taaso bɔ ɔwɔ Kilikia, kuro bɔ bɔ wale dumaa so niɛ. Mmvi kuro nwunyanwunya so. Mesrɛ wɔ, maa ndwudwo ngyire ɛlɔen ne.”

english_verse: The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
translation_verse: Na asraafoɛ panyi ne mane ye ate, yiti Pɔɔlo gyinane ndweleɛ ne aso, na ɔmane ye sa so bobole ɛlɔen ne. Na berɛ yɛle dinn ne, odwudwo hyirele bɛ wɔ Hebri dwudwolɛ nu kyɛ,

english_verse: When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
translation_verse: Mmerɛ bɔ bɛtele kyɛ ɔkã Hebri dwudwolɛ kyire bɛ ne, bɛyɛle konn paa, na osele bɛ kyɛ,

english_verse: I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
translation_verse: “Nde Yudaniɛ, bɛwole me Taaso bɔ ɔwɔ Kilikia manzini nu. Bɛtetele me wɔ kuro ye anu, na Gamaliɛl yeɛ ohyirele me nikye ɔ. Ɔfale yɛ nana mɔ mmeraa ne hyirele me nikyee pɛpɛɛpɛ, na nduli me nwo nziele berɛ mane Nyameɛ kyɛbɔ ɛnɛ ye ɛmɔ amukoraa bɛyɔ ne.

english_verse: I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women.
translation_verse: Ndanene bɛ bɔ beli Atee he si nye maa behuni bɛ. Ngyekyele mmienzua ne mmrasua maa bɛfale bɛ beguale kuku nu,

english_verse: The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
translation_verse: na ɔsɔfo panyi paa ɔne badwafoɛ ne amu di me adanzeɛ. Nyane tumi ngrataa mvili bɛ berɛ kyɛ mekwaafa mema me mmango Yudafoɛ bɔ bɛwɔ Damasko. Yiti nzili nu kyɛ mekwaahye berɛ agyidifoɛ na mefa bɛ meba Yerusalem maa bɛtwe bɛ so. Pɔɔlo ka kyɛbɔ osi yɛle gyidiniɛ ɔ (Asomafoɛ

english_verse: One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
translation_verse: “Na mbene atee so bɔ mekɔ na mbingyele Damasko nen, kɔyɛ eyiagyina mmerɛ ne, mvum nu, kanea totohyia bie fili nyameɛso ɔɔtale me nwo bra yiale.

english_verse: I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
translation_verse: Mbɛ mvini, na ndele kyɛ ebie dwudwo kyire me kyɛ, ‘Sɔɔlo, Sɔɔlo, nzu ati yeɛ ɛtane me nye ye?’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I answered. The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.”
translation_verse: Na mmisale kyɛ, ‘Wɔ nwa ɛne, Awurade?’ Na osele me kyɛ, ‘Me ole Yesu bɔ ofi Nasarɛte bɔ ɛtane ye nye ne.’

english_verse: Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
translation_verse: Mmenia bɔ né bɛboka me so ne nwuni kanea ne, , nakoso bande bɔ né ɔne me dwudwo ne komvi.

english_verse: I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?” Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.”
translation_verse: Na mmisale kyɛ, ‘Awurade, nzikyɛ yeɛ nyɔ ɔ?’ Na Awurade sele me kyɛ, ‘Dwɔso na kɔ Damasko, na berɛ yeɛ bɛkɔhã nikyee biala bɔ Nyameɛ ahyehyɛ kyɛ ɛyɔ bekohyire wɔ ɔ.’

english_verse: The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
translation_verse: Kyɛbɔ kanea ne si tale ne mane me nye sini, yiti bɛ bɔ né bɛboka me so ne sosɔle me sa fale me hɔle Damasko.

english_verse: In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there.
translation_verse: “Né biaa bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Anania, bɔ ɔte nyamesuroniɛ paa kyɛbɔ yɛ mmeraa si te ɔ wɔ kuro berɛ. Yudafoɛ mukoraa bɔ ye dumaa paa.

english_verse: He came to me and said, “Saul, my friend, you can now see again!” At once I could see.
translation_verse: Oogyinane me nwo berɛ sele me kyɛ, ‘Aliɛmaa Sɔɔlo, sa nwu nikye!’ Berɛ ne ala, nza nwuni nikye, na nwuni ye.

english_verse: Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice.
translation_verse: Na ɔhane kyɛ, ‘Yɛ nana mɔ Nyameɛ ne, waneanea nu waye wɔ kyɛ enwu ye apɛdeɛ, ná enwu ye Teneneeniɛ ne, na ɛte ye bɔbɔ ye noa nu dwirɛ,

english_verse: You must tell everyone what you have seen and heard.
translation_verse: ɔnate kyɛ ɛkɔyɛ ye danzeniɛ nã ahã bɔ anwu ye ne bɔ ate ne ahyire mmenia mukoraa.

english_verse: What are you waiting for? Get up! Be baptized, and wash away your sins by praying to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na afei, nzu ati yeɛ ɛyɛ ngyɛkyerɛ ɔ? Dwɔso nya Awurade nu gyidie, na ma bɛbɔ wɔ asu benwunzi wɔ bɔne begua.’ Pɔɔlo ka nzɛmba kyire Amaenmaensofoɛ

english_verse: After this I returned to Jerusalem and went to the temple to pray. There I had a vision
translation_verse: “Na ɔwale kyɛ nza male Yerusalem ná mebɔ mbaeɛ wɔ asɔneyɛɛ sua nu ne, ngɔle nyekyire tebea nu.

english_verse: of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
translation_verse: Nwuni Awurade, na osele me kyɛ, ‘Ma wɔ nwo yɛ nyera ná fi Yerusalem, ofikyɛ bengole w’adanzeɛ bɔ ekoli kɔfa me nwo ne ngɔto nu.’

english_verse: I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you.
translation_verse: Na me koso mmuale kyɛ, ‘Awurade, bɛse ye pefee kyɛ ngɔngyekyele bɛ bɔ bede wɔ bedi ne nguale kuku nu, na mmole bɛ wɔ nyianu sua biala nu.

english_verse: Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ behwie w’adanzeniɛ Setefano mogya begua ne, né me koso nwɔ berɛ bie, mbenene ye hunɛ ne aso, na nneane bɛ bɔ behuni ye ne ndaadeɛ so mane bɛ.’

english_verse: But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Na Awurade sele me kyɛ, ‘Kɔ, na ngɔsoma wɔ dedeede maa ɛkɔhɔ Amaenmaensofoɛ berɛ.’ ” Pɔɔlo ne Rome safohene ne

english_verse: The crowd listened until Paul said this. Then they started shouting, “Get rid of this man! He doesn't deserve to live.”
translation_verse: Ɛlɔen ne tiele Pɔɔlo tonn maa oodwuli edwirɛ he aso, na afei bɛteateane nu kyɛ, “Behu sɔ akoaa he befi aseɛ ye aso! Ɔnate kyɛ ɔmvata kyɛ ɔtena ase ɔ.”

english_verse: They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air. Paul and the Roman Army Commander
translation_verse: Na bɛteatea nu benwunya bɛ ndaadeɛ, ná bɛto mvuture bɛkɔ anwuro ne,

english_verse: The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
translation_verse: Roman safohene ne mane ye asraafoɛ nemɔ bɛfale Pɔɔlo bɛhɔle b’adwuma nu dɔ, na ɔhyɛle kyɛ befi ye mbire ma ɔha nikye horɛ bɔ yiti yeɛ batu bɛ noa bagua ye so sɔ ne.

english_verse: While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ bɛ́fa nyamaa bɛ́kyekye Pɔɔlo ne, obisale asraafoɛ ɛyaa so panyi bɔ ogyi ye nwo berɛ ne kyɛ, “Aso mmeraa ma ate kyɛ ɛmɔkofi ebie bɔ ɔte Romanniɛ mbire wɔ aberɛ bɔ bellili ye dwirɛ bebbuale ye foɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
translation_verse: Na asraafoɛ ɛyaa so panyi ne tele sɔ dwirɛ nen, ɔhɔle safohene ne berɛ oobisale ye kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ nikye yeɛ ɛbaayɔ e? Sɔ biaa he te Romanniɛ!”

english_verse: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
translation_verse: Yiti safohene ne wale Pɔɔlo nwo berɛ oobisale ye kyɛ, “Ɛte Romanniɛ anaa? Ka kyire me!” Na obuale kyɛ, “Yoo.”

english_verse: The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.” But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ safohene ne hane kyɛ, “Nduale sikaa piri paa koraa yeɛ mebaayɛ Romanniɛ ɔ.” Na Pɔɔlo koso buale kyɛ, “Me de, bɛfa bɛwole me.”

english_verse: The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains. Paul Is Tried by the Council
translation_verse: Na berɛ ne ala, bɛ bɔ ahaa bɛbaatie ye noa dwirɛ ne, bɛhwene bɛ nwo befili ye nwo berɛ; na safohene ne koso nwuni kyɛ Pɔɔlo te Romanniɛ ná koso wakyekye ye nen, osurole. Pɔɔlo gyi Yuda badwa nyunu

english_verse: The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.
translation_verse: Né safohene ne pena kyɛ onwu nikye horɛ bɔ Yudafoɛ nwa Pɔɔlo ayɔ ɔ. Yiti aleɛ hyene ne, ɔmaa bɛsangyele ngɔnzɔngɔnzɔ bɔ bafa bagua ye ne, na ɔhyɛle asɔfo mbanyi ne bɛ badwafoɛ ne amu maa beyiale, na ɔfale Pɔɔlo oogyinane bɛ nyunu berɛ.

english_verse: Paul looked straight at the council members and said, “My friends, to this day I have served God with a clear conscience!”
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo tole ye nye neane badwafoɛ ne haa na osele kyɛ, “Aliɛmaa mɔ, me tiboa mmua me foɛ wɔ me bra bɔ mabɔ wɔ Nyameɛ nyunu tonn maa waadwu ɛnɛ ye nwo.”

english_verse: Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth.
translation_verse: Na ɔsɔfo panyi paa Anania hyɛle bɛ bɔ begyigyi Pɔɔlo nwo berɛ ne kyɛ befi ye noa so.

english_verse: Paul turned to the high priest and said, “You whitewashed wall! God will hit you. You sit there to judge me by the Law of Moses. But at the same time you order men to break the Law by hitting me.”
translation_verse: Yeɛ Pɔɔlo koso sele ye kyɛ, “Wɔ yeɛ Nyameɛ kɔbɔ wɔ ɔ. Wɔ, fasue bɔ bahã ye nwo fufue ɔ! Wɔ yeɛ ɛte berɛ egyina mmeraa ne aso ebua me ndɛen ɔ, nakoso wɔ wora ebu mmeraa ne aso ɛhyɛ kyɛ bɛbɔ me!”

english_verse: The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
translation_verse: Na bɛ bɔ begyigyi berɛ ne sele ye kyɛ, “Yiti Nyameɛ sɔfo panyi paa yeɛ ɛwɔ ye safure ye?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo buale kyɛ, “Aliɛmaa mɔ Yisraelfoɛ, né menze kyɛ ɔte ɔsɔfo panyi paa ɔ; ofikyɛ bahyerɛ kyɛ, ‘Ɔnzɛ kyɛ ɛkã wɔ maen panyi nwo dwirɛ tɛɛ ɔ.’ ”

english_verse: When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
translation_verse: Na mmerɛ bɔ Pɔɔlo nwuni kyɛ mmenia ne bue bɛte Sadusiifoɛ, ná bɛ bue koso bɛte Farasiifoɛ nen, ɔteane nu wɔ badwa ne anu kyɛ, “Aliɛmaa mɔ, nde Farasiiniɛ, Farasiifoɛ awa; na ɔnate awufoɛ etingyelɛ ne ye nwo anyelasoɛ ti yeɛ bébua me ndɛen ye”

english_verse: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.
translation_verse: Na ɔhane sɔ dwirɛ ne pɛ, edwudwolɛ wale Farasiifoɛ ne Sadusiifoɛ nemɔ b’afia, na mmenia ne anu hyɛle nyɔ.

english_verse: The Sadducees do not believe in angels or spirits or that the dead will rise to life. But the Pharisees believe in all of these,
translation_verse: Ɔnate kyɛ Sadusiifoɛ ne nwa awufoɛ dwɔsolɛ anaa abɔfo anaa sunzum biala nne berɛ; nakoso Farasiifoɛ ne de, bede ye mukoraa bedi.

english_verse: and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
translation_verse: Bɛteateane nu serɛserɛ, na ahyerɛlɛfoɛ biemɔ bɔ bɛwɔ Farasiifoɛ fekue ne anu bedwɔso bedwudwole anyeborolɛ so kyɛ, “Yɛnnwu bɔne biala wɔ sɔ biaa he nwo. Ebie po a, né sunzum anaa abɔfo bie yeɛ odwudwo hyirele ye ɔ. Nnɛmɔma yɛko yɛtia Nyameɛ!”

english_verse: The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
translation_verse: Afei ɛtealɛ ne hɔle so serɛserɛ maa safohene ne surole kyɛ bɛkɔtete Pɔɔlo nu pasapasa koraa. Yiti ɔhyɛle ye asraafoɛ nemɔ kyɛ bedwu bɛhɔ mmenia ne anu dɔ beefoti ye befi bɛ sa nu, ná bɛfa ye bɛhɔ b’adwuma nu dɔ.

english_verse: That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.” A Plot To Kill Paul
translation_verse: Sɔ kɔngɔen ne, Awurade wale oogyinane Pɔɔlo nwo berɛ sele ye kyɛ, “Nnɛsuro! Na kyɛbɔ ali me nwo adanzeɛ wɔ Yerusalem nen, sɔ ala koso yeɛ odi kyɛ edi me nwo adanzeɛ wɔ Rome ɔ.” Yudafoɛ biemɔ bɔ Pɔɔlo ti so porɛ

english_verse: The next morning more than
translation_verse: Mmenia bɔ bɛbɔle sɔ porɛ ne bɛbo aburanna.

english_verse: Then some of them went to the chief priests and the nation's leaders and said, “We have promised God that we would not eat a thing until we have killed Paul.
translation_verse: Na bɛhɔle asɔfo mbanyi ne maen mbanyi nemɔ berɛ beesele bɛ kyɛ, “Yata ndaen kyɛ ɛhwee ngɔhã yɛ noa, sana yahu Pɔɔlo koraa.

english_verse: You and everyone in the council must go to the commander and pretend that you want to find out more about the charges against Paul. Ask for him to be brought before your court. Meanwhile, we will be waiting to kill him before he gets there.”
translation_verse: Yiti ɛmɔ ne badwafoɛ ne bɛbɔ nu bɛsoma ma beese Roman safohene ne kyɛ ɔma bɛfa Pɔɔlo bɛbrɛ ɛmɔ; kyɛ ɛmɔpena kyɛ ɛmɔneanea ye dwirɛ ne anu yé. Na yɛ de, kyɛ ɔyɛ na oodwu wa ne, né yahu ye dadaada.”

english_verse: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it.
translation_verse: Nakoso Pɔɔlo awosea bienzua tele kyɛ bɛkwaatɛ ye atunu; yiti ɔhɔle asraafoɛ nemɔ b’adwuma nu berɛ ɔɔbɔle Pɔɔlo amaneɛ.

english_verse: So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo frɛle asraafoɛ mbanyi ne ko sele ye kyɛ, “Fa sɔ aberandeɛ ye kɔ safohene ne berɛ, na ole dwirɛ kã kyire ye.”

english_verse: The officer took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner named Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.”
translation_verse: Yiti ɔfale aberandeɛ ne hɔle safohene ne berɛ, na ɔhane kyɛ, “Kukununiɛ Pɔɔlo frɛle me srɛle me kyɛ mva sɔ aberandeɛ ye mmra wɔ berɛ, na ole dwirɛ kã kyire wɔ.”

english_verse: The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
translation_verse: Na safohene ne sɔle aberandeɛ ne sa fale ye hɔle ahameɛ, na obisale ye kyɛ, “Nzikyɛ dwirɛ yeɛ ele ye kã kyire me ɔ?”

english_verse: He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him.
translation_verse: Na obuale kyɛ, “Yudafoɛ abɔ porɛ kyɛ bɛkɔɔsrɛ wɔ maa ɛhema ɛkɔfa Pɔɔlo kɔbrɛ badwafoɛ ne, kyɛ bɛkwaaneanea ye dwirɛ ne anu yé.

english_verse: The commander sent the young man away after saying to him, “Don't let anyone know you told me this.” Paul Is Sent to Felix the Governor
translation_verse: Na safohene ne hyɛle aberandeɛ ne kyɛ, “Nnɛbɔ so kyire ebiala kyɛ aha sɔ dwirɛ ne ahyire me!” Na afei ɔmaa ɔhɔle. Bɛfale Pɔɔlo bɛɛmane amrado Felise

english_verse: Get a horse ready for Paul and make sure he gets safely through to Felix the governor.”
translation_verse: Ɛ́mɔsiesie mbɔngɔ bɛ́ma Pɔɔlo, ná ɛ́mɔbɔ ye nwo waen bɛɛfa ye bɛma amrado Felise.”

english_verse: The commander wrote a letter that said:
translation_verse: Na safohene ne hyerɛle sɔ krataa he maa bɛhɔle:

english_verse: Greetings from Claudius Lysias to the Honorable Governor Felix:
translation_verse: “Me, Klɔdio Lisia yeɛ mekyerɛ krataa he mebrɛ Daasebrɛ amrado Felise ɔ; mebisa wɔ.

english_verse: Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
translation_verse: Yudafoɛ hyele sɔ biaa he, na ɔhale kãa bie maa behuni ye. Ndele kyɛ ɔte Romanniɛ, yiti me ne asraafoɛ nemɔ yɛhɔle berɛ yɛɛpepɛ yɛlele ye.

english_verse: I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council
translation_verse: Né mepena kyɛ menwu nikye horɛ bɔ bɛnwa wayɔ ɔ, yiti mvale ye ngɔle bɛ badwafoɛ nemɔ nyunu.

english_verse: and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
translation_verse: Nakoso nwuni kyɛ ɔyyɔle nikyee biala bɔ ɔfata ehunɛ anaakyɛ kuku nu tolɛ ɔ; na mmom bɛ bɔbɔ bɛ mmeraa nwo yeɛ babɔ ye kwaadu ɔ.

english_verse: As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
translation_verse: Afei ndele ye nwo bie kyɛ babɔ ye ti so porɛ bɔ bɛpena ye beku ye ɔ. Ɛhe ati nyɛle m’adwene berɛ ne ala kyɛ bɛfa ye bɛbrɛ wɔ; na mahã mahyire ye kwaadubɔlɛfoɛ nemɔ kyɛ bɛbra wɔ nyunu bɛɛbɔ ye kwaadu.”

english_verse: The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris.
translation_verse: Na kyɛbɔ safohene ne hyɛle asraafoɛ nen, bɛfale Pɔɔlo kɔngɔen ne bɛ ne ye hɔle tonn beedwuli Antipatri.

english_verse: The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, asraafoɛ bɔ bɛnate ase ne sa wale b’adwuma nu; na bɛyakyili pɔngɔhanɛfoɛ nemɔ maa bɛ ne Pɔɔlo toale so bɛhɔle.

english_verse: When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
translation_verse: Bɛ ne ye hɔle beedwuli Kaesarea, bɛyele krataa ne bɛmane amrado ne, na bɛfale Pɔɔlo koso bewurale ye sa.

english_verse: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
translation_verse: Amrado ne kengale krataa ne, na obisale Pɔɔlo manzini horɛ bɔ ofi nu ɔ. Na ɔtele kyɛ ofi Kilikia nen,

english_verse: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
translation_verse: ɔhane kyɛ, “Sɛ wɔ kwaadubɔlɛfoɛ nemɔ bɛba a, yeɛ ngotie wɔ noa dwirɛ ɔ.” Na ɔhyɛle kyɛ bɛfa Pɔɔlo besie Herode ahemvie ne anu.

english_verse: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
translation_verse: Ye elennu ne aso, ɔsɔfo panyi paa Anania ne maen mbanyi ne kyeame bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Tɛtulo wale Kaesarea, na bɛfale Pɔɔlo nwo dwirɛ bɛtole amrado Felise nyunu.

english_verse: So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him: Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off.
translation_verse: Bɛfrɛle Pɔɔlo maa ɔwale, na Tɛtulo hyɛle ye bo bɔle ye kwaadu kyɛ, “Daasebrɛ Felise, ɔnate kyɛ w’adaworoma yanya asomdwee paa, ná asa koso ɔnate wɔ ti mbonduo adwuma pee kɔ so bɔ ɔpagya maen ye ɔ ne ati,

english_verse: All of us are always grateful for what you have done.
translation_verse: Daasebrɛ Felise, daa yɛ nye sɔ bɔ ayɔ ne amu wɔ nekaa biala, na yɛyɛ wɔ mmo.

english_verse: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
translation_verse: Na kyɛbɔ ɔkɔyɛ na manzɛkye wɔ mmerɛ ne ati, mesrɛ wɔ ala, wɔ adaworoma, tie yɛ kãa bie.

english_verse: This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes.
translation_verse: Yanwu kyɛ sɔ akoaa he te busueniɛ bɔ ɔbɔ maen ɔ. Ɔfa manzoen toto Yudafoɛ amukoraa bɔ bɛwɔ ewiase amukoraa b’afia, na ye yeɛ ɔte Nasarɛtefoɛ fekue ne aso panyi ɔ.

english_verse: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
translation_verse: Na ɔhyɛle kyɛ ye kwaadubɔlɛfoɛ nemɔ bɛbra wɔ nyunu. Na sɛ wɔ bɔbɔ ebisa akoaa he tie ye noa dwirɛ a, ekonwu nikyee bɔ yiti yabɔ ye kwaadu ne.”

english_verse: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
translation_verse: Na Yudafoɛ nemɔ foale ye dwirɛ ne aso kyɛ ɔte nahorɛ. Pɔɔlo sa ye nwo wɔ amrado Felise nyunu

english_verse: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
translation_verse: Amrado ne yɛle kyɛ Pɔɔlo dwudwo, na obuale kyɛ, “Mese kyɛ ɛyɛle maen he aso ndɛenbualɛniɛ ɔ, afoɛ pee awa; yiti ɔyɛ me fɛ kyɛ ngyi wɔ nyunu meye me noa ɔ.

english_verse: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
translation_verse: Na kyɛbɔ wɔ bɔbɔ ɛse ne, eleburu ne nyɔ ɛhe yeɛ ngɔle Yerusalem kyɛ mekwaasɔne Nyameɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself.
translation_verse: Bannwu me kyɛ me ne ebiala yɛsu aporowaa wɔ asɔneyɛɛ sua ne anu, anaakyɛ metu mmenia foɛ tɛɛ wɔ nyianu sua nemɔ nu, anaa kuro ne anu.

english_verse: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
translation_verse: Yeɛ koso belle ɛsoentolɛ he nwo adanzeɛ biala benni bengyire wɔ.

english_verse: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
translation_verse: Na ɛhe de, mede meto nu wɔ wɔ nyunu kyɛ, Atee bɔ bɛnwa ɔte ngondombo atee ne yeɛ mefa so mesɔne yɛ nana mɔ Nyameɛ ɔ. Yeɛ mede nikyee biala bɔ bahyerɛ ye wɔ Mose mmeraa ne ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ nwomaa ne anu medi.

english_verse: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
translation_verse: Na anyelasoɛ komapɛ bɔ ɔla berɛ ma me wɔ Nyameɛ nu kyɛ mmenia mukoraa, teneneefoɛ ne bɔnefoɛ, kodwɔso kofi awufoɛ nu ne koso ala yeɛ ɔla berɛ ma bɛ ɔ.

english_verse: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
translation_verse: Ɛhe ati, mmerɛ biala mebɔ mmɔden kyɛ me tiboa ngobua me foɛ wɔ Nyameɛ ne kuro sona nyunu ɔ.

english_verse: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: “Na afei afoɛ pee asi, mmale kyɛ mebaayɛ me maen adɔeɛ ná mebɔ afɔleɛ mema Nyameɛ.

english_verse: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
translation_verse: Na nwɔ ɛhe aso bɔ meyɔ, wɔ mmerɛ bɔ mepete me nwo ne, yeɛ Yudafoɛ biemɔ bɔ befi Asia manzini nu nwuni me wɔ asɔneyɛɛ sua ne anu ɔ. Né ɛlɔen biala ɔbboka me so; yeɛ afei né basabasa biala nne berɛ.

english_verse: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
translation_verse: Na sɔ mmenia nemɔ yeɛ odi kyɛ ahaa bɛba wɔ nyunu wa, na sɛ bele me nwo dwirɛ bie a, babɔ me kwaadu.

english_verse: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
translation_verse: Anaakyɛ ma mmenia bɔ bɛwɔ wa kekesaala ye bɛha bɔne horɛ bɔ badwafoɛ ne nwuni ye me nwo wɔ bɛ nyunu ɔ;

english_verse: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
translation_verse: sana nikyee komapɛ bɔ ngyinane bɛ nyunu berɛ ndeane nu ngane ɔ, kyɛ, ‘Awufoɛ ewutingyelɛ nwo yeɛ ɛmɔbua me ndɛen ɛnɛ ye.’ ”

english_verse: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
translation_verse: Né Felise le Atee ne nwo nimdeɛ paa, yiti ɔmaa besale bɛ si, na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Sɛ safohene Lisia ba a, yeɛ ngɔnea ngoli ɛmɔ dwirɛ ne ɔ.”

english_verse: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
translation_verse: Afei osele asraafoɛ panyi bɔ Pɔɔlo wura ye sa ne kyɛ ɔfa ye sie, yeɛ nnɛmaa ɔyɔ ye nikyee biala; na sɛ ye nwo sona bie ba kyɛ ɔbaasra ye a, nnɛmaa besi ye ate. Felise ne Drusila tie Pɔɔlo noa dwirɛ

english_verse: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
translation_verse: Ngyẽa kãa bie asi ne, Felise ne ɔye Yudaniɛ bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Drusila bɛwale. Felise somane maa bɛɛfale Pɔɔlo bɛwale, na ɔmaa ɔhane Kristo Yesu nu gyidie nwo dwirɛ maa otiele.

english_verse: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo wɔ so bɔ ɔkã tenenee ne anwohyɛsoɛ ne ndɛenbualɛ kyẽa bɔ ɔbaawa ne nwo dwirɛ nen, Felise kunu tetele ye, na osele ye kyɛ, “Kekesaala ye de, kɔ; na sɛ menya ye nwo a, ngɔmaa bɛkɔɔfrɛ wɔ bieku.”

english_verse: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
translation_verse: Né ye nye la so kyɛ Pɔɔlo kɔma ye sikaa ná wayakyi ye, yiti né ɔtaa soma maa bɛkɔɔfrɛ ye maa ɔne ye bɛbɔ ngɔmɔ.

english_verse: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_verse: Afoɛ nyɔ asi ne, Pɔkio Festo sili amrado Felise gya nu. Né Felise pena kyɛ ɔyɔ nikyee ma Yudafoɛ ne nye sɔ, yiti ɔmaa Pɔɔlo hale kuku nu berɛ.

english_verse: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Festo wale manzini ne anu ne, ye ɛlɛsa ne aso ofili Kaesarea hɔle Yerusalem.

english_verse: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
translation_verse: Na asɔfo mbanyi ne Yuda mbanyi toatoale Pɔɔlo behyirele ye,

english_verse: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
translation_verse: na bɛsrɛle ye kyɛ ɔlo bɛ ná ɔsoma ma bɛfa Pɔɔlo bɛbra Yerusalem; ɔnate kyɛ né babɔ porɛ kyɛ bɛkɔtɛ ye atunu bekohu ye.

english_verse: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
translation_verse: Na Festo buale bɛ kyɛ, “Pɔɔlo la kuku nu wɔ Kaesarea, na me bɔbɔ po ɔngɔhyɛ ngosa ngɔhɔ dɔ.

english_verse: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
translation_verse: Yiti ɛ́mɔma ɛmɔ nu mbanyi nemɔ ne me hɔ Kaesarea, na sɛ akoaa ne ayɔ bɔne bie a, babɔ ye kwaadu.”

english_verse: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
translation_verse: Festo lili ɛlɛbɔtwɛ bɔ ɔkɔ eleburu wɔ Yerusalem, na afei osa hɔle Kaesarea. Aleɛ hyene ne, ɔɔtenane ye ndɛenbualɛ bia nu, na ɔmaa bɛɛfale Pɔɔlo bɛwale.

english_verse: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo wale ne, Yudafoɛ bɔ befili Yerusalem bɛwale ne, bɛpɛle ye nwo kango, na bɛpepɛle edwirɛ mbirikua pee beguale ye so, bɔ bɛ bɔbɔ po bangora bangyire nu ɔ.

english_verse: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
translation_verse: Nakoso Pɔɔlo sale ye nwo kyɛ, “Nnyɔle hwee nndiale Yudafoɛ mmeraa, anaa asɔneyɛɛ sua ne, anaa Roman hene Kaesare.”

english_verse: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
translation_verse: Nakoso né Festo kuro kyɛ ɔyɔ nikyee ma Yudafoɛ nemɔ nye sɔ, yiti obisale Pɔɔlo kyɛ, “Ekuro kyɛ ɛkɔ Yerusalem ɛkɔye kwaadu hemɔ noa wɔ me nyunu wɔ dɔ anaa?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo buale ye kyɛ, “Ngyi Kaesare bɔbɔ deinn ye kɔɔto, na ɛwa yeɛ ɔsɛ kyɛ bedi me dwirɛ ɔ. Na kyɛbɔ wɔ bɔbɔ ɛse ne, nnyɔle Yudafoɛ bɔne biala.

english_verse: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
translation_verse: Na sɛ mabu mmeraa ne aso, anaa mayɔ nikyee bɔ ɔfata ewue hɔ a, menzrɛ kyɛ nnɛma beku me. Nakoso sɛ nahorɛ biala nne kwaadu bɔ bafa babɔ me ne anu de a, ye de ebiala ngɔhora ngɔye me ngɔma bɛ. Yiti mefa me dwirɛ meto Kaesare nyunu.”

english_verse: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
translation_verse: Festo ne ye badwafoɛ hane bɛ ti purale, na obuale kyɛ, “Sɛ afa wɔ dwirɛ ato Kaesare nyunu de a, nzaade ɛkɔhɔ Kaesare dɔ.” Festo bɔ Nana Agripa amaneɛ

english_verse: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
translation_verse: Na ngyẽa kãa bie asi ne, Nana Agripa ne Bɛnise bɛwale Kaesarea kyɛ bɛbaasra Festo ná bɛyɛ ye akwaaba.

english_verse: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
translation_verse: Belili ngyẽa dɔnn wɔ berɛ ne, Festo fale Pɔɔlo nwo dwirɛ tole ɛhene ne nyunu kyɛ, “Biaa bie wɔ wa bɔ Felise yakyili ye kuku nu ɔ.

english_verse: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
translation_verse: Ngɔle Yerusalem nen, Yuda asɔfo mbanyi ne maen mbanyi bɔle ye kwaadu hyirele me, na bɛsrɛle me kyɛ mmua ye foɛ.

english_verse: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
translation_verse: Na me koso mmuale bɛ kyɛ, ɔtte yɛ Romanfoɛ mmeraa kyɛ yɛkɔye sona biala bɔ babɔ ye kwaadu kɔmaa bekohu ye ɔ; sana ɔne ye kwaadubɔlɛfoɛ nemɔ beyia bɛbɔ nguro, ná onya atee ye ye noa koraa.

english_verse: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
translation_verse: Ɛhe ati bɛwale wa nen, mammobɔ edwirɛ ne mando berɛ. Na aleɛ hyene ne, ndenane ase wɔ kɔɔto berɛ, na nyɛle kyɛ bɛfa biaa ne bɛbra.

english_verse: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
translation_verse: Ye kwaadubɔlɛfoɛ nemɔ dwɔsole, na bammɔ ye kwaadu biala wɔ nzɛmmɔne bɔ nzusuli kyɛ wali ne nwo;

english_verse: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
translation_verse: na mmom bɛ bɔbɔ bɛ nyamesom nwo aporowaa, ɔne Yesu bie bɔ wawu nakoso Pɔɔlo nwa ɔte ase nwo aporowaa yeɛ bɛ ne ye suli ɔ.

english_verse: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
translation_verse: Né mengora menwu atee horɛ bɔ mva so nneanea sɔ dwirɛ he anu ɔ. Yiti mmisale Pɔɔlo sɛ ebiaa okuro kyɛ ɔkɔ Yerusalem maa bekodi ye dwirɛ ne wɔ dɔ anaa.

english_verse: But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
translation_verse: Nakoso Pɔɔlo srɛle kyɛ bɛ́fa ye bésie, ná bɛ́fa edwirɛ ne bɛhɔ Kaesare nyunu mmom. Yiti mamaa bafa ye basie kodwu kyɛ ngɔmaa bɛ ne ye kɔhɔ Kaesare berɛ ɔ.”

english_verse: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Na Nana Agripa sele Festo kyɛ, “Mekuro kyɛ me bɔbɔ deinn metie biaa he noa dwirɛ.” Na obuale kyɛ, “Ɛhema né atie ye noa dwirɛ.” Pɔɔlo gyi Agripa ne Bɛnise nyunu

english_verse: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
translation_verse: Yiti aleɛ hyene ne, Nana Agripa ne Bɛnise hyehyɛle bɛ nwo wale ahomeka nu, na bɛ ne asraafoɛ mbanyi ne kuro ne anu mmenia titire hɔle nekaa bɔ bedi dwirɛ ne; na Festo maa bɛɛfale Pɔɔlo bɛwale.

english_verse: and said: King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death.
translation_verse: Festo hane kyɛ, “Nana Agripa ne ɛmɔ bɔ bayia wa mukoraa, ɛmɔanwu biaa he? Yudafoɛ amukoraa afa ye nwo dwirɛ ato me nyunu wɔ Yerusalem ne ɛwa, na bɛnwa ɔnzɛ kyɛ ɔtena ngoa nu ko ɔ.

english_verse: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
translation_verse: Nakoso, menea a, ɔyyɔle nikye fee bɔ ɔfata ewue ɔ. Na kyɛbɔ ye bɔbɔ ɔnwa bɛfa edwirɛ ne bɛhɔ Kaesare gya so ne ati, mayɛ kyɛ memaa bɛfa ye bɛkɔ.

english_verse: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
translation_verse: Nakoso mennwu edwirɛ pɔtee bɔ ngyina so ngyerɛ mva ye nwo ngɔma me mene Kaesare ɔ. Yiti mafa ye mawa ɛmɔ nyunu wa, ye titire, wɔ Nana Agripa nyunu; amaa sɛ yɛneanea ye dwirɛ ne anu a, manya edwirɛ bie mahyerɛ.

english_verse: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_verse: Ɔnate kyɛ menea a, nworɛ biala nne nu kyɛ ngɔmaa bɛkɔfa kukununiɛ bɛkɔhɔ ná mangyire kwaadu horɛ bɔ bafa babɔ ye ɔ.”

english_verse: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
translation_verse: “Nana Agripa, ɔyɛ me fɛ paa kyɛ ɛnɛ kyẽa ye ngyi wɔ nyunu mesa me nwo wɔ kwaadu wora bɔ Yudafoɛ babɔ me ne nwo ɔ,

english_verse: You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
translation_verse: ye titire ne, wɔ de ɛse Yudafoɛ amanneɛ mukoraa ne nningyein ahoroɔ bɔ yɛsu bɛ nwo aporowaa ɔ. Yiti mesrɛ wɔ ala, nya aboterɛ na tie me.

english_verse: All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other.
translation_verse: Bɛse me dada, na sɛ bekoli adanzeɛ po a, ofi ye ahyɛaseɛ ne amukoraa, nde Farisii fekue bɔ odi yɛ som mmeraa so pɛpɛɛpɛ ne anu niɛ.

english_verse: Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me.
translation_verse: Na sɔ bɔhyɛ komapɛ ne ala yeɛ yɛ mmusua kure buru ne nyɔ ne bɛ nye la so kyɛ bekonya ɔ, na bɛsɔne Nyameɛ alehyeleɛ ne alesaleɛ biala. Nana Agripa, ɔnate anyelasoɛ he ati yeɛ Yudafoɛ afa edwirɛ ato me so ye.

english_verse: Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
translation_verse: Na nzu ati yeɛ ɔyɛ se ma ɛmɔ, Yudafoɛ, kyɛ ɛmɔkole bekoli kyɛ Nyameɛ tingye awufoɛ ɔ?

english_verse: I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed.
translation_verse: Na nikyee bɔ nyɔle ye wɔ Yerusalem hɔ ɛne. Nyane tumi mvili asɔfo mbanyi nemɔ berɛ, na ndole agyidifoɛ pee kuku nu. Né beku bɛ po a, me koso mefoa so kyɛ behũ bɛ.

english_verse: I often had them punished in our synagogues, and I tried to make them give up their faith. In fact, I was so angry with them, that I went looking for them in foreign cities.
translation_verse: Ndaa ndwene bɛ so wɔ nyianu sua biala nu, na mmɔle mmɔden kyɛ ngɔhyɛ bɛ maa bɛkɔpa bɛ gyidie si ɔ. Me nye borole bɛ so paa maa afei de po ndanene bɛ nye alaa ngondwuli amanvrafoɛ nguro so. Pɔɔlo adwenesakyera nwo dwirɛ (Asomafoɛ

english_verse: King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests.
translation_verse: “Ɔnate ɛhe ati asɔfo mbanyi ne mane me ate ɔne tumi krataa kyɛ ngɔ Damasko.

english_verse: About noon I saw a light brighter than the sun. It flashed from heaven on me and on everyone traveling with me.
translation_verse: Atee ne anu, eyiagyina, Nana, yeɛ nwuni kyɛ kanea bie bɔ ɔta tra eyia fi nyameɛso wale ɔɔpɛle me ne me mmango bɔ me ne bɛ nate ne nwo bra yiale ɔ.

english_verse: We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
translation_verse: Yɛ mukoraa yɛpepɛ yɛfini, na ebie dwudwo hyirele me wɔ Hebri dwudwolɛ nu kyɛ, ‘Sɔɔlo, Sɔɔlo, nzu ati yeɛ ɛtane me nye ye? Ɔyɛ se kyɛ ekotu wɔ gya kɔfa kɔwɔ nandwiehanɛniɛ ye pɔmaa noa buralɛ ɔ.’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I asked. Then the Lord answered, “I am Jesus! I am the one you are so cruel to.
translation_verse: Na nzele kyɛ, ‘Wɔ nwa ɛne, Awurade?’ Na Awurade buale me kyɛ, ‘Me ole Yesu bɔ ɛtane ye nye ne.

english_verse: Now stand up. I have appeared to you, because I have chosen you to be my servant. You are to tell others what you have learned about me and what I will show you later.”
translation_verse: Nakoso dwɔso gyina wɔ gya so. Na ɛhe ati yeɛ ɔmaa nyele me nwo ali ngyirele wɔ ɔ; maye wɔ kyɛ ɛyɛ me somvoɛ ne danzeniɛ wɔ nningyein bɔ anwu ye ne bɔ mebaaye mekyire wɔ ne nwo.

english_verse: The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to.
translation_verse: Ngɔbɔ wɔ nwo waen ngofi Yisraelfoɛ ne Amaenmaensofoɛ bɔ mesoma wɔ maa ɛkɔ bɛ berɛ ne sa nu.

english_verse: I want you to open their eyes, so they will turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and by faith in me they will become part of God's holy people.”
translation_verse: Memaa ekobukye bɛ nye, ná ɛye bɛ fi awosii nu ba kanea nu, na ɛye bɛ fi Abɔnzam tumi bo ɛfa bɛ ba Nyameɛ berɛ; amaa banya bɔnefakyɛ, ne tenaberɛ wɔ bɛ bɔ bafa bɛ gyidie bɔ ɔwɔ me nu bate bɛ nwo nemɔ anu.’ Pɔɔlo ka ye adwumayɔlɛ nwo dwirɛ

english_verse: King Agrippa, I obeyed this vision from heaven.
translation_verse: “Yiti, Nana Agripa, manyɛ asoserɛ wɔ nyameɛso nyekyire ne nwo.

english_verse: First I preached to the people in Damascus, and then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea. Finally, I went to the Gentiles and said, “Stop sinning and turn to God! Then prove what you have done by the way you live.”
translation_verse: Na nnili moa ngane edwirɛ ne wɔ Damasko, afei Yerusalem, ɔne Yudea maen ne anu mukoraa, ɔne Amaenmaensofoɛ nu; kyɛ bɛsakyera b’adwene bɛbra Nyameɛ berɛ na bɛbɔ bra bɔ okyire kyɛ basakyera b’adwene ɔ.

english_verse: That is why some men grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.
translation_verse: Ɔnate ɛhe ati Yudafoɛ hyele me wɔ asɔneyɛɛ sua nu bɔ ahaa bɛpena kyɛ beku me ɔ.

english_verse: But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
translation_verse: Nakoso Nyameɛ abɔ me nwo waen alaa maa waadwu ɛnɛ kyẽa ye; yiti yeɛ ɔmaa ngyi wa medi adanzeɛ mekyire mmenia mukoraa ɔ: atitire ne kwahweabaa mɔ. Na edwirɛ bɔ ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ ne Mose hã tole berɛ kyɛ okosi ne ala yeɛ mekã ɔ:

english_verse: I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: kyɛ Kristo ne konwu amaneɛ okoli moa kodwɔso kofi awufoɛ nu ná wabɔ kanea ne nwo dawure wahyire Yudafoɛ ne Amaenmaensofoɛ.”

english_verse: Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo wɔ so bɔ ɔye ye noa nen, Festo teane ye kyɛ, “Pɔɔlo, w’adwene nyɛ adwuma! Wɔ nwomaa sualɛ pembe ne abɔ afa wɔ ti anu!”

english_verse: But Paul replied, “Honorable Festus, I am not crazy. What I am saying is true, and it makes sense.
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo buale kyɛ, “Daasebrɛ Festo, m’adwene yɛ adwuma! Na mmom nahorɛ turoloo yeɛ mekã ɔ.

english_verse: None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
translation_verse: Ofikyɛ Nana se sɔ dwirɛ hemɔ amu, na masi m’ahone yeɛ mekã mekyire ye ɔ; yeɛ mede medi koso kyɛ ɛhemɔ nu biala nne berɛ bɔ ɔnze ɔ, ɔnate kyɛ banyɔ ɛhemɔ nu biala wɔ mvealeɛ nu.

english_verse: Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
translation_verse: Nana Agripa, aso ede ngɔmhyɛlɛfoɛ nemɔ dwirɛ di? Mese kyɛ ede di.”

english_verse: Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
translation_verse: Na Agripa sele Pɔɔlo kyɛ, “Ɔhale kãa ná ɛmaa nyɛle Kristoniɛ!”

english_verse: Paul answered, “Whether it takes a short time or a long time, I wish you and everyone else who hears me today would become just like me! Except, of course, for these chains.”
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo buale kyɛ, “Sɛ ɔhale kãa oo, ɔhhale kãa oo, me de mesrɛ Nyameɛ kyɛ nna wɔ ngome, na mmom bɛ bɔ betie me ɛnɛ ye amukoraa koso kɔyɛ kyɛ me ala; sana ngɔnzɔngɔnzɔ bɔ ogua me ye yeɛ ɔbboka so ɔ!”

english_verse: Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up.
translation_verse: Afei ɛhene ne, amrado ne, yeɛ Bɛnise ne bɛ bɔ baha ne amu dwɔsole.

english_verse: But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
translation_verse: Befili berɛ bɛhɔle ahameɛ kãa, na besisele bɛ nwo kyɛ, “Sɔ biaa he ɔyyɔle nikye fee bɔ ɔfata ewue anaa kuku nu nnaa ɔ.”

english_verse: Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
translation_verse: Na Agripa sele Festo kyɛ, “Sɛ biaa he anga kyɛ okuro kyɛ ye dwirɛ ne dwu Kaesare nyunu de a, ahaa ɔsɛ kyɛ yɛyakyi ye maa ɔkɔ.”

english_verse: When it was time for us to sail to Rome, Captain Julius from the Emperor's special troops was put in charge of Paul and the other prisoners.
translation_verse: Nziɛ ye bɔ besili ye pi kyɛ ɔsɛ kyɛ yɛkɔ Yitalia nen, bɛfale Pɔɔlo ne kukunufoɛ biemɔ bewurale Roman asraafoɛ ɛyaa so panyi bie sa. Oli Yulio. Né ɔboka “Roman Panyi Asraafoɛ Fekue” ne aso.

english_verse: We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to some ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia sailed on the ship with us.
translation_verse: Yɛɛfole ɛlɛen bie bɔ ofi Adramitiom ɔkɔ Asia mbɔtam, na ɛlɛen ne tuli. Né Aristako, Makedonianiɛ bɔ ofi Tɛsalonika boka yɛ so.

english_verse: The next day we came to shore at Sidon. Captain Julius was very kind to Paul. He even let him visit his friends, so they could give him whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyene ne, yɛɛgyinane Sidon. Yulio yɛle Pɔɔlo paa paa. Ɔmane ye ate maa ɔhɔle ye damvo mɔ berɛ oolele nningyein kãa bɔ okohia ɔ.

english_verse: When we left Sidon, the winds were blowing against us, and we sailed close to the island of Cyprus to be safe from the wind.
translation_verse: Yɛtu yɛfili Sidon nen, né mvrama ne tu yia yɛ. Yiti yɛɛfale supɔ Kipro aseɛnwo dɔ nekaa bie bɔ né mvrama ndu nyia yɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Then we sailed south of Cilicia and Pamphylia until we came to the port of Myra in Lycia.
translation_verse: Yɛfale Kilikia ne Pamfilia manzini nu ɛpo so yɛwale Lisia manzini nu kuro bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Mira so.

english_verse: There the army captain found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy. So he ordered us to board that ship.
translation_verse: Berɛ yeɛ asraafoɛ ɛyaa so panyi ne nwuni ɛlɛen bie bɔ ofi Aleksandria kyɛ ɔkɔ Yitalia ɔ, na ɔmaa yɛɛfole.

english_verse: We sailed along slowly for several days and had a hard time reaching Cnidus. The wind would not let us go any farther in that direction, so we sailed past Cape Salmone, where the island of Crete would protect us from the wind.
translation_verse: Né ɛlɛen ne ngora kɔ paa biala, yiti yɛlili ngyẽa pee wɔ nzue so; na yɛfɛle paa koraa yeɛ yɛpingye Kinido ɔ. Mvrama ne amma yangɔ yɛ nyunu moa ko; yiti yɛɛfale supɔ Krete aseɛnwo dɔ nekaa bie bɔ né mvrama ndu nyia yɛ ɔ, na yɛtrale Salmone mboanoa.

english_verse: We went slowly along the coast and finally reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.
translation_verse: Yɛfale ɛpo ne noa alaa, na yɛfɛle paa koraa yeɛ yɛbaadwu nekaa bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye “Ɛlɛen Agyinaleɛ Paa” bɔ opingye Lasia kuro ne ɔ. Pɔɔlo tu akwandufoɛ nemɔ foɛ

english_verse: By now we had already lost a lot of time, and sailing was no longer safe. In fact, even the Great Day of Forgiveness was past.
translation_verse: Yɛsɛkyele mmerɛ pee wɔ berɛ; na nzue ne aso falɛ yɛle suro, ɔnate kyɛ né Bɔnefakyɛ Akɔngyere Kyẽa ne apɛnu. Yiti Pɔɔlo tuli bɛ foɛ kyɛ,

english_verse: Then Paul spoke to the crew of the ship, “Men, listen to me! If we sail now, our ship and its cargo will be badly damaged, and many lives will be lost.”
translation_verse: “Biamɔ, menwu ye kyɛ yɛ ateetulɛ ye anu kɔyɛ suro kɔma yɛ. Nna kyɛ nningyein pee yeɛ yɛkɔhwere, anaa ɛlɛen ne yeɛ ɔkɔsɛkye angome, na mmom annea a, yɛ ngoa po kɔpɛ so.”

english_verse: But Julius listened to the captain of the ship and its owner, rather than to Paul.
translation_verse: Nakoso asraafoɛ ɛyaa so panyi ne amva edwirɛ bɔ Pɔɔlo hane ne, na mmom ɔfale bɔ ɛlɛen mene ne ne ɛlɛenhanɛfoɛ ne hane ne.

english_verse: The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. Because of this, almost everyone agreed that we should at least try to sail along the coast of Crete as far as Phoenix. It had a harbor that opened toward the southwest and northwest, and we could spend the winter there. The Storm at Sea
translation_verse: Né ɛlɛen agyinaleɛ berɛ ɔtte mayee bɔ bedi prakasua mmerɛ ne berɛ a ɔyɛ yé ɔ, yiti mmeni soma yɛle kyɛ bɛkɔtoa ateetulɛ ne aso, na sɛ ɔkɔyɛ yee po a, baadwu Fonike na bali prakasua mmerɛ ne berɛ. Fonike te ɛlɛen agyinaleɛ wɔ Krete, na ɔla sorɔ ne eyia atɔleɛ, ɔne ngwaen ne eyia atɔleɛ b’afia. Mvrama piri bie tuli ɛpo ne aso

english_verse: When a gentle wind from the south started blowing, the men thought it was a good time to do what they had planned. So they pulled up the anchor, and we sailed along the coast of Crete.
translation_verse: Mvrama bɛtɛɛ bie hyɛle ye bo bɔ fili ngwaen na benyane adwene kyɛ bɛ nzusuleɛ ne kɔhɔ so kama. Yiti betuli sɛkyɛ ne, na yɛfale Krete ɛpo ne noa pɛɛ.

english_verse: days you have been so worried that you haven't eaten a thing.
translation_verse: Nakoso wangyɛ biala, mvrama piri bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye “Sorɔ-Afiteleɛ” bɔ fili supɔ ne aso.

english_verse: The wind struck the ship, and we could not sail against it. So we let the wind carry the ship.
translation_verse: Oofini ɛlɛen ne bɔ né yɛyɔ ye nwo hwee biala a ɔnyɛ yé ɔ, yiti yɛyakyili maa ɔhwene yɛ hɔle.

english_verse: We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place,
translation_verse: Ɔpale yɛ sɔ alaa maa yɛɛgyinane supɔ kaaba bie bɔ bɛfrɛ ye Klɔda so. Na yɛbɔle mmɔden yɛbɔle ɛlɛen ba bɔ bafa babɔ y’ɛlɛen piri ne nwo waen.

english_verse: but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
translation_verse: Bɛpagyale ɛlɛen ba ne, na bɛkyekyele bɛbɔle ɛlɛen piri ne. Né besuro kyɛ ɛlɛen ne kɔɔfofo Anweaa sire ne aso, yiti bɛfandili bɔ ɔsosɔ ɛlɛen ne anu maa mvrama ne fale ye hɔle.

english_verse: The storm was so fierce that the next day they threw some of the ship's cargo overboard.
translation_verse: Mvrama piri ne hɔle so fale yɛ hyinini alaa; yiti aleɛ hyene ne, ɛlɛenhanɛfoɛ nemɔ gyili ɛlɛen ne anu nningyein ne bie beguale nzue nu.

english_verse: Then on the third day, with their bare hands they threw overboard some of the ship's gear.
translation_verse: Ye ɛlɛsa ne aso, bɛ bɔbɔ befindini ɛlɛen ne nwo nningyein ne bie beguale.

english_verse: For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
translation_verse: Ngyẽa pee se hɔle bɔ né yɛ nye nnwuni eyia anaa nzramaa ɔ; yeɛ kyɛbɔ mvrama ne si gyinane yɛ so ne ati yɛ anyelasoɛ amukoraa yiele maa yɛnwuni kyɛ yɛ ti kekã. Pɔɔlo kyekye bɛ wora

english_verse: Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men: You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss.
translation_verse: Ngyẽa pee se hɔle bɔ né yɛllili hwee ɔ. Yiti Pɔɔlo dwɔso gyinane b’afia sele bɛ kyɛ, “Biamɔ, sɛ ɛmɔtiele me yeɛ yandu yamvi Krete a, ahaa yɛngonwu sɔ amaneɛ ne nningyein bɔ yahwere ye.

english_verse: But now I beg you to cheer up, because you will be safe. Only the ship will be lost.
